Moses said to Aaron, "Say to the whole community of the children of Israel: Come near before the Lord, for he has heard your grumbling."
As Aaron was speaking to the whole community of the children of Israel, they turned toward the wilderness, and there the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud.
The Lord said to Moses,

"I have heard the grumbling of the children of Israel. Speak to them: At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will have your fill of bread; then you will know that I am the Lord your God."
That very evening quails came up and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew all around the camp.
When the layer of dew lifted, there on the surface of the wilderness was a fine crust, fine as frost on the ground.
When the children of Israel saw it, they said to one another, "What is it?" for they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, "This is the bread the Lord has given you to eat.
This is what the Lord has commanded: Gather as much of it as each of you can eat, about two litres per person, according to the number of you; each of you is to take enough for those in his tent."
The children of Israel did so: they gathered it, some more, some less.
But when they measured it, the one who had gathered much had nothing left over, and the one who had gathered little had no lack: each had gathered as much as he could eat.
Moses said to them, "No one is to keep any of it until morning."
But some did not listen to Moses and kept part of it until morning; it became full of worms and stank, and Moses was angry with them.
They gathered it every morning, each as much as he could eat; and when the sun grew hot, it melted.
On the sixth day they gathered a double portion of bread, about four litres per person. All the leaders of the community came and reported it to Moses.

He said to them, "This is what the Lord has said: Tomorrow is a day of rest, a sabbath consecrated to the Lord. Bake what you want to bake, and boil what you want to boil, and put all that is left over in reserve until morning."
They put it in reserve until morning, as Moses had commanded, and it did not stink, nor were there any worms in it.
Moses said, "Eat it today, for today is the sabbath of the Lord; today you will find none in the fields.
For six days you will gather it, but on the seventh day, the sabbath, there will be none."
On the seventh day some of the people went out to gather it, but they found nothing.
The Lord said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to keep my commandments and my laws?
See: it is the Lord who has given you the sabbath; that is why on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. Let each of you stay where you are; let no one leave his place on the seventh day."
So the people rested from all work on the seventh day.
The house of Israel gave this bread the name manna. It was like coriander seed, white, and it tasted like a honey cake.

Moses said, "This is what the Lord has commanded: Fill a measure of about two litres with it, to be kept from age to age, so that they may see the bread with which I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of the land of Egypt."
Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar, put in it about two litres of manna, and set it before the Lord, to be kept from age to age."
As the Lord had commanded Moses, Aaron set it before the Testimony, to be kept.
The children of Israel ate the manna for forty years, until they came to a land where people lived; they ate the manna until they reached the borders of the land of Canaan.
The measure they used held about two litres.
The whole community of the children of Israel set out from the wilderness of Sin, moving by stages at the command of the Lord, and camped at Rephidim; but there was no water for the people to drink.
The people quarreled with Moses: "Give us water to drink!" Moses answered them, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you put the Lord to the test?"
There the people, thirsty, grumbled against Moses: "Why did you bring us up out of Egypt? To make us die of thirst, us and our children and our livestock?"
Moses cried out to the Lord, "What am I to do with this people? A little more and they will stone me!"
The Lord said to Moses, "Go on ahead of the people, take with you some of the elders of Israel, and take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
I will be standing there before you, on the rock at Horeb; you will strike the rock, and water will come out of it, and the people will drink." Moses did so, in the sight of the elders of Israel.

He named that place Massah and Meribah, that is, Testing and Quarreling, because of the quarreling of the children of Israel and because they had put the Lord to the test, saying, "Is the Lord among us or not?"
Then Amalek came and attacked Israel at Rephidim.
Moses said to Joshua, "Choose some men for us, and go out to fight Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill, with the staff of God in my hand."
Joshua did as Moses had told him and fought Amalek, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
Now as long as Moses held up his hand, Israel prevailed; but as soon as he let his hand drop, Amalek prevailed.

When Moses' hands grew heavy, they took a stone and put it under him; he sat on it, while Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side and one on the other; so his hands remained steady until sunset.
And Joshua overcame Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
The Lord said to Moses, "Write this down in a book as a memorial, and declare it to Joshua: I will completely blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven."
Moses built an altar and named it "The Lord is my banner."
He said, "A hand upon the banner of the Lord! The Lord is at war with Amalek from age to age."
Jethro, priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, heard of all that God had done for Moses and for Israel his people: that the Lord had brought Israel out of Egypt.
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses' wife, whom Moses had sent back,
and her two sons. One was named Gershom, for Moses had said, "I am a stranger in a foreign land";
the other was named Eliezer, for, "The God of my father came to my help; he delivered me from Pharaoh's sword."
So Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came to Moses in the wilderness, where he was camped at the mountain of God, bringing Moses' sons and wife.
He sent word to Moses, "I, Jethro, your father-in-law, am coming to you, with your wife and her two sons."
Moses went out to meet his father-in-law; he bowed down and kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent.
Moses told his father-in-law all that the Lord had done to Pharaoh and to Egypt for Israel's sake, all the hardships they had met on the way, and how the Lord had delivered them.
Jethro rejoiced over all the good that the Lord had done for Israel, delivering it from the hand of Egypt.
Jethro said, "Blessed be the Lord, who has delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of Pharaoh, who has snatched this people from the grip of Egypt!
Now I know that the Lord is greater than all the gods, for he acted against those who treated Israel with arrogance."
Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, offered a burnt offering and sacrifices to God; and Aaron and all the elders of Israel came to share the meal with Moses' father-in-law before God.
The next day Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood before Moses from morning till evening.

When his father-in-law saw all that Moses was doing for the people, he said, "What is this you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people stand before you from morning till evening?"
Moses answered his father-in-law, "It is because the people come to me to inquire of God.
When they have a dispute, it comes before me; I decide between one man and another, and I make known the decrees of God and his laws."
Moses' father-in-law said to him, "What you are doing is not good.
You will wear yourself out, you and this people who are with you, for the task is too heavy for you: you cannot do it alone.
Now listen to me, I will give you some advice, and may God be with you: be the representative of the people before God, and bring their disputes to God.
Teach them the decrees and the laws, and make known to them the way they are to walk and the conduct they are to keep.
But choose, from all the people, capable men who fear God, trustworthy men who cannot be bribed, and set them over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.

Let them render justice to the people at all times: every important matter they are to bring to you, but every minor matter they are to judge themselves. Ease your burden this way, and let them carry it with you.
If you do this, and God so commands you, you will be able to endure, and all this people too will go home in peace."
Moses listened to his father-in-law and did all that he had said.
Moses chose capable men out of all Israel and set them at the head of the people: leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens.
They rendered justice to the people at all times: the difficult matters they brought to Moses, but every minor matter they judged themselves.
Then Moses let his father-in-law go, and he returned to his own country.
In the third month after the children of Israel had left the land of Egypt, on that very day, they came to the wilderness of Sinai.
Having set out from Rephidim, they reached the wilderness of Sinai and camped there; Israel camped there, facing the mountain.
Moses went up to God, and the Lord called to him from the mountain: "This is what you are to say to the house of Jacob, what you are to declare to the children of Israel:
You have seen for yourselves what I did to Egypt, and how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.
Now then, if you listen to my voice and keep my covenant, you will be my own treasured possession among all the peoples, for all the earth is mine.
You will be for me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words you are to say to the children of Israel."
Moses went back and called the elders of the people and set before them all these words that the Lord had commanded him.
All the people answered with one voice, "Everything the Lord has said, we will do." And Moses brought the people's words back to the Lord.

The Lord said to Moses, "I am going to come to you in a dense cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may put their faith in you forever." And Moses told the Lord the people's words.
The Lord said to Moses, "Go to the people; today and tomorrow consecrate them, and have them wash their clothes.
Let them be ready for the third day, for on the third day the Lord will come down on Mount Sinai, in the sight of all the people.
You are to set a boundary for the people all around, saying: Take care not to go up the mountain or to touch its edge; whoever touches the mountain will be put to death.
No hand is to touch him: he will be stoned or shot through with arrows; whether beast or human, he will not live. When the ram's horn sounds a long blast, they may go up the mountain."
Moses came down from the mountain to the people; he consecrated the people, and they washed their clothes.
He said to the people, "Be ready for the third day; do not go near a woman."
On the third day, in the morning, there was thunder and lightning, a heavy cloud on the mountain, and a very loud blast of the horn: in the camp all the people trembled.
Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
Mount Sinai was all in smoke, because the Lord had come down on it in fire; the smoke rose from it like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain shook violently.
The blast of the horn grew louder and louder: Moses spoke, and God answered him in the thunder.
The Lord came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain; he called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
The Lord said to Moses, "Go down and warn the people not to break through toward the Lord to look, or many of them will perish.
Even the priests who approach the Lord must consecrate themselves, lest the Lord break out against them."
Moses said to the Lord, "The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for you yourself warned us: Set a boundary around the mountain and treat it as sacred."
The Lord said to him, "Go down; then you will come back up, you and Aaron with you. But do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to the Lord, lest he break out against them."
So Moses went down to the people and told them.
Then God spoke all these words:
"I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You shall have no other gods before my face.
You shall not make for yourself an idol, any image of what is in the heavens above, or on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.

You shall not bow down before them or serve them, for I, the Lord your God, am a jealous God, punishing the guilt of the fathers upon the children, to the third and fourth generation, of those who hate me,
but showing faithful love to the thousandth generation, to those who love me and keep my commandments.
You shall not invoke the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord will not leave unpunished anyone who invokes his name in vain.
Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
For six days you shall labour and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a sabbath for the Lord your God: you shall do no work, neither you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your manservant, nor your maidservant, nor your livestock, nor the stranger who resides in your towns.
For in six days the Lord made the heavens, the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and he rested on the seventh day; that is why the Lord blessed the sabbath day and made it holy.
Honour your father and your mother, so that your days may be long on the land that the Lord your God is giving you.
You shall not commit murder.
You shall not commit adultery.
You shall not steal.
You shall not give false testimony against your neighbour.

You shall not covet your neighbour's house; you shall not covet your neighbour's wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that belongs to your neighbour."
All the people perceived the thunder and the lightning, the sound of the horn and the smoking mountain. When they saw it, the people trembled and stood at a distance.
They said to Moses, "Speak to us yourself, and we will listen; but do not let God speak to us, or we will die."
Moses answered the people, "Do not be afraid, for God has come to test you, and so that the fear of him may remain before you, to keep you from sinning."
The people stood at a distance, while Moses approached the dense cloud where God was.
The Lord said to Moses, "This is what you are to say to the children of Israel: You have seen for yourselves that I have spoken to you from the heavens.
You shall not make gods of silver alongside me, and you shall not make yourselves gods of gold.

You shall make me an altar of earth, on which you will offer your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your cattle. In every place where I cause my name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
If you make me an altar of stones, you shall not build it of cut stones; for by using your chisel on it, you would profane it.
You shall not go up to my altar by steps, so that your nakedness may not be exposed on it."

titres.titre: The Book of the Covenant: slaves

versets.t: These are the rules you are to set before them.
When you buy a Hebrew slave, he is to serve for six years; in the seventh year he is to go free, without paying anything.
If he came alone, he is to go out alone; if he was married, his wife is to go out with him.
If his master gave him a wife, and she has borne him sons or daughters, the wife and her children belong to the master, and he is to go out alone.
But if the slave declares, 'I love my master, my wife, and my children; I do not want to go free,'
then his master is to bring him before God, lead him to the door or the doorpost, and pierce his ear with an awl; and he is to serve him forever.
When a man sells his daughter as a servant, she is not to go free as the male slaves go free.
If she does not please her master, who had intended her for himself, he is to let her be redeemed; he has no right to sell her to foreigners, since he would have betrayed her.
If he intends her for his son, he is to treat her according to the rights of daughters.
If he takes another wife, he is not to withhold from the first her food, her clothing, or her marital rights.
And if he does not grant her these three things, she is to go free without payment, without paying anything.
Whoever strikes a man and kills him is to be put to death.
But if he did not lie in wait for him, and God allowed him to fall into his hand, I will appoint for you a place where he may take refuge.
But if a man, in his cunning, attacks his neighbour to kill him by treachery, you are to take him even from my altar, so that he may die.
Whoever strikes his father or his mother is to be put to death.
Whoever kidnaps a man, whether he has sold him or the man is still found in his possession, is to be put to death.
Whoever curses his father or his mother is to be put to death.
When men quarrel, and one strikes the other with a stone or with his fist without killing him, but the man has to take to his bed,
if he gets up and can walk about outdoors with his staff, the one who struck him is to go unpunished; he is only to pay for the lost time and the cost of the recovery.
When a man strikes his slave or his servant with a rod, and the slave dies under his hand, he is to be punished.
But if the slave survives a day or two, he is not to be punished, for the slave is his own property.

When men are fighting and they strike a pregnant woman, if the child is born without further harm, the guilty man is to be fined, according to what the woman's husband demands of him, and he is to pay as the judges determine.
But if there is harm, you are to give life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
When a man strikes the eye of his slave or his servant and destroys it, he is to let him go free in compensation for his eye.
And if he knocks out a tooth of his slave or his servant, he is to let him go free in compensation for his tooth.
When an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox is to be stoned and its flesh is not to be eaten; but the owner of the ox is not to be held liable.

However, if the ox had been in the habit of goring, and its owner had been warned but did not keep it in, and the ox kills a man or a woman, the ox is to be stoned and its owner too is to be put to death.
If a ransom is imposed on him, he is to give to redeem his life all that is imposed on him.
If the ox gores a son or a daughter, the same rule is to be applied to him.
If the ox gores a slave or a servant, the owner is to give thirty pieces of silver to the master, and the ox is to be stoned.
When a man leaves a cistern open, or digs one and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
the owner of the cistern is to make it good: he is to compensate the owner of the animal in silver, and the dead animal will be his.
When one man's ox injures his neighbour's ox and it dies, they are to sell the live ox and divide its price between them; they are also to divide the dead animal.
But if it was known that the ox had been in the habit of goring, and its owner did not keep it in, he is to pay ox for ox, and the dead animal will be his.
When a man steals an ox or a sheep, and slaughters or sells it, he is to repay five oxen for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.
If a thief is caught breaking through a wall, and is struck so that he dies, there is no bloodguilt for him.
But if the sun had risen on him, there is bloodguilt for him. The thief must make restitution: if he has nothing, he is to be sold for his theft.
If the stolen animal, ox, donkey, or sheep, is found alive in his hands, he is to make twofold restitution.
When a man grazes a field or a vineyard bare, letting his livestock graze in another's field, he is to make restitution with the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.
When a fire breaks out and spreads to the brambles and consumes a stack of grain, standing grain, or a field, the one who started the fire is to make good the damage.
When a man entrusts silver or goods to another for safekeeping, and they are stolen from that man's house, the thief, if he is found, is to make twofold restitution.
If the thief is not found, the owner of the house is to present himself before God, to swear that he has not laid a hand on his neighbour's property.

In every case of fraud, whether it concerns an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost object of which someone says, 'That is it!' the case of both parties is to come before God; the one whom God declares guilty is to make twofold restitution to his neighbour.
When a man entrusts to another a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal for safekeeping, and it dies, is injured, or is carried off with no witness,

an oath before the Lord is to settle the matter between the two parties: the keeper is to swear that he has not laid a hand on his neighbour's property; the owner is to accept this oath, and the other is to make no restitution.
But if the animal was stolen from him, he is to compensate its owner.
If it was torn apart by a wild animal, he is to bring the proof of it: he is not to pay for what was torn.
When a man borrows an animal from his neighbour, and it is injured or dies in the owner's absence, he must make it good.
If the owner was present, he is to make no restitution; if the animal was hired, it is covered by the hire price.
When a man seduces a virgin who is not engaged, and lies with her, he is to pay the bride-price for her and take her as his wife.
If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he is to pay a sum equal to the bride-price for virgins.
You shall not let a sorceress live.
Whoever lies with an animal is to be put to death.
Whoever sacrifices to any gods other than the Lord alone is to be devoted to destruction.
You shall not mistreat the stranger or oppress him, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan.
If you do mistreat them and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry:
my anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword; your wives will become widows and your children orphans.
If you lend money to any of my people, to the poor person among you, you shall not be a usurer to him; you shall charge him no interest.
If you take your neighbour's cloak in pledge, you are to return it to him before sunset,
for it is his only covering, the garment for his body: in what else would he sleep? If he cries out to me, I will hear him, for I am compassionate.
You shall not blaspheme God, and you shall not curse a leader of your people.
You shall not delay to offer the firstfruits of your harvest and of your winepress. The firstborn of your sons you shall give to me.
You shall do the same for your cattle and your sheep: it is to stay seven days with its mother, and on the eighth day you shall give it to me.
You shall be holy men for me: you shall not eat the flesh of an animal torn apart in the fields; you shall throw it to the dogs.

titres.titre: The sabbath and the sabbatical year

versets.t: You shall not spread a false report. Do not join hands with the wicked by giving unjust testimony.
You shall not follow the crowd in doing wrong; in a lawsuit you shall not testify by siding with the majority so as to pervert justice.
Nor shall you show favour to the poor in his lawsuit.
If you come upon your enemy's ox or his donkey wandering off, you are to bring it back to him.
If you see the donkey of the one who hates you fallen under its load, do not leave it there: you are to help him unload it.
You shall not deny justice to the poor among you in his lawsuit.
Keep far from a false charge. Do not put to death the innocent and the righteous, for I will not acquit the guilty.
You shall accept no bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.
You shall not oppress the stranger: you know what the stranger feels, you who were strangers in the land of Egypt.
For six years you shall sow your land and gather in its produce.

But in the seventh year you shall let it rest and leave it fallow: the poor of your people will eat from it, and what they leave, the wild animals will eat. You shall do the same for your vineyard and your olive grove.
For six days you shall do your work; but on the seventh day you shall cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your maidservant and the stranger may be refreshed.
Be attentive to all that I have told you. You shall not utter the name of other gods; do not let it be heard on your lips.
Three times a year you shall celebrate a feast in my honour.

You shall keep the feast of unleavened bread: for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I have commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for it was in that month that you came out of Egypt; and no one is to appear before me empty-handed.

You shall also keep the feast of the Harvest, of the firstfruits of your labours, of what you have sown in the fields; and the feast of the Ingathering, at the end of the year, when you gather in from the fields the fruit of your labours.
Three times a year all your men are to appear before the Master, the Lord.
You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, and the fat of my feast shall not be kept until morning.
You shall bring the best firstfruits of your land to the house of the Lord your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk.
See, I am sending an angel ahead of you, to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.
Be on your guard in his presence and listen to his voice; do not defy him, for he would not forgive your rebellion: my name is in him.
But if you truly listen to his voice and do all that I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and an adversary to your adversaries.
For my angel will go ahead of you and bring you in among the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, and I will destroy them.
You shall not bow down before their gods, nor serve them, nor imitate their practices; but you shall utterly destroy them and shatter their sacred stones.
You shall serve the Lord your God: he will bless your bread and your water, and I will remove sickness from among you.
In your land there will be no woman who miscarries and none who is barren, and I will give you a full number of days.
I will send my terror ahead of you, I will throw into confusion all the peoples you come upon, and I will make all your enemies flee before you.
I will send the hornets ahead of you, to drive the Hivites, the Canaanites, and the Hittites out of your way.
I will not drive them out before you in a single year, lest the land become a desert and the wild animals multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them out before you, until you have increased and taken possession of the land.

I will set your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River; for I will hand over to you the inhabitants of the land, and you will drive them out before you.
You shall make no covenant with them or with their gods.
They shall not dwell in your land, lest they make you sin against me: if you served their gods, it would become a snare to you.
The Lord said to Moses, "Come up to the Lord, you, Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel; you are to bow down at a distance.
Moses alone is to approach the Lord; the others are not to come near, and the people are not to come up with him."
Moses came and reported to the people all the words of the Lord and all the rules. All the people answered with one voice, "Everything the Lord has said, we will do."
Moses wrote down all the words of the Lord. Early the next morning he built an altar at the foot of the mountain, with twelve sacred stones for the twelve tribes of Israel.
Then he sent young Israelites to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice young bulls to the Lord as peace offerings.
Moses took half of the blood and put it in basins; the other half he threw against the altar.
He took the book of the covenant and read it to the people, who declared, "Everything the Lord has said, we will do and we will obey."
Moses took the blood, sprinkled it on the people, and said, "This is the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made with you, on the basis of all these words."
Then Moses went up with Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel.
They saw the God of Israel: under his feet was something like a pavement of sapphire, as pure as heaven itself.
He did not lay a hand on these chosen ones of the children of Israel: they beheld God, and then they ate and drank.
The Lord said to Moses, "Come up to me on the mountain and stay there; I will give you the tablets of stone, the law and the commandment that I have written for their instruction."
Moses set out, with Joshua his servant, and Moses went up to the mountain of God.
He said to the elders, "Wait here for us until we return. You have Aaron and Hur with you: whoever has a dispute may go to them."
Moses went up the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
The glory of the Lord settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day the Lord called to Moses from within the cloud.
In the sight of the children of Israel, the glory of the Lord appeared like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain.
Moses entered the cloud and went up the mountain. He stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

titres.titre: The table for the bread of the Presence

versets.t: The Lord said to Moses:
Tell the children of Israel to set aside an offering for me; from everyone whose heart moves him, you are to receive my offering.
This is the offering you are to receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
violet purple, red purple, brilliant crimson, fine linen, and goat hair;
ram skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
oil for the lamp, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and other stones to be set for the ephod and the breastpiece.
They are to make me a sanctuary, and I will dwell among them.
You are to make everything according to the model of the Dwelling and all its furnishings that I am going to show you.
They are to make an ark of acacia wood, a metre twenty-five long, seventy-five centimetres wide, and seventy-five centimetres high.
You are to overlay it with pure gold, inside and out, and put a gold moulding around it.
You are to cast four gold rings for it and fasten them to its four feet: two rings on one side and two rings on the other.
You are to make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold,
and you are to insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry it.
The poles are to remain in the rings of the ark: they are not to be removed from it.
You are to place in the ark the Testimony that I will give you.
You are to make a mercy seat of pure gold, a metre twenty-five long and seventy-five centimetres wide.
You are to make two cherubim of gold, hammered work, at the two ends of the mercy seat:
make one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other; you are to make them of one piece with the mercy seat, at its two ends.
The cherubim are to have their wings spread upward, sheltering the mercy seat with their wings, facing each other, their gaze turned toward the mercy seat.
You are to place the mercy seat on top of the ark, and in the ark you are to put the Testimony that I will give you.
There I will meet with you; from above the mercy seat, between the two cherubim that are on the ark of the Testimony, I will give you all my commands for the children of Israel.
You are to make a table of acacia wood, a metre long, fifty centimetres wide, and seventy-five centimetres high.
You are to overlay it with pure gold and put a gold moulding around it.
You are to make for it a rim of about eight centimetres, with a gold moulding around the rim.
You are to make four gold rings for it and fasten them at the four corners, at its four feet.
The rings are to be placed close to the rim, to hold the poles used to carry the table.
You are to make the poles of acacia wood, overlaid with gold, and by them the table is to be carried.
You are to make its plates, its cups, its pitchers, and its bowls for the drink offerings: you are to make them of pure gold.
On the table you are to place before me, continually, the bread of the Presence.
You are to make a lampstand of pure gold; the lampstand is to be hammered work, its base and its shaft; its cups, its buds, and its flowers are to be of one piece with it.
Six branches are to extend from its sides: three branches of the lampstand on one side, three branches on the other.

On one branch, three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with bud and flower; on the next branch, three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with bud and flower: so for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
On the shaft of the lampstand itself, four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their buds and their flowers:
a bud under the first two branches, a bud under the next two, a bud under the last two, for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
The buds and the branches are to be of one piece with it: the whole, a single piece of pure gold, hammered work.
You are to make its seven lamps; they are to be set up so as to light the space in front of it.
Its snuffers and its trays are to be of pure gold.
It is to be made, with all these accessories, from about thirty-four kilos of pure gold.
See that you make everything according to the model that is shown to you on the mountain.

You are to make the Dwelling with ten curtains of finely twisted linen, violet purple, red purple, and brilliant crimson; you are to make them decorated with cherubim, the work of a skilled craftsman.
Each curtain is to be fourteen metres long and two metres wide: all the curtains are to be the same size.
Five curtains are to be joined to one another, and the other five likewise.
You are to make loops of violet purple along the edge of the first curtain, at the end of the set; you are to do the same along the edge of the last curtain of the second set.
You are to make fifty loops on the first curtain and fifty loops at the end of the curtain of the second set, the loops matching one another.
You are to make fifty gold clasps and join the curtains to one another with the clasps: so the Dwelling will form a single whole.
You are also to make curtains of goat hair to form a tent over the Dwelling; you are to make eleven of them.
Each curtain is to be fifteen metres long and two metres wide: the eleven curtains are to be the same size.
You are to join five curtains together and six curtains together, and you are to fold the sixth over at the front of the tent.
You are to make fifty loops along the edge of the last curtain of the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the curtain of the second set.
You are to make fifty bronze clasps, insert the clasps into the loops, and join the tent together so that it forms a single whole.
As for the surplus that hangs over from the curtains of the tent, the half curtain in excess is to hang over the back of the Dwelling.
The excess in the length of the curtains of the tent, about fifty centimetres on one side and fifty centimetres on the other, is to hang over the sides of the Dwelling, on both sides, to cover it.
You are to make for the tent a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
You are to make upright frames of acacia wood for the Dwelling.
Each frame is to be five metres high and seventy-five centimetres wide.
Each frame is to have two tenons joined to each other: you are to do the same for all the frames of the Dwelling.
You are to make the frames for the Dwelling: twenty frames for the south side, facing the noon sun.
You are to place forty silver bases under the twenty frames: two bases under one frame, for its two tenons, and two bases under each following frame.
For the second side of the Dwelling, the north side, twenty frames,
and their forty silver bases: two bases under one frame, two bases under the next.
For the rear of the Dwelling, toward the west, you are to make six frames.
You are to make two frames for the corners of the Dwelling, at the rear;
they are to be paired from the bottom and firmly joined at the top, at the level of the first ring: so it is to be for both, at the two corners.
So there will be eight frames, with their silver bases, sixteen bases: two bases under one frame, two bases under the next.
You are to make crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames of one side of the Dwelling,
five crossbars for the frames of the other side, and five crossbars for the frames at the rear, toward the west.
The middle crossbar, halfway up the frames, is to run from one end to the other.
You are to overlay the frames with gold, make their rings of gold to hold the crossbars, and overlay the crossbars with gold.
You are to set up the Dwelling according to the plan that was shown to you on the mountain.
You are to make a veil of violet purple, red purple, brilliant crimson, and finely twisted linen; it is to be made decorated with cherubim, the work of a skilled craftsman.
You are to hang it on four columns of acacia wood overlaid with gold, fitted with gold hooks and set on four silver bases.

You are to hang the veil beneath the clasps; there, behind the veil, you are to bring in the ark of the Testimony. The veil will be for you the separation between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies.
You are to place the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony, in the Holy of Holies.
You are to place the table outside the veil, and the lampstand opposite the table, on the south side of the Dwelling; the table you are to put on the north side.
For the entrance of the tent, you are to make a screen of violet purple, red purple, brilliant crimson, and finely twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.
You are to make for this screen five columns of acacia wood, which you are to overlay with gold; their hooks are to be of gold, and you are to cast for them five bronze bases.
You are to make the altar of acacia wood: two metres fifty long, two metres fifty wide, the altar is to be square, and a metre fifty high.
You are to make horns for it at its four corners; the horns are to be of one piece with it, and you are to overlay it with bronze.
You are to make its containers for gathering the greasy ashes, its shovels, its basins, its forks, and its firepans: all these utensils you are to make of bronze.
You are to make for it a grating of bronze, in the form of a grill, and fasten to the grill four bronze rings at its four corners.
You are to place it under the ledge of the altar, low down, so that it reaches halfway up the altar.
You are to make for the altar poles of acacia wood, which you are to overlay with bronze.
The poles are to be inserted into the rings, and they will be on both sides of the altar when it is carried.
You are to make it hollow, of boards. It is to be made as it was shown to you on the mountain.
You are to make the courtyard of the Dwelling. On the south side, facing the noon sun, the courtyard is to have curtains of finely twisted linen, fifty metres long for that side.
There are to be twenty columns, with their twenty bronze bases; the hooks of the columns and their rods are to be of silver.

Likewise on the north side, along its length, there are to be curtains fifty metres long, with twenty columns and their twenty bronze bases; the hooks of the columns and their rods are to be of silver.
Along the width of the courtyard, on the west side, there are to be curtains twenty-five metres long, with ten columns and their ten bases.
Along the width of the courtyard, on the east side, toward the sunrise, twenty-five metres,
there are to be curtains seven metres fifty long on one side of the entrance, with three columns and their three bases;
and on the other side, curtains seven metres fifty long, with three columns and their three bases.

For the gate of the courtyard there is to be a screen ten metres long, of violet purple, red purple, brilliant crimson, and finely twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer, with its four columns and their four bases.
All the columns of the courtyard are to be joined by silver rods; their hooks are to be of silver and their bases of bronze.
The courtyard is to be fifty metres long, twenty-five metres wide, and two metres fifty high; the curtains are to be of finely twisted linen, and the bases of bronze.
All the utensils for the service of the Dwelling, all its pegs, and all the pegs of the courtyard are to be of bronze.
You are to command the children of Israel to bring you pure olive oil, pressed out, for the lamp, so as to keep a lamp burning continually.

In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that is before the Testimony, Aaron and his sons are to tend it so that it burns from evening till morning before the Lord. This is a perpetual decree for the children of Israel, from age to age.

titres.titre: The gold plate and the other garments

versets.t: As for you, bring near to yourself, from among the sons of Israel, your brother Aaron and his sons with him, so that they may serve me as priests: Aaron, with Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron.
For your brother Aaron you shall make sacred garments, for glory and dignity.
You shall speak to all the skilled workers, whom I have filled with a spirit of skill, and they shall make Aaron's garments to consecrate him to serve me as priest.

These are the garments they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, an embroidered tunic, a headdress and a sash. They shall make sacred garments for your brother Aaron and for his sons, so that they may serve me as priests.
They shall use gold, violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, and fine linen.
They shall make the ephod of gold, of violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, and of finely twisted linen, the work of a skilled craftsman.
It shall have two shoulder pieces joined together, attached at its two edges.
The band that fastens it and is of one piece with it shall be of the same workmanship: gold, violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, and finely twisted linen.
You shall take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel:
six of their names on the first stone, and the six remaining names on the second, in the order of their birth.
As a gem-cutter engraves a seal, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel; you shall mount them in gold settings.
You shall fasten the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, as a memorial for the sons of Israel: Aaron shall bear their names before the Lord, on his two shoulders, as a memorial.
You shall make gold settings,
and two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords; and you shall attach the corded chains to the settings.
You shall make the breastpiece of judgment, the work of a skilled craftsman, made like the ephod: gold, violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, and finely twisted linen.
It shall be square and doubled, about twenty-five centimetres on each side.
You shall set in it mounted stones, in four rows. First row: a carnelian, a topaz and an emerald;
second row: a garnet, a sapphire and a diamond;
third row: an opal, an agate and an amethyst;
fourth row: a chrysolite, an onyx and a jasper. They shall be mounted in gold settings.
The stones shall bear the names of the sons of Israel: twelve, as many as their names; each engraved like a seal, with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
For the breastpiece you shall make chains of pure gold, twisted like cords.
For the breastpiece you shall make two gold rings, which you shall fasten at its two ends.
You shall pass the two gold cords through the two rings, at the ends of the breastpiece,
and the two ends of the two cords you shall fasten to the two settings, on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, at the front.
You shall make two more gold rings, which you shall place at the two ends of the breastpiece, on its inner edge, on the side facing the ephod.
You shall make yet two more gold rings, which you shall fasten low on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, at the front, near their point of attachment, above the waistband of the ephod.
The breastpiece shall be bound by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of violet, so that it stays above the waistband and does not come loose from the ephod.
So Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel on his heart, on the breastpiece of judgment, when he enters the sanctuary: a perpetual memorial before the Lord.

In the breastpiece of judgment you shall place the Urim and the Thummim, and they shall be on Aaron's heart when he comes before the Lord: thus Aaron shall bear the judgment of the sons of Israel on his heart continually, before the Lord.
You shall make the robe of the ephod entirely of violet.
In the middle there shall be an opening for the head, with a woven edge all around it, like the opening of a coat of mail, so that it does not tear.
On its lower hem you shall make pomegranates of violet, purple and bright crimson, all around, with gold bells between them, all around:
a gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, on the hem of the robe, all around.
Aaron shall wear it for the service: its sound will be heard when he enters the sanctuary before the Lord, and when he comes out, so that he may not die.
You shall make a plate of pure gold, and engrave on it, as on a seal: Consecrated to the Lord.
You shall fasten it with a cord of violet on the headdress, on the front of the headdress.

It shall be on Aaron's forehead: Aaron shall bear the guilt incurred in the holy things that the sons of Israel consecrate, in all their sacred gifts; it shall be on his forehead continually, so that they may find favour before the Lord.
You shall weave the tunic of fine linen, make a headdress of fine linen, and make a sash, the work of an embroiderer.
For Aaron's sons you shall make tunics and sashes; you shall make turbans for them, as a mark of glory and dignity.
You shall clothe your brother Aaron with them, and his sons with him; you shall anoint them, ordain them and consecrate them, so that they may serve me as priests.
Make linen undergarments for them to cover their naked flesh; they shall reach from the waist to the thighs.

Aaron and his sons shall wear them when they enter the tent of meeting, or when they approach the altar to minister in the sanctuary; thus they will not incur guilt and die. This is a perpetual decree for him and for his descendants after him.
This is what you shall do to consecrate them to serve me as priests. Take a young bull and two rams without blemish,
unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers brushed with oil; you shall make them of fine wheat flour.
You shall put them in a single basket and present them in the basket, together with the bull and the two rams.
You shall bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and wash them with water.
You shall take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod and the breastpiece; and you shall gird him with the waistband of the ephod.
You shall set the headdress on his head, and on the headdress fasten the sacred diadem.
You shall take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
You shall bring his sons forward and clothe them with tunics.
You shall gird Aaron and his sons with a sash and fasten the turbans on them. The priesthood shall belong to them by a perpetual decree. Thus you shall ordain Aaron and his sons.
You shall bring the bull before the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the bull's head.
You shall slaughter the bull before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
You shall take some of the bull's blood and put it with your finger on the horns of the altar; then you shall pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.
You shall take all the fat that covers the entrails, the fatty mass over the liver, the two kidneys and the fat around them, and burn it all on the altar.
But the flesh of the bull, its hide and its dung, you shall burn with fire outside the camp: it is a sin offering.
You shall take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the ram's head.
You shall slaughter the ram, take its blood, and splash it against the sides of the altar all around.
You shall cut the ram into pieces, wash its entrails and legs, and place them on its pieces and its head.
You shall burn the whole ram on the altar: it is a burnt offering to the Lord, a pleasing aroma, an offering made to the Lord by fire.
You shall take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the ram's head.

You shall slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear and of his sons', on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot; then you shall splash the blood against the sides of the altar all around.

You shall take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle them on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments: thus Aaron and his garments shall be consecrated, and his sons and their garments with him.
You shall take the fat of the ram, the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails, the fatty mass of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh, for this is the ram of ordination.
You shall also take, from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the Lord, one loaf of bread, one cake made with oil, and one wafer.
You shall put all of it in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and wave it as a wave offering before the Lord.
Then you shall take it back from their hands and burn it on the altar, on top of the burnt offering, as a pleasing aroma before the Lord: it is an offering made to the Lord by fire.
You shall take the breast of the ram of Aaron's ordination and wave it as a wave offering before the Lord: it shall be your portion.
You shall consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution, which were waved and set aside from the ram of ordination, for Aaron and for his sons.

This shall be, by a perpetual decree, the portion that Aaron and his sons receive from the sons of Israel, for it is a contribution; this contribution, taken from their peace offerings, shall be their contribution to the Lord.
Aaron's sacred garments shall pass after him to his sons, who shall wear them to receive their anointing and ordination.
Whichever of his sons becomes priest in his place and enters the tent of meeting to minister in the sanctuary shall wear them for seven days.
You shall take the ram of ordination and cook its flesh in a holy place.
Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram and the bread in the basket, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
They shall eat what was used to make atonement for their ordination and consecration; but no unauthorized person shall eat of it, for these are holy things.
If any of the flesh of the ordination or of the bread remains until morning, you shall burn what is left with fire: it shall not be eaten, for it is a holy thing.
You shall do for Aaron and his sons exactly as I have commanded you; you shall take seven days to ordain them.
Each day you shall offer a bull as a sin offering, for atonement; you shall purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it: thus the altar shall be most holy, and whatever touches the altar shall be holy.
This is what you shall offer on the altar: two lambs a year old, each day, without interruption.
You shall offer one lamb in the morning, and the other at twilight.
With the first lamb you shall offer about two litres of fine flour mixed with about one litre of virgin olive oil, and a drink offering of about one litre of wine.
The second lamb you shall offer at twilight, with the same grain offering and the same drink offering as in the morning, as a pleasing aroma, an offering made to the Lord by fire.
This shall be the perpetual burnt offering, throughout your generations, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the Lord: there I will meet you to speak with you.
There I will meet the sons of Israel, and that place will be consecrated by my glory.
I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar; I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests.
I will dwell among the sons of Israel, and I will be their God.
They shall know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt to dwell among them: I am the Lord their God.
You shall make an altar for burning incense; you shall make it of acacia wood.
It shall be square, fifty centimetres long and fifty centimetres wide, and one metre high; its horns shall be of one piece with it.
You shall overlay it with pure gold, the top, the walls all around, and the horns, and you shall put a gold moulding around it.
You shall make two gold rings for it, below the moulding, on its two sides; you shall place them on the two sides, to hold the poles used to carry it.
You shall make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
You shall place the altar in front of the veil that hides the ark of the Testimony, in front of the mercy seat that covers the Testimony, where I will meet you.
On this altar Aaron shall burn fragrant incense every morning, when he tends the lamps;
and when Aaron sets up the lamps at twilight, he shall burn it again: this is the perpetual incense before the Lord, throughout your generations.
You shall not offer on it any profane incense, nor burnt offering, nor grain offering, and you shall pour no drink offering on it.

Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on its horns: with the blood of the sin offering, offered for atonement, he shall make atonement on this altar once a year, throughout your generations. This altar is most holy to the Lord.
The Lord said to Moses:
When you take a census of the sons of Israel, counting them, each shall pay the Lord a ransom for his life at the time of the counting, so that no plague may strike them on that occasion.

This is what everyone included in the census shall give: a half measure of silver, according to the sanctuary standard weight, which is about eleven grams and is divided into twenty small parts; this half measure, about six grams, shall be the contribution set aside for the Lord.
Everyone included in the census, twenty years old and over, shall give the Lord's contribution.
The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than this half measure, when giving the Lord's contribution to ransom your lives.
You shall receive the ransom money from the sons of Israel and devote it to the service of the tent of meeting; it shall be a memorial for the sons of Israel before the Lord, to ransom your lives.
The Lord said to Moses:
You shall make a bronze basin, with its bronze stand, for washing; you shall place it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and feet in it.
When they enter the tent of meeting, they shall wash with this water, so that they may not die; likewise when they approach the altar to minister, to burn an offering to the Lord.
They shall wash their hands and feet, so that they may not die. This shall be a perpetual decree for them, for Aaron and for his descendants, throughout their generations.
The Lord said to Moses:
Take the finest spices: about six kilos of liquid myrrh, half as much fragrant cinnamon, that is about three kilos, about three kilos of fragrant cane,
about six kilos of cassia, according to the sanctuary standard weight, and about three and a half litres of olive oil.
You shall make of these a holy anointing oil, a fragrant blend prepared by the perfumer's art: this shall be the holy anointing oil.
With it you shall anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the Testimony,
the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offerings and all its utensils, the basin and its stand.
You shall consecrate them, and they shall be most holy: whatever touches them shall be holy.
You shall also anoint Aaron and his sons, and consecrate them to serve me as priests.
You shall say to the sons of Israel: This shall be my holy anointing oil, throughout your generations.
It shall not be poured on the body of just anyone, and you shall not make any other of the same composition: it is holy, and it shall be holy to you.
Whoever compounds anything like it, or puts any of it on an unauthorized person, shall be cut off from his people.
The Lord said to Moses: Take fragrant spices: stacte, onycha and galbanum, these spices with pure frankincense, in equal parts.
You shall make of these an incense, a fragrant blend by the perfumer's art, salted, pure and holy.
You shall grind part of it into fine powder, which you shall place before the Testimony, in the tent of meeting, where I will meet you: it shall be most holy to you.
The incense you make in this way, you shall not make any for yourselves of the same composition: it shall be holy to you, reserved for the Lord.
Whoever makes anything like it to enjoy its fragrance shall be cut off from his people.

titres.titre: The sabbath, sign of the covenant

versets.t: The Lord said to Moses:
See, I have called by name Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with the spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding and knowledge, for every kind of craft:
to design projects and carry them out in gold, silver and bronze,
to cut stones for setting, to work wood, and to do every kind of craft.
And I have appointed with him Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan. I have put skill in the heart of all the skilled workers, so that they may make everything I have commanded you:
the tent of meeting, the ark of the Testimony, the mercy seat that covers it, and all the furnishings of the tent,
the table and its utensils, the lampstand of pure gold and all its utensils, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offerings and all its utensils, the basin and its stand,
the ceremonial garments, the sacred garments of Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons for the priestly service,
the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense for the sanctuary. They shall make everything just as I have commanded you.
The Lord said to Moses:

As for you, speak to the sons of Israel: You shall keep my sabbaths, for the sabbath is a sign between me and you, throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am the Lord who makes you holy.
You shall keep the sabbath, for it is holy to you. Whoever profanes it shall be put to death: anyone who does any work on that day shall be cut off from among his people.
Work shall be done for six days; but the seventh day is a sabbath of complete rest, consecrated to the Lord. Whoever does any work on the sabbath day shall be put to death.
The sons of Israel shall keep the sabbath, celebrating it throughout their generations: it is a perpetual covenant.
Between me and the sons of Israel it is a sign forever; for in six days the Lord made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day he ceased his work and drew breath.
When he had finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the Testimony, tablets of stone written with the finger of God.

When the people saw that Moses was slow to come down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said to him: "Come, make us gods to go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him."
Aaron answered them: "Take off the gold rings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons and your daughters, and bring them to me."
So all the people took off the gold rings from their ears and brought them to Aaron.
He received the gold from their hands, shaped it with a tool, and made it into a calf of cast metal. Then they said: "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt."
When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before the calf and proclaimed: "Tomorrow, a feast to the Lord!"
The next day they rose early, offered burnt offerings and presented peace offerings. The people sat down to eat and drink, then got up to revel.
The Lord said to Moses: "Go, go down, for your people, whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves.

They have quickly turned aside from the way I commanded them: they have made themselves a calf of cast metal, they have bowed down to it, they have offered it sacrifices, and they have said: These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt."
The Lord said further to Moses: "I see that this people is a stiff-necked people.
Now leave me alone: let my anger blaze against them, and I will consume them; but of you I will make a great nation."
Moses implored the Lord his God, saying: "Why, Lord, should your anger blaze against your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt by your great power and your mighty hand?

Why should the Egyptians say: It was with evil intent that he brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them from the face of the earth? Turn back from the heat of your anger; relent from the harm you intend against your people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself: I will multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven, and all this land of which I have spoken, I will give to your descendants, and they shall possess it forever."
And the Lord relented from the harm he had said he would do to his people.
Moses turned and went down from the mountain, the two tablets of the Testimony in his hand, tablets written on both sides, on the one side and the other.
These tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
Joshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted, and he said to Moses: "There is a sound of battle in the camp."
Moses answered: "It is not the sound of a song of victory, nor the sound of a song of defeat: what I hear is the sound of singing."
As he approached the camp, Moses saw the calf and the dancing. His anger blazed; he threw down the tablets he was holding and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf they had made, burned it in the fire, ground it to powder, scattered it on the water, and made the sons of Israel drink it.
Moses said to Aaron: "What did this people do to you, that you brought such a great sin upon them?"
Aaron answered: "Do not let my lord's anger blaze! You yourself know that this people is bent on evil.
They said to me: Make us gods to go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him.
So I said to them: Whoever has gold, take it off. They took it off and gave it to me; I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf."
Moses saw that the people were running wild, for Aaron had let them run wild, to the derision of their enemies.
Moses stood at the gate of the camp and said: "Whoever is for the Lord, come to me!" And all the sons of Levi gathered around him.

He said to them: "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Let each man strap on his sword. Go back and forth through the camp from gate to gate, and let each man kill his brother, his friend, his neighbour."
The sons of Levi did as Moses had said, and about three thousand men of the people fell that day.
Moses said: "Today you have been ordained for the Lord, each at the cost of his son and his brother, so that he may grant you his blessing today."
The next day Moses said to the people: "You have committed a great sin. Now I will go up to the Lord: perhaps I can obtain forgiveness for your sin."
Moses returned to the Lord and said: "Alas! This people has committed a great sin: they have made themselves a god of gold.
And now, if you would only forgive their sin! But if not, then blot me out of the book you have written."
The Lord answered Moses: "Whoever has sinned against me, that one I will blot out of my book.
Now go, lead the people where I told you; behold, my angel will go before you. But on the day of my reckoning, I will hold them accountable for their sin."
And the Lord struck the people, because of the calf they had made, the one Aaron had made.

titres.titre: The Lord refuses to go up among the people

versets.t: The Lord said to Moses: "Go, set out from here, you and the people you brought up from the land of Egypt, to the land I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, saying: I will give it to your descendants.
I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite.
Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I myself will not go up among you, for you are a stiff-necked people, and I might destroy you on the way."
When the people heard this word of disaster, they mourned, and no one put on his ornaments.

The Lord had said to Moses: "Say to the sons of Israel: You are a stiff-necked people; if I were to go up among you for a single moment, I would destroy you. Now take off your ornaments, and I will see what I am to do with you."
So the sons of Israel stripped off their ornaments, from Mount Horeb onward.

Moses used to take the tent and pitch it for himself outside the camp, some distance away; he called it the tent of meeting. Anyone who sought the Lord would go out to the tent of meeting, outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise, each standing at the entrance of his own tent, and follow Moses with their eyes until he entered the tent.
As soon as Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance of the tent, and the Lord would speak with Moses.
All the people would see the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent; all the people would rise and bow down, each at the entrance of his own tent.

The Lord would speak with Moses face to face, as a man speaks with his friend. Then Moses would return to the camp; but his servant, the young Joshua, son of Nun, did not leave the inside of the tent.

Moses said to the Lord: "See, you tell me to lead this people up, but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. Yet you have said: I know you by name, and you have found favour in my sight.
Now, if I have truly found favour in your sight, make your ways known to me, that I may know you and continue to find favour in your sight. Consider that this nation is your people."
The Lord said: "I myself will go, and I will give you rest."
Moses said to him: "If you do not go yourself, do not lead us up from here.

How will it be known that I have found favour in your sight, I and your people, unless you go with us? It is by this that we shall be distinguished, I and your people, from all the peoples on the face of the earth."
The Lord said to Moses: "This very thing you have asked, I will do, for you have found favour in my sight and I know you by name."
Moses said: "Show me your glory, I pray."
The Lord answered: "I will make all my goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim before you the name of the Lord; I show favour to whom I show favour, and I have mercy on whom I have mercy.
But," he said, "you cannot see my face, for no one can see me and live."
The Lord said further: "Here is a place beside me: you shall stand on the rock.
When my glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
Then I will take away my hand, and you will see my back; but my face may not be seen."
The Lord said to Moses: "Cut two tablets of stone like the first ones, and I will write on these tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered.
Be ready in the morning; in the morning you shall come up Mount Sinai and stand there before me, on the top of the mountain.
No one shall come up with you, and no one shall be seen anywhere on the mountain; not even the flocks and herds shall graze in front of this mountain."
Moses cut two tablets of stone like the first ones; he rose early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the Lord had commanded him, carrying the two tablets of stone in his hand.
The Lord came down in the cloud and stood there beside him; and he proclaimed the name of the Lord.
The Lord passed before him and proclaimed: "The Lord, the Lord, a God of tenderness and compassion, slow to anger, rich in faithful love and faithfulness,

who keeps his faithful love for thousands of generations, who forgives fault, rebellion and sin, yet leaves nothing unpunished, and who punishes the fault of the fathers on the children and grandchildren, to the third and fourth generation."
At once Moses bowed to the ground and worshipped.
He said: "If I have truly found favour in your sight, Lord, may my Lord go among us! Yes, this is a stiff-necked people; but forgive our fault and our sin, and make us your heritage."

The Lord said: "Behold, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will work wonders such as have never been created on all the earth or in any nation; and all the people around you will see the work of the Lord, for what I am about to do with you is awesome.
Observe what I command you today. Behold, I am driving out before you the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite.
Take care not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land you are entering, lest they become a snare among you.
On the contrary, you shall tear down their altars, break their sacred pillars and cut down their sacred poles.
You shall not bow down to any other god; for the Lord, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.
Do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land: when they prostitute themselves to their gods and offer them sacrifices, they will invite you, and you will eat of their sacrifice;
you will take some of their daughters for your sons, and their daughters, prostituting themselves to their gods, will lead your sons to prostitute themselves to their gods.
You shall not make yourselves gods of cast metal.

You shall keep the feast of Unleavened Bread: for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I have commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of ripe grain, for it was in the month of ripe grain that you came out of Egypt.
Every firstborn of the womb is mine, as well as every firstborn male of your livestock, cattle and sheep alike.
The firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb; if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem. No one shall appear before me empty-handed.
Six days you shall work, but on the seventh day you shall rest; even in plowing time and harvest you shall rest.
You shall celebrate the feast of Weeks, that of the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the feast of Ingathering at the turn of the year.
Three times a year all your men shall appear before the Master, the Lord, the God of Israel.
For I will dispossess the nations before you and enlarge your territory, and no one will covet your land when you go up to appear before the Lord your God three times a year.
You shall not offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, and the sacrifice of the feast of Passover shall not remain overnight until morning.
You shall bring the best firstfruits of your soil to the house of the Lord your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk."
The Lord said to Moses: "Put these words in writing, for it is on these words that I make a covenant with you and with Israel."
Moses stayed there with the Lord forty days and forty nights, without eating bread or drinking water; and he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten words.

When Moses came down from Mount Sinai, the two tablets of the Testimony in his hand, as he came down from the mountain, he did not know that the skin of his face was radiant because he had spoken with the Lord.
Aaron and all the sons of Israel saw Moses: behold, the skin of his face was radiant, and they were afraid to come near him.
Moses called to them; Aaron and all the leaders of the community came back to him, and Moses spoke with them.
After that, all the sons of Israel came near, and he passed on to them all the commands the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
Whenever Moses went in before the Lord to speak with him, he would remove the veil until he came out; then he would come out and tell the sons of Israel what he had been commanded.
The sons of Israel would then see Moses' face, the skin of his face radiant; and Moses would put the veil back over his face, until he went in again to speak with the Lord.
Moses gathered the whole community of the sons of Israel and said to them: These are the things the Lord has commanded you to do.
For six days work shall be done, but the seventh day shall be for you a holy day, a sabbath of complete rest for the Lord; whoever does any work on it shall be put to death.
You shall not light a fire in any of your dwellings on the sabbath day.
Moses said to the whole community of the sons of Israel: This is what the Lord has commanded:
Set aside from your possessions an offering for the Lord. Let everyone whose heart is willing bring the Lord's offering: gold, silver and bronze;
violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, fine linen and goat hair;
ram skins dyed red, fine leather and acacia wood;
oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and other stones for setting in the ephod and the breastpiece.
Let all the skilled workers among you come and make everything the Lord has commanded:
the Dwelling, its tent and its covering, its clasps, its frames, its crossbars, its pillars and its bases;
the ark and its poles, the mercy seat and the veil that screens it;
the table, its poles and all its utensils, and the bread of the offering;
the lampstand for the light, its utensils and its lamps, and the oil for the light;
the altar of incense and its poles, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance, at the entrance of the Dwelling;
the altar of burnt offerings, its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils, the basin and its stand;
the hangings of the court, its pillars and bases, and the screen for the gate of the court;
the pegs of the Dwelling and the pegs of the court, with their ropes;
the ceremonial garments for ministering in the sanctuary, the sacred garments of Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons for the priestly service.
The whole community of the sons of Israel withdrew from Moses' presence.
Then everyone whose heart moved them, everyone whose spirit prompted them, came and brought the Lord's offering for the work of the tent of meeting, for all its service and for the sacred garments.
They came, both men and women, all who were generous of heart: they brought brooches, earrings, rings, necklaces, all kinds of gold objects, each presenting an offering of gold to the Lord.
Everyone who had violet, purple or bright crimson yarn, fine linen, goat hair, ram skins dyed red, or fine leather, brought them.
Everyone who set aside an offering of silver or bronze brought it as an offering to the Lord; and everyone who had acacia wood useful for the work brought it.
All the skilled women spun with their hands and brought what they had spun: violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, and fine linen.
All the women whose hearts moved them, with their skill, spun the goat hair.
The leaders brought the onyx stones and the stones for setting in the ephod and the breastpiece,
the spice and the oil for the light, for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense.
All the sons of Israel, men and women, whose hearts prompted them to contribute to the work the Lord had commanded to be done through Moses, brought a freewill offering to the Lord.
Moses said to the sons of Israel: See, the Lord has called by name Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
He has filled him with the spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding and knowledge for every kind of craft,
to design projects and carry them out in gold, silver and bronze,
to cut stones for setting, to work wood, and to carry out every kind of artistic craft.
He has also given him the gift of teaching, to him and to Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

He has filled them with skill to do every kind of work: of the engraver, the embroiderer, the weaver in violet, purple and bright crimson yarn and fine linen, and the weaver. They do every kind of work and design projects.

Bezalel, Oholiab and all the skilled workers, to whom the Lord had given wisdom and understanding to know how to carry out all the work of the service of the sanctuary, did everything as the Lord had commanded.
Moses called Bezalel, Oholiab and all the skilled workers to whom the Lord had given skill, all whose hearts prompted them to come forward to the work and carry it out.

They received from Moses the whole offering the sons of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary, to carry it out. Every morning the people kept bringing him freewill offerings.
Then all the skilled workers who were carrying out the various works of the sanctuary each left the work they were doing
and came to tell Moses: "The people are bringing much more than is needed for the work the Lord has commanded to be done."
So Moses sent this order through the camp: "Let no one, man or woman, prepare anything more for the offering of the sanctuary." So the people stopped bringing:
the materials were enough, and more than enough, to carry out all the work.

All the skilled workers among those who carried out the work made the Dwelling: ten curtains of finely twisted linen, of violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, decorated with cherubim, the work of a skilled craftsman.
Each curtain was fourteen metres long and two metres wide: all the curtains were the same size.
Five curtains were joined to one another, and likewise the other five.
Loops of violet were made along the edge of the outermost curtain of the first set, and likewise along the edge of the outermost curtain of the second set.
Fifty loops were made on the first curtain and fifty loops on the end curtain of the second set, the loops corresponding to one another.
Fifty gold clasps were made, and the curtains were joined to one another with the clasps: so the Dwelling formed a single whole.
Curtains of goat hair were made to form a tent over the Dwelling: eleven of them were made.
Each curtain was fifteen metres long and two metres wide: the eleven curtains were the same size.
Five curtains were joined together separately, and six curtains separately.
