Fifty loops were made along the edge of the outermost curtain of the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the curtain of the second set.
Fifty bronze clasps were made to join the tent together into a single whole.
For the tent a covering of ram skins dyed red was made, and over it a covering of fine leather.
For the Dwelling the frames of acacia wood were made, set upright.
Each frame was five metres high and seventy-five centimetres wide.
Each frame had two tenons joined to one another: this was done for all the frames of the Dwelling.
The frames of the Dwelling were made: twenty frames for the south side, toward the south.
Forty silver bases were placed under the twenty frames: two bases under one frame, for its two tenons, and two bases under each following frame.
For the second side of the Dwelling, the north side, twenty frames were made,
with their forty silver bases: two bases under one frame, two bases under the next.
For the rear of the Dwelling, toward the west, six frames were made.
Two frames were made for the corners of the Dwelling, at the rear;
they were paired from the bottom and joined together right up to the top, at the level of the first ring: this was done for both, at the two corners.
So there were eight frames, with their silver bases, sixteen bases: two bases under each frame.
Crossbars of acacia wood were made: five for the frames on one side of the Dwelling,
five crossbars for the frames on the other side, and five crossbars for the frames at the rear, toward the west.
The middle crossbar was made to run halfway up the frames, from one end to the other.
The frames were overlaid with gold, their rings to hold the crossbars were made of gold, and the crossbars were overlaid with gold.
The veil was made of violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, and finely twisted linen, decorated with cherubim, the work of a skilled craftsman.
Four pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold were made for it, with gold hooks, and four silver bases were cast for them.
For the entrance of the tent a screen was made of violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, and finely twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer,
with its five pillars and their hooks; their capitals and their rods were overlaid with gold, and their five bases were of bronze.
Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood: one metre twenty-five long, seventy-five centimetres wide and seventy-five centimetres high.
He overlaid it with pure gold, inside and out, and put a gold moulding around it.
He cast for it four gold rings, at its four feet: two rings on one side, two rings on the other.
He made poles of acacia wood, overlaid them with gold,
and inserted the poles into the rings, on the sides of the ark, to carry it.
He made a mercy seat of pure gold, one metre twenty-five long and seventy-five centimetres wide.
He made two cherubim of gold, hammered work, at the two ends of the mercy seat:
one cherub at one end, one cherub at the other; he made them of one piece with the mercy seat, at its two ends.
The cherubim had their wings spread upward, covering the mercy seat with their wings, facing each other, their gaze turned toward the mercy seat.
He made the table of acacia wood: one metre long, fifty centimetres wide and seventy-five centimetres high.
He overlaid it with pure gold and put a gold moulding around it.
He made around it a rim about eight centimetres wide, with a gold moulding around the rim.
He cast for it four gold rings, which he fastened at the four corners, at its four feet.
The rings were placed close to the rim, to hold the poles used to carry the table.
He made the poles of acacia wood, overlaid with gold, to carry the table.
He made of pure gold the utensils for the table: its plates, its dishes, its bowls and its pitchers for the drink offerings.
He made the lampstand of pure gold: the lampstand of hammered work, its base and its shaft; its cups, its buds and its blossoms were of one piece with it.
Six branches extended from its sides: three branches of the lampstand on one side, three branches on the other.

On one branch, three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with bud and blossom; on the next branch, three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with bud and blossom: so for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
On the shaft of the lampstand itself, four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their buds and their blossoms:
a bud under the first two branches, a bud under the next two, a bud under the last two, for the six branches extending from it.
The buds and the branches were of one piece with it: the whole, a single piece of pure gold, hammered work.
He made its seven lamps, its snuffers and its trays, of pure gold.
He made it, with all its utensils, from about thirty-four kilos of pure gold.
He made the altar of incense of acacia wood: fifty centimetres long, fifty centimetres wide, square, and one metre high; its horns were of one piece with it.
He overlaid it with pure gold, the top, the walls all around, and the horns, and he put a gold moulding around it.
He made two gold rings for it, below the moulding, on its two sides, to hold the poles used to carry it.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
He made the holy anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense, by the perfumer's art.

titres.titre: The altar of burnt offerings and the basin

versets.t: He made the altar of burnt offerings of acacia wood: two and a half metres long, two and a half metres wide, square, and one and a half metres high.
He made horns for it at its four corners; the horns were of one piece with it, and he overlaid it with bronze.
He made all the utensils of the altar: the pots for ashes, the shovels, the basins, the forks and the fire pans; he made all these utensils of bronze.
He made for the altar a bronze grating, in the form of a mesh, under its ledge, low down, reaching halfway up.
He cast four rings at the four corners of the bronze grating, to hold the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
He inserted the poles into the rings, on the sides of the altar, to carry it. He made it hollow, of planks.
He made the bronze basin, with its bronze stand, from the mirrors of the women who gathered at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He made the court. On the south side, toward the south, the hangings of the court, of finely twisted linen, for fifty metres,
with their twenty pillars and their twenty bronze bases; the hooks of the pillars and their rods were of silver.
On the north side, for fifty metres, with twenty pillars and their twenty bronze bases; the hooks of the pillars and their rods were of silver.
On the west side, hangings for twenty-five metres, with ten pillars and their ten bases; the hooks of the pillars and their rods were of silver.
On the east side, toward the sunrise, for twenty-five metres:
seven and a half metres of hangings on one side of the entrance, with three pillars and their three bases;
and on the other side, on either side of the gate of the court, seven and a half metres of hangings, with three pillars and their three bases.
All the hangings of the court, all around, were of finely twisted linen.
The bases of the pillars were of bronze, the hooks of the pillars and their rods of silver, and the overlay of their capitals of silver; all the pillars of the court were joined by silver rods.

The screen for the gate of the court was the work of an embroiderer, of violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, and finely twisted linen: ten metres long, two and a half metres high, like the hangings of the court.
Its four pillars and their four bases were of bronze, their hooks of silver, and the overlay of their capitals and their rods of silver.
All the pegs of the Dwelling and of the court, all around, were of bronze.
These are the accounts of the Dwelling, the Dwelling of the Testimony, drawn up at Moses' command, by the work of the Levites, under the direction of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, carried out all that the Lord had commanded Moses,
with Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver, a skilled craftsman and an embroiderer in violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, and fine linen.
All the gold used for the work, for all the labour of the sanctuary, this gold from the offerings, came to about one tonne, according to the sanctuary standard weight.
The silver collected at the census of the community came to about three and a half tonnes, according to the sanctuary standard weight:
about six grams a head, half the sanctuary standard weight, for everyone included in the census, twenty years old and over, that is six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty men.
The three and a half tonnes of silver were used to cast the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the veil: a hundred bases for these three and a half tonnes, about thirty-four kilos per base.
With the twenty kilos that remained, he made the hooks of the pillars, overlaid their capitals and joined them with rods.
The bronze of the offerings came to about two and a half tonnes.
With it he made the bases for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar with its bronze grating and all the utensils of the altar,
the bases of the court all around, the bases of the gate of the court, all the pegs of the Dwelling and all the pegs of the court, all around.

titres.titre: The work completed and presented to Moses

versets.t: With the violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, the ceremonial garments were made for ministering in the sanctuary, and the sacred garments of Aaron were made, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The ephod was made of gold, of violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, and of finely twisted linen.
The gold was hammered into thin plates and cut into threads to be worked into the violet, purple and bright crimson yarn and the fine linen, the work of a skilled craftsman.
For the ephod they made shoulder pieces joined together, attached at its two edges.
The band that fastened it was of one piece with it, of the same workmanship: gold, violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, and finely twisted linen, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
They worked the onyx stones, mounted in gold settings, engraved as a seal is engraved, with the names of the sons of Israel.
They fastened them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
They made the breastpiece, the work of a skilled craftsman, made like the ephod: gold, violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, and finely twisted linen.
It was square and doubled; they made it about twenty-five centimetres on each side, once folded.
They set in it four rows of stones. First row: a carnelian, a topaz and an emerald;
second row: a garnet, a sapphire and a diamond;
third row: an opal, an agate and an amethyst;
fourth row: a chrysolite, an onyx and a jasper, mounted in gold settings.
The stones bore the names of the sons of Israel, twelve for their names, engraved like seals, each with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
For the breastpiece they made chains of pure gold, twisted like cords.
They made two gold settings and two gold rings, which they fastened at the two ends of the breastpiece.
They passed the two gold cords through the two rings, at the ends of the breastpiece,
and fastened the two ends of the two cords to the two settings, on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, at the front.
They made two more gold rings, which they placed at the two ends of the breastpiece, on its inner edge, on the side facing the ephod.
They made yet two more gold rings, which they fastened low on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, at the front, near their attachment, above the waistband of the ephod.
They bound the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of violet, so that it stayed above the waistband and did not come loose from the ephod, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
They made the robe of the ephod, entirely woven of violet.
In the middle of the robe, an opening like that of a coat of mail, bordered with an edge all around, so that it would not tear.
On the hem of the robe they made pomegranates of violet, purple and finely twisted bright crimson.
They made bells of pure gold, which they placed between the pomegranates, on the hem of the robe, all around, between the pomegranates:
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, on the hem of the robe, all around, for the service, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
They made the tunics of fine linen, woven, for Aaron and his sons,
the headdress of fine linen, the turbans of fine linen, the undergarments of finely twisted linen,
and the sash of finely twisted linen, of violet, purple and bright crimson yarn, the work of an embroiderer, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
They made the plate of the sacred diadem, of pure gold, and engraved on it, as a seal is engraved: Consecrated to the Lord.
They fastened to it a cord of violet to attach it at the top of the headdress, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
So all the work of the Dwelling, of the tent of meeting, was completed. The sons of Israel had done everything as the Lord had commanded Moses; so they did.
They brought the Dwelling to Moses: the tent and all its furnishings, its clasps, its frames, its crossbars, its pillars and its bases;
the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the veil of separation;
the ark of the Testimony, its poles and the mercy seat;
the table, all its utensils and the bread of the offering;
the lampstand of pure gold, its lamps set in a row and all its utensils, and the oil for the light;
the golden altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tent;
the bronze altar, its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils, the basin and its stand;
the hangings of the court, its pillars and bases, the screen for the gate of the court, its ropes and its pegs, and all the utensils for the service of the Dwelling, for the tent of meeting;
the ceremonial garments for ministering in the sanctuary, the sacred garments of Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons for the priestly service.
The sons of Israel had carried out all the work exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses saw all the work: behold, they had carried it out as the Lord had commanded, they had done it well; and Moses blessed them.

titres.titre: The command to set up the Dwelling
The glory of the Lord fills the Dwelling

versets.t: The Lord said to Moses:
On the first day of the first month you shall set up the Dwelling, the tent of meeting.
You shall place in it the ark of the Testimony and screen the ark with the veil.
You shall bring in the table and arrange on it what is to be set out; you shall bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.
You shall place the golden altar of incense before the ark of the Testimony, and put the screen at the entrance of the Dwelling.
You shall place the altar of burnt offerings in front of the entrance of the Dwelling, of the tent of meeting.
You shall place the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
You shall set up the court all around, and put up the screen for the gate of the court.
You shall take the anointing oil and anoint the Dwelling and everything in it; you shall consecrate it with all its furnishings, and it shall be holy.
You shall anoint the altar of burnt offerings and all its utensils; you shall consecrate the altar, and the altar shall be most holy.
You shall anoint the basin and its stand, and consecrate it.
You shall bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and wash them with water.
You shall clothe Aaron with the sacred garments, anoint him and consecrate him to serve me as priest.
You shall bring his sons forward, clothe them with tunics,
and anoint them as you anointed their father, so that they may serve me as priests; their anointing shall confer on them a perpetual priesthood, throughout their generations.
Moses did everything as the Lord had commanded him: so he did.
On the first day of the first month of the second year, the Dwelling was set up.
Moses set up the Dwelling: he laid its bases, placed its frames, put in its crossbars and raised its pillars.
He spread the tent over the Dwelling and put the covering of the tent over it, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He took the Testimony and put it in the ark; he placed the poles on the ark and set the mercy seat on the ark, on top.
He brought the ark into the Dwelling, hung the veil of separation and so screened the ark of the Testimony, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the table in the tent of meeting, on the north side of the Dwelling, outside the veil;
and he arranged on it the bread in a row before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the lampstand in the tent of meeting, opposite the table, on the south side of the Dwelling,
and he set up the lamps before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the golden altar in the tent of meeting, in front of the veil,
and burned fragrant incense on it, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He put the screen at the entrance of the Dwelling.
He placed the altar of burnt offerings at the entrance of the Dwelling, of the tent of meeting, and on it he offered the burnt offering and the grain offering, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it for washing.
Moses, Aaron and his sons washed their hands and feet at it;
whenever they entered the tent of meeting or approached the altar, they washed, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He set up the court around the Dwelling and the altar, and put up the screen for the gate of the court. So Moses finished the work.
Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the Lord filled the Dwelling.
Moses could not enter the tent of meeting, for the cloud rested on it, and the glory of the Lord filled the Dwelling.
At each stage, whenever the cloud rose from over the Dwelling, the sons of Israel would set out;
but if the cloud did not rise, they would not set out, until the day it rose.
For the cloud of the Lord was over the Dwelling by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, at every stage of their journey.

titres.titre: The burnt offering: sheep and goats

versets.t: The Lord called Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When one of you wishes to present an offering to the Lord, he shall bring it from among his herd or his flock.
If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he shall present a male without blemish. He shall bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting, so that it may be accepted before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the animal, and this burnt offering will be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for his sins.

He shall slaughter the young bull before the Lord, and the priests, the sons of Aaron, shall present the blood and dash it against all sides of the altar that stands at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The animal shall be skinned and cut into pieces.
The sons of Aaron the priest shall kindle a fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire;
then the priests, the sons of Aaron, shall arrange the pieces, with the head and the fat, on the wood burning on the altar.
The entrails and the legs shall be washed with water, and the priest shall turn all of it into smoke on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If his offering is a burnt offering from the flock, a lamb or a goat, he shall present a male without blemish.
He shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar, before the Lord, and the priests, the sons of Aaron, shall dash its blood against all sides of the altar.
It shall be cut into pieces, with its head and its fat, and the priest shall arrange them on the wood burning on the altar.

The entrails and the legs shall be washed with water, and the priest shall offer all of it, turning it into smoke on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If his offering to the Lord is a burnt offering of birds, he shall present turtledoves or young pigeons.
The priest shall bring the bird to the altar, wring off its head with his nail, and turn it into smoke on the altar; and its blood shall be drained out against the side of the altar.
He shall remove its crop with its filth and throw it beside the altar, on the east side, at the place where the ashes are put.

Then he shall tear it open by its wings, without severing them, and the priest shall turn it into smoke on the altar, on the wood burning there. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord."
"When someone presents a grain offering to the Lord, his offering shall be of fine flour; he shall pour oil on it and put frankincense on it.

He shall bring it to the priests, the sons of Aaron. The priest shall take a handful of this fine flour moistened with oil, along with all the frankincense, and turn it into smoke on the altar as a memorial portion. It is an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The rest of the offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy portion among the offerings by fire to the Lord.
When you offer a grain offering baked in an oven, it shall be cakes of fine flour without leaven, mixed with oil, and wafers without leaven brushed with oil.
If your offering is cooked on a griddle, it shall be of fine flour without leaven, mixed with oil.
You shall break it into pieces and pour oil on it: it is a grain offering.
If your offering is cooked in a pan, it shall be made of fine flour and oil.
You shall bring to the Lord the grain offering prepared in this way; it shall be handed to the priest, who will bring it to the altar.
The priest shall take from it the memorial portion and turn it into smoke on the altar: it is an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The rest of the offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy portion among the offerings by fire to the Lord.
Every grain offering that you present to the Lord shall be prepared without leaven, for you shall never turn any leaven or honey into smoke as an offering by fire to the Lord.
You may present them to the Lord as an offering of firstfruits, but they shall not be placed on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
You shall salt every grain offering; you shall never let the salt of the covenant of your God be missing from your offering. With all your offerings you shall present salt.
If you present to the Lord an offering of firstfruits, you shall offer ears roasted in the fire, fresh grain crushed, as the offering of your firstfruits.
You shall pour oil on it and put frankincense on it: it is a grain offering.
The priest shall turn into smoke, as a memorial portion, part of the crushed grain and the oil, along with all the frankincense. It is an offering by fire to the Lord."

titres.titre: The peace offering: sheep and goats
The prohibition of fat and blood

versets.t: "If someone's offering is a peace offering, and he offers it from the herd, whether male or female, he shall present before the Lord an animal without blemish.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the victim and slaughter it at the entrance of the tent of meeting; and the priests, the sons of Aaron, shall dash the blood against all sides of the altar.
From this peace offering he shall present as an offering by fire to the Lord: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat attached to them,
the two kidneys with the fat that covers them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall detach near the kidneys.
The sons of Aaron shall turn this into smoke on the altar, on top of the burnt offering that lies on the burning wood. It is an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If he offers to the Lord a peace offering taken from the flock, whether male or female, he shall present it without blemish.
If he presents a lamb as his offering, he shall bring it before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the victim and slaughter it before the tent of meeting; and the sons of Aaron shall dash its blood against all sides of the altar.

From this peace offering he shall present as an offering by fire to the Lord its fat: the entire tail, cut off close to the backbone, the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat attached to them,
the two kidneys with the fat that covers them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall detach near the kidneys.
The priest shall turn this into smoke on the altar: it is food, an offering by fire to the Lord.
If his offering is a goat, he shall present it before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on its head and slaughter it before the tent of meeting; and the sons of Aaron shall dash its blood against all sides of the altar.
From this victim he shall present as an offering by fire to the Lord: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat attached to them,
the two kidneys with the fat that covers them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall detach near the kidneys.
The priest shall turn this into smoke on the altar: it is food, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma. All fat belongs to the Lord.
This is a perpetual statute for your descendants, wherever you live: you shall eat neither fat nor blood."

titres.titre: The sin offering for the priest
The sin offering for the community
The sin offering for a leader
The sin offering for a common person

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When someone sins unintentionally against one of the Lord's commandments, doing what is forbidden,

these are the rules. If it is the anointed priest who has sinned, bringing guilt upon the whole people, he shall offer to the Lord, for the sin he has committed, a young bull without blemish, as a sin offering.
He shall bring the bull to the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the Lord, lay his hand on its head, and slaughter it before the Lord.
The anointed priest shall take some of the bull's blood and bring it into the tent of meeting.
He shall dip his finger in it and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before the Lord, in front of the veil of the sanctuary.

The priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of incense, which stands before the Lord in the tent of meeting, then pour out all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He shall then remove all the fat of the bull offered for sin: the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat attached to them,
the two kidneys with the fat that covers them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which he shall detach near the kidneys.
He shall remove them as is done for the bull of the peace offering, and the priest shall turn them into smoke on the altar of burnt offering.
But the skin of the bull, all its flesh, with its head, its legs, its entrails, and its offal,
the whole bull, he shall carry outside the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are thrown, and burn it on a wood fire, on the heap of ashes.
If it is the whole community of Israel that has sinned unintentionally, without realizing it, doing one of the things the Lord has forbidden, and so becoming guilty,
as soon as the sin they committed becomes known, the assembly shall offer a young bull as a sin offering and bring it before the tent of meeting.
The elders of the community shall lay their hands on the head of the bull before the Lord, and it shall be slaughtered before the Lord.
The anointed priest shall bring some of the bull's blood into the tent of meeting.
He shall dip his finger in it and make seven sprinklings before the Lord, in front of the veil.

He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that stands before the Lord in the tent of meeting, then pour out all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He shall remove all the fat of the bull and turn it into smoke on the altar.
He shall treat this bull as he treated the one offered for his own sin: he shall do the same. Thus the priest shall make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
He shall carry the bull outside the camp and burn it as he burned the first. Such is the sin offering for the community.
If it is a leader who has sinned, unintentionally doing one of the things the Lord his God has forbidden, and so becoming guilty,
as soon as he becomes aware of his sin, he shall bring as his offering a male goat without blemish.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the goat and slaughter it where the burnt offerings are slaughtered, before the Lord: it is a sin offering.
The priest shall take some of the victim's blood with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out the rest at the base of the altar.
Then he shall turn all the fat into smoke on the altar, like the fat of the peace offering. Thus the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin, and he will be forgiven.
If it is one of the common people who has sinned unintentionally, doing one of the things the Lord has forbidden, and so becoming guilty,
as soon as he becomes aware of his sin, he shall bring as his offering a goat, a female without blemish, for the sin he has committed.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the victim and slaughter it where the burnt offerings are slaughtered.
The priest shall take some of the victim's blood with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out all the rest at the base of the altar.

He shall remove all the fat, as is done for the peace offering, and the priest shall turn it into smoke on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. Thus the priest shall make atonement for this man, and he will be forgiven.
If he brings a lamb as a sin offering, it shall be a female without blemish.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the victim and slaughter it as a sin offering, where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
The priest shall take some of the victim's blood with his finger, put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and pour out all the rest at the base of the altar.

He shall remove all the fat, as the fat of the lamb is removed in the peace offering, and the priest shall turn it into smoke on the altar, among the offerings by fire to the Lord. Thus the priest shall make atonement for this man, for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven."

titres.titre: Particular cases and the offerings of the poor

versets.t: "If someone sins because, called to testify under oath, he refuses to declare what he has seen or knows, he shall bear the weight of his fault.

If someone, without noticing, touches something unclean, the carcass of an unclean wild animal, of an unclean domestic animal, or of an unclean creeping thing, he himself becomes unclean and incurs guilt.
Likewise, if someone unwittingly touches human uncleanness of any kind that can defile him, and afterward becomes aware of it, he incurs guilt.
If someone, speaking rashly, swears to do harm or good, by a thoughtless oath, and afterward becomes aware of it, he incurs guilt in any of these cases.
So whoever incurs guilt in any of these cases shall confess the sin he has committed.
He shall bring to the Lord, in reparation for the sin committed, a female from the flock, a ewe or a goat, as a sin offering, and the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin.
If he cannot afford a ewe or a goat, he shall offer to the Lord, for the sin committed, two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a sin offering, the other as a burnt offering.
He shall bring them to the priest, who shall offer first the one for the sin offering. The priest shall wring off its head close to the neck, without severing it,
sprinkle some of its blood against the side of the altar, and drain out the rest at the base of the altar: it is a sin offering.
Of the other bird he shall make a burnt offering, according to the prescribed rite. Thus the priest shall make atonement for this man for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.

If he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall bring for his sin about two litres of fine flour as a sin offering. He shall put no oil or frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.
He shall bring it to the priest, who shall take a handful of it as a memorial portion and turn it into smoke on the altar, among the offerings by fire to the Lord: it is a sin offering.
Thus the priest shall make atonement for this man, for the sin committed in any of these cases, and he will be forgiven. The rest shall belong to the priest, as with the grain offering."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:

"If someone commits an act of unfaithfulness and sins unintentionally by misappropriating something from the offerings consecrated to the Lord, he shall bring to the Lord, as a guilt offering, a ram without blemish from the flock, valued in silver according to the official weight of the sanctuary: it shall be a guilt offering.

Moreover, he shall restore what he took from the sanctuary, adding a fifth to it, and hand it over to the priest. The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
If someone sins by unknowingly doing one of the things the Lord has forbidden, he is guilty and shall bear the weight of his fault.

He shall bring to the priest, as a guilt offering, a ram without blemish from the flock, according to the value you set. The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed unintentionally, without knowing it, and he will be forgiven.
It is a guilt offering: this man had indeed become guilty before the Lord."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"If someone sins and commits an act of unfaithfulness against the Lord by deceiving his neighbor concerning a deposit, a pledge entrusted to him, or something stolen, or by exploiting his neighbor,
or by lying about a lost object that he has found, and by swearing falsely about any of the sins that a person may commit,
then, having sinned and become guilty, he shall restore what he stole or extorted, the deposit entrusted to him, the lost object he found,
or anything about which he swore falsely. He shall restore it in full, adding a fifth of its value, and hand it over to its owner on the very day he offers his guilt offering.
He shall bring to the priest, to offer to the Lord as a guilt offering, a ram without blemish from the flock, according to the value you set.
The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and he will be forgiven for whatever fault he had become guilty of."

titres.titre: The law of the burnt offering and the perpetual fire
The law of the grain offering
The daily offering of the priests
The law of the sin offering

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:

"Give this command to Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering shall remain on the hearth of the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.

Each morning the priest shall put on his linen tunic and wear linen undergarments on his body; then he shall remove the ashes left on the altar by the fire that consumed the burnt offering, and place them beside the altar.
Then he shall take off these garments, put on others, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
The fire of the altar shall be kept burning and never go out: each morning the priest shall kindle wood on it, arrange the burnt offering on it, and turn into smoke the fat of the peace offerings.
A perpetual fire shall burn on the altar and never go out.
This is the law of the grain offering. The sons of Aaron shall present it before the Lord, in front of the altar.

The priest shall take from it a handful of fine flour with its oil, and all the frankincense that covers it, and turn it into smoke on the altar as a pleasing aroma, as a memorial portion to the Lord.
What remains of the offering, Aaron and his sons shall eat; they shall eat it without leaven, in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
It shall not be baked with leaven. This is the portion I have assigned to them from my offerings by fire. It is a most holy thing, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.

Every male among the descendants of Aaron may eat of it. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations, concerning the offerings by fire to the Lord. Whatever touches them shall become holy."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:

"This is the offering that Aaron and his sons shall present to the Lord on the day they are anointed: about two litres of fine flour, as a perpetual grain offering, half in the morning and half in the evening.
It shall be prepared on a griddle, with oil; you shall bring it well mixed and offer it in pieces, as a grain offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The priest among his sons who is anointed to succeed him shall also make this offering: it is a perpetual statute before the Lord; it shall be wholly turned into smoke.
Every grain offering of a priest shall be wholly turned into smoke: none of it shall be eaten."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to Aaron and his sons: This is the law of the sin offering. The victim for sin shall be slaughtered before the Lord, where the burnt offering is slaughtered: it is a most holy thing.
The priest who offers it shall eat it; it shall be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
Whatever touches its flesh shall become holy. If any of its blood spatters on a garment, you shall wash the spattered part in a holy place.
The earthenware vessel in which it was cooked shall be broken; if it was cooked in a bronze vessel, that vessel shall be scoured and rinsed with water.
Every male among the priests may eat of it: it is a most holy thing.
But no sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the sanctuary shall be eaten: it shall be burned in the fire."

titres.titre: The law of the guilt offering
The law of the peace offering
The prohibition of fat and blood
The portions reserved for the priests
Summary of the laws on the offerings

versets.t: "This is the law of the guilt offering: it is a most holy thing.
The victim for the guilt offering shall be slaughtered where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and its blood shall be dashed against all sides of the altar.
All its fat shall be offered: the tail, the fat that covers the entrails,
the two kidneys with the fat that covers them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, which shall be detached near the kidneys.
The priest shall turn them into smoke on the altar as an offering by fire to the Lord: it is a guilt offering.
Every male among the priests may eat its flesh; he shall eat it in a holy place: it is a most holy thing.
The guilt offering is in every way like the sin offering: one and the same law applies to both, and the victim belongs to the priest who has made atonement.
The priest who offers someone's burnt offering shall keep for himself the skin of the animal offered.
Every grain offering baked in an oven or prepared in a pan or on a griddle shall belong to the priest who offered it.
Every grain offering mixed with oil or dry shall belong to all the sons of Aaron equally.
This is the law of the peace offering that is offered to the Lord.

If it is offered in thanksgiving, one shall present, along with the victim, cakes without leaven mixed with oil, wafers without leaven brushed with oil, and fine flour well mixed into cakes mixed with oil.
To these shall be added cakes of leavened bread, in addition to the victim offered in thanksgiving in the peace offering.
From each of these offerings one shall present a portion set apart for the Lord; it shall belong to the priest who dashed the blood of the peace victim.
The flesh of the victim offered in thanksgiving shall be eaten on the day of the offering; none of it shall be left until morning.
If the victim is offered as a vow or as a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day of the offering, and what remains may be eaten the next day.
But whatever is left of the flesh on the third day shall be burned in the fire.

If any of the flesh of the peace offering is eaten on the third day, this offering will not be accepted: it shall not count for the one who offered it, it will be a repugnant thing, and whoever eats of it shall bear the weight of his fault.
Flesh that has touched anything unclean shall not be eaten: it shall be burned in the fire. As for the flesh of the offering, everyone who is clean may eat of it.
But anyone who, in a state of uncleanness, eats the flesh of the peace offering that belongs to the Lord shall be cut off from his people.

And anyone who touches something unclean, human defilement, an unclean animal, or any other repugnant uncleanness, and then eats the flesh of the peace offering that belongs to the Lord, shall be cut off from his people."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: You shall eat no fat of ox, sheep, or goat.
The fat of an animal that has died of itself or been torn by a wild beast may be used for any purpose, but you shall never eat it.
For whoever eats the fat of an animal offered to the Lord as an offering by fire shall be cut off from his people.
Wherever you live, you shall eat no blood, whether of bird or of animal.
Whoever eats any blood shall be cut off from his people."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: Whoever offers to the Lord a peace offering shall himself bring the portion set apart from it.
With his own hands he shall bring what is to be consumed by fire for the Lord: he shall bring the fat with the breast, the breast to be waved before the Lord as an offering.
The priest shall turn the fat into smoke on the altar, and the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.
From your peace offerings you shall also give the priest the right thigh as a portion set apart.
It shall belong to the one among the sons of Aaron who has offered the blood and the fat of the peace offerings.

For from the peace offerings of the sons of Israel I have reserved the breast that is waved and the thigh that is set apart, and I give them to Aaron the priest and to his sons: it is a perpetual due imposed on the sons of Israel.
This is the portion reserved for Aaron and his sons, by virtue of their anointing, from the offerings by fire to the Lord, from the day they are presented to serve the Lord as priests.
This is what the Lord commanded the sons of Israel to give them from the day of their anointing: a perpetual due throughout all their generations."
Such is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the offering of ordination, and the peace offering.
The Lord prescribed it to Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day he commanded the sons of Israel to present their offerings to the Lord, in the wilderness of Sinai.

titres.titre: The ordination of Aaron and his sons
The seven days of the ordination

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Take Aaron and his sons with him, the garments, the anointing oil, the bull of the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread,
and gather the whole community at the entrance of the tent of meeting."
Moses did what the Lord had commanded him, and the community assembled at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Moses said to the assembly, "This is what the Lord has commanded to be done."
He brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He clothed Aaron with the tunic, tied the sash around him, dressed him in the robe, and put the ephod on him, which he fastened with its band to secure it.
He put the breastpiece on him, in which he placed the Urim and the Thummim.
He set the turban on his head and fixed, on the front of the turban, the gold plate, the sacred diadem, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses took the anointing oil, anointed the Dwelling and everything in it, and consecrated them.
He sprinkled some of it seven times on the altar, then anointed the altar with all its utensils, as well as the basin and its stand, to consecrate them.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head and anointed him to consecrate him.
Moses also brought the sons of Aaron forward, clothed them with tunics, tied sashes around them, and bound headdresses on them, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He brought forward the bull of the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

Moses slaughtered it, took the blood, put some of it with his finger on the horns of the altar all around, and purified the altar; he poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar and consecrated it by making atonement on it.
He then took all the fat that covers the entrails, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and turned them into smoke on the altar.
But the bull, its skin, its flesh, and its offal, he burned outside the camp, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He brought forward the ram of the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
It was slaughtered, and Moses dashed the blood against all sides of the altar.
The ram was cut into pieces, and Moses turned the head, the pieces, and the fat into smoke.

The entrails and the legs were washed with water, and Moses turned the whole ram into smoke on the altar: it was a burnt offering of pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He brought forward the second ram, the ram of ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
Moses slaughtered it, took some of its blood, and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

He brought the sons of Aaron forward and put some blood on the lobe of their right ear, on the thumb of their right hand, and on the big toe of their right foot; then he dashed the rest of the blood against all sides of the altar.
He then took the fat, the tail, all the fat that covers the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh;
from the basket of unleavened bread placed before the Lord, he also took one unleavened cake, one cake of bread with oil, and one wafer, and set them on the fat and on the right thigh.
He put all of it in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and waved it as an offering before the Lord.
Then Moses took it back from their hands and turned it into smoke on the altar, on top of the burnt offering: it was the offering of ordination, of pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the Lord.
Moses took the breast of the ram of ordination and waved it as an offering before the Lord: this was his own portion, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood that was on the altar, and sprinkled it on Aaron and his garments, as well as on his sons and their garments. Thus he consecrated Aaron and his garments, and with him his sons and their garments.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons, "Cook the flesh at the entrance of the tent of meeting; there you shall eat it, with the bread of the basket of ordination, as I commanded, saying: Aaron and his sons shall eat it.
What remains of the flesh and the bread you shall burn in the fire.
For seven days you shall not leave the entrance of the tent of meeting, until the days of your ordination are completed; for your ordination will last seven days.
What has been done today, the Lord has commanded to be done for seven days, to make atonement for you.
You shall stay seven days, day and night, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and you shall keep the charge of the Lord, so that you do not die; for this is what I have been commanded."
Aaron and his sons did everything the Lord had commanded through Moses.

titres.titre: The eighth day: Aaron's first sacrifices
The glory of the Lord appears

versets.t: On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron, his sons, and the elders of Israel.
He said to Aaron, "Take a young calf for the sin offering and a ram for the burnt offering, both without blemish, and offer them before the Lord.
Then say to the sons of Israel: Take a male goat for the sin offering, a calf and a lamb, both a year old and without blemish, for the burnt offering,
an ox and a ram for the peace offering, to be sacrificed before the Lord, and a grain offering mixed with oil; for today the Lord will appear to you."
They brought before the tent of meeting what Moses had commanded, and the whole community drew near and stood before the Lord.
Moses said, "This is what the Lord commands you to do, and the glory of the Lord will appear to you."

Then Moses said to Aaron, "Come near to the altar, offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people; then present the offering of the people and make atonement for them, as the Lord has commanded."
Aaron came near to the altar and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering for his own sin.
His sons presented the blood to him; he dipped his finger in it, put some on the horns of the altar, and poured out the rest at the base of the altar.
He turned into smoke on the altar the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver of the sin offering, as the Lord had commanded Moses;
but the flesh and the skin he burned in the fire outside the camp.
He slaughtered the burnt offering; his sons presented the blood to him, and he dashed it against all sides of the altar.
They presented to him the burnt offering cut into pieces, with the head, and he turned them into smoke on the altar.
He washed the entrails and the legs, and turned them into smoke on the altar, on top of the burnt offering.
He then presented the offering of the people. He took the goat of the sin offering for the people, slaughtered it, and offered it for sin, like the first victim.
He offered the burnt offering in the same way, according to the rite.
He presented the grain offering, took a handful of it, and turned it into smoke on the altar, in addition to the morning burnt offering.
Finally, he slaughtered the bull and the ram as a peace offering for the people. His sons presented the blood to him, and he dashed it against all sides of the altar,
along with the fat of the bull and the ram: the tail, the fat that covers the entrails, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver.
They placed these portions of fat on the breasts, and Aaron turned them into smoke on the altar.
Then he waved the breasts and the right thigh before the Lord as a wave offering, as Moses had commanded.
Then Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them; then he came down, having offered the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offering.
Moses and Aaron entered the tent of meeting; when they came out, they blessed the people. And the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people:
fire came out from before the Lord and consumed the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. At this sight, all the people shouted for joy and fell on their faces to the ground.

titres.titre: The sin and death of Nadab and Abihu
Rules for the priests on duty
The dispute over the sin offering

versets.t: The sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, each took his censer, put fire in it, laid incense on it, and presented before the Lord unauthorized fire, which he had not commanded them.
Then fire came out from before the Lord and consumed them: they died before the Lord.
Moses said to Aaron, "This is what the Lord declared: Through those who come near me I will show my holiness; before all the people I will show my glory." And Aaron was silent.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, sons of Uzziel, Aaron's uncle, and said to them, "Come, carry your brothers away from the sanctuary, outside the camp."
They came and carried them outside the camp, still in their tunics, as Moses had commanded.

Moses said to Aaron, and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his sons, "Do not let your hair hang loose or tear your garments, or you will die and the wrath of God will fall upon the whole community. It is your brothers, the whole house of Israel, who will mourn those whom the fire of the Lord has consumed.
But you, do not leave the entrance of the tent of meeting, or you will die, for the anointing oil of the Lord is upon you." They did as Moses had said.
The Lord spoke to Aaron. He said:
"You and your sons shall drink no wine or strong drink when you enter the tent of meeting, or you will die: this is a perpetual statute throughout your generations,
so that you may distinguish the sacred from the profane, the unclean from the clean,
and that you may teach the sons of Israel all the statutes that the Lord has given them through Moses."

Moses said to Aaron, and to Eleazar and Ithamar, his remaining sons, "Take the grain offering that is left from the offerings by fire to the Lord, and eat it without leaven beside the altar, for it is a most holy thing.
You shall eat it in a holy place: it is the portion due to you and your sons from the offerings by fire to the Lord; for this is what I have been commanded.

You shall also eat, in a clean place, you, your sons, and your daughters, the breast that is waved and the thigh that is set apart; for these portions are given to you and your children from the peace offerings of the sons of Israel.

The thigh that is set apart and the breast that is waved shall be brought, along with the portions of fat to be consumed by fire, to be waved as an offering before the Lord; they shall belong to you and your sons by a perpetual statute, as the Lord has commanded."
Moses inquired about the goat of the sin offering, and learned that it had been burned. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons who remained to Aaron, and said to them:
"Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy place? It is a most holy thing, and the Lord gave it to you to bear the fault of the community and make atonement for them before the Lord.
Since its blood was not brought inside the sanctuary, you should have eaten it in the holy place, as I had commanded."

Aaron replied to Moses, "This very day they offered before the Lord their sin offering and their burnt offering, and yet such things have happened to me! If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have pleased the Lord?"
When Moses heard this, he found the answer satisfactory.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said to them:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: Of all the animals on the earth, these are the ones you may eat.
Any animal that has a divided hoof, completely split, and that chews the cud, you may eat.
But among those that chew the cud or have a divided hoof, you shall not eat these: the camel, which chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof, shall be unclean for you;
the rock badger, which chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof, shall be unclean for you;
the hare, which chews the cud but does not have a divided hoof, shall be unclean for you;
the pig, which has a divided hoof, completely split, but does not chew the cud, shall be unclean for you.
You shall not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses: they shall be unclean for you.
Of all the creatures that live in the water, these are the ones you may eat: anything that has fins and scales, in the seas or in the rivers, you may eat.
But anything that has neither fins nor scales, in the seas and the rivers, among the creatures that swarm in the water and all the living things found in it, you shall detest.
They shall be a repugnant thing to you: you shall not eat their flesh, and you shall regard their carcasses as repugnant.
Anything in the water that has neither fins nor scales, you shall detest.
Among the birds, these are the ones you shall detest; they shall not be eaten, for they are repugnant: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
the kite and all kinds of falcons,
all kinds of ravens,
the ostrich, the owl, the gull, and all kinds of hawks,
the little owl, the cormorant, and the great owl,
the barn owl, the pelican, and the carrion vulture,
the stork, all kinds of herons, the hoopoe, and the bat.
Every winged creature that walks on four legs, you shall detest.
But among these winged creatures that walk on four legs, you may eat those that have jointed legs above their feet for leaping on the ground.
These are the ones you may eat: all kinds of locusts, katydids, crickets, and grasshoppers.
Every other winged creature with four legs, you shall detest.
By these you will make yourselves unclean. Whoever touches the carcass of these creatures shall be unclean until evening,
and whoever carries away any part of them shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
Every animal that has a partly divided hoof, without being completely split, and that does not chew the cud, shall be unclean for you; whoever touches it shall become unclean.
Among the animals that walk on four legs, all that walk on their paws shall be unclean for you; whoever touches their carcass shall be unclean until evening,
and whoever carries it shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening. They shall be unclean for you.
Among the small creatures that swarm on the ground, these shall be unclean for you: the mole, the mouse, and all kinds of lizards,
the gecko, the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the salamander, and the chameleon.
These, among all the creeping things, shall be unclean for you: whoever touches them when they are dead shall be unclean until evening.

Anything on which one of these dead creatures falls shall become unclean: a wooden utensil, a garment, a skin, a sack, any object used for a purpose. It shall be plunged into water, remain unclean until evening, and then be clean.
If one of them falls into an earthenware vessel, everything in it shall become unclean, and you shall break the vessel.
Any food prepared with water from that vessel shall become unclean, and any drink it might contain shall become unclean.
Anything on which one of these dead creatures falls shall become unclean: an oven or a hearth shall be destroyed, for it is unclean and you shall regard it as unclean.
However, a spring or a cistern where water collects shall remain clean; but whoever touches the carcass shall be unclean.
If one of these dead creatures falls on seed that is to be sown, the seed shall remain clean;
but if water has been put on the seed and one of these dead creatures falls on it, you shall regard it as unclean.
If one of the animals that you use for food dies, whoever touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
Whoever eats of this carcass shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening; whoever carries it shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening.
Every creature that swarms on the ground is a repugnant thing: it shall not be eaten.
Of everything that swarms on the ground, whether it crawls on its belly, walks on four legs, or has many legs, you shall eat none, for they are repugnant.
Do not make yourselves repugnant by any of these swarming creatures, and do not make yourselves unclean by them, so as to be defiled by them.
For I am the Lord your God. Sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I am holy; do not defile yourselves by any of these creatures that swarm on the ground.
For I am the Lord, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God. Be holy, for I am holy."
This is the law concerning the animals, the birds, all the living creatures that move in the water, and all the creatures that swarm on the ground,
so that you may distinguish the unclean from the clean, the animal that may be eaten from the one that may not be eaten.

titres.titre: The purification of a woman after childbirth

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When a woman gives birth to a boy, she shall be unclean for seven days, as at the time of her menstruation.
On the eighth day, the child shall be circumcised.
Then she shall wait another thirty-three days to be purified of her blood; she shall touch nothing holy and shall not go to the sanctuary, until the days of her purification are completed.
If she gives birth to a girl, she shall be unclean for two weeks, as at the time of her menstruation, then she shall wait sixty-six days to be purified of her blood.

When the days of her purification are completed, whether for a son or a daughter, she shall present to the priest, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, a year-old lamb as a burnt offering, and a young pigeon or a turtledove as a sin offering.
The priest shall offer them before the Lord and make atonement for her, and she shall be purified of her blood. This is the law for the woman who gives birth to a boy or a girl.

If she cannot afford a lamb, she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for the burnt offering, the other for the sin offering; the priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean."

titres.titre: The diagnosis of leprosy on the skin
Leprosy after a boil or a burn
Scabby infection of the head or chin

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said:
"When a man has on his skin a swelling, a scab, or a white spot, and it develops into a mark of leprosy on his skin, he shall be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.

The priest shall examine the mark on the skin: if the hair in the mark has turned white and the mark appears deeper than the skin, it is a mark of leprosy; after examining him, the priest shall declare him unclean.
But if the spot on the skin is white without appearing deeper than the skin, and the hair has not turned white, the priest shall isolate for seven days the one who has the mark.
On the seventh day he shall examine him: if the mark appears to him to have remained unchanged, without spreading on the skin, he shall isolate him a second time for seven days.
On the seventh day he shall examine him again: if the mark has faded and has not spread, the priest shall declare him clean; it was only a scab. The man shall wash his garments and be clean.
But if the scab spreads on the skin after he has presented himself to the priest to be declared clean, he shall show himself to the priest a second time.
The priest shall examine him: if the scab has spread on the skin, he shall declare him unclean: it is leprosy.
When a man has a mark of leprosy, he shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall examine him: if there is on the skin a white swelling that has turned the hair white, with a trace of raw flesh in the swelling,
it is a chronic leprosy, settled in the skin; the priest shall declare him unclean. He shall not isolate him, for this man is already unclean.
But if the leprosy spreads over all the skin, so as to cover entirely, from head to foot, all that the priest can see,
then the priest shall examine him: if the leprosy covers the whole body, he shall declare clean the one who has the mark; having turned all white, he is clean.
But on the day raw flesh appears on him, he shall be unclean.
When the priest sees the raw flesh, he shall declare him unclean: the raw flesh is unclean, it is leprosy.
If the raw flesh changes and turns white again, he shall go to the priest.
The priest shall examine him: if the mark has turned white, he shall declare clean the one who has the mark; he is clean.
When a man has had on his skin a boil that has healed,
and in the place of the boil there forms a white swelling or a reddish-white spot, he shall show himself to the priest.
The priest shall examine him: if the spot appears lower than the skin and the hair in it has turned white, he shall declare him unclean: it is a mark of leprosy that has broken out in the boil.
But if the priest sees that there is no white hair in the spot, that it is not lower than the skin, and that it has faded, he shall isolate this man for seven days.
If during this time the spot spreads on the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean: it is a mark of leprosy.
But if the spot stays in its place without spreading, it is the scar of the boil: the priest shall declare him clean.
When a man has had on his skin a burn, and in the trace of the burn there forms a reddish-white or white spot,

the priest shall examine him: if the hair in the spot has turned white and it appears deeper than the skin, it is leprosy that has broken out in the burn; the priest shall declare him unclean: it is a mark of leprosy.
But if the priest sees that there is no white hair in the spot, that it is not lower than the skin, and that it has faded, he shall isolate this man for seven days.
On the seventh day he shall examine him: if the spot has spread on the skin, he shall declare him unclean: it is a mark of leprosy.
But if the spot has stayed in its place without spreading and has faded, it is the swelling of the burn; the priest shall declare him clean, for it is the scar of the burn.
When a man or a woman has a mark on the head or the chin,
the priest shall examine it: if the mark appears deeper than the skin, with yellowish, thin hair, he shall declare the person unclean: it is a scabby infection, a leprosy of the head or the chin.
But if the priest sees that the mark of the scabby infection does not appear deeper than the skin, though there is no black hair in it, he shall isolate for seven days the one who has this mark.
On the seventh day he shall examine the mark: if the scabby infection has not spread, there is no yellowish hair, and it does not appear deeper than the skin,
the person shall shave, except at the place of the infection, and the priest shall isolate the person a second time for seven days.

On the seventh day he shall examine the infection: if it has not spread on the skin and does not appear deeper than the skin, the priest shall declare the person clean; the person shall wash their garments and be clean.
But if, after having been declared clean, the infection spreads on the skin,
the priest shall examine the person: if the infection has spread, he need not look for yellowish hair: the person is unclean.
But if the infection appears to him to be stationary and black hair has grown in it, it is healed: the person is clean, and the priest shall declare the person clean.
When a man or a woman has on the skin spots, white spots,
the priest shall examine the person: if these spots on the skin are a dull white, it is a harmless rash: this person is clean.
When a man loses the hair of his head, he is bald, but he is clean.
If his hair falls out from the front, he is bald at the forehead, but he is clean.
But if, on the bald part of the head or the forehead, a reddish-white mark appears, it is a leprosy breaking out on that bald part.
The priest shall examine him: if the swelling of the mark, on the bald part of the head or the forehead, is reddish-white, resembling a leprosy of the skin,
he is a leprous man, he is unclean; the priest shall declare him unclean: his mark is on his head.
The leper afflicted with this mark shall wear torn garments and let his hair hang loose; he shall cover his upper lip and cry out: Unclean, unclean!
As long as he has this mark, he shall be unclean. He is unclean: he shall live apart, his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
When a mark of leprosy appears on a garment, of linen or of wool,
on linen or woolen thread, on leather, or on any object of leather,
if the mark is greenish or reddish, on the garment, the leather, the woven thread, or any object of leather, it is a mark of leprosy: it shall be shown to the priest.
The priest shall examine the mark and shut away the affected object for seven days.
On the seventh day he shall examine the mark: if it has spread on the garment, the woven thread, the leather, or any object of leather, it is a corrosive leprosy: the object is unclean.
The garment, the linen or woolen thread, or the leather object affected by the mark shall be burned, for it is a corrosive leprosy: the object shall be burned in the fire.
But if the priest sees that the mark has not spread on the garment, the woven thread, or any object of leather,
he shall have the affected object washed and shut it away a second time for seven days.

The priest shall examine it after this washing: if the mark has not changed its appearance, even without having spread, the object is unclean; you shall burn it in the fire, for the corrosion has eaten into it, whether on the front or the back.
But if the priest sees that the mark has faded after the washing, he shall tear it out of the garment, the leather, or the woven thread.
If it appears again afterward on the garment, the woven thread, or any object of leather, it is a spreading leprosy: you shall burn in the fire the affected object.
But the garment, the woven thread, or any object of leather that you have washed and from which the mark has disappeared shall be washed a second time, and it shall be clean.
This is the law concerning the mark of leprosy that attacks a garment of wool or linen, the woven thread, or any object of leather, for declaring them clean or unclean."

titres.titre: The rite of purification for the healed leper
The sacrifices of the eighth day

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"This is the law concerning the leper, for the day of his purification. He shall be brought to the priest,
and the priest shall go outside the camp to examine him. If the leper is healed of his mark of leprosy,
the priest shall order that there be taken, for the one to be purified, two living clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet thread, and hyssop.
The priest shall have one of the birds slaughtered over an earthenware vessel filled with fresh water.
Then he shall take the living bird, the cedar wood, the scarlet thread, and the hyssop, and dip them, with the living bird, in the blood of the bird slaughtered over the fresh water.
He shall sprinkle seven times the one to be purified of the leprosy, declare him clean, and release the living bird into the open country.
The one being purified shall wash his garments, shave off all his hair, bathe in water, and he shall be clean. Then he may return to the camp, but he shall stay outside his tent for seven days.
On the seventh day he shall again shave off all his hair: his head, his beard, his eyebrows, all his hair; he shall wash his garments, bathe his body in water, and he shall be clean.

On the eighth day he shall take two lambs without blemish, a year-old ewe without blemish, about six and a half litres of fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering, and a third of a litre of oil.
The priest who performs the purification shall present before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, the man being purified and all these offerings.
The priest shall take one of the lambs and offer it as a guilt offering, with the oil, and he shall wave them as an offering before the Lord.

He shall slaughter the lamb where the sin offerings and the burnt offering are slaughtered, in the holy place; for, in the guilt offering as in the sin offering, the victim belongs to the priest: it is a most holy thing.
The priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one being purified, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
Then he shall take some of the oil and pour it into the palm of his left hand.
He shall dip the finger of his right hand into this oil and sprinkle some of it seven times before the Lord.

From the rest of the oil in his hand, he shall put some on the lobe of the right ear of the one being purified, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
What then remains of the oil in his hand, the priest shall put on the head of the one being purified; and he shall make atonement for him before the Lord.
Then the priest shall offer the sin offering and make atonement for the one being purified of his uncleanness. Finally, he shall slaughter the burnt offering
and offer it on the altar with the grain offering. Thus he shall make atonement for this man, and he shall be clean.

But if he is poor and without much means, he shall take a single lamb, offered as a guilt offering and presented as a wave offering to make atonement, with about two litres of fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering, and a third of a litre of oil,
as well as two turtledoves or two young pigeons, according to his means, one for the sin offering, the other for the burnt offering.
On the eighth day he shall bring them to the priest for his purification, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the Lord.
The priest shall take the lamb of the guilt offering and the oil, and wave them as an offering before the Lord.

After slaughtering the lamb of the guilt offering, he shall take some of its blood and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one being purified, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall pour some of the oil into the palm of his left hand
and, with the finger of his right hand, sprinkle some of it seven times before the Lord.

He shall put some of this oil on the lobe of the right ear of the one being purified, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, at the place of the blood of the guilt offering.
What remains of the oil in his hand, he shall put on the head of the one being purified, to make atonement for him before the Lord.
Then he shall offer one of the turtledoves or one of the young pigeons that he was able to obtain,
one as a sin offering, the other as a burnt offering, with the grain offering. Thus the priest shall make atonement, before the Lord, for the one being purified.
This is the law for the purification of one who has a mark of leprosy and cannot afford to do more."
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said:
"When you have entered the land of Canaan, which I give you as a possession, if I put a mark of leprosy on a house in the land you will possess,
the owner of the house shall go and declare it to the priest, saying: I have noticed something like a mark of leprosy in my house.
Before entering to examine the mark, the priest shall have the house emptied, so that nothing in it becomes unclean; only then shall he enter to examine the house.
He shall examine the mark: if, on the walls, the mark shows greenish or reddish depressions that appear to be set deeper than the wall,
the priest shall go out to the door and have the house shut up for seven days.
On the seventh day he shall return: if he sees that the mark has spread on the walls,
he shall order the affected stones to be removed and thrown outside the town, in an unclean place.
He shall have the entire inside of the house scraped, and the scraped-off plaster shall be poured out outside the town, in an unclean place.
Other stones shall be taken to replace the first ones, and other mortar to replaster the house.
If the mark breaks out again in the house, after the stones have been removed, the house scraped and replastered,
the priest shall come to examine it: if the mark has spread, it is a corrosive leprosy in the house: it is unclean.
The house shall be torn down, its stones, its wood, and all its mortar, and all of it shall be carried outside the town, in an unclean place.
Whoever has entered the house while it was shut up shall be unclean until evening.
Whoever has slept in it shall wash his garments, and whoever has eaten in it shall also wash his garments.
But if the priest, on returning, sees that the mark has not spread after the house was replastered, he shall declare it clean, for the mark is healed.
To purify the house, he shall take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet thread, and hyssop.
He shall slaughter one of the birds over an earthenware vessel filled with fresh water.
He shall take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet thread, and the living bird, dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
Thus he shall purify the house with the blood of the bird, the fresh water, the living bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop, and the scarlet thread.
Then he shall release the living bird outside the town, into the open country. Thus he shall make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.
This is the law for every mark of leprosy and for the scabby infection,
for the leprosy of garments and of houses,
for swellings, scabs, and spots,
to make known when a thing is unclean and when it is clean. This is the law concerning leprosy."
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: Any man who has a genital discharge is, by that very fact, unclean.
This is what the uncleanness of his discharge consists in, whether his body lets the discharge flow or holds it back: in either case there is uncleanness.
Any bed on which he lies will be unclean, and any object on which he sits will be unclean.
Whoever touches his bed shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Whoever sits on an object where this man has sat shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Whoever touches the body of this man shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
If this man spits on someone who is clean, that person shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Any saddle on which he has ridden will be unclean.
Whoever touches an object that has been under him will be unclean until evening; whoever carries it shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Anyone whom this man touches without having rinsed his hands in water shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Any earthenware vessel he has touched shall be broken, and any wooden object shall be washed in water.
When this man is healed of his discharge, he shall count seven days for his purification, wash his clothes, bathe his body in fresh water, and he will be clean.
On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, come before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and give them to the priest.
The priest shall offer them, one as a sin offering, the other as a burnt offering, and he shall make atonement for him before the Lord, because of his discharge.
When a man has an emission of semen, he shall bathe his whole body in water and be unclean until evening.
Any clothing or any leather touched by this emission shall be washed in water and be unclean until evening.
When a man and a woman have united, both shall bathe in water and be unclean until evening.
When a woman has her period, a discharge of blood, she shall remain seven days in her uncleanness; whoever touches her will be unclean until evening.
Any furniture on which she lies during this time will be unclean, and any object on which she sits will be unclean.
Whoever touches her bed shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Whoever touches an object on which she has sat shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
Whether it is the bed or the object on which she has sat, whoever touches it will be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with her and her uncleanness reaches him, he will be unclean for seven days, and any bed on which he lies will be unclean.
