When a woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside her usual period, or when her discharge continues beyond it, she will be unclean the whole time of this discharge, as during her period.
Any bed on which she lies during this discharge will be like the bed of her period, and any object on which she sits will be unclean, as during her period.
Whoever touches them will be unclean: he shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.
When she is healed of her discharge, she shall count seven days, after which she will be clean.
On the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest shall offer them, one as a sin offering, the other as a burnt offering, and he shall make atonement for her before the Lord, because of the discharge that made her unclean.
In this way you shall keep the sons of Israel apart from their uncleannesses, lest they die by defiling my Dwelling, which is in their midst.
Such is the law concerning the man who has a discharge or is defiled by an emission of semen,
the woman during her period, anyone, man or woman, who has a discharge, and the man who lies with an unclean woman."

titres.titre: The rite of blood in the sanctuary
The goat sent into the wilderness
The perpetual law of the Day of Atonement

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron's two sons, who were struck down for approaching the presence of the Lord.

The Lord said to Moses: "Warn your brother Aaron: he must not enter at any time into the sanctuary, behind the veil, before the mercy seat that covers the ark, or he will die; for I appear in the cloud above the mercy seat.
This is how Aaron shall enter the sanctuary: with a young bull for the sin offering and a ram for the burnt offering.

He shall put on the sacred linen tunic, wear linen undergarments on his body, gird himself with a linen sash, and cover his head with a linen turban: these are the sacred garments, which he shall put on after bathing his body in water.
From the community of Israel he shall receive two goats for the sin offering and a ram for the burnt offering.
Aaron shall offer the bull of the sin offering for his own sin and make atonement for himself and for his household.
Then he shall take the two goats and set them before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Aaron shall cast lots over the two goats: one lot for the Lord, one lot for Azazel.
The goat on which the lot for the Lord has fallen, Aaron shall bring forward and offer as a sin offering.
The goat on which the lot for Azazel has fallen, he shall set alive before the Lord, to perform over it the rite of atonement, then release it into the wilderness, toward Azazel.
So Aaron shall offer the bull of the sin offering for his own sin and make atonement for himself and for his household. After slaughtering it,
he shall take a censer full of burning coals taken from the altar, before the Lord, and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense; he shall carry all this behind the veil
and put the incense on the fire, before the Lord, so that the cloud of incense covers the mercy seat that covers the ark of the Testimony: thus he will not die.

He shall take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the mercy seat, on the east side; then, before the mercy seat, he shall sprinkle some of this blood seven times with his finger.

He shall then slaughter the goat of the sin offering for the people and carry its blood behind the veil; he shall do with this blood as he did with the bull's, sprinkling it on the mercy seat and seven times before it.

Thus he shall make atonement for the sanctuary, because of the uncleannesses of the sons of Israel and all their transgressions; he shall do the same for the tent of meeting, which remains with them in the midst of their uncleannesses.

No one shall be in the tent of meeting from the moment Aaron enters to make atonement in the sanctuary until he comes out. He shall make atonement for himself, for his household, and for the whole assembly of Israel.

On coming out, he shall go to the altar that is before the Lord and make atonement for it: he shall take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood and put it on the horns of the altar, all around.
With his finger he shall sprinkle blood on the altar seven times; he shall cleanse it and consecrate it from the uncleannesses of the sons of Israel.
When he has finished making atonement for the sanctuary, the tent of meeting, and the altar, he shall present the live goat.

Aaron shall lay both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the transgressions of the sons of Israel, all their rebellions and all their sins; he shall put them thus on the head of the goat and send it into the wilderness by a man appointed for this.
The goat shall carry on itself all their transgressions to a solitary land, and it shall be released in the wilderness.
Then Aaron shall enter the tent of meeting, take off the linen garments he had put on to enter the sanctuary, and leave them there.
He shall bathe his body in water, in a holy place, put on his ordinary garments,
then he shall go out, offer his burnt offering and that of the people, make atonement for himself and for the people, and burn on the altar the fat of the sin offering.
The one who released the goat to Azazel shall wash his clothes, bathe his body in water, and only then return to the camp.
The bull and the goat of the sin offering, whose blood was carried into the sanctuary for atonement, shall be carried outside the camp, and their hide, their flesh, and their dung shall be burned.
The one who burned them shall wash his clothes, bathe his body in water, and only then return to the camp.

This shall be a perpetual law for you: in the seventh month (around September-October), on the tenth day of the month, you shall humble yourselves and do no work, neither the native nor the resident alien who lives among you.
For on this day atonement will be made for you, to cleanse you: you will be clean from all your sins before the Lord.
This shall be for you a sabbath, a complete rest, and you shall humble yourselves: it is a perpetual law.

The atonement shall be made by the priest who has received the anointing and has been installed to exercise the priesthood in place of his father. He shall put on the linen garments, the sacred garments,
and shall make atonement for the most holy sanctuary, for the tent of meeting and for the altar, as well as for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
This shall be a perpetual law for you: once a year, atonement shall be made for the sons of Israel, because of all their sins." And it was done as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the sons of Israel; say to them: This is what the Lord has commanded.
Any man of the house of Israel who, in the camp or outside the camp, slaughters an ox, a sheep, or a goat

without bringing it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to the Lord before his Dwelling, that man will be held responsible for bloodshed; he has shed blood, he will be cut off from among his people.

Thus, instead of sacrificing their animals out in the open, the sons of Israel shall bring them to the priest, before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and offer them as a peace offering to the Lord.
The priest shall pour the blood on the altar of the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
They shall no longer offer their sacrifices to demons, those idols to which they prostitute themselves. This shall be for them a perpetual law, from generation to generation.
You shall also say to them: Any man of the house of Israel, or any resident alien living among them, who offers a burnt offering or another sacrifice
without bringing it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to the Lord, that man will be cut off from among his people.
Any man of the house of Israel, or any resident alien living among them, who eats blood of any kind: I will set my face against the one who eats blood and cut him off from among his people.
For the life of every being is in the blood. This blood I have given you for the altar, so that it may make atonement for your lives; for it is the blood that makes atonement, because it is life.
That is why I have said to the sons of Israel: None of you shall eat blood, and the resident alien who lives among you shall not eat it either.
Any man among the sons of Israel, or any resident alien living among them, who catches in hunting an animal or a bird that may be eaten shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth;

for the life of every being is its blood, it is its very life. That is why I have said to the sons of Israel: You shall not eat the blood of any being, for the life of every being is its blood: whoever eats it will be cut off.
Anyone, native or resident alien, who eats an animal that has died or been torn by a wild beast shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and be unclean until evening; then he will be clean.
If he does not wash his clothes and bathe his body, he will bear the weight of his fault."

titres.titre: The call not to imitate the nations
Other prohibitions; the purity of the land

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: I am the Lord, your God.
You shall not act as they act in the land of Egypt, where you lived, nor as they act in the land of Canaan, where I am leading you; you shall not follow their customs.
It is my rules that you shall practice, my laws that you shall keep and follow. I am the Lord, your God.
You shall keep my laws and my rules: the one who puts them into practice will live by them. I am the Lord.
None of you shall approach a close relative to lie with her. I am the Lord.
You shall not lie with your mother: that would be to dishonour your father. She is your mother: you shall not have relations with her.
You shall not lie with another wife of your father: that would be to dishonour your father.
You shall not lie with your sister, whether she is the daughter of your father or of your mother, born in the house or outside.
You shall not lie with your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter: that would be to dishonour yourself.
You shall not lie with the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father: she is your sister.
You shall not lie with your father's sister: she is a close relative of your father.
You shall not lie with your mother's sister: she is a close relative of your mother.
You shall not dishonour your father's brother by approaching his wife: she is your aunt.
You shall not lie with your daughter-in-law: she is your son's wife, you shall not have relations with her.
You shall not lie with your brother's wife: that would be to dishonour your brother.
You shall not lie with a woman and also with her daughter; you shall not take her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to lie with them: they are close relatives, it is a crime.
You shall not take your wife's sister as a rival, lying with her while your wife is still alive.
You shall not approach a woman during her period to lie with her.
You shall not lie with your neighbour's wife: you would make yourself unclean with her.
You shall not hand over any of your children to be passed through the fire in honour of Molech; you shall not profane the name of your God in this way. I am the Lord.
You shall not lie with a man as one lies with a woman: it is an abomination.
You shall not lie with an animal: you would make yourself unclean with it. Nor shall a woman offer herself to an animal to mate with it: it is a perversion.
Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these practices, for it is by them that the nations I am about to drive out before you have defiled themselves.
The land has been defiled by it; I will call it to account for its fault, and the land will vomit out its inhabitants.
But you, you shall keep my laws and my rules, and you shall commit none of these abominations, neither the native nor the resident alien who lives among you.
For all these abominations the inhabitants of the land who were before you committed, and the land was defiled by them.
Thus the land will not vomit you out for having defiled it, as it vomited out the nations who were before you.
All who commit any of these abominations will be cut off from among their people.
You shall keep my precepts and follow none of these abominable customs practiced before you; thus you will not make yourselves unclean by them. I am the Lord, your God."

titres.titre: The duty of justice and charity
Love of the resident alien; just measures

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the whole community of Israel and say to them: Be holy, for I am holy, I the Lord, your God.
Each of you shall respect his mother and his father, and keep my sabbaths. I am the Lord, your God.
Do not turn to idols and do not make yourselves gods of cast metal. I am the Lord, your God.
When you offer a peace offering to the Lord, offer it in such a way as to be accepted.
It shall be eaten on the day of the offering or the next day; whatever is left until the third day shall be burned in the fire.
If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is a foul thing: the sacrifice will not be accepted.
Whoever eats it will bear the weight of his fault, for he profanes what is consecrated to the Lord: that man will be cut off from his people.
When you reap the harvest in your land, you shall not reap to the very edge of your field and you shall not gather the forgotten ears.
You shall not strip your vineyard bare and you shall not gather the fruit fallen from your orchard: you shall leave them for the poor and the resident alien. I am the Lord, your God.
You shall not steal; you shall not use lying or deceit with one another.
You shall not swear falsely by my name: that would be to profane the name of your God. I am the Lord.
You shall not exploit your neighbour and you shall not rob him. The wages of a hired worker shall not stay with you until the next morning.
You shall not curse a deaf person and you shall not put an obstacle before a blind person; you shall fear your God. I am the Lord.
You shall not commit injustice in judgment: you shall not favour the weak and you shall not flatter the powerful, but you shall judge your neighbour with justice.
You shall not spread slander among your people and you shall not seek the death of your neighbour. I am the Lord.
You shall not hate your brother in your heart; you shall reprove your neighbour, so as not to burden yourself with sin because of him.
You shall not take revenge and you shall not hold a grudge against your people. You shall love your neighbour as yourself. I am the Lord.
You shall keep my laws. You shall not mate two different kinds of livestock; you shall not sow your field with two kinds of seed; you shall not wear a garment woven of two kinds of thread.
If a man lies with a woman who is a slave promised to another, without her having been redeemed or set free, they will undergo a punishment, but they will not be put to death, for she was not free.
For his fault, the man shall bring to the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, a ram as a guilt offering.
With this ram the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, for the sin committed, and this sin will be forgiven him.
When you have entered the land and planted all kinds of fruit trees, you shall regard their fruit as forbidden: for three years they shall be forbidden to you, none shall be eaten.
In the fourth year all their fruit shall be consecrated to the Lord in thanksgiving.
In the fifth year you shall eat their fruit, and so the tree will give you more. I am the Lord, your God.
You shall not eat anything with blood. You shall practice neither divination nor sorcery.
You shall not cut your hair in a rounded shape at the temples and you shall not trim the edges of your beard.
You shall not make cuts on your body for a dead person and you shall not make tattoos on yourselves. I am the Lord.
Do not dishonour your daughter by handing her over to prostitution, lest the land give itself to debauchery and be filled with crimes.
You shall keep my sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the Lord.
Do not turn to those who invoke the dead or to soothsayers; do not consult them, so as not to make yourselves unclean by them. I am the Lord, your God.
You shall rise before grey hair and you shall honour the elderly; you shall fear your God. I am the Lord.
If a resident alien comes to live with you in your land, you shall not oppress him.
You shall treat the resident alien who lives among you as one of your own; you shall love him as yourself, for you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord, your God.
You shall not commit injustice, neither in judgment, nor in measures of length, weight, or capacity.
You shall have honest scales, honest weights, an honest measure for grain and an honest measure for liquids. I am the Lord, your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
You shall keep all my laws and all my rules, and put them into practice. I am the Lord."

titres.titre: The call to separation and holiness

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:

"You shall say to the sons of Israel: Any man, among the sons of Israel or among the resident aliens living in Israel, who hands over one of his children to Molech will be put to death: the people of the land will stone him.
And I, I will set my face against that man and cut him off from among his people, because he handed over one of his children to Molech, thus defiling my sanctuary and profaning my holy name.
If the people of the land close their eyes to that man when he hands over one of his children to Molech, and do not put him to death,
I, I will set my face against that man and against his family, and I will cut them off from among their people, him and all who prostitute themselves after him by giving themselves to Molech.
If anyone turns to those who invoke the dead and to soothsayers, prostituting himself after them, I will set my face against that man and cut him off from among his people.
Sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I am the Lord, your God.
You shall keep my laws and put them into practice. I am the Lord, who sanctifies you.
Any man who curses his father or his mother will be put to death: he has cursed his father or his mother, his blood is on his own head.
If a man commits adultery with his neighbour's wife, the adulterous man and woman will both be put to death.
If a man lies with his father's wife, thus dishonouring his father, they will both be put to death: their blood is on their own heads.
If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, they will both be put to death: they have committed a shameful thing, their blood is on their own heads.
If a man lies with a man as one lies with a woman, they have both committed an abomination: they will be put to death, their blood is on their own heads.
If a man takes as wives both a daughter and her mother, it is a crime: they shall be given over to the fire, him and them, so that such a crime may not exist among you.
The man who lies with an animal will be put to death, and you shall kill the animal.
If a woman approaches an animal to mate with it, you shall kill the woman and the animal: they will be put to death, their blood is on their own heads.

If a man takes his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother, and they lie together, it is a disgrace: they will be cut off before the eyes of their people. He has dishonoured his sister, he will bear the weight of his fault.
If a man lies with a woman during her period and dishonours her, he has laid bare the source of her blood, and she herself has uncovered it: they will both be cut off from among their people.
You shall not lie with your mother's sister or with your father's sister: that would be to dishonour your own flesh; they will bear the weight of their fault.
If a man lies with his aunt, he dishonours his uncle; they will bear the weight of their sin: they will die childless.
If a man takes his brother's wife, it is an impurity: he has dishonoured his brother, they will remain childless.
You shall keep all my laws and all my rules, and put them into practice, so that the land where I am leading you to live may not vomit you out.
You shall not follow the customs of the nations I am about to drive out before you; for they committed all these things, and I took them in disgust.

I have said to you: It is you who will possess their land; I will give it to you as a possession, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the Lord, your God, who has set you apart from the other peoples.

You shall therefore distinguish the clean animal from the unclean, the clean bird from the unclean, and you shall not make yourselves foul by animals, birds, or anything that crawls on the ground, which I have taught you to regard as unclean.
You shall be holy for me, for I am holy, I the Lord, and I have set you apart from the other peoples so that you may be mine.
Any man or any woman who invokes the dead or practices divination will be put to death: they shall be stoned, their blood is on their own heads."

titres.titre: The holiness of the high priest
The defects that bar from service

versets.t: The Lord said to Moses: "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them: None of them shall make himself unclean by contact with a dead person among his people,
except for a close relative: his mother, his father, his son, his daughter, his brother,
or his sister who has remained a virgin and is close to him, being unmarried; for her he may make himself unclean.
As a leader among his people, he shall not make himself unclean for others, for he would profane himself.
The priests shall not shave their heads, shall not trim the edges of their beard, and shall not make cuts in their flesh.
They shall be holy for their God and shall not profane his name, for they offer to the Lord the offerings by fire, the bread of their God: they shall therefore be holy.
They shall not marry a prostitute or a dishonoured woman, nor a woman repudiated by her husband, for the priest is holy for his God.
You shall regard him as holy, for he offers the bread of your God; he shall be holy for you, for I am holy, I the Lord, who sanctifies you.
If the daughter of a priest dishonours herself by prostitution, it is her father she dishonours: she shall be burned in the fire.

The high priest, the one preeminent among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been installed to wear the sacred garments, shall not leave his hair unkempt and shall not tear his garments.
He shall not approach any dead person; he shall not make himself unclean even for his father or his mother.
He shall not leave the sanctuary and shall not profane the sanctuary of his God, for the anointing oil of his God is like a diadem upon him. I am the Lord.
He shall take a virgin for his wife.
He shall not marry a widow, or a repudiated woman, one dishonoured or a prostitute, but he shall take for his wife a virgin from his people.
Thus he shall not dishonour his descendants among his people; for I am the Lord, who sanctifies him."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to Aaron and say to him: None of your descendants, in the generations to come, who has a defect, shall approach to offer the bread of his God.
No man who has a defect shall approach: neither the blind, nor the lame, nor one whose face is mutilated or who has a deformed limb,
nor one who has a fracture in the foot or the hand,
nor the hunchback, nor the dwarf, nor one who has a spot in the eye, scabs, a skin disease, or crushed testicles.
No descendant of the priest Aaron who has a defect shall approach to offer to the Lord the offerings by fire: having a defect, he shall not approach to offer the bread of his God.
He may eat the bread of his God, the most holy offerings as well as the holy offerings,
but he shall not go up to the veil and shall not approach the altar, because of his defect; he shall not profane my holy places, for I am the Lord, who sanctifies them."
Thus Moses spoke to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the sons of Israel.

titres.titre: The purity required to eat the holy things

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with respect the holy offerings that the sons of Israel consecrate to me, so as not to profane my holy name. I am the Lord.

Say to them: In the generations to come, any man of your descendants who, in a state of uncleanness, approaches the holy offerings that the sons of Israel consecrate to the Lord, that man will be cut off from my presence. I am the Lord.

Any descendant of Aaron afflicted with leprosy or a discharge shall not eat the holy offerings until he is clean. The same is true for one who touches a person made unclean by a corpse, for one who has an emission of semen,
for one who touches a crawling creature that makes him unclean, or an unclean man from whom he contracts uncleanness of any kind.
Whoever touches these things will be unclean until evening and shall not eat the holy offerings until he has bathed his body in water.
After sunset he will be clean and may eat the holy offerings, for they are his food.
He shall not eat an animal that has died or been torn, which would make him unclean. I am the Lord.
The priests shall keep my prescriptions, so as not to burden themselves with sin and die for having profaned the holy things. I am the Lord, who sanctifies them.
No layperson shall eat the holy offerings; neither a priest's guest nor his hired worker shall eat them.
But the slave whom the priest has bought with his money, he shall eat of them, as well as the one born in his house: these shall eat of his food.
The daughter of a priest married to a layperson shall not eat of what has been set aside from the holy offerings.

But if the daughter of a priest, having become a widow or been repudiated, without children, returns to her father's house as in the time of her youth, she shall eat of her father's food; no layperson, however, shall eat of it.
If someone eats a holy offering by mistake, he shall restore its value to the priest, adding a fifth to it.
The priests shall not profane the holy offerings that the sons of Israel set aside for the Lord;
they shall not make them bear the weight of a fault by letting them eat their holy offerings; for I am the Lord, who sanctifies them."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:

"Speak to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the sons of Israel; say to them: Any man of the house of Israel or any resident alien in Israel who presents his offering, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill gift, and offers it to the Lord as a burnt offering,
must, to be accepted, present a male without defect, taken from the oxen, the sheep, or the goats.
You shall not offer any animal that has a defect, for it would not be accepted.
When a man offers to the Lord cattle or flock as a peace offering, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill gift, the victim, to be accepted, must be perfect: it shall have no defect.
An animal that is blind, injured, mutilated, covered with sores, scabs, or skin disease, you shall not offer to the Lord; you shall not make of it on the altar an offering by fire to the Lord.
An ox or a sheep with a limb too long or too short, you may offer as a freewill gift; but to fulfill a vow, it would not be accepted.
You shall not offer to the Lord an animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn, or cut; you shall not do this in your land.
Nor shall you accept such animals from the hand of a foreigner to offer them as the bread of your God, for they are mutilated, they have a defect: they would not be accepted from you."
The Lord said to Moses:
"When a calf, a lamb, or a kid is born, it shall stay seven days with its mother; from the eighth day on, it may be accepted as an offering by fire to the Lord.
You shall not slaughter on the same day an animal and its young, whether it is an ox or a lamb.
When you offer to the Lord a thanksgiving sacrifice, offer it in such a way as to be accepted:
it shall be eaten that same day, leaving none of it until morning. I am the Lord.
You shall keep my commandments and put them into practice. I am the Lord.
You shall not profane my holy name, so that I may be acknowledged holy among the sons of Israel. I am the Lord, who sanctifies you,
I who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: These are the feasts of the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies; these are my feasts.
Work shall be done for six days, but the seventh day is a sabbath, a complete rest, marked by a holy assembly: you shall do no work. It is a rest consecrated to the Lord, wherever you live.
These are the feasts of the Lord, the holy assemblies that you shall proclaim at their appointed time.
In the first month (around March-April), on the fourteenth day, at twilight, is the Passover of the Lord.
On the fifteenth day of this month is the feast of Unleavened Bread in honour of the Lord: for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
On the first day you shall hold a holy assembly: you shall do no laborious work.
For seven days you shall offer the Lord offerings by fire. On the seventh day there will be a holy assembly: you shall do no laborious work."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you have entered the land I am giving you and reap its harvest, you shall bring the priest a sheaf, the first fruits of your harvest.
He shall wave it before the Lord so that it may be favourable for you; the priest shall wave it on the day after the sabbath.
On the day you wave this sheaf, you shall offer the Lord, as a burnt offering, a year-old lamb without defect.

The grain offering accompanying it shall be about four and a half litres of fine flour mixed with oil, as an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord; the drink offering of wine shall be about one litre.
You shall eat neither bread, nor roasted ears, nor new grain until this very day, until you have brought the offering of your God. It is a perpetual law for your generations, wherever you live.
From the day after the sabbath, the day on which you brought the sheaf to be waved, you shall count seven full weeks.
You shall count fifty days, until the day after the seventh sabbath, and you shall offer the Lord an offering of new grain.
From your dwellings you shall bring two loaves to be waved, made of about four and a half litres of fine flour and baked with leaven: these are the first fruits offered to the Lord.

With these loaves you shall offer as a burnt offering to the Lord seven year-old lambs without defect, one young bull, and two rams, with the grain offering and the drink offering that accompany them: it is an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
You shall also offer one goat as a sin offering, and two year-old lambs as a peace offering.
The priest shall wave them before the Lord with the bread of the first fruits and the two lambs, as a wave offering; they shall be consecrated to the Lord and shall go to the priest.
On that very day you shall make a proclamation and hold a holy assembly: you shall do no laborious work. It is a perpetual law for your generations, wherever you live.

When you reap the harvest in your land, you shall not reap to the very edge of your field and you shall not gather the forgotten ears: you shall leave them for the poor and the resident alien. I am the Lord, your God."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: In the seventh month (around September-October), on the first day, you shall have a solemn rest, commemorated by blasts of the horn, a holy assembly.
You shall do no laborious work and you shall offer the Lord offerings by fire."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"The tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement: you shall hold a holy assembly, you shall humble yourselves, and you shall offer the Lord offerings by fire.
On that day you shall do no work, for it is the Day of Atonement, on which atonement is made for you before the Lord, your God.
Anyone who does not humble himself on that day will be cut off from his people;
and anyone who does any work whatsoever on that day, I will make him perish from among his people.
You shall do no work: it is a perpetual law for your generations, wherever you live.
It shall be for you a sabbath, an absolute rest, and you shall humble yourselves. From the evening of the ninth day of the month until the following evening, you shall observe your rest."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the feast of Booths, celebrated for seven days in honour of the Lord.
On the first day there will be a holy assembly: you shall do no laborious work.

For seven days you shall offer the Lord offerings by fire. On the eighth day you shall hold a holy assembly and you shall offer the Lord offerings by fire: it is an assembly of closing, you shall do no laborious work.
These are the feasts of the Lord that you shall proclaim as holy assemblies, to offer the Lord offerings by fire, burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, each on its day,
in addition to the sabbaths of the Lord, your gifts, all your vows, and all the freewill offerings that you present to the Lord.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered the produce of the land, you shall celebrate the feast of the Lord for seven days; the first day shall be a solemn rest, and the eighth day as well.
On the first day you shall take fine fruit, palm branches, leafy boughs, and river willows, and you shall rejoice before the Lord, your God, for seven days.
You shall celebrate this feast in honour of the Lord seven days each year: it is a perpetual law for your generations; you shall celebrate it in the seventh month.
For seven days you shall live in huts of branches; all who are native-born in Israel shall live in huts,
so that your descendants may know that I made the sons of Israel live in huts when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord, your God."
Thus Moses made known to the sons of Israel the feasts of the Lord.

titres.titre: The lamp and the bread of the Presence

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Command the sons of Israel to bring you, for the lampstand, pure pressed olive oil, to keep the lamps burning continually.

In the tent of meeting, before the veil that screens the ark of the Testimony, Aaron shall tend these lamps from evening until morning, before the Lord, without interruption. It is a perpetual law for your generations.
He shall arrange the lamps on the lampstand of pure gold, so that they burn constantly before the Lord."
"You shall take fine flour and bake twelve loaves from it, each of about four and a half litres.
You shall arrange them in two rows of six on the table of pure gold, before the Lord.
On each row you shall put pure incense, which shall accompany the bread as a memorial portion, offered by fire to the Lord.
Every sabbath day these loaves shall be arranged before the Lord, without interruption, on behalf of the sons of Israel: it is a perpetual covenant.
They shall go to Aaron and his sons, who shall eat them in a holy place; for it is for them a most holy thing among the offerings by fire to the Lord. It is a perpetual law."
The son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian father went out among the sons of Israel, and a quarrel broke out in the camp between him and a man of Israel.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name and cursed it. They brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
They put him under guard, until the Lord should make known what was to be done.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Bring the blasphemer out of the camp; let all who heard him lay their hands on his head, and let the whole community stone him.
Then you shall say to the sons of Israel: Any man who curses his God will bear the weight of his sin;
and whoever blasphemes the name of the Lord will be put to death: the whole community shall stone him. Resident alien or native, whoever blasphemes the Name will be put to death.
Whoever strikes a man dead will be put to death.
Whoever strikes an animal dead shall make restitution for it: life for life.
If anyone injures his neighbour, it shall be done to him as he has done:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; the same injury he has inflicted on another shall be inflicted on him.
Whoever kills an animal shall make restitution for it, but whoever kills a man will be put to death.
You shall have one and the same law for the resident alien as for the native; for I am the Lord, your God."
When Moses had spoken to the sons of Israel, they brought the blasphemer out of the camp and stoned him. The sons of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses.

titres.titre: The redemption of the Israelite sold to a resident alien

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: When you have entered the land I am giving you, the land shall observe a rest, a sabbath for the Lord.
For six years you shall sow your field, prune your vineyard, and gather its produce.
But the seventh year shall be for the land an absolute rest, a sabbath for the Lord: you shall not sow your field and you shall not prune your vineyard.
You shall not reap what has grown of itself since your last harvest, and you shall not gather the grapes of your unpruned vine: it shall be a year of rest for the land.
What the land produces during this rest shall feed you, you, your manservant, your maidservant, your hired worker, and the guest who lives with you,
as well as your livestock and the wild animals of your land: all that it produces shall serve them as food.
You shall count seven weeks of years, seven times seven years, that is forty-nine years.
On the tenth day of the seventh month (around September-October), on the Day of Atonement, you shall sound the horn throughout all your land.
You shall sanctify the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty in the land for all its inhabitants. It shall be for you a jubilee: each of you shall return to his property and return to his family.
The fiftieth year shall be for you a jubilee: you shall not sow, you shall not reap what has grown of itself, and you shall not gather the grapes of the unpruned vine.
For it is a jubilee, it shall be sacred for you: you shall eat what the fields produce of themselves.
In this year of jubilee, each of you shall return to his property.
If you sell something to your neighbour or buy something from him, let no one wrong his brother.
You shall buy from your neighbour according to the number of years elapsed since the last jubilee, and he shall sell to you according to the number of harvest years that remain.
The more years remain, the higher the price will be; the fewer remain, the lower the price, for it is a number of harvests that he is selling you.
Let no one wrong his brother; fear your God, for I am the Lord, your God.
You shall put my laws into practice, keep my rules and apply them; thus you will live securely in the land.
The land will give its fruit, you will eat your fill and live there securely.
Perhaps you will say: What shall we eat in the seventh year, since we will neither sow nor reap?
I will send you my blessing in the sixth year, and it will produce enough to eat for three years.
When you sow in the eighth year, you will still be eating from the old harvest; until the ninth year, until the new harvest, you will eat from the old.
The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is mine, and with me you are only resident aliens and passing guests.
In all the land you possess, you shall grant a right of redemption on the land.
If your brother becomes poor and sells part of his property, his nearest relative shall come to redeem what his brother has sold.
If a man has no one to redeem for him, but himself obtains the means to do it,
he shall count the years elapsed since the sale, repay the surplus to the buyer, and return to his property.
If he does not find the means to repay, the property sold shall remain with the buyer until the year of jubilee; at the jubilee it shall be released, and the seller shall return to his property.
If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, he shall keep the right to redeem it until the end of the year of the sale: his right of redemption shall last a full year.
If the house in the walled city is not redeemed before the end of that year, it shall belong forever to the buyer and his descendants; it shall not be released at the jubilee.
But the houses of villages without a wall shall be counted as fields: they may be redeemed, and they shall be released at the jubilee.
As for the towns of the Levites and the houses they own in them, the Levites shall always keep the right to redeem them.
If someone redeems from a Levite a house, that house sold in his town shall be released at the jubilee, for the houses of the towns of the Levites are their property among the sons of Israel.
The fields surrounding their towns shall not be sold, for they are their property forever.
If your brother becomes poor and can no longer support himself beside you, you shall support him, as you would for a resident alien or a guest, so that he may live beside you.
Take from him neither interest nor profit, but fear your God, so that your brother may live beside you.
You shall not lend him your money at interest and you shall not give him your food for profit.
I am the Lord, your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
If your brother becomes poor beside you and sells himself to you, you shall not impose on him the work of a slave.
He shall be with you like a hired worker or a guest; he shall serve you until the year of jubilee.
Then he shall leave you, he and his children with him, he shall return to his family and return to the property of his fathers.
For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as slaves are sold.
You shall not rule over him with harshness, but you shall fear your God.
The slaves, male and female, that you may have, you shall take from the nations around you: from them you shall buy menservants and maidservants.
You may also buy some from among the children of the guests settled among you and from their families born in your land: they shall be your property.
You shall leave them as an inheritance to your children after you, as a permanent property. But among yourselves, your brothers the sons of Israel, no one shall rule over his brother with harshness.
If a resident alien or a guest settled among you grows rich, and your brother, having become poor beside him, sells himself to this resident alien or to the offspring of a resident alien's family,
he shall keep, after selling himself, the right to be redeemed: one of his brothers may redeem him,
or his uncle, or his uncle's son, or any close relative of his family; or else, if he has the means, he shall redeem himself.

With the one who bought him, he shall count the years from the year of the sale to the year of jubilee; the price of his release shall be fixed according to this number of years, valuing his time as that of a hired worker.
If many years remain, he shall pay his redemption in proportion, out of the price of his purchase;
if few years remain until the jubilee, he shall make the reckoning and pay his redemption in proportion to those years.
He shall be with his master like a worker hired by the year, and the master shall not treat him with harshness before your eyes.
If he is not redeemed in any of these ways, he shall go free in the year of jubilee, he and his children with him.
For it is to me that the sons of Israel are servants: they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the Lord, your God."
"You shall not make idols; you shall not set up statue or sacred stone, and you shall not place in your land any carved stone to bow down before it; for I am the Lord, your God.
You shall keep my sabbaths and revere my sanctuary. I am the Lord."
"If you follow my laws, if you keep my commandments and put them into practice,
I will send you the rains in their season; the land will give its produce and the trees of the fields their fruit.
The threshing of the wheat will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest until the sowing; you will eat your bread to the full and live securely in your land.
I will grant peace in the land: you will sleep with no one to frighten you. I will make the wild beasts disappear from the land, and the sword will not pass through it.
You will pursue your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
Five of you will pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you will pursue ten thousand; your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
I will turn toward you, I will make you fruitful, I will multiply you, and I will maintain my covenant with you.
You will eat harvests stored long ago, and you will have to clear out the old to make room for the new.
I will establish my Dwelling in your midst, and I will not take you in disgust.
I will walk in your midst, I will be your God, and you will be my people.
I am the Lord, your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be slaves there; I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk with head held high.
But if you do not listen to me and do not put into practice all these commandments,
if you despise my laws and take my rules in disgust, refusing to apply my commandments and breaking my covenant,

this is what I will do to you in turn: I will send upon you terror, the disease that consumes and the fever that dims the sight and drains life. You will sow in vain, for your enemies will eat your harvest.
I will turn against you, and you will be beaten by your enemies; those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee with no one pursuing you.
If, despite this, you do not listen to me, I will chastise you seven times more for your sins.
I will break the pride of your strength: I will make your sky hard as iron and your earth hard as bronze.
Your strength will be spent in vain: your land will no longer give its produce, and the trees of the land will no longer give their fruit.
If you continue to resist me and refuse to listen to me, I will strike you seven times more, according to your sins.
I will let loose against you the wild beasts, which will deprive you of your children, tear your livestock, and reduce you to a small number; and your roads will become deserted.
If, despite these chastisements, you do not let yourselves be corrected and continue to resist me,
I in turn will resist you and strike you, I too, seven times more for your sins.
I will bring against you the sword, avenger of my covenant; you will withdraw into your cities, but I will send the plague there, and you will be delivered into the hands of the enemy.
When I withdraw from you the bread, your support, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven and give it back to you weighed by ration; you will eat without being satisfied.
If, despite this, you do not listen to me and continue to resist me,
I will resist you with fury and chastise you, I too, seven times more for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons and the flesh of your daughters.
I will destroy your high places, tear down your incense altars, heap your corpses on those of your foul idols, and I will take you in abhorrence.
I will reduce your cities to ruins, lay waste your sanctuaries, and I will no longer breathe the pleasing aroma of your offerings.
I will lay waste the land, so that your enemies who settle there will be appalled at it.
You, I will scatter among the nations and I will draw the sword behind you; your land will be laid waste and your cities in ruins.
Then the land will pay off its sabbaths, all the time it remains laid waste while you are in the land of your enemies; then the land will rest and pay off its sabbaths.
All the time of its devastation, it will have the rest it did not have during your sabbaths, when you lived there.

To those of you who survive, I will put dread in their hearts in the land of their enemies: the sound of a wind-blown leaf will make them flee; they will flee as before the sword and fall with no one pursuing them.
They will stumble over one another as before the sword, with no one pursuing them; you will not be able to stand before your enemies.
You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will devour you.
Those of you who survive will waste away because of their faults, in the land of their enemies, and also because of the faults of their fathers that still weigh on them.
Then they will confess their fault and that of their fathers, the betrayals committed against me, and will acknowledge that, because they resisted me,
I too resisted them and led them into the land of their enemies. If then their uncircumcised heart, that closed heart, humbles itself and they accept the chastisement of their fault,
I will remember my covenant with Jacob, my covenant with Isaac, and my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.

The land, abandoned by them, will pay off its sabbaths while it remains laid waste far from them; and they will accept the chastisement of their fault, for having despised my rules and taken my laws in disgust.

In spite of everything, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them and will not take them in disgust to the point of exterminating them and breaking my covenant with them; for I am the Lord, their God.
For their sake I will remember the covenant made with their ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt before the eyes of the nations, to be their God. I am the Lord."
These are the laws, the rules, and the instructions that the Lord established between himself and the sons of Israel, on Mount Sinai, through Moses.

titres.titre: Vows concerning animals, houses, and fields
The firstborn, the ban, and the tithe

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them: If someone makes a vow concerning a person to be consecrated to the Lord, that person shall be valued as follows.
For a man from twenty to sixty years old, the valuation shall be fifty pieces of silver, according to the official weight of the sanctuary;
for a woman, it shall be thirty pieces.
From five to twenty years, the valuation shall be twenty pieces for a boy and ten for a girl.
From one month to five years, it shall be five pieces of silver for a boy and three for a girl.
At sixty years and beyond, it shall be fifteen pieces for a man and ten for a woman.
If the one who made the vow is too poor to pay this valuation, he shall be brought before the priest, who shall set the sum according to his means.
If it is an animal that may be offered to the Lord, everything of it that is thus given becomes a holy thing.
It shall not be replaced, a bad one shall not be put in place of a good one nor a good one in place of a bad one; if an animal is replaced by another, both shall become a holy thing.
If it is an unclean animal, that may not be offered to the Lord, it shall be brought before the priest,
who shall set its value according to whether it is good or bad; his valuation shall stand.
If one wishes to redeem it, he shall add a fifth to this valuation.
If someone consecrates his house to the Lord, the priest shall set its value according to whether it is good or bad; his valuation shall stand.
If the one who consecrated his house wishes to redeem it, he shall add a fifth to the estimated price, and it shall be his again.

If someone consecrates to the Lord part of his family field, the valuation shall be made according to the quantity of seed needed, at the rate of fifty pieces of silver for about two hundred litres of barley seed.
If he consecrates his field from the year of jubilee, his valuation shall stand;
but if he consecrates it after the jubilee, the priest shall calculate the price according to the number of years remaining until the jubilee, and the valuation shall be reduced accordingly.
If the one who consecrated his field wishes to redeem it, he shall add a fifth to the estimated price, and the field shall remain his.
If he does not redeem the field, or if he sells it to another, it may no longer be redeemed:
when it is released at the jubilee, this field shall be consecrated to the Lord, like a field devoted by ban, and it shall become the property of the priest.
If someone consecrates to the Lord a field he has bought and which is not part of his patrimony,
the priest shall calculate its price according to the valuation, up to the year of jubilee, and this man shall pay the sum that same day, as a thing consecrated to the Lord.
In the year of jubilee, the field shall return to the one from whom he bought it, to the one whose patrimony it is.
All your valuations shall be made according to the official weight of the sanctuary.
The firstborn of the livestock, however, may not be consecrated, for it already belongs to the Lord by reason of its birth: ox or sheep, it is the Lord's.
If it is an unclean animal, it shall be redeemed at the estimated price, adding a fifth to it; if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold at this price.

But nothing that a man has devoted by ban to the Lord, among all that belongs to him, whether man, animal, or field of his patrimony, may be sold or redeemed: everything devoted by ban is a most holy thing, belonging to the Lord.
No person devoted by ban may be redeemed: he shall be put to death.
Every tithe of the land, taken from the harvests of the fields or the fruit of the trees, belongs to the Lord: it is a thing consecrated to the Lord.
If someone wishes to redeem part of his tithe, he shall add a fifth to it.
As for the tithe of cattle and flock, of all that passes under the shepherd's staff, the tenth shall be consecrated to the Lord.

One shall not sort between the good and the bad and shall make no exchange; if one makes an exchange, the animal replaced and the one that replaces it shall both become a holy thing and may not be redeemed."
These are the commandments that the Lord gave to Moses for the sons of Israel, on Mount Sinai.
The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt. He said:
Take a census of the whole community of the sons of Israel, by their clans and families, counting the names of every male, head by head.
From twenty years old and upward, all in Israel who are able to bear arms, you and Aaron shall enroll them by their divisions.
There shall be with you one man from each tribe, each the head of his family.
These are the names of the men who will assist you. For Reuben: Elizur, son of Shedeur.
For Simeon: Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai.
For Judah: Nahshon, son of Amminadab.
For Issachar: Nethanel, son of Zuar.
For Zebulun: Eliab, son of Helon.
For the sons of Joseph: for Ephraim, Elishama, son of Ammihud; for Manasseh, Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur.
For Benjamin: Abidan, son of Gideoni.
For Dan: Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai.
For Asher: Pagiel, son of Ochran.
For Gad: Eliasaph, son of Deuel.
For Naphtali: Ahira, son of Enan.
These were the ones called from the community, the leaders of their ancestral tribes, the heads of the thousands of Israel.
Moses and Aaron took these men who had been designated by name,

and on the first day of the second month they gathered the whole community. They registered their genealogies by their clans and families, counting the names from twenty years old and upward, head by head,
as the Lord had commanded Moses. So he numbered them in the wilderness of Sinai.

The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: their descendants, by their clans and families, counting the names head by head, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to bear arms,
those enrolled from the tribe of Reuben were forty-six thousand five hundred.
The sons of Simeon: their descendants, by their clans and families, counting the names head by head, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to bear arms,
those enrolled from the tribe of Simeon were fifty-nine thousand three hundred.
The sons of Gad: their descendants, by their clans and families, counting the names, those from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to bear arms,
those enrolled from the tribe of Gad were forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.
The sons of Judah: their descendants, by their clans and families, counting the names, those from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to bear arms,
those enrolled from the tribe of Judah were seventy-four thousand six hundred.
The sons of Issachar: their descendants, by their clans and families, counting the names, those from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to bear arms,
those enrolled from the tribe of Issachar were fifty-four thousand four hundred.
The sons of Zebulun: their descendants, by their clans and families, counting the names, those from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to bear arms,
those enrolled from the tribe of Zebulun were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.
The sons of Joseph, for the sons of Ephraim: their descendants, by their clans and families, counting the names, those from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to bear arms,
those enrolled from the tribe of Ephraim were forty thousand five hundred.
For the sons of Manasseh: their descendants, by their clans and families, counting the names, those from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to bear arms,
those enrolled from the tribe of Manasseh were thirty-two thousand two hundred.
The sons of Benjamin: their descendants, by their clans and families, counting the names, those from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to bear arms,
those enrolled from the tribe of Benjamin were thirty-five thousand four hundred.
The sons of Dan: their descendants, by their clans and families, counting the names, those from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to bear arms,
those enrolled from the tribe of Dan were sixty-two thousand seven hundred.
The sons of Asher: their descendants, by their clans and families, counting the names, those from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to bear arms,
those enrolled from the tribe of Asher were forty-one thousand five hundred.
The sons of Naphtali: their descendants, by their clans and families, counting the names, those from twenty years old and upward, all who were able to bear arms,
those enrolled from the tribe of Naphtali were fifty-three thousand four hundred.
These are the ones counted by Moses and Aaron, together with the twelve leaders of Israel, one for each family.
All the sons of Israel enrolled by their families, from twenty years old and upward, all in Israel who were able to bear arms,
all those enrolled came to six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
But the Levites, by their ancestral tribe, were not enrolled among them.
For the Lord had said to Moses:
You shall not enroll the tribe of Levi or take a census of them among the sons of Israel.

Instead, put the Levites in charge of the Dwelling of the Testimony, all its furnishings, and everything that belongs to it. They shall carry the Dwelling and all its furnishings, they shall serve it, and they shall camp around the Dwelling.
When the Dwelling is to set out, the Levites shall take it down; when the Dwelling is to camp, the Levites shall set it up; any outsider who comes near it shall be put to death.
The sons of Israel shall camp each in his own camp, each by his own standard, according to their divisions.
But the Levites shall camp around the Dwelling of the Testimony, so that no wrath may fall upon the community of the sons of Israel; the Levites shall keep watch over the Dwelling of the Testimony.
The sons of Israel did all this; just as the Lord had commanded Moses, so they did.

titres.titre: The camp of Judah, to the east
The camp of Reuben, to the south
The camp of Ephraim, to the west
The camp of Dan, to the north

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said:
The sons of Israel shall camp each by his own standard, under the emblems of their families; they shall camp around the tent of meeting, at a distance.
At the front, toward the east, shall camp the standard of the camp of Judah, by its divisions. The leader of the sons of Judah is Nahshon, son of Amminadab;
his enrolled host numbers seventy-four thousand six hundred men.
Next to him shall camp the tribe of Issachar. The leader of the sons of Issachar is Nethanel, son of Zuar;
his enrolled host numbers fifty-four thousand four hundred men.
Then the tribe of Zebulun. The leader of the sons of Zebulun is Eliab, son of Helon;
his enrolled host numbers fifty-seven thousand four hundred men.
The total enrolled for the camp of Judah is one hundred and eighty-six thousand four hundred men, by their divisions. They shall set out first.
To the south, the standard of the camp of Reuben, by its divisions. The leader of the sons of Reuben is Elizur, son of Shedeur;
his enrolled host numbers forty-six thousand five hundred men.
Next to him shall camp the tribe of Simeon. The leader of the sons of Simeon is Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai;
his enrolled host numbers fifty-nine thousand three hundred men.
Then the tribe of Gad. The leader of the sons of Gad is Eliasaph, son of Deuel;
his enrolled host numbers forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty men.
The total enrolled for the camp of Reuben is one hundred and fifty-one thousand four hundred and fifty men, by their divisions. They shall set out second.
Then the tent of meeting shall set out, the camp of the Levites, in the middle of the other camps. They shall set out in the order in which they camp, each in his place, by his standard.
To the west, the standard of the camp of Ephraim, by its divisions. The leader of the sons of Ephraim is Elishama, son of Ammihud;
his enrolled host numbers forty thousand five hundred men.
Beside him, the tribe of Manasseh. The leader of the sons of Manasseh is Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur;
his enrolled host numbers thirty-two thousand two hundred men.
Then the tribe of Benjamin. The leader of the sons of Benjamin is Abidan, son of Gideoni;
his enrolled host numbers thirty-five thousand four hundred men.
The total enrolled for the camp of Ephraim is one hundred and eight thousand one hundred men, by their divisions. They shall set out third.
To the north, the standard of the camp of Dan, by its divisions. The leader of the sons of Dan is Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai;
his enrolled host numbers sixty-two thousand seven hundred men.
Next to him shall camp the tribe of Asher. The leader of the sons of Asher is Pagiel, son of Ochran;
his enrolled host numbers forty-one thousand five hundred men.
Then the tribe of Naphtali. The leader of the sons of Naphtali is Ahira, son of Enan;
his enrolled host numbers fifty-three thousand four hundred men.
The total enrolled for the camp of Dan is one hundred and fifty-seven thousand six hundred men. They shall set out last, by their standards.
These are the sons of Israel enrolled by their families. The total enrolled, camp by camp, by their divisions, was six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty men.
But the Levites were not enrolled among the sons of Israel, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The sons of Israel did everything the Lord had commanded Moses: they camped by their standards, and so they set out, each by his clan and his family.

titres.titre: The Levites in place of the firstborn

versets.t: This is the line of Aaron and Moses, at the time when the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab, the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the anointed priests who were ordained to serve as priests.

Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord when they offered unauthorized fire before him in the wilderness of Sinai; they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in the presence of Aaron their father.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Bring the tribe of Levi forward and present it before Aaron the priest, to serve him.
They shall carry out his duties and those of the whole community before the tent of meeting, performing the service of the Dwelling.
They shall have charge of all the furnishings of the tent of meeting and shall fulfill their duty for the sons of Israel, performing the service of the Dwelling.
You shall give the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they are given to him, given wholly from among the sons of Israel.
You shall appoint Aaron and his sons to guard their priesthood; any outsider who comes near shall be put to death.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
See, I have taken the Levites from among the sons of Israel in place of every firstborn, every first to open the womb among the sons of Israel; the Levites are mine.
For every firstborn is mine: on the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to myself every firstborn in Israel, both man and beast; they are mine. I am the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai. He said:
Enroll the sons of Levi by their families and their clans; you shall enroll every male from one month old and upward.
So Moses enrolled them at the command of the Lord, as he had been ordered.
These are the sons of Levi, by their names: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershon, by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath, by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari, by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These are the clans of Levi, by their families.
From Gershon came the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites: these are the clans of the Gershonites.
Their enrollment, counting every male from one month old and upward, was seven thousand five hundred.
The clans of the Gershonites camped behind the Dwelling, to the west.
The head of the ancestral house of the Gershonites was Eliasaph, son of Lael.
In the tent of meeting, the sons of Gershon had charge of the Dwelling and the tent, its covering, and the curtain for the entrance of the tent of meeting,
the hangings of the court, the curtain for the entrance of the court that surrounds the Dwelling and the altar, and its ropes, for all its service.
From Kohath came the clan of the Amramites, the clan of the Izharites, the clan of the Hebronites, and the clan of the Uzzielites: these are the clans of the Kohathites.
Counting every male from one month old and upward, they were eight thousand six hundred, charged with the care of the sanctuary.
The clans of the sons of Kohath camped on the south side of the Dwelling.
The head of the ancestral house of the Kohathite clans was Elizaphan, son of Uzziel.
They had charge of the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the sacred objects used in worship, and the veil, for all their service.
The chief leader of the Levites was Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest; he oversaw those charged with the care of the sanctuary.
From Merari came the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites: these are the clans of Merari.
Their enrollment, counting every male from one month old and upward, was six thousand two hundred.
The head of the ancestral house of the Merari clans was Zuriel, son of Abihail. They camped on the north side of the Dwelling.
To the sons of Merari were entrusted the frames of the Dwelling, its crossbars, its posts, its bases, and all its accessories, for all their service,
as well as the posts of the surrounding court, with their bases, their pegs, and their ropes.

In front of the Dwelling, to the east, in front of the tent of meeting, toward the sunrise, camped Moses, Aaron, and his sons, charged with the care of the sanctuary on behalf of the sons of Israel; any outsider who came near was put to death.
The total of the Levites enrolled by Moses and Aaron at the command of the Lord, by their clans, every male from one month old and upward, was twenty-two thousand.
The Lord said to Moses: Enroll every firstborn male of the sons of Israel, from one month old and upward, and count their names.

You shall take the Levites for me, I am the Lord, in place of all the firstborn of the sons of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the sons of Israel.
So Moses enrolled all the firstborn of the sons of Israel, as the Lord had commanded him.
All the firstborn males, counted by their names, from one month old and upward, came to twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three according to the enrollment.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the sons of Israel, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock; the Levites shall be mine. I am the Lord.
For the ransom of the two hundred and seventy-three firstborn of the sons of Israel who exceed the number of the Levites,
you shall take about fifty-seven grams of silver per head, according to the sanctuary standard weight, which divides into twenty small parts.
You shall give this silver to Aaron and his sons as the ransom for those who are in excess.
So Moses took the ransom silver from those who exceeded the number redeemed by the Levites;
he received this silver from the firstborn of the sons of Israel, about fifteen and a half kilograms, according to the sanctuary standard weight.
Moses gave the ransom silver to Aaron and his sons at the command of the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

titres.titre: The census of those who serve

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said:
Take a count of the sons of Kohath among the sons of Levi, by their clans and families,
from thirty years old up to fifty years old, all who are fit for service, to do the work in the tent of meeting.
This is the service of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting: the most holy things.
When the camp sets out, Aaron and his sons shall come and take down the veil of the screen and cover the ark of the Testimony with it.
They shall put over it a covering of fine leather, spread over that a cloth all of violet purple, and put the poles of the ark in place.

Over the table of the offering they shall spread a cloth of violet purple; on it they shall set the plates, the cups, the bowls, and the pitchers for the libations; the bread of the Presence shall remain on it.
Over these they shall spread a cloth of bright crimson, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put the poles in place.
They shall take a cloth of violet purple and cover the lampstand, its lamps, its snuffers, its trays, and all the oil vessels used for its service.
They shall wrap it and all its accessories in a covering of fine leather and place it on a carrying frame.
Over the golden altar they shall spread a cloth of violet purple, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put the poles in place.
They shall take all the objects used for the service of the sanctuary, wrap them in a cloth of violet purple, cover them with a covering of fine leather, and place them on a carrying frame.
They shall remove the greasy ashes from the altar and spread a cloth of red purple over it.

On it they shall place all the utensils used for its service: the firepans, the forks, the shovels, and the basins, all the utensils of the altar; over it they shall spread a covering of fine leather and put the poles in place.

When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all its objects, at the time the camp sets out, then the sons of Kohath shall come to carry them; but they shall not touch the holy things, or they will die. This is the burden of the sons of Kohath in the tent of meeting.

Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, shall have oversight of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the perpetual grain offering, and the anointing oil; he shall oversee the whole Dwelling and all that is in it, the sanctuary and its objects.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said:
Do not let the tribe of the Kohathite clans be cut off from among the Levites.
Do this for them, so that they may live and not die when they approach the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall go in and assign to each of them his service and his burden.
But they themselves shall not go in to look at the holy things, even for a moment, or they will die.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Take a count of the sons of Gershon also, by their families and clans.
From thirty years old up to fifty years old you shall enroll all who are fit to serve, to do the work in the tent of meeting.
This is the service of the Gershonite clans, what they shall do and carry:
they shall carry the hangings of the Dwelling, the tent of meeting and its covering, the covering of fine leather that is over it, the curtain for the entrance of the tent of meeting,

the hangings of the court, the curtain for the entrance of the gate of the court that surrounds the Dwelling and the altar, their ropes, and all the utensils for their service; they shall do all that needs to be done with these things.

All the service of the sons of Gershon, everything they carry and everything they do, shall be done at the command of Aaron and his sons; you shall assign to them the care of all that they must carry.
This is the service of the clans of the sons of Gershon in the tent of meeting; they shall be under the direction of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
As for the sons of Merari, you shall enroll them by their clans and families.
From thirty years old up to fifty years old you shall enroll all who are fit to serve, to do the work in the tent of meeting.
This is what they shall carry, for all their service in the tent of meeting: the frames of the Dwelling, its crossbars, its posts, and its bases,
the posts of the surrounding court, their bases, their pegs, and their ropes, all their accessories and everything that goes with them. You shall assign by name the objects they are to carry.
This is the service of the clans of the sons of Merari, for all their service in the tent of meeting, under the direction of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the community counted the sons of Kohath, by their clans and families,
from thirty years old up to fifty years old, all who were fit to serve in the tent of meeting.
Those enrolled by their clans were two thousand seven hundred and fifty.
These are those enrolled from the Kohathite clans, all who served in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the command of the Lord given through Moses.
Those enrolled from the sons of Gershon, by their clans and families,
from thirty years old up to fifty years old, all who were fit to serve in the tent of meeting,
those enrolled by their clans and families were two thousand six hundred and thirty.
These are those enrolled from the clans of the sons of Gershon, all who served in the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the command of the Lord.
Those enrolled from the clans of the sons of Merari, by their clans and families,
from thirty years old up to fifty years old, all who were fit to serve in the tent of meeting,
those enrolled by their clans were three thousand two hundred.
These are those enrolled from the clans of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the command of the Lord given through Moses.
The total of the Levites enrolled by Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel, by their clans and families,
from thirty years old up to fifty years old, all who were fit to do the work of service and the carrying in the tent of meeting:
those enrolled were eight thousand five hundred and eighty.
At the command of the Lord given through Moses, each was assigned his service and his burden; they were enrolled as the Lord had commanded Moses.

titres.titre: The sending away of the unclean

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Command the sons of Israel to send out of the camp everyone with a skin disease, everyone with a discharge, and anyone unclean through contact with a corpse.
Male or female, you shall send them away, you shall send them outside the camp, so that they do not defile their camp, in the midst of which I dwell.
The sons of Israel did so: they sent them outside the camp. As the Lord had told Moses, so the sons of Israel did.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Speak to the sons of Israel: When a man or a woman commits any of the wrongs by which one is unfaithful to the Lord, that person has incurred guilt.
They shall confess the wrong they have committed; the guilty one shall make full restitution for the harm done, add a fifth to it, and give it to the one he has wronged.

But if that man has no near relative to whom restitution can be made, the restitution due to the Lord shall go to the priest, in addition to the ram of atonement by which the priest makes atonement for him.
Every contribution taken from the holy things that the sons of Israel bring to the priest shall belong to him.
Each person's holy things are his own; whatever is given to the priest belongs to the priest.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Speak to the sons of Israel: If a man's wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him,
if another man has slept with her without her husband's knowledge, if she has defiled herself in secret with no witness against her and was not caught in the act,

and a spirit of jealousy comes over the husband, making him jealous of his wife who has defiled herself, or if a spirit of jealousy comes over him, making him jealous of a wife who has not defiled herself,

then the man shall bring his wife to the priest and bring an offering for her: about two litres of barley flour. He shall pour no oil on it and put no incense on it, for it is a grain offering of jealousy, an offering of remembrance that recalls a wrong.
The priest shall bring the woman forward and set her before the Lord.
The priest shall take holy water in an earthen vessel; he shall take some dust from the floor of the Dwelling and put it in the water.

The priest shall set the woman before the Lord, unbind her hair, and place in her hands the grain offering of remembrance, the grain offering of jealousy; and the priest shall hold in his hand the bitter water that brings the curse.

The priest shall put the woman under oath and say to her: If no man has slept with you, if you have not gone astray into defilement while under your husband's authority, then may you be unharmed by this bitter water that brings the curse.
But if you have gone astray while under your husband's authority, if you have defiled yourself and a man other than your husband has slept with you,
then, the priest shall say, putting the woman under an oath of imprecation, may the Lord make you a curse and an imprecation among your people, making your thigh waste away and your belly swell;
may this water that brings the curse enter your body to make your belly swell and your thigh waste away. And the woman shall answer: Amen! Amen!
