The priest shall write these curses on a scroll and then wash them off into the bitter water.
He shall make the woman drink the bitter water that brings the curse, and this water of the curse shall enter her and turn bitter.
The priest shall take from the woman's hand the grain offering of jealousy, wave it before the Lord, and bring it to the altar.
The priest shall take a handful of the offering as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar; then he shall make the woman drink the water.

When he has made her drink the water, if she has defiled herself and betrayed her husband, the water of the curse shall enter her and turn bitter, her belly shall swell and her thigh waste away; this woman shall become a curse among her people.
But if the woman has not defiled herself and is pure, she shall be unharmed and able to bear children.
This is the law concerning jealousy, when a woman goes astray while under her husband's authority and defiles herself,
or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and makes him jealous of his wife: he shall set the woman before the Lord, and the priest shall apply to her this whole law.
The man shall be free of any wrong, but this woman shall bear her own guilt.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Speak to the sons of Israel: If a man or a woman makes the special Nazirite vow, consecrating themselves to the Lord,
they shall abstain from wine and strong drink; they shall drink no vinegar of wine or vinegar of strong drink, drink no grape juice, and eat neither fresh grapes nor dried.
For the whole time of their consecration, they shall eat nothing that comes from the vine, from the seeds to the skin.

For the whole time of their Nazirite vow, no razor shall pass over their head; until the time for which they have consecrated themselves to the Lord is complete, they shall be holy and shall let the hair of their head grow freely.
For the whole time of their consecration to the Lord, they shall not go near any dead body.
Even for their father, their mother, their brother, or their sister, they shall not make themselves unclean at their death, for the sign of their consecration to their God is on their head.
For the whole time of their Nazirite vow, they are consecrated to the Lord.
If someone dies suddenly beside them and defiles their consecrated head, they shall shave their head on the day of their purification; they shall shave it on the seventh day.
On the eighth day, they shall bring to the priest two turtledoves or two young pigeons, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering; he shall make atonement for them for the guilt incurred through contact with the dead, and that same day they shall consecrate their head again.

They shall consecrate themselves to the Lord anew for the time of their Nazirite vow and bring a year-old lamb as a guilt offering; the preceding days shall be void, for their consecration had been defiled.
This is the law of the Nazirite. When the time of their consecration is complete, they shall be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting.
They shall present their offering to the Lord: a year-old lamb without blemish as a burnt offering, a year-old ewe lamb without blemish as a sin offering, a ram without blemish as a peace offering,
a basket of unleavened bread, cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers brushed with oil, together with the grain offering and the libations that go with them.
The priest shall present all this before the Lord and offer the sin offering and the burnt offering.
He shall offer the ram as a peace offering to the Lord, with the basket of unleavened bread; then the priest shall offer its grain offering and its libation.
The Nazirite shall shave their consecrated head at the entrance of the tent of meeting; they shall take the hair of their consecrated head and put it on the fire that is under the peace offering.

The priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram, one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put them in the hands of the Nazirite, after the Nazirite has shaved the consecrated head.

The priest shall wave them as a wave offering before the Lord: this is a holy portion that belongs to the priest, along with the breast that is waved and the thigh that is raised. After this, the Nazirite may drink wine.

This is the law of the Nazirite who makes a vow, and this is their offering to the Lord for their Nazirite vow, apart from whatever else their means allow; they shall fulfill their vow according to the law of their Nazirite vow.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Speak to Aaron and his sons: This is how you shall bless the sons of Israel. You shall say to them:
The Lord bless you and keep you.
The Lord make his face shine upon you and be gracious to you.
The Lord turn his face toward you and give you peace.
So they shall put my name upon the sons of Israel, and I will bless them.
On the day Moses finished setting up the Dwelling, when he anointed and consecrated it with all its furnishings, and anointed and consecrated the altar and all its utensils as well,
the leaders of Israel, the heads of their families, those who were at the head of the tribes and had presided over the census, presented their offering.
They brought it before the Lord: six covered wagons and twelve oxen, one wagon for every two leaders and one ox for each; they presented them before the Dwelling.
The Lord said to Moses:
Accept these from them: they shall be used for the service of the tent of meeting. You shall give them to the Levites, to each according to his service.
So Moses took the wagons and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
He gave two wagons and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, according to their service;
he gave four wagons and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, according to their service, under the direction of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
But he gave none to the sons of Kohath, because the service entrusted to them, that of the sacred objects, was carried on their shoulders.
The leaders presented their offering for the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed; they presented their offering before the altar.
The Lord said to Moses: Each day, in turn, one leader shall present his offering for the dedication of the altar.
On the first day, Nahshon, son of Amminadab, leader of the sons of Judah, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing about one and a half kilograms and one silver bowl of about eight hundred grams, according to the sanctuary standard weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering;
one gold pan of about one hundred and fifteen grams, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for the burnt offering;
one male goat for the sin offering;
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Nahshon, son of Amminadab.
On the second day, Nethanel, son of Zuar, leader of the sons of Issachar, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing about one and a half kilograms and one silver bowl of about eight hundred grams, according to the sanctuary standard weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering;
one gold pan of about one hundred and fifteen grams, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for the burnt offering;
one male goat for the sin offering;
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Nethanel, son of Zuar.
On the third day, Eliab, son of Helon, leader of the sons of Zebulun, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing about one and a half kilograms and one silver bowl of about eight hundred grams, according to the sanctuary standard weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering;
one gold pan of about one hundred and fifteen grams, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for the burnt offering;
one male goat for the sin offering;
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Eliab, son of Helon.
On the fourth day, Elizur, son of Shedeur, leader of the sons of Reuben, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing about one and a half kilograms and one silver bowl of about eight hundred grams, according to the sanctuary standard weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering;
one gold pan of about one hundred and fifteen grams, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for the burnt offering;
one male goat for the sin offering;
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Elizur, son of Shedeur.
On the fifth day, Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai, leader of the sons of Simeon, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing about one and a half kilograms and one silver bowl of about eight hundred grams, according to the sanctuary standard weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering;
one gold pan of about one hundred and fifteen grams, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for the burnt offering;
one male goat for the sin offering;
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day, Eliasaph, son of Deuel, leader of the sons of Gad, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing about one and a half kilograms and one silver bowl of about eight hundred grams, according to the sanctuary standard weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering;
one gold pan of about one hundred and fifteen grams, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for the burnt offering;
one male goat for the sin offering;
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Eliasaph, son of Deuel.
On the seventh day, Elishama, son of Ammihud, leader of the sons of Ephraim, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing about one and a half kilograms and one silver bowl of about eight hundred grams, according to the sanctuary standard weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering;
one gold pan of about one hundred and fifteen grams, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for the burnt offering;
one male goat for the sin offering;
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Elishama, son of Ammihud.
On the eighth day, Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur, leader of the sons of Manasseh, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing about one and a half kilograms and one silver bowl of about eight hundred grams, according to the sanctuary standard weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering;
one gold pan of about one hundred and fifteen grams, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for the burnt offering;
one male goat for the sin offering;
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur.
On the ninth day, Abidan, son of Gideoni, leader of the sons of Benjamin, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing about one and a half kilograms and one silver bowl of about eight hundred grams, according to the sanctuary standard weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering;
one gold pan of about one hundred and fifteen grams, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for the burnt offering;
one male goat for the sin offering;
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Abidan, son of Gideoni.
On the tenth day, Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai, leader of the sons of Dan, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing about one and a half kilograms and one silver bowl of about eight hundred grams, according to the sanctuary standard weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering;
one gold pan of about one hundred and fifteen grams, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for the burnt offering;
one male goat for the sin offering;
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai.
On the eleventh day, Pagiel, son of Ochran, leader of the sons of Asher, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing about one and a half kilograms and one silver bowl of about eight hundred grams, according to the sanctuary standard weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering;
one gold pan of about one hundred and fifteen grams, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for the burnt offering;
one male goat for the sin offering;
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Pagiel, son of Ochran.
On the twelfth day, Ahira, son of Enan, leader of the sons of Naphtali, presented his offering.

His offering was one silver plate weighing about one and a half kilograms and one silver bowl of about eight hundred grams, according to the sanctuary standard weight, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for the grain offering;
one gold pan of about one hundred and fifteen grams, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram, and one year-old lamb for the burnt offering;
one male goat for the sin offering;
and for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five year-old lambs. This was the offering of Ahira, son of Enan.
These were the gifts offered for the dedication of the altar, on the day it was anointed, from the leaders of Israel: twelve silver plates, twelve silver bowls, twelve gold pans.

Each silver plate weighed about one and a half kilograms, and each bowl about eight hundred grams; the silver of these objects came in all to about twenty-seven kilograms, according to the sanctuary standard weight.

The twelve gold pans full of incense weighed about one hundred and fifteen grams each, according to the sanctuary standard weight; the gold of these pans came in all to about one and a half kilograms.
The total of the livestock for the burnt offering: twelve bulls, twelve rams, twelve year-old lambs, with their grain offering; and twelve male goats for the sin offering.

The total of the livestock for the peace offering: twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, sixty year-old lambs. These were the gifts for the dedication of the altar, after it had been anointed.

When Moses went into the tent of meeting to speak with the Lord, he would hear the voice speaking to him from above the mercy seat that was on the ark of the Testimony, between the two cherubim; and it spoke to him.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Speak to Aaron: When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light in front of the lampstand.
Aaron did so: he set up the lamps of the lampstand toward the front, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
This is how the lampstand was made: of hammered gold, from its base to its flowers, hammered work; it was according to the pattern the Lord had shown Moses that the lampstand was made.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Take the Levites from among the sons of Israel and purify them.
This is how you shall purify them: sprinkle on them the water of purification; they shall pass a razor over their whole body, wash their clothes, and purify themselves.
They shall take a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, and you shall take a second young bull for the sin offering.
You shall bring the Levites forward before the tent of meeting and gather the whole community of the sons of Israel.
You shall bring the Levites forward before the Lord, and the sons of Israel shall lay their hands on the Levites.
Aaron shall present the Levites as a wave offering before the Lord, on behalf of the sons of Israel; thus they shall be set apart for the service of the Lord.
The Levites shall lay their hands on the heads of the bulls; you shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the Lord, to make atonement for the Levites.
You shall set the Levites before Aaron and his sons and present them as a wave offering to the Lord.
In this way you shall separate the Levites from among the sons of Israel, and the Levites shall be mine.
After that, the Levites shall come to do the service of the tent of meeting. You shall purify them and present them as a wave offering.
For they are wholly given to me from among the sons of Israel; I have taken them for myself in place of every first to open the womb, every firstborn of the sons of Israel.
For every firstborn among the sons of Israel is mine, both man and beast; on the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated them to myself.
I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the sons of Israel,

and I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons, from among the sons of Israel, to do the service of the sons of Israel in the tent of meeting and to make atonement for them, so that no plague may strike the sons of Israel when they approach the sanctuary.
Moses, Aaron, and the whole community of the sons of Israel acted toward the Levites exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses concerning them; so the sons of Israel acted toward them.
The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes; Aaron presented them as a wave offering before the Lord and made atonement for them to purify them.
After that, the Levites came to do their service in the tent of meeting, in the presence of Aaron and his sons. As the Lord had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so it was done for them.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
This concerns the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward, a Levite shall come to take part in the service of the tent of meeting.
From fifty years old, he shall withdraw from active service and serve no longer.
He may help his brothers in the tent of meeting by keeping guard, but he shall no longer do the service. This is how you shall deal with the Levites in their duties.
The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt, in the first month. He said:
Let the sons of Israel celebrate the Passover at its appointed time.
On the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight, you shall celebrate it at its appointed time; you shall celebrate it according to all its statutes and all its rites.
So Moses told the sons of Israel to celebrate the Passover,
and they celebrated it in the wilderness of Sinai, on the fourteenth day of the first month, at twilight. The sons of Israel did everything the Lord had commanded Moses.
Now there were some men who were unclean through contact with a corpse and could not celebrate the Passover that day. They came before Moses and Aaron that same day,
and these men said to him: "We are unclean through contact with a corpse; why should we be kept from presenting the Lord's offering at its appointed time, among the sons of Israel?"
Moses answered them: "Wait here, and let me hear what the Lord will command concerning you."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Speak to the sons of Israel: If any of you or your descendants is unclean through contact with a corpse, or is away on a distant journey, he may still celebrate the Passover for the Lord.
They shall celebrate it in the second month, on the fourteenth day, at twilight; they shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They shall leave none of it until morning and shall break none of its bones; they shall celebrate it according to all the statutes of the Passover.

But the man who is clean and not on a journey, if he refrains from celebrating the Passover, that person shall be cut off from his people; because he did not present the Lord's offering at its appointed time, that man shall bear his sin.

If a foreigner residing among you wishes to celebrate the Passover for the Lord, he shall celebrate it according to the statutes and rites of the Passover. There shall be one and the same statute for you, for the foreigner as for the native of the land.
On the day the Dwelling was set up, the cloud covered the Dwelling, the tent of the Testimony; in the evening it had the appearance of fire over the Dwelling, until morning.
So it was continually: the cloud covered it, and by night it had the appearance of fire.
Whenever the cloud lifted from over the tent, the sons of Israel set out; and wherever the cloud settled, there they camped.
At the command of the Lord the sons of Israel set out, and at the command of the Lord they camped; as long as the cloud remained over the Dwelling, they stayed camped.
When the cloud remained a long time over the Dwelling, the sons of Israel kept the Lord's charge and did not set out.
Sometimes the cloud remained only a few days over the Dwelling: at the command of the Lord they camped, and at the command of the Lord they set out.
Sometimes the cloud remained from evening until morning, and when it lifted in the morning, they set out; whether by day or by night, as soon as it lifted, they set out.
Whether the cloud stayed two days, a month, or a year over the Dwelling, the sons of Israel stayed camped and did not set out; but as soon as it lifted, they set out.
At the command of the Lord they camped, and at the command of the Lord they set out; they kept the Lord's charge, according to the command of the Lord given through Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Make yourself two trumpets; you shall make them of hammered silver. They shall serve you to summon the community and to give the signal for the camps to set out.
When both are sounded, the whole community shall gather to you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
If only one is sounded, the leaders, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather to you.
When you sound a blast, the camps stationed to the east shall set out.
When you sound a blast a second time, the camps stationed to the south shall set out: a blast shall be sounded for their departure.
To gather the assembly, you shall sound the trumpets too, but without the same blasts.
It is the sons of Aaron, the priests, who shall sound the trumpets; this shall be a perpetual decree for you, from generation to generation.
When you go to war in your land against an enemy who oppresses you, you shall sound the trumpets with a blast: so you will be remembered before the Lord your God and be delivered from your enemies.

On your days of joy, at your feasts, and at your new moons, you shall sound the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your peace offerings; they will bring you to remembrance before your God. I am the Lord your God.
In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud lifted from over the Dwelling of the Testimony.
The sons of Israel set out from the wilderness of Sinai, in their order of march, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
This was the first time they set out, at the command of the Lord given through Moses.
The standard of the camp of the sons of Judah set out first, by their divisions; at the head of its host was Nahshon, son of Amminadab.
At the head of the host of the tribe of the sons of Issachar was Nethanel, son of Zuar.
At the head of the host of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun was Eliab, son of Helon.
Then the Dwelling was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari set out, carrying it.
The standard of the camp of Reuben set out next, by their divisions; at the head of its host was Elizur, son of Shedeur.
At the head of the host of the tribe of the sons of Simeon was Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai.
At the head of the host of the tribe of the sons of Gad was Eliasaph, son of Deuel.
Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the sacred objects; the Dwelling was set up before their arrival.
The standard of the camp of the sons of Ephraim set out next, by their divisions; at the head of its host was Elishama, son of Ammihud.
At the head of the host of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh was Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur.
At the head of the host of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin was Abidan, son of Gideoni.
The standard of the camp of the sons of Dan, forming the rear guard of all the camps, set out last, by their divisions; at the head of its host was Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai.
At the head of the host of the tribe of the sons of Asher was Pagiel, son of Ochran.
At the head of the host of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali was Ahira, son of Enan.
This was the order of march of the sons of Israel, by their divisions, when they set out.

Moses said to Hobab, son of Reuel the Midianite, his father-in-law: "We are setting out for the place of which the Lord said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us, and we will do you good, for the Lord has promised good things to Israel."
Hobab answered him: "I will not go; I am going back to my own land and my own kindred."
Moses said again: "Please do not leave us; you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can be our guide.
If you come with us, whatever good the Lord grants us, we will share with you."
So they set out from the mountain of the Lord and marched for three days; the ark of the covenant of the Lord went ahead of them during those three days' march, to seek out a resting place for them.
The cloud of the Lord was over them by day, when they set out from the camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say: "Arise, Lord! May your enemies be scattered, may those who hate you flee before you!"
And whenever it came to rest, he would say: "Return, Lord, to the countless thousands of Israel!"
The people complained bitterly in the hearing of the Lord. The Lord heard it, and his anger was kindled: the fire of the Lord began to burn among them and consumed the edge of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses; Moses prayed to the Lord, and the fire died down.
That place was named Taberah, that is, the Burning, because the fire of the Lord had burned among them.
The mixed crowd that had joined the people was seized with craving; the sons of Israel themselves began to weep again and said: "Who will give us meat to eat?
We remember the fish we ate for nothing in Egypt, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions, and the garlic.
But now we are worn out; there is nothing at all, nothing before our eyes but this manna."
The manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance like that of bdellium.
The people would scatter to gather it; they ground it in a mill or crushed it in a mortar, boiled it in a pot, and made it into cakes; it tasted like a cake baked with oil.
When the dew came down on the camp during the night, the manna came down with it.
Moses heard the people weeping, family after family, each at the entrance of his tent. The anger of the Lord was kindled fiercely, and Moses was troubled.
Moses said to the Lord: "Why do you treat your servant so badly? Why have I not found favor in your eyes, that you lay the burden of all this people on me?
Did I conceive all this people? Did I give them birth, that you should say to me, Carry them in your arms, as a nurse carries an infant, to the land you promised on oath to their fathers?
Where am I to find meat to give to all this people? For they weep before me, saying, Give us meat to eat!
I cannot carry all this people by myself; the burden is too heavy for me.
If this is how you treat me, then kill me, I beg you, if I have found favor in your eyes, and let me not see my misery any longer!"

The Lord said to Moses: "Gather for me seventy men from among the elders of Israel, men you know to be elders of the people and its officers; bring them to the tent of meeting, and let them stand there with you.
I will come down and speak with you there; I will take some of the spirit that is on you and put it on them, so that they may share with you the burden of the people, and you will not carry it alone.

And say to the people: Sanctify yourselves for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat, since you have wept in the hearing of the Lord, saying, Who will give us meat to eat? How well off we were in Egypt! Now the Lord will give you meat, and you shall eat.
You shall eat it not for one day, nor two, nor five, nor ten, nor twenty,
but for a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and makes you sick; for you have rejected the Lord who is in your midst, and you have wept before him, saying, Why did we ever leave Egypt?"
Moses said: "The people among whom I am number six hundred thousand men on foot, and you say, I will give them meat, and they shall eat it for a whole month!
Are flocks and herds to be slaughtered for them, to be enough for them? Are all the fish of the sea to be gathered for them, to be enough for them?"
The Lord said to Moses: "Is the arm of the Lord too short? Now you will see whether or not my word comes true for you."
So Moses went out and told the people the words of the Lord. He gathered seventy men from among the elders of the people and stationed them around the tent.

The Lord came down in the cloud and spoke to him; he took some of the spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy elders. As soon as the spirit rested on them, they began to prophesy, but they did not do so again.

Two men had stayed in the camp; one was named Eldad, the other Medad. The spirit rested on them too, for they were among those registered, though they had not gone out to the tent: they prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran to tell Moses: "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!"
Joshua, son of Nun, who had served Moses from his youth, spoke up: "Moses, my lord, stop them!"
Moses answered him: "Are you jealous on my behalf? If only all the Lord's people were prophets, and the Lord would put his spirit on them!"
Then Moses withdrew into the camp, with the elders of Israel.
A wind sent by the Lord rose up: it brought quails from the direction of the sea and dropped them on the camp, about a day's journey on each side, all around the camp, about a metre above the ground.

The people got up and, all that day, all that night, and all the next day, gathered the quails; the one who gathered least had about two thousand two hundred litres, and they spread them out all around the camp.
The meat was still between their teeth, before it was even chewed, when the anger of the Lord was kindled against the people: the Lord struck the people with a very great plague.
That place was named Kibroth-hattaavah, that is, the Graves of Craving, because there they buried the people who had given in to their craving.
From Kibroth-hattaavah the people set out for Hazeroth, and they stopped at Hazeroth.
Miriam, together with Aaron, began to speak against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had taken; for he had married a Cushite.
They said: "Has the Lord spoken only through Moses? Has he not also spoken through us?" And the Lord heard it.
Now Moses was a very humble man, more so than anyone else on the face of the earth.
Suddenly the Lord said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam: "Come out, the three of you, to the tent of meeting." So the three of them came out.
The Lord came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent; he called Aaron and Miriam, and the two of them came forward.
He said: "Listen now to my words. If there is a prophet among you, it is in a vision that I, the Lord, make myself known to him, it is in a dream that I speak to him.
It is not so with my servant Moses: in all my house, he is faithful.
I speak with him mouth to mouth, plainly and not in riddles, and he beholds the form of the Lord. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?"
The anger of the Lord was kindled against them, and he departed.
When the cloud withdrew from over the tent, Miriam was covered with a skin disease, white as snow. Aaron turned toward Miriam: she was diseased.
Aaron said to Moses: "Please, my lord, do not hold against us the sin we have committed in our folly!
Do not let her be like the stillborn child whose flesh is half consumed when it comes from its mother's womb!"
Moses cried out to the Lord: "O God, heal her, I beg you!"
The Lord said to Moses: "If her father had spit in her face, would she not be in disgrace for seven days? Let her be shut out of the camp for seven days, and after that she may be brought back."
So Miriam was shut out of the camp for seven days, and the people did not set out until she was brought back.
After that, the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Send men to explore the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the sons of Israel. You shall send one man from each ancestral tribe, each of them a leader among his people.
So Moses sent them out from the wilderness of Paran, at the Lord's command; all of them were chiefs of the sons of Israel.
These are their names. For the tribe of Reuben: Shammua son of Zaccur.
For the tribe of Simeon: Shaphat son of Hori.
For the tribe of Judah: Caleb son of Jephunneh.
For the tribe of Issachar: Igal son of Joseph.
For the tribe of Ephraim: Hoshea son of Nun.
For the tribe of Benjamin: Palti son of Raphu.
For the tribe of Zebulun: Gaddiel son of Sodi.
For the tribe of Joseph, that is, of Manasseh: Gaddi son of Susi.
For the tribe of Dan: Ammiel son of Gemalli.
For the tribe of Asher: Sethur son of Michael.
For the tribe of Naphtali: Nahbi son of Vophsi.
For the tribe of Gad: Geuel son of Machi.
These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to explore the land. And Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.
Moses sent them to explore the land of Canaan, saying to them: "Go up through the Negev, then climb the hill country.
See what the land is like, and the people who live in it: are they strong or weak, few or many?
Is the land they live in good or bad? Are the towns they live in open camps or fortified strongholds?
Is the soil rich or poor, wooded or not? Be bold, and bring back some of the fruit of the land." It was the season of the first grapes.
So they went up and explored the land, from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, toward the entrance to Hamath.
They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, were living. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
They came to the valley of Eshcol, and there they cut a branch with a single cluster of grapes, which they carried on a pole between two of them, along with some pomegranates and figs.
That place was named the valley of Eshcol, that is, the valley of the Cluster, because of the cluster of grapes that the sons of Israel had cut there.
At the end of forty days they returned from exploring the land.

They went to Moses and Aaron and the whole community of the sons of Israel, in the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh; they gave their report to them and to the whole community, and showed them the fruit of the land.
This is the account they gave to Moses: "We went into the land where you sent us. It truly flows with milk and honey, and here is its fruit.
But the people who live there are strong, the towns are fortified and very large, and we even saw the descendants of Anak there.
Amalek lives in the region of the Negev; the Hittites, the Jebusites, and the Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live along the sea and beside the Jordan."
Caleb silenced the people before Moses and said: "Let us go up at once and take possession of the land, for we are well able to do it!"
But the men who had gone up with him said: "We cannot attack these people, for they are stronger than we are."

And they began to disparage before the sons of Israel the land they had explored: "The land we travelled through to explore it is a land that devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw there are of great stature.
There we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, of the race of giants; we seemed to ourselves like grasshoppers, and so we seemed to them."
The whole community raised their voices and cried out, and the people wept that night.
All the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole community said to them: "If only we had died in the land of Egypt, or if only we had died in this wilderness!
Why is the Lord leading us into this land, only to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will become plunder. Would it not be better for us to go back to Egypt?"
And they said to one another: "Let us choose a leader and go back to Egypt!"
Then Moses and Aaron fell face down before the whole assembly of the community of the sons of Israel.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had explored the land, tore their clothes
and said to the whole community of the sons of Israel: "The land we travelled through to explore it is an excellent land, truly excellent.
If the Lord is pleased with us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land that flows with milk and honey.
Only do not rebel against the Lord, and do not be afraid of the people of the land: we will swallow them up. Their protecting shade has left them, and the Lord is with us: do not be afraid of them!"
The whole community was talking of stoning them, when the glory of the Lord appeared at the tent of meeting to all the sons of Israel.
The Lord said to Moses: "How long will this people despise me? How long will they refuse to believe in me, in spite of all the signs I have done among them?
I will strike them with plague and disinherit them; and I will make of you a nation greater and mightier than they."
Moses said to the Lord: "The Egyptians will hear of it, they from whose midst you brought up this people by your power,

and they will tell it to the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that you, Lord, are in the midst of this people, that you, Lord, show yourself to them face to face, that your cloud stands over them, and that you go before them, by day in a pillar of cloud and by night in a pillar of fire.
If you put this people to death as one man, the nations that have heard of you will say:
It was because the Lord could not bring this people into the land he had promised them by oath that he slaughtered them in the wilderness.
Now let the power of the Lord be shown great, as you have said:

The Lord is slow to anger and rich in faithful love; he forgives fault and rebellion; yet he leaves nothing unpunished, visiting the fault of the fathers on the children, to the third and fourth generation.
Forgive, then, the fault of this people, in the greatness of your faithful love, as you have borne with this people from Egypt until now."
The Lord said: "I forgive them, as you have asked.
But as surely as I live and as the glory of the Lord fills the whole earth:
none of these men who have seen my glory and the signs I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and who have nonetheless tested me ten times already without listening to my voice,
will see the land I promised on oath to their fathers; none of those who despised me will see it.
But my servant Caleb, because a different spirit moves him and he has followed me fully, I will bring into the land he entered, and his descendants will possess it.
Since the Amalekites and the Canaanites are living in the valley, tomorrow turn back and set out again for the wilderness, by the way of the Red Sea."
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said:
"How long shall I bear with this wicked community that grumbles against me? The grumblings that the sons of Israel utter against me, I have heard them.
Tell them: As surely as I live, says the Lord, I will do to you the very thing you spoke in my hearing:
in this wilderness your corpses will fall, all of you who were counted, everyone twenty years old and above, you who grumbled against me.
You shall not enter the land where I swore with uplifted hand to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
But your little ones, who you said would become plunder, I will bring in, and they will know the land you scorned.
As for you, your corpses will fall in this wilderness,
and your children will wander in the wilderness for forty years, bearing the weight of your unfaithfulness, until the last of your corpses lies in the wilderness.

According to the number of days you spent exploring the land, forty days, a year for each day, you shall bear the weight of your faults for forty years, and you will know what it costs to have opposed me.
I, the Lord, have spoken: this is what I will do to this whole wicked community that has banded together against me. In this wilderness they will meet their end; here they will die."
The men whom Moses had sent to explore the land, and who on their return had led the whole community to grumble against him by disparaging the land,
these men who had disparaged the land died, struck down by a plague before the Lord.
Only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive of the men who had gone to explore the land.
Moses reported these words to all the sons of Israel, and the people mourned deeply.
Early the next morning they went up toward the top of the hill country, saying: "Here we are! We will go up to the place the Lord has promised, for we have sinned."
But Moses said: "Why are you transgressing the command of the Lord? It will not succeed.
Do not go up, for the Lord is not among you; do not let yourselves be beaten by your enemies.
The Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you, and you will fall by the sword; because you have turned away from the Lord, the Lord will not be with you."
Yet they stubbornly went up toward the top of the hill country; but neither the ark of the covenant of the Lord nor Moses left the camp.
Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down, struck them, and cut them to pieces as far as Hormah.

titres.titre: The offerings that accompany the sacrifices
The unintentional sin and the deliberate sin

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Speak to the sons of Israel: When you have entered the land where you are to live, which I am giving you,

and you offer to the Lord an offering by fire, a burnt offering or a sacrifice, whether to fulfil a vow or as a freewill offering, or at your appointed feasts, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord, from the herd or from the flock,
the one who presents his offering shall bring to the Lord a grain offering of about two litres of fine flour mixed with about one litre of oil.
You shall add about one litre of wine as a drink offering to the burnt offering or the sacrifice, for each lamb.
For a ram you shall present a grain offering of about four litres of fine flour mixed with about one and a half litres of oil,
and as a drink offering about one and a half litres of wine: you shall offer them as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If you offer a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfil a vow or as a peace offering to the Lord,
you shall present with the bull a grain offering of about six litres of fine flour mixed with about two litres of oil,
and you shall offer as a drink offering about two litres of wine: it is an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
This is to be done for each bull, for each ram, and for each lamb or young goat.
According to the number of animals you offer, you shall do this for each one, according to their number.
Every native of the land shall do these things in this way when he offers an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If a foreigner residing among you, or anyone living among you throughout your generations, offers an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord, he shall do as you do.

There shall be one rule for you, the people of the assembly, and for the foreigner residing among you: it is a perpetual rule throughout your generations; before the Lord it shall be the same for you and for the foreigner.
One law and one ordinance shall apply to you and to the foreigner residing among you.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Speak to the sons of Israel: When you have entered the land into which I am bringing you,
and you eat the bread of that land, you shall set aside a contribution for the Lord.
As the firstfruits of your dough, you shall set aside a loaf; you shall set it aside as the contribution from the threshing floor.
From the firstfruits of your dough you shall give the Lord a contribution, throughout your generations.
If you fail unintentionally and do not keep all these commandments that the Lord has given to Moses,
everything the Lord commanded you through Moses, from the day the Lord began to give his commands and onward, throughout your generations,

then, if the fault was committed unintentionally, without the community's knowledge, the whole community shall offer a young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord, with its grain offering and its drink offering according to the rule, and a male goat as a sin offering.

The priest shall make atonement for the whole community of the sons of Israel, and they will be forgiven, for it was an unintentional fault, and they have brought their offering, an offering by fire to the Lord, and their sin offering before the Lord, because of their unintentional fault.
The whole community of the sons of Israel and the foreigner residing among them will be forgiven, for all the people acted unintentionally.
If it is a single person who has sinned unintentionally, that person shall offer a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person who went astray by sinning unintentionally; he shall make atonement for that person, and it will be forgiven.
Whether it is a native among the sons of Israel or the foreigner residing among them, you shall have one law for anyone who acts unintentionally.
But whoever acts deliberately, whether native or foreigner, insults the Lord: that person shall be cut off from among his people.
Because he has despised the word of the Lord and broken his commandment, that man shall be cut off: his fault is upon him.
While the sons of Israel were in the wilderness, they caught a man gathering wood on the sabbath day.
Those who had caught him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and the whole community.
He was placed under guard, because what should be done to him had not yet been made clear.
The Lord said to Moses: This man shall be put to death; the whole community shall stone him outside the camp.
So the whole community brought him outside the camp and stoned him, and he died, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord said to Moses:
Speak to the sons of Israel, tell them to make for themselves, throughout their generations, tassels on the corners of their garments, and to put a thread of violet on the tassel of each corner.

This will be a tassel for you, and at the sight of it you will remember all the commandments of the Lord, to put them into practice, without letting yourselves be led astray by the desires of your heart and your eyes, which prostitute you as you follow them.
So you will remember all my commandments and put them into practice, and you will be holy to your God.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord your God.
Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, together with Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, all three of the tribe of Reuben, took the lead
and rose up against Moses, with two hundred and fifty men of the sons of Israel, leaders of the community, members of the assembly, men of standing.

They gathered against Moses and Aaron and said to them: "You have gone too far! The whole community, all of them are holy, and the Lord is among them. Why then do you set yourselves above the assembly of the Lord?"
When Moses heard this, he fell face down.
Then he said to Korah and his whole band: "Tomorrow morning the Lord will make known who is his, who is holy, and he will bring that one near to himself; the one he chooses, he will bring near.
This is what you shall do: take censers, you Korah and your whole band;
put fire in them and lay incense on them before the Lord, tomorrow. The one the Lord chooses, he is the holy one. You have gone too far, sons of Levi!"
Moses said to Korah: "Listen now, sons of Levi.

Is it not enough for you that the God of Israel has set you apart from the rest of the community of Israel, bringing you near to himself to do the service of the Dwelling of the Lord and to stand before the community to serve it?
He has brought you near, you and all your brothers, the sons of Levi, with you; and now you demand the priesthood as well!
It is against the Lord, then, that you and your whole band have banded together; for what is Aaron, that you should grumble against him?"
Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab. They answered: "We will not come up.
Is it not enough that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to make us die in the wilderness, that you must also set yourself up as our ruler?

It is not into a land flowing with milk and honey that you have led us, nor is it fields and vineyards that you have given us as an inheritance! Do you mean to gouge out the eyes of these men? We will not come up."
Moses fell into a great anger and said to the Lord: "Do not turn to their offering. I have not taken a single donkey from them, and I have not wronged any one of them."
Moses said to Korah: "You and your whole band, present yourselves tomorrow before the Lord, you, they, and Aaron.
Each of you take his censer, put incense on it, and present each his censer before the Lord, two hundred and fifty censers; you too, and Aaron, each his own."
So each of them took his censer, put fire in it, laid incense on it, and stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, with Moses and Aaron.
Korah gathered the whole community against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting. Then the glory of the Lord appeared to the whole community.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said:
"Separate yourselves from this community, so that I may destroy them in an instant."
They fell face down and said: "O God, God of the spirits of all flesh, one man has sinned, and will you be angry with the whole community?"
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the community: Move away from around the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram."
Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, followed by the elders of Israel.
He said to the community: "Move away from the tents of these wicked men and touch nothing that belongs to them, or you will be swept away with all their sins."

So they moved away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram had come out and were standing at the entrances of their tents, with their wives, their sons, and their little ones.
Moses said: "By this you will know that it is the Lord who sent me to do all these works, and that I do not act on my own:
if these men die as everyone dies, if their fate is that of all people, then it is not the Lord who has sent me.

But if the Lord does a wonder, if the earth opens its mouth and swallows them up, with all that belongs to them, and they go down alive to the realm of the dead, then you will know that these men have despised the Lord."
No sooner had he finished speaking these words than the ground split open beneath them:
the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up, with their households, together with all Korah's people and all their possessions.
They went down alive to the realm of the dead, they and all that belonged to them; the earth covered them over, and they vanished from the midst of the assembly.
At their cries, all Israel around them fled, for they said: "Let the earth not swallow us up too!"
And a fire came out from the Lord and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who were offering the incense.

titres.titre: The rod of Aaron that blossoms

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to take up the censers from the fire and scatter the coals far away, for they have become holy:

the censers of these men who sinned against their own lives. Let them be made into hammered plates to cover the altar, for they were presented before the Lord and have become holy; they will be a sign for the sons of Israel."
So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that the men consumed by fire had presented, and they were hammered out to cover the altar.

It is a memorial for the sons of Israel, so that no unauthorized person, no one outside the descendants of Aaron, may draw near to burn incense before the Lord and suffer the fate of Korah and his band, according to what the Lord had said through Moses.
The next day the whole community of the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying: "You have killed the people of the Lord!"
As the community gathered against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the tent of meeting: there the cloud was covering it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
Then Moses and Aaron came forward before the tent of meeting.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Move away from this community, so that I may destroy them in an instant." And they fell face down.

Moses said to Aaron: "Take the censer, put fire from the altar in it and lay on the incense; carry it quickly to the community and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from before the Lord: the plague has begun."
Aaron took it, as Moses had said, and ran into the midst of the assembly: the plague had already begun among the people. He put on the incense and made atonement for the people;
he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague stopped.
Those who died in this plague numbered fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who had died because of Korah.
Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the tent of meeting: the plague had been stopped.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Speak to the sons of Israel and take from them a rod for each ancestral tribe, from all their leaders, tribe by tribe: twelve rods. You shall write each man's name on his rod.
You shall write Aaron's name on the rod of Levi; for there shall be one rod for each head of an ancestral tribe.
You shall place them in the tent of meeting, before the Testimony, where I meet with you.
The rod of the man I choose will blossom; so I will put an end to the grumblings that the sons of Israel utter against you, turning them away from me."
Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and all their leaders handed him a rod, one rod for each leader, tribe by tribe: twelve rods; and Aaron's rod was among their rods.
Moses placed the rods before the Lord, in the tent of the Testimony.
The next day Moses entered the tent of the Testimony: there the rod of Aaron, for the house of Levi, had blossomed; it had put out buds, flowers had opened, and almonds had ripened.
Moses took all the rods out from before the Lord and presented them to all the sons of Israel; they looked at them, and each took back his own.
The Lord said to Moses: "Put Aaron's rod back before the Testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebels; so you will put an end to their grumblings against me, and they will not die."
Moses did so; as the Lord had commanded him, so he did.
The sons of Israel said to Moses: "We are perishing, we are lost, all of us lost!
Everyone who draws near to the Dwelling of the Lord dies. Are we all to perish?"

titres.titre: The duties of the priests and the Levites

versets.t: The Lord said to Aaron: You, your sons, and your family with you shall bear the weight of the faults committed against the sanctuary; you and your sons with you shall bear the weight of the faults of your priesthood.
Bring near also your brothers, the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father: let them join you and serve you, while you and your sons with you are before the tent of the Testimony.
They shall carry out your duties and the duties of the whole tent; but they shall not come near the holy objects or the altar, or they will die, they and you.
They shall join you and carry out the duties of the tent of meeting, for all the service of the tent; no unauthorized person shall come near you.
You shall carry out the service of the sanctuary and the service of the altar, so that wrath may no longer fall on the sons of Israel.
See, I myself have taken your brothers the Levites from among the sons of Israel; they are a gift for you, given to the Lord to do the service of the tent of meeting.

You and your sons with you shall exercise your priesthood in all that concerns the altar and what is behind the veil; that is your service. I give you your priesthood as a gift; the unauthorized person who comes near shall be put to death.
The Lord said to Aaron: See, I entrust to you the care of my contributions; of all the holy things of the sons of Israel, I give them to you and to your sons as a portion, by a perpetual decree.

This is what shall belong to you of the most holy things, of what is not consumed by fire: all their offerings, all their grain offerings, all their sin offerings, and all their guilt offerings that they render to me; these most holy things shall be for you and for your sons.
You shall eat them in a most holy place; every male may eat them; it shall be a holy thing for you.

This too shall belong to you: the contribution set aside from their gifts, from all the wave offerings of the sons of Israel; I give them to you, to your sons and your daughters with you, by a perpetual decree: everyone who is clean in your household may eat them.
All the best of the oil, all the best of the new wine and the grain, the firstfruits they give to the Lord, I give to you.
The first fruits of everything that grows in their land, which they bring to the Lord, shall be for you; everyone who is clean in your household may eat them.
Everything devoted by ban in Israel shall be for you.

Every firstborn of the womb, of all flesh, that they offer to the Lord, whether human or animal, shall be for you; only you shall have the firstborn of a human redeemed, and you shall have the firstborn of an unclean animal redeemed.

You shall have it redeemed from the age of one month, at the price you set: about fifty-seven grams of silver, according to the standard weight of the sanctuary, which is divided into twenty small parts.

But the firstborn of a cow, a sheep, or a goat you shall not have redeemed: it is holy. You shall pour out their blood on the altar and burn their fat: it is an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Their meat shall be for you, like the wave breast and the right thigh.

All the holy contributions that the sons of Israel set aside for the Lord, I give to you, to your sons and your daughters with you, by a perpetual decree. It is a covenant of salt, perpetual, before the Lord, for you and for your descendants with you.
The Lord said to Aaron: You shall have no inheritance in their land, and there will be no portion for you among them: I myself am your portion and your inheritance among the sons of Israel.
To the sons of Levi, see, I give as an inheritance every tithe in Israel, in exchange for the service they perform, the service of the tent of meeting.
The sons of Israel shall no longer come near the tent of meeting: they would take on a sin and die.

It is the Levite who shall do the service of the tent of meeting, and it is they who shall bear the weight of their faults. It is a perpetual decree throughout your generations; they shall have no inheritance among the sons of Israel.
For I give to the Levites as an inheritance the tithe that the sons of Israel set aside for the Lord; that is why I told them they would have no inheritance among the sons of Israel.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:

You shall speak to the Levites, you shall say to them: When you receive from the sons of Israel the tithe that I give you from them as your inheritance, you shall set aside from it a contribution for the Lord, a tithe of the tithe.
This contribution will be counted for you as the grain from the threshing floor and as the wine from the press.
So you too shall set aside a contribution for the Lord from all the tithes you receive from the sons of Israel; from them you shall give the Lord's contribution to Aaron the priest.
From all the gifts you receive, you shall set aside the whole contribution of the Lord: the best, the holy portion.
You shall say to them: When you have set aside the best of it, the rest will be counted to the Levites like the yield of the threshing floor and the yield of the press.
You may eat it in any place, you and your household, for it is your wages in exchange for your service in the tent of meeting.
You shall not take on any sin in this matter, once you have set aside the best of it; you shall not profane the holy things of the sons of Israel, and you shall not die.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said:
This is a prescription of the Law that the Lord has commanded: Tell the sons of Israel to bring you a red heifer, without defect, without blemish, that has never borne the yoke.
You shall hand it over to Eleazar the priest; it shall be taken outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
Eleazar the priest shall take some of the heifer's blood with his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tent of meeting.
Then the heifer shall be burned in his sight: its hide, its flesh, and its blood, together with its dung, shall be burned.
The priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and crimson yarn, and throw them into the middle of the fire that is consuming the heifer.
The priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; after that he may return to the camp, but he will remain unclean until evening.
The one who burned the heifer shall wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water; he will remain unclean until evening.

A clean man shall gather up the ashes of the heifer and deposit them outside the camp, in a clean place; they shall be kept for the community of the sons of Israel, for the water of purification: it is a sin offering.

The one who gathered up the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes and remain unclean until evening. This shall be a perpetual decree for the sons of Israel and for the foreigner residing among them.
Whoever touches a dead person, any human corpse, will be unclean for seven days.
He shall purify himself with this water on the third day and on the seventh day, and he will be clean; but if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not be clean.

Whoever touches a dead person, the body of someone who has died, and does not purify himself, defiles the Dwelling of the Lord: that person shall be cut off from Israel. Because the water of purification has not been sprinkled on him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still on him.
This is the law: when a man dies in a tent, everyone who enters the tent and everyone who is in it will be unclean for seven days.
Every open container, with no lid fastened on it, will be unclean.
Whoever, out in the open, touches someone killed by the sword or someone who has died naturally, or human bones, or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
For the unclean person, some of the ash of the victim burned as a sin offering shall be taken, and fresh water shall be poured over it in a vessel.

A clean man shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the objects and on the persons who were in it, and on the one who touched the bones, the person killed, the dead body, or the grave.

The clean man shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day, and on the seventh day he shall complete his purification; the man shall wash his clothes, bathe in water, and in the evening he will be clean.

The man who is unclean and does not purify himself, that one shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly, for he has defiled the sanctuary of the Lord: the water of purification has not been sprinkled on him, he is unclean.
This shall be a perpetual decree for them. The one who sprinkles the water of purification shall wash his clothes; and the one who touches the water of purification will be unclean until evening.
Everything the unclean person touches will be unclean, and the person who touches him will be unclean until evening.

titres.titre: The death of Miriam and the waters of Meribah

versets.t: The whole community of the sons of Israel came to the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people settled at Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
There was no water for the community; they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
The people turned on Moses: "If only we had perished when our brothers perished before the Lord!
Why did you bring the assembly of the Lord into this wilderness, for us to die here, we and our animals?
Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to bring us to this wretched place? It is not a place for sowing; there is no fig tree, no vine, no pomegranate, and not even water to drink!"
Moses and Aaron went away from the assembly toward the entrance of the tent of meeting and fell face down. Then the glory of the Lord appeared to them.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:

Take the staff, gather the community, you and Aaron your brother, and before their eyes speak to the rock, and it will give its water. You shall bring water out of the rock for them, and give the community and their animals to drink.
Moses took the staff that was before the Lord, as he had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly before the rock, and Moses said to them: "Listen now, you rebels! Are we to bring water out of this rock for you?"
Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff: water gushed out in abundance, and the community drank, and their animals too.
The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: "Because you did not have faith in me, to reveal my holiness in the eyes of the sons of Israel, you will not bring this assembly into the land I am giving them."
These are the waters of Meribah, that is, of the Quarrel, where the sons of Israel quarrelled with the Lord, and where he revealed his holiness among them.
From Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom: "This is what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardships we have met.
Our fathers went down to Egypt, where we stayed a long time; the Egyptians ill-treated us and our fathers.
We cried out to the Lord: he heard our voice, sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt. Here we are at Kadesh, a town on the edge of your territory.

Let us, please, pass through your land. We will not go through the fields or the vineyards, and we will not drink water from the wells; we will follow the King's Highway, turning aside neither to the right nor to the left, until we have crossed your territory."
Edom answered him: "You shall not pass through my land, or I will come out to meet you with the sword."
The sons of Israel said to him: "We will go up by the main road; if we drink your water, I and my flocks, I will pay the price. It is nothing, only let me pass through on foot."
Edom answered: "You shall not pass!" And Edom came out to meet him with a large force and a strong hand.
So Edom refused to let Israel cross his territory, and Israel turned away from him.
The whole community of the sons of Israel set out from Kadesh and came to Mount Hor.
At Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron. He said:
Aaron is about to be gathered to his people; he will not enter the land I am giving to the sons of Israel, because you rebelled against my command at the waters of Meribah.
Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up Mount Hor.
You shall strip Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son; there Aaron will be gathered to his people: he will die there.
Moses did what the Lord had commanded: they went up Mount Hor in the sight of the whole community.
Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on Eleazar his son; Aaron died there, on the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came back down the mountain.
The whole community saw that Aaron had breathed his last, and the whole house of Israel wept for Aaron for thirty days.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming by the way of Atharim; he attacked Israel and took some of them captive.
Then Israel made a vow to the Lord: "If you deliver this people into my hands, I will devote their towns to the ban."
The Lord listened to Israel's voice and delivered up the Canaanites; Israel devoted them to the ban, them and their towns, and that place was named Hormah, that is, the Anathema.
They set out from Mount Hor by the way of the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. On the way the people lost patience.
The people spoke against God and against Moses: "Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to die in the wilderness? There is no bread and no water, and we are disgusted with this miserable food!"
Then the Lord sent fiery serpents against the people; they bit the people, and many in Israel died.
The people came to Moses: "We have sinned," they said, "in speaking against the Lord and against you. Pray to the Lord to take these serpents away from us." And Moses prayed for the people.
The Lord said to Moses: "Make yourself a fiery serpent and set it on a pole; anyone who has been bitten and looks at it will live."
Moses made a bronze serpent and set it on the pole; and whenever a serpent had bitten someone, that person looked at the bronze serpent and lived.
The sons of Israel set out and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, in the wilderness that faces Moab, toward the east.
They set out from there and camped in the valley of Zered.
They set out from there and camped beyond the Arnon, in the wilderness that stretches from the territory of the Amorites; for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
That is why it is said in the Book of the Wars of the Lord: "Waheb in Suphah, and the ravines of the Arnon,
and the slope of the ravines that bends toward the site of Ar and leans against the border of Moab."
From there they went to Beer, that is, the Well: it is the well of which the Lord had said to Moses: "Gather the people, and I will give them water."
Then Israel sang this song: "Spring up, O well! Sing to it,
the well that princes dug, that the nobles of the people bored out, with the sceptre, with their staffs!" From the wilderness they went to Mattanah;
from Mattanah to Nahaliel; from Nahaliel to Bamoth;
from Bamoth to the valley in the fields of Moab, toward the top of Pisgah, which overlooks the wilderness.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites, to say to him:

"Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into the fields or the vineyards, and we will not drink water from the wells; we will follow the King's Highway until we have crossed your territory."
But Sihon would not let Israel cross his territory; he gathered his whole people and came out to meet Israel in the wilderness: he came to Jahaz and attacked Israel.
Israel put him to the edge of the sword and took possession of his land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the sons of Ammon; for the border of the sons of Ammon was fortified.
Israel took all these towns and settled in all the towns of the Amorites, in Heshbon and all its dependent villages.
For Heshbon was the town of Sihon, king of the Amorites; he had fought the former king of Moab and taken all his land from him as far as the Arnon.
That is why the poets say: "Come to Heshbon! Let it be rebuilt and fortified, the town of Sihon!
For a fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the city of Sihon; it devoured Ar of Moab, the lords of the heights of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You are lost, people of Chemosh! He has given up his sons as fugitives and his daughters as captives to Sihon, king of the Amorites.
We riddled them with arrows; Heshbon is destroyed as far as Dibon; we laid waste as far as Nophah, as far as Medeba."
So Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to scout out Jazer; they took its dependent villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.
Then they changed direction and went up by the way of Bashan. Og, king of Bashan, came out to meet them, he and all his people, to do battle at Edrei.

The Lord said to Moses: "Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hands, him, all his people, and his land; you shall treat him as you treated Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon."
So they struck him down, him, his sons, and all his people, until not a survivor was left him, and they took possession of his land.

titres.titre: The donkey and the Angel of the Lord

versets.t: The sons of Israel set out and camped in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites,
and Moab was gripped with great fear of this people, because they were so numerous; Moab was filled with dread in the face of the sons of Israel.
Moab said to the elders of Midian: "This horde is going to devour everything around us, as the ox grazes the grass of the fields." Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor, at Pethor, on the River, in the land of the sons of his people, to summon him with these words: "A people has come out of Egypt; it covers the face of the land and has settled opposite me.

Come now, I beg you, curse this people for me, for they are mightier than I am; perhaps then I will be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land. For I know: the one you bless is blessed, and the one you curse is cursed."
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian set out, the diviner's fee in hand; they came to Balaam and reported to him the words of Balak.
Balaam said to them: "Spend the night here, and I will give you an answer according to what the Lord tells me." So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
God came to Balaam and said: "Who are these men staying with you?"
Balaam answered God: "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent them to me to say:
The people that has come out of Egypt covers the face of the land; come now and curse them for me: perhaps then I will be able to fight them and drive them out."
God said to Balaam: "You shall not go with them, and you shall not curse this people, for they are blessed."
In the morning Balaam got up and said to the princes of Balak: "Return to your land, for the Lord refuses to let me go with you."
The princes of Moab got up, returned to Balak, and said to him: "Balaam refused to come with us."
Balak again sent princes, more numerous and more distinguished than the first.
They came to Balaam and said to him: "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: Do not let anything hold you back, I beg you, but come to me;
for I will heap honours upon you and do all that you tell me. Come now, I beg you, curse this people for me."
Balaam answered the servants of Balak: "Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go against the command of the Lord my God, in anything great or small.
Now stay here this night, you too, so that I may learn what else the Lord may tell me."
God came to Balaam during the night and said to him: "If these men have come to summon you, get up, go with them; but you shall do only what I tell you."
In the morning Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and set out with the princes of Moab.
But God's anger blazed because he was going, and the Angel of the Lord stationed himself on the road to bar his way. (Balaam was riding his donkey, accompanied by his two servants.)
The donkey saw the Angel of the Lord standing on the road, his drawn sword in his hand; she turned off the road and went into a field. Balaam struck the donkey to bring her back onto the road.
Then the Angel of the Lord stood in a sunken path between the vineyards, with a wall on one side and a wall on the other.
The donkey saw the Angel of the Lord; she pressed herself against the wall and crushed Balaam's foot against it, so he struck her again.
The Angel of the Lord went farther on and stood in a narrow place, where there was no room to turn aside either to the right or to the left.
The donkey saw the Angel of the Lord and lay down under Balaam. Balaam's anger blazed, and he struck the donkey with his staff.
Then the Lord opened the donkey's mouth, and she said to Balaam: "What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?"
Balaam answered the donkey: "You have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you on the spot."
The donkey said to Balaam: "Am I not your donkey, which you have ridden all your life to this day? Have I been in the habit of treating you this way?" He answered: "No."
Then the Lord opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the Angel of the Lord standing on the road, his drawn sword in his hand; he bowed low and fell face down.
The Angel of the Lord said to him: "Why have you struck your donkey these three times? It is I who came out to bar your way, for in my sight this road leads you to ruin.
The donkey saw me and turned aside from me these three times. If she had not turned aside, it is you I would have killed, while her I would have let live."
Balaam said to the Angel of the Lord: "I have sinned, for I did not know that you were standing before me on the road. Now, if this displeases you, I will turn back."
The Angel of the Lord said to Balaam: "Go with these men; but you shall say nothing except what I tell you." And Balaam went on with the princes of Balak.
Balak heard that Balaam was coming; he went out to meet him as far as the town of Moab, on the border of the Arnon, at the edge of the territory.
Balak said to Balaam: "Did I not send urgently to summon you? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to heap honours upon you?"
Balaam answered Balak: "Here I am, come to you; but am I able to say anything at all? The word that God puts in my mouth, that is what I will speak."
Balaam set out with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep, and sent some to Balaam and to the princes who were with him.
In the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal, from where he could see the edge of the people's camp.
Balaam said to Balak: "Build me seven altars here, and prepare me here seven bulls and seven rams."
Balak did as Balaam had said, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak: "Stand beside your burnt offering, and I will go off by myself: perhaps the Lord will come to meet me. Whatever he shows me, I will tell you." And he went off to a bare height.
God came to meet Balaam, who said to him: "I have set up the seven altars, and I have offered a bull and a ram on each altar."
The Lord put a word in Balaam's mouth and said: "Go back to Balak, and this is what you shall say."
Balaam went back to Balak, who was standing beside his burnt offering, he and all the princes of Moab.
