Then Balaam spoke his oracle: "From Aram Balak has brought me, from the mountains of the East the king of Moab: Come, curse Jacob for me; come, doom Israel to a curse!
How can I curse the one God does not curse? How can I doom to a curse the one the Lord does not reject?
From the top of the crags I see him, from the hills I behold him: a people that dwells apart, not counting itself among the nations.
Who can count the dust of Jacob, or number even a quarter of Israel? May I die the death of the righteous, and may my end be like theirs!"
Balak said to Balaam: "What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies, and here you are, heaping blessings upon them!"
He answered: "Must I not take care to speak only what the Lord puts in my mouth?"
Balak said to him: "Come with me, then, to another place, from where you can see them; you will see only the edge of them, not the whole: from there curse them for me."
He led him to the field of the Watchers, to the top of Pisgah; there he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak: "Stand here beside your burnt offering, and I will go over there to meet him."
The Lord came to meet Balaam, put a word in his mouth, and said: "Go back to Balak, and this is what you shall say."
He came back to him: Balak was standing beside his burnt offering, with the princes of Moab. Balak asked him: "What did the Lord say?"
Then Balaam spoke his oracle: "Rise, Balak, and listen! Give ear to me, son of Zippor!
God is not a man, that he should lie, nor a son of man, that he should change his mind. Has he said, and will he not do it? Has he spoken, and will he not fulfil it?
See, I have received the charge to bless: he has blessed, and I cannot change it.
He sees no iniquity in Jacob, he finds no misery in Israel. The Lord his God is with him, and the royal acclamation resounds in his midst.
God brought them out of Egypt; he is for them like the horns of the wild ox.
There is no magic against Jacob, no sorcery against Israel. In its time it will be said of Jacob and of Israel what God has done.
Here is a people that rises up like a lioness, that rears up like a lion; it does not lie down until it has devoured its prey and drunk the blood of those it has struck."
Balak said to Balaam: "Do not curse them, but at least do not bless them!"
Balaam answered Balak: "Did I not tell you: All that the Lord says, I will do?"
Balak said to Balaam: "Come now, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will please God for you to curse them for me from there."
Balak led Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the wilderness.
Balaam said to Balak: "Build me seven altars here, and prepare me here seven bulls and seven rams."
Balak did as Balaam had said, and he offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel; he did not go, as at other times, in search of omens, but turned his face toward the wilderness.
Lifting up his eyes, Balaam saw Israel camped tribe by tribe. Then the Spirit of God came upon him,
and he spoke his oracle: "Oracle of Balaam son of Beor, oracle of the man whose eye is opened,
oracle of the one who hears the words of God, who beholds the vision of the Almighty, who falls, and whose eyes are unveiled.
How beautiful are your tents, Jacob, and your dwellings, Israel!
They stretch out like valleys, like gardens beside a river, like aloes that the Lord has planted, like cedars beside the waters.
Water overflows from his two buckets, his seed is watered by abundant streams. His king rises higher than Agag, and his kingship grows.
God brought him out of Egypt; he is for him like the horns of the wild ox. He devours the nations that stand in his way, he breaks their bones and pierces them with his arrows.
He has crouched, he has lain down like a lion, like a lioness: who will rouse him? Blessed is the one who blesses you, cursed is the one who curses you!"
Balak's anger blazed against Balaam; he struck his hands together and said to Balaam: "It was to curse my enemies that I called you, and here you have heaped blessings upon them these three times!
Now flee to your own country. I had said I would heap honours upon you, but see, the Lord has kept the honour from you."
Balaam answered Balak: "Did I not already say to your messengers, whom you sent to me:
Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go against the command of the Lord, to do good or evil of my own accord; what the Lord says, that is what I will speak?
And now that I am returning to my people, come, I will tell you what this people will do to yours in the days to come."
Then he spoke his oracle: "Oracle of Balaam son of Beor, oracle of the man whose eye is opened,
oracle of the one who hears the words of God and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who beholds the vision of the Almighty, who falls, and whose eyes are unveiled.
I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near: a star comes out of Jacob, a sceptre rises from Israel. It crushes the temples of Moab and the skull of all the sons of tumult.
Edom becomes his possession, Seir, his enemy, becomes his possession, while Israel displays its valour.
Out of Jacob comes a ruler, who destroys what remains of the city."
Balaam saw Amalek and spoke his oracle: "Amalek, first of the nations, but its end is ruin."
He saw the Kenites and spoke his oracle: "Firm is your dwelling, your nest is set on the rock;
yet Kain will be given over to the fire, for how long? Asshur will carry you off into captivity."
He spoke his oracle again: "Alas! Who will survive when God does these things?
Ships come from the direction of Kittim; they oppress Asshur, they oppress Eber, but he too rushes to his ruin."
Then Balaam got up, set out, and returned home; and Balak, for his part, went on his way.
Israel settled at Shittim, and the people began to give themselves over to immorality with the daughters of Moab.
These invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods; the people ate and bowed down before their gods.
So Israel bound itself to the Baal of Peor, and the anger of the Lord blazed against Israel.
The Lord said to Moses: "Take all the chiefs of the people and hang them before the Lord, in the face of the sun, so that the burning anger of the Lord may turn away from Israel."
Moses said to the judges of Israel: "Each of you put to death those of his men who have bound themselves to the Baal of Peor."

Now one of the sons of Israel came and brought a Midianite woman to his brothers, in the sight of Moses and of the whole community of the sons of Israel, who were weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he rose from the midst of the community, took a spear in his hand,
followed the man of Israel into the alcove, and ran them both through, the man of Israel and the woman, right through the belly. Then the plague that was striking the sons of Israel stopped.
Twenty-four thousand died in that plague.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:

Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned my fury away from the sons of Israel, because he burned among them with my own jealousy; that is why I did not, in my jealousy, destroy the sons of Israel.
Therefore say: See, I grant him my covenant of peace.
It shall be, for him and for his descendants after him, the covenant of a perpetual priesthood, because he burned with zeal for his God and made atonement for the sons of Israel.
The man of Israel who was killed with the Midianite woman was named Zimri son of Salu; he was the leader of one of the families of the Simeonites.
And the woman, the Midianite who was killed, was named Cozbi daughter of Zur, a tribal chief, from one of the families of Midian.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Treat the Midianites as enemies and strike them,

for they treated you as enemies by the schemes they plotted against you in the affair of Peor, and in the affair of Cozbi, the daughter of the chief of Midian, their sister, who was killed on the day of the plague that came because of Peor.
Now, after the plague,
After the plague, the Lord spoke to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron, the priest. He said:
Take a census of the whole community of the sons of Israel, from twenty years old and upward, by their families: every man in Israel fit to bear arms.
So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho. They said:
Take a census of the people from twenty years old and upward, as the Lord had commanded Moses. These are the sons of Israel who came out of Egypt.
Reuben, the firstborn of Israel. The sons of Reuben: through Hanoch, the clan of the Hanochites; through Pallu, the clan of the Palluites;
through Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; through Carmi, the clan of the Carmites.
These are the clans of the Reubenites: those counted numbered forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty men.
The sons of Pallu: Eliab.
The sons of Eliab: Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. This is the Dathan and Abiram, members of the council, who rose up against Moses and Aaron with the company of Korah when it rose up against the Lord.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up together with Korah, when that company perished and the fire consumed two hundred and fifty men; and they became a warning sign.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
The sons of Simeon, by their clans: through Nemuel, the clan of the Nemuelites; through Jamin, the clan of the Jaminites; through Jachin, the clan of the Jachinites;
through Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites; through Shaul, the clan of the Shaulites.
These are the clans of the Simeonites: twenty-two thousand two hundred men.
The sons of Gad, by their clans: through Zephon, the clan of the Zephonites; through Haggi, the clan of the Haggites; through Shuni, the clan of the Shunites;
through Ozni, the clan of the Oznites; through Eri, the clan of the Erites;
through Arod, the clan of the Arodites; through Areli, the clan of the Arelites.
These are the clans of the sons of Gad, according to those counted: forty thousand five hundred men.
The sons of Judah: Er and Onan; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
These are the sons of Judah, by their clans: through Shelah, the clan of the Shelanites; through Perez, the clan of the Perezites; through Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites.
The sons of Perez were: through Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; through Hamul, the clan of the Hamulites.
These are the clans of Judah, according to those counted: seventy-six thousand five hundred men.
The sons of Issachar, by their clans: through Tola, the clan of the Tolaites; through Puvah, the clan of the Puvahites;
through Jashub, the clan of the Jashubites; through Shimron, the clan of the Shimronites.
These are the clans of Issachar, according to those counted: sixty-four thousand three hundred men.
The sons of Zebulun, by their clans: through Sered, the clan of the Seredites; through Elon, the clan of the Elonites; through Jahleel, the clan of the Jahleelites.
These are the clans of Zebulun, according to those counted: sixty thousand five hundred men.
The sons of Joseph, by their clans: Manasseh and Ephraim.
The sons of Manasseh: through Machir, the clan of the Machirites. Machir fathered Gilead; from Gilead, the clan of the Gileadites.
These are the sons of Gilead: through Iezer, the clan of the Iezerites; through Helek, the clan of the Helekites;
Asriel, from whom came the clan of the Asrielites; Shechem, from whom came the clan of the Shechemites;
Shemida, from whom came the clan of the Shemidaites; Hepher, from whom came the clan of the Hepherites.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, but only daughters; the names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the clans of Manasseh: those counted numbered fifty-two thousand seven hundred men.
These are the sons of Ephraim, by their clans: through Shuthelah, the clan of the Shuthelahites; through Becher, the clan of the Becherites; through Tahan, the clan of the Tahanites.
These are the sons of Shuthelah: through Eran, the clan of the Eranites.
These are the clans of the sons of Ephraim, according to those counted: thirty-two thousand five hundred men. These are the sons of Joseph, by their clans.
The sons of Benjamin, by their clans: through Bela, the clan of the Belaites; through Ashbel, the clan of the Ashbelites; through Ahiram, the clan of the Ahiramites;
through Shephupham, the clan of the Shuphamites; through Hupham, the clan of the Huphamites.
The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: through Ard, the clan of the Ardites; through Naaman, the clan of the Naamites.
These are the sons of Benjamin, by their clans; those counted numbered forty-five thousand six hundred men.
These are the sons of Dan, by their clans: through Shuham, the clan of the Shuhamites. These are the clans of Dan, by their clans.
The total of the clans of the Shuhamites, according to those counted: sixty-four thousand four hundred men.
The sons of Asher, by their clans: through Imnah, the clan of the Imnites; through Ishvi, the clan of the Ishvites; through Beriah, the clan of the Beriites.
Of the sons of Beriah: through Heber, the clan of the Heberites; through Malchiel, the clan of the Malchielites.
The daughter of Asher was named Serah.
These are the clans of the sons of Asher, according to those counted: fifty-three thousand four hundred men.
The sons of Naphtali, by their clans: through Jahzeel, the clan of the Jahzeelites; through Guni, the clan of the Gunites;
through Jezer, the clan of the Jezerites; through Shillem, the clan of the Shillemites.
These are the clans of Naphtali, by their clans; those counted numbered forty-five thousand four hundred men.
This is the total of the sons of Israel who were counted: six hundred and one thousand seven hundred and thirty men.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Among these the land shall be divided as an inheritance, according to the number of names.
To a large tribe you shall give a greater inheritance, and to a small tribe a smaller inheritance; to each its inheritance according to the number of those counted.
Yet the land shall be divided by lot: they shall receive their inheritance according to the names of their ancestral tribes.
By lot shall their inheritance be apportioned among the tribes, whether large or small.
These are the Levites counted, by their clans: through Gershon, the clan of the Gershonites; through Kohath, the clan of the Kohathites; through Merari, the clan of the Merarites.
These are the clans of Levi: the clan of the Libnites, the clan of the Hebronites, the clan of the Mahlites, the clan of the Mushites, the clan of the Korahites. Kohath fathered Amram.
The wife of Amram was named Jochebed, a daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt; she bore to Amram: Aaron, Moses, and Miriam their sister.
To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the Lord.

Those counted, all the males from one month old and upward, numbered twenty-three thousand. They were not counted among the sons of Israel, because no inheritance was given to them among the sons of Israel.
These are the men counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who took the census of the sons of Israel in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.
Among them there was not one of those whom Moses and Aaron the priest had counted in the wilderness of Sinai;
for the Lord had said of them, "They shall die in the wilderness." Not one of them was left, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

Then the daughters of Zelophehad came forward, son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. Their names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, and before the leaders and the whole community, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and they said:
"Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the company of those who banded together against the Lord, in the company of Korah, but he died for his own sin, and he had no sons.
Why should our father's name disappear from his clan because he had no son? Give us a holding among our father's kinsmen."
Moses brought their case before the Lord,
and the Lord said to Moses:
"The daughters of Zelophehad are right. You shall indeed give them a holding as an inheritance among their father's kinsmen, and you shall pass their father's inheritance on to them.
And you shall say to the sons of Israel: If a man dies leaving no son, you shall pass his inheritance on to his daughter.
If he has no daughter, you shall give his inheritance to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to his father's brothers.

And if his father has no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to the nearest relative in his clan, and that man shall possess it. This shall be a binding statute for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses."
The Lord said to Moses: "Go up onto this mountain of the Abarim and look at the land that I am giving to the sons of Israel.
When you have looked at it, you too shall be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother was gathered,

because in the wilderness of Zin, during the quarrel of the community, you rebelled against my command instead of showing my holiness before their eyes at the waters." These are the waters of Meribah at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin.
Moses spoke to the Lord. He said:
"May the Lord, the God who gives breath to all flesh, appoint a man over the community
who will go out and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the community of the Lord may not be like a flock without a shepherd."
The Lord said to Moses: "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom the Spirit dwells, and lay your hand upon him.
You shall have him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole community, and you shall commission him in their sight.
You shall confer on him part of your authority, so that the whole community of the sons of Israel may obey him.

He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall seek for him the decision of the Urim before the Lord; at his command they shall go out and at his command they shall come in, he, Joshua, and with him all the sons of Israel and the whole community."
Moses did as the Lord had commanded him: he took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole community;
then he laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the Lord had spoken through Moses.

titres.titre: The sabbath and the new moons

versets.t: The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Give this command to the sons of Israel: You shall be careful to present to me, at its appointed time, my offering, the food of my offerings by fire, as a pleasing aroma to me.
You shall say to them: This is the offering by fire that you shall offer to the Lord: each day two yearling lambs without defect, as a perpetual burnt offering.
You shall offer the first lamb in the morning, and the second at twilight,
together with a grain offering of about two litres of fine flour mixed with about one litre of oil from crushed olives.
This is the perpetual burnt offering that was instituted at Mount Sinai, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the Lord.
Its accompanying drink offering shall be about one litre for each lamb; in the holy place you shall pour out to the Lord this drink offering of strong drink.
You shall offer the second lamb at twilight; you shall do as with the morning grain offering and its drink offering: it is an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
On the sabbath day you shall offer two yearling lambs without defect, together with a grain offering of about four litres of fine flour mixed with oil, and its drink offering.
This is the burnt offering for every sabbath, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering and its drink offering.
At the beginning of your months you shall offer to the Lord as a burnt offering two young bulls, one ram, and seven yearling lambs without defect,
together with a grain offering for each bull of about six litres of fine flour mixed with oil; for the ram, about four litres of fine flour mixed with oil;
and for each lamb, about two litres of fine flour mixed with oil. This is a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the Lord.

Their drink offerings shall be about two litres of wine for a bull, about one and a half litres for a ram, and about one litre for a lamb. This is the burnt offering to be offered at the beginning of each month, throughout all the months of the year.
One male goat shall also be offered to the Lord as a sin offering, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering and its drink offering.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the Passover of the Lord.
On the fifteenth day of this month is a feast: for seven days unleavened bread shall be eaten.
On the first day there shall be a holy assembly: you shall do no servile work.
You shall offer to the Lord as an offering by fire, a burnt offering: two young bulls, one ram, and seven yearling lambs, which you shall take without defect,
together with their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: about six litres for a bull, about four litres for the ram,
and about two litres for each of the seven lambs.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
You shall do this without omitting anything from the morning burnt offering, which is the perpetual burnt offering.

You shall do the same each day, for seven days: it is the food of an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord; it shall be offered in addition to the perpetual burnt offering and its drink offering.
On the seventh day you shall have a holy assembly: you shall do no servile work.
On the day of the firstfruits, when you present to the Lord an offering of the new harvest, at your feast of Weeks, you shall have a holy assembly: you shall do no servile work.
You shall offer, as a burnt offering and a pleasing aroma to the Lord, two young bulls, one ram, and seven yearling lambs,
together with their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: about six litres for each bull, about four litres for the ram,
and about two litres for each of the seven lambs.
You shall also offer one male goat, to make atonement for you. You shall do this in addition to the perpetual burnt offering and its grain offering.
You shall take victims without defect, and you shall add their drink offerings.
In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a holy assembly: you shall do no servile work. It shall be for you a day when the horn is sounded.
You shall offer, as a burnt offering and a pleasing aroma to the Lord, one young bull, one ram, and seven yearling lambs without defect,
together with their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: about six litres for the bull, about four litres for the ram,
and about two litres for each of the seven lambs.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.

You shall do this in addition to the burnt offering of the new month with its grain offering, and the perpetual burnt offering with its grain offering and their drink offerings, according to the prescribed rule: these are offerings by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
On the tenth day of this seventh month you shall have a holy assembly, and you shall humble yourselves by fasting: you shall do no work at all.
You shall offer to the Lord, as a burnt offering and a pleasing aroma, one young bull, one ram, and seven yearling lambs, which you shall take without defect,
together with their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: about six litres for the bull, about four litres for the ram,
and about two litres for each of the seven lambs.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering of atonement, the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
On the fifteenth day of the seventh month you shall have a holy assembly: you shall do no servile work, and you shall celebrate a feast in honor of the Lord for seven days.
You shall offer a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord: thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen yearling lambs without defect,
together with their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: about six litres for each of the thirteen bulls, about four litres for each of the two rams,
and about two litres for each of the fourteen lambs.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
On the second day you shall offer twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen yearling lambs without defect,
with the grain offering and the drink offerings that belong to the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and the rule.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
On the third day you shall offer eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen yearling lambs without defect,
with the grain offering and the drink offerings that belong to the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and the rule.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
On the fourth day you shall offer ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen yearling lambs without defect,
with the grain offering and the drink offerings that belong to the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and the rule.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
On the fifth day you shall offer nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen yearling lambs without defect,
with the grain offering and the drink offerings that belong to the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and the rule.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
On the sixth day you shall offer eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen yearling lambs without defect,
with the grain offering and the drink offerings that belong to the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and the rule.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
On the seventh day you shall offer seven bulls, two rams, and fourteen yearling lambs without defect,
with the grain offering and the drink offerings that belong to the bulls, the rams, and the lambs, according to their number and the rule.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.
On the eighth day you shall have a solemn assembly: you shall do no servile work.
You shall offer a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one bull, one ram, and seven yearling lambs without defect,
with the grain offering and the drink offerings that belong to the bull, the ram, and the lambs, according to their number and the rule.
You shall also offer one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the perpetual burnt offering, its grain offering, and its drink offering.

These are the offerings you shall present to the Lord at your appointed feasts, in addition to your votive offerings and your freewill offerings: your burnt offerings, your grain offerings, your drink offerings, and your peace offerings.
Moses told the sons of Israel everything that the Lord had commanded him.
Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the sons of Israel. He said: This is what the Lord commands.
If a man makes a vow to the Lord, or binds himself by an oath to an obligation, he shall not break his word: he shall act according to all that has come out of his mouth.
If a woman, still a young girl in her father's house, makes a vow to the Lord and binds herself by an obligation,
and her father hears of her vow and the obligation she has imposed on herself, and keeps silent toward her, then all her vows shall stand, and every obligation she has imposed on herself shall stand.

But if, on the day he hears of it, her father overrules her, then none of her vows or the obligations she has imposed on herself shall stand; and the Lord will forgive her, because her father overruled her.
If she marries while under the weight of vows, or of a word that escaped her lips by which she bound herself,
and her husband, hearing of it, keeps silent toward her on the day he hears of it, then her vows shall stand, and the obligations she has imposed on herself shall stand.
But if, on the day he hears of it, her husband overrules her, he annuls the vow that was upon her and the word that escaped her lips by which she bound herself; and the Lord will forgive her.
The vow of a widow or a divorced woman, every obligation she has imposed on herself, shall stand for her.
If it is in her husband's house that a woman makes a vow or binds herself to an obligation by oath,
and her husband, hearing of it, keeps silent toward her and does not overrule her, then all her vows shall stand, and every obligation she has imposed on herself shall stand.

But if, on the day he hears of it, her husband annuls them, then nothing that has come out of her lips, whether vows or obligations, shall stand: her husband has annulled them, and the Lord will forgive her.
Every vow and every binding oath by which she commits herself to self-denial, her husband may confirm or annul.

If he keeps silent toward her from one day to the next, he thereby confirms all her vows and all the obligations that are upon her: he confirms them, because he kept silent on the day he heard of them.
But if he annuls them some time after he has heard of them, then he shall bear his wife's guilt.
These are the statutes that the Lord commanded Moses, between a husband and his wife, between a father and his daughter while still young, in her father's house.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Avenge the sons of Israel on the Midianites; after that, you shall be gathered to your people.
Moses spoke to the people. He said: Let some of your men arm themselves for war and march against Midian, to carry out the Lord's vengeance on Midian.
You shall send to the war a thousand men from each tribe, from all the tribes of Israel.
So there were levied, from the thousands of Israel, a thousand men from each tribe, twelve thousand men armed for war.
Moses sent them to battle, a thousand from each tribe, and with them Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, carrying in his hand the sacred objects and the trumpets for sounding the call.
They campaigned against Midian, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and they killed every male.
Besides those who fell in battle, they killed the kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, five kings of Midian; they also put Balaam son of Beor to the sword.
The sons of Israel took the women of Midian captive with their little ones; they plundered all their cattle, all their flocks, and all their goods,
and they burned with fire all the towns they inhabited and all their encampments.
Then, taking all the spoil and all the plunder, both people and animals,

they brought the captives, the plunder, and the spoil to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the community of the sons of Israel, at the camp in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the community went out to meet them, outside the camp.
But Moses was angry with the commanders of the army, the officers of thousands and the officers of hundreds, who were returning from that campaign.
He said to them: "Have you let all the women live?
Yet it was they who, on Balaam's advice, led the sons of Israel to be unfaithful to the Lord in the affair of Peor, so that the plague struck the community of the Lord.
Now then, kill every boy among the children, and kill every woman who has slept with a man.
But all the girls who have not slept with a man, keep alive for yourselves.
As for you, camp outside the camp for seven days. Whoever has killed a man and whoever has touched a corpse shall purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.
You shall also purify every garment, every article of leather, everything woven of goats' hair, and every wooden vessel."
Eleazar the priest said to the men of war who had returned from battle: "This is the requirement of the law that the Lord gave to Moses:
gold, silver, bronze, iron, tin, and lead,

everything that can withstand fire, you shall pass through the fire, and it will be clean; it shall also be purified with the water of purification. And everything that cannot withstand fire, you shall pass through the water.
You shall wash your garments on the seventh day, and you will be clean; after that you may return to the camp."
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Take a count of the plunder that was carried off, both people and animals, you, Eleazar the priest, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the community.
Then divide the plunder in two, between those who fought the campaign and went into battle, and the rest of the community.
From the share of the warriors who went to war, you shall set aside a levy for the Lord: one out of every five hundred, whether people, oxen, donkeys, or sheep.
You shall take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as a contribution for the Lord.

From the half belonging to the sons of Israel, you shall set apart one out of every fifty, whether people, oxen, donkeys, sheep, or any livestock, and give them to the Levites, who carry out the service of the Dwelling of the Lord.
Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The spoil, what remained of the plunder taken by the warriors, was six hundred and seventy-five thousand sheep,
seventy-two thousand oxen,
sixty-one thousand donkeys,
and thirty-two thousand people, the women who had not slept with a man.
The half belonging to the warriors was three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
of which six hundred and seventy-five were the levy for the Lord;
thirty-six thousand oxen, of which seventy-two were the levy for the Lord;
thirty thousand five hundred donkeys, of which sixty-one were the levy for the Lord;
and sixteen thousand people, of whom thirty-two were the levy for the Lord.
Moses gave the levy set aside for the Lord to Eleazar the priest, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
As for the half belonging to the sons of Israel, which Moses had separated from that of the warriors,
this half, the share of the community, was three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred sheep,
thirty-six thousand oxen,
thirty thousand five hundred donkeys,
and sixteen thousand people.

From this half belonging to the sons of Israel, Moses took one out of every fifty, both people and animals, and gave them to the Levites, who carry out the service of the Dwelling of the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The commanders of the thousands of the army, the officers of thousands and the officers of hundreds, came to Moses
and said to him: "Your servants have counted the warriors under our command, and not one of them is missing.
So we bring, as an offering to the Lord, the articles of gold that each of us found, armlets, bracelets, rings, earrings, and necklaces, to make atonement for ourselves before the Lord."
Moses and Eleazar the priest received from them this gold, all these crafted objects.
All the gold of the contribution that they presented to the Lord, from the officers of thousands and the officers of hundreds, weighed about one hundred and ninety-one kilograms.
The men of the army had each taken plunder for themselves.
Moses and Eleazar the priest took the gold of the officers of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting, as a memorial for the sons of Israel before the Lord.

titres.titre: Reuben and Gad settle in Transjordan

versets.t: The sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad had very numerous herds. Seeing that the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead were a region suited for raising livestock,
they came to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the leaders of the community, and said to them:
"Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon,
this land that the Lord has subdued before the community of Israel, is a region suited for raising livestock, and your servants have herds."
They added: "If we have found favor in your eyes, let this land be given to your servants as a holding; do not make us cross the Jordan."
Moses answered the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben: "Are your brothers to go to war while you stay here?
Why would you discourage the sons of Israel from crossing into the land that the Lord is giving them?
This is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to explore the land.
They went up to the Valley of Eshcol, saw the land, and discouraged the sons of Israel from entering the land that the Lord was giving them.
The Lord's anger blazed that day, and he swore this oath:
These men who came up from Egypt, twenty years old and upward, shall not see the land that I promised on oath to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, because they did not follow me wholeheartedly,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, and Joshua son of Nun, who did follow the Lord wholeheartedly.
The Lord's anger blazed against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil in the eyes of the Lord had died out.
And now here you are, taking your fathers' place, a brood of sinners, to stir up still more the fierceness of the Lord's anger against Israel!
For if you turn away from him, he will abandon this people again in the wilderness, and you will bring about the ruin of them all."
They came up to him and said: "We will build enclosures here for our herds and towns for our children;

but we ourselves will take up arms without delay to march at the head of the sons of Israel, until we have brought them to their place, while our children remain in the fortified towns, safe from the inhabitants of the land.
We will not return to our homes until each of the sons of Israel has taken possession of his inheritance,
for we will possess nothing with them on the other side of the Jordan, since our inheritance has fallen to us on this side of the Jordan, to the east."
Moses said to them: "If you do this, if you arm yourselves for battle before the Lord,
if all your armed men cross the Jordan before the Lord until he has dispossessed his enemies before him,

and if you return only once the land has been subdued before the Lord, then you will be free of obligation toward the Lord and toward Israel, and this territory shall become your holding before the Lord.
But if you do not act in this way, you sin against the Lord, and be sure that your sin will find you out.
So build towns for your children and enclosures for your herds, and do what your mouth has promised."
The sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben said to Moses: "Your servants will do as my lord commands.
Our children, our wives, our herds, and all our livestock will remain here, in the towns of Gilead,
while your servants, every man armed for the army, will cross over before the Lord to fight, as my lord says."
Then Moses gave orders concerning them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the sons of Israel.

He said to them: "If the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben cross the Jordan with you, all armed for battle before the Lord, and the land is subdued before you, then you shall give them the land of Gilead as a holding.
But if they do not cross over armed with you, they shall settle among you in the land of Canaan."
The sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben answered: "What the Lord has said to your servants, we will do.
We will cross over armed before the Lord into the land of Canaan, but the holding of our inheritance will remain ours on this side of the Jordan."

So Moses gave to the sons of Gad, to the sons of Reuben, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land with its towns and the surrounding territories.
The sons of Gad rebuilt Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
Atroth-shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
Beth-nimrah, and Beth-haran, fortified towns, and they made enclosures for the flocks.
The sons of Reuben rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
Nebo and Baal-meon, whose names were changed, and Sibmah; and they gave names to the towns they rebuilt.
The sons of Machir son of Manasseh marched against Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were there.
Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
Jair son of Manasseh marched and took their villages, which he called the Encampments of Jair.
Nobah marched and captured Kenath and its dependencies, and he called it Nobah, after his own name.

titres.titre: The stages of the wilderness journey
The command to conquer and divide the land

versets.t: These are the encampments of the sons of Israel when they came out of Egypt by their divisions, under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
At the Lord's command, Moses wrote down the starting points of their stages, camp by camp; so these are their encampments according to their starting points.
They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month: on the day after the Passover the sons of Israel went out with a high hand, in the sight of all Egypt,
while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom the Lord had struck down among them; for the Lord had executed judgment on their gods.
Setting out from Rameses, the sons of Israel camped at Succoth.
Setting out from Succoth, they camped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
Setting out from Etham, they turned back toward Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and camped before Migdol.
Setting out from Pi-hahiroth, they passed through the midst of the sea toward the wilderness; after three days' journey in the wilderness of Etham, they camped at Marah.
Setting out from Marah, they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
Setting out from Elim, they camped by the Red Sea.
Setting out from the Red Sea, they camped in the wilderness of Sin.
Setting out from the wilderness of Sin, they camped at Dophkah.
Setting out from Dophkah, they camped at Alush.
Setting out from Alush, they camped at Rephidim, where the people found no water to drink.
Setting out from Rephidim, they camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
Setting out from the wilderness of Sinai, they camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
Setting out from Kibroth-hattaavah, they camped at Hazeroth.
Setting out from Hazeroth, they camped at Rithmah.
Setting out from Rithmah, they camped at Rimmon-perez.
Setting out from Rimmon-perez, they camped at Libnah.
Setting out from Libnah, they camped at Rissah.
Setting out from Rissah, they camped at Kehelathah.
Setting out from Kehelathah, they camped at Mount Shepher.
Setting out from Mount Shepher, they camped at Haradah.
Setting out from Haradah, they camped at Makheloth.
Setting out from Makheloth, they camped at Tahath.
Setting out from Tahath, they camped at Terah.
Setting out from Terah, they camped at Mithkah.
Setting out from Mithkah, they camped at Hashmonah.
Setting out from Hashmonah, they camped at Moseroth.
Setting out from Moseroth, they camped at Bene-jaakan.
Setting out from Bene-jaakan, they camped at Hor-haggidgad.
Setting out from Hor-haggidgad, they camped at Jotbathah.
Setting out from Jotbathah, they camped at Abronah.
Setting out from Abronah, they camped at Ezion-geber.
Setting out from Ezion-geber, they camped in the wilderness of Zin, that is, at Kadesh.
Setting out from Kadesh, they camped at Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom.
Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at the Lord's command, and there he died, in the fortieth year after the sons of Israel came out of Egypt, in the fifth month, on the first day of the month.
Aaron was one hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
It was then that the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard of the coming of the sons of Israel.
Setting out from Mount Hor, they camped at Zalmonah.
Setting out from Zalmonah, they camped at Punon.
Setting out from Punon, they camped at Oboth.
Setting out from Oboth, they camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
Setting out from Iye-abarim, they camped at Dibon-gad.
Setting out from Dibon-gad, they camped at Almon-diblathaim.
Setting out from Almon-diblathaim, they camped in the mountains of Abarim, opposite Nebo.
Setting out from the mountains of Abarim, they camped in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.
They camped by the Jordan, from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim, in the plains of Moab.
The Lord spoke to Moses, in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho. He said:
Speak to the sons of Israel: When you have crossed the Jordan and entered the land of Canaan,
you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land before you, destroy all their carved stones and all their cast metal images, and demolish all their high places.
You shall take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land as a holding.

You shall divide the land by lot, according to your clans: to a large tribe a greater inheritance, to a small tribe a smaller inheritance; whatever the lot assigns to each shall be his, and you shall receive your inheritance according to your ancestral tribes.

But if you do not drive out before you the inhabitants of the land, then those you allow to remain will become thorns in your eyes and barbs in your sides, and they will harass you in the land where you settle.
Then what I had resolved to do to them, I will do to you.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Give this command to the sons of Israel: When you enter the land of Canaan, this is the territory that will fall to you as an inheritance, the land of Canaan according to its boundaries.
Your southern limit shall run from the wilderness of Zin along the edge of Edom; your southern border shall begin, on the east, at the end of the Salt Sea.
It shall turn south of the ascent of Akrabbim, pass by Zin, and end south of Kadesh-barnea; then it shall reach Hazar-addar and pass on toward Azmon.
From Azmon the border shall turn toward the Wadi of Egypt and end at the sea.
For the western border you shall have the Great Sea and its shore: this shall be your limit on the west.
This shall be your northern border: from the Great Sea you shall draw a line to Mount Hor;
from Mount Hor you shall draw a line to the entrance of Hamath, and the border shall end toward Zedad;
the border shall reach Ziphron and end at Hazar-enan: this shall be your limit on the north.
You shall draw your eastern border from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
From Shepham the border shall go down to Riblah, east of Ain, then it shall go down and run along the hills bordering the sea of Chinnereth on the east.
The border shall go down further along the Jordan and end at the Salt Sea. This shall be your land, according to its boundaries all around.
Moses gave this command to the sons of Israel. He said: This is the land that you shall divide by lot, which the Lord has commanded to be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
For the tribe of the sons of Reuben, by their ancestral houses, the tribe of the sons of Gad, by their ancestral houses, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their inheritance.
These two tribes and this half-tribe have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan, across from Jericho, to the east, toward the sunrise.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
These are the names of the men who shall divide the land among you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
You shall also take one leader from each tribe to divide the land.
These are the names of these men: for the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
for the tribe of the sons of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
for the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;
for the tribe of the sons of Dan, the leader Bukki son of Jogli;
for the sons of Joseph: for the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, the leader Hanniel son of Ephod;
and for the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, the leader Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
for the tribe of the sons of Zebulun, the leader Elizaphan son of Parnach;
for the tribe of the sons of Issachar, the leader Paltiel son of Azzan;
for the tribe of the sons of Asher, the leader Ahihud son of Shelomi;
for the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, the leader Pedahel son of Ammihud.
These are the ones whom the Lord commanded to divide the land of Canaan among the sons of Israel.
The Lord spoke to Moses, in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho. He said:
Command the sons of Israel to give the Levites, out of the inheritance they will possess, cities to live in; you shall also give them the pasturelands around these cities.
The cities shall be theirs to live in, and their pasturelands shall be for their cattle, their possessions, and all their animals.
The pasturelands of the cities that you give to the Levites shall extend, from the city wall, five hundred metres all around, outward.

Outside the city you shall measure a thousand metres on the east side, a thousand metres on the south side, a thousand metres on the west side, and a thousand metres on the north side, with the city in the center: these shall be the pasturelands of their cities.
Among the cities that you give to the Levites, there shall be the six cities of refuge, which you shall establish so that a killer may flee there; and you shall add to them forty-two other cities.
In all, the cities that you give to the Levites shall be forty-eight cities, with their pasturelands.

As for these cities that you set aside from the holding of the sons of Israel, you shall take more from the tribe that has more, and less from the one that has less: each shall give of its cities to the Levites in proportion to the inheritance it has received.
The Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
Speak to the sons of Israel: When you have crossed the Jordan and entered the land of Canaan,
you shall choose for yourselves cities to serve as cities of refuge, where a killer who has killed someone unintentionally may flee.
These cities shall serve you as a refuge from the avenger of blood, so that the killer is not put to death before he has stood trial before the community.
The cities that you designate shall be for you six cities of refuge.
You shall give three beyond the Jordan and three in the land of Canaan: these shall be the cities of refuge.
These six cities shall serve as a refuge for the sons of Israel, for the foreigner, and for the settler among you, so that anyone who has killed someone unintentionally may flee there.
But if he struck him with an iron object and death followed, he is a murderer: the murderer shall be put to death.
If he struck him with a stone in his hand capable of causing death, and death followed, he is a murderer: the murderer shall be put to death.
If he struck him with a wooden object in his hand capable of causing death, and death followed, he is a murderer: the murderer shall be put to death.
It is the avenger of blood who shall put the murderer to death: as soon as he meets him, he shall kill him.
If a man shoved his victim out of hatred, or threw something at him with premeditation, and he dies,
or if out of enmity he struck him with his hand and he dies, then the one who struck him shall be put to death: he is a murderer, and the avenger of blood shall kill him as soon as he meets him.
But if he shoved him by accident, without enmity, or threw an object at him without intent,
or if, without seeing him, he dropped on him a stone capable of causing death, and he dies, though he was not his enemy and was not seeking to harm him,
then the community shall judge, according to these rules, between the one who struck the blow and the avenger of blood.

The community shall rescue the killer from the hand of the avenger of blood and bring him back to the city of refuge to which he had fled; he shall stay there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the killer ever goes outside the territory of the city of refuge to which he has fled,
and the avenger of blood finds him outside the territory of his city of refuge and kills him, there shall be no bloodguilt for him;
for the killer was to remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest. After the death of the high priest, he may return to the land of his holding.
This shall be a binding statute for you, throughout your generations, wherever you live.
Whoever strikes a person dead, it is on the testimony of witnesses that the murderer shall be executed; but a single witness is not enough to condemn anyone to death.
You shall not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who deserves death: he shall be put to death.
Nor shall you accept a ransom allowing one who has fled to his city of refuge to return and live in the land before the death of the high priest.
You shall not profane the land where you are, for blood profanes the land; and for the land there is no atonement for the blood shed on it except by the blood of the one who shed it.
You shall not defile the land where you live, in the midst of which I dwell; for I, the Lord, dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel.

titres.titre: The inheritance of the daughters of Zelophehad

versets.t: The heads of the ancestral houses of the clan of the sons of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from among the clans of the sons of Joseph, came forward and spoke before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the ancestral houses of the sons of Israel.

They said: "The Lord commanded my lord to give the land by lot as an inheritance to the sons of Israel, and my lord received from the Lord the command to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters.

But if they marry one of the sons of another tribe of Israel, their inheritance will be taken from the inheritance of our fathers and added to that of the tribe into which they marry: it will be taken from our allotted inheritance.

And when the jubilee comes for the sons of Israel, their inheritance will be added to that of the tribe into which they have married, and it will be taken from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers."
At the Lord's command, Moses gave this command to the sons of Israel. He said: "The tribe of the sons of Joseph is right.
This is what the Lord commands concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: they may marry whomever they please, provided they marry within a clan of their father's tribe,
so that the inheritance of the sons of Israel does not pass from one tribe to another: each of the sons of Israel shall remain bound to the inheritance of his ancestral tribe.

Every daughter who possesses an inheritance in a tribe of the sons of Israel shall marry a man from a clan of her father's tribe, so that each of the sons of Israel may keep the inheritance of his fathers,
and that no inheritance may pass from one tribe to another: each of the tribes of the sons of Israel shall remain bound to its own inheritance."
As the Lord had commanded Moses, so the daughters of Zelophehad did.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married the sons of their uncles;
they married within the clans of the sons of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of their father's clan.
These are the commandments and the rules that the Lord gave to the sons of Israel through Moses, in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho.

titres.titre: The Sending of the Scouts and the Rebellion

versets.t: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah facing Suph, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It is eleven days' journey from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh-barnea.
In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses spoke to the sons of Israel according to all that the Lord had commanded him to tell them.
This was after he had defeated Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, who lived at Ashtaroth and at Edrei.
Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses undertook to expound this law. He said:
The Lord our God spoke to us at Horeb: "You have stayed long enough at this mountain.

Turn and set out; go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors, in the Arabah, the hill country, the lowland, the Negeb, and the seacoast, to the land of the Canaanites, and to Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Euphrates.
See, I set this land before you: go in and take possession of the land that the Lord swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give to them and to their descendants after them."
At that time I said to you: "I am not able to carry you by myself alone.
The Lord your God has multiplied you, and here you are today as numerous as the stars of heaven.
May the Lord, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times more numerous still, and bless you as he has promised you!
How can I bear by myself alone your weight, your burden, and your quarrels?
Choose from your tribes men who are wise, discerning, and respected, and I will set them at your head."
You answered me: "What you propose to do is good."
So I took the leaders of your tribes, men who were wise and respected, and I set them at your head: leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties, and of tens, and officers for your tribes.
At that time I gave this charge to your judges: "Hear the disputes between your brothers, and judge with justice between a man and his brother or the resident alien who lives with him.

You shall show no partiality in your judgments: hear the small and the great alike, fearing no one, for the judgment belongs to God; and if a case is too hard for you, bring it to me, and I will hear it."
At that time I laid down for you everything you were to do.
Setting out from Horeb, we crossed all that great and dreadful wilderness that you saw, toward the hill country of the Amorites, as the Lord our God had commanded us, and we came to Kadesh-barnea.
Then I said to you: "You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the Lord our God is giving us.
See, the Lord your God sets this land before you. Go up, take possession of it, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, has told you. Do not fear, do not be dismayed."
Then all of you came to me and said: "Let us send men ahead of us to explore the land; they will bring us word about the route we should take and the cities we will reach."
The proposal seemed good to me, and I chose twelve men from among you, one for each tribe.
They set out toward the hill country, came to the Valley of Eshcol, and explored it.
They took in their hands some of the fruit of the land, brought it down to us, and gave us this report: "It is a good land that the Lord our God is giving us."
But you were unwilling to go up: you rebelled against the command of the Lord your God.
You grumbled in your tents: "It is because the Lord hates us that he brought us out of Egypt, to hand us over to the Amorites and destroy us.

Where can we go up? Our brothers have made our hearts melt by saying: They are a people greater and taller than we are, with huge cities whose walls rise to the sky; and we even saw the sons of Anak there."
I said to you: "Do not tremble, do not be afraid of them.
The Lord your God, who goes before you, will himself fight for you, just as he did before your eyes in Egypt,
and in the wilderness, where you saw how the Lord your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all along the way you traveled until you reached this place."
Yet in spite of this, you did not trust in the Lord your God,
who went before you on the way to seek out a place for you to camp, in fire by night to show you the way to go, and in the cloud by day.
The Lord heard your words; he was angry and swore this oath:
"Not one of these men, of this evil generation, shall see the good land that I swore to give to your fathers,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh: he shall see it, and to him and to his sons I will give the land on which he has set foot, because he has fully followed the Lord."
The Lord was angry with me too, because of you, and he said: "You also shall not enter it.
It is Joshua son of Nun, your attendant, who shall enter it. Strengthen him, for it is he who will put Israel in possession of the land.
And your little ones, who you said would become plunder, your children who today do not know good from evil, it is they who shall enter it; to them I will give it, and they shall possess it.
As for you, turn and set out again for the wilderness, by the way of the Red Sea."

You answered me: "We have sinned against the Lord. We will go up and fight, as the Lord our God has commanded us." And each of you strapped on his weapons, thinking it easy to go up into the hill country.
The Lord said to me: "Tell them: Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not among you; do not let yourselves be defeated by your enemies."
I spoke to you, but you did not listen: you rebelled against the command of the Lord, and, full of presumption, you went up into the hill country.
Then the Amorites who lived in that hill country came out to meet you; they chased you as bees do and cut you to pieces, from Seir as far as Hormah.
On your return you wept before the Lord; but the Lord did not listen to your voice, he did not give ear to you.
And you stayed at Kadesh for many days, all the time you spent there.

titres.titre: Passing Through Edom, Moab, and Ammon

versets.t: Then we turned and set out for the wilderness, by the way of the Red Sea, as the Lord had commanded me, and for a long time we skirted Mount Seir.
The Lord said to me:
"You have skirted this mountain long enough; head north.
And give this command to the people: You are about to pass through the territory of your brothers, the sons of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you; but be very careful:
do not provoke them, for I will give you none of their land, not even enough to set the sole of your foot on; it is to Esau that I have given Mount Seir as his possession.
You shall buy from them with silver the food you eat, and even the water you drink you shall buy from them with silver.

For the Lord your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands; he has watched over your journey through this great wilderness. These forty years the Lord your God has been with you: you have lacked nothing."
So we passed by our brothers, the sons of Esau who live in Seir, leaving the road of the Arabah, from Elath and Ezion-geber; then we turned and took the road toward the wilderness of Moab.
The Lord said to me: "Do not attack Moab, do not engage them in battle, for I will give you none of their land as a possession: it is to the sons of Lot that I have given Ar as a possession."
Formerly the Emim lived there, a people great, numerous, and tall like the Anakim.
They too are counted as Rephaim, like the Anakim; but the Moabites call them Emim.
In Seir there once lived the Horites; the sons of Esau dispossessed them, destroyed them before them, and settled in their place, as Israel did in the land of its possession, which the Lord gave it.
"Now, up! Cross the Wadi Zered." And we crossed the Wadi Zered.

From Kadesh-barnea until the crossing of the Wadi Zered, our journey lasted thirty-eight years, until the whole generation of fighting men had disappeared from the camp, as the Lord had sworn to them.
The hand of the Lord was also against them, to make them disappear from the camp, until they were gone.
When death had made all the fighting men disappear from among the people,
the Lord spoke to me. He said:
"Today you are to pass through the territory of Moab, at Ar,

and you will draw near to the sons of Ammon. Do not attack them, do not provoke them, for I will give you none of the land of the sons of Ammon as a possession: it is to the sons of Lot that I have given it as a possession."
This too was counted as a land of the Rephaim; Rephaim once lived there, whom the Ammonites called Zamzummim:
a people great, numerous, and tall like the Anakim. The Lord destroyed them before the Ammonites, who dispossessed them and settled in their place.
He did the same for the sons of Esau, who live in Seir, when he destroyed the Horites before them: they dispossessed them and settled in their place to this day.
So too the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, were destroyed by the Caphtorim, who came from Caphtor and settled in their place.
"Up, set out, cross the Wadi Arnon! See, I hand over to you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin the conquest, engage him in battle!
This very day I will begin to spread dread and fear of you over all the peoples under heaven: at the report of your fame they will tremble and be in anguish before you."
From the wilderness of Kedemoth I sent messengers to Sihon, king of Heshbon, with words of peace:
"Let me pass through your land. I will keep to the highway, turning aside neither to the right nor to the left.
You shall sell me food for silver to eat, and give me water for silver to drink; I only want to pass through on foot,
as the sons of Esau who live in Seir did for me, and the Moabites who live in Ar, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord our God is giving us."
But Sihon, king of Heshbon, would not let us pass through his land, for the Lord your God had made his spirit stubborn and his heart hard, in order to hand him over to you, as you see this day.
The Lord said to me: "See, I have begun to hand over Sihon and his land to you; begin the conquest, to take possession of his land."
Sihon came out to meet us, with all his people, to give battle at Jahaz.
The Lord our God handed him over to us, and we defeated him, along with his sons and all his people.
At that time we captured all his cities, and we devoted every city to destruction, the men, the women, and the children, leaving no survivor;
we took as plunder for ourselves only the livestock and the spoil of the conquered cities.
From Aroer, on the edge of the Valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the valley, as far as Gilead, there was no city beyond our reach: the Lord our God handed them all over to us.
But you did not go near the land of the sons of Ammon, nor any part of the bank of the Wadi Jabbok, nor the cities of the hill country, nor anything that the Lord our God had forbidden.

titres.titre: The Victory over Og, King of Bashan

versets.t: We took the road toward Bashan and went up. Og, king of Bashan, came out to meet us, with all his people, to give battle at Edrei.

The Lord said to me: "Do not fear him, for I have handed him over to you, along with all his people and his land; you shall treat him as you treated Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon."
So the Lord our God handed over to us Og, king of Bashan, and all his people as well; we struck him down until not one survivor was left to him.
At that time we captured all his cities; there was not one that escaped us: sixty cities, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these cities were fortified with high walls, gates, and bars, besides a great many unwalled villages.
We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon, king of Heshbon, devoting every city to destruction, the men, the women, and the children;
but we took as plunder for ourselves all the livestock and the spoil of the cities.
So at that time we took from the two kings of the Amorites the land beyond the Jordan, from the Wadi Arnon to Mount Hermon
(the Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir):
all the cities of the tableland, all Gilead, and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

Og, king of Bashan, was the last survivor of the Rephaim. Here is his bed, a bed of iron: is it not at Rabbah, among the sons of Ammon? It is about four and a half metres long and two metres wide, by the common cubit.
At that time we took possession of this land. I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites the territory from Aroer, on the Valley of the Arnon, with half the hill country of Gilead and its cities.
To the half-tribe of Manasseh I gave the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og: the whole region of Argob. All this part of Bashan is called the land of the Rephaim.
Jair son of Manasseh received the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and he gave his name to Bashan, called the Encampments of Jair to this day.
To Machir I gave Gilead.
To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave part of Gilead as far as the Wadi Arnon, the middle of the valley serving as the boundary, and as far as the Wadi Jabbok, the border of the sons of Ammon,
together with the Arabah, the Jordan serving as the boundary, from Chinnereth to the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, at the foot of the slopes of Pisgah, on the east.

At that time I gave you this command: "The Lord your God has given you this land as your possession; but all of you fighting men shall cross over armed at the head of your brothers, the sons of Israel.
Only your wives, your children, and your livestock, for I know that you have much livestock, shall remain in the cities I have given you,

until the Lord has given rest to your brothers as to you, and they too take possession of the land that the Lord your God is giving them beyond the Jordan. Then each of you shall return to the inheritance I have given you."

At that time I gave this command to Joshua: "Your own eyes have seen all that the Lord your God has done to these two kings: so will the Lord do to all the kingdoms against which you are about to march.
Do not fear them, for it is the Lord your God who himself fights for you."
At that time I pleaded with the Lord. I said:
"Lord God, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your mighty hand. What god, in heaven or on earth, can perform works and mighty deeds like yours?
Let me cross over, I pray, and see this good land beyond the Jordan, this fine hill country, and Lebanon!"
But the Lord was angry with me, because of you, and he did not listen to me. He said to me: "Enough! Speak to me no more of this matter.
Go up to the top of Pisgah; lift up your eyes to the west, the north, the south, and the east, and behold the land with your eyes, for you shall not cross this Jordan.
Give your orders to Joshua, strengthen him and make him firm, for it is he who will cross over at the head of this people and put them in possession of the land you will see."
And we stayed in the valley, opposite Beth-peor.

titres.titre: A Call to Keep the Law
Exile and Return to the Lord
The Cities of Refuge East of the Jordan

versets.t: And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and the ordinances that I am teaching you to observe, so that you may live, and enter and take possession of the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, is giving you.
You shall not add to what I command you, nor take anything away from it, but you shall keep the commandments of the Lord your God that I lay upon you.
Your own eyes have seen what the Lord did on account of Baal-peor: everyone who had followed the Baal of Peor, the Lord your God destroyed from among you,
while you, who held fast to the Lord your God, are all alive today.
See, I have taught you statutes and ordinances, as the Lord my God commanded me, that you may observe them in the land you are entering to possess.

You shall keep them and observe them: this will be your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples, who, hearing of all these statutes, will say: Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people!
For what great nation has gods as near to it as the Lord our God is to us whenever we call upon him?
And what great nation has statutes and ordinances as just as all this law that I set before you today?

Only take great care, and watch closely over your soul, so that you do not forget what your eyes have seen, and do not let it fade from your heart a single day of your life; teach it instead to your children and to your children's children.

Remember the day you stood before the Lord your God at Horeb, when the Lord said to me: "Gather the people to me, that I may make them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days they live on the earth, and teach them to their children."
You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain. The mountain was ablaze with fire, a flame rising to the heart of the sky, in darkness, cloud, and gloom.
Then the Lord spoke to you out of the fire. You heard the sound of the words, but you saw no form: nothing but a voice.
He revealed to you his covenant, which he commanded you to observe, the ten words, and he wrote them on two tablets of stone.
At that time the Lord commanded me to teach you statutes and ordinances, that you might observe them in the land you are about to enter to possess.
Since you saw no form on the day the Lord spoke to you at Horeb out of the fire, watch carefully over your souls,
so that you do not act corruptly by making for yourselves an idol, the image of any form whatever: the figure of a man or a woman,
the figure of any beast on the earth, the figure of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
the figure of anything that crawls on the ground, the figure of any fish in the waters under the earth.

And when you lift up your eyes to the sky, when you see the sun, the moon, the stars, all the host of heaven, do not be led astray to bow down to them and serve them: the Lord your God has allotted them to all the peoples under heaven.
But you, the Lord took and brought out of Egypt, that iron furnace, to become the people of his inheritance, as you are today.
Now the Lord was angry with me, because of you, and he swore that I would not cross the Jordan and would not enter the good land that the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance.
I am going to die in this land, without crossing the Jordan; but you are going to cross over and take possession of that good land.
Take care not to forget the covenant that the Lord your God made with you, and not to make for yourselves an idol, the image of anything that the Lord your God has forbidden you;
for the Lord your God is a devouring fire, a jealous God.

When you have children and grandchildren, and have grown old in the land, if you act corruptly by making for yourselves an idol, the image of anything, if you do what is evil in the sight of the Lord your God, so as to provoke him,

I call heaven and earth to witness against you today: you will soon perish from the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess; you will not prolong your days on it, but will be utterly destroyed.
The Lord will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations to which he leads you.
There you will serve gods made by human hands, of wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or eat or smell.
From there you will seek the Lord your God, and you will find him, if you seek him with all your heart and with all your soul.
In your distress, when all these things come upon you, in the days to come you will return to the Lord your God and listen to his voice;
for the Lord your God is a compassionate God: he will not abandon you, he will not destroy you, he will not forget the covenant he swore to your fathers.

Ask, then, about the former times that came before you, from the day God created man on the earth, from one end of the sky to the other: has anything so great ever happened, has anything like it ever been heard of?
Has any people ever heard, as you have, the voice of God speaking out of the fire, and remained alive?

Has any god ever ventured to come and take for himself a nation from the midst of another, by trials, signs, and wonders, by war, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, by great terrors, as the Lord your God did for you in Egypt, before your very eyes?
All this was shown to you so that you might know that the Lord is God, and there is no other besides him.
From the sky he made you hear his voice to instruct you; on the earth he showed you his great fire, and you heard his words out of the fire.
Because he loved your fathers, he chose their descendants after them, and he brought you out of Egypt by his presence and by his great power,
to drive out before you nations greater and stronger than you, to bring you into their land and give it to you as an inheritance, as you see this day.
Know this today, and take it to heart: the Lord is God, in heaven above and on the earth below; there is no other.

Keep his statutes and his commandments that I lay upon you today, that you may be happy, you and your children after you, and that you may prolong your days, through the ages, on the land that the Lord your God is giving you forever.
Then Moses set apart three cities beyond the Jordan, to the east,
so that a killer could flee there, if he had killed his neighbor unintentionally, without having been his enemy before: by fleeing to one of these cities, he would save his life.
These were Bezer, in the wilderness, on the tableland, for the Reubenites; Ramoth, in Gilead, for the Gadites; and Golan, in Bashan, for the Manassites.
This is the law that Moses set before the sons of Israel.
These are the decrees, the statutes, and the ordinances that Moses laid down for the sons of Israel when they came out of Egypt,
beyond the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon and whom Moses and the sons of Israel defeated when they came out of Egypt.
They took possession of his land and of the land of Og, king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to the east,
from Aroer, on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, as far as Mount Sion, that is, Hermon,
together with all the Arabah beyond the Jordan, to the east, as far as the sea of the Arabah, at the foot of the slopes of Pisgah.
Moses summoned all Israel. He said: Hear, Israel, the statutes and the ordinances that I proclaim in your hearing today; learn them and take care to observe them.
The Lord our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
It was not with our fathers that the Lord made this covenant, but with us, who are all here alive today.
On the mountain, out of the fire, the Lord spoke with you face to face,
while I stood between the Lord and you to report his word to you, for you were afraid of the fire and had not gone up the mountain. He said:
"I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You shall have no other gods before my face.
You shall not make for yourself an idol, any image of what is up in the sky, or here below on the earth, or in the waters under the earth.

You shall not bow down before them and you shall not serve them; for I, the Lord your God, am a jealous God, punishing the guilt of the fathers upon the children, to the third and the fourth generation, of those who hate me,
