and showing faithful love to a thousand generations, of those who love me and keep my commandments.
You shall not invoke the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord will not leave unpunished the one who invokes his name in vain.
Observe the sabbath day, to keep it holy, as the Lord your God has commanded you.
For six days you shall labor and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a sabbath for the Lord your God: you shall do no work, neither you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your ox, nor your donkey, nor any of your animals, nor the resident alien who dwells in your towns, so that your male and female servants may rest as you do.

Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and that the Lord your God brought you out of there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm: that is why the Lord your God has commanded you to observe the sabbath day.
Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God has commanded you, so that your days may be prolonged and that you may be happy on the land that the Lord your God is giving you.
You shall not commit murder. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

You shall not covet your neighbor's wife; you shall not desire your neighbor's house, nor his field, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that belongs to your neighbor."

These are the words that the Lord spoke to your whole assembly, on the mountain, out of the fire, the cloud, and the gloom, with a loud voice; and he added nothing more. He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me.
Now, when you heard the voice out of the darkness, while the mountain was ablaze with fire, you came near to me, all your tribal leaders and your elders,

and you said: "See, the Lord our God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the fire; today we have seen that God can speak with a human being and the human being still live.
And now, why should we die? This great fire will consume us! If we continue to hear the voice of the Lord our God, we shall die.
For what creature has ever heard, as we have, the voice of the living God speaking out of the fire, and remained alive?
You, go near and hear all that the Lord our God will say; then you shall report to us all that the Lord our God tells you, and we will listen and observe it."
The Lord heard your words when you spoke to me, and the Lord said to me: "I have heard the words that this people has spoken to you: all that they have said is good.
If only they always kept this heart, to fear me and observe all my commandments, so that it might go well with them and their children forever!
Go, tell them: Return to your tents.

But you, stay here with me, and I will tell you all the commandments, the statutes, and the ordinances that you shall teach them, so that they may observe them in the land I am giving them to possess."
You shall take care to do what the Lord your God has commanded you: you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left.
You shall walk in every way that the Lord your God has laid down for you, so that you may live and be happy and prolong your days in the land you will possess.

titres.titre: Teaching Passed On to the Sons

versets.t: This is the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances that the Lord your God commanded me to teach you, so that you may observe them in the land you are crossing over to possess,

so that you may fear the Lord your God, keeping, all the days of your life, you, your son, and your son's son, all his statutes and all his commandments that I lay upon you, and so that your days may be prolonged.

Hear, then, Israel, and take care to observe them, that it may go well with you and that you may greatly multiply, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, has promised you, in a land flowing with milk and honey.
Hear, Israel: the Lord our God is the one and only Lord.
You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength.
These words that I give you today shall be upon your heart.
You shall repeat them to your children; you shall speak of them, sitting in your house or walking on the road, when you lie down and when you rise.
You shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be like a band between your eyes.
You shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
When the Lord your God has brought you into the land that he swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you, with great and fine cities that you did not build,
houses full of all kinds of good things that you did not fill, hewn cisterns that you did not hew, vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant; when you eat and are satisfied,
take care not to forget the Lord, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
The Lord your God you shall fear, him you shall serve, and by his name you shall swear.
You shall not go after other gods, those of the peoples around you,
for the Lord your God is in your midst, a jealous God: his anger would blaze against you, and he would wipe you from the face of the earth.
You shall not put the Lord your God to the test, as you did at Massah.
You shall carefully keep the commandments of the Lord your God, his decrees and his statutes that he has laid upon you.

You shall do what is right and good in the sight of the Lord, so that it may go well with you, and that you may enter and take possession of the good land that the Lord promised on oath to your fathers,
once he has driven out all your enemies before you, as the Lord has said.
When your son asks you tomorrow: "What are these decrees, these statutes, and these ordinances that the Lord our God has laid upon you?"
you shall say to your son: "We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out of Egypt with his mighty hand.
Before our eyes the Lord worked signs and wonders, great and terrible, against Egypt, against Pharaoh, and against all his household;
and he brought us out of there to lead us into the land he had promised on oath to our fathers, and to give it to us.
The Lord commanded us to observe all these statutes and to fear the Lord our God, so that it might always go well with us and that he might keep us alive, as he does today.
And it will be our righteousness to take care to observe all this commandment before the Lord our God, as he has commanded us."

titres.titre: A People Consecrated to the Lord

versets.t: When the Lord your God has brought you into the land you are about to possess, and has driven out before you many nations, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, seven nations more numerous and stronger than you,
when the Lord your God has handed them over to you and you have defeated them, you shall devote them to destruction: you shall make no covenant with them and show them no mercy.
You shall not intermarry with them: you shall not give your daughter to their son, and you shall not take their daughter for your son;
for she would turn your son away from following me, and he would serve other gods; the anger of the Lord would blaze against you, and he would destroy you at once.
This, rather, is how you shall deal with them: you shall tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, cut down their sacred poles, and burn their idols with fire.
For you are a holy people to the Lord your God; it is you that the Lord your God has chosen to be his own people, out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.
If the Lord became attached to you and chose you, it was not because you were more numerous than all the peoples, for you are the smallest of all;

it is because the Lord loves you and keeps the oath he swore to your fathers, that the Lord brought you out with his mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
Know this, then: the Lord your God is God, the faithful God, who keeps his covenant and his faithful love to a thousand generations, for those who love him and keep his commandments,
but who repays to his face the one who hates him, by making him perish: he does not delay with the one who hates him, but repays him to his face.
You shall therefore keep the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances that I lay upon you today, by observing them.
If you listen to these ordinances, if you keep them and observe them, then the Lord your God will keep for you the covenant and the faithful love that he swore to your fathers.

He will love you, bless you, and multiply you; he will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your soil, your grain, your new wine, and your oil, the offspring of your cattle and the young of your flock, on the land that he swore to your fathers to give you.
You will be blessed more than all the peoples: among you there will be no man or woman unable to bear children, and no barren animal in your herds.
The Lord will keep away from you every sickness; he will not inflict on you any of the deadly diseases of Egypt that you know, but he will bring them on all who hate you.
You shall consume all the peoples that the Lord your God is about to hand over to you; your eye shall show them no pity, and you shall not serve their gods, for that would be a snare to you.
Perhaps you will say in your heart: "These nations are more numerous than I am; how could I dispossess them?"
Do not fear them. Remember well what the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:

the great trials that your eyes saw, the signs and wonders, the mighty hand and the outstretched arm by which the Lord your God brought you out. So will the Lord your God do to all the peoples you dread.
The Lord your God will even send hornets against them, until those who have survived and hidden from you have disappeared.
Do not tremble before them, for the Lord your God is in your midst, a great and dreadful God.
The Lord your God will drive out these nations before you little by little; you will not be able to destroy them all at once, or the wild beasts would multiply against you.
The Lord your God will hand them over to you; he will throw them into great panic, until they are destroyed.
He will hand their kings over to you, and you will wipe out their name from under heaven; no one will stand against you, until you have destroyed them.

You shall burn the idols of their gods with fire; you shall not covet the silver and gold that covers them, you shall not take it for yourself, lest you be caught in it as in a snare, for it is an abomination to the Lord your God.
You shall not bring an abomination into your house, so as not to be devoted to destruction like it: you shall utterly loathe and detest it, for it is a thing devoted to destruction.
You shall take care to observe all the commandment that I lay upon you today, so that you may live and multiply, and enter and take possession of the land that the Lord swore to your fathers.

Remember the whole way that the Lord your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, to humble you, to test you and to know what was in your heart: whether or not you would keep his commandments.

He humbled you, he let you know hunger, and then he fed you with manna, which you did not know and which your fathers had not known, to teach you that man does not live by bread alone, but that man lives by all that comes from the mouth of the Lord.
Your clothing did not wear out on you, and your foot did not swell, during these forty years.
Acknowledge, then, in your heart that the Lord your God disciplines you as a man disciplines his son,
and keep the commandments of the Lord your God, walking in his ways and fearing him.
For the Lord your God is about to bring you into a good land, a land of streams, of springs, and of waters welling up in the valleys and the hills,
a land of wheat and barley, of vines, fig trees, and pomegranates, a land of olive trees, oil, and honey,
a land where you will eat bread without stint and lack nothing, a land whose stones are iron and out of whose hills you will mine copper.
You will eat and be satisfied, and you will bless the Lord your God for the good land he has given you.
Take care not to forget the Lord your God by neglecting his commandments, his ordinances, and his statutes that I lay upon you today.
When you eat and are satisfied, when you build fine houses to live in,
when your cattle and your sheep multiply, when you have silver and gold in abundance and all your possessions increase,
do not let your heart grow proud and forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery,
who led you through that great and dreadful wilderness, full of fiery serpents and scorpions, a parched land without water, who brought forth water for you from the hardest rock,
who fed you in the wilderness with manna unknown to your fathers, to humble you and test you, in order afterward to do you good.
Do not say in your heart: "It is my own strength and the might of my hand that have gained me this wealth."
Remember the Lord your God: it is he who gives you the strength to gain this wealth, so as to uphold, as he does today, the covenant he swore to your fathers.
But if you ever forget the Lord your God, to follow other gods, to serve them and bow down before them, I testify against you today: you will surely perish.
Like the nations that the Lord makes perish before you, so you will perish, for not having listened to the voice of the Lord your God.

titres.titre: Israel Does Not Enter Because of Its Righteousness

versets.t: Hear, Israel: today you are about to cross the Jordan to go and dispossess nations greater and stronger than you, great cities whose walls rise to the sky,
a people great and tall, the sons of Anak, whom you know and of whom you have heard it said: Who can stand against the sons of Anak?

Know this today: the Lord your God will himself cross over before you like a devouring fire; it is he who will destroy them, he who will subdue them before you; you will dispossess them and make them perish at once, as the Lord has told you.

When the Lord your God drives them out before you, do not say in your heart: "It is because of my righteousness that the Lord has brought me in to take possession of this land." No: it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the Lord is driving them out before you.

It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you are entering to take possession of their land; it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the Lord your God is driving them out before you, and to keep the word that he swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Know this, then: it is not because of your righteousness that the Lord your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stiff-necked people.
Remember, do not forget how greatly you provoked the Lord your God in the wilderness: from the day you came out of Egypt until you reached this place, you have been in rebellion against the Lord.
At Horeb itself you provoked the Lord, and the Lord was angry enough with you to want to destroy you.

I had gone up the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that the Lord had made with you; I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, eating no bread and drinking no water.
The Lord gave me the two tablets of stone, written by the finger of God, bearing all the words that he had spoken to you on the mountain, out of the fire, on the day of the assembly.
At the end of forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant,

and the Lord said to me: "Get up, go down quickly from here, for your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have acted corruptly. They have quickly turned aside from the way I laid down for them: they have made themselves an idol of cast metal."
The Lord said to me further: "I see that this people is a stiff-necked people.
Let me destroy them and wipe out their name from under heaven; I will make of you a nation stronger and more numerous than this people."
I turned and came down from the mountain, which was ablaze with fire, the two tablets of the covenant in my two hands.
I looked, and there you had sinned against the Lord your God; you had made yourselves a calf of cast metal, you had quickly turned aside from the way the Lord had laid down for you.
Then I seized the two tablets, threw them from my hands, and broke them before your eyes.

Then I fell down before the Lord, as the first time, forty days and forty nights, eating no bread and drinking no water, because of all the sin you had committed in doing what is evil in the sight of the Lord, so as to provoke him.
For I was afraid before the anger and fury with which the Lord was inflamed against you, to the point of wanting to destroy you. But this time too the Lord listened to me.
The Lord was also greatly angry with Aaron, to the point of wanting to make him perish; and I interceded for Aaron too at that time.
As for the object of your sin, the calf you had made, I took it, burned it in the fire, crushed it, and ground it to fine dust, which I threw into the stream that comes down from the mountain.
At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah, you again provoked the Lord.

And when the Lord sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying: Go up and take possession of the land I am giving you, you rebelled against the command of the Lord your God; you did not have faith in him and you did not listen to his voice.
You have been rebels against the Lord from the day I first knew you.
So I lay prostrate before the Lord those forty days and forty nights, because the Lord was speaking of destroying you.
I prayed to the Lord and said: "Lord God, do not destroy your people, your inheritance, whom you redeemed by your greatness and brought out of Egypt with your mighty hand.
Remember your servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; do not regard the stubbornness of this people, their wickedness and their sin,

lest the land from which you brought us out should say: It is because the Lord did not have the power to bring them into the land he had promised them, and because he hated them, that he brought them out to make them die in the wilderness.
Yet they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great power and by your outstretched arm!"

titres.titre: The Second Tablets and the Ark

versets.t: At that time the Lord said to me: "Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and come up to me on the mountain; make yourself also an ark of wood.
I will write on these tablets the words that were on the first, which you broke, and you shall place them in the ark."
So I made an ark of acacia wood, cut two tablets of stone like the first, and went up the mountain, the two tablets in my hand.
The Lord wrote on these tablets what he had written on the first, the ten words that he had spoken to you on the mountain, out of the fire, on the day of the assembly; then the Lord gave them to me.
I turned, came down from the mountain, and placed the tablets in the ark I had made; and there they have remained, as the Lord commanded me.
The sons of Israel set out from Beeroth Bene-jaakan toward Moserah. It was there that Aaron died and was buried; Eleazar, his son, became priest in his place.
From there they set out for Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah for Jotbathah, a land rich in streams.
At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the Lord to serve him and to bless in his name, as it does to this day.
That is why Levi has no share or inheritance with his brothers: the Lord is his inheritance, as the Lord your God told him.
I stood on the mountain, as the first time, forty days and forty nights, and this time too the Lord listened to me: the Lord was unwilling to destroy you.
The Lord said to me: "Get up, go and take the lead of the people; let them enter and take possession of the land that I swore to their fathers to give them."
And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you but to fear the Lord your God, walking in all his ways, loving him, and serving the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
keeping the commandments of the Lord and his statutes that I lay upon you today, for your own good?
See, to the Lord your God belong the heavens and the heaven of heavens, the earth and all that is in it.
Yet it was to your fathers alone that the Lord became attached, to love them, and after them it was their descendants, it was you that he chose out of all the peoples, as you see this day.
Circumcise, then, your heart, and stiffen your neck no longer.
For the Lord your God is the God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great, strong, and dreadful God, who shows no partiality and takes no bribe,
who does justice for the orphan and the widow, who loves the resident alien and gives him bread and clothing.
You shall love the resident alien, for you were resident aliens in the land of Egypt.
The Lord your God you shall fear and serve; to him you shall hold fast, and by his name you shall swear.
He is your praise, he is your God, who did for you these great and dreadful things that your eyes have seen.
Your fathers had gone down to Egypt, seventy persons in number, and now the Lord your God has made you as numerous as the stars of heaven.

titres.titre: Love the Lord and Keep His Commandments

versets.t: You shall love the Lord your God, and all your days you shall keep what he entrusts to you to keep, his statutes, his ordinances, and his commandments.
Acknowledge today, for I am not speaking to your children, who have not known or seen the lessons of the Lord your God: acknowledge his greatness, his mighty hand and his outstretched arm,
his signs and his works accomplished in the heart of Egypt, against Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and against all his land;
what he did to the army of Egypt, to its horses and its chariots, when he swept the waters of the Red Sea over them as they pursued you, and how the Lord destroyed them forever;
what he did for you in the wilderness, until you reached this place;

what he did to Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, son of Reuben, when the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, with their households, their tents, and all that followed them, in the midst of all Israel.
It is your own eyes that have seen all the great works accomplished by the Lord.
You shall therefore keep all the commandment that I lay upon you today, so that you may be strong, and enter and take possession of the land you are crossing over to possess,
and so that you may prolong your days on the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give them and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land you are about to enter to possess is not like the land of Egypt from which you came, which you sowed and watered by foot, like a vegetable garden.
The land you are crossing over to possess is a land of hills and valleys, which drinks the water of the rain from the sky,
a land that the Lord your God cares for, on which the Lord your God keeps his eyes continually, from the beginning to the end of the year.
If you truly listen to my commandments that I lay upon you today, loving the Lord your God and serving him with all your heart and with all your soul,
I will give your land its rain in its season, the autumn rain and the spring rain, and you will gather in your grain, your new wine, and your oil;
I will put grass in your fields for your livestock, and you will eat your fill.
Take care that your heart is not seduced, that you do not go astray to serve other gods and bow down before them.

The anger of the Lord would blaze against you: he would shut up the sky, there would be no more rain, the land would no longer yield its fruit, and you would quickly disappear from the good land that the Lord is giving you.
Put these words, then, in your heart and in your soul; bind them as a sign on your hand, and let them be like a band between your eyes.
Teach them to your children; speak of them, sitting in your house or walking on the road, when you lie down and when you rise.
Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
so that your days and the days of your children, on the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give them, may be as many as the days of the sky above the earth.
For if you carefully keep all this commandment that I command you to observe, loving the Lord your God, walking in all his ways, and holding fast to him,
the Lord will drive out all these nations before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and stronger than you.
Every place where the sole of your foot treads will be yours: your border will stretch from the wilderness to Lebanon, and from the River, the river Euphrates, to the western sea.
No one will stand against you: the Lord your God will spread, as he told you, the fear and dread of you over all the land you tread.
See, today I set before you a blessing and a curse.
The blessing, if you listen to the commandments of the Lord your God that I lay upon you today;
the curse, if you do not listen to the commandments of the Lord your God, and if you turn aside from the way I lay upon you today, to follow other gods that you have not known.
And when the Lord your God has brought you into the land you are going to possess, you shall pronounce the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Are these mountains not beyond the Jordan, to the west, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, near the oak of Moreh?
For you are about to cross the Jordan to enter and take possession of the land that the Lord your God is giving you; you shall possess it and dwell in it.
You shall therefore take care to observe all the statutes and all the ordinances that I set before you today.
These are the statutes and the ordinances that you shall take care to observe in the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, has given you to possess, all the days that you live on that soil.
You shall utterly destroy all the places where the nations you are about to dispossess served their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and under every green tree.
You shall tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, burn their sacred poles with fire, break in pieces the idols of their gods, and wipe out their name from those places.
You shall not act this way toward the Lord your God;
rather, you shall seek him at the place that the Lord your God will choose out of all your tribes, to set his name there and make it his dwelling, and there you shall go.
There you shall bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and what your hand has set apart, your votive and freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your cattle and your flock.
There you shall take your meals before the Lord your God, and you shall rejoice, you and your households, in all that your hand has acquired and by which the Lord your God has blessed you.
You shall not act as we do here today, each doing what seems right to him,
for you have not yet come to the rest and the inheritance that the Lord your God is giving you.

But you shall cross the Jordan and dwell in the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance; he will give you rest by delivering you from all the enemies around you, and you shall dwell in safety.

Then, at the place that the Lord your God will choose to make his name dwell there, that is where you shall bring all that I command you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and what your hand has set apart, and all the choice offerings that you have vowed to the Lord.
You shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you, your sons and your daughters, your male and female servants, and the Levite who is in your towns, for he has no share or inheritance with you.
Take care not to offer your burnt offerings in any place you see;
it is only at the place that the Lord will choose, in one of your tribes, that you shall offer your burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I command you.

However, whenever you desire, you may slaughter animals and eat meat in all your towns, according to the blessing that the Lord your God grants you; the clean and the unclean alike may eat of it, as one eats gazelle and deer.
Only, you shall not eat the blood: you shall pour it out on the ground like water.

You may not eat within your towns the tithe of your grain, of your new wine, and of your oil, nor the firstborn of your cattle and your flock, nor any offering that you have vowed, nor your freewill offerings, nor what your hand has set apart.

It is before the Lord your God, at the place he will choose, that you shall eat them, you, your son and your daughter, your male and female servants, and the Levite who is in your towns; you shall rejoice before the Lord your God in all that your hand has acquired.
Take care not to neglect the Levite, as long as you live on your soil.
When the Lord your God has enlarged your territory, as he promised you, and you say: I want to eat meat, because you feel the desire for it, you may eat meat whenever you wish.

If the place that the Lord your God will choose to set his name there is too far from you, you may slaughter some of the cattle and flock that the Lord has given you, as I have commanded you, and eat within your towns whenever you desire.
You shall eat it as one eats gazelle or deer: the clean and the unclean alike may eat of it.
Only, hold firmly to not eating the blood, for the blood is the life, and you shall not eat the life with the flesh.
You shall not eat it: you shall pour it out on the ground like water.
You shall not eat it, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, doing what is right in the sight of the Lord.
But the holy offerings that are your charge, and those you have vowed, you shall take and go to the place that the Lord will choose.

You shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood, on the altar of the Lord your God; for your other sacrifices, the blood shall be poured out on the altar of the Lord your God, and you shall eat the flesh.
Keep and heed all these words that I command you, so that it may go well forever with you and your children after you, doing what is good and right in the sight of the Lord your God.
When the Lord your God has cut off before you the nations you are about to dispossess, and you have dispossessed them and dwell in their land,

take care not to be trapped into imitating them, once they have been destroyed before you; take care not to inquire after their gods, saying: "How did these nations serve their gods? I too want to do the same."

You shall not act this way toward the Lord your God, for they did for their gods all the abominations that the Lord hates: they would even burn their sons and daughters in the fire in honor of their gods.
All that I command you, you shall take care to observe, adding nothing to it and taking nothing away from it.
If there arises among you a prophet or a man who has dreams, and he announces to you a sign or a wonder,
and if the sign or wonder announced comes to pass, and he says to you: "Let us go after other gods, gods you do not know, and let us serve them,"
you shall not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer, for the Lord your God is testing you to know whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
It is the Lord your God whom you shall follow, it is he whom you shall fear; you shall keep his commandments, you shall listen to his voice, you shall serve him, and you shall hold fast to him.

As for that prophet or that dreamer, he shall be put to death, for he has preached revolt against the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery; he has tried to turn you from the way the Lord your God commanded you to walk. So you shall purge the evil from among you.

If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son, or your daughter, or the wife who rests on your heart, or the friend who is dear to you as yourself, secretly tries to lead you astray, saying: "Let us go and serve other gods," gods that neither you nor your fathers have known,
from among the gods of the peoples around you, near you or far away, from one end of the earth to the other,
you shall not yield to him and you shall not listen to him; your eye shall show him no pity, you shall not spare him and you shall not shield him,
but you shall put him to death: your hand shall be the first to rise against him to put him to death, then the hand of all the people.
You shall overwhelm him with stones until he dies, because he sought to turn you away from the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
All Israel will hear of it and be seized with fear, and such an evil will never again be committed among you.
If you hear it said, of one of the cities that the Lord your God is giving you to dwell in,
that worthless men, come out from among you, have led astray the inhabitants of their city, saying: Let us go and serve other gods, gods you do not know,
you shall make inquiry, you shall examine, you shall question carefully; and if the matter is confirmed, if it is established that such an abomination has been committed among you,
then you shall put the inhabitants of that city to the sword, devoting it to destruction with all that is in it, and you shall put its livestock too to the sword.

You shall gather all its spoil into the middle of the square, and you shall burn the city entirely, with all its spoil, as a burnt offering to the Lord your God; it shall be forever a heap of ruins, never to be rebuilt.

Nothing of what has been devoted to destruction shall cling to your hand, so that the Lord may turn from the heat of his anger, show you mercy and take pity on you, and multiply you, as he swore to your fathers,
if you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, keeping all his commandments that I lay upon you today and doing what is right in the sight of the Lord your God.
You are the children of the Lord your God: you shall not gash yourselves and you shall not shave the front of your head for a dead person,
for you are a holy people to the Lord your God, and it is you that the Lord has chosen to be his own people, out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.
You shall not eat anything abominable.
These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat,
the deer, the gazelle, the roebuck, the ibex, the antelope, the wild ox, and the mountain sheep.
Every animal with a divided hoof, split into two claws, and that chews the cud, you may eat.
But among those that chew the cud or have a divided hoof, you shall not eat the camel, the hare, and the rock badger: they chew the cud, but do not have a divided hoof; they shall be unclean for you.
The pig, for its part, has a divided hoof, but does not chew the cud: it shall be unclean for you. You shall not eat their flesh and you shall not touch their carcass.
Among all that lives in the waters, this is what you may eat: everything that has fins and scales.
But everything that does not have fins and scales, you shall not eat: it is unclean for you.
You may eat every clean bird.
These are the ones you shall not eat: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the osprey,
the kite, the falcon, and every kind of vulture,
every kind of raven,
the ostrich, the owl, the gull, and every kind of hawk,
the little owl, the great owl, the ibis,
the pelican, the white vulture, the cormorant,
the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
Every winged insect shall be unclean for you: they shall not be eaten.
But you may eat every clean winged creature.

You shall not eat any animal that has died of itself. You shall give it to the resident alien who dwells in your towns, for him to eat, or you shall sell it to a foreigner, for you are a holy people to the Lord your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk.
You shall set apart the tithe of all that your sowing yields, of what your field produces each year.

You shall eat before the Lord your God, at the place he will choose to make his name dwell there, the tithe of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, as well as the firstborn of your cattle and your flock, so that you may learn to fear the Lord your God always.

But if the way is too long for you, if you cannot carry the tithe because the place that the Lord your God will choose to set his name there is too far from you, when the Lord your God has blessed you,
you shall convert it into silver; you shall clasp the silver in your hand and go to the place that the Lord your God will choose.

There you shall buy with this silver whatever you desire, cattle, sheep, wine, fermented drink, whatever your heart wishes; you shall eat there before the Lord your God and rejoice, you and your household.
You shall not neglect the Levite who is in your towns, for he has no share or inheritance with you.
Every three years, you shall set apart all the tithe of your produce for that year and deposit it in your towns;

then the Levite, who has no share or inheritance with you, the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow who are in your towns will come, and they will eat their fill, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
Every seven years, you shall grant a release of debts.

This is how this release shall be practiced: every creditor shall release what he has lent to his neighbor; he shall not press his neighbor or his brother, for the release of the Lord will have been proclaimed.
The foreigner you may press; but what your brother owes you, your hand shall release,
so that there may be no poor person among you. For the Lord will fill you with blessings in the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess,
provided only that you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, taking care to observe all this commandment that I lay upon you today.
Yes, the Lord your God will bless you, as he told you: you will lend to many nations, and you yourself will not borrow; you will rule over many nations, and they will not rule over you.

If there is among you a poor person, one of your brothers, in one of your towns, in the land that the Lord your God is giving you, you shall not harden your heart and you shall not close your hand to your poor brother;
rather, you shall open your hand to him and lend him enough to meet his need.

Take care not to let this wicked thought rise in your heart: "The seventh year, the year of release, is near!"; take care not to look with a grudging eye on your poor brother, to the point of giving him nothing: he would cry out against you to the Lord, and you would be charged with a sin.
You must give to him, and give without your heart regretting it; for because of this the Lord your God will bless you in all your work and in all that your hand undertakes.
The poor will never disappear from the land; that is why I give you this commandment: Open wide your hand to your brother, to the needy and the poor of your land.
If one of your Hebrew brothers, man or woman, sells himself to you, he shall serve you six years; in the seventh year, you shall send him away free from you.
And when you send him away free, you shall not send him away empty-handed:
you shall provide him generously from your flock, your threshing floor, and your winepress; you shall give him a share of the goods with which the Lord your God has blessed you.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt and that the Lord your God redeemed you: that is why I give you this commandment today.
But if he says to you: "I do not want to leave you," because he loves you, you and your household, and is well off with you,
then you shall take an awl, pierce his ear against the door, and he shall be your servant forever; you shall do the same for your female servant.
Do not find it hard to send him away free, for in serving you six years he has earned you twice the wages of a hired worker; and the Lord your God will bless you in all that you do.

Every firstborn male born of your cattle and your flock, you shall consecrate to the Lord your God; you shall not put the firstborn of your ox to work, and you shall not shear the firstborn of your flock.
It is before the Lord your God that you shall eat it each year, you and your household, at the place that the Lord will choose.
But if it has a defect, if it is lame or blind, or has any other blemish, you shall not offer it in sacrifice to the Lord your God.
You shall eat it within your towns; the clean and the unclean alike may eat of it, as one eats gazelle or deer.
Only, you shall not eat its blood: you shall pour it out on the ground like water.

Observe the month of Abib (around March-April) and celebrate the Passover in honor of the Lord your God, for it was in the month of Abib that the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt, during the night.
You shall sacrifice the Passover to the Lord your God, from the flock and the herd, at the place that the Lord will choose to make his name dwell there.

With it you shall not eat leavened bread; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, the bread of affliction, for it was in haste that you came out of Egypt, so that you may remember all your life the day you came out of Egypt.
No leaven shall be seen with you, in all your territory, for seven days; and none of the meat sacrificed on the evening of the first day shall remain overnight until morning.
You may not sacrifice the Passover in any of the towns that the Lord your God is giving you;
it is only at the place that the Lord your God will choose to make his name dwell there that you shall sacrifice the Passover, in the evening, at sunset, at the hour you came out of Egypt.
You shall cook it and eat it at the place that the Lord your God will choose; then, in the morning, you shall return to your tents.
For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a solemn assembly in honor of the Lord your God: you shall do no work.
You shall count seven weeks; from the moment the sickle is first put to the standing grain, you shall begin to count seven weeks,
and you shall celebrate the feast of Weeks in honor of the Lord your God, with the freewill offerings of your hand, which you shall make according to the blessing that the Lord your God grants you.

You shall rejoice before the Lord your God, at the place that the Lord your God will choose to make his name dwell there, you, your son and your daughter, your male and female servants, the Levite who is in your towns, as well as the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow who live among you.
You shall remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and you shall take care to observe these statutes.
You shall celebrate the feast of Booths for seven days, when you have gathered in the produce of your threshing floor and your winepress;
you shall rejoice at this feast, you, your son and your daughter, your male and female servants, as well as the Levite, the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow who are in your towns.

For seven days you shall celebrate the feast in honor of the Lord your God, at the place he will choose; for the Lord your God will bless you in all your harvest and in all the work of your hands, and you will be full of joy.

Three times a year, every male among you shall present himself before the Lord your God, at the place he will choose: at the feast of Unleavened Bread, at the feast of Weeks, and at the feast of Booths; and no one shall present himself before the Lord empty-handed:
each shall give according to his means, according to the blessing that the Lord your God grants you.
You shall appoint judges and officers in all the towns that the Lord your God is giving you, tribe by tribe, and they shall judge the people with justice.
You shall not pervert justice, you shall show no partiality, you shall take no bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the cause of the just.
Justice, and justice alone, is what you shall pursue, so that you may live and take possession of the land that the Lord your God is giving you.
You shall not plant any sacred pole, any tree, beside the altar that you build for the Lord your God;
and you shall not set up a sacred pillar, which the Lord your God hates.
You shall not sacrifice to the Lord your God any ox or lamb that has a defect or any blemish whatever, for that is an abomination to the Lord your God.
If there is found among you, in one of the towns that the Lord your God is giving you, a man or a woman who does what is evil in the sight of the Lord your God, transgressing his covenant,
who goes and serves other gods and bows down before them, before the sun, the moon, or all the host of heaven, which I have not commanded,

and the matter is reported to you, when you have heard of it, you shall make a thorough inquiry; and if the matter is confirmed, if it is established that such an abomination has been committed in Israel,
you shall bring out to the gates of the city the man or the woman guilty of this evil, and you shall stone them until they die.
It is on the word of two or three witnesses that the one who must die shall be put to death; he shall not be put to death on the word of a single witness.
The hand of the witnesses shall be the first to rise against him to put him to death, then the hand of all the people. So you shall purge the evil from among you.

If a case for judgment is too hard for you, whether it concerns a murder, a dispute, or an assault, any matter of litigation in your towns, you shall rise and go up to the place that the Lord your God will choose.
You shall go to the levitical priests and to the judge in office in those days; you shall consult them, and they will make known to you the verdict.
You shall act according to the verdict that they make known to you at the place that the Lord will choose, and you shall take care to act according to all that they teach you.
You shall act according to the instruction they give you and according to the verdict they pronounce, turning aside neither to the right nor to the left from what they have declared to you.
Whoever, out of pride, refuses to listen to the priest in office in the service of the Lord your God, or to the judge, that man shall die. So you shall purge the evil from Israel;
and all the people will hear of it, be seized with fear, and cease to act with pride.
When you have entered the land that the Lord your God is giving you, and have taken possession of it and dwell in it, if you say: "I want to set a king over me, like all the nations around me,"

it is a king chosen by the Lord your God that you shall set over you; it is from among your brothers that you shall take a king to set over you. You may not give yourself as king a foreigner, who is not your brother.
Only, he shall not have too many horses, and he shall not bring the people back to Egypt to multiply his horses, for the Lord has told you: "You shall never again take that road."
He shall not have too many wives either, lest his heart be turned away, nor too much silver and gold.
When he mounts the throne of his kingdom, he shall write for himself, in a book, a copy of this law, from the exemplar kept by the levitical priests.
He shall keep it near him and read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, to keep all the words of this law and all these statutes, by observing them,

so that his heart may not rise above his brothers and that he may not turn aside from the commandment to the right or to the left; thus he will prolong his days on his throne, he and his sons, in the midst of Israel.

titres.titre: The portion of the levitical priests

versets.t: The levitical priests, the whole tribe of Levi, shall have no portion or inheritance with Israel: they shall live on the offerings made by fire to the Lord, and on his inheritance.
Levi shall have no inheritance among his brothers: the Lord is his inheritance, as he told him.
This is what shall be due to the priests from the people, from those who offer a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep: they shall give the priest the shoulder, the jaws, and the stomach.
You shall give him the firstfruits of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, as well as the firstfruits of the shearing of your flock;
for it is he whom the Lord your God has chosen out of all your tribes to stand before the Lord and to minister in his name, he and his sons, forever.
If a Levite leaves one of your towns, wherever he lives in Israel, and comes, with all his heart's desire, to the place the Lord will choose,
he shall minister in the name of the Lord his God, like all his brothers the Levites who stand there before the Lord;
he shall receive for his food an equal portion with theirs, apart from what the sale of his patrimony brings him.
When you have entered the land the Lord your God is giving you, you shall not learn to imitate the abominations of those nations.
Let there not be found among you anyone who makes his son or daughter pass through the fire, who practices divination, augury, sorcery, or spells,
who casts charms, who consults spirits and mediums, who questions the dead;
for whoever does such things is an abomination to the Lord, and it is because of these abominations that the Lord your God is driving out those nations before you.
You shall belong wholly to the Lord your God.
These nations that you are about to dispossess listen to soothsayers and diviners; but to you, the Lord your God does not allow this.
The Lord your God will raise up for you, from your midst, from among your brothers, a prophet like me: it is to him that you shall listen.

This is exactly what you asked of the Lord your God at Horeb, on the day of the assembly, when you said: "Let me not hear the voice of the Lord my God any longer, and let me not see this great fire any more, lest I die!"
And the Lord said to me: "They have spoken well.
I will raise up for them, from among their brothers, a prophet like you; I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall tell them all that I command him.
And if anyone does not listen to my words, the words he speaks in my name, I myself will call him to account.
But the prophet who has the arrogance to speak in my name a word I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet shall die."
Perhaps you will say in your heart: "How shall we recognize the word the Lord has not spoken?"

Well, when the prophet speaks in the name of the Lord, if his word does not come true and does not happen, it is a word the Lord has not spoken: the prophet has spoken it out of arrogance, and you shall not fear him.
When the Lord your God has cut off the nations whose land the Lord your God is giving you, when you have dispossessed them and dwell in their towns and their houses,
you shall set apart three cities in the midst of the land the Lord your God is giving you to possess.

You shall keep in repair the roads that lead to them, and you shall divide into three the territory of the land the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance, so that any manslayer may take refuge there.
This is the case of the manslayer who may take refuge there and save his life: one who kills his neighbor by accident, without having been his enemy beforehand.

Thus, a man goes into the forest with another to cut wood; his hand swings the axe to fell the tree, but the iron head slips from the handle, strikes his companion, and kills him: that man shall take refuge in one of these cities and save his life.

Otherwise, the avenger of blood, pursuing the manslayer in the heat of his anger, might overtake him if the road were too long and strike him a mortal blow; and yet this man did not deserve death, since he had no hatred for his victim.
That is why I give you this command: Set apart three cities.
And if the Lord your God enlarges your territory, as he swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land he promised your fathers,
provided that you keep and put into practice this whole commandment I lay upon you today, loving the Lord your God and always walking in his ways, then you shall add three more cities to these three,
so that innocent blood may not be shed in the midst of the land the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance, and that this blood may not fall back upon you.
But if a man, hating his neighbor, lies in wait for him, throws himself upon him and strikes him a mortal blow, then flees to one of these cities,
the elders of his town shall send and seize him and hand him over to the avenger of blood, so that he may die.
Your eye shall show him no pity: you shall remove innocent blood from Israel, and you will be blessed.
You shall not move your neighbor's boundary marker, set by the ancestors, in the inheritance you receive in the land the Lord your God is giving you to possess.
A single witness shall not suffice against a man for any crime or fault whatever: it is on the word of two or three witnesses that the matter shall be established.
If a malicious witness rises against a man to accuse him of an offense,
the two men in dispute shall stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges in office in those days.
The judges shall make a careful inquiry; and if the witness is a false witness, if he has given false testimony against his brother,
you shall do to him what he intended to do to his brother. So you shall remove the evil from your midst.
The others will hear of it, will be seized with fear, and never again will such an evil be committed in your midst.
Your eye shall show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses, chariots, an army more numerous than you, you shall not fear them, for the Lord your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, is with you.
When the battle is about to begin, the priest shall come forward and speak to the people.
He shall say to them: "Hear, Israel! Today you are about to fight your enemies; do not let your heart grow faint, do not be afraid, do not tremble, and do not be terrified before them,
for the Lord your God marches with you, to fight for you against your enemies and to save you."
Then the officers shall speak to the people: "Who has built a new house without yet dedicating it? Let him go and return home, lest he die in battle and another dedicate it.
Who has planted a vineyard without yet gathering its first fruits? Let him go and return home, lest he die in battle and another enjoy it.
Who has become engaged to a woman without yet marrying her? Let him go and return home, lest he die in battle and another marry her."
The officers shall speak further to the people: "Who is afraid and feels his heart grow faint? Let him go and return home, so that the heart of his brothers may not melt like his own."
When the officers have finished speaking to the people, commanders of troops shall be placed at the head of the people.
When you approach a city to attack it, you shall offer it peace.
If it answers you with peace and opens its gates to you, all the people found in it shall be put to forced labor for you and shall serve you.
But if it refuses peace and wishes to make war on you, you shall lay siege to it;
and when the Lord your God has delivered it into your hands, you shall put all its males to the sword.
Only the women, the children, the livestock, and everything in the city, all its spoil, you shall take for yourself; you shall enjoy the spoil of your enemies, which the Lord your God has given you.
This is how you shall act toward all the cities very far from you, which are not cities of these nations here.
But in the cities of these peoples the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance, you shall leave alive nothing that breathes:
you shall devote them to destruction, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, as the Lord your God has commanded you,
so that they may not teach you to imitate all the abominations they do for their gods, leading you to sin against the Lord your God.

If you besiege a city for many days, fighting against it to capture it, you shall not destroy its trees with the axe, for you eat their fruit: you shall not cut them down. Is the tree of the field a man, that you should besiege it?
Only the trees you know are not fruit trees may you destroy and cut down, to build siege works against the city that makes war on you, until it falls.
If, on the soil the Lord your God is giving you to possess, a slain man is found lying in the fields, and it is not known who struck him,
your elders and your judges shall go out and measure the distance to the towns around the slain man.
For the town nearest the slain man, the elders of that town shall take a heifer that has not yet been put to work or pulled under the yoke.
The elders of that town shall bring the heifer down to a stream that never dries up, to a place neither tilled nor sown, and there, in the stream, they shall break its neck.

The priests, the sons of Levi, shall come forward, for it is they whom the Lord your God has chosen to serve him and to bless in the name of the Lord; and by their word every dispute and every case of violence is settled.
All the elders of that town, those nearest the slain man, shall wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the stream.
Then they shall declare: "Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it shed.
Forgive your people Israel, whom you have redeemed, Lord, and do not let innocent blood weigh upon your people Israel." And this blood shall be forgiven them.
So you shall remove innocent blood from your midst, by doing what is right in the eyes of the Lord.
When you go out to war against your enemies, and the Lord your God has delivered them into your hands and you take captives from them,
if you see among the captives a beautiful woman, and you are drawn to her and wish to marry her,
you shall bring her into your home; she shall shave her head and trim her nails,

she shall put off the garment of her captivity, she shall live in your house and mourn her father and mother for a month; after that, you may go to her, you shall be her husband and she shall be your wife.
But if she no longer pleases you, you shall let her go wherever she wishes; you may not sell her for money or treat her as a slave, since you have dishonored her.
If a man has two wives, one loved and the other unloved, and they have borne him sons, both the loved and the unloved, and if the firstborn is the son of the unloved,
on the day he divides his property among his sons, he may not treat the son of the loved wife as the firstborn to the detriment of the son of the unloved, who is the firstborn.
He shall acknowledge as firstborn the son of the unloved wife and give him a double share of all he has; for this son is the firstfruits of his vigor: to him belongs the right of the firstborn.
If a man has a stubborn and rebellious son, who obeys neither his father's voice nor his mother's, and does not listen to them even when they discipline him,
his father and mother shall seize him and bring him to the elders of his town, to the gate of his place.
They shall say to the elders of the town: "This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious, he does not obey our voice, he lives in debauchery and drunkenness."
Then all the men of his town shall stone him, and he shall die. So you shall remove the evil from your midst, and all Israel will hear of it and be seized with fear.
If a man guilty of a capital crime is put to death and you hang him on a tree,

his corpse shall not remain overnight on the tree: you shall bury him the same day, for one who is hanged is a curse of God, and you shall not defile the land the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance.
If you see your brother's ox or sheep straying, you shall not ignore it: you shall bring them back to your brother.
If your brother does not live near you or if you do not know him, you shall take the animal into your home, and it shall stay with you until your brother claims it; then you shall return it to him.
You shall do the same for his donkey, for his cloak, for anything your brother has lost and you have found: you may not ignore it.
If you see your brother's donkey or ox fallen on the road, you shall not ignore it: you shall help him raise them up.
A woman shall not wear a man's clothing, and a man shall not put on a woman's garment, for whoever does such things is an abomination to the Lord your God.
If you come upon a bird's nest along the way, in a tree or on the ground, with young or eggs, and the mother sitting on the young or the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the young:
you shall let the mother go and take only the young for yourself, so that you may be blessed and prolong your days.
When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet around your roof, so as not to bring the guilt of blood upon your house, should anyone fall from it.
You shall not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, lest the whole be forfeit, both the seed you have sown and the yield of the vineyard.
You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together.
You shall not wear a garment woven of wool and linen mixed together.
You shall make tassels on the four corners of the cloak with which you cover yourself.
If a man marries a woman, unites with her, then comes to dislike her,
charges her with shameful conduct and damages her reputation, saying: "I married this woman, but when I united with her I did not find her a virgin,"
the young woman's father and mother shall take the proofs of her virginity and bring them out to the elders of the town, at the gate.
The young woman's father shall say to the elders: "I gave my daughter as wife to this man, and he has come to dislike her;

now he charges her with shameful conduct, saying: I did not find your daughter a virgin. But here are the proofs of my daughter's virginity." And they shall spread out the garment before the elders of the town.
Then the elders of the town shall seize this man and punish him;

they shall impose on him a fine of one hundred pieces of silver, which they shall give to the young woman's father, for having damaged the reputation of a virgin of Israel. She shall remain his wife, and he may not send her away as long as he lives.
But if the charge is true, if the young woman's virginity is not established,

they shall bring her out to the entrance of her father's house, and the men of her town shall stone her until she dies, because she has committed an outrage in Israel, prostituting herself in her father's house. So you shall remove the evil from your midst.
If a man is caught lying with a married woman, both of them shall die, the man who lay with the woman, and the woman. So you shall remove the evil from the midst of Israel.
If a virgin girl is engaged to a man, and another meets her in the town and lies with her,

you shall bring both of them out to the gate of that town and stone them until they die: the girl because she did not cry out in the town, and the man because he dishonored his neighbor's wife. So you shall remove the evil from your midst.
But if it is in the fields that the man meets the engaged girl, and he seizes her and lies with her, only the man who lay with her shall die:
to the girl you shall do nothing, for there is in her no sin deserving death; this case is like that of a man who throws himself upon his neighbor and kills him.
It was in the fields that he met her; the engaged girl cried out, but there was no one to rescue her.
If a man meets a virgin girl, not engaged, and seizes her and lies with her, and they are caught,
the man who lay with her shall give the girl's father fifty pieces of silver; she shall be his wife, since he has dishonored her, and he may not send her away as long as he lives.

titres.titre: Access to the assembly of the Lord

versets.t: No one shall take his father's wife or lift the edge of his father's cloak.
The man whose organs are crushed or mutilated shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.
No child born of a forbidden union shall enter the assembly of the Lord; even his tenth generation shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.
The Ammonite and the Moabite shall not enter the assembly of the Lord; even their tenth generation shall never enter the assembly of the Lord,

because they did not come to meet you with bread and water on the way when you came out of Egypt, and because the king of Moab hired against you Balaam son of Beor, from Pethor in Mesopotamia, to curse you.
But the Lord your God refused to listen to Balaam; the Lord your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, for the Lord your God loves you.
You shall never seek their peace or their prosperity, as long as you live.
You shall not abhor the Edomite, for he is your brother; you shall not abhor the Egyptian, for you were an immigrant in his land.
The children born to them may, in the third generation, enter the assembly of the Lord.
When you camp in war against your enemies, you shall keep yourself from anything evil.
If there is among you a man made unclean by a nocturnal emission, he shall go outside the camp and not come back in;
toward evening he shall bathe in water, and at sunset he may return to the camp.
You shall have a place outside the camp, and that is where you shall go out;
you shall have a spade among your gear, and when you go to sit apart, you shall dig with it, then cover your excrement.

For the Lord your God walks in the midst of your camp to protect you and to deliver your enemies to you; your camp must therefore be holy, so that he may see nothing indecent among you and not turn away from you.
You shall not hand back to his master a slave who has fled from him to take refuge with you.
He shall dwell with you, in your midst, in the place he chooses, in one of your towns, wherever he is content; you shall not oppress him.
There shall be no sacred prostitute among the daughters of Israel, nor any sacred prostitute among the sons of Israel.
You shall not bring into the house of the Lord your God the wages of a prostitute or the earnings of a dog, in fulfillment of a vow, for both are an abomination to the Lord your God.
You shall not require any interest from your brother, neither for money, nor for food, nor for anything that is lent at interest.

From the foreigner you may require interest; but from your brother you shall not require it, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all that your hand undertakes, in the land you are about to enter to possess.
When you make a vow to the Lord your God, you shall not delay to fulfill it, for the Lord your God would call you to account for it, and you would be burdened with sin.
If you refrain from making vows, there will be no sin in you.
But the word that has gone out of your lips you shall keep and fulfill, as you freely vowed to the Lord your God and spoke with your mouth.
When you enter your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat grapes to your fill, as many as you wish, but you shall not put any in your basket.
When you enter your neighbor's standing grain, you may pluck ears with your hand, but you shall not put the sickle to your neighbor's grain.

When a man has married a woman and united with her, if she ceases to find favor in his eyes because he has found something indecent in her, he shall write her a certificate of divorce, put it in her hand, and send her from his house.
Once she has left his house, she may go and become another man's wife.
But if this second husband comes to dislike her, writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand and sends her from his house, or if he dies,

the first husband who sent her away may not take her again as his wife, after she has been made unclean: this would be an abomination before the Lord, and you shall not burden with sin the land the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance.
When a man is newly married, he shall not go out with the army, and no duty shall be laid upon him: he shall be free for his household for one year, and shall bring joy to the wife he has married.
No one shall take as a pledge the two millstones, nor even the upper millstone, for that would be to take life itself in pledge.
If a man is found who has kidnapped one of his brothers among the sons of Israel, reduced him to slavery or sold him, that kidnapper shall die. So you shall remove the evil from your midst.
In a case of leprosy, be careful to observe and do exactly all that the levitical priests teach you; what I have commanded them, you shall be careful to put into practice.
Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam along the way, when you came out of Egypt.
If you make your neighbor any kind of loan, you shall not enter his house to take his pledge:
you shall wait outside, and the man to whom you make the loan shall bring the pledge out to you.
If this man is poor, you shall not go to bed keeping his pledge:
you shall return it to him at sunset, so that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you; this will be for you a righteousness before the Lord your God.
You shall not exploit the poor and needy laborer, whether he is one of your brothers or one of the immigrants who live in your land, in your towns.

Each day you shall give him his wages, and do not let the sun set on this debt, for he is poor and waits for it with all his heart; otherwise he would cry out against you to the Lord, and you would be burdened with sin.
Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers: each shall be put to death for his own sin.
You shall not pervert the justice due to the immigrant or the orphan, and you shall not take the widow's garment as a pledge.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and that the Lord your God redeemed you from there: that is why I command you to act thus.

When you reap the harvest in your field and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, you shall not go back to get it: it shall be for the immigrant, the orphan, and the widow, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive trees, you shall not go over the branches again behind you: what remains shall be for the immigrant, the orphan, and the widow.
When you harvest your vineyard, you shall not glean behind you: what remains shall be for the immigrant, the orphan, and the widow.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt: that is why I command you to act thus.
If a dispute arises between men and they come to court, they shall be judged: the innocent acquitted and the guilty condemned.
If the guilty man deserves to be beaten, the judge shall have him lie down and be struck in his presence with a number of blows proportionate to his fault.
He shall be given forty lashes, no more, lest, by striking him with many more, your brother be degraded in your eyes.
You shall not muzzle the ox while it treads out the grain.

If brothers live together and one of them dies leaving no son, the wife of the deceased shall not marry outside, to a stranger; her brother-in-law shall come to her, take her as his wife, and fulfill toward her his duty as a brother-in-law.
The firstborn she bears shall carry on the name of the deceased brother, so that his name may not be blotted out from Israel.

But if this man does not wish to take his sister-in-law, she shall go up to the gate, to the elders, and say: "My brother-in-law refuses to carry on his brother's name in Israel; he will not fulfill toward me his duty as a brother-in-law."
The elders of his town shall summon him and speak with him. If he persists and says: "It does not please me to take her,"
his sister-in-law shall approach him before the elders, pull the sandal off his foot, spit in his face, and say: "So shall it be done to the man who will not build up his brother's house."
And his house shall be called in Israel the house of the unshod.
When men fight with one another, and the wife of one comes near to rescue her husband from the hand of the one striking him, if she reaches out her hand and seizes the latter by the private parts,
you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall show no pity.
You shall not have in your bag two kinds of weights, a heavy one and a light one.
You shall not have in your house two kinds of measures, a large one and a small one.
You shall have an exact and honest weight, an exact and honest measure, so that your days may be prolonged on the soil the Lord your God is giving you;
for whoever does such things, whoever commits fraud, is an abomination to the Lord your God.
Remember what Amalek did to you along the way, when you came out of Egypt:
he surprised you on the road and struck from behind all the stragglers, when you were exhausted and at the end of your strength; and he had no fear of God.

When the Lord your God has given you rest by delivering you from all your surrounding enemies, in the land the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess, you shall blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven: do not forget.

titres.titre: The mutual commitment of the covenant

versets.t: When you have entered the land the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance, and have taken possession of it and settled in it,

you shall take a portion of all the firstfruits of the produce of the soil that you harvest in the land the Lord your God is giving you; you shall put them in a basket and go to the place the Lord your God will choose to make his name dwell.
You shall present yourself to the priest in office in those days and say to him: "I declare today to the Lord your God that I have entered the land the Lord swore to our fathers to give us."
The priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it down before the altar of the Lord your God.

Then, taking up your words, you shall say before the Lord your God: "My father was a wandering Aramean; he went down to Egypt with few people and lived there as an immigrant; there he became a great, strong, and numerous nation.
The Egyptians mistreated us, humiliated us, and imposed harsh servitude on us.
Then we cried out to the Lord, the God of our fathers, and the Lord heard our voice; he saw our misery, our toil, and our oppression,
and the Lord brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, with signs and wonders.
He led us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now, here I bring the firstfruits of the produce of the soil that you have given me, Lord." You shall set them down before the Lord your God and bow down before the Lord your God.
Then you shall rejoice in all the good things the Lord your God has given you, you and your household, you, the Levite, and the immigrant who lives among you.

When you have finished setting aside the whole tithe of your produce, in the third year, the year of the tithe, and have given it to the Levite, the immigrant, the orphan, and the widow, so that they may eat their fill in your towns,

you shall say before the Lord your God: "I have removed from my house what is consecrated and have given it to the Levite, the immigrant, the orphan, and the widow, according to the whole commandment you gave me; I have neither transgressed nor forgotten any of your commandments.

I have eaten nothing of this portion during my mourning, I have removed nothing of it while unclean, I have offered nothing of it for a dead person; I have obeyed the voice of the Lord my God, I have done everything as you commanded me.
Look down from your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the soil you have given us, as you swore to our fathers, this land flowing with milk and honey."
Today the Lord your God commands you to put into practice these statutes and rules; you shall keep them and put them into practice with all your heart and all your soul.
You have made the Lord declare today that he will be your God, committing yourself to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, his commandments, and his rules, and to obey his voice.
And the Lord has made you declare today that you will be for him a treasured people, as he told you, keeping all his commandments,
and that he will raise you, in glory, in renown, and in splendor, above all the nations he has made, and that you will be a people holy to the Lord your God, as he has said.

titres.titre: The altar and the Law on Mount Ebal

versets.t: Moses, with the elders of Israel, gave this command to the people: Keep the whole commandment I lay upon you today.
On the day you cross the Jordan into the land the Lord your God is giving you, you shall set up large stones and coat them with plaster.

You shall write on them all the words of this law, as soon as you have crossed the Jordan to enter the land the Lord your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the Lord, the God of your fathers, promised you.
Once you have crossed the Jordan, you shall set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I command you today, and you shall coat them with plaster.
There you shall build an altar to the Lord your God, an altar of stones on which you shall not use iron:
you shall build the altar of the Lord your God with uncut stones, and you shall offer on it burnt offerings to the Lord your God;
you shall offer peace offerings, you shall eat there and rejoice before the Lord your God.
You shall write on these stones all the words of this law, in clear letters.
Then Moses and the levitical priests spoke to all Israel. They said: Be silent and listen, Israel! Today you have become the people of the Lord your God.
You shall therefore obey the voice of the Lord your God and put into practice his commandments and his statutes, which I lay upon you today.
That same day, Moses gave this command to the people:
When you have crossed the Jordan, these are the ones who shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin;
and these are the ones who shall stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
The Levites shall take up their voice and say in a loud voice to all the men of Israel:
Cursed be the man who makes a carved or cast idol, an abomination to the Lord, the work of a craftsman's hand, and sets it up in secret! And all the people shall answer: Amen!
Cursed be anyone who treats his father or mother with contempt! And all the people shall say: Amen!
Cursed be anyone who moves his neighbor's boundary marker! And all the people shall say: Amen!
Cursed be anyone who leads a blind man astray on the road! And all the people shall say: Amen!
Cursed be anyone who perverts the justice due to the immigrant, the orphan, and the widow! And all the people shall say: Amen!
Cursed be anyone who lies with his father's wife, for he lifts the edge of his father's cloak! And all the people shall say: Amen!
Cursed be anyone who lies with an animal! And all the people shall say: Amen!
Cursed be anyone who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother! And all the people shall say: Amen!
Cursed be anyone who lies with his mother-in-law! And all the people shall say: Amen!
Cursed be anyone who strikes down his neighbor in secret! And all the people shall say: Amen!
