Cursed be anyone who lets himself be paid to strike down a life and shed innocent blood! And all the people shall say: Amen!
Cursed be anyone who does not uphold the words of this law by putting them into practice! And all the people shall say: Amen!

If you truly obey the voice of the Lord your God, being careful to put into practice all his commandments that I lay upon you today, the Lord your God will raise you above all the nations of the earth.
Here are all the blessings that will come upon you and overtake you, if you obey the voice of the Lord your God.
You will be blessed in the city, and you will be blessed in the fields.
Blessed will be the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your soil, and the fruit of your livestock, the calving of your cattle and the young of your flock.
Blessed will be your basket and your kneading trough.
You will be blessed when you come in, and you will be blessed when you go out.
The Lord will rout before you the enemies who rise against you: coming out to attack you by one road, they will flee before you by seven.
The Lord will command the blessing to be with you in your barns and in all the work of your hand; he will bless you in the land the Lord your God is giving you.
The Lord will make you his holy people, as he swore to you, if you keep the commandments of the Lord your God and walk in his ways;
all the peoples of the earth will see that the name of the Lord is invoked over you, and they will fear you.
The Lord will fill you with good things, multiplying the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock, and the fruit of your soil, in the land he swore to your fathers to give you.

The Lord will open for you his good treasury, the heavens, to give in its time the rain to your land and to bless all the work of your hand; you will lend to many nations, and you yourself will not borrow.

The Lord will set you at the head and not at the tail; you will be only at the top, never at the bottom, if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God that I lay upon you today, being careful to put them into practice,
without turning aside, either to the right or to the left, from any of the words I lay upon you today, to follow other gods and serve them.

But if you do not obey the voice of the Lord your God, if you are not careful to put into practice all his commandments and all his statutes that I lay upon you today, here are all the curses that will come upon you and overtake you.
You will be cursed in the city, and you will be cursed in the fields.
Cursed will be your basket and your kneading trough.
Cursed will be the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your soil, the calving of your cattle and the young of your flock.
You will be cursed when you come in, and you will be cursed when you go out.

The Lord will send against you the curse, confusion, and rebuke in everything your hand undertakes, until you are destroyed and quickly perish, because of the wickedness of your deeds, by which you will have forsaken me.
The Lord will make the plague cling to you, until it has made you vanish from the soil you are about to enter to possess.
The Lord will strike you with wasting disease, fever, inflammation, scorching heat, drought, blight, and mildew, which will pursue you until you perish.
The sky above your head will be bronze, and the earth beneath your feet will be iron.
The Lord will give your land dust and sand for rain; they will come down from heaven upon you until you are destroyed.
The Lord will make you be beaten before your enemies: setting out to meet them by one road, you will flee before them by seven, and you will become a thing of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your corpse will be food for all the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth, with no one to frighten them away.
The Lord will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, scabs, and itch, from which you cannot be healed.
The Lord will strike you with madness, blindness, and confusion of mind;
at high noon you will grope like a blind man in the dark, and you will not succeed in your undertakings; day after day you will be nothing but oppressed and plundered, with no one to rescue you.
You will become engaged to a woman, and another will take her; you will build a house, and you will not live in it; you will plant a vineyard, and you will not enjoy it.

Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, and you will not eat of it; your donkey will be snatched from before you, and it will not be returned to you; your flock will be handed over to your enemies, with no one to rescue you.
Your sons and daughters will be handed over to another people; your eyes will see it and grow weary looking for them all day long, and your hand will be powerless.
The fruit of your soil and all your labor will be eaten by a people you do not know; you will be nothing but oppressed and crushed, day after day,
and you will go mad at what your eyes see.
The Lord will strike you with malignant boils on the knees and thighs, from which you cannot be healed, from the sole of your feet to the top of your head.
The Lord will carry you off, you and the king you set over yourself, to a nation you have not known, neither you nor your fathers, and there you will serve other gods, of wood and stone.
You will become an object of horror, a proverb, and a byword among all the peoples where the Lord will lead you.
You will carry much seed to the field, and you will harvest little, for the locust will devour it.
You will plant vineyards and cultivate them, but you will drink no wine and gather nothing, for the worm will eat them.
You will have olive trees throughout your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with oil, for your olives will fall.
You will father sons and daughters, but they will not be yours, for they will go into captivity.
The insect will take possession of all your trees and the fruit of your soil.
The immigrant who lives among you will rise higher and higher above you, while you sink lower and lower:
it is he who will lend to you, and not you who will lend to him; he will be at the head, and you at the tail.

All these curses will come upon you, pursue you, and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord your God, keeping the commandments and statutes he laid upon you.
They will be a sign and a wonder upon you and your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a glad heart, in the midst of abundance,
you will serve, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and lack of everything, the enemies the Lord will send against you; he will put a yoke of iron on your neck, until you are destroyed.
The Lord will raise against you, from afar, from the ends of the earth, a nation swooping like the eagle, a nation whose language you will not understand,
a nation of hard countenance, with no regard for the old man nor pity for the child.

It will devour the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your soil, until you are destroyed; it will leave you neither grain, nor new wine, nor oil, nor the calving of your cattle, nor the young of your flock, until you perish.

It will besiege you in all your towns, until, throughout your land, your high and strong walls in which you trusted come down; it will besiege you in all your towns, in all the land the Lord your God has given you.
In the anguish and distress to which your enemy reduces you, you will eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and daughters whom the Lord your God has given you.
The most refined and delicate man among you will look with a hard eye on his brother, the wife who rests on his heart, and the children who remain to him,
refusing to any of them the flesh of his children that he devours, because he will have nothing left, in the anguish and distress to which your enemy reduces you in all your towns.

The most refined and delicate woman among you, so refined and delicate that she would not have tried to set the sole of her foot on the ground, will look with a hard eye on the husband who rested on her heart, and on her son and daughter,

to the point of hiding from them the afterbirth that comes out from between her legs and the children she bears, for, in the lack of everything, she will eat them in secret, in the anguish and distress to which your enemy reduces you in your towns.
If you are not careful to put into practice all the words of this law, written in this book, fearing this glorious and awesome name, the Lord your God,
the Lord will make extraordinary your plagues and the plagues of your descendants, plagues great and lasting, illnesses severe and persistent.
He will bring back upon you all the diseases of Egypt before which you trembled, and they will cling to you.
What is more, the Lord will bring upon you every disease and every plague not written in the book of this law, until you are destroyed.
You will be left only few in number, you who were as numerous as the stars of the sky, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord your God.

Just as the Lord took pleasure in doing you good and multiplying you, so the Lord will take pleasure in making you perish and destroying you, and you will be torn from the soil you are about to enter to possess.
The Lord will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other, and there you will serve other gods that neither you nor your fathers have known, of wood and stone.
Among these nations you will find no tranquility, no rest for the sole of your feet; there the Lord will give you a trembling heart, failing eyes, and a languishing soul.
Your life will hang as if in suspense before you; you will tremble night and day and will not believe in your life.
In the morning you will say: "Ah, if only it were evening!" and in the evening: "Ah, if only it were morning!" because of the dread that will seize your heart and of what your eyes will see.

And the Lord will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by the way of which I had told you: "You shall not see it again." There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies, as male and female slaves, with no one willing to buy you.
These are the words of the covenant the Lord commanded Moses to make with the sons of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant he had made with them at Horeb.

titres.titre: The renewal of the covenant in Moab

versets.t: Moses summoned all Israel. He said: You have seen all that the Lord did before your eyes, in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, to all his servants, and to all his land,
the great trials your eyes have seen, those signs and great wonders.
But to this day the Lord has not given you a heart to understand, eyes to see, ears to hear.
I led you forty years in the wilderness: your clothes did not wear out on you, and your sandal did not wear out on your foot;
you ate no bread, you drank neither wine nor fermented drink, so that you might know that I am the Lord your God.
You came to this place; Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us in battle, and we defeated them.
We took their land and gave it as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Keep therefore the words of this covenant and put them into practice, so that you may succeed in all you do.
Today you all stand before the Lord your God, your leaders, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, all the men of Israel,
your children, your wives, and the immigrant who is in the midst of your camp, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water,
to enter into the covenant of the Lord your God and into the oath that the Lord your God is making with you today,
so as to establish you today as his people and to be himself your God, as he told you and swore to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
It is not with you alone that I make this covenant and this oath,
but with whoever stands here today with us before the Lord our God, and with whoever is not here with us this day.
You know well how we lived in the land of Egypt and how we passed through the nations you passed through;
you saw their horrors and their idols, of wood and stone, of silver and gold, that are among them.

Let there not be among you, then, any man, woman, clan, or tribe whose heart turns away today from the Lord our God, to go and serve the gods of these nations; let there not be among you any root producing poison and wormwood.

Let no one, on hearing the words of this oath, flatter himself in his heart, saying: "I will have peace, even if I walk in the stubbornness of my heart!": this is to sweep away the watered along with the parched.

The Lord will not consent to forgive him; his anger and his jealousy will then blaze against this man, all the curses written in this book will weigh upon him, and the Lord will blot out his name from under heaven.
The Lord will set him apart, for his ruin, from all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this book of the law.
The generation to come, your children who rise after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land, will see the plagues of this land and the diseases with which the Lord has struck it;

all this soil will be sulfur and salt, a burning waste; it will be neither sown nor fruitful, no grass will grow on it, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the Lord overthrew in his anger and his wrath.
Then all the nations will say: "Why has the Lord treated this land like this? What is the cause of this great burning anger?"
And the answer will be: "It is because they forsook the covenant of the Lord, the God of their fathers, which he had made with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt;
they went and served other gods and bowed down before them, gods they did not know and that he had not given them as a portion.
The anger of the Lord blazed against this land, and he brought upon it all the curses written in this book.
The Lord tore them from their soil with anger, with wrath, with great indignation, and cast them into another land, as is seen today."
The hidden things belong to the Lord our God; the revealed things are for us and for our children forever, so that we may put into practice all the words of this law.
When all these things have come upon you, the blessing and the curse I have set before you, and you take them again to heart, among all the nations where the Lord your God has driven you,
if you return to the Lord your God and obey his voice, you and your children, with all your heart and all your soul, according to all that I lay upon you today,
then the Lord your God will bring back your captives and have compassion on you; he will gather you again from among all the peoples where the Lord your God has scattered you.
Even if your exiles were at the end of the sky, from there the Lord your God will gather you, from there he will go to take you.
The Lord your God will bring you back to the land your fathers possessed, and you will possess it; he will do you good and make you more numerous than your fathers.
The Lord your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your descendants, so that you may love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul, and so live.
The Lord your God will bring all these curses down upon your enemies, upon those who have hated and persecuted you.
And you, once again, will obey the voice of the Lord and put into practice all his commandments that I lay upon you today.

The Lord your God will fill you with good things in all the work of your hand, in the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock, and the fruit of your soil; for the Lord will again rejoice over you, doing you good, as he rejoiced over your fathers,
if you obey the voice of the Lord your God, keeping his commandments and his statutes written in this book of the law, if you return to the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul.
This commandment I lay upon you today is not too difficult for you, nor beyond your reach.
It is not in heaven, that you should say: "Who will go up to heaven for us to get it and make us hear it, so that we may put it into practice?"
It is not beyond the sea, that you should say: "Who will cross the sea for us to get it and make us hear it, so that we may put it into practice?"
For the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, that you may put it into practice.
See: today I set before you life and good, death and evil.

What I command you today is to love the Lord your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his rules, so that you may live and multiply, and that the Lord your God may bless you in the land you are about to enter to possess.
But if your heart turns away, if you do not obey and let yourself be drawn to bow down before other gods and serve them,
I declare to you today that you will surely perish: you will not prolong your days on the land you are about to enter to possess, crossing the Jordan.
I call heaven and earth today as witnesses against you: I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. Choose life, then, so that you may live, you and your descendants,

by loving the Lord your God, obeying his voice, and holding fast to him; for he is your life and the length of your days, that you may dwell on the land the Lord swore to give to your fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

titres.titre: The song, a witness against Israel
The book of the Law beside the ark

versets.t: Moses spoke these further words to all Israel.
He said to them: "I am now a hundred and twenty years old, I can no longer come and go, and the Lord has told me: You shall not cross this Jordan.

It is the Lord your God who will cross over before you; it is he who will destroy these nations before you, and you will dispossess them. It is Joshua who will cross over before you, as the Lord has said.
The Lord will treat them as he treated Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and their land, which he destroyed.
The Lord will deliver them to you, and you will treat them according to the whole commandment I have given you.
Be strong and courageous, do not fear, do not tremble before them, for it is the Lord your God who marches with you: he will not forsake you or abandon you."

Then Moses called Joshua and said to him, before all Israel: "Be strong and courageous, for it is you who will enter with this people the land the Lord swore to their fathers to give them, and it is you who will give it to them as an inheritance.
It is the Lord who marches before you; it is he who will be with you, he will not forsake you or abandon you: do not fear, do not be dismayed."
Moses wrote this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and to all the elders of Israel.
Moses gave them this command: "Every seven years, at the time of the year of remission, at the feast of Booths,
when all Israel comes to present itself before the Lord your God, at the place he will choose, you shall read this law before all Israel, in their hearing.

Assemble the people, the men, the women, the children, and the immigrant who is in your towns, so that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord your God, and be careful to put into practice all the words of this law;
and their children, who do not know it, will hear it and learn to fear the Lord your God, all the days you live on the land where you are going, crossing the Jordan, to possess it."

The Lord said to Moses: "See, the day of your death is approaching. Call Joshua, and present yourselves at the tent of meeting, so that I may give him my orders." Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves at the tent of meeting,
and the Lord appeared at the tent, in a pillar of cloud; the pillar of cloud stood at the entrance of the tent.

The Lord said to Moses: "See, you are about to lie down with your fathers; and this people will rise and prostitute itself to the foreign gods of the land it is entering. It will forsake me and break the covenant I have made with it.

On that day my anger will blaze against it; I will abandon them and hide my face from them: it will be devoured, a multitude of evils and troubles will fall upon it, and on that day it will say: Is it not because my God is no longer in my midst that these evils have fallen upon me?
And I, on that day, will hide my face, because of all the evil it has done in turning to other gods.
Now, write down this song. Teach it to the sons of Israel, put it in their mouths, so that this song may serve me as a witness against the sons of Israel.

For I will bring it into the land flowing with milk and honey that I promised on oath to its fathers; it will eat, be filled, grow fat, then turn to other gods and serve them, it will despise me and break my covenant.

And when a multitude of evils and troubles have fallen upon it, this song will testify as a witness before it, for it will not be forgotten from the mouth of its descendants; for I know the intentions it is already forming today, even before I have brought it into the land I promised it on oath."
That day, Moses wrote this song and taught it to the sons of Israel.
The Lord gave his orders to Joshua son of Nun: "Be strong and courageous, for it is you who will bring the sons of Israel into the land I promised them on oath, and I will be with you."
When Moses had finished writing in a book the words of this law, to the very end,
he gave this command to the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord:
"Take this book of the law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God; it will be there as a witness against you.
For I know your rebellious spirit and the stiffness of your neck. See, today, while I am still alive among you, you have rebelled against the Lord: how much more after my death!
Gather to me all the elders of your tribes and your officers; I will speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth as witnesses against them.

For I know that after my death you will surely become corrupt, that you will turn from the way I have commanded you, and that disaster will overtake you in the days to come, because you will have done what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, provoking him by the work of your hands."
Then Moses spoke, in the hearing of the whole assembly of Israel, the words of this song, to the very end:
Heavens, give ear, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth!
Let my teaching stream down like rain, let my word fall like the dew, like showers on the greenery, like downpours on the grass!
For I will proclaim the name of the Lord: give glory to our God!
He is the Rock: his work is perfect, all his ways are just; he is a faithful God, without injustice; he is righteous and upright.
Against him they have acted corruptly, those who are no longer his children, but their blemish: a false and crooked generation.
Is this how you repay the Lord, foolish and senseless people? Is he not your father, your creator, the one who made you and established you?
Remember the days of old, consider the years, age after age; ask your father, and he will tell you, your elders, and they will inform you.
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he divided the sons of men, he fixed the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel;
for the Lord's portion is his people, Jacob is the share of his inheritance.
He found him in a desert land, in the howling solitude of the wild wastes; he surrounded him, he watched over him, he guarded him like the apple of his eye.
Like the eagle that stirs up its nest and hovers over its young, he spread his wings, he took him, he carried him on his pinions.
The Lord alone led him; no foreign god was with him.
He made him ride the heights of the land, and Israel ate the produce of the fields; he made him suck honey from the rock, oil from the hardest stone,
the cream of cows and the milk of sheep, with the fat of lambs, of rams of Bashan and of goats, with the finest of the wheat; and you drank the blood of the grape, the foaming wine.
Jeshurun grew fat and kicked, you grew fat, thick, gorged! He forsook the God who made him and scorned the Rock of his salvation.
They stirred his jealousy with foreign gods, they provoked him with abominations;
they sacrificed to demons that are not God, to gods they did not know, new gods, lately come, before whom your fathers had not trembled.
The Rock who begot you, you neglected; you forgot the God who brought you into the world.
The Lord saw it and was indignant, provoked by his sons and daughters.
He said: "I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end will be, for they are a crooked generation, children without faithfulness.
They stirred my jealousy with what is not God, they provoked me with their worthless idols; I too will stir their jealousy with what is not a people, I will provoke them with a senseless nation.
For a fire has been kindled in my anger, it burns to the depths of the realm of the dead; it devours the earth and its produce, it sets ablaze the foundations of the mountains.
I will heap disasters upon them, I will spend my arrows against them.
Wasted by hunger, devoured by fever and by bitter plague, I will loose against them the fangs of beasts, with the venom of reptiles that crawl in the dust.
Outside, the sword will make orphans, within, dread will reign; they will perish together, the young man and the young woman, the nursing infant and the old man.
I would have said: I will sweep them away, I will blot out their memory among men,
were it not that I dreaded the enemy's provocation; that their adversaries might mistake it and say: Our hand has triumphed, it is not the Lord who has done all this!"
For it is a nation that has lost its sense, and there is no understanding in them.
If they were wise, they would understand, they would discern the end that awaits them.
How could a single man pursue a thousand, how could two put ten thousand to flight, if their Rock had not sold them, if the Lord had not handed them over?
For their rock is not like our Rock: our very enemies are judges of this.
Their vine comes from the stock of Sodom and from the fields of Gomorrah; their grapes are poisoned grapes, and their clusters are bitter;
their wine is the venom of serpents, the deadly poison of vipers.
Is this not stored up with me, sealed in my treasuries?
Vengeance is mine, and recompense, for the time when their foot slips! For the day of their disaster is near, and their doom rushes upon them.
For the Lord will do justice for his people, he will relent in favor of his servants, when he sees that their strength is spent and that neither slave nor free man remains.
He will say: "Where are their gods, the rock in which they sought refuge,
those gods who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their libations? Let them rise and help you, let them be your shelter!
See now: it is I, I who am, and there is no other god but me. It is I who put to death and give life; I have wounded, and it is I who heal, and none delivers from my hand.
Yes, I lift my hand to heaven, and I say: I live forever!
When I sharpen the lightning of my sword and my hand seizes judgment, I will take vengeance on my adversaries and repay those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will feed on flesh, on the blood of the slain and the captives, on the long-haired heads of the enemy."
Nations, shout for joy with his people! For the Lord avenges the blood of his servants, he takes vengeance on his adversaries and makes atonement for his land, for his people.
Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Joshua son of Nun.
When Moses had finished addressing all these words to all Israel,
he said to them: "Take to heart all the words I proclaim before you today: you shall command them to your children, so that they may be careful to put into practice all the words of this law.
For it is not an empty word for you: it is your life, and by it you will prolong your days on the land you are about to take possession of by crossing the Jordan."
That same day, the Lord spoke to Moses. He said:
"Go up this mountain of the Abarim, Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab, facing Jericho, and behold the land of Canaan that I am giving as a possession to the sons of Israel.
On the mountain you go up, you will die and be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people,
because you were unfaithful to me among the sons of Israel, at the waters of Meribah of Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin, and because you did not manifest my holiness among the sons of Israel.
It is from afar that you will see the land, but you will not enter it, this land that I am giving to the sons of Israel."

titres.titre: The blessing of Moses on the tribes

versets.t: This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the sons of Israel before he died.
He said: The Lord came from Sinai, for them he rose from Seir, he shone forth from Mount Paran; he came from among the holy myriads, and from his right hand flashed for them a fire of law.
Yes, he loves the peoples; all the holy ones are in your hand. They sit at your feet, and each receives your words.
Moses prescribed for us a law, the inheritance of the assembly of Jacob.
He was king in Jeshurun, when the leaders of the people gathered, with the tribes of Israel.
May Reuben live and not die, though his men be few!
This is for Judah; he said: Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him back to his people; may his hands defend his cause, be his help against his enemies!
For Levi he said: To you the Urim and the Thummim, to the man faithful to you, whom you tested at Massah, with whom you contended at the waters of Meribah;
he who said of his father and mother: "I have not seen them," who did not acknowledge his brothers or wish to know his sons. Yes, they kept your word and observed your covenant;
they teach your rules to Jacob and your law to Israel; they present incense to your nostrils and the burnt offering on your altar.
Bless his strength, Lord, accept the work of his hands; break the loins of his adversaries and of those who hate him, that they may rise no more!
For Benjamin he said: Beloved of the Lord, he rests in safety beside him; the Lord protects him all the days, and he dwells between his shoulders.
For Joseph he said: May the Lord bless his land, with the best gift of heaven, the dew, and of the deep lying below,
with the best of the fruits ripened by the sun, with the best of what the moons bring forth,
with the firstfruits of the ancient mountains, with the best of the everlasting hills,
with the best of the earth and its abundance. May the favor of the one who dwells in the bush come upon the head of Joseph, upon the brow of the prince among his brothers!

To his firstborn bull, the glory! His horns are the horns of the wild ox: with them he will strike the peoples, all together, to the ends of the earth. Such are the myriads of Ephraim, such are the thousands of Manasseh.
For Zebulun he said: Rejoice, Zebulun, in your expeditions, and you, Issachar, in your tents!
They call the peoples to the mountain, there they offer sacrifices of righteousness; for they draw on the abundance of the seas and the treasures hidden in the sand.
For Gad he said: Blessed be the one who gives Gad room! He lies down like a lioness, he tears the arm and even the head.

He reserved for himself the firstfruits of the land, for there was the portion set aside for the leader; he came at the head of the people, he carried out the righteousness of the Lord and his judgments with Israel.
For Dan he said: Dan is a young lion that leaps from Bashan.
For Naphtali he said: Naphtali, filled with favors and full of the blessing of the Lord, take possession of the sea and the south!
For Asher he said: Blessed among the sons, Asher! May he be the favorite of his brothers and dip his foot in oil!
May your bolts be of iron and bronze, and may your vigor last as long as your days!
There is none like the God of Jeshurun, who rides the heavens to help you, and the clouds in his majesty.
The God of the beginnings is a refuge, and beneath stretch his eternal arms; he drove the enemy before you and said: "Destroy!"
Israel dwells in safety, the spring of Jacob flows apart, in a land of grain and new wine, and its heaven distills the dew.
Blessed are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the Lord? He is the shield of your help and the sword of your glory; your enemies will fawn on you, and you will tread on their heights.
From the plains of Moab, Moses went up Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, facing Jericho, and the Lord showed him the whole land: Gilead as far as Dan,
all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the western sea,
the Negev and the plain, the valley of Jericho, the city of palms, as far as Zoar.

The Lord said to him: "This is the land I promised on oath to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying: I will give it to your descendants. I have let you see it with your eyes, but you shall not enter it."
Moses, the servant of the Lord, died there, in the land of Moab, at the Lord's command.
He buried him in the valley, in the land of Moab, facing Beth-peor; and no one has known his tomb to this day.
Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died; his sight had not dimmed and his vigor had not left him.
The sons of Israel wept for Moses thirty days, in the plains of Moab; then the days of weeping ended, the mourning for Moses.
Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him; the sons of Israel obeyed him and did what the Lord had commanded Moses.
Never again has there risen in Israel a prophet like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,
by all the signs and wonders the Lord sent him to perform in the land of Egypt, against Pharaoh, all his servants, and all his land,
and by all the mighty hand and the great terrors that Moses performed in the sight of all Israel.
After the death of Moses, the servant of the Lord, the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, the assistant of Moses. He said:
"Moses my servant is dead. Now then, rise up, cross this Jordan, you and all this people, into the land that I am giving to the sons of Israel.
Every place where the sole of your foot treads I give to you, as I promised Moses.
From the wilderness and the Lebanon as far as the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and as far as the Great Sea to the west, such will be your territory.
No one will be able to stand against you all the days of your life; as I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you or forsake you.
Be strong and courageous, for it is you who will give this people possession of the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.

Only be strong and very courageous, taking care to act according to all the law that Moses my servant commanded you; do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may succeed wherever you go.

Do not let this book of the law depart from your mouth; meditate on it day and night, taking care to act according to everything written in it; then you will make your way prosper, then you will succeed.
Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous! Do not tremble, do not be dismayed, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go."
Joshua gave this command to the officers of the people:

"Go through the camp and give this command to the people: Prepare your provisions, for in three days you will cross this Jordan to go and take possession of the land that the Lord your God is giving you as your own."
Then Joshua said to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh:
"Remember the command that Moses the servant of the Lord gave you: The Lord your God has given you rest and has given you this land.

Your wives, your children, and your livestock will remain in the land that Moses gave you beyond the Jordan; but you, all the valiant men, will cross over armed at the head of your brothers, and you will help them,

until the Lord has given rest to your brothers as he has to you, and they too take possession of the land that the Lord your God is giving them. Then you may return to the land of your possession and take possession of it, the land that Moses the servant of the Lord gave you beyond the Jordan, to the east."
They answered Joshua: "Everything you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.
Just as we obeyed Moses in everything, so we will obey you; only may the Lord your God be with you, as he was with Moses!
Anyone who rebels against your orders and does not obey everything you command him will be put to death. Only be strong and courageous!"

titres.titre: Rahab and the Spies at Jericho

versets.t: From Shittim, Joshua son of Nun secretly sent out two spies, saying to them: "Go, survey the land, and Jericho." They set out, entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab, and lay down there.
It was reported to the king of Jericho: "Here, some men, sons of Israel, have come here tonight to explore the land."
The king of Jericho sent word to Rahab: "Bring out the men who came to you, who entered your house, for they have come to explore the whole land."
But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said: "It is true, these men came to me, but I did not know where they were from;
and when the city gate was about to be shut, at nightfall, they left. I do not know where they went. Quick, go after them, and you will catch up with them."
Now she had brought them up to the roof and hidden them under stalks of flax that she had laid out there.
The king's men pursued them along the road to the Jordan, toward the fords; and as soon as the pursuers had gone out, the gate was shut.
Before the spies lay down, Rahab came up to them on the roof.
She said to them: "I know that the Lord has given you this land: the terror of your name has fallen upon us, and all the inhabitants of the land are faint with fear before you.

For we have heard how the Lord dried up the waters of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you devoted to destruction.
When we heard it, our hearts melted, and everyone's courage failed before you, for the Lord your God is God, in heaven above and on the earth below.
Now then, swear to me by the Lord, since I have dealt kindly with you, that you too will deal kindly with my father's house; give me a sure sign
that you will spare the lives of my father, my mother, my brothers, my sisters, and all who belong to them, and that you will save us from death."
The men answered her: "Our lives for yours, if you do not reveal this business of ours! And when the Lord gives us the land, we will deal kindly and faithfully with you."
Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was built against the city wall: she lived on the rampart itself.
She said to them: "Go to the hills, so that the pursuers do not find you; hide there three days, until they return, and then go on your way."
The men said to her: "This is how we will keep the oath you have made us swear:

when we enter the land, you will tie this cord of scarlet thread in the window through which you are letting us down, and you will gather to yourself, in your house, your father, your mother, your brothers, and all your father's household.

If anyone passes through the door of your house to go outside, his blood will be on his own head, and we will be innocent; but if a hand is laid on any of those who are with you in the house, his blood will be on our head.
And if you reveal this business of ours, we will be free of the oath you have made us swear."
She answered: "Let it be as you say!" Then she sent them away, and they departed; and she tied the scarlet cord in the window.
They went off, reached the hills, and stayed there three days, until the pursuers returned; the pursuers had searched for them all along the road but had not found them.
The two men came back down from the hills, crossed the Jordan, and came to Joshua son of Nun, to whom they told everything that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua: "Yes, the Lord has handed over the whole land into our hands, and already all its inhabitants are faint with fear before us."
Joshua rose early in the morning; he set out from Shittim, he and all the sons of Israel, and they came to the Jordan, where they halted before crossing it.
At the end of three days, the officers went through the camp
and gave this command to the people: "When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, carried by the levitical priests, you will leave your camp and follow it,
but there will be a distance of about a thousand metres between you and it: do not come near it, so that you may know the way to go, for you have never traveled this way before."
Joshua said to the people: "Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the Lord will perform wonders among you."
Then Joshua said to the priests: "Take up the ark of the covenant and pass on ahead of the people." They took up the ark of the covenant and went ahead of the people.
The Lord said to Joshua: "Today I will begin to exalt you in the eyes of all Israel, so that they may know that I will be with you as I was with Moses.
As for you, give this command to the priests who carry the ark of the covenant: When you reach the edge of the waters of the Jordan, you will stand still in the Jordan."
Joshua said to the sons of Israel: "Come near and listen to the words of the Lord your God."

Joshua said: "By this you will know that the living God is among you and that he will surely drive out before you the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites.
Behold, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is about to pass ahead of you into the Jordan.
Now then, choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man from each tribe.

And as soon as the priests who carry the ark of the Lord, the Lord of all the earth, set the soles of their feet in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan will be cut off, the waters flowing down from upstream, and they will stand still in a single heap."
When the people left their tents to cross the Jordan, the priests carrying the ark of the covenant were marching at the head of the people.
As soon as those carrying the ark reached the Jordan and the feet of the priests dipped into the edge of the water, though the Jordan overflows all its banks throughout the harvest season,

the waters flowing down from upstream stood still and rose up in a single heap, very far off, near Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan; and those flowing down toward the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, were completely cut off. The people crossed over opposite Jericho.

The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel crossed on dry ground, until the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan.
When the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, the Lord said to Joshua:
"Choose twelve men from among the people, one man from each tribe,

and give them this command: From here, from the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the priests stood firm, take twelve stones; carry them over with you and set them down at the place where you will camp tonight."
Joshua called the twelve men he had appointed from among the sons of Israel, one man from each tribe,

and he said to them: "Pass on ahead of the ark of the Lord your God into the middle of the Jordan, and let each of you lift a stone onto his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Israel,
so that this may be a sign among you. When your children ask you one day: What do these stones mean to you?

you will say to them: The waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of the Lord; when it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. These stones will be a memorial forever for the sons of Israel."

The sons of Israel did as Joshua had commanded: they took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Israel, as the Lord had told Joshua; they carried them over to the camping place and set them down there.
Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, at the place where the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant had stood; they are there to this day.

The priests carrying the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan until everything was completed that the Lord had commanded Joshua to tell the people, according to all that Moses had commanded Joshua; and the people hurried across.
When all the people had finished crossing, the ark of the Lord crossed over, with the priests, at the head of the people.
The sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed at the head of the sons of Israel, as Moses had told them;
about forty thousand men, equipped for war, crossed over before the Lord to fight, toward the plains of Jericho.
That day the Lord exalted Joshua in the eyes of all Israel, and they revered him, as they had revered Moses, all the days of his life.
The Lord spoke to Joshua. He said:
"Command the priests who carry the ark of the Testimony to come up out of the Jordan."
So Joshua gave this command to the priests: "Come up out of the Jordan."

When the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord came up out of the middle of the Jordan and the soles of their feet touched dry ground, the waters of the river returned to their place and overflowed all its banks as before.
The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and they camped at Gilgal, on the eastern border of Jericho.
Those twelve stones they had taken from the Jordan, Joshua set up at Gilgal,
and he said to the sons of Israel: "When your children ask their fathers one day: What are these stones?
you will teach your children: Israel crossed this Jordan on dry ground,
for the Lord your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed, as the Lord your God had done at the Red Sea, which he dried up before us until we had crossed,
so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the hand of the Lord is mighty, and so that you may always revere the Lord your God."

titres.titre: The Passover and the End of the Manna
The Commander of the Lord's Army

versets.t: When all the kings of the Amorites west of the Jordan and all the kings of the Canaanites near the sea heard that the Lord had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the sons of Israel until they had crossed, their hearts melted and their courage failed before the sons of Israel.
At that time the Lord said to Joshua: "Make yourself flint knives and circumcise the sons of Israel again, a second time."
So Joshua made himself flint knives and circumcised the sons of Israel at the Hill of the Foreskins.
This is why Joshua circumcised them: all the people who came out of Egypt, the males, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness along the way, after their departure from Egypt.
All the people who came out had been circumcised; but all the people born in the wilderness along the way, after the departure from Egypt, had not been.

For the sons of Israel had walked forty years in the wilderness, until the whole nation had passed away, the men of war who came out of Egypt: they had not listened to the voice of the Lord, and the Lord had sworn to them that he would not let them see the land that he had promised on oath to their fathers to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
In their place he raised up their sons, and it was these whom Joshua circumcised, for they were uncircumcised: they had not been circumcised along the way.
When the whole nation had finished being circumcised, they stayed where they were, in the camp, until they were healed.
The Lord said to Joshua: "Today I have rolled away from you the disgrace of Egypt." And that place was given the name Gilgal, which it keeps to this day.
The sons of Israel camped at Gilgal, and they celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, on the plains of Jericho.
On the day after the Passover, that very day, they ate the produce of the land, unleavened bread and roasted grain.
And the manna ceased the next day, when they ate the produce of the land; there was no more manna for the sons of Israel, and that year they ate the harvest of the land of Canaan.
While Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw: there was a man standing before him, his drawn sword in his hand. Joshua went up to him and said: "Are you one of us or one of our enemies?"
He answered: "No, I am the commander of the Lord's army; now I have come." Joshua fell facedown to the ground, bowed low, and said to him: "What does my lord say to his servant?"
The commander of the Lord's army said to Joshua: "Take off your sandals from your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so.
Jericho was shut up tight and barred before the sons of Israel; no one went out, no one came in.
The Lord said to Joshua: "See, I have handed Jericho over into your hands, its king and its valiant warriors.
March around the city, all you men of war: encircle it once. You will do this for six days.
Seven priests will carry seven ram's-horn trumpets ahead of the ark; and on the seventh day you will march around the city seven times, and the priests will blow the trumpets.

When they sound a long blast on the ram's horn and you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people will raise a great shout, the wall of the city will collapse where it stands, and the people will charge up, each one straight ahead."
Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them: "Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven ram's-horn trumpets ahead of the ark of the Lord."
Then he said to the people: "Advance, march around the city, and let the armed vanguard pass on ahead of the ark of the Lord."

When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven ram's-horn trumpets before the Lord went forward blowing the trumpets, and the ark of the covenant of the Lord followed them.
The armed vanguard marched ahead of the priests who were blowing the trumpets, and the rear guard followed the ark; as they marched, the trumpets kept sounding.

Joshua had given this command to the people: "You will not shout, you will not let your voice be heard, no word will come out of your mouth, until the day I tell you: Shout! Then you will raise the shout."
The ark of the Lord went around the city once, then they returned to the camp and spent the night there.
Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the Lord.

The seven priests carrying the seven ram's-horn trumpets ahead of the ark of the Lord went forward blowing the trumpets; the armed vanguard marched ahead of them, and the rear guard followed the ark of the Lord; as they marched, the trumpets kept sounding.
On the second day they marched around the city once, then returned to the camp. They did the same for six days.
On the seventh day they rose at daybreak and marched around the city seven times, in the same way; only on that day did they march around it seven times.
The seventh time, as the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said to the people: "Raise the shout, for the Lord has given you the city!

The city will be devoted to destruction for the Lord, it and everything in it; only Rahab the prostitute will be spared, she and all who are with her in her house, because she hid the messengers we had sent.

But you, keep yourselves from what is devoted to destruction: do not, after devoting it to destruction, take any of it, for you would make the camp of Israel liable to destruction and bring disaster upon it.
All the silver and gold, all the objects of bronze and iron, will be consecrated to the Lord: they will go into the treasury of the Lord."

The people raised the shout, and the trumpets sounded. As soon as the people heard the sound of the trumpet, they raised a great shout, and the wall collapsed where it stood; the people charged up into the city, each one straight ahead, and they captured it.
They devoted to destruction, by the edge of the sword, everything in the city, men and women, young and old, down to the oxen, the sheep, and the donkeys.
Joshua said to the two men who had explored the land: "Go into the house of the prostitute and bring out that woman and all who belong to her, as you swore to her."

The young men, the spies, went in and brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers, and all who belonged to her; they brought out her whole clan and settled them outside the camp of Israel.
Then they burned the city and everything in it, except the silver, the gold, and the objects of bronze and iron, which they placed in the treasury of the house of the Lord.

But Rahab the prostitute, her father's household, and all who belonged to her, Joshua spared; she has lived in the midst of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers Joshua had sent to explore Jericho.

At that time Joshua pronounced this oath: "Cursed before the Lord be the man who rises up to rebuild this city, Jericho! At the cost of his firstborn he will lay its foundations, at the cost of his youngest he will set up its gates."
The Lord was with Joshua, and his fame spread throughout the whole land.

But the sons of Israel committed an act of unfaithfulness concerning what was devoted to destruction: Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was devoted to destruction, and the anger of the Lord blazed against the sons of Israel.
From Jericho, Joshua sent men to Ai, which is near Beth-aven, east of Bethel, saying to them: "Go up and explore the land." The men went up and explored Ai.
When they returned, they said to Joshua: "Do not let all the people go up! Let two or three thousand men go up to attack Ai; do not weary all the people with it, for its inhabitants are few."
About three thousand men of the people went up there, but they fled before the men of Ai.
The men of Ai killed about thirty-six of them; they pursued them from the gate as far as Shebarim and struck them down on the slope. Then the hearts of the people melted and became like water.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown to the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they threw dust on their heads.
Joshua said: "Ah, Lord God, why did you bring this people across the Jordan, only to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay beyond the Jordan!
Please, Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned its back before its enemies?
The Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it; they will surround us and wipe out our name from the earth. And what will you do then for your great name?"
The Lord said to Joshua: "Stand up! Why are you lying there facedown?

Israel has sinned: they have transgressed my covenant that I commanded them, they have taken some of what was devoted to destruction, they have stolen, they have lied, and they have hidden it among their own belongings!

This is why the sons of Israel cannot stand before their enemies: they turn their backs to them, for they themselves have become devoted to destruction. I will no longer be with you unless you remove from among you what is devoted to destruction.

Get up, consecrate the people and say to them: Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, for thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: There is something devoted to destruction in your midst, Israel; you will not be able to stand before your enemies until you have removed what is devoted to destruction from among you.

In the morning you will come forward tribe by tribe; the tribe that the Lord designates will come forward clan by clan, the clan that the Lord designates will come forward household by household, and the household that the Lord designates will come forward man by man.

The one who is designated as holding what is devoted to destruction will be given over to the fire, he and all that belongs to him, because he has transgressed the covenant of the Lord and committed an outrage in Israel."
The next morning Joshua rose early and had Israel come forward tribe by tribe, and the tribe of Judah was designated.
He had the clans of Judah come forward, and the clan of Zerah was designated; he had the clan of Zerah come forward man by man, and Zabdi was designated;
he had his household come forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was designated.
Joshua said to Achan: "My son, give glory to the Lord, the God of Israel, and pay him honor; confess to me what you have done, do not hide it from me."
Achan answered Joshua: "It is true, I am the one who sinned against the Lord, the God of Israel, and this is what I did:

I saw among the plunder a fine cloak from Shinar, about two and a half kilos of silver, and a bar of gold weighing about six hundred grams; I coveted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath."
Joshua sent messengers who ran to the tent: the objects were hidden there, with the silver underneath.
They took them from inside the tent, brought them to Joshua and to all the sons of Israel, and laid them out before the Lord.

Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the cloak, and the bar of gold, along with his sons, his daughters, his oxen, his donkeys, his sheep, his tent, and everything that belonged to him, and they brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said: "Why have you brought trouble on us? The Lord will bring trouble on you today." And all Israel stoned him; they gave them over to the fire and covered them with stones.

They raised over him a great heap of stones, which remains to this day, and the Lord turned back from the heat of his anger. That is why that place is called the Valley of Achor, that is, of Trouble, to this day.

The Lord said to Joshua: "Do not be afraid, do not be dismayed. Take with you all the men of war, rise up and go up against Ai; see, I have handed over into your hands the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his territory.
You will treat Ai and its king as you treated Jericho and its king; only, you may take its plunder and its livestock as spoil for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city."
Joshua rose up with all the men of war to go up against Ai; he chose thirty thousand valiant warriors and sent them out by night.
He gave them this command: "Pay attention: you will lie in ambush behind the city, not too far from it, and all of you keep ready.
I and all the people who are with me will approach the city; and when they come out to meet us as the first time, we will flee before them.
They will come out in pursuit of us until we have drawn them far from the city, for they will say: They are fleeing before us as the first time. And we will flee before them.
Then you will spring up from the ambush and seize the city; the Lord your God will hand it over into your hands.
When you have taken the city, you will set it on fire; you will act according to the word of the Lord. See, I have given you my orders."
Joshua sent them off, and they went and took up their position in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai; as for Joshua, he spent that night among the people.
Joshua rose early in the morning, reviewed the people, and went up against Ai at the head of the people, he and the elders of Israel.
All the men of war who were with him went up, drew near, and arrived opposite the city; they camped north of Ai, with the valley between them and the city.
Joshua took about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
The people set the whole camp north of the city, and the rear guard to the west; that night Joshua advanced into the middle of the valley.

Seeing this, the king of Ai and the people of the city hurried to rise early and went out to battle against Israel, the king and all his people, to the appointed place facing the Arabah, without knowing that an ambush had been set against him behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel let themselves be beaten before them and fled by the wilderness road.
All the people of the city were called together to pursue them; they pursued Joshua and let themselves be drawn far from the city.
Not a man was left in Ai or in Bethel who did not go out in pursuit of Israel; they left the city open and pursued Israel.
The Lord said to Joshua: "Stretch out toward Ai the javelin in your hand, for I am about to hand it over into your power." And Joshua stretched out toward the city the javelin in his hand.
As soon as he stretched out his hand, the men of the ambush rose quickly from their position, rushed forward, entered the city, seized it, and hurried to set it on fire.

The men of Ai turned around: they saw the smoke of the city rising toward the sky, and they no longer had the strength to flee in any direction, while the people who had been fleeing toward the wilderness turned back against their pursuers.
Seeing that the ambush had taken the city and that its smoke was rising, Joshua and all Israel turned about and struck down the men of Ai.

The others came out of the city to meet them, so that the men of Ai were caught between the forces of Israel, some on one side, some on the other; they were struck down, leaving neither survivor nor fugitive.
As for the king of Ai, they took him alive and brought him to Joshua.

When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the open country, in the wilderness where they had pursued them, and all had fallen by the edge of the sword to the last man, all Israel returned to Ai and put it to the edge of the sword.
The total number of those who fell that day, men and women, was twelve thousand, all people of Ai.
Joshua did not draw back the hand he held stretched out with the javelin, until he had devoted to destruction all the inhabitants of Ai.
Israel took for itself only the livestock and the plunder of that city, according to the order the Lord had given Joshua.
Joshua burned Ai and made it forever a ruin, a desolate place, which remains to this day.

He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening; at sunset, at Joshua's order, they took his body down from the tree, threw it at the entrance of the city gate, and raised over it a great heap of stones, which remains to this day.
Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded the sons of Israel, and as it is written in the book of the law of Moses: an altar of uncut stones, on which no one had lifted iron. On it they offered burnt offerings to the Lord and made peace offerings.
There, on the stones, Joshua wrote a copy of the law that Moses had written in the presence of the sons of Israel.

All Israel, its elders, its officers, and its judges, stood on either side of the ark, facing the levitical priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, the foreigner as well as the native: one half toward Mount Gerizim, one half toward Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the Lord had first commanded, to bless the people of Israel.
After that, Joshua read all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, according to everything written in the book of the law.
There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua did not read before the whole assembly of Israel, with the women, the children, and the foreigners who lived among them.

When they heard this, all the kings west of the Jordan, in the hill country, in the lowland, and along the whole coast of the Great Sea as far as the Lebanon, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites,
banded together with one accord to fight against Joshua and Israel.
But the inhabitants of Gibeon, learning how Joshua had treated Jericho and Ai,
resorted to trickery in their turn: they set out and passed themselves off as envoys, loading their donkeys with worn-out sacks and old wineskins, cracked and mended;
on their feet, worn-out, patched sandals, on themselves old clothes, and all the bread of their provisions was dry and crumbling.
They went to Joshua at the camp of Gilgal and said to him and to the men of Israel: "We come from a distant country; so make a covenant with us."
The men of Israel answered these Hivites: "Perhaps you live near us? How could we make a covenant with you?"
They said to Joshua: "We are your servants." Joshua asked them: "Who are you and where do you come from?"
They answered him: "Your servants come from a very distant country, because of the name of the Lord your God; for we have heard of him, of all that he did in Egypt,
and of what he did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, Sihon king of Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived at Ashtaroth.
Our elders and all the inhabitants of our country said to us: Take provisions for the road, go to meet them, and say to them: We are your servants; so make a covenant with us.
Here is our bread: it was warm when we packed it as provisions in our houses, on the day we set out to come to you, and now it is dry and crumbling.
These wineskins, we filled them brand-new, and here they are cracked; our clothes and our sandals are worn out from the great length of the journey."
The men of Israel took some of their provisions, but did not consult the mouth of the Lord;
and Joshua made peace with them, he concluded with them a covenant sparing their lives, and the leaders of the community swore it to them.
Now, three days after the covenant was concluded, it was learned that they were neighbors and that they lived in the midst of Israel.
The sons of Israel set out and reached their cities on the third day: Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.
They did not strike them, because of the oath the leaders of the community had sworn to them by the Lord, the God of Israel. The whole community grumbled against the leaders,
but all the leaders said to the whole community: "We have sworn to them by the Lord, the God of Israel; now we can no longer touch them.
This is how we will deal with them: we will let them live, so as not to bring wrath upon ourselves, because of the oath we swore to them."
"Let them live!" said the leaders. And they became woodcutters and water carriers for the whole community, as the leaders had told them.
Joshua summoned the Gibeonites and said to them: "Why did you deceive us by saying: We are very far from you, when you live in the midst of us?
Now you are cursed: none of you will ever cease to be a slave, a woodcutter and water carrier for the house of my God."

They answered Joshua: "It was clearly reported to your servants how the Lord your God had commanded Moses his servant to give you the whole land and to destroy all its inhabitants before you; we were very afraid for our lives at your approach, and that is why we acted in this way.
Now, here we are in your hands: treat us as seems good and right to you."
So Joshua dealt with them in this way: he delivered them from the hand of the sons of Israel, who did not put them to death.
That day Joshua made them woodcutters and water carriers for the community and for the altar of the Lord, at the place he would choose; and they still do so today.

Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction, treating Ai and its king as he had treated Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them.
He was seized with great fear, for Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities, even larger than Ai, and all its men were valiant.
Adoni-zedek, king of Jerusalem, sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, to Piram king of Jarmuth, to Japhia king of Lachish, and to Debir king of Eglon:
"Come up to me and help me strike Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and the sons of Israel."

The five kings of the Amorites, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon, gathered and went up with all their armies; they camped before Gibeon and laid siege to it.

The people of Gibeon sent word to Joshua at the camp of Gilgal: "Do not forsake your servants; come up quickly to us, save us, help us, for all the Amorite kings of the hill country have banded together against us."
Joshua went up from Gilgal, he, all the men of war, and all the valiant warriors.
The Lord said to Joshua: "Do not be afraid of them, for I have handed them over into your hands: not one of them will stand against you."
Joshua fell upon them by surprise, after marching up from Gilgal all night.

And the Lord threw them into confusion before Israel, which inflicted a great defeat on them at Gibeon, pursued them along the ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled before Israel, on the descent of Beth-horon, the Lord hurled great hailstones down on them from heaven as far as Azekah, and they died; those killed by the hailstones were more numerous than those the sons of Israel killed by the sword.

Then Joshua spoke to the Lord, on the day the Lord handed the Amorites over to the sons of Israel, and he said, in the sight of Israel: "Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and you, moon, over the Valley of Aijalon!"

And the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation had taken vengeance on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of the Just? The sun stood still in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.
There was no day like it, before or since, when the Lord obeyed the voice of a man; for the Lord was fighting for Israel.
Then Joshua, and all Israel with him, returned to the camp at Gilgal.
The five kings had fled and hidden in the cave at Makkedah.
It was reported to Joshua: "The five kings have been found hidden in the cave at Makkedah."
Joshua said: "Roll great stones against the mouth of the cave and post men there to guard them.
But you, do not stop: pursue your enemies and strike them from behind, do not let them get back into their cities, for the Lord your God has handed them over into your hands."
When Joshua and the sons of Israel had finished inflicting a very great defeat on them, to the point of destroying them, the survivors took refuge in the fortified cities,
and all the people returned safely to the camp, to Joshua, at Makkedah, and no one dared say anything against the sons of Israel.
Joshua said: "Open the mouth of the cave and bring me these five kings out of the cave."
They did so: they brought him the five kings, whom they had brought out of the cave, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.

When these kings had been brought out before Joshua, Joshua called all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the fighting men who had gone with him: "Come near, put your feet on the necks of these kings." They came near and put their feet on their necks.
Joshua said to them: "Do not be afraid, do not be dismayed; be firm and courageous, for this is how the Lord will treat all the enemies you fight."
After this, Joshua struck them down and put them to death; he hanged them on five trees, where they remained hanging until evening.

At sunset, at Joshua's order, they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden; they placed great stones at the mouth of the cave, and they are there to this very day.

That day Joshua captured Makkedah and put it to the edge of the sword, it and its king; he devoted to destruction every living being in it, leaving no survivor, and he treated the king of Makkedah as he had treated the king of Jericho.
From Makkedah, Joshua, and all Israel with him, went on to Libnah and attacked it.

The Lord handed it over too, with its king, into the hands of Israel, which put it to the edge of the sword, it and every living being in it, leaving no survivor, and he treated its king as he had treated the king of Jericho.
From Libnah, Joshua, and all Israel with him, went on to Lachish; he camped before it and attacked it.
The Lord handed Lachish over into the hands of Israel, which took it on the second day and put it to the edge of the sword, it and every living being in it, as he had done for Libnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer went up to help Lachish, but Joshua struck him down, him and his people, leaving him no survivor.
From Lachish, Joshua, and all Israel with him, went on to Eglon; they camped before it and attacked it.
They took it that same day and put it to the edge of the sword; that day Joshua devoted to destruction every living being in it, as he had done for Lachish.
From Eglon, Joshua, and all Israel with him, went up to Hebron, and they attacked it.

They took it and put it to the edge of the sword, it, its king, all its dependent towns, and every living being in it, leaving no survivor, as he had done for Eglon; he devoted it to destruction with every living being in it.
Then Joshua, and all Israel with him, turned toward Debir and attacked it.

He took it, it, its king, and all its dependent towns; they put them to the edge of the sword and devoted to destruction every living being in it, leaving no survivor. Joshua treated Debir and its king as he had treated Hebron, and as he had treated Libnah and its king.

Joshua struck the whole land: the hill country, the Negev, the lowland, and the slopes, with all their kings, leaving no survivor; he devoted to destruction everything that breathed, as the Lord, the God of Israel, had commanded.
Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and all the land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
Joshua captured all these kings and their land in a single campaign, for the Lord, the God of Israel, was fighting for Israel.
Then Joshua, and all Israel with him, returned to the camp at Gilgal.
When they heard this, Jabin, king of Hazor, sent a message to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, to the king of Achshaph,
and to the kings of the north, in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinnereth, in the lowland, and on the heights of Dor to the west;
to the Canaanites of the east and the west, to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites of the hill country, and the Hivites at the foot of Hermon, in the land of Mizpah.
They came out with all their armies, a people as numerous as the sand on the seashore, with a great many horses and chariots.
All these kings joined forces and came and camped together near the waters of Merom, to fight against Israel.
The Lord said to Joshua: "Do not be afraid of them, for tomorrow at this time I will hand them all over slain before Israel; you will hamstring their horses and burn their chariots."
Joshua, and all the men of war with him, fell upon them by surprise near the waters of Merom and threw himself upon them.

The Lord handed them over into the hands of Israel, which struck them down and pursued them as far as Greater Sidon, as far as Misrephoth-maim and the Valley of Mizpeh to the east; it struck them down, leaving no survivor.
Joshua treated them as the Lord had told him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots.
At that time Joshua turned back, captured Hazor, and struck its king down with the sword; for in earlier times Hazor was the capital of all these kingdoms.
They put to the edge of the sword every living being in it, devoting it to destruction; nothing that breathed was left, and Hazor was burned.
Joshua captured all the cities of these kings and all their kings; he put them to the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction, as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded.
But Israel burned none of the cities built on their mounds, except Hazor, the only one Joshua burned.

All the plunder of these cities and the livestock, the sons of Israel took as spoil for themselves; but they put all the people to the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them, leaving nothing that breathed.
What the Lord had commanded Moses his servant, Moses had commanded Joshua, and Joshua carried it out: he left nothing undone of all that the Lord had commanded Moses.
So Joshua captured this whole land: the hill country, all the Negev, all the district of Goshen, the lowland, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel and its lowland,
from the bare mountain that rises toward Seir as far as Baal-gad, in the Valley of Lebanon, at the foot of Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings, struck them down, and put them to death.
For many days Joshua made war on all these kings.
No city made peace with the sons of Israel, except the Hivites who lived in Gibeon: they took them all by force of arms.

For it was the Lord's design that these peoples should harden their hearts to fight against Israel, so that they might be devoted to destruction without mercy and wiped out, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

At that time Joshua set out and destroyed the Anakim of the hill country, of Hebron, of Debir, of Anab, of all the hill country of Judah and all the hill country of Israel; Joshua devoted them to destruction along with their cities.
No Anakim were left in the land of the sons of Israel; there remained some only at Gaza, at Gath, and at Ashdod.

Joshua captured the whole land, according to everything the Lord had told Moses, and Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel, in portions, according to their tribes. And the land had rest from war.

titres.titre: The Kings Defeated East of the Jordan
The Kings Defeated West of the Jordan

versets.t: These are the kings of the land whom the sons of Israel defeated and whose land they took beyond the Jordan, to the east, from the Wadi Arnon as far as Mount Hermon, with all the Arabah to the east:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled at Heshbon. His dominion extended from Aroer, on the edge of the Wadi Arnon, and from the middle of the valley, over half of Gilead, as far as the Wadi Jabbok, the border of the sons of Ammon,

over the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinnereth to the east, and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, to the east, toward Beth-jeshimoth, and to the south, at the foot of the slopes of Pisgah.
Then the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the last of the Rephaim, who ruled at Ashtaroth and at Edrei.

His dominion extended over Mount Hermon, over Salecah, over all Bashan as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and over half of Gilead, as far as the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses the servant of the Lord and the sons of Israel defeated them, and Moses the servant of the Lord gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings whom Joshua and the sons of Israel defeated on the west side of the Jordan, from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon as far as the bare mountain that rises toward Seir, land that Joshua gave as a possession to the tribes of Israel, according to their allotments,

in the hill country, in the lowland, in the Arabah, on the slopes, in the wilderness, and in the Negev: the land of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
