The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, near Bethel, one;
the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Sharon, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam, in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor, on the heights of Dor, one; the king of Goiim, in Galilee, one;
the king of Tirzah, one. In all, thirty-one kings.

titres.titre: The Land That Remains to Be Conquered
The Inheritance of the Half-Tribe of Manasseh

versets.t: Joshua was old, well advanced in years. The Lord said to him, "You are now old and advanced in years, and there still remains a very large land to be conquered.
This is the land that remains: all the districts of the Philistines and all the territory of the Geshurites,

from the Shihor, which lies east of Egypt, as far as the border of Ekron to the north, a region reckoned as Canaanite; the five rulers of the Philistines, the ruler of Gaza, the ruler of Ashdod, the ruler of Ashkelon, the ruler of Gath, and the ruler of Ekron; and the Avvites
in the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, up to the border of the Amorites;
the land of the Gebalites and all of Lebanon to the east, from Baal-gad at the foot of Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath;

all the inhabitants of the hill country, from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians. I myself will dispossess them before the sons of Israel; only allot the land to Israel as an inheritance, by lot, as I have commanded you.
Now therefore divide this land as an inheritance among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."
With the other half-tribe, the Reubenites and the Gadites had received the inheritance that Moses gave them beyond the Jordan to the east, just as Moses the servant of the Lord had given it to them:
from Aroer, on the rim of the Wadi Arnon, and from the town in the middle of the valley, all the tableland of Medeba as far as Dibon;
all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned at Heshbon, up to the border of the sons of Ammon;
Gilead, the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, all of Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah;
all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned at Ashtaroth and at Edrei; he was one of the last of the Rephaim. Moses defeated them and dispossessed them.
But the sons of Israel did not dispossess the Geshurites or the Maacathites, and Geshur and Maacah live in the midst of Israel to this day.
To the tribe of Levi alone Moses gave no inheritance: the offerings by fire to the Lord, the God of Israel, are its inheritance, as he had told him.
Moses had given to the tribe of the sons of Reuben a portion according to their clans.
Their territory ran from Aroer, on the rim of the Wadi Arnon, and from the town in the middle of the valley, with all the tableland near Medeba,
Heshbon and all its towns on the tableland, Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,
Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill of the valley,
Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, Beth-jeshimoth,

all the towns of the tableland and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned at Heshbon. Moses had defeated him, along with the princes of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, vassals of Sihon settled in the land.
Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, was also among those whom the sons of Israel put to the sword, along with the other slain.
The border of the sons of Reuben was the Jordan and its bank. This was the inheritance of the sons of Reuben, according to their clans, with their cities and their villages.
Moses had given to the tribe of Gad, to the sons of Gad, a portion according to their clans.
Their territory included Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, half the land of the sons of Ammon as far as Aroer, which is opposite Rabbah,
and from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the territory of Debir;

and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon; the Jordan and its bank, to the end of the Sea of Chinnereth, beyond the Jordan to the east.
This was the inheritance of the sons of Gad, according to their clans, with their cities and their villages.
Moses had given to the half-tribe of Manasseh, to the sons of Manasseh, a portion according to their clans.
Their territory ran from Mahanaim: all of Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the Encampments of Jair in Bashan, sixty towns;
half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, the royal cities of Og in Bashan, were given to the sons of Machir son of Manasseh, to half of the sons of Machir, according to their clans.
These are the portions that Moses distributed in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho, to the east.
But to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance: the Lord, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he had told them.

titres.titre: The Allotment West of the Jordan

versets.t: These are the inheritances that the sons of Israel received in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the families of the tribes of the sons of Israel allotted to them,
by lot, as the Lord had commanded through Moses, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe;
for Moses had given their inheritance to the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan, but to the Levites he had given no inheritance among them,

since the sons of Joseph formed two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. No portion was given to the Levites in the land, only cities to live in, with their pasture lands for their livestock and their possessions.
The sons of Israel did as the Lord had commanded Moses, and they divided the land.
The sons of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know what the Lord said to Moses the man of God concerning me and you at Kadesh-barnea.
I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the Lord sent me from Kadesh-barnea to explore the land, and I brought him back a report in the sincerity of my heart.
My brothers who had gone up with me made the heart of the people melt; but I followed the Lord my God wholeheartedly.
On that day Moses swore this oath: The land your foot has trodden shall be your inheritance and your children's forever, because you have followed the Lord my God wholeheartedly.
And now, the Lord has kept me alive, as he promised, these forty-five years since he spoke this word to Moses, while Israel walked in the wilderness; and here I am today, eighty-five years old.
I am still as strong today as on the day Moses sent me: my vigor then is my vigor now, for battle, for going out and coming in.

So give me this hill country of which the Lord spoke on that day; you yourself heard that the Anakim are there, and great fortified cities; perhaps the Lord will be with me, and I will dispossess them, as the Lord has said."
Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh, and he gave him Hebron as an inheritance.
So Hebron belongs to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he followed the Lord, the God of Israel, wholeheartedly.
Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba; Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war.

The portion that fell by lot to the tribe of the sons of Judah, according to their clans, reached toward the border of Edom, to the wilderness of Zin, in the south, at the far southern edge of Canaan.
Their southern border began at the end of the Salt Sea, from the bay that faces south;
it turned south of the ascent of Akrabbim, passed on to Zin, went up south of Kadesh-barnea, reached Hezron, went up to Addar, and turned toward Karka;
it then passed on to Azmon, joined the Wadi of Egypt, and ended at the sea: this is your southern border.
The eastern border was the Salt Sea as far as the mouth of the Jordan. The northern border began at the bay of the sea, at the mouth of the Jordan;
it went up to Beth-hoglah, passed north of Beth-arabah, and went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben;
it went up to Debir from the valley of Achor, turned north toward Gilgal, opposite the ascent of Adummim, which is south of the wadi, passed by the waters of En-shemesh, and ended at En-rogel;

it went up the valley of Ben-hinnom, along the southern flank of the city of the Jebusites, that is, Jerusalem, then rose to the top of the mountain that overlooks the valley of Hinnom on the west, at the northern end of the valley of Rephaim;
from the top of the mountain the border reached the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, ended at the cities of Mount Ephron, then stretched toward Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim;
from Baalah it turned west toward Mount Seir, passed along the northern flank of Mount Jearim, that is, Chesalon, went down to Beth-shemesh, and passed on to Timnah;
it ended at the northern flank of Ekron, stretched toward Shikkeron, passed on to Mount Baalah, reached Jabneel, and ended at the sea.
The western border was the Great Sea and its shore. Such were, on every side, the borders of the sons of Judah, according to their clans.
To Caleb son of Jephunneh was given a portion among the sons of Judah, at the command of the Lord to Joshua: Kiriath-arba, named after the father of Anak, that is, Hebron.
Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak.
From there he went up against the inhabitants of Debir, which was formerly called Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb said, "To whoever attacks Kiriath-sepher and takes it, I will give my daughter Achsah as wife."
Othniel son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as wife.
When she came to him, she urged him to ask her father for a field. As she got down from her donkey, Caleb said to her, "What do you wish?"
She answered, "Grant me a gift: since you have set me in the land of the Negev, give me also springs of water." And he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Judah, according to their clans.
These are the towns at the far edge of the tribe of the sons of Judah, toward the border of Edom, in the Negev: Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,
Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,
Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan,
Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,
Hazor-hadattah and Kerioth-hezron, that is, Hazor,
Amam, Shema, Moladah,
Hazar-gaddah, Heshmon, Beth-pelet,
Hazar-shual, Beer-sheba, and Biziothiah,
Baalah, Iim, Ezem,
Eltolad, Chesil, Hormah,
Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon: in all, twenty-nine towns, with their villages.
In the lowland: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,
Zanoah, En-gannim, Tappuah, Enam,
Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah,
Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim: fourteen towns, with their villages.
Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal-gad,
Dilean, Mizpeh, Joktheel,
Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,
Cabbon, Lahmam, Chitlish,
Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah: sixteen towns, with their villages.
Libnah, Ether, Ashan,
Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,
Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah: nine towns, with their villages.
Ekron, with its dependent towns and its villages;
from Ekron westward, all the towns near Ashdod, with their villages;
Ashdod, its dependent towns and its villages; Gaza, its dependent towns and its villages, as far as the Wadi of Egypt and the Great Sea, which is the boundary.
In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh,
Dannah, Kiriath-sannah, that is, Debir,
Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,
Goshen, Holon, and Giloh: eleven towns, with their villages.
Arab, Dumah, Eshan,
Janim, Beth-tappuah, Aphekah,
Humtah, Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, and Zior: nine towns, with their villages.
Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,
Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,
Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah: ten towns, with their villages.
Halhul, Beth-zur, Gedor,
Maarath, Beth-anoth, and Eltekon: six towns, with their villages.
Kiriath-baal, that is, Kiriath-jearim, and Rabbah: two towns, with their villages.
In the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin, Secacah,
Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En-gedi: six towns, with their villages.
As for the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem, the sons of Judah could not dispossess them: the Jebusites live with the sons of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.

The portion that fell by lot to the sons of Joseph began at the Jordan by Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho; then it was the wilderness that goes up from Jericho to Bethel through the hill country.
From Bethel it went to Luz and passed on to the territory of the Archites, at Ataroth;
then it went down westward to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the territory of Lower Beth-horon and as far as Gezer, ending at the sea.
This was the inheritance the sons of Joseph received, Manasseh and Ephraim.
This is the territory of the sons of Ephraim, according to their clans. The boundary of their inheritance was, on the east, Ataroth-addar as far as Upper Beth-horon;
it ended at the sea. To the north was Michmethath; then it turned eastward toward Taanath-shiloh, and passed along it on the east to Janoah;
from Janoah it went down to Ataroth and to Naarah, touched Jericho, and ended at the Jordan.
From Tappuah it went westward to the Wadi Kanah, ending at the sea. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, according to their clans,
together with the towns set apart for the sons of Ephraim within the inheritance of the sons of Manasseh, all these towns with their villages.
But they did not dispossess the Canaanites who lived in Gezer; the Canaanites have lived in the midst of Ephraim to this day, subject to forced labor.

titres.titre: The Claim of the Sons of Joseph

versets.t: A portion also fell by lot to the tribe of Manasseh, the firstborn of Joseph. To Machir, the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, fell Gilead and Bashan, for he was a man of war.

A portion was also assigned to the rest of the sons of Manasseh, according to their clans: to the sons of Abiezer, to the sons of Helek, to the sons of Asriel, to the sons of Shechem, to the sons of Hepher, and to the sons of Shemida. These are the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, according to their clans.
Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters; these are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They came before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua son of Nun, and before the princes, saying, "The Lord commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." So at the command of the Lord they were given an inheritance among the brothers of their father.
Thus ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan, which is beyond the Jordan;
for the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons, and the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the sons of Manasseh.
The border of Manasseh ran from Asher to Michmethath, which is opposite Shechem, then went to the right toward the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on the border of Manasseh, belonged to the sons of Ephraim.

The border went down to the Wadi Kanah, south of the wadi; these towns, in the midst of the towns of Manasseh, belonged to Ephraim; the border of Manasseh passed north of the wadi and ended at the sea.
The south was Ephraim's, the north was Manasseh's, and the sea formed the border; on the north they touched Asher, and on the east, Issachar.

Within the territories of Issachar and Asher, Manasseh possessed Beth-shean and its dependent towns, Ibleam and its dependent towns, the inhabitants of Dor and its dependent towns, the inhabitants of En-dor and its dependent towns, the inhabitants of Taanach and its dependent towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its dependent towns: this is the region of the three heights.
But the sons of Manasseh could not take possession of these towns, and the Canaanites persisted in remaining in that land.
When the sons of Israel grew stronger, they subjected the Canaanites to forced labor, but they did not dispossess them.
The sons of Joseph said to Joshua, "Why have you given me as an inheritance only one lot, a single portion, when I am a numerous people, since the Lord has blessed me so richly until now?"

Joshua said to them, "If you are a numerous people, go up to the forest and clear ground for yourselves there in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you."

The sons of Joseph replied, "The hill country is not enough for us, and all the Canaanites who live in the plain have chariots of iron, both those of Beth-shean and its dependent towns and those of the valley of Jezreel."
Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh, "You are a numerous people, and your strength is great: you shall not have only one lot,

for the hill country shall be yours. It is a forest: you shall clear it, and its farthest limits shall be yours; yes, you shall dispossess the Canaanites, despite their chariots of iron and their strength."
The whole congregation of the sons of Israel assembled at Shiloh, where they set up the tent of meeting; the land lay subdued before them.
There still remained, among the sons of Israel, seven tribes that had not yet received their inheritance.
Joshua said to the sons of Israel, "How long will you delay to go and take possession of the land that the Lord, the God of your fathers, has given you?
Appoint three men from each tribe; I will send them to go through the land, to make a survey of it for the division, and then to return to me.
They shall divide it into seven parts: Judah shall stay in its territory in the south, and the house of Joseph in its own in the north.
You shall make a survey of the land in seven parts and bring it here to me, so that I may cast lots for you here, before the Lord our God.

For the Levites have no portion among you: the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance. As for Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, they have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan to the east, the one that Moses the servant of the Lord gave them."

The men set out and went; Joshua commanded those who went to survey the land, "Go, walk through the land, make a survey of it, and return to me; then I will cast lots for you here, before the Lord, at Shiloh."
So the men went and passed through the land, and made a survey of it in a book, town by town, in seven parts; then they returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
Joshua cast lots for them at Shiloh before the Lord, and there Joshua divided the land among the sons of Israel, according to their portions.
The lot fell to the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, according to their clans; the territory allotted to them lay between the sons of Judah and the sons of Joseph.
On the north, their border began at the Jordan, went up to the northern flank of Jericho, climbed the hill country on the west, and ended at the wilderness of Beth-aven.
From there it passed to Luz, on the southern flank of Luz, that is, Bethel, then went down to Ataroth-addar, on the mountain south of Lower Beth-horon.

The border bent and turned, on the west, toward the south, from the mountain that faces Beth-horon on the south, and ended at Kiriath-baal, that is, Kiriath-jearim, a city of the sons of Judah: this was the western side.
On the south, the border began at the edge of Kiriath-jearim, went westward, and reached the spring of the waters of Nephtoah;

it went down to the edge of the mountain that overlooks the valley of Ben-hinnom, north of the valley of Rephaim, then went down through the valley of Hinnom, along the southern flank of the Jebusites, as far as En-rogel;
it bent northward, ended at En-shemesh, reached Geliloth, which is opposite the ascent of Adummim, and went down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben;
it passed along the northern flank of the mountain that faces the Arabah and went down into the Arabah;
it passed along the northern flank of Beth-hoglah and ended at the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the southern mouth of the Jordan: this was the southern border.
The Jordan formed its boundary on the east. This was the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin, by its borders all around, according to their clans.
The cities of the tribe of the sons of Benjamin, according to their clans, were: Jericho, Beth-hoglah, Emek-keziz,
Beth-arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel,
Avvim, Parah, Ophrah,
Chephar-ammoni, Ophni, and Geba: twelve towns, with their villages.
Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,
Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah,
Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,
Zela, Eleph, Jebus, that is, Jerusalem, Gibeath, and Kiriath: fourteen towns, with their villages. This was the inheritance of the sons of Benjamin, according to their clans.
The second lot fell to Simeon, to the tribe of the sons of Simeon, according to their clans; their inheritance lay within the inheritance of the sons of Judah.
They received as their inheritance: Beer-sheba, Sheba, Moladah,
Hazar-shual, Balah, Ezem,
Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,
Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susah,
Beth-lebaoth, and Sharuhen: thirteen towns, with their villages;
Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan: four towns, with their villages,
together with all the villages around these towns, as far as Baalath-beer, Ramah of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Simeon, according to their clans.

The inheritance of the sons of Simeon was taken from the portion of the sons of Judah; for the portion of the sons of Judah was too large for them, and so the sons of Simeon received their inheritance within their territory.
The third lot fell to the sons of Zebulun, according to their clans; the border of their inheritance reached as far as Sarid.
It went up westward toward Maralah, touched Dabbesheth and the wadi that flows before Jokneam;
from Sarid it turned back east, toward the sunrise, to the territory of Chisloth-tabor, reached Daberath, and went up to Japhia;
from there it passed east, toward the sunrise, to Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin, reached Rimmon, and bent toward Neah;
it turned north toward Hannathon and ended at the valley of Iphtah-el.
Along with Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve towns, with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the sons of Zebulun, according to their clans: these towns and their villages.
The fourth lot fell to Issachar, to the sons of Issachar, according to their clans.
Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem,
Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath,
Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez,
Remeth, En-gannim, En-haddah, and Beth-pazzez.
The border touched Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth-shemesh, and ended at the Jordan: sixteen towns, with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Issachar, according to their clans: the towns and their villages.
The fifth lot fell to the tribe of the sons of Asher, according to their clans.
Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,
Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal; on the west it touched Carmel and Shihor-libnath,
then turned eastward toward Beth-dagon, touched Zebulun and the valley of Iphtah-el, north of Beth-emek and Neiel, and ended at Cabul, on the left,
with Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Great Sidon;
the border turned back toward Ramah, as far as the fortified city of Tyre, turned toward Hosah, and ended at the sea, in the region of Achzib;
with Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob: twenty-two towns, with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Asher, according to their clans: these towns and their villages.
The sixth lot fell to the sons of Naphtali, according to their clans.
Their border ran from Heleph, from the oak of Zaanannim, toward Adami-nekeb and Jabneel, as far as Lakkum, and ended at the Jordan;
it turned west toward Aznoth-tabor, reached Hukkok, touched Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and the Jordan on the east.
The fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth,
Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,
Kedesh, Edrei, En-hazor,
Iron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh: nineteen towns, with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, according to their clans: the towns and their villages.
The seventh lot fell to the tribe of the sons of Dan, according to their clans.
The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-shemesh,
Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah,
Elon, Timnah, Ekron,
Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,
Jehud, Bene-berak, Gath-rimmon,
Me-jarkon, and Rakkon, with the territory facing Joppa.

But the territory of the sons of Dan slipped from their grasp; so the sons of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, took it, and put it to the sword; they took possession of it, settled in it, and called it Dan, after the name of Dan their father.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Dan, according to their clans: these towns and their villages.
When they had finished dividing the land according to its boundaries, the sons of Israel gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.
At the command of the Lord they gave him the city he asked for, Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim; he rebuilt the city and lived in it.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the families of the tribes of the sons of Israel distributed by lot at Shiloh, before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. So they finished dividing the land.
The Lord spoke to Joshua. He said, "Speak to the sons of Israel: Designate for yourselves the cities of refuge of which I spoke to you through Moses,
that I may set them apart for you.
Anyone who kills a person by accident, unintentionally, may flee there: they shall be for you a refuge from the avenger of blood.

The one who has killed shall flee to one of these cities; he shall stop at the entrance of the city gate and state his case before the elders of that city, who shall take him in among them in the city and give him a place to live with them.
If the avenger of blood pursues him, they shall not hand the one who has killed over to him, for he struck down his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him before.

He shall live in that city until he stands trial before the congregation, until the death of the high priest in office in those days; then the one who has killed may return to his city and his home, to the city from which he fled."
So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.

Beyond the Jordan, opposite Jericho, to the east, they designated Bezer in the wilderness, on the tableland, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan, from the tribe of Manasseh.

These were the cities assigned to all the sons of Israel and to the resident alien who lives among them, so that anyone who had killed a person by accident could take refuge there and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood before standing before the congregation.
The heads of the families of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the heads of the families of the tribes of the sons of Israel;
they spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, "The Lord commanded through Moses that we be given cities to live in, with their pasture lands for our livestock."
So the sons of Israel gave the Levites, out of their inheritance, at the command of the Lord, the following cities with their pasture lands.

The lot first designated the clans of the Kohathites: the sons of Aaron the priest, from among the Levites, obtained by lot thirteen cities from the tribe of Judah, the tribe of Simeon, and the tribe of Benjamin;
the rest of the sons of Kohath obtained by lot ten cities from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, the tribe of Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The sons of Gershon obtained by lot thirteen cities from the clans of the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
The sons of Merari, according to their clans, obtained twelve cities from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the tribe of Zebulun.
So the sons of Israel gave the Levites by lot these cities with their pasture lands, as the Lord had commanded through Moses.
From the tribe of the sons of Judah and the tribe of the sons of Simeon, they gave the cities named here:
these went to the sons of Aaron, from among the clans of the Kohathites, from among the sons of Levi, for the first lot fell to them.
They gave them, in the hill country of Judah, Kiriath-arba, named after the father of Anak, that is, Hebron, with its pasture lands all around;
but the fields of that city and its villages they gave as a possession to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
To the sons of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron, the city of refuge for the one who has killed, with its pasture lands, as well as Libnah and its pasture lands,
Jattir and its pasture lands, Eshtemoa and its pasture lands,
Holon and its pasture lands, Debir and its pasture lands,
Ain and its pasture lands, Juttah and its pasture lands, and Beth-shemesh and its pasture lands: nine cities from these two tribes.
From the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon and its pasture lands, Geba and its pasture lands,
Anathoth and its pasture lands, and Almon and its pasture lands: four cities.
In all, the cities of the priests, the sons of Aaron: thirteen cities, with their pasture lands.
The clans of the sons of Kohath, the rest of the Levites descended from Kohath, obtained by lot cities from the tribe of Ephraim.
They gave them Shechem, the city of refuge for the one who has killed, with its pasture lands, in the hill country of Ephraim, as well as Gezer and its pasture lands,
Kibzaim and its pasture lands, and Beth-horon and its pasture lands: four cities.
From the tribe of Dan: Eltekeh and its pasture lands, Gibbethon and its pasture lands,
Aijalon and its pasture lands, and Gath-rimmon and its pasture lands: four cities.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh: Taanach and its pasture lands, and Gath-rimmon and its pasture lands: two cities.
In all, ten cities with their pasture lands, for the clans of the rest of the sons of Kohath.

To the sons of Gershon, from among the clans of the Levites, they gave, from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan, the city of refuge for the one who has killed, with its pasture lands, and Beeshterah and its pasture lands: two cities.
From the tribe of Issachar: Kishion and its pasture lands, Daberath and its pasture lands,
Jarmuth and its pasture lands, and En-gannim and its pasture lands: four cities.
From the tribe of Asher: Mishal and its pasture lands, Abdon and its pasture lands,
Helkath and its pasture lands, and Rehob and its pasture lands: four cities.

From the tribe of Naphtali: Kedesh in Galilee, the city of refuge for the one who has killed, with its pasture lands, as well as Hammoth-dor and its pasture lands, and Kartan and its pasture lands: three cities.
In all, the cities of the Gershonites, according to their clans: thirteen cities, with their pasture lands.
To the clans of the sons of Merari, the rest of the Levites, they gave, from the tribe of Zebulun: Jokneam and its pasture lands, Kartah and its pasture lands,
Dimnah and its pasture lands, and Nahalal and its pasture lands: four cities.
From the tribe of Reuben: Bezer and its pasture lands, Jahaz and its pasture lands, Kedemoth and its pasture lands, and Mephaath and its pasture lands: four cities.

From the tribe of Gad: Ramoth in Gilead, the city of refuge for the one who has killed, with its pasture lands, as well as Mahanaim and its pasture lands, Heshbon and its pasture lands, and Jazer and its pasture lands: four cities.
In all, the cities assigned by lot to the sons of Merari, according to their clans, the rest of the clans of the Levites: twelve cities.
In all, the cities of the Levites within the possessions of the sons of Israel: forty-eight cities, with their pasture lands.
Each of these cities had its pasture lands all around it; so it was for all these cities.
So the Lord gave Israel all the land he had sworn to give to their fathers; they took possession of it and settled in it.
The Lord gave them rest on every side, as he had sworn to their fathers; not one of their enemies could stand against them, for the Lord delivered all of them into their hands.
Of all the good promises that the Lord had made to the house of Israel, not one failed: all were fulfilled.

titres.titre: The Dismissal of the Transjordan Tribes

versets.t: Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
He said to them, "You have kept all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded you, and you have obeyed my voice in all that I commanded you.
You have not abandoned your brothers throughout all this long time, to this day, and you have kept the charge of the Lord your God.
Now that the Lord your God has given rest to your brothers, as he promised them, return to your tents, to the land of your possession, which Moses the servant of the Lord gave you beyond the Jordan.

Only take great care to carry out the commandment and the law that Moses the servant of the Lord prescribed for you: to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to hold fast to him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul."
Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went off to their tents.

To one half of the tribe of Manasseh Moses had given a territory in Bashan, and to the other half Joshua gave a territory among their brothers on the west side of the Jordan. When he sent them away to their tents, Joshua blessed them

and said to them, "You are returning to your tents with great riches, very large herds, and quantities of silver, gold, bronze, iron, and clothing; share with your brothers the spoil of your enemies."

So the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh left the sons of Israel at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, to return to the land of Gilead, the possession they had received at the command of the Lord given through Moses.

When they reached the districts of the Jordan that are in the land of Canaan, the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there, by the Jordan, an altar imposing to see.

The sons of Israel heard of it: "Look, the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar facing the land of Canaan, at the districts of the Jordan, on the side of the sons of Israel."
At this news, the whole congregation of the sons of Israel gathered at Shiloh to march against them in war.
The sons of Israel sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, in the land of Gilead,
and with him ten princes, one from each family for each of the tribes of Israel, all of them heads of their families among the thousands of Israel.
When they came to the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, in the land of Gilead, they said to them,

"Thus says the whole congregation of the Lord: What is this unfaithfulness that you have committed against the God of Israel, in turning away this day from the Lord, in building yourselves an altar to rebel this day against the Lord?
Was the sin of Peor not enough for us, from which we are not yet cleansed to this day, despite the plague that struck the congregation of the Lord,
that you should turn away this day from the Lord? If you rebel this day against the Lord, tomorrow he will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.

If the land of your possession seems unclean to you, cross over into the land of the possession of the Lord, where the Dwelling of the Lord resides, and settle among us; but do not rebel against the Lord, and do not rebel against us by building yourselves an altar other than the altar of the Lord our God.

When Achan son of Zerah committed an unfaithfulness concerning the devoted things, did not wrath break out against the whole congregation of Israel? And he was not the only one to perish for his sin."
The sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the heads of the thousands of Israel:
"The Mighty One, God, the Lord! The Mighty One, God, the Lord, he knows, and let Israel know! If it was in rebellion, if it was in unfaithfulness against the Lord, do not save us this day!
If we have built ourselves an altar to turn away from the Lord, to offer burnt offerings and grain offerings on it and to make peace offerings on it, may the Lord himself call us to account!
In truth, it was out of anxiety that we acted, saying to ourselves: Tomorrow your sons will say to ours, What have you to do with the Lord, the God of Israel?
The Lord has set the Jordan as a border between us and you, sons of Reuben and sons of Gad; you have no share in the Lord. So your sons would make ours cease to fear the Lord.
So we said to ourselves: Let us set about building this altar, not for burnt offerings or for sacrifices,

but so that it may be a witness between us and you, and between our descendants after us, that we do indeed serve the Lord before his face with our burnt offerings, our sacrifices, and our peace offerings; so that your sons will not say tomorrow to ours, You have no share in the Lord.

We said to ourselves: If they should ever speak this way to us or to our descendants, we would answer, Look at the replica of the altar of the Lord that our fathers built, not for burnt offerings or for sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you.

Far be it from us to rebel against the Lord and to turn away this day from the Lord by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, and sacrifices, other than the altar of the Lord our God that stands before his Dwelling!"

When Phinehas the priest and the princes of the congregation, the heads of the thousands of Israel who were with him, heard the words of the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the sons of Manasseh, they were satisfied.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the sons of Manasseh, "Today we know that the Lord is in our midst, since you have not committed this unfaithfulness against the Lord; you have thus delivered the sons of Israel from the hand of the Lord."

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the princes left the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad, returned from the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the sons of Israel, and gave them their report.
The matter pleased the sons of Israel: they blessed God and spoke no more of marching against them in war to ravage the land where the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad lived.
The sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad named the altar Ed, that is, Witness, for, they said, it is a witness between us that the Lord is God.
A long time after the Lord had given Israel rest, delivering it from all its surrounding enemies, Joshua, now old and advanced in years,
summoned all Israel, its elders, its leaders, its judges, and its officers, and said to them, "I have grown old and advanced in years.
You yourselves have seen all that the Lord your God has done to all these nations before you; for it is the Lord your God who has fought for you.
See, I have allotted to you by lot, as an inheritance for your tribes, these nations that remain and all those I have destroyed, from the Jordan to the Great Sea in the west.
The Lord your God will himself push them back before you, he will dispossess them before you, and you will take possession of their land, as the Lord your God promised you.
Be very firm, then, in observing and carrying out all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, turning aside from it neither to the right nor to the left,
and not mingling with these nations that remain among you. Do not invoke the name of their gods, do not swear by them, do not serve them, and do not bow down before them;
but hold fast to the Lord your God, as you have done to this day.
The Lord has dispossessed before you nations great and strong, and no one has been able to stand before you to this day.
One of you would put a thousand to flight, for it is the Lord your God who fought for you, as he promised you.
Watch carefully over yourselves, to love the Lord your God.
For if you turn away, if you hold fast to the remnant of these nations that remain among you, if you unite with them in marriage and mingle with them, and they with you,

know this well: the Lord your God will cease to dispossess these nations before you; they will become for you a snare and a trap, a scourge on your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land that the Lord your God has given you.

Now I am about to go this day the way of all the earth. Acknowledge with all your heart and all your soul that, of all the good promises that the Lord your God spoke concerning you, not one has failed: all have been fulfilled for you, not one has fallen.

But just as all the good promises that the Lord your God made to you have been fulfilled for you, so the Lord will bring upon you all the words of calamity, until he has destroyed you from this good land he has given you.

If you transgress the covenant that the Lord your God has prescribed for you, if you go and serve other gods and bow down before them, the anger of the Lord will blaze against you, and you will quickly perish from the good land he has given you."
Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem; he summoned the elders of Israel, its leaders, its judges, and its officers, and they presented themselves before God.
Joshua said to all the people, "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago, your fathers, Terah, the father of Abraham and of Nahor, lived beyond the River and served other gods.
I took your father Abraham from beyond the River, I led him through all the land of Canaan, I multiplied his descendants, and I gave him Isaac.
To Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau; to Esau I gave Mount Seir as a possession; and Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
Then I sent Moses and Aaron, I struck Egypt with what I did in its midst, and afterward I brought you out.
I brought your fathers out of Egypt, and you came to the sea. The Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and horsemen as far as the Red Sea.

They cried out to the Lord, who put darkness between you and the Egyptians and brought the sea back over them, so that it covered them. Your own eyes saw what I did in Egypt, and then you lived a long time in the wilderness.

I brought you to the land of the Amorites, who lived beyond the Jordan; they fought against you, but I delivered them into your hands, you took possession of their land, and I destroyed them before you.
Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, rose up to fight against Israel; he sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
But I would not listen to Balaam: he had to bless you, and I delivered you from his hand.

You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The lords of Jericho fought against you, along with the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, and I delivered them into your hands.
I sent the hornets ahead of you, and they drove them out before you, along with the two kings of the Amorites: it was not by your sword or your bow.
I gave you a land you had not labored for, cities you had not built and in which you live, vineyards and olive groves you had not planted and whose fruit you eat.
Now, fear the Lord and serve him in sincerity and faithfulness; put away the gods your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.

And if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose this day whom you will serve, whether the gods your fathers served beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live. As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord."
The people answered, "Far be it from us to abandon the Lord to serve other gods!

For it is the Lord our God who brought us and our fathers up out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, who performed those great wonders before our eyes and kept us safe all along the way we traveled, among all the peoples through whom we passed.
The Lord drove out before us all these peoples, and the Amorites who lived in the land. We too will serve the Lord, for he is our God."
Joshua said to the people, "You will not be able to serve the Lord, for he is a holy God, he is a jealous God: he will not bear your rebellions and your sins.
If you abandon the Lord to serve foreign gods, he will turn, he will bring harm upon you and destroy you, after having done you good."
The people said to Joshua, "No! It is the Lord that we will serve."
Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the Lord to serve him." They answered, "We are witnesses."
"Now therefore put away the foreign gods that are among you, and turn your hearts toward the Lord, the God of Israel."
The people said to Joshua, "It is the Lord our God that we will serve, and it is his voice that we will obey."
That day Joshua made a covenant with the people, and at Shechem he set for them a statute and an ordinance.
Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God. He took a large stone and set it up there, under the oak, in the sanctuary of the Lord.

Then Joshua said to all the people, "See: this stone shall be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words that the Lord has spoken to us; it shall be a witness against you, so that you do not deny your God."
Then Joshua sent the people away, each to his own inheritance.
After these events, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died, at the age of a hundred and ten years.
They buried him in the territory of his inheritance, at Timnath-serah, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Israel served the Lord throughout the lifetime of Joshua and throughout the lifetime of the elders who outlived him and who knew all that the Lord had done for Israel.

The bones of Joseph, which the sons of Israel had brought up from Egypt, were buried at Shechem, in the plot of ground that Jacob had bought for a hundred pieces of silver from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem, and which became the possession of the sons of Joseph.
Eleazar son of Aaron also died; they buried him at Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.

titres.titre: The unfinished conquest of the land of Canaan

versets.t: After the death of Joshua, the sons of Israel consulted the Lord: "Which of us shall go up first to fight the Canaanites?"
The Lord answered: "Judah shall go up: I am giving the land into his hands."

Then Judah said to his brother Simeon: "Come up with me into the territory allotted to me, and let us fight the Canaanites together; then in turn I will go with you into yours." And Simeon went with him.
Judah went up to battle, and the Lord gave the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hands: they struck down ten thousand of them at Bezek.
There at Bezek they came upon Adoni-bezek; they attacked him and struck down the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
Adoni-bezek fled, but they pursued him, caught him, and cut off his thumbs and big toes.
Then Adoni-bezek said: "Seventy kings, their thumbs and big toes cut off, used to gather scraps under my table. What I have done, God has repaid me." They took him to Jerusalem, where he died.
The men of Judah attacked Jerusalem and captured it; they put it to the sword and set the city on fire.
Afterward they went down to fight the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Negev, and the lowland.
Judah marched against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron, formerly called Kiriath-arba, and defeated Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
From there he marched against the inhabitants of Debir, formerly called Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb declared: "To the man who attacks and captures Kiriath-sepher, I will give my daughter Achsah as wife."
It was Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, who captured it; and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as wife.
On the day she came to join him, Achsah urged him to ask her father for a field. As she got down from her donkey, Caleb asked her: "What do you want?"
She answered: "Grant me a favor: since you have settled me in a parched land, give me springs of water as well." And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
The descendants of the Kenite, Moses' brother-in-law, went up from the City of Palms with the men of Judah and came to settle among the people, in the wilderness of Judah, south of Arad.
Then Judah went with his brother Simeon; they struck down the Canaanites who lived in Zephath, utterly destroyed the city, devoted to the Lord, and named it Hormah.
Judah also captured Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron, each with its territory.
The Lord was with Judah, who took possession of the hill country; but he could not drive out the inhabitants of the plain, for they had iron chariots.
As Moses had said, Hebron was given to Caleb, who drove out from it the three sons of Anak.
The Benjaminites, however, did not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem: the Jebusites have remained there, among the Benjaminites, to this day.
The house of Joseph also went up, against Bethel, and the Lord was with them.
They sent men to reconnoiter Bethel, the city formerly called Luz.
The scouts saw a man coming out of the city and said to him: "Show us how to get into the city, and we will treat you kindly."
He showed them how to get in. They put the city to the sword, but let that man and his whole family go free.
The man then went to the land of the Hittites; there he built a city and called it Luz, the name it still bears today.
Manasseh did not dispossess Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, and Megiddo, nor their dependent villages: the Canaanites were determined to stay in that land.
When Israel grew stronger, it subjected the Canaanites to forced labor, but never drove them out.
Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites settled at Gezer: they remained among them, at Gezer.
Zebulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol: the Canaanites remained among them, but were subjected to forced labor.
Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob:
so the Asherites settled among the Canaanites of the land, since they had not driven them out.
Naphtali did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath: he settled among the Canaanites of the land, but subjected them to forced labor.
The Amorites pushed the Danites back into the hill country, not letting them come down into the plain.
They were determined to stay at Har-heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim; but the house of Joseph prevailed over them and subjected them to forced labor.
The territory of the Amorites ran from the ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela, and beyond.

titres.titre: The rebuke of the angel of the Lord at Bochim
Israel forsakes the Lord: the pattern of the judges

versets.t: The angel of the Lord went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said: "I brought you up out of Egypt and led you into the land I had sworn to your fathers to give you. I had said: I will never break my covenant with you;
but you, make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land, and tear down their altars. Yet you have not listened to me. What is this you have done?
So I declare to you: I will not drive them out before you; they will remain at your side, and their gods will be a snare to you."
When the angel of the Lord had spoken these words to all the sons of Israel, the people began to weep aloud.
They named that place Bochim, that is, the Weepers, and there they offered sacrifices to the Lord.
Joshua dismissed the people, and the sons of Israel went off, each to his own inheritance, to take possession of the land.
The people served the Lord throughout the lifetime of Joshua, and throughout the lifetime of the elders who outlived him and who had seen all the great work the Lord had done for Israel.
Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died at the age of a hundred and ten.
They buried him in the territory allotted to him, at Timnath-heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Then all that generation was gathered to its fathers, and another generation arose after it, which did not know the Lord or what he had done for Israel.
The sons of Israel did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord: they served the Baals.

They forsook the Lord, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of Egypt, and turned to other gods, those of the peoples around them; they bowed down before them and provoked the Lord to anger.
They forsook the Lord to serve Baal and the Ashtaroth.
The anger of the Lord blazed against Israel: he handed them over to raiders who plundered them, he sold them to the enemies around them, and they could no longer stand against them.
Whenever they went out to war, the hand of the Lord was against them for their harm, as he had said and sworn. They were reduced to great distress.
Then the Lord raised up judges for them, who delivered them from the hand of those who plundered them.

But they would not even listen to their judges: they prostituted themselves to other gods and bowed down before them. Quickly they turned aside from the way their fathers had followed in obeying the commandments of the Lord; they did nothing of the kind.

When the Lord raised up a judge for them, he was with that judge and delivered them from their enemies as long as the judge lived; for the Lord was moved to pity as he heard them groaning under those who oppressed and crushed them.

But at the death of the judge, they became corrupt again, worse than their fathers: they ran after other gods to serve them and bow down before them, giving up none of their practices or their stubborn ways.
The anger of the Lord blazed against Israel, and he said: "Since this nation has violated the covenant I laid down for its fathers and has not listened to me,
I too, from now on, will no longer drive out before it any of the nations Joshua left at his death.
Through them I will put Israel to the test: I will see whether or not it will keep the way of the Lord, as its fathers kept it."
So the Lord let those nations remain, in no hurry to drive them out: he had not given them into the hands of Joshua.

titres.titre: The nations left to test Israel
Ehud and Eglon, king of Moab

versets.t: These are the nations the Lord left in place to test Israel by them, all those who had not known the wars of Canaan;
he wished only to instruct the generations of Israel and to teach them warfare, at least those who had not known it before.
These nations were the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived in the mountains of Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon to the approach of Hamath.
They served to test Israel, to know whether it would obey the commandments the Lord had given its fathers through Moses.
So the sons of Israel lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
They married their daughters, gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods.
The sons of Israel did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord: they forgot the Lord their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
The anger of the Lord blazed against Israel: he sold them to Cushan-rishathaim, king of Mesopotamia, to whom the sons of Israel were subject for eight years.
The sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, and the Lord raised up for them a deliverer who set them free: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
The Spirit of the Lord came upon him: he governed Israel and went out to war. The Lord gave Cushan-rishathaim, king of Mesopotamia, into his hands, and his hand prevailed over him.
The land had rest for forty years, and then Othniel son of Kenaz died.
Once again the sons of Israel did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord; so the Lord gave strength to Eglon, king of Moab, against Israel, because they were doing this evil.
Eglon rallied the Ammonites and the Amalekites, set out, and defeated Israel; they seized the City of Palms.
The sons of Israel were subject to Eglon, king of Moab, for eighteen years.

The sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, and the Lord raised up for them a deliverer: Ehud son of Gera, a Benjaminite who was left-handed. By him the sons of Israel sent their tribute to Eglon, king of Moab.
Ehud made himself a double-edged sword about fifty centimeters long, and he strapped it under his clothes against his right thigh.
He presented the tribute to Eglon, king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
Once the tribute had been presented, Ehud dismissed the men who had carried it.
But he himself turned back at the idols near Gilgal and said: "I have a secret message for you, O king." The king ordered: "Silence!", and all those around him went out.
Ehud approached: the king was sitting alone in the coolness of his upper room. Ehud said: "I have a word from God for you." The king rose from his seat.
Then, with his left hand, Ehud seized the sword from his right thigh and drove it into the king's belly.
The hilt went in after the blade, and the fat closed over it, for Ehud did not pull the sword out of the belly; the blade came out at the back.
Ehud went out by the outer stairway, pulled the doors of the upper room shut behind him, and slid the bolt.
After he left, the servants came back and saw the doors bolted. They said to themselves: "No doubt he is relieving himself in the cool of the room."
They waited until they were embarrassed; and since he still did not open, they took the key and opened the doors: there lay their master on the floor, dead.
While they waited, Ehud had made his escape; he passed the idols and got away to Seirah.
As soon as he arrived, he sounded the horn in the hill country of Ephraim; the sons of Israel came down with him from the hills, and he took the lead.
He said to them: "Follow me, for the Lord has given your enemies, the Moabites, into your hands." They went down after him, seized the fords of the Jordan opposite Moab, and let no one cross.
They then struck down Moab, about ten thousand men, all of them strong and valiant; not one escaped.
That day Moab was brought low under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest for eighty years.
After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath. With an ox goad he struck down six hundred Philistines; he too was a deliverer of Israel.
After the death of Ehud, the sons of Israel again did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord.
The Lord sold them to Jabin, king of Canaan, who reigned at Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived at Harosheth-ha-goiim.
The sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, for Jabin had nine hundred iron chariots and had harshly oppressed them for twenty years.
At that time it was a prophetess, Deborah, wife of Lappidoth, who was judging Israel.
She would sit under the palm of Deborah, between Ramah and Bethel, in the hill country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel would go up to her for judgment.

She sent for Barak son of Abinoam, from Kedesh in Naphtali, and said to him: "This is the command of the Lord, the God of Israel: Go, march to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun.
Toward the Kishon River I will draw out to meet you Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, with his chariots and his troops, and I will give him into your hands."
Barak answered her: "If you come with me, I will go; if you do not come, I will not go."

"I will go with you, then," she said; "but on the path you are taking, the honor will not be yours, for the Lord will deliver Sisera into the hand of a woman." And Deborah rose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh; ten thousand men followed him, and Deborah went up with him.
Now Heber the Kenite had separated from the other Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, Moses' brother-in-law; he had pitched his tent as far as the oak of Zaanannim, near Kedesh.
It was reported to Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.
Sisera gathered all his chariots, nine hundred iron chariots, and all his troops, from Harosheth-ha-goiim to the Kishon River.
Then Deborah said to Barak: "Up! for this is the day the Lord has given Sisera into your hands. Is the Lord not marching before you?" Barak came down from Mount Tabor, followed by ten thousand men.
Before Barak the Lord threw Sisera into panic, with all his chariots and all his army, and they fell by the sword. Sisera himself leaped down from his chariot and fled on foot.
Barak pursued the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth-ha-goiim; the whole army of Sisera fell by the sword, and not one man escaped.
Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin, king of Hazor, and the house of Heber.
Jael came out to meet Sisera and said to him: "Come in, my lord, come in to me, do not be afraid." He went into her tent, and she hid him under a rug.
He said to her: "Give me a little water to drink, please, for I am thirsty." She opened the skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him again.
He said to her once more: "Stand at the entrance of the tent; and if anyone comes and asks you: Is there someone here? you will answer: No."
But Jael, wife of Heber, took a tent peg and a mallet, came to him quietly, and drove the peg through his temple into the ground; worn out, he was fast asleep. And he died.

Now here came Barak, in pursuit of Sisera. Jael came out to meet him and said: "Come, I will show you the man you are looking for." He went in with her: there lay Sisera, dead, the peg through his temple.
That day God brought low Jabin, king of Canaan, before the sons of Israel.
And the hand of the sons of Israel bore down harder and harder on Jabin, king of Canaan, until they had destroyed him.
That day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang this song:
When the leaders take the lead in Israel, when the people offer themselves willingly, bless the Lord!
Hear, O kings! Give ear, O princes! I, yes I, will sing to the Lord, I will make music to the Lord, the God of Israel.
Lord, when you went out from Seir, when you advanced from the country of Edom, the earth shook, the heavens poured, the clouds poured down rain.
Before the Lord the mountains quaked, this Sinai itself, before the Lord, the God of Israel.
In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the roads lay deserted, and travelers took winding paths.
The villages of Israel were forsaken, until I arose, I, Deborah, until I arose, a mother in Israel.
They had chosen new gods, and war came knocking at the gates: among forty thousand men of Israel, not a shield or a spear could be seen.
My heart goes out to the commanders of Israel, to those of the people who offered themselves willingly. Bless the Lord!
You who ride white donkeys, you who sit on rugs, you who walk along the roads, sing!
Listen to the voices of those who, at the watering places, recount the mighty deeds of the Lord, his mighty deeds for the villages of Israel. Then the people of the Lord went down to the gates.
Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, break into song! Up, Barak! Lead away your captives, son of Abinoam!
Then the remnant of the nobles came down; the people of the Lord came down to me among the warriors.
From Ephraim came those who took root against Amalek; behind you marched Benjamin, among your troops. From Machir came down commanders, and from Zebulun those who bear the staff of command.
The princes of Issachar were with Deborah; Issachar, faithful to Barak, rushed after him into the plain. Among the clans of Reuben there was much searching of heart.
Why did you stay among the sheepfolds, listening to the pipes of the shepherds? Among the clans of Reuben there was much searching of heart.
Gilead stayed beyond the Jordan, at home; and Dan, why did he linger by the ships? Asher remained at ease by the seashore, settled in his harbors.
But Zebulun is a people that risked its life to the point of death, and Naphtali too, on the heights of the field.
The kings came, they fought; then they fought, the kings of Canaan, at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo. But of plunder, not a piece of silver!
From the heights of heaven the stars fought, from their courses they fought against Sisera.
The torrent Kishon swept them away, the ancient torrent, the torrent Kishon. March on, my soul, in strength!
Then the horses' hooves hammered the ground: they gallop, they gallop, his mighty steeds.
Curse Meroz, says the angel of the Lord, curse, curse its inhabitants! For they did not come to the help of the Lord, to the help of the Lord, among the valiant.
Blessed be Jael among women, the wife of Heber the Kenite, blessed among women who dwell in tents!
He asked for water, she offered milk; in the bowl of princes she brought curds.
With her hand she seized the peg, with her right hand the workman's mallet; she strikes Sisera, she crushes his head, she shatters and pierces his temple.
At her feet he sinks down, he falls, he lies still; at her feet he sinks down, he falls; where he sinks down, there he lies, destroyed.
At the window the mother of Sisera leans out and, behind the lattice, she moans: "Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why are his teams so slow?"
The wisest of her ladies answer her, and she repeats their words to herself:

"Have they not found and divided the spoil? A girl, two girls for each warrior; for Sisera, dyed cloth as spoil, dyed and embroidered cloth, two embroidered pieces to adorn his neck, such is the spoil!"
So perish all your enemies, Lord! But may those who love you be like the sun when it rises in all its strength! And the land had rest for forty years.

titres.titre: Gideon tears down the altar of Baal

versets.t: The sons of Israel did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, and the Lord handed them over for seven years into the hands of Midian.
The hand of Midian bore down heavily on Israel. To escape Midian, the sons of Israel made themselves refuges in the mountains, caves and fortified strongholds.
Whenever Israel had sown, Midian would come up against it with Amalek and the people of the East, and they would attack it.
They would camp opposite Israel and lay waste the crops of the land as far as the outskirts of Gaza, leaving nothing to live on, no sheep, no oxen, no donkeys.
For they came up with their herds and their tents, as numerous as swarms of locusts; they and their camels were beyond counting, and they invaded the land to ravage it.
Israel was brought to great misery by Midian, and the sons of Israel cried out to the Lord.
When the sons of Israel had cried out to the Lord because of Midian,
the Lord sent them a prophet, who said to them: "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I am the one who brought you up from Egypt and led you out of the house where you were slaves.
I rescued you from the hand of the Egyptians and of all your oppressors; I drove them out before you and gave you their land.
And I said to you: I am the Lord your God; do not fear the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live. But you have not listened to me."
Then the angel of the Lord came and sat under the terebinth at Ophrah, which belonged to Joash of the family of Abiezer. Gideon, his son, was threshing wheat in the winepress to hide it from Midian.
The angel of the Lord appeared to him and said: "The Lord is with you, mighty warrior."

Gideon answered him: "Forgive me, my lord: if the Lord is with us, why has all this happened to us? Where then are the wonders our fathers told us of, when they said: Is it not the Lord who brought us up from Egypt? Now the Lord has abandoned us and handed us over to Midian."
The Lord turned to him and said: "Go, in this strength of yours, and deliver Israel from the hand of Midian. Am I not the one sending you?"
Gideon said to him: "Forgive me, Lord: how shall I deliver Israel? My clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."
The Lord answered him: "I will be with you, and you will strike down Midian as though it were a single man."
Gideon replied: "If I have found favor in your eyes, give me a sign that it is really you speaking to me.
Do not leave this place until I come back to bring you my offering and set it before you." The Lord said: "I will stay until you return."

Gideon went in, prepared a young goat and, with about twenty-two liters of flour, made unleavened bread. He put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, then came and offered them to him under the terebinth.
The angel of God said to him: "Take the meat and the unleavened bread, place them on this rock and pour out the broth." Gideon did so.

The angel of the Lord reached out the tip of the staff he was holding and touched the meat and the unleavened bread. At once fire sprang up from the rock and consumed the meat and the bread, and the angel of the Lord vanished from his sight.
Then Gideon realized that it was the angel of the Lord, and he cried out: "Alas, Lord my God, for I have seen the angel of the Lord face to face!"
The Lord said to him: "Peace be with you, do not be afraid, you will not die."
Gideon built an altar there to the Lord and called it "the Lord is peace." This altar is still at Ophrah of Abiezer today.
That night the Lord said to Gideon: "Take your father's young bull, the one seven years old. Tear down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father and cut down the sacred pole of Asherah beside it.
Then, on the top of this height, build a proper altar to the Lord your God. Take the second bull and offer it as a whole burnt offering, with the wood of the pole you have cut down."
Gideon took ten of his servants and did as the Lord had told him. Since he dared not act by day, for fear of his family and the men of the town, he did it by night.
Early the next morning, the men of the town got up: the altar of Baal was torn down, the sacred pole cut down, and the second bull offered on the newly built altar.
They asked one another: "Who did this?" After inquiry and investigation, they were told: "It was Gideon son of Joash."
Then the men of the town said to Joash: "Bring out your son: he must die, for he has torn down the altar of Baal and cut down the sacred pole beside it."

But Joash answered all those who confronted him: "Is it for you to defend Baal? Is it for you to save him? Whoever takes his side will be put to death before morning! If Baal is a god, let him defend himself, since his altar has been torn down."
That day Gideon was given the name Jerubbaal, meaning: "Let Baal defend himself against him, since he has torn down his altar."
All Midian, Amalek, and the people of the East gathered together, crossed the Jordan, and camped in the plain of Jezreel.
The Spirit of the Lord took hold of Gideon: he sounded the horn, and the Abiezrites fell in behind him.
He sent messengers throughout all Manasseh, which fell in behind him, then to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, who came up to meet him.
Gideon said to God: "If you really mean to deliver Israel by my hand, as you have said,

here: I will spread a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If the dew falls only on the fleece, while all the ground around stays dry, I will know that you will deliver Israel by my hand, as you have said."
And so it happened. The next day Gideon rose early, wrung out the fleece, and squeezed from it enough dew to fill a bowl.

Gideon said to God again: "Do not let your anger blaze if I speak one last time. Let me make just one more test with the fleece: let the fleece alone stay dry, and let the dew fall on all the ground around."
That night God did so: the fleece alone stayed dry, and all the ground was covered with dew.
Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, rose early with all his troops and camped near the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian was to the north of his, by the hill of Moreh, in the plain.
The Lord said to Gideon: "You have too many men with you for me to give Midian into their hands: Israel might boast at my expense and say: It was my own hand that saved me.
So proclaim this in the hearing of the people: Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him turn back and leave Mount Gilboa." Twenty-two thousand men turned back, and ten thousand remained.

The Lord said again to Gideon: "There are still too many. Bring them down to the water, and there I will sift them for you. The one of whom I say to you: This one shall go with you, shall go; and the one of whom I say: This one shall not go with you, shall not go."

Gideon brought the people down to the water, and the Lord said to him: "Those who lap the water with their tongues, as a dog does, put on one side; and on the other, all those who kneel down to drink."
Those who lapped the water, raising it to their mouths with their hands, numbered three hundred; all the rest had knelt down to drink.
Then the Lord said to Gideon: "It is with these three hundred men who lapped the water that I will save you and give Midian into your hands; let all the others go home."

The three hundred took the people's provisions and horns. Gideon sent all the other sons of Israel back, each to his tent, and kept only these three hundred men. The camp of Midian lay below him, in the plain.
That night the Lord said to Gideon: "Up, go down and attack the camp, for I have given it into your hands.
If you are afraid to attack, go down there first with your servant Purah;
you will hear what they are saying, and then you will have the courage to go down and attack the camp." So Gideon went down with his servant Purah to the outposts of the camp.
Midian, Amalek, and all the people of the East had spread out over the plain, as numerous as locusts, and their camels were beyond counting, like the sand on the seashore.

When Gideon arrived, a man was just then telling a dream to his comrade: "I had a dream," he was saying: "a loaf of barley bread came tumbling into the camp of Midian; it reached a tent, struck it, overturned it, and turned it upside down, and the tent collapsed."
His comrade answered: "This can only be the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite: God has given Midian and the whole camp into his hands."
When Gideon heard the dream and its meaning, he bowed down in worship. Then he went back to the camp of Israel and said: "Up! for the Lord has given the camp of Midian into your hands."
He divided the three hundred men into three companies and gave each man a horn and an empty jar, with a torch inside the jar.
He said to them: "Watch me and do as I do. As soon as I reach the edge of the camp, do exactly what I do.
When I sound the horn, I and all who are with me, you too shall sound the horn all around the camp, and shout: For the Lord and for Gideon!"

Gideon and the hundred men with him reached the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just after the changing of the guard. They sounded the horn and smashed the jars they were holding.

The three companies sounded the horn and smashed their jars; with their left hands they grasped the torches, with their right the horns to blow them, and they shouted: "A sword for the Lord and for Gideon!"
Each man stood in his place around the camp, while the whole camp was in turmoil, crying out and fleeing.

While the three hundred sounded their horns, the Lord set the swords of the Midianites against one another throughout the camp. They fled as far as Beth-shittah, toward Zererah, to the outskirts of Abel-meholah, near Tabbath.
The sons of Israel from Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh gathered and pursued Midian.

Gideon also sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim: "Come down to meet Midian and cut off their access to the water as far as Beth-barah, along with the fords of the Jordan." All the men of Ephraim gathered and occupied the watercourse as far as Beth-barah, together with the fords of the Jordan.

They captured two chiefs of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb. After pursuing Midian, they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon, on the other side of the Jordan.

titres.titre: Gideon captures the kings of Midian

versets.t: The men of Ephraim said to Gideon: "Why have you treated us like this? Why did you not call us when you went to fight Midian?" And they reproached him bitterly.
He answered them: "What have I done compared with you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim's grapes better than the whole vintage of Abiezer?
It was into your hands that God gave the chiefs of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. What have I been able to do compared with you?" At these words their anger against him died down.
Gideon reached the Jordan and crossed it with his three hundred men, exhausted but still in pursuit of the enemy.
He said to the people of Succoth: "Give my troops some loaves of bread, I beg you: they are exhausted, and I am pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."
But the leaders of Succoth answered: "Do you already hold Zebah and Zalmunna in your hand, that we should give bread to your troops?"
Gideon replied: "Very well, when the Lord has given Zebah and Zalmunna into my hands, I will thrash your flesh with thorns and briers of the desert."
From there he went up to Penuel and made the same request; the people of Penuel answered him as those of Succoth had.
So he declared to them: "When I return victorious, I will tear down this tower."
Zebah and Zalmunna were at Karkor with their army, about fifteen thousand men, all that remained of the army of the people of the East; a hundred and twenty thousand swordsmen had already fallen.
Gideon went up by the route of the nomads, east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and attacked the camp while it thought itself safe.
Zebah and Zalmunna fled; he pursued them, captured the two kings of Midian, and scattered their whole army.
Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle by the ascent of Heres.
He stopped a young man from Succoth and questioned him; the young man wrote down for him the names of the leaders and elders of Succoth, seventy-seven men.

Gideon then came to the people of Succoth and said: "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you mocked me, saying: Do you already hold Zebah and Zalmunna in your hand, that we should give bread to your exhausted men?"
He seized the elders of the town and punished the people of Succoth with thorns and briers of the desert.
He also tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the town.
Then he asked Zebah and Zalmunna: "What were the men like whom you killed at Tabor?" They answered: "They were like you: each had the bearing of a king's son."
He said: "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As the Lord lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you!"
He ordered Jether, his firstborn: "Up, kill them!" But the boy did not draw his sword: he was afraid, for he was still too young.
Zebah and Zalmunna said: "Get up yourself and strike us; for as the man is, so is his strength." Gideon got up, killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and took the crescents that adorned their camels' necks.
