Solomon left all these objects unweighed, they were so many: the weight of the bronze was not determined.
Solomon also made all the furnishings of the house of the Lord: the golden altar; the golden table, on which the bread of the offering was set;
the lampstands of pure gold, five on the right and five on the left in front of the sanctuary, with the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs of gold;

the basins, the knives, the bowls, the ladles, and the incense pans of pure gold; and the golden sockets for the doors of the inner sanctuary, the Holy of Holies, as for the doors of the great hall of the temple.

So all the work that King Solomon did in the house of the Lord was finished. Solomon brought in what David his father had consecrated, the silver, the gold, and the vessels, and he placed them in the treasuries of the house of the Lord.

titres.titre: The ark brought into the temple
The glory of the Lord fills the temple

versets.t: Then Solomon gathered around him at Jerusalem the elders of Israel, all the heads of the tribes and the leaders of the families of the sons of Israel, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the city of David, that is, Zion.
All the men of Israel gathered around King Solomon, in the month of Ethanim, the seventh month, during the feast.
When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the priests lifted the ark.
They brought up the ark of the Lord, the tent of meeting, and all the sacred objects that were in it: it was the priests and the Levites who carried them.
King Solomon and the whole community of Israel gathered around him stood before the ark; they sacrificed sheep and oxen in such numbers that they could not be counted or numbered.
The priests brought the ark of the covenant of the Lord to its place, in the sanctuary of the temple, the Holy of Holies, under the wings of the cherubim.
For the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, covering the ark and its poles from above.
The poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the great hall, in front of the sanctuary; but they could not be seen from outside. They are still there to this day.
There was nothing in the ark but the two stone tablets that Moses had placed there at Horeb, when the Lord made a covenant with the sons of Israel at their coming out of Egypt.
Now, as the priests came out of the sanctuary, the cloud filled the house of the Lord;
the priests could not remain to perform their service, because of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord filled the house of the Lord.
Then Solomon said, "The Lord has said that he would dwell in the dark cloud.
Indeed, I have built you a house to dwell in, a place where you will reside forever."
Then the king turned around and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly stood.
He said, "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who spoke with his own mouth to David my father and who, with his own hand, has fulfilled his promise:

From the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I had chosen no city, in any of the tribes of Israel, for a house to be built where my name would reside; but I chose David to rule over my people Israel.
David my father had it in his heart to build a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
But the Lord said to him: You had it in your heart to build a house for my name, and you did well.
Only, you are not the one who will build this house: it is your son, your own offspring, who will build it for my name.

The Lord has kept the word he gave: I have succeeded David my father, I have taken my seat on the throne of Israel as the Lord promised, and I have built the house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
There I have set a place for the ark, which holds the covenant that the Lord made with our fathers when he brought them out of Egypt."
Then Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord, facing the whole assembly of Israel; he spread out his hands toward heaven

and said, "Lord, God of Israel, there is no God like you, neither above in the heavens nor below on the earth: you keep the covenant and faithful love toward your servants who walk before you with all their heart.
You have kept toward your servant David, my father, the promise you made him: what you said with your mouth, you have fulfilled with your hand, as is seen today.

And now, Lord, God of Israel, keep toward your servant David, my father, this other promise: You will never lack before me a descendant seated on the throne of Israel, provided that your sons watch over their conduct, walking before me as you yourself have walked before me.
Yes, God of Israel, let it be fulfilled, the word you gave to your servant David, my father!
But will God really dwell on the earth? Behold, the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain you: how much less this house that I have built!
Yet be attentive to the prayer and supplication of your servant, Lord my God: listen to the cry and the prayer that your servant addresses to you today.
May your eyes be open, night and day, toward this house, toward this place of which you said: There my name will be; listen to the prayer that your servant offers toward this place.
Listen to the supplication of your servant and of your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Listen from heaven, where you reside; listen and forgive.
If a man sins against his neighbor and is made to take an oath to clear himself, and he comes to swear before your altar in this house,

then you, from heaven, listen and act: do justice for your servants, condemning the guilty, whose conduct you will bring back on his own head, and declaring the innocent righteous, repaying him according to his uprightness.
When your people Israel are defeated by an enemy for having sinned against you, if they return to you, if they praise your name, if they pray and plead with you in this house,
then you, from heaven, listen, forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave to their fathers.
When the sky is shut and withholds the rain, because they have sinned against you, if they pray toward this place, if they praise your name and turn away from their sin because you have humbled them,

then you, from heaven, listen, forgive the sin of your servants and of your people Israel, whom you will teach the good way in which to walk, and send rain on the land you gave as an inheritance to your people.
When there is famine or plague in the land, blight or mildew, locusts or grasshoppers; when the enemy besieges the people in one of their cities; whatever the calamity, whatever the disease,
whatever the prayer, whatever the supplication of any person or of all your people Israel, each one knowing the affliction of his own heart and spreading out his hands toward this house,
then you, from heaven where you reside, listen and forgive; act, and repay each one according to all his conduct, you who know his heart, for you alone know the heart of all people.
So they will fear you all the days of their life on the land you gave to our fathers.
And even the foreigner, the one who is not of your people Israel but who will come from a distant land because of your name
for they will hear of your great name, your mighty hand, and your outstretched arm, when he comes to pray in this house,

then you, from heaven where you reside, listen, and grant this foreigner all that he asks of you. So all the peoples of the earth will know your name, they will fear you as your people Israel do, and they will know that your name is invoked over this house that I have built.
When your people go out to war against their enemy, by the way you send them, if they pray to the Lord, turned toward the city you have chosen and toward the house I have built for your name,
listen from heaven to their prayer and their supplication, and do them justice.
When they sin against you, for there is no one who does not sin, and in your anger you hand them over to the enemy who carries them off captive to his land, distant or near,
if they come to their senses in the land of their captivity, if they return to you and plead with you in the land of those who hold them, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong, we are guilty';

if they return to you with all their heart and all their soul, in the land of the enemies who deported them, if they pray to you, turned toward the land you gave to their fathers, toward the city you have chosen, and toward the house I have built for your name,
listen from heaven, where you reside, to their prayer and their supplication, do them justice,
and forgive your people the sins they have committed against you. Make them worthy of compassion before those who hold them captive, so that these may have pity on them;
for they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of Egypt, from the midst of the iron furnace.
May your eyes be open to the supplication of your servant and to the supplication of your people Israel, to listen to them whenever they call on you;
for it is you who set them apart, from among all the peoples of the earth, to be your inheritance, as you declared through Moses your servant, when you brought our fathers out of Egypt, Lord God."
When Solomon had finished offering the Lord all this prayer and supplication, he rose from before the altar of the Lord, where he had knelt with his hands spread out toward heaven.
Standing, he blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice:
"Blessed be the Lord, who has given rest to his people Israel, according to all his promise! Of all the good words he spoke through Moses his servant, not one has failed.
May the Lord our God be with us, as he was with our fathers! May he not abandon us or forsake us,
but may he incline our hearts toward him, so that we walk in all his ways and keep the commandments, the statutes, and the rules he prescribed for our fathers.
May these words of my supplication before the Lord remain present to the Lord our God day and night, so that he may do justice, day after day, to his servant and to his people Israel,
so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord is God, and that there is no other.
As for you, let your heart be wholly with the Lord our God, to follow his statutes and keep his commandments, as today."
The king and all Israel with him offered sacrifices before the Lord.
Solomon sacrificed, as peace offerings, twenty-two thousand oxen and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. This is how the king and all the sons of Israel dedicated the house of the Lord.

That day the king consecrated the middle of the court, in front of the house of the Lord, for there he offered the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings: the bronze altar that stood before the Lord was too small to hold it all.

At that time Solomon kept the feast, and all Israel with him, a vast assembly gathered from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of Egypt; they stayed before the Lord our God seven days, then seven more days, fourteen days in all.
On the eighth day he sent the people away. They blessed the king, and each went home, glad and content in heart for all the good the Lord had done for David his servant and for Israel his people.

titres.titre: The Lord appears a second time

versets.t: When Solomon had finished building the house of the Lord, the royal palace, and all that he had desired to accomplish,
the Lord appeared to him a second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.

The Lord said to him, "I have heard the prayer and supplication you addressed to me. I have consecrated this house that you have built, to set my name there forever; there my eyes and my heart will always be.
And you, if you walk before me as David your father walked, with an undivided and upright heart, doing all that I have commanded you, keeping my statutes and my rules,
I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever, as I promised David your father: You will never lack a descendant on the throne of Israel.
But if you turn away from me, you and your sons, if you do not keep the commandments and the statutes I have set before you, and if you go and serve other gods and bow down before them,

I will cut Israel off from the land I have given it; this house that I have consecrated to my name, I will cast it away from my presence, and Israel will become a byword and an object of ridicule among all peoples.
This house, once so exalted, will fill with astonishment everyone who passes by it: he will hiss in horror and say, 'Why has the Lord dealt this way with this land and this house?'

And the answer will be, 'Because they abandoned the Lord their God, who brought their fathers out of Egypt, and clung to other gods, bowing down before them and serving them: that is why the Lord has brought all this disaster upon them.'"
At the end of twenty years, when Solomon had built the two structures, the house of the Lord and the royal palace,
since Hiram, king of Tyre, had supplied him with as much cedar timber, cypress, and gold as he wanted, King Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee.
Hiram came out from Tyre to see the cities that Solomon had given him, but they did not please him.
He said, "What cities are these you have given me, my brother?" And he called them the land of Cabul, the name they bear to this day.
Hiram had sent the king about four tons of gold.
This is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon raised to build the house of the Lord, his own palace, the Millo, and the wall of Jerusalem, as well as Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
Pharaoh, king of Egypt, had come up and seized Gezer; he had burned it, killed the Canaanites who lived there, and then given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife.
So Solomon rebuilt Gezer, as well as Lower Beth-horon,
Baalath and Tamar, in the wilderness of the land,

all the storage cities that belonged to Solomon, the cities for the chariots, the cities for the cavalry, and everything he wished to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout the land under his authority.
All that remained of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, those peoples who were not sons of Israel,

their descendants who remained after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel had been unable to devote to destruction, Solomon conscripted into the forced labor gangs, where they remain to this day.
But Solomon did not enslave any of the sons of Israel: they were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his charioteers, the commanders of his chariots and his cavalry.
The chief officers in charge of Solomon's works numbered five hundred fifty; they directed the people engaged in the work.
As soon as Pharaoh's daughter had come up from the city of David to the palace Solomon had built for her, he built the Millo.
Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the Lord, and he burned incense on the one before the Lord. So he completed the temple.
King Solomon built a fleet at Ezion-geber, near Elath, on the shores of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom.
Hiram sent his own servants on these ships, sailors who knew the sea, along with Solomon's servants.
They went to Ophir, from which they brought back about fourteen tons of gold, which they handed over to King Solomon.
The queen of Sheba heard of the fame that Solomon owed to the name of the Lord, and she came to test him with riddles.
She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large retinue, camels laden with spices, gold in great quantity, and precious stones. When she came to Solomon, she told him all that was on her heart,
and Solomon answered all her questions: nothing was hidden from the king, and he was able to explain everything to her.
When the queen of Sheba had seen all the wisdom of Solomon, the palace he had built,

the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his attendants and their attire, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he offered in the house of the Lord, it took her breath away.
She said to the king, "So it was true, what I had heard in my own country about you and about your wisdom!
I did not believe the reports until I came and saw with my own eyes; and behold, I had not been told the half of it! Your wisdom and your prosperity surpass everything the report had told me.
Happy are your people, happy are your servants, who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
Blessed be the Lord your God, who has shown you his favor by setting you on the throne of Israel! Because he loves Israel forever, he has made you king, to administer right and justice."

She gave the king about four tons of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again was there seen such an abundance of spices as that which the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
The ships of Hiram, which brought gold from Ophir, also brought from there a very great quantity of sandalwood and precious stones.

With this sandalwood the king made railings for the house of the Lord and for the royal palace, as well as lyres and harps for the singers. Never has such sandalwood come or been seen since, to this day.
King Solomon granted the queen of Sheba all she desired and asked for, besides gifts worthy of a king such as he. Then she set out to return to her own country, she and her servants.
The weight of the gold that came to Solomon each year was about twenty-two and a half tons,
besides what came from the merchants, the trade of the traders, all the kings of Arabia, and the governors of the land.
King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold, using about seven kilos of gold for each shield,
and three hundred small shields of hammered gold, using about one and a half kilos of gold for each; and the king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king also made a great throne of ivory, which he overlaid with pure gold.
This throne had six steps; its back was rounded at the top; on each side of the seat were armrests, beside which stood two lions.
Twelve lions stood there, on the six steps, six on each side. Nothing like it had ever been made in any kingdom.
All of King Solomon's cups were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold; nothing was of silver, which counted for nothing in Solomon's time.
For the king had at sea a fleet of Tarshish, along with Hiram's; every three years the fleet of Tarshish returned, laden with gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.
The whole world sought to see Solomon, to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart;
and each one brought his gift year by year: objects of silver and gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
Solomon gathered chariots and cavalry: he had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horses, which he stationed in the garrison cities and near the king, in Jerusalem.
The king made silver as common as stones in Jerusalem, and cedars as plentiful as the sycamores of the lowland.
Solomon's horses came from Egypt and from Kue; the king's merchants would go and buy them in droves, at a set price.

A chariot imported from Egypt cost six hundred pieces of silver, a horse a hundred and fifty; and through these merchants they were likewise exported to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
King Solomon loved many foreign women, besides Pharaoh's daughter: Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonian women, Hittites,

from those nations of which the Lord had said to the sons of Israel: You shall not go to them, and they shall not come to you, for they would surely turn your heart toward their gods. It was to these that Solomon clung in love.
He had seven hundred wives of princely rank and three hundred concubines; and his wives turned his heart away.
In Solomon's old age his wives inclined his heart toward other gods, and his heart was no longer wholly with the Lord his God, as the heart of David his father had been.
Solomon followed Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Milcom, the abominable idol of the Ammonites.
Solomon did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, and he did not follow the Lord fully, as David his father had done.
Then Solomon built, on the mountain facing Jerusalem, a high place for Chemosh, the abominable idol of Moab, and for Molech, the abominable idol of the sons of Ammon.
He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods.
The Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the Lord, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice
and had expressly forbidden him to follow other gods; but Solomon did not keep the Lord's command.

The Lord said to Solomon, "Since you have acted this way, and have not kept my covenant and the statutes I prescribed for you, I will surely tear the kingship from you and give it to one of your servants.
Yet for the sake of David your father, I will not do it in your lifetime: it is from the hand of your son that I will tear it away.
Even so, I will not tear away all the kingship: I will leave one tribe to your son, for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen."
The Lord raised up an adversary against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite, of the royal line of Edom.
Earlier, when David was at war with Edom, Joab the commander of the army had gone up to bury the dead and had struck down every male in Edom;
Joab and all Israel had stayed there six months, until they had exterminated every male in Edom.
But Hadad had fled toward Egypt, with some Edomites who had been in his father's service; Hadad was then only a young boy.

Setting out from Midian, they had come to Paran; there they had taken men with them, then arrived in Egypt, before Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who gave Hadad a house, provided for his upkeep, and granted him lands.
Hadad found great favor with Pharaoh, so that he gave him as a wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Queen Tahpenes.
The sister of Tahpenes bore him a son, Genubath, whom Tahpenes raised in Pharaoh's palace; so Genubath lived in the palace, among Pharaoh's sons.
When Hadad heard in Egypt that David had lain down with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army was dead, he said to Pharaoh, "Let me go to my own country."
Pharaoh said to him, "What do you lack with me, that you should want to go to your own country?" He answered, "Nothing, but let me go all the same."
God raised up against Solomon another adversary: Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer, king of Zobah.
He had gathered men around him and become the leader of a band, when David slaughtered the troops of Zobah. These men went to Damascus, settled there, and reigned there.
Rezon was an adversary of Israel throughout Solomon's reign, adding to the harm that Hadad did; he detested Israel and reigned over Aram.
Jeroboam too raised his hand against the king. He was the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite from Zeredah; his mother, a widow, was named Zeruah; he was in Solomon's service.
This is why he rebelled against the king. Solomon was building the Millo and closing the breach in the city of David his father.
Now Jeroboam was an energetic and capable man; Solomon, seeing how this young man got his work done, put him in charge of all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.
At that time, as Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah of Shiloh met him on the way; Ahijah was wrapped in a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the open country.
Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces
and said to Jeroboam, "Take ten pieces for yourself. For thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I am about to tear the kingship from the hand of Solomon and give you ten tribes.
One tribe alone will remain to him, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I have chosen from among all the tribes of Israel.

For they have abandoned me, they have bowed down before Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, before Chemosh, the god of Moab, and before Milcom, the god of the sons of Ammon; they have not walked in my ways, they have not done what is right in my eyes, they have not kept my statutes and my rules, as David, the father of Solomon, did.
Yet I will not take the whole kingship from him; I will keep him as prince all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant, whom I chose and who kept my commandments and my statutes.
It is from the hand of his son that I will take the kingship, and I will give you ten tribes.
I will give one tribe to his son, so that David my servant may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city I have chosen to set my name there.
You, I will take you so that you may reign over all that your heart desires: you will be king over Israel.

If you listen to all that I command you, if you walk in my ways and do what is right in my eyes, keeping my statutes and my commandments as David my servant did, I will be with you, I will build you an enduring house as I built one for David, and I will give you Israel.
Thus I will humble the descendants of David because of this; but not forever."
Solomon then sought to put Jeroboam to death; but Jeroboam fled to Egypt, to Shishak, king of Egypt, and he stayed there until the death of Solomon.
As for the rest of the acts of Solomon, all that he did and his wisdom, is it not written in the book of the Acts of Solomon?
Solomon reigned forty years in Jerusalem over all Israel.
Then Solomon lay down with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father. Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it, he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon, and there he remained.
They sent for him. So Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel came and said to Rehoboam:
"Your father made our yoke heavy. Now you, lighten the harsh service and the heavy yoke that your father laid on us, and we will serve you."
He answered them, "Go away for three days, then come back to me." And the people went away.
King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon while he was alive: "What do you advise me to answer this people?"
They said to him, "If today you make yourself the servant of this people, if you yield to them and answer them with kind words, they will be your servants forever."
But Rehoboam rejected the advice the elders gave him and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and were now in his service.
He said to them, "What do you advise me to answer this people who ask me to lighten the yoke my father laid on them?"

The young men who had grown up with him replied, "This is what you shall say to this people who ask you to lighten the yoke your father laid on them: My little finger is thicker than my father's waist!
My father loaded you with a heavy yoke, and I will make your yoke heavier still; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with whips studded with spikes."
Three days later, Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam, as the king had ordered: Come back to me in three days.
The king answered the people harshly. Rejecting the advice of the elders,

he spoke to them according to the advice of the young men: "My father made your yoke heavy, and I will make your yoke heavier still; my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with whips studded with spikes."
So the king did not listen to the people; for this turn of events came from the Lord, to fulfill the word he had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah of Shiloh.

When all Israel saw that the king would not listen to them, they answered the king: "What share do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse! To your tents, Israel! And you, David, look after your own house!" And Israel went off to their tents.
So Rehoboam reigned only over the sons of Israel who lived in the towns of Judah.
King Rehoboam sent out Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam barely managed to mount his chariot and flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they sent for him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. No one followed the house of David except the tribe of Judah alone.

When Rehoboam reached Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingship to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
But the word of God came to Shemaiah, the man of God:
"Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people:

Thus says the Lord: Do not go up to make war on your brothers, the sons of Israel. Let everyone return home, for this thing has come from me." They obeyed the word of the Lord and turned back, as the Lord had said.
Jeroboam fortified Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and settled there; then he went out from there and fortified Penuel.
Jeroboam said to himself, "The kingdom might well return to the house of David.

If this people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the Lord at Jerusalem, their heart will turn back to their lord Rehoboam, king of Judah; they will kill me and go back to Rehoboam, king of Judah."
After taking counsel, the king made two golden calves and said to the people, "You have gone up to Jerusalem long enough! Israel, here are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt."
He set one of the calves at Bethel and put the other at Dan.
This became an occasion of sin: the people would go all the way to Dan to bow down before one of them.
Jeroboam also built shrines on the high places and appointed priests from among the people, who were not sons of Levi.

He instituted a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, in imitation of the feast kept in Judah, and he went up to the altar. This he did at Bethel, sacrificing to the calves he had made, and at Bethel he installed the priests of the high places he had appointed.

So he went up to the altar he had made at Bethel, on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, the month he had chosen on his own initiative; he instituted a feast for the sons of Israel and went up to the altar to burn incense.

titres.titre: The man of God against the altar at Bethel
The disobedience of the man of God

versets.t: Now a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the word of the Lord, just as Jeroboam was standing by the altar to burn incense.

At the Lord's command he cried out against the altar: "Altar, altar! Thus says the Lord: A son shall be born to the house of David, named Josiah; on you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and human bones will be burned on you."
That same day he gave a sign: "This is the sign that the Lord has spoken: this altar will be torn apart, and the ashes on it will be scattered."

When King Jeroboam heard the word that the man of God cried out against the altar at Bethel, he stretched out his hand over the altar and said, "Seize him!" But the hand he had stretched out against him withered, and he could not draw it back.
The altar was torn apart and its ashes scattered, according to the sign the man of God had given at the Lord's command.

The king said to the man of God, "Entreat the favor of the Lord your God, I beg you, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored to me." The man of God entreated the Lord, and the king's hand was restored to him and became as it was before.
The king said to the man of God, "Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a gift."
But the man of God answered the king, "Even if you gave me half your house, I would not go in with you; I will not eat bread or drink water in this place.
For this is the command the word of the Lord gave me: You shall not eat bread or drink water, and you shall not return by the way you came."
So he went off by another way and did not return by the way he had come to Bethel.

Now there was an old prophet living in Bethel. His sons came and told him all that the man of God had done that day at Bethel, and the words he had spoken to the king. When they had reported them to their father,
he asked them, "Which way did he go?" His sons had seen the way taken by the man of God who had come from Judah.
He said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." They saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it.
He set off after the man of God and found him sitting under a terebinth. He asked him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" He answered, "I am."
The prophet said to him, "Come home with me and eat some bread."
But he replied, "I cannot turn back with you or go in with you; I will not eat bread or drink water with you in this place,
for the word of the Lord told me: You shall not eat bread or drink water there, and you shall not return by the way you came."

The other said to him, "I too am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me at the Lord's command: Bring him back with you to your house, that he may eat bread and drink water." He was lying to him.
So the man of God went back with him, ate bread and drank water in his house.
While they were at table, the word of the Lord came to the prophet who had brought him back,
and he cried out to the man of God who had come from Judah: "Thus says the Lord: Because you have disobeyed the mouth of the Lord and have not kept the command the Lord your God gave you,
because you have come back to eat bread and drink water in the place of which he said, You shall not eat bread or drink water there, your body shall not enter the tomb of your fathers."
After he had eaten and drunk, the old prophet saddled the donkey for the prophet he had brought back.
He set off, but on the way a lion met him and killed him. His body lay stretched out on the road; the donkey stood beside it, and the lion too stood beside the body.
Some passersby saw the body lying on the road and the lion standing beside it, and they spoke of it when they came to the town where the old prophet lived.

When the prophet who had brought him back from the road heard of it, he said, "It is the man of God who disobeyed the mouth of the Lord; the Lord has given him to the lion, which has mauled him and killed him, according to the word the Lord had spoken to him."
Then he said to his sons, "Saddle the donkey for me." They saddled it,
he set off and found the body lying on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it; the lion had neither devoured the body nor mauled the donkey.
The prophet lifted up the body of the man of God, laid it on the donkey and brought it back to the town, to mourn for him and bury him.
He laid the body in his own tomb, and they mourned over him: "Alas, my brother!"
After burying him, he said to his sons, "When I die, bury me in the tomb where the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his.
For the word he cried out at the Lord's command against the altar at Bethel and against all the shrines of the high places in the towns of Samaria will surely come to pass."

Even after this, Jeroboam did not turn back from his evil way: once again he appointed priests of the high places from among the people; anyone who wished, he installed, and the man became a priest of the high places.
This was the sin of the house of Jeroboam, the cause of its ruin and its wiping out from the face of the earth.

titres.titre: The reign of Rehoboam in Judah

versets.t: At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam fell ill.

Jeroboam said to his wife, "Get up, disguise yourself so that no one will recognize the wife of Jeroboam, and go to Shiloh. That is where the prophet Ahijah is, the one who told me I would reign over this people.
Take ten loaves, some cakes and a jar of honey, and go to him: he will tell you what is to happen to the boy."
Jeroboam's wife did so: she got up, went to Shiloh and came to Ahijah's house. Now Ahijah could no longer see, for his eyes were dim with age.
But the Lord had said to Ahijah, "The wife of Jeroboam is coming to consult you about her son, who is ill. You shall say such and such to her. When she arrives, she will pretend to be someone else."
As soon as Ahijah heard the sound of her steps at the door, he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why pretend to be someone else? I have a harsh message for you.
Go and tell Jeroboam: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I raised you up from among the people and made you leader over my people Israel,

I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you; but you have not been like my servant David, who kept my commandments and followed me with all his heart, doing only what is right in my eyes.
You have done more evil than all who came before you: you have gone and made yourself other gods, idols of cast metal, to provoke me, and you have thrown me behind your back.

Therefore I am going to bring disaster on the house of Jeroboam; I will cut off from Jeroboam every male, slave or free, in Israel, and I will sweep away the house of Jeroboam as one sweeps away dung, until none of it is left.
Anyone belonging to the house of Jeroboam who dies in the town, the dogs will eat; anyone who dies in the open country, the birds of the sky will eat. For the Lord has spoken.
As for you, get up and go home: the moment your feet enter the town, the child will die.
All Israel will mourn for him and bury him; for of the house of Jeroboam he alone will be given a grave, because he alone is the one in whom the Lord, the God of Israel, has found something good.
The Lord will raise up for himself a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam. This is the day! Indeed, even now.

The Lord will strike Israel, as a reed sways in the water; he will uproot Israel from this good land he gave to their fathers and scatter them beyond the Euphrates, because they have made themselves sacred poles, provoking the Lord.
He will give Israel up because of the sins that Jeroboam committed and made Israel commit."
Jeroboam's wife got up and left for Tirzah. As she crossed the threshold of the house, the child died.
They buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word the Lord had spoken through his servant, the prophet Ahijah.
The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he waged war and how he reigned, are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel.
Jeroboam reigned twenty-two years, then lay down with his fathers. Nadab his son reigned in his place.

Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the Lord had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother's name was Naamah, the Ammonite.
Judah did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, and by the sins they committed they stirred up his jealousy more than their fathers had done.
They too built themselves high places, with standing stones and sacred poles, on every high hill and under every green tree.
There were even in the land men who prostituted themselves in the pagan cults. They imitated all the abominable practices of the nations the Lord had driven out before the sons of Israel.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt marched against Jerusalem.
He seized the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the royal palace: he took everything, even the gold shields Solomon had made.
In their place King Rehoboam made shields of bronze, which he entrusted to the commanders of the guard who watched the entrance of the palace.
Whenever the king went to the house of the Lord, the guards carried them, then brought them back to the guardroom.
The rest of the acts of Rehoboam, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
There was continual war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.
Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried beside them in the city of David. His mother's name was Naamah, the Ammonite. Abijam his son reigned in his place.
In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijam became king of Judah.
He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Maacah, daughter of Absalom.
He gave himself over to all the sins his father had committed before him, and his heart was not wholly with the Lord his God, as the heart of David his father had been.
But for David's sake the Lord his God left him a lamp in Jerusalem, raising up a son after him and keeping Jerusalem secure.
For David had done what is right in the eyes of the Lord and had not turned aside, all his life, from any of his commandments, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam as long as they lived.
The rest of the acts of Abijam, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah? There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
Abijam lay down with his fathers and was buried in the city of David. Asa his son reigned in his place.
In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa became king of Judah.
He reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem. His grandmother's name was Maacah, daughter of Absalom.
Asa did what is right in the eyes of the Lord, like David his ancestor.
He drove the male cult prostitutes out of the land and did away with all the idols his fathers had made.
He even removed his grandmother Maacah from her rank as queen mother, because she had set up an obscene image for Ashtoreth. Asa cut down her image and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
The high places, it is true, did not disappear; but Asa's heart was wholly with the Lord all his life.
He brought into the house of the Lord what his father and he himself had consecrated: silver, gold and vessels.
There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel as long as they lived.
Baasha king of Israel marched against Judah and fortified Ramah, to block the movements of Asa king of Judah.

Then Asa took all the silver and gold left in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the royal palace; he handed them to his servants and sent them to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon son of Hezion, king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, with this message:

"Let there be an alliance between me and you, as between my father and your father. Here, I am sending you a gift of silver and gold: go, break your alliance with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."
Ben-hadad listened to King Asa: he sent his army commanders against the towns of Israel and struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah and all Chinneroth, along with the whole land of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard of it, he stopped fortifying Ramah and stayed at Tirzah.
King Asa summoned all Judah, exempting no one: they carried off the stones and timber with which Baasha had been fortifying Ramah, and with them King Asa fortified Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

The rest of all the acts of Asa, all his exploits, all that he did and the towns he built, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah? Only, in his old age, his feet became diseased.
Asa lay down with his fathers and was buried beside them in the city of David his ancestor. Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.
Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned two years over Israel.
He did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord: he followed the way of his father and the sin into which he had led Israel.
Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him and struck him down at Gibbethon, a Philistine town that Nadab and all Israel were besieging.
Baasha put him to death in the third year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place.
When he became king, he struck down the whole house of Jeroboam; he left not a soul alive, wiping them out, according to the word the Lord had spoken through his servant Ahijah of Shiloh,
because of the sins Jeroboam had committed and made Israel commit, thereby provoking the Lord, the God of Israel.
The rest of the acts of Nadab, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel as long as they lived.
In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel at Tirzah; he reigned twenty-four years.
He did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord: he followed the way of Jeroboam and the sin into which he had led Israel.
The word of the Lord came to Jehu son of Hanani, against Baasha:
"I raised you up from the dust and made you leader over my people Israel; but you have followed the way of Jeroboam and have made my people Israel sin, provoking me with their sins.
Therefore I am about to sweep away Baasha and his house; I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat.
Anyone belonging to the house of Baasha who dies in the town, the dogs will eat; anyone of his who dies in the open country, the birds of the sky will eat."
The rest of the acts of Baasha, what he did and his exploits, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Baasha lay down with his fathers and was buried at Tirzah. Elah his son reigned in his place.

The word of the Lord, through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani, had been directed against Baasha and his house, because of all the evil he had done in the eyes of the Lord, provoking him by the work of his hands, imitating the house of Jeroboam, and also because he had wiped out that house.
In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel at Tirzah; he reigned two years.
His servant Zimri, commander of half the chariots, conspired against him. Elah was at Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, the steward of the royal palace at Tirzah.
Zimri came in, struck him down and killed him, in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah; and he reigned in his place.
As soon as he was king, seated on his throne, he struck down the whole house of Baasha: he did not leave him a single male, whether kinsman or friend.
So Zimri wiped out the whole house of Baasha, according to the word the Lord had spoken against Baasha through the prophet Jehu,
because of all the sins that Baasha and his son Elah had committed and made Israel commit, provoking with their idols the Lord, the God of Israel.
The rest of the acts of Elah, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigned seven days at Tirzah. The people were then encamped against Gibbethon, a Philistine town.
When the people who were encamped heard that Zimri had conspired and killed the king, that very day, in the camp, all Israel proclaimed Omri, the army commander, king.
Omri, with all Israel, went up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah.
When Zimri saw that the town was taken, he withdrew into the keep of the royal palace, burned the palace down over himself, and died,
because of the sins he had committed in doing what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, in following the way of Jeroboam and the sin into which he had led Israel.
The rest of the acts of Zimri and the conspiracy he plotted, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Then the people of Israel were divided in two: half followed Tibni son of Ginath, to make him king, the other half followed Omri.
Omri's supporters prevailed over those of Tibni son of Ginath. Tibni died, and Omri became king.
In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri became king of Israel; he reigned twelve years, six of them at Tirzah.
Then he bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer for about sixty-eight kilograms of silver; he built a town on the hill and called it Samaria, after the name of Shemer, the former owner of the hill.
Omri did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, acting more wickedly than all his predecessors.
He followed in everything the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat and the sin into which he had led Israel, provoking with their idols the Lord, the God of Israel.
The rest of the acts of Omri, what he did and the exploits he accomplished, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Omri lay down with his fathers and was buried at Samaria. Ahab his son reigned in his place.
Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, and he reigned twenty-two years over Israel at Samaria.
Ahab son of Omri did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, more than all his predecessors.

As if it were too little for him to give himself over to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, he took as his wife Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians; he went and served Baal and bowed down before him.
He set up an altar to Baal in the temple of Baal that he built at Samaria,
and Ahab also set up a sacred pole. Ahab did more to provoke the Lord, the God of Israel, than all the kings of Israel before him.

In his time Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho: he laid its foundations at the cost of Abiram his firstborn, and set up its gates at the cost of Segub his youngest, according to the word the Lord had spoken through Joshua son of Nun.

titres.titre: Elijah and the widow of Zarephath

versets.t: Elijah the Tishbite, of Gilead, said to Ahab: "As the Lord lives, the God of Israel before whom I stand: there will be neither dew nor rain these years, except at my word."
The word of the Lord came to him:
"Leave this place, head eastward and hide by the Wadi Cherith, east of the Jordan.
You shall drink from the wadi, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there."
He set out and did according to the word of the Lord: he went and settled by the Wadi Cherith, east of the Jordan.
The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the wadi.
But after some time the wadi dried up, for no rain had fallen in the land.
Then the word of the Lord came to him:
"Get up, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and stay there; I have commanded a widow there to feed you."
He got up and went to Zarephath. As he arrived at the town gate, a widow was there gathering wood. He called to her and said, "Fetch me a little water in a jar, I beg you, that I may drink."
She was going to fetch it when he called after her, "Bring me a piece of bread too, I beg you, in your hand."

She answered, "As the Lord your God lives, I have nothing baked! Only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug. Here I am gathering a couple of sticks to go in and prepare this last bit, for myself and my son; we will eat it, and then we will die."
Elijah said to her, "Do not be afraid. Go and do as you have said; only, first make me a little cake from it and bring it to me, then make some for yourself and your son.
For thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: The jar of flour will not run out, the jug of oil will not fail, until the day the Lord sends rain on the land."
She went and did as Elijah had said; and for a long time she had food to eat, she, her household and Elijah.
The jar of flour did not run out, the jug of oil did not fail, according to the word the Lord had spoken through Elijah.
After these events, the son of the mistress of the house fell ill; his illness was so severe that no breath was left in him.
The woman then said to Elijah, "What do you want with me, man of God? Have you come to me to bring my sins to mind and put my son to death?"
He answered her, "Give me your son." He took him from his mother's arms, carried him up to the upper room where he was staying and laid him on his own bed.
Then he cried out to the Lord: "Lord my God, will you bring disaster even on this widow who is sheltering me, by putting her son to death?"
He stretched himself out three times over the child and cried out to the Lord: "Lord my God, I beg you, let this child's breath return to him!"
The Lord heard the voice of Elijah: the child's breath returned to him, and he came back to life.
Elijah took the child, brought him down from the upper room into the house and gave him to his mother: "See, your son is alive."
The woman said to Elijah, "Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the Lord in your mouth is truth."

titres.titre: The challenge of the prophets of Baal
The fire of the Lord and the rain

versets.t: Many days passed, and the word of the Lord came to Elijah, in the third year: "Go and present yourself before Ahab, and I will send rain on the land."
Elijah went to present himself before Ahab. The famine had become severe in Samaria.
Ahab summoned Obadiah, the steward of his palace. Now Obadiah greatly feared the Lord:
when Jezebel was massacring the prophets of the Lord, Obadiah had taken a hundred prophets and hidden them in groups of fifty in caves, where he fed them with bread and water.
Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go through the land, to all the springs and all the wadis: perhaps we will find grass to keep the horses and mules alive, and not have to slaughter any livestock."
They divided the land between them to go through it: Ahab went one way alone, Obadiah another way alone.
As Obadiah was on his way, suddenly Elijah came to meet him. Recognizing him, he fell face down and said, "Is it really you, my lord Elijah?"
He answered him, "It is I. Go tell your master: Here is Elijah."
Obadiah said, "What sin have I committed, that you would hand your servant over to Ahab to put me to death?

As the Lord your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my master has not sent to look for you; and when they answered, He is not here, he made the kingdom or the nation swear that you had not been found.
And now you tell me: Go tell your master: Here is Elijah!

But no sooner will I have left you than the Spirit of the Lord will carry you off I know not where; I will go to warn Ahab, he will not find you, and he will kill me. Yet your servant has feared the Lord from his youth.
Has it not been reported to my lord what I did when Jezebel was massacring the prophets of the Lord? I hid a hundred of them, in groups of fifty, in caves, and fed them with bread and water.
And now you tell me: Go tell your master: Here is Elijah! He will kill me."
But Elijah replied, "As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand: this very day I will present myself before Ahab."
So Obadiah went to meet Ahab and warned him, and Ahab came to meet Elijah.
As soon as he caught sight of Elijah, Ahab said to him, "So it is you, the scourge of Israel!"
Elijah answered, "It is not I who am the scourge of Israel; it is you and your father's house, by abandoning the commandments of the Lord to follow the Baals.
Now have all Israel gathered to me at Mount Carmel, with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of Ashtoreth who eat at Jezebel's table."
Ahab sent word to all the sons of Israel and gathered the prophets at Mount Carmel.
Elijah approached all the people and said, "How long will you go limping on both legs? If the Lord is God, follow him; if it is Baal, follow him!" And the people answered him not a word.
Elijah said again to the people, "I am the only prophet of the Lord left, while the prophets of Baal are four hundred and fifty.

Let two bulls be given to us; let them choose one for themselves, cut it up and lay it on the wood, without setting fire to it; and I will prepare the other bull, lay it on the wood, without setting fire to it.
Then you will call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the Lord: the god who answers by fire, he is God." All the people answered, "Well said!"
Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "Choose one of the bulls for yourselves and prepare it first, since you are the more numerous; then call on the name of your god, but do not set fire to it."

They took the bull that was given them and prepared it; and they called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, crying, "Baal, answer us!" But there was no voice, no answer. And they danced around the altar they had made.
At noon Elijah mocked them: "Cry louder! He is a god! No doubt he is absorbed, or busy, or on a journey; perhaps he is asleep, and will wake up."
They cried louder and, according to their custom, gashed themselves with swords and lances until the blood streamed down over them.
When noon was past, they raved on until the hour of the evening offering; but there was no voice, no answer, no sign of attention.
Then Elijah said to all the people, "Come here to me." All the people came to him, and he repaired the altar of the Lord, which had been torn down.
Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the Lord had said: Israel shall be your name.
With these stones he built an altar in the name of the Lord; around the altar he dug a trench large enough to hold about fifteen litres of seed.
He arranged the wood, cut up the bull and laid it on the wood.
Then he said, "Fill four jars with water and pour it over the burnt offering and over the wood." He said, "Do it again," and they did it again. He said, "A third time," and they did it a third time.
The water ran all around the altar, and he even had the trench filled with water.

At the hour of the evening offering, the prophet Elijah stepped forward and said, "Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, let it be known today that you are God in Israel, that I am your servant, and that it is by your word that I have done all this.
Answer me, Lord, answer me, so that this people may know that you, Lord, are God, and that it is you who turn their hearts back!"
Then the fire of the Lord fell: it devoured the burnt offering, the wood, the stones and the dust, and licked up the water in the trench.
At this sight, all the people fell face down, crying, "The Lord is God! The Lord is God!"
Elijah said to them, "Seize the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape!" They seized them; Elijah brought them down to the Wadi Kishon, where he slaughtered them.
Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up, eat and drink, for there is the rumble of rain."
Ahab went up to eat and drink; but Elijah climbed to the top of Carmel, bent down to the ground and put his face between his knees.
He said to his servant, "Go up, look toward the sea." The servant went up, looked and said, "There is nothing." Seven times Elijah told him, "Go back."

The seventh time, the servant said, "There is a little cloud, like the palm of a hand, rising from the sea." Elijah said, "Go tell Ahab: Harness your chariot and go down, so that the rain does not stop you."
In an instant the sky grew dark with clouds, the wind rose, and a heavy rain fell. Ahab mounted his chariot and set off for Jezreel.
The hand of the Lord was on Elijah: he girded his loins and ran ahead of Ahab all the way to the entrance of Jezreel.

titres.titre: The Lord in the gentle breeze

versets.t: Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and how he had killed all the prophets with the sword.
Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, "May the gods deal with me with the utmost severity, if by this time tomorrow I have not made your life like the life of one of them!"
Elijah was afraid; he got up and fled for his life. When he reached Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, he left his servant there
and went a day's journey into the wilderness. He came and sat down under a broom tree and asked to die: "It is enough, Lord! Now take my life, for I am no better than my fathers."
Then he lay down and fell asleep under the broom tree. But suddenly an angel touched him and said, "Get up, eat."
He looked: at his head there was a cake baked on hot stones and a jug of water. He ate, drank, and lay down again.
The angel of the Lord came back a second time, touched him and said, "Get up, eat, for the journey is too long for you."
He got up, ate and drank; then, strengthened by that food, he walked forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God.
There he entered the cave and spent the night. Now the word of the Lord came to him: "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

He answered, "I have been filled with burning zeal for the Lord, the God of hosts; for the sons of Israel have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars and killed your prophets with the sword. I alone am left, and they are seeking to take my life."

The Lord said, "Go out and stand on the mountain, before the Lord, for the Lord is about to pass by." And behold: before the Lord, a great and mighty wind tore the mountains apart and shattered the rocks; but the Lord was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
After the earthquake, a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire. And after the fire, the murmur of a gentle breeze.
When he heard it, Elijah wrapped his face in his cloak, went out and stood at the entrance of the cave. And behold, a voice came to him: "What are you doing here, Elijah?"

He answered, "I have been filled with burning zeal for the Lord, the God of hosts; for the sons of Israel have abandoned your covenant, torn down your altars and killed your prophets with the sword. I alone am left, and they are seeking to take my life."
The Lord said to him, "Go back on your way toward the wilderness of Damascus. When you arrive, you shall anoint Hazael as king over Aram;
you shall anoint Jehu son of Nimshi as king over Israel, and you shall anoint Elisha son of Shaphat, of Abel-meholah, as prophet in your place.
Whoever escapes the sword of Hazael, Jehu will put to death; whoever escapes the sword of Jehu, Elisha will put to death.
But I will keep for myself in Israel seven thousand men: all those whose knees have not bent before Baal and whose mouths have not kissed him."
Leaving there, Elijah found Elisha son of Shaphat plowing: twelve pairs of oxen were going before him, and he was driving the twelfth. Elijah passed by him and threw his cloak over him.
Elisha left the oxen, ran after Elijah and said, "Let me kiss my father and mother goodbye, and I will follow you." Elijah answered him, "Go, turn back! But remember what I have done to you."

Elisha left him, took the pair of oxen and offered them in sacrifice; with the wood of the yoke he cooked their flesh and gave it to his people to eat. Then he got up, followed Elijah and entered his service.

titres.titre: The second campaign of the Arameans

versets.t: Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered his whole army; he had with him thirty-two kings, along with horses and chariots. He marched up, laid siege to Samaria and attacked it.
He sent messengers into the city, to Ahab king of Israel,
to say to him, "Thus says Ben-hadad: Your silver and your gold are mine, your wives and your finest sons are mine."
The king of Israel answered, "As you say, my lord king: I am yours, I and all that I have."
The messengers came back and said, "Thus says Ben-hadad: I sent to you to demand your silver and your gold, your wives and your sons;
well then, tomorrow at this time I will send my servants to search your house and the houses of your servants, and they will lay hands on everything precious to you and carry it off."

The king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said, "See, recognize that this man is seeking our ruin! He demanded my wives and my sons, my silver and my gold, and I did not refuse them to him."
All the elders and all the people said to him, "Do not listen, do not agree."

So he answered Ben-hadad's messengers, "Tell my lord the king: All that you demanded of your servant the first time I will do; but this thing I cannot do." The messengers went off to carry back the reply.
Ben-hadad sent word to him, "May the gods deal with me with the utmost severity, if there is enough dust left in Samaria to fill the hand of all the people who follow me!"
The king of Israel answered, "Tell him: Let not the one who buckles on his belt boast like the one who unbuckles it!"
On hearing this reply, Ben-hadad, who was drinking with the kings in the tents, said to his servants, "To your posts!" And they took up position against the city.
Now a prophet approached Ahab king of Israel and said, "Thus says the Lord: Do you see all this great multitude? This very day I am giving it into your hands, and you will know that I am the Lord."
Ahab asked, "By whom?" He answered, "Thus says the Lord: By the cadets of the provincial commanders." Ahab said, "Who will open the battle?" He answered, "You."
Ahab reviewed the cadets of the provincial commanders: they were two hundred and thirty-two. After them he reviewed the whole army, all the sons of Israel: they were seven thousand.
They made a sortie at noon, while Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk in the tents, he and the thirty-two kings who had come to his aid.
The cadets of the provincial commanders went out first. Ben-hadad sent out scouts, and they reported to him, "Men have come out of Samaria."
He said, "If they have come out for peace, take them alive; if they have come out for battle, take them alive."
Now, as soon as they had come out of the city, these cadets of the provincial commanders, followed by the army,
each struck down his man; the Arameans took flight, and Israel pursued them. Ben-hadad king of Aram escaped on horseback, with some horsemen.
The king of Israel went out, cut down the horses and chariots, and inflicted a great defeat on the Arameans.

Then the prophet approached the king of Israel and said to him, "Go, strengthen yourself; consider carefully what you must do, for at the turn of the year the king of Aram will march up against you again."

The servants of the king of Aram said to him, "Their God is a God of the mountains; that is why they were stronger than us. But let us fight them on the plain, and surely we will be stronger than they.
Do this too: remove each of these kings from his post and replace them with governors;
raise an army equal to the one you lost, with as many horses and chariots. Let us fight them on the plain, and surely we will be stronger than they." He listened to their advice and did so.
At the turn of the year, Ben-hadad reviewed the Arameans and marched up to Aphek to fight Israel.
The sons of Israel, reviewed as well and provisioned, advanced to meet them. The sons of Israel camped opposite them, like two small flocks of goats, while the Arameans filled the countryside.

The man of God approached and said to the king of Israel, "Thus says the Lord: Because the Arameans have said that the Lord is a God of the mountains and not a God of the valleys, I will give this whole great multitude into your hands, and you will know that I am the Lord."
They camped seven days facing one another. On the seventh day the battle was joined, and the sons of Israel killed a hundred thousand Aramean foot soldiers in a single day.
The rest fled to Aphek, into the city, where the wall collapsed on twenty-seven thousand survivors. Ben-hadad also fled and took refuge in the city, going from room to room.

His servants said to him, "We have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful kings. Let us put sackcloth on our loins and ropes on our heads, and go out to the king of Israel: perhaps he will spare your life."
They put sackcloth on their loins and ropes on their heads, went to the king of Israel and said, "Your servant Ben-hadad asks: Spare my life!" Ahab answered, "Is he still alive? He is my brother!"
The men took this as a good omen and hastened to take him at his word: "Yes, Ben-hadad is your brother!" Ahab said, "Go and get him." Ben-hadad came out to him, and Ahab had him mount his chariot.

Ben-hadad said to him, "I give back to you the towns my father took from yours, and you may set up your trading quarters in Damascus, as my father did in Samaria." Ahab answered, "And I, I let you go with this treaty." He made a covenant with him and let him go.
Now one of the sons of the prophets said to his companion, at the Lord's command, "Strike me, I beg you." But the man refused to strike him.
He said to him, "Because you have not obeyed the voice of the Lord, behold: as soon as you leave me, a lion will strike you down." The man left him, and a lion, meeting him, struck him down.
The prophet found another man and said, "Strike me, I beg you." This one struck him and wounded him.
The prophet went and stationed himself on the king's road, disguised, with a bandage over his eyes.

As the king passed by, he called out to him, "Your servant had gone out into the thick of the battle, when a man came and handed me a prisoner, saying: Guard this man; if he goes missing, you will pay with your life for his, or you will pay out about thirty-four kilograms of silver.
But while your servant was busy here and there, the man disappeared." The king of Israel said to him, "That is your sentence: you have pronounced it yourself."
At once the prophet took the bandage from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized that he was one of the prophets.
The prophet said to him, "Thus says the Lord: Because you have let slip from your hand the man I had devoted to destruction, you will pay with your life for his, and with your people for his people."
Sullen and angry, the king of Israel went home and came to Samaria.
After these events, this happened. Naboth of Jezreel had a vineyard at Jezreel, next to the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.
Ahab said to Naboth, "Give me your vineyard to make into a vegetable garden, since it adjoins my house; I will give you a better vineyard in exchange or, if you prefer, its worth in money."
But Naboth answered Ahab, "The Lord forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers!"
Ahab went home, sullen and angry at the answer Naboth of Jezreel had given him: "I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers." He lay down on his bed, turned his face away and refused to eat.
His wife Jezebel came to him and said, "Why is your spirit so sullen, and why do you not eat?"

He answered her, "I spoke to Naboth of Jezreel; I told him: Give me your vineyard for money, or, if you prefer, I will give you another vineyard in its place. But he answered: I will not give you my vineyard."
Jezebel his wife said to him, "Is it you, or is it not, who exercise kingship over Israel? Get up, eat, and let your heart be glad: I myself will give you the vineyard of Naboth of Jezreel."
She wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with the royal seal, and sent them to the elders and nobles of the town where Naboth lived.
This is what she wrote: "Proclaim a fast and place Naboth at the head of the people.
Set opposite him two scoundrels who will testify against him: You have cursed God and the king! Then take him outside, stone him, and let him die."
The men of Naboth's town, the elders and nobles who lived there, did as Jezebel had ordered them, as was written in the letters she had sent them.
They proclaimed a fast and placed Naboth at the head of the people.
The two scoundrels came and sat opposite him and testified against Naboth before the people: "Naboth has cursed God and the king!" They took him outside the town, stoned him, and he died.
Then they sent word to Jezebel: "Naboth has been stoned, he is dead."

As soon as Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, she said to Ahab, "Get up, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth of Jezreel, which he refused to give you for money: Naboth is no longer alive, he is dead."
When he heard that Naboth was dead, Ahab got up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth of Jezreel and take possession of it.
Then the word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite:
"Get up, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who lives in Samaria: he is there in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession of it.

You shall say to him: Thus says the Lord: You have murdered, and now you take possession! Then you shall say to him: Thus says the Lord: In the very place where the dogs licked up the blood of Naboth, the dogs will also lick up your blood."
Ahab said to Elijah, "So you have found me out, my enemy?" He answered, "I have found you out. Because you have sold yourself to do what is evil in the eyes of the Lord,
behold, I am bringing disaster upon you: I will sweep you away, I will cut off from Ahab every male, slave or free, in Israel,
and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because you have provoked me to anger and made Israel sin.
Against Jezebel too the Lord has spoken: The dogs will devour Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel.
Anyone belonging to the house of Ahab who dies in the town, the dogs will eat; anyone who dies in the open country, the birds of the sky will eat."
Truly, there was never anyone like Ahab for selling himself to do what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, urged on by Jezebel his wife.
He behaved in the most abominable way, following idols, as the Amorites had done, whom the Lord had driven out before the sons of Israel.
When he heard these words, Ahab tore his clothes, put sackcloth on his bare skin and fasted; he slept in the sackcloth and walked with slow steps.
The word of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite:

"Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the disaster in his lifetime; it is in the lifetime of his son that I will bring the disaster on his house."

titres.titre: The death of Ahab at Ramoth

versets.t: For three years they remained without war between Aram and Israel.
In the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to the king of Israel.
The king of Israel said to his servants, "Do you know that Ramoth-gilead belongs to us? And we are doing nothing to take it back from the king of Aram!"
He said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you come with me to fight at Ramoth-gilead?" Jehoshaphat answered the king of Israel, "I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."
Then Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "First, I beg you, consult the word of the Lord."

The king of Israel gathered the prophets, about four hundred, and asked them, "Shall I go to fight at Ramoth-gilead, or shall I give it up?" They answered, "Go up, the Lord will give it into the hand of the king."
But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no longer here a prophet of the Lord, through whom we may consult him?"

The king of Israel answered Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we could consult the Lord; but I hate him, for he never prophesies anything good about me, only evil: it is Micaiah son of Imlah." Jehoshaphat said, "Let the king not speak so!"
The king of Israel called a eunuch and said to him, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly."

The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting each on his throne, in royal robes, on a threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had made himself iron horns and said, "Thus says the Lord: With these horns you will gore the Arameans until they are destroyed."
And all the prophets prophesied the same: "Go up to Ramoth-gilead, you will win: the Lord will give it into the hand of the king."
The messenger who had gone to fetch Micaiah said to him, "See, with one voice the prophets are foretelling success to the king; let your word be like the word of each of them: foretell success."
Micaiah answered, "As the Lord lives, I will speak what the Lord tells me."
He came to the king, who asked him, "Micaiah, shall we go to fight at Ramoth-gilead, or shall we give it up?" He answered, "Go up, you will win: the Lord will give it into the hand of the king."
The king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear to tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the Lord?"
Micaiah answered, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep without a shepherd, and the Lord said: These people have no master any longer; let everyone go home in peace."
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you? He prophesies nothing good about me, only evil."
Micaiah went on, "Hear then the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord seated on his throne, with all the host of heaven standing near him, on his right and on his left.
The Lord said: Who will deceive Ahab, so that he goes up to Ramoth-gilead and falls there? One answered one way, another another way.
Then a spirit came forward, stood before the Lord and said: I will deceive him. The Lord asked him: How?
He answered: I will go and become a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. The Lord said: You will deceive him, you will succeed; go, do so.
And now, behold, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours; but the Lord has pronounced disaster against you."
Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came up, struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, "Which way did the Spirit of the Lord pass from me to speak to you?"
Micaiah answered, "You will see on the day you go from room to room to hide yourself."
The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and hand him over to Amon, governor of the city, and to Joash, the king's son.
You shall tell them: Thus says the king: Put this man in prison and feed him on bread of misery and water of misery, until I return in peace."
Micaiah said, "If you really return in peace, then the Lord has not spoken through me." And he added, "Hear, all you peoples!"
The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself to go into battle; you, keep your royal robes." And the king of Israel disguised himself before going into battle.
Now the king of Aram had given this order to his thirty-two chariot commanders: "Attack neither small nor great, but only the king of Israel."
When the chariot commanders caught sight of Jehoshaphat, they said, "Surely that is the king of Israel!" and they turned to attack him. But Jehoshaphat cried out,
and the chariot commanders, seeing that he was not the king of Israel, turned back from him.
Then a man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the pieces of his armor. The king said to his charioteer, "Turn around and take me out of the battle, for I am wounded."
The battle raged that day. The king remained standing in his chariot, facing the Arameans, and he died in the evening; the blood from the wound had run into the bottom of the chariot.
At sunset this cry ran through the camp: "Everyone to his own town, everyone to his own land!"
So the king died; he was brought back to Samaria, where he was buried.
They washed the chariot at the pool of Samaria: the dogs licked up Ahab's blood and the prostitutes bathed there, according to the word the Lord had spoken.
The rest of the acts of Ahab, all that he did, the ivory palace he built and all the towns he fortified, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Ahab lay down with his fathers. Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king of Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah, daughter of Shilhi.
He followed in everything the way of his father Asa, without turning aside from it, doing what is right in the eyes of the Lord.
Only, the high places did not disappear: the people continued to offer sacrifices and incense there.
Jehoshaphat was at peace with the king of Israel.
