The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, the exploits he accomplished and the wars he waged, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
He rid the land of the rest of the male cult prostitutes who were still there in the time of Asa his father.
There was then no king in Edom; a governor ruled in place of a king.
Jehoshaphat built ships of Tarshish to go and fetch gold from Ophir; but they never sailed, for they were wrecked at Ezion-geber.
Then Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, "Let my servants go with yours on the ships." But Jehoshaphat refused.
Jehoshaphat lay down with his fathers and was buried beside them in the city of David his ancestor. Joram his son reigned in his place.
Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel at Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah; he reigned two years over Israel.
He did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, following the way of his father and that of his mother, as well as the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had made Israel sin.
He served Baal and bowed down before him, provoking the Lord, the God of Israel, exactly as his father had done.
After the death of Ahab, Moab rebelled against Israel.

Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and was injured. He sent messengers with these orders: "Go and consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will recover from this injury."

But the angel of the Lord said to Elijah the Tishbite: "Get up and go to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say to them: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?
Therefore this is what the Lord says: You will not leave the bed you have taken to; you will surely die." And Elijah went off.
The messengers returned to the king, who asked them, "Why have you come back?"

They answered him: "A man came up to meet us and told us: Go back to the king who sent you and say to him: This is what the Lord says: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you send to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you will not leave the bed you have taken to; you will surely die."
The king asked them, "What did the man look like who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?"
They answered, "He was a man in a garment of hair, with a leather belt around his waist." The king said, "It is Elijah the Tishbite."
At once he sent to him a captain with his company of fifty men. The captain went up to Elijah, who was sitting on the top of a hill, and said to him, "Man of God, the king commands: Come down!"
Elijah answered the captain, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men!" And fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.
The king sent another captain to him, with his fifty. This one spoke up: "Man of God, this is what the king commands: Hurry, come down!"
Elijah answered, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men!" And the fire of God came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.

The king sent yet a third captain with his fifty. This third captain went up, fell on his knees before Elijah, and pleaded with him: "Man of God, let my life and the lives of these fifty men, your servants, be precious in your sight!
Fire came down from heaven and consumed the first two captains and their fifties; but now, let my life be precious in your sight!"
The angel of the Lord said to Elijah, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of him." So Elijah got up and went down with him to the king.

He said to him: "This is what the Lord says: Because you sent messengers to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, as if there were no God in Israel whose word you could consult, therefore you will not leave the bed you have taken to; you will surely die."
Ahaziah died, according to the word the Lord had spoken through Elijah. Since he had no son, Joram became king in his place, in the second year of Joram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.
As for the rest of the acts of Ahaziah, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
This is how the Lord took Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind. Elijah and Elisha were setting out from Gilgal.

Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here, I beg you, for the Lord is sending me as far as Bethel." But Elisha answered, "As the Lord lives and as you live, I will not leave you!" So they went down to Bethel.
The sons of the prophets at Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the Lord is going to take your master away from you?" He answered, "Yes, I know it too; be quiet."
Elijah said to him, "Elisha, stay here, I beg you, for the Lord is sending me to Jericho." He answered, "As the Lord lives and as you live, I will not leave you!" So they came to Jericho.
The sons of the prophets at Jericho came up to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the Lord is going to take your master away from you?" He answered, "Yes, I know it too; be quiet."
Elijah said to him, "Stay here, I beg you, for the Lord is sending me to the Jordan." He answered, "As the Lord lives and as you live, I will not leave you!" So the two of them went on together.
Fifty of the sons of the prophets followed and stood at a distance, facing them, while the two of them stopped at the edge of the Jordan.
Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the water, which parted to the one side and the other; and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
Once they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I should do for you before I am taken from you." Elisha answered, "Let a double share of your spirit come to me!"
Elijah said, "You have asked a difficult thing. If you see me at the moment I am taken from you, it will be granted to you; if not, it will not."
They were still walking on and talking together when a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah went up to heaven in the whirlwind.
Elisha, who was watching, cried out, "My father, my father, chariot of Israel and its horsemen!" Then he saw him no more. So he took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two.
He picked up the cloak that had fallen from Elijah, came back, and stood at the edge of the Jordan.

With the cloak that had fallen from Elijah, he struck the water and said, "Where is the Lord, the God of Elijah?" When he had struck the water, it parted to the one side and the other, and Elisha crossed over.
The sons of the prophets from Jericho, who were opposite, saw him and said, "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha." They came to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.

They said to him: "Among your servants there are fifty strong men; let them go and search for your master. Perhaps the Spirit of the Lord has carried him off and set him down on some mountain or in some valley." He answered, "Do not send anyone."
But they pressed him until he was embarrassed, and he said, "Send them." So they sent fifty men, who searched for Elijah for three days without finding him.
They came back to Elisha, who had stayed at Jericho, and he said to them, "Did I not tell you not to go?"
The people of the city said to Elisha, "The site of the city is good, as my lord can see, but the water is bad and the land is unfruitful."
He said, "Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it." They brought it to him,
and he went out to the spring of water, threw the salt into it, and said, "This is what the Lord says: I have made this water wholesome; from it there will come no more death or barrenness."
And the water has been wholesome to this day, according to the word Elisha had spoken.
From there he went up to Bethel. As he was going up the road, some young boys came out of the town and jeered at him, shouting, "Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!"
He turned around, looked at them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord. Then two she-bears came out of the forest and mauled forty-two of the children.
From there he went on to Mount Carmel, and then he returned to Samaria.

titres.titre: Joram of Israel and the war with Moab

versets.t: Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel at Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, though not as far as his father and mother had gone: he did away with the sacred pillar of Baal that his father had set up.
But he clung to the sins into which Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel, and he did not turn away from them.
Mesha, king of Moab, was a sheep-breeder; he used to pay the king of Israel a tribute of a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.
But when Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
That day King Joram set out from Samaria and mustered all Israel.

Then he sent word to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah: "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you come with me to fight against Moab?" He answered, "I will go up; I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."
Then he asked, "By which road shall we go up?" Joram answered, "By the road through the wilderness of Edom."
So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out. After a roundabout march of seven days, there was no water left for the army or for the animals that followed them.
Then the king of Israel said, "Alas! The Lord has called these three kings together to hand them over to Moab!"

But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no prophet of the Lord here, through whom we may consult him?" One of the servants of the king of Israel answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here, the one who used to pour water on the hands of Elijah."
Jehoshaphat said, "The word of the Lord is with him." So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom went down to him.

Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father and the prophets of your mother!" The king of Israel answered, "No, for it is the Lord who has called these three kings together to hand them over to Moab."
Elisha replied: "As the Lord of hosts lives, before whom I stand: were it not for my regard for Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, I would pay no attention to you, I would not even look at you.
Now bring me a harpist." And while the musician played, the hand of the Lord came upon Elisha.
He said: "This is what the Lord says: Dig this valley full of trenches upon trenches.
For this is what the Lord says: You will see neither wind nor rain, yet this valley will be filled with water; and you will drink, you, your flocks, and your animals.
But this is a small thing in the sight of the Lord: he will also hand Moab over to you.
You will strike every fortified city and every choice town, you will cut down every fruit tree, stop up every spring, and ruin every good field with stones."
In the morning, at the hour when the offering is presented, water came by the road from Edom, and the land was filled with it.
Now all the Moabites had heard that the kings were coming up to attack them; every man able to bear arms, and even beyond, was called up, and they took their stand at the border.
When they rose early in the morning and the sun shone on the water, the Moabites saw the water opposite them red as blood.
They said, "This is blood! The kings must have fought and killed one another! Now to the plunder, Moab!"
But when they reached the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and struck the Moabites, who fled before them; and they pushed on into the country, striking down Moab.

They destroyed the cities; on every good field each man threw his stone until it was covered; they stopped up every spring and cut down every fruit tree. Only the stones of Kir-hareseth were left, surrounded and battered by the slingers.
When the king of Moab saw that he was losing the battle, he took seven hundred men with him, swords drawn, to break through to the king of Edom; but they could not.
So he took his firstborn son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. A great wrath came upon Israel; they raised the siege and returned to their own land.

titres.titre: The Shunammite woman and her son
The poisoned pot and the loaves of barley

versets.t: A certain woman, one of the wives of the sons of the prophets, cried out to Elisha: "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that he feared the Lord. Now his creditor has come to take my two children to be his slaves."
Elisha said to her, "What can I do for you? Tell me what you have in the house." She answered, "Your maidservant has nothing in the house but a jar of oil."
He said: "Go and borrow vessels from outside, from all your neighbors, empty vessels, and do not borrow too few.
Then go in, shut the door behind you and your sons, pour oil into all these vessels, and set aside each one as it is filled."
She left him, shut the door behind herself and her sons; they kept bringing the vessels to her, and she kept pouring.
When the vessels were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." He answered, "There is not one left." And the oil stopped.
She went and reported this to the man of God, who said, "Go and sell the oil and pay your debt; and you and your sons can live on what is left."
One day Elisha was passing through Shunem. There was a wealthy woman there who urged him to stay for a meal; and whenever he passed by, he would stop there to eat.
She said to her husband: "I can see that this man who always passes our way is a holy man of God.
Let us make a small room on the roof for him; let us put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp there for him, so that he can stay there when he comes to us."
So one day when Elisha arrived, he withdrew to the upper room and lay down there.
He said to Gehazi, his servant, "Call this Shunammite woman." He called her, and she came and stood before him.

Elisha said to Gehazi: "Tell her: You have taken all this trouble for us; what can be done for you? Should a word be put in for you with the king or the commander of the army?" She answered, "I live among my own people."
Elisha asked, "What then can be done for her?" Gehazi answered, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is old."
Elisha said, "Call her." He called her, and she stood at the door.
He said to her, "At this same season next year, you will hold a son in your arms." She answered, "No, my lord, man of God, do not deceive your maidservant!"
But the woman conceived and bore a son the following year at the same season, just as Elisha had told her.
The child grew. One day, when he had gone out to his father among the reapers,
he said to his father, "My head! My head!" The father said to a servant, "Carry him to his mother."
The servant took him and brought him to his mother; the child stayed on her lap until noon, and then he died.
She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door on him, and went out.
She called her husband: "Send me, I beg you, one of the servants and a donkey; I will hurry to the man of God and come straight back."
He said, "Why go to him today? It is neither new moon nor sabbath." She answered, "It is all right."
She had the donkey saddled and said to her servant, "Lead on; go, and do not slow down for me unless I tell you."
So she set out and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her in the distance, he said to Gehazi, his servant: "Here is the Shunammite woman.
Run to meet her and ask her: Are you well? Is your husband well? Is your child well?" She answered, "Well."

But when she reached the man of God on the mountain, she took hold of his feet. Gehazi came up to push her away, but the man of God said, "Leave her alone, for her soul is in bitterness, and the Lord has hidden it from me; he has not told me."
Then she said, "Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say to you: Do not deceive me?"
Elisha said to Gehazi: "Fasten your belt, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him; if anyone greets you, do not answer. Lay my staff on the face of the child."
But the child's mother said, "As the Lord lives and as you live, I will not leave you!" So Elisha got up and followed her.
Gehazi had gone on ahead of them; he laid the staff on the child's face, but there was no sound and no response. He came back to meet Elisha and told him, "The child has not woken up."
When Elisha entered the house, there was the child, dead, laid out on his bed.
He went in, shut the door on the two of them, and prayed to the Lord.
Then he climbed up and stretched himself out on the child: he put his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, his hands on his hands, and as he bent over him, the child's body grew warm.
He got up, walked back and forth in the house, then went up again and bent over him; then the child sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
Elisha called Gehazi, "Call the Shunammite woman." He called her; she came, and he said to her, "Take your son."
She came and fell at his feet and bowed to the ground; then she took her son and went out.

Elisha returned to Gilgal while there was a famine in the land. As the sons of the prophets were sitting before him, he said to his servant, "Put the large pot on and boil some stew for the sons of the prophets."

One of them went out into the fields to gather herbs; he found a kind of wild vine and gathered from it a lapful of wild gourds. He came back and cut them up into the pot of stew, though no one knew what they were.
They served the men to eat; but as soon as they tasted the stew, they cried out, "There is death in the pot, man of God!" And they could not eat it.
Elisha said, "Bring some flour." He threw it into the pot and said, "Serve the people, and let them eat." And there was nothing harmful left in the pot.
A man came from Baal-shalishah, bringing the man of God bread from the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley and fresh grain in his sack. Elisha said, "Give it to the people to eat."

His servant answered, "How can I set this before a hundred people?" But Elisha said again, "Give it to the people to eat; for this is what the Lord says: They will eat, and there will be some left over."
So he served the people; they ate, and there was some left over, according to the word of the Lord.
Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man and highly regarded by his master, for through him the Lord had given victory to Aram. But this strong and valiant man was a leper.
Now the Arameans, going out in raiding bands, had carried off captive a young girl from the land of Israel, who served Naaman's wife.
She said to her mistress, "If only my lord could present himself to the prophet who is in Samaria! He would cure him of his leprosy."
Naaman went and reported to his master, "The girl from the land of Israel spoke in such and such a way."
The king of Aram said, "Go, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So he set out, taking with him about 340 kilograms of silver, 68 kilograms of gold, and ten changes of clothing.
He delivered the letter to the king of Israel, which said: "Along with this letter, I am sending you my servant Naaman, for you to cure him of his leprosy."

When he read the letter, the king of Israel tore his clothes and said, "Am I a god, to give death and life, that this man sends to me to cure someone of his leprosy? See how he is trying to pick a quarrel with me!"

When Elisha, the man of God, heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent word to him: "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come to me, and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel."
So Naaman came with his horses and his chariot and stopped at the entrance of Elisha's house.
Elisha sent a messenger out to him to say, "Go and wash seven times in the Jordan; your flesh will be restored to you, and you will be clean."
But Naaman became angry and went off, saying: "I said to myself: Surely he will come out, stand there, call on the name of the Lord his God, wave his hand over the diseased spot, and cure the leper.
Are not the Abana and the Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?" And he turned to go off in a rage.

But his servants came up and said to him: "My father, if the prophet had asked you to do something difficult, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he tells you: Wash, and you will be clean."
So he went down and plunged into the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God; and his flesh became like the flesh of a little child: he was clean.

He returned to the man of God with his whole retinue. He went in, stood before him, and said, "Now I know that there is no other God in all the earth except in Israel. So accept a gift from your servant."
But Elisha answered, "As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will accept nothing." Naaman urged him to accept, but he refused.

Then Naaman said: "If not, then let your servant be given as much earth of this land as a pair of mules can carry; for your servant will no longer offer burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but to the Lord alone.

Only, may the Lord pardon your servant in this: when my master goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship there, leaning on my arm, and I bow down too in the temple of Rimmon, may the Lord be willing to pardon your servant this bowing down!"
Elisha said to him, "Go in peace." So Naaman left him and had gone some distance

when Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said to himself: "See how my master has spared Naaman, this Aramean, by refusing what he brought. As the Lord lives, I will run after him and get something from him."
So Gehazi set off in pursuit of Naaman. When Naaman saw him running toward him, he got down from his chariot to meet him and asked, "Is everything all right?"

Gehazi answered: "Everything is all right. My master has sent me to say: Two young men of the hill country of Ephraim, from the sons of the prophets, have just come to me; give for them, I beg you, about 34 kilograms of silver and two changes of clothing."
Naaman said, "Please accept 68 kilograms." He urged him, tied up this sum of silver in two bags with two changes of clothing, and gave them to two of his servants, who carried them ahead of Gehazi.
When he reached the hill, Gehazi took the bags from their hands, stored them in the house, and sent the men away, and they left.
Then he went in and stood before his master. Elisha asked him, "Where have you been, Gehazi?" He answered, "Your servant has not gone anywhere."

But Elisha said to him: "Was not my spirit present when that man got down from his chariot to meet you? Is this the time to accept silver, to accept clothing, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and cattle, male and female servants?
The leprosy of Naaman will cling to you and to your descendants forever." And Gehazi left his presence, a leper, white as snow.
The sons of the prophets said to Elisha: "Look, the place where we live near you is too cramped for us.
Let us go to the Jordan; each of us will take a beam there, and we will make a place there to live." He answered, "Go."
One of them said, "Please agree to come with your servants." He answered, "I will go."
So he went with them. When they reached the Jordan, they cut down wood.
As one of them was felling a trunk, the iron head fell into the water. He cried out, "Alas, my lord! And it was borrowed!"
The man of God asked, "Where did it fall?" When he showed him the place, he cut off a piece of wood, threw it in there, and made the iron float.
He said, "Lift it out." The man reached out his hand and took it.
The king of Aram was at war with Israel. In council with his servants, he would say, "My camp will be at such and such a place."
But the man of God would send word to the king of Israel: "Take care not to pass by such a place, for the Arameans are going down there."
So the king of Israel would send to check the place the man of God had pointed out to him, and he would be on his guard there; this happened not once or twice.
The heart of the king of Aram was troubled by this; he called his servants and said to them, "Can you not tell me who among us is on the side of the king of Israel?"
One of his servants answered, "No one, my lord the king. It is Elisha, the prophet in Israel, who reports to the king of Israel even the words you speak in your bedroom."
The king said, "Go and find out where he is, and I will send to seize him." He was told, "He is in Dothan."
So he sent horses, chariots, and a strong force there; they arrived by night and surrounded the city.

Early the next morning the servant of the man of God got up, went out, and there was the force surrounding the city, with horses and chariots. The servant said to Elisha, "Alas, my lord, what shall we do?"
He answered, "Do not be afraid: those who are with us are more than those who are with them."
Then Elisha prayed, "Lord, open his eyes, that he may see." The Lord opened the servant's eyes: he looked, and there was the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
As the Arameans came down toward him, Elisha prayed to the Lord, "Strike this force with blindness." And the Lord struck them with blindness, according to the word of Elisha.
Elisha said to them, "This is not the road, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will lead you to the man you are looking for." And he led them to Samaria.
When they entered Samaria, Elisha said, "Lord, open the eyes of these men, that they may see." The Lord opened their eyes: they looked, and there they were, in the middle of Samaria.
When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, "Shall I kill them, shall I kill them, my father?"

He answered: "Do not kill them. Would you kill men you have taken captive with your sword and your bow? Set bread and water before them, so that they may eat and drink, and then let them go back to their master."

So the king of Israel had a great feast prepared for them; they ate and drank, and then he sent them away, and they went back to their master. And the raiding bands of Aram came no more into the territory of Israel.
After this, Ben-hadad, king of Aram, gathered his whole army, marched up, and laid siege to Samaria.
There was a great famine in Samaria; the siege was so severe that a donkey's head sold for eighty pieces of silver, and a quarter litre of dove's dung for five pieces of silver.
As the king was passing along the wall, a woman cried out to him, "Help, my lord the king!"
He answered, "If the Lord does not help you, where could I find help for you? From the threshing floor or the winepress?"
Then the king asked her, "What is the matter with you?" She answered: "This woman said to me: Give up your son, and we will eat him today, and tomorrow we will eat mine.
So we cooked my son and ate him. The next day I said to her: Give up your son, and we will eat him; but she had hidden her son."
When the king heard the woman's words, he tore his clothes. As he was passing along the wall, the people saw that he had sackcloth underneath, against his skin.
He declared, "May God do the very worst to me if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat stays on his shoulders today!"

Now Elisha was sitting in his house, with the elders sitting beside him, when the king sent a man ahead. But before the messenger arrived, Elisha said to the elders: "Do you see how this son of a murderer is sending someone to cut off my head? Watch: when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold it fast against him. Is not the sound of his master's feet already behind him?"
He was still speaking to them when the messenger came down to him and said, "See, this disaster comes from the Lord; what more can I hope for from him?"

titres.titre: Elisha foretells the end of the famine
The four lepers discover the empty camp

versets.t: Elisha said: "Hear the word of the Lord! This is what the Lord says: Tomorrow at this hour, at the gate of Samaria, seven litres of fine flour will sell for a piece of silver, and fourteen litres of barley for a piece of silver."

The officer on whose arm the king leaned answered the man of God, "Even if the Lord were to open floodgates in the sky, could this happen?" Elisha said, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."
Now there were four lepers at the entrance of the gate. They said to one another: "Why sit here waiting to die?

If we decide to go into the city, the famine is there, and we will die; if we stay here, we will die too. Come, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans: if they spare us, we will live; if they kill us, we will die."
At dusk they got up to go to the camp of the Arameans; but when they reached the edge of the camp, there was no one there.

For the Lord had made the camp of the Arameans hear a sound of chariots, a sound of horses, the din of a great army, and they had said to one another: The king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt against us to attack us.
So they had got up and fled at dusk, abandoning their tents, horses, and donkeys, the camp just as it was, and they had fled to save their lives.

These lepers, having reached the edge of the camp, went into a tent, ate and drank, and carried off silver, gold, and clothing, which they hid; then they came back, went into another tent, carried things off from there, and hid them too.
Then they said to one another: "We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news; if we keep silent and wait until morning, we will be punished. Come, let us go and inform the king's palace."

So they came and called out to the gatekeepers of the city and announced to them: "We went to the camp of the Arameans: there is no one there, not a human voice, only the horses and donkeys tied up, and the tents just as they were."
The gatekeepers shouted the news, and it was reported inside the palace.

The king got up in the night and said to his servants: "Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know we are starving, so they have left the camp to hide in the open country, saying: When they come out of the city, we will take them alive and enter the city."

One of his servants answered: "Let five of the horses that are still left in the city be taken; their fate will be that of all the multitude of Israel still here, all the multitude that is dying here. Let us send them out to see."
So they took two chariot teams, and the king sent them after the Aramean army: "Go and see."

They followed them as far as the Jordan, and there was the whole road strewn with clothing and gear that the Arameans had thrown away in their headlong flight. The messengers returned and reported it all to the king.

Then the people went out and plundered the camp of the Arameans, and seven litres of fine flour sold for a piece of silver, and fourteen litres of barley for a piece of silver, according to the word of the Lord.

The king had put the officer on whose arm he leaned in charge of the gate; but the people trampled him at the gate, and he died, according to the word the man of God had spoken when the king had come down to him.

It had happened exactly as the man of God had told the king: "Tomorrow at this hour, at the gate of Samaria, fourteen litres of barley will sell for a piece of silver and seven litres of fine flour for a piece of silver,"

and the officer had answered the man of God, "Even if the Lord were to open floodgates in the sky, could this happen?" Elisha had said, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."
And that is exactly what happened to him: the people trampled him at the gate, and he died.

titres.titre: The Shunammite woman recovers her property

versets.t: Elisha had said to the woman whose son he had brought back to life: "Get up and go away with your household, and settle wherever you can, for the Lord has summoned a famine, and it is coming upon the land for seven years."
The woman had got up and done as the man of God had said: she had gone with her household to settle in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
At the end of the seven years, she came back from the land of the Philistines and went to appeal to the king about her house and her field.
Now the king was talking with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God: "Tell me about all the great things Elisha has done."

And just as he was telling the king how Elisha had brought a dead man back to life, there was the woman whose son he had brought back to life, coming to appeal to the king about her house and her field. Gehazi said, "My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha brought back to life!"

The king questioned the woman, and she told him her story. Then the king gave her an official with these orders: "Have everything that belongs to her restored, along with all the income from the field from the day she left the land until now."
Elisha went to Damascus. Ben-hadad, king of Aram, was ill, and he was told, "The man of God has come this far."
The king said to Hazael, "Take a gift, go to meet the man of God, and through him consult the Lord: Will I survive this illness?"

Hazael went to meet Elisha, taking with him a gift of all the finest things of Damascus, a load for forty camels. He stood before him and said, "Your son Ben-hadad, king of Aram, has sent me to ask you: Will I survive this illness?"
Elisha answered, "Go and tell him: You will surely survive. Yet the Lord has shown me that he will surely die."
Then the man of God fixed Hazael with a steady stare until he was ill at ease, and he began to weep.

Hazael asked, "Why is my lord weeping?" He answered: "Because I know the evil you will do to the sons of Israel: you will set fire to their fortified cities, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little children to pieces, and rip open their pregnant women."
Hazael said, "But what is your servant, a mere dog, to do such great things?" Elisha answered, "The Lord has shown me that you will be king of Aram."
Hazael left Elisha and returned to his master, who asked him, "What did Elisha say to you?" He answered, "He told me that you would surely survive."
But the next day Hazael took a coverlet, soaked it in water, and spread it over the king's face, and he died. And Hazael became king in his place.
In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Joram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, like the house of Ahab, for his wife was a daughter of Ahab; and he did what is evil in the sight of the Lord.
But the Lord was unwilling to destroy Judah, for the sake of David his servant, to whom he had promised to leave a lamp always, for him and his sons.
In his time Edom freed itself from the rule of Judah and set up a king of its own.
Joram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots; he got up in the night and struck down the Edomites who had surrounded him, along with the chariot commanders; but the army fled to their tents.
So Edom has been free from the rule of Judah to this day. Libnah also rebelled at that same time.
As for the rest of the acts of Joram, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Joram slept with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of David. Ahaziah his son became king in his place.
In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Joram became king of Judah.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah, granddaughter of Omri, king of Israel.
He walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, like the house of Ahab, to which he was joined by marriage.
He went with Joram son of Ahab to fight against Hazael, king of Aram, at Ramoth-gilead; but the Arameans wounded Joram.

King Joram returned to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds the Arameans had inflicted on him at Ramoth while he fought Hazael, king of Aram. And Ahaziah son of Joram, king of Judah, went down to Jezreel to visit Joram son of Ahab, who was sick.
Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him: "Fasten your belt, take this jar of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
When you get there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi. Go up to him, make him rise from among his companions, and take him into an inner room.
Take the jar of oil, pour it on his head, and say: This is what the Lord says: I anoint you king over Israel. Then open the door and flee without delay."
So the young man, the prophet's servant, set out for Ramoth-gilead.
When he arrived, the commanders of the army were sitting there. He said, "Commander, I have a word for you." Jehu asked, "For which one of us?" He answered, "For you, commander."

Jehu got up and went into the house; the young man poured the oil on his head and said to him: "This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: I anoint you king over the people of the Lord, over Israel.
You will strike down the house of Ahab, your master, so that I may avenge on Jezebel the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the Lord.
The whole house of Ahab will perish: I will cut off from Ahab every male, slave or free, in Israel.
I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
As for Jezebel, the dogs will devour her in the field of Jezreel, and no one will bury her." Then he opened the door and fled.
Jehu went out to rejoin his master's servants, who asked him, "Is all well? Why did this madman come to you?" He answered, "You know the man and his ranting."
They replied, "That is not true! Tell us." He said, "He spoke to me in such and such a way: This is what the Lord says: I anoint you king over Israel."
At once each man took his cloak and spread it under him, on the bare steps; they blew the horn and shouted, "Jehu is king!"
Jehu son of Jehoshaphat, son of Nimshi, conspired against Joram. Now Joram, with all Israel, had been defending Ramoth-gilead against Hazael, king of Aram;

but King Joram had returned to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds the Arameans had inflicted on him while he fought Hazael, king of Aram. Jehu said, "If this is your wish, let no one slip out of the city to go and carry the news to Jezreel."
He mounted his chariot and set out for Jezreel, where Joram was lying ill and where Ahaziah, king of Judah, had come down to visit him.
The sentry posted on the tower of Jezreel saw the company of Jehu coming and announced, "I see a company." Joram said, "Take a horseman and send him to meet them to ask: Is it peace?"

The horseman went to meet him and said, "This is what the king says: Is it peace?" Jehu answered, "What have you to do with peace? Fall in behind me." The sentry announced, "The messenger has reached them, but he is not coming back."
A second horseman was sent; when he reached them, he said, "This is what the king says: Is it peace?" Jehu answered, "What have you to do with peace? Fall in behind me."
The sentry announced, "He has reached them, but he is not coming back. And the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi: he drives like a madman."

Joram said, "Harness up!" His chariot was harnessed. Joram, king of Israel, and Ahaziah, king of Judah, went out, each in his chariot, to meet Jehu, and they met him at the field of Naboth the Jezreelite.
As soon as he saw Jehu, Joram asked, "Is it peace, Jehu?" He answered, "What peace, as long as the harlotries of your mother Jezebel and her many sorceries go on?"
Joram wheeled around and fled, crying out to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
But Jehu drew his bow and struck Joram between the shoulders; the arrow pierced his heart, and Joram sank down in his chariot.

Jehu said to Bidkar, his aide: "Take him and throw him into the field of Naboth the Jezreelite. Remember: when you and I were riding together behind Ahab his father, the Lord pronounced this sentence against him:

As surely as I saw yesterday the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons, says the Lord, I will repay you in this very field, says the Lord. So take him and throw him into this field, according to the word of the Lord."

When Ahaziah, king of Judah, saw this, he fled by the road to Beth-haggan. Jehu pursued him, shouting, "Strike him down too, in his chariot!" They struck him at the ascent of Gur, near Ibleam; he fled to Megiddo, where he died.
His servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb, with his fathers, in the city of David.
Ahaziah had become king of Judah in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab.
Jehu came to Jezreel. When Jezebel heard of it, she painted her eyes, adorned her head, and looked down from the window.
As Jehu was passing through the gate, she called out to him, "Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of his master?"
He looked up at the window and said, "Who is on my side? Who?" Two or three eunuchs looked down toward him,
and he said, "Throw her down!" They threw her down: her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and Jehu trampled her underfoot.
Then he went in, ate and drank, and said, "See to that accursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter."
But when they went to bury her, they found nothing of her but the skull, the feet, and the palms of the hands.
They came back and reported it to Jehu, who said: "This is the word the Lord had spoken through his servant Elijah the Tishbite: In the field of Jezreel the dogs will devour the flesh of Jezebel;
the corpse of Jezebel will be like dung on the field, in the field of Jezreel, so that no one will be able to say: This is Jezebel."

titres.titre: Jehu wipes out the house of Ahab
Jehu wipes out the worship of Baal

versets.t: There were seventy sons of Ahab in Samaria. Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the officials of the city, to the elders, and to the guardians of the sons of Ahab. He said:
"You have with you the sons of your master, as well as chariots, horses, a fortified city, and weapons. As soon as this letter reaches you,
choose the best and worthiest of your master's sons, set him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's house."
But they were seized with great fear and said, "See, the two kings could not stand against him; how could we stand?"

So the steward of the palace, the governor of the city, the elders, and the guardians sent word to Jehu: "We are your servants, and we will do everything you tell us; we will proclaim no one king. Do what you think best."

Jehu wrote them a second letter: "If you are on my side and will obey me, take the heads of your master's sons and come to me at Jezreel tomorrow at this hour." Now the seventy sons of the king were being raised by the leading men of the city.
As soon as they received the letter, they took the king's sons, slaughtered the seventy men, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to Jehu at Jezreel.
A messenger came and told him, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." He said, "Put them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning."
In the morning he went out, stood before all the people, and said: "You are innocent! It was I who conspired against my master and killed him; but all these, who struck them down?
Know then that nothing of the word of the Lord falls to the ground, of what the Lord has spoken against the house of Ahab: the Lord has done what he foretold through his servant Elijah."
Then Jehu struck down all who were left of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, all his great men, his close friends, and his priests, until not a single survivor was left.
After that he set out for Samaria. On the way, when he was at Beth-eked of the Shepherds,

Jehu met the relatives of Ahaziah, king of Judah. He asked, "Who are you?" They answered, "We are the relatives of Ahaziah; we are going down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother."
Jehu ordered, "Take them alive." They took them alive and slaughtered them at the cistern of Beth-eked, forty-two of them; he did not leave a single one.

When he left there, he met Jonadab son of Rechab, who was coming to meet him. He greeted him and said, "Is your heart as loyal to mine as mine is to yours?" Jonadab answered, "It is." Jehu said, "Then give me your hand." He gave him his hand, and Jehu had him come up beside him in the chariot,
saying, "Come with me, and you will see my zeal for the Lord." So he took him along in his chariot.
When he reached Samaria, Jehu struck down all who were left of the house of Ahab in Samaria, until he had wiped it out, according to the word the Lord had spoken to Elijah.
Then Jehu gathered all the people and said to them: "Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.

So summon to me all the prophets of Baal, all his worshipers, and all his priests, not one missing, for I have a great sacrifice to offer to Baal; whoever is missing will not live." But Jehu was acting with cunning, to destroy the worshipers of Baal.
Jehu said, "Proclaim a solemn assembly in honor of Baal." So it was proclaimed.
Jehu sent word throughout all Israel, and all the worshipers of Baal came, not one of them absent; they entered the temple of Baal, and it was filled from end to end.
Jehu said to the keeper of the wardrobe, "Bring out vestments for all the worshipers of Baal." So he brought out vestments for them.

Then Jehu went into the temple of Baal with Jonadab son of Rechab and said to the worshipers of Baal, "Search and make sure there is no servant of the Lord here among you, but only worshipers of Baal."

They went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had posted eighty men outside, warning them, "If any of those I am handing over to you escapes, you will pay for his life with your own."

When he had finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu said to the guards and the officers, "Go in, strike them down, and let none get out!" They put them to the sword, threw them outside, and then went into the inner sanctuary of the temple of Baal.
They dragged out the sacred pillars and burned them;
they tore down the pillar of Baal, tore down the temple of Baal, and made it into a latrine, which it still is today.
So Jehu wiped out Baal from Israel.
But Jehu did not turn away from the sins into which Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel: the golden calves of Bethel and Dan.

The Lord said to Jehu: "Because you have done well in carrying out what is right in my sight and have done to the house of Ahab all that I had in my heart, your sons will sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation."
Yet Jehu was not careful to walk with all his heart in the law of the Lord, the God of Israel: he did not turn away from the sins into which Jeroboam had led Israel.
In those days the Lord began to reduce the territory of Israel. Hazael defeated them along the whole frontier:
east of the Jordan, all the land of Gilead, the territory of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh, from Aroer, on the Wadi Arnon, as far as Gilead and Bashan.
As for the rest of the acts of Jehu, all that he did and all his exploits, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Jehu slept with his fathers, and he was buried in Samaria. Jehoahaz his son became king in his place.
Jehu had reigned twenty-eight years over Israel, in Samaria.
Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, seeing that her son was dead, set out to destroy the whole royal line.

But Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah, stole him away from among the king's sons who were being murdered, and hid him, with his nurse, in the bedchamber. In this way he was concealed from Athaliah, and he was not put to death.
He remained hidden with her in the house of the Lord for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

In the seventh year, Jehoiada sent for the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and of the guards and had them come to him in the house of the Lord. He made a covenant with them, put them under oath in the house of the Lord, and then showed them the king's son.
He gave them these orders: "This is what you will do. The third of you who come on duty on the sabbath will keep guard over the royal palace;
another third will be at the gate of Sur, and another at the gate behind the guards; you will keep watch over the house, to bar its approach.
Your two other divisions, those who go off duty on the sabbath, will keep guard over the house of the Lord around the king.
You will surround the king on every side, each man with his weapons in hand; anyone who breaks through the ranks is to be put to death. Stay close to the king wherever he goes."
The commanders of hundreds carried out all the orders of Jehoiada the priest. Each took his men, both those coming on duty on the sabbath and those going off, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
The priest handed over to the commanders of hundreds the spears and the shields of King David, which were in the house of the Lord.
The guards took their posts, each man with his weapons in hand, from the right side of the house to the left, near the altar and the house, all around the king.

Then Jehoiada brought out the king's son, placed the crown on him, gave him the document of the covenant, and proclaimed him king by anointing him. They clapped their hands and shouted, "Long live the king!"
When Athaliah heard the shouting of the guards and the people, she came to the crowd in the house of the Lord.

She looked, and there was the king standing on the platform, according to custom; beside him were the officers and the trumpeters; all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing the trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, "Treason! Treason!"

But Jehoiada the priest gave this order to the commanders of hundreds in charge of the army: "Bring her out through the ranks, and let anyone who follows her be killed with the sword." For the priest had said, "Do not put her to death in the house of the Lord."
So they made way for her, and she reached the royal palace by the road of the horses' entrance; there she was put to death.
Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord, the king, and the people, by which Israel would be the people of the Lord; he also made a covenant between the king and the people.

All the people of the land went into the temple of Baal and tore it down; they smashed its altars and its images to pieces and killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, in front of the altars. Then Jehoiada the priest set overseers over the house of the Lord.

He took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the guards, and all the people of the land; they brought the king down from the house of the Lord and entered the palace by the gate of the guards. Joash took his seat on the throne of the kings.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. As for Athaliah, they had put her to death by the sword in the royal palace.

titres.titre: The threat of Hazael; the death of Joash

versets.t: Joash was seven years old when he became king.
In the seventh year of Jehu, Joash became king; he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah, from Beersheba.
Joash did what is right in the sight of the Lord all the time that Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
Only, the high places did not disappear: the people went on offering sacrifices and incense there.

Joash said to the priests: "All the consecrated money that is brought to the house of the Lord, the money from the personal assessments, the money paid for the redemption of persons according to the valuation, and all the money that anyone is moved in his heart to bring to the house of the Lord,
let the priests receive it, each from those he deals with, and let them repair whatever damage is found in the house, wherever it may be found."
But by the twenty-third year of King Joash, the priests had still not repaired the damage to the house.

So King Joash called Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and said to them: "Why are you not repairing the damage to the house? From now on, do not take any more money from those you deal with, but hand it over for the damage to the house."
The priests agreed no longer to receive money from the people, but also no longer to repair the damage to the house themselves.

Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the altar, on the right as one enters the house of the Lord; the priests who guarded the threshold put into it all the money brought to the house of the Lord.

Whenever they saw that there was a large amount of money in the chest, the king's secretary would come up with the high priest; they would count and put into bags the money found in the house of the Lord.
Once it was weighed, they would hand it over to the foremen in charge of the house of the Lord, who would pay the carpenters and the builders working on the house of the Lord,
the masons and the stonecutters; they also bought the timber and the dressed stone to repair the damage to the house of the Lord, and they covered all the costs of the restoration.
But with the money brought to the house of the Lord, no silver basins, knives, bowls, or trumpets were made, nor any article of gold or silver:
it was given to the workmen, who used it to repair the house of the Lord.
No accounting was required of the men to whom the money was handed over to pay the workmen, for they acted with honesty.
The money from the guilt offerings and the sin offerings was not brought to the house of the Lord: it belonged to the priests.
At that time Hazael, king of Aram, marched up to attack Gath and captured it; then he turned to march up against Jerusalem.

Then Joash, king of Judah, took all the consecrated objects dedicated by his fathers, the kings of Judah Jehoshaphat, Joram, and Ahaziah, and those he had consecrated himself, and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of the royal palace, and he sent it all to Hazael, king of Aram, who withdrew from Jerusalem.
As for the rest of the acts of Joash, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
His servants rose up and conspired against him; they struck Joash down in the house of the Millo, on the descent to Silla.
It was Jozacar son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer, his servants, who struck him, and he died. He was buried with his fathers in the city of David. Amaziah his son became king in his place.

titres.titre: Joash of Israel and the death of Elisha

versets.t: In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria; he reigned seventeen years.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord: he followed the sins into which Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel, and he did not turn away from them.
The anger of the Lord blazed out against Israel, and again and again he handed them over to Hazael, king of Aram, and to Ben-hadad son of Hazael.
But Jehoahaz pleaded with the Lord, and the Lord heard him, for he saw the oppression that the king of Aram was inflicting on Israel.
The Lord gave Israel a deliverer, who freed them from the grip of Aram, and the sons of Israel dwelt in their own tents again, as before.
Yet they did not turn away from the sins into which the house of Jeroboam had led Israel; they went on in them, and the sacred pole even remained standing in Samaria.

The king of Aram had left Jehoahaz no troops but fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers; for the king of Aram had destroyed the rest and ground them to dust to be trampled underfoot.
As for the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, all that he did and his exploits, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Jehoahaz slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria. His son Joash reigned in his place.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash, king of Judah, Joash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria; he reigned sixteen years.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord; he did not turn away from any of the sins into which Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel; he went on in them.
As for the rest of the acts of Joash, all that he did, his exploits, and his war against Amaziah, king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Joash slept with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat on his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
Now Elisha had fallen ill with the sickness of which he was to die. Joash, king of Israel, went down to him, wept over his face, and said, "My father, my father, chariot of Israel and its horsemen!"
Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows." So he took a bow and arrows.
Elisha said to the king of Israel, "Draw the bow with your hand." He drew it; then Elisha laid his hands on the king's hands

and said, "Open the window toward the east." He opened it. Elisha said, "Shoot!" He shot. Elisha said, "The Lord's arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram! You will strike the Arameans at Aphek until they are wiped out."
Then he said, "Take the arrows." He took them. Elisha said to the king of Israel, "Strike the ground." He struck it three times and stopped.
The man of God was angry with him: "You should have struck five or six times; then you would have struck down Aram until it was wiped out. As it is, you will strike Aram only three times."
Elisha died, and they buried him. Now bands of Moabites used to raid the land at the turn of the year.

One day, as some men were burying another, they suddenly saw one of these bands; they threw the dead man into Elisha's tomb and hurried off. The moment the man touched Elisha's bones, he came back to life and stood up on his feet.
Hazael, king of Aram, had oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

But the Lord was gracious to them, took pity on them, and turned toward them for the sake of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; he was unwilling to destroy them, and he did not yet cast them out from his presence.
Hazael, king of Aram, died, and his son Ben-hadad reigned in his place.

Then Joash son of Jehoahaz took back from Ben-hadad son of Hazael the towns that Hazael had seized in war from his father Jehoahaz. Three times Joash struck him down, and he recovered the towns of Israel.
In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddin, of Jerusalem.
He did what is right in the sight of the Lord, though not the equal of David his ancestor; he acted in every way like Joash his father.
Only the high places did not disappear: the people went on offering sacrifices and incense there.
As soon as the kingship was firmly in his hands, he struck down the servants who had killed the king his father.

But he did not put to death the children of the murderers, in keeping with what is written in the book of the law of Moses, where the Lord commands: The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, nor the children for the fathers; each shall be put to death for his own sin.
It was he who struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and took Sela by storm, calling it Joktheel, the name it bears to this day.
Then Amaziah sent messengers to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, to say, "Come, let us meet face to face."

Joash, king of Israel, sent back word to Amaziah, king of Judah: "The thistle of Lebanon sent word to the cedar of Lebanon: Give your daughter to my son as a wife. But the wild beasts of Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
You have struck down Edom, and your heart has grown proud. Enjoy your glory and stay at home. Why court disaster and fall, you and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah would not listen. So Joash, king of Israel, marched up; he and Amaziah, king of Judah, met face to face at Beth-shemesh in Judah.
Judah was defeated before Israel, and everyone fled to his tent.

At Beth-shemesh, Joash, king of Israel, captured Amaziah, king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Ahaziah. He marched on Jerusalem and made a breach two hundred metres wide in its wall, from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.
He seized all the gold and silver and all the vessels found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the royal palace, along with hostages, and returned to Samaria.
As for the rest of the acts of Joash, all that he did, his exploits, and his war against Amaziah, king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Joash slept with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. His son Jeroboam reigned in his place.
Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
As for the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
A conspiracy was hatched against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; but men were sent after him to Lachish, and there they put him to death.
They brought him back on horseback, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers, in the city of David.
Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
It was he who rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king had slept with his fathers.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash became king over Israel in Samaria; he reigned forty-one years.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord; he did not turn away from any of the sins into which Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel.

It was he who restored the borders of Israel, from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word that the Lord, the God of Israel, had spoken through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet, of Gath-hepher.
For the Lord had seen the very bitter distress of Israel, where neither slave nor free man was left, and no one to help Israel.
The Lord had not yet resolved to blot out the name of Israel from under heaven; he saved them by the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.

As for the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, all that he did, his exploits, his wars, and how he brought back to Israel Damascus and Hamath, which had belonged to Judah, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Jeroboam slept with his fathers, the kings of Israel. His son Zechariah reigned in his place.

titres.titre: The procession of the kings of Israel

versets.t: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam, king of Israel, Uzziah son of Amaziah became king of Judah.
He was sixteen years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah, of Jerusalem.
He did what is right in the sight of the Lord, in every way like Amaziah his father.
Only the high places did not disappear: the people went on offering sacrifices and incense there.
The Lord struck the king, and he was a leper until the day of his death; he lived in a house set apart, while Jotham the king's son was over the palace and governed the people of the land.
As for the rest of the acts of Uzziah, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Uzziah slept with his fathers, and they buried him beside them in the city of David. His son Jotham reigned in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Uzziah, king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria; he reigned six months.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, like his fathers; he did not turn away from the sins into which Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel.
Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him; he struck him down in front of the people, put him to death, and reigned in his place.
The rest of the acts of Zechariah are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel.
So was fulfilled the word that the Lord had spoken to Jehu: Your sons shall sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation. And so it was.
Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah, king of Judah; he reigned one full month in Samaria.
Menahem son of Gadi came up from Tirzah, came to Samaria, struck down Shallum son of Jabesh there, put him to death, and reigned in his place.
The rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy he hatched, are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel.

It was then that Menahem, setting out from Tirzah, struck down Tiphsah and everyone in it, along with all its territory, because it had not opened its gates to him; he struck it down and ripped open all its pregnant women.
In the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah, king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel; he reigned ten years in Samaria.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord; all his life he did not turn away from the sins into which Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel.
Pul, king of Assyria, invaded the land. Menahem gave him about thirty-four tonnes of silver so that he would support him and secure the kingship in his hands.

Menahem raised this silver from Israel, from all the wealthy men, at about 570 grams of silver each, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back and did not stay there in the land.
As for the rest of the acts of Menahem, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Menahem slept with his fathers. His son Pekahiah reigned in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Uzziah, king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king over Israel in Samaria; he reigned two years.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord; he did not turn away from the sins into which Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel.

Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him; he struck him down in Samaria, in the keep of the royal palace, together with Argob and Arieh, having with him fifty men of Gilead. He put him to death and reigned in his place.
The rest of the acts of Pekahiah, all that he did, are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Uzziah, king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria; he reigned twenty years.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord; he did not turn away from the sins into which Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel.

In the days of Pekah, king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, came and seized Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali, and he deported the inhabitants to Assyria.
Hoshea son of Elah conspired against Pekah son of Remaliah; he struck him down, put him to death, and reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
The rest of the acts of Pekah, all that he did, are written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah became king of Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.
He did what is right in the sight of the Lord, in every way like Uzziah his father.
Only the high places did not disappear: the people went on offering sacrifices and incense there. It was he who built the upper gate of the house of the Lord.
As for the rest of the acts of Jotham, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
In those days the Lord began to send against Judah Rezin, king of Aram, and Pekah son of Remaliah.
Jotham slept with his fathers and was buried beside them in the city of David his ancestor. His son Ahaz reigned in his place.
In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what is right in the sight of the Lord his God, as David his ancestor had done,
but he walked in the way of the kings of Israel. He even passed his son through the fire, following the abominable practices of the nations that the Lord had driven out before the sons of Israel.
He offered sacrifices and incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.
Then Rezin, king of Aram, and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, marched up to attack Jerusalem; they besieged Ahaz but could not overcome him.
At that time Rezin, king of Aram, recovered Elath for Aram; he drove the Judeans out of Elath, and the Edomites came and settled there, where they remain to this day.

Ahaz sent messengers to say to Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, "I am your servant and your son; come up and save me from the hand of the king of Aram and the king of Israel, who have risen up against me."
Ahaz took the silver and gold found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the royal palace, and sent them as a gift to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria listened to him: he marched up against Damascus, captured it, deported its inhabitants to Kir, and put Rezin to death.
King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria. When he saw the altar in Damascus, he sent the priest Uriah its model and its detailed plan.
The priest Uriah built the altar: he made it exactly according to the model that King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, and finished it before the king returned.
When the king arrived from Damascus, he saw the altar; he approached it and went up on it.
On it he burned his burnt offering and his grain offering, poured out his libation, and dashed the blood of his peace offerings against the altar.

As for the bronze altar that stood before the Lord, he moved it away from the front of the house, from between the new altar and the house of the Lord, and placed it on the north side of the new altar.

Then King Ahaz gave this order to the priest Uriah: "On the great altar you shall burn the morning burnt offering, the evening grain offering, the king's burnt offering and his grain offering, the burnt offering of all the people of the land, their grain offerings and their libations; on it you shall dash all the blood of the burnt offerings and all the blood of the sacrifices. As for the bronze altar, I will decide how it is to be used."
The priest Uriah did everything that King Ahaz had ordered.
King Ahaz also cut off the panels of the stands and removed the basins from them; he took the Sea down from the bronze oxen that supported it and set it on a stone pavement.
Out of deference to the king of Assyria, he also removed from the house of the Lord the Sabbath canopy that had been built there and the outer entrance reserved for the king.
As for the rest of the acts of Ahaz, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Ahaz slept with his fathers and was buried beside them in the city of David. His son Hezekiah reigned in his place.

titres.titre: Hoshea, the last king of Israel

versets.t: In the twelfth year of Ahaz, king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king over Israel in Samaria; he reigned nine years.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, though not as far as the kings of Israel who had preceded him.
Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, marched up against him; Hoshea became his vassal and paid him tribute.

But the king of Assyria discovered that Hoshea was plotting: he had sent messengers to So, king of Egypt, and no longer paid the yearly tribute to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria had him arrested and thrown in chains into prison.
Then the king of Assyria invaded the whole land, marched up against Samaria, and besieged it for three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria took Samaria and deported Israel to Assyria; he settled them in Halah, on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

This came about because the sons of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had brought them up out of Egypt, out of the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and because they had feared other gods.
They followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had driven out before them, and those that the kings of Israel had introduced.
The sons of Israel secretly did against the Lord their God things that were not right. They built themselves high places in all their towns, from the watchtower to the fortified city.
They set up sacred stones and sacred poles for themselves on every high hill and under every green tree.
There, on all the high places, they burned incense like the nations that the Lord had deported before them; they did evil deeds, provoking the Lord to anger.
They served idols, though the Lord had told them: You shall not do this.

The Lord had nonetheless warned Israel and Judah through all his prophets and all his seers: Turn back from your evil ways, keep my commandments and my statutes, according to the whole law that I gave your fathers and sent to you through my servants the prophets.
But they did not listen; they stiffened their necks, like their fathers who had not trusted in the Lord their God.

They rejected his laws, the covenant he had made with their fathers, and the warnings he had given them. They ran after emptiness and became empty themselves, imitating the surrounding nations that the Lord had forbidden them to imitate.
They abandoned all the commandments of the Lord their God: they made themselves two calves of cast metal, set up a sacred pole, bowed down before all the host of heaven, and served Baal.
They passed their sons and daughters through the fire, practiced divination and sorcery, and sold themselves to do what is evil in the sight of the Lord, provoking him to anger without ceasing.
So the Lord was deeply angry with Israel and removed them from his presence; only the tribe of Judah was left.
But Judah too did not keep the commandments of the Lord their God: they followed the customs that Israel had introduced.
So the Lord rejected all the offspring of Israel, humbled them, and handed them over to plunderers, until he had cast them out from his presence.
For when he had torn Israel from the house of David, they had proclaimed Jeroboam son of Nebat king; and Jeroboam had drawn Israel away from the Lord and led them into a great sin.
The sons of Israel followed all the sins that Jeroboam had committed; they did not turn away from them,

until the Lord removed Israel from his presence, as he had announced through all his servants the prophets. And Israel was deported far from its own land to Assyria, where it has remained to this day.

The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, from Cuthah, from Avva, from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and settled them in the towns of Samaria in place of the sons of Israel; they took possession of Samaria and lived in its towns.
At the beginning of their settlement there, they did not fear the Lord, and the Lord sent lions among them that killed them.

Word was brought to the king of Assyria: "The nations you deported and settled in the towns of Samaria do not know the proper way to serve the god of the land; he has sent lions among them that are killing them, because they do not know how to serve the god of the land."
The king of Assyria ordered: "Send back there one of the priests you deported from it; let him go and settle there and teach them the proper way to serve the god of the land."
So one of the priests who had been deported from Samaria came and settled in Bethel, and he taught them how to fear the Lord.
But each nation made its own gods and set them up in the shrines of the high places that the Samaritans had built, each nation in the town where it lived.
The people of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, those of Cuthah made Nergal, those of Hamath made Ashima;
the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the people of Sepharvaim burned their children in the fire in honour of Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
They also feared the Lord; from among the people they appointed for themselves priests of the high places, who offered sacrifices for them in the shrines of the high places.
So they feared the Lord while serving their own gods, according to the custom of the nations from which they had been deported.

To this day they follow their old customs. They do not truly fear the Lord and do not conform to the statutes, the ordinances, the law, and the commandments that the Lord gave to the sons of Jacob, to whom he gave the name Israel.

The Lord had made a covenant with them and had given them this command: You shall not fear other gods, you shall not bow down before them, you shall not serve them, and you shall not offer them sacrifices.
But the Lord, who brought you up out of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm, he is the one you shall fear, before him you shall bow down, to him you shall offer sacrifices.
The statutes, the ordinances, the law, and the commandments that he wrote for you, you shall be careful to observe forever, and you shall not fear other gods.
You shall not forget the covenant that I made with you, and you shall not fear other gods.
But the Lord your God is the one you shall fear, and it is he who will deliver you from the hand of all your enemies.
They did not listen, but followed their old customs.
So these nations feared the Lord while serving their idols; and their children and grandchildren do to this day what their fathers did.
In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz became king of Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abi daughter of Zechariah.
He did what is right in the sight of the Lord, in every way like David his ancestor.

He did away with the high places, smashed the sacred stones, cut down the sacred pole, and broke into pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made; for until then the sons of Israel had been burning incense to it: it was called Nehushtan.
He put his trust in the Lord, the God of Israel; among all the kings of Judah, before him or after him, none was his equal.
Holding fast to the Lord, he did not turn away from him and kept the commandments that the Lord had given Moses.
So the Lord was with him, and he succeeded in everything he undertook. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and stopped serving him.
He struck down the Philistines as far as Gaza and ravaged their territory, from the watchtower to the fortified city.
In the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, marched up against Samaria and besieged it.
It was taken at the end of three years: in the sixth year of Hezekiah, the ninth year of Hoshea, king of Israel, Samaria was taken.
The king of Assyria deported Israel to Assyria; he settled them in Halah, on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes,
because they had not obeyed the voice of the Lord their God, but had broken his covenant: they had neither listened to nor carried out what Moses, the servant of the Lord, had commanded.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, marched up against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
