Hezekiah, king of Judah, sent word to the king of Assyria at Lachish: "I have done wrong; withdraw from me, and I will bear whatever you impose on me." The king of Assyria imposed on Hezekiah, king of Judah, about ten tonnes of silver and one tonne of gold.
Hezekiah gave all the silver found in the house of the Lord and in the treasuries of the royal palace.
At that time Hezekiah stripped the gold from the doors of the temple of the Lord and from the doorposts that he himself had overlaid, and he gave it to the king of Assyria.

From Lachish the king of Assyria sent to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, his commander-in-chief, his chief officer, and his chief cupbearer, with a large army. They marched up, came to Jerusalem, and halted by the conduit of the upper pool, on the road to the Fuller's Field.
They called for the king. Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the master of the palace, came out to them, along with Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph the recorder.
The chief cupbearer said to them, "Tell Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: What is this confidence you rely on?
You imagine that mere words serve for the strategy and strength needed for war! In whom, then, do you trust, that you rebel against me?
Look, you are trusting in Egypt, that broken reed which pierces and runs through the hand of anyone who leans on it. Such is Pharaoh, king of Egypt, to all who trust in him.

Perhaps you will tell me: It is in the Lord our God that we trust. But is it not he whose high places and altars Hezekiah has done away with, ordering Judah and Jerusalem: It is before this altar in Jerusalem that you shall bow down?
Now make a wager with my master, the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you can find riders to mount them!
How could you drive back a single governor, the least of my master's servants? And you are trusting in Egypt for chariots and horsemen!
Besides, is it apart from the will of the Lord that I have marched up to destroy this place? It is the Lord who said to me: March up against this land and destroy it."

Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah said to the chief cupbearer, "Speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand that language; do not speak to us in the language of Judah, within hearing of the people on the wall."

But the chief cupbearer replied, "Is it to your master and to you that my master sent me to say these things? Is it not rather to these men sitting on the wall, doomed like you to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?"
Then the chief cupbearer stood up and shouted in a loud voice, in the language of Judah: "Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria!
Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he cannot deliver you from my hand.
Do not let Hezekiah make you put your trust in the Lord by saying: The Lord will surely deliver us, and this city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.

Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of Assyria: Make peace with me, surrender to me, and each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and each will drink the water of his own cistern,

until I come and take you away to a land like your own, a land of grain and wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees, oil, and honey; then you will live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah; he is leading you astray by saying: The Lord will deliver us.
Have the gods of the nations each delivered their own land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Did they deliver Samaria from my hand?
Among all the gods of these lands, which ones have delivered their land from my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?"
The people kept silent and did not answer him a word, for the king had ordered: Do not answer him.

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the master of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with their garments torn, and reported to him the words of the chief cupbearer.
When he heard this report, King Hezekiah tore his garments, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the house of the Lord.
He sent Eliakim, the master of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and the elders of the priests, covered in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him, "Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of distress, of punishment, and of disgrace; the children have come to the point of birth, and there is no strength to bring them forth.

Perhaps the Lord your God will hear all the words of the chief cupbearer, sent by his master, the king of Assyria, to insult the living God; perhaps he will punish him for the words that the Lord your God has heard. So lift up a prayer for the remnant that still survives."
The servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah,

and Isaiah said to them, "This is what you shall say to your master: Thus says the Lord: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, by which the underlings of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
I am about to put such a spirit in him that, on hearing a report, he will return to his own land; and there I will make him fall by the sword."
The chief cupbearer went back and found the king of Assyria attacking Libnah, for he had learned that he had left Lachish.
Now the king of Assyria received a report about Tirhakah, king of Cush: They say he has set out to make war on you. He again sent messengers to Hezekiah with this order:
"You shall speak thus to Hezekiah, king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying: Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.
You have surely heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, dooming them to destruction: and you, would you be delivered?
Did their gods deliver them, those nations that my fathers destroyed: Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and of Ivvah?"
Hezekiah took the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it; then he went up to the house of the Lord and spread it out before the Lord.
Hezekiah prayed before the Lord: "Lord, God of Israel, enthroned upon the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth, you who made the heavens and the earth.
Lord, incline your ear and hear; Lord, open your eyes and see! Hear the words of Sennacherib, who has sent to insult the living God.
It is true, Lord, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands,
and that they have thrown their gods into the fire; but these were not gods, only the work of human hands, wood and stone: that is why they could destroy them.
Now, Lord our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone, Lord, are God."
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I have heard the prayer you have made to me concerning Sennacherib, king of Assyria.
This is the word that the Lord speaks against him: She despises you, she mocks you, the virgin daughter of Zion; she shakes her head behind you, the daughter of Jerusalem.
Whom have you insulted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes so high? Against the Holy One of Israel!

By your messengers you have insulted the Lord; you have said: With my many chariots I have climbed the summits of the mountains, the heights of Lebanon; I have cut down its tallest cedars, its finest cypresses; I have reached its farthest peak, its forest garden.
I have dug wells and drunk foreign waters; under the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.
Have you not heard? Long ago I prepared it, from ancient days I shaped it, and now I bring it to pass: you turn fortified cities into heaps of ruins.
Their inhabitants, drained of strength, are dismayed and confounded; they are like the grass of the fields, the tender green, the grass of the housetops, the grain scorched before it ripens.
Whether you sit down, go out, or come in, I know it; and I know your rage against me.
Because you rage against me and your arrogance has come up to my ears, I will put my ring in your nose and my bit in your lips, and I will lead you back by the way you came.
And this shall be the sign for you: this year you will eat what grows of itself; the second year, what springs up again; but in the third year, sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
What has escaped of the house of Judah, what remains, will again take root below and bear fruit above.
For from Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and from Mount Zion a band of survivors. This is what the zeal of the Lord of hosts will do.

Therefore, thus says the Lord concerning the king of Assyria: He will not enter this city, he will not shoot an arrow into it, he will not confront it with a shield, he will not raise a siege ramp against it.
He will return by the way he came, and he will not enter this city, says the Lord.
I will protect this city to save it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant."
That night the angel of the Lord went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand men in the Assyrian camp; when they rose in the morning, they were all dead bodies.
Sennacherib, king of Assyria, broke camp, departed, went home, and stayed at Nineveh.
As he was worshiping in the temple of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer, his sons, struck him down with the sword and then fled to the land of Ararat. His son Esarhaddon reigned in his place.

titres.titre: The illness and healing of Hezekiah

versets.t: In those days Hezekiah fell mortally ill. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, "Thus says the Lord: Put your house in order, for you are going to die; you will not recover."
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord:
"I beg you, Lord, remember that I have walked before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and that I have done what is good in your sight." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Isaiah had not yet left the middle court when the word of the Lord came to him:

"Turn back and say to Hezekiah, the leader of my people: Thus says the Lord, the God of David your ancestor: I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; behold, I am healing you; in three days you will go up to the house of the Lord.
I will add fifteen years to your life; I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will protect this city for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant."
Isaiah said, "Bring a cake of figs." They brought it, applied it to the boil, and Hezekiah recovered.
Hezekiah had asked Isaiah, "What will be the sign that the Lord will heal me and that, in three days, I will go up to the house of the Lord?"
Isaiah answered, "This, from the Lord, is the sign that he will fulfil the word he has given: shall the shadow go forward ten steps, or back ten steps?"
Hezekiah said, "It is a small thing for the shadow to go forward ten steps; no, let it rather go back ten steps!"
Then the prophet Isaiah called on the Lord, who made the shadow go back the ten steps by which it had already gone down on the steps of the sundial of Ahaz.
At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent a letter and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard of his illness.

Hezekiah was pleased and showed the envoys his whole treasure house: the silver, the gold, the spices, the fine oil, all his armoury, everything found in his storehouses. There was nothing in his house or in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them.
But the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and asked him, "What did these men say, and where did they come from to you?" Hezekiah answered, "They came from a distant land, from Babylon."
Isaiah asked, "What did they see in your house?" Hezekiah answered, "They saw everything in my house; there is nothing in my storehouses that I did not show them."
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the Lord:
Behold, days are coming when everything in your house, everything that your fathers have amassed to this day, will be carried off to Babylon; nothing will be left, says the Lord.
And some of your sons, your own offspring, whom you will father, will be taken to be made eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon."
Hezekiah answered Isaiah, "The word of the Lord that you have spoken is good." For he thought: At least there will be peace and security in my lifetime.

As for the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, all his exploits, and how he made the reservoir and the conduit to bring water into the city, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Hezekiah slept with his fathers. His son Manasseh reigned in his place.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hephzibah.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, imitating the abominable practices of the nations that the Lord had driven out before the sons of Israel.

He rebuilt the high places that Hezekiah his father had destroyed; he raised altars to Baal, set up a sacred pole, as Ahab, king of Israel, had done, and bowed down before all the host of heaven and served it.
He built altars in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord had said: It is in Jerusalem that I will set my name.
He built altars to all the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the Lord.

He passed his son through the fire, practiced astrology and divination, and dealt with mediums and spiritists: he multiplied what is evil in the sight of the Lord, provoking him to anger without ceasing.

He placed the image of Ashtoreth that he had made in the house of which the Lord had said to David and to his son Solomon: It is in this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, that I will set my name forever.

I will no longer make Israel's foot wander from the land I gave to their fathers, provided only that they are careful to carry out all that I have commanded them, the whole law that my servant Moses gave them.
But they did not obey; Manasseh led them astray, so that they did more evil than the nations that the Lord had destroyed before the sons of Israel.
Then the Lord spoke through his servants the prophets:
"Because Manasseh, king of Judah, has committed these abominations, doing worse than all that the Amorites did before him, and because he has led Judah into sin with his idols,
thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Behold, I am about to bring on Jerusalem and Judah such disaster that the ears of everyone who hears of it will tingle.
I will stretch over Jerusalem the measuring line of Samaria and the plumb line of the house of Ahab; I will wipe out Jerusalem as one wipes out a dish, wiping it and turning it over.
I will abandon the remnant of my heritage; I will hand them over to their enemies, and they will become the prey and spoil of all their enemies,
because they have done what is evil in my sight and have provoked me to anger from the day their fathers came out of Egypt to this day."
Manasseh also shed so much innocent blood that he filled Jerusalem with it from end to end, besides the sin into which he led Judah by doing what is evil in the sight of the Lord.
As for the rest of the acts of Manasseh, all that he did and the sin he committed, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Manasseh slept with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his palace, the garden of Uzza. His son Amon reigned in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz, of Jotbah.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, like Manasseh his father.
He followed in every way the path of his father, served the idols his father had served, and bowed down before them;
he abandoned the Lord, the God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the Lord.
The servants of Amon conspired against him and killed the king in his palace.
But the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amon, and they made his son Josiah king in his place.
As for the rest of the acts of Amon, what he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
They buried him in his tomb, in the garden of Uzza. His son Josiah reigned in his place.

titres.titre: Josiah and the book of the Law

versets.t: Josiah was eight years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jedidah daughter of Adaiah, of Bozkath.
He did what is right in the sight of the Lord; he followed in every way the path of David his ancestor, turning aside neither to the right nor to the left.
In the eighteenth year of King Josiah, the king sent to the house of the Lord the secretary Shaphan son of Azaliah, son of Meshullam, with this charge:
"Go up to the high priest Hilkiah; have him count up the money brought to the house of the Lord, gathered from the people by the keepers of the threshold,
and let it be handed over to the foremen appointed over the house of the Lord; they will pay the workmen who labour on the house of the Lord to repair its damage,
the carpenters, the builders, and the masons, and they will use it to buy the timber and dressed stone needed to repair the house.
But no accounting shall be required of them for the money handed over to them, for they act with honesty."
Then the high priest Hilkiah said to the secretary Shaphan, "I have found the book of the Law in the house of the Lord." And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, who read it.
The secretary Shaphan returned to the king and reported to him: "Your servants have poured out the money that was in the house and handed it over to the foremen appointed over the house of the Lord."
Then the secretary Shaphan announced to the king, "The priest Hilkiah has given me a book." And Shaphan read it aloud before the king.
When he heard the words of the book of the Law, the king tore his garments.
Then he gave this order to the priest Hilkiah, to Ahikam son of Shaphan, to Achbor son of Micaiah, to the secretary Shaphan, and to Asaiah the king's servant:

"Go, consult the Lord for me, for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that has been found; for great is the anger of the Lord that has blazed out against us, because our fathers did not obey the words of this book by acting according to all that is written in it for us."

The priest Hilkiah, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to the prophetess Huldah, wife of Shallum son of Tikvah, son of Harhas, the keeper of the wardrobe; she lived in Jerusalem, in the Second Quarter. They spoke to her,
and she said to them, "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Tell the man who sent you to me:
Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am about to bring disaster on this place and on its inhabitants, according to all the words of the book that the king of Judah has read;
for they have abandoned me and have offered incense to other gods, provoking me to anger by all their works. My anger has blazed out against this place, and it will not be quenched.
And you shall say to the king of Judah, who is sending you to consult the Lord: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning the words you have heard:

Because your heart has softened and you have humbled yourself before the Lord on hearing what I have pronounced against this place and its inhabitants, who will become an object of horror and a curse, and because you have torn your garments and wept before me, I too have heard you, says the Lord.

This is why I will gather you to your fathers; you will be laid in your tomb in peace, and your eyes will not see all the disaster that I am about to bring on this place." They brought this answer back to the king.
The king sent to gather to himself all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

Then the king went up to the house of the Lord, with all the men of Judah, all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, the prophets, and all the people, from the least to the greatest; and he read to them all the words of the book of the covenant, found in the house of the Lord.

Standing on the platform, the king made the covenant before the Lord, binding himself to follow the Lord, to keep his commandments, his ordinances, and his laws with all his heart and all his soul, so as to carry out the words of this covenant written in this book. And all the people joined in the covenant.

The king ordered the high priest Hilkiah, the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the threshold to remove from the temple of the Lord all the objects made for Baal, for Ashtoreth, and for all the host of heaven; he burned them outside Jerusalem, in the fields of the Kidron, and had their ashes carried to Bethel.

He removed the idolatrous priests whom the kings of Judah had appointed to burn incense on the high places, in the towns of Judah and around Jerusalem, along with those who offered incense to Baal, to the sun, to the moon, to the constellations, and to all the host of heaven.

He took the sacred pole out of the house of the Lord and carried it outside Jerusalem, to the Kidron Valley, where he burned it; he ground it to dust and threw its dust on the graves of the common people.
He demolished the houses of the male temple prostitutes that were in the house of the Lord, where women wove hangings for Ashtoreth.

He brought all the priests from the towns of Judah and defiled the high places where these priests had burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba. He demolished the high places of the gates, at the entrance of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, on the left as one enters the city gate.
However, the priests of the high places did not go up to the altar of the Lord in Jerusalem, but they ate unleavened bread among their brothers.
He also defiled Topheth, in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, so that no one could pass his son or his daughter through the fire in honour of Molech.

He did away with the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun, at the entrance of the house of the Lord, near the room of the eunuch Nathan-melech, in the outbuildings; and he burned the chariots of the sun.

The altars built by the kings of Judah on the roof, near the upper chamber of Ahaz, and those that Manasseh had built in the two courts of the house of the Lord, the king demolished; he broke them to pieces and threw their dust into the Kidron Valley.

The king also defiled the high places facing Jerusalem, south of the Mount of Destruction, which Solomon, king of Israel, had built for Ashtoreth, the abominable idol of the Sidonians, for Chemosh, the abominable idol of Moab, and for Milcom, the abomination of the sons of Ammon.
He smashed the sacred stones, cut down the sacred poles, and filled the place they had occupied with human bones.

Even the altar at Bethel and the high place that Jeroboam son of Nebat had built, the one who had led Israel into sin, that altar and that high place he demolished; he burned the high place and ground it to dust, and he burned the sacred pole.

Turning around, Josiah caught sight of the tombs that were there on the mountain; he had the bones taken out of them, burned them on the altar, and defiled it, according to the word that the Lord had spoken through the man of God who had announced these things.

Then he asked, "What is this monument that I see?" The people of the town answered him, "It is the tomb of the man of God who came from Judah, the one who announced what you have just done against the altar at Bethel."
The king said, "Leave it; let no one touch his bones." So they let his bones be, along with those of the prophet who came from Samaria.

Josiah also did away with all the shrines of the high places that were in the towns of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had built to provoke the Lord to anger; he dealt with them exactly as he had done at Bethel.
He slaughtered on the altars all the priests of the high places who were there, burned human bones on them, and then returned to Jerusalem.
The king gave this order to all the people: "Celebrate the Passover in honour of the Lord your God, as it is written in this book of the covenant."
Never had such a Passover been celebrated since the days of the judges who governed Israel, nor throughout all the days of the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah.
It was in the eighteenth year of King Josiah that this Passover was celebrated, in honour of the Lord, in Jerusalem.

Josiah also did away with the mediums, the spiritists, the household idols, the images, and all the detestable things to be seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, so as to carry out the words of the Law written in the book that the priest Hilkiah had found in the house of the Lord.
Before him there had been no king who, like him, turned to the Lord with all his heart, all his soul, and all his strength, according to the whole law of Moses; and after him none like him arose.
Yet the Lord did not turn back from the heat of his great anger, kindled against Judah because of all the provocations of Manasseh.
The Lord said, "I will also remove Judah from my presence, as I removed Israel; I will reject this city, Jerusalem, which I had chosen, and this house of which I had said: There my name shall be."
As for the rest of the acts of Josiah, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
In his days Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt, marched up to the king of Assyria, to the river Euphrates. King Josiah went out to meet him, but Neco killed him at Megiddo, as soon as he saw him.

His servants carried his body from Megiddo to Jerusalem on a chariot, and buried him in his tomb. The people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah, anointed him, and made him king in place of his father.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah, of Libnah.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, in every way like his fathers.

Pharaoh Neco put him in chains at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, so that he would no longer reign in Jerusalem; and he imposed on the land a tribute of about three and a half tonnes of silver and thirty-four kilos of gold.
Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of his father Josiah, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. As for Jehoahaz, he took him to Egypt, where he died.

Jehoiakim gave Pharaoh the silver and the gold, but he taxed the land to provide the sum demanded: each according to his assessment, he levied on the people of the land the silver and the gold to be handed over to Pharaoh Neco.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zebidah daughter of Pedaiah, of Rumah.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, in every way like his fathers.

titres.titre: Zedekiah, the last king of Judah

versets.t: In his days Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, took the field; Jehoiakim was his vassal for three years, then rebelled against him again.

The Lord sent against Jehoiakim bands of Chaldeans, bands of Arameans, bands of Moabites, and bands of Ammonites; he sent them against Judah to destroy it, according to the word that the Lord had spoken through his servants the prophets.
It was solely by the order of the Lord that this disaster came upon Judah, to remove it from his presence, because of all the sins of Manasseh,
and because of the innocent blood he had shed, with which he had filled Jerusalem: the Lord was unwilling to forgive.
As for the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, all that he did, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Jehoiakim slept with his fathers. His son Jehoiachin reigned in his place.
The king of Egypt did not march out of his country again, for the king of Babylon had taken all that belonged to the king of Egypt, from the Wadi of Egypt to the river Euphrates.
Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Nehushta daughter of Elnathan, of Jerusalem.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, in every way like his father.
At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, marched up against Jerusalem, and the city was besieged.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came in person before the city while his servants were besieging it.

Then Jehoiachin, king of Judah, went out to surrender to the king of Babylon, with his mother, his servants, his officials, and his eunuchs; and the king of Babylon took him prisoner in the eighth year of his reign.

He carried off from there all the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the royal palace, and he broke to pieces all the gold objects that Solomon, king of Israel, had made for the temple of the Lord, as the Lord had announced.
He deported all Jerusalem, all the officials and all the valiant warriors, ten thousand deportees, along with all the craftsmen and the smiths; only the poorest people of the land were left.
He deported Jehoiachin to Babylon; he deported from Jerusalem to Babylon the king's mother, the king's wives, his eunuchs, and the notables of the land.
All the fighting men, seven thousand in number, the craftsmen and the smiths, a thousand in number, all valiant and fit for war, the king of Babylon led away captive to Babylon.
In place of Jehoiachin, the king of Babylon made his uncle Mattaniah king, and changed his name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah, of Libnah.
He did what is evil in the sight of the Lord, in every way like Jehoiakim.
This happened to Jerusalem and Judah because of the anger of the Lord, until the day he cast them out from his presence. Now Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

titres.titre: The Temple and the city burned

versets.t: In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came with his whole army to attack Jerusalem; he pitched his camp before it and built siege works all around it.
The city remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
On the ninth of the fourth month, the famine was so severe in the city that there was no more bread for the people of the land.

A breach was made in the city; then, by night, all the fighting men fled by way of the gate between the two walls, near the king's garden, while the Chaldeans surrounded the city. They took the road to the Arabah.
But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, where all his army scattered from him.
They seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where sentence was passed on him.
They slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; then they put out his eyes, bound him with bronze chains, and took him to Babylon.
On the seventh day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, servant of the king of Babylon, entered Jerusalem.
He burned the house of the Lord, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem; he set fire to all the great houses.
The whole army of the Chaldeans, under the captain of the guard, demolished the walls surrounding Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, deported the rest of the people left in the city, the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.
The captain of the guard left only some of the poor of the land as vinedressers and plowmen.
The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars of the house of the Lord, the stands, and the bronze Sea that were in the house of the Lord, and carried their bronze off to Babylon.
They took the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the dishes, and all the bronze utensils used in the worship.
The captain of the guard also took the firepans and the sprinkling bowls, everything made of gold and everything made of silver.
As for the two pillars, the one Sea, and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of the Lord, the bronze of all these objects could not be weighed.
One pillar was nine metres high; it bore a bronze capital one and a half metres high, surrounded by latticework and pomegranates, all of bronze; the second pillar, with its latticework, was the same.
The captain of the guard took Seraiah the high priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold.

In the city he took an officer who was in command of the fighting men, five of the king's counsellors found in the city, the secretary of the army commander responsible for conscripting the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land present in the city.
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
The king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah, in the land of Hamath. So Judah was deported far from its own land.
As for the people who remained in the land of Judah, left there by Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, he appointed over them as governor Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan.

When all the commanders of the troops and their men heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, they came to him at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth of Netophah, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
Gedaliah swore this oath to them and to their men: "Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans; remain in the land, serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you."

But in the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal line, came with ten men; they struck down Gedaliah, along with the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
Then all the people, from the least to the greatest, together with the commanders of the troops, set out and went to Egypt, out of fear of the Chaldeans.

In the thirty-seventh year of the deportation of Jehoiachin, king of Judah, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, Evil-merodach, king of Babylon, in the year he came to the throne, raised up the head of Jehoiachin, king of Judah, and brought him out of prison.
He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat higher than those of the other kings held with him at Babylon.
Jehoiachin took off his prison clothes and ate at the king's table regularly, all the rest of his life.
His allowance was provided by the king, day by day, all the rest of his life.

titres.titre: From Adam to the sons of Noah
The sons of Shem, down to Abraham
The descendants of Esau and the kings of Edom

versets.t: Adam, Seth, Enosh,
Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,
Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,
Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittim, and the Rodanim.
The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush became the father of Nimrod, who was the first man to be a mighty warrior on the earth.
Mizraim became the father of the Ludim, the Anamim, the Lehabim, the Naphtuhim,
the Pathrusim, the Casluhim, from whom the Philistines came, and the Caphtorim.
Canaan became the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and of Heth,
as well as the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
the Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites.
The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram; Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
Arpachshad became the father of Shelah, and Shelah became the father of Eber.
To Eber were born two sons: one was named Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother was named Joktan.
Joktan became the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Ebal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab: all these were the sons of Joktan.
Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah,
Eber, Peleg, Reu,
Serug, Nahor, Terah,
Abram, that is, Abraham.
The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael.
These are their descendants. The firstborn of Ishmael was Nebaioth, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,
Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah: these are the sons of Ishmael.
The sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine: she bore Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.
The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.
Abraham became the father of Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.
The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek.
The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam; and Lotan's sister was Timna.
The sons of Shobal: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. The sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah.
The sons of Anah: Dishon. The sons of Dishon: Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. The sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the sons of Israel: Bela son of Beor; his city was named Dinhabah.
Bela died, and Jobab son of Zerah, of Bozrah, reigned in his place.
Jobab died, and Husham, from the land of the Temanites, reigned in his place.
Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad, who defeated Midian in the country of Moab, reigned in his place; his city was named Avith.
Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.
Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth on the River reigned in his place.
Shaul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place.
Baal-hanan died, and Hadad reigned in his place; his city was named Pai, and his wife's name was Mehetabel, daughter of Matred, daughter of Me-zahab.
Hadad died. The chiefs of Edom were: chief Timna, chief Aliah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, chief Iram: these are the chiefs of Edom.
These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, and Shelah; these three were born to him of the daughter of Shua, the Canaanite. Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the eyes of the Lord, and the Lord put him to death.
Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law, bore him Perez and Zerah. The sons of Judah were five in all.
The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara: five in all.
The sons of Carmi: Achar, who brought disaster on Israel by violating the ban.
The sons of Ethan: Azariah.
The sons who were born to Hezron: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.
Ram became the father of Amminadab; Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, prince of the sons of Judah;
Nahshon became the father of Salma; Salma became the father of Boaz;
Boaz became the father of Obed; Obed became the father of Jesse;
Jesse became the father of Eliab, his firstborn, Abinadab the second, Shimea the third,
Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
Ozem the sixth, David the seventh.
Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, three.
Abigail bore Amasa, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.
Caleb son of Hezron had children by Azubah his wife and by Jerioth. These are the sons of Azubah: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
Azubah died, and Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur.
Hur became the father of Uri, and Uri became the father of Bezalel.
Afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead; he was sixty years old when he married her, and she bore him Segub.
Segub became the father of Jair, who had twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead.
But Geshur and Aram took from them the Encampments of Jair, along with Kenath and its dependencies, sixty cities. All these were the sons of Machir, the father of Gilead.
After the death of Hezron at Caleb-ephrathah, Abijah, Hezron's wife, bore him Ashhur, the father of Tekoa.
The sons of Jerahmeel, Hezron's firstborn, were: Ram the firstborn, then Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
Jerahmeel had another wife, named Atarah, the mother of Onam.
The sons of Ram, Jerahmeel's firstborn: Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
The sons of Onam: Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.
The name of Abishur's wife was Abihail; she bore him Ahban and Molid.
The sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim. Seled died without sons.
The sons of Appaim: Ishi. The sons of Ishi: Sheshan. The sons of Sheshan: Ahlai.
The sons of Jada, Shammai's brother: Jether and Jonathan. Jether died without sons.
The sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These are the sons of Jerahmeel.
Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. He had an Egyptian slave named Jarha;
he gave his daughter to Jarha as a wife, and she bore him Attai.
Attai became the father of Nathan; Nathan became the father of Zabad;
Zabad became the father of Ephlal; Ephlal became the father of Obed;
Obed became the father of Jehu; Jehu became the father of Azariah;
Azariah became the father of Helez; Helez became the father of Eleasah;
Eleasah became the father of Sismai; Sismai became the father of Shallum;
Shallum became the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah became the father of Elishama.
The sons of Caleb, Jerahmeel's brother: Mesha his firstborn, the father of Ziph, and the sons of Mareshah, the father of Hebron.
The sons of Hebron: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema became the father of Raham, the father of Jorkeam; and Rekem became the father of Shammai.
The son of Shammai: Maon; and Maon was the father of Beth-zur.
Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran became the father of Gazez.
The sons of Jahdai: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
Maacah, Caleb's concubine, bore Sheber and Tirhanah;
she also bore Shaaph, the father of Madmannah, and Sheva, the father of Machbenah and of Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.
These were the sons of Caleb. The sons of Hur, Ephrathah's firstborn: Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim;
Salma, the father of Bethlehem; Hareph, the father of Beth-gader.
Shobal, the father of Kiriath-jearim, had as descendants: Haroeh and half the Menuhoth.
The families of Kiriath-jearim were: the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites; from them came the people of Zorah and Eshtaol.
The sons of Salma: Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, half the Manahathites, and the Zorites,
as well as the families of the scribes who lived at Jabez: the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These are the Kenites, descended from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.

titres.titre: The kings of Judah, from Solomon to the exile

versets.t: These are the sons of David who were born to him at Hebron: the firstborn, Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel; the second, Daniel, by Abigail of Carmel;
the third, Absalom, son of Maacah, daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur; the fourth, Adonijah, son of Haggith;
the fifth, Shephatiah, by Abital; the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah, his wife.
These six were born to him at Hebron, where he reigned seven years and six months; then he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
These are those who were born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, four, by Bathsheba, daughter of Ammiel;
then Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet: nine.
These are all the sons of David, besides the sons of the concubines; and Tamar was their sister.
The son of Solomon: Rehoboam; Abijah, his son; Asa, his son; Jehoshaphat, his son;
Joram, his son; Ahaziah, his son; Joash, his son;
Amaziah, his son; Azariah, his son; Jotham, his son;
Ahaz, his son; Hezekiah, his son; Manasseh, his son;
Amon, his son; Josiah, his son.
The sons of Josiah: the firstborn, Johanan; the second, Jehoiakim; the third, Zedekiah; the fourth, Shallum.
The sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah, his son; Zedekiah, his son.
The sons of Jeconiah, the captive: Shealtiel, his son,
Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
The sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei. The sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah; Shelomith was their sister;
then Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-hesed: five.
The sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah; the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shecaniah.
The sons of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. The sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat: six.
The sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam: three.
The sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani: seven.
The sons of Judah: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Reaiah, son of Shobal, became the father of Jahath; Jahath became the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These are the families of the Zorathites.
These are the descendants of the father of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash; and their sister was named Hazzelelponi.
Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer the father of Hushah. These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, the father of Bethlehem.
Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives: Helah and Naarah.
Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, the Temenites, and the Haahashtarites: these are the sons of Naarah.
The sons of Helah: Zereth, Zohar, and Ethnan.
Koz became the father of Anub, Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel, son of Harum.
Jabez was more honored than his brothers; his mother had named him Jabez, saying, I bore him in pain.

Jabez called upon the God of Israel: "If only you would truly bless me and enlarge my territory, if only your hand were with me and kept me from harm, so that I would not know pain!" And God granted him what he had asked.
Chelub, Shuhah's brother, became the father of Mehir, the father of Eshton.
Eshton became the father of Beth-rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, the father of Ir-nahash. These are the men of Recah.
The sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah. The sons of Othniel: Hathath and Meonothai.
Meonothai became the father of Ophrah. Seraiah became the father of Joab, the father of the Valley of Craftsmen, for they were craftsmen.
The sons of Caleb, son of Jephunneh: Iru, Elah, and Naam. The son of Elah: Kenaz.
The sons of Jehallelel: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
The sons of Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. The wife of Mered bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah, the father of Eshtemoa.
His Judahite wife bore Jered, the father of Gedor, Heber, the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel, the father of Zanoah. These are the sons of Bithiah, daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered had married.
The sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham: the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maacathite.
The sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-hanan, and Tilon. The sons of Ishi: Zoheth and Ben-zoheth.
The sons of Shelah, son of Judah: Er, the father of Lecah, Laadah, the father of Mareshah, and the families of the linen workers of Beth-ashbea,
Jokim, the men of Cozeba, Joash, and Saraph, who ruled over Moab and then returned to Bethlehem. These are ancient records.
These were the potters, inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah; they lived there, in the king's service, for his work.
The sons of Simeon: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul;
Shallum, his son; Mibsam, his son; Mishma, his son.
The sons of Mishma: Hammuel, his son; Zaccur, his son; Shimei, his son.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brothers did not have many children, and their families did not multiply as much as the sons of Judah.
They lived at Beer-sheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual,
Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,
Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,
Beth-marcaboth, Hazar-susim, Beth-biri, and Shaaraim: these were their cities until the reign of David,
along with their villages; they also had Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan, five cities,
and all the villages around them, as far as Baal. These were their settlements, and they kept their genealogical records.
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah son of Seraiah son of Asiel,
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
and Ziza son of Shiphi son of Allon son of Jedaiah son of Shimri son of Shemaiah:
these men, mentioned by name, were princes in their families, and their ancestral houses increased greatly.
They went toward the entrance of Gedor, to the east of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks.
They found rich and good pasture, a land broad, quiet, and peaceful; its former inhabitants were descended from Ham.

These men, recorded by name, came in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah; they destroyed the tents and the Meunites who were found there, put them under the ban to this day, and settled in their place, for there was pasture there for their flocks.
Five hundred of these sons of Simeon went to Mount Seir, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.
They struck down the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped, and they have lived there to this day.

The sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn. He was the firstborn; but because he had defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, son of Israel, though Joseph was not enrolled as firstborn in the genealogies;
for Judah prevailed over his brothers, and from him came a prince; but the birthright belonged to Joseph.
The sons of Reuben, Israel's firstborn: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
The sons of Joel: Shemaiah, his son; Gog, his son; Shimei, his son;
Micah, his son; Reaiah, his son; Baal, his son;
Beerah, his son, whom Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, carried into exile: he was prince of the Reubenites.
His brothers, by families, as they are enrolled in the genealogies according to their generations: the chief, Jeiel; then Zechariah;
and Bela, son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel. He lived at Aroer, as far as Nebo and Baal-meon;
to the east he extended as far as the edge of the wilderness that stretches toward the Euphrates, for their livestock were numerous in the land of Gilead.
In the days of Saul, they made war on the Hagrites, who fell into their hands; and they lived in their tents throughout the whole eastern side of Gilead.
The sons of Gad lived opposite them, in the land of Bashan, as far as Salecah.
Joel was the chief, Shapham the second, then Janai and Shaphat, in Bashan.
Their brothers, by ancestral houses, were: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber: seven.
They were the sons of Abihail, son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.
Ahi, son of Abdiel, son of Guni, was the chief of their ancestral houses.
They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its dependent villages, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon to their limits.
All these were enrolled in the genealogies in the days of Jotham, king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam, king of Israel.

The sons of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh numbered forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty valiant men, who carried shield and sword, drew the bow, and were trained for war, ready to go out on campaign.
They made war on the Hagrites, on Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.

They were helped against them: the Hagrites and all their allies were given into their hands, for they had cried out to God in the battle, and he answered them because they had put their trust in him.
They carried off their livestock: fifty thousand camels, two hundred fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys, and a hundred thousand persons.
Many fell slain, for the war was of God. And they settled in their place until the exile.
The sons of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land, from Bashan to Baal-hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon; they were numerous.
These are the chiefs of their ancestral houses: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel, mighty and valiant men, men of renown, chiefs of their houses.
But they were unfaithful to the God of their fathers and prostituted themselves to the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God had destroyed before them.

So the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul, king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, who carried away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh; he brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river Gozan, where they remain to this day.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The children of Amram: Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar became the father of Phinehas; Phinehas became the father of Abishua;
Abishua became the father of Bukki; Bukki became the father of Uzzi;
Uzzi became the father of Zerahiah; Zerahiah became the father of Meraioth;
Meraioth became the father of Amariah; Amariah became the father of Ahitub;
Ahitub became the father of Zadok; Zadok became the father of Ahimaaz;
Ahimaaz became the father of Azariah; Azariah became the father of Johanan;
Johanan became the father of Azariah: it was he who served as priest in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem;
Azariah became the father of Amariah; Amariah became the father of Ahitub;
Ahitub became the father of Zadok; Zadok became the father of Shallum;
Shallum became the father of Hilkiah; Hilkiah became the father of Azariah;
Azariah became the father of Seraiah; Seraiah became the father of Jehozadak;
and Jehozadak went into exile when the Lord sent Judah and Jerusalem into captivity by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
The sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of Levi according to their fathers.
Of Gershon: Libni, his son; Jahath, his son; Zimmah, his son;
Joah, his son; Iddo, his son; Zerah, his son; Jeatherai, his son.
The sons of Kohath: Amminadab, his son; Korah, his son; Assir, his son;
Elkanah, his son; Ebiasaph, his son; Assir, his son;
Tahath, his son; Uriel, his son; Uzziah, his son; Shaul, his son.
The sons of Elkanah: Amasai and Ahimoth;
Elkanah, his son; Zophai, his son; Nahath, his son;
Eliab, his son; Jeroham, his son; Elkanah, his son.
The sons of Samuel: the firstborn, Joel, and Abijah.
The sons of Merari: Mahli; Libni, his son; Shimei, his son; Uzzah, his son;
Shimea, his son; Haggiah, his son; Asaiah, his son.
These are the men whom David appointed to direct the singing in the house of the Lord, after the ark had a resting place.
They ministered with song before the Dwelling, the tent of meeting, until Solomon had built the house of the Lord in Jerusalem; they carried out their duty according to their rule.
These are the men who served, with their sons. Of the Kohathites: Heman, the singer, son of Joel, son of Samuel,
son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah,
son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai,
son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah,
son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah,
son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.
His brother Asaph, who stood at his right hand: Asaph, son of Berechiah, son of Shimea,
son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malchijah,
son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Adaiah,
son of Ethan, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei,
son of Jahath, son of Gershon, son of Levi.
The sons of Merari, their brothers, on the left: Ethan, son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch,
son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of Shemer,
son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.
Their brothers, the Levites, were assigned to all the service of the Dwelling, the house of God.

But Aaron and his sons made the offerings smoke on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense; they performed all the service of the most holy place and made atonement for Israel, according to all that Moses, the servant of God, had commanded.
These are the sons of Aaron: Eleazar, his son; Phinehas, his son; Abishua, his son;
Bukki, his son; Uzzi, his son; Zerahiah, his son;
Meraioth, his son; Amariah, his son; Ahitub, his son;
Zadok, his son; Ahimaaz, his son.
These are their dwelling places, according to their settlements within their territories. To the sons of Aaron, of the family of the Kohathites, fell the first lot by the casting of lots;
they were given Hebron, in the land of Judah, with its surrounding pasturelands;
but the fields of the city and its villages were given to Caleb, son of Jephunneh.
To the sons of Aaron were given the city of refuge Hebron, along with Libnah and its pasturelands, Jattir, Eshtemoa and its pasturelands,
Hilen and its pasturelands, Debir and its pasturelands,
Ashan and its pasturelands, Beth-shemesh and its pasturelands;
and from the tribe of Benjamin, Geba and its pasturelands, Alemeth and its pasturelands, Anathoth and its pasturelands: in all, thirteen cities according to their families.
The rest of the sons of Kohath received by lot ten cities from the families of the tribe, from the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The sons of Gershon, according to their families, received thirteen cities from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Manasseh, in Bashan.
The sons of Merari, according to their families, received by lot twelve cities from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.
The sons of Israel gave the Levites these cities with their pasturelands.
They gave by lot, from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin, the cities designated by name.
For the other families of the sons of Kohath, the cities of their territory were taken from the tribe of Ephraim.
They were given the city of refuge Shechem and its pasturelands, in the hill country of Ephraim, along with Gezer and its pasturelands,
Jokmeam and its pasturelands, Beth-horon and its pasturelands,
Aijalon and its pasturelands, Gath-rimmon and its pasturelands;
and from the half-tribe of Manasseh, Aner and its pasturelands, Bileam and its pasturelands: for the families of the rest of the sons of Kohath.
To the sons of Gershon were given: from the half-tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan and its pasturelands, Ashtaroth and its pasturelands;
from the tribe of Issachar, Kedesh and its pasturelands, Daberath and its pasturelands,
Ramoth and its pasturelands, Anem and its pasturelands;
from the tribe of Asher, Mashal and its pasturelands, Abdon and its pasturelands,
Hukok and its pasturelands, Rehob and its pasturelands;
and from the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee and its pasturelands, Hammon and its pasturelands, Kiriathaim and its pasturelands.
To the rest of the Levites, the sons of Merari, were given: from the tribe of Zebulun, Rimmono and its pasturelands, Tabor and its pasturelands;
beyond the Jordan, opposite Jericho, to the east of the Jordan: from the tribe of Reuben, Bezer in the wilderness and its pasturelands, Jahzah and its pasturelands,
Kedemoth and its pasturelands, Mephaath and its pasturelands;
and from the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead and its pasturelands, Mahanaim and its pasturelands,
Heshbon and its pasturelands, Jazer and its pasturelands.
The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron: four.

The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Samuel, chiefs of their ancestral houses descended from Tola, valiant men according to their generations; in the days of David their number was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
The sons of Uzzi: Izrahiah. The sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah, five, all of them chiefs.
They had with them, according to their generations and their ancestral houses, thirty-six thousand troops for war, for they had many wives and sons.
Their brothers, throughout all the families of Issachar, valiant men, were in all eighty-seven thousand, all enrolled in the genealogies.
The sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, and Jediael: three.
The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri, five chiefs of ancestral houses, valiant men, enrolled in the genealogies: twenty-two thousand thirty-four.
The sons of Becher: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth: all these were the sons of Becher,
enrolled in the genealogies according to their generations, chiefs of their ancestral houses, valiant men: twenty thousand two hundred.
The sons of Jediael: Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar:
all these were the sons of Jediael, chiefs of ancestral houses, valiant men, seventeen thousand two hundred, ready to go out on campaign for war.
Shuppim and Huppim were the sons of Ir, and Hushim the son of Aher.
The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum, the sons of Bilhah.
The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, whom his Aramean concubine bore to him; she also bore Machir, the father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife for Huppim and Shuppim; his sister was named Maacah. The name of the second son was Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had only daughters.
Maacah, Machir's wife, bore a son whom she named Peresh; his brother was named Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rekem.
The sons of Ulam: Bedan. These are the sons of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh.
His sister Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
The sons of Shemida were: Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
The sons of Ephraim: Shuthelah; Bered, his son; Tahath, his son; Eleadah, his son; Tahath, his son;
Zabad, his son; Shuthelah, his son; Ezer and Elead, whom the men of Gath, born in the land, killed because they had come down to carry off their livestock.
Their father Ephraim mourned for them a long time, and his brothers came to comfort him.
Then he went in to his wife, who conceived and bore a son; he named him Beriah, because misfortune had struck his house.
His daughter was Sheerah, who built Lower Beth-horon and Upper Beth-horon, as well as Uzzen-sheerah.
Rephah, his son, and Resheph; Telah, his son; Tahan, his son;
Ladan, his son; Ammihud, his son; Elishama, his son;
Nun, his son; Joshua, his son.

Their possessions and their settlements were: Bethel and its dependencies; to the east, Naaran; to the west, Gezer and its dependencies, Shechem and its dependencies, as far as Ayyah and its dependencies.

In the hands of the sons of Manasseh were Beth-shean and its dependencies, Taanach and its dependencies, Megiddo and its dependencies, Dor and its dependencies. It was there that the sons of Joseph, son of Israel, lived.
The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and Serah, their sister.
The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel, the father of Birzaith.
Heber became the father of Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and Shua, their sister.
The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath: these are the sons of Japhlet.
The sons of Shemer: Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram.
The sons of Helem, his brother: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
All these were the sons of Asher, chiefs of ancestral houses, choice and valiant men, chiefs among the princes; their number enrolled for military service was twenty-six thousand men.
Benjamin became the father of Bela, his firstborn, Ashbel the second, Aharah the third,
Nohah the fourth, and Rapha the fifth.
The sons of Bela: Addar, Gera, Abihud,
Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,
Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
These are the sons of Ehud, chiefs of the families that lived at Geba and were deported to Manahath:
Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera; it was he who deported them; he became the father of Uzza and Ahihud.
Shaharaim had children in the land of Moab, after he had sent away his wives Hushim and Baara.
By his wife Hodesh he had: Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,
Jeuz, Sachia, and Mirmah: these are his sons, chiefs of families.
By Hushim he had Abitub and Elpaal.
The sons of Elpaal: Eber, Misham, and Shemed, who built Ono, Lod, and its dependencies.
Beriah and Shema, chiefs of the families that lived at Aijalon, put to flight the inhabitants of Gath.
Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth,
Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,
Michael, Ishpah, and Joha were the sons of Beriah.
Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,
Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab were the sons of Elpaal.
Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,
Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,
Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were the sons of Shimei.
Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,
Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,
Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah,
Iphdeiah, and Penuel were the sons of Shashak.
Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,
Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri were the sons of Jeroham.
These were chiefs of families, chiefs according to their generations; they lived in Jerusalem.
At Gibeon lived the father of Gibeon; his wife was named Maacah.
His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, and Zecher.
Mikloth became the father of Shimeah. They too lived near their brothers in Jerusalem, together with them.
Ner became the father of Kish; Kish became the father of Saul; Saul became the father of Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
The son of Jonathan: Merib-baal; Merib-baal became the father of Micah.
The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz became the father of Jehoaddah; Jehoaddah became the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; Zimri became the father of Moza.
Moza became the father of Binea; Raphah, his son; Eleasah, his son; Azel, his son.
Azel had six sons, whose names are these: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan: all these were the sons of Azel.
The sons of Eshek, his brother: Ulam, his firstborn, Jeush the second, and Eliphelet the third.
The sons of Ulam were valiant men, archers; they had many sons and grandsons, a hundred and fifty. All these were among the sons of Benjamin.

titres.titre: The priests and Levites of Jerusalem

versets.t: So all Israel was enrolled in the genealogies, which are recorded in the book of the kings of Israel. And Judah was carried into exile to Babylon because of its unfaithfulness.
The first inhabitants to return to their possessions, in their cities, were the Israelites, the priests, the Levites, and the temple servants.
In Jerusalem lived some of the sons of Judah, some of the sons of Benjamin, and some of the sons of Ephraim and Manasseh:
of the sons of Perez, son of Judah: Uthai, son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani;
of the Shilonites: Asaiah, the firstborn, and his sons;
of the sons of Zerah: Jeuel, and their brothers: six hundred ninety;
of the sons of Benjamin: Sallu, son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah;
Ibneiah, son of Jeroham; Elah, son of Uzzi, son of Michri; Meshullam, son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah;
and their brothers, according to their generations: nine hundred fifty-six. All these men were chiefs of families according to their ancestral houses.
Of the priests: Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin,
Azariah, son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the chief officer of the house of God;
Adaiah, son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah; Maasai, son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer;
and their brothers, chiefs of their ancestral houses: one thousand seven hundred sixty men able for the service of the house of God.
Of the Levites: Shemaiah, son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Merari;
Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, Mattaniah, son of Micah, son of Zichri, son of Asaph;
Obadiah, son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah, son of Asa, son of Elkanah, who lived in the villages of the Netophathites.
The gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their brothers; Shallum was the chief.
He is still so today, at the king's gate on the east. These are the gatekeepers for the camp of the sons of Levi.

Shallum, son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his brothers of his father's house, the Korahites, had charge of guarding the thresholds of the tent; their fathers had guarded the entrance to the camp of the Lord.
Phinehas, son of Eleazar, had formerly been their chief, and the Lord was with him.
Zechariah, son of Meshelemiah, was gatekeeper at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

All those who were chosen as gatekeepers of the thresholds numbered two hundred twelve, enrolled in the genealogies of their villages. David and Samuel the seer had established them in their office of trust.
They and their sons guarded the gates of the house of the Lord, the house of the tent.
The gatekeepers were stationed on the four sides: to the east, to the west, to the north, and to the south.
Their brothers, who lived in their villages, had to come from time to time to join them for seven days.
For the four chief gatekeepers, the Levites, were constantly on duty; they also had charge of the chambers and the treasuries of the house of God.
They spent the night around the house of God, of which they had the guard, and they had to open it each morning.
Some of them had charge of the utensils of the service, which they counted as they brought them in and took them out.
Others were appointed over the furnishings, over all the sacred objects, over the fine flour, the wine, the oil, the incense, and the spices.
Some of the sons of the priests prepared the mixture of the spices.
Mattithiah, one of the Levites, the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was in charge of what was baked on the griddle.
Some of their brothers, among the Kohathites, were in charge of preparing the bread of the Presence for each Sabbath.
These are the singers, chiefs of Levitical families; they lodged in the chambers, free from other duties, for they were engaged in their work day and night.
These are the chiefs of Levitical families, chiefs according to their generations; they lived in Jerusalem.
At Gibeon lived the father of Gibeon, Jeiel; his wife was named Maacah.
His firstborn son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.
Mikloth became the father of Shimeam. They too lived near their brothers in Jerusalem, together with them.
Ner became the father of Kish; Kish became the father of Saul; Saul became the father of Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.
The son of Jonathan: Merib-baal; Merib-baal became the father of Micah.
The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, and Tarea.
Ahaz became the father of Jarah; Jarah became the father of Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; Zimri became the father of Moza.
Moza became the father of Binea; Rephaiah, his son; Eleasah, his son; Azel, his son.
Azel had six sons, whose names are these: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan: these are the sons of Azel.
The Philistines fought against Israel; the men of Israel fled before them and fell, slain, on Mount Gilboa.
The Philistines pressed hard after Saul and his sons, and they killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul.
The battle pressed hard against Saul; the archers found him, and he was seized with panic before them.

Saul said to his armor-bearer, "Draw your sword and run me through, before these uncircumcised men come and abuse me." But the armor-bearer refused, gripped by great fear. So Saul took his own sword and threw himself on it.
When the armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he too threw himself on his sword and died.
So Saul and his three sons perished; all his house perished together.
When the men of Israel in the valley saw that the army had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and fled; and the Philistines came and settled in them.
The next day, the Philistines came to strip the dead and found Saul and his sons lying on Mount Gilboa.
They stripped him, carried off his head and his weapons, and sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to proclaim the news before their idols and before the people.
They placed Saul's weapons in the temple of their gods and fastened his skull in the temple of Dagon.
When all Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
all the brave men arose, took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons, brought them back to Jabesh, buried their bones under the terebinth of Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
Saul died because of the unfaithfulness he had committed against the Lord: he had not kept the word of the Lord, and he had consulted a medium,
instead of consulting the Lord. So the Lord put him to death and transferred the kingship to David, son of Jesse.
All Israel gathered to David at Hebron and said, "Here we are, we are your bone and your flesh.

In the past, even when Saul was king, it was you who led Israel out on campaign and brought it back. And the Lord your God said to you: It is you who shall shepherd my people Israel, it is you who shall be ruler over my people Israel."

So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron; there David made a covenant with them before the Lord, and they anointed David king over Israel, according to the word that the Lord had spoken through Samuel.
David marched with all Israel against Jerusalem, that is, Jebus, where the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, lived.
The inhabitants of Jebus said to David, "You shall not enter here." But David captured the stronghold of Zion, that is, the city of David.
David had said, "Whoever strikes down the Jebusites first shall become chief and commander." Joab, son of Zeruiah, went up first, and he became chief.
David settled in the stronghold; that is why it was called the city of David.
He fortified the city all around, from the Millo and all around, while Joab restored the rest.
David grew greater and greater, and the Lord of hosts was with him.
These are the chiefs of David's mighty men, who, with all Israel, supported him in his kingship to make him king, according to the word of the Lord concerning Israel.
Here is the list of David's mighty men. Jashobeam, son of Hachmoni, chief of the officers; it was he who brandished his spear against three hundred men and killed them at one time.
After him, Eleazar, son of Dodo, the Ahohite; he was one of the three mighty men.
He was with David at Pas-dammim, where the Philistines had gathered for battle. There was there a field full of barley, and the army fled before the Philistines;
but they took their stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines, and the Lord granted a great victory.
Three of the thirty chiefs went down to David, to the rock, at the cave of Adullam, while the camp of the Philistines was pitched in the Valley of Rephaim.
David was then in the stronghold, and there was a Philistine garrison at Bethlehem.
David had a longing and said, "Who will give me water to drink from the cistern that is at the gate of Bethlehem?"

At once the three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines, drew water from the cistern at the gate of Bethlehem, carried it off, and brought it to David. But David would not drink it: he poured it out as a libation to the Lord

and said, "God forbid that I should do this! Should I drink the blood of these men at the risk of their lives? For it was at the risk of their lives that they brought it." And he refused to drink it. Such were the deeds of these three mighty men.
Abishai, brother of Joab, was the chief of the Three; he brandished his spear against three hundred men and killed them, and he made a name for himself among the Three.
He was the most honored of the Three and became their commander, but he did not equal the first three.

Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, son of a valiant man, rich in exploits, from Kabzeel: it was he who struck down the two champions of Moab; it was he who went down and killed the lion in the bottom of a cistern, on a snowy day.

It was he too who struck down an Egyptian of great height, measuring nearly two and a half meters; the Egyptian held in his hand a spear like a weaver's beam; Benaiah went down to him with a staff, snatched the spear from the Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear.
Such were the deeds of Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, and he made a name for himself among the three mighty men.
He was more honored than the Thirty, but he did not equal the Three. David put him in charge of his personal guard.
Mighty men of the army: Asahel, brother of Joab; Elhanan, son of Dodo, of Bethlehem;
Shammoth, of Harod; Helez, the Pelonite;
Ira, son of Ikkesh, of Tekoa; Abiezer, of Anathoth;
Sibbecai, the Hushathite; Ilai, the Ahohite;
Maharai, of Netophah; Heled, son of Baanah, of Netophah;
Ithai, son of Ribai, of Gibeah of the sons of Benjamin; Benaiah, of Pirathon;
Hurai, of the ravines of Gaash; Abiel, of the Arabah; Azmaveth, of Bahurim; Eliahba, of Shaalbon;
the sons of Hashem, the Gizonite; Jonathan, son of Shagee, the Hararite;
Ahiam, son of Sacar, the Hararite;
Eliphal, son of Ur;
Hepher, the Mecherathite; Ahijah, the Pelonite;
Hezro, of Carmel; Naarai, son of Ezbai;
Joel, brother of Nathan; Mibhar, son of Hagri;
Zelek, the Ammonite; Naharai, of Beeroth, armor-bearer of Joab, son of Zeruiah;
Ira, of Jattir; Gareb, of Jattir;
Uriah, the Hittite; Zabad, son of Ahlai;
Adina, son of Shiza, the Reubenite, chief of the Reubenites, and thirty with him;
Hanan, son of Maacah; Jehoshaphat, the Mithnite;
Uzzia, of Ashtaroth; Shama and Jeiel, sons of Hotham, of Aroer;
Jediael, son of Shimri; Joha, his brother, the Tizite;
Eliel, the Mahavite; Jeribai and Joshaviah, sons of Elnaam; Ithmah, the Moabite; Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel, of Zobah.

titres.titre: The warriors who rallied at Ziklag
The tribes make David king at Hebron

versets.t: These are the men who joined David at Ziklag, when he still had to keep away from Saul, son of Kish; they were among the mighty men who helped him in battle.
They were archers, able to sling stones and shoot arrows with the right hand as well as the left; they were kinsmen of Saul, of Benjamin.
At their head, Ahiezer, then Joash, both sons of Shemaah, of Gibeah; Jeziel and Pelet, sons of Azmaveth; Beracah; Jehu, of Anathoth;
Ishmaiah, of Gibeon, a mighty man among the Thirty and a chief of the Thirty; Jeremiah; Jahaziel; Johanan; Jozabad, of Gederah;
Eluzai; Jerimoth; Bealiah; Shemariah; Shephatiah, of Haruph;
Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites;
Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham, of Gedor.

From the Gadites, mighty men went over to David at the stronghold in the wilderness: warriors trained for battle, wielding shield and spear, with faces like lions, as swift as gazelles on the mountains.
Ezer was the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third,
Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth,
Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh,
Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth,
Jeremiah the tenth, Machbannai the eleventh.
These sons of Gad were chiefs of the army: the least was worth a hundred, and the greatest, a thousand.
It was they who crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it overflows all its banks, and who put to flight all the inhabitants of the valleys, to the east and to the west.
Some of the sons of Benjamin and Judah also came to David at the stronghold.
