David went out to meet them and said to them, "If you come to me as friends, to help me, my heart will be knit to yours; but if it is to betray me to my enemies, when there is no violence in my hands, may the God of our fathers see it and judge!"

Then the Spirit clothed Amasai, chief of the officers, and he said, "We are yours, David! With you, son of Jesse! Peace, peace to you, and peace to him who helps you, for your God helps you!" David welcomed them and placed them among the chiefs of his troop.

Some men of Manasseh also went over to David, when he went with the Philistines to fight against Saul; but he did not help them, for the Philistine princes, after deliberation, sent him away, saying, "At the risk of our own heads, he might go over to his master Saul."
As he was returning to Ziklag, there went over to him, from Manasseh: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, chiefs of thousands in Manasseh.
They helped David against the raiding bands, for they were all mighty warriors, and they became commanders in the army.
Day after day, men came to David to help him, until it grew into a great army, like an army of God.
This is the number of the men armed for war who came to David at Hebron, to transfer to him the kingship of Saul, according to the command of the Lord.
Sons of Judah, bearing shield and spear: six thousand eight hundred armed for war.
Of the sons of Simeon, mighty warriors: seven thousand one hundred.
Of the sons of Levi: four thousand six hundred;
with Jehoiada, chief of the house of Aaron, and three thousand seven hundred with him;
and Zadok, a brave young man, with twenty-two chiefs of his ancestral house.
Of the sons of Benjamin, kinsmen of Saul: three thousand; for until then, most of them had remained loyal to the house of Saul.
Of the sons of Ephraim: twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty warriors, men of renown in their ancestral houses.
Of the half-tribe of Manasseh: eighteen thousand, designated by name to go and make David king.
Of the sons of Issachar, who knew how to discern the times to know what Israel should do: two hundred chiefs, with all their kinsmen under their command.
Of Zebulun: fifty thousand, fit to go out on campaign, ready for battle with all their weapons, resolute with one heart.
Of Naphtali: a thousand chiefs, and with them thirty-seven thousand men bearing shield and spear.
Of the Danites, ready for battle: twenty-eight thousand six hundred.
Of Asher, fit to go out on campaign and ready for battle: forty thousand.
And from beyond the Jordan, of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, with all the weapons of war: one hundred and twenty thousand.
All these men of war, in battle array, came with a sincere heart to Hebron to make David king over all Israel; and all the rest of Israel were of one heart to make David king.
They stayed there three days with David, eating and drinking, for their kinsmen had prepared provisions for them.

And even their neighbors, as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, brought provisions on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen: flour, cakes of figs, raisins, wine, oil, cattle and sheep in abundance; for there was joy in Israel.

titres.titre: The first attempt to bring back the ark

versets.t: David took counsel with the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, with all the leaders.

Then he said to the whole assembly of Israel, "If it seems good to you and if it comes from the Lord our God, let us quickly send word to the rest of our kinsmen, in all the regions of Israel, and also to the priests and Levites in their towns and pasturelands, that they may join us,
and let us bring back to us the ark of our God; for we did not concern ourselves with it in the days of Saul."
The whole assembly agreed to do so, for the thing seemed right to all the people.
So David gathered all Israel, from the Shihor of Egypt to the entrance of Hamath, to bring back from Kiriath-jearim the ark of God.

David, with all Israel, went up to Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim, which belongs to Judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, the Lord who is enthroned on the cherubim, the ark over which his name is invoked.
They carried the ark of God on a new cart and brought it from the house of Abinadab; Uzza and Ahio drove the cart.
David and all Israel danced with all their might before God, singing, to the sound of lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
When they came to the threshing floor of Chidon, Uzza reached out his hand to steady the ark, for the oxen had stumbled.
Then the anger of the Lord blazed against Uzza, and he struck him down for reaching out his hand to the ark; and Uzza died there, before God.
David was distressed that the Lord had broken out against Uzza, striking him; and that place is called to this day Perez-uzza, the Breach of Uzza.
David was afraid of God that day and said, "How can I bring the ark of God home to me?"
He did not take it home to himself, in the city of David, but had it taken to the house of Obed-edom, of Gath.
The ark of God remained three months in the house of Obed-edom, with his household; and the Lord blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belonged to him.
Hiram, king of Tyre, sent messengers to David, with cedar wood, stonecutters, and carpenters, to build him a palace.
David then recognized that the Lord had established him as king over Israel, and that his kingship was highly exalted, for the sake of his people Israel.
David took more wives at Jerusalem, and he fathered more sons and daughters.
These are the names of the children he had at Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,
Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
The Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over all Israel, and they all went up in search of him. David heard of it and went out to meet them.
The Philistines came and spread out in the Valley of Rephaim.
David inquired of God, "Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver them into my hand?" The Lord answered, "Go up, I will deliver them into your hand."

They went up to Baal-perazim, where David struck them down. And David said, "By my hand, God has broken through my enemies, like a breach made by waters." That is why that place was named Baal-perazim, the Master of Breaches.
The Philistines abandoned their gods there, and David ordered them to be given over to the fire.
The Philistines spread out again in the valley.
David again inquired of God, who answered him, "Do not go up after them; go around them and come upon them opposite the balsam trees.
When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, then go out to battle, for God will have gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines."
David did as God had commanded him, and they struck down the army of the Philistines from Gibeon to Gezer.
The fame of David spread through all the lands, and the Lord made all the nations fear him.

titres.titre: The bringing up of the ark in joy

versets.t: David built himself houses in the city of David; he prepared a place for the ark of God and pitched a tent for it.
Then David said, "No one is to carry the ark of God except the Levites, for it is they whom the Lord chose to carry the ark of the Lord and to serve it forever."
David gathered all Israel at Jerusalem to bring up the ark of the Lord to the place he had prepared for it.
David assembled the sons of Aaron and the Levites:
of the sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief, with his kinsmen: one hundred and twenty;
of the sons of Merari, Asaiah the chief, with his kinsmen: two hundred and twenty;
of the sons of Gershon, Joel the chief, with his kinsmen: one hundred and thirty;
of the sons of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief, with his kinsmen: two hundred;
of the sons of Hebron, Eliel the chief, with his kinsmen: eighty;
of the sons of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, with his kinsmen: one hundred and twelve.
David called the priests Zadok and Abiathar, and the Levites Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab,
and he said to them, "You are the heads of the Levitical families; sanctify yourselves, you and your kinsmen, and bring up the ark of the Lord, the God of Israel, to the place I have prepared for it.
For the first time, it was not you who carried it, and the Lord our God broke out against us, because we did not seek him according to the rule."
The priests and the Levites sanctified themselves to bring up the ark of the Lord, the God of Israel.
The sons of Levi carried the ark of God on their shoulders, with the poles, as Moses had commanded according to the word of the Lord.
David told the chiefs of the Levites to appoint their kinsmen, the singers, with musical instruments, lyres, harps, and cymbals, to sound aloud with songs of joy.
So the Levites appointed Heman, son of Joel; among his kinsmen, Asaph, son of Berechiah; among the sons of Merari, their kinsmen, Ethan, son of Kushaiah;

and with them, in the second rank, their kinsmen: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, the gatekeepers.
The singers Heman, Asaph, and Ethan sounded the bronze cymbals;
Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah played the lyre in the manner of maidens;
Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah held the harps at the lower octave, to lead the singing.
Chenaniah, chief of the Levites for the transport, directed the transport, for he was skilled at it.
Berechiah and Elkanah were gatekeepers beside the ark.
The priests Shebaniah, Jehoshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer sounded the trumpet before the ark of God; Obed-edom and Jehiah were gatekeepers beside the ark.
David, the elders of Israel, and the commanders of thousands set out to bring up, with joy, the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the house of Obed-edom.
And because God helped the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
David was clothed in a robe of fine linen, like all the Levites who carried the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah, the master of the transport; David also wore a linen ephod.
All Israel brought up the ark of the covenant of the Lord amid shouts of joy, to the sound of the horn, trumpets, and cymbals, sounding aloud with lyres and harps.
Now as the ark of the covenant of the Lord came to the city of David, Michal, daughter of Saul, looked out of the window; seeing King David leaping and dancing, she despised him in her heart.

titres.titre: The ark placed in the tent
The service before the ark and at Gibeon

versets.t: They brought in the ark of God and set it in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; then they offered before God burnt offerings and peace offerings.
When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord.
Then he distributed to all the Israelites, men and women, to each a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins.
David appointed before the ark of the Lord some Levites to minister, to invoke, celebrate, and praise the Lord, the God of Israel.
These were Asaph, the chief; Zechariah, the second; then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-edom, and Jeiel, with lyres and harps; and Asaph sounded the cymbals;
the priests Benaiah and Jahaziel sounded the trumpet continually before the ark of the covenant of God.
That day, for the first time, David charged Asaph and his kinsmen to praise the Lord:
Give thanks to the Lord, call upon his name, make known his deeds among the peoples!
Sing to him, play for him, tell of all his wonders!
Glory in his holy name; let the heart of those who seek the Lord rejoice!
Seek the Lord and his strength, seek his face continually!
Remember the wonders he has done, his marvels and the judgments of his mouth,
you, offspring of Israel his servant, sons of Jacob, his chosen ones!
He is the Lord our God; his judgments reach over all the earth.
Remember his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
the covenant made with Abraham, the oath sworn to Isaac,
which he established as a decree for Jacob, as an everlasting covenant for Israel,
saying, "To you I will give the land of Canaan, as the portion of your inheritance."
You were then only few in number, of little account, strangers in the land;
they wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people;
but he let no one oppress them, and he rebuked kings on their account:
"Do not touch my anointed ones, do no harm to my prophets!"
Sing to the Lord, all the earth! Proclaim his salvation from day to day!
Recount his glory among the nations, his wonders among all the peoples!
For the Lord is great and most worthy of praise, to be feared above all gods;
all the gods of the peoples are nothing but idols, but the Lord made the heavens.
Splendor and majesty are before him, strength and joy are in his dwelling.
Ascribe to the Lord, families of the peoples, ascribe to the Lord glory and power,
ascribe to the Lord the glory of his name! Bring an offering, come into his presence, bow down before the Lord in his sacred splendor!
Tremble before him, all the earth! Yes, the world stands firm, unshaken.
Let the heavens rejoice, let the earth exult! Let them say among the nations, "The Lord is king!"
Let the sea roar, and all that fills it, let the countryside exult, with all that is in it,
let the trees of the forest cry out for joy before the Lord, for he comes to judge the earth!
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his faithful love endures forever!
Say, "Save us, God of our salvation, gather us and rescue us from the nations, that we may celebrate your holy name and glory in praising you!"
Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! And all the people said, "Amen!" and, "Praise the Lord!"
David left there, before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, Asaph and his kinsmen, to minister continually before the ark according to each day's service;
with Obed-edom and his kinsmen, sixty-eight in number; Obed-edom, son of Jeduthun, and Hosah as gatekeepers.
He left the priest Zadok and his kinsmen, the priests, before the Dwelling of the Lord, on the high place of Gibeon,
to offer to the Lord burnt offerings on the altar of burnt offering, continually, morning and evening, according to all that is written in the law that the Lord had prescribed to Israel.
With them were Heman, Jeduthun, and the rest of those who had been chosen and designated by name, to give thanks to the Lord, for his faithful love endures forever.
With them, Heman and Jeduthun had the trumpets and the cymbals for the musicians, as well as the instruments for accompanying the songs of God; the sons of Jeduthun were at the gate.
Then all the people went away, each to his own home, and David returned to bless his household.
When David was settled in his palace, he said to the prophet Nathan, "Here I am living in a palace of cedar, while the ark of the covenant of the Lord is under a tent!"
Nathan answered David, "Do all that you have in mind, for God is with you."
But that night, the word of God came to Nathan:
"Go and tell my servant David: Thus says the Lord: It is not you who shall build me a house to dwell in.
For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought Israel up from Egypt to this day; I have gone from one tent to another, from one dwelling to another.
Wherever I have walked with all Israel, did I ever say to any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd my people: Why have you not built me a house of cedar?
Now you shall tell my servant David: Thus says the Lord of hosts: It was I who took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people Israel.
I have been with you wherever you went, I have cut off all your enemies before you, and I have made you a name like that of the great ones of the earth.
I have appointed a place for my people Israel; I have planted them there so that they may dwell there and be troubled no more, and that the wicked may no longer oppress them as before,
in the time when I had appointed judges over my people Israel. I have humbled all your enemies. And I declare to you: the Lord will build you a house.
When your days are fulfilled and you go to join your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, one of your sons, and I will establish his kingship.
It is he who will build me a house, and I will establish his throne forever.
I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me; I will not withdraw my faithful love from him, as I withdrew it from the one who reigned before you.
I will establish him forever in my house and in my kingdom, and his throne will be firm forever."
Nathan reported to David all these words and all this vision.
Then King David went in, stood before the Lord, and said, "Who am I, Lord God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
And even this is little in your eyes, O God: you have spoken of the house of your servant for a distant future, and you have looked on me as a man of high rank, Lord God.
What more could David say to you for the honor granted to your servant? You, you know your servant.
Lord, it is for the sake of your servant and according to your heart that you have accomplished all this greatness, making known all these great things.
Lord, there is none like you, and there is no God but you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

What other nation on earth is like your people Israel, whom God came to redeem to make them his people, making yourself a name by great and awesome wonders, driving out nations before your people whom you redeemed from Egypt?
You made your people Israel your people forever, and you, Lord, became their God.
Now, Lord, let the word you have spoken concerning your servant and his house stand forever, and act according to your word!

Let it stand, and let your name be glorified forever, so that it may be said: The Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, is God for Israel! And let the house of your servant David be established before you!
For it is you, my God, who have revealed to your servant that you would build him a house; that is why your servant has dared to pray to you.
And now, Lord, it is you who are God, and you have made this fair promise to your servant.
Be pleased, then, to bless the house of your servant, that it may remain forever before you; for what you bless, Lord, is blessed forever."
After this, David struck down the Philistines and subdued them; he took Gath and its dependencies from the hand of the Philistines.
He struck down Moab, and the Moabites became subject to David, paying him tribute.
David struck down Hadadezer, king of Zobah, toward Hamath, as he was going to establish his dominion over the river Euphrates.
David took from him a thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers; he hamstrung all the chariot horses, keeping only a hundred.
The Arameans of Damascus came to the aid of Hadadezer, king of Zobah, but David killed twenty-two thousand of them.
David placed garrisons in Aram of Damascus, and the Arameans became subject to David, paying him tribute. The Lord gave victory to David wherever he went.
David took the gold shields carried by the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.
From Tibhath and Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David took a great quantity of bronze, from which Solomon made the bronze Sea, the columns, and the objects of bronze.
When Tou, king of Hamath, heard that David had struck down the whole army of Hadadezer, king of Zobah,

he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and congratulate him for having fought and defeated Hadadezer, for Tou was constantly at war with Hadadezer; he sent all kinds of objects of gold, silver, and bronze.
King David consecrated these to the Lord, along with the silver and gold he had taken from all the nations: from Edom, from Moab, from the sons of Ammon, from the Philistines, and from Amalek.
Abishai, son of Zeruiah, struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
He placed garrisons in Edom, and all Edom became subject to David. The Lord gave victory to David wherever he went.
David reigned over all Israel, exercising right and justice for all his people.
Joab, son of Zeruiah, commanded the army; Jehoshaphat, son of Ahilud, was recorder;
Zadok, son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech, son of Abiathar, were priests; Shavsha was secretary;
Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, commanded the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David were the chief officials at the king's side.
After this, Nahash, king of the sons of Ammon, died, and his son reigned in his place.

David said, "I want to show kindness to Hanun, son of Nahash, for his father showed it to me." And David sent messengers to console him concerning his father. But when David's servants came to the land of the sons of Ammon, to Hanun, to console him,

the princes of the sons of Ammon said to Hanun, "Do you think it is to honor your father that David sends you consolers? Is it not rather to explore, overthrow, and spy out the land that his servants have come?"
Then Hanun seized David's servants, shaved them, cut their garments off halfway, up to the hips, and sent them away.

Someone came and informed David of what had happened to his men, and he sent to meet them, for they were covered with shame. The king had them told, "Stay at Jericho until your beards have grown back, then return."

The sons of Ammon saw that they had made themselves odious to David. Then Hanun and the sons of Ammon sent about thirty-four tonnes of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from the Arameans of Mesopotamia, of Maacah, and of Zobah.
They hired thirty-two thousand chariots, as well as the king of Maacah and his army, who came and camped before Medeba. The sons of Ammon gathered from their cities and came to battle.
David heard of it and sent against them Joab with the whole army of the mighty men.
The sons of Ammon came out and drew up in battle at the entrance of the city, while the kings who had come to their aid stood apart, in the open country.
Seeing that he had a battle front before and behind him, Joab chose an elite from Israel and deployed it against the Arameans;
he entrusted the rest of the army to his brother Abishai, who deployed it against the sons of Ammon,
and he said, "If the Arameans are stronger than I, you shall come to my aid; if the sons of Ammon are stronger than you, I will help you.
Be courageous! Let us show ourselves valiant for our people and for the cities of our God, and may the Lord do what seems good to him."
Joab advanced with his men to attack the Arameans, who fled before him.
Seeing the Arameans in flight, the sons of Ammon also fled before Abishai, brother of Joab, and went back into the city. Then Joab returned to Jerusalem.
Seeing themselves defeated by Israel, the Arameans sent messengers to bring the Arameans from beyond the River, with Shophach, commander of Hadadezer's army, at their head.

This was announced to David, who gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, marched against them, and drew up in battle against them. David deployed his army against the Arameans, and they engaged in combat.
But the Arameans fled before Israel; David killed of the Arameans seven thousand chariot teams and forty thousand foot soldiers, and he put to death Shophach, the commander of the army.
The vassals of Hadadezer, seeing themselves defeated by Israel, made peace with David and became subject to him. And the Arameans would no longer help the sons of Ammon.

titres.titre: The capture of Rabbah and the giants

versets.t: At the turn of the year, at the time when kings go out on campaign, Joab led a strong army, ravaged the land of the sons of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah, while David remained at Jerusalem. Joab struck Rabbah and destroyed it.

David took the crown from the head of their king; it weighed about thirty-four kilos of gold and bore a precious stone. It was placed on David's head, and he carried off a very great spoil from the city.
He brought out the inhabitants and set them to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. David did the same to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. Then David and all the army returned to Jerusalem.
After this, a battle took place at Gezer against the Philistines. It was then that Sibbecai, the Hushathite, killed Sippai, one of the descendants of the giants, and the Philistines were subdued.
There was again a battle against the Philistines; Elhanan, son of Jair, killed Lahmi, brother of Goliath of Gath, whose spear had a shaft like a weaver's beam.
There was again a battle at Gath. There was there a man of great height, who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in all; he too was descended from the giants.
He defied Israel, and Jonathan, son of Shimea, brother of David, killed him.
These men were descendants of the giants of Gath; they fell by the hand of David and his servants.

titres.titre: The Altar on the Threshing Floor of Ornan

versets.t: Satan rose up against Israel and incited David to take a census of Israel.
So David said to Joab and the commanders of the people, "Go, count Israel from Beersheba to Dan, and bring me a report, so that I may know their number."
Joab replied, "May the Lord increase his people a hundredfold! My lord the king, are they not all my lord's servants? Why does my lord want this? Why should he bring guilt upon Israel?"
But the king's word prevailed over Joab. So Joab set out, went throughout all Israel, and then returned to Jerusalem.
Joab gave David the result of the census: in all Israel there were one million one hundred thousand men who drew the sword, and in Judah four hundred and seventy thousand.
Joab had not counted Levi and Benjamin among them, for the king's command was repugnant to him.
This matter was displeasing to God, and he struck Israel.
David said to God, "I have sinned greatly in doing this. Now, I beg you, take away the guilt of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."
The Lord spoke to Gad, David's seer:
"Go and say to David: Thus says the Lord: I offer you three things; choose one of them, and I will carry it out against you."
So Gad came to David and said to him, "Thus says the Lord: Take your choice:

either three years of famine, or three months of fleeing before your foes while the sword of your enemies pursues you, or three days of the sword of the Lord and plague upon the land, with the angel of the Lord ravaging the whole territory of Israel. Now decide what answer I am to give to the one who sent me."
David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let me fall into the hands of the Lord, for his mercy is very great; but let me not fall into the hands of men."
So the Lord sent a plague upon Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.

God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it; but as he was destroying it, the Lord looked and relented of the disaster, and he said to the destroying angel, "Enough! Now stay your hand." The angel of the Lord was then standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

David looked up and saw the angel of the Lord standing between earth and heaven, with a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem. Then David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell face down on the ground.

David said to God, "Was it not I who ordered the people to be counted? It is I who have sinned, I who have done wrong; but these sheep, what have they done? Lord my God, let your hand be against me and against my father's house, but not against your people, to strike them."
The angel of the Lord commanded Gad to tell David to go up and set up an altar to the Lord on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
So David went up, according to the word that Gad had spoken in the name of the Lord.
Ornan, who was threshing wheat, turned around and saw the angel; his four sons who were with him hid themselves.
As David came toward Ornan, Ornan looked, recognized David, came out from the threshing floor, and bowed down before him with his face to the ground.
David said to Ornan, "Give me the site of the threshing floor, so that I may build an altar to the Lord on it; give it to me for its full price, so that the plague may be lifted from the people."

Ornan said to David, "Take it, and let my lord the king do what seems good to him. See, I give the oxen for the burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for the wood, and the wheat for the grain offering: I give it all."
But King David said to Ornan, "No! I insist on buying it for its full price, for I will not take for the Lord what is yours, nor offer a burnt offering that costs me nothing."
So David gave Ornan about seven kilograms of gold for the site.
David built there an altar to the Lord and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called upon the Lord, who answered him with fire from heaven upon the altar of burnt offering.
Then the Lord spoke to the angel, who put his sword back into its sheath.
At that time, seeing that the Lord had answered him on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, David offered sacrifices there.
The Dwelling of the Lord, which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering were at that time on the high place at Gibeon;
but David could not go before that altar to seek God, so terrified was he by the sword of the angel of the Lord.

titres.titre: David Prepares for Building the Temple

versets.t: David said, "Here is the house of the Lord God, and here is the altar of burnt offering for Israel."
David gave orders to gather the foreigners residing in the land of Israel, and he appointed stonecutters to prepare dressed stones for building the house of God.
David prepared iron in quantity for the nails of the door panels and for the clamps, along with a mass of bronze too great to be weighed,
and cedar timbers beyond counting, for the Sidonians and the Tyrians had brought David an abundance of them.

David said, "My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the Lord must be so magnificent that it becomes renowned and glorious in every land; so I will make preparations for it." And David made extensive preparations before his death.
He called his son Solomon and charged him to build a house for the Lord, the God of Israel.
David said to Solomon, "My son, I had it in my heart to build a house for the name of the Lord my God.
But the word of the Lord came to me: You have shed much blood and waged great wars; you shall not build a house for my name, because you have shed so much blood before me on the earth.

Behold, a son will be born to you who will be a man of peace; I will give him rest from all his enemies around him. His name will be Solomon, and I will give Israel peace and quiet during his lifetime.
He is the one who will build a house for my name; he will be a son to me, and I will be a father to him, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel forever.
Now, my son, may the Lord be with you! May you succeed and build the house of the Lord your God, as he has said of you.
May the Lord grant you only wisdom and understanding when he sets you over Israel, so that you may keep the law of the Lord your God!
Then you will succeed, if you take care to carry out the statutes and ordinances that the Lord commanded Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous, without fear or dread!

See, at great cost I have provided for the house of the Lord about three thousand four hundred tonnes of gold and thirty-four thousand tonnes of silver; as for the bronze and iron, they cannot be weighed, there is so much. I have also provided timber and stone, and you will add to them still.
You have with you a multitude of workers, stonecutters, masons, carpenters, and men skilled in every kind of work.
The gold, the silver, the bronze, and the iron are beyond counting. Arise, set to work, and may the Lord be with you!"
David commanded all the leaders of Israel to help his son Solomon:
"Is not the Lord your God with you? Has he not given you rest on every side? For he has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand, and the land is subdued before the Lord and his people.

Now set your heart and soul to seek the Lord your God. Arise and build the sanctuary of the Lord God, to bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord and the sacred vessels of God into the house that is to be built for the name of the Lord."
When David was old and full of years, he made his son Solomon king over Israel.
He gathered together all the leaders of Israel, the priests, and the Levites.
The Levites thirty years old and upward were counted; their number, head by head, man by man, was thirty-eight thousand.
"Of these," said David, "let twenty-four thousand direct the service of the house of the Lord; six thousand will be scribes and judges,
four thousand gatekeepers, and four thousand will praise the Lord with the instruments I have made for praising him."
David divided them into groups according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.
Sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, then Zetham and Joel: three.
Sons of Shimei: Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran: three. These were the heads of the families descended from Ladan.
Sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zizah, Jeush, and Beriah. These were the four sons of Shimei.
Jahath was the chief and Zizah the second; but Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons and were counted as a single family.
Sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel: four.

Sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart to be consecrated as most holy, he and his sons forever, to burn incense before the Lord, to serve him, and to pronounce blessings in his name forever.
As for Moses, the man of God, his sons were counted among the tribe of Levi.
Sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.
Sons of Gershom: Shubael the chief.
Sons of Eliezer: Rehabiah the chief; Eliezer had no other sons, but the sons of Rehabiah were very many.
Sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.
Sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth.
Sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, Isshiah the second.
Sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. Sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.
Eleazar died without sons, having only daughters; their cousins, the sons of Kish, married them.
Sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth: three.

These were the sons of Levi according to their families, heads of families according to their enrollment, counted by name, head by head, charged with the service of the house of the Lord from twenty years old and upward.
For David had said, "The Lord, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people, and he will dwell in Jerusalem forever;
so the Levites no longer have to carry the Dwelling and all the vessels for its service."
It was according to David's last instructions that the sons of Levi were counted from twenty years old and upward.
Their duty was to assist the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the Lord: the courts, the chambers, the purification of all the holy things, and the work of the service of the house of God;

they were responsible for the bread of the offering, the fine flour for the grain offerings, the unleavened wafers, whatever is baked on the griddle and whatever is kneaded, as well as all measures of quantity and length.
They were to stand every morning and every evening to give thanks and praise to the Lord,
and to offer all the burnt offerings to the Lord on the sabbaths, the new moons, and the appointed feasts, according to the number prescribed by the rule, continually, before the Lord.
Thus they carried out the service of the tent of meeting, the service of the sanctuary, and the service alongside their brothers the sons of Aaron, for the service of the house of the Lord.
These are the divisions of the sons of Aaron. Sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died before their father, leaving no sons; so Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
David, together with Zadok of the descendants of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the descendants of Ithamar, divided them into groups according to their service.
Since more chief men were found among the sons of Eleazar than among the sons of Ithamar, they were divided into sixteen heads of families for the sons of Eleazar and eight for the sons of Ithamar.
They were divided by lot, one group like another, for there were officials of the sanctuary and officials of God among the sons of Eleazar as well as among the sons of Ithamar.

The scribe Shemaiah, son of Nethanel, a Levite, recorded them in the presence of the king, the officials, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of the priestly and Levitical families: one family was drawn for Eleazar, then one for Ithamar.
The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah,
the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim,
the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin,
the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,
the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah,
the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim,
the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer,
the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez,
the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel,
the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul,
the twenty-third to Delaiah, the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.
These were their divisions for the service, when they entered the house of the Lord according to the rule received from their father Aaron, as the Lord, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
Here are the heads of the rest of the Levites. Of the sons of Amram: Shubael; of the sons of Shubael: Jehdeiah.
Of Rehabiah, of the sons of Rehabiah: Isshiah the chief.
Of the Izharites: Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth: Jahath.
Sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, Jekameam the fourth.
Sons of Uzziel: Micah; of the sons of Micah: Shamir;
the brother of Micah: Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah: Zechariah.
Sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi; sons of Jaaziah, his son.
Sons of Merari, through Jaaziah his son: Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
Of Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons;
of Kish, the sons of Kish: Jerahmeel.
Sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were the sons of the Levites according to their families.

They too cast lots, like their brothers the sons of Aaron, in the presence of King David, of Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the priestly and Levitical families: the head of a family the same as the youngest of his brothers.

David and the commanders of the army set apart for the service certain sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun, who prophesied to the sound of the harp, the lyre, and the cymbals. This is the list of those who performed this service:
Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah, under the direction of Asaph, who prophesied according to the orders of the king.

Of Jeduthun, his sons: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied to the sound of the harp to give thanks and praise to the Lord.
Of Heman, his sons: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shubael, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth.
All these were sons of Heman, the king's seer according to the words of God, to exalt his power: God had given Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

All these were under the direction of their father for the singing in the house of the Lord, with cymbals, lyres, and harps, for the service of the house of God, under the orders of the king, of Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman.
Their number, together with their brothers trained in singing to the Lord, all who were skilled, was two hundred and eighty-eight.
They cast lots for their duties, small and great alike, teacher and pupil.
The first lot fell, for Asaph, to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, with his brothers and sons: twelve;
the third to Zaccur, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the fourth to Izri, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the seventh to Jesharelah, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the tenth to Shimei, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the eleventh to Azarel, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the thirteenth to Shubael, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the fourteenth to Mattithiah, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the eighteenth to Hanani, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the twenty-first to Hothir, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and his brothers: twelve;
the twenty-fourth to Romamti-ezer, his sons and his brothers: twelve.
These are the divisions of the gatekeepers. Of the Korahites: Meshelemiah, son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph.
Sons of Meshelemiah: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth,
Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Eliehoenai the seventh.
Sons of Obed-edom: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peullethai the eighth; for God had blessed Obed-edom.
To his son Shemaiah were born sons who governed their father's house, for they were valiant men.
Sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad and his brothers, valiant men, Elihu and Semachiah.
All these were sons of Obed-edom; they, their sons, and their brothers, capable and able men for the service, numbered sixty-two, descended from Obed-edom.
Meshelemiah had sons and brothers, valiant men: eighteen.
Hosah, of the sons of Merari, had as sons: Shimri the chief, whom his father had appointed chief although he was not the firstborn,
Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth. The sons and brothers of Hosah were thirteen in all.
These divisions of the gatekeepers, led by these chief men, had their duties, like their brothers, in the service of the house of the Lord.
They cast lots, small and great alike, according to their families, for each gate.
The lot for the east side fell to Shelemiah. Lots were also cast for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and the north side fell to him.
To Obed-edom fell the south side, and to his sons the storehouse.
To Shuppim and Hosah fell the west side, with the Shalleketh Gate, on the road that goes up: one guard post facing another.
On the east there were six Levites a day; on the north four a day; on the south four a day; and at the storehouse two by two;
at the western court, four for the road and two for the court.
These are the divisions of the gatekeepers, descended from the sons of Korah and the sons of Merari.
The Levites, their brothers, were in charge of the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated offerings.
Of the sons of Ladan, the Gershonites descended from Ladan, heads of the families of Ladan the Gershonite: Jehiel.
The sons of Jehiel, Zetham and Joel his brother, were in charge of the treasuries of the house of the Lord.
Among the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites:
Shubael, son of Gershom, son of Moses, was chief officer over the treasuries.
His brothers, through Eliezer: Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son, Shelomith his son.

This Shelomith and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated offerings that King David, the heads of families, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the commanders of the army had dedicated:
they had dedicated them from the spoils of war for the upkeep of the house of the Lord.
Everything that Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner, and Joab son of Zeruiah had dedicated, every dedicated object, was under the care of Shelomith and his brothers.
Among the Izharites, Kenaniah and his sons were in charge of the external affairs of Israel, as scribes and judges.
Among the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, one thousand seven hundred valiant men, had oversight of Israel west of the Jordan, for all the work of the Lord and the service of the king.

Among the Hebronites, Jeriah was the chief. In the fortieth year of David's reign, a search was made concerning the Hebronites according to their genealogies and families, and valiant men were found among them at Jazer in Gilead.

His brothers, valiant men, numbered two thousand seven hundred heads of families. King David set them over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, for every matter of God and matter of the king.

These are the sons of Israel according to their number: heads of families, commanders of thousands and hundreds, and officers in the king's service for everything concerning the divisions that came and went month by month, all the months of the year; each division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
Over the first division, for the first month, was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel; his division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
He was of the sons of Perez and commanded all the troop commanders for the first month.
Over the division of the second month was Dodai the Ahohite, with Mikloth as officer; his division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
The commander of the third division, for the third month, was Benaiah, son of Jehoiada the priest; his division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
This Benaiah was a mighty man among the Thirty and their leader; his son Ammizabad commanded his division.
The fourth, for the fourth month, was Asahel, brother of Joab, and after him his son Zebadiah; his division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
The fifth, for the fifth month, was the commander Shamhuth the Izrahite; his division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
The sixth, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh, of Tekoa; his division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
The seventh, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, of the sons of Ephraim; his division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
The eighth, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites; his division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
The ninth, for the ninth month, was Abiezer of Anathoth, of the sons of Benjamin; his division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
The tenth, for the tenth month, was Maharai of Netophah, of the Zerahites; his division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
The eleventh, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah of Pirathon, of the sons of Ephraim; his division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
The twelfth, for the twelfth month, was Heldai of Netophah, of the family of Othniel; his division numbered twenty-four thousand men.
Over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites, Eliezer son of Zichri; of the Simeonites, Shephatiah son of Maacah;
of the Levites, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;
of Judah, Elihu, one of David's brothers; of Issachar, Omri son of Michael;
of Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; of Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel;
of the sons of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Azaziah; of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;
of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; of Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner;
of Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the chiefs of the tribes of Israel.
David did not count those twenty years old and under, for the Lord had promised to make Israel as numerous as the stars of the sky.
Joab son of Zeruiah had begun the census but did not finish it, for divine wrath came upon Israel because of it, and the total was not entered in the records of King David.
Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the king's treasuries; Jonathan son of Uzziah, of the stores in the fields, towns, villages, and towers;
Ezri son of Chelub, of the farm laborers who tilled the ground;
Shimei of Ramah, of the vineyards; Zabdi of Shepham, of the stores of wine in the vineyards;
Baal-hanan of Geder, of the olive and sycamore trees in the lowland; Joash, of the stores of oil;
Shitrai of Sharon, of the cattle grazing in Sharon; Shaphat son of Adlai, of the cattle in the valleys;
Obil the Ishmaelite, of the camels; Jehdeiah of Meronoth, of the donkeys;
Jaziz the Hagrite, of the flocks. All these were the overseers of the property of King David.
Jonathan, David's uncle, an intelligent and learned man, was a counselor; Jehiel son of Hachmoni attended the king's sons.
Ahithophel was the king's counselor, and Hushai the Archite was the king's friend;
after Ahithophel came Jehoiada son of Benaiah, and Abiathar. Joab was the commander of the king's army.

titres.titre: David Presents Solomon and the Plan of the Temple

versets.t: David gathered at Jerusalem all the leaders of Israel: the chiefs of the tribes, the commanders of the divisions in the king's service, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the overseers of all the property and livestock of the king and his sons, along with the officials, the mighty men, and all the men of valor.

King David rose to his feet and said, "Listen to me, my brothers and my people. I had it in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of the covenant of the Lord, the footstool of our God, and I had made preparations to build it.
But God said to me: You shall not build a house for my name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.

The Lord, the God of Israel, chose me out of all my father's house to be king over Israel forever: for he chose Judah as leader, then within Judah the house of my father, and among the sons of my father he was pleased to make me king over all Israel.
And out of all my sons, for the Lord has given me many, he has chosen my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the Lord over Israel.
He said to me: It is your son Solomon who will build my house and my courts, for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be a father to him.
I will establish his kingdom forever, if he remains steadfast, as he is today, in carrying out my commandments and ordinances.

Now therefore, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the Lord, and in the hearing of our God: keep and seek out all the commandments of the Lord your God, so that you may possess this good land and pass it on as an inheritance to your sons after you forever.

And you, my son Solomon, know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and a willing soul, for the Lord searches every heart and understands every intention of the thoughts. If you seek him, he will let himself be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will reject you forever.
See then: the Lord has chosen you to build a house that will be his sanctuary. Be strong, and set to work!"
David gave his son Solomon the plan of the vestibule and the buildings of the temple, of the treasury rooms, the upper chambers, and the inner rooms, as well as the room of the mercy seat;
the plan of all that he had in mind for the courts of the house of the Lord, for all the surrounding chambers, for the treasuries of the house of God and the treasuries of the dedicated offerings;
for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, for all the service of the house of the Lord, and for all the vessels for that service.
He specified the weight of gold for the gold vessels of each service, and the weight of silver for the silver vessels of each service;
the weight of the gold lampstands and their gold lamps, according to the use of each lampstand, and the weight of the silver lampstands, according to the use of each;
the weight of gold for the tables of the bread of the offering, table by table, and the silver for the silver tables;
the pure gold for the forks, the sprinkling bowls, and the pitchers; the weight of each gold bowl, of each silver bowl;
the refined gold, by weight, for the altar of incense; and the plan of the chariot, the golden cherubim spreading their wings to cover the ark of the covenant of the Lord.
"All this," said David, "all the work of this plan, the Lord made clear to me in a writing from his own hand."

David said to his son Solomon, "Be strong and courageous, and set to work! Have no fear or dread, for the Lord God, my God, is with you; he will not fail you or forsake you, until all the work for the service of the house of the Lord is finished.

Here are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for all the service of the house of God; you have with you, for all the work, every willing man skilled in every craft; and the leaders, with all the people, are at your command."

titres.titre: Solomon Proclaimed King; the Death of David

versets.t: King David said to the whole assembly, "My son Solomon, the only one whom God has chosen, is young and inexperienced, and the work is immense, for this palace is not for a man, but for the Lord God.

With all my strength I have provided for the house of my God gold for what is to be of gold, silver for what is to be of silver, bronze for what is to be of bronze, iron for what is to be of iron, wood for what is to be of wood, onyx stones and stones for setting, sparkling stones of every color, all kinds of precious stones, and marble in abundance.
Moreover, in my love for the house of my God, the gold and silver that I possess as my own I give for the house of my God, in addition to all that I have provided for the sanctuary:
about one hundred and two tonnes of gold, gold of Ophir, and two hundred and thirty-eight tonnes of refined silver, to overlay the walls of the rooms,
gold for what is to be of gold, silver for what is to be of silver, and for all the work of the craftsmen. Who then is willing today to freely make an offering to the Lord?"
Then the heads of families, the chiefs of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and hundreds, and the king's overseers made their offerings freely.

They gave, for the service of the house of God, about one hundred and seventy tonnes of gold and ten thousand gold coins, three hundred and forty tonnes of silver, six hundred tonnes of bronze, and three thousand four hundred tonnes of iron.
Those who possessed precious stones handed them over to the treasury of the house of the Lord, into the care of Jehiel the Gershonite.
The people rejoiced at these freewill offerings, made with a whole heart to the Lord; and King David also felt great joy.
Before the whole assembly, David blessed the Lord; he said, "Blessed are you, Lord, God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting!
Yours, O Lord, is the greatness, the power, the splendor, the glory, and the majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth is yours; yours, O Lord, is the kingship and sovereignty over every being.
From you come riches and honor; you rule over all; in your hand are strength and power, and it is yours to make everything great and strong.
Now therefore, our God, we give you thanks and praise your glorious name.
For who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to offer so freely like this? Everything comes from you, and we give you only what we have received from your hand.
Before you we are strangers and passing guests, like all our fathers; our days on the earth are like a shadow, without hope.
Lord our God, all this abundance that we have prepared to build you a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and it is all yours.

I know, my God, that you search hearts and love uprightness; it is in the uprightness of my heart that I have offered all this, and now with joy I see your people, here present, offering their gifts to you freely.
Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep forever such purposes in the heart of your people, and turn their hearts toward you.
To my son Solomon, give a whole heart to keep your commandments, your precepts, and your laws, to accomplish everything and build the palace for which I have made preparations."

Then David said to the whole assembly, "Bless the Lord your God!" And the whole assembly blessed the Lord, the God of their fathers; they bowed low and prostrated themselves before the Lord and before the king.

The next day they offered sacrifices to the Lord and presented burnt offerings to him: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
That day they ate and drank before the Lord with great joy. For a second time they proclaimed Solomon son of David king, anointing him for the Lord as ruler, and Zadok as priest.
Solomon sat on the throne of the Lord as king in place of David his father; he prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.
All the leaders, the mighty men, and even all the sons of King David submitted to King Solomon.
The Lord raised Solomon to the highest degree in the sight of all Israel, and gave his reign a glory that no king before him in Israel had possessed.
David son of Jesse had reigned over all Israel.
The time of his reign over Israel was forty years: he reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
He died at a good old age, full of years, riches, and honor; and his son Solomon reigned in his place.
The acts of King David, from first to last, are written in the records of Samuel the seer, of Nathan the prophet, and of Gad the seer,
together with all his reign, his power, and the events that befell him, Israel, and all the kingdoms of the other lands.

titres.titre: Solomon at Gibeon: the gift of wisdom

versets.t: Solomon, son of David, grew strong on his throne, for the Lord his God was with him and made him surpassingly great.
Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to all the leaders of all Israel, the heads of families;
then, with the whole assembly, he went up to the high place at Gibeon, for that was where the tent of meeting of God stood, the one that Moses, the servant of the Lord, had made in the wilderness.
The ark of God, however, David had brought up from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.
The bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made was also there, before the Dwelling of the Lord; and Solomon and the assembly sought the Lord there.
There, on the bronze altar that stood before the Lord beside the tent of meeting, Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings.
That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what you would have me give you."
Solomon answered God, "You showed great and faithful love to David my father, and you have made me king in his place.
Now, Lord God, let your word to David my father come true, for you have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
Give me, then, wisdom and discernment, that I may know how to lead this people. For who, without that, could govern this people of yours, so great?"

God said to Solomon, "Since this is your desire, since you have not asked for riches, wealth, or glory, nor for the death of your enemies, nor even for long life, but have asked for yourself wisdom and discernment to govern my people, over whom I have made you king,
wisdom and discernment are given to you. And I will also give you riches, wealth, and glory such as no king before you has had and none after you shall have."
So Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, back to Jerusalem, and he reigned over Israel.
Solomon gathered chariots and horses: he had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the garrison cities and near the king in Jerusalem.
The king made silver and gold as common as stones in Jerusalem, and cedars as plentiful as the sycamores of the lowland.
Solomon's horses came from Egypt; the king's merchants procured them in droves at a fixed price.

They imported from Egypt a chariot for six hundred pieces of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty; and in the same way the merchants supplied them to all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.
Solomon resolved to build a house for the name of the Lord, and a royal palace for himself.

titres.titre: The preparations; the agreement with Hiram of Tyre

versets.t: Solomon counted out seventy thousand carriers, eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred overseers to direct them.
Then Solomon sent word to Hiram, king of Tyre, "Do for me as you did for David my father, to whom you sent cedars so that he could build himself a house to live in.

See, I am building a house for the name of the Lord my God, to consecrate it to him, to burn fragrant incense before him, to set out continually the bread of the offering, and to present the burnt offerings of morning and evening, of the sabbaths, the new moons, and the appointed feasts of the Lord our God: this is a lasting rule for Israel.
The house I am building will be great, for our God is greater than all gods.
Yet who has the strength to build him a house, when the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain him? And who am I to build him a house, except to burn incense before him?

So send me a man skilled in working gold, silver, bronze, and iron, with red purple, crimson, and violet purple, and versed in the art of engraving; he will work with my craftsmen in Judah and Jerusalem, those whom David my father prepared.
Send me also from Lebanon cedar, cypress, and sandalwood, for I know that your servants know how to fell the trees of Lebanon; and my servants will go with yours
to prepare timber for me in abundance, for the house I am building will be great and magnificent.

To the woodcutters who fell the trees, your servants, I will provide for their food about four million four hundred thousand litres of wheat and as much barley, four hundred and forty thousand litres of wine and as much oil."
Hiram, king of Tyre, answered in a letter that he sent to Solomon, "It is because he loves his people that the Lord has made you king over them."

And Hiram added, "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, for giving King David a wise son, endowed with sense and understanding, to build a house for the Lord and a royal palace for himself!
So I am sending you a skilled and discerning man, Huram-abi,

the son of a woman among the daughters of Dan and of a Tyrian father. He knows how to work gold and silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, violet purple, crimson, fine linen, and red purple; he excels at every kind of engraving and can carry out any design entrusted to him. He will work with your craftsmen and those of my lord David, your father.
So let my lord send his servants the wheat, barley, oil, and wine that he has spoken of;
and we will cut as much timber from Lebanon as you need, ship it to you in rafts by sea as far as Joppa, and you will haul it up to Jerusalem."

Solomon took a census of all the resident aliens who were in the land of Israel, following the count that David his father had made: they were found to be one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.
Of these he assigned seventy thousand to carry burdens, eighty thousand to cut stone in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred as overseers to keep the people at work.

Solomon began to build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, on Mount Moriah, where the Lord had appeared to David his father, at the place David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
He began the building on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
These are the measurements Solomon laid down for building the house of God: the length, by the old standard, was thirty metres, and the width ten metres.
The portico across the front was as wide as the house, ten metres, and sixty metres high. Solomon overlaid its interior with pure gold.
He paneled the great hall with cypress wood, overlaid it with fine gold, and had palm trees and chainwork carved on it.
He inlaid the house with precious stones for beauty; the gold was gold of Parvaim.
He overlaid the house with gold, the beams, the thresholds, the walls, and the doors, and had cherubim carved on the walls.
He made the room of the Holy of Holies: its length, matching the width of the house, was ten metres, and its width ten metres. He overlaid it with fine gold, to the value of about twenty tonnes.
The weight of the gold for the nails came to about five hundred and seventy grams. He also overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
In the room of the Holy of Holies he made two cherubim of sculptured work, and they overlaid them with gold.

The wings of the cherubim together spanned ten metres: one wing of the first, two and a half metres long, touched the wall of the house, and the other, two and a half metres, touched the wing of the second cherub;
likewise one wing of the second cherub, two and a half metres, touched the wall of the house, and the other, two and a half metres, met the wing of the first.
These cherubim spread their wings over ten metres; they stood upright, their faces turned toward the great hall.
Solomon made the veil of violet purple, red purple, crimson, and fine linen, and embroidered cherubim on it.
In front of the house he set up two columns seventeen and a half metres high, each topped by a capital two and a half metres high.
He made chainwork, as in the sanctuary, and set it on top of the columns; he made a hundred pomegranates and fastened them to the chainwork.
He raised the columns in front of the temple, one on the right, the other on the left; he named the one on the right Jachin, and the one on the left Boaz.
He made a bronze altar ten metres long, ten metres wide, and five metres high.
He made the Sea of cast bronze: five metres from rim to rim, perfectly round, two and a half metres high; a cord of fifteen metres measured its circumference.
Below the rim, figures of oxen encircled it, ten to the half metre, going all the way around the Sea in two rows; these oxen had been cast in one piece with it.
It rested on twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, three facing east; the Sea rested on them, and all their hindquarters were turned inward.
Its thickness was about eight centimetres; its rim, shaped like the rim of a cup, flared out like a lily blossom. It held about sixty-six thousand litres.
He made ten basins: five on the right, five on the left, for washing; in them they rinsed what was being prepared for the burnt offering. The Sea, however, was for the priests to wash in.
He made the ten golden lampstands according to the prescribed rule and placed them in the great hall, five on the right and five on the left.
He made ten tables and placed them in the great hall, five on the right and five on the left; and he made a hundred golden sprinkling bowls.
He made the court of the priests and the great courtyard, with its gates, and he overlaid their doors with bronze.
He placed the Sea on the right side, toward the southeast.
Huram made the ash pots, the shovels, and the sprinkling bowls. So Huram finished the work he was doing for King Solomon in the house of God:
the two columns; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the columns; the two networks to cover the two bowl-shaped capitals;
the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowl-shaped capitals on the columns;
he made the stands and the basins on the stands;
the single Sea and the twelve oxen beneath it;
the ash pots, the shovels, and the forks. All these objects that Huram-abi made for King Solomon, for the house of the Lord, were of polished bronze.
The king had them cast in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground, between Succoth and Zeredah.
Solomon made all these objects in such great quantity that the weight of the bronze was never checked.
Solomon also made all the objects for the house of God: the golden altar; the tables for the bread of the offering;
the lampstands with their lamps of fine gold, to burn before the sanctuary according to the rule;
the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs of gold, the purest gold;

the knives, the sprinkling bowls, the ladles, and the censers of fine gold; and, at the entrance of the house, the golden doors of the inner room, that of the Holy of Holies, and those of the doorway of the great hall.

titres.titre: The ark brought into the temple

versets.t: So all the work that Solomon did for the house of the Lord was completed. Solomon brought in what David his father had consecrated, the silver, the gold, and all the vessels, and he placed them in the treasuries of the house of God.

Then Solomon assembled at Jerusalem the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the families of the sons of Israel, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the City of David, that is, from Zion.
All the men of Israel gathered before the king for the feast, the one in the seventh month.
When all the elders of Israel had arrived, the Levites lifted up the ark
and brought it up, along with the tent of meeting and all the sacred objects that were in it: the levitical priests carried them.
King Solomon and the whole assembly of Israel gathered around him stood before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen in such numbers that they could not be counted or reckoned.
The priests brought the ark of the covenant of the Lord to its place, into the sanctuary of the house, the Holy of Holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim;
for the cherubim spread their wings over the place of the ark, covering the ark and its poles from above.
These poles were so long that their ends could be seen from the holy place, in front of the sanctuary, but not from outside; and there they have remained to this day.
There was nothing in the ark but the two tablets that Moses had placed there at Horeb, when the Lord made a covenant with the sons of Israel as they came out of Egypt.
Now as the priests came out of the holy place (for all the priests present had sanctified themselves, without regard to their divisions of service,

and all the levitical singers, Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, with their sons and their kinsmen, clothed in fine linen, cymbals, lyres, and harps in hand, stood on the east side of the altar, surrounded by a hundred and twenty priests sounding trumpets),

at the moment when the trumpeters and singers, in unison, made one single voice heard in celebration and praise of the Lord, when the trumpets, the cymbals, and the instruments were raised in praise of the Lord, "for he is good, for his faithful love is everlasting!", then the house, the house of the Lord, was filled with a cloud.
The priests could no longer stand there to minister, because of the cloud: the glory of the Lord filled the house of God.
Then Solomon declared, "The Lord has said that he would dwell in the dark cloud.
And I have built you an exalted house, a place for you to dwell in forever."
Then the king turned around and blessed the whole assembly of Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood.
He said, "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who has fulfilled with his hand what he promised with his mouth to David my father, when he said:

Since the day I brought my people out of the land of Egypt, I have chosen no city, in any tribe of Israel, for a house to be built there where my name would reside, nor have I chosen any man to be the leader of my people Israel;
but I have chosen Jerusalem for my name to reside there, and I have chosen David to govern my people Israel.
David my father had it in his heart to build a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
But the Lord said to David my father: You had it in your heart to build a house for my name, and you did well;
yet you are not the one who will build the house, but your son, sprung from you: he is the one who will build the house for my name.
The Lord has kept the word he spoke: I have succeeded David my father, I sit on the throne of Israel, as the Lord promised, and I have built the house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
There I have placed the ark, in which is the covenant that the Lord made with the sons of Israel."
Then Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord, facing the whole assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands.

For Solomon had made a bronze platform, two and a half metres long, two and a half metres wide, and a metre and a half high, and had set it up in the middle of the court. He mounted it, knelt down in front of the whole assembly of Israel, stretched out his hands toward heaven,
and said, "Lord, God of Israel, there is no God like you, in heaven or on earth: you keep the covenant and the faithful love toward your servants who walk before you with all their heart.
You have kept toward your servant David my father the promise you made him: what you spoke with your mouth you have accomplished with your hand, as is seen today.

And now, Lord, God of Israel, keep toward your servant David my father this further promise: You will never fail to have before me a descendant seated on the throne of Israel, provided your sons watch their conduct and walk in my law, as you yourself have walked before me.
And now, Lord, God of Israel, let the word you spoke to your servant David come true!
But will God really dwell with man on earth? Behold, the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain you: how much less this house that I have built!
Yet be attentive to the prayer and the plea of your servant, Lord my God: listen to the cry and the prayer that your servant makes to you.
May your eyes remain open day and night upon this house, upon the place of which you said you would put your name there: listen to the prayer that your servant makes toward this place.
Listen to the pleas of your servant and of your people Israel, when they pray toward this place; listen from the place where you dwell, from heaven: listen and forgive.
If a man sins against his neighbor and is required to take an oath, and he comes to swear before your altar in this house,

then you, from heaven, listen and act: do justice for your servants, repay the guilty by bringing his conduct down on his own head, and declare the innocent righteous by treating him according to his uprightness.
When your people Israel are defeated by an enemy because they have sinned against you, if they return to you, praise your name, pray, and plead with you in this house,
then you, from heaven, listen, forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave to them and to their fathers.
When the heavens are shut and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, if they pray toward this place, praise your name, and turn from their sin because you have humbled them,

then you, from heaven, listen, forgive the sin of your servants and of your people Israel, teach them the good way in which to walk, and send rain on the land you have given your people as their inheritance.
When famine strikes the land, or plague, blight and mildew, locusts and grasshoppers, when an enemy besieges the people in their cities, whatever the scourge or disease,
every prayer, every plea from any single person or from all your people Israel, each one knowing his own affliction and pain and stretching out his hands toward this house,
then you, from heaven, from the place where you dwell, listen and forgive: render to each according to all his conduct, you who know his heart, for you alone know the hearts of the children of men,
so that they may fear you and walk in your ways all the days they live on the land you gave to our fathers.

Even the foreigner, the one who is not of your people Israel but comes from a distant land because of your great name, your mighty hand, and your outstretched arm, if he comes to pray toward this house,

then you, from heaven, from the place where you dwell, listen, and act according to all that this foreigner asks of you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name, may fear you as your people Israel do, and may know that your name is invoked over this house that I have built.
When your people go out to war against their enemies, by the way you send them, if they pray to you, turned toward this city that you have chosen and toward the house that I have built for your name,
listen from heaven to their prayer and their plea, and do justice for them.
When they sin against you, for there is no one who does not sin, and in your anger you hand them over to an enemy who carries them off captive to a land far or near,
if they come to their senses in the land of their captivity, if they repent and plead with you in the land of their exile, saying: We have sinned, we have done wrong, we have been guilty;

if they return to you with all their heart and all their soul in the land of the captivity where they were carried off, and if they pray, turned toward the land you gave their fathers, toward the city you have chosen, and toward the house I have built for your name,
listen from heaven, from the place where you dwell, to their prayer and their plea, do justice for them, and forgive your people their sins against you.
Now, O my God, may your eyes be open and your ears attentive to the prayer made in this place!
And now, arise, Lord God, come to your resting place, you and the ark of your strength! May your priests, Lord God, be clothed with salvation, and may your faithful ones rejoice in your goodness!
Lord God, do not turn away the face of your anointed; remember the faithful love promised to David, your servant."

titres.titre: The glory of the Lord fills the temple
The Lord appears to Solomon again

versets.t: When Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the Lord filled the house.
The priests could not enter the house of the Lord, for the glory of the Lord filled the house of the Lord.

Seeing the fire come down and the glory of the Lord upon the house, all the sons of Israel bowed low, faces to the ground on the pavement, prostrated themselves, and praised the Lord, "For he is good, for his faithful love is everlasting!"
The king and all the people offered sacrifices before the Lord.
King Solomon offered in sacrifice twenty-two thousand oxen and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

The priests stood at their posts; the Levites too, with the musical instruments of the Lord that King David had made for praising the Lord, "for his faithful love is everlasting," when David offered praise through them. Facing them, the priests sounded trumpets, and all Israel stood.

Solomon consecrated the middle of the court that is in front of the house of the Lord: there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar he had made could not hold the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the fat.
At that time Solomon kept the feast for seven days, and all Israel with him, an immense assembly, come from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of Egypt.
