On the eighth day they held the closing assembly, for they had celebrated the dedication of the altar for seven days, and the feast for seven days.

On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent the people back to their tents, joyful and glad of heart for the good that the Lord had done for David, for Solomon, and for Israel his people.
Solomon finished the house of the Lord and the king's palace; he brought to completion all that he had planned for the house of the Lord and for his own.
The Lord appeared to him by night and said to him, "I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place for myself as a house of sacrifice.
When I shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, when I command the locusts to devour the land, or when I send plague among my people,

if my people, over whom my name is invoked, humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from their evil ways, then, from heaven, I will listen, I will forgive their sin, and I will heal their land.
From now on my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayer made in this place.
For I have chosen and sanctified this house so that my name may dwell there forever; my eyes and my heart will always be there.
And as for you, if you walk before me as David your father walked, doing all that I have commanded you, keeping my laws and my rules,
I will make firm the throne of your kingship, according to the covenant I made with David your father, when I said: You will never fail to have a descendant to rule Israel.
But if you turn away, if you abandon my laws and my commandments that I have given you, if you go and serve other gods and bow down before them,

then I will uproot you from my soil, the land I gave you; and this house that I have consecrated to my name, I will cast it out of my presence and make it a byword and an object of scorn among all peoples.
This house, once so exalted, everyone who passes by it will be appalled and say: Why has the Lord treated this land and this house like this?

And the answer will be: Because they abandoned the Lord, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of Egypt, and clung to other gods, bowed down before them, and served them; that is why he brought all this disaster upon them."

titres.titre: Worship and the expeditions to Ophir

versets.t: At the end of the twenty years during which Solomon built the house of the Lord and his own,
he rebuilt the cities that Hiram had given him and settled sons of Israel in them.
Solomon marched on Hamath-zobah and seized it.
He built Tadmor in the wilderness and all the store cities he constructed in the land of Hamath.
He built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, fortified cities, with walls, gates, and bars;

he built Baalath and all the store cities that belonged to him, all the cities for the chariots, the cities for the horses, and everything he wished to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout the land of his dominion.
All that remained of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, peoples not belonging to Israel,
that is, their descendants left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel had not exterminated, Solomon conscripted as forced laborers, as they remain to this day.
But Solomon made none of the sons of Israel a slave for his work: they were his men of war, the commanders of his officers, the commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.
The chief overseers of King Solomon numbered two hundred and fifty, charged with directing the people.

Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh from the City of David to the house he had built for her, for he said, "My wife shall not live in the house of David, king of Israel, for the places where the ark of the Lord has entered are holy."
Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the Lord on the altar of the Lord that he had built in front of the portico,
offering each day what Moses had prescribed, on the sabbaths, the new moons, and the three annual feasts: the feast of Unleavened Bread, the feast of Weeks, and the feast of Booths.

According to the rule of David his father, he established the divisions of the priests for their service, the Levites in their duties, to praise the Lord and to minister before the priests according to the daily rite, and the gatekeepers by their divisions at each gate: for so David, the man of God, had commanded.
They did not depart in anything from the king's orders concerning the priests and the Levites, nor in any matter, nor regarding the treasuries.
So all of Solomon's work was accomplished, from the day the house of the Lord was founded until it was completed: the house of the Lord was finished.
Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Eloth, on the seashore, in the land of Edom.
Hiram sent him, by his servants, ships and experienced sailors. With Solomon's servants they went to Ophir, took about fifteen tonnes of gold there, and brought it back to King Solomon.

titres.titre: The glory and wealth of Solomon

versets.t: The queen of Sheba, hearing of Solomon's fame, came to Jerusalem to test him with riddles. She had a very large retinue, camels laden with spices, gold in great quantity, and precious stones. When she came to Solomon, she told him all that was on her heart,
and Solomon answered all her questions: nothing was hidden from him that he could not explain to her.
When the queen of Sheba had seen Solomon's wisdom, the house he had built,

the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the service of his officers and their robes, his cupbearers and their robes, and the stairway by which he went up to the house of the Lord, it took her breath away,
and she said to the king, "So it was true, what I heard in my own country about you and your wisdom!
I did not believe the reports until I came and saw with my own eyes; and now I see that not even half of your great wisdom was told me: you surpass everything that fame had led me to expect.
Happy are your people, happy are your servants, who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!

Blessed be the Lord your God, who has delighted in you and set you on his throne as king for the Lord your God! Because your God loves Israel and wills to establish it forever, he has made you king over it, to exercise right and justice."
She gave the king about four tonnes of gold, a very great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again were there such spices as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
The servants of Hiram and those of Solomon, who brought the gold of Ophir, also brought sandalwood and precious stones.
From this sandalwood the king made stairways for the house of the Lord and for the royal palace, as well as harps and lyres for the singers: never before had such wood been seen in the land of Judah.
King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all she desired and asked for, more than she had brought to the king. Then she returned to her own country, she and her servants.
The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in a single year was about twenty-two and a half tonnes,
not counting what the traders and the merchants brought; all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land also brought gold and silver to Solomon.
King Solomon made two hundred large shields of beaten gold, using about seven kilos of gold for each shield,
and three hundred small shields of beaten gold, using about three and a half kilos of gold for each shield; and the king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king made a great throne of ivory, which he overlaid with pure gold.
This throne had six steps and a golden footstool, fastened to the throne; on either side of the seat were armrests, and two lions stood beside the armrests;
twelve lions stood there, on the six steps, six on each side. Nothing like it had ever been made in any kingdom.
All of King Solomon's drinking vessels were of gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of fine gold; silver counted for nothing in Solomon's day.
For the king had ships that went to Tarshish with Hiram's servants; once every three years these ships of Tarshish came back laden with gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in wealth and in wisdom.
All the kings of the earth sought to see Solomon, to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart,
and each one brought his gift: objects of silver and objects of gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses, and mules; and this year after year.
Solomon had four thousand stalls for his horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the garrison cities and near the king in Jerusalem.
He ruled over all the kings from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt.
The king made silver as common as stones in Jerusalem, and cedars as plentiful as the sycamores of the lowland.
Horses were imported for Solomon from Egypt and from all lands.

The rest of the acts of Solomon, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Nathan the prophet, in the prophecy of Ahijah of Shiloh, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?
Solomon reigned forty years in Jerusalem over all Israel.
Then Solomon lay down with his fathers and was buried in the City of David, his father; and his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.

titres.titre: The schism: Israel breaks away from Judah

versets.t: Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it (he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon), he returned from Egypt.
They sent for him, and Jeroboam came with all Israel. They said to Rehoboam:
"Your father made our yoke heavy. Now lighten the harsh servitude your father imposed on us and the heavy yoke he laid upon us, and we will serve you."
He answered them, "Come back to me in three days." So the people went away.
King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon while he was alive, asking, "What do you advise me to answer this people?"
They said to him, "If you are good to this people, if you please them and speak kindly to them, they will be your servants forever."
But Rehoboam set aside the counsel the elders had given him and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and were in his service.
He said to them, "What do you advise me to answer this people, who ask me to lighten the yoke my father laid on them?"

The young men who had grown up with him answered, "To this people who say to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you lighten it for us,' you should reply: My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.
So then, my father laid a heavy yoke on you; I will make it heavier still. My father disciplined you with whips; I will do it with barbed whips."
Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had ordered when he said, "Come back to me on the third day."
The king answered them harshly. Setting aside the counsel of the elders,
he spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men: "My father made your yoke heavy; I will make it heavier still. My father disciplined you with whips; I will do it with barbed whips."
So the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events was brought about by God, to fulfill the word the Lord had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah of Shiloh.

When all Israel saw that the king would not listen to them, they answered him, "What share do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse! To your tents, Israel! Look now to your own house, David!" And all Israel went off to their tents.
So Rehoboam reigned only over the sons of Israel who lived in the towns of Judah.
Then King Rehoboam sent out Hadoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but the sons of Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam barely managed to mount his chariot and flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.

titres.titre: Rehoboam gives up war; his fortresses
The priests and the faithful flock to Judah

versets.t: When Rehoboam reached Jerusalem, he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight Israel and win the kingdom back for Rehoboam.
But the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, the man of God:
"Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin:
Thus says the Lord: Do not go up to make war on your brothers! Let everyone return home, for this is my doing." They heeded the word of the Lord and gave up their march against Jeroboam.
Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and built fortified cities in Judah.
He built Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
Beth-zur, Soco, Adullam,
Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,
Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,
Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, fortified cities in Judah and Benjamin.
He strengthened their defenses, placed commanders in them, and stores of food, oil, and wine.
In each one he put shields and spears, and made them very strong. So Judah and Benjamin were his.
The priests and Levites throughout all Israel, from every part of their territory, took their stand with him;
for the Levites left their pasturelands and their holdings and came to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had barred them from serving as priests of the Lord,
appointing his own priests for the high places, for the goat-demons and the calves he had made.
Following them, those from all the tribes of Israel who set their hearts on seeking the Lord, the God of Israel, came to Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the Lord, the God of their fathers.
They strengthened the kingdom of Judah and supported Rehoboam son of Solomon for three years, for during those three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon.
Rehoboam took as his wife Mahalath, daughter of Jerimoth son of David, and of Abihail daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
She bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham.
After her he took Maacah daughter of Absalom, who bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than all his other wives and concubines; he had eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as chief prince among his brothers, for he intended to make him king.
He acted wisely, dispersing some of his sons throughout all the regions of Judah and Benjamin, in every fortified city; he supplied them with abundant provisions and sought many wives for them.
When Rehoboam's kingship was established and strong, he abandoned the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, because they had been unfaithful to the Lord, Shishak king of Egypt marched up against Jerusalem
with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen; and the army that came with him from Egypt was beyond counting: Libyans, Sukkiim, and Ethiopians.
He captured the fortified cities of Judah and reached Jerusalem.

Then the prophet Shemaiah came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah, who had gathered at Jerusalem before Shishak, and said to them, "Thus says the Lord: You have abandoned me; so I too abandon you into the hand of Shishak."
Then the leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The Lord is just."

When the Lord saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them. Soon I will grant them deliverance, and my wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
But they will become his servants, so that they may learn the difference between serving me and serving the kingdoms of other lands."

So Shishak king of Egypt marched up against Jerusalem. He took the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king's house; he took everything, even the gold shields Solomon had made.
In their place King Rehoboam made bronze shields and entrusted them to the officers of the guard who kept watch at the entrance of the king's house.
Whenever the king went to the house of the Lord, the guards would come and carry them, then return them to the guardroom.
Because Rehoboam humbled himself, the anger of the Lord turned away from him and did not destroy him completely; and there was still some good in Judah.

King Rehoboam established himself firmly in Jerusalem and reigned. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the Lord had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
He did evil, for he did not set his heart to seek the Lord.

The acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, with the genealogies? There was continual warfare between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.
Rehoboam slept with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. His son Abijah reigned in his place.

titres.titre: Abijah, king of Judah, against Jeroboam

versets.t: In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king of Judah;
he reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel, of Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
Abijah went into battle with an army of valiant warriors, four hundred thousand chosen men; and Jeroboam drew up his line against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, valiant warriors.
From the top of Mount Zemaraim, in the hill country of Ephraim, Abijah stood up and said, "Listen to me, Jeroboam and all Israel!
Do you not know that the Lord, the God of Israel, gave the kingship over Israel forever to David and his sons, by a covenant of salt?
Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
Worthless men, scoundrels, gathered around him and forced themselves upon Rehoboam son of Solomon; Rehoboam was young and irresolute, unable to stand against them.

And now you think you can stand against the kingship of the Lord, which is in the hands of the sons of David! You are a great multitude, and you have with you the golden calves Jeroboam made you for gods.

Have you not driven out the priests of the Lord, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made priests for yourselves as the peoples of other lands do? Whoever comes to be consecrated with a young bull and seven rams becomes a priest of what are not gods.
But as for us, the Lord is our God, and we have not abandoned him; our priests who serve the Lord are sons of Aaron, and the Levites are at their tasks.

Every morning and every evening they send up to the Lord burnt offerings and fragrant incense; they set out the bread of the offering on the pure table and light the golden lampstand and its lamps every evening. For we keep the charge of the Lord our God, while you have abandoned him.

See, God is with us, at our head, and his priests, with their blaring trumpets, are ready to sound the alarm against you. Sons of Israel, do not fight the Lord, the God of your fathers, for you will not succeed!"
Now Jeroboam had sent a body of men circling around to lie in ambush behind Judah, so that his troops faced Judah while the ambush was to the rear.
When the men of Judah turned, they found themselves attacked front and rear. They cried out to the Lord, the priests blew the trumpets,
and the men of Judah raised the battle cry. At that cry God struck Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
The sons of Israel fled before Judah, and God delivered them into their hands.
Abijah and his people inflicted a great slaughter on them: five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell, run through.
So the sons of Israel were humbled at that time, and the sons of Judah prevailed because they relied on the Lord, the God of their fathers.
Abijah pursued Jeroboam and took cities from him: Bethel with its dependent villages, Jeshanah with its dependent villages, and Ephron with its dependent villages.
Jeroboam did not regain his strength in the days of Abijah; the Lord struck him, and he died.
But Abijah grew powerful; he took fourteen wives and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
The rest of the acts of Abijah, his conduct and his words, are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.
Abijah slept with his fathers and was buried in the City of David. His son Asa reigned in his place. In his days the land was at rest for ten years.

titres.titre: Asa, king of Judah: the reform
The victory over Zerah the Ethiopian

versets.t: Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the Lord his God. He did away with the foreign altars and the high places,
broke down the sacred pillars, and cut down the sacred poles.
He commanded Judah to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, and to keep the law and the commandment.
He removed the high places and the incense altars from all the towns of Judah; and the kingdom was at peace under his reign.
He built fortified cities in Judah, for the land was at peace; he had no war during those years, because the Lord had given him rest.

He said to Judah, "Let us build these cities and surround them with walls, towers, gates, and bars, while the land is still open to us: we have sought the Lord our God, we have sought him, and he has given us rest on every side." So they built and prospered.

Asa had an army of three hundred thousand men from Judah, bearing shield and spear, and two hundred and eighty thousand from Benjamin, bearing the small shield and drawing the bow: all of them valiant warriors.
Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and advanced as far as Mareshah.
Asa went out to meet him, and they drew up for battle in the Valley of Zephathah, near Mareshah.

Asa cried out to the Lord his God, "Lord, when it comes to helping, you make no distinction between the mighty and the powerless. Help us, Lord our God, for we rely on you, and in your name we march against this multitude. Lord, you are our God: let no mere man prevail against you!"
The Lord struck the Ethiopians before Asa and before Judah, and the Ethiopians fled.

Asa and his people pursued them as far as Gerar. So many Ethiopians fell that they could not recover: they were broken before the Lord and before his army. Asa and his people carried off a very great spoil;
they struck down all the cities around Gerar, for the terror of the Lord was upon them, and they plundered them all, for there was great plunder in them.
They also struck down the camps of the herdsmen and carried off great numbers of sheep and camels; then they returned to Jerusalem.

titres.titre: The prophecy of Azariah; the covenant renewed

versets.t: The Spirit of God came upon Azariah son of Oded;

he went out to meet Asa and said to him, "Listen to me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin. The Lord is with you while you are with him; if you seek him, he will let himself be found by you; but if you abandon him, he will abandon you.
For a long time Israel was without the true God, without a priest to teach, without law;
but in their distress they turned back to the Lord, the God of Israel; they sought him, and he let himself be found.
In those times there was no safety for anyone coming or going, for great turmoil weighed on all the inhabitants of the lands:
nation clashed against nation and city against city, for God troubled them with every kind of distress.
But you, be strong; do not let your hands grow weak, for your work will have its reward."

When Asa heard these words, the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage. He did away with the abominable idols throughout the whole land of Judah and Benjamin and the towns he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim, and he restored the altar of the Lord that stood before the vestibule of the Lord.

He gathered all Judah and Benjamin, together with those from Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon who had come to settle among them; for many from Israel had come over to his side when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.
They gathered at Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
That day, from the spoil they had brought back, they sacrificed to the Lord seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.
They solemnly bound themselves to seek the Lord, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and all their soul:
whoever would not seek the Lord, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, small or great, man or woman.
They swore their oath to the Lord in a loud voice, with shouts of acclamation, to the sound of trumpets and horns.
All Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn it with all their heart and had sought the Lord willingly; and he let himself be found by them, and the Lord gave them rest on every side.

King Asa even removed his mother Maacah from her rank as queen mother, because she had made an abominable image for Ashtoreth. Asa cut down her image, ground it to dust, and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
The high places, however, did not disappear from Israel; yet Asa's heart remained whole all his life.
He brought into the house of God the things dedicated by his father and by himself: silver, gold, and vessels.
There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.

titres.titre: The alliance with Aram; Asa's final days

versets.t: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha king of Israel marched up against Judah and fortified Ramah, to block the movements of Asa king of Judah.
Asa took silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the Lord and of the king's house, and sent them to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who resided in Damascus, with this message:
"There is an alliance between us, as there was between your father and mine. Here I am sending you silver and gold: go, break your alliance with Baasha king of Israel, so that he withdraws from me."
Ben-hadad heeded King Asa: he sent his army commanders against the cities of Israel and struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and all the storehouse cities of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard of it, he stopped fortifying Ramah and abandoned his work.
Then King Asa mobilized all Judah: they carried off the stones and timber with which Baasha had been fortifying Ramah, and with them he fortified Geba and Mizpah.

At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you relied on the king of Aram, and not on the Lord your God, the army of the king of Aram has slipped out of your hand.
Did not the Ethiopians and the Libyans have an immense army, with a vast number of chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on the Lord, he delivered them into your hand.
For the eyes of the Lord range over all the earth to sustain those whose heart is wholly his. In this you have acted foolishly; from now on you will have wars."
Asa was enraged at the seer and threw him in prison, so angry was he at these words. At the same time Asa oppressed some of the people.
The acts of Asa, from first to last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa developed a disease in his feet, which grew very severe; but even in his illness he did not seek the Lord, he sought the physicians.
Asa slept with his fathers; he died in the forty-first year of his reign.

They buried him in the tomb he had cut out for himself in the City of David. They laid him on a bier filled with spices and perfumes prepared by the perfumer's art, and they made a huge fire in his honor.
His son Jehoshaphat reigned in his place and strengthened himself against Israel.
He stationed troops in all the fortified cities of Judah and set garrisons in the land of Judah and in the towns of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
The Lord was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the earlier ways of his father David and did not seek the Baals;
he sought the God of his father and followed his commandments, without imitating the practices of Israel.
The Lord established the kingship firmly in his hand; all Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, and he had riches and honor in abundance.
His heart grew bold in the ways of the Lord, and he further did away with the high places and the sacred poles from Judah.
In the third year of his reign, he sent his officials, Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah, to teach in the towns of Judah;
and with them the Levites Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-adonijah, and with these Levites the priests Elishama and Joram.
They taught in Judah, having with them the book of the law of the Lord; they went through all the towns of Judah and instructed the people.
The terror of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands surrounding Judah, so that they did not make war on Jehoshaphat.
Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute; the Arabs too brought him flocks, seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred goats.
Jehoshaphat grew greater and greater, to the highest degree. He built fortresses and storehouse cities in Judah,
and he had large supplies in the towns of Judah, as well as warriors, valiant men, in Jerusalem.
This is their enrollment by families. For Judah, commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, with three hundred thousand valiant warriors;
at his side Jehohanan the commander, with two hundred and eighty thousand men;
at his side Amasiah son of Zichri, who had willingly consecrated himself to the Lord, with two hundred thousand valiant warriors.
For Benjamin: Eliada, a valiant man, with two hundred thousand men armed with bow and shield;
at his side Jehozabad, with a hundred and eighty thousand men equipped for war.
These were the men who served the king, apart from those he had stationed in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.

titres.titre: Jehoshaphat allied with Ahab; the prophet Micaiah

versets.t: Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance; then he allied himself by marriage with Ahab.
Some years later he went down to Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered for him and for his retinue great numbers of sheep and oxen, and urged him to go up against Ramoth-gilead.
Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead?" He answered, "You and I, your people and mine, are as one: we will go into battle with you."
Then Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Inquire first, I pray you, for the word of the Lord."

The king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and asked them, "Shall we go to attack Ramoth-gilead, or shall I refrain?" They answered, "Go up: God will deliver it into the king's hand."
But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no longer a prophet of the Lord here, through whom we might inquire?"

The king of Israel answered Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we could inquire of the Lord; but I hate him, for he never prophesies anything good for me, only evil: it is Micaiah son of Imlah." Jehoshaphat said, "Let the king not speak so!"
So the king of Israel summoned a eunuch and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah at once."

The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting each on his throne, arrayed in their royal robes, on a threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had made himself horns of iron and said, "Thus says the Lord: With these you will gore the Arameans until they are destroyed."
And all the prophets prophesied the same, saying, "Go up to Ramoth-gilead, and you will triumph! The Lord will deliver it into the king's hand."
The messenger who had gone to fetch Micaiah said to him, "The prophets with one voice are foretelling good for the king; let your word agree with theirs: foretell good."
Micaiah answered, "As the Lord lives, whatever my God says, that is what I will say!"
When he came to the king, the king asked him, "Micaiah, shall we go to attack Ramoth-gilead, or shall I refrain?" He answered, "Go up, you will triumph: they will be delivered into your hands."
The king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear to tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the Lord?"
Micaiah answered, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep without a shepherd; and the Lord said: These have no master; let each return home in peace."
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you? He prophesies nothing good for me, only evil."
Micaiah went on, "Hear then the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord seated on his throne, with all the host of heaven standing at his right hand and his left.
And the Lord asked: Who will entice Ahab king of Israel, so that he will go up to Ramoth-gilead and fall there? One answered one way, another said another.
Then a spirit came forward, stood before the Lord, and said: I will entice him. The Lord asked him: How?
He answered: I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. The Lord said: You will entice him, and you will succeed: go, do so.
And now, see, the Lord has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets of yours; for the Lord has pronounced disaster against you."
Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came up, struck Micaiah on the cheek, and said, "Which way did the Spirit of the Lord pass from me to speak to you?"
Micaiah answered, "You will see on the day you go from room to room to hide."
The king of Israel ordered, "Seize Micaiah and take him back to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son.
Say: Thus says the king: Put this man in prison and feed him bread and water in scant measure until I return in peace."
Micaiah said, "If you really return in peace, then the Lord has not spoken through me." And he added, "Hear, all you peoples!"
The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself to go into battle; you, keep your royal robes on." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into battle.
Now the king of Aram had given this order to his chariot commanders: "Attack no one, small or great, but only the king of Israel."

When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "That is the king of Israel!" and they surrounded him to attack him. But Jehoshaphat cried out, and the Lord helped him, and God drew them away from him.
When the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.
Then a man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the plates of his armor. The king said to his charioteer, "Turn around, take me out of the battle, for I am wounded."
The battle raged that day. The king of Israel was held propped up in his chariot, facing the Arameans, until evening; and he died at sunset.

titres.titre: Jehoshaphat rebuked; the reform of justice

versets.t: Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned safe and sound to his house in Jerusalem.
Jehu son of Hanani, the seer, went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the Lord? For this, the wrath of the Lord is upon you.
Yet some good has been found in you, for you did away with the sacred poles from the land and have set your heart to seek God."
Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem. Once more he went out among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to the Lord, the God of their fathers.
He appointed judges in the land, in each of the fortified cities of Judah.
He said to them, "Take care what you do, for you judge not for men but for the Lord: he is with you when you render a verdict.
Now let the fear of the Lord be upon you; take care to act well, for with the Lord our God there is no injustice, no partiality, and no bribery."
In Jerusalem too Jehoshaphat appointed Levites, priests, and heads of the families of Israel, to render the judgments of the Lord and settle the disputes of the city's inhabitants.
He gave them this charge: "You will act in this way in the fear of the Lord, with fidelity and a whole heart.

In every case that comes to you from your brothers living in their towns, whether concerning bloodshed, or law, or commandment, or statutes, or rules, warn them not to incur guilt before the Lord, so that his wrath does not fall upon you and your brothers: act in this way, and you will not incur guilt.

See: Amariah the chief priest will be over you in all matters of the Lord, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the house of Judah, in all matters of the king; the Levites will be your officers. Take courage, to work, and may the Lord be with the good man!"

titres.titre: The war against Moab and Ammon; the victory

versets.t: After this the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, together with some of the Meunites, came to attack Jehoshaphat.
Word came to him: "A great multitude is marching against you from beyond the Dead Sea, from Edom; they are already at Hazazon-tamar, that is, En-gedi."
Seized with fear, Jehoshaphat resolved to turn to the Lord and proclaimed a fast throughout Judah.
Judah gathered to seek help from the Lord; from every town of Judah they came to seek the Lord.
Jehoshaphat stood in the midst of the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the Lord, before the new courtyard,
and said, "Lord, God of our fathers, are you not God in heaven? Do you not rule over all the kingdoms of the nations? In your hand are strength and power, and no one can withstand you.
Was it not you, our God, who drove out the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and gave it forever to the descendants of Abraham your friend?
They settled in it and built you a sanctuary there for your name, saying:

If disaster comes upon us, sword, judgment, plague, or famine, we will stand before this house and before you, for your name is on this house; we will cry out to you in our distress, and you will hear and save.
And now here are the sons of Ammon, of Moab, and of Mount Seir, the peoples whom you did not allow Israel to invade when they came from Egypt: they turned away from them and did not destroy them;
and see how they repay us: they come to drive us out of your possession, which you gave us as our own.
O our God, will you not judge them? For we are powerless before this great multitude that is marching against us; we do not know what to do, but our eyes are turned to you."
All Judah stood before the Lord, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
Then, in the midst of the assembly, the Spirit of the Lord came upon Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph.

He said, "Give heed, all Judah, inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you, King Jehoshaphat! Thus says the Lord to you: Do not fear or be dismayed before this great multitude, for this battle is not yours but God's.
Tomorrow, go down against them: they are coming up by the ascent of Ziz; you will find them at the end of the valley, facing the wilderness of Jeruel.

You will not have to fight in this matter: take your position, stand still, and see the victory the Lord will give you. Judah and Jerusalem, do not fear or be dismayed; tomorrow, go out to meet them, and the Lord will be with you."
Jehoshaphat bowed with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before the Lord to worship him.
The Levites, of the sons of Kohath and the sons of Korah, rose to praise the Lord, the God of Israel, with a very loud voice.

Early the next morning they rose and set out for the wilderness of Tekoa. As they set out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Listen to me, Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Have faith in the Lord your God, and you will stand firm; have faith in his prophets, and you will succeed."

After conferring with the people, he appointed singers who, arrayed in sacred vestments, marched at the head of the army, praising the Lord: "Give thanks to the Lord, for his faithful love endures forever!"
As they began their song of praise, the Lord set an ambush against the sons of Ammon, of Moab, and of Mount Seir who had come against Judah, and they were routed.
The sons of Ammon and of Moab rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to devote them to destruction; and when they had finished with the men of Seir, they turned to help destroy one another.
When the men of Judah reached the watchtower of the wilderness and looked toward the multitude, there were only corpses lying on the ground; no one had escaped.

Jehoshaphat and his people came to plunder their spoil: they found among them a great quantity of goods, clothing, and precious objects, and carried off so much that they could not take it all. The plundering lasted three days, so great was the spoil.
On the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah: there they blessed the Lord; that is why this place is called the Valley of Beracah, that is, of Blessing, to this day.
Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem, Jehoshaphat at their head, joyfully made their way back to Jerusalem, for the Lord had filled them with joy at the expense of their enemies.
They entered Jerusalem, coming to the house of the Lord with lyres, harps, and trumpets.
The terror of God fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands at the news that the Lord had fought against the enemies of Israel.
And the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was at peace, for his God gave him rest on every side.
Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
He walked in the way of his father Asa, without turning from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the Lord.
Only the high places did not disappear, and the people had not yet firmly set their hearts on the God of their fathers.
The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from first to last, are written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani, which are included in the book of the kings of Israel.
After this Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined with Ahaziah king of Israel, whose conduct was wicked.
He joined with him to build ships to sail to Tarshish; they built them at Ezion-geber.

Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu, of Mareshah, prophesied against Jehoshaphat: "Because you have joined with Ahaziah, the Lord has destroyed your work." And the ships were wrecked, unable to reach Tarshish.

titres.titre: The letter of Elijah; the end of Joram

versets.t: Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried beside them in the City of David. His son Joram reigned in his place.
Joram had brothers, sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariahu, Michael, and Shephatiah; all were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
Their father had given them rich gifts, silver, gold, and precious objects, along with fortified cities in Judah; but he left the kingship to Joram, because he was the firstborn.
When Joram had taken hold of his father's kingdom and secured himself in it, he put all his brothers to the sword, along with some of the leaders of Israel.
Joram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, like the house of Ahab, for he had married a daughter of Ahab; and he did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord.
But the Lord was unwilling to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant he had made with him: he had promised to leave a lamp forever for him and his sons.
In his days Edom rebelled against the rule of Judah and set up a king of their own.
Joram crossed the border with his commanders and all his chariots. Rising up by night, he struck the Edomites who had surrounded him, along with the chariot commanders.
So Edom broke free from the rule of Judah, and remains so to this day. Libnah too broke free from his rule at that time, because Joram had abandoned the Lord, the God of his fathers.
Moreover, he made high places in the mountains of Judah; he led the inhabitants of Jerusalem into prostitution and led Judah astray.

Then a letter came to him from the prophet Elijah: "Thus says the Lord, the God of David your father: Because you have not walked in the ways of your father Jehoshaphat, nor in those of Asa king of Judah,

but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, have led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem into prostitution as the house of Ahab did, and have killed your brothers, your father's house, who were better than you:
see, the Lord is about to strike your people, your children, your wives, and all your possessions with a great plague;
and you yourself will be struck with severe illness, a disease of the bowels, until, day after day, your bowels come out because of the disease."
The Lord stirred up against Joram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians.

They marched up against Judah, broke into it, and plundered all the wealth of the king's house; they also carried off his sons and his wives, so that he was left with no son except Ahaziah, the youngest.
After all this, the Lord struck him in the bowels with an incurable disease.
As the days passed, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of the disease, and he died in terrible agony. His people made no fire in his honor, as they had done for his fathers.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He passed away unmourned; they buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

titres.titre: Athaliah usurps the throne; Joash is saved

versets.t: The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, his youngest son, king in his place, for the raiders who had come with the Arabs into the camp had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah son of Joram, king of Judah, began to reign.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah daughter of Omri.
He too walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor in doing evil.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the Lord, like the house of Ahab; for after his father's death they were his counselors, to his ruin.
It was on their advice that he set out with Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, to fight Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead; and the Arameans wounded Joram.

Joram returned to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds he had received at Ramoth in his battle against Hazael king of Aram. And Ahaziah son of Joram, king of Judah, went down to Jezreel to visit Joram son of Ahab, because he was ailing.
It was God's will, for the ruin of Ahaziah, that he should go to Joram. When he arrived, he went out with Joram to meet Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
Now while Jehu was executing judgment on the house of Ahab, he came upon the leaders of Judah and the nephews of Ahaziah, who were in his service, and he killed them.

He searched for Ahaziah, who was captured at Samaria, where he had hidden; they brought him to Jehu and put him to death. Yet they gave him a burial, for they said, He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart. And there was no one left of the house of Ahaziah able to reign.
When Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, she set about destroying the whole royal line of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, the king's daughter, took Joash son of Ahaziah, spirited him away from among the king's sons who were being slaughtered, and put him with his nurse in the bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, daughter of King Joram and wife of Jehoiada the priest, sister of Ahaziah, hid him from Athaliah, who did not put him to death.
He remained hidden with them six years in the house of God, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

titres.titre: Jehoiada restores Joash; the death of Athaliah

versets.t: In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage and made a pact with the commanders of hundreds: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
They went through Judah, gathered the Levites from all the towns of Judah and the heads of the families of Israel, and came to Jerusalem.
The whole assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. Jehoiada said to them, "Here is the king's son! Let him reign, as the Lord promised concerning the sons of David.
This is what you will do: a third of you, priests and Levites, who come on duty on the sabbath will guard the gates;
another third will be at the king's house, and the last third at the Gate of the Foundation; and all the people will be in the courtyards of the house of the Lord.
Let no one enter the house of the Lord except the priests and the Levites on duty: they may enter, for they are consecrated; but all the people are to keep the charge of the Lord.
The Levites will surround the king on every side, each with his weapons in hand; whoever enters the house is to be put to death. Stay with the king, whether he comes in or goes out."

The Levites and all Judah did everything Jehoiada the priest had ordered. Each took his men, those coming on duty and those going off duty on the sabbath, for Jehoiada the priest had dismissed none of the divisions.
Jehoiada the priest handed over to the commanders of hundreds the spears and the shields, large and small, of King David, which were in the house of God.
He stationed all the people, each with his weapon in hand, from the right side of the house to the left, near the altar and the house, all around the king.
They brought out the king's son, put the diadem and the testimony on him, and proclaimed him king; Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, crying out, "Long live the king!"
When Athaliah heard the clamor of the people running and acclaiming the king, she came to the people in the house of the Lord.

She looked, and there stood the king on his platform at the entrance; near him were the commanders and the trumpets; all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing the trumpets, and the singers with their instruments were leading the acclamations. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, "Treason! Treason!"

Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds, at the head of the troops, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and let anyone who follows her be put to the sword!" For the priest had said, "Do not put her to death in the house of the Lord."
So they made way for her; she reached the entrance of the Horse Gate by the king's house, and there they put her to death.
Jehoiada made a covenant between himself, all the people, and the king, that they would be the people of the Lord.
All the people went into the temple of Baal and tore it down; they broke its altars and its images, and killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, before the altars.

Jehoiada entrusted the care of the house of the Lord to the levitical priests whom David had assigned to the house of the Lord to offer the burnt offerings to the Lord, as it is written in the law of Moses, amid the songs of joy set in order by David.
He stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the Lord, so that no one unclean in any way might enter.

Then he took the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, those in authority over the people, and all the people of the land, and brought the king down from the house of the Lord. They entered the king's house through the Upper Gate and seated the king on the royal throne.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet; as for Athaliah, they had put her to death by the sword.

titres.titre: The apostasy of Joash; the murder of Zechariah

versets.t: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah, of Beersheba.
Joash did what was right in the eyes of the Lord all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
Jehoiada found two wives for him, and he had sons and daughters.
After this, Joash set his heart on restoring the house of the Lord.

He gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go through the towns of Judah and collect, from all Israel, silver year by year to repair the house of your God; do it without delay." But the Levites did not hurry.

The king summoned Jehoiada, the chief of the priests, and said to him, "Why have you not seen to it that the Levites bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the levy fixed by Moses the servant of the Lord and by the assembly of Israel, for the tent of the testimony?
For that wicked woman Athaliah and her sons have ransacked the house of God, and out of all the holy things of the house of the Lord they have made offerings to the Baals."
At the king's command, they made a chest and placed it outside, at the gate of the house of the Lord.
A proclamation was made throughout Judah and Jerusalem that they should bring to the Lord the levy that Moses the servant of God had imposed on Israel in the wilderness.
All the leaders and all the people rejoiced; they brought their dues and threw them into the chest until it was full.

Whenever the time came to bring the chest for royal inspection, by the hands of the Levites, and they saw that there was much silver in it, the king's secretary and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty it, then put it back in its place. They did this every day, and collected silver in abundance.

The king and Jehoiada handed it over to the overseers of the work on the house of the Lord; these hired stonecutters and carpenters to restore the house of the Lord, as well as workers in iron and bronze to reinforce it.
The workmen set to work, and the restoration progressed under their hands; they put the house of God back in order and reinforced it.

When the work was finished, they brought the rest of the silver before the king and Jehoiada; from it were made objects for the house of the Lord, vessels for the service and for the burnt offerings, bowls, and other objects of gold and silver. And burnt offerings were offered continually in the house of the Lord as long as Jehoiada lived.
Jehoiada grew old and full of days, and died at the age of a hundred and thirty.
They buried him in the City of David with the kings, because he had done good in Israel, toward God and his house.
After the death of Jehoiada, the leaders of Judah came and bowed down before the king, and the king listened to them.
They abandoned the house of the Lord, the God of their fathers, and served the sacred poles and the idols. The wrath of the Lord fell upon Judah and Jerusalem because of this guilt.
The Lord sent them prophets to bring them back to him; they warned them, but they would not listen.

Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest; he stood before the people and said, "Thus says God: Why do you transgress the commandments of the Lord? You will gain nothing by it. Since you have abandoned the Lord, he too abandons you."
They conspired against him and, at the king's command, stoned him in the courtyard of the house of the Lord.

King Joash did not remember the faithfulness that Jehoiada, the father of Zechariah, had shown him: he had his son put to death. As he was dying, Zechariah said, "May the Lord see and call to account!"

At the turn of the year, the army of the Arameans marched up against Joash: they entered Judah and Jerusalem, wiped out all the leaders of the people, and sent all their spoil to the king of Damascus.

The army of the Arameans had come with few men, but the Lord delivered into their hands a very large army, because they had abandoned the Lord, the God of their fathers; so the Arameans executed judgment on Joash.

When they withdrew, leaving him covered with wounds, his servants conspired against him because of the blood of the son of Jehoiada the priest; they killed him on his bed, and he died. They buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.
These are the ones who conspired against him: Zabad son of Shimeath, an Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith, a Moabite woman.

As for his sons, the many oracles pronounced against him, and the restoration of the house of God, all this is written in the commentary on the book of the Kings. His son Amaziah reigned in his place.

titres.titre: The idolatry of Amaziah; the war against Israel

versets.t: Amaziah became king at twenty-five years of age, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan, of Jerusalem.
He did what is right in the eyes of the Lord, but not with an undivided heart.
When the kingship was firmly in his hands, he put to death those of his servants who had killed the king, his father.

But he did not put their sons to death, keeping to what is written in the Law, in the book of Moses, where the Lord commanded: Fathers shall not be put to death for their sons, nor sons for their fathers; each shall be put to death for his own sin.

Amaziah gathered the men of Judah and drew them up by families, under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin. He counted those twenty years old and upward, and found three hundred thousand chosen men, fit for war, able to handle spear and shield.
He also hired from Israel a hundred thousand brave warriors, for about three and a half tonnes of silver.
But a man of God came and said to him: "O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the Lord is not with Israel, with all these sons of Ephraim.
Even if you go into battle and prove yourself brave, God will make you stumble before the enemy, for God has the power both to help and to bring down."

Amaziah said to the man of God: "And what shall I do about the three and a half tonnes of silver that I have given to the troop of Israel?" The man of God answered: "The Lord can give you far more than that."
So Amaziah set apart the troop that had come to him from Ephraim, sending them home. These men blazed with anger against Judah and returned home furious.
Amaziah took courage, led out his people, went to the Valley of Salt, and there struck down ten thousand men of Seir.
The sons of Judah also captured ten thousand alive, led them to the top of a rock, and threw them down from the top of the rock: all of them were dashed to pieces.

Meanwhile, the men of the troop that Amaziah had sent back so that they would not go into battle with him fell upon the towns of Judah, from Samaria to Beth-horon; they killed three thousand people there and carried off great plunder.
When Amaziah returned from striking down the Edomites, he brought back the gods of the sons of Seir: he made them his own gods, bowed down before them, and offered them incense.
The anger of the Lord blazed against Amaziah; he sent him a prophet, who said to him: "Why have you sought out the gods of this people, gods who could not deliver their own people from your hand?"

While he was still speaking, the king said to him: "Have we made you a counselor to the king? Stop! Do you want to be struck down?" The prophet stopped, then said: "I know that God has resolved to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel."
After taking counsel, Amaziah, king of Judah, sent word to Joash, son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel: "Come, let us meet face to face!"

Joash, king of Israel, sent this reply to Amaziah, king of Judah: "The thistle of Lebanon sent word to the cedar of Lebanon: Give your daughter to my son as wife. But the wild beasts of Lebanon passed by and trampled the thistle.
You say to yourself: See, I have struck down Edom, and your heart grows proud to the point of boasting. Stay at home! Why provoke disaster and fall, you and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah would not listen, for this came from God: he meant to hand them over to the enemy, because they had sought out the gods of Edom.
So Joash, king of Israel, marched up, and they met face to face, he and Amaziah, king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh in Judah.
Judah was defeated by Israel, and everyone fled to his tent.

At Beth-shemesh, Joash, king of Israel, captured Amaziah, king of Judah, son of Joash, son of Jehoahaz. He brought him to Jerusalem and made a breach of two hundred metres in the wall, from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.
He took all the gold and silver, all the objects found in the house of God with Obed-edom, along with the treasures of the king's house; he also took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
Amaziah, son of Joash, king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
As for the rest of the acts of Amaziah, from first to last, are they not written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel?
From the time when Amaziah turned away from the Lord, a conspiracy was formed against him in Jerusalem; he fled to Lachish, but men were sent after him to Lachish, and he was put to death there.
They brought him back on horses and buried him with his fathers in the City of Judah.

titres.titre: The pride and leprosy of Uzziah

versets.t: All the people of Judah took Uzziah, sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father, Amaziah.
It was he who rebuilt Eloth and restored it to Judah, after the king had lain down with his fathers.
Uzziah was sixteen years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah, of Jerusalem.
He did what is right in the eyes of the Lord, in everything just as his father Amaziah had done.
He devoted himself to seeking God as long as Zechariah lived, who taught him the fear of God; and as long as he sought the Lord, God made him prosper.
He went to war against the Philistines, tore down the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, and built towns in the territory of Ashdod and among the Philistines.
God helped him against the Philistines, against the Arabs settled at Gur-baal, and against the Meunites.
The Ammonites paid tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread as far as the border of Egypt, so powerful had he become.
Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem, at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate, and at the angle of the walls, and he fortified them.

He also built towers in the wilderness and dug many cisterns, for he had large herds in the lowland and on the plateau, as well as farmers and vinedressers in the hills and the fertile lands, for he loved the soil.

Uzziah had an army of warriors who went out to battle by divisions, according to the muster made by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, under the command of Hananiah, one of the king's officers.
The total number of the heads of families, brave warriors, was two thousand six hundred.
They commanded an army of three hundred seven thousand five hundred fighting men, a formidable force to support the king against the enemy.
Uzziah equipped this whole army with shields, spears, helmets, breastplates, bows, and slingstones.

In Jerusalem he had engines made, the invention of skilled men, to be set on the towers and the corners of the walls to shoot arrows and large stones. His fame spread far and wide, for he was marvelously helped until he became powerful.
But once he was powerful, his heart grew proud to his own ruin: he was unfaithful to the Lord, his God, and entered the sanctuary of the Lord to burn incense on the altar of incense.
The priest Azariah went in after him, with eighty priests of the Lord, courageous men;

they confronted King Uzziah and said to him: "It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the Lord, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated for this. Leave the sanctuary, for you have been unfaithful, and this will bring you no honor before the Lord God."

Uzziah, censer in hand, ready to offer the incense, flew into a rage; and while he was raging at the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead, before the priests, in the house of the Lord, beside the altar of incense.
The high priest Azariah and all the priests turned toward him: he had leprosy on his forehead! They rushed him out, and he himself hurried to leave, for the Lord had struck him.

King Uzziah remained a leper until his death. He lived in a separate house, a leper, cut off from the house of the Lord, while his son Jotham, in charge of the palace, governed the people of the land.
The rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, were written by the prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz.
Uzziah lay down with his fathers; they buried him with them, in the field of the burial ground of the kings, for they said: He is a leper. His son Jotham reigned in his place.
Jotham was twenty-five years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerushah, daughter of Zadok.
He did what is right in the eyes of the Lord, in everything just as his father Uzziah had done; only he did not enter the sanctuary of the Lord. But the people went on in their corrupt ways.
Jotham built the Upper Gate of the house of the Lord and did extensive work on the wall of the Ophel.
He built towns in the hill country of Judah, and forts and towers in the woods.

He made war on the king of the Ammonites and prevailed over them. That year the Ammonites gave him about three and a half tonnes of silver, two million two hundred thousand litres of wheat and as much barley; they gave him the same amount in the second and third years.
Jotham became powerful, because he ordered his ways before the Lord, his God.
The rest of the acts of Jotham, all his wars and his conduct, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Jotham lay down with his fathers; they buried him in the City of David. His son Ahaz reigned in his place.

titres.titre: The prophet Oded; the captives released

versets.t: Ahaz was twenty years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what is right in the eyes of the Lord, unlike David, his father.
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel; worse still, he made cast-metal idols for the Baals.
He burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, and he made his sons pass through the fire, following the abominable practices of the nations that the Lord had driven out before the sons of Israel.
He offered sacrifices and incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.

The Lord, his God, handed him over to the king of Aram: the Arameans defeated him, took a great number of prisoners, and carried them off to Damascus. He was also handed over to the king of Israel, who inflicted a great defeat on him.
Pekah, son of Remaliah, killed in a single day, in Judah, a hundred twenty thousand men, all of them brave, because they had forsaken the Lord, the God of their fathers.
Zichri, a warrior of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah, the king's son, Azrikam, in charge of the palace, and Elkanah, second to the king.
The sons of Israel took, from among their kinsmen, two hundred thousand captives, women, sons, and daughters; they also took from them great plunder, which they carried off to Samaria.

There was there a prophet of the Lord, named Oded. He went out to meet the army returning to Samaria and said to them: "See: in his anger against Judah, the Lord, the God of your fathers, has handed them over to you; and you have slaughtered them with a fury that rises up to heaven.
And now you intend to subject the sons of Judah and Jerusalem as your slaves and servant girls! But you yourselves, are you not guilty before the Lord, your God?
Listen to me, then: send back the captives you have taken from among your kinsmen, for the fierce anger of the Lord is upon you."

Then some of the leaders of the sons of Ephraim, Azariah son of Jehohanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai, rose up against those who were returning from the war

and said to them: "You shall not bring these captives in here, for you mean to load us with guilt before the Lord and to add to our sins and our guilt; and our guilt is already great, and the fierce anger of the Lord is upon Israel."
So the soldiers gave up the captives and the plunder before the leaders and the whole assembly.

Men designated by name stood up, took charge of the captives, and with the plunder clothed all who were naked; they gave them garments and sandals, gave them to eat and drink, anointed them with oil, and, carrying the weakest on donkeys, brought them to Jericho, the city of palms, to their kinsmen. Then they returned to Samaria.
At that time King Ahaz sent to ask the king of Assyria for help.
For the Edomites had come again, had defeated Judah, and had carried off captives;

and the Philistines had raided the towns of the lowland and the Negeb of Judah: they had taken Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco and its villages, Timnah and its villages, Gimzo and its villages, and had settled in them.
For the Lord was humbling Judah because of Ahaz, king of Israel, who had let loose disorder in Judah and had been grievously unfaithful to the Lord.
Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, marched against him, but he oppressed him instead of supporting him.
Ahaz had even stripped the house of the Lord, the king's house, and the houses of the officials to make gifts to the king of Assyria; yet it was of no use to him.
In his very distress, King Ahaz became still more unfaithful to the Lord.

He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus who had defeated him, saying: "Since the gods of the kings of Aram help them, I will offer them sacrifices so that they may help me too." But they were his ruin and the ruin of all Israel.
Ahaz gathered up the objects of the house of God, cut them to pieces, shut the doors of the house of the Lord, and set up altars for himself at every corner of Jerusalem.
In each of the towns of Judah he set up high places to burn incense to other gods, provoking the Lord, the God of his fathers.
The rest of his acts and all his conduct, from first to last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
Ahaz lay down with his fathers; they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, but they did not place him in the tombs of the kings of Israel. His son Hezekiah reigned in his place.

titres.titre: Hezekiah: the purification of the Temple

versets.t: Hezekiah became king at twenty-five years of age, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abijah, daughter of Zechariah.
He did what is right in the eyes of the Lord, in everything just as his father David had done.
In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he reopened the doors of the house of the Lord and repaired them.
He summoned the priests and the Levites, gathered them in the square on the east side,
and said to them: "Listen to me, Levites! Sanctify yourselves now, sanctify the house of the Lord, the God of your fathers, and carry out of the sanctuary all that is unclean.
For our fathers were unfaithful, they did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, our God; they forsook him, they turned their faces away from the dwelling of the Lord and turned their backs on him.
They even shut the doors of the vestibule, put out the lamps, and stopped burning incense and offering the burnt offering to the God of Israel in the sanctuary.
And so the anger of the Lord fell upon Judah and Jerusalem: he made them an object of horror, of dismay, and of mockery, as you see with your own eyes.
That is why our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons, our daughters, and our wives are in captivity.
Now it is on my heart to make a covenant with the Lord, the God of Israel, so that the heat of his anger may turn away from us.
My sons, do not be negligent, then, for it is you whom the Lord has chosen to stand before him in his service, to be his ministers and to offer him incense."

Then the Levites arose: Mahath son of Amasai, and Joel son of Azariah, of the sons of Kohath; of the sons of Merari, Kish son of Abdi, and Azariah son of Jehallelel; of the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah, and Eden son of Joah;
of the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeiel; of the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
of the sons of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; of the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
They gathered their kinsmen, sanctified themselves, and came, according to the king's order in keeping with the words of the Lord, to purify the house of the Lord.

The priests went into the interior of the house of the Lord to purify it; all the uncleanness they found in the sanctuary they carried out into the court of the house of the Lord, from where the Levites took it out to the Wadi Kidron.

They began the purification on the first day of the first month; on the eighth day they reached the vestibule of the Lord; they purified the house of the Lord in eight days, and finished on the sixteenth day of the first month.
Then they went in to King Hezekiah and said: "We have purified the whole house of the Lord, the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, the table of the offering and all its utensils.
All the objects that King Ahaz, in his unfaithfulness, had cast aside during his reign, we have restored and sanctified: here they are before the altar of the Lord."
King Hezekiah rose early, gathered the officials of the city, and went up to the house of the Lord.

They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats, as a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. The king ordered the priests, the sons of Aaron, to offer them on the altar of the Lord.

They slaughtered the bulls; the priests collected the blood and threw it against the altar. They slaughtered the rams and threw the blood against the altar; they slaughtered the lambs and threw the blood against the altar.
Then they brought forward the goats of the sin offering before the king and the assembly, who laid their hands on them.
The priests slaughtered them and with their blood made atonement at the altar for all Israel; for it was for all Israel that the king had ordered the burnt offering and the sin offering.

Hezekiah stationed the Levites in the house of the Lord with cymbals, lyres, and harps, according to the order of David, of Gad, the king's seer, and of Nathan the prophet; for this order came from the Lord, through his prophets.
The Levites took their places with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.

Hezekiah ordered the burnt offering to be offered on the altar. At the moment the burnt offering began, the song of the Lord and the trumpets began as well, accompanied by the instruments of David, king of Israel.
The whole assembly bowed in worship, the song rang out and the trumpets sounded, all this until the burnt offering was finished.
When the burnt offering was completed, the king and all who were with him knelt down and bowed in worship.
King Hezekiah and the officials told the Levites to praise the Lord with the words of David and of Asaph the seer; they praised him with joy, bowed their heads, and worshiped.

Then Hezekiah spoke again: "You are now consecrated to the Lord. Come forward, bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the Lord." The assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and all whose hearts were generous offered burnt offerings.
The number of burnt offerings brought by the assembly was seventy bulls, a hundred rams, and two hundred lambs, all as a burnt offering to the Lord.
They also consecrated six hundred oxen and three thousand sheep.

But the priests, too few in number, could not skin all the burnt offerings; their kinsmen, the Levites, helped them until the task was done and until the other priests had sanctified themselves, for the Levites had been more wholehearted than they in sanctifying themselves.
There were, moreover, a great many burnt offerings, along with the fat of the peace offerings and the libations for the burnt offerings. So the service of the house of the Lord was restored.
Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced at what God had arranged for the people, for the thing had come about so quickly.

Hezekiah sent messengers to all Israel and Judah; he even wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, inviting them to come to the house of the Lord in Jerusalem to keep the Passover in honor of the Lord, the God of Israel.
The king, his officials, and the whole assembly in Jerusalem had decided to keep the Passover in the second month,
for they had been unable to keep it at its proper time, since there were not enough sanctified priests and the people had not gathered in Jerusalem.
The plan seemed right to the king and to the whole assembly.

They decided to make a proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, that people should come to Jerusalem to keep the Passover in honor of the Lord, the God of Israel; for it had not been kept in large numbers, as it is written.

The couriers set out with the letters from the king and his officials throughout all Israel and Judah, carrying this order of the king: "Sons of Israel, return to the Lord, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and he will return to the remnant of you who have escaped from the hand of the kings of Assyria.
Do not be like your fathers and your kinsmen, who were unfaithful to the Lord, the God of their fathers, so that he gave them over to devastation, as you see.

Do not be stiff-necked, like your fathers; hold out your hand to the Lord, come to his sanctuary, which he has sanctified forever, serve the Lord, your God, and the heat of his anger will turn away from you.

For if you return to the Lord, your kinsmen and your sons will find compassion from those who took them captive, and they will return to this land; for the Lord, your God, is gracious and merciful: he will not turn his face away from you if you return to him."
The couriers went from town to town through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, as far as Zebulun; but people laughed at them and mocked them.
Only a few men of Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
In Judah too the hand of God was at work to give them one heart and to make them carry out the order of the king and the officials, according to the word of the Lord.
A great many people gathered in Jerusalem to keep the feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month: it was an immense assembly.
They arose, did away with the altars in Jerusalem, removed all the incense altars, and threw them into the Wadi Kidron.

They slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and the Levites, overcome with shame, sanctified themselves and brought burnt offerings into the house of the Lord.
They stood at their posts, according to their rule, according to the law of Moses, the man of God; the priests threw the blood that they received from the hand of the Levites.
Since many in the assembly had not sanctified themselves, the Levites were charged with slaughtering the Passover victims for all who were not clean, so as to consecrate them to the Lord.

Indeed, a large part of the people, many from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, had not purified themselves, and they ate the Passover without conforming to what is written. But Hezekiah prayed for them: "May the Lord, who is good, pardon
everyone who has set his heart to seek God, the Lord, the God of his fathers, even if he does not have the purity required for the sanctuary."
The Lord heard Hezekiah and healed the people.

The sons of Israel present in Jerusalem kept the feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days, with great joy; and each day the Levites and the priests praised the Lord, with powerful instruments, in honor of the Lord.
