Hezekiah spoke to the heart of all the Levites who showed a fine understanding of the service of the Lord. They ate the festival victims for seven days, offering peace offerings and giving thanks to the Lord, the God of their fathers.
Then the whole assembly decided to keep seven more days; and they kept those seven days with joy,

for Hezekiah, king of Judah, had provided the assembly with a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, and the officials had provided a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep; and a great number of priests had sanctified themselves.

The whole assembly of Judah rejoiced, along with the priests, the Levites, all the assembly that had come from Israel, and the resident aliens who had come from the land of Israel or who were settled in Judah.
There was great joy in Jerusalem: since the days of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel, nothing like this had been seen in Jerusalem.
The levitical priests arose and blessed the people; their voice was heard, and their prayer reached the holy dwelling of the Lord, all the way to heaven.

When all this was finished, all the Israelites present set out for the towns of Judah; they smashed the pillars, cut down the sacred poles, and tore down the high places and the altars throughout all Judah and Benjamin, as well as in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they were completely destroyed. Then all the sons of Israel returned home, each to his own property.

Hezekiah reestablished the divisions of the priests and the Levites, each according to his function, priests and Levites, for the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, for the service, the praise, and the singing, at the gates of the camp of the Lord.

From his own possessions he provided the king's portion for the burnt offerings, those of the morning and the evening, those of the sabbaths, the new moons, and the feasts, as it is written in the law of the Lord.
He ordered the people of Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, so that they could devote themselves to the law of the Lord.

As soon as the order was spread abroad, the sons of Israel gave abundantly the firstfruits of the grain, the new wine, the oil, the honey, and all the produce of the fields; they also brought in abundantly the tithe of everything.

The sons of Israel and Judah who lived in the towns of Judah also gave the tithe of the herds and flocks, and the tithe of the holy things consecrated to the Lord, their God; they made great heaps of them.
They began these heaps in the third month and finished them in the seventh.
When Hezekiah and the officials came and saw the heaps, they blessed the Lord and his people Israel.
Hezekiah questioned the priests and the Levites about these heaps;

and the high priest Azariah, of the house of Zadok, answered him: "Since the offerings began to be brought to the house of the Lord, we have eaten our fill, and much is left over, for the Lord has blessed his people: here is all this that remains."
Hezekiah had storerooms prepared in the house of the Lord; they prepared them,
and faithfully brought in the offerings, the tithe, and the consecrated things. The Levite Conaniah was in charge of them, with his brother Shimei as second.

Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were overseers, under the command of Conaniah and his brother Shimei, by decision of King Hezekiah and of Azariah, the chief of the house of God.
The Levite Kore, son of Imnah, keeper of the East Gate, was in charge of the freewill offerings made to God, to distribute what was set aside for the Lord and the most holy things.

Under his command, Eden, Miniamin, Joshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah faithfully made, in the towns of the priests, the distributions to their kinsmen, great and small, according to their divisions,
apart from the males enrolled, three years old and upward, who entered the house of the Lord for the daily service, according to their functions and their divisions.
The priests were enrolled by families, and the Levites from twenty years old and upward, according to their functions and their divisions.
The register included all their little children, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, the whole community; for they faithfully consecrated themselves to the holy things.

As for the sons of Aaron, the priests who lived in the lands attached to their towns, in each town there were men designated by name to distribute the portions to every male among the priests and to every Levite enrolled.
This is what Hezekiah did throughout all Judah: he did what is good, right, and true before the Lord, his God.
In every undertaking he began, for the service of the house of God, for the law and the commandment, seeking his God, he acted with all his heart, and he prospered.

titres.titre: The illness and death of Hezekiah

versets.t: After these acts of faithfulness, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, entered Judah, camped before the fortified towns, and resolved to take them.
When Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and was turning against Jerusalem to attack it,
he took counsel with his officials and his warriors to stop up the springs of water outside the city, and they helped him do it.
A great many people gathered and stopped up all the springs and the wadi that flowed through the land, saying: "Why should the kings of Assyria find abundant water when they arrive?"

Hezekiah took courage: he rebuilt the whole ruined wall, raised towers on it, built a second wall outside, strengthened the Millo in the City of David, and made a great quantity of weapons and shields.
He appointed military commanders over the people, gathered them around him in the square by the city gate, and spoke to their heart:
"Be strong and courageous, do not fear, do not be dismayed before the king of Assyria and all the multitude with him, for there is more with us than with him.
With him there is only an arm of flesh; with us there is the Lord, our God, to help us and to fight our battles." And the people leaned on the words of Hezekiah, king of Judah.
After this, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, who was besieging Lachish with all his forces, sent his servants to Jerusalem, to Hezekiah, king of Judah, and to all the Judeans in Jerusalem, to say:
"Thus says Sennacherib, king of Assyria: In what do you place your trust, that you remain besieged in Jerusalem?
Is not Hezekiah deceiving you, handing you over to death by hunger and thirst, when he says: The Lord, our God, will save us from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Is it not he, Hezekiah, who removed the high places and the altars of this god, saying to Judah and Jerusalem: You shall bow down before one altar only, and there you shall burn incense?
Do you not know what my fathers and I have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of those lands able to deliver their land from my hand?
Among all the gods of those nations that my fathers devoted to destruction, which one was able to deliver his people from my hand? And could your god deliver you from it?

So do not let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you like this, and do not trust him: no god of any nation or kingdom has been able to deliver his people from my hand or from the hand of my fathers; how much less will your god deliver you from my hand!"
The servants of Sennacherib spoke still more against the Lord God and against Hezekiah, his servant.

He also wrote a letter to insult the Lord, the God of Israel, and to speak against him: "Just as the gods of the nations of the lands did not deliver their people from my hand, so the god of Hezekiah will not deliver his own."
Then his servants shouted in a loud voice, in Hebrew, to the people of Jerusalem posted on the wall, to frighten and terrify them and so seize the city.
They spoke of the God of Jerusalem as of the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands.
Then King Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz, began to pray and cried out to heaven.

The Lord sent an angel, who destroyed all the warriors, the princes, and the commanders in the camp of the king of Assyria. He returned, covered with shame, to his own land; and when he entered the temple of his god, he fell there by the sword of some of his own sons.
So the Lord saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib, king of Assyria, and from all their enemies, and he gave them rest on every side.
Many brought offerings to the Lord in Jerusalem and rich gifts to Hezekiah, king of Judah, who from then on was exalted in the eyes of all the nations.
In those days Hezekiah fell mortally ill. He prayed to the Lord, who answered him and granted him a sign.
But Hezekiah did not respond to the kindness he had received: his heart grew proud, and the anger of the Lord was upon him, upon Judah, and upon Jerusalem.
Then Hezekiah humbled himself for the pride of his heart, he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the anger of the Lord did not come upon them during Hezekiah's lifetime.
Hezekiah had great wealth and glory. He made for himself treasuries of silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of precious objects;
storehouses for the harvests of grain, new wine, and oil, stalls for every kind of livestock, and pens for the flocks.
He built towns for himself and had numerous herds and flocks, for God had given him very great possessions.
It was also he, Hezekiah, who stopped up the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and directed them downward, to the west of the City of David. Hezekiah prospered in all his undertakings.

However, in the affair of the envoys whom the princes of Babylon sent to him to inquire about the wonder that had happened in the land, God left him to himself, to test him and to know all that was in his heart.
The rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his acts of devotion are written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz, and in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

Hezekiah lay down with his fathers; they buried him on the ascent to the tombs of the sons of David, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem paid him honor at his death. His son Manasseh reigned in his place.
Manasseh was twelve years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem.
He did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, following the abominable practices of the nations that the Lord had driven out before the sons of Israel.
He rebuilt the high places that his father Hezekiah had destroyed, raised altars to the Baals, made sacred poles, bowed down before all the host of heaven, and served it.
He built altars in the house of the Lord, of which the Lord had said: It is in Jerusalem that my name shall be forever.
He built altars to all the host of heaven, in the two courts of the house of the Lord.

He made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, practiced astrology, omens, and sorcery, and appointed mediums and diviners: he multiplied what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, provoking him without ceasing.

He placed the carved idol that he had made in the house of God, of which God had said to David and to his son Solomon: It is in this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, that I will put my name forever.

I will no longer make the foot of Israel wander from the land that I destined for your fathers, provided they take care to do all that I have commanded them, all the law, the statutes, and the ordinances given through Moses.
But Manasseh led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem astray, so that they did more evil than the nations that the Lord had destroyed before the sons of Israel.
The Lord spoke to Manasseh and to his people, but they paid no attention.
Then the Lord brought against them the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria: they took Manasseh with hooks, bound him with chains of bronze, and led him off to Babylon.
In his distress, he implored the Lord, his God, and humbled himself deeply before the God of his fathers.
He prayed to him, and God, allowing himself to be moved, heard his plea and brought him back to Jerusalem, to his kingship. Then Manasseh knew that the Lord is God.

After this, he built an outer wall for the City of David, to the west, toward Gihon in the valley, as far as the entrance of the Fish Gate; he carried it around the Ophel and raised it very high. He also placed military commanders in all the fortified towns of Judah.

He did away with the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the Lord, along with all the altars he had built on the mountain of the house of the Lord and in Jerusalem, and he threw them outside the city.
He restored the altar of the Lord, offered on it peace offerings and thank offerings, and ordered Judah to serve the Lord, the God of Israel.
The people, however, went on sacrificing at the high places, but only to the Lord, their God.
The rest of the acts of Manasseh, his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the Lord, the God of Israel, are found in the acts of the kings of Israel.

His prayer and how God was moved by it, all his sin and his unfaithfulness, the sites where he built high places and set up sacred poles and idols before he humbled himself, all this is written in the records of the Seers.
Manasseh lay down with his fathers; they buried him in his house. His son Amon reigned in his place.
Amon was twenty-two years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem.
He did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, like his father Manasseh: he sacrificed to all the idols that his father Manasseh had made, and served them.
But he did not humble himself before the Lord, as his father Manasseh had humbled himself; on the contrary, he, Amon, multiplied his guilt.
His servants conspired against him and put him to death in his house.
But the people of the land struck down all those who had conspired against King Amon, and made his son Josiah king in his place.

titres.titre: The book of the Law rediscovered

versets.t: Josiah was eight years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
He did what is right in the eyes of the Lord, walked in the ways of David, his father, and turned aside neither to the right nor to the left.

In the eighth year of his reign, while still a boy, he began to seek the God of David, his father; and in the twelfth year he set about purifying Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the sacred poles, the carved idols, and the cast idols.

The altars of the Baals were torn down before him; he cut down the incense altars that stood above them, broke the sacred poles, the carved and cast idols, ground them to dust, and scattered it on the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.
He burned the bones of the priests on their altars, and so purified Judah and Jerusalem.
In the towns of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and as far as Naphtali, amid their ruins,
he tore down the altars, ground to dust the sacred poles and the carved idols, and cut down all the incense altars throughout the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.

In the eighteenth year of his reign, once the land and the House had been purified, he sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah son of Joahaz the recorder, to repair the house of the Lord, his God.

They went to the high priest Hilkiah and handed over to him the silver brought to the house of God, which the Levites who kept the threshold had collected from Manasseh, Ephraim, all the rest of Israel, all Judah and Benjamin, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
They entrusted it to the master workmen in charge of the house of the Lord, who gave it to the workers laboring on the house of the Lord to repair and restore it.
They gave it to the carpenters and the masons to buy dressed stone and timber for beams, and to lay the rafters of the buildings that the kings of Judah had let fall into ruin.

These men worked faithfully. Over them, as overseers, were the Levites Jahath and Obadiah, of the sons of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of Kohath, to direct them; and other Levites, all skilled with musical instruments,
supervised the porters and directed all the workers at each task. Among the Levites there were also scribes, officers, and gatekeepers.
As they were taking out the silver brought to the house of the Lord, the priest Hilkiah found the book of the law of the Lord given through Moses.
Then Hilkiah said to Shaphan, the secretary: "I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord." And he handed it to Shaphan.
Shaphan brought the book to the king and gave him an account: "Your servants have carried out everything entrusted to them:
they have collected the silver found in the house of the Lord and handed it over to the master workmen and the workers."
Then Shaphan, the secretary, announced to the king: "The priest Hilkiah has given me a book." And Shaphan read from it before the king.
When he heard the words of the law, the king tore his garments.
He gave this order to Hilkiah, to Ahikam son of Shaphan, to Abdon son of Micah, to Shaphan the secretary, and to Asaiah the king's servant:

"Go, inquire of the Lord for me and for what remains of Israel and Judah, concerning the words of the book that has been found; for great is the anger of the Lord, poured out upon us, because our fathers did not keep the word of the Lord by acting according to all that is written in this book."

Hilkiah and the king's envoys went to the prophetess Huldah, wife of Shallum, son of Tokhath, son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe; she lived in Jerusalem, in the Second Quarter. They spoke to her to this effect,
and she answered them: "Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Tell the man who sent you to me:
Thus says the Lord: I am going to bring disaster upon this place and upon its inhabitants, all the curses written in the book that has been read before the king of Judah,
because they have forsaken me and have offered incense to other gods, provoking me by all the works of their hands. My anger has been poured out upon this place, and it will not be quenched.
And to the king of Judah who sends you to inquire of the Lord, you shall say: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning the words you have heard:

Because your heart was touched and you humbled yourself before God when you heard his words against this place and its inhabitants, because you humbled yourself before me, tore your garments, and wept before me, I too have heard you, oracle of the Lord.

I will gather you to your fathers, you will be laid in peace in your tomb, and your eyes will not see all the disaster that I am going to bring upon this place and its inhabitants." They brought this reply back to the king.
The king had all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem assembled.

He went up to the house of the Lord with all the men of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, the Levites, and all the people, from the greatest to the least, and he read to them all the words of the book of the covenant found in the house of the Lord.

Standing on his platform, the king made the covenant before the Lord: he pledged to follow the Lord, to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his laws with all his heart and all his soul, and to carry out the words of the covenant written in this book.
He had all who were in Jerusalem and in Benjamin give their assent to it; and the inhabitants of Jerusalem acted according to the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.

Josiah did away with all the abominations from all the territories belonging to the sons of Israel, and he required all who were in Israel to serve the Lord, their God. As long as he lived, they did not turn away from the Lord, the God of their fathers.
Josiah kept the Passover in Jerusalem in honor of the Lord; the Passover lamb was slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month.
He reestablished the priests in their functions and encouraged them in the service of the house of the Lord.

He said to the Levites who taught all Israel and who were consecrated to the Lord: "Place the holy ark in the house that Solomon, son of David, king of Israel, built; you no longer have to carry it on your shoulders. From now on, serve the Lord, your God, and his people Israel.
Hold yourselves ready, by families, according to your divisions, following the regulation of David, king of Israel, and that of his son Solomon.
Take your stand in the sanctuary, at the disposal of the families of your kinsmen, the people, one division of Levites for each group of families.
Slaughter the Passover lamb, sanctify yourselves, and prepare it for your kinsmen, conforming to the word of the Lord given through Moses."

Josiah set aside from his own possessions, for the people present, small livestock, lambs and young goats, to the number of thirty thousand, all intended for the Passover offerings, and three thousand oxen.

His officials made a freewill gift to the people, to the priests, and to the Levites: Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, chiefs of the house of God, gave the priests, for the Passover offerings, two thousand six hundred lambs and three hundred oxen.

Conaniah, Shemaiah, and Nethanel, his brothers, along with Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, chiefs of the Levites, gave the Levites, for the Passover offerings, five thousand lambs and five hundred oxen.
When the service was thus organized, the priests took their posts and the Levites according to their divisions, as the king had ordered.
They slaughtered the Passover lamb; the priests threw the blood they received from the Levites, while the Levites skinned the victims.

They set aside the portions intended for the burnt offering to give them to the groups of families of the people, so that they might offer them to the Lord, as it is written in the book of Moses; they did the same for the oxen.
They roasted the Passover lamb over the fire, according to the rule, and boiled the holy offerings in pots, cauldrons, and kettles, then distributed them quickly to all the people.

Afterward they prepared the Passover for themselves and for the priests; for the priests, the sons of Aaron, were busy until nightfall offering the burnt offerings and the fat. That is why the Levites prepared it for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.

The singers, the sons of Asaph, were at their posts, according to the order of David, of Asaph, of Heman, and of Jeduthun, the king's seer; and the gatekeepers kept each gate, without having to leave their service, for their kinsmen the Levites prepared the Passover for them.
So all the service of the Lord was organized that day for keeping the Passover and offering the burnt offerings on the altar of the Lord, according to the order of King Josiah.
The sons of Israel present kept the Passover at that time, and the feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

No Passover like it had been kept in Israel since the days of the prophet Samuel; none of the kings of Israel had kept a Passover like the one Josiah kept, with the priests, the Levites, all Judah, all Israel that was present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
This Passover was kept in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign.
After all this, when Josiah had put the House in order, Neco, king of Egypt, marched up to fight at Carchemish, on the Euphrates; and Josiah went out to meet him.

Neco sent messengers to him to say: "What have I to do with you, king of Judah? It is not against you that I come today, but against another house with which I am at war; and God has told me to hurry. Stop opposing God, who is with me, lest he destroy you."
But Josiah would not turn away from him: he disguised himself to fight him, did not listen to the words of Neco, which came from the mouth of God, and advanced to give battle in the plain of Megiddo.
The archers shot at King Josiah, and the king said to his servants: "Take me away, for I am badly wounded."

His servants pulled him out of his chariot, placed him in his second chariot, and brought him to Jerusalem. He died and was buried in the tombs of his fathers. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah.
Jeremiah composed a lament for Josiah; and all the male and female singers speak of Josiah in their laments to this day: it has become a custom in Israel, and these songs are recorded in the Laments.
The rest of the acts of Josiah, his deeds of devotion in keeping with what is written in the law of the Lord,
his acts, from first to last, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
The people of the land took Jehoahaz, son of Josiah, and made him king in Jerusalem in place of his father.
Jehoahaz was twenty-three years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.
The king of Egypt deposed him at Jerusalem and imposed on the land a tribute of about three and a half tonnes of silver and thirty-four kilograms of gold.
The king of Egypt made Eliakim, brother of Jehoahaz, king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed his name to Jehoiakim; then Neco carried off his brother Jehoahaz to Egypt.
Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, his God.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, marched up against him and bound him with chains of bronze to carry him off to Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar also carried off to Babylon objects from the house of the Lord and placed them in his temple, in Babylon.
The rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, the abominations he committed, and what was found against him, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. His son Jehoiachin reigned in his place.
Jehoiachin was eighteen years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord.
At the turn of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar had him brought to Babylon, along with the precious objects of the house of the Lord, and made Zedekiah, his kinsman, king over Judah and Jerusalem.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he came to the throne, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.
He did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, his God, and did not humble himself before the prophet Jeremiah, who spoke to him on behalf of the Lord.
He even rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear an oath by God; he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart, refusing to return to the Lord, the God of Israel.

Likewise, all the chiefs of the priests and the people multiplied their acts of unfaithfulness, following all the abominations of the nations, and defiled the house of the Lord, which he had sanctified in Jerusalem.
The Lord, the God of their fathers, sent them warnings without ceasing through his messengers, for he had pity on his people and on his dwelling;
but they mocked the messengers of God, despised his words, and scoffed at his prophets, until the anger of the Lord rose against his people, past all remedy.

Then he brought up against them the king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men by the sword in their sanctuary, sparing neither the young man, nor the young woman, nor the old, nor the gray-haired: the Lord handed everything over to him.
All the objects of the house of God, great and small, the treasures of the house of the Lord, those of the king and his officials, Nebuchadnezzar carried everything off to Babylon.
They burned the house of God, tore down the wall of Jerusalem, set fire to all its palaces, and destroyed all its precious objects.
Those who had escaped the sword, Nebuchadnezzar deported to Babylon, where they became slaves to him and to his sons, until the coming of the kingdom of Persia.

So the word of the Lord, spoken through the mouth of Jeremiah, was fulfilled, until the land had paid off its sabbaths: throughout the time of its desolation it rested, until seventy years were completed.

In the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia, to fulfill the word of the Lord spoken through the mouth of Jeremiah, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, king of Persia, who had a proclamation made by word of mouth and in writing throughout all his kingdom:

"Thus says Cyrus, king of Persia: The Lord, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and it is he who has charged me to build him a house at Jerusalem, in Judah. Whoever among you belongs to all his people? May the Lord, his God, be with him, and let him go up!"

titres.titre: The return; the vessels of the Temple

versets.t: In the first year of Cyrus, king of Persia, to fulfill the word of the Lord spoken through Jeremiah, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, king of Persia, so that he issued a proclamation throughout his whole kingdom, both by word of mouth and in writing:
"Thus says Cyrus, king of Persia: The Lord, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has charged me to build him a house at Jerusalem, in Judah.
Whoever among you belongs to his people, may his God be with him! Let him go up to Jerusalem, in Judah, and build the house of the Lord, the God of Israel: he is the God who is in Jerusalem.

And wherever any survivor still resides, let the people of that place assist him with silver and gold, with goods and livestock, along with the freewill offerings for the house of God that is in Jerusalem."
Then the heads of the families of Judah and Benjamin, the priests and the Levites, everyone whose spirit God had stirred up, set out to go and build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.
All their neighbors supported them with articles of silver and gold, with goods, livestock, and precious things, over and above all the freewill offerings.
King Cyrus brought out the vessels of the house of the Lord that Nebuchadnezzar had carried off from Jerusalem and placed in the temple of his god.
Cyrus, king of Persia, handed them over to Mithredath the treasurer, who counted them out to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.
This was their number: thirty gold basins, a thousand silver basins, twenty-nine knives,
thirty gold bowls, four hundred and ten silver bowls of a second kind, and a thousand other vessels.
In all, there were five thousand four hundred vessels of gold and silver. Sheshbazzar brought all of them along when the exiles went up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

titres.titre: The list of those who returned

versets.t: These are the people of the province who came back from exile, those whom Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had carried off to Babylon, and who returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town.
They came back with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. This is the number of the men of the people of Israel:
the sons of Parosh, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;
the sons of Shephatiah, three hundred and seventy-two;
the sons of Arah, seven hundred and seventy-five;
the sons of Pahath-Moab, of the line of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve;
the sons of Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the sons of Zattu, nine hundred and forty-five;
the sons of Zaccai, seven hundred and sixty;
the sons of Bani, six hundred and forty-two;
the sons of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-three;
the sons of Azgad, one thousand two hundred and twenty-two;
the sons of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-six;
the sons of Bigvai, two thousand and fifty-six;
the sons of Adin, four hundred and fifty-four;
the sons of Ater, of the family of Hezekiah, ninety-eight;
the sons of Bezai, three hundred and twenty-three;
the sons of Jorah, one hundred and twelve;
the sons of Hashum, two hundred and twenty-three;
the sons of Gibbar, ninety-five;
the sons of Bethlehem, one hundred and twenty-three;
the men of Netophah, fifty-six;
the men of Anathoth, one hundred and twenty-eight;
the sons of Azmaveth, forty-two;
the sons of Kiriath-Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty-three;
the sons of Ramah and Geba, six hundred and twenty-one;
the men of Michmas, one hundred and twenty-two;
the men of Bethel and Ai, two hundred and twenty-three;
the sons of Nebo, fifty-two;
the sons of Magbish, one hundred and fifty-six;
the sons of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the sons of Harim, three hundred and twenty;
the sons of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred and twenty-five;
the sons of Jericho, three hundred and forty-five;
the sons of Senaah, three thousand six hundred and thirty.
The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred and seventy-three;
the sons of Immer, one thousand and fifty-two;
the sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;
the sons of Harim, one thousand and seventeen.
The Levites: the sons of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the family of Hodaviah, seventy-four.
The singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred and twenty-eight.
The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akkub, the sons of Hatita, and the sons of Shobai, one hundred and thirty-nine in all.
The temple servants: the sons of Ziha, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,
the sons of Keros, the sons of Siaha, the sons of Padon,
the sons of Lebanah, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Akkub,
the sons of Hagab, the sons of Shalmai, the sons of Hanan,
the sons of Giddel, the sons of Gahar, the sons of Reaiah,
the sons of Rezin, the sons of Nekoda, the sons of Gazzam,
the sons of Uzza, the sons of Paseah, the sons of Besai,
the sons of Asnah, the sons of Meunim, the sons of Nephusim,
the sons of Bakbuk, the sons of Hakupha, the sons of Harhur,
the sons of Bazluth, the sons of Mehida, the sons of Harsha,
the sons of Barkos, the sons of Sisera, the sons of Temah,
the sons of Neziah, and the sons of Hatipha.
The sons of the servants of Solomon: the sons of Sotai, the sons of Sophereth, the sons of Peruda,
the sons of Jaalah, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Giddel,
the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hattil, the sons of Pochereth-hazzebaim, and the sons of Ami.
The total of the temple servants and the sons of the servants of Solomon was three hundred and ninety-two.
These are the ones who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, but who could not prove that their family and their descent were truly of Israel:
the sons of Delaiah, the sons of Tobiah, and the sons of Nekoda, six hundred and fifty-two.
And among the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, and the sons of Barzillai, the one who had married one of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and had taken their name.
These searched for their entry in the genealogical records, but it could not be found; so they were excluded from the priesthood as unclean,
and the governor forbade them to eat the most holy food until a priest should arise to consult God by the Urim and Thummim.
The whole assembly numbered forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty people,
besides their male and female servants, of whom there were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; and there were also two hundred male and female singers.
They had seven hundred and thirty-six horses, two hundred and forty-five mules,
four hundred and thirty-five camels, and six thousand seven hundred and twenty donkeys.
When they arrived at the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, some of the heads of families made freewill offerings toward the house of God, to raise it again on its site.
According to their means, they gave to the treasury of the work sixty-one thousand gold coins, about two and a half tonnes of silver, and one hundred priestly tunics.
So the priests, the Levites, some of the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants settled in their towns; and all Israel lived in its towns.

titres.titre: The altar rebuilt; the feast of Booths
The laying of the foundations of the Temple

versets.t: When the seventh month came, the sons of Israel being in their towns, the people gathered as one at Jerusalem.

Jeshua son of Jozadak, with his fellow priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, with his kinsmen, set about rebuilding the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
They set up the altar on its old foundations, despite their fear of the peoples of the surrounding lands, and on it they offered burnt offerings to the Lord, the morning and evening offerings.
They celebrated the feast of Booths, as it is written, offering day by day the burnt offerings in the number appointed for each day.
After that, they offered the perpetual burnt offering, those for the new moons and for all the feasts consecrated to the Lord, and those of everyone who made a freewill offering to the Lord.
From the first day of the seventh month they had begun to offer burnt offerings to the Lord, though the foundations of the sanctuary had not yet been laid.

They gave money to the stonecutters and carpenters, and food, drink, and oil to the Sidonians and the Tyrians, so that they would bring cedar wood from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, according to the authorization they had received from Cyrus, king of Persia.

In the second year after their arrival at the house of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, and the rest of their kinsmen, the priests and the Levites, all those who had returned from captivity to Jerusalem, began the work and appointed the Levites twenty years old and upward to supervise the work on the house of the Lord.

Jeshua, with his sons and his kinsmen, Kadmiel with his sons, the sons of Judah, took charge with one accord of directing the workers on the house of God; so too the sons of Henadad, with their sons and their kinsmen, all Levites.

When the builders laid the foundations of the sanctuary of the Lord, the priests were stationed in their vestments with the trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with the cymbals, to praise the Lord according to the directions of David, king of Israel.

They took up praise and thanksgiving to the Lord: "For he is good, for his faithful love toward Israel endures forever!" And all the people gave a great shout of praise to the Lord, because the foundations of the house of the Lord were being laid.

But many of the priests, Levites, and elderly heads of families, who had seen the first House, wept aloud as they watched the foundations of this one being laid, while many others raised shouts of joy.
The people could no longer distinguish the sound of the shouts of joy from the sound of their weeping, for the people raised an immense clamor that could be heard far off.

titres.titre: The letters of accusation to the king

versets.t: When the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the returning exiles were building a sanctuary to the Lord, the God of Israel,

they came to Zerubbabel and the heads of families and said to them, "Let us build with you, for like you we seek your God, and we have been offering sacrifices to him since the days of Esarhaddon, king of Assyria, who brought us up here."

But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the heads of families of Israel answered them, "It is not for you and us together to build a house to our God; we alone will build it to the Lord, the God of Israel, as King Cyrus, king of Persia, has commanded us."
Then the people of the land set about discouraging the people of Judah and frightening them to keep them from building.
They bribed officials against them to frustrate their plan throughout the reign of Cyrus, king of Persia, and down to the reign of Darius, king of Persia.
In the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.
And in the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of their associates wrote to Artaxerxes, king of Persia; the letter was written in Aramaic script and composed in Aramaic.
Rehum the governor and Shimshai the secretary wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes, worded as follows.

Rehum the governor, Shimshai the secretary, and the rest of their associates, the judges, the envoys, and the officials, the Persians, the men of Erech, of Babylon, and of Susa, that is, the Elamites,
and the rest of the peoples whom the great and illustrious Osnappar deported and settled in the city of Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River. And now:
This is a copy of the letter they sent to him: "To King Artaxerxes, from your servants, the men Beyond the River. And now:
Let the king know that the Jews who came up from you to us have arrived at Jerusalem: they are rebuilding that rebellious and wicked city, raising its walls and restoring its foundations.
Now let the king know that if this city is rebuilt and its walls raised, they will no longer pay tax, tribute, or toll, and the royal treasury will suffer for it.
Since we eat the salt of the palace, and it is not fitting for us to see the king wronged, we send this word to inform the king,

so that a search may be made in the annals of your fathers: there you will find and learn that this city is a rebellious city, harmful to kings and provinces, and that revolts have been stirred up within it since ancient times. That is why this city was destroyed.
We therefore inform the king that if this city is rebuilt and its walls raised, you will soon possess nothing at all Beyond the River."

The king sent this reply: "To Rehum the governor, to Shimshai the secretary, and to the rest of their associates who live in Samaria and in the rest of the province Beyond the River: Greetings! And now:
The letter you sent us has been read clearly before me.
At my command a search was made, and it was found that this city has from ancient times risen up against kings, and that rebellion and sedition have been stirred up within it.
There were mighty kings in Jerusalem who ruled over the whole region Beyond the River, and tax, tribute, and toll were paid to them.
Now give orders to make these men stop: this city is not to be rebuilt until a further order comes from me.
Be careful not to be negligent in this matter, lest the damage grow to the harm of kings."

As soon as the copy of King Artaxerxes' letter had been read before Rehum, Shimshai the secretary, and their associates, they went in haste to Jerusalem, to the Jews, and by force compelled them to stop the work.
So the work on the house of God in Jerusalem was interrupted, and it remained at a standstill until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of Persia.

titres.titre: The work resumes; the inquiry of Tattenai

versets.t: Now the prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied to the Jews of Judah and Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel who was over them.
Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and resumed building the house of God in Jerusalem, supported by the prophets of God.
At that time Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates came to them and asked, "Who authorized you to build this house and to raise these walls?"
They also asked us the names of the men who were putting up this building.
But the eye of their God was watching over the elders of the Jews, so they were not stopped until the matter could be referred to Darius and a written reply come back concerning it.
This is a copy of the letter that Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and his associates, the officials Beyond the River, sent to King Darius.
They sent him a report worded as follows: "To King Darius, all peace!

Let the king know that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. It is being built with dressed stones, and beams are being set in the walls; this work is being done with care and is prospering in their hands.
We questioned those elders and asked them: Who authorized you to build this house and to raise these walls?
We also asked them their names, so as to make them known to you and to record the names of their leaders.

This is the answer they gave us: We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the house that was built long ago, many years past, which a great king of Israel had built and completed.
But because our fathers provoked the God of heaven, he handed them over to Nebuchadnezzar the Chaldean, king of Babylon, who destroyed this house and deported the people to Babylon.
Yet in the first year of Cyrus, king of Babylon, King Cyrus gave the order to rebuild this house of God.

Moreover, the vessels of gold and silver of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the sanctuary in Jerusalem and carried to the temple of Babylon, King Cyrus took out of the temple of Babylon and handed over to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he made governor.
He said to him: Take these vessels, go and deposit them in the sanctuary in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be rebuilt on its site.
So this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem; and from that time until now it has been under construction, and it is not yet finished.

Now, if it please the king, let a search be made in the royal treasuries there in Babylon, to find out whether King Cyrus did indeed give the order to rebuild this house of God in Jerusalem; and let the king send us his decision on the matter."

titres.titre: The completion and dedication of the Temple

versets.t: Then King Darius gave the order to make a search in the archives where the treasures were stored in Babylon.
And at Ecbatana, the fortress in the province of Media, a scroll was found in which the following was recorded:

"In the first year of King Cyrus, King Cyrus gave this order concerning the house of God in Jerusalem: Let this house be rebuilt as a place of sacrifices, and let its foundations be firmly laid; its height shall be thirty metres and its width thirty metres.
There shall be three courses of dressed stones and one course of timber; the cost shall be paid from the royal treasury.

Moreover, the vessels of gold and silver of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the sanctuary in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, shall be returned: let them go back to the sanctuary in Jerusalem, to their place, and be deposited in the house of God."
"Now therefore, Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and your associates, the officials Beyond the River, keep away from there.
Let the work on this house of God go on; let the governor of the Jews and their elders rebuild this house of God on its site.

Here are my orders concerning how you are to help these elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God: from the royal revenue, that is, the taxes of the province Beyond the River, the cost is to be paid in full to these men, without interruption.

Whatever they need for the burnt offerings of the God of heaven, young bulls, rams, and lambs, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and oil, is to be supplied to them day by day, without fail, according to the directions of the priests in Jerusalem,
so that they may offer sacrifices of a pleasing aroma to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and his sons.

I also decree this: if anyone violates this edict, a beam is to be pulled from his house, and he is to be impaled on it and fastened there, and his house is to be made a heap of rubble for this offense.

And may the God who caused his name to dwell there overthrow any king or people who would stretch out a hand to violate this decree and destroy this house of God in Jerusalem! I, Darius, have given this order: let it be carried out exactly."
Then Tattenai, governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates carried out exactly the order of King Darius.

The elders of the Jews built successfully, supported by the prophecies of Haggai and of Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished the construction according to the command of the God of Israel and the order of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, king of Persia.
This house was finished on the third day of the month of Adar (around February and March), in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
The sons of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the returning exiles celebrated with joy the dedication of this house of God.
For the dedication they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs, and, as a sin offering for all Israel, twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
They appointed the priests according to their divisions and the Levites according to their groups for the service of God in Jerusalem, as it is written in the book of Moses.
The returning exiles celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
The priests and the Levites had purified themselves as one; all were clean. They slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the returning exiles, for their fellow priests, and for themselves.

The sons of Israel who had come back from exile ate it, together with all those who had separated themselves from the impurity of the nations of the land to join them in seeking the Lord, the God of Israel.

For seven days they celebrated with joy the feast of Unleavened Bread, for the Lord had made them glad by turning the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of God, the God of Israel.
After these events, in the reign of Artaxerxes, king of Persia, Ezra son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub,
son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth,
son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki,
son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the high priest:

this Ezra came up from Babylon. He was a scribe skilled in the law of Moses, given by the Lord, the God of Israel; and since the hand of the Lord his God was upon him, the king granted him everything he asked.
Some of the sons of Israel, and some of the priests, the Levites, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants also went up to Jerusalem, in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes.
Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of the seventh year of the king.
He had set out from Babylon on the first day of the first month, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month, for the gracious hand of his God was upon him.
For Ezra had set his heart to study the law of the Lord, to practice it, and to teach its statutes and rules in Israel.
This is a copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra, the priest and scribe, learned in the words of the commandments of the Lord and of his statutes for Israel:
"Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra, priest and scribe learned in the law of the God of heaven: perfect peace. And now:
I decree that any member of the people of Israel, of its priests and its Levites, residing in my kingdom, who wishes to go to Jerusalem, may go with you.
For you are sent by the king and his seven counselors to inquire about Judah and Jerusalem according to the law of your God, which you have in hand,
and to carry there the silver and gold that the king and his counselors have freely offered to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem,

together with all the silver and gold that you will collect throughout the province of Babylon, along with the freewill offerings of the people and the priests for the house of their God in Jerusalem.

With this money you shall be careful to buy bulls, rams, and lambs, along with the grain offerings and the drink offerings that go with them, and you shall offer them on the altar of the house of your God in Jerusalem.
As for the rest of the silver and gold, do with it, you and your brothers, whatever seems good to you, according to the will of your God.
The vessels handed over to you for the service of the house of your God, deposit them before the God of Jerusalem.
And the rest of what is needed for the house of your God, whatever falls to you to provide, you shall take from the royal treasury.
I, King Artaxerxes, decree to all the treasurers of the province Beyond the River: whatever Ezra, priest and scribe learned in the law of the God of heaven, asks of you shall be carried out exactly,
up to about three and a half tonnes of silver, twenty-two thousand liters of wheat, two thousand two hundred liters of wine, two thousand two hundred liters of oil, and salt without limit.
Let whatever the God of heaven commands be done promptly for the house of the God of heaven, lest his wrath fall upon the kingdom of the king and his sons.
We further make known to you that it is not permitted to impose tax, tribute, or toll on any of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, or workers of this house of God.

And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of your God that is in you, appoint judges and magistrates to administer justice to all the people Beyond the River, to all who know the laws of your God; and those who do not know them, instruct them.
Whoever does not observe the law of your God and the law of the king, let the sentence be strictly applied to him: death, banishment, a fine, or imprisonment."
Blessed be the Lord, the God of our fathers, who has thus put it into the heart of the king to glorify the house of the Lord in Jerusalem,

and who has directed toward me the favor of the king, his counselors, and all his powerful officials! Strengthened by the hand of the Lord my God, which was upon me, I gathered leaders of Israel to go up with me.
These are the heads of families, with their genealogy, of those who came up with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes:
of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; of the sons of David, Hattush,
of the sons of Shecaniah; of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him a hundred and fifty men enrolled;
of the sons of Pahath-Moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred men;
of the sons of Shecaniah, the son of Jahaziel, and with him three hundred men;
of the sons of Adin, Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty men;
of the sons of Elam, Isaiah son of Athaliah, and with him seventy men;
of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty men;
of the sons of Joab, Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred and eighteen men;
of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him a hundred and sixty men;
of the sons of Bebai, Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men;
of the sons of Azgad, Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him a hundred and ten men;
of the sons of Adonikam, the last ones, whose names are these: Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah, and with them sixty men;
of the sons of Bigvai, Uthai and Zabbud, and with them seventy men.
I gathered them by the river that flows toward Ahava, and we camped there three days. When I reviewed the people and the priests, I found none of the sons of Levi among them.
So I sent for the leaders Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, another Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, as well as the teachers Joiarib and Elnathan.

I dispatched them to Iddo, the leader of the place called Casiphia, telling them what to say to Iddo and his brothers, the temple servants at Casiphia, so that they might bring us ministers for the house of our God.

Since the gracious hand of our God was upon us, they brought us a man of understanding, from among the sons of Mahli, son of Levi, son of Israel: Sherebiah, with his sons and his brothers, eighteen men;
Hashabiah, and with him Isaiah, from among the sons of Merari, with his brothers and their sons, twenty men;
and, from among the temple servants whom David and the leaders had assigned to the service of the Levites, two hundred and twenty temple servants, all designated by name.
There, by the river of Ahava, I proclaimed a fast, to humble ourselves before our God and to ask him for a safe journey for us, our children, and all our goods.

For I would have been ashamed to ask the king for an escort of soldiers and horsemen to protect us from the enemy on the way, since we had told the king, "The hand of our God watches for good over all who seek him, but his power and his wrath are against all who forsake him."
So we fasted and implored our God about this, and he answered us.
Then I set apart twelve of the leading priests, Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers,
and I weighed out before them the silver, the gold, and the vessels, the offering that the king, his counselors, his officials, and all Israel present had contributed for the house of our God.
I weighed out and handed over to them about twenty-two tonnes of silver, silver vessels worth three and a half tonnes, three and a half tonnes of gold,
twenty gold bowls worth a thousand gold coins, and two vessels of fine, gleaming bronze, precious as gold.
And I said to them, "You are consecrated to the Lord, and these vessels are holy; this silver and gold are a freewill offering to the Lord, the God of your fathers.
Guard them carefully until you weigh them out in Jerusalem, before the leaders of the priests and the Levites and the heads of families of Israel, in the chambers of the house of the Lord."
So the priests and the Levites received the silver, the gold, and the vessels by weight, to carry them to Jerusalem, to the house of our God.

We set out from the river of Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month to go to Jerusalem; the hand of our God was upon us, and he delivered us on the way from the hand of the enemy and from ambushes.
When we arrived in Jerusalem, we rested there three days.

On the fourth day the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed out in the house of our God into the hands of the priest Meremoth son of Uriah; with him were Eleazar son of Phinehas, and the Levites Jozabad son of Jeshua and Noadiah son of Binnui.
Everything was counted and weighed, and the total weight was recorded in writing at that time.

The exiles who had returned, the sons of the captivity, offered as a burnt offering to the God of Israel twelve bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering, all as a burnt offering to the Lord.
They delivered the king's edicts to the king's satraps and to the governors of the province Beyond the River, who supported the people and the house of God.

When these things were finished, the leaders came to me and said, "The people of Israel, the priests, and the Levites have not kept themselves separate from the peoples of the lands and their abominable practices, those of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.

For they have taken some of their daughters as wives for themselves and for their sons, and the holy race has mingled with the peoples of the lands; and in this unfaithfulness the hand of the leaders and the magistrates has been foremost."
At this news I tore my garment and my cloak, pulled hair from my head and my beard, and sat down appalled.
Around me gathered all who trembled at the words of the God of Israel, because of the unfaithfulness of the exiles; and I sat there appalled until the evening offering.
At the evening offering I rose from my dejection, my garment and cloak torn, and I fell to my knees, my hands stretched out toward the Lord my God.
I said, "My God, I am too ashamed and disgraced to lift my face to you, my God; for our sins have risen higher than our heads, and our guilt has mounted up to heaven.

From the days of our fathers until this day our guilt has been great; because of our sins we, our kings, and our priests have been handed over to the kings of the lands, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to shame, as is still the case today.

And now, for a brief moment, the Lord our God has shown us grace: he has left us a remnant and given us a foothold in his holy place; so our God brightens our eyes and grants us a little life in our slavery.

For we are slaves; yet in our slavery our God has not abandoned us: he has won us the favor of the kings of Persia, to give us new life, to raise up the house of our God, to repair its ruins, and to give us a refuge in Judah and Jerusalem.
And now, our God, what shall we say after this? For we have forsaken your commandments,

which you had given us through your servants the prophets, saying: The land you are entering to take possession of it is a land defiled by the impurity of the peoples who inhabit it, by the abominations with which they have filled it from end to end with their uncleanness.

So do not give your daughters to their sons, do not take their daughters for your sons, and never seek their peace or their prosperity, so that you may grow strong, eat the best produce of the land, and hand it down as an inheritance to your sons forever.
After all that has come upon us for our evil deeds and our great guilt, even though you, our God, have spared us more than our sins deserved and have left us this remnant,
were we to break your commandments again and ally ourselves with these abominable peoples? Would you not be angry with us until you destroyed us, leaving neither remnant nor survivor?
Lord, God of Israel, you are just, and that is why only a remnant of survivors remains today: here we are before you with our guilt, unable, because of it, to stand in your presence."

titres.titre: The pledge to send away the foreign wives

versets.t: While Ezra was praying and confessing in this way, weeping and prostrate before the house of God, a very great assembly of Israel, men, women, and children, gathered around him, and the people wept bitterly.

Then Shecaniah son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, spoke up and said to Ezra, "We have been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women taken from the peoples of the land; but in spite of this, there is still hope for Israel.

Let us now make a covenant with our God: let us send away all these women and the children born of them, according to the counsel of my lord and of those who tremble at the commandments of our God; let it be done according to the Law.
Rise up, for this is your task, and we are with you. Take courage, and act!"
Ezra rose and made the leaders of the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to do what had just been said; and they swore it.

Then Ezra left the front of the house of God and went to the room of Jehohanan son of Eliashib; there he spent the night without eating bread or drinking water, mourning over the unfaithfulness of the exiles.
A proclamation was made throughout Judah and Jerusalem that all the returning exiles were to gather at Jerusalem:
anyone who did not come within three days, according to the decision of the leaders and the elders, would have all his goods confiscated and would himself be excluded from the assembly of the exiles.

So all the men of Judah and Benjamin gathered at Jerusalem within the three days; it was the twentieth day of the ninth month. All the people sat in the square before the house of God, trembling because of the matter and because of the rains.
The priest Ezra rose and said to them, "You have been unfaithful by marrying foreign women, adding to the guilt of Israel.
Now give glory to the Lord, the God of your fathers, and do his will: separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign women."
The whole assembly answered with a loud voice, "Yes, we must do as you have said!
But the people are many, it is the rainy season, and we cannot stand outside; besides, this is not the work of a day or two, for we are many who have sinned in this matter.

Let our leaders act on behalf of the whole assembly; then, at appointed times, let all those in our towns who have married foreign women come, with the elders and judges of each town, until the fierce anger of our God is turned away from us in this affair."
Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah opposed this, backed by Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite.

The returning exiles did what had been decided. The priest Ezra and heads of families, all designated by name, set themselves apart and took their seats on the first day of the tenth month to examine the matter.
By the first day of the first month they had finished dealing with all the men who had married foreign women.
Among the sons of the priests, some were found who had married foreign women: of the sons of Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers, Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah;
they pledged to send away their wives and, acknowledging their guilt, to offer a ram for their sin.
Of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
Of the sons of Harim: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
Of the sons of Pashhur: Eliehoenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
Among the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (that is, Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
Among the singers: Eliashib. Among the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
Among the Israelites: of the sons of Parosh, Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah;
of the sons of Elam, Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah;
of the sons of Zattu, Eliehoenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza;
of the sons of Bebai, Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai;
of the sons of Bani, Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Ramoth;
of the sons of Pahath-Moab, Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh;
of the sons of Harim, Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Simeon,
Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah;
of the sons of Hashum, Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei;
of the sons of Bani, Maadai, Amram, Uel,
Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhi,
Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,
Mattaniah, Mattenai, Jaasu,
Bani, Binnui, Shimei,
Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah,
Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,
Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,
Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph;
of the sons of Nebo, Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.
All these had married foreign women, and some of them had had children by these women.
The words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev (around November-December), in the twentieth year, while I was in Susa, in the citadel,
Hanani, one of my brothers, arrived with some men from Judah. I questioned them about the Jews who had survived, those who had escaped captivity, and about Jerusalem.
They answered me: 'The survivors, those who escaped captivity, are back there in the province in great misery and disgrace; the walls of Jerusalem are broken down, and its gates have been burned.'
When I heard this, I sat down and wept; for several days I mourned, fasting and praying before the God of heaven.
I said: 'Ah, Lord, God of heaven, great and awesome God, you who keep the covenant and mercy toward those who love you and keep your commandments,

let your ear be attentive and your eyes open, to hear the prayer of your servant, which I now offer to you day and night for your servants, the sons of Israel. I confess the sins of the sons of Israel, those we have committed against you; I myself and my father's house, we have sinned.
We have acted very wickedly toward you: we have not kept the commandments, the laws, and the rules that you gave to Moses your servant.
Remember the word that you commanded Moses your servant to speak: If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the peoples;

but if you return to me, if you keep my commandments and put them into practice, then even if your exiles are at the ends of the heavens, from there I will gather them and bring them back to the place I have chosen to make my name dwell.
They are your servants and your people, whom you redeemed by your great power and your mighty hand.

Ah, Lord, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant and to the prayer of your servants who delight to fear your name! Grant success to your servant today, and let him find favor before this man!' At that time I was the king's cupbearer.

titres.titre: The night inspection of the walls

versets.t: In the month of Nisan (around March-April), in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, the wine was before him; I took it and offered it to him. I tried not to appear sad in his presence,
but the king said to me: 'Why is your face sad? You are not ill. This can only be sorrow of the heart.' I was seized with great fear,
and I answered the king: 'May the king live forever! How could my face not be sad, when the city where my ancestors are buried lies in ruins and its gates have been burned?'
The king said to me: 'What do you wish to ask?' I prayed to the God of heaven,
and I answered the king: 'If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor with you, send me to Judah, to the city where my ancestors are buried, so that I may rebuild it.'
The king, with the queen seated beside him, said to me: 'How long will your journey take, and when will you return?' It pleased the king to send me, and I set him a date.
Then I said to the king: 'If it pleases the king, let me be given letters for the governors of the province Beyond the River, so that they will let me pass through to Judah;

and a letter for Asaph, the keeper of the royal forest, so that he may supply me with timber for the beams of the gates of the fortress near the temple, for the city wall, and for the house where I will stay.' The king granted me these letters, for the gracious hand of my God was upon me.
So I went to the governors of the province Beyond the River and handed them the king's letters. The king had sent army officers and horsemen with me.
When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard of this, they were greatly displeased that someone had come to work for the good of the sons of Israel.
I arrived in Jerusalem and stayed there three days.
Then I got up in the night with a few men, without telling anyone what my God had put in my heart to do for Jerusalem. I had no animal with me except the one I was riding.
I went out by night through the Valley Gate, toward the Dragon's Spring and the Dung Gate, and I examined the broken-down walls of Jerusalem and its burned gates.
I went on toward the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, but there was no room for my mount to pass.
So I went up by night through the ravine, examining the wall; then I turned back, reentered through the Valley Gate, and returned to my lodging.

The officials did not know where I had gone or what I was planning, for until then I had said nothing to the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials, or the rest of those who would carry out the work.
Then I said to them: 'You see the trouble we are in: Jerusalem lies in ruins, its gates have been burned. Come, let us rebuild the wall of Jerusalem, so that we may no longer be in disgrace.'

I told them how the gracious hand of my God had been upon me, and the words the king had spoken to me. They replied: 'Let us rise up and build!' And they set their hands courageously to this good work.
When Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard of it, they mocked us with contempt: 'What is this you are doing? Are you rebelling against the king?'
I answered them: 'The God of heaven will grant us success. We, his servants, are going to start rebuilding; but you have no share, no right, and no memorial in Jerusalem.'

titres.titre: The mockery of Sanballat and Tobiah

versets.t: Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests set to work rebuilding the Sheep Gate; they consecrated it and set its doors in place, then they repaired the wall and consecrated it as far as the Tower of the Hundred and the Tower of Hananel.
Next to them the men of Jericho were building, and next to them, Zaccur son of Imri.
The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate; they laid its beams and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place.
Next to them Meremoth son of Uriah son of Hakkoz made repairs; next to him, Meshullam son of Berechiah son of Meshezabel; next to him, Zadok son of Baana;
next to them the people of Tekoa made repairs, but their nobles refused to put their shoulders to the work of their Lord.
Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate; they laid its beams and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place.
Next to them Melatiah the Gibeonite and Jadon the Meronothite made repairs, along with the men of Gibeon and Mizpah, under the jurisdiction of the governor of the province Beyond the River.
Next to them Uzziel son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs; next to him, Hananiah, one of the perfumers. They restored Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
Next to them Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.
Next to them Jedaiah son of Harumaph made repairs opposite his house; next to him, Hattush son of Hashabneiah.
Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath-Moab repaired another section, as well as the Tower of the Ovens.
Next to him Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of the other half of the district of Jerusalem, made repairs, together with his daughters.

Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate; they rebuilt it and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place, and they also built about four hundred and fifty meters of wall, as far as the Dung Gate.
Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem, repaired the Dung Gate; he rebuilt it and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place.

Shallun son of Col-hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate; he rebuilt it, roofed it, and set its doors, its bolts, and its bars in place. He also built the wall of the Pool of Siloam by the King's Garden, as far as the steps that go down from the City of David.

After him Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth-zur, made repairs as far as a point opposite the tombs of David, as far as the reservoir built there and the House of the Mighty Men.
After him the Levites made repairs under the direction of Rehum son of Bani; next to him, Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his district.
After him their brothers made repairs under the direction of Bavvai son of Henadad, ruler of the other half of the district of Keilah.
Next to him Ezer son of Joshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section, opposite the ascent to the armory, at the angle.
After him Baruch son of Zabbai zealously repaired another section, from the angle to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
After him Meremoth son of Uriah son of Hakkoz repaired another section, from the door of the house of Eliashib to the end of that house.
After him the priests, the men of the plain of the Jordan, made repairs.
After them Benjamin and Hasshub made repairs opposite their house. After them Azariah son of Maaseiah son of Ananiah made repairs beside his house.
After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from the house of Azariah to the angle and the corner.
Palal son of Uzai made repairs opposite the angle and the high tower that projects from the upper part of the king's house, near the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh,
and the temple servants living on the Ophel made repairs as far as a point opposite the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.
After him the people of Tekoa repaired another section, opposite the great projecting tower, as far as the wall of the Ophel.
Above the Horse Gate the priests made repairs, each one opposite his own house.
After them Zadok son of Immer made repairs opposite his house; after him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, keeper of the East Gate, made repairs.
After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun the sixth son of Zalaph repaired another section. After them Meshullam son of Berechiah made repairs opposite his dwelling.
After him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, made repairs as far as the house of the temple servants and the merchants, opposite the Muster Gate, and as far as the upper room at the corner.
And between the upper room at the corner and the Sheep Gate the goldsmiths and the merchants made repairs.
When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he flew into a great rage and, full of spite, mocked the Jews.

In front of his brothers and the soldiers of Samaria he said: 'What do these feeble Jews think they are doing? Will they be left to it? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Will they bring these stones back to life out of the heaps of rubble, burned as they are?'
Tobiah the Ammonite, at his side, added: 'Let them build all they like! If even a fox climbs up on it, he will break down their wall of stones.'
Hear, O our God, for we are despised! Turn their insults back on their own heads, and hand them over as plunder in a land of exile.
Do not cover their guilt, and let their sin not be blotted out before you, for they have flung defiance at the builders.
Yet we rebuilt the wall, and the whole circuit was joined together to half its height, for the people had a mind to work.

titres.titre: One hand on the work, the other on a weapon

versets.t: When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people of Ashdod heard that the repair of the walls was advancing and that the gaps were beginning to close, they flew into a great fury.
They all plotted together to come and attack Jerusalem and throw it into confusion.
So we prayed to our God, and we set a guard against them day and night to protect ourselves.
Meanwhile, in Judah, people were saying: 'The strength of the carriers is failing, and there is too much rubble; we will not be able to rebuild the wall.'
And our enemies were saying: 'They will know nothing, they will see nothing, until we come into their midst; then we will slaughter them and put a stop to the work.'
The Jews who lived near them came and warned us ten times over that from every side our adversaries were coming up against us.
So I stationed the people by families at the lowest spots behind the wall, in the exposed places, all of them with their swords, their spears, and their bows.

After inspecting everything, I stood up and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people: 'Do not be afraid of them! Remember the Lord, great and awesome, and fight for your brothers, your sons and daughters, your wives and your homes!'
When our enemies heard that we had been warned and that God had thwarted their plan, we all returned to the wall, each to his own work.
But from that day on, half of my men did the work, while the other half held the spears, the shields, the bows, and the breastplates; and the leaders stood behind the whole house of Judah.
Among those who were building the wall, the laborers who carried burdens worked with one hand on the work and held a weapon with the other;
and each of the builders had his sword strapped at his side as he built. The trumpeter stood beside me.
I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people: 'The work is vast and spread out, and we are scattered along the wall, far from one another.
Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, rally to us there: our God will fight for us.'
So we carried on the work, half of us holding the spears, from the break of dawn until the stars came out.
At that time I also said to the people: 'Let each man, with his servant, spend the night inside Jerusalem: they will serve as our guard by night and our workforce by day.'
And none of us, neither I, nor my brothers, nor my men, nor the guards who followed me, took off our clothes; each one removed them only for washing.
