There arose a great outcry from the common people and their wives against their fellow Jews.
Some were saying: 'We are many, we, our sons and our daughters; let us be given grain to eat and stay alive.'
Others were saying: 'We are having to pledge our fields, our vineyards, and our houses to get grain during the famine.'
Still others were saying: 'To pay the king's tax, we have borrowed money against our fields and our vineyards.

And yet we are of the same flesh as our brothers, our children are as good as theirs; and now we must hand over our sons and daughters into slavery, and some of our daughters are already enslaved, and we can do nothing about it, for our fields and vineyards belong to others.'
I was filled with indignation when I heard their outcry and these words.
After thinking it over within myself, I reproached the nobles and the officials: 'You are lending at interest, each to his own brother!' And I called a great assembly against them.

I said to them: 'As far as we could, we have bought back our fellow Jews who had been sold to the nations; and now you yourselves would sell your own brothers, so that they have to be bought back by us!' They were silent, finding nothing to say.
I went on: 'What you are doing is not right. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, to escape the taunts of the nations, our enemies?
I too, along with my brothers and my servants, have lent them money and grain. Let us give up this debt.

Give them back this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves, and their houses, and remit the hundredth part of the money, the grain, the new wine, and the oil that you have exacted from them as interest.'
They replied: 'We will give it all back, and we will demand nothing more from them; we will do as you say.' Then I called the priests and made them swear to act according to this promise.

Then I shook out the fold of my cloak, saying: 'So may God shake out of his house and his possessions every man who does not keep this promise; may he be shaken out like this and left empty!' The whole assembly answered: 'Amen!' and they praised the Lord; and the people acted according to this promise.

Moreover, from the day the king appointed me governor of the land of Judah, that is, from the twentieth to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, for twelve years, neither I nor my brothers ate the food allowance of the governor.

The former governors, my predecessors, laid heavy burdens on the people: they took from them food and wine, besides forty pieces of silver; even their servants oppressed the people. But I did not act this way, out of the fear of God.
I even devoted myself to the work on this wall; we bought no land, and all my men were there, gathered for the work.
At my table I had a hundred and fifty men, Jews and officials, besides those who came to us from the surrounding nations.

Here is what was prepared each day at my expense: one ox, six choice sheep, and poultry; and every ten days, wine in abundance. Even so, I never claimed the food allowance of the governor, for the work already lay heavily on this people.
Remember for my good, O my God, all that I have done for this people!
When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and that not a gap was left in it, though I had not yet set the doors in the gates,
Sanballat and Geshem sent word to me: 'Come, let us meet together in one of the villages on the plain of Ono.' But they were plotting to do me harm.
I sent messengers to answer them: 'I am carrying out a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it to come down to you?'
They sent me the same proposal four times, and each time I gave them the same answer.
A fifth time Sanballat sent me his servant in the same way, with an open letter in his hand.

In it was written: 'It is reported among the nations, and Geshem affirms it, that you and the Jews are planning a revolt, and that this is why you are rebuilding the wall; according to these rumors, you mean to become their king.
You are even said to have appointed prophets to proclaim about you in Jerusalem: There is a king in Judah! Now the king will hear of all this. So come, and let us take counsel together.'
I sent back this reply: 'Nothing that you say has happened: you are inventing it out of your own heart.'
For they were all trying to frighten us, thinking: 'Their hands will grow slack and drop the work, and it will never be finished.' Now, O my God, strengthen my hands!

I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah son of Mehetabel, who had shut himself in. He said to me: 'Let us meet together in the house of God, inside the temple, and let us close its doors; for they are coming to kill you, and it is by night that they will come to kill you.'
I answered: 'Should a man like me run away? And how could a man like me go into the temple to save his life? I will not go in.'
Then I realized that God had not sent him: he had pronounced this prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
He had been paid to frighten me, to make me act in this way and sin, which would have given them grounds to give me a bad name and cover me with shame.
Remember, O my God, Tobiah and Sanballat, for these deeds! Remember too the prophetess Noadiah and the other prophets who tried to frighten me.
The wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul (around August-September), in fifty-two days.
When all our enemies heard of it, all the surrounding nations were seized with fear: they felt humbled and recognized that this work had been accomplished with the help of our God.
In those days too, the nobles of Judah kept sending many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah kept answering them.
For many in Judah were bound to him by oath: he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
In my presence they even sang his praises, and they reported my words to him. And Tobiah kept sending letters to frighten me.

titres.titre: The census of the first returnees

versets.t: When the wall had been rebuilt and I had set the doors in the gates, the gatekeepers, the singers, and the Levites were appointed for oversight.
I put my brother Hanani and Hananiah the commander of the citadel in charge of Jerusalem, for he was a faithful man who feared God more than many others.

I said to them: 'The gates of Jerusalem are not to be opened until the sun grows hot; and in the evening, while the guards are still at their posts, let the doors be shut and the bars put up. Appoint guards as well from among the inhabitants of Jerusalem, each at his post, each in front of his own house.'
The city was wide and large, but its population was sparse, and the houses had not yet been rebuilt.

My God put it in my heart to gather the nobles, the officials, and the people, to register them by families. I found the genealogical record of those who had returned first, and I read in it the following:
These are the people of the province who came back from exile, those whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported and who returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his own town.
They returned with Zerubbabel, Joshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. This is the number of the men of the people of Israel:
the sons of Parosh: two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;
the sons of Shephatiah: three hundred and seventy-two;
the sons of Arah: six hundred and fifty-two;
the sons of Pahath-Moab, of the line of Joshua and Joab: two thousand eight hundred and eighteen;
the sons of Elam: one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the sons of Zattu: eight hundred and forty-five;
the sons of Zaccai: seven hundred and sixty;
the sons of Binnui: six hundred and forty-eight;
the sons of Bebai: six hundred and twenty-eight;
the sons of Azgad: two thousand three hundred and twenty-two;
the sons of Adonikam: six hundred and sixty-seven;
the sons of Bigvai: two thousand and sixty-seven;
the sons of Adin: six hundred and fifty-five;
the sons of Ater, namely of the family of Hezekiah: ninety-eight;
the sons of Hashum: three hundred and twenty-eight;
the sons of Bezai: three hundred and twenty-four;
the sons of Hariph: one hundred and twelve;
the sons of Gibeon: ninety-five;
the men of Bethlehem and Netophah: one hundred and eighty-eight;
the men of Anathoth: one hundred and twenty-eight;
the men of Beth-azmaveth: forty-two;
the men of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth: seven hundred and forty-three;
the men of Ramah and Geba: six hundred and twenty-one;
the men of Michmas: one hundred and twenty-two;
the men of Bethel and Ai: one hundred and twenty-three;
the men of the other Nebo: fifty-two;
the sons of the other Elam: one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
the sons of Harim: three hundred and twenty;
the men of Jericho: three hundred and forty-five;
the men of Lod, Hadid, and Ono: seven hundred and twenty-one;
the sons of Senaah: three thousand nine hundred and thirty.
The priests: the sons of Jedaiah, of the house of Joshua: nine hundred and seventy-three;
the sons of Immer: one thousand and fifty-two;
the sons of Pashhur: one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;
the sons of Harim: one thousand and seventeen.
The Levites: the sons of Joshua and Kadmiel, of the family of Hodevah: seventy-four.
The singers: the sons of Asaph: one hundred and forty-eight.
The gatekeepers: the sons of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai: one hundred and thirty-eight.
The temple servants were the sons of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,
Keros, Sia, Padon,
Lebana, Hagaba, Shalmai,
Hanan, Giddel, Gahar,
Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda,
Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah,
Besai, Meunim, Nephushesim,
Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur,
Bazlith, Mehida, Harsha,
Barkos, Sisera, Temah,
Neziah, and Hatipha.
The sons of Solomon's servants: the sons of Sotai, Sophereth, Perida,
Jaala, Darkon, Giddel,
Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth-hazzebaim, and Amon.
In all, the temple servants and the sons of Solomon's servants were three hundred and ninety-two.
The following are those who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, but who could not prove that their families and their ancestry were truly of Israel:
the sons of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda: six hundred and forty-two.
And among the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai, the one who had married one of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and had taken their name.
They searched for their registration in the genealogies, but it could not be found; so they were excluded from the priesthood as unclean,
and the governor forbade them to eat the most holy food, until a priest should arise to consult God by the Urim and Thummim.
The whole assembly numbered forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty persons,
besides their male and female servants, who numbered seven thousand three hundred and thirty-seven; there were also two hundred and forty-five male and female singers.
They had seven hundred and thirty-six horses, two hundred and forty-five mules,
four hundred and thirty-five camels, and six thousand seven hundred and twenty donkeys.
Some of the heads of families contributed to the work. The governor gave to the treasury a thousand pieces of gold, fifty basins, and five hundred and thirty priestly garments.
Some of the heads of families gave to the treasury of the work twenty thousand pieces of gold and about one ton and one hundred kilograms of silver.
And the rest of the people gave twenty thousand pieces of gold, about one ton of silver, and sixty-seven priestly garments.
So the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel settled in their towns.

titres.titre: The solemn reading of the Law

versets.t: When the seventh month came (around September-October), the sons of Israel being settled in their towns, all the people gathered as one man on the square in front of the Water Gate. They asked Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the Lord had commanded Israel.
On the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brought the Law before the assembly: the men, the women, and all who were able to understand.

On the square in front of the Water Gate he read from it from daybreak until noon, before the men, the women, and all who could understand; and all the people listened attentively to the book of the Law.

Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform that had been made for the occasion. At his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah; at his left, Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people, for he stood above the assembly; and as he opened it, all the people rose to their feet.
Ezra blessed the Lord, the great God, and all the people, lifting up their hands, answered: 'Amen! Amen!' Then they bowed down and worshiped the Lord with their faces to the ground.
Joshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the other Levites explained the Law to the people, who remained in their places.
They read distinctly from the book of the law of God and gave its meaning, so that the people understood the reading.

Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who were instructing the people said to them all: 'This day is holy to the Lord your God; do not mourn or weep!' For all the people were weeping as they heard the words of the Law.

Nehemiah added: 'Go, eat rich food, drink sweet drinks, and send portions to those who have nothing prepared, for this day is holy to our Lord. Do not be grieved: the joy of the Lord is your strength!'
The Levites calmed all the people, saying: 'Be still, for this day is holy. Do not be grieved!'
And all the people went away to eat and drink, to send portions and to rejoice greatly, because they had understood the words that had been made known to them.
On the second day, the heads of families of all the people, with the priests and the Levites, gathered around Ezra the scribe to study more deeply the words of the Law.
They found written in the Law, which the Lord had given through Moses, that the sons of Israel were to dwell in booths during the feast of the seventh month (around September-October),

and that they were to make this proclamation heard in all their towns and in Jerusalem: 'Go out to the hills and bring back branches of olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm, and leafy trees, to make booths, as it is written.'

The people went out, brought back branches, and made themselves booths, each on his own roof, in their courtyards, in the courts of the house of God, on the square by the Water Gate, and on the square by the Gate of Ephraim.

The whole assembly of those who had returned from exile made booths and lived in them. From the days of Joshua son of Nun until that day, the sons of Israel had done nothing like it. And the joy was very great.
Each day, from the first to the last, they read from the book of the law of God. They kept the feast for seven days, and on the eighth day there was the solemn assembly, according to the rule.

titres.titre: The people fast and confess their sins
The great prayer: the Creator and Deliverer God
Israel's rebellions and the present distress

versets.t: On the twenty-fourth day of that month, the sons of Israel gathered for a fast, dressed in sackcloth and covered with dust.
Those of the race of Israel separated themselves from all the sons of foreigners; standing, they confessed their sins and the iniquities of their fathers.

Standing in their places, they read from the book of the law of the Lord their God for a quarter of the day; and for another quarter they confessed their sins and bowed down before the Lord their God.
On the platform of the Levites stood Joshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani, who cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God.

Then the Levites Joshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said: 'Rise up, bless the Lord your God from everlasting to everlasting! Let them bless your glorious name, which surpasses all blessing and praise!

You alone are the Lord. You made the heavens, the highest heavens and all their host, the earth and all it bears, the seas and all they contain. To all these you give life, and the host of heaven bows down before you.
You are the Lord, the God who chose Abram, who brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans, and who gave him the name Abraham.

You found his heart faithful before you, and you made a covenant with him: to give to his descendants the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, and the Girgashites. And you kept your word, for you are righteous.
You saw the misery of our fathers in Egypt, you heard their cry at the shore of the Red Sea.

You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, against all his servants and all the people of his land, for you knew with what arrogance they treated them; and you made yourself a name that endures to this day.
You split the sea before them, and they crossed on dry ground; but those who pursued them you cast into the depths, like a stone into the mighty waters.
By day you led them by a pillar of cloud; by night by a pillar of fire, to light the road they were to follow.
You came down on Mount Sinai, you spoke to them from heaven, and you gave them just decisions, true laws, and excellent precepts and commandments.
You made known to them your holy sabbath, and you prescribed for them, through Moses your servant, commandments, precepts, and a law.
For their hunger you gave them bread from heaven; for their thirst you brought water out of the rock. And you told them to go in and take possession of the land you had sworn to give them.
But they, our fathers, grew proud, stiffened their necks, and did not listen to your commandments.

They refused to obey, forgot the wonders you had done for them, stiffened their necks, and in their rebellion appointed a leader to return to their slavery. But you are a God of forgiveness, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and rich in faithful love: you did not abandon them.
Even when they made themselves a molten calf and proclaimed: This is your God, who brought you out of Egypt, and grievously insulted you,

you, in your great mercy, did not abandon them in the wilderness: the pillar of cloud did not leave them, guiding them by day on their way, nor the pillar of fire, lighting for them by night the road they were to follow.
You gave them your good spirit to make them wise; you did not withhold your manna from their mouths, and you gave them water for their thirst.
For forty years you provided for their needs in the wilderness: they lacked nothing, their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
You handed over to them kingdoms and peoples, and you allotted them their territories; they possessed the land of Sihon king of Heshbon and the land of Og king of Bashan.
You multiplied their sons like the stars of heaven, and you led them into the land you had promised their fathers they would enter and possess.

Their sons went in and took possession of it. Before them you subdued the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and you handed them over, with their kings and the peoples of the land, to do with them as they wished.

They captured fortified cities and a fertile land; they took possession of houses full of all kinds of goods, cisterns already dug, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. They ate and were satisfied, grew fat, and lived in delight, through your great goodness.
And yet they rebelled and revolted against you. They cast your law behind their backs, killed your prophets who warned them to turn them back to you, and committed great blasphemies.

So you handed them over to their oppressors, who afflicted them. But in the time of their distress they cried out to you, and you, from heaven, heard them; in your great mercy you gave them saviors who rescued them from the hand of their oppressors.

But once they had rest, they went back to doing evil before you. Then you abandoned them to the hand of their enemies, who ruled over them. Again they cried out to you, and you, from heaven, heard them and rescued them many times, in your mercy.

You warned them to bring them back to your law; but they, full of pride, did not listen to your commandments. They sinned against your decisions, those that give life to whoever practices them; they turned a rebellious shoulder, stiffened their necks, and would not listen.
For many long years you bore with them patiently; you warned them by your spirit, through the mouth of your prophets, but they did not listen. So you handed them over to the hand of foreign peoples.
But in your great mercy you did not destroy them or abandon them, for you are a gracious and compassionate God.

And now, our God, great, mighty, and awesome God, you who keep the covenant and faithful love, do not treat as a small thing all the hardships that have come upon us, upon our kings, our leaders, our priests, our prophets, our fathers, and all your people, from the time of the kings of Assyria until this day.
In all that has come upon us you have been righteous: you have acted faithfully, while we have done evil.
Our kings, our leaders, our priests, and our fathers did not put your law into practice; they paid no attention to your commandments or to the warnings you gave them.
In their kingdom, filled with the many blessings you granted them, in this vast and fertile land you had given them, they did not serve you and did not turn away from their evil deeds.
And here we are today, slaves! Slaves in the land you had given our fathers to eat its fruit and enjoy its goods!
Its rich harvests go to the kings you have set over us because of our sins. They do as they please with our persons and our livestock, and we are in great distress.'

titres.titre: The sealed agreement and its signatories

versets.t: In view of all this, we made a firm agreement, which we put in writing; and our leaders, our Levites, and our priests set their seal to it.
These are those who set their seal to it: Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah.
Zedekiah, Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah,
Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah,
Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,
Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,
Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,
Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,
Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah: these were the priests.
The Levites: Joshua son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel,
and their brothers Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,
Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.
The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,
Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,
Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,
Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,
Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai,
Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,
Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,
Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,
Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,
Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,
Ahiah, Hanan, Anan,
Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.

The rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the temple servants, and all those who had separated themselves from the peoples of the other lands to follow the law of God, together with their wives, their sons, and their daughters, all who were able to understand,

joined their brothers and their nobles. Under penalty of a curse and by oath, they bound themselves to follow the law of God, given through Moses the servant of God, and to observe and put into practice all the commandments of the Lord our God, his decisions, and his laws.
In particular: we would not give our daughters to the peoples of the land or take their daughters for our sons;

if these peoples brought merchandise or grain to sell on the sabbath day, we would buy nothing from them on that day or on the other holy days; in the seventh year we would let the land rest and would cancel every debt.
We took upon ourselves the duty of giving each year about four grams of silver for the service of the house of our God:

for the bread of the Presence, for the perpetual grain offering and burnt offering, for the sacrifices of the sabbaths, the new moons, and the feasts, for the holy offerings, for the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and for all the service of the house of our God.

We also cast lots, priests, Levites, and people, for the offering of wood: each family was to bring it in turn to the house of our God, at fixed times, year after year, to burn on the altar of the Lord our God, as it is written in the Law.
We committed ourselves to bring each year to the house of the Lord the first produce of our soil and the first fruits of all our trees;
to present at the house of our God, to the priests who serve there, the firstborn of our sons and of our livestock, as it is written in the Law, as well as the firstborn of our cattle and our flocks;

to bring to the priests, in the chambers of the house of our God, the best of our dough, our offerings, the fruit of all our trees, the new wine and the oil; and to deliver to the Levites the tithe of our soil, for it is the Levites who collect the tithe in all the towns where we work the land.
A priest, a son of Aaron, will accompany the Levites when they collect the tithe; and the Levites will bring the tithe of the tithe to the house of our God, into the chambers of the treasury.

For the sons of Israel and the Levites will bring into these chambers the offering of grain, new wine, and oil; there are kept the vessels of the sanctuary, the priests who serve, the gatekeepers, and the singers. So we will not neglect the house of our God.

titres.titre: The other towns of Judah and Benjamin

versets.t: The leaders of the people settled in Jerusalem. The rest of the people cast lots to bring one in ten to settle in Jerusalem, the holy city, while the other nine remained in the other towns.
And the people blessed all those who freely offered to live in Jerusalem.

These are the chiefs of the province who settled in Jerusalem. In the towns of Judah, each lived on his own property, in his own town: Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants, and the sons of Solomon's servants.

In Jerusalem there settled some of the sons of Judah and some of the sons of Benjamin. Among the sons of Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah son of Zechariah son of Amariah son of Shephatiah son of Mahalalel, of the line of Perez;
and Maaseiah son of Baruch son of Col-hozeh son of Hazaiah son of Adaiah son of Joiarib son of Zechariah son of Shelah.
The sons of Perez who settled in Jerusalem numbered four hundred and sixty-eight valiant men.
These are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam son of Joed son of Pedaiah son of Kolaiah son of Maaseiah son of Ithiel son of Jeshaiah;
and after him Gabbai and Sallai: nine hundred and twenty-eight.
Joel son of Zichri was their chief, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command over the city.
Among the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jachin,
Seraiah son of Hilkiah son of Meshullam son of Zadok son of Meraioth son of Ahitub, the chief of the house of God,
and their brothers who carried out the service of the house: eight hundred and twenty-two; then Adaiah son of Jeroham son of Pelaliah son of Amzi son of Zechariah son of Pashhur son of Malchijah,
and his brothers, heads of families: two hundred and forty-two; then Amashsai son of Azarel son of Ahzai son of Meshillemoth son of Immer,
and their brothers, valiant men: one hundred and twenty-eight. Their chief was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.
Among the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub son of Azrikam son of Hashabiah son of Bunni;
Shabbethai and Jozabad, in charge of the external affairs of the house of God, among the chiefs of the Levites;
Mattaniah son of Mica son of Zabdi son of Asaph, who led the song of praise at prayer; Bakbukiah, second among his brothers; and Abda son of Shammua son of Galal son of Jeduthun.
In all, the Levites in the holy city were two hundred and eighty-four.
The gatekeepers, Akkub, Talmon, and their brothers, who guarded the gates, were one hundred and seventy-two.
The rest of Israel, the priests, and the Levites lived in all the towns of Judah, each on his own estate.
The temple servants lived on the hill of the Ophel; Ziha and Gishpa were at their head.
The chief of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani son of Hashabiah son of Mattaniah son of Mica, of the line of Asaph, the singers in charge of the service of the house of God.
There was a royal order concerning them, fixing a daily allowance for the singers.
Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, of the line of Zerah son of Judah, was the king's deputy for all the affairs of the people.
As for the villages and their lands, some of the sons of Judah settled in Kiriath-arba and its dependencies, in Dibon and its dependencies, in Jekabzeel and its villages,
in Jeshua, Moladah, Beth-pelet,
Hazar-shual, Beersheba and its dependencies,
Ziklag, Meconah and its dependencies,
En-rimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth,
Zanoah, Adullam and their villages, Lachish and its lands, Azekah and its dependencies. So they settled from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom.
Some of the sons of Benjamin settled from Geba onward: at Michmash, Aija, Bethel and its dependencies,
Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
Lod and Ono, in the valley of the craftsmen.
Some groups of Levites, attached to Judah, were joined to Benjamin.

titres.titre: The priests and Levites of the return
The line of the high priests

versets.t: These are the priests and Levites who returned with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and with Joshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. These were the chiefs of the priests and of their brothers in the days of Joshua.
The Levites: Joshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah, this last being in charge, with his brothers, of the song of praise;
Bakbukiah and Unni, their brothers, formed the choir that answered them.
Joshua fathered Joiakim; Joiakim fathered Eliashib; Eliashib fathered Joiada;
Joiada fathered Jonathan; and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.
In the days of Joiakim, these were the priests, heads of families: for Seraiah, Meraiah; for Jeremiah, Hananiah;
for Ezra, Meshullam; for Amariah, Jehohanan;
for Malluchi, Jonathan; for Shebaniah, Joseph;
for Harim, Adna; for Meraioth, Helkai;
for Iddo, Zechariah; for Ginnethon, Meshullam;
for Abijah, Zichri; for Miniamin and Moadiah, Piltai;
for Bilgah, Shammua; for Shemaiah, Jonathan;
for Joiarib, Mattenai; for Jedaiah, Uzzi;
for Sallai, Kallai; for Amok, Eber;
for Hilkiah, Hashabiah; for Jedaiah, Nethanel.
In the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, the Levites were recorded as heads of families, as were the priests, during the reign of Darius the Persian.
The sons of Levi, heads of families, were recorded in the Book of the Chronicles, up to the time of Johanan son of Eliashib.

The chiefs of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Joshua son of Kadmiel; with their brothers facing them, they praised and gave thanks to God, according to the command of David the man of God, one group answering the other.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers; they kept watch over the storehouses at the gates.
They lived in the days of Joiakim son of Joshua son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and of Ezra, the priest and scribe.

For the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem, the Levites were brought from wherever they lived, to celebrate the dedication with joy, with thanksgiving and songs, to the sound of cymbals, harps, and lyres.
The singers gathered from the countryside around Jerusalem, from the villages of the Netophathites,
from Beth-gilgal and the lands of Geba and Azmaveth, for the singers had built themselves villages around Jerusalem.
The priests and the Levites purified themselves, and then they purified the people, the gates, and the wall.
I brought the leaders of Judah up onto the wall and formed two great processional choirs. The first went to the right, along the wall, toward the Dung Gate.
Behind it walked Hoshaiah and half the leaders of Judah,
with Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah;
then some priests with trumpets: Zechariah son of Jonathan son of Shemaiah son of Mattaniah son of Micaiah son of Zaccur son of Asaph,
and his brothers Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God. Ezra the scribe walked at their head.
At the Fountain Gate, straight ahead of them, they went up the steps of the City of David, by the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, as far as the Water Gate on the east.
The second choir went in the opposite direction; I followed it, with half the people, along the wall, above the Tower of the Ovens as far as the Broad Wall,
then above the Gate of Ephraim, the Old Gate, the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate; they halted at the Gate of the Guard.
The two choirs took their places in the house of God, as did I and half the officials who accompanied me,
with the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with trumpets,
and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. The singers made their songs ring out, under the direction of Jezrahiah.
That day they offered great sacrifices and rejoiced, for God had given the people great joy. The women and children rejoiced too, and the joy of Jerusalem was heard far away.

At that time men were appointed to watch over the chambers that served as storehouses for the offerings, the first produce, and the tithes: they were to gather into them, from the lands of the towns, the portions that the Law assigns to the priests and the Levites. For Judah rejoiced to see the priests and the Levites at their posts,
carrying out the service of their God and the service of the purifications, as did the singers and the gatekeepers, according to the command of David and his son Solomon.
For long ago, in the days of David and Asaph, there was a chief of the singers and of the songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.

In the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, all Israel gave day by day the portions of the singers and the gatekeepers; they set aside the holy offerings for the Levites, and the Levites set aside a portion for the sons of Aaron.

titres.titre: The exclusion of foreigners from the assembly

versets.t: At that time the book of Moses was read to the people, and in it was found written that the Ammonite and the Moabite were never to enter the assembly of God,
because they had not come to meet the sons of Israel with bread and water, and had hired Balaam to curse them; but our God had turned the curse into a blessing.
On hearing this law, they separated from Israel all those of mixed descent.
Now before this, the priest Eliashib, who was in charge of the chambers of the house of our God and a close relative of Tobiah,

had fitted out for him a large chamber where formerly they used to store the offerings, the incense, the vessels, and the tithe of grain, new wine, and oil prescribed for the Levites, the singers, and the gatekeepers, as well as the priests' portion.
At that time I was not in Jerusalem: in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had gone back to the king. Some time later I asked his permission
to return to Jerusalem. There I discovered the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, in fitting out a chamber for him in the courts of the house of God.
I was deeply grieved, and I threw all Tobiah's furniture out of the chamber.
Then I ordered the chambers to be purified, and I put back in them the vessels of the house of God, the offerings, and the incense.
I also learned that the portions of the Levites had not been given, and that the Levites and the singers who carried out the service had each gone back to his own land.
I reproached the officials and said to them: 'Why is the house of God neglected?' Then I gathered the Levites and the singers and restored them to their posts.
Then all Judah brought the tithe of grain, new wine, and oil into the storehouses.

I put in charge of the storehouses the priest Shelemiah, the scribe Zadok, and Pedaiah, one of the Levites; and I assigned to them Hanan son of Zaccur son of Mattaniah, for they were considered faithful. Their task was to make the distributions to their brothers.
Remember me for this, my God, and do not blot out the acts of faithfulness I have performed for the house of my God and for its service!

In those days I saw in Judah people treading the winepress on the sabbath day, bringing in sheaves, loading donkeys with wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of burdens, and bringing them to Jerusalem on the sabbath day. I warned them on the day they were selling these goods.
Some Tyrians settled in the city were bringing in fish and all kinds of merchandise and selling them on the sabbath day to the sons of Judah, even in Jerusalem.
I reproached the nobles of Judah and said to them: 'What is this evil you are doing? You are profaning the sabbath day!

Is this not just what your fathers did, and is it not for this that our God brought all these calamities on us and on this city? And now you are bringing still more wrath on Israel by profaning the sabbath!'

So, as soon as the gates of Jerusalem grew dark at the approach of the sabbath, I ordered the doors to be shut, and I forbade them to be reopened until the sabbath was over. I also stationed some of my men at the gates, so that no burden might come in on the sabbath day.
Once or twice the merchants and sellers of all kinds of goods spent the night outside Jerusalem.
I warned them in these terms: 'Why do you spend the night in front of the wall? If you do it again, I will lay hands on you.' From then on, they no longer came on the sabbath day.

Then I ordered the Levites to purify themselves and come to guard the gates, to keep the sabbath day holy. For this too, remember me, my God, and have pity on me according to your great faithful love!
In those days I also saw Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, or the language of one people or another, and no longer knew how to speak the language of Judah.

I reproached them and cursed them; I struck some of them, pulled out their hair, and made them swear in the name of God: 'You shall not give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.

Was it not over this that Solomon king of Israel sinned? Among so many nations there was no king like him: he was loved by his God, who had made him king over all Israel; and yet even he was led into sin by foreign women.
Must we then hear that you are committing this great evil and betraying our God by marrying foreign women?'
One of the sons of Joiada son of the high priest Eliashib was the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite: I drove him away from me.
Remember them, my God, for they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priests and the Levites!
So I purified them from everything foreign. I fixed the duties of the priests and the Levites, each in his own service,
and I arranged for the offering of wood at the appointed times, and for the first produce. Remember me, my God: show me favor!
Tobit was of the tribe of Naphtali, from a town in upper Galilee, above Naasson, to the west, with the town of Sephet on his left.
He was carried off into captivity in the days of Shalmaneser, king of Assyria; yet even in exile he did not abandon the way of truth.
I, Tobit, shared each day whatever I could with my kinsmen, those of my people who had been carried into captivity along with me.
Though I was the youngest of the tribe of Naphtali, there was nothing childish in my conduct.
While everyone else went to worship the golden calves that Jeroboam, king of Israel, had made, I alone kept away from that crowd;
I would go up to Jerusalem, to the temple of the Lord, to worship there the Lord, the God of Israel, faithfully offering the firstfruits and the tithes of my goods.
Every three years I gave the whole of my tithe to the foreigners and the newcomers.
I kept these rules, and many others, according to the law of God, from my youth.
When I came of age, I married a woman of my own tribe named Anna; by her I had a son, whom I named Tobias, after my own name,
and whom I trained from childhood to fear God and to keep away from every sin.
Carried off as a captive to Nineveh with my wife and my son, where my whole tribe was,
while all the others ate the food of the pagans, I kept my soul pure and never defiled myself with their meats.
Because I remembered the Lord faithfully, God granted me favor in the eyes of King Shalmaneser,
who let me go wherever I wished and do whatever I pleased.
So I would go and visit all the captives and give them wise counsel.
One day I went to Rages, a city of Media, carrying ten bags of silver that the king's generosity had allowed me to set aside.
There, among my many countrymen, I saw a man of my own tribe named Gabael, who was in need, and I entrusted this sum to him against a receipt.
Long afterward, King Shalmaneser died, and his son Sennacherib reigned in his place. Since this prince deeply hated the sons of Israel,
each day I went to visit those of my kindred; I consoled them and shared my goods with each, according to my means;
I fed those who were hungry, I clothed those who were naked, and I took great care to bury the dead and those who had been killed.

When King Sennacherib, having fled back from Judea after the defeat with which God had struck him for his blasphemies, put a great number of the sons of Israel to death in his fury, I buried their bodies.
The king learned of it and ordered me to be put to death, and he stripped me of all my goods.
But I fled with my son and my wife; destitute of everything, I managed to hide, for I had many friends.
Forty-five days later, the king was killed by his own sons.
Then I returned home, and all my goods were restored to me.

titres.titre: The kid goat and Anna's taunt

versets.t: Some time later, on a feast day of the Lord, a great meal was prepared in my house.
I said to my son, "Go and bring some men of our tribe who fear God, so that they may eat with us."
My son went out; on his return he announced that a son of Israel had been murdered and was lying in the street. At once I rose from the table, left the meal untouched, and went to the dead man.
I took him up, carried him quietly to my house, to bury him carefully after sunset.
Once the body was hidden, I ate my meal in tears and trembling,
remembering the word that the Lord had spoken through the prophet Amos: "Your feast days will be turned into mourning and lamentation."
Then, when the sun had set, I went out and laid the body in the ground.
All my neighbors reproached me: "You were already sentenced to death for this, and scarcely have you escaped the sentence than you take up burying the dead again!"
But I, who feared God more than the king, went on removing the bodies of the victims, hiding them in my house, and burying them by night.
One day, when I had worn myself out burying the dead, I came home, lay down at the foot of the wall, and fell asleep.
While I slept, warm droppings fell from a swallows' nest onto my eyes, and I became blind.
God allowed this trial so that my patience, like that of the holy man Job, might serve as an example to the generations to come.
For, having always feared God from my childhood and kept his commandments, I did not complain against God about the trial that had struck me,
but I remained steadfast in the fear of God, giving him thanks every day of my life.
As the powerful had insulted the blessed Job, so my relatives and friends mocked my way of life, saying:
"What has become of your hope, for which you gave alms and buried the dead?"
I would rebuke them: "Do not speak like that;
for we are the children of the saints, and we look for that life which God will give to those who never withdraw their faithfulness from him."
Anna, my wife, went out each day to weave cloth, and by the work of her hands she brought home our living.
One day she received a young goat and brought it home.
Hearing the goat bleat, I said, "See whether this goat may have been stolen, and give it back to its owner; we are not allowed to eat, or even to touch, anything that comes from a theft."
My wife answered angrily, "It is plain that your hope was empty: see what your almsgiving has brought you!"
With these words and others like them she overwhelmed me.
Then I heaved a sigh and began to pray in tears.
I said: "You are just, O Lord; just are all your judgments, and all your ways are mercy, truth, and justice.
And now, Lord, remember me; do not take vengeance for my sins, do not call to mind my faults or those of my ancestors.
For we have not obeyed your commandments; therefore we have been handed over to plunder, to captivity, and to death, made the byword and the shame of the nations among which you have scattered us.
And now, Lord, your chastisements are just, for we have not acted according to your commandments nor walked sincerely before you.
And now, Lord, deal with me according to your will, and command that my spirit be received in peace; for it is better for me to die than to live."
That same day, at Ecbatana, a city of Media, Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, also heard the insults of one of her father's servants.
For she had been given in turn to seven husbands, and a demon named Asmodeus had killed them as soon as they approached her.
When Sarah rebuked this servant for a fault, the girl answered her, "May we never see son or daughter of yours on the earth, you murderer of your husbands!

Do you mean to kill me too, as you have already killed seven husbands?" At these words Sarah went up to the upper room of her house and stayed there three days and three nights, without eating or drinking.
But, persevering in prayer, she begged God, weeping, to deliver her from this disgrace.
On the third day she finished her prayer and blessed the Lord.
She said: "Blessed be your name, O God of our fathers! Even in your anger you show mercy, and in the time of distress you forgive the sins of those who call upon you.
To you, Lord, I turn my face; to you I lift up my eyes.
I ask you, Lord, to release me from the bonds of this disgrace, or else to take me away from this earth.
You know, Lord, that I have never desired a husband, and that I have kept my soul pure from all lust.
Never have I joined in frivolous amusements or kept company with men of loose life.
It was in fear of you, and not to follow my passion, that I consented to take a husband.
Either I was not worthy of them, or they were not worthy of me; perhaps you have kept me for another husband.
Man cannot penetrate your designs.

But whoever honors you holds this for certain: that his life, if it has been tested, will be rewarded; if he has known distress, he will be delivered; and if chastisement has come upon him, he will be able to obtain your mercy.
For you do not take pleasure in our ruin: after the storm you bring back the calm, and after tears and weeping you pour out joy.
May your name, O God of Israel, be blessed through all ages!"
These two prayers were heard at the same time before the glory of the Most High God;
and the holy angel of the Lord, Raphael, was sent to heal them both, Tobit and Sarah, whose prayers had risen at the same moment before the Lord.
That day, believing his prayer answered and his death near, Tobit called his son Tobias to him,
and said to him: "Listen, my son, to the words of my mouth, and lay them as a firm foundation in your heart.
When God has received my soul, lay my body in the ground. Honor your mother all the days of her life;
remember all that she suffered and the dangers she faced for you when she carried you in her womb.
And when she too has finished her life, bury her beside me.
All the days of your life, keep God present in your mind; take care not to consent to sin or to neglect the commandments of the Lord your God.
Give alms from your goods, and do not turn your face away from any poor person; so the face of God will not be turned away from you.
Be merciful according to your means.
If you have much, give generously; if you have little, be careful to share that little with a willing heart.
In this way you will lay up for yourself a fine treasure for the day of need,
for almsgiving delivers from death and keeps one from falling into the darkness.
For all who practice it, almsgiving is a great ground of confidence before the Most High God.
Guard yourself, my son, from all impurity; apart from your wife, let your conscience never have to reproach you with a fault.
Never let pride rule over your heart or your words, for it is through pride that all misfortunes began.
When a man has worked for you, pay him his wages at once, and let the wages of the laborer not stay with you for a moment.
What you would hate to have done to you, take care not to do to another.
Share your bread with those who are hungry and with the destitute, and cover the naked with your clothing.
Offer your bread and your wine for the burial of the just, but do not eat or drink of it with sinners.
Always seek counsel from a wise man.
Bless God at all times; ask him to direct your way, so that all your plans may succeed through him.
I also inform you, my son, that when you were still a little child I entrusted ten bags of silver to Gabael, at Rages, a city of Media, and that I have kept his receipt.
Make haste, then, to go and find him and withdraw this sum, and you will give him back his receipt.
Do not be afraid, my son. It is true that we lead a poor life; but we shall have great wealth if we fear God, if we shun all sin and do good."

titres.titre: Tobias looks for a traveling companion
The angel welcomed into Tobit's house

versets.t: Tobias answered his father: "All that you have commanded me, I will do, father.
But I do not know how I shall be able to withdraw this money. This man does not know me, and I do not know him; what sign shall I give him? I do not even know the road that leads there."
His father answered him: "I have his receipt in my hands; as soon as you show it to him, he will repay you.
But first go and find a trustworthy man to go with you, for a wage, so that you may recover this sum while I am still alive."
Tobias went out and found a handsome young man, standing with his belt about his waist, as though ready to set out on a journey.
Not knowing that he was an angel of God, he greeted him and said, "Where do you come from, good young man?"
The angel answered, "I am a son of Israel." Tobias said to him, "Do you know the road that leads to the land of Media?"
He answered, "I know it; I have often traveled all these roads, and I have lodged with our brother Gabael, who lives at Rages, a city of Media, in the mountainous region of Ecbatana."
Tobias said to him, "Wait for me, I beg you, while I tell this to my father."
Tobias went in and told his father everything. Filled with wonder, his father asked that the young man be brought in.
The man came in and greeted him: "May joy be always with you!"
Tobit answered, "What joy can I have, I who sit in darkness and do not see the light of heaven?"
The young man said to him, "Take heart! It is easy for God to heal you."
Tobit replied, "Could you lead my son to Gabael, at Rages, a city of Media? On your return I will give you your wage."
"I will lead him," answered the angel, "and I will bring him back to you."
Tobit said to him, "Tell me, I beg you, of what family and of what tribe are you?"
The angel Raphael answered him, "Are you looking for the family of your guide, or the guide himself who is to accompany your son?
But, so as not to worry you, I am Azarias, son of the great Ananias."
"You are of a noble line," said Tobit. "But do not be angry, I beg you, that I wished to know your family."
The angel said to him, "I will lead your son safe and sound, and I will bring him back to you safe and sound."
Tobit added, "Have a good journey! May God be on your road and his angel accompany you!"
When all was ready for the journey, Tobias said farewell to his father and mother, and he set out with the angel.
After they had left, the mother began to weep: "You have taken from us the staff of our old age and sent him far away!
Ah, if only that money, for which you sent him, had never existed!
Our poverty was enough for us, for it was a wealth to us to see our son."
Tobit answered her, "Do not weep; our son will arrive safe and sound and will come back to us safe and sound; your eyes will see him again.
For I believe that a good angel of God accompanies him and will bring to a happy end everything that befalls him, so that he will come back to us in joy."
At these words his mother stopped weeping and was silent.
Tobias set out, followed by the dog, and made his first halt on the bank of the Tigris.
As he went down to the shore to wash his feet, a huge fish darted up to devour him.
Terrified, Tobias gave a great cry: "Lord, it is rushing at me!"
The angel said to him, "Take it by the gills and pull it toward you." Tobias did so, dragged it onto dry land, and the fish thrashed at his feet.
The angel said to him, "Clean this fish, and keep the heart, the gall, and the liver: they are useful remedies."
Tobias obeyed; he roasted part of the flesh, which they took along for the road, and salted the rest, enough to last as far as Rages, a city of Media.
Tobias questioned the angel: "Azarias, my brother, tell me, I beg you, what healing power these parts of the fish have, which you have had me keep."

The angel answered him, "If you lay a little of the heart on live coals, the smoke that rises from it drives away every kind of demon, whether from a man or a woman, so that it can no longer come near.
And the gall heals eyes covered with a film, when they are rubbed with it."
Tobias said to him, "Where would you have us stop?"
The angel answered, "There is a man here of your tribe and your family, named Raguel; he has a daughter, Sarah, but no other child, neither son nor daughter.
All his property is to come to you, and it is she whom you must take as your wife.
Ask her, then, of her father, and he will give her to you as your wife."
Tobias answered, "I have heard that she has already married seven husbands, and that they are all dead; I have even been told that a demon killed them.
I am afraid the same thing may happen to me; and since I am the only son of my parents, I would bring their old age down to the grave in grief."
The angel Raphael said to him, "Listen to me, and I will teach you over whom the demon has power.

It is those who enter marriage banishing God from their heart and their thoughts to give themselves over to their passion, like the horse and the mule that have no reason: over such the demon has power.
But you, once married, go into the chamber and live with her in continence for three days, thinking of nothing but praying to God with her.
On the first night, burn the fish's liver in the fire, and the demon will flee.
On the second night, you will be admitted into the company of the holy patriarchs.
On the third night, you will receive the blessing promised to their descendants, so that children full of vigor may be born to you.

The third night past, you will take the young woman in the fear of the Lord, guided far more by the desire for children than by passion, so that in your sons you may obtain the blessing promised to the race of Abraham."

titres.titre: The marriage of Tobias and Sarah

versets.t: They entered the house of Raguel, who received them with joy.
On seeing Tobias, Raguel said to Edna, his wife, "How this young man resembles my cousin!"
Then he asked the travelers, "Where are you from, young men, our brothers?" They answered, "We are of the tribe of Naphtali, among the captives of Nineveh."
Raguel said to them, "Do you know Tobit, my kinsman?" "We know him," they answered.
As Raguel spoke much good of Tobit, the angel said to him, "This Tobit of whom you speak is the father of this young man."
At once Raguel rushed toward him, embraced him, and wept on his neck.
"Be blessed, my son," he said, "for you are the son of a good man, the best of men!"
And Edna, his wife, and Sarah, their daughter, shed tears.
After this exchange, Raguel had a ram killed and a feast prepared; as he invited them to come to the table,
Tobias said, "I will neither eat nor drink here today until you have granted my request and promised to give me your daughter Sarah."

At these words Raguel was afraid, knowing what had happened to the seven husbands who had approached her, and he feared that the same misfortune might strike this one. As he hesitated and gave no answer to Tobias's request,
the angel said to him, "Do not be afraid to give your daughter to this young man: it is to him, who fears God, that she must come as his wife; that is why no other has been able to keep her."
Then Raguel said, "I have no doubt: God has received my prayers and my tears before him.
I believe that he has brought you to me so that my daughter may marry a man of her kindred, according to the law of Moses. Have no more doubt: I give her to you."

Taking his daughter's right hand, he placed it in the right hand of Tobias: "May the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob be with you; may he himself unite you and pour out on you his full blessing!"
Then they drew up the marriage contract in writing.
After that, they shared in the feast, blessing God.
Raguel called Edna, his wife, and asked her to prepare another room.
She led her daughter Sarah there, who began to weep.
Edna said to her, "Take heart, my daughter. May the Lord of heaven give you joy in place of the sorrow you have known!"

titres.titre: The demon driven off, the prayer of the couple

versets.t: When the meal was over, the young man was brought in to Sarah.
Remembering the angel's words, Tobias took from his bag a piece of the liver and laid it on live coals.
Then the angel Raphael seized the demon and bound it in the desert of Upper Egypt.

Then Tobias encouraged the young woman: "Sarah, get up, and let us pray to God today, tomorrow, and the day after; during these three nights we will stay united to God, and after the third night we will live out our marriage.
For we are children of the saints, and we cannot be united like the nations that do not know God."
They both rose and prayed earnestly that God might grant them safety.
Tobias said: "Lord, God of our fathers, may heaven and earth bless you, and the sea, the springs and the rivers, with all the creatures they contain!
You made Adam from the clay of the earth, and you gave him Eve as his companion.
And now, Lord, you know it: it is not to satisfy my passion that I take as my wife the one given to me, but only in the desire to leave descendants who will bless your name through all ages."
Sarah said in her turn: "Have mercy on us, Lord, have mercy on us, and may we come together to old age in full health!"
At cockcrow, Raguel summoned his servants, and they went out with him to dig a grave.
For he said to himself, "The same thing may well have happened to him as to the seven other husbands who approached her."
The grave ready, Raguel came back to his wife and said to her:
"Send one of your maidservants to see whether he is dead, so that I may bury him before daybreak."
Edna sent a maidservant. Entering the room, she found them safe and sound, asleep side by side.
She came back to announce the good news, and Raguel and Edna, his wife, blessed the Lord:
"We bless you, Lord, God of Israel, for the misfortune we dreaded has not come.
You have shown us mercy and have driven away from us the enemy who persecuted us.

You have had pity on two only children. Grant, Lord, that they may bless you more and more and offer you a sacrifice of praise for their deliverance, so that all the nations may recognize that you alone are God over all the earth."
At once Raguel ordered his servants to fill in before daybreak the grave they had dug.
He told his wife to prepare a feast and all that was needed to refresh travelers.
He had two fat cows and four rams killed to prepare a meal for all his neighbors and all his friends.
And Raguel urged Tobias to stay with him for two weeks.
Of all that he owned, Raguel gave half to Tobias, and he drew up a document so that the other half should also come to him after their death.

titres.titre: Raphael goes to fetch the money from Gabael

versets.t: Then Tobias called the angel to him, whom he took for a man, and said to him, "Azarias, my brother, I beg you to listen to my words.
Even if I gave myself to you as a slave, I could never repay all your care.

Yet I make this one more request of you: take beasts of burden and servants with you, and go to Gabael at Rages, a city of Media; give him back his receipt, receive the money from him, and ask him to come to my wedding.
For you yourself know that my father is counting the days, and that the least delay will plunge his heart into sorrow.
You see too how Raguel has begged me to stay here, and that I cannot resist his pleading."
Then Raphael took four of Raguel's servants and two camels, and went to Rages, a city of Media. There he found Gabael, gave him back his receipt, and received all the money;
then, after telling him all that had happened to Tobias, son of Tobit, he brought him along to the wedding.
When Gabael entered Raguel's house, he found Tobias at the table. Tobias rose at once; they embraced, and Gabael wept as he blessed God.
He said, "May the God of Israel bless you, for you are the son of an excellent man, just, God-fearing, and generous in almsgiving!
May the blessing rest also on your wife and on your parents!
May you see your sons and the sons of your sons, to the third and fourth generation! May your descendants be blessed by the God of Israel, who reigns forever and ever!"
All answered, "Amen!" Then they sat down at the table, and it was in the fear of God that they held the wedding feast.

titres.titre: The departure of Tobias and Sarah

versets.t: While Tobias was delaying his departure because of the wedding, his father Tobit grew anxious and said to himself, "Why is my son delayed? What can be keeping him in that country?
Could Gabael be dead, with no one to give back the money?"
So he began to grieve deeply, he and Anna, his wife, and they both began to weep, because their son had not come back on the appointed day.

His mother especially shed endless tears: "Alas! alas! my son, why did we send you so far away, you the light of our eyes, the staff of our old age, the comfort of our life, and the hope of our descendants?
We who had everything in you alone, we should not have sent you away from us."
Tobit would say to her, "Stop your lamenting and do not be troubled: our son is well, and the man with whom we sent him is perfectly faithful."

But nothing could console her: each day she went out of the house, looked in every direction, and walked along all the roads by which he might return, hoping to catch sight of him from afar if she could.
Meanwhile Raguel said to his son-in-law, "Stay here, and I will send your father Tobit news of your welfare."
Tobias answered him, "I know that my father and mother are counting the days and that their hearts are troubled."

Raguel pressed him at length, but Tobias would not listen. Then Raguel handed over to him Sarah, with half of all his goods, menservants and maidservants, flocks, camels, cattle, and a large sum of money, and he let him go in full health and joy.
He said to him, "May the holy angel of the Lord be on your way and lead you home safe and sound; may you find everything prosperous with your parents, and may my eyes see your children before I die!"
Then Raguel and Edna took their daughter, embraced her, and let her go,
after urging her to honor her parents-in-law, to love her husband, to manage her household well, and to keep herself beyond reproach.
On the way back, they reached Haran on the eleventh day, a town halfway to Nineveh.
The angel then said, "Tobias, my brother, you know in what state you left your father.
If you agree, let us go on ahead; let your servants follow at a slower pace, with your wife and your flocks."
Tobias agreed. Raphael said to him, "Take some of the fish's gall with you, for you will need it." Tobias took the gall, and they set off.
Anna, meanwhile, went each day to sit by the road, on the top of a height from which she could see far off.
Watching thus for her son's return, she caught sight of him far off, coming back; recognizing him, she ran to tell her husband, "Here comes your son!"
At the same time, Raphael said to Tobias, "When you have entered your house, worship the Lord your God at once and give him thanks; then, going up to your father, embrace him,

and apply at once to his eyes this fish's gall that you are carrying; know that his eyes will open on the spot, that your father will see the light of heaven, and that the sight of you will fill him with joy."
Then the dog, which had gone with them throughout the journey, ran ahead of them as if to announce the news, wagging its tail, full of joy.
The blind father rose and began to run; as he stumbled, he stretched out his hand to a servant to go to meet his son.
He took him in his arms and kissed him, as did his wife also, and both shed tears of joy.
After they had worshiped God and given him thanks, they sat down.
At once Tobias took some of the fish's gall and applied it to his father's eyes.
After about half an hour's wait, a white film, like the skin of an egg, began to peel away from his eyes.
Tobias took hold of it and pulled it from his father's eyes, and at once his father recovered his sight.
They gave glory to God, he, his wife, and all who knew them.
Tobit said, "I bless you, Lord, God of Israel, because you have chastised me and you have healed me; and behold, I see my son Tobias!"
Seven days later Sarah, his son's wife, also arrived, in good health, with all her servants, the flocks and the camels, as well as the marriage dowry and the money paid back by Gabael.
Tobias told his parents all the benefits with which God had blessed him through the man who had led him.
Ahikar and Nadab, kinsmen of Tobit, came to see him, full of joy, and congratulated him on all the good that God had done for him.
And for seven days, all together, they held great rejoicings.

titres.titre: The reward offered to the angel

versets.t: Then Tobit called his son and said to him, "What shall we give to this holy man who accompanied you on your journey?"
Tobias answered his father, "Father, what reward could we offer him? Is there anything that matches his services?

He led me and brought me back safe and sound; it was he who went to fetch the money from Gabael; he obtained a wife for me and drove the demon out of her, and he filled her parents with joy; he saved me from the fish that was about to devour me; he made you see the light of heaven again, and through him we have been filled with every kind of good. What could we give him to equal all this?
I beg you, father, ask him whether he would accept half of all that we have brought back."
So they called him, took him aside, both of them, and asked him to accept half of all they had brought back.
Then the angel, alone with them, said to them: "Bless the God of heaven and give him glory before every living being, for he has shown you his mercy.
It is good to keep hidden the secret of a king; but it is a fine thing to reveal and proclaim the works of God.
Prayer is good with fasting, and almsgiving is worth more than gold and treasures.
For almsgiving delivers from death; it is what wipes away sins and brings a man to find mercy and eternal life.
But those who commit sin and injustice are their own enemies.
So I will disclose the truth to you, hiding nothing from you.
When you prayed in tears and buried the dead, when you left your meal to hide the dead in your house by day and bury them by night, it was I who presented your prayer to the Lord.
And because you were pleasing to God, it was necessary that you pass through the trial.
Now the Lord has sent me to heal you and to deliver from the demon Sarah, your son's wife.
I am the angel Raphael, one of the seven who stand in the presence of the Lord."
On hearing these words, they were overwhelmed and, all trembling, fell face down on the ground.
The angel said to them, "Peace be with you! Do not be afraid.
For when I was with you, I was there by the will of God; bless him, then, and sing his praises.
It seemed to you that I ate and drank with you; but I fed on an invisible food and a drink that the eye of man cannot see.
It is now time for me to return to him who sent me; as for you, bless God and proclaim all his wonders."
After these words, he vanished from their sight, and they could no longer see him.
Then, prostrate for three hours, their faces to the ground, they blessed God; then they rose and recounted all his wonders.
Then old Tobit opened his mouth and blessed the Lord: "You are great, Lord, for eternity, and your reign extends through all ages.
For you chastise and you save, you lead down to the grave and you bring back up; no one can escape your hand.
Praise the Lord, sons of Israel, and extol him before the nations.
For he has scattered you among nations that do not know him, so that you may recount his wonders and make known to them that there is no other almighty God but he alone.
He has chastised us because of our faults, and he will save us because of his mercy.
See what he has done for us; bless him with fear and trembling, and glorify by your deeds the King of the ages.
As for me, I will bless him in this land where I am a captive, for he has shown his greatness to a guilty nation.
Turn back, then, sinners, and do what is just before God, in the confidence that he will show you mercy!
As for me, I will rejoice in him with all my soul.
Bless the Lord, all you his chosen people; keep days of joy and sing his praises!
Jerusalem, city of God, the Lord has chastised you for the works of your hands.
Glorify the Lord by your good deeds and bless the God of the ages, that he may rebuild his sanctuary in you, bring back to you all the captives, and that you may rejoice forever and ever.
You will shine with a dazzling light, and all the lands of the earth will bow down before you.
The nations will come to you from distant countries, bringing gifts; they will worship the Lord within your walls and revere your land as a holy place,
for they will invoke the great Name in your midst.
Cursed be those who despise you, condemned those who blaspheme you, blessed those who rebuild you.
And you, you will rejoice in your children, for they will all be blessed and will gather together to the Lord.
Happy are all who love you and rejoice in your peace!
My soul, bless the Lord, for he has delivered Jerusalem, his city, from all her distresses, he, the Lord, our God!
Happy shall I be if there remain offshoots of my race to see the splendor of Jerusalem!
The gates of Jerusalem will be built of sapphires and emeralds, and the whole circuit of her walls of precious stones.
Stones of spotless whiteness will pave her squares, and in her streets they will sing: Alleluia!
Blessed be the Lord, who has given this glory to Jerusalem! May he reign over her forever and ever! Amen!"
So ended the words of Tobit. After recovering his sight, he lived on for forty-two years, and he saw the children of his grandchildren.
He lived in all one hundred and two years, and he was buried with honor at Nineveh.
He was fifty-six years old when he lost his sight, and he recovered it at sixty.
All the rest of his life passed in joy; the more he grew in the fear of God, the more he tasted peace.
At the hour of his death, he called to him his son Tobias and Tobias's seven young sons, his grandsons, and he said to them:
"The ruin of Nineveh is near, for the word of God will be fulfilled; and our brothers scattered far from the land of Israel will return to it.
All the land of Israel, after having been a desert, will be repopulated; the house of God, after having been burned, will be rebuilt, and all who fear God will return to it.
The nations will abandon their idols; they will come to Jerusalem to dwell there,
and all the kings of the earth will rejoice in it, worshiping the King of Israel.
Listen, then, to your father, my children: serve the Lord in truth, and strive to do what is pleasing to him.
Charge your children to practice justice, to give alms, to remember God and to bless him at all times, in truth and with all their strength.
Listen to me now, my children: do not stay in this city. On the very day when you have buried your mother beside me in one same tomb, set out to leave this place;
for I see it, the injustice of Nineveh will bring about its ruin."
After his mother's death, young Tobias left Nineveh with his wife, his children, and his children's children, and returned to his parents-in-law.

He found them in good health, in a happy old age; he took care of them and closed their eyes; he received the whole inheritance of the house of Raguel, and he saw his children's children to the fifth generation.
After living ninety-nine years in the fear of the Lord, he was buried by his children in joy.
All those of his kindred and all his descendants persevered in a good and holy life, so that they were loved by God, by men, and by all the inhabitants of the country.
Arphaxad, king of the Medes, had brought many nations under his empire. He built a very powerful city of dressed stone, which he named Ecbatana.
He surrounded it with walls thirty-five metres high and fifteen metres thick, and he raised towers on it fifty metres high,
square, each side six metres wide; and he made the gates as high as the towers.
He gloried in himself as invincible, in the strength of his army and the multitude of his chariots.
Now in the twelfth year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Assyrians, who reigned in Nineveh the great city, made war on Arphaxad and defeated him
in the great plain called Ragau, with the support of the peoples settled near the Euphrates, the Tigris and the Jadason, in the plain of Erioch, king of the Elicians.
Then the dominion of Nebuchadnezzar grew, his heart swelled with pride, and he sent messengers to all the inhabitants of Cilicia, of Damascus and of Mount Lebanon,
to the peoples of Carmel and Kedar, to the inhabitants of Galilee, in the great plain of Esdraelon,
to all those of Samaria and beyond the Jordan, as far as Jerusalem, and throughout the whole land of Goshen up to the borders of Ethiopia.
To all these peoples Nebuchadnezzar, king of Assyria, sent messengers.
But with one accord they all refused; they sent them away empty-handed and treated them with contempt.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar flew into a rage against all these lands, and he swore by his throne and his kingdom that he would take vengeance on all these regions.

titres.titre: Holofernes is launched against the West

versets.t: In the thirteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, on the twenty-second day of the first month, it was decided, in the palace of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Assyria, that he would take his revenge.
He summoned all the elders, all his commanders and his warriors, and held a secret council with them.
He laid before them his plan: to bring the whole earth under his empire.
When this design had been approved by all, King Nebuchadnezzar sent for Holofernes, commander-in-chief of his army,
and said to him: "March against all the kingdoms of the West, and above all against those who have scorned my order.
Your eye shall spare no kingdom, and you shall subject to me all the fortified cities."

Then Holofernes summoned the commanders and officers of the Assyrian army, and, according to the king's order, he enrolled for the expedition one hundred and twenty thousand foot soldiers and twelve thousand mounted archers.
He sent ahead of his army a countless multitude of camels, with abundant provisions for his soldiers, and innumerable herds of oxen and flocks of sheep.
He had grain from all Syria made ready along his route.
He took immense sums of gold and silver from the king's treasury.
Then he set out, he and all his army, with the chariots, the horsemen and the archers, who covered the face of the earth like locusts.
Having crossed the border of Assyria, he reached the great mountains of Ange, north of Cilicia; he penetrated all their strongholds and seized all their fortifications.
He took by storm the famous city of Melitene, plundered all the inhabitants of Tarsus and the sons of Ishmael settled facing the desert, south of the land of Cellon.
He crossed the Euphrates, passed into Mesopotamia, and forced all the strongholds of the region, from the Wadi Habor as far as the sea.
He then seized all the territory along the Euphrates, from Cilicia to the borders of Japheth, toward the south.
He carried off captive all the sons of Midian, plundered all their wealth, and put to the sword all who resisted him.
Then he went down into the countryside of Damascus, at harvest time, burned all the crops, and had all the trees and vines cut down.
And the terror of his arms seized all the inhabitants of the earth.
Then the kings and princes of all the cities and lands, of Mesopotamia, of Syria of Zobah, of Libya and of Cilicia, sent ambassadors who presented themselves before Holofernes and said to him:
"Calm your anger against us; it is better, keeping our lives, to serve the great king Nebuchadnezzar and to submit to you, than to die suffering all the miseries of slavery.
All our cities, all our goods, our mountains, our hills, our fields, our herds of oxen, sheep, goats, horses and camels, all our resources and our households, everything is before you.
Let all that we possess be at your disposal.
We and our children are your servants.
Come to us as a peaceful master, and make use of our service as you please."
Then Holofernes came down from the mountains with his horsemen, in great force, and made himself master of all the cities and all the inhabitants of the land.
From every city he took, as auxiliaries, valiant men, chosen for war.
Such was the fear that lay upon these provinces that, in all the cities, the magistrates and the most honored men, along with the common people, went out to meet him,
welcoming him with garlands and torches, dancing to the sound of tambourines and flutes.
But even by this submission they could not soften the ferocity of his heart:
he destroyed their cities and cut down their sacred groves.
For Nebuchadnezzar had ordered him to wipe out all the gods of the earth, so that he alone might be called God by all the nations that the power of Holofernes could subdue.
After passing through Syria and Zobah, all Apamea and all Mesopotamia, he came to the Idumeans, in the land of Gabaa;
he took their cities and stayed there thirty days, during which he gathered together all the troops of his army.

titres.titre: Israel prepares and cries out to the Lord
