let him plead a man's cause with God, as one pleads for his neighbor!
For the numbered years pass, and I set out on the road of no return.

titres.titre: Only the grave is left to me
My hope goes down to the realm of the dead

versets.t: My breath fails, my days flicker out; only the grave is left to me.
Yes, I am surrounded by mockers, and my eye keeps watch amid their taunts.
O God, lay down yourself a pledge for me, with you: who else would strike his hand in mine as surety?
For you have closed their hearts to understanding; that is why you will not let them triumph.
One who denounces his friends for profit, the eyes of his children will fail.
I have been made the byword of the peoples, the man in whose face they spit.
My eye has grown dim with grief, and my whole body is nothing but a shadow.
Upright men are appalled at this, and the innocent is stirred against the godless.
The just man, nonetheless, holds to his way, and those with clean hands grow stronger still.
But all of you, come back and try again: I will not find a single wise man among you!
My days have passed, my plans are shattered, all that my heart desired.
These men turn night into day: "the light," they say, "is near," when darkness falls.
What have I to hope for? The realm of the dead will be my house; in the darkness I have made my bed.
I have said to the pit, "You are my father," and to the worms, "My mother, my sister!"
Where, then, is my hope? And who still catches sight of it?
Will it go down with me to the gates of the realm of the dead? Will we sink together into the dust?

titres.titre: Bildad's second speech: the lamp of the wicked goes out
The wicked man dragged to the King of terrors

versets.t: Then Bildad of Shuah spoke and said:
How long will you go on setting these snares of words? Think first, and then we will speak.
Why be counted as cattle, held stupid in your eyes?
You who tear yourself apart in your fury, must the earth, for your sake, be abandoned, must the rock leave its place?
Yes, the light of the wicked will go out, the flame of his hearth will cease to shine.
The brightness will darken in his tent, and his lamp above him will go out.
His confident steps will be hemmed in, and his own scheming will bring him down.
For his feet drive him into the net, he walks straight onto the mesh.
A snare catches him by the heel, a noose closes on him.
A rope is hidden for him on the ground, a trap lies waiting on his path.
On every side terrors frighten him and dog him at every step.
Hunger drains his vigor, and disaster stands ready at his side.
It devours patches of his skin, the firstborn of death devours his limbs.
He is torn from his tent where he thought himself secure, and dragged toward the King of terrors.
Fire settles in his tent, sulfur is scattered over his dwelling.
Below, his roots dry up; above, his branches wither.
His memory vanishes from the earth, his name is spoken no more abroad.
He is driven from light into darkness, he is banished from the world.
He leaves neither son nor descendant among his people, no survivor where he lived.
At his ruin, those of the west are appalled, and those of the east are seized with dread.
Such is what becomes of the dwelling of the unjust, such is the place of the one who does not know God.

titres.titre: Job replies: God has assailed me
I know that my Redeemer lives

versets.t: Then Job spoke and said:
How long will you torment me and crush me with your speeches?
Ten times now you have insulted me; you are not ashamed to mistreat me.
Even if I had committed a fault, it would concern me alone.
But you, do you really mean to prevail over me and turn my disgrace against me?
Know this, then: it is God who wrongs me and who has thrown his net over me.
I cry out, 'Violence!' and no one answers; I call for help, and there is no justice.
He has barred my road, I can pass no more; he has plunged my paths into darkness.
He has stripped me of my glory, he has taken the crown from my head.
He demolishes me on every side, and I collapse; he has uprooted my hope like a tree.
His anger has blazed against me, he treats me as an enemy.
His troops have come in force, they have cut their road up to me and camp around my tent.
He has driven my brothers far from me, and those who knew me have turned away.
My kinsmen have left me, my close friends have forgotten me.
The guests of my house and my maidservants treat me as a stranger; I am an unknown in their eyes.
I call my servant, he does not answer; I must plead with him with my own mouth.
My breath is repugnant to my wife, I am loathsome to my own brothers.
Even the little boys despise me; when I rise, they mock me.
All my closest friends loathe me, and those I loved have turned against me.
My bones cling to my skin and my flesh, I have survived only by the skin of my teeth.
Have pity, have pity on me, you at least, my friends, for the hand of God has struck me!
Why do you pursue me as God pursues me, never sated with my flesh?
Ah, if only my words were written down, if only they were engraved in a book,
chiseled with an iron point and lead, cut forever in the rock!
But I know that my Redeemer lives, and that at the last he will stand upon the dust.
After my skin has been destroyed, then, from my flesh, I shall see God.
Yes, I myself will see him; my own eyes will behold him, he and no other. My heart is consumed with longing within me.
You will say then, "How did we hound him?" when the root of the matter turns back against you.
Fear the sword for yourselves, for your fury is a crime deserving the sword; and you will know that there is a judgment.

titres.titre: Zophar's reply: the joy of the wicked is brief

versets.t: Then Zophar of Naamah spoke and said:
This is why my thoughts press me to answer: the turmoil burns within me.
I have heard a rebuke that insults me, but my understanding prompts my reply.
Do you not know this? From all time, since man was placed on the earth,
the triumph of the wicked is brief, and the joy of the godless lasts but a moment.
Though his pride mount up to the sky and his head touch the clouds,
he perishes forever, swept away like his own dung, and those who saw him ask, "Where is he?"
He flies off like a dream, nowhere to be found, chased away like a vision of the night.
The eye that glimpsed him sees him no more, and his house finds him no longer.
His sons will have to beg from the poor, and his own hands will give back what he stole.
His bones, still full of the vigor of his youth, will lie down with him in the dust.
Evil was sweet in his mouth, he hid it under his tongue,
he kept it, refusing to let it go, he held it at the back of his palate:
but this food turns rotten in his belly, it becomes within him a viper's venom.
He has swallowed riches: he will vomit them up; God will wrench them from his belly.
He sucked the venom of vipers, the tongue of the adder will kill him.
He will no longer see the streams flow, the torrents of honey and cream.
He will give back his gain without swallowing it, he will have no joy of his profits.
For he crushed and abandoned the poor, he plundered a house he did not build.
His appetite knew no rest; he will save nothing of what he craved.
Nothing escaped his greed; that is why his prosperity will not last.
At the height of abundance, anguish seizes him; the full weight of misery falls upon him.
When he is about to fill his belly, God looses upon him the heat of his anger and rains it down into his very flesh.
If he flees from weapons of iron, the bow of bronze pierces him through.
The arrow comes out of his back, the gleaming point leaves his liver, and terrors fall upon him.
Total darkness lies in wait for his treasures; a fire that no one has kindled devours him and consumes what was left under his tent.
The heavens will reveal his guilt, and the earth will rise up against him.
The goods of his house will be gone, swept away on the day of wrath.
Such is the lot God reserves for the wicked, the heritage God assigns to him.

titres.titre: Job replies: why do the wicked prosper?
One same fate for the just and the godless
Your consolations are nothing but lies

versets.t: Then Job spoke and said:
Listen, listen closely to my words: let this, at least, be your way of consoling me.
Bear with me while I speak; after that, you may mock.
Is it of a man that I complain? How could I not lose patience?
Turn to me, and be struck with astonishment, lay your hand over your mouth.
When I think of it, I am appalled, and a shudder runs through my flesh.
Why do the wicked stay alive, grow old, and increase in power?
Their offspring are established before their eyes, their descendants prosper in their sight.
Their houses are at peace, with nothing to fear; the rod of God does not touch them.
Their bull breeds without fail, their cow calves and never miscarries.
They let their little ones out like a flock, and their children leap for joy.
They sing to the tambourine and the lyre, they make merry to the sound of the flute.
They pass their days in happiness, and go down in peace to the realm of the dead.
Yet they were saying to God, "Depart from us, we have no wish to know your ways.
What is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What would we gain by praying to him?"
Is their happiness not in their own hands? Far be it from me, though, to share the thoughts of the wicked!
How often does one see the lamp of the wicked go out, misfortune fall upon them, God deal out sorrows to them in his anger?
Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff carried off by the storm?
"God," you say, "stores up the punishment for the guilty man's children." Let him repay the man himself, so that he feels it!
Let his own eyes see his ruin, let him drink for himself the fury of the Almighty!
For what does he care about his house after him, once the count of his months is ended?
Is it God who would be taught knowledge, he who judges the highest of beings?
One dies in full prosperity, perfectly happy and at ease,
his flanks plump, the marrow of his bones well nourished.
Another dies with a bitter heart, never having tasted happiness.
Both lie down alike in the dust, and the worms cover them both.
Ah, I know your thoughts well, and the unjust judgments you pass on me.
You ask, "Where is the house of the great lord, where is the tent the wicked lived in?"
Have you never questioned those who travel the roads? Do you not heed their testimony?
On the day of disaster the wicked man is spared; on the day of wrath he is brought to safety.
Who, to his face, reproaches him for his conduct? Who repays him for what he has done?
He is led in procession to the tomb, and a watch is kept over his grave.
The soil of the valley lies light upon him; behind him walks the crowd, and before him a countless multitude.
How, then, can you console me with wind? Of your answers, nothing is left but lies.

titres.titre: Eliphaz's third speech: your sins are great
Do you think God sees nothing?
Return to the Almighty, and you will be restored

versets.t: Then Eliphaz of Teman answered and said:
Can a man be of use to God? No, the wise man is of use only to himself.
What does it matter to the Almighty that you are righteous? What does he gain if you lead an upright life?
Is it for your piety that he corrects you and enters into judgment with you?
Is it not rather that your wickedness is great, and your sins beyond counting?
You demanded pledges from your brothers for no reason, you stripped the clothes from those who had nothing.
You refused water to the exhausted, and to the hungry you refused bread.
The land belonged to the strong man, and the favored one settled upon it.
You sent widows away empty-handed, and you broke the arms of orphans.
That is why snares surround you, and why a sudden terror appalls you;
that is why the light has turned to darkness so that you see nothing, and why the waters engulf you.
Is God not in the highest heavens? Look at the topmost stars: how far above they are!
And you say: 'What does God know? Can he judge through the dark clouds?
The clouds hide him, he sees nothing, he walks upon the vault of heaven.'
Will you then keep to the ancient road, the one the wicked have trodden,
those cut down before their time, whose foundations a torrent swept away?
They said to God: 'Depart from us! What could the Almighty do to us?'
Yet it was he who had filled their houses with good things. But far be from me the thoughts of the wicked!
The righteous see their ruin and rejoice, the innocent mocks them:
'See how our adversaries are wiped out, and fire has devoured what was left of them!'
Be reconciled with God, then, make peace, and happiness will come back to you.
Receive instruction from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart.
If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored; put injustice far from your tent.
Throw your gold to the dust, and the gold of Ophir to the pebbles of the torrent:
the Almighty himself will be your gold, he will be for you heaps of silver.
Then you will find your delight in the Almighty, and you will lift up your face to God.
You will pray to him, and he will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
Whatever you decide will come to pass, and light will shine upon your paths.
When others are cast down, you will say, 'Rise up!', and God will save the one who lowers his eyes.
He will deliver even the guilty, and it is the purity of your hands that will save him.

titres.titre: Job's reply: if only I could find him!
Not to be found, yet he knows my way

versets.t: Then Job answered and said:
Even today my complaint is rebellion, and his hand weighs heavy upon my groaning.
Oh, if only I knew where to find him, how to reach his seat!
I would lay out my case before him, I would fill my mouth with arguments.
I would know what he would answer me, I would understand what he had to say.
Would he plead against me with all his power? No, it would be enough for him to listen to me.
There an upright man could argue with him, and I would be acquitted forever by my judge.
But if I go east, he is not there; if west, I do not perceive him;
if he works in the north, I cannot make him out; if he turns to the south, I do not see him.
Yet he knows the road I walk: let him test me, and I will come out pure as gold.
My foot has held fast to his steps; I have kept his way without turning aside.
I have not strayed from the commands of his lips; I have treasured in my heart the words of his mouth.
But he alone decides, who could make him change? What he wills, he does.
He will carry out the decree he has pronounced against me, and of such designs he has many more.
That is why I am terrified before him; when I think of it, I tremble.
God has made my courage fail, the Almighty has filled me with dread;
and yet I am not silenced by the darkness, nor by the gloom that veils my face.

titres.titre: Why does God not set a time for judgment?
The final lot of the wicked

versets.t: Why does the Almighty not set times for judgment? Why do those who know him never see his days?
Men move the boundary stones, they seize a flock and lead it to pasture.
They drive off the orphan's donkey, they take the widow's ox in pledge.
They push the poor off the road, and all the humble of the land must hide themselves.
Like wild donkeys of the desert, these wretched ones go out to their toil, searching from dawn for food; the wasteland alone feeds their children.
They harvest in a field that is not their own, they glean the vineyard of the wicked.
They spend the night naked, without clothing, with nothing to cover them from the cold.
Drenched by the mountain rains, with no shelter, they huddle against the rock.
The orphan is torn from the breast, the poor man's infant is taken in pledge.
These go about naked, without a garment; starving, they carry the sheaves of others;
they press oil between the walls of the rich, they tread the winepress, and still they thirst.
In the city the dying groan, the throats of the wounded cry out for help, and God finds nothing in it to reproach!
There are also the enemies of the light: they know nothing of its ways and keep to none of its paths.
At daybreak the murderer rises, he kills the poor and the needy, and by night he prowls like a thief.
The eye of the adulterer watches for the dusk: 'No eye will see me,' he says, and he covers his face.
In the dark men break into houses; by day these people shut themselves away: they want nothing to do with the light.
For all of them, morning is like the shadow of death, for they are at home with the terrors of the night.
Swiftly swept along the surface of the waters, the wicked man has on earth only a cursed plot; no one takes the road to his vineyards anymore.
As drought and heat drink up the melted snow, so the realm of the dead swallows the sinner.
The womb that bore him forgets him, the worms feast on him; no one remembers him, and injustice is broken like a tree.
He who preyed on the barren woman, the childless, and refused all kindness to the widow.
But God, by his strength, carries off the mighty; let him rise, and no one is sure of his life.
He grants them security, and they lean upon it, but his eyes watch over their ways.
Raised up for a moment, they are gone; they sink down, cut off like all the rest, cropped like the heads of grain.
If this is not so, who will prove me a liar, who will reduce my words to nothing?

titres.titre: Bildad's last word: man is nothing before God

versets.t: Then Bildad of Shuah answered and said:
Dominion and dread belong to him; he makes peace reign in his heights.
Can his armies be numbered? Upon whom does his light not rise?
How then could man be righteous before God? How could he be pure, one born of woman?
See: even the moon is without brightness, the stars are not pure in his eyes;
how much less man, that worm, the son of man, that maggot!

titres.titre: Job's reply: what fine help yours is!
God, master of the abyss and the heavens

versets.t: Then Job answered and said:
How well you help the weak, how you rescue the arm without strength!
What good counsel you give to the ignorant, what wisdom you pour out in abundance!
But to whom do you address these speeches? What breath has come out of you?
Before him the shades tremble, beneath the waters, with those who dwell there.
The realm of the dead lies bare before him, and destruction has no veil.
He stretches out the northern sky over the void, he suspends the earth upon nothing.
He shuts up the waters in his clouds, yet the cloud does not burst under their weight.
He veils the face of his throne, spreading his clouds over it.
He has drawn a circle on the surface of the waters, at the boundary of light and darkness.
The pillars of heaven sway, appalled at his rebuke.
By his power he stirred up the sea; by his understanding he shattered Rahab.
By his breath he makes the heavens clear; his hand has pierced the fleeing serpent.
And this is but the fringe of his works, the faint echo we catch of them: the thunder of his power, who then could grasp it?

titres.titre: The lot reserved for the wicked

versets.t: Job took up his poem again and said:
As surely as God lives, who denies me justice, as surely as the Almighty lives, who fills my soul with bitterness:
as long as a breath remains in me, as long as the breath of God is in my nostrils,
my lips will speak nothing wicked, my tongue will murmur no lie.
Far be it from me to grant you the right! Until my last breath, I will not give up my integrity.
I hold fast to my righteousness, I will not let it go; my conscience reproaches me for none of my days.
May my enemy meet the fate of the wicked, my adversary that of the unjust!
For what hope is left to the godless when God cuts him off and takes away his life?
Will God hear his cry, on the day disaster falls upon him?
Will he find his delight in the Almighty? Will he call upon God at all times?
I will teach you the way God works, hiding nothing of the designs of the Almighty.
You have all seen it for yourselves: why then speak such empty words?
This is the portion God reserves for the wicked, the inheritance the violent receive from the Almighty:
if his sons multiply, it is for the sword, and his offspring will never have bread enough.
Those who survive him, the plague lays in the grave, and their widows do not weep for them.
He may heap up silver like dust and pile up clothing like clay,
but he heaps it up, and the righteous is the one who wears it, and the silver, it is the innocent who shares it out.
He has built his house as flimsy as the moth's, as the hut of a vineyard watchman.
Rich he lies down, but for the last time; he opens his eyes, and it has all vanished.
Terrors sweep over him like a flood, in the dead of night a storm carries him off.
The east wind lifts him and bears him away, it tears him from his home.
It hurls itself upon him without mercy, and he flees headlong from its grasp.
Men clap their hands at his downfall, and from every side they hiss at him.

titres.titre: Man knows how to draw out the treasures of the earth
But wisdom, where can it be found?
God alone knows the way to wisdom

versets.t: Silver has its mine, and gold a place where it is refined.
Iron is drawn from the ground, and molten rock yields copper.
Man drives back the darkness, he searches to the ends of the world the stone buried in gloom and the shadow of death.
Far from any village he sinks a shaft; forgotten by passersby, he goes down and swings, hanging far from other men.
The earth, from which bread comes, is turned over deep below as if by fire.
Its rocks hold the sapphire, and in it are found flecks of gold.
That path the bird of prey does not know, the falcon's eye has not spotted it;
the wild beasts have not trodden it, the lion has never passed that way.
Man sets his hand to the hardest rock, he overturns the mountains at their roots.
He cuts galleries through the stone, and his eye discovers every precious thing.
He dams up the seeping springs, and brings to light what was hidden.
But wisdom, where can it be found? Where does understanding dwell?
Man does not know the way to it, it is not to be found in the land of the living.
The abyss declares: 'It is not in me'; the sea replies: 'Nor with me.'
It cannot be bought with solid gold, nor its price weighed out in silver.
Neither the gold of Ophir can match it, nor precious onyx, nor sapphire.
Gold and crystal do not equal it, no vessel of fine gold is worth the exchange.
Beside it, coral and glass count for nothing; to possess wisdom is worth more than pearls.
The topaz of Ethiopia does not equal it, and the purest gold does not reach its price.
Where then does wisdom come from? Where does understanding dwell?
It is hidden from the eyes of all the living, it escapes even the birds of heaven.
Destruction and Death confess: 'With our ears we have caught only a rumor of it.'
God alone knows the way to it, he alone knows where it dwells.
For his gaze reaches the ends of the earth, he sees all that is under the heavens.
When he fixed the weight of the wind and measured out the waters,
when he gave the rain its law and a path to the crashing lightning,
then he saw wisdom and measured it, he established it and searched it to the depths.
Then he said to man: 'To fear the Lord, that is wisdom; to shun evil, that is understanding.'
Job took up his poem again and said:
Oh, who will give me back the months of old, the days when God watched over me,
when his lamp shone above my head and by its light I walked through the darkness!
As I was in the days of my full vigor, when the friendship of God rested over my tent,
when the Almighty was still with me and my children were all around me,
when my steps were bathed in cream and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!
When I went out to the city gate and set up my seat in the square,
the young men, seeing me, drew aside, and the old men rose and stood.
The leading men held back their words and laid a hand upon their mouths;
the voices of the chiefs fell silent, their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.
The ear that heard me called me blessed, the eye that saw me bore me witness.
For I delivered the poor who cried for help, and the orphan whom no one came to aid.
The blessing of the dying came upon me, and I brought joy again to the widow's heart.
I clothed myself in righteousness, and it clothed me; my justice was my robe and my turban.
I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
I was a father to the poor, and the cause of the stranger I searched out to the bottom.
I broke the jaws of the unjust, and from between his teeth I tore his prey.
I said to myself: 'I will die in my nest, after days as many as the sand.
My roots reach out to the water, and the dew lies all night on my branches.
My glory will stay forever fresh, and my bow in my hand will keep its strength.'
Men listened to me, waiting, they fell silent to gather in my counsel.
After I had spoken, no one spoke again, and my words fell drop by drop upon them.
They waited for me as for the rain, they opened their mouths as for the spring showers.
When I smiled at them, they could scarcely believe it, and the light of my face they would not let fade.
I chose their road and sat at their head; I was like a king among his troops, like one who comforts the mourners.

titres.titre: And now I am their laughingstock
God has thrown me into the dust

versets.t: And now I am mocked by men younger than I, whose fathers I would not have set with the dogs of my flock.
What would I have done with the strength of their arms? All their vigor had left them.
Worn out by want and hunger, they gnaw the parched ground, in the night of the ravaged wasteland.
They pick the bitter herbs of the bushes, they feed on the roots of the broom.
They are driven out from among men, people shout after them as after a thief.
They lodge in the gullies of the ravines, in holes of the earth and the rocks.
Among the scrub their braying is heard; under the nettles they crowd together.
Sons of nobodies, men without a name, whipped out of the land.
And now I am the subject of their songs, the target of their taunts.
They loathe me, they keep their distance, they do not hold back from spitting in my face.
Since God has loosened the string of my bow and humbled me, they cast off all restraint before me.
On my right rises this brood, they make my feet slip and lay against me their paths of ruin.
They have torn up my track, they labor at my downfall, and no one holds them back.
They pour in through a wide breach, they roll over me amid the rubble.
Terrors turn against me; my dignity is swept away as by the wind, and my deliverance has fled like a cloud.
And now my life ebbs away within me, days of misery have seized me.
By night my bones are pierced through, and the gnawing pain never sleeps.
With great violence my garment is deformed, it clings to me like the collar of a tunic.
God has thrown me into the mire, and now I am like dust and ashes.
I cry out to you, and you do not answer; I stand up, and you barely look at me.
You have turned cruel toward me, you strike me with all the strength of your hand.
You lift me up, you make me ride the wind, you dissolve me in the crash of the storm.
Yes, I know it, you are bringing me back to death, to the meeting place of all the living.
Yet does not the drowning man stretch out his hand? In his ruin, does he not call for help?
And I, did I not weep for the one whose days were hard? Did my heart not ache for the poor?
I hoped for good, and evil came; I waited for light, and there was darkness.
Within me, everything churns without rest; days of misery have come to meet me.
I go about darkened, but not by the sun; in the assembly I stand and cry for help.
I have become a brother to the jackals, a companion to the ostriches.
My skin blackens and falls away, my bones burn with fever.
My harp knows only mourning now, and my flute only the voice of weeping.

titres.titre: His justice toward the poor and the orphan

versets.t: I had made a covenant with my eyes: how then could I have gazed upon a young woman?
What portion, otherwise, would God have reserved for me from on high, what lot would the Almighty have sent me from his heights?
Is not ruin for the unjust, disaster for those who work evil?
Does God not see my conduct, does he not count all my steps?
If I have walked in falsehood, if my foot has hurried toward deceit,
let God weigh me on a just scale, and he will recognize my integrity!
If my steps have left the straight path, if my heart has followed my eyes, if any stain has clung to my hands,
let another eat what I sow, and let my crops be uprooted!
If my heart has been enticed by a woman, if I have lain in wait at my neighbor's door,
let my wife grind at the mill for another, and let others bend over her!
For that would be an infamy, a crime for the judges to punish,
a fire that devours to the point of ruin and would have consumed my whole harvest.
If I have scorned the right of my servant or my maidservant when they had a grievance against me,
what would I do when God rises up? When he calls me to account, what would I answer him?
Did not he who made me in my mother's womb make them as well? Did not one same God form us in the womb?
Have I refused the poor what they longed for, let the widow's eyes grow dim?
Have I eaten my morsel of bread alone, without the orphan sharing in it?
No: from my youth I raised him as a father, and from my mother's womb I guided the widow.
Have I seen a wretch without a garment, a poor man with nothing to cover him,
and he did not bless me with all his heart, warmed by the fleece of my lambs?
Have I raised my hand against the orphan, knowing I had the judges at the gate to back me?
Then let my shoulder fall from its socket, let my arm break off at the elbow!
For I dread the punishment of God, and before his majesty I can do nothing.
Have I put my trust in gold, have I said to fine metal, 'You are my security'?
Have I rejoiced in my great fortune, in all that my hand had amassed?
Seeing the sun blaze forth and the moon move on in splendor,
has my heart been secretly enticed, has my hand sent a kiss to my mouth?
That too would be a crime to punish, for I would have denied the God on high.
Have I rejoiced at the ruin of my enemy, have I exulted when evil struck him?
No, I did not let my mouth sin by calling for his death with a curse.
Did not the people of my tent say, 'Who has not been filled at his table?'
The resident alien did not spend the night outside: I opened my door to the traveler.
Have I, as men do, hidden my faults, buried my sin in my heart,
for fear of the crowd, dreading the scorn of the clans, so as to keep silent and no longer dare to go out?
Oh, who will give me someone to hear me? Here is my signature: let the Almighty answer me! And let my adversary draw up his indictment!
I would carry it on my shoulder, I would bind it on my brow like a crown.
I would give him an account of my every step, I would approach him like a prince.
If my land has cried out for vengeance against me, if its furrows have wept together,
if I have eaten its fruit without paying for it and made its tenants breathe their last,
then let thorns grow there instead of wheat, and stinking weeds instead of barley! The words of Job are ended.

titres.titre: Elihu, young and indignant, steps forward
Now it is my turn to speak

versets.t: These three men stopped answering Job, because he held himself to be righteous in his own eyes.
Then the anger of Elihu son of Barachel, the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, was kindled. It was kindled against Job, because he claimed to be more righteous than God,
and against his three friends, because they had found nothing to answer and yet condemned Job.
Elihu had waited while the others spoke to Job, for they were older than he.
But when he saw that these three men had nothing more to answer, his anger was kindled.
Then Elihu son of Barachel, the Buzite, spoke and said: I am young, and you are old; that is why I held back, not daring to tell you what I know.
I said to myself, 'Let age speak, and let long years teach wisdom.'
But it is the spirit in man, the breath of the Almighty, that gives understanding.
It is not the old who are wisest, nor the aged who best understand justice.
So I say: Listen to me; I too will tell what I know.
I waited while you spoke, I gave ear to your reasonings, while you searched for words.
I followed you closely: none of you confuted Job, none of you answered his arguments.
Do not say, 'We have found wisdom; it is God who will confound him, not man.'
It was not to me that he addressed his speeches, and it is not with your arguments that I will answer him.
There they stand dismayed, without a word; speech fails them.
And should I wait, because they are silent, because they stand there with no reply?
No: I will speak in my turn, I too will tell what I know.
For I am full of words, the spirit within me presses me on.
Within me it is like wine under pressure, like new wineskins ready to burst.
I must speak to find relief, I must open my lips and answer.
I will take no one's side, I will flatter no one;
for I do not know how to flatter: my Maker would carry me off at once.

titres.titre: God speaks through dreams and suffering
The angel who intercedes and the ransom

versets.t: Now then, Job, hear my words, give ear to all that I say.
See: I open my mouth, my tongue speaks against my palate.
My words will spring from an upright heart, my lips will speak frankly what they know.
It is the spirit of God that made me, the breath of the Almighty that gives me life.
Answer me, if you can; prepare your defense and stand firm.
Before God, I am your equal; I too was pinched from clay.
So no dread of me will terrify you, and I will not crush you with any weight.
Now, you have said in my hearing, I have heard the sound of your words:
'I am pure, without sin; I am clean, there is no fault in me.
But God seeks pretexts against me, he treats me as an enemy;
he puts my feet in the stocks, he watches all my steps.'
Well, on this point you are wrong, I declare it to you, for God is greater than man.
Why bring this charge against him, on the ground that he answers none of your words?
For God speaks in one way, then in another, though no one heeds it.
He speaks in a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls upon men slumbering on their beds.
Then he opens their ears and seals within them his warnings,
to turn man away from his evil deed and to keep him from pride,
to spare his soul the pit, and his life the passage by the fatal blade.
He corrects him too by pain on his bed, by the constant shuddering of his bones.
Now he is sick of bread, and his appetite turns from the choicest food.
His flesh wastes away and vanishes, his bones once unseen jut out.
His soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the messengers of death.
If then there is beside him an angel, an intercessor, one among a thousand, to remind man of his duty,
God is gracious to him and says, 'Spare him from going down to the pit, I have found his ransom.'
His flesh takes on the freshness of youth, he recovers the days of his vigor.
He prays to God, who receives him with favor; he sees his face again with cries of joy, and God restores his innocence.
He sings before men and declares, 'I had sinned, I had twisted what was right, and God did not treat me as my fault deserved.
He has redeemed my soul from the passage to the pit, and my life beholds the light.'
See, all this God does, twice, three times, for a man,
to bring his soul back from the pit and light him with the light of the living.
Attend, Job, listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
If you have anything to say, answer me; speak, for I would gladly grant you the right.
If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.

titres.titre: Elihu's second speech: God cannot be unjust
The Almighty sees all and judges each
Is it for you to dictate the judgment?

versets.t: Elihu resumed and said:
You who are wise, hear my words; you who have knowledge, give me your ear.
For the ear tests words, as the palate tastes food.
Let us discern together what is right, let us recognize among ourselves what is good.
Job has said, 'I am innocent, and God denies me justice;
for all my right, I am called a liar; my wound is incurable, though I have not sinned.'
Is there a man like Job, who drinks in mockery like water,
who keeps company with those who work evil and walks with the wicked?
For he has said, 'Man gains nothing by seeking the favor of God.'
So listen to me, men of sense: far be wickedness from God, far be injustice from the Almighty!
He repays a man according to his deeds, he treats each according to his conduct.
No, in truth, God does no wrong, the Almighty does not pervert justice.
Who entrusted the earth to him? Who placed the whole world in his charge?
If he thought only of himself, if he withdrew to himself his spirit and his breath,
all flesh would perish in an instant, and man would return to the dust.
If you have understanding, hear this, give ear to the sound of my words.
Could an enemy of justice govern? Would you dare condemn the Just One, the Mighty,
he who says to a king, 'Scoundrel!', and to nobles, 'Villains!',
he who shows no favor to princes and does not prefer the rich to the poor, since all are the work of his hands?
In an instant they die: in the heart of the night a people is shaken and passes away, and the mighty is removed by no human hand.
For his eyes are fixed on the conduct of man, he sees each of his steps.
There is no darkness, no shadow of death, where those who work evil can hide.
God has no need to watch a man long to summon him to justice before him.
He shatters the mighty without inquiry and sets up others in their place.
He knows their works, then: he overturns them in a night, and there they are, crushed.
He strikes them down as guilty men, in a place where all can see,
because they turned away from him and took no account of any of his ways,
making the cry of the poor rise up to him, so that he heard the plea of the wretched.
If he stays silent, who will condemn him? If he hides his face, who can behold him? Yet he watches over nations as over each man,
to keep the godless from reigning and setting snares for the people.
Has anyone said to God, 'I have been punished, I will do wrong no more;
what I do not see, show me; if I have done injustice, I will not do it again'?
Is it for you that God must fix the reward, on the ground that you reject his judgment? It is for you to decide, not for me: say, then, what you know.
Men of sense will tell me so, and every wise man who hears me:
'Job speaks without knowledge, his words lack discernment.'
Oh, let Job be tested to the end, he who answers in the manner of the wicked!
To his fault he adds rebellion, he claps his hands in our midst and multiplies his words against God.

titres.titre: Your righteousness adds nothing to God
Why God does not answer the cries of pride

versets.t: Elihu spoke again and said:
Do you think you are in the right when you claim, 'I am right against God'?
For you ask, 'What good is it to be righteous? What do I gain by it more than if I had sinned?'
Well, I will answer you, you and your friends with you.
Lift your eyes to the heavens and look, contemplate the clouds, so high above you.
If you sin, what harm do you do him? If your faults pile up, what do you do to him?
If you are righteous, what do you give him? What does he receive from your hand?
Your wickedness touches only a man like yourself, and your righteousness benefits only mortals.
Men groan under the weight of oppression, they cry out under the arm of the powerful,
but no one says, 'Where is God, my Makers, who puts songs into the night,
who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of heaven?'
Then they cry out, but he does not answer, because of the pride of the wicked.
No, God does not listen to empty complaints, the Almighty pays them no heed.
And when you say you do not see him, know that your case is before him: wait for him.
But because his anger has not yet struck and he seems to ignore rebellion,
Job opens his mouth to say nothing and heaps up words without knowledge.

titres.titre: Elihu's last speech: God teaches through suffering
The rain, the clouds, the thunder

versets.t: Elihu went on and said:
Bear with me a little, and I will teach you: I have yet more to say on God's behalf.
I will draw my knowledge from afar, to do justice to my Maker.
Be assured, my words are no lie; before you stands a man of sound judgment.
See: God is mighty, but he despises no one; his power goes hand in hand with the wisdom of his heart.
He does not let the wicked live, and he grants justice to the afflicted.
He does not turn his eyes from the righteous; with kings on the throne he sets him forever, and there he is, exalted.
And if they are bound in chains, prisoners in the cords of misery,
he shows them their deeds, their faults and their pride;
he opens their ears to the lesson and calls them to turn from evil.
If they listen and submit, they end their days in happiness, their years in delight.
But if they do not listen, they perish by the sword and die for lack of knowledge.
The godless in heart nurse their anger; bound by God, they do not cry for help.
They die in the midst of youth, their life goes out like that of male prostitutes.
But God saves the afflicted by his very affliction, he opens his ear through the ordeal.
You too he would have drawn out from the jaws of distress into open space without limit, and your table would have overflowed with rich food.
But you are full of the case of the godless; judgment and sentence lay hold of you.
Beware that anger does not lead you into rebellion, and that a heavy ransom does not turn you aside.
Would your wealth be enough to spare you distress, with all the exertions of your strength?
Do not long for the night when peoples are carried off from their place.
Guard yourself from turning to evil, for that is what you seem to prefer to the ordeal.
See: God is sublime in his power; what master is like him?
Who has traced out his road for him? Who can say to him, 'You have done wrong'?
Remember rather to exalt his work, which men have sung.
All mortals contemplate it, each admires it from afar.
Yes, God is great, beyond what we know, and the number of his years is past our searching.
He draws up the drops of water, which distill as rain in his mist;
the clouds pour them down and make them stream upon the multitude of men.
Who then will understand the spreading of the clouds, the crashing of his tent?
See how he spreads his light around him and covers the depths of the sea.
By these he governs the peoples and gives food in abundance.
He holds the lightning in his hands and assigns it its mark.
The thunder announces his coming, and even the cattle sense the storm.

titres.titre: The voice of God in the storm
Job, consider the wonders of God
Before his majesty, man falls silent

versets.t: At this my heart trembles and leaps out of its place.
Listen, listen to the rumbling of his voice, the roll that comes out of his mouth!
Under the whole sky he unleashes it, and his lightning flashes to the ends of the earth.
Then a roar follows: he thunders with his majestic voice, and nothing holds him back when his voice resounds.
God thunders with a marvelous voice; he does great things beyond our grasp.
He says to the snow, 'Fall on the earth'; to the downpour and the torrential rains, he gives his mighty command.
He then seals the hand of every man, so that all may acknowledge his work.
The beasts reach their lair and stay in their dens.
From its chamber in the south comes the hurricane, and from the north winds comes the cold.
At the breath of God the ice forms, and the expanse of the waters freezes solid.
He loads the clouds with moisture and scatters the cloud of his lightning.
And it swirls this way and that, under his guidance, to carry out all his orders over the face of the inhabited world.
He sends it now to chastise the earth, now as a sign of faithful love.
Give ear to this, Job; stop and consider the wonders of God.
Do you know how God gives them their orders and makes the lightning of his cloud flash?
Do you understand how the clouds are balanced, those wonders of him whose knowledge is perfect?
You whose garments are hot when the earth grows drowsy under the south wind,
can you, like him, hammer out the sky until it is hard as a mirror of bronze?
Teach us, then, what we should say to him: in our ignorance we cannot find our words.
Must he be warned when I wish to speak? Has a man ever asked for his own ruin?
See: no one can fix his eyes on the brightness blazing in the clouds; but let a wind pass and sweep them away,
and out of the north comes a golden brightness. Around God shines a fearsome majesty.
The Almighty, we cannot reach him: great in strength, great in justice and full righteousness, he crushes no one.
That is why men fear him; but he does not regard those who think themselves wise.

titres.titre: The Lord answers out of the storm
Have you fathomed the sea, death, the light?
Do you govern the stars and the clouds?

versets.t: Then the Lord answered Job out of the storm, and said:
Who is this that darkens my design with words devoid of knowledge?
Come, gird up your loins like a man: I will question you, and you will instruct me.
Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell me, if your knowledge is so great.
Who fixed its measurements, do you know? Who stretched the measuring line over it?
On what are its bases sunk? Who laid its cornerstone,
while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
Who shut up the sea behind doors, when it burst forth from the womb,
when I gave it the cloud for a cloak and thick mist for swaddling bands,
when I set my limit for it, put doors and bars on it,
and said to it, 'This far you may come, no farther; here the pride of your waves shall halt'?
Since you came into being, have you ever commanded the morning, assigned the dawn its post,
that it might seize the earth by its edges and shake the wicked out of it?
Then the earth takes shape like clay under the seal, and everything stands out on it like the folds of a garment;
from the wicked their light is withheld, and the arm already raised is broken.
Have you gone down to the springs of the sea? Have you walked in the depths of the abyss?
Have the gates of death appeared to you? Have you seen the gates of the land of darkness?
Have you measured with your eye the whole expanse of the earth? Speak, if you know all this.
Where is the way to the dwelling of light? And the darkness, where does it reside,
that you might lead them to their domain and know the path to their home?
You know, of course, since you were already born, and your days are so many!
Have you entered the storehouses of the snow? Have you seen the granaries of the hail,
which I keep in reserve for times of distress, for days of battle and war?
By what way is the light spread abroad, and the east wind let loose upon the earth?
Who has cut a channel for the downpour and traced a road for the crashing lightning,
to bring rain on a land without men, on the desert where no one lives,
to water the desolate wastes and make the green grass spring up there?
Has the rain a father? Who begets the drops of dew?
From whose womb has the ice come? The frost of heaven, who gives it birth,
when the waters harden like stone and the surface of the abyss locks fast?
Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades or loose the cords of Orion?
Do you bring out the constellations in their season? Do you lead the Bear with her cubs?
Do you know the laws of the heavens? Do you fix their rule over the earth?
Do you raise your voice to the clouds so that a mass of water covers you?
Do you send out the lightnings, and do they say to you, 'Here we are'?
Who put wisdom in the clouds, who gave the sky its discernment?
Who has the skill to number the clouds, and to tip over the wineskins of heaven,
when the dust melts into a mass and the clods stick together?
Is it you who hunt the prey for the lioness and satisfy the hunger of the lion cubs,
when they crouch in their dens, lying in wait in the thicket?
Who prepares food for the raven, when its young cry out to God and wander for lack of food?

titres.titre: The wild beasts, free and untamed

versets.t: Do you know when the wild goats give birth? Have you watched the does in labor?
Have you counted the months of their carrying, do you know the time of their delivery,
when they crouch down, bring forth their young and are rid of their pangs?
Their fawns grow strong and thrive in the open; they go off, and return to them no more.
Who set the wild donkey free? Who loosed the bonds of the onager,
to whom I gave the steppe for a home and the salt land for a dwelling?
It scorns the din of the towns, it hears no driver's shouts.
It ranges the mountains for its pasture, searching for the least bit of green.
Will the wild ox be willing to serve you, will it spend the night at your manger?
Will you bind it with a rope to the furrow, will it harrow the valleys behind you?
Will you trust it because its strength is great? Will you leave your hard labor to it?
Will you count on it to bring in your harvest and gather it on your threshing floor?
The ostrich's wing beats merrily, but are its wing and plumage those of the stork?
No: she abandons her eggs to the ground and lets them warm on the sand,
forgetting that a foot may crush them, that a wild beast may trample them.
She is hard toward her young, as though they were not her own; little does she care to have labored in vain,
for God has denied her wisdom and given her no discernment.
But let her rise and take off, and she laughs at the horse and its rider.
Is it you who give the horse his valor and clothe his neck with a quivering mane?
Do you make him leap like the locust? His proud neighing spreads terror.
He paws in the valley, glorying in his strength, he charges into the fray of arms.
He laughs at fear, nothing frightens him, he does not shrink from the sword.
On him rattle the quiver, the flashing spear and the javelin.
Quivering, fierce, he devours the distance; at the sound of the horn, he cannot stand still.
At every blast he neighs, 'Forward!' From afar he scents the battle, the thundering voice of the chiefs and the war cries.
Is it by your wisdom that the falcon soars and spreads its wings toward the south?
Is it at your command that the eagle rises high and builds its nest on the heights?
It dwells on the rock, it spends the night there, on the crag of the stone, in its stronghold.
From up there it spies out its prey; its eyes reach far off.
Its young lap up blood; where the corpses are, there it is.

titres.titre: Job falls silent before the Lord
Second speech: have you the arm of God?

versets.t: The Lord spoke again to Job and said:
Will the one who contends with the Almighty give up? Let him who accuses God answer, then!
Then Job answered the Lord:
I am so slight: what could I answer you? I lay my hand upon my mouth.
I have spoken once, I will not answer again; twice, and I will add nothing more.
Then the Lord answered Job out of the storm, and said:
Gird up your loins like a man: I will question you, and you will instruct me.
Will you really annul my judgment, condemn me to put yourself in the right?
Have you an arm like God's? Can your voice thunder like his?
Then deck yourself with grandeur and height, clothe yourself in splendor and majesty!
Pour out the floods of your anger, with a glance bring down every proud man.
With a glance make every proud man bow, crush the wicked where they stand;
bury them all together in the dust, imprison their faces in the darkness.
Then I too will pay you homage, for your own right hand will have saved you.
Look now at Behemoth, which I made as I made you: it feeds on grass like the ox.
See what strength is in its loins, what power in the muscles of its belly!
It stiffens its tail like a cedar; the sinews of its thighs are knit together.
Its bones are tubes of bronze, its frame, bars of iron.
It is the masterwork of God; only its Maker can approach it, sword in hand.
The mountains offer it their pasture, there where all the wild beasts play.
It lies down under the lotus plants, hidden in the reeds of the marsh.
The lotus plants shelter it with their shade, the willows of the wadi surround it.
Let the river rage, it is not alarmed; it would stay calm though the Jordan surged up to its mouth.
Who will catch it by the eyes, pierce its nose with a snare?
Can you draw out Leviathan with a hook, or bind its tongue with a cord?
Can you pass a rush through its nostrils, or pierce its jaw with a hook?
Will it plead with you at length, address you with soft words?
Will it make a pact with you, will you take it as a slave for life?
Will you play with it as with a bird, will you leash it to amuse your daughters?
Will the fishermen put it up for sale, will the merchants divide it among themselves?
Will you riddle its skin with harpoons, or pierce its head with a fishing spear?
Just lay a hand on it: at the memory of the struggle, you will not try again.

titres.titre: The fire and the armor of the monster
The king over all the proud

versets.t: See: before it, all hope is dashed; the mere sight of it throws you to the ground.
No one is fool enough to rouse it. Who then would dare stand before me?
Who has given to me first, that I should repay him? Everything under heaven is mine.
I will not keep silent about its limbs, its power, or the grace of its build.
Who has ever stripped off the front of its armor? Who will enter its double row of teeth?
Who has opened the doors of its jaws? Around its fangs reigns terror.
Its back is made of rows of shields, welded as with a tight seal.
They touch one another, not even air passes between them.
They cling, they grip fast, inseparable.
Its sneezes throw off flashes of light, its eyes are like the gleams of dawn.
From its jaws come torches, sparks of fire leap out.
From its nostrils escapes smoke, as from a pot boiling over the reeds.
Its breath sets the coals ablaze, a flame comes out of its mouth.
In its neck lodges strength, and before it leaps dismay.
The folds of its flesh are welded, cast solid upon it, immovable.
Its heart is hard as stone, hard as the lower millstone.
When it rises up, the mighty are afraid, and terror drives them back.
The sword that reaches it does not hold, nor the lance, nor the dart, nor the arrow.
Iron, to it, is mere straw, and bronze, rotten wood.
The arrow does not put it to flight, sling stones are to it but chaff.
The club seems to it a wisp of straw, it laughs at the whir of the javelin.
Its underside bristles with sharp shards: it drags through the mud like a threshing sledge.
It makes the deep boil like a pot, it turns the sea into a jar of ointment.
Behind it a shining wake: you would think the abyss had turned white.
On earth it has no equal; it was made to fear nothing.
It looks down on all that thinks itself great: it is the king over all the proud beasts.

titres.titre: God vindicates Job before his friends
The Lord restores to Job double

versets.t: Then Job answered the Lord and said:
I know it: you can do all things, no plan is beyond your reach.
'Who is this that darkens my design without knowing anything?' Yes, I have spoken without understanding, of wonders beyond me that I do not know.
'Listen to me,' you said, 'and I will speak; I will question you, and you will instruct me.'
I knew you only by hearsay, but now my eyes have seen you.
That is why I retract and repent, upon the dust and ashes.

After speaking these words to Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz of Teman: 'My anger is kindled against you and your two friends, because you have not spoken of me with what is right, as my servant Job has done.

Now take seven bulls and seven rams, go to my servant Job and offer for yourselves a burnt offering. My servant Job will pray for you, and out of regard for him I will not deal with you according to your folly; for you have not spoken of me with what is right, as my servant Job has done.'
So Eliphaz of Teman, Bildad of Shuah and Zophar of Naamah went and did as the Lord had told them, and the Lord had regard for the prayer of Job.
And the Lord restored the fortunes of Job while he was praying for his friends; he even gave back to him double all that he had once possessed.

All his brothers, all his sisters and all who had known him before came to him and shared a meal with him in his house. They grieved with him and comforted him for all the misfortune the Lord had brought upon him, and each gave him a piece of silver and a ring of gold.
The Lord blessed the latter years of Job more than the first: he had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen and a thousand female donkeys.
He also had seven sons and three daughters.
He named the first Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
In all the land no women were as beautiful as the daughters of Job, and their father gave them a share of inheritance among their brothers.
After this, Job lived a hundred and forty years, and he saw his sons and his sons' sons, to the fourth generation.
Then Job died, old and full of days.
Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, who does not stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the company of mockers,
but who finds his joy in the law of the Lord and meditates on it day and night.
He is like a tree planted beside a stream: it yields its fruit in its season, its leaves do not wither, and all that he does prospers.
Not so the wicked: they are like chaff that the wind scatters.
So the wicked will not stand firm on the day of judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous.
For the Lord watches over the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked leads to ruin.
Why this raging of the nations, these hopeless plots of the peoples?
The kings of the earth rise up, the princes conspire together against the Lord and against his Anointed:
"Let us break their bonds," they say, "and throw off their chains from us!"
He who sits enthroned in the heavens laughs; the Lord makes sport of them.
Then he speaks to them in his anger, and his wrath fills them with terror:
"It is I who have established my king on Zion, my holy mountain."
I will proclaim the decree of the Lord. He said to me: "You are my Son; today I have begotten you.
Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, the whole earth as your domain.
You will break them with a rod of iron, you will shatter them like a potter's vessel."
And now, O kings, be wise; be instructed, you judges of the earth.
Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
Pay homage to the Son, lest he be angered and you perish on the way, for his anger is quick to blaze. Blessed are all who take refuge in him!
A song of David, when he fled from his son Absalom.
Lord, how many are my foes! How many rise up against me!
Many are saying of me: "For him there is no salvation in God!" Selah.
But you, Lord, are my shield; you are my glory, you lift up my head.
Aloud I cry to the Lord, and he answers me from his holy mountain. Selah.
I lie down and sleep; I wake again, for the Lord sustains me.
I have no fear of these countless people who beset me on every side.
Arise, Lord! Save me, my God! You strike all my enemies on the cheek, you break the teeth of the wicked.
Salvation belongs to the Lord! May your blessing rest upon your people! Selah.
To the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A psalm of David.
When I call, answer me, O God who upholds my right! In my distress you set me free; have pity on me and hear my prayer.
Sons of men, how long will you insult my glory, love what is empty and chase after lies? Selah.
Know this: the Lord has set apart his faithful one; the Lord hears when I call to him.
Tremble, and sin no more! Speak to your heart, in the night, upon your bed, and be silent. Selah.
Offer the sacrifices that please God, and put your trust in the Lord.
Many are asking: "Who will show us better days?" Let the light of your face shine upon us, Lord!
You have put into my heart more joy than they have when their grain and new wine abound.
In peace I lie down and at once fall asleep: you alone, Lord, make me dwell in safety.

titres.titre: A Morning Prayer Against the Wicked

versets.t: To the choirmaster. For the flutes. A psalm of David.
Give ear to my words, Lord, hear my whispered plea.
Attend to my cry for help, my King and my God! It is to you that I pray.
Lord, at daybreak you hear my voice; at daybreak I turn to you and wait.
For you are not a God who delights in evil; with you the wicked has no place.
The arrogant cannot stand before your eyes; you hate all who do evil.
You destroy those who speak lies; the man of blood and deceit the Lord abhors.
But I, through your great faithful love, will enter your house; filled with awe, I will bow down toward your holy temple.
Lord, lead me in your righteousness, for my enemies lie in wait; make your way straight before me.
Nothing in their mouth is sincere, their heart is nothing but ruin; their throat is an open grave, and their tongue turns smooth and flattering.
Make them pay, O God! Let them fall by their own designs! Drive them out for their countless crimes, for they have rebelled against you.
Then all who take refuge in you will rejoice; they will shout for joy without end, and you will protect them; those who love your name will exult in you.
For you, Lord, bless the righteous; your favor surrounds him like a shield.

titres.titre: The Plea of a Man Sorely Tried

versets.t: To the choirmaster. With stringed instruments, upon the octave. A psalm of David.
Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, do not chastise me in your wrath.
Have pity on me, Lord, for I am spent; heal me, Lord, for my bones tremble.
My soul is deeply shaken. And you, Lord, how long?
Turn back, Lord, deliver my soul; save me, for the sake of your faithful love.
For in death no one remembers you; in the realm of the dead, who will praise you?
I am worn out with groaning; every night I drench my bed with tears, I flood my couch with weeping.
My eyes waste away with grief; they fail because of all my oppressors.
Away from me, all you who do evil, for the Lord has heard the sound of my weeping.
The Lord has heard my plea, the Lord receives my prayer.
All my enemies will be covered with shame and terror; suddenly they will fall back, seized with shame.

titres.titre: An Appeal to the Just Judgment of God

versets.t: A lament of David, which he sang to the Lord concerning the words of Cush the Benjaminite.
Lord my God, in you I take refuge; save me from all my persecutors, deliver me,
lest they tear me apart like a lion and carry me off, with no one to rescue me.
Lord my God, if I have done this, if my hands are guilty,
if I have repaid with evil the one at peace with me, I who spared even my unjust adversary,
then let the enemy pursue me and overtake me, let him trample my life to the ground and lay my glory in the dust. Selah.
Arise, Lord, in your anger; rise up against the fury of my adversaries; awake for me, you who have decreed justice.
Let the assembly of the peoples gather around you; take your place above them, on high.
The Lord judges the peoples. Do me justice, Lord, according to my uprightness and my innocence.
Put an end to the malice of the wicked, and make the righteous stand firm, you who search hearts and inmost thoughts, O righteous God.
My shield is God, who saves the upright of heart.
God is a righteous judge, a God who each day makes his warning heard.
If the wicked will not turn back, God sharpens his sword, he bends his bow and takes aim;
he readies his deadly weapons, he sets his arrows aflame.
See the wicked man in labor with evil: he has conceived trouble and gives birth to lies.
He digs a pit, he makes it deep, and he falls into the hole he has made.
His malice recoils upon his own head, his violence comes down upon his own skull.
I will give thanks to the Lord for his justice, I will sing the name of the Lord, the Most High.

titres.titre: The Greatness of God and the Dignity of Man

versets.t: To the choirmaster. To the tune of Gath. A song of David.
Lord, our Lord, how magnificent is your name in all the earth! Your majesty is set above the heavens.
From the mouths of little children and infants you have fashioned praise, against your foes, to silence the enemy and the rebel.
When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars that you have set in place,
I ask: what is man, that you should think of him, the son of man, that you should care for him?
You have made him a little less than God, you have crowned him with glory and honor.
You have given him rule over the works of your hands, you have put all things under his feet:
sheep and oxen, all of them, and even the beasts of the wild,
the birds of the sky, the fish of the sea, all that travels the paths of the waters.
Lord, our Lord, how magnificent is your name in all the earth!

titres.titre: Praise to God, the Righteous Judge

versets.t: To the choirmaster. To the tune "Death to the Son." A psalm of David.
I will give thanks to the Lord with all my heart, I will tell of all your wonders.
I will rejoice and exult in you, I will sing your name, O Most High.
My enemies fall back, they stumble and vanish before you.
For you have upheld my right and my cause; upon your throne you sit as a righteous judge.
You have rebuked the nations, you have destroyed the wicked, you have blotted out their name forever and ever.
The enemy is finished, in everlasting ruins! You have razed their cities, and their memory has perished.
But the Lord is enthroned forever; he has set up his throne for judgment.
He judges the world with justice, he governs the peoples with fairness.
The Lord is a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of distress.
Those who know your name trust in you, for you do not forsake those who seek you, Lord.
Sing to the Lord, who dwells in Zion, proclaim his deeds among the peoples.
For he who avenges bloodshed remembers them; he does not forget the cry of the afflicted.
"Have pity on me, Lord! See the misery my enemies inflict on me, you who lift me up from the gates of death,
that I may proclaim all your praises at the gates of Zion and rejoice in your salvation."
The nations have fallen into the pit they dug; their foot is caught in the net they hid.
The Lord has made himself known, he has done justice; the wicked is snared by the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah.
Let the wicked return to the realm of the dead, all the nations that forget God.
For the poor will not be forgotten forever, the hope of the afflicted will not perish for all time.
Arise, Lord! Let no mortal prevail! Let the nations be judged before you!
Strike them with dread, Lord; let the nations know that they are only men! Selah.
Why, Lord, do you stand so far off? Why do you hide yourself in times of distress?
In his pride the wicked man hunts down the afflicted: may he be caught in the schemes he has devised!
The wicked man boasts of his greed; the extortioner blasphemes and despises the Lord.
Head held high, the wicked man does not seek God: "There is no God," is all his thought.
His affairs prosper at every turn. Your judgments are too lofty for him, he pays them no heed; his foes he sweeps away with a breath.
He says to himself: "Nothing will shake me; from age to age I will be safe from harm."
His mouth is full of cursing, deceit, and violence; under his tongue are malice and iniquity.
He lies in ambush near the villages; from hiding he kills the innocent; his eyes spy out the helpless.
Crouched in hiding like a lion in its thicket, he lies in wait to seize the poor; he seizes the poor, dragging him off in his net.
He stoops, he crouches, and the helpless fall into his clutches.
He says to himself: "God forgets, he hides his face, he never sees anything."
Arise, Lord! O God, lift up your hand! Do not forget the afflicted!
Why does the wicked man despise God? Why does he say to himself: "You will not call me to account"?
But you have seen! You yourself look upon trouble and grief, to take them in hand. To you the helpless entrusts himself; you are the helper of the orphan.
Break the arm of the wicked and evil man; call him to account for his crime, and it will be found no more.
The Lord is king forever and ever; the nations have vanished from his land.
Lord, you hear the desire of the humble; you strengthen their heart, you bend your ear,
to do justice for the orphan and the oppressed, so that man, formed from the earth, may spread terror no more.

titres.titre: The Confidence of the Righteous in the Midst of Danger

versets.t: To the choirmaster. Of David. In the Lord I take refuge. How can you say to me: "Flee to your mountain, like a bird!
For see, the wicked bend the bow, they fit their arrow to the string to shoot from the shadows at the upright of heart.
When the foundations are torn down, what can the righteous do?"
The Lord is in his holy temple, the Lord has his throne in the heavens. His eyes observe, his gaze examines mankind.
The Lord tests the righteous; but he hates the wicked and the lover of violence.
On the wicked he will rain down burning coals, fire, and brimstone; a scorching wind is the cup they will share.
For the Lord is righteous, he loves justice; the upright will see his face.
To the choirmaster. Upon the octave. A song of David.
Help, Lord! The faithful are gone, loyalty has vanished from among men.
They lie to one another; they speak with flattering lips and a double heart.
May the Lord cut off all flattering lips and the tongue that speaks with arrogance,
those who say: "Our strength is our word; our lips are our weapon: who could be our master?"
"Because of the oppression of the humble and the groaning of the poor, I will now arise, says the Lord; to the one who is despised I will bring salvation."
The words of the Lord are pure words, silver refined in the fire of the furnace, purified seven times.
You, Lord, will guard us; you will keep us forever safe from this breed.
All around us the wicked prowl, and vileness rises high among men.
To the choirmaster. A song of David.
How long, Lord? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?
How long must I bear anguish in my soul, and grief in my heart day after day? How long will my enemy prevail over me?
Look, and answer me, Lord my God! Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death,
lest my enemy say: "I have overcome him!" and my adversaries rejoice at my fall.
But I trust in your faithful love; my heart will exult in your salvation. I will sing to the Lord for the good he has done me.

titres.titre: The Folly of Those Who Deny God

versets.t: To the choirmaster. Of David. The fool says in his heart: "There is no God." They are corrupt, their deeds are abominable; not one does good.
From the height of heaven the Lord looks down on mankind to see if there is one who has understanding, one who seeks God.
All have turned away, all alike are corrupted; not one does good, not even one.
Have they understood nothing, all these evildoers who devour my people as they eat bread, and never call upon the Lord?
They will suddenly be seized with terror, for God is with the righteous.
You would mock the hope of the poor, but the Lord is his refuge.
Who will bring from Zion the deliverance of Israel? When the Lord restores the fortunes of his people, Jacob will exult, Israel will rejoice.

titres.titre: The Guest Worthy of the House of God

versets.t: A psalm of David. Lord, who may be received in your tent? Who may dwell on your holy mountain?
The one who walks without blame and does what is right, who speaks the truth from the depths of his heart.
He does not slander, he does no harm to another, he casts no dishonor on his neighbor.
In his eyes the vile man is contemptible, but he honors those who fear the Lord. Though he has sworn to his own hurt, he does not go back on his word.
He does not lend his money at interest and takes no bribe against the innocent. Whoever acts thus will never be shaken.

titres.titre: The Lord, My Inheritance and My Joy

versets.t: A poem of David. Keep me, O God: in you I take refuge.
I say to the Lord: "You are my Lord; you alone are my happiness."
As for the faithful who live in the land, those noble ones, all my delight is in them.
They multiply their idols, they run after other gods; but I will not pour out their offerings of blood, I will not take their names upon my lips.
Lord, my portion of inheritance and my cup, it is you who hold my destiny.
The measuring line has marked out for me a delightful place; yes, a splendid inheritance has fallen to me.
I bless the Lord who counsels me; even at night my conscience instructs me.
I keep the Lord ever before me; since he is at my right hand, I will not be shaken.
So my heart rejoices, my soul exults, and my body itself rests in safety.
For you will not abandon me to the realm of the dead, you will not let your faithful one see corruption.
You will make known to me the path of life: before your face, fullness of joy; at your right hand, delights forever.

titres.titre: The Prayer of a Righteous Man Persecuted

versets.t: A prayer of David. Lord, hear a just cause, attend to my cry; give ear to my prayer, which does not come from lying lips.
Let my vindication come from you, let your eyes discern what is right.
You have searched my heart, you have visited me by night, you have tested me in the crucible and found nothing: my mouth does not betray my thoughts.
Faced with the deeds of men, faithful to the word of your lips, I have kept myself from the paths of violence.
My steps have held to your tracks, my feet have not stumbled.
I call on you, for you answer me, O God; turn your ear to me, hear my word.
Show the wonder of your faithful love, you who save from their assailants those who take refuge at your right hand.
Keep me as the apple of your eye, hide me in the shadow of your wings,
far from the wicked who assail me, from the deadly enemies who surround me.
They shut themselves up in their fat, their mouths speak with arrogance.
Now they are upon my steps; already they encircle me, they watch for the moment to throw me to the ground.
They are like a lion hungry to tear, like a young beast crouching in ambush.
Arise, Lord, confront him, bring him down! By your sword, deliver me from the wicked;

by your hand, Lord, deliver me from these men, from these men whose portion is in this life. You fill their belly with your stores; their sons have their fill and leave still more to their little ones.
But I, in my uprightness, will see your face; when I awake, I will be satisfied with your presence.

titres.titre: The Thanksgiving of the Delivered King

versets.t: To the choirmaster. Of the servant of the Lord, David, who addressed to the Lord the words of this song on the day the Lord had delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.
He said: I love you, Lord, my strength!
Lord, my rock, my fortress, my deliverer; my God, the rock where I take shelter, my shield, the horn of my salvation, my stronghold!
I call on the Lord, worthy of praise, and I am saved from my enemies.
The bonds of death encircled me, the torrents of destruction terrified me;
the bonds of the realm of the dead surrounded me, the snares of death closed in on me.
In my distress I called on the Lord, I cried to my God; from his temple he heard my voice, and my cry reached his ears.
The earth quaked and shook, the foundations of the mountains trembled, convulsed by his anger.
Smoke rose from his nostrils, a devouring fire came from his mouth, blazing coals poured out from it.
He bent the heavens and came down, a dark cloud beneath his feet.
Mounted on a cherub, he flew, he soared on the wings of the wind.
He made darkness his hiding place, his tent around him: dark waters, somber clouds.
From the brightness before him his clouds burst forth, with hail and blazing coals.
The Lord thundered in the heavens, the Most High let his voice resound, with hail and blazing coals.
He loosed his arrows and scattered the enemy, he hurled his lightning and put them to flight.
Then the bed of the waters appeared, the foundations of the world were laid bare, at your rebuke, Lord, at the blast of the breath of your anger.
He reached down his hand from on high and seized me, he drew me out of the mighty waters.
He delivered me from a powerful enemy, from my adversaries stronger than I.
They had surprised me on the day of my calamity, but the Lord was my support.
He brought me out into open ground, he delivered me, because he loves me.
The Lord has dealt with me according to my righteousness, he has rewarded me according to the cleanness of my hands.
For I have kept the ways of the Lord, I have not turned from my God to evil.
All his ordinances were before me, I did not put aside his laws.
I was blameless before him, I kept myself from sin.
The Lord has rewarded me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands under his gaze.
With the good man you are good; with the man of integrity you are upright;
with the pure man you are pure; but with the crooked you deal shrewdly.
For you save the humble people, but you bring down the haughty eyes.
Yes, you light my lamp; the Lord my God brightens my darkness.
With you I charge the armed troop; with my God I leap over the wall.
God! His way is perfect, the word of the Lord is tried and true: he is a shield for all who take refuge in him.
Who is God, but the Lord? Who is a rock, but our God?
It is this God who girds me with strength and makes my way perfect,
who makes my feet swift as the deer's and holds me firm upon the heights,
who trains my hands for battle and my arms to bend the bow of bronze.
You give me your shield that saves, your right hand upholds me, your goodness makes me great.
You widen the road beneath my steps, and my ankles do not give way.
I pursue my enemies, I overtake them, and I do not return until I have finished them.
I strike them down, they cannot rise, they fall beneath my feet.
You gird me with strength for the battle, you make my adversaries bow beneath me.
You put my enemies to flight before me, and I destroy those who hate me.
They cry out, but no one saves them; they cry to the Lord, who does not answer.
I grind them like dust in the wind, I trample them like mud in the streets.
You deliver me from the revolts of the people, you set me at the head of the nations; a people I did not know is subject to me.
At the first word they obey me; foreigners cringe before me.
Foreigners lose heart, they come trembling from their strongholds.
The Lord lives! Blessed be my rock! Glory to the God who saves me,
this God who avenges me and subdues peoples under me,
who delivers me from my enemies! Yes, you raise me above my adversaries, you save me from the man of violence.
Therefore I will praise you among the nations, Lord, and I will sing your name.
To his king he gives great victories; he shows his faithful love to the one he has anointed, to David and his descendants, forever.

titres.titre: The Glory of God in Creation and the Law

versets.t: To the choirmaster. A song of David.
The heavens declare the glory of God, the firmament reveals the work of his hands.
Day speaks of it to day, night imparts knowledge to night.
It is not speech, there are no words; their voice is not heard.
Yet their call goes out through all the earth, and their language to the ends of the world. There, on high, God has pitched a tent for the sun;
