it comes out like a bridegroom from his chamber, joyful as a champion setting out on his course.
It rises at one end of the sky, its circuit ends at the other; nothing escapes its heat.
The law of the Lord is perfect: it restores life to the soul. The charter of the Lord is sure: it makes the simple wise.
The precepts of the Lord are right: they gladden the heart. The commandment of the Lord is clear: it gives light to the eyes.
The fear of the Lord is pure: it endures forever. The judgments of the Lord are true: all together they are just.
More desirable than gold, than the finest gold; sweeter than honey dripping from the comb.
Your servant too is enlightened by them; in keeping them there is great reward.
Who perceives his own errors? Cleanse me of those that escape me.
Keep your servant also from pride: let it not rule over me! Then I will be blameless and clear of any great sin.
May the words of my mouth and the murmuring of my heart find favor before you, Lord, my rock and my Redeemer!

titres.titre: A Prayer for the King on the Day of Battle

versets.t: To the choirmaster. A psalm of David.
May the Lord answer you on the day of distress! May the name of the God of Jacob protect you!
May he send you help from the sanctuary, and from Zion sustain you!
May he remember all your offerings and accept your sacrifices! Selah.
May he give you what your heart desires and bring all your plans to fulfillment!
Then we will shout for joy at your victory, we will raise the banner in the name of our God. May the Lord grant all your requests!
Now I know: the Lord has saved the one he has anointed; he answers him from his most holy heaven, by the victorious power of his right hand.
Some trust in chariots, others in horses; but we, in the name of the Lord our God!
They bow down and fall; but we rise up and stand firm.
Lord, save the king! Answer us on the day we call to you.
To the choirmaster. A psalm of David.
Lord, the king rejoices in your strength; how great is his joy in your help!
You have given him what his heart desired, you have not refused what his lips requested. Selah.
You came to meet him with rich blessings, you set on his head a crown of pure gold.
He asked you for life, and you gave it: length of days, forever and ever.
Through your help his glory is great; you clothe him with splendor and majesty.
You make him a source of blessings forever, you fill him with joy in your presence.
For the king trusts in the Lord; through the faithful love of the Most High, he will not be shaken.
Your hand will reach all your enemies, your right hand will strike those who hate you.
You will make them a blazing furnace on the day you appear; the Lord will engulf them in his anger, and fire will devour them.
You will wipe their offspring from the earth, their race from among men.
They plotted evil against you, they devised schemes: they will fail.
For you will put them to flight, you will bend your bow against them.
Arise, Lord, in your strength! We will sing and celebrate your power.

titres.titre: My God, My God, Why Have You Forsaken Me?

versets.t: To the choirmaster. To the tune "The Doe of the Dawn." A psalm of David.
My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? You stay far from my cry, far from my deliverance.
My God, I call by day, and you do not answer; by night, and I find no rest.
Yet you are holy, you who are enthroned amid the praises of Israel.
In you our fathers put their trust; they trusted, and you delivered them.
They cried to you and were saved; they trusted in you and were not disappointed.
But I am a worm and no longer a man, the scorn of the people, despised by all.
All who see me mock me; they sneer and shake their heads:
"He commits himself to the Lord: let him deliver him, let him save him, since he loves him!"
Yes, it was you who drew me from my mother's womb, who gave me trust at her breast.
From my birth I have been entrusted to you; from my mother's womb you are my God.
Do not stay far from me, for anguish is near, and there is no one to help.
Many bulls encircle me, the mighty beasts of Bashan close in on me.
They open their jaws against me, like a lion tearing and roaring.
I am poured out like water, all my bones are out of joint; my heart is like wax, it melts within me.
My strength is dried up like a potsherd, my tongue sticks to my palate; you lay me down in the dust of death.
Dogs surround me, a band of evildoers encircles me; they have pierced my hands and my feet.
I can count all my bones; they look on and gloat over me.
They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my tunic.
But you, Lord, do not stay far off! You, my strength, come quickly to my help!
Deliver my life from the sword, my very being from the grip of the dog!
Save me from the lion's jaws, rescue me from the horns of the wild ox! You have answered me!
I will proclaim your name to my brothers, I will praise you in the midst of the assembly:
"You who fear the Lord, praise him! All you descendants of Jacob, glorify him! Stand in awe of him, all you race of Israel!
For he has not despised nor rejected the poor in his misery; he has not hidden his face from him, but has heard him when he cried out to him."
From you comes my praise in the great assembly; I will fulfill my vows before those who fear you.
The poor will eat and be satisfied; those who seek the Lord will praise him. May you have life forever!
All the ends of the earth will remember and return to the Lord; all the families of the nations will bow down before him.
For kingship belongs to the Lord; he rules over the nations.
All the mighty of the earth will eat and bow down; before him will kneel all who go down to the dust, those who cannot keep themselves alive.
My descendants will serve him; the Lord will be proclaimed to the generations to come.
They will come and proclaim his righteousness to a people yet to be born: this is what he has done.
A psalm of David. The Lord is my shepherd: I lack nothing.
In green pastures he lets me rest; to still waters he leads me;
he restores my life. He guides me along the right path, for the honor of his name.
Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I fear no evil, for you are with me: your crook and your staff, they comfort me.
You set a table before me, in the sight of my enemies; you anoint my head with oil, my cup overflows.
Surely goodness and faithful love will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for length of days.

titres.titre: The Entrance of the King of Glory

versets.t: A psalm of David. To the Lord belong the earth and its riches, the world and all who dwell in it!
For it is he who founded it upon the seas and established it upon the waters.
Who will climb the mountain of the Lord? Who will stand in his holy place?
The one with innocent hands and a pure heart, who does not surrender his soul to falsehood and does not swear in order to deceive.
He will receive the blessing of the Lord and justice from the God who saves him.
Such is the people of those who seek him, who seek your face, God of Jacob! Selah.
Gates, lift up your lintels; rise up, ancient doors: let him enter, the King of glory!
Who then is this King of glory? It is the Lord, strong and mighty, the Lord, mighty in battle.
Gates, lift up your lintels; rise up, ancient doors: let him enter, the King of glory!
Who then is this King of glory? It is the Lord of hosts: he is the King of glory! Selah.

titres.titre: A Prayer of Trust and Forgiveness

versets.t: A psalm of David. To you, Lord, I lift up my soul.
My God, in you I trust: let me not be disappointed, let my enemies not triumph over me!
None who hope in you will be disappointed; shame is for those who betray without cause.
Lord, make your ways known to me, teach me your paths.
Guide me in your truth, instruct me, for you are the God who saves me; all day long I hope in you.
Remember, Lord, your tenderness and your faithful love: they are from all eternity.
Do not remember the sins and rebellions of my youth; in your faithful love remember me, for the sake of your goodness, Lord.
The Lord is good and upright: to those who stray he shows the way.
He leads the humble in justice, he teaches the humble his way.
All the paths of the Lord are love and faithfulness for those who keep his covenant and his precepts.
For the sake of your name, Lord, pardon my sin, great as it is.
To the one who fears the Lord, he shows the way to choose.
He himself will live in happiness, and his descendants will possess the land.
The Lord confides in those who fear him; he makes his covenant known to them.
I keep my eyes ever toward the Lord, for it is he who frees my feet from the net.
Turn to me, have pity on me, for I am alone and wretched.
Anguish grips my heart; draw me out of my distress!
See my misery and my pain, and forgive all my sins.
See how many are my enemies, how violent the hatred they bear me!
Guard my soul and deliver me; let me not be disappointed for having made you my refuge!
Let integrity and uprightness protect me, for I hope in you.
O God, deliver Israel from all its anguish!

titres.titre: The Prayer of an Upright Man

versets.t: Of David. Do me justice, Lord, for I have walked without blame; I trust in the Lord, I do not waver.
Examine me, Lord, test me, put my heart and my thoughts to the crucible.
For your love is before my eyes, and I walk in your truth.
I have not sat with liars, I do not associate with hypocrites;
I hate the company of evildoers, I do not sit with the wicked.
I wash my hands in innocence, and I go around your altar, Lord,
to proclaim your praise and tell of all your wonders.
Lord, I love the house where you dwell, the place where your glory resides.
Do not sweep me away with sinners, do not take my life with men of blood,
those whose hands are full of crime and whose right hand is laden with bribes.
But I walk without blame: deliver me, have pity on me.
My foot stands on level ground; in the assembly I will bless the Lord.

titres.titre: The Lord, My Light and My Salvation

versets.t: Of David. The Lord is my light and my salvation: whom shall I fear? The Lord is the stronghold of my life: before whom shall I tremble?
When the wicked advance against me to devour me, it is they, my adversaries and my enemies, who stagger and fall.
Though an army encamp against me, my heart is without fear; though war rise up against me, I keep my trust.
One thing I ask of the Lord, this I seek: to dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to taste the sweetness of the Lord and to gaze upon his sanctuary.
For he shelters me under his roof on the day of misfortune, he hides me in the secret of his tent, he lifts me high upon a rock.
Already my head rises above the enemies around me; in his tent I will offer sacrifices with shouts of joy, I will sing and make music to the Lord.
Hear, Lord, I call to you! Have pity on me, answer me!
My heart repeats your word: "Seek my face." It is your face, Lord, that I seek.
Do not hide your face from me, do not turn away your servant in anger. You are my help: do not leave me, do not forsake me, O God who saves me!
Though my father and my mother forsake me, the Lord will take me in.
Teach me your way, Lord; lead me along a safe path, because of those who lie in wait for me.
Do not hand me over to the fury of my adversaries: false witnesses rise against me, men who breathe only violence.
I am sure of this: I will see the goodness of the Lord in the land of the living.
Hope in the Lord! Be strong, take courage, and hope in the Lord!

titres.titre: A Cry to the Lord, My Rock

versets.t: Of David. To you, Lord, I cry; my rock, do not be deaf to me! If you keep silent, I will be like those who go down to the pit.
Hear my pleading voice when I cry to you, when I lift up my hands toward your most holy sanctuary.
Do not sweep me away with the wicked and the evildoers, who speak of peace to their neighbor while their heart is full of malice.
Repay them according to their deeds and their misdeeds; repay them according to the work of their hands, give them their due.
For they have no regard for the works of the Lord, for the labor of his hands; may he tear them down and never build them up again!
Blessed be the Lord, for he has heard my pleading voice!
The Lord is my strength and my shield; in him my heart trusts. He has helped me: my heart exults, and I praise him with my song.
The Lord is the strength of his people, the refuge that saves the one he has anointed.
Save your people, bless your inheritance; be their shepherd and carry them forever.

titres.titre: The Voice of the Lord in the Storm

versets.t: A psalm of David. Give to the Lord, you heavenly beings, give to the Lord glory and power!
Give to the Lord the glory of his name, worship the Lord, radiant in holiness.
The voice of the Lord is over the waters; the God of glory makes the thunder roll, the Lord is over the vast waters.
The voice of the Lord is mighty, the voice of the Lord is majestic.
The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars, the Lord shatters the cedars of Lebanon;
he makes Lebanon leap like a young bull, and Mount Sirion like a young wild ox.
The voice of the Lord flashes forth flames of fire.
The voice of the Lord shakes the wilderness, the Lord shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.
The voice of the Lord makes the deer give birth and strips the forests bare; and in his temple all cry: "Glory!"
The Lord was enthroned above the flood; the Lord sits enthroned as king forever.
The Lord will give strength to his people; the Lord will bless his people with peace.

titres.titre: Thanksgiving of One Rescued from Death

versets.t: A psalm. A song for the dedication of the Temple. Of David.
I exalt you, Lord: you have lifted me up, you have not let my enemies rejoice over me.
Lord my God, I cried to you, and you healed me.
Lord, you brought me up from the realm of the dead, you gave me back my life as I was going down to the pit.
Sing to the Lord, you his faithful ones; celebrate the memory of his most holy name.
His anger lasts but a moment, but his favor lasts a lifetime; at evening come tears, and at morning, shouts of joy.
In my carefree days I said to myself: "Nothing will ever shake me!"
Lord, by your favor you had set me on a strong mountain; but you hid your face, and I was overwhelmed.
To you, Lord, I cried, I pleaded with my God:
"What good is my death, my descent into the grave? Will the dust praise you? Will it proclaim your faithfulness?
Hear, Lord, have pity on me; Lord, come to my help!"
Then you changed my mourning into dancing; you loosened my garment of mourning and clothed me with joy.
So my heart will sing to you and not be silent. Lord my God, I will praise you forever.

titres.titre: Trust and Distress: Into Your Hands I Commit My Spirit

versets.t: To the choirmaster. A psalm of David.
Lord, in you I take refuge: let me never be disappointed! In your justice, deliver me.
Turn your ear to me, hasten to deliver me! Be for me a protecting rock, a fortress where I find salvation.
Yes, you are my rock and my fortress: for the honor of your name, you guide me and lead me.
You will free me from the net they have set for me, for you are my shelter.
Into your hands I commit my spirit; you will deliver me, Lord, God of truth.
I hate those who cling to empty idols; but I, I trust in the Lord.
I will exult with joy in your faithful love, for you have seen my misery, you have known the anguish of my soul.
You have not handed me over to the enemy, you have set my feet in open ground.
Have pity on me, Lord, for I am in distress; grief consumes my eyes, my soul, and my inmost being.
My life wastes away in sorrow, my years in groaning; my strength fails under the weight of my guilt, and my bones waste away.
To all my adversaries I have become an object of scorn, a burden to my neighbors, a terror to my friends; those who see me outside flee far from me.
I am forgotten like a dead man, erased from memory; I am like a broken vessel.
I hear the slander of the crowd, terror on every side; they conspire against me, they plot to take my life.
But I trust in you, Lord; I say: "You are my God!"
My days are in your hand; deliver me from the hand of my enemies and my persecutors.
Let your face shine upon your servant, save me by your faithful love.
Lord, let me not be disappointed for having called on you! Let shame be for the wicked; let them go down in silence to the realm of the dead!
Let them be silenced, the lying lips that speak with arrogance against the righteous, full of pride and contempt!
How great is your goodness! You keep it in store for those who fear you, you lavish it, in the sight of all, on those who take refuge in you.
You hide them in the shelter of your presence, far from the intrigues of men; you shelter them under your tent, far from the tongues that assail them.
Blessed be the Lord: his faithful love for me has done wonders, he has set me in a fortified city.
In my alarm I had said: "I am driven far from your sight!" But you heard my pleading voice when I cried to you.
Love the Lord, all you his faithful ones! The Lord watches over the faithful, but he repays the proud in full.
Be strong, take courage, all you who hope in the Lord!
Of David. A meditation. Blessed is the man whose fault is taken away, whose sin is pardoned!
Blessed is the man to whom the Lord charges no guilt, and in whose spirit there is no deceit!
As long as I kept silent, my strength was spent in groaning all day long.
Day and night your hand lay heavy on me; my sap dried up as in the heat of summer. Selah.
Then I confessed my sin to you, I no longer hid my fault. I said: "I will confess my rebellions to the Lord," and you took away the weight of my sin. Selah.
So let every faithful one pray to you in the time of favor! Even if the great waters overflow, they will not reach him.
You are my shelter, you guard me from distress, you surround me with songs of deliverance. Selah.
"I will instruct you, I will show you the way to go; I will counsel you, my eye upon you.
Do not be like the horse or the mule, without understanding, that must be curbed with bit and bridle to be brought near you."
The wicked man has many torments, but whoever trusts in the Lord, faithful love surrounds him.
Righteous ones, rejoice in the Lord and exult! Shout for joy, all you upright of heart!

titres.titre: A Hymn to the Faithful Creator God

versets.t: Righteous ones, shout for joy to the Lord! Praise befits the upright.
Give thanks to the Lord on the harp, make music to him on the ten-stringed lute.
Sing to him a new song, blend your instruments skillfully with your shouts of joy.
For the word of the Lord is upright, and all his work is faithful.
He loves justice and right; the earth is filled with the faithful love of the Lord.
By the word of the Lord the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of his mouth.
He gathers the waters of the sea as in a wineskin, he stores up the depths in reservoirs.
Let all the earth fear the Lord, let all who dwell in the world stand in awe of him!
For he spoke, and it was; he commanded, and it came to be.
The Lord frustrates the plans of the nations, he brings to nothing the designs of the peoples.
But the plans of the Lord stand forever, and the thoughts of his heart from age to age.
Blessed is the nation whose God is the Lord, blessed the people he has chosen as his inheritance!
From the height of heaven the Lord looks down and sees all mankind;
from the place where he dwells he observes all who live on the earth,
he who shapes the heart of each and discerns all their deeds.
It is not the great army that saves the king, nor his great strength that delivers the warrior.
The horse can save no one, and all its vigor does not guarantee victory.
The gaze of the Lord watches over those who fear him, over those who hope in his faithful love,
to snatch their life from death and keep them alive in time of famine.
Our soul waits for the Lord: he is our help and our shield.
In him our heart finds its joy, in his holy name we place our trust.
May your faithful love, Lord, be upon us, as we put our hope in you!

titres.titre: Taste and See That the Lord Is Good

versets.t: Of David, when he feigned madness before Abimelech and was driven away by him.
I will bless the Lord at all times, his praise always on my lips.
I glory in the Lord: let the humble hear and rejoice!
Magnify the Lord with me, let us exalt his name together.
I sought the Lord, and he answered me, he delivered me from all my fears.
Those who look to him are radiant with joy, their faces will never be ashamed.
This poor man cried out, the Lord heard him, he saved him from all his troubles.
The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him, and he delivers them.
Taste and see that the Lord is good! Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him!
Fear the Lord, you his holy ones: those who fear him lack nothing.
Young lions know want and hunger, but those who seek the Lord lack nothing good.
Come, my sons, listen to me: I will teach you the fear of the Lord.
Which of you loves life and longs for many days of happiness?
Guard your tongue from evil and your lips from deceitful words;
turn away from evil and do good, seek peace and pursue it.
The eyes of the Lord turn toward the righteous, his ears toward their cry.
But the Lord sets his face against those who do evil, to blot out their memory from the earth.
The righteous cry out, the Lord hears them, he delivers them from all their troubles.
The Lord is close to the brokenhearted, he saves those whose spirit is crushed.
The righteous man knows many misfortunes, but from them all the Lord delivers him:
he guards each of his bones, not one will be broken.
Evil will slay the wicked, and the enemies of the righteous will be punished.
The Lord redeems the life of his servants; none who take refuge in him will be punished.
Of David. Lord, contend with those who contend with me, make war on those who make war on me!
Take up shield and buckler, arise to help me!
Brandish spear and lance against my pursuers; say to my soul: "I am your salvation!"
Shame and rout to those who seek my life! Let them fall back, covered with shame, those who plot my ruin!
Let them be like chaff before the wind, driven off by the angel of the Lord!
Let their way be dark and slippery, with the angel of the Lord at their heels!
For without cause they hid their net to trap me, without cause they dug a pit for my life.
Let ruin come upon him unawares, let the hidden net catch him, let him fall into it and perish!
Then my soul will exult in the Lord, rejoicing in his salvation.
With my whole being I will say: "Lord, who is like you? You deliver the weak from the one stronger than he, the weak and the poor from the one who plunders them."
False witnesses rise up, they question me about things I do not know.
They repay me evil for good: here I am, alone and forsaken.
Yet I, when they were sick, wore a garment of mourning, I humbled myself with fasting, and my prayer kept returning to my heart.
As for a friend, for a brother, I went about; as in mourning for a mother, I was bowed down with grief.
But when I stumbled, they rejoiced and gathered together; people I do not know band against me, they tear at me without ceasing.
Like true profaners, mockers and scoffers, they gnash their teeth at me.
Lord, how long will you look on? Snatch my life from their ravages, my only treasure from these lions.
I will praise you in the great assembly, I will celebrate you before a numerous people.
Let them not rejoice over me, these enemies without cause! Let them not wink the eye, those who hate me without reason!
For they do not speak of peace; against the peaceful of the land they devise deceits.
With mouths wide open against me, they say: "Aha! Aha! We have seen it with our own eyes!"
You, Lord, have seen: do not keep silent! Lord, do not stay far from me!
Awake, arise for my cause, my God and my Lord, to defend my case!
Judge me according to your justice, Lord my God, and let them not rejoice over me!
Let them not say to themselves: "At last, we have what we wanted!" Let them not say: "We have swallowed him up!"
Shame and rout, all together, to those who rejoice at my misfortune! Let them be covered with shame and contempt, those who triumph over me!
Joy and gladness to those who desire my vindication! Let them say without ceasing: "Glory to the Lord, who desires the peace of his servant!"
And my tongue will retell your justice, your praise, all day long.

titres.titre: The Malice of Man and the Source of Life

versets.t: To the choirmaster. Of David, the servant of the Lord.
Sin speaks to the wicked man, deep in his heart; before his eyes there is no fear of God.
For he flatters himself, so much that he does not see his fault or hate it.
The words of his mouth are falsehood and malice; he has given up understanding and doing good.
Upon his bed he plots evil; he sets himself on an evil course, refusing to reject what is wrong.
Lord, your love rises to the heavens, your faithfulness to the clouds.
Your justice is like the high mountains, your judgments like the vast deep. Man and beast, Lord, you save.
How precious is your faithful love, O God! Men take refuge in the shadow of your wings.
They feast on the abundance of your house, you give them to drink from the torrent of your delights.
For in you is the source of life, and by your light we see light.
Keep your faithful love for those who know you, your justice for the upright of heart.
Let not the foot of the proud crush me, nor the hand of the wicked drive me away!
There they lie fallen, the evildoers; struck down, they cannot rise.

titres.titre: The Fate of the Righteous and the Wicked

versets.t: Of David. Do not fret over the wicked, do not envy those who do evil.
Quickly, like grass, they are cut down; like the green herb, they wither.
Trust in the Lord and do good; dwell in the land and cultivate faithfulness.
Find your delight in the Lord, and he will give you what your heart desires.
Commit your way to the Lord; trust in him, and he will act.
He will make your justice shine like the light, and your right like the noonday sun.
Be still before the Lord and hope in him; do not fret over the one who prospers, over the man who carries out his schemes.
Let go of anger, forsake wrath; do not fret: it leads only to evil.
For the wicked will be cut off, but those who hope in the Lord will possess the land.
A little while, and the wicked man is no more; you look for his place, and he has vanished.
But the meek will possess the earth, they will enjoy deep peace.
The wicked man plots against the righteous, he gnashes his teeth at him;
but the Lord laughs at him, for he sees his day coming.
The wicked draw the sword, they bend the bow to strike down the poor and the afflicted, to slaughter the upright.
Their sword will enter their own heart, and their bows will be broken.
Better the little of the righteous than the wealth of all the wicked;
for the arms of the wicked will be broken, but the Lord upholds the righteous.
The Lord knows the days of the blameless; their inheritance will last forever.
In time of misfortune they will not be disappointed; in days of famine they will be satisfied.
But the wicked will perish; the enemies of the Lord, like the splendor of the meadows, will go up in smoke, they will vanish.
The wicked man borrows and does not repay; but the righteous is generous and gives.
Those whom the Lord blesses will possess the land, those whom he curses will be cut off.
The Lord makes firm the steps of a man, he delights in his way.
Though he falls, he does not stay down, for the Lord holds him by the hand.
I was young, and now I am old: never have I seen the righteous forsaken, nor his children begging for bread.
All day long he is generous and lends; his descendants will be blessed.
Turn away from evil and do good: you will dwell forever.
For the Lord loves justice, he does not forsake his faithful ones; they are guarded forever, but the descendants of the wicked will be cut off.
The righteous will possess the land, they will dwell in it forever.
The mouth of the righteous murmurs wisdom, his tongue speaks what is right.
The law of his God is in his heart, and his steps do not falter.
The wicked man watches the righteous, he seeks to put him to death;
but the Lord does not abandon him to his hands, nor let him be condemned at the judgment.
Wait for the Lord and keep his way: he will raise you up, and you will possess the land; you will see the wicked cut off.
I saw the wicked man, arrogant, spreading himself like a tree full of sap;
I passed by again: he was no more; I looked for him, and he could not be found.
Observe the blameless man, look at the upright man: there is a future for the man of peace.
But the rebels will all be destroyed, the future of the wicked will be cut off.
The salvation of the righteous comes from the Lord: he is their refuge in time of distress.
The Lord helps them and delivers them; he delivers them from the wicked and saves them, because they take refuge in him.

titres.titre: The Plea of a Sinner Overwhelmed

versets.t: A psalm of David. For remembrance.
Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger, do not chastise me in your wrath.
For your arrows have struck me, your hand has come down on me.
Nothing is sound in my flesh because of your anger; nothing is whole in my bones because of my sin.
My faults rise above my head, they crush me like a burden too heavy.
My wounds are foul and festering, because of my folly.
Bent low, utterly crushed, all day long I go about in mourning.
My loins burn with fever, and nothing is sound in my flesh.
I am worn out, crushed beyond measure; the groaning of my heart makes me cry out.
Lord, all my longing is before you, and my sighing is not hidden from you.
My heart pounds, my strength fails me, and even the light of my eyes goes out.
My friends and companions keep away from my affliction; my kin stand far off.
Those who seek my life set snares for me; those who seek my ruin utter threats and, all day long, plot deceit.
But I, like a deaf man, do not hear; like a mute, I do not open my mouth.
I am like a man who hears nothing and has no reply on his lips.
For it is in you, Lord, that I hope; you will answer, Lord my God.
I said to myself: "Let them not rejoice over me, let them not triumph if my foot slips!"
For I am near to falling, my pain is ever before me.
Yes, I confess my guilt, my sin fills me with anguish.
But my enemies, full of life, are strong; many are those who hate me without cause.
They repay me evil for good, they accuse me because I seek the good.
Do not forsake me, Lord! My God, do not stay far from me!
Come quickly to my help, Lord, my salvation!
To the choirmaster, for Jeduthun. A song of David.
I said to myself: "I will watch over my conduct, so as not to sin with my tongue; I will put a curb on my mouth as long as the wicked is before me."
I stayed silent, in stillness; I held my peace, saying nothing, even of the good. But my pain grew worse,
my heart burned within me; as I brooded, a fire was kindled, and the word burst from my tongue:
"Make known to me, Lord, the end of my life, the measure of my days; let me know how frail I am.
See: you have made my days a few handbreadths, and my lifetime is nothing before you. Yes, every man, however firm he stands, is but a breath. Selah.
Yes, man passes like a shadow; he bustles about for nothing, he heaps up wealth without knowing who will gather it.
And now, Lord, what am I to hope for? My hope is in you.
Deliver me from all my faults; do not make me the scorn of the fool.
I am silent, I open my mouth no more, for it is you who act.
Take your blows away from me; under the harshness of your hand, I am undone.
When you correct a man, punishing him for his fault, you consume like a moth what he holds most dear. Yes, every man is but a breath. Selah.
Hear my prayer, Lord, give ear to my cry, do not be deaf to my tears. For with you I am a resident alien, a passing guest, like all my fathers.
Turn your gaze away from me, that I may breathe a little, before I depart and am no more."

titres.titre: Here I Am, I Come to Do Your Will

versets.t: To the choirmaster. Of David. A psalm.
I waited and waited for the Lord; he bent down to me, he heard my cry.
He drew me up from the fatal pit, from the mire of the bog; he set my feet upon the rock, he made my steps firm.
He put into my mouth a new song, a praise to our God. Many will see, they will fear the Lord and put their trust in him.
Blessed is the man who puts his trust in the Lord, who does not turn to the proud nor to the followers of lies!
How many wonders you have done, Lord my God, how many plans for us! None can compare with you. I would tell them and proclaim them, but they are beyond all telling.
You wanted neither sacrifice nor offering, but you have fashioned a body for me; you asked neither burnt offering nor sin offering.
Then I said: "Here I am, I come. In the scroll of the book it is written of me
that I should do your will, O my God; and your law is deep within my heart."
I have proclaimed your justice in the great assembly; I have not closed my lips, Lord, you know it.
I have not hidden your justice deep in my heart; I have proclaimed your faithfulness and your salvation, I have not concealed your love and your truth before the great assembly.
You, Lord, do not withhold your tenderness from me; may your love and your truth always keep me!
For misfortunes without number besiege me, my faults have overtaken me and I can no longer see; they are more numerous than the hairs of my head, and my heart fails me.
Be pleased, Lord, to deliver me! Lord, come quickly to my aid!
Shame and rout to all who seek my life! Let them fall back, covered with shame, those who seek my ruin!
Let them be struck with dismay and shame, those who jeer at me: "Aha! Aha!"
But joy and gladness in you to all who seek you! Let them say without ceasing: "Glory to the Lord!" those who love your salvation.
I, poor and afflicted, the Lord thinks of me. You are my help and my deliverer: my God, do not delay!

titres.titre: The Prayer of a Sick Man Betrayed

versets.t: To the choirmaster. A psalm of David.
Blessed is the one who considers the poor! On the day of misfortune, the Lord will deliver him.
The Lord will guard him and keep him alive, happy on the earth; he will not hand him over to the greed of his enemies.
The Lord will sustain him on his bed of suffering; in his sickness, you remake his whole bed.
I say: "Lord, have pity on me, heal me, for I have sinned against you!"
My enemies wish me the worst: "When will he die? When will his name be blotted out?"
If one of them comes to see me, he speaks only emptiness; his heart gathers up malice, and outside he spreads it.
All who hate me whisper together against me; against me they imagine my ruin:
"A deadly plague has fastened on him; there he lies, he will rise no more!"
Even my friend, in whom I trusted and who ate my bread, has lifted his heel against me.
But you, Lord, have pity on me, raise me up, and I will repay them their due.
By this I will know that you love me: if my enemy does not triumph over me.
As for me, you uphold me in my integrity, you establish me forever in your presence.
Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! Amen! Amen!
For the choirmaster. Of the sons of Korah. A poem.
As a deer longs for streams of water, so my soul longs for you, O God.
My soul thirsts for God, for the living God: when shall I come and appear before God?
My tears have been my bread, day and night, while they say to me all day long, "Where is your God?"
I remember, and my soul melts within me: how I walked with the throng, leading the procession to the house of God, amid shouts of joy and thanksgiving, a multitude keeping festival.
Why are you cast down, O my soul, why do you groan within me? Hope in God! For I will praise him again, my Saviour and my God.
My soul is downcast within me; therefore I remember you, from the land of the Jordan, from Hermon and Mount Mizar.
Deep calls to deep at the roar of your cataracts; all your waves and your breakers have swept over me.
By day the Lord sends forth his faithful love; by night his song is with me, a prayer to the God of my life.
I say to God, my rock, "Why have you forgotten me? Why must I go about in mourning, oppressed by the enemy?"
My bones are crushed when my persecutors taunt me, saying to me all day long, "Where is your God?"
Why are you cast down, O my soul, why do you groan within me? Hope in God! For I will praise him again, my Saviour and my God.

titres.titre: Prayer to return to the altar of God

versets.t: Do me justice, O God, and defend my cause against a faithless people; from the deceitful and wicked man, deliver me.
For you are the God of my strength. Why have you rejected me? Why must I go about in mourning, oppressed by the enemy?
Send forth your light and your truth: let them guide me, let them lead me to your holy mountain, to your dwelling.
Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my joy and my gladness; I will praise you with the harp, O God, my God.
Why are you cast down, O my soul, why do you groan within me? Hope in God! For I will praise him again, my Saviour and my God.
For the choirmaster. Of the sons of Korah. A poem.
O God, we have heard with our own ears, our fathers have told us: the work you did in their days, in days of old.
With your hand you drove out nations to plant them; you struck down peoples to let them flourish.
It was not their sword that won the land, nor their arm that saved them, but your right hand, your arm, and the light of your face, for you loved them.
You are my king, O God: ordain the victories of Jacob!
Through you we drive back our enemies; through your name we trample our foes.
For I do not trust in my bow, and my sword will not save me.
It is you who save us from our enemies and put to shame those who hate us.
In God we glory all day long; we will praise your name for ever. Selah.
Yet you have rejected us and put us to shame; you no longer go out with our armies.
You make us retreat before the enemy, and those who hate us plunder us.
You hand us over like sheep for slaughter, you scatter us among the nations.
You sell your people for nothing, gaining no profit from the sale.
You make us the scorn of our neighbours, the mockery and derision of those around us.
You make us a byword among the nations; the peoples shake their heads at us.
All day long my disgrace is before me, and shame covers my face,
at the taunts and insults, before the enemy bent on revenge.
All this has come upon us, though we had not forgotten you, nor betrayed your covenant.
Our heart has not turned back, our steps have not strayed from your path;
yet you have crushed us in the haunt of jackals, and covered us with the shadow of death.
If we had forgotten the name of our God and stretched out our hands to a foreign god,
would God not have found it out, he who knows the secrets of the heart?
But for your sake we are slain all day long, treated as sheep for slaughter.
Awake! Why do you sleep, O Lord? Rise up, do not reject us for ever!
Why do you hide your face, forgetting our misery and our distress?
For our soul is sunk down in the dust, our body clings to the ground.
Rise up, come to our help! Redeem us, for the sake of your faithful love.

titres.titre: A song for the king's wedding

versets.t: For the choirmaster. To the tune "The Lilies." Of the sons of Korah. A poem. A love song.
My heart overflows with a noble song; I dedicate my work to the king. May my tongue be the ready pen of a skilled scribe!
You are the fairest of the children of men, grace is poured upon your lips: therefore God has blessed you for ever.
Gird your sword upon your side, O warrior, in your splendour and your majesty!
In your majesty, ride forth; ride on for truth, meekness, and justice; may your right hand achieve deeds of awe!
Your arrows are sharp, peoples fall beneath your feet, they pierce the hearts of the king's enemies.
Your throne, O God, endures for ever; your royal sceptre is a sceptre of justice.
You love justice and hate evil; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions.
Myrrh, aloes, and cassia perfume all your robes; from palaces of ivory, the lyres gladden you.
Daughters of kings are among your favourites; at your right hand stands the queen, adorned with the gold of Ophir.
"Listen, my daughter, look and incline your ear: forget your people and your father's house.
The king will desire your beauty. He is your lord: bow down before him.
Then, with gifts, the city of Tyre and the richest of peoples will seek your favour."
All glorious, the king's daughter comes within, clothed in a robe woven with gold.
In embroidered garments she is led to the king; behind her, her companions, the maidens, are brought to you.
They are led in joy and gladness, they enter the palace of the king.
Your sons will take the place of your fathers; you will make them princes over all the earth.
I will make your name live from age to age; therefore the peoples will praise you for ever and ever.

titres.titre: God, our refuge and our strength

versets.t: For the choirmaster. Of the sons of Korah. For the maidens' voices. A song.
God is our refuge and our strength, an ever-present help in distress.
Therefore we fear not, though the earth be shaken, though the mountains topple into the heart of the seas,
though its waters roar and foam, though their fury shakes the mountains. Selah.
A river and its streams gladden the city of God, the holiest dwelling of the Most High.
God is in her midst: she will not be moved; at the break of day, God comes to her help.
Nations rage, kingdoms totter; he lifts his voice, and the earth melts away.
The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. Selah.
Come, see the mighty deeds of the Lord, the desolations he has brought upon the earth!
He puts an end to wars to the ends of the earth, he breaks the bow, snaps the spear, and burns the chariots with fire:
"Be still, and know that I am God, sovereign over the nations, sovereign over the earth!"
The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. Selah.

titres.titre: God, king of all the earth

versets.t: For the choirmaster. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.
All you peoples, clap your hands; acclaim God with shouts of joy!
For the Lord, the Most High, is awesome, a great king over all the earth.
He subdues peoples under us, and nations beneath our feet.
He chooses our heritage for us, the pride of Jacob, whom he loves. Selah.
God ascends amid shouts of joy, the Lord, to the sound of the trumpet.
Sing to God, sing! Sing to our king, sing!
For God is king of all the earth: sing his praise with skill!
God reigns over the nations, God sits on his holy throne.
The princes of the peoples gather with the people of the God of Abraham. For to God belong the shields of the earth: he is greatly exalted.
A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
Great is the Lord, highly to be praised in the city of our God! His holy mountain,
beautiful in its height, the joy of all the earth, is Mount Zion, in the far north, the city of the great king.
Within her palaces, God has shown himself a sure refuge.
See how kings had banded together, together they advanced.
The moment they saw her, they were astounded; seized with panic, they fled.
There trembling took hold of them, anguish like a woman in labour.
By the east wind you shattered the ships of Tarshish.
What we had heard, we have now seen in the city of the Lord of hosts, the city of our God: God makes her secure for ever. Selah.
O God, we recall your faithful love within your temple.
Like your name, O God, your praise reaches the ends of the earth. Your right hand is full of justice.
Let Mount Zion rejoice, let the towns of Judah exult because of your judgements!
Walk about Zion, go all around her, count her towers;
consider her ramparts, review her palaces, that you may tell the next generation:
Such is God, our God for ever and ever: he it is who will lead us.
For the choirmaster. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
Hear this, all you peoples; give ear, all you inhabitants of the world,
both low and high, rich and poor alike.
My mouth will speak wisdom, my heart murmurs deep thoughts.
I turn my ear to a proverb, I unfold my riddle to the sound of the harp.
Why should I fear in evil days, when the malice of my foes surrounds me?
They trust in their wealth, they boast of their great riches.
Yet no one can redeem himself, or pay to God his ransom:
the price of a life is too high, it can never suffice,
to live on for ever and never see the grave.
Everyone sees it: the wise die, just as the fool and the senseless perish, leaving their wealth to others.
They thought their houses eternal, their dwellings made to last from age to age, and they gave their own names to their lands.
But man in his splendour does not endure: he is like the beasts that perish.
Such is the fate of the presumptuous, and of those who follow after, delighting in their words. Selah.

Like a flock they are herded into the realm of the dead; death shepherds them. In the morning the upright will rule over them; their beauty will dissolve in the realm of the dead, far from their home.
But God will redeem my life from the grasp of the realm of the dead, for he will take me to himself. Selah.
Do not be dismayed when someone grows rich, when the splendour of his house increases:
at his death he will take nothing away, his splendour will not go down with him.
Though in life he counted himself blessed, and men praise you when you do well for yourself,
you will go to join the line of your fathers, who will never again see the light.
Man in his splendour, without understanding, is like the beasts that perish.
A psalm of Asaph. God, the Lord God, speaks: he summons the earth, from the rising of the sun to its setting.
From Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines forth.
He comes, our God, and will not keep silent; before him a fire devours; around him the storm rages.
He summons the heavens above and the earth, to judge his people:
"Gather my faithful ones before me, who sealed my covenant by sacrifice."
And the heavens proclaim his justice: it is God who is judge. Selah.
"Listen, my people, and I will speak; O Israel, I bring a charge against you: I am God, your God.
It is not for your sacrifices that I reprove you: your burnt offerings are ever before me.
I will take no bull from your house, nor goats from your pens.
For all the animals of the forest are mine, the beasts of the mountains in their thousands;
I know all the birds of the heights, and whatever moves in the fields is mine.
If I were hungry, I would not tell you, for the world is mine, and all it holds.
Shall I eat the flesh of bulls, or drink the blood of goats?
Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and fulfil your vows to the Most High;
and call upon me in the day of distress: I will deliver you, and you will give me glory."
But to the wicked, God says: "What right have you to recite my precepts and take my covenant on your lips,
you who hate correction and cast my words behind you?
When you see a thief, you are pleased with him; you make common cause with adulterers.
You give your mouth to evil, your tongue weaves deceit;
you sit and accuse your brother, you slander your own mother's son.
This you have done, and I kept silent; you imagined that I was like you. But now I will reprove you and set it all before your eyes.
Understand this, you who forget God, lest I tear you to pieces, with no one to deliver you.
Whoever offers thanksgiving gives me glory, and to the one who orders his way, I will show the salvation of God."

titres.titre: The Miserere: the prayer of the repentant sinner

versets.t: For the choirmaster. A psalm of David,
when the prophet Nathan came to him, after his sin with Bathsheba.
Have mercy on me, O God, in your faithful love; in your great tenderness, blot out my transgressions.
Wash me thoroughly from my guilt, and cleanse me from my sin.
For I acknowledge my transgressions, and my sin is ever before me.
Against you, you alone, have I sinned, and done what is evil in your sight: so you are just when you pronounce sentence, blameless when you judge.
See: I was born in guilt, a sinner from my mother's womb.
See: you desire truth in the depths of the heart; in secret, you teach me wisdom.
Take away my sin with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
Let me hear the songs of joy: the bones you have crushed will dance.
Turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my guilt.
Create in me a pure heart, O God; renew within me a steadfast spirit.
Do not cast me away from your presence, nor take from me your holy spirit.
Give me back the joy of your salvation; may a generous spirit sustain me.
To the straying I will teach your ways, and sinners will return to you.
Deliver me from bloodshed, O God, God of my salvation, and my tongue will acclaim your justice.
Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will proclaim your praise.
You do not want sacrifice, or I would offer it; the burnt offering does not please you.
The sacrifice that pleases God is a broken spirit; a heart broken and crushed, O God, you will not despise.
In your goodwill, do good to Zion, rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.
Then you will delight in true sacrifices, in offerings and burnt offerings; then bulls will be offered on your altar.

titres.titre: Against the wicked who boasts of evil

versets.t: For the choirmaster. A poem of David,
when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul: "David has entered the house of Ahimelech."
Why boast of evil, O mighty man? The faithful love of God endures for ever.
Your tongue plots only ruin; deceitful, it is like a sharpened razor.
You prefer evil to good, and lies to truthful speech. Selah.
You love every destroying word, O deceitful tongue!
So God will bring you down for ever, snatch you up and tear you from your tent, and uproot you from the land of the living. Selah.
The just will see, and be filled with awe; they will laugh at him:
"Here is the man who would not make God his stronghold, but trusted in his great wealth and thought himself strong in his malice!"
But I, like a green olive tree in the house of God, trust in the faithful love of God for ever and ever.
I will praise you for ever for what you have done; before your faithful ones, I will hope in your name, for it is good.
For the choirmaster. In a plaintive tone. A poem of David.
The fool says in his heart, "There is no God." They are corrupt, their deeds are abominable; not one does good.
From the heights of heaven, God looks down on the children of men to see if there is one who is wise, one who seeks God.
All have turned away, all alike are corrupt; not one does good, not even one.
Have they no understanding, all these evildoers who devour my people as they eat bread, and never call upon God?
They will tremble with terror where there is nothing to fear. For God scatters the bones of him who besieges you; you will put them to shame, for God rejects them.
Who will bring from Zion the deliverance of Israel? When God restores the fortunes of his people, Jacob will exult, Israel will rejoice.

titres.titre: Prayer of one handed over to his enemies

versets.t: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A poem of David,
when the Ziphites came and said to Saul: "David is hiding among us."
O God, save me by your name, and do me justice by your power.
O God, hear my prayer, give ear to the words of my mouth.
Strangers rise up against me, violent men seek my life; they do not keep God before their eyes. Selah.
But see: God is my helper, the Lord is the upholder of my life.
Let evil recoil upon my foes! In your faithfulness, silence them.
With a willing heart I will offer you sacrifice; I will praise your name, Lord, for it is good.
For he delivers me from every trouble, and my eyes look in triumph on my enemies.

titres.titre: The lament against the treacherous friend

versets.t: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A poem of David.
O God, give ear to my prayer, do not hide from my supplication.
Listen to me, and answer me! I am restless in my lament, and I groan,
at the threats of the enemy, at the oppression of the wicked; for they bring trouble down upon me, and pursue me in fury.
My heart writhes within me, and the terrors of death assail me.
Fear and trembling overwhelm me, and horror sweeps over me.
And I say: "Oh, that I had wings like a dove! I would fly away and find rest;
I would flee far off, and lodge in the desert. Selah.
I would hurry to a shelter from the raging wind, from the storm."
Destroy them, Lord, confuse their tongues! For I see violence and strife in the city:
day and night they prowl upon its walls; within, there is malice and trouble;
ruin dwells in her midst, and oppression and fraud never leave her streets.
If an enemy had insulted me, I could bear it; if a rival had risen against me, I could hide from him.
But it was you, another self, my companion, my friend!
Together we enjoyed sweet fellowship; amid the throng, we walked to the house of God.
Let death come upon them, let them go down alive to the realm of the dead! For evil dwells among them, in their very heart.
As for me, I call upon God, and the Lord will save me.
Evening, morning, and noon, I complain and groan; and he will hear my voice.
He will redeem my life and give me peace in the battle waged against me, for many are against me.
God will hear; he will humble them, he who is enthroned from of old. Selah. For they do not change, and they have no fear of God.
This man has laid his hand on his allies, he has broken his covenant.
His mouth is smoother than butter, but war is in his heart; his words are softer than oil, yet they are drawn swords.
Cast your burden on the Lord, and he will sustain you; never will he let the just be shaken.
But you, O God, will bring them down to the pit of death; men of blood and deceit will not reach half their days. As for me, I trust in you.
For the choirmaster. To the tune "The Silent Dove of Distant Lands." A poem of David, when the Philistines seized him at Gath.
Have mercy on me, O God: men harass me; all day long they fight against me and press me hard.
All day long my foes harass me; many fight against me in their pride.
On the day I am afraid, I put my trust in you.
In God, whose word I praise, in God I trust without fear: what can a mere mortal do to me?
All day long they twist my words; all their thoughts are bent on my harm.
They band together, they lie in wait, they watch my steps, seeking my life.
For such crimes, shall they escape? In your anger, O God, cast down these peoples!
My wanderings you have counted; gather my tears in your flask: are they not in your book?
Then my enemies will retreat on the day I call to you. This I know: God is for me.
In God, whose word I praise, in the Lord, whose word I praise,
in God I trust without fear: what can man do to me?
O God, I owe you the fulfilment of my vows; I will offer you sacrifices of thanksgiving.
For you have delivered my life from death, and kept my feet from stumbling, that I may walk before God in the light of the living.

titres.titre: In the shadow of your wings

versets.t: For the choirmaster. "Do Not Destroy." A poem of David, when, pursued by Saul, he took refuge in the cave.
Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me, for in you I seek refuge; in the shadow of your wings I take shelter, until the trouble has passed.
I cry to God Most High, to the God who does all things for me.
From heaven he will send his salvation, when my persecutor heaps insults on me. Selah. God will send his love and his faithfulness.
I lie among lions, greedy to devour the children of men; their teeth are spears and arrows, their tongue a sharp sword.
Be exalted above the heavens, O God! Let your glory shine over all the earth!
They had spread a net for my steps, and I was already bowed low; they had dug a pit before me, and into it they fell. Selah.
My heart is steadfast, O God, my heart is steadfast; I will sing and make music to you.
Awake, my soul! Awake, harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn.
I will praise you among the peoples, Lord, I will sing to you among the nations.
For your love reaches to the heavens, your faithfulness to the clouds.
Be exalted above the heavens, O God! Let your glory shine over all the earth!
For the choirmaster. "Do Not Destroy." A poem of David.
Is it truly justice that you pronounce, you mighty ones? Do you judge the children of men with fairness?
No: deliberately you work evil; in the land, your hands deal out violence.
The wicked go astray from the womb; from birth the liars wander off.
They have venom like the venom of a serpent, like the deaf viper that stops its ear
and will not hear the voice of the charmer, of the most skilful enchanter.
O God, break the teeth in their mouths; Lord, tear out the fangs of these lions!
Let them drain away like water that runs off! When they take aim, let their arrows be blunted!
Let them be like the slug that melts as it goes, like a stillborn child that never sees the sun!
Before your pots feel the fire of the thorns, green or dry, the storm will sweep them away.
The just will rejoice to see justice done; he will bathe his feet in the blood of the wicked.
And it will be said: "Truly, the just has his reward; truly, there is a God who judges the earth!"
For the choirmaster. "Do Not Destroy." A poem of David, when Saul had the house watched in order to put him to death.
Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; set me beyond the reach of my assailants.
Deliver me from the evildoers, and save me from the men of blood.
See how they lie in wait for my life; violent men gather against me, though I have committed neither fault nor sin, O Lord.
Despite my innocence, they rush and make ready. Awake, come to me, and see!
You, Lord, God of hosts, God of Israel, rise up to punish all these nations; show no mercy to these treacherous evildoers. Selah.
They return at evening, snarling like dogs, prowling about the city.
Their mouths overflow with insults, swords are on their lips: "Who then hears us?" they say.
But you, Lord, laugh at them, you mock all these nations.
O my strength, I look to you, for God is my stronghold.
The God who loves me will come to me; God will let me gaze on the defeat of my enemies.
Do not kill them all at once, lest my people forget; by your power scatter them, bring them down, Lord, our shield!
Every word of their mouth is a sin; let them be caught in their own pride, for the curses and lies they utter!
Destroy them in your wrath, destroy them, till they are no more! And it will be known that God rules over Jacob, to the ends of the earth. Selah.
They return at evening, snarling like dogs, prowling about the city.
They wander in search of food; and if they are not filled, they growl.
But I will sing of your strength; at daybreak I will acclaim your faithful love. For you have been a stronghold for me, a refuge in the day of my distress.
O my strength, I will sing to you, for God is my stronghold, the God who loves me.
For the choirmaster. To the tune "The Lily of the Testimony." A poem of David, to be taught,
when he fought the Arameans of Mesopotamia and of Zobah, and Joab returned and struck down twelve thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt.
O God, you have rejected us, you have broken our ranks; you were angry: return to us!
You have made the land quake, you have split it open: mend its breaches, for it is tottering!
You have made your people endure hard trials, you have made us drink a wine that reels the head.
But to those who fear you, you have given a banner, to be raised in the name of your truth. Selah.
That your beloved may be delivered, save with your right hand, and answer me!
God has spoken in his sanctuary: "In triumph I will divide up Shechem, and parcel out the Valley of Succoth.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine! Ephraim is the helmet on my head, and Judah my sceptre.
Moab is the basin where I wash; on Edom I cast my sandal; over the land of the Philistines I raise my shout of victory."
Who will lead me to the fortified city? Who will bring me into Edom?
Is it not you, O God, who had rejected us, you who no longer went out with our armies?
Bring us help against the oppressor, for the help of man is worthless.
With God we will do mighty deeds; it is he who will trample our foes.
For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. Of David.
O God, hear my cry, be attentive to my prayer.
From the end of the earth I call to you, my heart growing faint: lead me to the rock that is too high for me.
For you are my refuge, a strong tower against the enemy.
I long to dwell in your tent for ever, to take shelter under your wings. Selah.
Yes, O God, you hear my vows; you have given me the heritage of those who fear your name.
Add days to the days of the king; may his years endure from age to age!
May he reign for ever before God! May your love and your faithfulness watch over him!
Then I will ever sing to your name, and fulfil my vows day after day.

titres.titre: The soul's rest in God alone

versets.t: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A psalm of David.
In God alone my soul finds rest; from him comes my salvation.
He alone is my rock, my salvation, my stronghold: I will not be shaken.
How long will you assail a man to strike him down, all of you together, like a leaning wall, a tottering fence?
Truly, they plan only to topple him from his place; they delight in lies. With their mouths they bless, but in their hearts they curse. Selah.
In God alone, O my soul, find rest; from him comes my hope.
He alone is my rock, my salvation, my stronghold: I will not be shaken.
In God rest my salvation and my glory; my mighty rock, my refuge is in God.
Trust in him at all times, O people; pour out your hearts before him: God is our refuge. Selah.
Men are but a breath, the great are but a lie; on the scales they rise, all together lighter than a breath.
Do not trust in violence, nor set vain hopes on plunder; if riches increase, do not set your heart on them.
Once God has spoken, twice have I heard this: that power belongs to God;
and to you, Lord, belongs faithful love. For you repay each one according to his deeds.

titres.titre: Thirst for God in the desert

versets.t: A psalm of David, when he was in the desert of Judah.
O God, you are my God, I seek you at the break of dawn; my soul thirsts for you, my flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary land without water.
So in the sanctuary I gazed on you, to see your strength and your glory.
Your faithful love is better than life: my lips will speak your praise.
So I will bless you all my life, and in your name lift up my hands.
My soul is satisfied as with a feast, and with joy on my lips my mouth praises you.
When I remember you on my bed, I meditate on you through the watches of the night.
For you are my help: in the shadow of your wings I cry out for joy.
My soul clings to you, and your right hand upholds me.
But those who seek my ruin will sink into the depths of the earth:
they will be given over to the edge of the sword, and become the prey of jackals.
Then the king will rejoice in God; all who swear by him will glory, for the mouths of liars will be stopped.

titres.titre: Against the plots of the wicked

versets.t: For the choirmaster. A psalm of David.
O God, hear my complaint as I groan; guard my life from the enemy who terrifies me.
Hide me from the plot of the wicked, from the raging mob of evildoers.
They sharpen their tongues like a sword, they aim their arrows, those bitter words,
to shoot from cover at the innocent: they shoot suddenly, and fear nothing.
They urge one another on to evil, they scheme where to hide their snares; they say, "Who will see them?"
They plot injustice: "Our plan is ready, well laid!" The inward mind and heart of man are unfathomable.
But God shoots his arrow at them: in an instant they are wounded.
Their own tongue brings them down; all who see them shake their heads.
Then all are seized with fear; they proclaim the work of God and understand what he has done.
The just rejoices in the Lord and takes refuge in him; all the upright of heart glory in him.

titres.titre: Thanksgiving for creation and the harvest

versets.t: For the choirmaster. A psalm of David. A song.
To you belongs praise, O God, in Zion; to you vows are fulfilled.
You who hear prayer, to you all flesh will come.
The weight of our sins overwhelmed me: our transgressions, it is you who forgive them.
Blessed is the one you choose and bring near, to dwell in your courts! We will be filled with the good things of your house, of your holy temple.
By wonders you answer us in your justice, O God of our salvation, hope of the ends of the earth and of the distant seas.
By his strength he sets the mountains firm; he is girded with power.
He stills the roaring of the seas, the roaring of their waves, and the tumult of the peoples.
Before your wonders the dwellers at the ends of the earth are filled with awe; you make the dawn and the dusk shout for joy.
You visit the earth and give it water, you fill it with riches; the stream of God brims with water. You prepare the grain: so you make the earth fruitful.
You water its furrows, you level its ridges; you soften it with showers, and bless its growth.
You crown the year with your bounty; abundance flows in your tracks.
The pastures of the wilderness overflow, and the hills are girded with joy.
The meadows are clothed with flocks, the valleys robed with grain: they shout and sing together.

titres.titre: A universal call to praise God

versets.t: For the choirmaster. A song. A psalm. All the earth, acclaim God!
Sing the glory of his name, give him glorious praise!
Say to God: "How awesome are your works! Before your great power your enemies cringe.
Let all the earth bow down before you, let it sing to you, let it sing praise to your name!" Selah.
Come and see the works of God, his awesome deeds toward the children of men.
He turned the sea into dry land; they crossed the river on foot. There we rejoiced in him.
By his power he rules for ever; his eyes keep watch on the nations: let no rebels rise up! Selah.
Bless our God, you peoples, and make the sound of his praise ring out!
He has kept our soul among the living, and has not let our feet slip.
For you have tested us, O God, you have refined us like silver.
You led us into the net, you laid a heavy burden on our backs,
you let men ride over our heads. We went through fire and water, but you brought us out into abundance.
I come into your house with sacrifices; to you I fulfil my vows,
the vows my lips pronounced, that my mouth spoke in the day of my distress.
I offer you sacrifices of fatlings, with the smoke of rams; I offer bulls and goats. Selah.
Come and hear, all you who fear God: I will tell what he has done for me.
To him my mouth cried out, and his praise was already on my tongue.
Had I cherished evil in my heart, the Lord would not have listened to me.
But God has listened, he has heeded the voice of my prayer.
Blessed be God, who has not rejected my prayer, nor withheld from me his faithful love!

titres.titre: A blessing that all peoples may praise God

versets.t: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.
May God be gracious to us and bless us, may he make his face shine upon us! Selah.
Then your way will be known on earth, your salvation among all the nations.
Let the peoples praise you, O God, let all the peoples praise you!
Let the nations be glad and shout for joy, for you judge the peoples with fairness and guide the nations on the earth. Selah.
Let the peoples praise you, O God, let all the peoples praise you!
The earth has given its harvest; may God, our God, bless us!
May God bless us, and may all the ends of the earth fear him!
For the choirmaster. A psalm of David. A song.
Let God arise, and his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee before him!
As smoke is blown away, you drive them away; as wax melts before the fire, the wicked perish before God.
But the just rejoice, they exult before God, carried away with gladness.
Sing to God, celebrate his name! Prepare the way for him who rides upon the clouds; the Lord is his name, exult before him!
Father of orphans, defender of widows, such is God in his holy dwelling.
To the lonely God gives a home; he brings the captives out to freedom and prosperity; only the rebels remain in a scorched land.
O God, when you went out at the head of your people, when you marched through the wilderness, Selah,
the earth trembled, the very heavens melted before God; Sinai trembled before God, the God of Israel.
You poured down, O God, a rain of bounty; your inheritance was worn out, and you revived it.
Your flock found there a home; in your goodness, O God, you provided for the poor.
The Lord gives the command: the women who bear the good news are a mighty host.
"The kings of the armies flee, they flee!" And the woman at home divides the spoil.
Though you lay among the sheepfolds, the wings of the dove were sheathed in silver, its feathers in the sheen of gold.
When the Almighty scattered the kings there, snow fell on Zalmon.
Mountain of God, mountain of Bashan, mountain of many peaks, mountain of Bashan!
Why do you look with envy, you mountains of many peaks, at the mountain God has chosen for his dwelling? The Lord will dwell there for ever.
The chariots of God are myriads, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them, at Sinai, in his sanctuary.
You went up to the height, you led captives away; you received men as tribute, even rebels, that they might dwell with the Lord God.
Blessed be the Lord! Day after day he carries our burden; he is the God who saves us. Selah.
Our God is a God who delivers; to the Lord God belong the ways of escape from death.
Yes, God shatters the head of his enemies, the hairy skull of him who persists in his sins.
The Lord has said: "From Bashan I will bring them back; I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,
that you may plunge your foot in blood, and the tongues of your dogs have their share of the enemy."
They have seen your procession, O God, the procession of my God, my king, into the sanctuary.
In front, the singers; then the musicians; in the midst, the maidens beating tambourines.
"In your assemblies, bless God, the Lord, you who are the fountain of Israel!"
There is Benjamin, the least, leading the way; the princes of Judah in a throng, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
Summon your power, O God; confirm, O God, what you have done for us.
Because of your temple, above Jerusalem, kings will bring you gifts.
Rebuke the beast of the reeds, the herd of bulls and the calves of the peoples, till they submit, bearing pieces of silver. Scatter the peoples who delight in war!
Nobles will come from Egypt; Ethiopia will quickly stretch out its hands to God.
Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God, celebrate the Lord, Selah,
him who rides on the heavens, the ancient heavens! See, he sends forth his voice, his mighty voice.
Acknowledge the power of God! His majesty is over Israel, his power is in the clouds.
Awesome is God from his sanctuary! The God of Israel gives his people strength and power. Blessed be God!

titres.titre: The distress of the just man drowning in the waters

versets.t: For the choirmaster. To the tune "The Lilies." Of David.
Save me, O God: the waters are up to my throat.
I sink in deep mire, with no foothold; I have come into deep waters, and the current sweeps me away.
I am worn out with crying, my throat is parched; my eyes fail as I wait for my God.
More numerous than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause; mighty are those who would destroy me, my lying enemies. What I did not steal, I must now restore!
O God, you know my folly, and my faults are not hidden from you.
Let not those who hope in you be ashamed because of me, O Lord, God of hosts! Let not those who seek you be humbled on my account, O God of Israel!
For it is for your sake that I bear insult, that shame covers my face.
I have become a stranger to my brothers, an alien to the sons of my mother.
Zeal for your house consumes me, and the insults of those who revile you fall upon me.
I weep and fast: and for this they reproach me.
I put on sackcloth: and I become their byword.
Those who sit at the gate talk of me, and the drinkers make me their song.
But I offer my prayer to you, Lord: this is the time of favour. O God, in your great love, answer me with your faithful salvation.
Draw me out of the mire, that I sink no more; let me be delivered from my foes and from the deep waters!
Let the current not sweep me away, let the abyss not swallow me, let the pit not close its mouth over me!
Answer me, Lord, for your faithful love is tender; in your great mercy, turn to me.
Do not hide your face from your servant; I am in anguish: answer me quickly!
Come near to me, redeem me; for the sake of my enemies, deliver me.
You know my insult, my shame, and my dishonour; all my oppressors are before you.
Insult has broken my heart, and I am spent; I looked for compassion, but there was none; for comforters, but I found none.
For my food they gave me poison; in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
Let their table become a snare for them, a trap for their guests!
Let their eyes grow dim, and see no more; make their loins tremble without end.
Pour out your fury upon them, let the heat of your anger overtake them!
Let their camp be laid waste, let no one dwell in their tents!
For they hound the one you have struck, they add to the pain of those you have wounded.
Charge them with guilt upon guilt, let them not enter into your justice.
Let them be blotted out of the book of life, and not enrolled among the just.
But I am wretched and in pain: let your salvation, O God, raise me up!
I will praise the name of God with a song, I will exalt him with thanksgiving;
this will please the Lord more than an ox, more than a beast with horns and hooves.
The humble will see it and rejoice; you who seek God, may your hearts revive!
For the Lord hears the poor, and does not despise his own who are captive.
Let heaven and earth praise him, the seas and all that moves in them!
For God will save Zion and rebuild the towns of Judah; men will settle there and possess it.
The offspring of his servants will inherit it, and those who love his name will dwell there.
For the choirmaster. Of David. As a memorial.
O God, come quickly to deliver me! Lord, come quickly to my help!
Shame and confusion to those who seek my life! Let them fall back, covered with shame, those who seek my ruin!
Let them turn back, humiliated, those who jeer at me, "Aha! Aha!"
But joy and gladness in you to all who seek you! May they always say, "God is great!", those who love your salvation.
But I am poor and needy, O God, come quickly to me! You are my help and my deliverer: Lord, do not delay!

titres.titre: A trusting prayer in old age

versets.t: In you, Lord, I take refuge: let me never be put to shame!
In your justice, deliver me and set me free; incline your ear to me and save me.
Be for me a rock of refuge, to which I may always come. You have decreed my salvation, for you are my rock and my stronghold.
My God, deliver me from the hand of the wicked, from the grip of the unjust and cruel man.
For you are my hope, O Lord my God, my trust from my youth.
On you I have leaned from the womb; it is you who brought me forth from my mother's body: you are my praise without end.
To the crowd I am like a portent, but you are my sure refuge.
My mouth is filled with your praise, all day long with your splendour.
Do not cast me off in the time of old age; when my strength fails, do not forsake me.
For my enemies speak of me, and those who watch for my life take counsel together:
"God has forsaken him," they say; "pursue him, seize him, for he has no one to defend him!"
O God, do not stay far from me; my God, come quickly to my help!
Shame and ruin to those who accuse me! Covered with shame and scorn, those who seek my harm!
But I will always hope, and add still more to your praise.
My mouth will tell of your justice, all day long of your salvation, though I cannot number it.
I will come to tell the mighty deeds of the Lord my God; I will recall your justice, yours alone.
O God, you have taught me from my youth, and to this day I proclaim your wonders.
Now that I am old and grey, O God, do not forsake me, that I may make known your strength to this generation, your power to those still to come.
Your justice, O God, reaches the heights, you who have done great things: O God, who is like you?
You have made me see distress, many and cruel; you will make me live again, and from the depths of the earth you will raise me up once more.
You will increase my greatness, and turn again to comfort me.
Then I will praise you with the harp, O my God, for your faithfulness; I will make music to you on the lyre, O Holy One of Israel.
My lips will shout for joy as I make music to you, and my soul as well, which you have redeemed.
All day long my tongue will tell of your justice, for they are put to shame, they blush, those who sought my harm.

titres.titre: The reign of peace of the king

versets.t: Of Solomon. O God, give the king your judgements, and your justice to the king's son.
May he govern your people with justice, and your poor with fairness!
May the mountains bring peace to the people, and the hills, justice!
May he give justice to the poor of the people, save the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor!
May they fear you as long as the sun endures, as long as the moon shines, from age to age!
May he come down like rain on the grass, like showers that water the earth!
In his days may justice flourish, and peace abound, till the moon is no more!
He will rule from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth.
Before him the desert nomads will bow, and his enemies will lick the dust.
The kings of Tarshish and the islands will bring tribute, the kings of Sheba and Seba will offer gifts.
All kings will bow down before him, all nations will serve him.
For he will deliver the poor who cry out, and the wretched who have no helper.
He will have pity on the weak and the poor, and save the lives of the poor.
From oppression and violence he will redeem them: their blood will be precious in his eyes.
Long may he live! May the gold of Sheba be given to him; may prayer be made for him without ceasing, and blessing on him all day long.
May grain abound in the land, to the tops of the mountains! May its ears wave like the cedars of Lebanon, and the city teem with people like the grass of the fields!
May his name endure for ever! As long as the sun shines, may his name live on! In him all the families of the earth will be blessed; all nations will call him blessed.
Blessed be the Lord God, the God of Israel, who alone does wonders!
Blessed be his glorious name for ever! May all the earth be filled with his glory! Amen! Amen!
Here end the prayers of David, son of Jesse.

titres.titre: The fate of the wicked understood in the sanctuary

versets.t: A psalm of Asaph. Truly God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart!
Yet my feet had almost given way; a little more, and I would have slipped.
For I grew envious of the arrogant, seeing the prosperity of the wicked.
For them there are no pangs; their bodies are sound and sleek.
They know nothing of human toil; they are not stricken like other people.
So pride is their necklace, and violence the cloak that wraps them.
Their eyes bulge out with fatness; the fancies of their hearts overflow.
