They sneer and speak with malice of oppression; from on high they look down.
Their mouths lay claim to heaven, and their tongues range over the earth.
So the people turn to them and drink in their words to the full.
They say, "How would God know? Can the Most High have knowledge?"
Look at the wicked: always at ease, they pile up wealth.
Was it for nothing that I kept my heart pure and washed my hands in innocence?
All day long I am stricken, and every morning brings new pain.
Had I said, "I will speak like them," I would have betrayed the family of your children.
I sought to understand it: it was too heavy a burden for me,
until the day I entered the sanctuary of God and understood how they end.
Truly you set them on slippery ground; you make them fall into ruin.
In a moment, what devastation! Swept away, engulfed by terror!
Like a dream when one awakes, O Lord, when you rouse yourself, you dismiss their phantom.
When my heart grew embittered and I was pierced to the depths,
I was stupid and uncomprehending; before you I was a brute beast.
Yet I am always with you; you hold me by my right hand.
You guide me with your counsel, and afterward you will take me into glory.
Whom else have I in heaven? With you, I desire nothing on earth.
My flesh and my heart may fail, but the rock of my heart, my portion, is God forever.
Those who forsake you perish; you bring to nothing all who are unfaithful to you.
But as for me, my happiness is to be near God; in the Lord God I make my refuge, to tell of all your works.
A poem of Asaph. Why, O God, have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smolder against the flock you shepherd?
Remember your people, whom you acquired long ago, redeemed to be the tribe of your inheritance; remember Mount Zion, where you dwelt.
Turn your steps toward these endless ruins: in the sanctuary the enemy has laid everything waste.
Your foes have roared in the heart of your holy place; there they have set up their standards as trophies.
They were like woodsmen raising the axe against a thicket of trees.
And now all its carved paneling they have shattered with axe and hammer.
They have set fire to your sanctuary; they have razed and profaned the dwelling of your name.
They said in their hearts, "Let us crush them all together!" And they burned every meeting place of God throughout the land.
We no longer see our signs; there is no prophet left, and no one among us knows how long this will last.
How long, O God, will the oppressor taunt? Will the enemy revile your name forever?
Why do you hold back your hand, keeping your right hand hidden in your bosom?
Yet you, O God, are my king from of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.
It was you who split the sea by your power, who broke the heads of the monsters on the waters.
It was you who crushed the heads of Leviathan, giving him as food to the beasts of the desert.
It was you who opened springs and torrents, you who dried up ever-flowing rivers.
Yours is the day, yours also the night; it was you who set the moon and the sun in place.
It was you who fixed all the borders of the earth; summer and winter, you made them both.
Remember this: the enemy insults the Lord, a foolish people reviles your name.
Do not hand over the life of your dove to the wild beasts; do not forget forever the life of your poor.
Look to your covenant! For the dark corners of the land are full of dens of violence.
Let not the oppressed turn back in shame; let the poor and the afflicted praise your name!
Rise up, O God, defend your cause; remember how the fool insults you all day long.
Do not forget the shouts of your adversaries, the ever-rising uproar of those who hate you.

titres.titre: God, the just judge, brings low and lifts up

versets.t: For the choirmaster. "Do Not Destroy." A psalm of Asaph. A song.
We give you thanks, O God, we give you thanks; your name is near, and your wonders are told.
"At the time I have appointed, I will judge with uprightness.
The earth trembles with all who dwell in it, but it is I who hold firm its pillars." Selah.
I say to the boastful, "Boast no more," and to the wicked, "Do not lift up your heads!
Do not lift your heads so high, do not speak with insolent necks!"
For neither from the east nor the west, nor from the desert, does exaltation come:
it is God who judges; he brings one low and lifts up another.
The Lord holds in his hand a cup where spiced wine foams; he pours it out, and all the wicked of the earth will drink it to the dregs.
But as for me, I will proclaim it forever; I will sing to the God of Jacob.
I will break all the power of the wicked, but the power of the righteous will be lifted high.
For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.
In Judah God is known; in Israel his name is great.
In Salem is his tent, on Zion his dwelling.
There he shattered the flashing arrows, the shield, the sword, the weapons of war. Selah.
Radiant with light, you are more majestic than the mountains laden with plunder.
The stouthearted have been stripped of their spoil; they sleep their last sleep, and all those warriors are left without strength in their arms.
At your rebuke, O God of Jacob, chariot and horse lay stunned.
You, you are to be feared: who can stand before you when your anger flares?
From heaven you pronounced the sentence; the earth was afraid and fell silent,
when God arose to judge, to save all the humble of the land. Selah.
Even human fury turns to your praise; with the remnant of their rage you gird yourself.
Make vows to the Lord your God and keep them; let all around him bring gifts to the God who is to be feared!
He curbs the pride of princes; he is terrible to the kings of the earth.

titres.titre: Remembering God's works in the time of trial

versets.t: For the choirmaster. According to Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph.
My voice rises to God, and I cry out; my voice rises to God, that he may hear me.
In the day of my distress I seek the Lord; by night I stretch out my hands without ceasing; my soul refuses to be comforted.
I remember God, and I groan; I meditate, and my spirit grows faint. Selah.
You hold my eyelids open; I am troubled and cannot speak.
I think back on the days of old, on the years long past.
By night I recall my song; I meditate in my heart, and my spirit asks:
"Will the Lord reject us forever, never again show his favor?
Is his faithful love gone for good? Is his word finished for all ages?
Has God forgotten to be merciful? Has he, in his anger, shut off his compassion?" Selah.
And I say, "What makes me suffer is that the right hand of the Most High has changed."
I will call to mind the deeds of the Lord; yes, I remember your wonders of old.
I will meditate on all your work, and ponder your mighty deeds.
O God, your way is holy: what god is as great as our God?
You are the God who works wonders; you have shown your power among the peoples.
By your arm you redeemed your people, the sons of Jacob and of Joseph. Selah.
The waters saw you, O God, the waters saw you and trembled; the depths were shaken.
The clouds poured down their waters, the skies thundered forth their voice, and your arrows flew in every direction.
Your thunder rolled in the whirlwind, the lightning lit up the world; the earth quivered and quaked.
Your road ran through the sea, your path through the mighty waters, and your footprints could not be seen.
You led your people like a flock, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

titres.titre: The history of Israel, a lesson in faithfulness

versets.t: A poem of Asaph. Listen, O my people, to my teaching; incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in parables; I will bring forth the mysteries of ancient times.
What we have heard and learned, what our fathers have told us,
we will not hide from their children; to the coming generation we will tell the glorious deeds of the Lord, his power and the wonders he has done.
He set up a decree in Jacob, established a law in Israel, and commanded our fathers to teach it to their children,
so that the next generation might know it, the children yet to be born; that they in turn might rise and tell it to their children,
so that they might put their trust in God, never forgetting his works, and keep his commandments;
that they might not be like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, whose heart was fickle, whose spirit was unfaithful to God.
The sons of Ephraim, skilled with the bow, turned back on the day of battle.
They did not keep God's covenant; they refused to walk in his law;
they forgot his deeds, the wonders he had shown them.
Before their fathers he had worked marvels, in the land of Egypt, in the plain of Zoan.
He split the sea to let them pass, holding the waters up like a wall.
By day he led them with the cloud; all night long by a glow of fire.
He split the rocks in the wilderness and gave them drink as from the great deep.
From the crag he brought out streams and made water run down like rivers.
But they sinned against him still, rebelling against the Most High in the parched land.
In their hearts they put God to the test, demanding food for their craving.
They spoke against God, saying, "Can God spread a table in the wilderness?
He struck the rock, and water flowed, the streams overflowed; but can he give bread as well, provide meat for his people?"
The Lord heard and was furious; a fire blazed against Jacob, and anger rose against Israel,
because they had no faith in God and did not trust in his help.
Yet he commanded the clouds above and opened the doors of heaven;
he rained down manna for them to eat and gave them the grain of heaven.
Each one ate the bread of angels; he sent them food in plenty.
In the heavens he stirred up the east wind and by his power drove on the south wind;
he rained meat on them like dust, birds like the sand of the seas.
He made them fall in the midst of the camp, all around their tents.
They ate and were filled to excess, for he had given them what they craved.
But before their craving was satisfied, the food still in their mouths,
the anger of God rose against them: he struck down their strongest, he laid low the young men of Israel.
Despite all this, they sinned still, and had no faith in his wonders.
So he made their days vanish like a breath, their years in sudden terror.
When he struck them with death, they sought him; they turned back, eager for God;
they remembered that God was their rock, the Most High God their Redeemer.
But they flattered him with their mouths and lied to him with their tongues;
their hearts were not firm toward him, they were not faithful to his covenant.
Yet he, full of compassion, forgave their guilt and did not destroy them; again and again he held back his anger and did not stir up all his wrath.
He remembered that they were but flesh, a breath that passes and does not return.
How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and grieved him in the wastelands!
Again and again they put God to the test and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
They no longer remembered his hand, the day he delivered them from the oppressor,
when he worked his signs in Egypt, his wonders in the plain of Zoan:
he turned their rivers to blood, and they could no longer drink from their streams;
he sent swarms of flies to devour them, frogs to lay them waste;
he gave their crops to the locust, the fruit of their labor to the grasshopper;
he destroyed their vines with hail, their sycamores with frost;
he gave up their cattle to the hail, their herds to the lightning bolts.
He unleashed on them the heat of his anger, fury, rage, and distress, a whole company of destroying angels.
He cleared a path for his anger; he did not spare them from death but gave their lives over to the plague.
He struck down all the firstborn of Egypt, the firstfruits of manhood in the tents of Ham.
Then he led out his people like sheep and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.
He led them safely, and they were unafraid, while the sea engulfed their enemies.
He brought them to his holy domain, to the mountain his right hand had won.
Before them he drove out nations; he apportioned to them an inheritance by the measuring line and settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
But they tested the Most High God again; they rebelled and did not keep his decrees.
They turned away, treacherous like their fathers, warped like a faulty bow.
They angered him with their high places and stirred his jealousy with their idols.
God heard and was furious, and he utterly rejected Israel.
He abandoned his dwelling at Shiloh, the tent where he lived among men.
He gave up his strength to captivity, his splendor into the hand of the enemy.
He gave up his people to the sword and was furious with his inheritance.
Fire devoured their young men, and their maidens had no wedding song.
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows could not even weep.
Then the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a warrior overcome with wine;
he struck his enemies from behind and covered them with everlasting shame.
He rejected the tent of Joseph and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim;
but he chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loves.
He built his sanctuary high as the heavens, firm as the earth he founded forever.
He chose David his servant and took him from the sheepfolds;
from tending the ewes he called him to shepherd Jacob his people, Israel his inheritance.
And David shepherded them with an upright heart and led them with a skillful hand.
A psalm of Asaph. O God, the nations have invaded your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem a heap of ruins.
They have given the corpses of your servants as food to the birds of the sky, the flesh of your faithful to the wild beasts.
They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there is no one to bury them.
We have become the scorn of our neighbors, the mockery and derision of those around us.
How long, O Lord? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire?
Pour out your fury on the nations that do not know you, on the kingdoms that do not call on your name;
for they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his home.
Do not hold against us the sins of our forefathers; let your compassion come swiftly to meet us, for we are brought very low.
Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of your name; deliver us and forgive our sins, for your name's sake.
Why should the nations say, "Where is their God?" Before our eyes, among the nations, let the avenging of your servants' blood be known, that blood poured out!
Let the groaning of the captive come before you; by the strength of your arm, spare those doomed to die.
Repay our neighbors sevenfold, O Lord, for the insult they hurled at you!
Then we, your people, the flock you shepherd, will give you thanks forever; from age to age we will tell your praise.

titres.titre: "O God, restore us": the vine of Israel

versets.t: For the choirmaster. To the tune "The Lilies of the Testimony." A psalm of Asaph.
Shepherd of Israel, hear us, you who lead Joseph like a flock; you who are enthroned upon the cherubim, shine forth!
Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, rouse your power and come to save us!
O God, restore us; let your face shine, and we shall be saved.
Lord, God of hosts, how long will you be angry at the prayer of your people?
You have fed them with the bread of tears and given them tears to drink in full measure.
You make us an object of strife to our neighbors, and our enemies mock us.
God of hosts, restore us; let your face shine, and we shall be saved.
Out of Egypt you tore up a vine; you drove out nations to plant it.
You cleared the ground before it: it took root and filled the land.
Its shade covered the mountains, its branches the cedars of God;
it stretched out its shoots to the Sea, its runners to the River.
Why have you broken down its walls, so that all who pass by pluck its fruit?
The boar from the forest ravages it, and the creatures of the field feed on it.
God of hosts, turn back! From heaven look down and see; watch over this vine,
protect what your right hand has planted, the son you have chosen for yourself.
It is burned with fire, cut to the ground; at your rebuke they perish.
Let your hand be upon the man at your right hand, upon the son of man you have chosen for yourself.
Then we will not turn away from you again; restore us to life, and we will call on your name.
Lord, God of hosts, restore us; let your face shine, and we shall be saved.

titres.titre: A call to feast and to listen to God

versets.t: For the choirmaster. According to the Gittith. Of Asaph.
Sing for joy to God our strength; shout aloud to the God of Jacob!
Raise a song, sound the tambourine, the sweet harp and the lyre.
Blow the horn at the new moon, at the full moon, on the day of our feast;
for it is a statute for Israel, a law of the God of Jacob.
He made it a decree for Joseph when he went out against the land of Egypt. I hear a voice I did not know:
"I lifted the burden from his shoulder; his hands were freed from the basket.
In distress you called, and I delivered you; I answered you from the heart of the storm; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah.
Listen, my people, and I will warn you; O Israel, if only you would listen to me!
Let there be no foreign god among you; do not bow down to any strange god.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
But my people did not listen to my voice; Israel would have none of me.
So I gave them over to their stubborn hearts, to follow their own devices.
Ah, if only my people would listen to me, if Israel would walk in my ways,
how quickly I would humble their enemies and turn my hand against their oppressors!
Those who hate the Lord would cringe before him, and their doom would be sealed forever.
But him I would feed with the finest wheat, and satisfy with honey from the rock."
A psalm of Asaph. God stands in the divine assembly; in the midst of the gods he renders judgment:
"How long will you judge unjustly and show favor to the wicked? Selah.
Give justice to the weak and the orphan; uphold the right of the afflicted and the destitute;
rescue the weak and the poor; deliver them from the hand of the wicked."
They know nothing, they understand nothing; they walk about in darkness; all the foundations of the earth are shaken.
"I said, You are gods, you are all sons of the Most High.
Yet you will die like men, you will fall like any prince."
Rise up, O God, judge the earth, for all the nations are your inheritance!
A song. A psalm of Asaph.
O God, do not keep silent; do not hold your peace, do not remain unmoved, O God!
For see, your enemies are in an uproar; those who hate you lift up their heads.
Against your people they lay a crafty plot; they conspire against those you protect.
"Come," they say, "let us wipe them out as a nation; let the name of Israel be remembered no more!"
With one accord they plot together; against you they make a covenant:
the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, Philistia with the people of Tyre;
Assyria too has joined them; it lends its arm to the sons of Lot. Selah.
Deal with them as with Midian, as with Sisera, as with Jabin at the Wadi Kishon:
destroyed at Endor, they became dung for the ground.
Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said, "Let us seize the dwellings of God for ourselves!"
My God, make them like whirling leaves, like chaff driven before the wind.
As fire devours the forest, as flame sets the mountains ablaze,
so pursue them with your tempest and terrify them with your storm.
Cover their faces with shame, that they may seek your name, O Lord.
Let them be disgraced and terrified forever, humbled to the point of perishing!
Let them know that you alone, whose name is the Lord, are the Most High over all the earth.
For the choirmaster. According to the Gittith. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
How lovely is your dwelling place, O Lord of hosts!
My soul longs, it faints for the courts of the Lord; my heart and my flesh cry out for joy to the living God.
Even the sparrow finds a home, and the swallow a nest for her young: your altars, O Lord of hosts, my king and my God!
Blessed are those who dwell in your house: they can praise you without ceasing! Selah.
Blessed are those whose strength is in you, whose hearts are set on the holy pilgrimages!
As they pass through the Valley of Tears, they make it a place of springs; the autumn rain covers it with blessings.
They go from strength to strength, and appear before God in Zion.
Lord, God of hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob! Selah.
Look upon our shield, O God; turn your eyes to the face of your anointed one.
A single day in your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere; I would rather stand at the threshold of the house of my God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.
For the Lord God is a sun and a shield; he gives grace and glory, and withholds no good thing from those who walk in integrity.
O Lord of hosts, blessed is the one who trusts in you!
For the choirmaster. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
O Lord, you have loved your land; you have brought back the captives of Jacob;
you have taken away the guilt of your people; you have covered all their sins. Selah.
You have withdrawn all your wrath; you have turned back from your burning anger.
Restore us, O God of our salvation; give up your resentment against us.
Will you be angry with us forever, prolonging your wrath from age to age?
Will you not turn back and give us life again, that your people may rejoice in you?
Show us your faithful love, O Lord, and grant us your salvation.
I will listen to what God the Lord will say: he speaks peace to his people and to his faithful, provided they do not return to their folly.
Surely his salvation is near to those who fear him, and glory will dwell again in our land.
Faithful love and truth meet together; justice and peace embrace.
Truth will spring up from the earth, and justice will look down from heaven.
The Lord himself will grant prosperity, and our land will yield its fruit.
Justice will walk before him and make his footsteps a path.

titres.titre: A poor man's prayer to the God of goodness

versets.t: A prayer of David. Incline your ear, O Lord, and answer me, for I am poor and afflicted.
Guard my life, for I am faithful to you; save your servant, O my God, who trusts in you.
Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I cry to you all day long.
Gladden the soul of your servant, for to you, O Lord, I lift up my soul.
You are good, O Lord, and forgiving, rich in faithful love to all who call on you.
Give ear to my prayer, O Lord; attend to my pleading voice.
In the day of my distress I call on you, for you answer me.
There is none like you among the gods, O Lord, and nothing equals your works.
All the nations you have made will come and bow down before you, O Lord, and give glory to your name.
For you are great and do wondrous things; you alone are God.
Teach me your way, O Lord, that I may walk in your truth; give me an undivided heart to fear your name.
I will praise you with all my heart, O Lord my God, and glorify your name forever;
for great is your faithful love toward me: you have drawn me up from the depths of the realm of the dead.
O God, the arrogant have risen against me; a band of violent men seeks my life, with no regard for you.
But you, O Lord, are a God of tenderness and compassion, slow to anger, rich in love and faithfulness.
Turn to me and have mercy on me; give your strength to your servant, and save the son of your handmaid.
Show me a sign of your goodness, that my enemies may see it and be put to shame, for you, O Lord, have helped me and comforted me.
A psalm of the sons of Korah. A song. He has founded it on the holy mountains.
The Lord loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things are said of you, O city of God! Selah.
"I count Rahab and Babylon among those who know me; here are Philistia, Tyre, and Cush: this one was born there."
And of Zion it will be said, "In her, everyone was born, and the Most High himself makes her firm."
The Lord records in the register of the peoples: "This one was born there." Selah.
And they sing as they dance: "All my springs are in you."

titres.titre: The prayer out of the darkness

versets.t: A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the choirmaster. To be sung in a mournful tone. A poem of Heman the Ezrahite.
O Lord, God of my salvation, by day and by night I cry out before you;
let my prayer come before you; incline your ear to my cry!
For my soul is filled with troubles, and my life draws near to the realm of the dead.
I am counted among those who go down to the pit; I am like a man beyond help.
My place is among the dead, like the slain lying in the grave, those whom you remember no more, cut off from your hand.
You have laid me in the depths of the pit, in the darkness, in the abyss.
Your fury weighs upon me; you overwhelm me with all your waves. Selah.
You have taken my friends far from me; you have made me loathsome to them; I am shut in and cannot escape,
my eyes waste away with grief. I call on you all day long, O Lord; I stretch out my hands to you.
Do you work wonders for the dead? Do the shades rise up to praise you? Selah.
Is your faithful love told in the grave, your faithfulness in the place of ruin?
Are your wonders known in the darkness, your justice in the land of oblivion?
But I, O Lord, cry out to you; in the morning my prayer comes before you.
Why, O Lord, do you reject me and hide your face from me?
Afflicted and at the point of death since my youth, I bear your terrors; I am worn out.
Your wrath has swept over me; your terrors have destroyed me.
Like a flood they surround me all day long; they close in on me from every side.
You have taken my friends and neighbors far from me; my only companion is the darkness.

titres.titre: The covenant with David in the time of trial

versets.t: A poem of Ethan the Ezrahite.
The faithful love of the Lord I will sing forever; from age to age my mouth will make known your faithfulness.
For I have said: your love is an everlasting building; in the heavens you have founded your faithfulness.
"I have made a covenant with my chosen one; I have sworn this oath to David my servant:
I will establish your offspring forever and build up your throne for all ages." Selah.
The heavens celebrate your wonders, O Lord, and your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones.
For who in the skies is equal to the Lord? Who is like the Lord among the heavenly beings?
God is dreaded in the council of the holy ones, terrible above all who surround him.
Lord, God of hosts, who is like you? You are mighty, O Lord, and your faithfulness surrounds you.
You rule the raging of the sea; when its waves rise, it is you who still them.
You crushed Rahab like a corpse; with your mighty arm you scattered your enemies.
Yours are the heavens, yours also the earth; the world and all it holds, you founded them.
The north and the south, you created them; Tabor and Hermon cry out for joy at your name.
Your arm is full of might; your hand is strong, your right hand lifted high.
Justice and right are the foundation of your throne; faithful love and faithfulness go before you.
Blessed are the people who know how to acclaim you, who walk in the light of your face, O Lord!
In your name they rejoice all day long; by your justice they are lifted up.
For you are the splendor of their strength; by your favor our power is raised high.
Truly our shield belongs to the Lord, our king to the Holy One of Israel.
Long ago, in a vision, you spoke to your faithful ones: "I have given help to a hero; I have raised up a young man from among the people.
I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him.
My hand will always be with him, and my arm will make him strong.
The enemy will not ensnare him, nor the wicked overwhelm him.
Before him I will crush his foes and strike down those who hate him.
My faithfulness and my love will be with him; through my name his power will grow.
I will set his hand upon the sea, his right hand upon the rivers.
He will call to me, You are my father, my God, the rock of my salvation.
And I will make him my firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
I will keep my faithful love for him forever, and my covenant with him will stand firm.
I will make his offspring endure forever, and his throne as lasting as the heavens.
If his sons forsake my law and do not follow my decrees,
if they violate my precepts and do not keep my commandments,
I will punish their rebellion with the rod, their guilt with blows;
but I will not take my love from him, nor betray my faithfulness.
I will not violate my covenant, nor change the word that has gone out from my lips.
Once and for all I have sworn by my holiness: I will never lie to David.
His offspring will endure forever, and his throne before me like the sun;
like the moon it will stand firm forever, a faithful witness in the skies." Selah.
Yet you have rejected and spurned him; you have raged against your anointed.
You have renounced the covenant with your servant, defiled his crown and cast it to the ground.
You have breached all his walls and laid his strongholds in ruins.
All who pass by plunder him; he has become the scorn of his neighbors.
You have raised high the right hand of his oppressors and made all his enemies rejoice.
You have blunted the edge of his sword and given him no support in battle.
You have put an end to his splendor and cast his throne to the ground.
You have cut short the days of his youth and covered him with shame. Selah.
How long, O Lord? Will you hide yourself forever? Will your fury burn like fire?
Remember how brief my life is, for what emptiness you have created all men.
What man can live and never see death? Who can escape the hand of the realm of the dead? Selah.
Where, O Lord, is your love of old, which in your faithfulness you swore to David?
Remember, O Lord, the insult flung at your servants; I bear in my heart the reproach of so many peoples,
the reproach of your enemies, O Lord, their insults hurled at the footsteps of your anointed.
Blessed be the Lord forever! Amen! Amen!

titres.titre: The frailty of man and the eternity of God

versets.t: A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, from age to age you have been our refuge.
Before the mountains were born, before you brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting you are God.
You turn man back to dust; you say, "Return, children of Adam!"
A thousand years in your eyes are like yesterday, a day already gone, like a watch in the night.
You sweep them away like a dream; in the morning they are like the grass that springs up:
in the morning it flowers and grows; by evening it withers and dries away.
Yes, your anger consumes us, your wrath fills us with terror.
You have set our sins before you, our secrets in the light of your face.
All our days flee away under your anger; our years come to an end like a sigh.
The span of our days? Seventy years, eighty for the strongest; and their pride is only toil and misery, for time passes swiftly, and we fly away.
Who can measure the force of your anger? Who fears you as your wrath deserves?
Teach us the true measure of our days, that we may gain a wise heart.
Return, Lord! How long? Have pity on your servants.
Fill us at daybreak with your faithful love, and we will sing for joy all the days of our life.
Give us joy for as many days as you have humbled us, for as many years as we have known misfortune.
Let your work appear to your servants, and your splendour to their children!
May the kindness of the Lord our God be upon us! Give lasting worth to the work of our hands; yes, give lasting worth to the work of our hands!

titres.titre: In the shadow of the Most High

versets.t: Whoever dwells in the shelter of the Most High rests in the shadow of the Almighty.
I say to the Lord, "My refuge, my fortress, my God, in whom I trust!"
For it is he who delivers you from the fowler's snare and from the deadly plague.
With his wings he covers you; under his feathers you find shelter; his faithfulness is a shield, a coat of armour.
You will not fear the terror of the night, nor the arrow that flies by day,
nor the plague that prowls in the darkness, nor the scourge that lays waste at noon.
Though a thousand fall at your side, ten thousand at your right hand, you will remain beyond its reach.
You need only open your eyes to see the reward of the wicked.
Yes, you have said, "The Lord is my refuge!" You have made the Most High your shelter.
No harm will overtake you, no scourge will come near your tent.
For he will command his angels to guard you on all your ways.
On their hands they will bear you up, lest your foot strike against a stone.
You will tread on the lion and the viper, you will trample the young lion and the serpent.
"Because he clings to me, I deliver him; I protect him, because he knows my name.
He calls to me, and I answer him; I am with him in distress; I deliver him and give him honour.
I fill him with length of days, and I let him see my salvation."

titres.titre: A song for the sabbath day

versets.t: A psalm. A song for the sabbath day.
It is good to give thanks to the Lord, to sing to your name, O Most High,
to proclaim your love in the morning, and your faithfulness through the nights,
on the ten-stringed lyre and the lute, to the sweet sound of the harp.
You gladden me, Lord, by your deeds; before the works of your hands I sing for joy.
How great are your works, Lord, how deep are your thoughts!
The stupid cannot know it, the fool cannot see it:
though the wicked spring up like grass, though all evildoers flourish, it is only to be destroyed for ever.
But you, Lord, are the Most High for ever.
See how your enemies, Lord, see how your enemies perish; they scatter, all the evildoers.
You lift up my strength like the horn of the wild ox; you have poured fresh oil upon me.
My eyes look down on those who watch for me, my ears hear the fate of the wicked who rise against me.
The just will grow like the palm tree, they will rise like the cedar of Lebanon.
Planted in the house of the Lord, they will flourish in the courts of our God.
Even in old age they still bear fruit, full of sap and green,
to proclaim that the Lord is upright: he is my rock, and in him there is no injustice.

titres.titre: The Lord is king, the world stands firm

versets.t: The Lord is king, robed in majesty; the Lord has robed himself, girded himself with strength. Yes, the world stands firm, it shall not be shaken.
Your throne stands firm from of old; you are from all eternity.
The rivers rise, Lord, the rivers raise their voice, the rivers raise their thunder.
Mightier than the voice of the great waters, mightier than the powerful waves of the sea, the Lord is majestic on high.
Your decrees are sure; holiness adorns your house, Lord, for the length of days.
God who renders justice, Lord, God who renders justice, appear!
Rise up, judge of the earth, give the proud what they deserve!
How long shall the wicked, Lord, how long shall the wicked triumph?
They pour out insolence, they boast, all these evildoers.
Lord, they crush your people, they oppress your heritage;
they kill the widow and the resident alien, they murder the orphans,
and they say, "The Lord sees nothing, the God of Jacob pays no heed."
Understand, then, you dull-witted among the people! You fools, when will you grow wise?
He who planted the ear, does he not hear? He who formed the eye, does he not see?
He who chastises the nations, does he not punish, he who teaches knowledge to mankind?
The Lord knows the thoughts of men: they are but a breath.
Happy the one whom you chastise, Lord, whom you teach from your law,
to give him peace in the days of evil, until the pit is dug for the wicked.
For the Lord does not forsake his people, he does not abandon his heritage:
judgment will return to justice, and all the upright of heart will follow it.
Who will rise up for me against the wicked? Who will stand for me against the evildoers?
If the Lord were not my help, I would soon dwell in the land of silence.
When I say, "My foot is slipping," your faithful love, Lord, holds me up.
When cares press in upon me, your consolations are my delight.
Can it be allied with you, this seat of ruin that works evil in the name of law?
They band against the life of the just, they condemn innocent blood.
But the Lord is my fortress, my God is the rock where I take refuge.
He will bring their crime back upon them, he will destroy them by their own malice; he will destroy them, the Lord our God!

titres.titre: "Come, let us sing for joy": do not harden your hearts

versets.t: Come, let us sing for joy to the Lord, let us acclaim the rock who saves us!
Let us come before him with thanksgiving, acclaim him with our songs!
For the Lord is the great God, the great king above all gods.
In his hand are the depths of the earth; the peaks of the mountains are his.
His is the sea, for he made it; the dry land too, his hands shaped it.
Come, let us bow down and worship, let us kneel before the Lord who made us!
For he is our God, and we are the people he leads, the flock guided by his hand. Today, if only you would hear his voice!
"Do not harden your hearts as at Meribah, as on the day of Massah in the desert,
where your fathers provoked me and put me to the test, though they had seen my works.
For forty years that generation wearied me, and I said: A people whose heart goes astray, who have not known my ways!
So in my anger I swore: They shall not enter my rest."

titres.titre: Sing to the Lord a new song

versets.t: Sing to the Lord a new song, sing to the Lord, all the earth!
Sing to the Lord, bless his name! From day to day proclaim his salvation;
tell of his glory among the nations, his wonders to all the peoples.
For the Lord is great, worthy of all praise, to be feared above all gods;
for all the gods of the peoples are nothing, but the Lord made the heavens.
Splendour and majesty are before him, power and beauty in his sanctuary.
Render to the Lord, you families of the peoples, render to the Lord glory and power;
render to the Lord the glory of his name! Bring your offering, enter his courts;
bow down before the Lord, radiant in holiness; tremble before him, all the earth!
Say among the nations, "The Lord is king!" Yes, the world stands firm, it shall not be shaken; he judges the peoples with fairness.
Joy in the heavens, gladness on the earth! Let the sea roar and all that fills it!
Let the fields exult with all they hold, let all the trees of the forest cry out for joy
before the Lord, for he comes, for he comes to judge the earth! He will judge the world with justice, and the peoples in his faithfulness.

titres.titre: The Lord is king, let the earth exult

versets.t: The Lord is king: let the earth exult, let the countless islands rejoice!
Cloud and mist surround him; justice and right are the foundation of his throne.
A fire goes before him and devours his foes on every side.
His lightning lights up the world; the earth sees it and trembles.
The mountains melt like wax before the Lord, before the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens proclaim his justice, and all the peoples see his glory.
Shame on all who worship carved images, who boast in their idols! Before him all the gods bow down.
Zion hears and rejoices, the towns of Judah exult because of your judgments, Lord.
For you, Lord, are the Most High over all the earth, exalted far above all gods.
You who love the Lord, hate evil! He guards the lives of his faithful, he delivers them from the hand of the wicked.
A light dawns for the just, and joy for the upright of heart.
You just, rejoice in the Lord, give thanks as you recall his holiness!

titres.titre: A new song for the victory of God

versets.t: A psalm. Sing to the Lord a new song, for he has done wonders; his right hand, his most holy arm has won him victory.
The Lord has made known his salvation, he has revealed his justice in the sight of the nations.
He has remembered his love and his faithfulness towards the house of Israel; to the ends of the earth the salvation of our God has been seen.
Acclaim the Lord, all the earth; break into cries of joy and music!
Make music to the Lord on the harp, on the harp, to the sound of song!
With trumpets and the blast of the horn, acclaim the King, the Lord!
Let the sea roar and all that fills it, the world and those who dwell in it!
Let the rivers clap their hands, let the mountains together cry out for joy
before the Lord, for he comes to judge the earth! He will judge the world with justice, and the peoples with fairness.

titres.titre: The God who is king, thrice holy

versets.t: The Lord is king: the peoples tremble; he is enthroned on the cherubim: the earth quakes.
The Lord is great in Zion, exalted above all the peoples.
Let them praise your name, great and awesome! He is holy.
Mighty is the King who loves right: it is you who established fairness, you who work in Jacob right and justice.
Exalt the Lord our God, bow down before his footstool. He is holy.
Moses and Aaron among his priests, Samuel among those who called on his name: they cried to the Lord, and he answered them.
In the pillar of cloud he spoke to them; they kept his decrees, the law he had given them.
Lord our God, you answered them; you were for them a God who forgives, yet did not leave their sins unpunished.
Exalt the Lord our God, bow down towards his holy mountain, for he is holy, the Lord our God!
A psalm for thanksgiving. Acclaim the Lord, all the earth!
Serve the Lord with gladness, come before him with songs of joy.
Acknowledge that the Lord is God. It is he who made us, and we are his; we, his people, the flock he leads.
Enter his gates with thanksgiving, his courts with songs of praise; give him thanks, bless his name.
For the Lord is good: his love is everlasting, his faithfulness endures from age to age.

titres.titre: The charter of the upright ruler

versets.t: Of David. A psalm. I will sing of faithful love and of right; it is you, Lord, that I praise.
I will follow the way of integrity: when will you come to me? I will walk with an upright heart within my house.
I will set nothing evil before my eyes; I hate crooked ways, they will get no hold on me.
The false heart will keep far from me, I want no part in evil.
Whoever slanders his neighbour in secret, him I will silence; the haughty look and the swollen heart, these I will not endure.
My eyes turn to the faithful of the land, that they may dwell beside me; whoever follows the way of integrity will be my servant.
He will not dwell in my house, the man of deceit; the liar will not stand before my eyes.
Every morning I will silence all the wicked of the land, to cut off from the city of the Lord all the evildoers.

titres.titre: The prayer of an afflicted soul and the eternity of God

versets.t: The prayer of an afflicted man, when he grows faint and pours out his lament before the Lord.
Lord, hear my prayer, let my cry come to you.
Do not hide your face from me in the day of my distress; turn your ear to me, on the day I call; be quick, answer me!
For my days vanish like smoke, my bones burn like a furnace.
Struck down like grass, my heart withers; I even forget to eat my bread.
From the force of my groaning, I am nothing but skin and bones.
I am like the owl of the desert, I am like the screech owl among the ruins.
I lie awake, and I am like a lonely bird on a rooftop.
All day long my enemies insult me; raging against me, they make my name a curse.
I eat ashes like bread, I mix my tears with my drink,
because of your anger and your indignation, for you have lifted me up and cast me far away.
My days are like a lengthening shadow, and I wither like grass.
But you, Lord, are enthroned for ever; your renown endures from age to age.
You will rise up and have pity on Zion, for it is time to show her pity: the hour has come.
Your servants cherish even her stones, they are moved with pity over her ruins.
Then the nations will fear the name of the Lord, and all the kings of the earth, your glory.
For the Lord rebuilds Zion, he appears in his glory;
he turns to the prayer of the destitute, he does not despise their plea.
Let this be written for the generation to come, and a people yet to be born will praise the Lord:
he has looked down from his holy height, from heaven the Lord has gazed upon the earth,
to hear the groaning of the captive, to set free those condemned to death,
that the name of the Lord may be proclaimed in Zion, and his praise in Jerusalem,
when peoples and kingdoms gather together to serve the Lord.
Along the way he has broken my strength, he has cut short my days.
I say: My God, do not take me away in the midst of my days, you whose years endure from age to age.
Long ago you founded the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They will perish, but you remain; they will all wear out like a garment, you will change them like clothing, and they will pass away.
But you are the same, and your years will have no end.
The children of your servants will have a home, and their offspring will stand firm before you.
Of David. Bless the Lord, O my soul; let all that is within me bless his holy name!
Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget none of his benefits!
It is he who forgives all your sins, who heals all your diseases;
it is he who redeems your life from the pit, who crowns you with faithful love and tenderness;
it is he who fills your desires with good things, and your youth is renewed like the eagle's.
The Lord does justice, he grants their right to all the oppressed.
He made known his ways to Moses, his mighty deeds to the children of Israel.
The Lord is tenderness and pity, slow to anger and rich in faithful love.
He does not always accuse, he does not hold his anger for ever.
He does not treat us as our sins deserve, he does not repay us according to our faults.
As high as the heavens are above the earth, so strong is his faithful love for those who fear him.
As far as the east is from the west, so far does he remove our sins from us.
As a father has pity on his children, the Lord has pity on those who fear him.
For he knows of what we are made, he remembers that we are dust.
Man! His days are like grass; he flowers like the flower of the field:
let a breath pass over it, and it is gone, and its place knows it no more.
But the faithful love of the Lord, for those who fear him, is from everlasting to everlasting, and his justice for their children's children,
for those who keep his covenant and remember to carry out his precepts.
The Lord has set his throne in the heavens, and his kingship rules over all.
Bless the Lord, you his angels, mighty heroes who carry out his word, attentive to the voice of his word!
Bless the Lord, all you his hosts, his servants who do his will!
Bless the Lord, all you his works, in every place of his dominion! Bless the Lord, O my soul!

titres.titre: A hymn to God the creator

versets.t: Bless the Lord, O my soul! Lord my God, you are infinitely great! You are clothed in splendour and majesty,
wrapped in light as in a robe. You spread out the heavens like a tent,
you build your dwelling on the waters above; you make the clouds your chariot, you ride on the wings of the wind.
You make the winds your messengers, flames of fire your servants.
You have set the earth on its foundations: it is unshakeable for ever.
You had covered it with the deep as with a garment; the waters stood above the mountains.
At your rebuke they fled; at the roar of your thunder they took flight.
The mountains rose up, the valleys sank down, to the place you had fixed for them.
You set a boundary they may not cross: never again will they cover the earth.
You send the springs into the ravines; they run between the mountains,
they give drink to all the beasts of the field; the wild donkeys quench their thirst.
Along their banks the birds of the sky settle, singing among the leaves.
From your lofty dwelling you water the mountains; the earth is filled with the fruit of your works.
You make the grass grow for the cattle, and the plants for the labour of man, that he may draw his bread from the earth,
the wine that gladdens the heart of man, the oil that makes his face shine, and the bread that sustains his heart.
They are well watered, the trees of the Lord, the cedars of Lebanon that he planted.
There the birds make their nests, and the stork makes its home in the cypress trees.
To the high mountains, the wild goats; to the rocks, the shelter of the rock badgers.
You made the moon to mark the seasons, and the sun that knows the hour of its setting.
You spread the darkness, and it is night: then all the beasts of the forest prowl.
The young lions roar after their prey, seeking their food from God.
When the sun rises, they withdraw and lie down in their dens.
Man goes out then to his labour, to his work, until evening.
How many are your works, Lord! In wisdom you have made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
Here is the sea, vast and wide: there teem, beyond counting, creatures small and great.
There the ships move along, and the Leviathan you formed to play in the waves.
All of them look to you to give them their food in due season.
You give it to them, they gather it up; you open your hand, they are filled with good things.
You hide your face: they are dismayed; you take away their breath: they die and return to their dust.
You send forth your breath: they are created, and you renew the face of the earth.
To the glory of the Lord, for ever! May the Lord rejoice in his works!
He looks at the earth, and it trembles; he touches the mountains, and they smoke.
I will sing to the Lord as long as I live, I will make music to my God as long as I have being.
May my song be pleasing to him! As for me, my joy is in the Lord.
May sinners vanish from the earth, may the wicked be no more! Bless the Lord, O my soul! Hallelujah!

titres.titre: The story of salvation, from Abraham to the promised land

versets.t: Give thanks to the Lord, call on his name, make known his deeds among the peoples!
Sing to him, make music for him, recount all his wonders!
Glory in his holy name; joy in the heart for those who seek the Lord!
Seek the Lord and his strength, seek his face without ceasing.
Remember the wonders he has done, his marvels, the judgments from his mouth,
you, the offspring of Abraham his servant, the children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is the Lord our God; his judgments reach over all the earth.
He remembers his covenant for ever, the word he promised for a thousand generations,
the covenant he made with Abraham, the oath he swore to Isaac.
He made it a law for Jacob, an everlasting covenant for Israel,
saying, "To you I give the land of Canaan: it will be your share of inheritance."
They were then few in number, a handful of resident aliens in that land;
they wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
He let no one oppress them, he rebuked kings on their account:
"Do not touch those I have anointed, do no harm to my prophets!"
He called down famine on the land, he cut off all supply of bread.
He sent a man ahead of them: Joseph, sold as a slave.
They bruised his feet with fetters, they put an iron collar on him,
until the day his word came true, when the oracle of the Lord proved him right.
The king had him set free, the ruler of peoples released him.
He made him master of his house, governor of all his possessions,
to instruct his princes as he pleased and teach wisdom to his elders.
Then Israel came into Egypt, Jacob lived as a stranger in the land of Ham.
God made his people very fruitful, stronger than their foes.
He turned their hearts to hate his people and to plot against his servants.
He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron, whom he had chosen.
Among them they performed his signs, his wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness, and it was night: they had not defied his word.
He turned their waters into blood and made their fish die.
Their land swarmed with frogs, even in the chambers of their kings.
He spoke a word: the gadflies came, the gnats over all their territory.
Instead of rain he gave them hail, flames of fire over their land.
He struck their vines and their fig trees, he shattered the trees of their country.
He spoke a word: the locusts came, the young locusts beyond number.
They devoured all the grass of the land, they devoured the fruit of their fields.
He struck down all the firstborn of the land, the firstfruits of all their vigour.
He brought out his people laden with silver and gold, and not one among their tribes stumbled.
Egypt rejoiced at their going, for the dread of Israel had seized it.
He spread a cloud to shelter them, and fire to light up the night.
At their asking he brought quail, and with bread from heaven he filled them.
He opened the rock: water gushed out, it flowed like a river through the parched land.
For he remembered his holy word, and Abraham his servant.
He brought out his people with rejoicing, his chosen ones with cries of joy.
He gave them the lands of the nations: they reaped the fruit of the peoples' toil,
that they might keep his precepts and observe his laws. Hallelujah!
Hallelujah! Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his faithful love is everlasting.
Who can tell the mighty deeds of the Lord, who can utter all his praise?
Happy those who keep what is right, who do justice at all times!
Remember me, Lord, in your favour towards your people; visit me with your salvation,
that I may see the good fortune of your chosen ones, that I may share the joy of your people and the pride of your heritage.
We have sinned like our fathers, we have done wrong, we have acted wickedly.
Our fathers in Egypt did not grasp your wonders; they forgot your great faithful love, they rebelled by the sea, the Red Sea.
Yet he saved them for the sake of his name, to make known his power.
He rebuked the Red Sea: it dried up, and he led them through the deep as through the open desert.
He saved them from the hand of the foe, he redeemed them from the hand of the oppressor.
The waters covered their adversaries: not one of them survived.
Then they believed his words, they sang his praise.
But quickly they forgot his works, they did not wait for his counsel;
in the desert they were seized with craving, in the wastelands they put God to the test.
He gave them what they demanded, but he sent a wasting disease upon them.
In the camp they grew jealous of Moses and of Aaron, the holy one of the Lord.
The earth opened, swallowed Dathan, and closed over the company of Abiram.
A fire blazed against their company, the flame devoured the wicked.
At Horeb they made a calf, they bowed down before an idol of metal.
They exchanged their glory for the image of an ox that feeds on grass.
They forgot God their saviour, who had done great things in Egypt,
wonders in the land of Ham, awesome deeds at the Red Sea.
He spoke of destroying them; but Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him, to turn back his destroying fury.
They scorned a land of delights, they did not believe his word;
in their tents they grumbled, they did not listen to the voice of the Lord.
So he raised his hand against them, swearing to make them fall in the desert,
to scatter their offspring among the nations, to disperse them across every land.
They yoked themselves to Baal of Peor, they ate sacrifices offered to the dead.
They provoked the Lord by their deeds, and a plague broke out among them.
But Phinehas rose up, he did justice, and the plague was stopped.
This was counted to him as justice, from age to age, for ever.
At the waters of Meribah they provoked the Lord, and Moses suffered because of them:
they embittered his spirit, and his lips spoke rashly.
They did not destroy the peoples the Lord had marked out for them;
they mingled with the nations and learned their ways.
They served their idols, which became a snare for them.
They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons;
they shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters, sacrificed to the idols of Canaan; and the land was defiled with this blood.
They made themselves unclean by their deeds, they prostituted themselves by their conduct.
The anger of the Lord blazed against his people; he came to abhor his heritage.
He handed them over to the nations; those who hated them ruled over them.
Their enemies oppressed them, they were crushed under their hand.
Many times he delivered them; but they, stubborn in their designs, sank deeper into their guilt.
Yet he looked on their distress, when he heard their cry.
For their sake he remembered his covenant; he relented, in his great faithful love.
He made them pitied by all who held them captive.
Save us, Lord our God, gather us from among the nations, that we may give thanks to your holy name and take our pride in praising you!
Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! And let all the people say: Amen! Hallelujah!

titres.titre: Let the redeemed give thanks to the Lord

versets.t: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his faithful love endures forever!
Let them say so, the redeemed of the Lord, those he has redeemed from the hand of the enemy
and gathered in from every land, from east and west, from north and from the sea.
They wandered in the wilderness, on lonely tracks, finding no city to live in.
Hungry and thirsty, they felt their life ebbing away.
In their distress they cried to the Lord, and he delivered them from their anguish.
He led them by a straight path to a city where they could live.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his faithful love, for his wonders on behalf of the children of men!
For he has quenched the thirst of the thirsty, and filled the hungry with good things.
They dwelt in darkness and the shadow of death, prisoners of misery and of iron,
for they had rebelled against the words of God and scorned the purpose of the Most High.
He bent their hearts low with hardship; they stumbled, and no one came to help.
In their distress they cried to the Lord, and he saved them from their anguish.
He drew them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and broke their chains.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his faithful love, for his wonders on behalf of the children of men!
For he has shattered the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron.
Fools, they suffered for their evil ways, brought low because of their sins.
All food was loathsome to them; they came to the very gates of death.
In their distress they cried to the Lord, and he saved them from their anguish.
He sent forth his word and healed them, and snatched them from the grave.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his faithful love, for his wonders on behalf of the children of men!
Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving, and recount his works with shouts of joy!
Others went out to sea in ships, doing their trade on the vast waters:
these have seen the works of the Lord, his wonders in the heart of the deep.
He spoke, and raised a stormy wind that lifted the waves high.
They rose up to the sky, they plunged into the depths; their courage melted away in the ordeal.
Reeling and staggering like drunken men, all their skill was lost.
In their distress they cried to the Lord, and he drew them out of their anguish.
He stilled the storm to a whisper, and the waves fell silent.
They rejoiced at the calm, and he led them to the haven they longed for.
Let them give thanks to the Lord for his faithful love, for his wonders on behalf of the children of men!
Let them exalt him in the assembly of the people, and praise him in the council of the elders!
He turns rivers into desert, springs of water into thirsty ground,
fruitful land into a waste of salt, because of the wickedness of those who live there.
He turns the desert into pools, parched land into springs of water.
There he settles the hungry, and they found a city to live in;
they sow fields and plant vineyards, and gather their fruit.
He blesses them, and they multiply, and he does not let their cattle grow few.
Then, brought low and humbled under the weight of misfortune and sorrow,
he who pours contempt on the mighty makes them wander in a trackless waste;
but he raises the poor from their misery, and makes their families as numerous as flocks.
The upright see it and rejoice, but all injustice shuts its mouth.
Whoever is wise will take these things to heart and understand the faithful love of the Lord.

titres.titre: A song of trust and victory

versets.t: A song. A psalm of David.
My heart is steadfast, O God; I will sing and make music to you. Awake, my glory!
Awake, harp and lyre! I will awaken the dawn.
I will praise you among the peoples, Lord; I will sing to you among the nations.
For your love rises higher than the heavens, and your faithfulness to the clouds.
Be exalted above the heavens, O God! Let your glory shine over all the earth!
That those you love may be delivered, save with your right hand and answer me!
God has spoken in his sanctuary: "In triumph I will parcel out Shechem, I will measure out the valley of Succoth.
Gilead is mine, Manasseh is mine! Ephraim is the helmet on my head, Judah my scepter.
Moab is the basin where I wash; on Edom I cast my sandal; over the land of the Philistines I raise my shout of victory."
Who will lead me to the fortified city? Who will bring me as far as Edom?
Is it not you, O God, who had cast us off, you who no longer went out with our armies?
Bring us help against the oppressor, for the help of man is worth nothing.
With God we will do mighty deeds; it is he who will trample our enemies.

titres.titre: Prayer of a man overwhelmed by hatred

versets.t: For the choirmaster. A psalm of David. God of my praise, do not stay silent!
For the mouth of the wicked, the mouth of the deceitful, is opened against me; they speak to me with lying tongues,
they assail me with words of hatred, they fight against me without cause.
In return for my friendship they accuse me; but I am nothing but prayer.
They repay me evil for good, and hatred for my love.
Set a wicked man against him, let an accuser stand at his right hand!
When he is judged, let him come out guilty, and let his very prayer be counted as sin!
Let his days be cut short, let another take his office!
Let his children become orphans, and his wife a widow!
Let his children wander and beg, driven from their ruined homes!
Let the creditor seize all he owns, let strangers plunder the fruit of his toil!
Let no one show him kindness, let no one pity his orphans!
Let his descendants be doomed to vanish, his name blotted out in the next generation!
Let the guilt of his fathers be remembered before the Lord, and the sin of his mother never be blotted out!
Let them be ever before the Lord, and may he cut off their memory from the earth!
For this man never thought to show mercy; he hounded the poor, the afflicted, the brokenhearted, even to death.
He loved cursing: let it fall upon him! He despised blessing: let it stay far from him!
He wrapped himself in cursing like a cloak: let it seep into him like water, like oil into his bones!
Let it be the garment that wraps him, the belt that always binds him!
Such is the wage the Lord holds ready for my accusers, for those who speak evil against me.
But you, Lord my God, act for me, for the sake of your name; in your great faithful love, deliver me.
For I am poor and afflicted, and my heart is wounded within me.
I fade like the evening shadow; I am shaken off like a locust.
From fasting my knees give way, and my body has grown gaunt.
I have become an object of scorn to them; they see me and shake their heads.
Help me, Lord my God, save me in your faithful love!
Let them know that this is your hand, that you, Lord, have done it!
They may curse, but you will bless; let them rise up covered in shame, and let your servant rejoice!
Let my accusers be clothed in disgrace, wrapped in their own dishonor like a cloak!
With a loud voice I will give thanks to the Lord; I will praise him in the midst of the throng;
for he stands at the right hand of the poor, to save him from those who condemn him.

titres.titre: The Messiah, king and priest at God's right hand

versets.t: A psalm of David. The Lord says to my lord: "Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool for your feet."
From Zion the Lord will extend the scepter of your power: "Rule in the midst of your enemies!"
Yours is sovereignty on the day of your power, in holy splendor; from the womb, before the dawn, I have begotten you.
The Lord has sworn and will not go back on it: "You are a priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek."
The Lord is at your right hand: on the day of his wrath he shatters kings.
He judges the nations, he heaps up the dead, he shatters heads over the wide earth.
On the way he drinks from the stream; and so he lifts up his head.

titres.titre: The works of the Lord, worthy of praise

versets.t: Hallelujah! I give thanks to the Lord with all my heart, in the circle of the upright, in the assembly.
Great are the works of the Lord, worth studying for all who love them.
Splendor and beauty mark all that he does, and his justice stands forever.
He has left a memorial of his wonders; the Lord is tender and compassionate.
He gives food to those who fear him; he remembers his covenant forever.
He has shown his people the power of his works, giving them the inheritance of the nations.
Truth and justice are the works of his hands; sure are all his precepts,
established forever and ever, made of truth and uprightness.
He has sent deliverance to his people, sealed his covenant forever; holy and awesome is his name.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: all who live by it are truly prudent. His praise stands forever.

titres.titre: The happiness of the man who fears God

versets.t: Hallelujah! Happy the man who fears the Lord, who takes great delight in his commandments!
His descendants will be mighty on the earth; the generation of the upright will be blessed.
Plenty and wealth are in his house, and his justice stands forever.
For the upright a light rises in the darkness: he is tender, compassionate, and just.
Happy the man who is generous and lends, who orders his affairs with justice!
He will never be shaken; the just man will be remembered forever.
He has no fear of bad news; his heart is steadfast, trusting in the Lord.
His heart is firm, he is without fear, and in the end he will look down on his enemies.
He gives to the poor with open hands, his justice stands forever, his head is lifted high in glory.
The wicked man sees it and is angry; he gnashes his teeth and wastes away: the desire of the wicked will come to nothing.

titres.titre: The God who casts down and raises up

versets.t: Hallelujah! Praise, O servants of the Lord, praise the name of the Lord!
Blessed be the name of the Lord, now and forever!
From the rising of the sun to its setting, praised be the name of the Lord!
The Lord is high above all nations, his glory rises above the heavens.
Who is like the Lord our God? He is enthroned on high,
and stoops down to look upon the heavens and the earth.
From the dust he lifts up the weak; from the refuse heap he raises the poor,
to seat him among princes, the princes of his people.
To the barren woman he gives a home, a happy mother in the midst of her children. Hallelujah!
When Israel came out of Egypt, when the house of Jacob left a people of foreign tongue,
Judah became God's sanctuary, and Israel his domain.
The sea saw it and fled, the Jordan turned back to its source;
the mountains leaped like rams, the hills like lambs.
What ails you, sea, that you flee? And you, Jordan, that you turn back to your source?
And you, mountains, that you leap like rams, and you, hills, like lambs?
Tremble, O earth, before the Lord, before the God of Jacob,
who turns the rock into a pool, the hard stone into a gushing spring.

titres.titre: The true God and the mute idols

versets.t: Not to us, Lord, not to us, but to your name give the glory, for your love, for your faithfulness!
Why should the nations say, "Where, then, is their God?"
Our God is in the heavens: whatever he wills, he does.
Their idols are silver and gold, the work of human hands.
They have mouths but do not speak, eyes but do not see,
ears but do not hear, a nose but do not smell,
hands but do not touch, feet but do not walk; from their throat comes no sound.
Let those who make them become like them, and all who trust in them!
Israel, trust in the Lord: he is their help and their shield.
House of Aaron, trust in the Lord: he is their help and their shield.
You who fear the Lord, trust in the Lord: he is their help and their shield.
The Lord has remembered us: he will bless! He will bless the house of Israel, he will bless the house of Aaron,
he will bless those who fear the Lord, the small together with the great.
May the Lord fill you with his gifts, you and your children!
May you be blessed by the Lord, who made heaven and earth!
The heavens are the heavens of the Lord; the earth he has given to the children of men.
It is not the dead who praise the Lord, nor any who go down into silence,
but we, the living, we bless the Lord, now and forever. Hallelujah!

titres.titre: Thanksgiving of one saved from death

versets.t: I love the Lord, for he hears my pleading voice;
for he has turned his ear to me, and all my life I will call upon him.
The cords of death bound me tight, the anguish of the realm of the dead had gripped me; I was caught in distress and sorrow.
Then I called on the name of the Lord: "Lord, I beg you, save my life!"
The Lord is gracious and just; our God is full of tenderness.
The Lord watches over the little ones; I was brought low, and he saved me.
Return to your rest, O my soul, for the Lord has been good to you.
Yes, you have saved my life from death, my eyes from tears, my feet from stumbling.
I will walk before the Lord, in the land of the living.
I keep my faith, even when I say, "I am utterly brought low."
In my dismay I said, "Every man is a liar."
How can I repay the Lord for all the good he has done me?
I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord.
I will fulfill my vows to the Lord in the presence of all his people.
Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of his faithful ones.
Lord, I beg you, I am your servant, your servant, the son of your handmaid; you have loosed my bonds.
I will offer you a sacrifice of thanksgiving and call on the name of the Lord.
I will fulfill my vows to the Lord in the presence of all his people,
in the courts of the house of the Lord, in your midst, O Jerusalem. Hallelujah!
Praise the Lord, all you nations; extol him, all you peoples!
For his love toward us is strong, and the faithfulness of the Lord stands forever. Hallelujah!

titres.titre: The stone rejected, become the cornerstone

versets.t: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his faithful love endures forever!
Let Israel say, "Yes, his faithful love endures forever!"
Let the house of Aaron say, "Yes, his faithful love endures forever!"
Let those who fear the Lord say, "Yes, his faithful love endures forever!"
In my distress I called on the Lord; the Lord answered me and set me free.
The Lord is on my side, I fear nothing: what can man do to me?
The Lord is on my side, he is my help; I will look on the defeat of my enemies.
Better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in man.
Better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in the mighty.
All the nations surrounded me: in the name of the Lord I cut them down.
They surrounded me, they closed in on me: in the name of the Lord I cut them down.
They surrounded me like bees; they blazed up like a fire of thorns: in the name of the Lord I cut them down.
I was pushed hard, pushed to make me fall, but the Lord came to my help.
My strength and my song is the Lord; he has been my salvation.
Shouts of joy and victory ring out in the tents of the just: "The right hand of the Lord has done a mighty deed!
The right hand of the Lord is lifted high, the right hand of the Lord has done a mighty deed!"
No, I will not die: I will live to recount the works of the Lord.
The Lord has disciplined me hard, but he has not handed me over to death.
Open to me the gates of justice: I will enter through them to give thanks to the Lord.
This is the gate of the Lord: the just will enter through it.
I give you thanks, for you have answered me and become my salvation.
The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
This is the Lord's doing: it is a wonder in our eyes.
This is the day the Lord has made: let us be filled with joy and gladness in it!
Lord, I beg you, grant salvation! Lord, I beg you, grant victory!
Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! From the house of the Lord we bless you.
The Lord is God, and he gives us light. Begin the festal procession, branches in hand, up to the horns of the altar.
You are my God, and I give you thanks; my God, I exalt you.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his faithful love endures forever!

titres.titre: The love of the law of God

versets.t: Happy those whose way is blameless, who walk according to the law of the Lord!
Happy those who keep his decrees, who seek him with all their heart,
who do no wrong and walk in his ways!
You yourself have given your precepts, to be kept with care.
May my ways be steadfast in keeping your statutes!
Then I will have no shame when I look upon all your commandments.
I will praise you with an upright heart as I learn your just decisions.
Your statutes I long to keep: do not utterly forsake me.
How will a young man keep his way pure? By watching over it according to your word.
I seek you with all my heart: do not let me stray from your commandments.
I treasure your promise deep in my heart, so as not to sin against you.
Blessed are you, Lord! Teach me your statutes.
With my lips I recount all the decisions of your mouth.
Following your decrees is my joy, more than all riches.
I long to meditate on your precepts, to keep my eyes on your paths.
I delight in your statutes; I do not forget your word.
Do good to your servant: I will live and keep your word.
Open my eyes, that I may behold the wonders of your law.
I am a stranger on the earth: do not hide your commandments from me.
My soul is consumed with longing for your decisions at all times.
You rebuke the proud, those accursed ones who stray from your commandments.
Take away from me shame and contempt, for I keep your decrees.
Though princes sit and speak against me, your servant meditates on your statutes.
Yes, your decrees are my delight: they are my counselors.
My soul clings to the dust: give me life according to your word.
I laid my ways before you, and you answered me: teach me your statutes.
Make me understand the way of your precepts, and I will meditate on your wonders.
My soul weeps for sorrow: raise me up according to your word.
Keep the way of falsehood far from me, and graciously grant me your law.
I have chosen the way of faithfulness; I set your decisions before me.
I hold fast to your decrees: Lord, do not put me to shame.
I run in the way of your commandments, for you enlarge my heart.
Teach me, Lord, the way of your statutes, and I will keep it to the end.
Give me understanding, and I will keep your law, and observe it with all my heart.
Lead me along the path of your commandments, for in it I find my joy.
Incline my heart to your decrees, and not to gain.
Turn my eyes away from worthless things; give me life in your way.
Keep your promise to your servant, the promise you make to those who fear you.
Take away the insult that I dread, for your decisions are good.
See how I long for your precepts: in your justice, give me life.
Let your faithful love come upon me, Lord, and your salvation, according to your promise!
Then I will answer those who insult me, for I trust in your word.
Do not take the word of truth from my mouth, for I hope in your decisions.
I will keep your law without ceasing, always and forever.
I will walk in freedom, for I seek your precepts.
Before kings I will speak of your decrees, and not be ashamed.
Your commandments are my delight; I love them.
I lift up my hands to your commandments, which I love, and I meditate on your statutes.
Remember your word to your servant: in it you have given me hope.
This is my comfort in my misery: your promise gives me life.
The proud heap their mockery on me: I do not turn away from your law.
I remember your decisions of old, Lord, and in them I find comfort.
Anger seizes me at the wicked who forsake your law.
Your statutes are the theme of my songs, in my house of exile.
By night I remember your name, Lord, and I keep your law.
This has fallen to me: to keep your precepts.
My portion, Lord, I have said, is to keep your words.
I implore you with all my heart: have mercy on me according to your promise.
I consider my ways, and turn my steps back to your decrees.
I hurry, without delay, to observe your commandments.
Though the snares of the wicked surround me, I do not forget your law.
In the middle of the night I rise to give you thanks for your just decisions.
I am a friend to all who fear you, to those who keep your precepts.
The earth is full of your faithful love, Lord: teach me your statutes.
You have done good to your servant, Lord, according to your word.
Teach me good sense and discernment, for I believe in your commandments.
Before I was humbled, I went astray; now I keep your promise.
You who are good and do good, teach me your statutes.
The proud smear me with lies; but I, with all my heart, keep your precepts.
Their heart is gross like fat; but I delight in your law.
It was good for me to be humbled, that I might learn your statutes.
The law of your mouth is worth more to me than mountains of gold and silver.
Your hands have made me and formed me: give me understanding to learn your commandments.
Those who fear you will see me and rejoice, for I hope in your word.
I know, Lord, that your decisions are just, and that in faithfulness you have humbled me.
Let your faithful love console me, according to the promise made to your servant!
Let your tenderness come upon me, and I will live, for your law is my delight.
Shame on the proud who wrong me without cause! But I meditate on your precepts.
Let them turn to me, those who fear you, those who know your decrees!
Let my heart be blameless toward your statutes, that I may not be put to shame.
My soul longs for your salvation; I hope in your word.
My eyes long for your promise; I say, "When will you comfort me?"
Here I am like a wineskin dried in the smoke; yet I do not forget your statutes.
How many are the days of your servant? When will you bring judgment on my persecutors?
The proud have dug pits for me, in defiance of your law.
All your commandments are faithful; I am persecuted without cause: help me!
They nearly made an end of me on the earth; but I do not forsake your precepts.
In your faithful love, give me life, and I will keep the decrees of your mouth.
Forever, Lord, your word stands, firm in the heavens.
Age after age your faithfulness endures; you set the earth in place, and it stands.
All things stand today by your decisions, for the whole universe serves you.
Had your law not been my delight, I would have perished in my misery.
I will never forget your precepts, for by them you have given me life.
I am yours: save me, for I seek your precepts.
The wicked lie in wait to destroy me; but I attend to your decrees.
