There was also a covenant with David, son of Jesse, of the tribe of Judah: the king's inheritance passes from son to single son, while the inheritance of Aaron goes to all his descendants.
May the Lord give you wisdom in your heart to judge his people with justice, so that their prosperity may not vanish, nor their glory in the ages to come!

Valiant in war was Joshua, son of Nun, successor of Moses in the prophetic office; true to his name, he was great in saving the Lord's chosen ones, in punishing the enemies who rebelled, and in putting Israel in possession of its inheritance.
What glory when he raised his hands and brandished the sword against the cities!
Who before him had ever stood firm like that? For it was the Lord himself who delivered the enemies to him.
Was it not at a gesture of his hand that the sun stood still, and one day counted as two?
He called on the Most High, the Sovereign, while he pressed the enemies on every side, and the great Lord answered him with hailstones of fearsome force:

he fell upon the enemy nation and annihilated it in the descent, so that the nations might know the power of his arms and know that he fought under the eyes of the Lord; for he followed the Almighty faithfully.

Already, in the time of Moses, he had shown his faithfulness, he and Caleb, son of Jephunneh, by standing up to the assembly, by keeping the people from sinning, and by silencing the murmuring of the wicked.
So these two alone were spared, out of six hundred thousand men on foot, to enter the inheritance, the land flowing with milk and honey.
The Lord gave Caleb a vigor that stayed with him into old age, so that he might climb the heights of the land, whose inheritance his descendants kept,
that all Israel might know that it is good to follow the Lord.
And the Judges, each according to his name, all those whose hearts did not play the harlot and who did not turn away from the Lord: may their memory be a blessing!
May their bones flower again from their tomb, and may their name live again in their illustrious sons!
Samuel was beloved of his Lord; a prophet of the Lord, he established the kingship and anointed princes for his people.
He judged the assembly according to the law of the Lord, and the Lord watched over Jacob;
by his faithfulness he proved a true prophet, and by his words he was known to be a truthful seer.
He called on the sovereign Lord when the enemies pressed him on every side, offering a suckling lamb;
and the Lord thundered from heaven, making his voice ring out with a crash;
he crushed the enemy leaders and all the princes of the Philistines.
Before the hour of his eternal rest, Samuel called the Lord and his anointed to witness: "From no one have I taken a gift, not even a pair of sandals"; and no one could accuse him.
Even after he had fallen asleep, he prophesied and foretold the king his end; from the depths of the earth he raised his voice to blot out, by his prophecy, the iniquity of the people.
After him came Nathan, to prophesy in the days of David.
As the fat is set apart from the peace offering, so David was set apart among the sons of Israel.
He played with lions as with young goats, with bears as with lambs.
While still young, did he not strike down the giant and remove the people's shame, when, with a sling-shot, he brought down the insolence of Goliath?
For he called on the Lord, the Most High, who gave strength to his right hand to lay low the mighty warrior and raise up the power of his people.
So they celebrated him for his ten thousands, they praised him for the blessings of the Lord, they offered him the crown of glory;
for he crushed the enemies all around, annihilated the Philistines, his adversaries, and broke their power forever.
In all his works, he gave thanks to the Holy One, the Most High, with words of praise; with all his heart he sang hymns and loved the One who made him.
He set up singers before the altar, to whose voices he had sweet melodies sung;
he gave brilliance to the feasts and splendor to the festivals, while the holy name of the Lord was celebrated and, from early morning, the sanctuary resounded.
The Lord forgave his faults and exalted his power forever; he assured him a royal covenant and a throne of glory in Israel.
After him arose a son full of wisdom who, thanks to his father, lived in ease:
Solomon reigned in days of peace, God having given him rest all around, so that he might build a house for his name and prepare an everlasting sanctuary.
How wise you were in your youth, overflowing with intelligence like a river!
Your spirit covered the earth, you filled it with profound sayings;
your name reached the distant islands, and you were loved for your peace;
for your songs, your proverbs, your parables and your answers, the world admired you.
In the name of the Lord God, called the God of Israel, you amassed gold like tin and heaped up silver like lead.
But you gave your loins to women and gave them power over your body;
you tarnished your glory, profaned your race, and drew down anger on your children. I groan over your folly,
for it split the empire in two and brought forth from Ephraim a rebellious kingdom.

But the Lord does not abandon his mercy, and none of his works perishes; he will not cut off the posterity of his chosen one, he will not destroy the race of the one who loved him: he has left a remnant to Jacob, and to David a shoot from his stock.

Solomon rested with his fathers, leaving behind one of his own, the folly of the people, devoid of good sense: Rehoboam, who by his decisions drove the people to revolt, and Jeroboam, son of Nebat, who made Israel sin and opened to Ephraim the way of sin;
their faults multiplied so greatly that they were carried far from their land;
they sought out every kind of evil, until vengeance fell upon them.
Then arose Elijah, a prophet like fire, whose word burned like a torch.
He brought famine upon them and, by his zeal, reduced the people to a small number;
by the word of the Lord he shut up the sky and three times brought fire down from it.
How you covered yourself with glory, Elijah, by your wonders! Who can boast of being your equal?
You who raised a dead man from the realm of the dead, by the word of the Most High;
you who cast kings down into ruin and illustrious men from their beds into death;
you who, at Sinai, heard rebukes, and at Horeb decrees of vengeance;
you who anointed kings to punish, and prophets to succeed you;
you who were taken up in a whirlwind of fire, on a chariot with horses of fire;
you who were appointed, in the warnings for the times to come, to appease anger before it breaks out, to turn the hearts of fathers toward their children and to restore the tribes of Jacob.
Happy are those who will see you and who have fallen asleep in love, for we too shall live!
When Elijah was enveloped in the whirlwind, Elisha was filled with his spirit; in his days no prince shook him, and no one dominated him.
Nothing was impossible for him, and even in the tomb his body prophesied:
in his lifetime he worked wonders, and in death he accomplished marvels.

Despite all this, the people did not repent and did not renounce sin, until they were deported far from their land and scattered over all the earth. Only a small people remained, with a leader of the house of David.
Some of them did what pleases the Lord, others multiplied their faults.
Hezekiah fortified his city and brought water into it; with iron he cut through the rock and built reservoirs.
In his time Sennacherib came up, who sent the Rabshakeh; this man raised his hand against Zion and boasted insolently.
Then hearts and hands trembled, and they were in anguish like a woman in labor;
they called on the merciful Lord, hands stretched out toward him, and from heaven the Holy One heard at once and delivered them through the ministry of Isaiah.
He struck the camp of the Assyrians, and his angel exterminated them;
for Hezekiah did what pleases the Lord and held firm in the ways of David his father, according to the counsel of Isaiah, the great prophet, truthful in his visions.
In his time the sun went back, and he prolonged the king's life.
By a mighty inspiration, he saw the future, consoled the mourners of Zion, and foretold what must happen until the end of time, the hidden things before they came to pass.
The memory of Josiah is a perfume blended by the art of the perfumer; in every mouth it is sweet as honey, like music at a banquet.
He conducted himself well in bringing the people back to conversion and in doing away with the abominations of impiety;
he turned his whole heart to the Lord, and in the days of the godless he strengthened piety.
Apart from David, Hezekiah, and Josiah, all fell short: having forsaken the law of the Most High, the kings of Judah ran to their ruin,
for they handed over their power to others and their glory to a foreign nation.
They burned the chosen holy city, they left its streets deserted,
as Jeremiah had foretold, whom they had mistreated, he who was consecrated a prophet from his mother's womb to uproot, destroy, and ruin, but also to build and to plant.
Ezekiel beheld the vision of glory that the Lord showed him on the chariot of the cherubim;
he called to mind the threatening storm against the enemies, and did good to those who walked the straight way.
As for the twelve prophets, may their bones flower again from their tomb, for they comforted Jacob and saved him by a firm hope!
How shall we celebrate Zerubbabel? He was like a signet ring on the right hand;
so too Jeshua, son of Jozadak: the two of them, in their days, rebuilt the house of God and raised up the holy temple of the Lord, destined for eternal glory.
Great too is the memory of Nehemiah, who raised up our walls in ruins, restored our gates and their bars, and rebuilt our houses.
No man was created on earth like Enoch, for he was taken up from the earth;
no man was born like Joseph, leader of his brothers, support of his people, whose bones were kept with care.
Shem and Seth were glorified among men, but above every living being, in creation, is Adam.
Simon, son of Onias, the high priest, repaired in his lifetime the house of the Lord and, in his days, strengthened the temple;
by him were laid the foundations that doubled the height of the rampart supporting the temple enclosure;
in his time the reservoir of waters was dug, a bronze basin as vast as the sea.
He watched over his people to preserve them from ruin and fortified the city against siege.
How majestic he was, surrounded by his people, when he came out from behind the veil!
Like the morning star amid the clouds, like the full moon,
like the sun shining on the temple of the Most High, like the rainbow gleaming in the clouds of glory,
like the rose in spring, like the lily by the waters, like the branch of the terebinth in summer,
like incense on the fire of the censer, like a vessel of solid gold adorned with all kinds of precious stones,
like the olive tree laden with fruit, like the cypress that rises toward the clouds.
When he put on the robe of honor and arrayed himself in all his ornaments, going up to the holy altar, he made the whole sanctuary enclosure resplendent;

when he received from the hands of the priests the portions of the victims, standing by the hearth of the altar, surrounded by his brothers as by a crown, he appeared like a majestic cedar of Lebanon, and they, like the trunks of palm trees around him;
all the sons of Aaron, in their splendid array, held in their hands the offering of the Lord, before the whole assembly of Israel.
Completing the service of the altars and arranging the offering of the Most High Almighty, he reached out his hand toward the cup of libations and poured out the juice of the grape;
he poured it at the foot of the altar, a fragrance pleasing to the Most High, the great King.
Then the sons of Aaron raised a shout, sounded their trumpets of beaten metal and made a mighty clamor ring out, as a memorial before the Most High.
And all the people, with one accord, fell face down on the ground to worship their Lord, the Almighty God, the Most High.
The singers made their praises heard, and the vast temple resounded with sweet harmonies.
The people begged the Lord Most High, in prayer before the Merciful One, until the service of the Lord was completed and the liturgy fulfilled.
Then the high priest came down, raised his hands over the whole assembly of the sons of Israel, to give from his lips the blessing of the Lord and to glory in his name;
and the people bowed down again to receive the blessing of the Most High.
And now, bless the Lord of all, who everywhere does great things, who has exalted our days from our mother's womb and treats us according to his mercy.
May he give us gladness of heart, and may peace reign in our days in Israel, as in the days of old;
may his mercy remain faithfully with us, and may he deliver us in his time!
There are two nations that my soul detests, and the third is not even a nation:
the inhabitants of Mount Seir, the Philistines, and the foolish people who dwell in Shechem.
I have set down in this book a teaching of wisdom and knowledge, I, Joshua son of Sira, of Jerusalem, who have poured out wisdom from my heart.
Happy is the one who devotes himself to it: by keeping these things in his heart, he will grow wise;
for if he puts them into practice, he will be strong in all things, because the light of the Lord is his path.
I will celebrate you, O Lord, my King, and praise you, O God my Savior; I give thanks to your name,
for you have been my protector and my support: you have saved my body from ruin, from the snare of the slanderous tongue, from lips that forge falsehood; in the face of my adversaries,

you have been my support and delivered me, in your great mercy and for your name's sake, from those who gnashed their teeth, ready to devour me, from the hand of those who sought my life, from all the distresses that beset me,
from the suffocation of a fire that encircled me, from a fire I had not kindled,
from the depths of the realm of the dead, from the impure tongue, from the lying word carried to the king, from the slander of an unjust tongue.
My soul was near to death, my life was going down to the realm of the dead, below;
they surrounded me on every side, and there was no one to help me; I looked for support among men, and there was none.
Then I remembered your mercy, O Lord, and your works of old: you save those who hope in you and deliver them from the hand of their enemies.
And, prostrate on the ground, I sent up my prayer, begging you to save me from death;
I called on the Lord, the father of my Lord, that he might not abandon me in the days of distress, in the time of the proud, when no one was helping:
"I will praise your name without ceasing and will sing it in thanksgiving." And my prayer was heard:
you saved me from ruin and delivered me in the time of misfortune. Therefore I will celebrate you and praise you, and I will bless the name of the Lord.
When I was young, before my travels, I openly sought wisdom in my prayer.
Before the temple I asked for her, and to the very end I will seek her.
As I watched her blossom like the ripening grape, my heart rejoiced in her; my foot walked straight, and from my youth I followed her track.
I bent my ear a little, and I received her, and in her I found rich instruction;
thanks to her, I made great progress: to the One who gives me wisdom, I will give glory!
For I resolved to put her into practice; I sought after the good, and I will not be put to shame.
My soul struggled for her, I was attentive to my deeds; I stretched out my hands toward heaven and lamented my ignorance.
Toward her I directed my soul, and in purity I found her; with her, from the beginning, I gained understanding, and so I will not be forsaken.
My heart was stirred to seek her: and so I gained a precious possession.
The Lord gave me as a reward the gift of speech, and I will use it to praise him.
Come to me, you who are untaught, and take up your place in the house of instruction:
why remain deprived of her, your souls so thirsty?
I have opened my mouth and spoken: acquire her without money;
bend your neck under her yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is close at hand, within reach.
See with your own eyes: I have labored little, and I have found great rest.
Receive instruction, even at great cost: through her you will gain much gold.
May your soul rejoice in the mercy of the Lord, and do not blush to praise him.
Do your work before the appointed time, and in his time he will give you your reward.

titres.titre: The vision of Isaiah concerning Judah and Jerusalem
A worship without justice, which God rejects
The unfaithful city, purified by judgment

versets.t: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Hear, O heavens! Give ear, O earth! For the Lord speaks: I reared children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against me.
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's stall; but Israel does not know, my people do not understand.
Woe! A sinful nation, a people weighed down with guilt, a brood of evildoers, corrupt children! They have forsaken the Lord, despised the Holy One of Israel, they have turned their backs on him.
Where will you be struck again, you who persist in rebellion? The whole head is sick, the whole heart is faint.
From the sole of the foot to the crown of the head, nothing is sound: only wounds, bruises, and open sores, neither cleansed nor bandaged nor soothed with oil.
Your country lies desolate, your cities are burned with fire; before your eyes, strangers devour your soil: it is a devastation, like the ravage of invaders.
The daughter of Zion is left alone, like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a field of cucumbers, like a besieged city.
Had the Lord of hosts not left us a small remnant, we would be like Sodom, we would resemble Gomorrah.
Hear the word of the Lord, you rulers of Sodom! Give ear to the teaching of our God, you people of Gomorrah!

What are your countless sacrifices to me? says the Lord. I have had enough of rams offered as burnt offerings and the fat of fattened calves; the blood of bulls and lambs and goats, in it I take no pleasure.
When you come to appear before me, who has asked this of you, this trampling of my courts?
Stop bringing worthless offerings: incense is an abomination to me. New moons, sabbaths, assemblies, I cannot endure iniquity joined to your solemn feasts.
Your new moons and your festivals I hate: they have become a burden to me, I am weary of bearing them.
When you stretch out your hands, I hide my eyes from you; though you multiply your prayers, I do not listen: your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean! Remove your evil deeds from my sight. Cease to do evil,
learn to do good. Seek justice, come to the aid of the oppressed, defend the fatherless, plead for the widow.
Come now, let us reason together, says the Lord: though your sins are as scarlet, they shall become white as snow; though they are red as crimson, they shall become like wool.
If you are willing and obey, you shall eat the best of the land;
but if you refuse and rebel, the sword shall devour you. Yes, the mouth of the Lord has spoken.
How has she become a prostitute, the faithful city? She was full of uprightness, justice dwelt in her; and now, murderers!
Your silver has turned to dross, your wine is watered down.
Your princes are rebels, partners with thieves; all of them love bribes and chase after gifts; they do not defend the fatherless, and the cause of the widow never reaches them.
Therefore, this is the oracle of the Master, the Lord of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel: Ah, I will rid myself of my adversaries, I will avenge myself on my enemies.
I will turn my hand against you, I will smelt away your dross as with lye, I will remove all your impurities.
I will restore your judges as at the first, your counsellors as at the beginning. Then you shall be called City of Justice, Faithful City.
Zion shall be redeemed by justice, and those who return, by righteousness.
But rebels and sinners shall be broken together, and those who forsake the Lord shall perish.
Yes, you shall be ashamed of the sacred oaks you so loved, you shall blush for the gardens you cherished.
For you shall be like an oak whose foliage withers, like a garden without water.
The strong man shall become tinder, and his work a spark; the two shall burn together, with no one to quench them.

titres.titre: The mountain of the Lord, goal of the nations
The day of the Lord against pride

versets.t: The word that Isaiah son of Amoz received in a vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
It shall come to pass, in the last days, that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established as the highest of the mountains, towering over the hills. To it all the nations shall stream,

and many peoples shall set out and say: "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob! He will teach us his ways, and we will walk in his paths." For out of Zion comes instruction, and out of Jerusalem the word of the Lord.

He shall be the arbiter of the nations, the judge of many peoples. They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Never again shall one nation raise the sword against another, nor shall they learn war anymore.
House of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the Lord!
Yes, you have abandoned your people, the house of Jacob, because it is filled with diviners from the East and sorcerers like the Philistines, and it strikes bargains with foreigners.
Their land is filled with silver and gold, their treasures without end; their land is filled with horses, their chariots without number.
Their land is filled with idols; they bow down before the work of their hands, before what their fingers have made.
But man shall be brought low, everyone shall be humbled: do not forgive them!
Go into the rock, hide in the dust, before the terror of the Lord and the splendour of his majesty!
The haughty eyes of man shall be lowered, the pride of the mighty shall be brought down; the Lord alone shall be exalted, on that day.
For the Lord of hosts shall have his day against all that is proud and arrogant, against all that is lifted up, to bring it low:
against all the cedars of Lebanon, lofty and lifted up, and against all the oaks of Bashan;
against all the high mountains and all the lofty hills;
against every proud tower and every fortified wall;
against all the ships of Tarshish and all that delights the eye.
The arrogance of man shall be bowed down, the pride of the mighty shall be brought low; the Lord alone shall be exalted, on that day.
As for the idols, they shall vanish altogether.
Men shall take refuge in the caves of the rocks and in holes in the ground, before the terror of the Lord and the splendour of his majesty, when he rises to terrify the earth.
On that day, man shall cast to the rats and the bats his idols of silver and his idols of gold, which he made for himself to worship,
and he shall take refuge in the clefts of the rocks and the crevices of the cliffs, before the terror of the Lord and the splendour of his majesty, when he rises to terrify the earth.
Stop relying on man, who has but a breath in his nostrils: what is he worth?

titres.titre: The collapse of Jerusalem and its leaders
Against the pride of the daughters of Zion

versets.t: See now, the Master, the Lord of hosts, is about to take away from Jerusalem and Judah all support and all resource, every store of bread and every store of water,
the hero and the soldier, the judge and the prophet, the diviner and the elder,
the commander of fifty and the dignitary, the counsellor, the skilled craftsman and the expert enchanter.
I will make mere boys their leaders, and children shall rule over them.
Among the people, they will oppress one another, each his neighbour; the young will rise against the old, the base against the honoured.
A man will seize his brother in his father's house: "You have a cloak, be our leader, take charge of these ruins!"
But the other, on that day, will protest: "I will not be your healer! In my house there is neither bread nor cloak. Do not make me leader of the people!"
Yes, Jerusalem stumbles and Judah falls, for their words and their deeds oppose the Lord and defy his glorious gaze.
The look on their faces testifies against them; like Sodom, they parade their sin, hiding nothing. Woe to them! They bring disaster upon themselves.
Tell the righteous that all is well: they shall eat the fruit of their deeds.
Woe to the wicked! Disaster shall fall on him, for he shall be repaid for what his hands have done.
My people! Children oppress them, women rule over them. My people! Those who guide you lead you astray and confuse the path you walk.
The Lord rises to plead his case, he stands to judge the peoples.
The Lord enters into judgment against the elders and leaders of his people: "It is you who have ravaged the vineyard! What you have stolen from the poor is in your houses.
By what right do you crush my people and grind the faces of the afflicted?" Oracle of the Master, the Lord of hosts.
The Lord says: The daughters of Zion are haughty, they walk with necks outstretched and provocative eyes, mincing along with tripping steps, jingling the bangles on their feet;
so the Lord will cover the heads of the daughters of Zion with scabs, and he will lay bare their brows.
On that day, the Lord will take away all this finery: the anklets, the headbands, and the crescent pendants;
the earrings, the bracelets, and the veils;
the diadems, the ankle chains, and the sashes;
the perfume flasks and the amulets, the rings and the nose rings;
the festal robes, the great tunics, the cloaks, and the purses;
the mirrors, the fine linen, the turbans, and the wide veils.

Then, instead of perfume there will be rot; instead of a sash, a rope; instead of well-dressed hair, a bald head; instead of a flowing robe, sackcloth; instead of beauty, the brand of the searing iron.
Your men shall fall by the sword, your warriors in battle.
The gates of Zion shall mourn and lament; stripped bare, she shall sit on the ground.

titres.titre: Seven women for a single man
The branch of the Lord, glory of the saved remnant

versets.t: On that day, seven women shall cling to a single man and say: "We will eat our own bread, we will wear our own clothes; only let us bear your name: take away our disgrace!"
On that day, the branch of the Lord shall be beauty and glory, and the fruit of the land shall be the pride and adornment of the survivors of Israel.
Then those who remain in Zion, those who are spared in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, all who are enrolled for life in Jerusalem.
When the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and cleansed Jerusalem of the blood shed within her, by a spirit of judgment, by a spirit of burning,

then the Lord will create, over all the expanse of Mount Zion and over its assemblies, a cloud by day, and smoke with the glow of a flaming fire by night; yes, over all its glory there shall spread a canopy,
and there shall be a tent to give shade by day against the heat, and to serve as a shelter, a refuge against storm and rain.

titres.titre: The wrath of God and the invasion to come

versets.t: Let me sing for my friend the song of my beloved concerning his vineyard. My beloved had a vineyard on a fertile hillside.
He turned the soil, cleared it of stones, and planted it with choice vines; he built a tower in it and hewed out a winepress. He waited for fine grapes, but it yielded bad grapes.
"And now, inhabitants of Jerusalem, people of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard!
What more was there to do for my vineyard that I did not do? I waited for fine grapes: why did it yield only bad grapes?
Now I will tell you what I am going to do to my vineyard: I will tear away its hedge, and it shall be grazed bare; I will break down its wall, and it shall be trampled.
I will make it a wasteland: neither pruned nor hoed, it shall be overrun with briers and thorns; and I will command the clouds to drop no rain upon it."

Now the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel; the people of Judah are the planting he cherished. He waited for justice, but behold, bloodshed; for righteousness, but behold, a cry of distress.
Woe to those who add house to house and join field to field, until there is no more room, and they dwell alone in the midst of the land!
In my ears the Lord of hosts has sworn: Surely these great houses shall become ruins; splendid and vast, they shall be left without inhabitant.
Yes, a great vineyard shall yield but a single measure of wine, and ten sacks of seed sown shall yield only one.
Woe to those who rise early to chase after drink, and linger late, inflamed by wine!
Harp and lyre, tambourine, flute, and wine are at their feasts; but the work of the Lord they do not heed, the deed of his hands they do not see.
Therefore my people go into exile without even understanding it; their nobles die of hunger, their multitude is parched with thirst.
Therefore the realm of the dead widens its throat and opens its mouth beyond measure: down it goes, the splendour of Zion, with its noisy, revelling crowd.
Man shall be brought low, everyone shall be humbled, and the eyes of the proud shall be cast down.
But the Lord of hosts shall be exalted by his judgment, the holy God shall show himself holy by his righteousness.
Lambs shall graze there as in their own pasture, and nomads shall feed among the ruins of the rich.
Woe to those who drag guilt along with cords of falsehood, and sin as with cart ropes!
those who say: "Let him make haste, let him hurry his work, so that we may see it! Let it come and be fulfilled, the plan of the Holy One of Israel, and then we shall know!"
Woe to those who call evil good, and good evil, who put darkness for light, and light for darkness, who put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own judgment!
Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine, champions at mixing strong drink,
who for a bribe acquit the guilty and deny the righteous his right!

Therefore, as the tongue of fire devours the stubble and as the dry grass collapses into the flame, their root shall rot and their blossom shall blow away like dust; for they have rejected the teaching of the Lord of hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

Therefore the anger of the Lord has blazed against his people: he has stretched out his hand against them and struck them; the mountains trembled, and the corpses lay like refuse in the streets. For all this, his anger has not turned away, and his hand is still raised.
He raises a signal for a distant nation, he whistles for it from the ends of the earth; and behold, it comes, swift and light.
Among them none is weary or stumbling, none slumbers or sleeps; no belt at their waist is loosened, no sandal strap is broken.
Their arrows are sharpened, all their bows are bent; the hooves of their horses are hard as flint, and the wheels of their chariots like the whirlwind.
Their roar is like the lion's; like a young lion they roar, they growl, they seize their prey and carry it off, and no one can snatch it away.
On that day, a growling shall rise against the people, like the growling of the sea. One looks toward the land: only darkness and distress, and the light itself grows dark beneath the clouds.

titres.titre: The vision of the Lord thrice holy

versets.t: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and lofty, and the hem of his robe filled the Temple.
Seraphim stood above him, each with six wings: with two they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they flew.
And they called out to one another: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts! The whole earth is filled with his glory."
At the sound of their voices, the pivots of the doorposts began to tremble, and the Temple was filled with smoke.
Then I said: "Woe is me! I am lost, for I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips, and my eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts!"
But one of the seraphim flew to me, holding a live coal he had taken with tongs from the altar.
He touched my mouth with it and said: "See: this has touched your lips; your guilt is taken away, your sin is forgiven."
Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying: "Whom shall I send? Who will go for us?" I answered: "Here I am: send me!"
He said: "Go, and say to this people: You will listen and listen, but never understand; you will look and look, but never perceive.
Harden the heart of this people, make their ears deaf and shut their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and turn back to me and be healed."
I asked: "How long, O Lord?" He answered: "Until the cities lie ruined, without inhabitant, the houses empty of people, and the land reduced to a wasteland;
until the Lord has driven the people far away, and the land is nothing but a vast desolation.
And though a tenth still remains in it, it too shall be given over to the fire; but as the terebinth and the oak, once felled, keep their stump, this stump shall be a holy seed."

titres.titre: Ahaz before the threat of the two kings
The days of devastation to come

versets.t: In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram marched up with Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, to attack Jerusalem; but they could not overcome it.
When the house of David was told, "Aram has camped in Ephraim," the heart of the king and the heart of his people trembled as the trees of the forest tremble before the wind.
The Lord said to Isaiah: "Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-jashub, at the end of the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Fuller's Field.
Say to him: Take heed, be calm, do not fear, let not your heart faint before these two smouldering stumps of firewood, before the fury of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.
Because Aram has plotted evil against you, along with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, saying:
Let us march against Judah, throw it into terror, break through its defences, and set up as king within it the son of Tabeel.
Thus says the Lord God: It shall not stand, it shall not come to pass!
For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim shall be shattered, no longer a people.
The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in faith, you shall not stand at all!"
The Lord spoke again to Ahaz:
"Ask a sign of the Lord your God, ask it deep as the realm of the dead, or high as the heights above!"
But Ahaz replied: "I will not ask, I will not put the Lord to the test."
Then Isaiah said: "Hear now, O house of David! Is it too little for you to weary men, that you weary my God also?
Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: Behold, the Virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
He shall eat curds and honey until he knows how to reject the evil and choose the good.
For before the child knows how to reject the evil and choose the good, the land of the two kings you dread shall be forsaken.
The Lord will bring upon you, upon your people, and upon your father's house, such days as have not come since Ephraim broke away from Judah: he will bring the king of Assyria."
On that day, the Lord will whistle for the fly that is at the mouths of the streams of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
They shall all come and settle in the steep ravines, in the clefts of the rocks, on every thornbush and every watering place.
On that day, with a razor hired from beyond the Euphrates, the king of Assyria, the Lord will shave the head and the hair of the legs, and remove the beard as well.
On that day, each man shall keep alive but a young cow and two sheep;
yet because of the abundance of their milk, he shall eat curds. Indeed, all who are left in the land shall live on curds and honey.
On that day, every place where there were a thousand vines, worth a thousand pieces of silver, shall be nothing but briers and thorns.
Men shall go there with bow and arrows, for the whole land shall be briers and thorns.
And on the hillsides once tilled with the hoe, you shall no longer dare to go, for fear of the briers and thorns; it shall be a pasture where oxen are let loose, land trampled by the sheep.

titres.titre: Maher-shalal-hash-baz, sign of the coming plunder
The waters of the River: the Assyrian invasion
Fear God alone, sanctuary and stone of stumbling
Consult not the dead, but God

versets.t: The Lord said to me: "Take a large tablet and write on it, in ordinary letters: Swift-to-the-spoil, quick-to-the-plunder."
I took as trustworthy witnesses the priest Uriah and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.
Then I drew near to the prophetess; she conceived and bore a son. The Lord said to me: "Name him Swift-to-the-spoil-quick-to-the-plunder.
For before the child knows how to say, My father, my mother, the wealth of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be carried off before the king of Assyria."
The Lord spoke to me again:
"Because this people has despised the waters of Shiloah, which flow gently, and rejoices over Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
therefore the Lord is about to bring up over them the waters of the River, mighty and deep: the king of Assyria and all his glory. It shall rise over all its channels and overflow all its banks,
it shall sweep on into Judah, flood it and pass through, reaching up to the neck; and its outspread wings shall fill the whole breadth of your land, O Immanuel."
Rage, O peoples, and be shattered! Give ear, all you distant lands! Arm yourselves, and be shattered! Arm yourselves, and be shattered!
Devise a plan: it shall be thwarted; give an order: it shall not stand, for God is with us!
Yes, thus the Lord spoke to me, when his hand seized me and turned me away from walking in the way of this people:
"Do not call conspiracy all that this people calls conspiracy; do not fear what it fears, do not let yourselves be terrified.
It is the Lord of hosts whom you shall hold holy; he is the one you shall fear, he is the one you shall dread.
He shall be a sanctuary, but also a stone of stumbling, a rock that makes them fall for the two houses of Israel, a snare and a trap for the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Many shall stumble over it, fall and be broken, be snared and captured."
Bind up this testimony, seal this teaching among my disciples.
As for me, I wait for the Lord, who hides his face from the house of Jacob, and in him I put my hope.
Here I am, and the children the Lord has given me: we are signs and portents in Israel, from the Lord of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.
When they say to you, "Consult those who summon the dead, the diviners who whisper and mutter," should not a people consult its God? Should the living inquire of the dead?
To the teaching and to the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, it is because there is no dawn for this people.
They shall wander through the land, distressed and hungry; and in their hunger, seized with fury, they shall curse their king and their God. They shall turn their faces upward,
then look to the earth: only distress and darkness, a night of anguish; and there they are, thrust into the gloom.

But the darkness shall not endure over the land that was in anguish. In former times, God brought contempt upon the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter times, he will bring glory to the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.

titres.titre: The Child who is born to us
The hand raised against proud Israel

versets.t: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; on those who dwelt in the land of the shadow of death, a light has shone.
You have multiplied the nation, you have increased its joy; they rejoice before you as men rejoice at the harvest, as they exult when dividing the spoil.
For the yoke that weighed on him, the bar across his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, you have broken, as on the day of Midian.
For every soldier's boot that thundered in battle, and every cloak soaked in blood, shall be given to the flames, devoured by fire.
For a child is born to us, a son is given to us; the sovereignty rests upon his shoulders. And his name is proclaimed: Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

That the sovereignty may increase in a peace without end, upon the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish and uphold it in justice and righteousness, from now and for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this.
The Lord has sent a word against Jacob, and it has fallen upon Israel.
The whole people shall know it, Ephraim and the inhabitants of Samaria, those who say in their pride, with hearts swollen with arrogance:
"The bricks have fallen? We will rebuild with dressed stone! The sycamores are felled? We will replace them with cedars!"
But the Lord raises up against them the adversaries of Rezin, he stirs up their enemies:
Aram from the east, the Philistines from the west, and they devour Israel with open mouth. For all this, his anger has not turned away, and his hand is still raised.
But the people have not returned to him who struck them, they have not sought the Lord of hosts.
So the Lord cuts off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in a single day.
The elder and the dignitary are the head; the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
The guides of this people lead them astray, and those they guide are swallowed up.

Therefore the Lord does not rejoice over their young men, he has no pity on their fatherless and their widows; for all are godless and evildoers, and every mouth utters folly. For all this, his anger has not turned away, and his hand is still raised.
Yes, wickedness burns like a fire that devours briers and thorns, kindles the thickets of the forest, and the smoke rises in swirling columns.
By the fury of the Lord of hosts the land is set ablaze, and the people have become fuel for the fire; no one spares his brother.

They snatch on the right, and are still hungry; they devour on the left, and are not satisfied; each devours the flesh of his own arm: Manasseh devours Ephraim, Ephraim devours Manasseh, and together they both turn against Judah.
For all this, his anger has not turned away, and his hand is still raised.

titres.titre: Assyria, rod of God, broken for its pride
The march on Jerusalem and the forest felled

versets.t: Woe to those who enact unjust laws and draw up decrees of oppression,
to turn the weak away from the courts and rob the poor of my people of their rights, to make widows their prey and plunder the fatherless!
What will you do on the day of reckoning, when the disaster comes from afar? To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your riches?
Nothing remains but to crouch among the prisoners or fall among the slain. For all this, his anger has not turned away, and his hand is still raised.
Woe to Assyria, the rod of my anger! The club it holds in its hand is my fury.
I send it against a godless nation, I loose it against the people of my wrath, to plunder and take spoil, and to trample them like the mud of the streets.
But this is not how she sees it, this is not her intent: her mind is only to destroy, to cut off many nations.
She says: "Are not my commanders all kings?
Have I not treated Calno like Carchemish, Hamath like Arpad, Samaria like Damascus?
My hand has reached kingdoms full of idols, whose images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria:
what I have done to Samaria and its false gods, shall I not do to Jerusalem and its idols?"
But when the Lord has finished all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, he will punish the fruit of the proud heart of the king of Assyria and the arrogance of his haughty gaze.

For she has said: "By the strength of my hand I have done this, and by my wisdom, for I am shrewd! I have removed the boundaries of peoples, plundered their treasures, and like a mighty one brought down those enthroned.
My hand has seized the wealth of peoples as one seizes a nest; as one gathers abandoned eggs, I have gathered all the earth, with none to flap a wing, open a beak, or utter a chirp!"

Does the axe boast against the one who wields it? Does the saw rise up against the one who moves it? As if the rod could brandish the one who lifts it, as if the club could raise the one who is not wood!
Therefore the Master, the Lord of hosts, will send wasting upon his sturdy warriors, and beneath his splendour a blaze shall be kindled, like a burning fire.
The Light of Israel shall become a fire, his Holy One a flame, which shall burn and devour its briers and thorns in a single day.
The glory of its forest and its orchard he will destroy, body and soul; it shall be like a sick man wasting away.
What remains of the trees of its forest shall be so few that a child could count them and write them down.
On that day, the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob shall no longer lean on him who struck them, but shall lean in truth on the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
A remnant shall return, the remnant of Jacob, to the Mighty God.
For though your people Israel were as numerous as the sand of the sea, only a remnant shall return. Destruction is decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
Yes, this decreed destruction the Master, the Lord of hosts, will carry out in all the land.
Therefore, thus says the Master, the Lord of hosts: My people who dwell in Zion, do not fear Assyria! She strikes you with the rod, she raises the club against you, as Egypt once did;
but in a very little while my fury will cease, and my anger will turn to their destruction.
Then the Lord of hosts will raise the whip against her, as he struck Midian at the rock of Oreb; he will lift his rod over the sea, as he did in Egypt.
On that day, the burden of Assyria shall slip from your shoulder, its yoke from your neck, and the yoke shall be broken.
There he comes to Aiath, he passes through Migron, at Michmash he stores his baggage.
They cross the pass: "We will camp at Geba!" Ramah trembles, Gibeah of Saul takes flight.
Cry aloud with all your might, daughter of Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Answer her, Anathoth!
Madmenah scatters, the inhabitants of Gebim seek shelter.
This very day he halts at Nob; he shakes his fist against the mountain of the daughter of Zion, against the hill of Jerusalem.
But behold, the Master, the Lord of hosts, lops off the boughs with a great crash: the tallest are cut down, the loftiest brought low.
He hews down the thickets of the forest with iron, and Lebanon falls by the hand of the Mighty One.

titres.titre: The shoot of Jesse, a king filled with the Spirit
The gathering of the scattered remnant

versets.t: A shoot shall come out of the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall spring from his roots.
On him shall rest the Spirit of the Lord: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the Lord.
His delight shall be in the fear of the Lord. He shall not judge by appearances, nor decide by hearsay;

but he shall judge the weak with justice, and defend the right of the humble of the land. He shall strike the land with the word of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked.
Righteousness shall be the belt of his waist, and faithfulness the belt of his loins.
The wolf shall dwell with the lamb, the leopard shall lie down beside the kid; the calf, the young lion, and the fatling together, and a little child shall lead them.
The cow and the bear shall share the same pasture, their young shall lie down together, and the lion shall eat straw like the ox.
The nursing child shall play over the hole of the cobra, and over the den of the viper the weaned child shall lay its hand.
They shall do no harm, they shall destroy no more on all my holy mountain; for the land shall be filled with the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the bed of the sea.
On that day, the root of Jesse shall stand as a banner for the peoples; the nations shall seek him, and his dwelling shall be glorious.

On that day, the Lord will stretch out his hand a second time to redeem the remnant of his people, those who remain in Assyria and Egypt, in Pathros, in Cush, in Elam, in Babylonia, in Hamath, and in the islands of the sea.
He will raise a banner for the nations, gather the exiles of Israel, and reunite the scattered of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
The jealousy of Ephraim shall vanish, the hostilities of Judah shall cease; Ephraim shall no longer envy Judah, and Judah shall no longer be Ephraim's enemy.

Together they shall swoop down on the Philistine slopes to the west, they shall plunder the sons of the East; they shall stretch out their hand against Edom and Moab, and the sons of Ammon shall obey them.
The Lord will dry up the gulf of the sea of Egypt; with a scorching breath he will raise his hand against the Euphrates and split it into seven streams, so that it may be crossed in sandals.
Thus a highway shall open for the remnant of his people, for those who remain in Assyria, as there was for Israel on the day it came up out of Egypt.
On that day, you shall say: I praise you, Lord! You were angry with me, but your anger is turning away, and you console me.
Behold, the God who saves me: I trust, I am no longer afraid. For my strength and my song is the Lord; he has become my salvation.
With joy you shall draw water from the springs of salvation,
and you shall say, on that day: Give thanks to the Lord, call upon his name! Make his deeds known among the peoples, proclaim that his name is exalted!
Sing to the Lord, for he has done wonders: let it be known throughout all the earth!
Cry out for joy, shout aloud, O inhabitant of Zion, for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel!

titres.titre: The fall of Babylon by the Medes

versets.t: Oracle concerning Babylon, which Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
On a bare hill raise a banner! Call to them aloud, wave the hand, that they may enter the gates of the princes!
I myself have given orders to my consecrated ones, I have summoned my warriors to serve my anger, those who exult proudly in my majesty.
Listen, on the mountains, an uproar, like that of a vast people! Listen to the din of kingdoms, of nations gathered together: it is the Lord of hosts mustering his army for war.
They come from a distant land, from the ends of the horizon, the Lord and the instruments of his fury, to ravage the whole earth.
Wail, for the day of the Lord is near: it comes like a devastation from the Almighty!
Therefore all hands go limp, and every heart melts.
They are seized with panic, gripped by convulsions and pangs; they writhe like a woman in labour; they stare at one another, aghast, their faces aflame.
Behold, the day of the Lord comes, a cruel day, of fury and burning anger, to make the earth a desolation and destroy the sinners in it.
For the stars of the heavens and their constellations give no light; the sun is darkened at its rising, and the moon sheds no glow.
I will punish the world for its evil, the wicked for their guilt; I will break the arrogance of the proud and humble the pride of tyrants.
I will make men rarer than fine gold, rarer than the gold of Ophir.
Therefore I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth shall be shaken from its place, by the fury of the Lord of hosts, on the day his anger blazes.
Then, like a hunted gazelle, like a flock no one gathers, each shall turn to his own people, each shall flee to his own land.
All who are found shall be run through, all who are caught shall fall by the sword.
Before their eyes their little children shall be dashed to pieces, their houses plundered, their wives ravished.
Behold, I am stirring up against them the Medes, who care nothing for silver and have no desire for gold.
Their bows shall strike down the young men; they shall have no pity on the fruit of the womb, no compassionate glance for children.
And Babylon, jewel of kingdoms, the pride and glory of the Chaldeans, shall be like Sodom and Gomorrah, overthrown by God.
Never again shall she be peopled, never inhabited through the ages; the nomad shall not pitch his tent there, and shepherds shall not let their flocks rest there.
The beasts of the desert shall lie there, her houses shall be full of owls; ostriches shall dwell there, and wild goats shall leap about.
Hyenas shall howl in her towers, jackals in her palaces of pleasure. Her time is near, and her days shall not be prolonged.

titres.titre: The return and rest of Israel
The taunting song on the fall of the tyrant

versets.t: Yes, the Lord will have compassion on Jacob, he will once again choose Israel and settle them on their own soil; the resident alien shall join them and attach himself to the house of Jacob.

Peoples shall take them and bring them back to their own place; and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord as menservants and maidservants. They shall take captive those who had deported them, and rule over their oppressors.
On the day the Lord gives you rest from your pain, your torment, and the hard servitude that was laid upon you,
you shall take up this taunting song against the king of Babylon: How the tyrant has come to an end! How his insolence has ceased!
The Lord has broken the rod of the wicked, the sceptre of the rulers,
who struck the peoples in fury, unceasingly, who subdued the nations in anger, pursuing them without respite.
The whole earth is at rest, at peace; it breaks into shouts of joy.
Even the cypresses rejoice at your fall, and the cedars of Lebanon: "Since you were laid low, no one comes up to cut us down!"
Below, the realm of the dead stirs to meet you at your coming; it rouses the shades for you, all the mighty of the earth, it raises from their thrones all the kings of the nations.
All of them speak up to say to you: "You too are now as weak as we are, you have become like us!"
Your pomp has been brought down to the realm of the dead, with the music of your harps; beneath you a bed of maggots, and worms for your covering.
How you have fallen from heaven, morning star, son of the dawn! How you have been cut down to the ground, you who laid the nations low!
You who said in your heart: "I will ascend to the heavens, above the stars of God I will raise my throne; I will sit enthroned on the mount of assembly, in the far reaches of the north;
I will ascend above the tops of the clouds, I will be like the Most High!"
But behold, you are brought down to the realm of the dead, to the depths of the pit.
Those who see you stare at you, they ponder over you: "Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who shook kingdoms,
who turned the world into a desert, razed its cities, and would not let his prisoners go home?"
All the kings of the nations, all of them, lie in honour, each in his own tomb;
but you have been cast out, far from your grave, like a branch that is despised, covered with corpses pierced by the sword, flung down on the stones of the pit, like a carcass trampled underfoot.
You shall not join them in burial, for you have ruined your land, you have slaughtered your people. Never again shall the name of that brood of evildoers be spoken.
Prepare the slaughter of his sons for the guilt of their fathers! Let them not rise up to conquer the earth and cover the world with their cities!
I will rise up against them, oracle of the Lord of hosts; from Babylon I will cut off name and remnant, offspring and posterity, oracle of the Lord.
I will make her a haunt of hedgehogs, a swamp, and I will sweep her away with the broom of destruction, oracle of the Lord of hosts.
The Lord of hosts has sworn: "Surely, as I have planned, so it shall be, and as I have purposed, so it shall stand:
I will break Assyria in my land, I will trample her on my mountains. Then her yoke shall be lifted from my people, her burden removed from their shoulders.
This is the plan resolved against all the earth, this is the hand stretched out against all the nations.
For the Lord of hosts has decreed: who can thwart him? His hand is stretched out: who can turn it back?"
In the year that King Ahaz died, this oracle was spoken:
Do not rejoice, all Philistia, that the rod which struck you is broken! For from the root of the serpent shall come forth a viper, and its offspring shall be a flying fiery serpent.
The poorest shall find their pasture, and the afflicted shall lie down in safety; but you, I will kill your offspring with famine, and what remains of you shall be slaughtered.
Wail, O gate! Cry out, O city! Tremble, all Philistia! For from the north comes smoke, and no one falls out of its ranks.
What answer shall be given to the messengers of that nation? That the Lord has founded Zion, and in her the poor of his people find refuge.
Oracle concerning Moab. Yes, in the night it was laid waste, Ar of Moab was destroyed! In the night it was laid waste, Kir of Moab was destroyed!
They go up to the temple, to Dibon, to the high places, to weep; over Nebo and over Medeba, Moab wails. Every head is shaved, every beard cut off.
In her streets they put on sackcloth; on the rooftops and in the squares, everyone wails and dissolves in tears.
Heshbon and Elealeh cry out, they are heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore the warriors of Moab tremble, their souls seized with terror.
My heart cries out over Moab; her fugitives flee as far as Zoar, as far as Eglath-shelishiyah. Up the ascent of Luhith they climb weeping, and on the road to Horonaim they raise heartrending cries.
For the waters of Nimrim are dried up, the grass is withered, the greenery gone, nothing grows any longer.
So what they could save, their stores, they carry off beyond the Wadi of the Willows.
For the cry has gone round the territory of Moab; her wailing reaches as far as Eglaim, her wailing as far as Beer-elim.
For the waters of Dimon are full of blood. And I will bring still more upon Dimon: a lion against the survivors of Moab, against what remains in the land.

titres.titre: The call to welcome the fugitives of Moab
The pride of Moab and the ravaged vineyard

versets.t: "Send the lamb to the ruler of the land, from Sela, across the desert, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion."
Like fleeing birds, like a scattered brood, so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon.
"Give us counsel, be our arbiter! At high noon, cast your shadow over us like the night; hide the outcasts, do not betray the fugitives.

Let the outcasts of Moab find shelter with you, be a refuge for them against the destroyer. When the oppression has ceased, when the devastation has ended, when the invader has vanished from the land,
then a throne shall be established in faithfulness, and on it, in loyalty, under the tent of David, shall sit a judge devoted to justice and swift to do right."
"We know the pride of Moab, the utterly proud, his arrogance, his conceit, his insolence and his empty boasting."
Therefore Moab wails over Moab, everyone wails! For the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, mourn, stricken with grief!

For the fields of Heshbon languish, and the vine of Sibmah as well; the lords of the nations have broken down its clusters, which reached as far as Jazer, straying into the desert, sending out shoots afar and crossing the sea.
Therefore I weep, with Jazer, over the vine of Sibmah; I drench you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh, for over your fruit and your harvest the battle cry has fallen.
Joy and gladness have vanished from the orchards; in the vineyards, no more singing, no more shouts of joy; no one treads the wine in the presses: I have silenced the joyful shout of the winepress.
Therefore my inmost being throbs like a harp for Moab, and my heart for Kir-heres.
Moab shall be seen wearing itself out on the high places, entering its sanctuary to pray, but gaining nothing.
This is the word the Lord spoke concerning Moab long ago.

And now the Lord declares: "Within three years, counted like the years of a hired labourer, the glory of Moab and all its great multitude shall be brought to contempt; only a remnant shall be left, tiny, feeble, and without strength."

titres.titre: The roar of the nations dispersed

versets.t: Oracle concerning Damascus. Behold, Damascus ceases to be a city: it shall be nothing but a heap of ruins!
The cities of Aroer are abandoned, given over to the flocks; they lie down there, and no one frightens them.
The fortress shall vanish from Ephraim, the kingship from Damascus; and what remains of Aram shall share the fate of the glory of Israel, oracle of the Lord of hosts.
On that day, the glory of Jacob shall fade, and the fat of his body shall waste away.
It shall be as when the reaper gathers the standing grain and harvests the ears by the handful, as when one gleans the ears in the Valley of Rephaim.
Only a meagre gleaning shall be left, as after the beating of an olive tree: two or three olives at the very top, four or five on the branches of the tree, oracle of the Lord, the God of Israel.
On that day, man shall look to his Maker, and his eyes shall turn to the Holy One of Israel.
He shall no longer look to the altars, the work of his hands; he shall no longer gaze at what his fingers have made, the sacred poles and the incense altars.
On that day, his fortified cities shall be like the abandoned places of the woods and the heights, deserted long ago before the sons of Israel: it shall be a desolation.
For you have forgotten the God who saves you, you have not remembered the Rock, your refuge. Therefore you plant lovely gardens and set in them vines from abroad;
the day you plant them, you see them sprout, and by morning your seed blooms; but the harvest flees away on the day of suffering and incurable pain.
Woe! An uproar of many peoples, who roar like the roaring of the sea! A tumult of nations, who thunder like the thunder of mighty waters!
The nations thunder like the thunder of great waters. But God rebukes them: they flee far away, driven like chaff on the hills before the wind, like whirling dust before the storm.
At evening, terror; before morning, they are no more. Such is the portion of those who plunder us, the lot of those who despoil us.

titres.titre: God bides his time, then cuts down

versets.t: Woe to the land where wings whir, beyond the rivers of Cush,

which sends envoys by sea in vessels of papyrus over the waters! Go, swift messengers, to that tall and smooth-skinned nation, to that people feared far and wide, a nation mighty and conquering, whose land is furrowed by rivers.
All you inhabitants of the world, you who dwell on the earth: when the banner is raised on the mountains, look! When the trumpet sounds, listen!
For thus the Lord has spoken to me: "I will remain quiet and look on from my dwelling, like the clear heat under the sun, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest."
For before the harvest, when the blossoming is past and the flower has become a ripening grape, he will cut off the shoots with the pruning knife, and remove and cast away the branches.
Together they shall be left to the vultures of the mountains and the beasts of the earth; the vultures shall feed on them all summer, and the beasts of the earth all winter.

In that time, an offering shall be brought to the Lord of hosts from that tall and smooth-skinned people, from that people feared far and wide, a nation mighty and conquering, whose land is furrowed by rivers: it shall be brought to the place where the name of the Lord of hosts abides, to Mount Zion.

titres.titre: Egypt shall turn to the Lord

versets.t: Oracle concerning Egypt. Behold, the Lord, riding on a swift cloud, comes into Egypt: the idols of Egypt tremble before him, and the heart of Egypt melts within her.
I will stir up Egypt against Egypt: they shall fight brother against brother, friend against friend, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
The spirit of Egypt shall be emptied within her, and I will confound her plans; they shall consult the idols and the sorcerers, those who summon the dead and the diviners.
I will hand Egypt over to a harsh master, and a ruthless king shall rule over her, oracle of the Master, the Lord of hosts.
The waters of the sea shall dry up, the river shall run dry and be parched.
The canals shall stink, the branches of the Nile shall dwindle and dry up, reeds and rushes shall wither.
The meadows along the Nile, at its mouth, and all the sown fields beside the Nile shall dry up, blow away, and be no more.
The fishermen shall groan and mourn, all who cast the hook into the river; those who spread the net upon the water shall despair.
Those who work the combed flax and those who weave cotton shall be put to shame.
The pillars of Egypt shall be shattered, and all her labourers shall be sick at heart.
The princes of Zoan are nothing but fools; Pharaoh's wisest counsellors give stupid advice. How dare you say to Pharaoh: "I am a son of the wise, a descendant of the kings of old"?
Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you, if they know, what the Lord of hosts has decreed against Egypt!
The princes of Zoan have lost their heads, the princes of Memphis are deluded; they lead Egypt astray, they who are its cornerstone.
The Lord has poured into her midst a spirit of dizziness: they make Egypt stagger in all she undertakes, as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.
And nothing shall avail Egypt, whatever head or tail, palm branch or reed may do.
On that day, Egypt shall be like a trembling woman: she shall shudder in fear when she sees the Lord of hosts raise his hand, when he brandishes it against her.
The land of Judah shall become the terror of Egypt: whenever it is mentioned to her, she shall tremble, because of the plan the Lord of hosts has resolved against her.
On that day, there shall be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the Lord of hosts; one of them shall be called City of the Sun.
On that day, there shall be an altar to the Lord in the midst of the land of Egypt, and near the border a pillar set up for the Lord.
It shall be a sign and a witness to the Lord of hosts in the land of Egypt: when they cry to the Lord, crushed by their oppressors, he will send them a saviour, a defender, to deliver them.
The Lord shall make himself known to Egypt, and on that day Egypt shall know the Lord; they shall offer sacrifices and offerings, they shall make vows to the Lord and fulfill them.
The Lord shall strike Egypt, striking and healing; they shall turn to the Lord, and he shall be moved by their prayers and heal them.
On that day, there shall be a highway from Egypt to Assyria; the Assyrian shall come into Egypt and the Egyptian into Assyria, and Egypt shall serve the Lord together with Assyria.
On that day, Israel shall be a third with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the earth.
And the Lord of hosts shall bless them, saying: "Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance!"

titres.titre: Isaiah, a living sign against Egypt and Cush

versets.t: In the year that the commander in chief, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, came and attacked Ashdod, besieged it, and captured it,
at that time the Lord spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz: "Go, take off the sackcloth you wear on your loins and remove the sandals from your feet." Isaiah obeyed and walked naked and barefoot.
Then the Lord said: Just as my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years, as a sign and a portent against Egypt and Cush,
so the king of Assyria shall lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old, naked and barefoot, with buttocks bared, to the shame of Egypt.
Then they shall be dismayed and put to shame, because of Cush, their hope, and Egypt, their pride.

And the inhabitants of this coastland shall say, on that day: "See what has become of the one in whom we hoped, to whom we meant to flee for help, to escape the king of Assyria! And we, how shall we escape?"

titres.titre: The fall of Babylon, the desert by the sea

versets.t: Oracle concerning the desert by the sea. Like whirlwinds sweeping through the Negev, it comes from the desert, from a fearsome land.
A grim vision has been revealed to me: the plunderer plunders, the destroyer destroys! Go up to the attack, Elam! Lay siege, Media! I put an end to all her groaning.
Therefore my loins are filled with anguish, pangs seize me, like the pangs of a woman in labour. I writhe at what I hear; I am shaken at what I see.
My mind reels, horror grips me; the twilight I longed for has been turned into terror for me.
They set the table, they spread the rugs, they eat, they drink. Rise up, commanders! Oil the shields!
For thus the Lord has spoken to me: "Go, post a watchman, and let him report what he sees.
If he sees a column of riders, horsemen in pairs, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, let him watch closely, very closely!"
Then the lookout cried like a lion: "On the watchtower, Lord, I stand all day; at my post I remain every night.
And behold, here comes a column of riders, horsemen in pairs!" Then he took up again: "Fallen, fallen is Babylon! All the images of her gods he has shattered to the ground!"
O my people, threshed and trodden on my threshing floor! What I have heard from the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, I have declared to you.
Oracle concerning Dumah. Someone calls to me from Seir: "Watchman, how far is the night? Watchman, how far is the night?"
The watchman answers: "Morning comes, and also the night. If you would inquire, inquire; come back again!"
Oracle concerning Arabia. You shall spend the night in the scrub of the steppe, caravans of Dedan.
To meet the thirsty, bring water! Inhabitants of the land of Tema, go out to the fugitive with bread!
For they have fled from the sword, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, from the fury of battle.
For thus the Lord has spoken to me: "Within a year, counted like the years of a hired labourer, all the glory of Kedar shall come to an end;
and of the archers, those valiant sons of Kedar, scarcely any shall remain." The Lord, the God of Israel, has spoken.

titres.titre: The Valley of Vision: Jerusalem feasts instead of weeping
Eliakim, a servant raised up, then cast down

versets.t: Oracle concerning the Valley of Vision. What ails you, that you have all gone up on the rooftops,
you noisy city, full of tumult, exultant town? Your slain did not fall by the sword, they did not die in battle.
Your leaders have all fled together, captured without a bow being drawn; all your people were taken together, though they had fled far away.
Therefore I said: "Turn your eyes away from me, let me weep bitterly! Do not hasten to console me over the ruin of the daughter of my people."
For it is a day of panic, of trampling and confusion, sent by the Master, the Lord of hosts, in the Valley of Vision: walls are battered down, and cries go up to the mountain.
Elam has taken up the quiver, coming with chariots and horsemen; Kir has uncovered the shield.
Your fairest valleys are filled with chariots, and horsemen take their stand at your gates,
and the defence of Judah falls. On that day, you turn your eyes to the weapons in the Palace of the Forest.
You see the many breaches in the city of David, and you store up the waters of the lower pool.
You count the houses of Jerusalem, and you tear some down to reinforce the wall.
You dig a reservoir between the two walls for the waters of the old pool. But you have not looked to him who did all this, you have not seen him who planned it long ago.
On that day, the Master, the Lord of hosts, called you to weep and mourn, to shave your heads and put on sackcloth.
But instead, joy and feasting: they slaughter oxen and kill sheep, they gorge on meat and drink wine: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"
The Lord of hosts has revealed in my ears: Surely this sin shall never be forgiven you, until you die, says the Master, the Lord of hosts.
Thus says the Master, the Lord of hosts: Go to that steward, Shebna, the master of the palace, and say to him:
"What are you doing here, and by what right, that you have hewn out a tomb for yourself here, cutting a sepulchre on the heights, carving a dwelling in the rock?
Behold, the Lord is about to hurl you away with a mighty grip, he is about to seize you,
roll you into a ball and fling you like a ball into a vast land. There you shall die, there shall your splendid chariots end, O disgrace of your master's house.
I will drive you from your post, the Lord will pull you down from your place."
On that day, I will summon my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
I will clothe him with your tunic, gird him with your sash, and place your authority in his hands; he shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
I will lay on his shoulder the key of the house of David: what he opens, none shall shut; what he shuts, none shall open.
I will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he shall become a throne of glory for his father's house.
All the glory of his father's house shall hang on him, his offspring and his descendants, down to the smallest vessel, from the bowls to the jars.
On that day, oracle of the Lord of hosts, the peg driven into the firm place shall give way: it shall be cut down and fall, and the load it bore shall be shattered. Yes, the Lord has spoken.

titres.titre: Oracle concerning Tyre: the fall of the merchant city
Tyre forgotten, then consecrated to the Lord

versets.t: Oracle concerning Tyre. Wail, ships of Tarshish, for your harbour is destroyed, nothing remains! It was on their way back from the land of Cyprus that they learned of it.
Be silent, inhabitants of the coast, you whom the merchants of Sidon, those who cross the sea, once filled with plenty.
On the great waters, the grain of the Nile, the harvest of the river was her revenue; she was the marketplace of the nations.
Blush with shame, Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea: "I have known no labour pains, I have borne no children, I have raised neither sons nor daughters."
When Egypt hears of it, she shall tremble at the news of the fall of Tyre.
Cross over to Tarshish, wail, inhabitants of the coast!
Is this your joyous city, so ancient, whose feet carried her far off to found colonies?
Who has decreed this against Tyre, the city that crowned kings, whose merchants were princes and whose traders were the great of the earth?
It is the Lord of hosts who has decreed it, to defile the pride of all that glitters, to humble all the great of the earth.
Overflow your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish: there is no longer a harbour to hold you back.
The Lord has stretched out his hand over the sea, he has made kingdoms tremble; he has decreed against Canaan the ruin of its strongholds.
He has said: "You shall exult no more, dishonoured virgin, daughter of Sidon! Rise up, cross over to Cyprus: there too you shall find no rest."
Look at the land of the Chaldeans: this people that did not exist, Assyria destined it for the beasts of the desert; they raised their siege towers, razed her palaces, and made her a ruin.
Wail, ships of Tarshish, for your stronghold is destroyed.
On that day, Tyre shall be forgotten for seventy years, the lifetime of a king. At the end of seventy years, it shall be with Tyre as in the song of the harlot:
"Take your harp, go round the city, forgotten harlot; play your best, multiply your songs, that you may be remembered."
At the end of seventy years, the Lord will attend to Tyre: she shall return to her hire and prostitute herself to all the kingdoms of the world, on the face of the earth.

But her gain and her wages shall be consecrated to the Lord; they shall not be hoarded or stored up: this gain shall go to those who dwell before the Lord, that they may eat their fill and clothe themselves splendidly.

titres.titre: The judgment of the whole earth
The songs of the remnant and the terror to come

versets.t: Behold, the Lord is about to lay waste the earth and empty it, to overturn its surface and scatter its inhabitants.
It shall be the same for priest as for people, for master as for servant, for mistress as for maid, for seller as for buyer, for lender as for borrower, for creditor as for debtor.
The earth shall be utterly laid waste and utterly plundered: the Lord has spoken this word.
The earth mourns and wastes away; the world languishes and wastes away; the elite of the land waste away with it.
The earth is defiled beneath the feet of its inhabitants, for they have transgressed the laws, violated the commandment, broken the everlasting covenant.
Therefore a curse devours the earth, and its inhabitants bear the penalty; therefore they are consumed, and few are the people left.
The new wine mourns, the vine languishes, all the merry-hearted groan.
The gay sound of the tambourines is stilled, the din of revellers has ceased, the joy of the harp is silenced.
No longer do they drink wine with song, and the drink is bitter to those who drink it.
It lies in ruins, the city of chaos; every house is shut, no one enters.
In the streets there is an outcry for lack of wine; all gladness has faded, joy has left the earth.
In the city, only rubble remains, and the shattered gates lie in pieces.
For it shall be in the midst of the earth, among the peoples, as at the beating of an olive tree, as at the gleaning after the vintage.
These lift up their voices, they shout for joy; from the sea, they acclaim the majesty of the Lord:
"Give glory to the Lord in the regions of the dawn, to the name of the Lord, the God of Israel, in the islands of the west!"
From the ends of the earth we hear songs: "Glory to the Righteous One!" But I said: "I waste away, I waste away, woe is me! The plunderers plunder, the plunderers plunder without measure!"
Terror, the pit, and the snare await you, inhabitant of the earth.

Whoever flees at the sound of terror shall fall into the pit; whoever climbs out of the pit shall be caught in the snare. For the floodgates of heaven are opened, and the foundations of the earth are shaken.
The earth is torn apart, the earth splits open, the earth reels.
The earth staggers like a drunkard, it sways like a hut; its guilt weighs upon it, and it falls, never to rise again.
On that day, the Lord shall punish, on high, the host of heaven, and on the earth, the kings of the earth.
They shall be gathered together as captives in a dungeon, shut up in a prison; and after many days they shall be punished.
The moon shall be put to shame and the sun confounded, for the Lord of hosts reigns on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and before his elders his glory shines forth.

titres.titre: Praise for the city of tyrants brought low
The feast on the mountain and death swallowed up
The joy of salvation, the fall of Moab

versets.t: Lord, you are my God, I will exalt you, I will praise your name, for you have done wonders; your plans, formed long ago, are sure and faithful.
You have turned the city into a heap of stones, the fortified town into a ruin; the citadel of foreigners is no longer a city, and shall never be rebuilt.
Therefore a mighty people gives you glory, the city of ruthless nations reveres you.
