You have been a refuge for the weak, a refuge for the poor in his distress, a shelter from the storm, a shade from the heat. For the breath of tyrants is like a storm beating against a wall,
like heat upon a parched land. You silence the uproar of foreigners; as heat is subdued under the shadow of a cloud, so the triumph song of tyrants is stilled.
On this mountain, the Lord of hosts will prepare for all peoples a feast of rich fare, a feast of aged wines, of fat meats full of marrow, of aged, clarified wines.
On this mountain, he will tear away the veil that shrouded all peoples, the covering spread over all nations.
He will swallow up death for ever. The Lord God will wipe away the tears from every face, and will remove from all the earth the disgrace of his people. Yes, the Lord has spoken.
On that day it shall be said: "Behold, this is our God, in whom we hoped for salvation! This is the Lord, in whom we hoped: let us exult and rejoice in his salvation!"
For the hand of the Lord shall rest on this mountain. But Moab shall be trampled where it stands, as straw is trampled in the dung pit.
In the midst of that mire, it shall spread out its hands as a swimmer spreads them to swim; but the Lord shall bring down its pride, despite all the efforts of its hands.
Your high fortified ramparts he shall bring down, lay low, and cast to the ground, into the dust.

titres.titre: The canticle of the strong city
The waiting of the righteous in the night
To hide for the time of wrath

versets.t: On that day, this song shall be sung in the land of Judah: We have a strong city! To protect it, God has set up salvation as wall and rampart.
Open the gates! Let the righteous nation enter, the one that keeps faith.
To the steadfast mind you grant peace, peace, because it trusts in you.
Trust in the Lord for ever, for the Lord is the eternal Rock.
He has brought low those who dwelt on high; the proud city he has humbled, humbled to the ground, cast into the dust.
It is trodden underfoot, under the feet of the poor, under the steps of the afflicted.
The way of the righteous is straight; you make level the path of the righteous straight before him.
Yes, on the path of your judgments, we waited for you, Lord; your name, your remembrance were the desire of our soul.
My soul longed for you in the night, deep within me my spirit sought you; for when your judgments are at work on the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
If grace is shown to the wicked, he does not learn righteousness: in the land of uprightness he acts wickedly and does not see the majesty of the Lord.
Lord, your hand is raised, but they do not see it. Let them see your jealous love for your people, and be put to shame! Let the fire reserved for your enemies devour them!
Lord, you grant us peace, for even all that we accomplish, it is you who do it for us.
Lord our God, other masters than you have ruled over us; but it is you alone, your name alone, that we praise.
The dead shall not live again, the shades shall not rise: you intervened, you destroyed them, you wiped out even their memory.
You have enlarged the nation, Lord, you have enlarged the nation and revealed your glory, you have extended all the borders of the land.
Lord, in distress they sought you; they poured out a whispered prayer when you were chastening them.
As a pregnant woman, near to giving birth, writhes and cries out in her pangs, so were we before you, Lord.
We conceived, we writhed, but we gave birth only to wind; we brought no salvation to the earth, and the inhabitants of the world were not born into the light.

Your dead shall live again, their bodies shall rise! Awake and shout for joy, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is a dew of light, and the earth shall give back to the day those it had swallowed up.
Go, my people, enter your chambers, shut your doors behind you; hide yourself for a brief moment, until the wrath has passed.

For behold, the Lord comes out from his dwelling to call the inhabitants of the earth to account for their crimes; then the earth shall disclose the blood shed upon it, and shall no longer conceal its slain.

titres.titre: The great gathering at the sound of the trumpet

versets.t: On that day, the Lord will punish, with his sword hard and great and strong, Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan the coiling serpent, and he will slay the monster that dwells in the sea.
On that day it shall be said: "Sing of the delightful vineyard!
I, the Lord, am its keeper; I water it at every moment; lest any harm it, night and day I guard it.
I have no more wrath. Let there be briers and thorns to fight against me: I will march against them, I will burn them all together.
Or else, let them take refuge under my protection, let them make peace with me, yes, let them make peace with me!"
In the days to come, Jacob shall take root, Israel shall blossom and bud, and fill the whole face of the world with its fruit.
Has the Lord struck Israel as he struck those who struck them? Has he slain them as their slayers were slain?
No: it is with measure, by driving them out, by sending them into exile, that you make your case against them; he drove them off with his fierce breath, on the day of the east wind.

Thus the guilt of Jacob shall be forgiven, and this shall be the full fruit of the pardon of his sin: when he reduces all the stones of the altars to crumbling chalk, when the sacred poles and the incense altars stand no more.
For the strong city is nothing but a solitude, a dwelling forsaken and abandoned like the desert; there the calf grazes, there it lies down and browses the branches.
When the boughs are dry, they are broken off; women come to set them on fire. For this people is without understanding; therefore its Maker has no pity on it, and he who formed it shows it no grace.
On that day, the Lord will thresh the grain from the course of the Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt, and you shall be gathered up one by one, sons of Israel.

On that day, a great trumpet shall sound; then those who were lost in the land of Assyria shall return, and those who were banished to the land of Egypt, and they shall bow down before the Lord on the holy mountain, in Jerusalem.

titres.titre: Woe to Ephraim, crown of the drunkards
The Lord, crown of the remnant
Priests and prophets drowned in wine
The parable of the plowman: the wisdom of God

versets.t: Woe to the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim, to the fading flower of its glorious adornment, set on the head of a fertile valley, over men whom wine lays low!
Behold, from the Lord comes one strong and mighty: like a storm of hail, a destroying tempest, like a flood of raging waters overflowing, he casts everything to the ground with violence.
It shall be trampled underfoot, the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim;
and the fading flower of its glorious adornment, on the head of the fertile valley, shall be like an early fig before summer: as soon as one sees it, as soon as it is in the hand, it is swallowed.
On that day, the Lord of hosts shall be a glorious crown, a splendid diadem for the remnant of his people;
a spirit of justice for the one who renders justice, and strength for those who drive back the assault at the gates.

But these too stagger with wine, they reel with strong drink: priest and prophet stagger with strong drink, they are swallowed up in wine, led astray by drink; they reel when they have visions, they stumble when they render judgment.
All the tables are covered with filthy vomit, there is not a clean spot left.
"Whom does he think to teach wisdom? To whom would he make his message understood? To children barely weaned, barely taken from the breast?
It is only command upon command, command upon command, rule upon rule, rule upon rule, a little here, a little there!"
Well then, it is with stammering lips, in a foreign tongue, that the Lord will speak to this people.
He had said to them: "This is the place of rest, let the weary rest; this is the repose." But they would not listen.

So the word of the Lord shall be to them command upon command, command upon command, rule upon rule, rule upon rule, a little here, a little there, so that as they walk they shall fall backward, be broken, be snared and captured.
Hear then the word of the Lord, you scoffers, you rulers of this people in Jerusalem!
You say: "We have made a pact with death, an agreement with the realm of the dead. When the flood sweeps by, it will not reach us, for we have made falsehood our refuge and deceit our shelter."
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am laying in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation: whoever leans on it in faith shall not be shaken.
I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb; the hail shall sweep away the refuge of falsehood, and the waters shall carry off your shelter.
Your pact with death shall be annulled, your agreement with the realm of the dead shall not stand: when the flood sweeps by, it shall crush you.
As often as it passes, it shall carry you off; it shall pass morning after morning, by day and by night, and it shall be sheer terror to understand this message.
For, as the proverb says, the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too narrow to wrap oneself in.
Yes, the Lord shall rise up as at Mount Perazim, he shall rage as in the Valley of Gibeon, to do his work, his strange work, to accomplish his task, his astonishing task.
Now then, stop your scoffing, lest your bonds be drawn tighter; for I have heard: the destruction of the whole land is decreed by the Lord of hosts.
Give ear and hear my voice; be attentive and hear my word.
Does the plowman who wants to sow spend all his time plowing, opening and harrowing his soil?
Once the ground is levelled, does he not scatter the dill, sow the cumin, and set the wheat, the barley, and the spelt each in its place, along the edge?
It is his God who has taught him this, who instructs him in the right way.
The dill is not threshed with a sledge, nor is the cartwheel rolled over the cumin: the dill is beaten with a stick, and the cumin with a rod.
The grain is crushed, but not endlessly ground; the cartwheel and the horses are driven over it, but it is not crushed to bits.
This too comes from the Lord of hosts: his counsel is wonderful, and his wisdom great.

titres.titre: Woe to Ariel, the besieged city
The blindness and the sealed book
The reversal: the deaf shall hear

versets.t: Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David encamped! Add year to year, let the feasts run their round:
I will press hard on Ariel, and there shall be mourning and lamentation; she shall become for me a true altar hearth ablaze.
I will encamp in a circle around you, I will hem you in with armed posts, I will raise siegeworks against you.

Brought low, you shall speak from the ground, and from the dust your muffled voice shall rise; your voice shall come out of the ground like that of a ghost, and your words shall rise from the dust like a whisper.
But the multitude of your enemies shall be like fine dust, the horde of warriors like flying chaff. And suddenly, in an instant,
you shall be visited by the Lord of hosts, with thunder and earthquake and great noise, with whirlwind and tempest and the flame of a devouring fire.
Then the multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel, all who besiege her and her stronghold and press hard upon her, shall be like a dream, a vision of the night.

As a hungry man dreams that he is eating and wakes with an empty stomach, as a thirsty man dreams that he is drinking and wakes exhausted, his throat dry, so shall it be with the multitude of the nations that fight against Mount Zion.
Be stunned and stupefied! Blind yourselves and stay blind! They are drunk, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.
For the Lord has poured over you a spirit of stupor; he has shut your eyes, the prophets, he has veiled your heads, the seers.
And every vision has become for you like the words of a sealed book. It is handed to one who can read: "Read this!" He replies: "I cannot, the book is sealed."
It is handed to one who cannot read: "Read this!" He replies: "I cannot read."

The Lord says: This people draws near to me with words, honouring me with their lips, but their heart is far from me; the worship they offer me is nothing but a human precept, a lesson learned by rote.
Therefore I will once again astound this people with strange wonders: the wisdom of its wise shall perish, and the understanding of its learned shall vanish.
Woe to those who hide from the Lord to conceal their plans, who work in darkness and say: "Who sees us? Who knows us?"
What a perversion! Shall the potter be regarded as the clay, that the thing made should say of its maker: "He did not make me," and the vessel say of the potter: "He understands nothing"?
In a very little while, shall not Lebanon be turned into an orchard, and the orchard be counted as a forest?
On that day, the deaf shall hear the words of the book, and out of gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind shall see.
The humble shall rejoice more and more in the Lord, and the poorest shall exult in the Holy One of Israel.
For the oppressor shall be no more, the scoffer shall have vanished, and all who watch for a chance to do evil shall be cut off:
those who, with a word, condemn a man, who lay a snare for the judge at the city gate, and who, on false grounds, deprive the innocent of his right.
Therefore, thus says the Lord to the house of Jacob, he who redeemed Abraham: Jacob shall no longer be ashamed, his face shall no longer grow pale.
For when he sees, he and his children, the work of my hands in their midst, they shall hallow my name, they shall hallow the Holy One of Jacob, and revere the God of Israel.
Those whose spirits went astray shall learn wisdom, and the discontented shall receive instruction.

titres.titre: Woe to the alliance with Egypt
A people that refuses to hear
In calm and trust, your strength
The Lord waits to be gracious
The coming of the Lord against Assyria

versets.t: Woe to the rebellious children, oracle of the Lord, who make plans, but not from me, who forge alliances, but not by my Spirit, heaping sin upon sin!
They go down to Egypt without consulting me, to take shelter under the protection of Pharaoh, to hide in the shadow of Egypt.
But the protection of Pharaoh shall turn to your shame, and the shelter in the shadow of Egypt to your disgrace.
Though his princes are at Zoan, and his envoys reach as far as Hanes,
all shall be disappointed by a people that serves no purpose, that brings neither help nor profit, but only shame and dishonour.

Oracle concerning the beasts of the Negev. Through a land of anguish and distress, from which come the lioness and the lion, the viper and the flying serpent, they carry their riches on the backs of donkeys, their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people that is of no use.
The help of Egypt is empty and worthless; therefore I name her: "Rahab who sits still."
Go now, inscribe this on a tablet before them, write it in a book, that it may remain a witness for the days to come, for ever.
For this is a rebellious people, lying children, children who refuse to hear the teaching of the Lord.
They say to the seers: "See nothing!" and to the prophets: "Do not tell us the truth! Tell us flattering things, prophesy illusions to us!
Get out of the way, leave the path, stop confronting us with the Holy One of Israel!"
Therefore, thus says the Holy One of Israel: Because you reject this word, and put your trust in violence and deceit and lean upon it,
this guilt shall become for you like a threatening crack, a bulge in a high wall, that suddenly, in an instant, collapses.
It shall break as an earthenware jar breaks, shattered without pity, so that among its fragments not even a shard is found to take fire from the hearth or scoop water from the cistern.
For thus has spoken the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel: In conversion and calm you would be saved; in serenity and trust would be your strength. But you would not.
You said: "No! We will flee on horseback!" Very well, you shall flee! "We will ride on swift steeds!" Very well, your pursuers shall be swifter still!
A thousand of you shall flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five you shall all flee, until you are left like a flagstaff planted on a mountaintop, like a signal on a hill.
Yet the Lord waits for the moment to be gracious to you, he will rise to show you his tenderness; for the Lord is a God of justice. Blessed are all who hope in him!
Yes, people of Zion, inhabitant of Jerusalem, you shall weep no more. At your first cry, he will be gracious to you; as soon as he hears you, he will answer.
The Lord will give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, but he who teaches you will hide himself no longer: with your own eyes you shall see your teacher,
and with your own ears you shall hear, behind you, a voice saying: "This is the way, walk in it!" whenever you turn to the right or to the left.
You shall treat as unclean your idols overlaid with silver, your images plated with gold; you shall throw them away like a defiled thing: "Out!" you shall say to them.
Then the Lord will give rain for the seed you sow in the ground, and the bread, the fruit of the soil, shall be rich and nourishing; on that day, your flocks shall graze in broad pastures.
The oxen and donkeys that work the ground shall eat salted fodder, winnowed with shovel and fork.
On every high mountain, on every lofty hill, streams shall flow, on the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.

The light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, like the light of seven days together, on the day the Lord binds up the wound of his people and heals the injuries he had inflicted.
Behold, the name of the Lord comes from afar: his anger burns, heavy and weighty; his lips overflow with fury, his tongue is a devouring fire,
his breath a torrent that overflows and rises up to the neck. He comes to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction, to put in the jaws of the peoples the bridle that leads them astray.
Then you shall sing as in the night when the festival is kept, your heart glad as one who marches to the sound of the flute to go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the Rock of Israel.
The Lord shall make the majesty of his voice resound, and show his arm coming down in the heat of his anger, in the flame of a devouring fire, the storm, the downpour, and the hail.
At the voice of the Lord, Assyria shall be terror-struck, beneath the blows of his rod.
At every stroke of the appointed rod that the Lord brings down on her, tambourines and harps shall resound; and he shall fight against her with uplifted arm.

For long ago the Topheth was made ready, that pyre prepared even for the king, dug deep and wide, with fire and wood in abundance; and the breath of the Lord, like a torrent of brimstone, sets it ablaze.

titres.titre: Woe to those who rely on Egypt
The Lord protects Zion like a lion and like a bird

versets.t: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on horses, who put their trust in chariots because they are many and in horsemen because they are strong, but do not look to the Holy One of Israel and do not seek the Lord!
Yet he too is wise: he brings disaster, he does not take back his words; he will rise up against the house of the wicked and against the help of evildoers.
The Egyptian is a man, not a god; his horses are flesh, not spirit. When the Lord stretches out his hand, the protector shall stumble, the protected shall fall, and both shall perish together.

For thus the Lord has said to me: As the lion, the young lion, growls over its prey when a whole band of shepherds is called out against it, and is not frightened by their shouting or dismayed by their number, so the Lord of hosts shall come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its hill.
As birds spread their wings over their nest, so the Lord of hosts shall protect Jerusalem: he shall protect and deliver her, he shall spare and save her.
Return to the one from whom you have so deeply strayed, sons of Israel!
For on that day, everyone shall cast away his idols of silver and his idols of gold, which your guilty hands have made.
Then Assyria shall fall by a sword that is not of man, a sword not of mortals shall devour her; she shall flee before the sword, and her young men shall be put to forced labour.
Her rock shall pass away in terror, and her officers, panic-stricken, shall desert the banner, oracle of the Lord, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.

titres.titre: The king of justice and the new order
A warning to the complacent women
The Spirit poured out, peace the fruit of justice

versets.t: Behold, a king shall reign in justice, and princes shall rule in righteousness.
Each shall be like a shelter from the wind, a refuge from the storm, like streams of water on a parched land, like the shade of a great rock in a dry country.
Then the eyes of those who see shall no longer be closed, and the ears of those who hear shall be attentive.
The heart of the rash shall learn to understand, and the stammering tongue shall speak quickly and clearly.
No longer shall the fool be called noble, nor the scoundrel be said to be great,
for the fool utters folly and his heart plots only evil: he acts without reverence for God, he speaks error about the Lord, he leaves the hungry with an empty belly and deprives the thirsty of drink.
The weapons of the scoundrel are treacherous; he devises schemes to ruin the humble with lies, and the poor even when he pleads his just cause.
But the noble man has noble purposes, and by his nobility he shall stand firm.
Complacent women, rise up, hear my voice! Overconfident daughters, give ear to my word!
In a year and some days, you shall tremble, you complacent ones, for there shall be no vintage, and the gathering of fruit shall not come.
Be in dread, complacent ones! Tremble, you who thought yourselves secure! Strip off your fine clothes, bare yourselves, put a mourning cloth about your loins.
They beat their breasts in grief over the pleasant fields, over the fruitful vines,
over the land of my people, where thorns and briers spring up, over all the houses of pleasure in the exultant city.
For the palace is deserted, the noisy city abandoned; the Ophel and the watchtower shall become dens for ever, the joy of wild donkeys, the pasture of flocks,
until the Spirit is poured out on us from on high: then the desert shall become an orchard, and the orchard be counted as a forest.
Justice shall dwell in the desert, and righteousness shall abide in the orchard.
The work of righteousness shall be peace, and the fruit of righteousness, quietness and security for ever.
My people shall dwell in an abode of peace, in secure dwellings, in tranquil places of rest.
The forest shall come down beneath the hail, and the city shall be laid low to the ground.
Blessed shall you be, you who sow beside all the waters, and let the ox and the donkey range freely!

titres.titre: Woe to the destroyer, a prayer for grace
The distress of the land and the Lord who rises up
Who shall dwell near the devouring fire?
The king in his beauty, Zion unshaken

versets.t: Woe to you, destroyer, whom no one has destroyed; plunderer, whom no one has plundered! When you have finished destroying, you shall be destroyed; when you have done plundering, you shall be plundered.
Lord, have mercy on us, in you we hope! Be our strength each morning, our salvation in time of distress.
At the sound of your thunder, the peoples flee; when you rise up, the nations scatter.
Your spoil is gathered as the locust gathers, men rush upon it like a swarm of grasshoppers.
The Lord is exalted, for he dwells on high; he fills Zion with justice and righteousness.
He will make your days secure: wisdom and knowledge are the riches that save, and the fear of the Lord, that is your treasure.
Behold, the valiant cry out in the streets, and the messengers of peace weep bitterly.
The highways lie deserted, no one passes on the roads. The enemy has broken the treaty, despised the cities, has no regard for anyone.
The land mourns and wastes away; Lebanon is shamed and withered; Sharon has become a steppe, and Bashan and Carmel shed their leaves.
Now I will rise up, says the Lord, now I will lift myself up, now I will be exalted.
You conceive chaff, you shall give birth to straw; your breath is a fire that shall devour you.
The peoples shall be burned as for the making of lime, set ablaze like cut thorns thrown on the fire.
You who are far off, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge my power!
In Zion the sinners tremble, and terror seizes the godless: "Who among us can endure the devouring fire? Who among us can endure the everlasting flames?"

He who walks in righteousness and speaks with uprightness, who refuses gains wrung by extortion, who waves away his hand so as not to touch a bribe, who stops his ears against talk of bloodshed and shuts his eyes so as not to look on evil:
he shall dwell on the heights, a fortress of rock shall be his refuge, his bread shall be assured, his water shall never fail.
Your eyes shall behold the king in his beauty, they shall see a land that stretches far away.
Your heart shall recall its former terrors: "Where is the one who counted? Where is the one who weighed the tribute? Where is the one who counted the towers?"
You shall see no more that insolent people, that people of obscure speech that cannot be understood, of stammering, unintelligible tongue.
Look upon Zion, the city of our festivals! Your eyes shall see Jerusalem, a peaceful abode, a tent that shall never be moved, whose pegs shall never be pulled up, none of whose cords shall be broken.
For there the Lord is majestic for us; it is a place of rivers and broad canals, where no oared boat shall pass, and no great ship shall venture.
For the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king: it is he who will save us.
Your rigging hangs loose, it no longer holds the mast upright or the sail spread out. Then a vast spoil shall be divided, and even the lame shall take their share of the plunder.
No inhabitant shall say any longer: "I am sick." The people who dwell in Zion have received the pardon of their guilt.

titres.titre: The judgment of all the nations
The sword of the Lord upon Edom

versets.t: Draw near, nations, to listen! Peoples, be attentive! Let the earth hear, it and all it holds, the world and all it brings forth.
For the Lord is angry with all the nations, furious with all their armies: he has devoted them to destruction, given them over to slaughter.
Their slain shall be cast out unburied, their corpses shall give off a stench, and the mountains shall run with their blood.

All the host of the heavens shall dissolve, the heavens shall be rolled up like a scroll, and all their stars shall fall as the leaf falls from the vine, as the withered fruit falls from the fig tree.
My sword has drunk its fill in the heavens; behold, it descends upon Edom, upon the people I have devoted to destruction, to bring it to judgment.

The sword of the Lord is full of blood, gorged with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams. For the Lord holds a sacrifice at Bozrah, a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
With them fall the wild oxen, and the young bulls with the sturdy beasts. Their land is drenched with blood, their dust gorged with fat.
For it is a day of vengeance for the Lord, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.
The torrents of Edom shall be turned into pitch, its dust into brimstone, and its land shall become burning pitch.
Neither by night nor by day shall it be quenched, its smoke shall rise for ever; from generation to generation it shall lie waste, and no one shall pass through it ever again.
The owl and the hedgehog shall take possession of it, the screech owl and the raven shall dwell in it. The Lord shall stretch over it the measuring line of chaos and the plumb line of emptiness.
Its nobles shall be there no longer to proclaim a king, and all its princes shall be reduced to nothing.
Thorns shall overrun its palaces, briers and thistles its fortresses; it shall be a haunt of jackals, an enclosure for ostriches.
The beasts of the desert shall meet the hyenas, and the wild goats shall call to one another; there too the creature of the night shall prowl, and find its resting place.
There the serpent shall make its nest and lay its eggs, it shall hatch and gather its young under its shadow; there too the vultures shall gather, each with its mate.

Search in the book of the Lord, and read: not one of these creatures shall be missing, none shall lack its mate; for it is the mouth of the Lord that has ordered it, and it is his breath that has gathered them.
It is he who has cast the lot for them, his hand that has apportioned the land to them by the measuring line; for ever they shall possess it, from generation to generation they shall dwell in it.

titres.titre: Behold your God who comes to save
The way of holiness to Zion

versets.t: The desert and the parched land shall rejoice, the steppe shall exult and blossom; like the crocus,

it shall burst into bloom, it shall exult and shout for joy. The glory of Lebanon shall be given to it, the splendour of Carmel and Sharon. They shall see the glory of the Lord, the splendour of our God.
Strengthen the feeble hands, make firm the tottering knees!
Say to those whose hearts are troubled: "Take courage, do not fear! Behold your God: he comes to bring justice, the recompense of God; he himself comes to save you."
Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
Then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute shall shout for joy. For waters shall break forth in the desert, and torrents in the steppe;
the burning sand shall become a pool, the thirsty ground springs of water; the haunt where jackals lay shall become an enclosure of reeds and rushes.

There shall be a road there, a highway, which shall be called the Way of Holiness. No unclean person shall pass along it: it is reserved for those who walk it, and even fools shall not go astray on it.
There shall be no lion there, no ravenous beast shall come up on it, none shall be found there: only the redeemed shall walk on it.
The redeemed of the Lord shall return, they shall enter Zion with shouts of joy, everlasting gladness on their faces; joy and gladness shall overtake them, sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

titres.titre: The challenge of the chief cupbearer
The threats shouted to the people

versets.t: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
From Lachish the king of Assyria sent to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, his chief cupbearer with a large force. He halted near the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Fuller's Field.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, master of the palace, went out to meet him, with Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder.
The chief cupbearer said to them: "Say to Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria: On what does this confidence of yours rest?
Do you think that mere words are a match for strategy and might in war? In whom do you trust, that you dare to rebel against me?
See, you are relying on the support of that broken reed, Egypt, which pierces and wounds the hand of anyone who leans on it: such is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.

And if you tell me: It is in the Lord our God that we trust, is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, commanding Judah and Jerusalem: You shall bow down before this altar only?
Come now, make a wager with my master, the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you can find riders to mount them!
How could you repel a single governor, even the least of my master's servants? And it is on Egypt that you rely for chariots and horsemen!
Besides, is it without the Lord's consent that I have come up against this land to destroy it? It was the Lord himself who said to me: Go up against this land and destroy it!"

Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the chief cupbearer: "Speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it; do not speak to us in the language of Judah, in the hearing of the people on the wall."

But the chief cupbearer replied: "Is it to your master and to you that my master sent me to speak these words? Is it not rather to the men sitting on the wall, doomed with you to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?"
Then the chief cupbearer stood and cried out in a loud voice, in the language of Judah: "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he cannot deliver you.
Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the Lord by saying: The Lord will surely deliver us, this city shall not fall into the hands of the king of Assyria.

Do not listen to Hezekiah! For thus says the king of Assyria: Make peace with me, surrender to me, and each of you shall eat the fruit of his own vine and fig tree, and each shall drink the water of his own cistern,
until I come to take you away to a land like your own, a land of grain and wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
Do not let Hezekiah mislead you when he says: The Lord will deliver us. Have the gods of the nations delivered, each his own land, from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they deliver Samaria from my hand?
Among all the gods of these lands, which have delivered their land from my hand, that the Lord should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?"
They kept silent and answered him not a word, for the king had given this order: "You shall not answer him."

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, master of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their garments torn, and reported to him the words of the chief cupbearer.

titres.titre: The prayer of Hezekiah in the Temple

versets.t: On hearing this report, King Hezekiah tore his garments, covered himself with sackcloth, and went to the house of the Lord.
He sent Eliakim, master of the palace, Shebna the secretary, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him: "Thus says Hezekiah: This is a day of anguish, of chastisement and of disgrace; the children are ready to be born, but there is no strength to bring them forth.

Perhaps the Lord your God will hear the words of the chief cupbearer, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to insult the living God; perhaps he will punish him for the words he has heard. Lift up a prayer, then, for the remnant that still survives."
The servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah,
and Isaiah said to them: "Say to your master: Thus says the Lord: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, those blasphemies of the servants of the king of Assyria against me.
Behold, I will put in him such a spirit that, at a report he will hear, he will return to his own land; and there, in his own land, I will make him fall by the sword."
The chief cupbearer turned back and found the king of Assyria attacking Libnah, for he had learned that his master had left Lachish.
Now the king of Assyria received a report about Tirhakah king of Cush: "He has set out to fight against you." On hearing this, he again sent messengers to Hezekiah, with this message:
"Say to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying: Jerusalem shall not fall into the hands of the king of Assyria.
You have surely heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, how they have devoted them to destruction. And you, would you be delivered?
Did their gods deliver them, those nations my fathers destroyed, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the sons of Eden who were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena and Ivvah?"
Hezekiah took the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the house of the Lord and spread it out before the Lord.
And Hezekiah prayed before the Lord:
"Lord of hosts, God of Israel, you who are enthroned above the cherubim, you alone are God of all the kingdoms of the earth, you who made the heavens and the earth.
Incline your ear, Lord, and hear! Open your eyes, Lord, and see! Hear all the words of Sennacherib, who has sent to insult the living God.
It is true, Lord, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste all these nations and their lands,
that they have thrown their gods into the fire; but these were not gods, only the work of human hands, wood and stone: that is why they could destroy them.
Now, Lord our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone, Lord, are God!"
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah: "Thus says the Lord, God of Israel: I have heard the prayer you have offered to me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria.
This is the word the Lord speaks against him: She despises you, she scorns you, the virgin daughter of Zion; she wags her head behind you, the daughter of Jerusalem.
Whom have you insulted, whom have you reviled? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted haughty eyes? Against the Holy One of Israel!

By your servants you have insulted the Lord, you have said: With my countless chariots I have climbed the tops of the mountains, the heights of Lebanon; I have cut down its tallest cedars, its finest cypresses, I have reached its remotest peak, its deepest forest.
I have dug wells and drunk their waters; under the soles of my feet I have dried up all the canals of Egypt.
Have you not heard that long ago I prepared this? From ancient times I formed it, and now I bring it to pass: that is why you turn fortified cities into heaps of ruins.
Their inhabitants, powerless, are dismayed and confounded; they are like the grass of the fields, the tender greenery, the grass of the rooftops, the grain scorched before it has grown.
But I know when you sit down, when you go out and when you come in, and I know your fury against me.
Because you are furious against me and your arrogance has reached my ears, I will put my ring in your nose and my bit in your lips, and I will make you return by the way you came.

And this shall be the sign for you: this year you shall eat what grows of itself; the second year, what springs from that; but in the third year, you shall sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
What has survived of the house of Judah, the remnant, shall again take root below and bear fruit above.
For out of Jerusalem shall come a remnant, out of Mount Zion survivors. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this.

Therefore, thus says the Lord concerning the king of Assyria: He shall not enter this city, he shall not shoot an arrow there, he shall not confront it with a shield, he shall not raise a siege ramp against it.
He shall return by the way he came, and he shall not enter this city, oracle of the Lord.
I will protect this city and save it, for my own sake and for the sake of David my servant."
Then the angel of the Lord went out and struck down, in the Assyrian camp, a hundred and eighty-five thousand men; when the people rose in the morning, there they were, all corpses.
Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp, departed, and stayed at Nineveh.

One day, as he was worshipping in the temple of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword, then fled to the land of Ararat. And his son Esarhaddon reigned in his place.

titres.titre: The illness and healing of Hezekiah

versets.t: In those days, Hezekiah fell ill, near to death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said: "Thus says the Lord: Set your house in order, for you are going to die, you shall not recover."
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord:
"I beseech you, Lord, remember that I have walked before you in faithfulness and with a whole heart, and that I have done what is good in your eyes." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the word of the Lord came to Isaiah:
"Go and say to Hezekiah: Thus says the Lord, the God of David your father: I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; behold, I am adding fifteen years to your life.
I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria, and I will protect this city.
And this shall be the sign for you from the Lord, that he will carry out the word he has spoken:
Behold, I will make the shadow that has gone down on the dial of Ahaz go back ten steps." And the sun went back ten steps on the dial where the shadow had gone down.
A poem of Hezekiah king of Judah, when he was ill and recovered from his illness:
I said: In the midst of my days I must depart; at the gates of the realm of the dead I am deprived of the rest of my years.
I said: I shall no longer see the Lord, the Lord, in the land of the living; I shall no longer see anyone among the inhabitants of the world.
My dwelling is pulled up and carried away from me like a shepherd's tent. Like a weaver, I had rolled up my life: he cuts me off from the loom. From day to night you make an end of me.
I cried out until morning; like a lion, he broke all my bones. From day to night you make an end of me.
Like the swallow, like the crane, I chirp; I moan like the dove. My eyes grow weary looking upward. Lord, I am hard pressed, be my surety!
What can I say? He has spoken to me, and it is he who has acted. I will walk humbly all the rest of my years, remembering the bitterness of my soul.
Lord, by these things men live, and in all of them is the life of my spirit. You heal me and restore me to life:
behold, my sharpest bitterness is turned to peace. You have drawn my soul back from the pit of perdition, you have cast all my sins behind your back.
For the realm of the dead does not praise you, death does not extol you; those who go down to the pit no longer hope in your faithfulness.
It is the living, the living, who praise you, as I do this day; the father makes known to his children your faithfulness.
The Lord has come to save me: we will make the strings of our harps resound all the days of our life, in the house of the Lord.
Isaiah had said: "Let a cake of figs be taken and applied to the sore, and the king will recover."
And Hezekiah had asked: "By what sign shall I know that I will go up to the house of the Lord?"

titres.titre: The envoys of Babylon and the announcement of exile

versets.t: At that time, Merodach-baladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent a letter and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard of his illness and his recovery.

Hezekiah rejoiced at their coming and showed them his treasure house, the silver and the gold, the spices and the precious oil, all his armoury, all that his storehouses contained; there was nothing in his palace or in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them.
Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and asked him: "What did these men say, and where have they come from to see you?" Hezekiah answered: "They have come from a distant land, from Babylon."
Isaiah went on: "What have they seen in your palace?" Hezekiah answered: "They have seen everything in it; there is nothing in my storehouses that I have not shown them."
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah: "Hear the word of the Lord of hosts:
Days are coming when all that is in your palace, all that your fathers have amassed to this day, shall be carried off to Babylon; nothing shall be left, says the Lord.
And some of your own sons, those born to you, whom you have begotten, shall be taken to become eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon."
Hezekiah answered Isaiah: "The word of the Lord that you have spoken is good." For he thought to himself: "At least there will be peace and security in my lifetime."

titres.titre: A voice crying in the wilderness
The grass withers, the word remains
Here is your God, the almighty shepherd
None can be compared to the Creator
Those who hope renew their strength

versets.t: Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.
Speak to the heart of Jerusalem, cry out to her that her service is ended, that her guilt is atoned for, that she has received from the hand of the Lord double for all her sins.
A voice cries: In the wilderness, prepare the way of the Lord! Make level in the desert a highway for our God!
Let every valley be filled in, every mountain and hill brought low; let the rugged heights become a plain, and the cliffs a broad valley!
Then the glory of the Lord will be revealed, and all people together will see it; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.
A voice says, "Cry out!" And I answer, "What shall I cry?" All flesh is like grass, all its beauty like the flower of the field:
the grass withers, the flower fades when the breath of the Lord blows upon it. Truly, the people are like grass.
The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God stands forever.

Climb a high mountain, you who bring good news to Zion! Lift up your voice with strength, you who bring good news to Jerusalem! Lift it up without fear, say to the cities of Judah, "Here is your God!"
See, the Lord God comes with power, his arm secures his dominion; see, his reward is with him, and before him goes the fruit of his work.
Like a shepherd he pastures his flock: with his arm he gathers the lambs, he carries them against his heart, he gently leads the ewes that nurse their young.

Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, gauged the span of the heavens with a handbreadth, gathered all the dust of the earth in a basket, weighed the mountains on scales and the hills in a balance?
Who has measured the spirit of the Lord, who has been his counselor to instruct him?
Whom did he consult for enlightenment, who taught him the path of justice, gave him knowledge, showed him the way of understanding?
See: the nations are like a drop from a bucket, they count as a speck of dust on the scales; see, the coastlands weigh as little as fine dust.
Lebanon would not be enough to feed the fire, its beasts would not be enough for a sacrifice.
All the nations are as nothing before him; in his eyes they count as nothing and emptiness.
To whom, then, will you compare God? What image will you find for him?
An idol? The craftsman casts it, the goldsmith overlays it with gold and forges silver chains for it.
One too poor for such an offering chooses wood that does not rot; he seeks out a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple.
Do you not know? Have you not heard? Were you not told from the beginning? Have you not understood since the earth was founded?
He is enthroned above the disk of the earth, whose inhabitants are like grasshoppers; he stretches out the heavens like a veil, he spreads them like a tent to dwell in.
He reduces princes to nothing, he makes the judges of the earth an emptiness:
scarcely planted, scarcely sown, scarcely has their stem taken root, he blows upon them, they wither, and the storm carries them off like straw.
To whom will you compare me, to whom shall I be equal? says the Holy One.

Lift up your eyes on high and look: who created all this? He who leads out their host in order and calls them all by name; before the greatness of his power and his sovereign strength, not one is missing.
Why do you say, Jacob, why do you repeat, Israel, "My way is hidden from the Lord, my right escapes my God"?
Do you not know? Have you not heard? The Lord is an eternal God, who created the ends of the earth; he does not grow tired, he does not grow weary, and his wisdom is beyond searching.
He gives strength to the weary, he gives fresh vigor to the exhausted.
Young men grow tired and weary, the most vigorous stumble,
but those who hope in the Lord renew their strength: they spread their wings like eagles, they run without growing weary, they walk without tiring.

titres.titre: The Lord, master of history, summons the nations
Israel, my servant, do not fear
Water for the poor, the desert transformed

versets.t: Coastlands, be silent to listen to me, let the peoples renew their strength! Let them approach, then let them speak; let us come together for judgment.

Who has raised up, from the east, one whom victory attends at every step? Who hands the nations over to him and subdues kings before him? His sword reduces them to dust, his bow scatters them like straw.
He pursues them, he advances in peace, by a way his feet had never trodden.
Who has done this, who has accomplished it? He who calls the generations from the beginning: I, the Lord, who am the first, and who will still be there with the last.
The coastlands see it and are afraid, the ends of the earth tremble; they draw near, they come.
Each one helps his companion, each says to his brother, "Take courage!"

The craftsman encourages the goldsmith, the one who smooths with the hammer supports the one who strikes the anvil; he says of the soldering, "It is good," then he fastens the idol with nails so it will not topple.
But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham, my friend,
you whom I took from the ends of the earth, whom I called from its farthest regions, to whom I said, "You are my servant, I have chosen you, I have not rejected you,"
do not fear, for I am with you; do not look about you in dread, for I am your God. I make you strong, I come to your aid, I uphold you with my victorious right hand.
They will be ashamed and humiliated, all who raged against you; they will be reduced to nothing, they will perish, those who sought a quarrel with you.
You will look for them and not find them, those who fought against you; they will be reduced to nothing, annihilated, those who made war on you.
For I, the Lord, your God, take you by the right hand and say to you, "Do not fear, it is I who come to your help."
Do not fear, poor worm of Jacob, feeble remnant of Israel: it is I who come to your help, oracle of the Lord; your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
See: I make of you a threshing-sledge, new and studded with points; you will crush the mountains, you will grind them, you will reduce the hills to fine chaff.
You will winnow them, the wind will carry them off, the storm will scatter them; and you, you will exult in the Lord, you will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
The poor and the afflicted seek water, and there is none; their tongue is parched with thirst. I, the Lord, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them.
I will make rivers gush from the bare hills, springs in the depths of the valleys; I will turn the desert into a pool, the parched land into gushing springs.
I will plant in the desert the cedar, the acacia, the myrtle, and the olive; I will set in the wilderness the cypress, the plane tree, and the box tree, all together,
so that people may see and know, may observe and understand, that the hand of the Lord has done this, that the Holy One of Israel has created it.
Present your case, says the Lord; produce your proofs, says the King of Jacob.
Let them come forward and tell us what is to happen! The events of the past, explain to us what they were, that we may take the lesson to heart; or else announce to us the future!
Reveal what is to come hereafter, and we will know that you are gods! Do good or do evil, that we may be struck with wonder and fear together!
But you are nothing, your work is emptiness; whoever chooses you chooses an abomination.
I have raised him up from the north, and he comes; from the rising of the sun, he calls upon my name; he tramples the governors like mud, as the potter treads the clay.
Who announced it from the start, that we might know, long in advance, that we might say, "It is right"? No one announced it, no one made it heard, no one gathered a word from you!
I was the first to say to Zion, "Here they are!" and I send to Jerusalem a messenger of good news.
I look: no one! Not one counselor among them whom I could question and who would answer me.
See: they are all nothing but emptiness, their works are void, their idols are wind.

titres.titre: The first Song of the Servant
The covenant of the people, the light of the nations
A new song to all the earth
Israel, a blind and deaf servant

versets.t: Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen one, in whom I delight: I have put my Spirit upon him, he will bring justice to the nations.
He will not cry out, he will not raise his voice, he will not make it heard in the streets.
He will not break the bruised reed, he will not quench the wick that still smolders; faithfully he will proclaim justice.
He will not falter, he will not let himself be crushed, until he has established justice on the earth; and the coastlands await his teaching.

Thus says God, the Lord, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and all that it brings forth, who gives breath to the people who dwell on it, and life to those who walk upon it:
I, the Lord, have called you in righteousness, I take you by the hand, I keep you; I make you the covenant of the people, the light of the nations,
to open the eyes of the blind, to bring the prisoner out of the dungeon, and out of the prison those who dwell in darkness.
I am the Lord, that is my name; I will not give my glory to another, nor my honor to idols.
The former things have come to pass, and now I announce new ones; before they spring forth, I make them known to you.
Sing to the Lord a new song, sing his praise from the ends of the earth! Let the sea proclaim it, and all that fills it, the coastlands and those who dwell in them!
Let the desert and its cities lift up their voice, the encampments where Kedar dwells! Let the inhabitants of Sela cry out for joy, let them shout their acclamations from the mountaintops!
Let them give glory to the Lord, let them proclaim his praise in the coastlands!
The Lord goes forth like a hero, like a warrior he rouses his ardor; he raises the battle cry, a resounding cry, he triumphs over his enemies.
For a long time I have kept silent, I have held my peace, I have restrained myself; now, like a woman giving birth, I cry out, I gasp and I pant.
I will lay waste mountains and hills, I will wither all their greenery; I will turn the rivers into dry land, I will dry up the pools.

I will lead the blind by a way they do not know, I will guide them along unknown paths; before them I will turn the darkness into light, the crooked places into a straight road. This is what I will do, and I will not fail.
They will draw back, covered with shame, those who trust in idols, who say to metal statues, "You are our gods!"
You who are deaf, listen! You who are blind, look and see!
Who is blind but my servant? Who is deaf like the messenger I send? Who is blind like the one I bound to myself, blind like the servant of the Lord?
You have seen many things without retaining any; your ears open, you have heard nothing.
The Lord was pleased, for the sake of his righteousness, to give a law great and glorious.

Yet here is this people plundered and stripped: they have all been trapped in pits, shut up in dungeons; they are plundered, and no one delivers them; they are stripped, and no one says, "Give them back!"
Who among you will give ear to this, will be attentive and listen for the time to come?
Who handed Jacob over to the plunderer, Israel to the despoilers? Was it not the Lord, against whom we have sinned, whose ways they would not follow, whose law they would not heed?
So he poured out upon them the heat of his anger and the violence of war; the fire enveloped them, but they did not understand; it consumed them, but they did not take the lesson to heart.

titres.titre: Do not fear, I have redeemed you
Israel, witness of the one God
Deliverance from Babylon, the new thing
The people's sin, the free pardon

versets.t: Now, thus says the Lord, he who created you, Jacob, he who formed you, Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; through the rivers, they will not sweep you away; when you walk through fire, you will not be burned, the flame will not consume you.
For I, the Lord, am your God; the Holy One of Israel is your savior. I have given Egypt as your ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in exchange for you.
Because you are precious in my eyes, because you have worth and I love you, I give people in exchange for you, nations in exchange for your life.
Do not fear, for I am with you. From the east I will bring back your offspring; from the west I will gather you.
I will say to the north, "Give them up!" and to the south, "Do not hold them back!" Bring back my sons from distant lands, my daughters from the ends of the earth,
all who bear my name, whom I created for my glory, whom I formed, whom I made.
Bring out the people who are blind, though they have eyes, the deaf, though they have ears!

Let all the nations assemble, let the peoples gather! Who among them announced this, who made us hear the events of the past? Let them produce their witnesses to justify themselves, that people may listen and say, "It is true!"

You are my witnesses, oracle of the Lord, you and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may acknowledge, believe me, and understand that I am he. Before me no god was formed, and after me there will be none.
It is I, I the Lord, and there is no savior but me.
It is I who announced, who saved, who made it heard, and no foreign god among you. You are my witnesses, oracle of the Lord: it is I who am God.
And from all time I am he; no one can snatch from my hand. What I do, who will undo it?
Thus says the Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I send my orders against Babylon; I will bring down all the bars, and the Chaldeans will see their rejoicing turned to lament.
I am the Lord, your Holy One, the creator of Israel, your king.
Thus says the Lord, he who opened a way in the sea, a path in the mighty waters,
who set chariots and horses in motion, army and warriors: together they lay down, never to rise again, they were snuffed out, quenched like a wick.
Remember no more the events of long ago, dwell no longer on the past.
See, I am doing a new thing: it is already springing up, do you not see it? Yes, I will make a way in the desert, I will cause rivers to flow in the wasteland.
The wild beasts will give me glory, the jackals and the ostriches, because I will have put water in the desert, rivers in the wasteland, to give drink to my people, my chosen ones,
this people whom I formed for myself, that they might proclaim my praise.
Yet it is not me you called upon, Jacob; you grew weary of me, Israel.
You did not bring me your lambs for sacrifice, you did not honor me with your offerings. I did not burden you with demands for offerings, I did not weary you by asking for incense.
You did not buy me fragrant cane with silver, you did not fill me with the fat of your victims. On the contrary, it is you who burdened me with your sins, who wearied me with your faults.
But it is I, I who blot out your transgressions, for my own sake, and I will remember your sins no more.
Refresh my memory, let us plead together, set out your case yourself to justify yourself.
Your first ancestor sinned, your spokesmen rebelled against me.
That is why I removed the leaders of the sanctuary, I gave Jacob over to the ban and delivered Israel to insults.

titres.titre: The Spirit poured out on the offspring
The first and the last, apart from whom nothing exists
Return to me, I have redeemed you
The Creator who raises up Cyrus

versets.t: Now listen, Jacob, my servant, Israel, whom I have chosen.
Thus says the Lord, he who made you, who formed you from your mother's womb and who helps you: Do not fear, Jacob, my servant, you, Israel, whom I have chosen.
For I will pour water on the thirsty ground, streams on the parched land; I will pour out my Spirit on your offspring, my blessing on your descendants.
They will sprout like grass by the water, like willows along the streams.
One will say, "I belong to the Lord," another will call himself by the name of Jacob; this one will write on his hand, "To the Lord," and take the name of Israel.
Thus says the Lord, king of Israel and its Redeemer, the Lord of hosts: I am the first and I am the last; apart from me there is no God.
Who is like me? Let him proclaim it, let him declare it, let him set it out before me! Since I founded the people of old, let him announce the future and what is to come!
Do not tremble, do not fear! Have I not announced it to you, revealed it long ago? You are my witnesses. Is there any God besides me? There is no other Rock, I know of none.
The makers of idols are all nothing, and their masterpieces are of no use; their own witnesses see nothing, understand nothing, to their great shame.
Who, then, fashions a god, casts an idol, for no profit at all?
See: all its worshipers will be covered with shame, and the craftsmen are only men! Let them all assemble, let them come forward: they will tremble and be humiliated together.

The blacksmith works the iron with a chisel, passes it through the coals, shapes it with the hammer, forges it with his strong arm. But he grows hungry and loses his strength, he has drunk no water and is worn out.

The wood-carver stretches out his line, traces the shape with chalk, roughs it out with the chisel, measures it with the compass; he makes it into a human figure, a fine image of a man, to sit enthroned in a house.
He had cut down cedars for himself, he had taken an oak, a durmast, letting it grow among the trees of the forest; he had planted a pine that the rain made grow.

All this serves the man as fuel: he takes some to warm himself, he lights it to bake his bread, and from this same wood he makes a god that he worships, he makes it into an idol before which he bows down!
He burns half of it in the fire; over these coals he roasts his meat, he eats his roast and is satisfied; he warms himself too and says, "Ah! now I am warm, I see the flame!"
With the rest he makes himself a god, his idol; he bows down before it, he worships it, he prays to it, saying, "Save me, for you are my god!"
They know nothing, they understand nothing: their eyes are shut, unable to see, their hearts unable to understand.

No one reflects, no one has the intelligence or the good sense to say, "I burned half of this wood in the fire, I baked bread over its coals, I roasted meat and ate it; and with the rest shall I make an abomination, shall I bow down before a block of wood!"
This man feeds on ashes, his deluded heart leads him astray; he cannot save himself, nor say, "Is not what I hold in my hand a lie?"
Remember all this, Jacob, Israel, for you are my servant: I formed you to be my servant; Israel, I will not forget you.
I have wiped away your transgressions like a cloud, your sins like a mist: return to me, for I have redeemed you.

Cry out for joy, O heavens, for the Lord has acted! Shout, O depths of the earth! Break into cries of joy, O mountains, and you forests, with all your trees! For the Lord has redeemed Jacob, he displays his glory in Israel.
Thus says the Lord, your Redeemer, he who formed you from your mother's womb: It is I, the Lord, who made all things, I alone who stretched out the heavens and firmly set the earth. Who was with me?
I thwart the signs of the false prophets, I make fools of the diviners, I turn back the wise and turn their knowledge into folly.

But I fulfill the word of my servant, I carry out the plan announced by my envoys. I say of Jerusalem, "Let it be inhabited!" and of the cities of Judah, "Let them be rebuilt! I will raise up their ruins."
I say to the ocean, "Be dry! I will dry up your rivers."
I say of Cyrus, "He is my shepherd, he will accomplish all my will." He will say of Jerusalem, "Let it be rebuilt!" and of the Temple, "Let your foundations be laid!"

titres.titre: The oracle concerning Cyrus, the anointed of the Lord
No one contends with his Creator
The nations will acknowledge the hidden God
Turn to me, and you will be saved

versets.t: Thus says the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus, whom I have grasped by the right hand to subdue the nations before him and disarm kings, to open the gates before him so that no doors are shut against him:
I myself will go before you, I will level the heights, I will shatter the gates of bronze, I will cut through the bars of iron.
I will give you the treasures hidden in darkness, the riches buried in secret places, so that you may know that it is I, the Lord, the God of Israel, who call you by name.
For the sake of Jacob, my servant, of Israel, my chosen one, I have called you by name, I have given you a title of honor, though you did not know me.
I am the Lord, and there is no other; apart from me, there is no God. I armed you, though you did not know me,
so that people may know, from the rising of the sun to its setting, that there is nothing apart from me. I am the Lord, and there is no other:
I form the light and create the darkness, I make well-being and create woe. It is I, the Lord, who do all this.

Heavens, pour down your dew from above, let the clouds rain down righteousness! Let the earth open and bring forth salvation, let it make righteousness spring up at the same time! I, the Lord, create all this.

Woe to the one who contends with the one who formed him, a mere potsherd among the potsherds of the earth! Does the clay say to the one who shapes it, "What are you making?" and your work say, "He has no hands"?
Woe to the one who says to a father, "Why do you beget?" and to a woman, "Why do you give birth?"
Thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, the one who shapes it: Would you dare question me about my children, give me orders about the work of my hands?
It is I who made the earth and created the man who dwells on it; it is I whose hands stretched out the heavens, I who command all their host.
It is I who raised him up, Cyrus, in my righteousness, and I will make all his ways level. It is he who will rebuild my city and send back my exiles, without ransom or gifts, says the Lord of hosts.

Thus says the Lord: The gains of Egypt, the profits of Ethiopia, and the tall Sabeans will pass over to you and belong to you; they will walk behind you, they will pass by in chains, they will bow down before you and plead with you, "God is with you alone, there is no other, there is no other god!"
Truly, you are a hidden God, God of Israel, Savior!
They are all ashamed and humiliated, they go off covered with confusion, the makers of idols.
But Israel, the Lord saves with an everlasting salvation: never, through the ages to come, will you have to blush or be confounded.

For thus says the Lord, he who created the heavens, the God who formed the earth and made it, who established it, who did not create it as a chaos but formed it to be inhabited: I am the Lord, and there is no other.
I did not speak in secret, in some dark corner of the earth. I did not say to the offspring of Jacob, "Seek me in vain." I, the Lord, speak what is right, I announce what is just.
Gather and come, draw near together, survivors of the nations! They understand nothing, those who carry about their wooden idol and pray to a god unable to save.

Announce, present your proofs, take counsel together! Who made this heard long ago, who announced it from the start? Was it not I, the Lord? There is no other God than me, a God just and saving; there is no other.
Turn to me and you will be saved, all you ends of the earth, for I am God, and there is no other.
I swear by myself, from my mouth goes forth righteousness, a word that will not be revoked: before me every knee will bend, every tongue will swear by me.
Of me it will be said, "In the Lord alone are righteousness and strength." People will come to him, and they will be confounded, all who raged against him.
It is in the Lord that all the offspring of Israel will find righteousness and glory.

titres.titre: The gods of Babylon that must be carried
The God who carries his people

versets.t: Bel collapses, Nebo topples; their statues are loaded onto animals, onto beasts of burden. These idols that you carried in procession are loaded like a heavy burden on weary beasts.
Together they topple and collapse; unable to save their own load, they themselves go off into captivity.
Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all you remnant of the house of Israel: I have carried you since your birth, upheld you since your mother's womb.
To your old age I remain the same; to your gray hairs I will carry you. I have done it, and I will carry you still; I will uphold you, I will save you.
To whom will you compare me, to whom will you make me equal? To whom will you liken me, that we should be alike?
Some pour out gold from their purse, weigh silver on the scales, pay a goldsmith to make it into a god, then they bow down and worship it.
They load it on their shoulder, they carry it, they set it in its place, and there it stays, without moving. In vain they cry out to it, it does not answer, it saves no one from distress.
Remember this and stand firm; you rebels, take it to heart!
Recall the events of long ago, the times of old: yes, it is I who am God, and there is no other; I am God, and none is like me.
From the beginning I announce the end; long in advance, what is not yet. I say, "My plan will stand, I will accomplish all that I please."
From the east I call a bird of prey; from a distant land, the man of my purpose. I have spoken it, I will bring it about; I have decided it, I will carry it out.
Listen to me, you who are hard of heart, you who stay far from righteousness.
I bring my righteousness near, it is no longer far off; my salvation will not delay. I will grant salvation to Zion, and my glory to Israel.

titres.titre: The fall of Babylon the queen
The pride of her who thought herself eternal
The powerlessness of spells and astrologers

versets.t: Come down, sit in the dust, virgin daughter of Babylon! Sit on the ground, without a throne, daughter of the Chaldeans! For you will no longer be called the delicate, the refined.
Take the millstone, grind the flour! Remove your veil, lift your train, bare your legs, cross the rivers!
Let your nakedness be exposed, let your shame be seen! I will take vengeance, sparing no one.
Our Redeemer, his name is the Lord of hosts, the Holy One of Israel.
Sit in silence, sink into the darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans! For you will no longer be called the queen of kingdoms.
I was angry with my people, I let my heritage be profaned, I handed them over into your hands. But you showed them no pity; even on the old you laid your yoke heavily.
You said, "I will be queen forever!" and you did not reflect on any of this, you did not consider what would come of it in the end.
Now listen to this, you lover of pleasure, sitting securely, you who said in your heart, "I, and no one else! Never will I be a widow, never will I lose my children."

These two calamities will fall upon you, suddenly, in a single day: the loss of your children and widowhood, they will overwhelm you completely, despite your many spells, despite the power of your enchantments.
You trusted in your wickedness, you said, "No one sees me." Your wisdom and your knowledge led you astray, and you said in your heart, "I, and no one else!"
But calamity will fall upon you, and you will not know how to ward it off, disaster will overwhelm you, and you will not be able to turn it aside, ruin will reach you suddenly, before you suspect it.
Persist, then, in your enchantments and in your many spells, to which you have devoted yourself from your youth! Perhaps you will profit from them, perhaps you will inspire dread!

You have worn yourself out with your many consultations. Let them come forward, then, and save you, those who carve up the sky, who scan the stars, who at each new moon announce what is to happen to you!
See, they are like straw: the fire consumes them, they cannot save their lives from the flame. This will be no ember to warm oneself by, no fire to sit before.
This is what they come to for you, those for whom you wore yourself out, those with whom you traded from your youth: each flees his own way, not one saves you.

titres.titre: Spared for the sake of God's name
The first and the last, creator and guide

versets.t: Listen to this, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel, sprung from the source of Judah, you who swear by the name of the Lord and invoke the God of Israel, but with no sincerity or uprightness!
For they call themselves after the holy city and lean on the God of Israel, whose name is the Lord of hosts.
Long ago I announced the former events; they went out from my mouth, I proclaimed them; then, suddenly, I acted, and they came to pass.
Because I knew you were stubborn, your neck stiff as an iron bar, your forehead of bronze,
I announced them to you long ago, revealed them before they happened, so that you could not say, "It was my idol that did them, my statue of wood or metal that ordained them."
You have heard it, and now you see it fulfilled: will you not testify to it? From now on I make you hear new things, kept secret, that you did not know.
It is now that they are created, not before; until this day you had heard nothing of them, so that you could not say, "There, I already knew it!"
No, you have heard nothing, known nothing, your ear had perceived nothing; for I knew how treacherous you are, you who are called a rebel from your mother's womb.
For the sake of my name I restrain my anger; for the sake of my glory I hold back toward you, so as not to destroy you.
See: I have passed you through the fire, but not as silver; I have tested you in the furnace of affliction.
It is for my own sake, for my sake alone, that I act: how could I let my name be profaned? I will not give my glory to another.
Listen to me, Jacob, and you, Israel, whom I have called: it is I, I the first, I also the last.
It was my hand that founded the earth, my right hand that stretched out the heavens; I call them, and together they come forward.
Gather, all of you, and listen: which of the idols announced this? The one whom the Lord loves will carry out his good pleasure against Babylon, his arm will strike the Chaldeans.
I, I have spoken, I have called him, I have brought him, and his way will succeed.
Draw near to me, listen to this: from the beginning I have not spoken in secret; at the moment it comes to pass, I am there. And now, the Lord God sends me, with his Spirit.
Thus says the Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I, the Lord, your God, teach you for your good, I lead you on the way you must go.
Ah, if only you had been attentive to my commandments, your peace would be like a river, your righteousness like the waves of the sea;
your offspring would be like the sand, the children of your body like its grains; never would their name be cut off or blotted out before me.
Go out from Babylon, flee the Chaldeans! Announce it with cries of joy, proclaim it, carry the news to the ends of the earth! Say, "The Lord has redeemed his servant Jacob!
They did not thirst when he led them through the deserts: for them he made water gush from the rock; he split the rock, and the water flowed."
There is no peace for the wicked, says the Lord.

titres.titre: The second Song of the Servant
Kings will bow before the Servant
The nations bring back the children of Zion

versets.t: Coastlands, listen to me! Distant peoples, pay attention! The Lord called me from my mother's womb, from her body he pronounced my name.
He made my mouth a sharp sword, he hid me in the shadow of his hand; he made me a polished arrow, he kept me close in his quiver.
He said to me, "You are my servant, Israel, in you I will display my glory."
And I had said, "I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nothing, for emptiness." Yet my right is with the Lord, my reward is with my God.
And now the Lord speaks, he who formed me from my mother's womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him and gather Israel to him: I count in the eyes of the Lord, and my God is my strength.

He says, "It is too small a thing that you should be my servant, to raise up the tribes of Jacob and bring back the survivors of Israel: I make you the light of the nations, that my salvation may reach the ends of the earth."

Thus says the Lord, the Redeemer and the Holy One of Israel, to the one despised, abhorred by the nation, the slave of tyrants: Kings will see you and rise, princes will bow down, because of the Lord who is faithful, of the Holy One of Israel who has chosen you.

Thus says the Lord: In the time of favor I answer you; on the day of salvation I come to your help. I have kept you, I make you the covenant of the people, to restore the land, to reapportion the ravaged heritages,
to say to the prisoners, "Go out!" and to those in darkness, "Show yourselves!" Along the roads they will find their pasture, on all the bare heights their pasturelands.
They will neither hunger nor thirst, neither the scorching wind nor the sun will strike them, for the one who loves them will lead them, he will guide them to gushing springs.
Of all my mountains I will make roads, and my highways will be raised up.
See, these come from afar; see, these from the north and the west; and those from the land of Syene.
Heavens, cry out for joy! Earth, exult! Mountains, break into acclamations! For the Lord has comforted his people, he has taken pity on his afflicted.
Zion said, "The Lord has abandoned me, my Master has forgotten me."
Does a woman forget her nursing child, does she cease to cherish the son of her womb? Even should she forget, I will never forget you.
See, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands, your walls are always before my eyes.
Your builders hasten back, while those who tore you down and ravaged you go away from you.

Lift up your eyes all around and look: they all gather, they come to you. As surely as I live, oracle of the Lord, you will wear them all like an ornament, you will adorn yourself with them like a bride with her sash.
Yes, your ruins, your rubble, your devastated land will now be too narrow for all your inhabitants, and those who devoured you will be far away.
They will yet say to you, these children you thought lost, "This place is too narrow for me; make room for me, that I may settle here."
And you will say in your heart, "Who has borne me all these? I was bereft of children, barren, exiled and cast off: these, who raised them? I was left all alone: these, where do they come from?"
Thus says the Lord God: See, I lift my hand toward the nations, I raise my banner to the peoples; they will bring back your sons in their arms, they will carry your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will be your guardians, their princesses your nurses; faces to the ground, they will bow down before you, they will lick the dust of your feet. Then you will know that I am the Lord, and that those who hope in me will not be disappointed.
Can the prey be taken from the warrior? Can the captive of a tyrant escape him?

Yet thus says the Lord: Yes, the captive of the warrior will be taken from him, the prey of the tyrant will escape him. Your adversaries, it is I who will fight them; your children, it is I who will save them.
