To your oppressors I will make eat their own flesh, they will get drunk on their own blood as on new wine. And all flesh will know that I, the Lord, am your Savior, that your Redeemer is the Mighty One of Jacob.

titres.titre: The people's sin, not God's divorce
The third Song of the Servant
To walk in trust or in one's own fire

versets.t: Thus says the Lord: Where is it, the certificate of divorce by which I would have sent your mother away? To which of my creditors have I sold you? It was for your faults that you were sold, for your sins that your mother was sent away.

I came: why was there no one? I called: why did no one answer? Is my hand too short to deliver? Have I not the strength to save? With a rebuke I dry up the sea, I turn the rivers into desert; their fish rot for lack of water, they die of thirst.
I clothe the heavens in black, I cover them with a garment of mourning.
The Lord God has given me the tongue of the disciples, that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word. Each morning he awakens, he awakens my ear that I may listen, like a disciple.
The Lord God has opened my ear, and I did not resist, I did not draw back.
I gave my back to those who struck me, my cheeks to those who tore out my beard; I did not hide my face from insults and spittle.
The Lord God comes to my help: that is why the outrages do not reach me, why I have set my face hard as flint, knowing that I will not be disappointed.
He is near, the one who vindicates me. Who wants to bring a case against me? Let us stand together! Who is my accuser? Let him come forward to me!
The Lord God comes to my help: who then will condemn me? See, they all fray like a garment, eaten away by moths.
Who among you fears the Lord and listens to the voice of his servant? Whoever walks in darkness, deprived of light, let him trust in the name of the Lord, let him lean on his God!

But all you who kindle a fire and arm yourselves with flaming arrows, go then into the flames of your fire, into the midst of the arrows you have set ablaze! This is what my hand holds for you: you will lie down in torment.

titres.titre: Look to the rock from which you were hewn
It is I who comfort you
Awake, Jerusalem, the cup taken away

versets.t: Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the Lord: look to the rock from which you were hewn, to the quarry from which you were dug.
Look to Abraham, your father, and to Sarah who bore you: he was alone when I called him, and I blessed him, I multiplied him.
Yes, the Lord comforts Zion, he comforts all her ruins; he turns her desert into Eden, her wasteland into the garden of the Lord. Joy and gladness will be found there, thanksgiving and song.
Be attentive to me, my people; my nation, give ear to me! For from me will go forth the teaching, and I will establish my justice as a light for the peoples.
My righteousness is near, my salvation is about to appear, my arm will judge the peoples; the coastlands hope in me, they count on my arm.

Lift up your eyes to the sky, lower your gaze to the earth: the heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment, its inhabitants will die like flies. But my salvation will last forever, my righteousness will not fail.
Listen to me, you who know righteousness, people who carry my law in their heart: do not fear the insults of men, do not be dismayed at their outrages!
For the moth will devour them like a garment, the grub will gnaw them like wool. But my righteousness will last forever, my salvation from generation to generation.
Awake, awake, clothe yourself with strength, arm of the Lord! Awake as in the days of old, as in the times long past! Was it not you who cut Rahab to pieces, who pierced the dragon?
Was it not you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great abyss, who opened a way in the depths of the sea for the redeemed to pass through?
So the redeemed of the Lord will return, they will enter Zion with cries of joy, everlasting gladness on their faces; joy and gladness will fill them, sorrow and sighing will flee away.
It is I, it is I who comfort you. Who are you, then, to fear a mortal man, a son of man doomed to pass like the grass,

to forget the Lord, your creator, who stretched out the heavens and founded the earth? You tremble all day long, without respite, before the fury of the oppressor, poised to destroy you. But where is it now, the fury of the oppressor?
Soon the bowed prisoner will be set free; he will not die in his pit, nor will bread fail him.
For I am the Lord, your God, who stirs up the sea and makes its waves roar; the Lord of hosts is my name.
I have put my words in your mouth, I have sheltered you in the shadow of my hand, I who stretch out the heavens and found the earth, I who say to Zion, "You are my people."
Awake, awake, stand up, Jerusalem! You who drank from the hand of the Lord the cup of his anger, who drank to the dregs the chalice that makes one reel!
Of all the children she bore, not one to guide her; of all the children she raised, not one to take her by the hand.
Two calamities have struck you, and who will grieve for you? Devastation and ruin, famine and the sword: who will comfort you?
Your children lie fainting at the corner of every street, like an antelope caught in a net, saturated with the fury of the Lord, with the rebuke of your God.
So listen to this, afflicted one, you who are drunk, but not with wine:
Thus says your Master, the Lord, your God, who defends his people: See, I take from your hand the cup that makes one reel; the chalice of my anger, you will never drink it again.
I will put it in the hand of your tormentors, those who said to you, "Lie down, that we may walk over you!" and you made your back like the ground, like a street for those who passed by.

titres.titre: The beautiful feet of the messenger of peace
Go out, carry the vessels of the Lord
The Servant exalted after his humiliation

versets.t: Awake, awake, clothe yourself with strength, Zion! Put on your festive garments, Jerusalem, holy city! For the uncircumcised and the unclean will no longer enter you.
Shake off your dust, rise up, take your throne, Jerusalem! Loose the chains from your neck, captive daughter of Zion!
For thus says the Lord: You were sold for nothing, and you will be redeemed without money.
For thus says the Lord God: Long ago my people went down to Egypt to sojourn there; then Assyria oppressed them without cause.

And now, what have I here, oracle of the Lord, since my people have been carried off for nothing? Their tyrants howl in triumph, oracle of the Lord, and all day long, without ceasing, my name is reviled.
Therefore my people will know my name; on that day they will know that it is I who say, "Here I am!"
How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings the good news of happiness, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, "Your God reigns!"
Listen to your watchmen: they lift up their voice, together they cry out for joy, for with their own eyes they see the Lord returning to Zion.
Break into cries of joy together, ruins of Jerusalem! For the Lord has comforted his people, he has redeemed Jerusalem.
The Lord has bared his holy arm in the sight of all the nations; and to the ends of the earth, all will see the salvation of our God.
Depart, depart, go out from there, touch nothing unclean! Go out from her midst, purify yourselves, you who carry the sacred vessels of the Lord!
But you will not depart in haste, you will not go off as fugitives, for the Lord marches before you, and the God of Israel closes your march.
See, my servant will succeed; he will rise, he will be lifted up, he will be raised to the highest heights.
Just as many were appalled to see him, so disfigured was his appearance, so little human, his face no longer anything of a man's,
so he will astonish many nations; before him kings will stand speechless, for they will see what they had never been told, they will understand what they had never heard.

titres.titre: The silent lamb led to the slaughter
The fruitful sacrifice of the Servant

versets.t: Who has believed what we have heard? To whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
He grew up before him like a frail shoot, like a root out of dry ground; he had neither form nor beauty to draw our gaze, nor splendor to attract us.
Despised, forsaken by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with suffering, like one from whom people hide their faces, despised, and we held him of no account.
Yet it was our sufferings that he bore, our sorrows that he carried; and we, we thought of him as one punished, struck down by God, and humbled.
But he was pierced for our transgressions, crushed for our faults; the punishment that brings us peace fell upon him, and by his wounds we are healed.
We were all straying like sheep, each one following his own way; and the Lord laid on him the guilt of us all.
Mistreated, he humbles himself, he does not open his mouth, like the lamb led to the slaughter, like the sheep silent before its shearers: he does not open his mouth.
Arrested, judged, he was taken away; and among his contemporaries, who cared that he was cut off from the land of the living, struck down for the sins of my people?
He was given his grave among the wicked, his tomb among the rich, though he had committed no violence and there was no lie in his mouth.

But it pleased the Lord to crush him with suffering. If he offers his life as an offering for sin, in reparation, he will see offspring, he will prolong his days, and through him the will of the Lord will be accomplished.
After the torments of his soul, he will see the light and be satisfied. By his knowledge, the just one, my servant, will make a multitude righteous, bearing their faults himself.

Therefore I will give him a portion among the great, he will share the spoil with the mighty, because he gave himself up to death and was counted among the criminals, while he bore the sin of the multitudes and interceded for the guilty.

titres.titre: The joy of the barren wife
The husband who takes back his wife
The city rebuilt with precious stones

versets.t: Cry out for joy, barren woman, you who bore no children! Break into cries of joy, you who never knew the pangs of birth! For the children of the forsaken one are more numerous than those of the wife, says the Lord.
Enlarge the space of your tent, spread out unsparingly the curtains of your dwelling, lengthen your ropes, drive your pegs down firmly!
For you will overflow to the right and to the left, your offspring will take possession of the nations and repopulate the deserted cities.
Do not fear, you will not be disappointed; do not be ashamed, you will not have to blush: you will forget the shame of your youth, you will remember no more the dishonor of your widowhood.
For your husbands are your Makers: the Lord of hosts is his name; your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel, who is called the God of all the earth.
Yes, like a woman abandoned, her heart broken, the Lord calls you back; like the wife of one's youth who had been cast off, says your God.
For a brief moment I had abandoned you, but with immense tenderness I gather you back.
In an outburst of anger, for a moment, I had hidden my face from you; but with an everlasting love I have pity on you, says your Redeemer, the Lord.
For me it is as in the days of Noah: I had sworn that the waters of Noah would never again flood the earth; so I swear no longer to be angry with you or to threaten you.
Though the mountains should depart, though the hills should be shaken, my love will not depart from you, my covenant of peace will not be shaken, says the Lord, who has pity on you.
Afflicted one, battered by the storm, without consolation, see, I am going to set your stones on a bed of jewels, I will lay your foundations on sapphires.
I will make your battlements of rubies, your gates of carbuncle, all your walls of precious stones.
All your children will be disciples of the Lord, and great will be the peace of your children.
You will be established in righteousness; far from you oppression, you will have nothing to fear; far from you terror, it will no longer come near you.
If anyone bands together against you, it will not come from me; whoever attacks you will fall before you.
See: it is I who created the blacksmith, the one who blows on the coals and forges from them a weapon for its use; and it is I who created the destroyer to ravage.

No weapon forged against you will succeed, and every tongue that accuses you in court, you will confound it. Such is the heritage of the servants of the Lord, the righteousness that comes to them from me, oracle of the Lord.

titres.titre: Come, all you who are thirsty
Seek the Lord while he is near
My thoughts are not your thoughts

versets.t: O all you who are thirsty, come to the water! Even without money, come, buy something to eat; come, buy without money, without paying, wine and milk.
Why spend your money for what does not nourish, your labor for what does not satisfy? Listen to me, then, and you will eat good things, you will feast on rich food.
Give ear and come to me, listen, and you will live! I will make with you an everlasting covenant, faithfully keeping the promises made to David.
See: I have made him a witness to the peoples, a leader, a guide for the nations.
See, you will call a nation you did not know, and nations that did not know you will hasten to you, because of the Lord, your God, of the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you.
Seek the Lord while he lets himself be found, call upon him while he is near.
Let the wicked forsake his way, the unjust man his thoughts; let him return to the Lord, who will show him grace, to our God, who pardons without measure.
For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways, oracle of the Lord.
As high as the heavens are above the earth, so far do my ways surpass yours, and my thoughts your thoughts.

The rain and the snow come down from heaven and do not return there without having watered the earth, without having made it fruitful and bring forth, giving seed to the sower and bread to the one who eats.
So my word, gone out from my mouth, does not return to me empty: it accomplishes what I will, it achieves what I sent it to do.
Yes, you will go out in joy, you will be led back in peace; before you, mountains and hills will break into cries of joy, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
In place of the thorn will grow the cypress, in place of the nettle, the myrtle; this will be for the Lord a title of glory, an everlasting sign that will never be blotted out.

titres.titre: The blessing of the one who keeps the sabbath
The foreigner and the eunuch welcomed
The blind watchmen and the greedy shepherds

versets.t: Thus says the Lord: Observe what is right, do justice, for my salvation is close at hand, my righteousness is about to be revealed.
Blessed is the man who acts thus, the human being who holds fast to it: he keeps the sabbath without profaning it, he keeps his hand from all evil.
Let not the foreigner joined to the Lord say, "Surely the Lord will exclude me from his people." And let not the eunuch say, "See, I am a dry tree."
For thus says the Lord: To the eunuchs who keep my sabbaths, who choose what pleases me and hold fast to my covenant,
I will give in my house, within my walls, a monument and a name better than sons and daughters; I will give them an everlasting name, that will never be blotted out.
As for the foreigners joined to the Lord to serve him, to love his name and become his servants, all who keep the sabbath without profaning it and hold fast to my covenant,

I will lead them to my holy mountain, I will fill them with joy in my house of prayer; their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar. For my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
Oracle of the Lord God, who gathers the exiles of Israel: to those already gathered, I will add still others.
All you beasts of the field, come and devour! And you, beasts of the forest!
The watchmen of Israel are all blind, they know nothing; they are all mute dogs, unable to bark; they lie dreaming, they love to doze.
They are greedy dogs, never satisfied; and they are shepherds unable to understand! They all follow their own way, each seeking his own gain, down to the last.
"Come," they say, "I will fetch wine, let us get drunk on strong drink! And tomorrow will be like today, a day of feasting, greater still!"

titres.titre: The just one carried off from the coming evil

versets.t: The just one perishes, and no one takes it to heart; faithful men are carried off, and no one understands that the just one is carried off to be spared the coming evil.
He enters into peace; they rest on their beds, those who walked uprightly.
But you, come here, sons of the sorceress, offspring of the adulterer and the prostitute!
At whom are you mocking? Against whom do you open your mouth wide and stick out your tongue? Are you not children of rebellion, an offspring of lies,
you who burn with lust beside the sacred oaks, under every green tree, who slaughter your children in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks?
Your portion is the smooth stones of the wadi: yes, that is your lot! To them you have poured out libations, presented offerings. Am I to be content with this?
On a high and lofty mountain you have made your bed, and there you go up to offer your sacrifices.

Behind the door and its post you have set up your object of worship. Far from me you uncover your bed, you climb into it, you make your bed wide; you bargain with those whose bed you love, you gaze at their nakedness.
You go to the king with oil, you multiply your perfumes; you send your messengers far away, you stoop down to the realm of the dead.
With all your journeys you wear yourself out, but you do not say, "It is hopeless." You find fresh vigor, and that is why you do not weaken.

Who, then, made you so afraid, who terrified you, that you betrayed me, that you no longer thought of me, that you gave it no heed at all? Is it not because I have kept silent for so long that you no longer fear me?
Well then, I will expose your righteousness and your works, which will do you no good!

When you cry for help, let them deliver you, your heaps of idols! A breath will carry them all off, a mere nothing will make them vanish. But the one who takes refuge in me will inherit the land, he will possess my holy mountain.
And it will be said: Build up, build up, prepare the way! Remove every obstacle from the road of my people!

For thus says the Most High, he who dwells forever and whose name is Holy: I dwell in a high and holy place, but I am also with the crushed and humble, to give life to the spirit of the humble, to give life to the heart of the crushed.
No, I do not want to accuse without end, nor to remain angry forever, or else the breath before me would fail, the life that I myself created.
His guilty greed made me angry; I struck him, I hid myself in my fury; but he, in rebellion, followed the inclination of his heart.
I have seen his conduct, and yet I will heal him; I will lead him, I will restore consolation to him, to him and to those who mourn with him,
I will bring forth praise on their lips. Peace, peace to the one who is far off as to the one who is near, says the Lord, and I will heal him.
But the wicked are like a troubled sea that cannot be calmed, whose waves churn up mire and mud.
There is no peace for the wicked, says my God.

titres.titre: The fast that does not please God
The true fast: to free and to share

versets.t: Cry out with full voice, do not hold back! Make your voice ring out like the trumpet! Denounce to my people their rebellion, to the house of Jacob their sins.

Day after day they seek me, they want to know my ways, like a nation that practices righteousness and has not forsaken the commandment of its God. They ask me for just judgments, they would have God draw near:
"What use is fasting, if you do not see it? What use is denying ourselves, if you pay no attention?" But on the day of your fast, you go about your own business and drive all your workers hard.
You fast amid disputes and quarrels, even striking with a wicked fist. It is not by fasting as you do today that you will make your voice heard on high.
Is this the fast that pleases me, a day when a man denies himself? To bow the head like a reed, to lie down on sackcloth and ashes, is this what you call a fast, a day pleasing to the Lord?
The fast that I prefer, is it not rather this: to loose the chains of injustice, to untie the cords of the yoke, to send the oppressed away free, to break every yoke?
Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, to welcome into your home the poor without shelter, to clothe the one you see naked, not to turn away from your own flesh and blood?
Then your light will break forth like the dawn, your wound will quickly heal; your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the Lord will close your march.
Then you will call, and the Lord will answer; you will cry out, and he will say, "Here I am!" If you drive away from your midst the yoke, the accusing finger, the malicious word,
if you share your bread with the hungry, if you satisfy the desires of the afflicted, your light will rise in the darkness, and your night will be like the full noonday.
The Lord will guide you continually, he will satisfy you in the parched places, he will give fresh vigor to your limbs; you will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.
Your own people will rebuild the ancient ruins, you will raise up foundations laid long ago; you will be called the repairer of the breaches, the one who makes the roads fit to live along.

If you cease to trample the sabbath, to go about your business on my holy day; if you call the sabbath a delight, and the day consecrated to the Lord honorable; if you honor it by giving up your travels, your business, and idle chatter,
then you will find your joy in the Lord; I will make you ride in triumph over the heights of the land, I will let you enjoy the heritage of Jacob, your father. Yes, the mouth of the Lord has spoken.

titres.titre: The sins that separate from God

versets.t: No, the hand of the Lord is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear;
but your faults have dug a gulf between you and your God; your sins have hidden his face from you, keeping him from hearing you.
For your hands are stained with blood, your fingers with crime; your lips utter lies, your tongue murmurs perversity.
No one brings a charge in accordance with right, no one pleads in accordance with truth; people rely on emptiness, they invoke lies; they conceive evil and give birth to crime.
They hatch vipers' eggs and weave spiders' webs: whoever eats their eggs dies, and if one of them is crushed, out comes a serpent.
Their webs will never make a garment, their work will cover no one; their acts are criminal acts, their hands do nothing but violence.
Their feet run toward evil, they hurry to shed innocent blood; their thoughts are thoughts of crime, ruin and disaster mark their road.
They do not know the way of peace, there is no uprightness in their steps; they make their paths crooked, and whoever walks on them knows no peace.
That is why justice stays far from us, and righteousness does not reach us; we waited for light, and here is darkness; for brightness, and we walk in the gloom.
We grope along the wall like blind men, we feel our way like people with no eyes; we stumble at midday as at twilight, in full health we are like the dead.
We all growl like bears, we moan without ceasing like doves; we waited for justice, it does not come; for salvation, it stays far from us.
For our rebellions have multiplied before you, and our sins testify against us; yes, our rebellions do not leave us, and our faults, we know them:
to rebel and deny the Lord, to turn away from our God, to speak only of oppression and revolt, to conceive and brood in our heart over words of falsehood.
So justice has drawn back, righteousness stands at a distance; for truth stumbles in the public square, and uprightness finds no way in.
Truth has vanished, and whoever turns from evil is plundered. The Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no longer any justice.
He saw that there was no one, he was astonished that no one intervened; then his own arm brought him salvation, and his righteousness upheld him.
He put on righteousness like a breastplate, set the helmet of salvation on his head; he clothed himself with vengeance as with a garment, he wrapped himself in his ardor as in a cloak.
He will repay each one according to his deeds: fury to his adversaries, just recompense to his enemies; to the distant coastlands he will repay their due.
Then, from the west, they will fear the name of the Lord, and from the rising of the sun, they will fear his glory; for he will come like a rushing torrent, driven by the breath of the Lord.
He will come as Redeemer for Zion, for those of Jacob who turn from their rebellion, oracle of the Lord.

And this is the covenant I make with them, says the Lord: my Spirit that rests on you, and my words that I have put in your mouth will never leave your mouth, nor the mouth of your children, nor the mouth of your children's children, says the Lord, from now on and forever.
Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you!
See, darkness covers the earth, a thick night wraps the peoples; but upon you the Lord rises, upon you his glory appears.
The nations will walk toward your light, and kings toward the brightness of your dawn.
Lift up your eyes, look around you: they all gather, they come to you; your sons arrive from afar, your daughters are carried in the arms.
At the sight, you will grow radiant, your heart will thrill and open wide, for toward you will stream the riches of the sea, the treasures of the nations will come to you.
Throngs of camels will cover you, the young dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all those of Sheba will come, laden with gold and incense, proclaiming the praises of the Lord.
All the flocks of Kedar will gather to you, the rams of Nebaioth will be at your service; they will go up on my altar as a pleasing offering, and I will make splendid my house of glory.
Who are these, who fly like clouds, like doves to their cotes?

They are the coastlands that hope in me, with the ships of Tarshish in the lead, to bring back your sons from afar, with their silver and their gold, to honor the name of the Lord, your God, the Holy One of Israel, for he has filled you with glory.
Foreigners will rebuild your walls, their kings will be at your service; for I struck you in my anger, but in my favor I have had pity on you.
Your gates will always be open; never, by day or by night, will they be shut, to let into you the treasures of the nations, led by their kings.
For the nation or kingdom that refuses to serve you will perish; those nations will be utterly destroyed.
The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the cypress, the plane tree, and the box tree all together, to adorn the place of my sanctuary; I will make glorious the place where my feet rest.
The sons of your oppressors will come to you, heads bowed; all who despised you will bow down at your feet; they will call you the City of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
You who were forsaken, hated, with no one to pass through you, I will make you a pride forever, the joy of all generations.
You will drink the milk of the nations, you will be nursed at the breast of kings; and you will know that I, the Lord, am your Savior, that your Redeemer is the Mighty One of Jacob.
In place of bronze I will bring gold; in place of iron, silver; in place of wood, bronze; in place of stones, iron. I will make peace your governor, righteousness your ruler.
No longer will violence be heard of in your land, nor ravage or ruin within your borders; you will call your walls Salvation, and your gates Praise.
The sun will no longer be your light by day, nor the moon give you its glow: the Lord will be for you an everlasting light, your God will be your splendor.
Your sun will no longer set, your moon will no longer wane, for the Lord will be for you an everlasting light, and your days of mourning will be ended.
In your people, all will be righteous, they will possess the land forever; they are the shoot that I have planted, the work of my hands, to display my glory.
The least will become a thousand, the weakest a mighty nation. I, the Lord, when the time comes, will hasten it all.

titres.titre: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me
The restoration and the priesthood of the people
The joyful song of the bride

versets.t: The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me, for the Lord has consecrated me by anointing. He has sent me to bring good news to the poor, to heal those who are brokenhearted, to announce release to the captives and freedom to the prisoners,
to proclaim a year of favor from the Lord, a day of vengeance from our God, to comfort all who mourn,

and to give to those who mourn in Zion a diadem in place of ashes, the oil of joy in place of mourning, festive garments in place of a downcast spirit. They will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the Lord for his glory.
They will rebuild the ancient ruins, they will raise up the rubble of the past, they will restore the ruined cities, devastated for generations.
Foreigners will be there to tend your flocks, the sons of the foreigner will be your plowmen and your vinedressers.
But you, you will be called priests of the Lord, you will be named ministers of our God. You will enjoy the riches of the nations, you will adorn yourselves with their glory.

In place of your shame, you will receive a double portion; in place of dishonor, you will cry out for joy over your heritage. So, in your land, you will have a double portion, and your joy will be everlasting.
For I, the Lord, love justice, I hate robbery and injustice; I will faithfully give them their reward, I will make with them an everlasting covenant.
Their offspring will be renowned among the nations, their descendants in the midst of the peoples; all who see them will acknowledge that they are an offspring blessed by the Lord.

I thrill with joy in the Lord, my soul exults in my God, for he has clothed me in the garments of salvation, he has wrapped me in the robe of righteousness, as the bridegroom crowns himself with a diadem, as the bride adorns herself with her jewels.
For, as the earth brings forth its shoots, as a garden makes its seeds spring up, so the Lord God will make righteousness and praise spring up before all the nations.

titres.titre: The watchmen who will not be silent

versets.t: For the sake of Zion I will not be silent; for the sake of Jerusalem I will have no rest, until her righteousness rises like the dawn, and her salvation like a burning torch.
The nations will see your righteousness, all the kings will see your glory, and you will be called by a new name that the mouth of the Lord will fix.
You will be a magnificent crown in the hand of the Lord, a royal diadem in the hand of your God.

No longer will you be called Forsaken, no longer will your land be called Devastated; but you will be called My-Delight-Is-in-Her, and your land, Espoused. For the Lord will take his delight in you, and your land will have a husband.
As a young man marries a young woman, so the one who rebuilds you will marry you; as the bride is the joy of the bridegroom, so you will be the joy of your God.
On your walls, Jerusalem, I have posted watchmen; never, by day or by night, will they be silent. You who call upon the Lord, grant yourselves no rest,
and give him no rest, until he restores Jerusalem and makes her the praise of all the earth.
The Lord has sworn by his right hand, by his mighty arm: Never again will I give your grain as food to your enemies, never again will foreigners drink the wine for which you have toiled.
Those who have harvested the grain will eat it, praising the Lord, those who have gathered the grapes will drink the wine in the courts of my sanctuary.
Pass through, pass through the gates! Prepare the way for the people! Build up, build up the road, remove the stones from it! Raise a banner for the peoples!
See what the Lord proclaims to the ends of the earth: Say to the daughter of Zion, "See, your Savior comes; his reward is with him, and the fruit of his work goes before him."
They will be called the Holy People, the Redeemed of the Lord; and you, you will be called the Sought-After, the City-Never-Forsaken.

titres.titre: The remembrance of the Lord's kindnesses
The memory of the Exodus and of Moses
The prayer: return, you are our father

versets.t: Who is this who comes from Edom, from Bozrah, in crimson garments? Magnificent in his robe, he strides forward in the fullness of his strength. It is I, who speak with righteousness, I, the mighty one who saves.
Why this red on your robe, these garments stained like those who tread the winepress?
I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the peoples not one was with me. I trod them in my anger, trampled them in my fury; their juice spurted on my garments, and I stained all my robe.
For a day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my deliverance had come.
I looked: no one to help; I was astounded: no one to sustain me. Then my own arm brought me salvation, and my fury sustained me.
I crushed the peoples in my anger, I made them drunk with my fury, I poured out their blood on the ground.

I will recall the faithful love of the Lord, the praises of the Lord, for all that he has done for us, for the immense love he has shown to the house of Israel in his tenderness and the richness of his faithful love.
He had said, "Truly, they are my people, children who will not deceive me." And he became for them a savior.

In all their distress, he himself was in distress, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and his pity, it was he who redeemed them; he lifted them up, he carried them, all through the days of old.
But they rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit; then he turned against them as an enemy, he himself made war on them.
Then his people remembered the days of old, of Moses: Where is the one who brought them up from the sea with the shepherd of his flock? Where is the one who put his Holy Spirit in their midst,
who made his glorious arm march at the right hand of Moses, who split the waters before them to make himself an everlasting name,
who led them through the depths, sure as a horse in the open desert, without ever stumbling?
Like the flock that goes down into the valley, the Spirit of the Lord led them to rest. So you led your people, to make yourself a glorious name.
Look down from heaven, see, from your holy and magnificent dwelling: where are your jealous love and your power? Your stirred heart, your tenderness toward me, have they then held back?
For you are our father. Abraham does not know us, Israel does not acknowledge us; but you, Lord, you are our father, our Redeemer: that is your name from all time.
Why, Lord, do you let us stray far from your ways, why do you harden our heart so that we no longer fear you? Return, for the love of your servants, of the tribes that are your heritage!
For but a little while, your holy people possessed the land; and now our enemies have trampled your sanctuary.

For a long time we have been like a people over whom you do not reign, who do not bear your name. Ah, if only you would tear open the heavens, if only you would come down, the mountains would melt away before you!

titres.titre: The plea: come down, O God
You are our father, we are the clay

versets.t: like a fire that sets dry wood ablaze, like a fire that makes water boil, to make your name known to your adversaries, so that the nations tremble before you,
by working wonders we did not expect! You would come down, and the mountains would quake before you!
Never has it been heard, never learned, no eye has seen a God other than you act thus for the one who hopes in him.

You come to meet the one who joyfully practices righteousness, the one who remembers you by following your ways. But see, you were angry, for we sinned; for a long time we have been in our faults: will we be saved?
We had all become like unclean beings, and all our good deeds were like a soiled cloth; we all withered like the leaf, and our faults carried us off like the wind.
No one called upon your name, no one roused himself to hold fast to you; for you had hidden your face from us, you let us melt under the weight of our faults.
And yet, Lord, you are our father; we are the clay, and you the potter: we are all the work of your hand.
Do not be angry beyond measure, Lord, do not remember our faults forever; look, then: we are all your people!
Your holy cities have become a desert; Zion is a desert, Jerusalem a ruin.
Our holy and magnificent house, where our fathers praised you, has been given over to the flames, and all that was dear to us is nothing but rubble.
Before all this, Lord, will you hold back? Will you keep silent and afflict us beyond measure?

titres.titre: The remnant saved, the rebels punished
The fate of the servants and of the rebels
New heavens and a new earth

versets.t: I let myself be consulted by those who asked nothing, be found by those who did not seek me. I said, "Here I am! Here I am!" to a nation that did not call upon my name.
All day long I stretched out my hands to a rebellious people, who follow an evil way after their own devices,
a people who, endlessly, provoke me to my face: they sacrifice in the gardens, burn incense on bricks,
settle in the tombs, spend the night in hidden places, eat the flesh of pigs and fill their dishes with unclean food,
and say, "Keep your distance, do not come near me, for I am too holy for you!" These people are a smoke in my nostrils, a fire that burns without ceasing.
See, it is written before me: I will not be silent until I have repaid them their due, poured it out into their very lap,
your faults and those of your fathers together, says the Lord; they who burned incense on the mountains and insulted me on the hills, I will first measure out to them the wages of their past conduct.
Thus says the Lord: When juice is found in a cluster, people say, "Do not destroy it, there is a blessing in it." So I will do for my servants: I will not destroy them all.
From Jacob I will bring forth offspring, and from Judah an heir of my mountains; my chosen ones will possess them, my servants will dwell there.
Sharon will become a pasture for the sheep, the valley of Achor a fold for the cattle, for the benefit of my people, of those who will have sought me.
But you who forsake the Lord, who forget my holy mountain, who set a table for Gad, the god of Fortune, and fill a cup for Meni, the god of Destiny,

I destine you to the sword, you will all bow down to be slaughtered. For I called, and you did not answer; I spoke, and you did not listen; you did what is evil in my eyes, you chose what displeases me.
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: See, my servants will eat, and you will go hungry; my servants will drink, and you will go thirsty; my servants will rejoice, and you will be put to shame;
my servants will sing, their hearts glad, and you will cry out, your hearts grieved, you will wail, your spirits broken.
You will leave your name as a curse to my chosen ones: "May the Lord God put you to death like this!" But his servants he will call by another name.

Whoever wishes to be blessed in the land will bless himself by the God of truth, and whoever takes an oath in the land will swear by the God of truth; for the anguish of former times will be forgotten, hidden from my eyes.
See: I create new heavens and a new earth; the past will be remembered no more, it will rise no longer to the heart.
Rejoice, rather, exult forever in what I am about to create; for see, I create Jerusalem for joy, and her people for gladness.
I will exult over Jerusalem, I will rejoice over my people; no longer will the sound of weeping be heard there, nor the cry of anguish.

No longer will there be a child carried off after a few days, nor an old man who does not live out his years; to die at a hundred will be to die young, and the sinner will be cursed only at a hundred.
They will build houses and live in them, they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
They will not build for another to live in, they will not plant for another to eat; for the days of my people will equal those of the trees, and my chosen ones will enjoy the work of their hands.
They will no longer labor in vain, they will no longer bear children for terror; for they are an offspring blessed by the Lord, they and their descendants with them.
Before they call, I will answer; they will still be speaking when I have already heard them.
The wolf and the lamb will graze together, the lion will eat straw like the ox, and the serpent will feed on dust. No longer will they do evil or ravage on all my holy mountain, says the Lord.

titres.titre: True worship: the humble and the broken heart
The city that gives birth all at once

versets.t: Thus says the Lord: Heaven is my throne, the earth the footstool of my feet. What house could you build me, what place for my rest?
All this my hand has made, and all this exists, oracle of the Lord. This is the one to whom I look: the humble, the one who has a broken heart and who trembles at my word.

But whoever slaughters an ox also kills a man; whoever sacrifices a sheep strangles a dog; whoever presents an offering offers pig's blood; whoever burns incense as a memorial blesses an idol. Since they have chosen their own ways and delight in their abominations,

I too will choose to deal harshly with them, I will bring upon them what they dread; for I called, and no one answered, I spoke, and they did not listen; they did what is evil in my eyes, they chose what displeases me.

Listen to the word of the Lord, you who tremble at his word: Your brothers who hate you and reject you because of my name have said, "Let the Lord show his glory, that we may see your joy!" But it is they who will be covered with shame.
An uproar rises from the city, a clamor rises from the Temple: it is the voice of the Lord repaying his enemies what they deserve.
Before going into labor, she gave birth; before the pangs came upon her, she brought a boy into the world.
Who has ever heard such a thing, who has ever seen anything like it? Is a land born in a single day? Does a nation come into the world all at once? Yet scarcely in labor, Zion gave birth to her sons!
Would I open the womb and not bring to birth? says the Lord. I who bring to birth, would I close the womb? says your God.
Rejoice with Jerusalem, exult over her, all you who love her! Share her overflowing joy, all you who bore her mourning,
that you may nurse to your fill at her comforting breast, that you may savor with delight the abundance of her glory!
For thus says the Lord: See, I will make peace flow toward her like a river, and the wealth of the nations like an overflowing torrent; you will be nursed, carried on the hip, dandled on the knees.
As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you; it is in Jerusalem that you will be comforted.
At the sight of this, your heart will rejoice, your limbs will regain vigor like fresh grass. The hand of the Lord will make itself known to his servants, but his anger to his enemies.
For see the Lord coming in fire, his chariots like the whirlwind, to pour out his anger in a blaze, his threats in flames of fire.
Yes, by fire and by the sword, the Lord will do justice on all flesh, and many will be those whom the Lord has struck down.

Those who sanctify and purify themselves to enter the gardens, following the one who stands at the center, those who eat pig's flesh, loathsome creatures, and mice, all together they will perish, oracle of the Lord.
I know their deeds and their thoughts. The time is coming to gather all the nations and all the tongues: they will come and see my glory.

I will set a sign among them, and I will send some survivors to the nations, to Tarshish, to Put and to Lud, those peoples of archers, to Tubal and to Javan, to the distant coastlands that have never heard of me and have not seen my glory: they will proclaim my glory among the nations.

They will bring back all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the Lord, on horses, chariots, litters, mules, and dromedaries, to my holy mountain, to Jerusalem, says the Lord, as the sons of Israel bring their offering in a clean vessel to the house of the Lord.
And from among them too I will take some for priests and for Levites, says the Lord.
For, just as the new heavens and the new earth that I am about to create will endure before me, oracle of the Lord, so will your offspring and your name endure.
At each new moon, at each sabbath, all flesh will come to bow down before me, says the Lord.
And when they go out, they will see the corpses of those who rebelled against me: their worm will not die, their fire will not go out, and they will be a horror to all flesh.

titres.titre: Two Visions: The Almond Branch and the Boiling Pot

versets.t: The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who lived at Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin.
The word of the Lord came to him in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign,

and again in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, down to the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the exile of Jerusalem in the fifth month (about July to August).
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Before I formed you in the womb I knew you; before you came out of it I set you apart: I am making you a prophet to the nations."
I answered, "Ah, Lord God, I do not know how to speak, I am only a child!"
But the Lord said to me, "Do not say, 'I am only a child.' You will go to everyone I send you to, and you will say everything I command you.
Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to rescue you, oracle of the Lord."
Then the Lord reached out his hand, touched my mouth, and said to me, "Now I have put my words in your mouth.
See, today I set you over the nations and over the kingdoms, to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and to demolish, to build and to plant."
The word of the Lord came to me: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I answered, "I see a branch of the almond tree, the tree that keeps watch."
The Lord said to me, "You have seen well, for I am watching over my word to carry it out."
The word of the Lord came to me a second time: "What do you see?" I answered, "I see a boiling pot, and it is tilting from the north."
The Lord said to me, "From the north disaster will break loose upon all who live in the land.

For I am now calling all the peoples of the northern kingdoms, oracle of the Lord. They will come, and each will set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, against all its surrounding walls and against all the towns of Judah.
I will pronounce my judgments against them for all their wickedness: they have abandoned me, they have burned incense to other gods and bowed down before the work of their own hands.
So you, gird your loins, stand up, and tell them everything I command you. Do not be shattered before them, or I will shatter you before them.
Today I make you a fortified city, an iron pillar, a wall of bronze, against the whole land, against the kings of Judah, its officials, its priests, and the people.
They will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, for I am with you to rescue you, oracle of the Lord."

titres.titre: The Betrayed Love of the Betrothal
A People Who Think Themselves Innocent

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:

Go and cry out in the hearing of Jerusalem: Thus says the Lord: I remember the devotion of your youth, your love as a young bride, when you followed me through the wilderness, through a land that is never sown.
Israel was a holy portion for the Lord, the first fruits of his harvest; all who fed on it became guilty, and disaster fell upon them, oracle of the Lord.
Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob, and all you families of the house of Israel!
Thus says the Lord: What wrong did your fathers find in me, that they went so far from me, chasing after emptiness until they themselves became empty?

They did not ask, "Where is the Lord, who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, that parched and gullied land, a land of drought and deathly shadow, which no one crosses and where no one lives?"
I brought you into a land of orchards, to eat its fruits and its good things; but once you had entered, you defiled my land and made my inheritance an abomination.

The priests did not ask, "Where is the Lord?" Those who handle the law did not know me, the shepherds rebelled against me, and the prophets prophesied by Baal and chased after gods that are powerless.
Therefore I will bring my case against you again, oracle of the Lord, and against your children's children.
Cross over to the coasts of Kittim and look, send to Kedar and observe closely: see whether anything like this has ever happened.
Does a nation change its gods? And these are not even gods! Yet my people have traded their glory for what is worthless.
Be appalled at this, O heavens, shudder with horror, be utterly aghast, oracle of the Lord.
For my people have committed two crimes: they have abandoned me, the spring of living water, to dig themselves cisterns, cracked cisterns that hold no water.
Is Israel a slave, a servant born in the house? Why then has he been handed over to plunder?
Against him the lions roar, they raise their cry; they have reduced his land to a wasteland, his towns burned down and left without inhabitants.
Even the men of Memphis and Tahpanhes shave your head.
Have you not brought this on yourself by abandoning the Lord your God, when he was leading you along the way?
And now, what will you gain on the road to Egypt, going to drink the waters of the Nile? What will you gain on the road to Assyria, going to drink the waters of the River?

Your own wickedness will punish you, your faithlessness will chastise you. Know it and see how evil and bitter it is to have abandoned the Lord your God, with no reverence for me, oracle of the Lord, the God of hosts.
Long ago you broke your yoke and snapped your bonds, and you said, "I will not serve!" And on every high hill, under every green tree, you lay down like a prostitute.
I had planted you as a choice vine, all of it from sound stock. How did you turn against me into the wild shoots of a foreign vine?
Though you scrub yourself with lye and use much soap, the stain of your guilt remains before me, oracle of the Lord God.
How dare you say, "I am not defiled, I have not chased after the Baals"? Look at your tracks in the Valley, acknowledge what you have done: a restless young camel running this way and that,
a wild donkey at home in the desert, sniffing the wind in her burning desire; who can restrain her heat? Those who seek her need not tire themselves: at mating time they will find her.
Keep your feet from going bare and your throat from going dry! But you say, "It is no use! I love strangers, and after them I will go."
As a thief is disgraced when he is caught, so the house of Israel will be disgraced, they, their kings, their officials, their priests, and their prophets,

who say to a piece of wood, "You are my father," and to a stone, "You gave me birth." They have turned their backs to me and not their faces; but in the day of disaster they cry, "Rise up and save us!"
Where are they, the gods you made for yourself? Let them rise up, if they can save you in the day of disaster! For you have as many gods as you have towns, Judah.
Why do you bring a case against me? You have all rebelled against me, oracle of the Lord.
In vain I struck your sons: they learned nothing from it. Your own sword devoured your prophets like a ravaging lion.
You of this generation, consider the word of the Lord: Have I been a wilderness to Israel, a land of deep darkness? Why then do my people say, "We are free to roam, we will come to you no more"?
Does a young woman forget her jewelry, a bride her sash? Yet my people have forgotten me for days without number.
How skilled you are at marking out your way to seek love! You have even taught your ways to the worst of women.
On the hem of your garments is found the blood of the innocent poor, whom you did not even catch breaking in. Yet in spite of all this,
you say, "I am innocent; surely his anger has turned away from me." Now I will bring you to judgment, because you say, "I have not sinned."
How lightly you go about changing your course! Egypt will shame you as Assyria has already shamed you.
From there too you will come away with your hands on your head, for the Lord has rejected those in whom you trust: you will have no success with them.

There is a saying: if a man divorces his wife, and she leaves him and becomes another man's wife, will he go back to her again? Would not that land be utterly defiled? Now you have prostituted yourself with many lovers, and you would return to me? oracle of the Lord.

Lift up your eyes to the bare heights and look: where have you not let yourself be defiled? By the roadsides you sat waiting for them, like a nomad in the desert, and you have defiled the land with your prostitution and your wickedness.
So the showers were withheld, and the spring rains failed. But you had the forehead of a prostitute, you refused to blush.
And now, do you not call to me, "My father, friend of my youth!
Will he keep his anger forever? Will he hold on to it without end?" This is what you say, while doing all the evil you can.

In the days of King Josiah the Lord said to me: Have you seen what unfaithful Israel has done? She has gone up on every high mountain and under every green tree, and there she has prostituted herself.
I said to myself: After she has done all this, she will return to me. But she did not return; and her sister, treacherous Judah, saw it.

She saw that I had divorced faithless Israel for all her adulteries and had given her a certificate of divorce; yet her sister, treacherous Judah, was not afraid: she too went and prostituted herself.
Through her blatant immorality she defiled the land, committing adultery with wood and stone.
And in spite of all this, her sister, treacherous Judah, did not return to me with all her heart, but only in pretense, oracle of the Lord.
The Lord said to me: Faithless Israel has shown herself more upright than treacherous Judah.

Go and proclaim these words toward the north; say: Return, faithless Israel, oracle of the Lord. I will not look on you in anger, for I am faithful, oracle of the Lord, and I do not hold my anger forever.
Only acknowledge your guilt: you rebelled against the Lord your God, you scattered your ways among strangers under every green tree, and you did not listen to my voice, oracle of the Lord.
Return, faithless children, oracle of the Lord, for I am your master. I will take you, one from a town and two from a family, and bring you to Zion.
I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will lead you with understanding and wisdom.

In those days, when you have become many and fruitful in the land, oracle of the Lord, people will no longer say, "the ark of the covenant of the Lord." It will no longer come to mind; no one will remember it, or miss it, or make another.

At that time Jerusalem will be called "the throne of the Lord." All the nations will gather there, in the name of the Lord, to Jerusalem, and they will no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.
In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel; together they will come from the land of the north to the land I gave your fathers as their inheritance.

I said to myself: How I would love to count you among my sons and give you a land of delights, the fairest jewel of the nations! I said: You will call me "My father," and you will never stop following me.
But as a woman betrays her partner, so you have betrayed me, house of Israel, oracle of the Lord.
On the bare heights a cry is heard: the pleading weeping of the sons of Israel, for they have twisted their way and forgotten the Lord their God.
Return, faithless children, and I will heal your faithlessness. "Here we are, we come to you, for you are the Lord our God.
Yes, the hills and the tumult on the mountains are a lie! Yes, it is in the Lord our God that the salvation of Israel is found.
From our youth that shameful thing has devoured the fruit of our fathers' labor, their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.

Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us! For we have sinned against the Lord our God, we and our fathers, from our youth to this day, and we have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God."

titres.titre: The Prophet's Anguish and the Chaos

versets.t: If you will return, Israel, oracle of the Lord, it is to me that you must return. If you put away your detestable idols out of my sight and no longer wander,
and if you swear "As the Lord lives!" in truth, in uprightness, and in justice, then the nations will call themselves blessed in him, and in him they will glory.
For thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and of Jerusalem: Break up your fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns.

Circumcise yourselves for the Lord, remove the foreskin of your hearts, men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, lest my anger break out like fire and burn with no one to quench it, because of the wickedness of your deeds.
Announce it in Judah, proclaim it in Jerusalem, sound the trumpet throughout the land, cry aloud: Gather together, let us flee to the fortified cities!
Raise a signal toward Zion, flee without delay! For from the north I am bringing disaster, a great destruction.
A lion has come up from his thicket, the destroyer of nations is on the march; he has left his lair to make your land a wasteland: your towns will be ruined, emptied of their inhabitants.
Put on sackcloth, mourn and wail, for the burning anger of the Lord has not turned away from us.
On that day, oracle of the Lord, the courage of the king and the officials will fail, the priests will be appalled and the prophets aghast.
Then I said, Ah, Lord God, how you have deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, "You will have peace," while the sword is at our throat!

At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: A scorching wind from the bare heights of the desert blows toward the daughter of my people, but not for winnowing or cleansing the grain.
A wind too strong for that comes at my bidding. Now I myself will pronounce their sentence.
Look, he comes up like the clouds; his chariots are like the storm, his horses swifter than eagles. Woe to us, we are ruined!
Wash the evil from your heart, Jerusalem, that you may be saved. How long will you keep your wicked thoughts deep within you?
A voice from Dan brings the news; from the hills of Ephraim it proclaims disaster.
Make it known to the nations, proclaim it against Jerusalem: besiegers are coming from a distant land, hurling their cries against the towns of Judah.
Like those who guard a field, they surround Jerusalem, for she has rebelled against me, oracle of the Lord.
This is what your ways and your deeds have brought upon you. This is the fruit of your wickedness: it is bitter, it reaches to your very heart.
My anguish, my anguish! I writhe in pain! The walls of my heart, my heart pounds, I cannot keep silent, for I hear the sound of the trumpet, the battle cry.
Ruin upon ruin is announced: the whole land is laid waste. In an instant my tents are destroyed, in a moment my shelters.
How long must I see the signal, hear the sound of the trumpet?
For my people are foolish: they do not know me. They are senseless children, without understanding: skilled in doing evil, they do not know how to do good.
I look at the earth: it is formless and empty; at the heavens: their light is gone.
I look at the mountains: they are quaking, and all the hills sway.
I look: there is no one left, and all the birds of the sky have fled.
I look: the orchard has become a desert, all its towns are torn down before the Lord, before the heat of his anger.
For thus says the Lord: The whole land will be ruin, though I will not make an end of it altogether.
Because of this the earth mourns and the heavens above grow dark, for I have spoken and decided: I will not relent, I will not turn back.
At the noise of horsemen and archers, the whole town takes flight; they hide in the woods, they climb up the rocks. Every town is abandoned, no one lives in them.

And you, devastated one, what will you do? Though you dress in purple, deck yourself with gold jewelry, and enlarge your eyes with paint, in vain you make yourself beautiful: your lovers despise you, it is your life they are after.

I hear a cry like that of a woman in labor, the anguish of a mother giving birth for the first time: it is the voice of the daughter of Zion, gasping for breath, stretching out her hands: "Woe is me! I faint before the killers."

titres.titre: Searching for One Just Man in Jerusalem
The Wicked and the False Prophets

versets.t: Roam the streets of Jerusalem, look, inquire, search its squares: can you find a single person who does justice and seeks faithfulness? Then I will pardon the city.
Even when they say "As the Lord lives!" it is a false oath they swear.
Lord, do your eyes not look for faithfulness? You struck them, but they felt no pain; you crushed them, but they refused correction. They made their faces harder than rock, they refused to return.
I said to myself: These are only the poor; they act like fools, for they do not know the way of the Lord or the law of their God.
I will go, then, to the great and speak to them, for they know the way of the Lord, the law of their God. But they too, all together, have broken the yoke and snapped the bonds.

Therefore the lion from the forest strikes them, the wolf from the desert ravages them, the panther lies in wait by their towns: whoever comes out is torn apart. For their rebellions are many, their acts of faithlessness have multiplied.
Why should I pardon you? Your sons have abandoned me, they swear by what is not God. I gave them their fill, and they became adulterers; they crowd to the house of the prostitute.
Well-fed, roaming stallions, each neighing after his neighbor's wife.
Should I not punish them for this? oracle of the Lord. On a nation like this, should I not take my revenge?
Climb up her vine terraces and ravage them, but do not destroy completely; strip away her branches, for they do not belong to the Lord.
For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have been utterly unfaithful to me, oracle of the Lord.
They have denied the Lord, they have said, "He is nothing! Disaster will not come upon us, we will see neither sword nor famine.
The prophets are only wind, the word is not in them: let what they announce fall on themselves!"
Therefore, thus says the Lord, the God of hosts: Because you speak this way, I am now making my words in your mouth a fire, and this people the wood that the fire will devour.
I am bringing against you a nation from afar, house of Israel, oracle of the Lord: a mighty nation, an ancient nation, a nation whose language you do not know and whose speech you do not understand.
Its quiver is an open grave; they are all warriors.

It will devour your harvest and your bread, it will devour your sons and your daughters, it will devour your flocks and your herds, it will devour your vine and your fig tree. With the sword it will beat down the fortified cities in which you trust.
Yet even in those days, oracle of the Lord, I will not make an end of you altogether.

And when you ask, "Why has the Lord our God done all this to us?" you will answer them, "As you abandoned me to serve foreign gods in your own land, so you will serve strangers in a land that is not yours."
Announce this in the house of Jacob, proclaim it in Judah:
Hear this, foolish and senseless people, who have eyes but do not see, ears but do not hear!

Will you not fear me? oracle of the Lord. Will you not tremble before me, who set the sand as a boundary for the sea, an everlasting barrier it cannot cross? Its waves may toss, but they are powerless; they may roar, but they do not go beyond it.
But this people have a stubborn and rebellious heart; they have turned aside and gone their way.
They did not say in their hearts, "Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives the rain, the autumn rain and the spring rain, in their season, and keeps for us the appointed weeks of harvest."
Your wrongs have upset this order, your sins have deprived you of these good things.
For among my people there are wicked men: lurking, crouching like fowlers, they set traps and catch people.
Like a cage full of birds, their houses are full of fraud; so they have become great and rich,
fat and sleek. They overflow with wickedness: they give no justice, they do not defend the cause of the orphan, yet they prosper; they do not uphold the rights of the poor.
Should I not punish this? oracle of the Lord. On a nation like this, should I not take my revenge?
Something appalling and horrible is happening in the land:
the prophets prophesy falsehood, the priests rule in league with them, and my people love it that way! But what will you do when the end comes?

titres.titre: A People Who Refuse to Listen

versets.t: Flee, sons of Benjamin, from the midst of Jerusalem! Sound the trumpet in Tekoa, raise a signal over Beth-haccherem! For from the north disaster looms, a great destruction.
The lovely and delicate one, the daughter of Zion, I am destroying her.
Shepherds come to her with their flocks; they pitch their tents all around, each grazing his own portion.
Prepare for battle against her: up! let us attack at noon! Woe to us, the day is fading, the evening shadows are lengthening.
Up! let us attack by night, let us destroy her palaces!
For thus says the Lord of hosts: Cut down her trees, throw up a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This is the city that must be punished: there is nothing in her but oppression.
As a well makes its water gush out, so she makes her wickedness gush out. Violence and ruin are all that is heard in her; her wounds and sores are constantly before my eyes.
Take correction, Jerusalem, or I will turn away from you, I will make you a wasteland, an uninhabited land.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: They will glean thoroughly, like a vine, the remnant of Israel; pass your hand again over the branches, like a grape gatherer.
To whom can I speak, whom can I warn so that they will listen? Their ears are uncircumcised, unable to hear. The word of the Lord has become an insult to them, they take no pleasure in it.

I am full of the anger of the Lord, I am weary of holding it in. Pour it out on the child in the street, on the young men gathered together! For all will be taken, husband and wife alike, the old man along with the man weighed down with years.
Their houses will pass to others, along with their fields and their wives, for I am stretching out my hand against the inhabitants of the land, oracle of the Lord.
From the least to the greatest, all are greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, all practice deceit.
They dress the wound of the daughter of my people lightly, saying, "Peace, peace!" when there is no peace.

They should be ashamed of their detestable deeds, but they no longer know how to blush, they know nothing of shame. Therefore they will fall among those who fall; on the day I punish them, they will stumble, says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord: Stand at the crossroads and look, ask about the ancient paths: where is the way of good? Walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they answered, "We will not walk in it."
I posted sentinels near you: "Pay attention to the sound of the trumpet!" But they answered, "We will pay no attention."
Therefore hear, O nations, and know, O assembly of the peoples, what is going to happen to them.
Hear, O earth: I am bringing disaster on this people, the fruit of their own scheming, for they have paid no attention to my words and have rejected my law.
What is the incense from Sheba to me, the fragrant cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings do not please me, your sacrifices are not pleasing to me.
Therefore, thus says the Lord: I am placing obstacles before this people; they will stumble over them, fathers and sons together, neighbor and friend will perish.
Thus says the Lord: A people is coming from the land of the north, a great nation rising from the ends of the earth.
They grasp the bow and the javelin; they are cruel and merciless; their voice roars like the sea; they ride on horses, drawn up as one man for battle, against you, daughter of Zion.
At the news of their approach, our hands have gone limp, anguish has seized us, pain like that of a woman in labor.
Do not go out into the fields, do not walk on the roads, for the enemy holds the sword: terror is on every side.
Daughter of my people, put on sackcloth, roll in ashes, mourn as for an only son, weep bitterly, for suddenly the destroyer is upon us.
I have set you among my people as an assayer who tests metals, so that you may observe and examine their conduct.
They are all hardened rebels, spreaders of slander; they are bronze and iron, all of them corrupt.
The bellows have blown, but the lead stays intact in the fire; smelt and smelt again, the wicked are not separated out.
They will be called "rejected silver," for the Lord has rejected them.

titres.titre: Topheth and the Valley of Slaughter

versets.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord:
Stand at the gate of the house of the Lord and proclaim this word there: Hear the word of the Lord, all you men of Judah who enter these gates to bow down before the Lord.
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Amend your ways and your deeds, and I will let you live in this place.
Do not trust the lying words of those who repeat, "This is the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord!"
For if you truly amend your ways and your deeds, if you truly do justice between one man and his neighbor,
if you do not oppress the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow, if you do not shed innocent blood in this place, if you do not chase after other gods to your own ruin,
then I will let you live in this place, in the land I gave your fathers for all time.
But look, you are trusting in lying words that are of no use to you.
What! Steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal, chase after other gods you do not know,
then come and stand before me in this house that bears my name and say, "We are safe!" only to go on with all these abominations?
In your eyes, has this house that bears my name become a den of robbers? I too have seen it well, oracle of the Lord.
Go now to my dwelling at Shiloh, where I first made my name dwell, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel.
And now, because you have done all these things, oracle of the Lord, because I spoke to you again and again and you did not listen, because I called you and you did not answer,
I will do to this house that bears my name, in which you put your trust, this place I gave to you and your fathers, as I did to Shiloh.
I will cast you away from me, as I cast away all your brothers, all the offspring of Ephraim.
As for you, do not intercede for this people, raise for them neither cry nor prayer, do not press me, for I will not listen to you.
Do you not see what they are doing in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem?
The children gather wood, the fathers light the fire, the women knead the dough to make cakes for the queen of heaven; and they pour out drink offerings to other gods, to provoke me.
Is it me they provoke? oracle of the Lord. Is it not themselves, to their own shame?
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: My anger and my fury are about to pour out on this place, on man and beast, on the trees of the field and the fruit of the ground; it will burn and not be quenched.
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices, and eat the meat yourselves!
For on the day I brought your fathers out of the land of Egypt, I said nothing to them, gave them no command about burnt offerings and sacrifices.
This, rather, is the command I gave them: Listen to my voice, and I will be your God, and you will be my people; walk in all the ways I command you, and it will be well with you.
But they did not listen, they did not incline their ear; they followed their own schemes, the stubbornness of their evil hearts; they went backward and not forward.
From the day your fathers came out of Egypt until today, I have sent you all my servants the prophets, day after day, again and again.
But they did not listen to me, they did not incline their ear; they stiffened their necks, they did worse than their fathers.
You will tell them all this, and they will not listen to you; you will call them, and they will not answer you.
Then you will say to them: This is the nation that did not listen to the voice of the Lord its God, that would not accept correction. Faithfulness has perished, it has vanished from their lips.
Cut off your hair and throw it away, raise a lament on the bare heights, for the Lord has rejected and cast off the generation that provokes his anger.
The sons of Judah have done what is evil in my sight, oracle of the Lord: they have set up their detestable idols in the house that bears my name, to defile it.
They have built the high places of Topheth, in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to burn their sons and daughters in the fire, which I never commanded and which never even entered my mind.

Therefore, the days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when it will no longer be called "Topheth" or "the Valley of Ben-hinnom," but "the Valley of Slaughter"; and they will bury in Topheth for lack of room elsewhere.
The corpses of this people will become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth, with no one to frighten them away.
In the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem I will silence the sounds of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the bride, for the land will have become a wasteland.
At that time, oracle of the Lord, the bones of the kings of Judah, of its officials, of the priests, of the prophets, and of the inhabitants of Jerusalem will be brought out of their graves.

They will be spread out before the sun, the moon, and all the host of heaven, those stars they loved, served, followed, consulted, and worshiped. They will not be gathered up or buried: they will become dung on the ground.
And all the survivors of this evil race will prefer death to life, in every place where I have driven them, oracle of the Lord of hosts.
You will say to them: Thus says the Lord: When people fall, do they not get up again? When they go astray, do they not turn back?
Why then does this people of Jerusalem go astray without end? They cling to falsehood, they refuse to return.
I have paid attention, I have listened: they do not speak rightly; no one repents of his wickedness and says, "What have I done?" Every one resumes his course, like a horse charging into battle.
Even the stork in the sky knows her seasons; the turtledove, the swallow, and the crane observe the time of their return; but my people do not know the law of the Lord.
How can you say, "We are wise, the law of the Lord is with us," when the lying pen of the scribes has turned it into a lie?
The wise will be put to shame, dismayed and trapped. They have rejected the word of the Lord: what wisdom is left to them?
Therefore I will give their wives to others, their fields to new owners. For from the least to the greatest, all are greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, all practice deceit.
They dress the wound of the daughter of my people lightly, saying, "Peace, peace!" when there is no peace.

They should be ashamed of their detestable deeds, but they no longer know how to blush, they know nothing of shame. Therefore they will fall among those who fall; on the day I punish them, they will collapse, says the Lord.
I will sweep them away completely, oracle of the Lord: no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree, and even the leaves are withered; what I gave them will slip away from them.

"Why are we sitting here? Gather together, let us flee to the fortified cities and perish there! For the Lord our God is making us perish, he is giving us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against him.
We waited for peace: nothing good comes; for the time of healing: only terror!"
From Dan is heard the snorting of his horses; at the neighing of his stallions, the whole earth trembles. They come, they devour the land and its riches, the town and its inhabitants.
I am sending against you serpents, vipers that no charm can soothe: they will bite you, oracle of the Lord.
There is no more cure for my grief, my heart faints within me.

Listen, the cry of distress of the daughter of my people rises from a distant land: "Is the Lord no longer in Zion? Is her king no longer there?" Why have they provoked me with their idols, with these foreign nothings?
"The harvest is past, the summer is over, and we are not saved!"
I am broken by the wound of the daughter of my people, I am in mourning, horror has seized me.
Is there no more balm in Gilead, no physician there? Why then does the wound of the daughter of my people not heal?
Who will turn my head into a spring of water, my eyes into a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people?

titres.titre: The Mourning Women and the True Ground for Boasting

versets.t: Who will give me a traveler's lodging in the desert? I would abandon my people, I would go far away from them! For they are all adulterers, a band of traitors.
They bend their tongues like a bow; it is falsehood, not truth, that rules in the land. They go from evil to evil, and me, they do not know, oracle of the Lord.
Let each be on guard against his friend, and trust no brother: for every brother does nothing but supplant, and every friend spreads slander.
They deceive one another, they do not tell the truth; they have trained their tongues to lie, they wear themselves out doing wrong.
You live in the midst of bad faith; out of bad faith they refuse to know me, oracle of the Lord.
Therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts: I am going to put them in the furnace and test them. What else can I do in the face of the daughter of my people?
Their tongue is a deadly arrow, it speaks only lies; with the mouth one wishes peace to his neighbor, and in his heart he sets a trap for him.
Should I not punish them for this? oracle of the Lord. On a nation like this, should I not take my revenge?

On the mountains I raise a wailing and a lament; over the pastures of the desert, a song of mourning, for they are burned up, no one passes through them anymore, the cry of the flocks is heard no more. From the birds of the sky to the cattle, all have fled, all have vanished.
I will make Jerusalem a heap of stones, a lair of jackals; I will make the towns of Judah a desolation, without inhabitants.
