Who is the wise man who will understand this? To whom has the mouth of the Lord spoken, that he may declare it? Why is the land ruined, burned up like the desert that no one crosses?
The Lord answers: It is because they abandoned my law, which I set before them, because they did not listen to my voice or follow it.
They followed the stubbornness of their hearts and chased after the Baals, as their fathers had taught them.
Therefore, thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I am going to feed this people wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink.
I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send the sword after them until I have destroyed them.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: Call the mourning women, let them come! Send for the most skilled, let them come!
Let them quickly raise a lament over us, that our eyes may run with tears and our eyelids stream with water.
For a lament rises from Zion: "How devastated we are, covered with shame! We must leave the land, for our houses have been torn down."
Women, hear the word of the Lord, let your ear receive the word of his mouth. Teach your daughters a lament, each one her neighbor a song of mourning.
For death has climbed in through our windows, it has entered our palaces, to cut off the child in the street and the young men in the squares.
Say: Thus says the Lord: The corpses will fall like dung on the fields, like sheaves behind the reaper, with no one to gather them.
Thus says the Lord: Let not the wise boast in his wisdom, let not the strong boast in his strength, let not the rich boast in his riches.

But let the one who would boast, boast in this: that he has the understanding to know me, the Lord, who acts with faithful love, justice, and righteousness on the earth. Yes, in this I take delight, oracle of the Lord.
The days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when I will punish everyone circumcised in the flesh but not in the heart:
Egypt, Judah, Edom, the sons of Ammon, Moab, and all who shave their temples and live in the desert. For all these nations are uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.

titres.titre: The Idols and the Living God

versets.t: Hear the word the Lord speaks to you, house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord: Do not learn the ways of the nations, do not be terrified by the signs in the sky, even though the nations are terrified by them.
For the customs of the peoples are nothing but wind: a tree is cut down in the forest, the craftsman's hand works it with the chisel,
it is decorated with silver and gold, fastened with hammer and nails so that it will not totter.
Such gods are like a scarecrow in a cucumber field: they cannot speak, they must be carried, for they cannot walk. Do not be afraid of them: they can do no harm, but neither can they do any good.
There is none like you, Lord: you are great, and great is your name in its power.
Who would not fear you, King of the nations? This fear is indeed your due. For among all the wise of the nations and in all their kingdoms, there is none like you.
They are all, together, stupid and foolish: what they teach is worthless, it is nothing but wood.
Hammered silver brought from Tarshish, gold from Uphaz, the work of the sculptor and the hands of the goldsmith; they are clothed in violet and red: all of it is the work of artisans.
But the Lord is the true God; he is the living God, the eternal King. At his anger the earth trembles, and the nations cannot withstand his fury.
This is what you will say to them: "The gods who did not make the heavens and the earth will vanish from the earth and from under the heavens."
He, by his power, made the earth; by his wisdom he established the world; by his understanding he stretched out the heavens.
At his voice the waters gather in the sky; he makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth, he sends the lightning with the rain, he brings out the wind from his storehouses.
Everyone is stupid, without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idol, for his metal image is a lie: there is no breath in it.
It is nothing but wind, a work of mockery; on the day of reckoning it will vanish.
The portion of Jacob is not like these: he formed all things, and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance. His name is "the Lord of hosts."
Gather up your bundle from the ground, you who are under siege!
For thus says the Lord: This time I am going to fling out the inhabitants of the land; I will press them hard, so that they feel it.
Woe is me, what a wound! My injury is grievous. And I who said, "This is only a sickness, I will bear it."
My tent is destroyed, all my cords are snapped; my children have left me, they are no more; there is no one to set up my tent again or raise my shelters.
The shepherds are stupid: they did not seek the Lord. That is why they have not prospered and all their flock is scattered.
A rumor! Here it comes, a great uproar rising from the land of the north, to make the towns of Judah a desert, a lair of jackals.
I know, Lord, that a man's way does not belong to him, that it is not for the one who walks to direct his own steps.
Correct me, Lord, but with measure, not in your anger, or you will reduce me to nothing.

Pour out your fury on the nations that do not know you, on the peoples that do not call on your name; for they have devoured Jacob, they have devoured him, they are finishing him off and laying waste his home.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord:
Hear the words of this covenant, and speak of them to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
You will say to them: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant,

the covenant I commanded your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron-smelting furnace, saying: Listen to my voice, do everything I command you, and you will be my people, and I will be your God;
so I will fulfill the oath I swore to your fathers to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is today. I answered, "Amen, Lord!"
The Lord said to me: Proclaim all these words in the towns of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem: Hear the words of this covenant and put them into practice.
For I solemnly warned your fathers, from the day I brought them up from the land of Egypt until today; I warned them again and again: Listen to my voice.

But they did not listen, they did not incline their ear; each followed the stubbornness of his evil heart. So I brought down on them all the words of this covenant, which I had commanded them to keep and which they did not keep.
The Lord said to me: A conspiracy has been formed among the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They have gone back to the sins of their earliest fathers, who refused to obey my words; they have chased after other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant I made with their fathers.
Therefore, thus says the Lord: I am bringing on them a disaster they cannot escape; they will cry out to me, but I will not listen to them.
The towns of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods to whom they burn incense; but these gods will not save them at all in the time of their disaster.
For you have as many gods as you have towns, Judah; and you have set up as many shameful altars, as many altars for burning incense to Baal, as there are streets in Jerusalem.
As for you, do not intercede for this people, raise for them neither plea nor prayer, for I will not listen when they cry out to me in the time of their disaster.
What is my beloved doing in my house, she who weaves so much treachery? Can vows and consecrated meat turn disaster away from you, so that you can still rejoice?
"A flourishing olive tree, adorned with beautiful fruit," that is the name the Lord had given you. But with a great roar he sets it on fire, and its branches are shattered.
The Lord of hosts, who planted you, has decreed disaster against you, because of the crime of the house of Israel and the house of Judah: they provoked me by burning incense to Baal.
The Lord warned me, and I knew; then he showed me their scheming.

I was like a gentle lamb led to the slaughter, and I did not know they were plotting against me: "Let us destroy the tree with its fruit, let us cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name will be remembered no more!"
But you, Lord of hosts, who judge righteously, who probe the heart and mind, let me see the vengeance you take on them, for to you I have committed my cause.
Therefore, thus says the Lord concerning the men of Anathoth who seek your life and who say, "Do not prophesy in the name of the Lord, or you will die by our hand";
therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts: I am going to punish them. The young men will die by the sword, their sons and daughters will die of famine.
Not one of them will be left, for I will bring disaster on the men of Anathoth in the year I punish them.

titres.titre: The Fate of the Wicked Neighbors

versets.t: You are too just, Lord, for me to argue with you; yet I would plead a case before you: why does the way of the wicked succeed? Why do all the treacherous live at ease?
You plant them, they take root; they grow and bear fruit. You are near their mouth, but far from their heart.
You, Lord, know me, you see me, you test my heart toward you. Drag them off like sheep for the slaughter, set them apart for the day of killing.
How long will the land mourn, the grass of every field wither? Because of the wickedness of its inhabitants, beasts and birds perish, for they say, "He will not see our end."
If you have run with those on foot and they have worn you out, how will you compete with horses? If you feel safe only in peaceful country, what will you do in the thickets of the Jordan?
For even your brothers, your own father's house, betray you; they too cry out loudly behind you. Do not trust them, even when they speak kindly to you.
I have abandoned my house, forsaken my inheritance, handed the one I love over to her enemies.
My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest: she has roared against me, and so I have come to hate her.
Has my inheritance become to me a speckled bird of prey, with birds of prey circling all around it? Go, gather all the beasts of the field, bring them to the feast!
Many shepherds have ravaged my vineyard, trampled my portion; they have made the field I loved a desolate wasteland.
They have made it a ruin; laid waste, it mourns before me. The whole land is ravaged, and no one takes it to heart.
Over all the bare heights of the desert the destroyers come, for the Lord has a sword that devours from one end of the land to the other: no living thing will have peace.
They have sown wheat and reap thorns; they have worn themselves out for nothing. Be ashamed of your harvests, because of the burning anger of the Lord.

Thus says the Lord against all my wicked neighbors who lay hands on the inheritance I gave my people Israel: I am going to uproot them from their soil, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.
But after I have uprooted them, I will again have compassion on them and bring them back, each to his own inheritance, each to his own land.
And if they learn the ways of my people, if they swear by my name, "As the Lord lives!" as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they will be established in the midst of my people.
But if they will not listen, I will uproot that nation, uproot it and destroy it, oracle of the Lord.
Thus the Lord said to me: "Go and buy yourself a linen belt, put it around your waist, but do not dip it in water."
I bought the belt, according to the word of the Lord, and put it around my waist.
The word of the Lord came to me a second time:
"Take the belt you bought and are wearing around your waist; get up, go to the Euphrates, and hide it there in a crevice in the rock."
I went and hid it by the Euphrates, as the Lord had commanded me.
Many days later the Lord said to me, "Get up, go to the Euphrates and take back the belt I commanded you to hide there."
I went to the Euphrates, dug, and took back the belt from the place where I had hidden it: it was ruined, good for nothing.
The word of the Lord came to me:
Thus says the Lord: In the same way I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.
This evil people, who refuse to obey my words, who follow the stubbornness of their hearts and chase after other gods to serve them and bow down before them, will be like this belt, good for nothing.

For as a belt clings to a man's waist, so I had bound to myself the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah, oracle of the Lord, that they might be my people, my renown, my honor, and my glory. But they did not listen.
You will tell them this word: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Every jar is to be filled with wine. They will answer you, "Do we not know that every jar is to be filled with wine?"

Then you will say to them: Thus says the Lord: I am going to fill with drunkenness all the inhabitants of this land, the kings who sit on David's throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
I will smash them one against another, fathers and sons together, oracle of the Lord; without pity, without mercy, without compassion, I will destroy them.
Listen, incline your ear, do not be proud, for it is the Lord who speaks.

Give glory to the Lord your God, before the darkness comes, before your feet stumble on the darkening mountains. You look for light: he will turn it into the shadow of death, he will make it deep gloom.
If you will not listen, I will weep in secret over your pride; my eyes will run with tears, they will stream, for the flock of the Lord is carried off into captivity.
Say to the king and the queen mother: Come down from your seat, sit on the ground, for it has fallen from your head, your crown of glory.
The towns of the Negev are shut up, with no one to open them; all Judah is deported, deported entirely.
Lift up your eyes and look at those who come from the north. Where is it, the flock entrusted to you, the sheep that were your pride?
What will you say when the Lord sets over you those you had made your intimate friends? Will not the pangs seize you like a woman in labor?
And if you ask yourself, "Why has all this happened to me?" it is because of your countless sins that your skirts have been lifted and your heels bruised.
Can a Cushite change his skin, or a leopard its spots? And you, could you do good, you who are accustomed to doing evil?
I will scatter them like chaff swept away by the desert wind.
This is your lot, the portion I have measured out to you, oracle of the Lord, because you have forgotten me and trusted in falsehood.
I too will lift your skirts over your face, and your shame will be seen.
Your adulteries, your lust, your shameless prostitution: on the hills, out in the open country, I have seen your abominations. Woe to you, Jerusalem! How much longer will you remain unclean?
The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought.
Judah mourns, its gates languish, prostrate on the ground, and the cry of Jerusalem rises up.
The great send their servants for water; they go to the cisterns, find no water, and come back with their jars empty; disappointed and ashamed, they cover their heads.
The ground is cracked, for lack of rain on the land; the plowmen, disappointed, cover their heads.
Even the doe in the field gives birth and then abandons her young, for there is no more grass.
The wild donkeys stand on the bare heights, panting for air like jackals; their eyes grow dim, for there is no more greenery.
Though our wrongs testify against us, Lord, act for the honor of your name! Yes, our acts of faithlessness are many, we have sinned against you.
You, the hope of Israel, its savior in time of distress, why would you be like a resident alien in the land, like a traveler who pitches his tent for a night?
Why would you be like a bewildered man, like a warrior unable to save? Yet you are in our midst, Lord, and your name is invoked over us: do not abandon us!

Thus says the Lord concerning this people: Yes, they love to wander here and there, they cannot hold back their feet. The Lord no longer takes pleasure in them; now he will remember their wrongs and punish their sins.
The Lord said to me, "Do not intercede for the well-being of this people.
Even if they fast, I will not listen to their plea; even if they offer me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. For I mean to make an end of them by sword, famine, and plague."
I answered, "Ah, Lord God, look, the prophets tell them: You will not see the sword, famine will not reach you, I will give you assured peace in this place."

The Lord said to me, "It is falsehood that these prophets are proclaiming in my name. I did not send them, I gave them no command, I did not speak to them. Lying visions, empty divinations, deceptions of their own hearts, that is what they prophesy to you."

Therefore, thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who prophesy in my name though I did not send them, who say, "There will be neither sword nor famine in this land": by sword and famine those very prophets will perish.

And the people to whom they prophesy will be thrown into the streets of Jerusalem, victims of famine and the sword, with no one to bury them, they, their wives, their sons, and their daughters. I will pour out on them their own wickedness.
You will say this word to them: Let my eyes run with tears, night and day, without ceasing, for the virgin daughter of my people is struck with a great disaster, a most grievous wound.
If I go out into the fields, there are the victims of the sword; if I enter the town, there are the torments of hunger. Both prophet and priest wander to a land they do not know.
Have you utterly rejected Judah? Have you come to loathe Zion? Why have you struck us with no possible healing? We waited for peace: nothing good comes; for the time of healing: only terror.
We acknowledge, Lord, our wickedness and the guilt of our fathers: yes, we have sinned against you.
For the sake of your name, do not despise us, do not dishonor the throne of your glory. Remember, do not break your covenant with us.
Among the hollow idols of the nations, is there one that can bring rain? Is it the sky that gives the showers? Is it not you, Lord our God? We hope in you, for it is you who do all this.
The Lord answered me: Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my heart would not turn toward this people. Drive them away from me, let them go!

And if they ask you, "Where shall we go?" you will say to them: Thus says the Lord: Those for death, to death; those for the sword, to the sword; those for famine, to famine; those for captivity, to captivity.
I will appoint over them four kinds of destroyers, oracle of the Lord: the sword to kill, the dogs to drag away, the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
I will make them an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, for all that he did in Jerusalem.
Who will have pity on you, Jerusalem? Who will grieve for you? Who will turn aside to ask how you are?
You have rejected me, oracle of the Lord, you have turned your back on me; so I stretch out my hand against you to destroy you, I am weary of relenting.
I have winnowed them with the fork at the gates of the land; I have bereaved my people of children, I have made them perish, for they will not turn back from their ways.
Their widows are more numerous than the sand of the sea. On the mother of the young man I bring the destroyer at noon, I let anguish and terror fall on her suddenly.

The mother of seven sons grows faint, she breathes her last; her sun sets in broad daylight, she is dismayed, covered with shame. Those who remain I will hand over to the sword before their enemies, oracle of the Lord.
Woe is me, my mother, that you gave me birth, a man of strife and quarrel for the whole land! I have not lent, no one has lent to me, and yet everyone curses me.
The Lord said: Truly, I will strengthen you for your good; truly, in the time of disaster and distress I will make your enemy come to plead with you.
Can iron be broken, iron from the north, and bronze?
Your wealth and your treasures I will hand over to plunder, without payment, because of all your sins committed throughout your territory.
I will make you pass with your enemies into a land you do not know, for a fire is kindled in my anger: it will burn against you.
You know it, Lord! Remember me, take care of me, avenge me on my persecutors; in your patience, do not let me be swept away. See: it is for you that I bear insult.
As soon as your words came, I devoured them; they were my joy, the gladness of my heart, for your name is invoked over me, Lord, God of hosts.
I did not sit in the company of revelers to make merry with them; under the grip of your hand I sat alone, for you had filled me with your indignation.
Why is my pain unending, my wound incurable, refusing to heal? Would you be to me like a deceptive stream, water that cannot be relied on?

Therefore, thus says the Lord: If you return to me, I will restore you, you will stand before me; if you can draw the precious from the worthless, you will be as my mouth. It is they who will turn to you, not you who will turn to them.
I will make you to this people an unshakable wall of bronze; they will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, for I am with you to save and deliver you, oracle of the Lord.
I will deliver you from the hand of the wicked, I will redeem you from the grasp of the violent.

titres.titre: The Unmarried Prophet, a Sign of Disaster
The Nations Will Acknowledge the True God

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
You shall not take a wife, and you shall have neither sons nor daughters in this place.
For thus says the Lord concerning the sons and daughters born in this place, the mothers who bear them and the fathers who beget them in this land:

They will die of deadly diseases, unmourned and unburied; they will be like dung on the ground. They will perish by sword and famine, and their corpses will become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.

For thus says the Lord: Do not enter a house of mourning, do not go to weep or lament with them, for I have withdrawn my peace from this people, oracle of the Lord, my faithful love and my compassion.
Great and small will die in this land, without burial or tears; no one will gash himself or shave his head for them.
No one will break bread for the mourner to comfort him for the dead, no one will offer him the cup of consolation for his father or his mother.
Do not enter a house of feasting either, to sit with them to eat and drink.
For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: I am about to silence in this place, before your eyes and in your days, the sounds of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the bride.

When you announce all this to this people, they will say to you, "Why has the Lord decreed such a great disaster against us? What is our wrong, what is the sin we have committed against the Lord our God?"
You will answer them, "It is because your fathers abandoned me, oracle of the Lord; they chased after other gods, served them and worshiped them; they abandoned me and did not keep my law.
And you, you have done worse than your fathers: each of you follows the stubbornness of his evil heart, without listening to me.
So I will hurl you out of this land, into a land unknown to you and your fathers, where you will serve other gods day and night, for I will show you no favor."
Therefore, the days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when it will no longer be said, "As the Lord lives, who brought the sons of Israel up from the land of Egypt,"

but, "As the Lord lives, who brought the sons of Israel up from the land of the north and from all the lands where he had driven them." For I will bring them back to their own soil, the land I gave their fathers.

I am sending for many fishermen, oracle of the Lord, and they will catch them; after that I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them down on every mountain, every hill, and in the crevices of the rocks.
For my eyes follow all their ways; they are not hidden from me, and their guilt is not concealed from my sight.
First I will repay their wrong and their sin double, because they have defiled my land, filling my inheritance with the carcasses of their detestable idols.

Lord, my strength, my stronghold, my refuge in the day of distress, to you the nations will come from the ends of the earth, and they will say: Our fathers inherited nothing but falsehood, empty idols of no profit.
Can a man make gods for himself? These are not gods!
Therefore, this time I am going to make them know, I am going to make them know my hand and my power, and they will know that my name is the Lord.

titres.titre: Cursed Is the Man, Blessed Is the Man

versets.t: The sin of Judah is written with an iron stylus, engraved with a diamond point on the tablet of their heart and on the horns of their altars.
As they remember their children, so they remember their altars and their sacred poles, beside the green trees, on the high hills.
O my mountain in the open country, I will hand over to plunder your wealth, all your treasures and your high places, because of the sin committed throughout your territory.

Through your own fault you will have to let go of the inheritance I gave you; I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, for you have kindled the fire of my anger: it will burn forever.
Thus says the Lord: Cursed is the man who puts his trust in man, who makes a mortal his strength and turns his heart away from the Lord!
He is like a bush in the wasteland: he sees no good come; he lives in the burned-out places of the desert, in a salt land where no one can live.
Blessed is the man who puts his trust in the Lord, whose confidence is the Lord!

He is like a tree planted by the water, sending out its roots toward the stream: he does not fear the coming of the heat, his foliage stays green; he is not anxious in the year of drought, he never stops bearing fruit.
The heart is more deceitful than anything, it is beyond cure: who can understand it?
I, the Lord, probe the heart, I test the mind, to repay each one according to his conduct, according to the fruit of his deeds.
Like the partridge that hatches eggs it did not lay, so is the one who amasses a fortune unjustly: in the midst of his days it will leave him, and in the end he will prove a fool.
A throne of glory, exalted from the beginning, such is the place of our sanctuary.
Lord, hope of Israel, all who abandon you will be put to shame; those who turn away from you will be written in the dust, for they have abandoned the Lord, the spring of living water.
Heal me, Lord, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for you are my praise.
They keep saying to me, "Where is the word of the Lord? Let it come to pass!"
I have not refused to be a shepherd in your service, I have not desired the day of disaster, you know it; what came from my lips was before you.
Do not become a terror to me, you who are my refuge in the day of disaster!
Let my persecutors be put to shame, and not me; let them tremble, and not me! Bring on them the day of disaster, break them with a double breaking.
Thus the Lord said to me: Go and stand at the gate of the sons of the people, through which the kings of Judah enter and leave, and then at all the gates of Jerusalem,
and say to them: Hear the word of the Lord, kings of Judah, and all Judah, and all you inhabitants of Jerusalem who enter these gates.
Thus says the Lord: Be careful for your own sakes: carry no load on the Sabbath day, and bring none in through the gates of Jerusalem.
Carry no load out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and do no work; keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers.
But they did not listen, they did not incline their ear; they stiffened their necks so as not to listen, refusing correction.
If you truly listen to me, oracle of the Lord, and bring no load in through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, if you keep that day holy by doing no work on it,

then through the gates of this city will enter kings and officials seated on David's throne, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their officials, the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and this city will be inhabited forever.

People will come from the towns of Judah and the surroundings of Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the lowlands, from the hill country and from the Negev, bringing burnt offerings and sacrifices, grain offerings and incense, offering thank offerings in the house of the Lord.

But if you do not listen to me, if you do not keep the Sabbath day holy, if you carry loads and bring them in through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will set fire to those gates: it will devour the palaces of Jerusalem and will not be quenched.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord:
Get up, go down to the potter's house; there I will let you hear my word.
I went down to the potter's house: he was working at the wheel.
But the vessel he was shaping from the clay was spoiled in his hand; so he made it into another vessel, as it seemed best to him.
The word of the Lord came to me:
Can I not deal with you as this potter does, house of Israel? oracle of the Lord. Yes, like clay in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.
At one moment I decide, concerning a nation or a kingdom, to uproot it, to tear it down and destroy it.
But if that nation I have threatened turns from its wickedness, then I relent of the disaster I had planned to bring on it.
At another moment I decide, concerning a nation or a kingdom, to build it up and to plant it.
But if that nation does what is evil in my sight, refusing to obey my voice, then I relent of the good I had promised to do for it.

Now then, speak to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Thus says the Lord: I am shaping disaster against you, I am devising a plan against you. Turn back, each of you, from your evil ways, and amend your ways and your deeds.
But they say, "It is no use! We will follow our own ideas, each of us will act according to the stubbornness of his evil heart."
Therefore, thus says the Lord: Ask the nations: who has ever heard anything like this? She has done a horrible thing, the virgin of Israel!
Does the snow of Lebanon leave the rocky heights? Do the cool, flowing waters from afar run dry?
Yet my people have forgotten me, they burn incense to hollow idols. They have been made to stumble on their ways, the ancient roads, to take side paths, an unmade road,
and to make their land an object of horror, a byword forever. All who pass by will be appalled and shake their heads.
Like the east wind, I will scatter them before the enemy; I will show them my back and not my face, in the day of their disaster.

They said, "Come, let us plot against Jeremiah! For the law will not be lost to the priest, nor counsel to the wise, nor the word to the prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and pay no attention to any of his words."
Give me your attention, Lord, hear what my adversaries are saying!
Is evil repaid for good? Yet they are digging a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you to speak on their behalf, to turn your anger away from them.

Therefore, hand their children over to famine, give them up to the edge of the sword! Let their wives be bereft of children and husbands, let their men die of plague, let their young men fall struck by the sword in battle!
Let a cry go up from their houses, when you suddenly bring armed bands against them! For they have dug a pit to catch me, they have hidden snares for my feet.
You, Lord, know all their plots to kill me. Do not forgive their wrong, do not blot out their sin from before you; let them be brought down before you, act against them in the time of your anger.
Thus the Lord said: Go, buy from the potter an earthen jar. Take with you some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests,
go out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, at the entrance of the Potsherd Gate, and proclaim there the words I tell you.

You will say: Hear the word of the Lord, kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: I am bringing on this place a disaster such that the ears of all who hear of it will ring.

For they have abandoned me, they have made this place unrecognizable, they have burned incense here to foreign gods that neither they nor their fathers nor the kings of Judah ever knew, and they have filled this place with the blood of the innocent.
They have built the high places of Baal to burn their children in the fire, as burnt offerings to Baal, which I never commanded or spoke of, which never entered my mind.
Therefore, the days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when this place will no longer be called "Topheth" or "the Valley of Ben-hinnom," but "the Valley of Slaughter."

In this place I will bring to nothing the plans of Judah and Jerusalem; I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies, by the hand of those who seek their life, and I will give their corpses as food to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.
I will make this city an object of horror and mockery: everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will scoff at all its wounds.
I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and their daughters; they will devour one another, in the anguish and distress to which their enemies will reduce them, those who seek their life.
Then you will break the jar before the eyes of the men who came with you,

and you will say to them: Thus says the Lord of hosts: I will break this people and this city as one breaks a potter's vessel, which can never be repaired; and they will bury in Topheth for lack of room elsewhere.
This is what I will do to this place and its inhabitants, oracle of the Lord: I will make this city like Topheth.

The houses of Jerusalem and the palaces of the kings of Judah will become unclean like this place of Topheth, all those houses on whose roofs incense was burned to all the host of heaven and drink offerings poured out to foreign gods.
Jeremiah came back from Topheth, where the Lord had sent him to prophesy; he stood in the court of the house of the Lord and said to all the people:

"Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: I am about to bring on this city and on all the towns that depend on it every disaster I have pronounced against it, because they have stiffened their necks so as not to obey my words."

titres.titre: The Curse on the Day of His Birth

versets.t: The priest Pashhur son of Immer, who was chief overseer in the house of the Lord, heard Jeremiah speak these prophecies.
He struck the prophet Jeremiah and had him put in the stocks at the Upper Gate of Benjamin, in the house of the Lord.
The next day, Pashhur released Jeremiah from the stocks. Jeremiah said to him, "The Lord no longer calls you Pashhur, but Terror-on-every-side.

For thus says the Lord: I am handing you over to terror, you and all your friends; they will fall by the sword of their enemies, and your own eyes will see it. I will also hand over all Judah into the hands of the king of Babylon: he will carry them off captive to Babylon and strike them with the sword.

I will hand over all the wealth of this city, all its labor, all its precious things, all the treasures of the kings of Judah; I will hand them over to their enemies, who will plunder them, seize them, and carry them off to Babylon.

And you, Pashhur, with all who live in your house, will go into captivity; you will go to Babylon, and there you will die and be buried, you and all your friends to whom you have prophesied falsehood."
You enticed me, Lord, and I let myself be enticed; you were stronger than I, and you prevailed. All day long I am a laughingstock, everyone mocks me.
Whenever I speak, I must cry out, I must proclaim violence and ruin; the word of the Lord brings me insult and mockery all day long.

I said to myself, "I will think of him no more, I will speak no more in his name." But there was in my heart something like a burning fire, shut up in my bones; I wore myself out holding it in, and I could not.

I heard the whispering of the crowd: "Terror on every side! Denounce him! Let us denounce him!" All who were at peace with me watched for my fall: "Perhaps he will let himself be trapped; then we will overcome him and take our revenge."
But the Lord is with me, like a mighty warrior; therefore my persecutors will stumble, they will not prevail. Their failure will cover them with everlasting shame, never to be forgotten.
Lord of hosts, you who test the righteous, who see the heart and mind, let me see your vengeance on them, for to you I have committed my cause.
Sing to the Lord, praise the Lord, for he has delivered the poor from the hand of the wicked!
Cursed be the day I was born! Let the day my mother bore me not be blessed!
Cursed be the man who brought my father the news, "A boy is born to you!" and filled him with joy.
Let that man be like the towns the Lord overthrew without pity! Let him hear the cry of alarm in the morning, the din of war at noon,
because he did not kill me in the womb: my mother would have been my grave, her womb would have held me forever!
Why did I come out of the womb? To see toil and sorrow, to spend my days in shame?

titres.titre: The Way of Life and the Way of Death

versets.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, to say:
"Inquire of the Lord for us, for Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, is making war on us. Perhaps the Lord will do wonders for us as he has before, and the enemy will withdraw from us."
Jeremiah answered them: This is what you will say to Zedekiah:

Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I am about to turn back against you the weapons in your hands, with which you fight outside the walls against the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who besiege you, and I will gather them into the midst of this city.
And I myself will fight against you, with outstretched hand and mighty arm, in anger, fury, and great wrath.
I will strike the inhabitants of this city, both man and beast: they will die of a great plague.

After that, oracle of the Lord, I will hand over Zedekiah, king of Judah, his servants and the people, all who in this city survive the plague, the sword, and the famine, into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, into the hands of their enemies and those who seek their life. He will put them to the edge of the sword, without sparing them, without pity or compassion.
And you will say to this people: Thus says the Lord: I am setting before you the way of life and the way of death.
Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, famine, or plague; whoever goes out and surrenders to the Chaldeans who besiege you will live: he will escape with his life as his spoil.
For I have turned my face against this city for disaster and not for good, oracle of the Lord: it will be handed over to the king of Babylon, who will burn it down.
To the royal house of Judah, you will say: Hear the word of the Lord,

house of David! Thus says the Lord: Do justice each morning, rescue the oppressed from the hand of the oppressor, lest my anger break out like fire and burn with no one to quench it, because of the wickedness of your deeds.
I am against you, enthroned in the valley, rock of the plain, oracle of the Lord, you who say, "Who will come down against us? Who will penetrate our lairs?"
I will punish you according to the fruit of your deeds, oracle of the Lord; I will set fire to your forest, and it will devour everything around it.

titres.titre: A Call to Justice at the Royal Palace

versets.t: Thus says the Lord: Go down to the palace of the king of Judah and proclaim this word there.
You will say: Hear the word of the Lord, king of Judah, you who sit on the throne of David, you, your servants, and your people, who enter these gates.

Thus says the Lord: Practice justice and righteousness, rescue the oppressed from the hand of the oppressor; the resident alien, the orphan, and the widow, do not mistreat them, do not do violence to them, do not shed innocent blood in this place.
If you truly carry out this word, then kings seated on the throne of David will enter through the gates of this palace, riding in chariots and on horses, they, their servants, and their people.
But if you do not obey these words, I swear by myself, oracle of the Lord, this palace will become a ruin.
For thus says the Lord concerning the palace of the king of Judah: You are to me like Gilead, like the summit of Lebanon; yet I will make you a wasteland, towns without inhabitants.
I set apart destroyers against you, each with his tools; they will cut down your finest cedars and throw them into the fire.
Many nations will pass by this city and say to one another, "Why has the Lord dealt this way with this great city?"
And the answer will be, "Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord their God, bowed down before other gods and served them."
Do not weep for the one who is dead, do not mourn for him; weep rather for the one who goes away, for he will never return, he will never again see his native land.
For thus says the Lord concerning Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who reigned in place of his father and who has gone away from this place: He will never return;
he will die in the place where he was led captive, and he will never see this land again.
Woe to him who builds his house by injustice, his upper rooms by iniquity, who makes his neighbor work for nothing and does not give him his wages!
He says, "I will build myself a vast palace, with spacious upper rooms"; he cuts windows in it, panels it with cedar, and paints it red.
Do you think you are a king because you outdo others in cedar? Did your father not eat and drink too? But he practiced justice and righteousness, and it went well with him.
He judged the cause of the poor and the needy, and all went well. Is this not what it means to know me? oracle of the Lord.
But you have eyes and heart only for your own gain, for shedding innocent blood, for practicing oppression and violence.

Therefore, thus says the Lord concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: They will not mourn for him, saying, "Alas, my brother! Alas, my sister!" They will not mourn for him, saying, "Alas, lord! Alas, majesty!"
He will be buried as a donkey is buried, dragged off and thrown outside the gates of Jerusalem.
Go up to Lebanon and cry out, raise your voice in Bashan, cry from the heights of Abarim, for all your lovers are shattered.
I spoke to you in the time of your prosperity; you said, "I will not listen." This has been your way since your youth: you have not obeyed my voice.
The wind will drive away all your shepherds, your lovers will go into captivity; then you will be covered with shame and confusion for all your wickedness.
You who dwell in Lebanon, who nest in the cedars, how you will groan when the pangs come upon you, the convulsions of a woman in labor!
As I live, oracle of the Lord: even if Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet ring on my right hand, I would tear you off from there.
I will hand you over to those who seek your life, to those before whom you tremble, into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and the Chaldeans.
I will hurl you, and the mother who bore you, into a foreign land where you were not born, and there you will die.
To this land where they will long to return, they will not return.
Is he then a despised, broken vessel, this man, this Jeconiah, an object no one wants? Why have they been cast out, he and his offspring, thrown into a land they did not know?
O land, land, land, hear the word of the Lord!
Thus says the Lord: Record this man as childless, a man who will not prosper in his lifetime; for none of his offspring will succeed in sitting on the throne of David or ruling again over Judah.

titres.titre: The Righteous Branch, King of Justice

versets.t: Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! oracle of the Lord.

Therefore, thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning the shepherds who tend my people: You have scattered my sheep, you have driven them away, you have not cared for them. Now I am going to deal with you, because of the wickedness of your deeds, oracle of the Lord.
I myself will gather the remnant of my sheep from all the lands where I have driven them, and I will bring them back to their pasture; they will be fruitful and multiply.
I will give them shepherds who will tend them; they will no longer be afraid or terrified, and not one of them will be missing, oracle of the Lord.
The days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch: he will reign as a wise king, he will do justice and righteousness in the land.
In his days Judah will be saved, Israel will dwell in security, and this is the name by which he will be called: "The Lord our righteousness."
Therefore, the days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when it will no longer be said, "As the Lord lives, who brought the sons of Israel up from the land of Egypt,"

but, "As the Lord lives, who brought up and led back the descendants of the house of Israel from the land of the north and from all the lands where I had driven them." And they will dwell on their own soil.
Concerning the prophets. My heart is broken within me, all my bones tremble; I am like a drunken man, like someone overcome by wine, because of the Lord and his holy words.
For the land is full of adulterers; because of the curse, the land mourns, the pastures of the desert are dried up. These people run to evil, they put their strength in injustice.
Prophet and priest alike are godless; even in my house I have found their wickedness, oracle of the Lord.
Therefore their way will be for them slippery in the darkness: they will be driven into it, they will fall there; for I will bring disaster on them in the year I punish them, oracle of the Lord.
Among the prophets of Samaria I saw folly: they prophesied by Baal and led my people Israel astray.

But among the prophets of Jerusalem I saw something horrible: they commit adultery and live in falsehood, they encourage the wicked so that none turns from his wickedness. They are all to me like Sodom, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem like Gomorrah.

Therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts concerning the prophets: I am going to make them eat wormwood and drink poisoned water, for from the prophets of Jerusalem godlessness has spread throughout the land.

Thus says the Lord of hosts: Do not listen to the words of these prophets who prophesy to you; they fill you with false hopes, they tell you visions from their own hearts, not what comes from the mouth of the Lord.
To those who despise me, they dare to say, "The Lord has spoken: you will have peace"; and to all who follow the stubbornness of their hearts, they say, "No disaster will come upon you."
But who has stood in the council of the Lord to see and hear his word? Who has paid attention to his word and heard it?
Look, the storm of the Lord, his fury, breaks out; the whirlwind swirls, it bursts upon the heads of the wicked.
The anger of the Lord will not turn back until he has acted and carried out the purposes of his heart; in the days to come you will understand it fully.
I did not send these prophets, yet they run! I did not speak to them, yet they prophesy!
If they had stood in my council, they would have made my people hear my words, they would have turned them back from their evil ways and their wicked deeds.
Am I a God only near at hand, oracle of the Lord, and not a God far off as well?
Can a man hide in some corner without my seeing him? oracle of the Lord. Do I not fill heaven and earth? oracle of the Lord.
I have heard what these prophets say who prophesy falsehood in my name, repeating, "I had a dream, I had a dream!"
How long? Is there anything in the hearts of these prophets who prophesy falsehood, these prophets of their own deceit?
With the dreams they tell one another, they think they can make my people forget my name, as their fathers forgot my name for Baal.
Let the prophet who has had a dream tell his dream; but let the one who has my word report my word faithfully. What has straw to do with wheat? oracle of the Lord.
Is not my word like fire, oracle of the Lord, like a hammer that shatters the rock?
Therefore I am against these prophets, oracle of the Lord, who steal my words from one another.
I am against these prophets, oracle of the Lord, who wag their tongues to declare, "Oracle of the Lord!"

I am against those who prophesy lying dreams, oracle of the Lord, who tell them and lead my people astray with their lies and their reckless boasting. I did not send them, I gave them no command, they are of no use at all to this people, oracle of the Lord.
When this people, or a prophet or a priest, asks you, "What is the burden of the Lord?" you will answer them, "You are the burden, and I am going to cast you off, oracle of the Lord."
And the prophet, the priest, or the ordinary person who still says, "Burden of the Lord," I will punish him and his household.
This is how you will speak among yourselves, each to his brother: "What has the Lord answered?" or "What has the Lord said?"
But you will no longer say, "Burden of the Lord," for each one's burden will be his own word. You twist the words of the living God, the Lord of hosts, our God.
This is how you will speak to the prophet: "What has the Lord answered you?" or "What has the Lord said?"
But if you still say, "Burden of the Lord," then, thus says the Lord: Because you use this word, "Burden of the Lord," when I had told you not to say it,
very well, I will lift you up like a burden and cast you away from me, you and the city I gave to you and your fathers;
I will bring on you everlasting shame, unending disgrace, never to be forgotten.

The Lord showed me two baskets of figs set before the temple of the Lord. This was after Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had carried off captive from Jerusalem to Babylon Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, along with the officials of Judah, the craftsmen, and the smiths.
One of the baskets held very good figs, like those of the first harvest; the other held very bad figs, so bad they could not be eaten.
The Lord said to me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I answered, "Figs: the good ones are very good, the bad ones very bad, so bad they cannot be eaten."
The word of the Lord came to me:
Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: As one regards these good figs, so I will look with favor on the exiles of Judah whom I have sent from this place to the land of the Chaldeans.
I will set my eyes on them for good, I will bring them back to this land; I will build them up and not tear them down, I will plant them and not uproot them.
I will give them a heart to know me, a heart that will know that I am the Lord; they will be my people and I will be their God, for they will return to me with all their heart.

And as one treats the bad figs, so bad they cannot be eaten, thus says the Lord, so I will treat Zedekiah, king of Judah, his officials, and the remnant of Jerusalem, those who remain in this land and those who live in Egypt.
I will make them an object of horror and disaster to all the kingdoms of the earth, a disgrace, a byword, a taunt, and a curse, in all the places where I drive them.
I will send against them the sword, famine, and plague, until they have vanished from the soil I gave to them and their fathers.

titres.titre: Seventy Years of Servitude to Babylon
The Cup of Wrath for the Nations

versets.t: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, that is, the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
The prophet Jeremiah spoke it to all the people of Judah and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem:

From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until today, for twenty-three years now the word of the Lord has come to me, and I have spoken to you again and again; but you have not listened.
The Lord sent you all his servants the prophets, again and again, but you did not listen, you did not incline your ear to hear.
They said, "Turn back, each of you, from your evil way and your wicked deeds, and you will dwell in the land the Lord gave to you and your fathers, forever.
Do not chase after other gods to serve and worship them, do not provoke me with the work of your hands, and I will do you no harm."
But you did not listen to me, oracle of the Lord, and you provoked me with the work of your hands, to your own harm.
Therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts: Because you have not listened to my words,

I am going to send for all the peoples of the north, oracle of the Lord, and for Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, my servant; I will bring them against this land, against its inhabitants, and against all the surrounding nations. I will devote them to destruction, I will make them an object of horror, a hissing, an everlasting ruin.
I will silence among them the sounds of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the bride, the sound of the millstone and the light of the lamp.
This whole land will become a ruin, a wasteland, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.

But when these seventy years are completed, I will call the king of Babylon and that nation to account for their guilt, oracle of the Lord, in the land of the Chaldeans, and I will make it an everlasting ruin.
I will bring upon that land all the words I have spoken against it, everything written in this book, all that Jeremiah has prophesied against all the nations.
For they too will be enslaved by many nations and great kings; I will repay them according to their deeds and according to the work of their hands.
For thus the Lord, the God of Israel, said to me: Take from my hand this cup of the wine of my wrath and make all the nations to whom I send you drink from it.
They will drink, they will stagger, they will lose their senses before the sword I send among them.
I took the cup from the hand of the Lord and made all the nations to whom the Lord sent me drink from it:
Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin, an object of horror, mockery, and cursing, as they are today;
Pharaoh, king of Egypt, his servants, his officials, and all his people;
all the mixed peoples; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the land of the Philistines, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
Edom, Moab, and the sons of Ammon;
all the kings of Tyre, all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the coastlands beyond the sea;
Dedan, Tema, Buz, and all who shave their temples;
all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed peoples who live in the desert;
all the kings of Zimri, all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of Media;
all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another, and all the kingdoms of the world spread over the earth. And after them all, the king of Sheshach will drink too.
You will say to them: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Drink, get drunk, vomit, fall and do not rise, before the sword I send among you!
And if they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink, you will say to them: Thus says the Lord of hosts: You shall drink!

For look: it is with the city that bears my name that I begin to bring disaster, and would you go unpunished? No, you will not go unpunished, for I am calling the sword against all the inhabitants of the earth, oracle of the Lord of hosts.

You will prophesy all this to them, and you will say to them: The Lord roars from on high, from his holy dwelling he thunders his voice; he roars mightily against his home, he raises the shout of the grape treader against all the inhabitants of the earth.
The uproar reaches the ends of the earth, for the Lord brings a case against the nations: he enters into judgment with all flesh, he hands the wicked over to the sword, oracle of the Lord.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: Look, disaster spreads from nation to nation, a great storm rises from the ends of the earth.
On that day the slain of the Lord will lie from one end of the earth to the other; they will not be mourned, gathered up, or buried: they will be like dung on the ground.
Wail, shepherds, and cry out! Roll in the dust, leaders of the flock, for your days have come, the day of slaughter: you will fall and be shattered like a precious vessel.
There will be no refuge for the shepherds, no escape for the leaders of the flock!
Hear the cry of the shepherds, the wailing of the leaders of the flock, for the Lord is ravaging their pasture.
The peaceful meadows are destroyed, before the burning anger of the Lord.
Like a lion, he has left his thicket; their land has become a wasteland, before the devastating sword, before the burning anger of the Lord.

titres.titre: Jeremiah threatened with death at the Temple
The prophet Uriah put to death

versets.t: At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord:

Thus says the Lord: Stand in the court of the house of the Lord, and to all the people of the towns of Judah who come to worship there, speak all the words I have commanded you to tell them; do not cut short a single word.
Perhaps they will listen and turn back, each from his evil way; then I will relent of the disaster I intend to bring on them because of the wickedness of their deeds.
You shall say to them: Thus says the Lord: If you will not listen to me, if you will not follow the law I have set before you,
if you will not heed the words of my servants the prophets, whom I have sent to you again and again, though you have not listened,
then I will treat this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse for all the nations of the earth.
The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speak these words in the house of the Lord.
And when Jeremiah had finished saying all that the Lord had commanded him to say to all the people, the priests, the prophets, and all the people seized him, shouting: "You shall die!

Why do you prophesy in the name of the Lord, saying, 'This house shall be like Shiloh, and this city shall be laid waste, emptied of its inhabitants'?" And all the people crowded around Jeremiah in the house of the Lord.
When the officials of Judah heard these things, they went up from the king's palace to the house of the Lord and took their seats at the entrance of the New Gate.
Then the priests and the prophets said to the officials and to all the people: "This man deserves death, for he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your own ears."
Jeremiah answered all the officials and all the people: "It was the Lord who sent me to prophesy against this house and this city everything you have heard.
Now then, amend your ways and your deeds, and obey the voice of the Lord your God, and the Lord will relent of the disaster he has pronounced against you.
As for me, here I am in your hands: do with me whatever seems good and right to you.

Only know this: if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood upon yourselves, upon this city and its inhabitants, for in truth the Lord has sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing."
Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets: "This man does not deserve death, for he has spoken to us in the name of the Lord our God."
Some of the elders of the land rose and said to the whole assembly of the people:

"Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah, king of Judah, and he said to all the people of Judah: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Zion shall be plowed like a field, Jerusalem shall become a heap of ruins, and the mountain of the Temple a wooded height.

Did Hezekiah, king of Judah, and all Judah put him to death for it? Did they not rather fear the Lord and entreat his favor, so that the Lord relented of the disaster he had pronounced against them? And are we to bring so great a crime upon ourselves?"
There was also a man who prophesied in the name of the Lord, Uriah son of Shemaiah, from Kiriath-jearim; he prophesied against this city and this land exactly as Jeremiah did.
When King Jehoiakim, all his warriors, and all his officials heard his words, the king sought to put him to death. Uriah heard of it, was afraid, and fled to Egypt.
But King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt, Elnathan son of Achbor, and others with him.
They brought Uriah out of Egypt and led him to King Jehoiakim, who had him put to the sword and threw his body into the common grave.
But Ahikam son of Shaphan protected Jeremiah with his own hand, so that he was not handed over to the people to be put to death.
At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord.
Thus the Lord said to me: Make yourself thongs and a yoke, and put them on your neck.
Then send word to the king of Edom, the king of Moab, the king of the Ammonites, the king of Tyre, and the king of Sidon, by the envoys who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah, king of Judah;
give them this message for their masters: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel. This is what you shall say to your masters:
It was I who, by my great power and my outstretched arm, made the earth, humankind, and the animals that live on it, and I give it to whomever I please.
Now I have handed over all these lands to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, my servant; I have even made the beasts of the field subject to him.
All the nations shall serve him, and his son and his grandson, until the time of his own land comes in turn; then many nations and great kings shall make him their slave.

The nation or kingdom that will not serve him, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, that will not put its neck under his yoke, that nation I will punish with sword, famine, and plague, oracle of the Lord, until I have handed it over to him.
As for you, do not listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dreams, your soothsayers, or your sorcerers, who tell you: 'You shall not serve the king of Babylon.'
For it is a lie they prophesy to you, to drive you far from your land, so that I banish you and you perish.
But the nation that will put its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serve him, I will leave in peace on its own soil, oracle of the Lord; it shall till it and dwell there.
To Zedekiah, king of Judah, I spoke in exactly the same way: Put your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, serve him and his people, and you shall live.
Why should you die, you and your people, by sword, famine, and plague, as the Lord has declared for the nation that refuses to serve the king of Babylon?
Do not listen to the words of the prophets who tell you, 'You shall not serve the king of Babylon,' for it is a lie they prophesy to you.
I have not sent them, oracle of the Lord; it is falsely that they prophesy in my name, so that I banish you and you perish, you and the prophets who prophesy to you.

To the priests and to all this people I said: Thus says the Lord: Do not listen to the words of your prophets who announce to you, 'Behold, the vessels of the house of the Lord will soon be brought back from Babylon.' For it is a lie they prophesy to you.
Do not listen to them; serve the king of Babylon, and you shall live. Why should this city become a ruin?

If they are prophets, if the word of the Lord is with them, let them intercede with the Lord of hosts that the vessels left in the house of the Lord, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem may not go to Babylon!
For thus says the Lord of hosts concerning the pillars, the bronze Sea, the stands, and the rest of the vessels left in this city,
those Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, did not take when he carried off from Jerusalem to Babylon Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem.
Yes, thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the vessels left in the house of the Lord, in the palace of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem:
They shall be carried to Babylon, and there they shall remain until the day I attend to them, oracle of the Lord; then I will bring them up and restore them to this place.

That same year, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month (around July-August), the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur, from Gibeon, said to me in the house of the Lord, before the priests and all the people:
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two years I will bring back to this place all the vessels of the house of the Lord that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, took from here and carried to Babylon.
I will also bring back to this place Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the exiles of Judah who went to Babylon, oracle of the Lord, for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Then the prophet Jeremiah answered the prophet Hananiah, before the priests and all the people present in the house of the Lord.
The prophet Jeremiah said: Amen! May the Lord do so! May he fulfill the words you have just prophesied, bringing back from Babylon to this place the vessels of his house and all the exiles!
Yet listen to this word that I speak in your hearing and in the hearing of all the people:
The prophets who preceded us, you and me, from ancient times, prophesied war, disaster, and plague against many lands and great kingdoms.
But the prophet who prophesies peace, it is when his word comes true that it will be known that the Lord has truly sent him.
Then the prophet Hananiah took the yoke off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah and broke it.

And Hananiah declared before all the people: Thus says the Lord: This is how, within two years, I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, from the neck of all the nations. And the prophet Jeremiah went his way.
After the prophet Hananiah had broken the yoke off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah:
Go and say to Hananiah: Thus says the Lord: You have broken a wooden yoke, but in its place you shall have an iron yoke.

For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: I am putting an iron yoke on the neck of all these nations, to make them serve Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon; they shall serve him, and I have even given him the beasts of the field.
Then the prophet Jeremiah said to the prophet Hananiah: Listen, Hananiah! The Lord has not sent you, and you have made this people trust in a lie.
Therefore, thus says the Lord: I am about to send you from the face of the earth; this very year you shall die, for you have preached rebellion against the Lord.
And the prophet Hananiah died that year, in the seventh month (around September-October).

titres.titre: Plans for peace and not for disaster
Against the false prophets of the exile

versets.t: This is the text of the letter that the prophet Jeremiah sent from Jerusalem to the rest of the elders in captivity, to the priests, the prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had deported from Jerusalem to Babylon,
after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the court officials, the officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen, and the smiths had left Jerusalem.
He entrusted it to Elasah son of Shaphan and to Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah, king of Judah, was sending to Babylon to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. It read:
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, to all the exiles I have deported from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their fruit.
Take wives and have sons and daughters; find wives for your sons, give your daughters in marriage, so that they too may have sons and daughters; multiply there, do not dwindle.
Seek the welfare of the city to which I have deported you, and pray to the Lord on its behalf, for in its welfare lies your own.
For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Do not let yourselves be misled by the prophets among you or by your diviners, and do not listen to the dreams you conjure up.
For it is a lie they prophesy to you in my name: I have not sent them, oracle of the Lord.
For thus says the Lord: When seventy years are completed for Babylon, I will visit you and fulfill for you my promise of good, bringing you back to this place.
For I know the plans I have made for you, oracle of the Lord: plans for peace and not for disaster, to give you a future and a hope.
Then you will call upon me, you will come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.
You will seek me and find me, if you seek me with all your heart.

I will let myself be found by you, oracle of the Lord; I will restore your fortunes, I will gather you from all the nations and all the places to which I have banished you, oracle of the Lord, and I will bring you back to the place from which I exiled you.
You say: 'The Lord has raised up prophets for us in Babylon.'
Well, this is what the Lord says concerning the king seated on the throne of David, all the people who live in this city, and your kindred who did not go with you into exile.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: I am sending against them the sword, famine, and plague, and I will make them like rotten figs, too bad to be eaten.

I will pursue them with sword, famine, and plague; I will make them an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, an example of cursing, dismay, mockery, and shame among all the nations to which I have banished them,
because they did not listen to my words, oracle of the Lord, though I sent them my servants the prophets again and again; but you did not listen, oracle of the Lord.
But you, hear the word of the Lord, all you exiles I have sent from Jerusalem to Babylon.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who prophesy a lie to you in my name: I am handing them over to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, who will put them to death before your eyes.
And from them shall come a curse used by all the exiles of Judah in Babylon: 'May the Lord treat you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire!'

because they have committed an outrage in Israel, committing adultery with their neighbors' wives and speaking in my name lies that I did not command them. I myself know it and am a witness to it, oracle of the Lord.
To Shemaiah the Nehelamite you shall say:
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: In your own name you have sent letters to all the people of Jerusalem, to the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and to all the priests, saying:
'The Lord has made you priest in place of the priest Jehoiada, to be the overseers in the house of the Lord: every madman who plays the prophet you must put in the stocks and the collar.
So why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who plays the prophet among you?
For he has even been able to send word to us in Babylon: It will be long; build houses and live in them, plant gardens and eat their fruit.'
The priest Zephaniah read this letter to the prophet Jeremiah.
Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah:
Send word to all the exiles: Thus says the Lord concerning Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you though I did not send him, and has made you trust in a lie,

therefore, thus says the Lord: I am going to punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants: none of his line shall live among this people, and he shall not see the good I will do for my people, oracle of the Lord, for he has preached rebellion against the Lord.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord:
Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Write in a book all the words I have spoken to you.

For behold, the days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when I will restore the fortunes of my people, Israel and Judah, says the Lord; I will bring them back to the land I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.
These are the words the Lord spoke concerning Israel and Judah.
Thus says the Lord: We have heard a cry of terror: it is dread, and there is no peace.
Ask now and see: can a man give birth? Why then do I see every man with his hands on his loins like a woman in labor? Why has every face turned pale?
Alas! For that day is so great that there is none like it. It is a time of anguish for Jacob, yet he shall be delivered from it.
On that day, oracle of the Lord of hosts, I will break the yoke that weighs on your neck, I will snap your bonds, and strangers shall no longer enslave you.
They shall serve the Lord their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

So you, do not fear, my servant Jacob, oracle of the Lord; do not be dismayed, Israel. For behold, I will save you from the distant land, your offspring from the land of their exile. Jacob shall return, he shall be quiet and at ease, with no one to make him afraid.

For I am with you to save you, oracle of the Lord. I will make an end of all the nations among which I scattered you; but with you I will not make an end: I will discipline you with measure, yet I will by no means leave you unpunished.
For thus says the Lord: Your wound is incurable, your injury beyond healing.
No one pleads your cause; for your sore there is no remedy, no cure.
All your lovers have forgotten you; they care nothing for you. For I have struck you as an enemy strikes, with cruel chastisement, because of your many sins, your countless offenses.
Why cry out over your wound, over your incurable pain? It is because of your many sins, your countless offenses, that I have done this to you.
But all who devour you shall be devoured, and all your oppressors shall go into captivity; those who plunder you shall be plundered, and all who despoil you I will hand over to despoiling.
For I will restore your health and heal your wounds, oracle of the Lord, you whom they called 'the Outcast,' 'Zion whom no one cares for.'
Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will restore the tents of Jacob and have compassion on his dwellings; the city shall be rebuilt on its ruins, and the palace shall stand in its rightful place.
From them shall rise songs of praise and shouts of joy. I will multiply them, and they shall not dwindle; I will honor them, and they shall not be despised.
His children shall be as of old, his community shall stand firm before me, and I will punish all his oppressors.
His leader shall be one of his own, his ruler shall come from his own midst; I will bring him near, and he shall approach me. For who otherwise would dare to approach me? oracle of the Lord.
You shall be my people, and I will be your God.
Behold, the storm of the Lord, his wrath, bursts forth; the tempest rages, it whirls down upon the head of the wicked.
The burning anger of the Lord will not turn back until he has acted and carried out the purposes of his heart; in the days to come you will understand it.
At that time, oracle of the Lord, I will be the God of all the families of Israel, and they shall be my people.
Thus says the Lord: The people who survived the sword found grace in the wilderness; Israel goes forward to its rest.
From afar the Lord appeared to me: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have kept my faithfulness toward you.
I will build you again, and you shall be rebuilt, virgin Israel; again you shall adorn yourself with your tambourines and go forth in the joyful dances.
Again you shall plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria; those who plant them shall enjoy their fruit.
For a day is coming when the watchmen will cry out on the hills of Ephraim: 'Arise, let us go up to Zion, to the Lord our God!'
For thus says the Lord: Shout for joy over Jacob, acclaim the first of the nations! Make yourselves heard, sing praises, and say: 'Lord, save your people, the remnant of Israel!'

Behold, I am bringing them back from the land of the north, gathering them from the ends of the earth. Among them the blind and the lame, the woman with child and the one in labor: a great throng returns here.
They come back weeping; I lead them amid their pleas; I guide them to streams of water by a level road where they will not stumble. For I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
Nations, hear the word of the Lord, and proclaim it in the distant coastlands: 'He who scattered Israel will gather him and guard him as a shepherd his flock.
For the Lord has ransomed Jacob and redeemed him from a hand stronger than his own.'

They shall come and shout for joy on the heights of Zion; they shall stream to the bounty of the Lord: the grain, the new wine, the oil, the sheep and the cattle. Their life shall be like a watered garden, and they shall languish no more.
Then the young woman shall rejoice in the dance, young men and old together; I will turn their mourning into joy, I will comfort them and give them gladness after their sorrow.
I will fill the priests with abundance, and my people shall be satisfied with my bounty, oracle of the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: In Ramah a lament is heard, bitter weeping: it is Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted, for they are no more.
Thus says the Lord: Hold back your voice from weeping, your eyes from tears, for your labor shall have its reward, oracle of the Lord: they shall return from the land of the enemy.
There is hope for your future, oracle of the Lord: your children shall return to their own land.
I have surely heard Ephraim lamenting: 'You disciplined me, and I was disciplined like an untrained young bull. Bring me back, and I will return, for you are the Lord my God.
After turning away, I repented; after coming to understand, I struck my breast. I am ashamed and confounded, for I bear the disgrace of my youth.'

Is Ephraim so dear a son to me, so cherished a child? For as often as I speak of him, I still remember him with tenderness. Therefore my heart yearns for him; yes, I will surely have mercy on him, oracle of the Lord.
Set up road markers for yourself, plant guideposts; mark well the highway, the road you have traveled. Return, virgin Israel, return to these your cities.
How long will you waver, wayward daughter? For the Lord creates something new on the earth: a woman shall encompass a man.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Once more this word shall be spoken in the land of Judah and in its towns, when I restore their fortunes: 'May the Lord bless you, home of righteousness, holy mountain!'
There Judah and all its towns shall dwell together, the farmers and those who move about with the flocks.
For I will give drink to the weary and satisfy all who languish.
At this I awoke and looked; my sleep had been sweet to me.
Behold, the days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with a seed of men and a seed of beasts.
And just as I watched over them to uproot, tear down, overthrow, destroy, and bring harm, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, oracle of the Lord.
