In those days they shall no longer say: 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.'
Each shall die for his own sin: whoever eats sour grapes, his own teeth shall be set on edge.
Behold, the days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.

It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers, on the day I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, a covenant they broke, though I was their husband, oracle of the Lord.

This is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, oracle of the Lord: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

No longer shall anyone teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, 'Know the Lord!' For they shall all know me, from the least to the greatest, oracle of the Lord; for I will forgive their iniquity and remember their sin no more.
Thus says the Lord, who gives the sun to light the day, who orders the moon and the stars to light the night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar, whose name is 'the Lord of hosts':
If ever this order were to vanish from before me, oracle of the Lord, only then would the offspring of Israel cease to be a nation before me forever.

Thus says the Lord: If the heavens above could be measured and the foundations of the earth below be searched out, only then would I reject all the offspring of Israel for all they have done, oracle of the Lord.
Behold, the days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when this city shall be rebuilt for the Lord, from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
The measuring line shall stretch out farther, straight to the hill of Gareb, then turn toward Goah.

And the whole valley of the corpses and the ashes, all the fields as far as the Kidron valley, to the corner of the Horse Gate on the east, shall be holy to the Lord: never again shall they be uprooted or overthrown.

titres.titre: The purchase of the field at Anathoth

versets.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the tenth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah, that is, the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
The army of the king of Babylon was then besieging Jerusalem, and the prophet Jeremiah was confined in the court of the guard, in the palace of the king of Judah.
Zedekiah, king of Judah, had had him confined, reproaching him: "Why do you prophesy this: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am handing this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will take it;
Zedekiah, king of Judah, shall not escape the hands of the Chaldeans; he shall be handed over to the king of Babylon, and shall speak with him face to face and see him eye to eye;
Nebuchadnezzar will take Zedekiah to Babylon, where he shall remain until I attend to him, oracle of the Lord; if you fight the Chaldeans, you will not succeed?"
Jeremiah said: The word of the Lord came to me:
Behold, Hanamel son of your uncle Shallum is coming to say to you: 'Buy my field at Anathoth, for you have the right of redemption to acquire it.'

Hanamel, my uncle's son, came to me in the court of the guard, as the Lord had said, and told me: 'Buy my field at Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin, for the right of inheritance and redemption is yours: buy it!' Then I knew that this was the word of the Lord.
So I bought the field at Anathoth from Hanamel, my uncle's son, and weighed out the silver for him: about two hundred grams of silver.
I drew up the deed, sealed it, called witnesses, and weighed out the silver on the scales.
Then I took the deed of purchase, the sealed copy with its terms and conditions, and the open copy,

and I gave this deed to Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah, in the presence of Hanamel my uncle's son, of the witnesses who had signed the deed, and of all the Judeans sitting in the court of the guard.
Before them I gave Baruch this order:
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Take these deeds, the sealed deed of purchase and the open deed, and put them in an earthenware jar, so that they may last a long time.
For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Houses, fields, and vineyards shall again be bought in this land.
After giving the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the Lord:
Ah, Lord God, it is you who made heaven and earth by your great power and your outstretched arm; nothing is impossible for you.
You show faithful love to thousands, but you repay the guilt of the fathers into the laps of their children after them; O great and mighty God, whose name is the Lord of hosts,
great in counsel and mighty in deed, whose eyes are open to all the ways of men, to reward each according to his conduct, according to the fruit of his deeds.
It is you who performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and to this day in Israel and among all people, and so made a name for yourself, as is seen today.
It is you who brought your people Israel out of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror.
You gave them this land that you had sworn to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
They entered it and took possession of it; but they did not obey your voice or follow your law, they did none of what you had commanded them; that is why you have brought upon them all this disaster.
Behold, the siege ramps reach the city to take it; by sword, famine, and plague it is being handed over to the Chaldeans who attack it. What you foretold is happening, and you see it.
And yet, Lord God, it is you who told me: 'Buy the field with silver and call witnesses,' even as the city is handed over to the Chaldeans!
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah:
I am the Lord, the God of all flesh: is anything impossible for me?
Therefore, thus says the Lord: Behold, I am handing this city over to the Chaldeans and to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and he will take it.

The Chaldeans who attack this city will enter it, set it on fire, and burn it, together with the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Baal and poured out libations to other gods, provoking me.

For from their youth the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah have done nothing but evil in my sight; the sons of Israel have done nothing but provoke me by the work of their hands, oracle of the Lord.
This city has done nothing but stir up my anger and my wrath, from the day it was built until today, so that I will remove it from my sight,

because of all the evil the sons of Israel and the sons of Judah have done to provoke me, they, their kings, their officials, their priests, their prophets, the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
They turned their backs to me and not their faces; though I taught them again and again, they would not listen or accept correction.
They set up their abominable idols in the house that bears my name, to defile it.

They built the high places of Baal in the valley of Ben-hinnom, to offer their sons and daughters to Molech: something I had not commanded, something that never entered my mind. They committed this horror to make Judah sin.
And now, thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning this city of which you say: 'It will be handed over to the king of Babylon by sword, famine, and plague.'
Behold, I will gather them from all the lands to which I banished them in my anger, my wrath, and my great indignation; I will bring them back to this place and make them dwell in safety.
They shall be my people, and I will be their God.
I will give them one heart and one way, so that they may fear me always, for their own good and the good of their children after them.
I will make with them an everlasting covenant: I will never cease to do good to them, and I will put the fear of me in their hearts, so that they will not turn away from me.
I will rejoice in doing them good, and I will plant them firmly in this land, with all my heart and all my soul.
For thus says the Lord: Just as I brought all this great disaster on this people, so I will bring on them all the good I promise them.
Fields shall again be bought in this land of which you say: 'It is a wasteland, without man or beast, handed over to the Chaldeans.'

Fields shall be bought with silver, deeds shall be drawn up, sealed, and witnessed, in the land of Benjamin, in the districts around Jerusalem, in the towns of Judah, those of the hill country, those of the Shephelah, and those of the Negeb; for I will restore their fortunes, oracle of the Lord.

titres.titre: The righteous Branch and the covenant with David

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still confined in the court of the guard:
Thus says the Lord, who carries out his work, the Lord who shapes it to bring it about, whose name is 'the Lord':
Call to me, and I will answer you; I will reveal to you great things, hidden things you do not know.
For thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning the houses of this city and the palaces of the kings of Judah, torn down to face the siege ramps and the sword,

while they go to fight the Chaldeans: these houses will be filled with the corpses of the men I strike down in my anger and my wrath, I who have hidden my face from this city because of all their wickedness.
Behold, I will bring it health and healing; I will heal them and reveal to them an abundance of lasting peace and security.
I will restore the fortunes of Judah and Israel, and rebuild them as of old.
I will cleanse them of all the guilt they incurred against me, and forgive all the sins by which they sinned and rebelled against me.

This city will become for me a source of joy, of praise, and of glory before all the nations of the earth, who will hear of all the good I do for it; they will be seized with fear and tremble at all the good fortune and peace I give it.

Thus says the Lord: In this place of which you say, 'It is a wasteland, without man or beast,' in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, now desolate, without man, without inhabitant, without beast, there shall again be heard

the sounds of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the bride, the voice of those who say: 'Give thanks to the Lord of hosts, for the Lord is good, his faithful love endures forever!' as they bring their thank offerings to the house of the Lord. For I will restore the fortunes of the land as at the first, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: In this wasteland, without man or beast, and in all its towns, there shall again be pastures where shepherds rest their flocks.

In the towns of the hill country, of the Shephelah, and of the Negeb, in the land of Benjamin, in the districts around Jerusalem, and in the towns of Judah, the flocks shall again pass under the hand of the one who counts them, says the Lord.
Behold, the days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when I will fulfill the promise of good I made concerning the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
In those days and at that time I will make a righteous Branch spring up for David, who will execute justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah shall be saved and Jerusalem shall dwell in safety, and this is the name by which it will be called: 'the Lord, our righteousness.'
For thus says the Lord: David shall never lack a descendant to sit on the throne of the house of Israel,
and the levitical priests shall never lack before me a man to offer the burnt offering, to send up in smoke the grain offering, and to present the sacrifice, all the days.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah:
Thus says the Lord: If you could break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night, so that day and night no longer came at their appointed time,
only then could my covenant with David my servant be broken, so that he would have no son to reign on his throne, and my covenant with the levitical priests, my ministers.
As the host of heaven cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the offspring of David my servant and the Levites who minister to me.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah:
Have you not noticed what this people says: 'The two families the Lord had chosen, he has rejected them'? So they despise my people, no longer regarding them as a nation.
Thus says the Lord: If I have not established my covenant with day and night, nor fixed the laws of heaven and earth,

then I will also reject the offspring of Jacob and of David my servant, and cease to take from his offspring rulers for the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. But no! I will restore their fortunes and have mercy on them.

titres.titre: The slaves freed and taken back

versets.t: The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, when Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, with all his army, all the kingdoms of the earth under his rule, and all the peoples, were fighting against Jerusalem and all the towns that depended on it:
Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Go and speak to Zedekiah, king of Judah, and tell him: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am handing this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it.

You yourself shall not escape his hand: you shall be captured and handed over to him; your eyes shall see the eyes of the king of Babylon, he shall speak with you face to face, and you shall go to Babylon.
Yet hear the word of the Lord, Zedekiah, king of Judah! Thus says the Lord concerning you: You shall not die by the sword,

you shall die in peace. And as spices were burned for your fathers, the former kings who preceded you, so they shall burn them for you, and they shall lament for you, saying: 'Alas, lord!' For it is I who have spoken, oracle of the Lord.
The prophet Jeremiah spoke all these words to Zedekiah, king of Judah, in Jerusalem,

while the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against the towns of Judah that still held out, Lachish and Azekah; for among the fortified towns of Judah, these were the only ones left.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, after King Zedekiah had made an agreement with all the people of Jerusalem to proclaim the release of the slaves:
each was to set free his male and female slave, Hebrew man or Hebrew woman, and no one was to keep a fellow Judean in bondage.
All the officials and all the people who had entered into this agreement consented to set free each his male and female slave and to hold them in bondage no longer; they agreed and set them free.
But afterward they changed their minds: they took back the slaves, men and women, whom they had freed, and forced them back into slavery.
Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah:
Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: I made a covenant with your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, saying:

At the end of seven years, each of you shall set free his Hebrew brother who has sold himself to you; he shall serve you six years, then you shall send him away free. But your fathers did not listen to me or incline their ear.
You today had turned back to me and done what is right in my eyes by proclaiming freedom, each for his neighbor; you had made an agreement before me, in the house that bears my name.
But you changed your minds and profaned my name: each took back his male and female slave, whom you had set free to be their own masters, and forced them back to be your slaves.

Therefore, thus says the Lord: You have not obeyed me by proclaiming freedom, each for his brother, each for his neighbor; well then, I proclaim against you a release, oracle of the Lord: a release to the sword, to plague, and to famine, and I will make you an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
The men who have transgressed my covenant, who have not kept the terms of the agreement made before me, I will make like the calf they cut in two to pass between its pieces.
The officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the court officials, the priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the pieces of the calf,
I will hand them over to their enemies, to those who seek their lives; their corpses shall become food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.
And Zedekiah, king of Judah, and his officials, I will hand over to their enemies, to those who seek their lives, to the army of the king of Babylon that has just withdrawn from you.

Behold, I am giving the command, oracle of the Lord, and I will bring them back against this city; they shall attack it, take it, and burn it. And I will make the towns of Judah a wasteland, without inhabitants.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
Go to the clan of the Rechabites, speak to them, bring them to the house of the Lord, into one of the chambers, and offer them wine to drink.
So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah son of Habazziniah, his brothers, all his sons, the whole clan of the Rechabites,

and brought them into the house of the Lord, into the chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God, next to the chamber of the officials, above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold.
I set before the Rechabites pitchers full of wine, and cups, and said to them: 'Drink some wine.'
But they answered: 'We drink no wine, for our ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab gave us this command: You shall never drink wine, neither you nor your sons;

you shall not build houses, you shall not sow, you shall not plant vineyards or own them; all your lives you shall live in tents, so that you may live long on the land where you dwell as resident aliens.
We have obeyed in everything the voice of our ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab: we never drink wine, neither we, nor our wives, nor our sons, nor our daughters;
we build no houses to live in, and we have no vineyard, no field, no sown land;
we live in tents, faithful to all that our ancestor Jonadab commanded us.

But when Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, marched against this land, we said to ourselves: Come, let us take refuge in Jerusalem from the army of the Chaldeans and the army of Aram. And so here we are, settled in Jerusalem.'
Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah:
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Go and say to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Will you not accept correction and heed my words? oracle of the Lord.

The words of Jonadab son of Rechab have been kept: he ordered his sons not to drink wine, and they have drunk none to this day, in obedience to their ancestor. But I have spoken to you again and again, and you have not listened to me.

I sent you all my servants the prophets, again and again, to say: Turn back, each from his evil way; amend your deeds; do not go after other gods to serve them, and you shall dwell in the land I gave to you and your fathers. But you did not incline your ear or listen to me.
Yes, the sons of Jonadab son of Rechab have kept the command their ancestor gave them; but this people does not listen to me.

Therefore, thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing upon Judah and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disaster I threatened against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen, I called to them and they did not answer.

And Jeremiah said to the clan of the Rechabites: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Because you have obeyed the command of your ancestor Jonadab, kept all his commands, and done all he prescribed for you,
therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Jonadab son of Rechab shall never lack a descendant to stand before me.
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord:
Take a scroll and write on it all the words I have spoken to you against Israel, against Judah, and against all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you, in the days of Josiah, until today.
Perhaps the house of Judah, hearing of all the disaster I intend to bring on them, will turn back, each from his evil way; then I will forgive their iniquity and their sin.
So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on the scroll, at Jeremiah's dictation, all the words the Lord had spoken to him.
Then Jeremiah gave Baruch this order: 'I am prevented; I cannot go to the house of the Lord.

You shall go; on the day of fasting, in the house of the Lord, you shall read to the people the words of the Lord from the scroll you wrote at my dictation; you shall also read them to all the Judeans who come from their towns.
Perhaps their plea will rise before the Lord, and they will turn back, each from his evil way, for great is the anger the Lord has expressed against this people.'
Baruch son of Neriah did all that the prophet Jeremiah had commanded him: he read from the book the words of the Lord, in the house of the Lord.

In the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month (around November-December), a fast before the Lord was proclaimed for all the people of Jerusalem and for all who came from the towns of Judah.

Then Baruch read from the book the words of Jeremiah, in the house of the Lord, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the secretary, in the upper court, at the entrance of the New Gate of the Temple, before all the people.
Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of the Lord read from the book.

He went down to the king's palace, to the secretary's chamber, where all the officials were sitting: Elishama the secretary, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the other officials.
Micaiah reported to them all the words he had heard when Baruch read to the people.

Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to say to Baruch: 'Take the scroll you read to the people, and come.' Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll and went to them.
They said to him: 'Sit down and read it to us.' Baruch read it to them.
When they had heard all these words, they looked at one another in alarm and said to Baruch: 'We must report all this to the king.'
Then they questioned Baruch: 'Tell us how you wrote all these words at his dictation.'
Baruch answered them: 'He dictated all these words to me from his own mouth, and I wrote them in the book with ink.'
Then the officials said to Baruch: 'Go and hide, you and Jeremiah; let no one know where you are.'
Then, leaving the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the secretary, they went to the king in the court and reported the whole matter to him.
The king sent Jehudi to fetch the scroll. Jehudi took it from the chamber of Elishama the secretary and read it to the king and to all the officials standing around him.
The king was sitting in his winter apartments, for it was the ninth month, and a brazier was burning before him.
Each time Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king would cut them off with the scribe's knife and throw them into the fire of the brazier, until the whole scroll was consumed in it.
Neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words was afraid or tore their garments.
Even though Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah had begged the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them.
The king then ordered Jerahmeel the king's son, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the secretary and Jeremiah the prophet; but the Lord kept them hidden.
After the king had burned the scroll containing the words Baruch had written at Jeremiah's dictation, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah:
Take another scroll and write on it all the words that were in the first, the one Jehoiakim, king of Judah, burned.

And you shall say to Jehoiakim, king of Judah: Thus says the Lord: You have burned this scroll, saying, 'Why have you written in it that the king of Babylon will surely come and ravage this land and wipe out man and beast from it?'

Therefore, thus says the Lord concerning Jehoiakim, king of Judah: None of his line shall sit on the throne of David; his corpse shall be thrown out, exposed to the heat of the day and the frost of the night.

I will punish him, his descendants, and his servants for their guilt; I will bring on them, on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and on the men of Judah all the disaster I threatened against them, though they would not listen.

So Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the secretary, who wrote on it, at Jeremiah's dictation, all the words of the book Jehoiakim, king of Judah, had burned; and many similar words were added to them.
King Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned in place of Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim: it was Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, who had made him king over the land of Judah.
Neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land listened to the words the Lord had spoken through the prophet Jeremiah.
King Zedekiah sent Jucal son of Shelemiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah to say to the prophet Jeremiah: 'Please intercede for us with the Lord our God.'
Jeremiah was still coming and going among the people; he had not yet been put in prison.
The army of Pharaoh had come out of Egypt; on hearing the news, the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem had withdrawn from it.
Then the word of the Lord came to the prophet Jeremiah:
Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: This is what you shall say to the king of Judah who sent you to consult me: The army of Pharaoh, which came out to help you, is going to return home to Egypt.
And the Chaldeans will come back to fight this city; they will take it and burn it.
Thus says the Lord: Do not deceive yourselves, saying, 'The Chaldeans have left for good.' For they will not leave.
Even if you struck down the whole army of the Chaldeans fighting against you, so that only the wounded remained, each would rise from his tent to come and burn this city.
Now while the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of the army of Pharaoh,
Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin to receive his share of property there, among the people.
But when he reached the Benjamin Gate, the captain of the guard, a certain Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah, arrested the prophet Jeremiah, saying: 'You are deserting to the Chaldeans!'
Jeremiah answered: 'That is false, I am not deserting to the Chaldeans!' But Irijah would not listen to him; he arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
The officials, furious with Jeremiah, had him beaten and imprisoned in the house of Jonathan the scribe, which they had turned into a prison.
Jeremiah went down into the vaulted dungeon and stayed there many days.
Then King Zedekiah sent for him. He questioned him secretly in his palace: 'Is there any word from the Lord?' Jeremiah answered: 'Yes,' and added: 'You shall be handed over to the king of Babylon.'
Jeremiah went on to say to King Zedekiah: 'How have I sinned against you, your servants, or this people, that you have put me in prison?
Where now are your prophets who told you: The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land?
Now hear me, my lord the king: let my plea find favor before you. Do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, where I would die.'

King Zedekiah ordered that Jeremiah be kept in the court of the guard and given each day a loaf of bread from the Bakers' Street, until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard.
Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words Jeremiah was speaking to all the people:

'Thus says the Lord: Whoever stays in this city shall die by sword, famine, or plague; but whoever goes out and surrenders to the Chaldeans shall live: he shall escape with his life as spoils, and he shall live.
Thus says the Lord: This city shall be handed over to the army of the king of Babylon, and he will take it.'

Then the officials said to the king: 'Let this man be put to death! He is discouraging the warriors who remain in the city, and all the people, by speaking such words to them. This man does not seek the welfare of this people, but their ruin.'
King Zedekiah answered: 'He is in your hands, for the king can do nothing against you.'

So they took Jeremiah and lowered him into the cistern of Malchiah the king's son, in the court of the guard; they let him down with ropes. There was no water, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mud.
Ebed-melech, a Cushite, a eunuch of the royal palace, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the cistern. The king was then sitting at the Benjamin Gate.
Ebed-melech went out of the palace and said to the king:

'My lord the king, these men have done wrong in the way they have treated the prophet Jeremiah; they have thrown him into the cistern, where he will die of hunger, for there is no more bread in the city.'
Then the king gave this order to Ebed-melech the Cushite: 'Take thirty men with you and pull the prophet Jeremiah up from the cistern before he dies.'
Ebed-melech took the men with him, went into the palace, to a place beneath the treasury, took some old rags and worn-out clothes, and let them down by ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern.
Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah: 'Put these rags and worn-out clothes under your armpits, under the ropes.' Jeremiah did so.
They pulled him up with the ropes and lifted him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard.
King Zedekiah sent for the prophet Jeremiah and had him brought to the third entrance of the house of the Lord. The king said to him: 'I have a question to ask you; hide nothing from me.'
Jeremiah answered Zedekiah: 'If I answer you, will you not put me to death? And if I advise you, you will not listen to me.'
King Zedekiah swore this oath to Jeremiah in secret: 'As the Lord lives, who has given us this life, I will not put you to death, nor will I hand you over to these men who seek your life.'

Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: If you go out and surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, you shall escape with your life, this city shall not be burned, and you shall live, you and your household.
But if you do not go out and surrender to the officers of the king of Babylon, this city shall be handed over to the Chaldeans, who will burn it, and you yourself shall not escape them.'
King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah: 'I dread the Judeans who have deserted to the Chaldeans: I may be handed over to them, and they will mock me.'
Jeremiah answered: 'You will not be handed over. Obey, then, the voice of the Lord in what I tell you: all will go well for you, and you shall escape with your life.
But if you refuse to go out, this is what the Lord has revealed to me:

all the women left in the palace of the king of Judah shall be led out to the officers of the king of Babylon, and they shall say: Your friends deceived you and prevailed over you; your feet sank in the mud, and they slipped away.
All your wives and children shall be led out to the Chaldeans, and you yourself shall not escape them: you shall be seized by the king of Babylon, and this city shall be burned.'
Zedekiah said to Jeremiah: 'Let no one know anything of this conversation, and you shall not die.
If the officials hear that I spoke with you and come to ask you: Tell us what you said to the king and what the king said to you, hide nothing from us, or we will put you to death,
you shall answer them: I laid my plea before the king, that he not send me back to the house of Jonathan, where I would die.'
All the officials did indeed come to question Jeremiah; he answered them exactly as the king had instructed. So they let him alone, for the conversation had not been overheard.
So Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard until the day Jerusalem was taken, and he was still there when Jerusalem was taken.
In the ninth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah, in the tenth month (around December-January), Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came with all his army to besiege Jerusalem.
In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, on the ninth day of the fourth month (around June-July), a breach was opened in the city.

All the officers of the king of Babylon entered and took their seats at the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, keeper of the treasury, Nebo-sarsekim, chief of the eunuchs, Nergal-sharezer, chief of the magi, and all the other officers of the king of Babylon.

When Zedekiah, king of Judah, and all his warriors saw them, they fled, leaving the city by night by way of the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls; they took the road toward the Jordan plain.

But the army of the Chaldeans pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They captured him and brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, who pronounced sentence on him.
At Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; he also slaughtered all the nobles of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him with two bronze chains to take him to Babylon.
The Chaldeans burned the royal palace and the houses of the people and tore down the walls of Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards, deported to Babylon the rest of the people left in the city, the deserters who had gone over to him, and the rest of the artisans.
Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards, left in the land of Judah some of the poorest, who owned nothing, and gave them vineyards and fields that day.
Concerning Jeremiah, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had given this order to Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards:
'Take him, look after him, do him no harm, but deal with him as he asks you.'
Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards, Nebushazban, chief of the eunuchs, Nergal-sharezer, chief of the magi, and all the nobles of the king of Babylon
sent for Jeremiah from the court of the guard and entrusted him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, to take him home. And Jeremiah dwelt among the people.
The word of the Lord had come to Jeremiah, while he was confined in the court of the guard:

Go and say to Ebed-melech the Cushite: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am about to carry out my words against this city, for disaster and not for good; on that day you shall see it with your own eyes.
But you, I will deliver you on that day, oracle of the Lord; you shall not be handed over to the men you dread.
Yes, I will let you escape; you shall not fall by the sword: you shall escape with your life as spoils, because you have put your trust in me, oracle of the Lord.

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, after Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards, had released him from Ramah, having found him bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah who were being deported to Babylon.
The chief of the guards took Jeremiah and said to him: 'The Lord your God had foretold this disaster against this place,
and he has brought it about; the Lord has done as he had said, because you sinned against him and did not obey his voice. That is why this has happened to you.

Today I am freeing you from the chains on your wrists. If you wish to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you; if you do not wish to come with me to Babylon, stay. See, the whole land is before you: go wherever you please.'

As Jeremiah was slow to leave, he added: 'Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has set over the towns of Judah, and dwell with him among the people; or go wherever you wish.' The chief of the guards gave him provisions and a gift, then let him go.
Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, and dwelt with him among the people who remained in the land.

All the officers of the troops who were in the countryside, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam governor of the land and had entrusted to him the men, women, children, and the poorest of the land who had not been deported to Babylon.

They came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan swore to them and to their men: 'Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans; settle in the land, serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.

As for me, I will remain at Mizpah to represent you before the Chaldeans who come to us. But you, gather the wine, the fruit, and the oil, put them in your storehouses, and live in the towns you occupy.'

Likewise, all the Judeans who were in Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom, and in other lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah and had appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan.
Then all these Judeans came back from all the places to which they had been scattered, reached the land of Judah, came to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and gathered wine and fruit in abundance.
Now Johanan son of Kareah and all the officers of the troops who were in the countryside came to Gedaliah at Mizpah
and said to him: 'Do you know that Baalis, king of the Ammonites, has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to assassinate you?' But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Then Johanan son of Kareah said secretly to Gedaliah at Mizpah: 'Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah, with no one knowing. Why should he take your life? All the Judeans gathered around you would be scattered, and what remains of Judah would perish.'
But Gedaliah son of Ahikam answered Johanan son of Kareah: 'Do not do this: what you say about Ishmael is false.'

In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, of royal blood, one of the king's nobles, came with ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. As they were eating together at Mizpah,
Ishmael son of Nethaniah rose with his ten men and struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan with the sword. Thus he killed the one the king of Babylon had appointed governor of the land,
along with all the Judeans who were with him at Mizpah, and the Chaldean soldiers who were there.
On the day after the murder of Gedaliah, when no one yet knew of it,
eighty men arrived from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria, their beards shaved, their clothes torn, their bodies gashed; they were bringing offerings and incense for the house of the Lord.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he walked. When he reached them, he said: 'Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam.'
But as soon as they had entered the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and his men slaughtered them and threw them into the cistern.
Ten of them, however, said to Ishmael: 'Do not kill us, for we have hidden stores of wheat, barley, oil, and honey in the fields.' So he held back and did not kill them, unlike their companions.

The cistern into which Ishmael threw all the corpses of the men he had killed on account of Gedaliah was the one King Asa had dug in the face of Baasha, king of Israel; Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with corpses.

Then Ishmael led away captive all the rest of the people at Mizpah, the king's daughters and all those whom Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards, had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah led them away as prisoners and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.
Johanan son of Kareah and all the officers of the troops who were with him heard of all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done.
They mustered their men and set out to fight Ishmael son of Nethaniah; they caught up with him near the great pool of Gibeon.
When all the captives held by Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the officers of the troops with him, they rejoiced.
All those whom Ishmael had led captive from Mizpah turned back and went over to Johanan son of Kareah.
But Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men and fled to the Ammonites.

Johanan son of Kareah and all the officers of the troops with him took charge of all the rest of the people whom Ishmael son of Nethaniah had led away from Mizpah after killing Gedaliah: warriors, women, children, and court officials, whom they brought back from Gibeon.
They set out and stopped at the caravansary of Chimham, near Bethlehem, intending to go on to Egypt,
away from the Chaldeans, whom they dreaded, for Ishmael son of Nethaniah had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed governor of the land.

titres.titre: Stay in the land, do not flee to Egypt

versets.t: Then all the officers of the troops, with Johanan son of Kareah and Azariah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, approached

and said to the prophet Jeremiah: 'Let our plea find favor before you. Intercede for us with the Lord your God, on behalf of all this remnant of Judah; for from many, we are now reduced to a few, as you see with your own eyes.
May the Lord your God show us the way we should go and what we should do.'
The prophet Jeremiah answered them: 'I have heard you. I will pray to the Lord your God as you ask, and whatever the Lord answers you I will make known to you, hiding nothing from you.'
Then they said to Jeremiah: 'May the Lord be a true and faithful witness against us, if we do not act in everything according to the word the Lord your God sends you to give us.
Whether it is pleasant or not, we will obey the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may go well with us for having obeyed the voice of the Lord our God.'
At the end of ten days, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah.
He called Johanan son of Kareah, all the officers of the troops who were with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest,
and said to them: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to present your plea:
If you stay quietly in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down, I will plant you and not uproot you, for I relent of the harm I have done to you.
Do not fear the king of Babylon, of whom you are afraid; do not fear him, oracle of the Lord, for I am with you to save you and rescue you from his hand.
I will win you his compassion: he will have pity on you and let you return to your own soil.
But if you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' thus refusing to obey the voice of the Lord your God,
if you say, 'No! We will go to Egypt, where we shall see no more war, where we shall hear no more the trumpet, where we shall no longer hunger for bread, and there we will live,'
then hear the word of the Lord, remnant of Judah! Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: If you are resolved to go to Egypt and settle there,
the sword you dread shall overtake you there, in the land of Egypt, and the famine you fear shall pursue you there, and there you shall die.
All the men resolved to go to Egypt and settle there shall die by sword, famine, and plague; none of them shall survive or escape the disaster I am going to bring on them.

For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Just as my anger and my wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my wrath will be poured out on you when you enter Egypt; you shall become an object of cursing, horror, imprecation, and shame, and you shall never see this place again.
Remnant of Judah, the Lord tells you: Do not go to Egypt! Know well that I warn you solemnly today.
You have deceived yourselves by sending me to the Lord your God, saying, 'Intercede for us with the Lord our God; whatever the Lord our God says, tell it to us, and we will do it.'
I have told it to you today, but you have not obeyed the voice of the Lord your God, nothing of what he sent me to tell you.
So know well now: by sword, famine, and plague you shall die, in the place where you wish to go and settle.
When Jeremiah had finished telling all the people all the words of the Lord their God, all that the Lord their God had charged him to convey to them,
Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah: 'You are lying! The Lord our God did not send you to tell us: Do not go to settle in Egypt.
It is Baruch son of Neriah who is inciting you against us, to hand us over to the Chaldeans, to have us put to death or deported to Babylon.'
So Johanan son of Kareah, all the officers of the troops, and all the people refused to obey the voice of the Lord, who was commanding them to stay in the land of Judah.
Johanan son of Kareah and all the officers of the troops took all the remnant of Judah, those who had come back from all the nations to which they had been scattered, to settle in the land of Judah:

men, women, children, the king's daughters, and all those whom Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards, had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, along with the prophet Jeremiah and Baruch son of Neriah.
They entered Egypt, disobeying the voice of the Lord, and reached Tahpanhes.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah at Tahpanhes:
Take some large stones and hide them, before the eyes of the men of Judah, in the mortar of the brick terrace at the entrance of Pharaoh's palace at Tahpanhes.

Then say to them: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am going to send for my servant Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon; I will set his throne on these stones I have hidden, and he will spread his canopy over them.
He will come and strike Egypt: to death, those destined for death; to captivity, those destined for captivity; to the sword, those destined for the sword.

I will set fire to the temples of the gods of Egypt; he will burn them and carry off their idols. He will wrap himself in Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak, and then depart from there in peace.
He will shatter the obelisks of the temple of the Sun in Egypt, and burn down the temples of the gods of Egypt.

titres.titre: Against the idolatry of the Judeans in Egypt

versets.t: The word that came to Jeremiah for all the Judeans settled in Egypt, at Migdol, at Tahpanhes, at Memphis, and in the region of Pathros:
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: You have seen all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the towns of Judah; today they lie in ruins, without inhabitants,
because of the evil they committed to provoke me, going to offer incense and homage to other gods whom neither they, nor you, nor your fathers had known.
I sent you all my servants the prophets, again and again, to tell you: Do not commit this abomination that I hate.
But they did not listen or incline their ear to turn from their wickedness and cease offering incense to other gods.
So my indignation and my anger were poured out, blazing through the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, now in ruins and desolate.

And now, thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, the God of Israel: Why do you bring on yourselves this great evil? You are exposing yourselves to being cut off from the midst of Judah, men and women, children and infants, until not one of you is left,

provoking me by the work of your hands, offering incense to other gods in this land of Egypt where you have come to settle! You are rushing to your ruin, and you will become an object of cursing and shame among all the peoples of the earth.
Have you forgotten the crimes of your fathers, those of the kings of Judah, those of their wives, your own crimes and those of your wives, committed in the land of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem?
To this day they have felt neither remorse nor fear; they have not followed my law or my commandments, which I set before you and your fathers.
Therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am setting my face against you, for disaster, to cut off all Judah.

I will take the remnant of Judah, those who turned their eyes toward Egypt to settle there: they shall all perish there, by sword and famine; small and great, they shall die; they shall become an object of execration, horror, cursing, and shame.
I will punish those living in Egypt as I punished Jerusalem, by sword, famine, and plague.

Of the remnant of Judah that came to settle in Egypt, none shall escape or survive to return to the land of Judah, to which they long so deeply to return: they shall not return, except a few fugitives.
Then all the men who knew that their wives were offering incense to other gods, all the women gathered in a great crowd, and all the people settled in Egypt, at Pathros, answered Jeremiah:
'As for the word you have spoken to us in the name of the Lord, we will not listen to you.

We will rather do all that we have promised: offer incense to the queen of heaven and pour out libations to her, as we did, we and our fathers, our kings and our officials, in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. We had bread in plenty then; we were well off and knew no misfortune.
But since we stopped offering incense to the queen of heaven and pouring out libations to her, we have lacked everything and perished by sword and famine.'
And the women added: 'When we offer incense to the queen of heaven and pour out libations to her, is it without our husbands' knowledge that we make cakes in her image and pour out libations to her?'
Then Jeremiah answered all the people, the men, the women, all those who had spoken to him in this way:

'That incense you burned in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, you and your fathers, your kings and your officials, together with the people of the land, did the Lord not remember it? Did it not rise up to his heart?

The Lord could no longer bear it, faced with the wickedness of your deeds and the abominations you were committing; that is why your land has become a desolate, cursed ruin, without inhabitants, as it is today.
It is because you offered that incense, sinned against the Lord, and refused to obey his voice, his law, his statutes, and his decrees, that this disaster has struck you, as it is today.'
Then Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women: 'Hear the word of the Lord, all you men of Judah who are in Egypt.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: You and your wives have said with your mouths and done with your hands: Yes, we will fulfill the vows we made to offer incense to the queen of heaven and to pour out libations to her. Well then, keep your vows, carry them out to the full!

But hear the word of the Lord, all you men of Judah living in Egypt: Behold, I swear by my great name, says the Lord: my name shall no longer be pronounced throughout Egypt by the mouth of any man of Judah saying: As the Lord God lives!
Behold, I am watching over them for disaster and not for good; all the men of Judah who are in Egypt shall perish by sword and famine, until they are wiped out.
Those who escape the sword, few in number, shall return from Egypt to the land of Judah; and all the remnant of Judah that came to settle in Egypt shall know whose word comes true, mine or theirs.
This shall be the sign for you, oracle of the Lord, that I will punish you in this place, so that you may know that my words will surely come true against you, for disaster:

Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am going to hand over Pharaoh Hophra, king of Egypt, to his enemies and to those who seek his life, just as I handed over Zedekiah, king of Judah, to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life.'
The word that the prophet Jeremiah spoke to Baruch son of Neriah, when he wrote these words in a book at Jeremiah's dictation, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah:
Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning you, Baruch.
You say: 'Woe is me! The Lord adds grief to my sorrow; I am worn out with groaning and find no rest.'
This is what you shall say to him: Thus says the Lord: What I built, I am tearing down; what I planted, I am uprooting; and this holds for the whole land.
And you, would you seek great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For behold, I am bringing disaster on all flesh, oracle of the Lord; but to you I will grant your life as spoils, wherever you go.

titres.titre: Against Egypt: the defeat at Carchemish

versets.t: The word of the Lord that came to the prophet Jeremiah concerning the nations.

On Egypt. Against the army of Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt, which was near the Euphrates, at Carchemish, and which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, defeated in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
Ready the buckler and the shield, advance for battle!
Harness the horses, mount up, riders! Take your positions, helmets on! Polish the spears, put on the breastplates!
What do I see? They are struck with terror, they are falling back! Their warriors are beaten down, they flee without looking back: terror is everywhere! oracle of the Lord.
Let not the swiftest flee, let not the bravest escape! In the north, on the banks of the Euphrates, they have stumbled, they have fallen.
Who is this rising like the Nile, whose waters surge like torrents?
It is Egypt rising like the Nile, with surging waters. She said: 'I will rise, I will cover the earth, I will destroy the cities and their inhabitants.'
Charge, horses! Chariots, drive on! March out, warriors, Cushites and Libyans who carry the shield, Lydians who bend the bow!

But this day belongs to the Lord, the God of hosts, a day of vengeance when he avenges himself on his enemies. The sword devours and is sated, it drinks its fill of their blood; for it is a sacrifice to the Lord, the God of hosts, in the land of the north, on the banks of the Euphrates.
Go up to Gilead and get balm, virgin daughter Egypt! In vain you multiply remedies: for you there is no healing.
The nations have heard of your shame, your cries of distress fill the earth; for warrior stumbles against warrior, and both fall together.
The word the Lord spoke to the prophet Jeremiah about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, to strike the land of Egypt.
Announce it in Egypt, proclaim it in Migdol, in Memphis, and in Tahpanhes! Say: Take your positions, be ready, for the sword already devours around you!
Why is your mighty god struck down? He did not stand, for the Lord threw him to the ground.
He makes many stumble; they fall one over another and say: 'Get up, let us go back to our own people, to our native land, away from the deadly sword!'
There they cry: 'Pharaoh, king of Egypt, is only noise: he has let the hour slip by!'
As I live, oracle of the King whose name is 'the Lord of hosts': as surely as Tabor towers above the mountains and Carmel above the sea, he is coming.
Pack your baggage for exile, enthroned daughter Egypt, for Memphis shall become a wasteland, burned down, without inhabitants.
Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but from the north a gadfly swoops upon her.

Even her mercenaries in her midst are like fattened calves: they too turn their backs and flee together without resisting, for the day of their disaster has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
Egypt hisses like a fleeing serpent, while they advance in force, axe in hand, like woodcutters.
They cut down her forest, oracle of the Lord, dense as it was, for they are more numerous than locusts, beyond counting.
Daughter Egypt is covered with shame, handed over to a people of the north.
The Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, has said: Behold, I am going to punish Amon of Thebes, together with Pharaoh, Egypt, her gods, her kings, and all who trust in Pharaoh.
I will hand them over to those who seek their lives, to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and his servants. But afterward Egypt shall be inhabited again as in former times, oracle of the Lord.

So you, do not fear, my servant Jacob; do not be dismayed, Israel. For behold, I will save you from the distant land, your offspring from the land of their exile. Jacob shall return, he shall be quiet and at ease, with no one to make him afraid.

You, do not fear, my servant Jacob, oracle of the Lord, for I am with you. I will make an end of all the nations among which I scattered you; but with you I will not make an end: I will discipline you with measure, yet I will by no means leave you unpunished.
The word of the Lord that came to the prophet Jeremiah concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.

Thus says the Lord: Behold, waters are rising from the north; they become an overflowing torrent, they flood the land and all that is in it, the city and its inhabitants. The people cry out, all the inhabitants of the land wail,
at the thunder of the hooves of his stallions, at the rumble of his chariots, at the clatter of his wheels. Fathers no longer turn back for their children, so limp are their hands,
for the day has come to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off the last allies of Tyre and Sidon. Yes, the Lord is about to destroy the Philistines, the remnant of the island of Caphtor.
Gaza has shaved its head, Ashkelon is reduced to silence. You who remain in the plain, how long will you gash yourselves?
Ah, sword of the Lord, when will you find rest? Go back into your sheath, stop, and be still!
But how can it rest, when the Lord has given it his orders? Against Ashkelon and the seacoast, that is where he sends it.

titres.titre: Against Moab: the ruin of the cities
The pride of Moab brought down

versets.t: On Moab. Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Woe to Nebo, for it is ravaged! Kiriathaim is covered with shame, it is captured; the stronghold is covered with shame, it is thrown down.
The glory of Moab is no more! At Heshbon they plot her ruin: 'Come, let us cut her off from among the nations!' You too, Madmen, shall be reduced to silence: the sword is on your trail.
Cries rise from Horonaim: devastation, great ruin!
Moab is broken; her little ones cry out.
On the ascent of Luhith they go up weeping; on the descent of Horonaim the cries of distress are heard.
Flee, save your lives, be like a shrub in the wilderness!
Because you trusted in your works and your treasures, you too shall be captured; Chemosh shall go into exile, with his priests and his officials, all together.
The destroyer shall fall on every city, and none shall escape; the valley shall be ruined, the plateau laid waste, as the Lord has said.
Give wings to Moab, that she may fly away! Her cities shall become a wasteland, without inhabitants.
Cursed be the one who does the work of the Lord carelessly! Cursed be the one who withholds his sword from blood!
From his youth Moab has lived at ease, resting on his dregs, never poured from vessel to vessel, never going into exile. So he has kept his flavor, and his aroma is unchanged.
Therefore, behold, the days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when I will send him men to pour him out: they will empty his vessels and smash his jars.
Then Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, in which it trusted.
How can you say, 'We are warriors, valiant men in battle'?
Moab is ravaged, her cities go up in smoke, the flower of her young men goes down to the slaughter, oracle of the King whose name is the Lord of hosts.
The ruin of Moab is near, her disaster hurries on at great speed.
Mourn for her, all you her neighbors, all you who know her name; say: 'How the strong staff is broken, the glorious scepter!'
Come down from your glory, sit on the parched ground, enthroned daughter Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you, he has ruined your ramparts.
Stand by the road and watch, inhabitant of Aroer; question the fugitive, the woman who escapes; ask: 'What has happened?'
Moab is covered with shame, it is shattered. Wail, cry out! Announce by the Arnon that Moab is ravaged!
Judgment has come on the land of the plateau: on Holon, on Jahzah, on Mephaath,
on Dibon, on Nebo, on Beth-diblathaim,
on Kiriathaim, on Beth-gamul, on Beth-meon,
on Kerioth, on Bozrah, and on all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near.
The horn of Moab is cut off, his arm is broken, oracle of the Lord.
Make him drunk, for he rose up against the Lord! Let Moab wallow in his own vomit and become an object of ridicule in his turn!
Was not Israel an object of ridicule to you? Was he caught among thieves, that you shake your head whenever you speak of him?
Leave the cities, dwell among the rocks, inhabitants of Moab! Be like the dove that nests at the edge of the abyss.
We have heard of the pride of Moab, that immense pride: his loftiness, his arrogance, his insolence, the presumption of his heart.
I know his insolence well, oracle of the Lord, his baseless boasts, his deeds without substance.
Therefore I lament over Moab, over all Moab I cry out; there is groaning for the men of Kir-heres.
More than for Jazer, I weep for you, vine of Sibmah. Your tendrils stretched beyond the sea, they reached the sea of Jazer; on your harvest and your vintage the destroyer has fallen.

Joy and gladness have vanished from the orchards and the land of Moab. I have dried up the wine from the vats; no longer do they tread the grapes with shouts of joy: the shout raised is no shout of joy.
From Heshbon to Elealeh and as far as Jahzah they raise their cry; from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath-shelishiyah, for even the waters of Nimrim are dried up.
I will make an end of Moab, oracle of the Lord, of the one who goes up to the high place and offers incense to his god.
So my heart moans for Moab like a flute; my heart moans like a flute for the men of Kir-heres, for all they had amassed is lost.
Every head is shaved, every beard cut off; all hands are gashed, all loins covered with sackcloth.
On all the roofs of Moab and in her squares there is nothing but lamentation, for I have broken Moab like a vessel no one wants, oracle of the Lord.
How it is shattered! Wail! How shamefully Moab has turned his back! Moab has become the ridicule and the terror of all his neighbors.
For thus says the Lord: Behold, the enemy swoops like an eagle, spreading his wings over Moab.
Kerioth is captured, the strongholds are seized; on that day the heart of Moab's warriors shall be like the heart of a woman in labor.
Moab is wiped out from among the peoples, because he rose up against the Lord.
Terror, pit, and snare are upon you, inhabitant of Moab! oracle of the Lord.
Whoever flees from the terror shall fall into the pit; whoever climbs out of the pit shall be caught in the snare; for I am bringing on Moab the year of his punishment, oracle of the Lord.
In the shadow of Heshbon the exhausted fugitives halt; but a fire has gone out from Heshbon, a flame from the palace of Sihon: it has devoured the brow of Moab, the skull of the sons of tumult.
Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh is lost! Your sons are carried off into exile, your daughters into captivity.
But in the days to come I will restore the fortunes of Moab, oracle of the Lord. Here ends the judgment of Moab.
Against the Ammonites. Thus says the Lord: Has Israel no sons, no heir? Why then has Milcom taken possession of Gad, and his people settled in its towns?

Therefore, behold, the days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when I will sound the battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It shall become a heap of ruins, its villages shall be set on fire, and Israel shall dispossess those who dispossessed him, says the Lord.
Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is ravaged! Cry out, daughters of Rabbah, put on sackcloth, mourn, roam among the sheepfolds; for Milcom goes into exile, with his priests and his officials.
Why do you boast of your valleys, of your fruitful valley, wayward daughter, you who trust in your treasures, saying, 'Who would dare attack me?'
Behold, I am bringing terror upon you from every side, oracle of the Lord, the God of hosts; you shall be driven out, each straight ahead, with no one to rally the fugitives.
But afterward I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites, oracle of the Lord.
Against Edom. Thus says the Lord of hosts: Is there no more wisdom in Teman? Have the prudent run out of counsel? Has their wisdom vanished?
Flee, turn back, hide in the depths of the caves, inhabitants of Dedan! For I am bringing ruin on Esau, at the time I punish him.
If grape-gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings? If thieves came by night, would they not take only their fill?
But I have stripped Esau bare, uncovered his hiding places: he can no longer conceal himself. His offspring is ravaged, his brothers and neighbors too, and he is no more.
Leave your orphans; I will keep them alive, and let your widows trust in me.
For thus says the Lord: Those who were not meant to drink this cup shall surely drink it; and are you the one to go unpunished? No, you shall not go unpunished: you shall drink it, that is certain.
For I swear by myself, oracle of the Lord: Bozrah shall become an object of horror and shame, a ruin and a curse, and all its towns shall be ruins forever.
I have received a message from the Lord, and a herald has been sent among the nations: 'Assemble, march against her, rise up for battle!'
For behold, I make you small among the nations, despised among men.

The terror you inspired has led you astray, along with the pride of your heart, you who dwell in the clefts of the rocks and hold the summit of the hills. Though you build your nest as high as the eagle, from there I will bring you down, oracle of the Lord.
Edom shall become an object of horror; all who pass by shall be aghast and shall hiss at all its wounds.
As at the overthrow of Sodom, Gomorrah, and their neighboring cities, says the Lord, no one shall live there, no one shall settle in it.

Behold, like a lion coming up from the thickets of the Jordan to an ever-green pasture, in an instant I will drive them away from it and set over it whomever I choose. For who is like me? Who would challenge me? What shepherd could stand against me?

Hear then the decision the Lord has made against Edom, the plans he devises against the inhabitants of Teman: surely they shall be dragged off like helpless sheep, and their pasture shall be aghast at their fate.
At the sound of their fall the earth trembles; their cry resounds as far as the Red Sea.
Behold, the enemy rises and takes flight like an eagle, spreading his wings over Bozrah; and on that day the heart of Edom's warriors shall be like the heart of a woman in labor.
Against Damascus. Hamath and Arpad are in confusion, for they have received bad news; they melt with fear, like the tossing sea that cannot be calmed.
Damascus loses courage, she turns to flee, seized with panic; anguish and pangs grip her, like a woman in labor.
How is it that the famous city is not spared, the town of my joy?
So her young men shall fall in her squares, and all her warriors shall perish on that day, oracle of the Lord of hosts.
I will kindle a fire in the walls of Damascus, and it shall devour the palaces of Ben-hadad.
Against Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, defeated. Thus says the Lord: Arise! March against Kedar, ravage the people of the East!
Let their tents and their flocks be seized, their tent-cloths, all their goods and their camels carried off! Let them cry out to them: Terror on every side!

Flee, get away quickly, hide in the depths of the caves, inhabitants of Hazor! oracle of the Lord. For Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, has formed a plan against you, he has devised a scheme against you.
Arise! March against a nation at ease, that dwells in security, oracle of the Lord, without gates or bars, dwelling apart.
Their camels shall be your plunder, their countless herds your spoil. I will scatter to every wind these men with shaven temples, and from every side I will bring ruin upon them, oracle of the Lord.
Hazor shall become a haunt of jackals, a desolation forever; no one shall live there, no one shall settle in it.
The word of the Lord that came to the prophet Jeremiah concerning Elam, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah:
Thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I am going to break the bow of Elam, the mainstay of its might.
I will bring upon Elam four winds from the four corners of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds; there shall be no nation to which the fugitives of Elam do not come.

I will make Elam tremble before its enemies, before those who seek its life; I will bring disaster upon them, the fire of my burning anger, oracle of the Lord, and I will send the sword after them until I have consumed them.
I will set my throne in Elam and destroy from there king and officials, oracle of the Lord.
But in the days to come I will restore the fortunes of Elam, oracle of the Lord.

titres.titre: The punishment of Babylon, the deliverance of Israel

versets.t: The word the Lord spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, through the prophet Jeremiah.

Announce it among the nations, proclaim it, raise a signal! Proclaim it, hide nothing: Babylon is captured! Bel is covered with shame, Merodach is shattered; her idols are covered with shame, her false gods shattered.
For from the north a people is coming up against her: it will make her land a wasteland, without inhabitants; man and beast have fled, they are gone.
In those days and at that time, oracle of the Lord, the sons of Israel shall return, together with the sons of Judah; they shall walk weeping and seek the Lord their God.
They shall ask the way to Zion, their faces turned toward it: 'Come, let us bind ourselves to the Lord by an everlasting covenant that shall never be forgotten!'
My people were a flock of lost sheep; their shepherds led them astray, drawing them off to the mountains; they wandered from mountain to hill, forgetting their fold.
All who found them devoured them, and their enemies said: 'We are not guilty, since they sinned against the Lord, the abode of righteousness, against the Lord, the hope of their fathers.'
Flee from the midst of Babylon, leave the land of the Chaldeans, be like the he-goats leading the flock!

For behold, I am going to rouse against Babylon a coalition of great peoples from the land of the north; they shall array themselves against her, and from there she shall be captured. Their arrows are those of a skilled warrior who never returns empty-handed.
Chaldea shall be plundered; all who plunder her shall have their fill, oracle of the Lord.
Rejoice, exult, you plunderers of my heritage! Frisk like a heifer in the grass, neigh like stallions!
But your mother is covered with shame, she who bore you blushes for confusion. Behold, the last of the nations: a wilderness, a steppe, a parched land.
Because of the wrath of the Lord, she shall no longer be inhabited; she shall be nothing but a desolation; everyone who passes by Babylon shall be aghast and shall hiss at all her wounds.
Array yourselves all around Babylon, all you archers! Shoot at her, spare no arrows, for she has sinned against the Lord.

Raise the battle cry against her on every side! She surrenders, her towers collapse, her walls are thrown down. This is the vengeance of the Lord: take vengeance on her, treat her as she has treated others.
Cut off from Babylon the sower and the reaper who wields the sickle at harvest time. Before the deadly sword, let each return to his own people, let each flee to his own land.
Israel was a sheep hunted by lions. The first devoured her, the king of Assyria; then this other one crushed her bones, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
Therefore, thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am going to punish the king of Babylon and his land, as I punished the king of Assyria.
I will bring Israel back to his pasture: he shall graze on Carmel and Bashan, and satisfy himself on the hills of Ephraim and Gilead.

In those days and at that time, oracle of the Lord, the guilt of Israel shall be sought, and it shall be no more, and the sin of Judah, and it shall not be found; for I will forgive the remnant I have spared.
Go up against the land of Merathaim, against the inhabitants of Pekod! Pursue them, slaughter them, destroy them utterly, oracle of the Lord; do all that I command you.
The noise of battle is in the land, and great destruction!
How is it broken and shattered, the hammer of the whole earth? How has Babylon become an object of horror among the nations?
I set a trap for you, and you were caught, Babylon, without knowing it; you were taken by surprise and seized, for you had defied the Lord.
The Lord has opened his armory and brought out the weapons of his wrath; for the Lord, the God of hosts, has a task to accomplish in the land of the Chaldeans.
Come against her from every direction, throw open her granaries, pile her up like heaps of grain, destroy her utterly, let nothing be left of her!
Slaughter all her bulls, let them go down to the slaughter! Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their punishment.
Listen! Fugitives and survivors from the land of Babylon come to announce in Zion the vengeance of the Lord our God, the vengeance for his Temple.

Summon the archers against Babylon, all who bend the bow! Camp around her, let no one escape! Repay her according to her deeds, treat her as she has treated others; for she has defied the Lord, the Holy One of Israel.
Therefore her young men shall fall in her squares, and all her warriors shall perish on that day, oracle of the Lord.
Behold, I am against you, insolent one! oracle of the Lord, the God of hosts; for your day has come, the time when I punish you.
The insolent one shall stumble and fall, with no one to raise her up; I will set fire to her cities, and it shall devour all around her.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: The sons of Israel are oppressed, and with them the sons of Judah; all who deported them hold them fast, refusing to let them go.
But their Redeemer is strong: his name is 'the Lord of hosts'; he will firmly defend their cause, to give rest to the earth and make the inhabitants of Babylon tremble.
A sword against the Chaldeans, oracle of the Lord, against the inhabitants of Babylon, against her officials and her sages!
A sword against her diviners, that they lose their reason! A sword against her warriors, that they tremble!
A sword against her horses and her chariots, against all the mixed rabble in her midst, that they become like women! A sword against her treasures, that they be plundered!
A drought upon her waters, that they dry up! For it is a land of idols, a people crazed by their dread images.
So the beasts of the desert and the jackals shall dwell there, and the ostriches shall make their home there; never again shall she be peopled, never again inhabited, from age to age.
As when God overthrew Sodom, Gomorrah, and their neighboring cities, oracle of the Lord, no one shall live there, no one shall settle in it.
Behold, a people comes from the north, a great nation and many kings arise from the ends of the earth.
They grip bow and javelin, cruel and without pity; their voice roars like the sea; they ride on horses, arrayed like one man for battle, against you, daughter Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard the news, and his hands have gone limp; anguish has seized him, pain like that of a woman in labor.

Behold, like a lion coming up from the thickets of the Jordan to an ever-green pasture, in an instant I will drive them away from it and set over it whomever I choose. For who is like me? Who would challenge me? What shepherd could stand against me?

Hear then the decision the Lord has made against Babylon, the plans he devises against the land of the Chaldeans: surely they shall be dragged off like helpless sheep, and their pasture shall be aghast at their fate.
At the news of Babylon's capture the earth trembles, and a cry resounds among the nations.

titres.titre: The scroll thrown into the Euphrates

versets.t: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am going to rouse against Babylon, against the inhabitants of Chaldea, a destroying wind.
I will send winnowers against Babylon, who will winnow her and empty her land; they will fall upon her from every side, on the day of disaster.
Let the archer bend his bow against the archer, against the one who struts in his breastplate! Do not spare her young men, put her whole army under the ban.
Let the fatally wounded fall in the land of the Chaldeans, the pierced in the streets of Babylon!
For Israel and Judah are not widowed of their God, the Lord of hosts, while the land of the Chaldeans is filled with crimes against the Holy One of Israel.
Flee from the midst of Babylon, let each save his life! Do not perish for her guilt, for this is the time of the Lord's vengeance: he is repaying her what she deserves.
Babylon was a golden cup in the hand of the Lord, making all the earth drunk; the nations drank her wine, and so they went mad.
Suddenly Babylon has fallen, she is broken! Wail over her, get balm for her wound: perhaps she can be healed.
'We tried to heal Babylon, but she is beyond healing. Leave her, let us go, each to his own land, for her judgment reaches to the heavens, it rises to the clouds.'
The Lord has brought forth our vindication; come, let us recount in Zion the work of the Lord our God.

Sharpen the arrows, take up the shields! The Lord has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, for his purpose against Babylon is to destroy her: this is the vengeance of the Lord, the vengeance for his Temple.

Raise the signal against the walls of Babylon, strengthen the siege, post the sentries, set the ambushes! For the Lord has formed a purpose, and he carries out what he said against the inhabitants of Babylon.
You who dwell by many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your plunder.
The Lord of hosts has sworn by himself: I will fill you with men like locusts, and they shall raise the victory shout over you.
It is he who made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, spread out the heavens by his understanding.
When he thunders, the waters gather in the sky; he raises clouds from the ends of the earth, he makes lightning flash for the rain, he brings out the wind from his storehouses.
Every man is stupid, without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idol, for his molten image is a lie, there is no breath in it.
They are nothing, a work of mockery; at the time of their punishment they shall perish.
The portion of Jacob is not like these: he is the one who formed all things; Israel is the tribe of his heritage, and his name is the Lord of hosts.
You are my hammer, my weapon of war: with you I shatter nations, with you I destroy kingdoms;
with you I shatter horse and rider, with you I shatter chariot and driver;
with you I shatter man and woman, with you I shatter old and young, with you I shatter young man and maiden;
with you I shatter shepherd and flock, with you I shatter plowman and team, with you I shatter governors and officials.
But I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea for all the evil they did to Zion, before your eyes, oracle of the Lord.
Behold, I am against you, mountain of destruction that ravages all the earth, oracle of the Lord; I stretch out my hand against you, I roll you down from the crags and make you a burned-out mountain.
No cornerstone or foundation stone shall be taken from you: you shall be a ruin forever, oracle of the Lord.

Raise a signal on the earth, sound the trumpet among the nations! Consecrate the nations against her, summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz! Appoint a marshal against her, send up the horses like a swarm of bristling locusts.
