Consecrate the nations against her: the kings of the Medes, their governors, their officers, and all the lands under their rule.
The earth trembles and writhes, for the Lord's purpose against Babylon is being carried out: to make her land a wasteland, without inhabitants.
The warriors of Babylon have ceased to fight, they stay in their strongholds; their strength is spent, they have become like women. Her dwellings are set on fire, the bars of her gates are broken.
Runner runs to meet runner, and messenger to meet messenger, to tell the king of Babylon that his city is captured on every side,
that the fords are seized, the reed marshes burned, and the warriors gripped with terror.
For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Daughter Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trodden; a little while yet, and the time of her harvest will come.
'He devoured me, he crushed me, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon; he left me like an empty vessel. Like a monster he swallowed me, he filled his belly with my finest morsels, then cast me out.'
'May the violence done to me, may my flesh fall back on Babylon!' the inhabitant of Zion will say. 'May my blood fall back on the inhabitants of Chaldea!' Jerusalem will say.
Therefore, thus says the Lord: Behold, I am taking up your cause and carrying out your vengeance; I will dry up her sea and make her spring run dry.
Babylon shall become a heap of stones, a haunt of jackals, an object of horror and mockery, without inhabitants.
Together they roar like lions, they growl like lion cubs.
While they are inflamed, I will prepare them a banquet, I will make them drunk so that they exult, then they shall fall into an everlasting sleep from which they will never wake, oracle of the Lord.
I will bring them down to the slaughter like lambs, like rams and he-goats.
How Sheshach is captured, the pride of all the earth conquered! How has Babylon become an object of horror among the nations?
The sea has risen over Babylon, it has covered her with the roar of its waves.
Her cities have become an object of horror, a parched and desolate land, where no one lives, where no one passes.
I will punish Bel in Babylon, I will tear from his mouth what he has swallowed, and the nations shall no longer stream to him. The very wall of Babylon has fallen.
Come out from her midst, my people! Let each save his life from the burning anger of the Lord.
Do not let your hearts grow faint, do not be afraid at the rumors that spread through the land: one year a rumor, the next year another; violence in the land, tyrant against tyrant.
Therefore, behold, the days are coming when I will punish the idols of Babylon; all her land shall be covered with shame, and all her slain shall lie in her midst.
The heavens, the earth, and all that is in them shall shout for joy over Babylon, for from the north the destroyers shall come upon her, oracle of the Lord.
Babylon must fall, O slain of Israel, as on account of Babylon the slain of all the earth have fallen.
You who have escaped the sword, go, do not linger! From the distant land, remember the Lord, and let Jerusalem come to mind!
We were covered with shame at hearing the insult, confusion veiled our faces, for strangers had entered the sanctuary of the house of the Lord.
Therefore, behold, the days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when I will punish her idols, and throughout her land the fatally wounded shall groan.
Though Babylon should mount up to the heavens, though she should make her high stronghold unassailable, at my command destroyers would come upon her, oracle of the Lord.
A clamor rises from Babylon, great destruction in the land of the Chaldeans!
For the Lord lays Babylon waste, he silences her great noise; the enemy's waves roar like mighty waters, they make their din resound.
The destroyer has come upon her, upon Babylon; her warriors are captured, their bows are broken, for the Lord is a God who repays each his due: he pays in full.

I will make her officials and her sages drunk, her governors, her magistrates, and her warriors; they shall fall into an everlasting sleep from which they will never wake, oracle of the King whose name is the Lord of hosts.

Thus says the Lord of hosts: The broad walls of Babylon shall be razed to the ground, her high gates set on fire. So the peoples have exhausted themselves for nothing, the nations have toiled only for the fire.

The order that the prophet Jeremiah gave to Seraiah son of Neriah son of Mahseiah, when he went to Babylon with Zedekiah, king of Judah, in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the quartermaster.
Jeremiah had written in a book all the disaster that was to come upon Babylon, all these words written against her.
Jeremiah said to Seraiah: 'When you reach Babylon, see that you read aloud all these words,
and say: Lord, it is you who have foretold, concerning this place, that you would destroy it, that no one would live there, neither man nor beast, and that it would be a ruin forever.
Then, when you have finished reading this book, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates,
saying: So shall Babylon sink, never to rise again from the disaster I am bringing upon her, and her people shall collapse.' Here end the words of Jeremiah.

titres.titre: The fall of Jerusalem and the fate of Zedekiah
The deportations and the pardon of Jeconiah

versets.t: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah, of Libnah.
He did what is evil in the eyes of the Lord, in everything as Jehoiakim had done.
That is why the anger of the Lord came down on Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them out of his presence. Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month (around December-January), Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came with all his army against Jerusalem; they encamped before it and built siege works all around it.
The city remained under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
On the ninth day of the fourth month (around June-July), the famine was so severe in the city that there was no more bread for the people of the land.

A breach was opened in the city. All the warriors fled, leaving by night through the gate between the two walls, near the king's garden, while the Chaldeans surrounded the city, and they took the road toward the plain.
But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, while all his army scattered from him.
They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, who pronounced sentence on him.
At Riblah the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before their father's eyes; he also slaughtered all the officials of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes, bound him with two bronze chains, took him to Babylon, and kept him in prison until the day of his death.

On the tenth day of the fifth month (around July-August), in the nineteenth year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards, in the service of the king of Babylon, entered Jerusalem.
He burned the house of the Lord, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem; he set fire to all the great mansions.
The whole army of the Chaldeans accompanying the chief of the guards tore down the walls surrounding Jerusalem.

Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards, deported some of the poorest of the people, along with the rest of the population left in the city, the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the artisans.
But he left some of the poorest of the land as vinedressers and plowmen.
The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars of the house of the Lord, along with the stands and the bronze Sea that were there, and carried all the bronze to Babylon.
They also took the ash pans, the shovels, the snuffers, the sprinkling bowls, the dishes, and all the bronze utensils used in the worship.
The chief of the guards also took the basins, the censers, the sprinkling bowls, the ash pans, the lampstands, the dishes, and the libation cups, everything of gold and everything of silver.

As for the two pillars, the one Sea, the twelve bronze oxen that supported it, and the stands that King Solomon had made for the house of the Lord, the bronze of all these objects was beyond weighing.
Each pillar was about eight metres high; a cord of about five and a half metres measured its circumference; it was four fingers thick, about seven centimetres, and hollow.
It bore a bronze capital, a little more than two metres high; around the capital ran a lattice and pomegranates, all of bronze. The second pillar was the same, with its pomegranates.
There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides, and a hundred pomegranates in all around the lattice.
The chief of the guards took prisoner Seraiah the high priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold.

In the city he took an officer who commanded the warriors, seven of the king's personal advisers who were found in the city, the secretary of the army commander in charge of conscripting the people of the land, and sixty men of the land who were there.
Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards, took them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
There, at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon had them struck down and put to death. So Judah was deported far from its land.
This is the number of captives carried off by Nebuchadnezzar: in the seventh year, three thousand twenty-three Judeans;
in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, eight hundred thirty-two persons from Jerusalem;
in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan, chief of the guards, deported another seven hundred forty-five Judeans. In all, four thousand six hundred persons.

In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jeconiah, king of Judah, on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month (around February-March), Evil-merodach, king of Babylon, in the year of his accession to the throne, pardoned Jeconiah, king of Judah, and brought him out of prison.
He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat higher than those of the other kings held with him in Babylon.
Jeconiah took off his prison garments and from then on ate at the king's table every day of his life.
The king of Babylon provided for his upkeep, regularly, day by day, until his death, all the days of his life.
How lonely she sits, the city once so full of people! She has become like a widow, she who was great among the nations. A queen among the provinces, she is put to forced labour.
Bitterly she weeps in the night, tears upon her cheeks. Of all her lovers, not one to console her; all her friends have betrayed her, they have become her enemies.
Judah has gone into exile, weighed down with misery and harsh servitude. She dwells among the nations and finds no rest; those who pursued her have overtaken her in the depths of distress.
The roads to Zion are in mourning, for no one comes to her festivals anymore. All her gates are deserted, her priests groan, her young women are afflicted, and she herself is in bitterness.
Her foes have gained the upper hand, her enemies live at ease, for the Lord has afflicted her for her countless sins. Her little children have gone away as captives before the oppressor.
The daughter of Zion has lost all her splendour. Her princes are like stags that find no pasture; they flee, worn out, before their pursuers.

In the days of her misery and wandering, Jerusalem remembers all the treasures she once possessed. Now that her people have fallen into the hands of the enemy, with no one to help her, her foes look on and laugh at her ruin.
Jerusalem has sinned so grievously that she has become an unclean thing. All who honoured her now despise her, for they have seen her nakedness; she herself groans and turns away.
Her defilement clings to the hem of her robe; she gave no thought to her end. Her downfall is astounding, and there is no one to console her. "Look, Lord, on my misery: the enemy triumphs!"
The enemy has laid hands on all her treasures. She has seen nations enter her sanctuary, those nations of whom you had said, "They shall not enter your assembly."
All her people are groaning, searching for bread; they give away their treasures for food, to regain their strength. "Look, Lord, and see how despised I am!"
"All you who pass along the way, look and see: is there any sorrow like the sorrow that crushes me, whom the Lord has struck on the day of his burning anger?
From on high he sent a fire into my bones, and it consumes them. He spread a net for my feet and threw me backward. He has left me desolate, faint all the day long.
Out of my transgressions he has made a yoke; knotted by his hand, they weigh upon my neck and break my strength. The Lord has handed me over to those I cannot withstand.
The Lord has rejected all the mighty men within me. He has summoned an army against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trodden in the winepress the virgin daughter of Judah.
This is why I weep; my eyes, my eyes flow with tears. For he is far from me, the one who would console me and give me back my life. My sons are desolate, for the enemy has prevailed."
Zion stretches out her hands, but there is no one to console her. The Lord has loosed against Jacob his enemies on every side; Jerusalem has become an unclean thing in their midst.
"The Lord is just, for I rebelled against his word. Listen, then, all you peoples, and see my sorrow: my young women and my young men have gone into exile.
I called to my lovers, and they betrayed me. My priests and my elders perished in the city while searching for food to regain their strength.
Look, Lord, on my anguish: my inmost being is in turmoil, my heart recoils within me, for I have grievously rebelled. Outside, the sword bereaves; inside, there is death.

They hear my groaning, but there is no one to console me. All my enemies have learned of my misfortune and rejoice at what you have done. Bring on the day you have proclaimed, and let them become like me!
Let all their wickedness come before you, and deal with them as you have dealt with me for all my sins. For my groans are without number, and my heart is sick."

titres.titre: The anger of the Lord against Zion

versets.t: How the Lord in his anger has covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud! He has cast down from heaven to earth the splendour of Israel, and on the day of his anger he no longer remembered the footstool of his feet.

The Lord has destroyed without pity all the dwellings of Jacob. In his fury he has torn down the strongholds of the daughter of Judah; he has thrown them to the ground, he has profaned the kingdom and its princes.
In the heat of his anger he has broken all the strength of Israel. He has withdrawn his right hand before the enemy, and he has kindled in Jacob a blazing fire that devours all around.

He has bent his bow like an enemy, his right hand has risen like that of an assailant, and he has killed all that was pleasing to the eye. On the tent of the daughter of Zion he has poured out his fury like fire.
The Lord has become like an enemy: he has swallowed up Israel, swallowed up all her palaces, destroyed her strongholds. He has multiplied mourning and lamentation in the daughter of Judah.

He has laid waste his dwelling like the fence of a garden, he has destroyed his place of assembly. The Lord has made festival and sabbath forgotten in Zion; in the heat of his anger he has spurned king and priest.
The Lord has rejected his altar, disdained his sanctuary. He has handed over to the enemy the walls of her palaces; they raised a shout in the house of the Lord as on a day of festival.

The Lord resolved to destroy the rampart of the daughter of Zion. He stretched out the measuring line and did not withdraw his hand until all was laid low; he has put wall and outer wall into mourning: together they collapse.

Her gates have sunk into the ground, he has broken and shattered their bars. Her king and her princes are among the nations; there is no more law, and even her prophets receive no vision from the Lord.
They sit on the ground in silence, the elders of the daughter of Zion. They have thrown dust on their heads and put on sackcloth; the young women of Jerusalem bow their heads to the ground.

My eyes are worn out with weeping, my inmost being is in turmoil, my heart is poured out on the ground at the ruin of the daughter of my people, as children and infants faint in the squares of the city.
They say to their mothers, "Where is bread and wine?" as they faint like the wounded in the squares of the city, breathing out their lives on their mothers' breasts.
What can I say for you? To what can I compare you, daughter of Jerusalem? Who could be your equal to console you, virgin daughter of Zion? For your wound is vast as the sea: who could heal you?
Your prophets had for you visions empty and deceptive. They did not lay bare your guilt, which would have spared you exile; they proclaimed to you oracles hollow and false.
They clap their hands at you, all who pass by; they hiss and shake their heads at the daughter of Jerusalem: "Is this the city that was called perfect in beauty, the joy of all the earth?"
They open their mouths against you, all your enemies; they hiss, they gnash their teeth, they say, "We have swallowed her up! This is the day we waited for; here it is, we see it!"

The Lord has done what he had decided, he has carried out the word he spoke in days of old. He has destroyed without pity, he has made the enemy rejoice over you, he has raised up the strength of your foes.
Their heart cries out to the Lord. O rampart of the daughter of Zion, let your tears run down like a torrent, day and night! Give yourself no relief, let your eyes have no rest!

Arise, cry out in the night, at the start of the watches! Pour out your heart like water before the Lord. Lift up your hands to him for the lives of your little children, who faint from hunger at the corner of every street.
"Look, Lord, and consider: whom have you ever treated like this? Must women eat their own offspring, the children they have borne? Must priest and prophet be slaughtered in the sanctuary of the Lord?
The child and the old man lie on the ground in the streets; my young women and my young men have fallen by the sword. You have killed on the day of your anger, you have slaughtered without pity.

As one summons to a day of festival, you have summoned terrors against me from every side. On the day of the Lord's anger there was neither fugitive nor survivor: those I had borne and raised, my enemy has destroyed."

titres.titre: The afflicted man under the rod of God
Hope in the faithfulness of the Lord
Let us return to the Lord
The prayer answered and the appeal for justice

versets.t: I am the man who has known affliction under the rod of his anger.
He has led me and made me walk in darkness, far from the light.
Against me alone he turns his hand, again and again, all the day long.
He has worn away my flesh and my skin, he has broken my bones.
He has built up against me, he has hemmed me in with bitterness and hardship.
He has made me dwell in darkness, like those long dead.
He has walled me in, I can no longer escape; he has made my chains heavy.
Though I cry out and call for help, he shuts out my prayer.
He has walled up my ways with dressed stone, he has twisted my paths.
He has been to me a bear lying in wait, a lion in ambush.
He has turned my steps aside and torn me to pieces, he has left me desolate.
He has bent his bow and set me up as a target for his arrows.
He has driven into my vitals the arrows of his quiver.
I am the laughingstock of all my people, their song all the day long.
He has filled me with bitterness, he has made me drink wormwood.
He has broken my teeth on gravel, he has ground me into the ashes.
My soul is deprived of peace, I have forgotten what happiness is.
And I said, "My strength is gone, and my hope in the Lord."
Remember my misery and my wandering, the wormwood and the poison.
My soul remembers it without ceasing, and it sinks within me.
This is what I call to mind, and therefore I have hope:
The faithful love of the Lord is not exhausted, his mercies are not at an end.
They are new every morning. Great is your faithfulness!
"The Lord is my portion," says my soul; "therefore I hope in him."
The Lord is good to those who hope in him, to the soul that seeks him.
It is good to wait in silence for the salvation of the Lord.
It is good for a man to bear the yoke in his youth.
Let him sit apart and keep silent, when the Lord lays it upon him.
Let him put his mouth in the dust: perhaps there is still hope.
Let him offer his cheek to the one who strikes him, let him be filled with insults.
For the Lord does not cast off forever.
Though he afflicts, he has compassion, so great is his faithful love.
For it is not from his heart that he humbles and afflicts the children of men.
When all the captives of a land are crushed underfoot,
when a man is denied his right before the Most High,
when someone is wronged in his lawsuit, does the Lord not see it?
Who has spoken, and it came to pass, unless the Lord had ordained it?
Is it not from the mouth of the Most High that both evil and good come?
Why should any living man complain? Let each one complain rather of his own sins.
Let us examine our conduct and search it out, and return to the Lord.
Let us lift up our hearts, with our hands, to God who is in the heavens:
"We have sinned, we have rebelled, and you have not forgiven.
Wrapped in anger, you have pursued us; you have killed without sparing.
You have covered yourself with a cloud, so that no prayer could pass through.
You have made us sweepings and refuse in the midst of the peoples."
They open their mouths against us, all our enemies.
Terror and the pit have been our lot, devastation and ruin.
My eyes flow with streams of tears at the ruin of the daughter of my people.
My eyes weep without ceasing, without relief,
until the Lord looks down and sees from the heavens.
What my eyes see brings pain to my soul, because of all the daughters of my city.
They have hunted me like a bird, those who hate me without cause.
They tried to silence me in the pit, they hurled stones at me.
The waters closed over my head; I said, "I am lost!"
I called on your name, Lord, from the depths of the pit.
You heard my voice; do not close your ear to my sigh, to my cry.
You drew near on the day I called to you; you said, "Do not be afraid."
Lord, you took up my cause, you redeemed my life.
You have seen, Lord, the wrong done to me: give me justice!
You have seen all their spite, all their schemes against me.
You have heard their insults, Lord, all their schemes against me,
the words of my adversaries, what they mutter against me all the day long.
Whether they sit or stand, look: I am their song.
You will repay them what they deserve, Lord, according to the work of their hands.
You will harden their hearts; may your curse be upon them!
You will pursue them in anger and blot them out from under the heavens of the Lord.

titres.titre: The guilt of the prophets and the priests
Edom and the end of the ordeal

versets.t: How the gold has grown dim, how the pure gold has changed! The sacred stones are scattered at the corner of every street.
The precious sons of Zion, once worth their weight in fine gold, are now reckoned as clay pots, the work of a potter's hands.
Even the jackals offer the teat and nurse their young; but the daughter of my people has become cruel, like the ostriches of the desert.
The tongue of the infant sticks to the roof of its mouth for thirst; little children beg for bread, and no one gives them any.
Those who once ate delicacies now faint in the streets; those raised in purple now embrace the dung heap.
The guilt of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom, which was overthrown in an instant, with no hand laid upon her.
Her princes were brighter than snow, whiter than milk; their bodies more ruddy than coral, their beauty cut like sapphire.
Now they are darker than soot, unrecognized in the streets; their skin clings to their bones, dry as wood.
Happier the victims of the sword than the victims of famine, who waste away little by little, exhausted for lack of the fruits of the field.
With their own hands, tender-hearted women have cooked their children; they served as food for them, in the ruin of the daughter of my people.
The Lord has spent his fury, he has poured out the heat of his anger; he has kindled in Zion a fire that has devoured her foundations.
They would not have believed it, the kings of the earth and all the inhabitants of the world, that the adversary, the enemy, would pass through the gates of Jerusalem.
It was because of the sins of her prophets, the offenses of her priests, who shed the blood of the just in her midst.
They wandered like blind men in the streets, defiled with blood, so that no one could touch their garments.
"Away, unclean!" people cried at them. "Away, away, do not touch him!" They fled and wandered, and it was said among the nations, "They shall not stay here."
The face of the Lord has scattered them, he looks on them no more. No regard was shown to the priests, no pity to the old men.
And we, our eyes wore out watching for help that never came. From our towers we looked out for a nation unable to save.
They dogged our steps, so that we could no longer walk in our squares. Our end drew near, our days were numbered; yes, our end had come.
Those who pursued us were swifter than the eagles of the sky; they hunted us down on the mountains, lay in wait for us in the desert.
The breath of our life, the anointed of the Lord, was caught in their traps, he of whom we said, "In his shadow we shall live among the nations."
Rejoice and exult, daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz! To you too the cup will pass: you will drink yourself drunk and strip yourself bare.
Your punishment is complete, daughter of Zion: he will exile you no more. But he will punish your guilt, daughter of Edom, he will lay bare your sins.
Remember, Lord, what has happened to us; look and see our humiliation.
Our inheritance has passed to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
We have become orphans, fatherless; our mothers are like widows.
We drink our own water for a price, and our wood we must pay for.
We are pursued, the yoke on our necks; worn out, we have no rest.
We stretch out our hands to Egypt and to Assyria, to have enough bread.
Our fathers sinned, and they are no more, and we bear the weight of their guilt.
Slaves rule over us, and no one snatches us from their hands.
We risk our lives to find our bread, under the threat of the sword of the desert.
Our skin burns like an oven, so fierce is the fever of hunger.
Women have been violated in Zion, young women in the towns of Judah.
With their own hands they have hanged princes; they showed no regard for the old men.
Young men have carried the millstone, children have stumbled under loads of wood.
The elders have deserted the city gate, the young men have ceased their songs.
Joy has left our hearts, our dancing has turned to mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!
This is why our heart is sick, why our eyes grow dim:
the mountain of Zion is desolate, and jackals prowl over it.
But you, Lord, reign forever; your throne endures from age to age.
Why would you forget us forever, forsake us for so many days?
Bring us back to you, Lord, and we will return; renew our days as of old.
Or have you utterly rejected us, and raged against us beyond measure?

titres.titre: The book read to the exiles in Babylon

versets.t: These are the words of the book that Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, son of Zedekiah, son of Hasadiah, son of Hilkiah, wrote in Babylon,
in the fifth year, on the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans had captured Jerusalem and burned it.
Baruch read the words of this book aloud before Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and before all the people who had come to hear the reading,
before the nobles and the sons of the king, before the elders, before all the people, from the least to the greatest, all who were living in Babylon by the river Sud.
When they heard it, they wept, fasted, and prayed before the Lord.
Then they collected money, each according to his means,
and sent it to Jerusalem, to the priest Jehoiakim son of Hilkiah, son of Shallum, to the other priests, and to all the people who were with him in Jerusalem.

At that time Baruch had recovered the vessels of the house of the Lord, which had been carried off from the Temple, to send them back to the land of Judah, on the tenth day of the month of Sivan (around May-June): the silver vessels that Zedekiah son of Josiah, king of Judah, had had made,
after Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had deported from Jerusalem to Babylon Jeconiah, the princes, the prisoners, the nobles, and the people of the land.

They wrote: 'Here we are sending you money. Buy with this money victims for the burnt offerings and the sin offerings, along with incense; prepare offerings and present them on the altar of the Lord our God.
Pray for the life of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and for the life of Belshazzar his son, that their days on earth may be like the days of heaven.

Then the Lord will give us strength and make the light shine in our eyes: we shall live under the shadow of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and under the shadow of Belshazzar his son; we shall serve them for a long time and find favor in their sight.
Pray also for us to the Lord our God, for we have sinned against him, and to this day his anger and his wrath have not turned away from us.
Read out, finally, this book that we are sending you, so that it may be read aloud in the house of the Lord, on the days of festival and assembly.'
You shall say: To the Lord our God belongs justice, and to us shame upon our faces, as it is this day, to us the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
to our kings and our princes, to our priests and our prophets, and to our ancestors.
We have sinned before the Lord,
we have disobeyed him, we have not listened to his voice, so as to walk according to the commandments he set before us.
From the day the Lord brought our ancestors out of the land of Egypt until this day, we have been rebellious against the Lord our God, and in our folly we have turned away from his voice.

That is why the calamities and the curse have clung to us that the Lord proclaimed through his servant Moses, on the day he brought our ancestors out of Egypt to give us a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day.
We have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, despite all the words of the prophets he sent us.
Each of us has followed the inclination of his own evil heart, serving foreign gods and doing what is evil in the sight of the Lord our God.

That is why the Lord our God carried out the word he had spoken against us, against our judges who governed Israel, against our kings and our leaders, and against all the people of Israel and of Judah.
He brought upon us such great calamities that nowhere under heaven had anything like what happened to Jerusalem ever occurred, in accordance with what is written in the law of Moses:
we came to eat, one the flesh of his son, another the flesh of his daughter.
He handed them over to the power of all the kingdoms around us, to make them an object of shame and horror among all the peoples where the Lord has scattered us.
We were brought low instead of ruling, because we sinned against the Lord our God by not listening to his voice.
To the Lord our God belongs justice; to us and to our ancestors shame upon our faces, as it is this day.
All these calamities with which the Lord had threatened us have come upon us,
and we did not entreat the Lord to turn each of us away from the thoughts of our evil heart.
So the Lord kept watch over the calamity and brought it upon us; for the Lord is just in all that he has commanded us,
and we did not listen to his voice by following the precepts he set before us.

And now, Lord, God of Israel, you who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, with signs and wonders, with your great power and outstretched arm, you who made yourself a name to this day:
we have sinned, we have been ungodly, we have done wrong, Lord our God, against all your commandments.
Let your anger turn away from us, for we are only a small remnant among the nations where you have scattered us.
Hear, Lord, our prayer and our supplication; deliver us for your own sake, and grant us favor in the sight of those who deported us,
so that all the earth may know that you are the Lord our God, since your name has been invoked over Israel and over his descendants.
Look down, Lord, from your holy Dwelling, and think of us; incline your ear and hear us.
Open your eyes and see: it is not the dead in the realm of the dead, whose breath has left their bodies, who give glory and justice to the Lord;
it is the one weighed down by the greatness of his misery, who walks bent and feeble, whose eyes are failing and whose soul is hungry, it is he who gives you glory and justice, Lord.
It is not on account of the righteousness of our ancestors and our kings that we pour out our supplication before you, Lord our God.
For you poured out on us your anger and your fury, as you had announced through your servants the prophets, saying:
Thus says the Lord: 'Bend your shoulders and your neck, serve the king of Babylon, and you shall remain in the land I gave to your ancestors.
But if you do not listen to the voice of the Lord by serving the king of Babylon,
I will silence in the cities of Judah and in Jerusalem the sounds of joy and gladness, the song of the bridegroom and the bride, and the whole land will become a desert without inhabitants.'

We did not listen to your voice by serving the king of Babylon, and you carried out the words you had spoken through your servants the prophets: that the bones of our kings and of our ancestors would be dragged from their tombs.
And indeed, they have been thrown out to the heat of the day and the cold of the night. Our ancestors died in cruel suffering, by famine, by the sword, and by plague.
You have reduced to its present state the house that bears your name, because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
Yet you have dealt with us, Lord our God, according to all your kindness and all your great tenderness,
as you had announced through your servant Moses, on the day you commanded him to write your law before the sons of Israel, saying:
'If you do not listen to my voice, this great and numerous multitude will be reduced to a very small number among the nations where I will scatter them.
For I know that they will not listen to me, because they are a stiff-necked people. But in the land of their exile they will come to their senses
and they will know that I am the Lord their God. I will give them a heart that understands and ears that hear;
they will praise me in the land of their exile and remember my name.
They will turn from their stubbornness and their evil conduct, for they will remember the fate of their ancestors, who sinned before the Lord.

Then I will bring them back to the land I promised by oath to their ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, and they will be its masters; I will multiply them, and they will no longer diminish.
I will make with them an everlasting covenant: I will be their God, and they will be my people; and I will never again drive my people Israel out of the land I have given them.'
Lord Almighty, God of Israel, it is a soul in anguish, a spirit weighed down, that cries out to you.
Hear, Lord, and have mercy, for we have sinned before you.
You are enthroned forever; and we, we perish without return.

Lord Almighty, God of Israel, hear the prayer of the dead of Israel, of the sons of those who sinned before you and did not listen to the voice of the Lord their God: that is why these calamities have clung to us.
Do not remember the wrongdoings of our ancestors, but remember now your power and your name.
For you are the Lord our God, and we want to praise you, Lord.

That is why you have put your fear in our hearts, so that we would call upon your name. We want to praise you in our exile, for we have driven from our hearts the wrongdoing of our ancestors who sinned before you.

Here we are today in the land of our exile, where you have scattered us, given over to shame, to the curse, and to punishment, because of all the wrongdoing of our ancestors who turned away from the Lord our God.
Hear, Israel, the commandments of life; give ear to learn understanding.
How is it, Israel, that you are in the land of your enemies, that you are growing old in a foreign land, that you are defiled by contact with the dead,
that you are counted among those who go down to the realm of the dead?
It is because you have forsaken the fountain of wisdom.
If you had walked in the way of God, you would dwell in peace forever.
Learn where understanding is, where strength and discernment are, and you will know at the same time where length of days and life are, where the light of the eyes and peace are.
Who then has found the place of wisdom, who has entered her treasuries?
Where are the rulers of the nations, those who tame the beasts of the earth,
those who sport with the birds of the sky, those who hoard the silver and gold in which people put their trust, never ceasing to acquire more,
those who work silver with anxious care, whose works cannot even be found?
They have vanished, they have gone down to the realm of the dead, and others have taken their place.
Younger generations have seen the light and dwelt on the earth, but they have not known the way of wisdom,
they have not discovered her paths; nor have their children grasped her, they have stayed far from her way.
She has not been heard of in Canaan, nor seen in Teman.

The sons of Hagar, who seek understanding here below, the merchants of Merran and Teman, the tellers of tales and the seekers of understanding have not known the way of wisdom, they have not remembered her paths.
O Israel, how great is the house of God! How vast is the domain that belongs to him!
It is immense and without limit, of a height beyond measure.
There, in the beginning, the famous giants were born, of great stature, skilled in war.
But it was not these that God chose, nor did he make known to them the way of wisdom;
and they perished for lack of discernment, they perished through their folly.
Who has gone up to heaven to seize wisdom and bring her down from the clouds?
Who has crossed the sea to find her and bring her back at the price of the purest gold?
No one knows her way, no one discerns her path.
But the one who knows all things knows her; he discovered her by his understanding, he who established the earth forever and filled it with animals;
he who sends out the light, and it goes, who calls it back, and it obeys him, trembling.
The stars have shone at their posts, rejoicing;
he called them, and they answered, 'Here we are!' and they shone with joy for the one who made them.
This is our God, and no other can be compared to him.
He found the whole way of wisdom and gave her to Jacob his servant, to Israel his beloved.
Afterward she appeared on earth and lived among mankind.
She is the book of the commandments of God, the law that endures forever. All who hold fast to her attain to life; those who forsake her go to death.
Return, Jacob, and take hold of her; walk toward the splendor of her light.
Do not yield your glory to another, nor your privileges to a foreign people.
Happy are we, Israel, for what pleases God has been revealed to us.
Take courage, my people, you who keep alive the name of Israel!
You were sold to the nations, but not for your destruction: it is because you provoked the anger of God that you were handed over to your adversaries.
For you angered the one who made you, by offering sacrifices to demons and not to God.
You forgot the one who nourished you, the eternal God, and you grieved the one who raised you, Jerusalem.
She saw the anger of God fall upon you, and she said: 'Listen, you neighbors of Zion: God has sent me great mourning.
I have seen my sons and daughters go into captivity, whom the eternal God let be carried away.
I had nourished them with joy, and I saw them go away in tears and mourning.
Let no one rejoice over me, a widow, abandoned by so many of my own! I am left alone because of the sins of my children, who turned away from the law of God,
who refused to know his commandments or to walk in the way of his precepts, or to follow the paths of discipline according to his justice.
Let them come, the neighbors of Zion! Remember the captivity of my sons and daughters, whom the eternal God let be carried away.
For he brought against them a distant nation, a nation without pity, of a foreign tongue,
who had no respect for the old and no pity for the child. They carried off the widow's beloved sons, they left her alone, bereft of her daughters.
And I, how could I help you?
The one who brought these calamities upon you, it is he who will snatch you from the hands of your enemies.
Go, my children, go your way; as for me, I remain alone.
I have taken off the robe of peace, I have put on the sackcloth of my supplication; I will cry out to the Most High all the days of my life.
Take courage, my children, cry out to God: he will snatch you from the violence, from the hands of your enemies.
For I look to the eternal God for your salvation, and joy has come to me from the Holy One, because of the mercy that will soon reach you from your eternal Savior.
I saw you go away in tears and mourning, but God will give you back to me in joy and gladness, forever.
As the neighbors of Zion have seen your captivity, so they will soon see the salvation that comes to you from God, with great glory, with the great splendor of the eternal God.
My children, endure with patience the anger that has come upon you from God. Your enemy has persecuted you, but soon you will see his ruin and set your foot on his neck.
My delicate sons have walked rough roads, carried off like a flock seized by the enemy.
Take courage, my children, cry out to God: the one who allowed this will remember you.
As much as your thoughts strayed far from God, so, once you have returned, seek him ten times more earnestly.
For the one who brought these calamities upon you will bring you, in saving you, eternal joy.'
Take courage, Jerusalem! The one who gave you your name will console you.
Wretched are those who mistreated you, who rejoiced at your fall!
Wretched the cities where your children were slaves! Wretched the one who received them!
For, just as she rejoiced at your ruin and exulted at your fall, so she will grieve at her own devastation.
I will take away from her the joy her multitude gave her, and her pride will turn into mourning.
A fire from the eternal God will fall upon her for long days, and she will long be inhabited by demons.
Look to the east, Jerusalem, and see the joy that comes to you from God.
Here they come, your sons whom you saw go away; they return, gathered from east to west, at the voice of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.
Take off, Jerusalem, your robe of mourning and affliction, and put on forever the splendor of the glory that comes to you from God.
Wrap yourself in the mantle of the justice of God, place on your head the diadem of the glory of the eternal God.
For God will show your brightness to all that is under heaven.
God will give you forever this name: 'Peace of Justice' and 'Glory of Godliness.'
Arise, Jerusalem! Stand on the height, look to the east and see your children gathered from west to east at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing because God has remembered them.
They had left you on foot, led away by their enemies; God brings them back to you carried in glory, as on a royal throne.
For God has ordered every high mountain and the everlasting hills to be brought low, and the valleys to be filled to level the ground, so that Israel may go forward in safety in the glory of God.
The forests and every fragrant tree have given their shade to Israel, at the command of God.
For God will lead Israel in joy, by the light of his glory, with the mercy and justice that come from him.

titres.titre: The Letter of Jeremiah: the warning against idols
Idols made by hand and powerless
The vain worship offered to idols
Neither kings nor nature obey them
They are not worth as much as the creatures

versets.t: Because of the sins you have committed before God, you are going to be carried off captive to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians.
When you arrive in Babylon, you will remain there many years, a long time, up to seven generations; after that I will bring you out from there in peace.
There you will see gods of silver, gold, and wood, carried on people's shoulders, which strike fear into the nations.
Be careful not to imitate these foreigners, be careful not to be overcome by fear of these gods
when you see the crowd pressing in front of them and behind them to worship them. Say rather in your heart: 'It is you, Lord, that we must worship.'
For my angel is with you, and he watches over your lives.
The tongue of these gods was polished by a craftsman; they are gilded and silvered, but they are nothing but lies, incapable of speaking.
As for a young girl who loves finery, they take gold and prepare crowns for the heads of these gods.
It even happens that the priests steal gold and silver from their gods for their own use,
and give some of it to the prostitutes of the house. These gods of silver, gold, and wood are dressed like people, in rich garments;
but they cannot protect themselves from rust or from worms.
They may be clothed in purple, yet their faces still have to be wiped, because of the dust of the temple that covers them in a thick layer.
Here is one holding a scepter, like a provincial governor: he will not put to death the one who offends him.
Another holds in his hand a sword or an axe, but he cannot defend himself from the enemy or from thieves. This shows well that they are not gods:
so do not fear them. A jar, once broken, is of no more use; the same is true of these gods.
Set up in a house, their eyes fill with the dust raised by those who enter.
As the doors of a prison are bolted upon a condemned man, the priests barricade the temple of their gods with doors, locks, and bolts, for fear that thieves might strip them.
They light lamps for them, more than for themselves, and these gods can see none of them.
They are like a beam of the temple: it is said that the vermin that come up from the ground gnaw their hearts and devour their garments, without their feeling it.
Their faces blacken from the smoke that rises in the temple.
Over their bodies and their heads flit the owls, the swallows, and other birds; cats too frolic there.
By this you recognize that they are not gods: so do not fear them.
The gold that covers them to adorn them, unless someone rubs off the tarnish, they will not make it shine; and indeed they felt nothing when they were being cast.
They were bought at a high price, but there is in them no breath of life.
Having no feet, they are carried on shoulders, thus displaying their shameful helplessness. Let those who serve them blush!

If they fall to the ground, they cannot get up by themselves; set upright, they do not move on their own; leaning, they do not straighten up. It is as to the dead that offerings are presented to them.
The priests resell for their own profit the victims that are offered; their wives salt some away and give none of it to the poor or the sick.
Women in childbirth or in a state of impurity touch these sacrifices. Knowing, then, that they are not gods, do not fear them.
And how can they be called gods? It is women who bring their offerings to these gods of silver, gold, and wood,
and in their temples the priests sit, their tunics torn, their heads and beards shaved, their skulls bare.
They roar and cry out before their gods as at a funeral banquet.
The priests take the garments off the idols to clothe their wives and children with them.
Whether they are treated with harm or with kindness, the idols cannot repay it; they cannot set up a king or depose one.
They cannot give riches or even a coin. If someone makes them a vow and does not fulfill it, they demand nothing.
They will save no one from death, they will not snatch the weak from the hand of the powerful.
They will not give sight to the blind, they will deliver no one from distress.
They will have no pity on the widow, they will do no good to the orphan.
These idols of wood plated with gold and silver are like stones torn from the mountain; those who serve them will be covered with shame.
How can anyone believe or say that they are gods?
The Chaldeans themselves dishonor them: when they see someone mute, they bring him to Bel and beg it to make him speak, as if this god could hear.
They realize it, and yet they cannot give up these idols, for they have no sense.
Women, a cord around their waists, sit along the roads and burn bran;
and when one of them, drawn aside by a passerby, has lain with him, she reproaches her neighbor for not having been judged worthy of the same honor and for not having seen her cord broken.
Everything done around these idols is nothing but a lie. How can anyone believe or say that they are gods?
They were made by craftsmen and goldsmiths; they are nothing other than what the workers wanted them to be.
And these workers who made them do not have long to live: how could their works be gods?
They have left to their descendants nothing but lies and shame.
Should war or disaster come, the priests confer together about where to hide with their gods.
How can anyone fail to understand that they are not gods, they who cannot save themselves from war or from disaster?

One day it will be recognized that these idols of wood plated with gold and silver are nothing but a lie; it will be clear to all the nations and all the kings that they are not gods, but the work of human hands, with nothing divine in them.
To whom, then, is it not obvious that they are not gods?
They will never set up a king over a land, they will not give rain to people.
They will not settle their own cases, they will not deliver the oppressed, for they can do nothing, like crows between heaven and earth.
And when fire takes hold of the temple of these gods of wood plated with gold and silver, their priests will flee and save themselves, but the gods will burn like beams in the midst of the flames.
They will withstand neither a king nor an army. How can anyone accept or think that they are gods?
These gods of wood plated with silver and gold will escape neither thieves nor robbers.
Men stronger than they will carry off the gold and silver and the rich garments that cover them, and these gods will not be able to help themselves.
Better a king who displays his strength, or a useful jar that its owner puts to use, than these false gods; better a door that guards the house, or a wooden pillar in a palace, than these false gods.
The sun, the moon, and the stars, which shine and were sent for the service of people, obey God.
So too the lightning, when it flashes, is beautiful to see, and the wind blows over the whole land;
the clouds, when God orders them to travel over the whole earth, carry out his command;
and fire, sent from on high to consume mountains and forests, does what it is commanded. But these idols resemble them in nothing, neither in beauty nor in power.
So one must neither think nor say that they are gods, since they can neither render justice nor do good to people.
Knowing, then, that they are not gods, do not fear them.
They can neither curse nor bless kings.
They show the nations no sign in the sky; they do not shine like the sun, they give no light like the moon.
The beasts are worth more than they: the beasts, at least, can flee to shelter and help themselves.
In no way is it apparent to us that they are gods: so do not fear them.
As a scarecrow in a cucumber field protects nothing, so are these gods of wood plated with gold and silver.
They are like a thornbush in a garden, on which every bird perches, or like a corpse thrown out into the darkness: that is what these gods of wood plated with gold and silver are worth.
The purple and scarlet that rot on them show well that they are not gods; they themselves will end up gnawed away, and they will become a disgrace in the land.
Better the righteous man who has no idols: he will have no shame to fear.

titres.titre: The vision of God's chariot by the Kebar River
The glory of the Lord on the throne

versets.t: In the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month (around June or July), while I was among the exiles by the Kebar River, the heavens opened and I saw visions of God.
On the fifth day of the month, in the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin,
the word of the Lord came to Ezekiel the priest, son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans, by the Kebar River. It was there that the hand of the Lord came upon him.
I looked, and a storm wind was coming out of the north, a great cloud, a mass of fire flashing on every side, and at its center gleamed something like glowing metal.
In the middle of it I saw four living creatures. This was their appearance: they had a human form,
but each had four faces and four wings.
Their legs were straight, and their feet were like a calf's hooves, glittering like polished bronze.
Under their wings, on their four sides, were human hands; all four had their faces and their wings.
Their wings touched one another. As they moved, they did not turn: each went straight ahead.
This was the form of their faces: a human face, and on the right a lion's face, on the left a bull's face, and an eagle's face, for all four.
Such were their faces. Their wings spread upward; each had two that joined those of its neighbors, and two that covered its body.
Each went straight ahead: they went wherever the spirit drove them, without turning as they moved.
These living creatures looked like burning coals, like torches; a fire moved among them, a dazzling fire from which lightning flashed.
And the creatures darted back and forth, swift as lightning.
I looked at the living creatures, and there on the ground beside each of them stood a wheel, in front of their four faces.
The wheels gleamed like chrysolite, all four alike, and they seemed to be made of a wheel within a wheel.
As they moved, they could go in any of the four directions, without turning as they went.
Their rims were high and awesome, and the rims of all four were covered with eyes all around.
When the creatures moved, the wheels moved beside them; when the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose too.
They went wherever the spirit drove them, and the wheels rose along with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
When the creatures moved, the wheels moved; when they stopped, the wheels stopped; when they rose from the ground, the wheels rose with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
Above the heads of the living creatures spread something like a firmament, gleaming like crystal, stretched out over their heads.
Beneath this firmament their wings stretched out toward one another, and each had two that covered its body.

I heard the sound of their wings as they moved: a sound like rushing waters, like the voice of the Almighty, an uproar like the noise of an army on the march; and when they stopped, they let their wings drop.
A voice rang out above the firmament stretched over their heads; when they stopped, they let their wings drop.
Above the firmament that covered their heads was something like a sapphire stone in the shape of a throne, and on this throne-shape, high above, was a figure with a human appearance.
From what seemed to be his waist upward, I saw what looked like gleaming metal, surrounded by fire; and from his waist downward, I saw what looked like fire, and a brightness enveloped him.

Like the rainbow that appears in the clouds on a rainy day, so was the brightness that surrounded him. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. At the sight of it, I fell face down, and I heard a voice speaking.
He said to me: "Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you."
As he spoke to me, the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet, and I heard the one who was speaking to me.
He said to me: "Son of man, I am sending you to the sons of Israel, to those rebellious nations that have revolted against me; they and their fathers have betrayed me to this very day.
These sons with hard faces and stubborn hearts, it is to them that I am sending you. You shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God.
Then, whether they listen or not, for they are a rebellious house, they will know that a prophet has been among them.

And you, son of man, do not be afraid of them, do not fear their words, even if you are surrounded by nettles and thorns and live among scorpions. Do not fear their words, do not tremble before them, for they are a rebellious house.
You shall speak my words to them, whether they listen or not, for they are rebels.
And you, son of man, listen to what I say to you: do not be rebellious like this rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I give you."
I looked, and a hand was stretched out toward me, holding a scroll.
He unrolled it before me; it was covered with writing on the front and the back, and written on it were dirges, laments, and words of woe.

titres.titre: Sent to the exiles at the Kebar River
The watchman of the house of Israel
The prophet bound and struck dumb

versets.t: He said to me: "Son of man, eat what is before you; eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel."
I opened my mouth, and he made me eat the scroll.
He said to me: "Son of man, feed yourself, fill your stomach with this scroll that I give you." I ate it, and in my mouth it was as sweet as honey.
Then he said to me: "Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak my words to them.
You are not being sent to a people of obscure speech and difficult language, but to the house of Israel;
not to many peoples of obscure speech and difficult language, whose words you could not understand. If I sent you to them, they would listen to you.
But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to me; the whole house of Israel has a hard forehead and a stubborn heart.
So now I make your face as hard as theirs, and your forehead as hard as theirs.
I make your forehead like a diamond, harder than flint. Do not fear them, do not tremble before them, for they are a rebellious house."
He said to me further: "Son of man, take into your heart all the words that I shall speak to you, and listen to them with your ears.
Go, present yourself to the exiles, your own people; speak to them and say: Thus says the Lord God, whether they listen or not."
Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me a great rumbling: "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from his dwelling place!"
It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them, a great rumbling.
The Spirit lifted me up and carried me off, and I went away, bitter and angry in spirit, with the hand of the Lord pressing heavily upon me.
I came to Tel-abib, to the exiles who lived by the Kebar River, where they dwelt; and there I stayed seven days, stunned in their midst.
At the end of seven days, the word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, I make you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, you shall warn them on my behalf.

If I say to the wicked man: You shall die, and you do not warn him, if you do not speak to turn the wicked man from his evil way so that he may live, that wicked man will die in his sin, but I will hold you accountable for his blood.
But if you warn the wicked man and he does not renounce his wickedness or his evil way, he will die in his sin, but you will have saved your own life.

If a righteous man turns away from his righteousness to do evil, and I set a snare before him, he will die; because you did not warn him, he will die in his sin, and the righteousness he practiced will no longer be remembered, but I will hold you accountable for his blood.
But if you warn the righteous man not to sin, and he does not sin, he will live because he was warned, and you will have saved your own life."
There again the hand of the Lord was upon me, and he said to me: "Get up, go out to the plain, and there I will speak to you."
I got up and went out to the plain; and there stood the glory of the Lord, like the glory I had seen by the Kebar River; and I fell face down.
The Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet. Then he spoke to me and said: "Go, shut yourself inside your house.
As for you, son of man, they are going to bind you with ropes, they will tie you up, and you will not be able to go out among them.
I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth: you will be mute and unable to reprove them, for they are a rebellious house.

But when I speak to you, I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God. Whoever will listen, let him listen; whoever will refuse, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house."

titres.titre: The brick: the siege of Jerusalem enacted
Lying on his side: the years of guilt
The rationed bread of the siege

versets.t: As for you, son of man, take a brick, set it before you, and engrave on it a city, Jerusalem.
Then lay siege to it: build a siege tower against it, throw up a ramp, set up camps, and place battering rams all around it.

Next take an iron plate and set it up as an iron wall between you and the city; turn your face against it: now it is besieged, and you are the one besieging it. This will be a sign for the house of Israel.
Then lie down on your left side, and take upon yourself the guilt of the house of Israel: for as many days as you lie there, you shall bear their guilt.
I have assigned you one day for each year of their guilt: for three hundred and ninety days you shall bear the guilt of the house of Israel.
When these days are over, you shall lie down a second time, on your right side, and you shall bear the guilt of the house of Judah for forty days; I have assigned you one day for each year.
You shall turn your face and your bared arm against besieged Jerusalem, and you shall prophesy against it.
See, I bind you with ropes, so that you cannot turn from one side to the other, until the days of your siege are completed.

Take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt; put them in a single container and make them into your bread. You shall eat it during the three hundred and ninety days that you lie on your side.
Your daily ration will be about 230 grams, which you shall eat at set times.
You shall drink water by measure, a little over half a litre, which you shall drink at set times.
You shall eat all this in the form of barley cakes, baked before everyone's eyes over human excrement."
The Lord added: "This is how the sons of Israel will eat their defiled bread, among the nations where I will drive them."

I replied: "Ah, Lord God, I have never defiled myself: from my childhood until now I have never eaten an animal that died of itself or was torn by beasts, and no unclean meat has ever entered my mouth."
He said to me: "Very well! I grant you cow's dung instead of human excrement: you shall bake your bread over that."
Then he added: "Son of man, I am going to cut off the supply of bread to Jerusalem: they will eat rationed bread in anguish, and drink measured water in dismay,
for bread and water will fail them. They will waste away, one and all, consumed by their guilt.

titres.titre: The shaved hair divided in three
Jerusalem judged more than the nations

versets.t: As for you, son of man, take a sharp blade; use it as a barber's razor and pass it over your head and your beard. Then take a balance and divide the hair you have cut off.

You shall burn a third of it in the fire, in the middle of the city, when the days of the siege are completed; you shall take another third and strike it with the sword all around the city; and the last third you shall scatter to the wind, and I will draw the sword after them.
But you shall keep a small amount, tucked into the fold of your cloak;
and from this remnant again you shall take some and throw it into the fire to burn it. From there a fire will spread against the whole house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord God: Here is Jerusalem! I had set her in the middle of the nations, surrounded by vast lands.
But she has rebelled against my decrees with more wickedness than the nations, and against my laws more than the surrounding lands; for they have rejected my decrees and have not followed my laws.

Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Because you have been more turbulent than the nations around you, because you have not followed my laws or kept my decrees, and have not even acted according to the ordinances of the surrounding nations,
therefore, thus says the Lord God: Here I am against you, I too! I will carry out my judgments in your midst, before the eyes of the nations.
Because of all your abominations, I will do to you what I have never done and will never do again.
In your midst, fathers will devour their sons, and sons will devour their fathers. I will carry out my judgments against you and scatter to every wind all that remains of you.
As surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God: because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your horrors and abominations, I too will cut you off, without a look of pity, sparing no one.

A third of your people will die of plague or be consumed by famine in your midst; a third will fall by the sword around you; and the last third I will scatter to every wind, drawing the sword after them.
Then my anger will subside, I will satisfy my fury against them and be avenged; and they will know that I, the Lord, have spoken in my jealousy, when I have spent my fury upon them.
I will make you a ruin and an object of shame among the surrounding nations, in the sight of all who pass by.

You will be an object of shame and derision, a warning and a horror to the nations around you, when I carry out my judgments against you, with anger, with fury, with furious punishments. I, the Lord, have spoken.
When I loose against them the deadly arrows of famine, made to destroy, those I will shoot to destroy you, I will make the famine worse and cut off your supply of bread.
I will send against you famine and wild beasts, which will rob you of your children; plague and bloodshed will pass over you, and I will bring the sword upon you. I, the Lord, have spoken.

titres.titre: Against the mountains and high places of Israel
A remnant will remember among the nations

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, turn your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.

You shall say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God. Thus says the Lord God to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys: I am about to bring the sword against you, and I will destroy your high places.
Your altars will be laid waste, your incense stands smashed, and I will make your slain fall before your idols.
I will lay the corpses of the sons of Israel before their idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.

Wherever you live, the cities will be destroyed and the high places laid waste: your altars will be razed and made desolate, your idols smashed and done away with, your incense stands cut down, and everything you have made wiped out.
The slain will fall in your midst, and you will know that I am the Lord.
Yet I will leave you a remnant: survivors of the sword among the nations, when you are scattered through the lands.

Then, among the nations where they have been carried captive, your survivors will remember me, when I have broken their adulterous heart that turned away from me, and their adulterous eyes that ran after idols; and they will loathe themselves for the evil and the abominations they have committed.
Then they will know that I am the Lord, and that I did not threaten in vain to bring this disaster upon them.
Thus says the Lord God: Clap your hands, stamp your foot, and cry: Alas! over all the abominations of the house of Israel, for it will fall by the sword, famine, and plague.
Whoever is far off will die of plague, whoever is near will fall by the sword, whoever survives and is spared will die of hunger: thus I will satisfy my fury against them.

You will know that I am the Lord when their slain lie among their idols, around their altars, on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree and every leafy oak, wherever they offered fragrant incense to their idols.
I will stretch out my hand against them, and I will make the land a desolate waste, from the wilderness to Diblah, wherever they live; and they will know that I am the Lord."

titres.titre: The end comes upon the land
Neither silver nor gold will deliver

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
"As for you, son of man, thus says the Lord God to the land of Israel: The end! The end is coming upon the four corners of the land!
Now the end is upon you. I will loose my anger against you, judge you according to your conduct, and bring upon you all your abominations.
My eye will show no pity, I will not spare: I will bring your conduct down upon you, and your abominations will remain in your midst; and you will know that I am the Lord.
Thus says the Lord God: A disaster, a singular disaster, is coming!
The end is coming, the end arrives, it rouses itself against you: here it is!
Your turn has come, you who live in the land. The time is coming, the day is near: a day of panic, not of joyful shouts on the mountains.
Soon I will pour out my fury upon you and spend my anger against you, judge you according to your conduct, and bring upon you all your abominations.
My eye will show no pity, I will not spare: I will deal with you according to your conduct, and your abominations will remain in your midst; and you will know that it is I, the Lord, who strikes.
Here is the day, here it comes! Your turn has arrived. Insolence has blossomed, pride has budded.
Violence has risen up to become a rod of wickedness. Nothing will remain of them, nothing of their multitude, nothing of their uproar, nothing of their splendor.
The time is coming, the day draws near! Let the buyer not rejoice, let the seller not grieve, for wrath falls upon all their multitude.
The seller will not recover what he sold, even if he is still alive, for the vision concerning all their multitude will not be revoked, and no one, through his sin, will save his life.
The trumpet is sounded, everything is made ready, but no one marches to battle, for my wrath is upon all their multitude.
Outside, the sword; inside, plague and famine. Whoever is in the fields will die by the sword, whoever is in the city will be devoured by famine and plague.
And if any escape, they will roam the mountains like the doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each over his own sin.
Every hand goes limp, every knee turns to water.
They put on sackcloth, terror envelops them, shame is on every face, and every head is shaved.

They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will fill them with loathing: neither silver nor gold will be able to deliver them on the day of the Lord's wrath. They will not satisfy their hunger with it, nor fill their stomachs, for this gold has been the cause of their downfall.
Out of their jewels, in which they took pride, they made their abominable idols: that is why I will turn it into an object of loathing for them.
I will hand it over as plunder to strangers, as spoil to the wicked of the earth, who will profane it.
I will turn my face away from them: they will profane my treasured place; robbers will enter it and profane it.
Prepare the chains, for the land is full of bloodshed and the city full of violence.
I will bring the most cruel of the nations, and they will seize their houses; I will put an end to the pride of the mighty, and their sanctuaries will be profaned.
Anguish is coming: they will seek peace, but there will be none.
Disaster upon disaster, rumor upon rumor: they will demand a vision from the prophet, but instruction will fail the priest and counsel the elders.

The king will mourn, the prince will be clothed in desolation, and the hands of the people of the land will tremble. I will deal with them according to their conduct, I will judge them by their own standards; and they will know that I am the Lord."

titres.titre: Carried in vision to the temple of Jerusalem
The elders and their hidden cults
The weeping for Tammuz and the worship of the sun

versets.t: In the sixth year, on the fifth day of the sixth month (around August or September), I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah were sitting before me, when the hand of the Lord God fell upon me there.
I looked: a form with a human appearance, like fire; from what seemed to be his waist downward it was fire, and from his waist upward it was like a brightness, like gleaming metal.

He stretched out the form of a hand and seized me by a lock of my hair; and the Spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and carried me to Jerusalem, in visions of God, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces north, where the idol of jealousy stood, the one that provokes God's jealousy.
And there stood the glory of the God of Israel, just as I had seen it in the plain.
He said to me: "Son of man, lift up your eyes toward the north." I lifted my eyes toward the north, and there, north of the altar gate, at the entrance, stood this idol of jealousy.

He said to me: "Son of man, do you see what they are doing? The great abominations that the house of Israel commits here, to drive me far from my sanctuary? Well, you will see abominations greater still."
He brought me to the entrance of the court. I looked: there was a hole in the wall.
He said to me: "Son of man, dig through this wall." I dug through the wall, and there was a doorway.
He said to me: "Go in, and look at the dreadful abominations they are committing here."
I went in, I looked: all kinds of crawling creatures and unclean beasts, and all the idols of the house of Israel, were drawn on the wall all around.
Before them stood seventy men, elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them; each held his censer in his hand, and a cloud of fragrant incense rose from them.

He said to me: "Have you seen, son of man, what the elders of the house of Israel do in the dark, each in his room covered with images? For they say: The Lord does not see us, the Lord has abandoned the land."
He said to me: "You will see abominations greater still."
He brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the Lord; and there sat women, weeping for the god Tammuz.
He said to me: "Have you seen, son of man? You will see abominations greater still."

Then he brought me into the inner court of the house of the Lord; and there, at the entrance of the sanctuary, between the portico and the altar, were about twenty-five men, with their backs to the sanctuary of the Lord and their faces toward the east, bowing down to the rising sun.

He said to me: "Have you seen, son of man? Is it not enough for the house of Judah to commit the abominations they commit here? Must they also fill the land with violence and keep provoking me again and again, holding the branch to their noses?
Well, I too will act in fury: my eye will show no pity, I will not spare; though they cry aloud in my ears, I will not listen to them."

titres.titre: The mark on the foreheads of those who grieve
The slaughter begins at the sanctuary

versets.t: Then he cried out in a loud voice in my ears: "Draw near, you who watch over the city, each with his weapon of destruction in his hand!"

And behold, six men came by way of the upper gate that faces north, each with his deadly weapon in his hand; among them stood a man clothed in linen, with a scribe's writing case at his belt. They came in and stood beside the bronze altar.

Then the glory of the God of Israel rose from the cherub on which it rested and moved toward the threshold of the temple. The Lord called to the man clothed in linen, the one who carried the writing case at his belt,
and said to him: "Pass through the middle of the city, through the middle of Jerusalem, and mark with a sign the foreheads of the men who sigh and groan over all the abominations committed there."
Then, in my hearing, he said to the others: "Pass through the city behind him, and strike. Let your eye show no pity, do not spare:
old men, young men, young women, children, women, kill them all. But do not go near anyone who bears the mark. And begin at my sanctuary." So they began with the elders who stood before the temple.
He said to them: "Defile the temple, fill the courts with the slain. Go!" So they went out and struck down people in the city.
As they were striking and I was left alone, I fell face down and cried out: "Ah, Lord God, are you going to destroy all that remains of Israel by pouring out your fury on Jerusalem?"

He answered me: "The guilt of the house of Israel and Judah is immense; the land is full of bloodshed and the city full of injustice. For they say: The Lord has abandoned the land, the Lord sees nothing.
Well, my eye will show no pity, I will not spare: I will bring their conduct down upon their own heads."
Then the man clothed in linen, with the writing case at his belt, came to report: "I have done as you commanded me."

titres.titre: The burning coals scattered over the city
The glory leaves the threshold of the temple

versets.t: I looked: on the firmament that covered the heads of the cherubim there was something like a sapphire stone, something resembling a throne, above them.

The Lord said to the man clothed in linen: "Go in among the wheels, beneath the cherubim, fill your hands with burning coals taken from among the cherubim, and scatter them over the city." And he went in as I watched.
The cherubim were standing to the right of the temple when the man went in, and the cloud filled the inner court.
The glory of the Lord rose up from above the cherubim toward the threshold of the temple; the temple filled with the cloud, and the court was flooded with the brightness of the glory of the Lord.
The sound of the wings of the cherubim could be heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Almighty when he speaks.
When the Lord had commanded the man clothed in linen: "Take fire from among the wheels, from among the cherubim," the man went in and stood beside a wheel.
A cherub reached out his hand toward the fire that was among the cherubim, took some, and put it into the hands of the man clothed in linen, who received it and went out.
Under the wings of the cherubim there appeared something like a human hand.
I looked: four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel next to each cherub, and these wheels gleamed like chrysolite.
All four looked alike, as if each wheel were within another wheel.
