As they moved, they could go in any of the four directions without turning; they followed the direction the head faced, without swerving as they went.
Their whole bodies, their backs, their hands and their wings, along with the wheels, were covered with eyes all around, for all four.
As for these wheels, I heard them called the Whirlwind.
Each cherub had four faces: the first was the face of a cherub, the second a human face, the third a lion's face, the fourth an eagle's face.
Then the cherubim rose up: these were the living creatures I had seen by the Kebar River.
When the cherubim moved, the wheels moved beside them; when they lifted their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels did not part from them.
When they stopped, the wheels stopped; when they rose, the wheels rose with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in them.
The glory of the Lord left the threshold of the temple and came to rest above the cherubim.

As I watched, the cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the ground, the wheels with them; they halted at the entrance of the east gate of the house of the Lord, and the glory of the God of Israel rested above them, high up.
These were the living creatures I had seen beneath the God of Israel by the Kebar River; and I understood that they were cherubim.
Each had four faces and four wings, and under their wings something like human hands.
Their faces looked like the ones I had seen by the Kebar River: the same appearance, the same beings. Each went straight ahead.

titres.titre: Against the wicked counselors of the city
The promise of a new heart

versets.t: The Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the gate of the house of the Lord that faces east. And there, at the entrance of the gate, stood twenty-five men; among them I saw Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.
The Lord said to me: "Son of man, these are the men who plot evil and give wicked counsel in this city;
they say: Disaster is not so near; let us build houses! This city is the pot, and we are the meat.
Therefore prophesy against them, prophesy, son of man."
The Spirit of the Lord fell upon me, and he said to me: "Speak: Thus says the Lord. This is how you talk, house of Israel, but what rises in your minds, I know it well.
You have multiplied your killings in this city and filled its streets with corpses.
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: The slain you have laid in her midst, they are the meat, and the city is the pot; but you, you will be brought out of it.
You dread the sword: I will bring the sword upon you, oracle of the Lord God.
I will bring you out of the city, hand you over to strangers, and carry out my judgments against you.
You will fall by the sword; I will judge you at the border of Israel, and you will know that I am the Lord.
This city will not be a pot for you, and you will not be the meat in it; it is at the border of Israel that I will judge you,
and you will know that I am the Lord, whose decrees you did not follow and whose laws you did not keep, acting instead according to the customs of the nations around you."
Now, as I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. I fell face down and cried out at the top of my voice: "Ah, Lord God, are you going to annihilate all that remains of Israel?"
The word of the Lord came to me:

"Son of man, your brothers, yes, your brothers, your kinsmen, and the whole house of Israel, these are the ones of whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem say: Stay far from the Lord; this land has been given to us as our possession.

Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord God. Yes, I have sent them far off among the nations, I have scattered them through the lands; but I have been a sanctuary for them, for a time, in the lands where they have gone.
So say to them: Thus says the Lord God. I will gather you from among the peoples, I will bring you back from the lands where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.
They will enter it and remove from it all its horrors and all its abominations.
I will give them a single heart and put a new spirit within them; I will remove from their flesh the heart of stone and give them a heart of flesh,
so that they may follow my decrees, keep and practice my laws. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
But as for those whose heart follows their abominable idols, I will bring their conduct down upon their own heads, oracle of the Lord God."
Then the cherubim lifted their wings, the wheels moved with them, and the glory of the God of Israel rested above them.
The glory of the Lord rose up from the middle of the city and halted on the mountain to the east of the city.
The Spirit lifted me up and brought me back to Chaldea, to the exiles, in the vision given by the Spirit of God. Then the vision I had seen rose away from me,
and I told the exiles all that the Lord had shown me.

titres.titre: The prophet enacts the departure into exile
The fate of the prince of Jerusalem
The vision will no longer be delayed

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, you live in the midst of a rebellious house, people who have eyes to see but do not see, ears to hear but do not hear, for they are a rebellious house.

As for you, son of man, pack yourself an exile's baggage, and go into exile by day, before their eyes; before their eyes, leave the place where you are for another. Perhaps they will understand that they are a rebellious house.
Bring out your baggage, like an exile's baggage, by day, before their eyes; and you, set out in the evening, before their eyes, as exiles set out.
Before their eyes, dig a hole through the wall, and bring your baggage out through it.
Before their eyes, lift it onto your shoulder and carry it out in the dark; cover your face so as not to see the land, for I make you a sign for the house of Israel."

I did as he had commanded me: I brought out my baggage by day, like an exile's baggage; in the evening I dug through the wall with my hand; and I brought the baggage out in the dark, carrying it on my shoulder, before their eyes.
In the morning, the word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, has not the house of Israel, that rebellious house, asked you: What are you doing?
Say to them: Thus says the Lord God. This oracle concerns the prince who is in Jerusalem and all the house of Israel who are within it.
Say: I am a sign for you; as I have done, so it will be done to them: they will go into exile, into captivity.

The prince who is among them will lift his baggage onto his shoulder in the dark and set out; they will dig through the wall to bring him out; he will cover his face, so as not to see the land with his own eyes.
I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my trap; I will bring him to Babylon, to the land of the Chaldeans, but he will not see it, and there he will die.
All those around him, his guards and all his troops, I will scatter to every wind, and I will pursue them with drawn sword.
They will know that I am the Lord, when I have scattered them among the nations and dispersed them through the lands.
But I will let a few of them escape the sword, famine, and plague, so that they may recount all their abominations among the nations where they go; and they will know that I am the Lord."
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, eat your bread trembling, and drink your water in worry and anguish.

And you shall say to the people of the land: Thus says the Lord God concerning the inhabitants of Jerusalem, in the land of Israel. They will eat their bread in anguish and drink their water in dismay, for their land will be stripped of all that fills it, because of the violence of all who live in it.
The populous cities will become ruins, the land will be a desolation, and you will know that I am the Lord."
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, what is this saying you repeat in the land of Israel: The days pass, and no vision comes true?

Well, say to them: Thus says the Lord God. I am going to silence this saying: it will no longer be repeated in Israel. Say to them instead: The days are near, and with them the fulfillment of every vision.
For there will be no more deceptive vision or flattering divination in the midst of the house of Israel.
For I, the Lord, will speak, and the word I speak will be fulfilled without further delay. Yes, in your days, rebellious house, I will pronounce a word and carry it out, oracle of the Lord God."
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, the house of Israel is saying: The vision he has is for distant days; he prophesies for far-off times.
Well, say to them: Thus says the Lord God. None of my words will be delayed any longer: the word I speak will be fulfilled, oracle of the Lord God."

titres.titre: The whitewashed wall that will collapse

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel, prophesy, and say to those who prophesy out of their own imagination: Hear the word of the Lord.
Thus says the Lord God: Woe to the foolish prophets, who follow their own inspiration without having seen anything!
Your prophets, Israel, are like foxes among the ruins.
You have not gone up to the breaches, nor rebuilt a wall around the house of Israel, to stand firm in battle on the day of the Lord.
They have vain visions and lying omens, these men who say: Oracle of the Lord, when the Lord has not sent them; and they wait for their word to be fulfilled!
Are they not vain, the visions you have? Lying, the divinations you pronounce, when you say: Oracle of the Lord, though I have not spoken?
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Because you spout emptiness and see lies, here I am against you, oracle of the Lord God.

My hand will fall upon the prophets with vain visions and lying omens: they will not be in the council of my people, they will not be enrolled in the register of the house of Israel, they will not enter the land of Israel; and you will know that I am the Lord God.
For they lead my people astray, crying: Peace! when there is no peace. My people build a rickety wall, and there they are, coating it with plaster!
Tell these whitewashers that the wall will fall. A driving rain will come, I will send hailstones falling, and a storm wind will break loose.
And when the wall has fallen, will you not be asked: Where is the plaster you coated it with?
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: In my fury I will unleash a storm wind; in my anger, a driving rain; and hailstones, in my fury, to destroy everything.

I will tear down the wall you have coated with plaster, I will throw it to the ground, and its foundations will be laid bare; it will collapse, and you will perish beneath its rubble, and you will know that I am the Lord.
I will spend my fury against the wall and against those who coated it with plaster, and I will say to you: No more wall! No more of those who whitewashed it,
those prophets of Israel who prophesied about Jerusalem and saw for her visions of peace, when there was no peace, oracle of the Lord God!
As for you, son of man, turn your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own imagination, and prophesy against them.

You shall say: Thus says the Lord God. Woe to those who sew magic bands for every wrist and make veils for heads of every height, to trap souls! You trap the souls of my people, and would you keep your own souls alive?

You have dishonored me before my people for a few handfuls of barley and a few scraps of bread, putting to death souls that should not die and keeping alive souls that should not live, by lying to my people who listen to lies.
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Here I am against your magic bands, by which you trap souls like birds; I will tear them from your arms and set free the souls you trapped like birds.
I will tear off your veils, I will rescue my people from your hands, and they will no longer be prey in your hands; and you will know that I am the Lord.
Because you discourage the heart of the righteous with lies, when I myself did not grieve him, and because you strengthen the hands of the wicked so that he does not turn from his evil way and live,
therefore you will no longer have vain visions or practice divination: I will rescue my people from your hands, and you will know that I am the Lord."

titres.titre: The idolaters who come to inquire
No one saves any but himself: Noah, Daniel, Job

versets.t: Some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat down before me.
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, these men have set up their idols in their hearts and placed before them what makes them fall into sin: am I to let myself be consulted by them?

So speak to them and say to them: Thus says the Lord God. Any man of the house of Israel who sets up his idols in his heart and places before him what makes him fall into sin, if he comes to the prophet, I, the Lord, will answer him myself, as the multitude of his idols deserves,
so as to win back the hearts of the house of Israel, who have turned away from me for all their idols.
Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God. Return, turn away from your idols, and turn your faces away from all your abominations.

For any man of the house of Israel, or any resident alien living in Israel, who turns away from me, sets up his idols in his heart, and places before him what makes him fall into sin, if he comes to the prophet to consult me through him, I, the Lord, will answer him myself.
I will turn my face against that man, I will make him a sign and a byword, I will cut him off from the midst of my people; and you will know that I am the Lord.

And if the prophet lets himself be seduced and speaks a word, it is I, the Lord, who will have seduced that prophet; I will stretch out my hand against him and destroy him from the midst of my people Israel.
They will bear the weight of their guilt: the guilt of the one who inquires will be like the guilt of the prophet,
so that the house of Israel may no longer stray far from me or defile themselves any longer with all their sins. Then they will be my people, and I will be their God, oracle of the Lord God."
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, if a land were to sin against me by unfaithfulness, and I stretched out my hand against it, cutting off its supply of bread, sending famine upon it, and doing away with man and beast,
and if these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it, they would save only their own lives by their righteousness, oracle of the Lord God.
If I loosed wild beasts across that land and they left it childless, so that it lay desolate and impassable because of them,
and if these three men were in it, as surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God, they would save neither sons nor daughters; they alone would be saved, but the land would be laid waste.
Or if I brought the sword upon that land, saying: Let the sword pass through the land! and did away with man and beast,
and if these three men were in it, as surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God, they would save neither sons nor daughters; they alone would be saved.
Or if I sent plague upon that land and poured out my fury upon it in bloodshed, doing away with man and beast,
and if Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it, as surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God, they would save neither sons nor daughters; they would save only their own lives by their righteousness.
Now, thus says the Lord God: How much worse when I have sent against Jerusalem my four dreadful scourges, the sword, famine, wild beasts, and plague, to do away with man and beast!

Yet there will remain in it a remnant of survivors, sons and daughters who will be brought out. Here they come to you; you will see their conduct and their deeds, and you will be consoled over the disaster I have brought upon Jerusalem, over all that I have brought upon it.
They will console you, when you see their conduct and their deeds, and you will know that it was not without reason that I did all that I did to it, oracle of the Lord God."

titres.titre: The wood of the vine, fit only for burning

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, how is the wood of the vine better than any other wood, than a branch that grows among the trees of the forest?
Is wood taken from it to make anything? Is even a peg made from it to hang an object on?
See, it is thrown into the fire to be consumed; the fire devours both its ends, and the middle is burned: can it still be of any use?
Even when it was whole, nothing could be made from it; how much less, once the fire has devoured and burned it, can it serve any purpose at all?
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I give to the fire to consume, so I will give up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
I will turn my face against them: they have come out of one fire, and a fire will devour them; and you will know that I am the Lord, when I turn my face against them.
I will make the land a desolation, because they have been unfaithful to me, oracle of the Lord God."

titres.titre: Jerusalem, the abandoned child taken in by God
God takes her as his bride and lavishes gifts on her
The judgment of the adulterous wife

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, make known to Jerusalem her abominations.
You shall say: Thus says the Lord God to Jerusalem. By your origin and your birth, you are from the land of Canaan; your father was an Amorite and your mother a Hittite.
At your birth, the day you came into the world, your cord was not cut, you were not washed in water to be cleansed, nor rubbed with salt, nor wrapped in swaddling clothes.
No eye looked on you with enough pity to do even one of these things for you; you were thrown out into the open field, in loathing of you, on the day of your birth.
I passed by you and saw you struggling in your blood, and I said to you, as you lay in your blood: Live! Yes, I said to you in your blood: Live!
I made you grow like the grass of the fields; you grew, you developed, and you became of perfect beauty; your breasts formed, your hair grew, but you were naked, utterly naked.

I passed by you again and saw you: your time had come, the time for love. I spread the fold of my cloak over you and covered your nakedness; I made you a pledge, I entered into a covenant with you, oracle of the Lord God, and you were mine.
I bathed you in water, I washed the blood from you and anointed you with oil.
I clothed you in embroidered garments, I shod you with fine leather, I bound your head with linen and covered you with silk.
I adorned you with jewels: bracelets on your wrists, a necklace at your throat,
a ring in your nose, earrings in your ears, and on your head a magnificent crown.
You were adorned with gold and silver, clothed in linen, silk, and embroidery; you fed on fine flour, honey, and oil. You became extraordinarily beautiful and rose to royalty.
Your fame spread among the nations because of your beauty, for it was perfect, thanks to the splendor with which I had adorned you, oracle of the Lord God.
But you put your trust in your beauty; relying on your fame, you prostituted yourself, lavishing your favors on every passerby, giving yourself to him.
You took some of your garments to make yourself gaudy high places, and there you prostituted yourself, as had never been seen and will never be seen again.
You took your jewelry made of my gold and my silver, which I had given you, and made yourself images of men, and prostituted yourself before them.
You took your embroidered garments to cover them, and you set my oil and my incense before them.
The bread I had given you, the fine flour, the oil and the honey with which I fed you, you set before them as a pleasing aroma. This is what happened, oracle of the Lord God.
You even took your sons and your daughters, whom you had borne to me, and offered them to them as food. Was your prostitution not enough,
that you had to slaughter my sons and hand them over, making them pass through the fire in their honor?
In the midst of all your abominations and your prostitutions, you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked, utterly naked, struggling in your blood.
After all your wickedness, woe, woe to you! oracle of the Lord God,
you built yourself a platform and raised a mound in every square.
At every crossroads you raised your mound; you debased your beauty, you offered yourself to every passerby, you multiplied your prostitutions.
You prostituted yourself to the Egyptians, your lustful neighbors, and you multiplied your prostitutions to provoke me.
So I stretched out my hand against you, I cut back your portion, and I handed you over to the will of your enemies, the daughters of the Philistines, who themselves blushed at your shameful conduct.
You prostituted yourself to the Assyrians, for you were never satisfied; and after prostituting yourself to them, you still were not satisfied.
You multiplied your prostitutions as far as the land of merchants, Chaldea, and even that did not satisfy you.
How weak your heart is, oracle of the Lord God, to act like this, like the most brazen of prostitutes!
When you built your platform at every crossroads and raised your mound in every square, you were not even like a prostitute, for you scorned payment.
Adulterous wife, who takes strangers instead of her husband!
To all prostitutes a gift is given; but you, it was you who gave gifts to all your lovers, paying them to come to you from all around for your prostitutions.
In your prostitutions you did the opposite of other women: no one ran after you; it was you who paid instead of being paid. That is how you were the reverse of others.
Therefore, prostitute, hear the word of the Lord.

Thus says the Lord God: Because you have poured out your lust and uncovered your nakedness in your prostitutions with your lovers and all your abominable idols, and because of the blood of your children whom you handed over to them,

behold, I will gather all your lovers, those you loved as well as those you hated; I will gather them against you from all around, I will uncover your nakedness before them, and they will see your nakedness in full.
I will judge you by the law that condemns adulterous women and those who shed blood, and I will make you a victim of fury and jealousy.
I will hand you over into their hands: they will tear down your platform, demolish your high places, strip you of your garments, take your jewels, and leave you naked, utterly naked.
They will stir up a crowd against you, they will stone you and run you through with their swords.
They will burn your houses and carry out judgment against you, before the eyes of many women. Thus I will put an end to your prostitutions, and you will make gifts no more.
I will satisfy my fury upon you, then my jealousy will turn away from you; I will grow calm and be angry no longer.

Because you did not remember the days of your youth and provoked me with all this, in turn I bring your conduct down upon your own head, oracle of the Lord God; have you not added lewdness to all your abominations?
See, everyone who makes proverbs will make one about you: Like mother, like daughter!

You are indeed the daughter of your mother, who rejected her husband and her children; you are indeed the sister of your sisters, who rejected their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
Your older sister is Samaria, who lives to the north with her daughters; your younger sister, who lives to the south, is Sodom with her daughters.
You did not merely follow their ways and imitate their abominations: as if that were too little, you corrupted yourself more than they did in all your conduct.
As surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God, your sister Sodom, she and her daughters, did not do what you have done, you and your daughters.
This was the crime of Sodom, your sister: pride, plenty, the careless ease in which she lived with her daughters, while she did not support the hand of the poor and the needy.
They grew proud and committed abomination before me; so I did away with them, as you have seen.
Samaria did not commit half your sins; you multiplied your abominations more than they did, and by all your abominations you made your sisters appear righteous.

So bear your shame, you too, you who condemned your sisters: by your sins more abominable than theirs, they are found more righteous than you. Blush, you too, and bear your shame, since you made your sisters appear righteous.
I will restore their fortunes, those of Sodom and her daughters, those of Samaria and her daughters, and your fortunes along with theirs,
so that you may bear your shame and blush for all you have done to console them.
Your sister Sodom and her daughters will return to their former state, Samaria and her daughters will return to their former state, and you and your daughters will return to your former state.
The name of your sister Sodom did not pass your lips in the days of your pride,
before your wickedness was laid bare. Now you are like her, an object of insult to the daughters of Syria and all her neighbors, to the daughters of the Philistines who despise you on every side.
Your lewdness and your abominations, you bear their weight, oracle of the Lord.
For thus says the Lord God: I will deal with you as you have acted, you who despised the oath by breaking the covenant.
But I will remember the covenant I made with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish with you an everlasting covenant.
Then you will remember your conduct and be ashamed of it, when you welcome your sisters, the older and the younger; I will give them to you as daughters, but not by virtue of your covenant.
I will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am the Lord,
so that you may remember and blush, and never again dare to open your mouth, in your shame, when I forgive you all you have done, oracle of the Lord God."

titres.titre: The riddle of the two eagles
The explanation: the treachery of Zedekiah
The shoot planted on the mountain

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, pose a riddle, tell a parable to the house of Israel.
You shall say: Thus says the Lord God. The great eagle, with great wings, broad in span, with thick, many-colored plumage, came to Lebanon and seized the top of the cedar.
He plucked off its highest shoot, carried it to the land of merchants, and set it down in a city of traders.
Then he took a seedling of the land and put it in fertile soil; beside abundant water he planted it like a willow.

The seedling sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height, whose branches turned toward the eagle and whose roots reached down beneath him. So it became a vine, which produced shoots and put out branches.

Now there was another great eagle, with great wings and abundant plumage. And behold, this vine bent its roots eagerly toward him and pushed out its branches in his direction, so that he might water it, away from the bed where it was planted.
Yet it had been planted in good soil, beside abundant water, so that it might put out foliage, bear fruit, and become a magnificent vine.

Say: Thus says the Lord God. Will it thrive? Will its roots not be torn out, its fruit cut off, and left to wither? All the fresh shoots it has put out will dry up. It will take no mighty arm or great crowd to tear it up by the roots.
There it is, planted: will it thrive? As soon as the east wind touches it, will it not dry up? On the bed where it grew, it will dry up."
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Say to the rebellious house: Do you not understand what this means? Say: The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem; he took its king and its officials and carried them off to his own land, to Babylon.
He took a member of the royal family, made a covenant with him, and put him under oath; he carried off the powerful men of the land,
so that the kingdom would stay lowly, unable to raise itself up, and would survive only by keeping his covenant.

But this king rebelled against him, sending messengers to Egypt to obtain horses and a large army. Will he succeed? Will he escape, the man who does such things? He has broken the covenant, and will he escape?
As surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God: in the land of the king who put him on the throne, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, there, in Babylon, he will die.
And Pharaoh, with his great army and his vast host, will do nothing for him in the battle, when ramps are raised and siege works are built to destroy many lives.
He despised the oath by breaking the covenant, though he had given his hand on it! He did all this; he will not escape.
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: As surely as I live, it is my oath that he despised, my covenant that he broke; I will bring it down upon his head.
I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my trap; I will bring him to Babylon, and there I will call him to account for the treachery he committed against me.
All the fugitives of his troops will fall by the sword, and those who remain will be scattered to every wind; and you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken.

Thus says the Lord God: I myself will take a shoot from the top of the great cedar and set it in the ground; from the highest of its branches I will pluck a tender shoot, and I myself will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.

I will plant it on the high mountain of Israel; it will put out branches, bear fruit, and become a magnificent cedar. All the birds will dwell beneath it, in the shade of its branches they will make their nests.

And all the trees of the field will know that I, the Lord, bring low the tall tree and raise up the low tree, dry up the green tree and make the dry tree flourish. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will do it."

titres.titre: The wicked man who repents will live

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
"Why do you repeat this proverb about the land of Israel: The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge?
As surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God: you will no longer have reason to repeat this proverb in Israel.
Behold: all lives are mine, the life of the father as well as the life of the son; the one who sins, he is the one who will die.
Suppose a righteous man, who practices justice and righteousness.
He does not eat on the mountains, he does not lift his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel; he does not dishonor his neighbor's wife, he does not approach a woman during her period;
he oppresses no one, he returns to the debtor his pledge, he does not steal, he gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with a garment;
he does not lend at interest or take a profit, he keeps his hand from injustice, he renders a true judgment between one person and another;
he follows my precepts and keeps my laws faithfully. Such a man is righteous; he will live, oracle of the Lord God.
But suppose he fathers a violent son, who sheds blood and commits against his brother one of these faults,
though the father himself committed none of them. This son eats on the mountains, dishonors his neighbor's wife,
oppresses the poor and the needy, commits robbery, does not return the pledge, lifts his eyes to the idols, commits abominations,
lends at interest and takes a profit. Will he live? No, he will not live. He has committed all these abominations; he will die; his blood will be on his own head.
But suppose this son in turn fathers a son who sees all the sins his father committed, sees them, and does not act likewise.
He does not eat on the mountains, does not lift his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, does not dishonor his neighbor's wife,
oppresses no one, keeps no pledge, does not steal; he gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with a garment;
he does not lay his hand heavily on the poor, takes neither interest nor profit, keeps my laws and follows my precepts. Such a man will not die for his father's guilt: he will live.
As for his father, who practiced oppression, robbed his brother, and did evil among his people, he will die for his own guilt.
You ask: Why does the son not bear his father's guilt? Because the son practiced justice and righteousness, kept all my precepts and carried them out: he will live.

The one who sins, he is the one who will die. The son will not bear the father's guilt, nor the father the son's guilt: the righteousness of the righteous will be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked upon him.
As for the wicked man, if he turns away from all the sins he has committed, keeps all my precepts, and practices justice and righteousness, he will live; he will not die.
None of the faults he has committed will be remembered; because of the righteousness he has practiced, he will live.
Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked, oracle of the Lord God? Would I not rather that he turn from his conduct and live?

But if the righteous man turns away from his righteousness to do evil, imitating all the abominations of the wicked, will he live? None of the righteousness he practiced will be remembered; because of the unfaithfulness and the sin of which he is guilty, he will die.
You say: The Lord's way is not just. Listen then, house of Israel: is it my way that is not just? Is it not yours that are unjust?
When the righteous man turns away from his righteousness to do evil, and dies for it, it is because of the evil he has done that he dies.
And when the wicked man turns away from the wickedness he has committed to practice justice and righteousness, he saves his life.
He has opened his eyes and turned away from all the faults he had committed: he will live; he will not die.
Yet the house of Israel says: The Lord's way is not just. Are my ways the ones that are not just, house of Israel? Is it not yours that are unjust?
Therefore I will judge you, each according to his conduct, house of Israel, oracle of the Lord God. Return, turn away from all your faults, so that injustice may not bring about your ruin.
Cast away from you all the faults you have committed, and make yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, house of Israel?
For I take no pleasure in the death of anyone who dies, oracle of the Lord God. So repent, and live!"
As for you, raise a lament over the princes of Israel.
You shall say: What was your mother? A lioness lying among lions; among the young lions she reared her cubs.
She raised one of her cubs, who became a young lion; he learned to tear his prey and devoured men.
The nations heard of him; he was caught in their pit, and they led him off with hooks in his jaws to the land of Egypt.
Seeing her hope disappointed and her expectation lost, the lioness took another of her cubs and made him a young lion.
He prowled among the lions, became a young lion, learned to tear his prey and devoured men.
He ravaged their strongholds and laid waste their cities; the land and all it held were terrified at the sound of his roar.
Then the surrounding nations rose up against him, spread their nets over him, and he was caught in their pit.
They put him in a cage, with hooks in his jaws, and led him off to the king of Babylon; they shut him up in a stronghold, so that his voice would no longer be heard on the mountains of Israel.
Your mother was like a vine, planted by the waters in the time of your prosperity; she was fruitful and lush, thanks to abundant waters.
She had strong branches, fit for the scepters of kings; her height rose among the thick foliage, and she was seen in her loftiness, with the abundance of her shoots.
But she was uprooted in fury and thrown to the ground; the east wind dried up her fruit. Her strong branches were broken, dried up, devoured by fire.
Now she is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land.
A fire has gone out from her own branches and devoured her fruit; no strong branch remains on her, no scepter for ruling. This is a lament, and it has become a lament.

titres.titre: The gathering and judgment to come

versets.t: In the seventh year, on the tenth day of the fifth month (around July or August), some of the elders of Israel came to consult the Lord and sat down before me.
The word of the Lord came to me:

"Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and say to them: Thus says the Lord God. Have you come to consult me? As surely as I live, I will not let myself be consulted by you, oracle of the Lord God.
Will you judge them, son of man, will you judge them? Make known to them the abominations of their fathers.

Say to them: Thus says the Lord God. On the day I chose Israel, when I swore with uplifted hand to the descendants of Jacob, when I made myself known to them in Egypt, I swore to them with uplifted hand: I am the Lord your God.
On that day I swore to them that I would bring them out of Egypt and lead them into a land I had chosen for them, flowing with milk and honey, the jewel of all lands.
I said to them: Each of you, cast away the idols your eyes covet; do not defile yourselves with the abominations of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.

But they rebelled against me and refused to listen to me; none of them cast away the idols their eyes coveted, they did not abandon the abominations of Egypt. I thought of pouring out my fury upon them, of spending my anger against them in the midst of Egypt.

But I acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned before the eyes of the nations among whom they lived, before whose eyes I had made myself known to them in bringing them out of Egypt.
I brought them out of Egypt and led them into the wilderness.
I gave them my precepts and made known to them my laws, the ones by which whoever practices them will have life.
I also gave them my sabbaths, to serve as a sign between me and them, so that they would know that I am the Lord who sanctifies them.

But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness: they did not follow my precepts, they rejected my laws, the ones by which whoever practices them will live, and they gravely profaned my sabbaths. I thought of pouring out my fury upon them in the wilderness, to destroy them.
But I acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned before the eyes of the nations before whose eyes I had brought them out.
Yet I also swore to them with uplifted hand, in the wilderness, that I would not bring them into the land I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, the jewel of all lands,
because they had rejected my laws, had not followed my precepts, and had profaned my sabbaths, for their hearts followed their idols.
But my eye had pity on them; I did not destroy them or exterminate them in the wilderness.
I said to their children in the wilderness: Do not follow the rules of your fathers, do not keep their customs, do not defile yourselves with their idols.
I am the Lord your God: follow my precepts, keep my laws and practice them;
keep my sabbaths holy, so that they may be a sign between me and you, so that you may know that I am the Lord your God.

But the children rebelled against me: they did not follow my precepts, did not keep my laws, the ones by which whoever practices them will live, and they profaned my sabbaths. I thought of pouring out my fury upon them, of spending my anger against them in the wilderness.
But I held back my hand and acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned before the eyes of the nations before whose eyes I had brought them out.
Yet I also swore to them with uplifted hand, in the wilderness, that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the lands,
because they had not practiced my laws, had rejected my precepts, profaned my sabbaths, and their eyes ran after the idols of their fathers.
I even gave them precepts that were not good, laws by which they could not live.
I let them defile themselves with their offerings, making every firstborn pass through the fire: thus I filled them with horror, so that they would know that I am the Lord.
Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel and say to them: Thus says the Lord God. In this also your fathers outraged me, by their unfaithfulness toward me.

When I had brought them into the land I had sworn with uplifted hand to give them, as soon as they saw a high hill or a leafy tree, they offered their sacrifices there, presented there their provoking offerings, set there their soothing incense, and poured out there their drink offerings.
I said to them: What is this high place you go to? And it has been called High Place to this day.
Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God. What! You defile yourselves in the manner of your fathers, you prostitute yourselves after their abominations!

By presenting your offerings, by making your children pass through the fire, you defile yourselves with all your idols to this day, and shall I let myself be consulted by you, house of Israel? As surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God, I will not let myself be consulted by you.
It will not come to pass, the thought that rises in your minds when you say: We will be like the nations, like the peoples of other lands, serving wood and stone.
As surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God, with a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and an outpouring of fury I will reign over you.
I will bring you out from among the peoples, I will gather you from the lands where you have been scattered, with a strong hand, an outstretched arm, and an outpouring of fury.
I will lead you into the wilderness of the peoples, and there I will enter into judgment with you, face to face.
As I entered into judgment with your fathers in the wilderness of Egypt, so I will enter into judgment with you, oracle of the Lord God.
I will make you pass under the staff and bring you into the bonds of the covenant.

I will separate from you the rebels and those who have turned away from me; I will bring them out of the land where they live, but they will not enter the land of Israel, and you will know that I am the Lord.

As for you, house of Israel, thus says the Lord God: Go, serve your idols, each of you! But afterward, you will listen to me, most surely, and you will no longer profane my holy name with your offerings and your idols.

For on my holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, oracle of the Lord God, there all the house of Israel, all those in the land, will serve me; there I will receive them with favor, there I will require your contributions and the first of your gifts, with all your sacred offerings.

I will receive you as a pleasing aroma, when I have brought you out from among the peoples and gathered you from the lands where you are scattered; and through you I will show my holiness before the eyes of the nations.
You will know that I am the Lord, when I have brought you back to the land of Israel, to the land I swore with uplifted hand to give to your fathers.
There you will remember your conduct and all the deeds by which you defiled yourselves, and you will loathe yourselves for all the evil you have done.
You will know that I am the Lord, when I deal with you for the sake of my name, and not according to your evil conduct and your corrupt deeds, house of Israel, oracle of the Lord God."

titres.titre: The fire against the forest of the south
The sword drawn from the scabbard
The king of Babylon at the crossroads

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, turn your face toward the south, direct your word toward the south, and prophesy against the forest of the southern countryside.

Say to the forest of the south: Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God: I am about to kindle a fire in you, which will devour every green tree and every dry tree in you; the blazing flame will not be quenched, and every face will be scorched by it, from south to north.
And all will see that it is I, the Lord, who kindled it; it will not be quenched."
Then I said: "Ah, Lord God, they say of me: Does he not always speak in parables?"
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, turn your face toward Jerusalem, direct your word toward the sanctuary, and prophesy against the land of Israel.
Say to the land of Israel: Thus says the Lord. Here I am against you: I will draw my sword from its scabbard and cut off from you both the righteous and the wicked.
Since I am going to cut off from you the righteous and the wicked, my sword will come out of its scabbard against everyone, from south to north.
And all will know that it is I, the Lord, who drew my sword from its scabbard; it will not go back in again.
As for you, son of man, groan! With breaking heart, in bitterness, groan before their eyes.

And when they ask you: Why do you groan? you shall answer: Because of a report that is coming. Then every heart will melt, every hand will go limp, every spirit will faint, every knee will turn to water. Here it comes, it is done, oracle of the Lord God."
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, prophesy. You shall say: Thus says the Lord. Say: A sword, a sword! It is sharpened, it is polished.
Sharpened for the slaughter, polished to flash like lightning. How can we rejoice? The scepter of my son despises all wood.
It has been given to be polished, to be grasped; it is sharpened, this sword, it is polished to be put in the hand of the slayer.
Cry out and wail, son of man, for it is against my people, against all the princes of Israel, handed over to the sword along with my people. So strike your thigh!
For the test has been made; and what if that scepter full of scorn should disappear? oracle of the Lord God.
As for you, son of man, prophesy, clap your hands: let the sword strike twice, three times over! It is the sword of slaughter, the sword of great slaughter that hems them in.
So that hearts may melt and the victims may be many, I have set the deadly sword at all their gates. Ah! it is made to flash like lightning, polished for the slaughter.
Strike to the right, strike to the left, wherever your edge turns!
I too will clap my hands and satisfy my fury. I, the Lord, have spoken."
The word of the Lord came to me:
"As for you, son of man, trace two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to travel; let them both set out from the same land. Then carve a signpost, carve it where the road to each city begins.
Trace a road for the sword to Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another to Judah, against fortified Jerusalem.
For the king of Babylon halts at the crossroads, at the head of the two roads, to consult the omens: he shakes the arrows, questions his idols, examines the liver of the victims.

In his right hand falls the omen for Jerusalem: there, to set up battering rams, to open the mouth for the cry of slaughter, to raise the war cry, to set up battering rams against the gates, to raise ramps, to build siege works.
In their eyes it is only a false divination, they who have sworn sacred oaths; but he will call their guilt to mind, and they will be taken.

Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Because you yourselves bring your guilt to mind, laying bare your revolts, exposing your sins in all your conduct, because you thus bring yourselves to remembrance, you will be seized by force.
As for you, profaned, wicked prince of Israel, whose day has come, at the time when guilt is at its height,
thus says the Lord God: Take off the turban, remove the crown! Nothing will be as it was: what is low will be raised, what is high will be brought down.
Ruin, ruin, ruin, that is what I will make of it! And it will be no more, until he comes to whom the right belongs, and to him I will give it.

As for you, son of man, prophesy. You shall say: Thus says the Lord God against the Ammonites and their insults. Say: A sword, a sword is drawn for the slaughter, polished to devour and flash like lightning,
while they give you vain visions and lying omens, to lay you on the necks of the wicked who are handed over to the sword, whose day has come, at the time when guilt is at its height.
Put the sword back in its scabbard. In the place where you were created, in the land of your origin, I will judge you.
I will pour out my fury upon you, I will blow against you the fire of my anger, I will hand you over to brutal men, craftsmen of destruction.
You will be fuel for the fire, your blood will flow in the midst of the land, you will be remembered no more; for I, the Lord, have spoken."

titres.titre: The city of bloodshed and its crimes
The impure metal in the crucible

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
"And you, son of man, will you judge her, will you judge the city of bloodshed? Make known to her all her abominations.
You shall say: Thus says the Lord God. City that sheds blood within her walls to hasten her hour, and covers herself with idols to defile herself!

By the blood you have shed, you have made yourself guilty; by the idols you have made, you have defiled yourself; you have hastened your days and reached the end of your years. Therefore I make you the shame of the nations and the mockery of all the lands.
Near and far, all will jeer at you, city of defiled name, full of disorder.
See: in you, the princes of Israel each use their power to shed blood.
In you, father and mother are despised; in your midst, the resident alien is mistreated; in you, the orphan and the widow are oppressed.
You despise my holy things and profane my sabbaths.
In you, there are men who slander to cause bloodshed; in you, they eat on the mountains, they commit infamies in your midst.
In you, a man uncovers his father's nakedness; in you, a man violates a woman during her period.
One commits abomination with his neighbor's wife, another defiles his daughter-in-law by incest, another still violates his sister, his own father's daughter.
In you, they take bribes to shed blood; you lend at interest, you take a profit, you rob your neighbor by violence, and me you forget, oracle of the Lord God.
See, I clap my hands over the dishonest gain you have made and over the blood shed in your midst.
Will your heart hold firm, will your hands stay strong, on the day I act against you? I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will act.
I will scatter you among the nations, I will disperse you through the lands, and I will purge your defilement from you.
You will be dishonored before the eyes of the nations, and you will know that I am the Lord."
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me: they are all bronze, tin, iron, and lead at the bottom of the crucible, the dross of silver.
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Because you have all become dross, I am going to gather you into the middle of Jerusalem.

As silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin are heaped at the bottom of a crucible and the fire is blown upon them to melt them, so in my anger and my fury I will gather you, throw you in there, and melt you.
I will gather you and blow upon you the fire of my fury, and you will be melted in the middle of the city.
As silver melts at the bottom of the crucible, so you will be melted in her midst; and you will know that I, the Lord, have poured out my fury upon you."
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, say to this land: You are a land that has not been cleansed, that the rain has not washed on the day of wrath.
Her prophets hatch a conspiracy in her; like a roaring lion tearing its prey, they devour the people, seize wealth and treasures, and multiply the widows in her midst.

Her priests violate my law and profane my holy things; they do not distinguish the sacred from the profane, they do not teach the difference between the unclean and the clean; they close their eyes to my sabbaths, and I am profaned among them.
Her officials, in her midst, are like wolves tearing their prey: they shed blood and destroy lives for dishonest gain.
And her prophets whitewash all this for them with vain visions and lying omens; they say: Thus says the Lord God, when the Lord has not spoken.
The people of the land multiply violence and robbery, oppress the poor and the needy, and mistreat the resident alien in defiance of justice.
I sought among them someone to rebuild the wall and stand in the breach before me, on behalf of the land, so that I would not destroy it; but I found no one.
So I poured out my fury upon them, I consumed them with the fire of my anger, and I brought their conduct down upon their own heads, oracle of the Lord God."

titres.titre: The two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah
The judgment of the two sisters

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, there were two women, daughters of the same mother.
They prostituted themselves in Egypt; from their youth they prostituted themselves. There their breasts were fondled, there their maiden bosoms were pressed.
These are their names: Oholah, the elder, and Oholibah, her sister. They were mine and bore sons and daughters. Their names: Oholah is Samaria; Oholibah is Jerusalem.
Oholah was unfaithful to me: she burned for her lovers, the Assyrians, her neighbors,
clothed in purple, governors and magistrates, all of them handsome young men, horsemen mounted on their horses.
She prostituted herself to them, to all the elite of Assyria, and defiled herself with all the idols of those for whom she burned.
Nor did she give up her prostitutions from Egypt, where men had lain with her from her youth, pressing her maiden bosom and pouring out their lust upon her.
Therefore I handed her over into the hands of her lovers, into the hands of the Assyrians for whom she burned.
They uncovered her nakedness, took her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became a byword among women, for judgment had been carried out on her.
Her sister Oholibah saw all this, and her lust was even more depraved, her prostitutions worse than her sister's.
She burned for the Assyrians, governors and officials, her richly clothed neighbors, horsemen mounted on their horses, all of them handsome young men.
I saw that she too was defiling herself: both followed the same way.
But she carried her prostitutions further: she saw men drawn on the wall, images of Chaldeans traced in vermilion,
with belts around their waists, their heads wrapped in ample turbans, all with the look of officers, in the likeness of the Babylonians whose native land is Chaldea.
She burned for them as soon as her eyes saw them, and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
The Babylonians came to her on the bed of love and defiled her with their prostitutions; she defiled herself with them, then turned from them in disgust.
She flaunted her prostitutions and uncovered her nakedness, and I turned from her in disgust as I had turned from her sister.
She multiplied her prostitutions still more, recalling the days of her youth, when she prostituted herself in Egypt.
She burned for their debauched men, whose flesh is like the flesh of donkeys and whose ardor is like that of stallions.
So you returned to the crimes of your youth, when the Egyptians fondled your breasts, that maiden bosom.
Therefore, Oholibah, thus says the Lord God: I am going to rouse against you your lovers, those from whom you turned in disgust, and I will bring them against you from every side,

the Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, men of Pekod, Shoa, and Koa, and with them all the Assyrians, handsome young men, all of them governors and magistrates, officers and men of rank, all mounted on their horses.

They will come against you with weapons, chariots, and wagons, a multitude of peoples; they will surround you with large and small shields and helmets. I will hand the judgment over to them, and they will judge you by their own laws.

I will turn my jealousy against you, and they will deal with you in fury: they will cut off your nose and your ears, and what is left of you will fall by the sword; they will take your sons and daughters, and the rest will be devoured by fire.
They will strip you of your garments and take away your jewels.
Thus I will put an end to your infamy and your prostitutions begun in Egypt: you will no longer lift your eyes toward them, you will remember Egypt no more.
For thus says the Lord God: I am going to hand you over into the hands of those you hate, into the hands of those from whom you turned in disgust.
They will deal with you in hatred, carry off all the fruit of your labor, and leave you naked, utterly naked; thus your debauchery and your shamelessness, your prostitutions, will be laid bare.
This is what will be done to you, because you prostituted yourself to the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.
You have followed the way of your sister: I will put her cup into your hand.
Thus says the Lord God: You will drink your sister's cup, a cup deep and wide, which will bring laughter and mockery, so much does it hold.
You will be filled with drunkenness and grief. It is a cup of ruin and desolation, the cup of your sister Samaria.
You will drink it, you will drain it, you will gnaw its shards and tear your breasts with them. Yes, I have spoken, oracle of the Lord God.
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Because you have forgotten me and cast me behind your back, bear then, you too, the weight of your infamy and your prostitutions."
The Lord said to me: "Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Denounce to them their abominations.

For they have committed adultery, they have blood on their hands; they have committed adultery with their idols, and even the sons they had borne to me, they made them pass through the fire to give them as food to their idols.
They did this to me as well: on the same day, they defiled my sanctuary and profaned my sabbaths.
After slaughtering their sons to their idols, they entered that very day into my sanctuary to profane it: this is what they did within my house.
They even sent for men from far away; no sooner was the messenger sent to them than they arrived. For them you bathed yourself, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with jewels.
You sat on a stately couch, with a table spread before you, on which you had set my incense and my oil.

The sound of a carefree crowd was heard there; to these common folk were joined drinkers brought from the wilderness, who put bracelets on the wrists of the two sisters and magnificent crowns on their heads.
Then I said, about this woman worn out by adultery: Now they will prostitute themselves with her, and she with them?
And they went in to her as one goes to a prostitute. So they went in to Oholah and Oholibah, those criminal women.
But righteous men will judge them by the law for adulterous women and for those who shed blood; for they are adulteresses and have blood on their hands.
Thus says the Lord God: Let an assembly be brought up against them, and let them be handed over to terror and plunder.
Let the assembly pelt them with stones and cut them to pieces with the sword; let their sons and daughters be killed, and their houses burned.
Thus I will put an end to infamy in the land; all women will take the lesson from it and will not imitate your debauchery.
Your infamy will be brought down upon you, you will bear the weight of your sins of idolatry, and you will know that I am the Lord God."

titres.titre: The death of the prophet's wife, a sign

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me, in the ninth year, on the tenth day of the tenth month (around December or January):
"Son of man, write down the date of this day, this very day: today the king of Babylon has thrown himself upon Jerusalem.
Tell a parable to the rebellious house. You shall say to them: Thus says the Lord God. Set the pot on the fire, set it on, and pour in water.
Pile in the pieces, all the good pieces, the thigh and the shoulder; fill it with the best bones.
Take the best of the flock, heap up the wood under the pot, bring it to a rolling boil, and let even the bones cook in it.
For thus says the Lord God: Woe to the city of bloodshed, that rusted pot whose rust will not come off! Empty it piece by piece, without even casting lots.
For the blood she shed is in her midst: she left it on the bare rock, without pouring it on the ground to cover it with dust.
To stir up my fury and take vengeance, I have left her blood on the bare rock, so that it would not be covered.
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: Woe to the city of bloodshed! I too will build a great pyre.
Heap up the wood, kindle the fire, cook the meat, boil down the broth, and let the bones be burned.
Then set the empty pot on the coals, so that the bronze may heat and glow, its filth melt within it, and its rust disappear.
All in vain! Its coat of rust is so thick that it resists the fire.

Your defilement is an outrage. Because I sought to cleanse you and you would not let yourself be cleansed, you will no longer be cleansed of your defilement, until I have satisfied my fury against you.

I, the Lord, have spoken: it is coming, and I will do it. I will not draw back, I will not have pity, I will not relent; you will be judged according to your conduct and your deeds, oracle of the Lord God."
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, behold, I am about to take away from you, at a single stroke, the delight of your eyes. But you shall not mourn, you shall not weep, you shall let no tears fall.
Groan in silence, do not mourn for the dead: keep your turban on your head and your sandals on your feet, do not cover the lower part of your face, do not eat the bread of mourners."
In the morning I spoke to the people; in the evening my wife died; and the next morning I did as I had been commanded.
The people said to me: "Will you not explain to us what your behavior means for us?"
I answered them: "The word of the Lord came to me:

Say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God. Behold, I am about to profane my sanctuary, the pride of your strength, the delight of your eyes, the longing of your soul; and your sons and daughters whom you left behind will fall by the sword.
Then you will do as I have done: you will not cover the lower part of your face, you will not eat the bread of mourners,
you will keep your turban on your head and your sandals on your feet; you will not mourn, you will not weep, but you will waste away in your guilt, groaning to one another.
Ezekiel will be a sign for you: everything he has done, you will do; and when it comes to pass, you will know that I am the Lord God.
As for you, son of man, on the day I take from them their stronghold, their joy and their glory, the delight of their eyes and the longing of their soul, their sons and daughters,
on that day a fugitive will come to bring you the news.
On that day your mouth will open at the same time as the fugitive speaks; you will speak, you will no longer be mute, and you will be a sign for them; and they will know that I am the Lord."
The word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, set your face toward the Ammonites and prophesy against them.

Say to the Ammonites: Hear the word of the Lord God. Thus says the Lord God: Because you cried out, 'Aha! Aha!' over my sanctuary when it was profaned, over the land of Israel when it was laid waste, and over the house of Judah when it went into exile,

therefore I am about to hand you over as a possession to the people of the East. They will pitch their camps among you and set up their tents in your midst; they will eat your fruit and drink your milk.
I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels and the land of the Ammonites a fold for sheep; and you will know that I am the Lord.
For thus says the Lord God: Because you clapped your hands, stamped your feet, and rejoiced with utter contempt over the land of Israel,

therefore I now stretch out my hand against you: I will give you as plunder to the nations, cut you off from among the peoples, and make you vanish from the lands; I will destroy you, and you will know that I am the Lord.
Thus says the Lord God: Because Moab and Seir said, 'Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations,'
therefore I will lay open the flank of Moab, stripping it of its cities, of all its cities, the glory of the land: Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim.
I will hand it over, along with the land of the Ammonites, as a possession to the people of the East, so that the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations.
I will execute my judgments on Moab, and they will know that I am the Lord.
Thus says the Lord God: Because Edom took cruel revenge on the house of Judah and made itself deeply guilty by avenging itself on them,
therefore thus says the Lord God: I will stretch out my hand against Edom, cut off from it man and beast, and make it a ruin; from Teman to Dedan they will fall by the sword.
I will take my vengeance on Edom by the hand of my people Israel; they will deal with Edom according to my anger and my wrath, and Edom will know my vengeance, oracle of the Lord God.
Thus says the Lord God: Because the Philistines acted in vengeance and took revenge with contempt, driven by endless hatred, bent on destruction,
therefore thus says the Lord God: I now stretch out my hand against the Philistines; I will cut off the Cherethites and destroy what remains on the seacoast.
I will wreak terrible vengeance on them, furious punishments; and they will know that I am the Lord, when I bring my vengeance upon them."

titres.titre: Tyre and the fall of Jerusalem

versets.t: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me:
"Son of man, because Tyre said of Jerusalem, 'Aha! The gateway of the peoples is shattered! It has swung open to me; I will grow rich now that she lies in ruins!'
therefore thus says the Lord God: I am against you, Tyre! I will bring up against you many nations, as the sea heaves up its waves.
They will destroy the walls of Tyre and tear down her towers; I will scrape away even her dust and make her a bare rock.
In the midst of the sea she will become a place for spreading nets. Yes, I have spoken, oracle of the Lord God; she will be plunder for the nations.
Her daughter-towns on the mainland will be put to the sword, and they will know that I am the Lord.

For thus says the Lord God: I am bringing against Tyre, from the north, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, with horses, chariots, cavalry, and a great host of troops and a numerous people.
He will put your daughter-towns on the mainland to the sword; he will throw up siege works against you, raise ramps, and set up a roof of shields against you.
He will drive his battering rams against your walls and tear down your towers with his iron bars.
His horses will be so many that their dust will cover you; at the din of cavalry, wheels, and chariots your walls will shake, when he enters your gates as men enter a city that has been breached.
With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets; he will put your people to the sword, and your proud pillars will crash to the ground.
They will plunder your wealth and loot your merchandise; they will break down your walls, demolish your fine houses, and cast your stones, your timber, and your rubble into the depths of the waters.
I will silence the sound of your songs, and the music of your lyres will be heard no more.
I will make you a bare rock, a place for spreading nets; you will never be rebuilt, for I the Lord have spoken, oracle of the Lord God.
Thus says the Lord God to Tyre: At the crash of your fall, when your wounded groan and the slaughter rages within you, will the coastlands not tremble?

Then all the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones, lay aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments; clothed in terror, they will sit on the ground, trembling without end, appalled at your fate.

They will raise a lament over you and say to you: How you have perished, you who were peopled from the seas, O celebrated city, once mighty upon the waves, you and your inhabitants, who spread your terror over all who dwelt nearby!
Now the coastlands tremble on the day of your fall; the islands of the sea are appalled at your end.
For thus says the Lord God: When I make you a deserted city, like cities that have no inhabitants, when I bring the deep up over you and the great waters cover you,

I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of long ago; I will make you dwell in the depths of the earth, among everlasting ruins, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not be inhabited; and I will restore glory to the land of the living.
I will make you an object of horror, and you will be no more; you will be sought, but never again will you be found, oracle of the Lord God."

titres.titre: The shipwreck in the heart of the seas

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me:
"You, son of man, raise a lament over Tyre.
Say to Tyre, enthroned at the gateways of the sea, trading with the peoples of many distant coastlands: Thus says the Lord God. Tyre, you said, 'I am perfect in beauty.'
Your domain lies in the heart of the seas; your builders made your beauty perfect.
They made all your planking of cypress from Senir; they took a cedar of Lebanon to make you a mast.
From oaks of Bashan they made your oars; they made your deck of ivory inlaid in boxwood from the coasts of Kittim.
Embroidered linen from Egypt formed your sail and served as your banner; violet and scarlet from the coasts of Elishah formed your awnings.
The people of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; your own skilled men, Tyre, were aboard as your pilots.
The elders of Gebal and its craftsmen were there to caulk your seams. All the ships of the sea and their sailors came to you to carry on your trade.
Men of Persia, Lud, and Put served in your army; they hung shield and helmet within you and gave you your splendor.
The men of Arvad and your own army manned your walls all around, and valiant warriors held your towers; they hung their shields on your walls all around, making your beauty perfect.
Tarshish traded with you because of your abundant wealth: silver, iron, tin, and lead they gave in payment for your wares.
Javan, Tubal, and Meshech traded with you: they exchanged slaves and articles of bronze for your merchandise.
Those of Beth-togarmah paid for your wares with draft horses, war horses, and mules.
The people of Dedan traded with you; the commerce of many coastlands passed through your hands, and they paid you with tusks of ivory and ebony.
Aram traded with you because of your abundant goods; they paid for your wares with garnet, purple, embroidery, fine linen, coral, and rubies.
Judah and the land of Israel traded with you: they exchanged wheat from Minnith, millet, honey, oil, and balm for your merchandise.
Damascus traded with you because of your abundant goods and great wealth: it brought wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
Vedan and Javan, from Uzal, paid for your wares with wrought iron, cassia, and fragrant cane.
Dedan traded with you in saddlecloths.
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar traded with you: they dealt in lambs, rams, and goats.
The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded with you: they paid for your wares with the finest spices, all kinds of precious stones, and gold.
Haran, Canneh, and Eden, the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad traded with you.
They brought you luxury goods: cloaks of purple and brocade, chests of embroidered garments, cords tightly and strongly woven, in your marketplaces.
The ships of Tarshish were the caravans of your trade; you were filled and laden with glory in the heart of the seas.
Out on the great waters your rowers carried you; the east wind broke you in the heart of the seas.

Your wealth, your wares, your cargo, your sailors and your pilots, your caulkers, the brokers of your trade, all your men of war, and the whole crowd aboard will sink into the heart of the seas on the day of your fall.
At the cry of your pilots the shorelands will tremble.
All who handle the oar will come down from their ships; the sailors, all the pilots of the sea, will stand on the land.
They will lift up their voice over you, cry out bitterly, throw dust on their heads, and roll in ashes.
For you they will shave their heads, put on sackcloth, and weep over you with bitter soul, in wrenching sobs.
In their grief they will raise a lament over you and mourn thus: Who was ever like Tyre, now silenced in the midst of the sea?
When your wares came in from the seas, you satisfied many peoples; with your abundant goods and trade you enriched the kings of the earth.
Now that you are broken by the seas, sunk in the depths of the waters, your wares and all your crew have gone down with you.
All who dwell on the coastlands are appalled at you; their kings are seized with horror, their faces distraught.
The merchants of the peoples hiss at you; you have become an object of horror, and forever you are no more."

titres.titre: Lament over the king of Tyre

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me in these terms:

"Son of man, say to the prince of Tyre: Thus says the Lord God: Your heart has grown proud, and you have said, 'I am a god; I sit on a divine throne in the heart of the seas.' But you are only a man, and no god, though you think yourself as wise as a god.
So you are wiser than Daniel! No secret is hidden from you!
By your wisdom and understanding you have made yourself a fortune, and you have heaped up gold and silver in your treasuries.
By your great skill in trade you have increased your wealth, and your wealth has made your heart proud.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you thought yourself as wise as a god,
I am bringing against you foreigners, the most brutal of the nations. They will draw their swords against the masterworks of your wisdom and profane your splendor.
They will thrust you down into the pit, and you will die the death of the slain in the heart of the seas.
Will you still say, 'I am a god,' before the one who kills you? You will be only a man, and no god, in the hands of those who slay you.
You will die the death of the uncircumcised at the hand of foreigners. Yes, I have spoken, oracle of the Lord God."
The word of the Lord came to me in these terms: "Son of man, raise a lament over the king of Tyre,
and say to him: Thus says the Lord God: You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.

You were in Eden, the garden of God. Every kind of precious stone covered you: carnelian, topaz, and diamond, chrysolite, onyx, and jasper, sapphire, garnet, and emerald, set in gold. Your tambourines and your flutes were in your service, prepared on the very day you were created.
You were the guardian cherub, the one I had consecrated. I had set you on the holy mountain of God, and you walked among the stones of fire.
Your conduct was blameless from the day you were created, until the day iniquity was found in you.
Through your widespread trade you were filled with violence, and you sinned. So I banished you from the mountain of God, and I destroyed you, O guardian cherub, from among the stones of fire.
Your heart grew proud because of your beauty; your splendor corrupted your wisdom. I threw you to the ground; I made you a spectacle before kings.

By your many sins, by the dishonesty of your trade, you profaned your sanctuaries. So I brought fire out of your midst; it devoured you, and I reduced you to ashes on the ground, before the eyes of all who watched you.
Among the peoples all who knew you are appalled at you. You have become an object of horror, and forever you are no more."
The word of the Lord came to me in these terms:
"Son of man, set your face toward Sidon and prophesy against her.
Say: Thus says the Lord God: I am against you, Sidon, and I will show my glory in your midst. They will know that I am the Lord, when I execute my judgments against her and reveal my holiness in her.
I will send plague against her, and blood will flow in her streets. In her midst the slain will fall by the sword that strikes her on every side. And they will know that I am the Lord.
Then the house of Israel will no longer have a pricking briar or a tearing thorn among all its neighbors who despise it. And they will know that I am the Lord God.

Thus says the Lord God: When I gather the house of Israel from among the peoples where they are scattered, I will reveal my holiness through them in the sight of the nations. They will dwell on their own land, the land I gave to my servant Jacob.

They will dwell there in safety, build houses, and plant vineyards. They will dwell in safety, when I have executed my judgments on all their neighbors who despise them. And they will know that I am the Lord their God."

titres.titre: Pharaoh, the crocodile of the Nile

versets.t: In the tenth year, on the twelfth day of the tenth month (around December-January), the word of the Lord came to me in these terms:
"Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt and prophesy against him and against all of Egypt.
Speak and say: Thus says the Lord God: I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt, great crocodile lying in the midst of your rivers, you who say, 'My Nile is mine; I made it myself.'
I will put hooks in your jaws and make the fish of your rivers cling to your scales; I will pull you up out of the midst of your rivers, with all the fish of your rivers clinging to your scales.
I will fling you into the desert, you and all the fish of your rivers. You will fall in the open field, not gathered or buried. I give you as food to the beasts of the earth and the birds of the sky.
Then all the inhabitants of Egypt will know that I am the Lord. For they have been only a staff of reed to the house of Israel.
When they grasped you in their hand, you splintered and tore open their whole shoulder; when they leaned on you, you broke and made their backs give way.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: I am bringing the sword against you, and I will cut off from you man and beast.
The land of Egypt will become a desolate ruin, and they will know that I am the Lord. Because you said, 'The Nile is mine; I made it,'
therefore I am against you and against your rivers. I will make the land of Egypt an utter waste and desolation, from Migdol to Syene, as far as the border of Cush.
No foot of man will pass through it, no foot of beast will cross it: it will remain uninhabited for forty years.

I will make the land of Egypt a desolation among the devastated lands; its cities, among the ruined cities, will lie desolate for forty years. And I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands.
For thus says the Lord God: At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples among whom they were scattered.
I will restore the fortunes of Egypt and bring them back to the land of Pathros, their land of origin, and there they will be a lowly kingdom.
Egypt will be the lowliest of kingdoms; it will never again raise itself above the nations. I will make it so small that it will never again rule over the nations.
It will no longer be a source of confidence for the house of Israel; rather it will recall Israel's guilt in turning to it. And they will know that I am the Lord God."
In the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month (around March-April), the word of the Lord came to me in these terms:

"Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made his army labor hard against Tyre: every head was rubbed bald and every shoulder chafed raw. Yet neither he nor his army got anything from Tyre in return for the labor he waged against her.
