Therefore thus says the Lord God: I am giving the land of Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. He will carry off its wealth, plunder it, and strip it bare: this will be the wages of his army.
As the wages for his labor against Tyre, I am giving him the land of Egypt, because they worked for me, oracle of the Lord God.
On that day I will make a horn sprout for the house of Israel, and to you I will grant to open your mouth among them. And they will know that I am the Lord."
The word of the Lord came to me in these terms:
"Son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord God: Wail, 'Alas for the day!'
For the day is near, near is the day of the Lord! A day of clouds, the appointed time for the nations!
A sword will come upon Egypt, and anguish will seize Cush, when the slain fall in Egypt, when its wealth is carried off and its foundations are torn down.
Cush, Put, and Lud, all the mixed multitude, Cub, and the people of the covenant land will fall with them by the sword.
Thus says the Lord: They will fall, the supports of Egypt, and the pride of her strength will collapse. From Migdol to Syene they will fall by the sword within her, oracle of the Lord God.
Egypt will lie desolate among the devastated lands, and its cities will be counted among the ruined cities.
And they will know that I am the Lord, when I set fire to Egypt and all her allies are broken.
On that day messengers will go out from me in boats to terrify Cush in its complacency, and anguish will seize it as on the day of Egypt. Look, it is coming!
Thus says the Lord God: I will put an end to the horde of Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
He and his people, the most brutal of the nations, will be brought in to ravage the land. They will draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.
I will dry up the rivers and hand the land over to cruel men; by the hand of foreigners I will lay waste the land and everything in it. I the Lord have spoken.
Thus says the Lord God: I will destroy the idols and put an end to the false gods of Noph. There will be no more prince in the land of Egypt, and I will spread terror throughout it.
I will make Pathros desolate, set fire to Zoan, and execute my judgments against No.
I will pour out my wrath on Sin, the stronghold of Egypt, and cut off the horde of No.
I will set fire to Egypt: Sin will writhe in anguish, No will be breached, and Noph will face the enemy in broad daylight.
The young men of Aven and Bubastis will fall by the sword, and these cities themselves will go into captivity.
At Tahpanhes the day will grow dark, when I break there the yoke of Egypt and the pride of her strength comes to an end. A cloud will cover her, and her daughter-towns will go into captivity.
I will execute my judgments against Egypt, and they will know that I am the Lord."
In the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month (around March-April), the word of the Lord came to me in these terms:
"Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. And look: it has not been bound up or treated with remedies, no bandage has been set to heal it, to give it strength to hold a sword.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will break both his arms, the strong one and the one already broken, and I will make the sword fall from his hand.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands.
I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon and put my sword in his hand; but I will break the arms of Pharaoh, who will groan before him like a man wounded to death.

I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon, and the arms of Pharaoh will fall limp. And they will know that I am the Lord, when I put my sword in the hand of the king of Babylon and he brandishes it against the land of Egypt.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands. And they will know that I am the Lord."

titres.titre: The allegory of the great cedar
Its descent to the realm of the dead

versets.t: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month (around May-June), the word of the Lord came to me in these terms:
"Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to all his horde: Whom do you resemble in your greatness?
Look: Assyria was a cedar of Lebanon, with splendid branches, dense shade, and towering height, its crown lost among the clouds.
The waters made it grow, the deep made it tall, sending its streams around the place where it was planted and directing its channels to all the trees of the field.
So its height surpassed all the trees of the field; its boughs multiplied and its branches grew long, thanks to the abundant waters that nourished it.
In its boughs all the birds of the sky nested, under its branches all the beasts of the field gave birth, and in its shade dwelt many nations.
It was magnificent in its greatness and the spread of its boughs, for its roots reached down to abundant waters.

The cedars in the garden of God did not overshadow it, the cypresses could not match its boughs, the plane trees could not compare with its branches: no tree in the garden of God rivaled it in beauty.
I made it so beautiful, with its abundant foliage, that all the trees of Eden envied it, in the garden of God.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because it towered so high, lifting its crown among the clouds, and its heart grew proud of its height,
I handed it over to the lord of the nations, to deal with it as its wickedness deserved. Because of its wickedness I cast it out.

Foreigners, the most brutal of the nations, cut it down and left it there. On the mountains and in all the valleys its boughs fell; its broken branches lie in all the ravines of the land. All the peoples of the earth left its shade and abandoned it.
On its fallen trunk all the birds of the sky settle, and among its branches lodge all the beasts of the field.

So no tree planted by the waters will ever again tower so high or lift its crown among the clouds; none that drinks the water will ever stand tall in its pride. For all are doomed to death, to the depths of the earth, mingled with the sons of men, with those who go down to the pit.

Thus says the Lord God: On the day it went down to the realm of the dead, I made a mourning; because of it I veiled the deep and held back its rivers, and the great waters were stopped; because of it I darkened Lebanon, and all the trees of the field withered away.

At the crash of its fall I made the nations tremble, when I cast it down to the realm of the dead with those who go down to the pit. Then, in the depths of the earth, all the trees of Eden were consoled, the choicest and most magnificent of Lebanon, all that drank the waters.
They too went down with it to the realm of the dead, to those slain by the sword; they had been its arm, dwelling in its shade among the nations.

So whom do you resemble in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? You will be cast down with the trees of Eden into the depths of the earth; you will lie among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword. Such is the fate of Pharaoh and all his horde, oracle of the Lord God."

titres.titre: Egypt's descent to the realm of the dead

versets.t: In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month (around February-March), the word of the Lord came to me in these terms:

"Son of man, raise a lament over Pharaoh king of Egypt. Say to him: Lion of the nations, you are destroyed! You were like the crocodile in the seas, thrashing in your rivers, churning the waters with your feet and stirring up their channels.
Thus says the Lord God: I will spread my net over you, by means of a great assembly of peoples, and they will haul you up in my dragnet.
I will abandon you on the ground, hurl you into the open field; I will make all the birds of the sky settle on you, the beasts of all the earth gorge themselves on you.
I will scatter your flesh on the mountains and fill the valleys with your remains.
I will drench the land with the flow of your blood, up to the mountains, and the ravines will be filled with you.
When you are snuffed out, I will veil the heavens and darken their stars; I will cover the sun with clouds, and the moon will no longer give its light.
Because of you I will darken all the shining lights in the sky, and I will spread darkness over your land, oracle of the Lord God.
I will trouble the hearts of many peoples, when I bring news of your ruin among nations, in lands you have not known.

Because of you I will strike many peoples with horror; their kings will shudder with dread when I brandish my sword before them, and they will tremble at every moment, each for his own life, on the day of your fall.
For thus says the Lord God: The sword of the king of Babylon will come upon you.
I will make your horde fall by the swords of warriors, the most brutal of the nations. They will break the pride of Egypt, and all her horde will be destroyed.
I will make all her cattle vanish from beside the great waters; no foot of man will trouble them again, no hoof of beast will stir them.
Then I will make her waters run clear and her rivers flow like oil, oracle of the Lord God,
when I turn Egypt into a wasteland, when the land is stripped of all it holds, when I strike down all who dwell in it. And they will know that I am the Lord.
This is the lament that will be chanted. The daughters of the nations will chant it; they will chant it over Egypt and all her horde, oracle of the Lord God."
In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month, the word of the Lord came to me in these terms:
"Son of man, wail over the horde of Egypt, and bring her down, her and the daughters of the mighty nations, to the depths of the earth, with those who go down to the pit.
Are you more beautiful than any other? Go down and lie with the uncircumcised!
They will fall among those slain by the sword. The sword is ready: drag off Egypt and all her hordes!
From the midst of the realm of the dead, the mightiest of the heroes will speak to him, with his allies: They have come down, they lie still, these uncircumcised, slain by the sword!
There is Assyria with all her army, her graves around her: all of them slain, all fallen by the sword.
Her graves are set in the deepest part of the pit, her army ranged around her tomb: all of them slain, all fallen by the sword, they who once spread terror in the land of the living.

There is Elam and all her horde around her tomb: all of them slain, all fallen by the sword, gone down uncircumcised to the depths of the earth, they who once spread terror in the land of the living. They bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

Among the slain a bed has been made for her, amid all her horde, her graves around her: all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword, for they spread terror in the land of the living. They bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit; they have been laid among the slain.
There are Meshech, Tubal, and all their horde, their graves around them: all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword, for they spread terror in the land of the living.

They do not lie with the heroes fallen of old, who went down to the realm of the dead with their weapons, their swords laid under their heads; but their guilt rests on their bones, for these heroes spread terror in the land of the living.
You too will be broken among the uncircumcised, and lie with those slain by the sword.
There is Edom, with its kings and all its princes who, for all their valor, were laid among those slain by the sword. They lie with the uncircumcised, with those who go down to the pit.

There are all the princes of the north and all the Sidonians: they went down with the slain, in shame despite the terror their valor inspired. They lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword, and they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.
Pharaoh will see them and be consoled over all his horde: Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, oracle of the Lord God.
For I had spread his terror in the land of the living; and now he lies among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword, he, Pharaoh, and all his horde, oracle of the Lord God."

titres.titre: Each answers for his own way
A people who listen without acting

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me in these terms:
"Son of man, speak to the children of your people. Say to them: When I bring the sword upon a land, and the people of that land take one of their own and set him up as their watchman,
and this man, seeing the sword come upon the land, blows the horn to warn the people,
then, if anyone hears the horn but takes no warning, and the sword comes and carries him off, his blood will be on his own head.
He heard the horn but took no warning: his blood will be on himself. Had he taken warning, he would have saved his life.

But if the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the horn, so that the people are not warned, and the sword comes and carries off one of them, that man will be carried off for his own guilt, but I will hold the watchman accountable for his blood.
You, son of man, I have made a watchman for the house of Israel. When you hear a word from my mouth, you will warn them on my behalf.

When I say to the wicked, 'Wicked man, you will surely die,' if you do not speak to warn him to turn from his way, that wicked man will die in his guilt, but I will hold you accountable for his blood.
But if you warn the wicked to turn from his way, and he does not turn, he will die in his guilt, and you will have saved your life.
You, son of man, say to the house of Israel: You keep saying, 'Our offenses and our sins weigh on us; because of them we are wasting away; how then can we live?'

Say to them: As surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that he turn from his way and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why should you die, house of Israel?

You, son of man, say to the children of your people: The righteousness of the righteous will not save him on the day he rebels, and the wickedness of the wicked will not bring him down on the day he turns from it; the righteous will not be able to live by his righteousness on the day he sins.
When I tell the righteous that he will surely live, if he trusts in his righteousness and does evil, none of his righteous deeds will be remembered: because of the evil he has done, he will die.
And when I say to the wicked, 'You will surely die,' if he turns from his sin and does what is just and right,
if he returns the pledge, restores what he has stolen, follows the statutes that give life, and stops doing evil, then he will surely live; he will not die.
None of the sins he committed will be remembered: he has done what is just and right; he will surely live.
The children of your people say, 'The way of the Lord is not just.' But it is their own way that is not just.
When a righteous man turns from his righteousness and does evil, he dies for it.
And when a wicked man turns from his wickedness and does what is just and right, he lives by it.
Yet you say, 'The way of the Lord is not just!' I will judge each of you according to his ways, house of Israel."
In the twelfth year of our exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month (around December-January), a fugitive from Jerusalem came to me and announced, "The city has fallen."
Now, the evening before, the hand of the Lord had been on me, and he had opened my mouth before the fugitive arrived in the morning. My mouth was opened, and I was no longer mute.
The word of the Lord came to me in these terms:

"Son of man, the inhabitants of these ruins, in the land of Israel, keep saying: 'Abraham was only one man, and he received the land as his possession; we are many, so the land is surely given to us as a possession.'
Therefore say to them: Thus says the Lord God: You eat meat with the blood, you lift your eyes to your idols, you shed blood, and would you possess the land?
You rely on your sword, you commit abominations, each of you dishonors his neighbor's wife, and would you possess the land?

This is what you will say to them: Thus says the Lord God: As surely as I live, those who are in the ruins will fall by the sword; those in the open country I will give as food to the beasts; and those in the strongholds and caves will die of plague.
I will make the land a desolate waste, the pride of its strength will end, and the mountains of Israel will be so desolate that no one will pass through them.
And they will know that I am the Lord, when I have made the land a desolate waste, because of all the abominations they have committed.

As for you, son of man, the children of your people gossip about you along the walls and at the doorways of the houses. They say to one another, 'Come, let's go hear what word has come from the Lord!'
They come to you in crowds, my people sit before you and listen to your words; but they do not put them into practice. On their lips they make a song of it, while their hearts run after gain.
Look, to them you are like a love song, a beautiful voice backed by skilled music. They listen to your words, but they do not put them into practice.
When this comes to pass, and it is coming, they will know that a prophet was among them."

titres.titre: The Lord, shepherd of his people

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me in these terms:

"Son of man, prophesy against the shepherds of Israel. Prophesy and say to them, to those shepherds: Thus says the Lord God: Woe to the shepherds of Israel, who only feed themselves! Should not shepherds feed the flock?
You eat the fat, you clothe yourselves with the wool, you slaughter the fattened animals, but you do not feed the flock.
You have not strengthened the weak, healed the sick, bound up the injured, brought back the strayed, or sought the lost; instead you have ruled them with violence and harshness.
For lack of a shepherd they were scattered and became prey for all the wild beasts.
My sheep wander over all the mountains and on every high hill; they are scattered over the whole face of the land, and no one cares for them, no one searches for them.
Therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord:

As surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God: because my sheep have been given up to plunder and have become prey for all the wild beasts, for lack of a shepherd, because my shepherds did not search for my sheep but fed themselves and did not feed the flock,
therefore, shepherds, hear the word of the Lord:

Thus says the Lord God: I am against the shepherds. I will require my sheep from their hand; I will no longer let them feed the flock, and they will no longer feed themselves. I will rescue my sheep from their mouths: they will no longer be food for them.
For thus says the Lord God: Here I am! I myself will care for my sheep and watch over them.

As a shepherd watches over his flock on the day he is among his scattered sheep, so I will watch over my sheep. I will rescue them from all the places where they were scattered on a day of clouds and darkness.

I will bring them out from among the peoples, gather them from the various lands, and lead them back to their own soil. I will feed them on the mountains of Israel, in the valleys, and in all the inhabited places of the land.
I will feed them in good pastures, and their fold will be on the high mountains of Israel. There they will rest in a good fold and graze on rich pasture on the mountains of Israel.
I myself will feed my sheep, I myself will make them lie down, oracle of the Lord God.
I will seek the lost, bring back the strayed, bind up the injured, and strengthen the sick; but the fat and the strong I will destroy. I will feed my flock with justice.
As for you, my sheep, thus says the Lord God: I am about to judge between one sheep and another, between the rams and the goats.
Is it not enough for you to graze on good pasture, that you must also trample the rest of your pasture with your feet? to drink clear water, that you must foul the rest with your feet?
And must my sheep graze on what your feet have trampled and drink what your feet have fouled?
Therefore thus says the Lord God: Here I am! I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean sheep.
Because you shove with flank and shoulder and butt all the weak sheep with your horns until you have driven them away,
I will save my flock: they will no longer be plunder, and I will judge between one sheep and another.
I will raise up over them one shepherd to feed them, my servant David: he will feed them, and he will be their shepherd.
I, the Lord, will be their God, and my servant David will be prince among them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
I will make with them a covenant of peace and rid the land of wild beasts; they will dwell in safety in the wilderness and sleep in the forests.
I will make them and the places around my hill a blessing. I will send down the rain in its season: they will be showers of blessing.

The trees of the field will give their fruit, the earth will give its yield, and they will live in safety on their own soil. They will know that I am the Lord, when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hand of those who enslaved them.
They will no longer be prey for the nations, and the wild beasts will no longer devour them; they will dwell in safety, with no one to frighten them.
I will raise up for them a planting of renown; they will no longer be swept away by famine in the land, nor bear the insults of the nations.
Then they will know that I, the Lord their God, am with them, and that they, the house of Israel, are my people, oracle of the Lord God.
You, my sheep, the flock of my pasture, you are human beings; and I am your God, oracle of the Lord God."
The word of the Lord came to me in these terms:
"Son of man, set your face toward Mount Seir and prophesy against it.
Say to it: Thus says the Lord God: I am against you, Mount Seir. I will stretch out my hand against you and make you a desolate waste.
I will lay your cities in ruins, and you will become a desolation, and you will know that I am the Lord.
Because you nursed an endless hatred and handed over the sons of Israel to the sword, in the day of their distress, at the time of their final punishment,
therefore, as surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God: I will give you over to blood, and blood will pursue you; since you did not hate bloodshed, blood will pursue you.
I will make Mount Seir a desolate waste and cut off from it all who come and go.
I will fill its mountains with the slain; on your hills, in your valleys, and in all your ravines those pierced by the sword will fall.
I will make you a perpetual desolation, and your cities will not be inhabited, and you will know that I am the Lord.
Because you said, 'These two nations and these two lands will be mine, we will take possession of them,' though the Lord was there,

therefore, as surely as I live, oracle of the Lord God: I will deal with you according to the anger and jealousy you showed in your hatred against them, and I will make myself known among them when I judge you.
Then you will know that I, the Lord, have heard all the insults you uttered against the mountains of Israel, when you said, 'They are laid waste; they are given to us to devour.'
You defied me with your speeches and multiplied your words against me: I heard them.
Thus says the Lord God: To the joy of all the earth, I will make you a desolation.
As you rejoiced over the devastated inheritance of the house of Israel, so I will treat you: you will be a desolation, Mount Seir, and you too, all of Edom. And they will know that I am the Lord."

titres.titre: The new heart and the new spirit

versets.t: "And you, son of man, prophesy to the mountains of Israel. Say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord:
Thus says the Lord God: Because the enemy said of you, 'Aha! These ancient heights are ours now,'

therefore prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord God: Yes, you were laid waste and hounded from every side, so that you became the possession of the rest of the nations; you have become the talk of gossips and the object of people's ridicule.

Therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord God. Thus says the Lord God to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys, to the desolate ruins and the abandoned cities, given over to plunder and to the mockery of the rest of the surrounding nations.

Therefore thus says the Lord God: Yes, in the fire of my jealousy I have spoken against the rest of the nations and against all of Edom, who claimed my land for themselves, hearts full of joy and souls full of contempt, to empty it out by plunder.

Therefore prophesy concerning the land of Israel. Say to the mountains and hills, to the ravines and valleys: Thus says the Lord God: Look, I have spoken in my jealousy and my wrath, because you have borne the insults of the nations.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: I swear with uplifted hand: the nations around you will bear their own insults.
But you, mountains of Israel, you will put out your branches and bear your fruit for my people Israel, for their return is near.
Look, I am for you, I turn toward you: you will be tilled and sown.
I will multiply people upon you, the whole house of Israel. The cities will be inhabited again, and the ruins rebuilt.
I will multiply man and beast upon you; they will be many and fruitful. I will make you populous as of old, and do you more good than at your beginnings, and you will know that I am the Lord.
I will make people walk upon you, my people Israel. They will possess you, you will be their inheritance, and you will never again rob them of their children.
Thus says the Lord God: Because they say to you, 'You devour people, you rob your nation of its children,'
therefore you will no longer devour people or rob your nation of its children, oracle of the Lord God.
I will no longer let you hear the insults of the nations; you will no longer bear the mockery of the peoples, and you will no longer make your nation stumble, oracle of the Lord God."
The word of the Lord came to me in these terms:
"Son of man, when the people of the house of Israel dwelt on their own soil, they defiled it by their conduct and their deeds; their conduct was before me like the uncleanness of a defilement.
So I poured out my wrath on them, because of the blood they had shed on the land and the idols with which they had defiled it.
I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the lands; I judged them according to their conduct and their deeds.
But when they came among the nations, they profaned my holy name there, for it was said of them, 'These are the people of the Lord, and yet they had to leave his land.'
So I was concerned for my holy name, which the house of Israel had profaned among the nations where they had gone.
Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: It is not for your sake that I act, house of Israel, but for my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations where you have gone.

I will sanctify my great name, profaned among the nations, which you have profaned in their midst. And the nations will know that I am the Lord, oracle of the Lord God, when through you I reveal my holiness before their eyes.
I will take you out from the nations, gather you from all the lands, and bring you back to your own soil.
I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean; from all your defilements and all your idols I will cleanse you.
I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; I will remove from your flesh the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
I will put my Spirit within you and cause you to walk according to my laws, to keep my statutes and observe them.
You will dwell in the land I gave to your fathers; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
I will save you from all your defilements. I will summon the grain and multiply it, and I will no longer send famine upon you.
I will multiply the fruit of the trees and the crops of the fields, so that you will no longer bear, among the nations, the disgrace of famine.
Then you will remember your evil ways and your deeds that were not good, and you will loathe yourselves for your sins and your abominations.
It is not for your sake that I act, oracle of the Lord God, know this well. Be ashamed and blush for your conduct, house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord God: On the day I cleanse you of all your sins, I will resettle the cities, and the ruins will be rebuilt.
The devastated land will be tilled, land that once lay desolate in the sight of all who passed by.
People will say: 'This land, once devastated, has become like the garden of Eden; the cities that were in ruins, desolate and overthrown, are now fortified and inhabited.'
Then the nations that remain around you will know that I, the Lord, have rebuilt what was overthrown and replanted what was ravaged. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will do it.
Thus says the Lord God: This too I will let the house of Israel ask of me, to act on their behalf: I will multiply their people like a flock.
Like the consecrated flocks, like the flocks that fill Jerusalem on its feast days, so the ruined cities will be filled with flocks of people. And they will know that I am the Lord."

titres.titre: The vision of the dry bones

versets.t: The hand of the Lord was upon me. By his Spirit he brought me out and set me down in the middle of the plain; it was covered with bones.
He led me all around them: there were very many on the floor of the plain, and they were utterly dry.
He said to me, "Son of man, can these bones live again?" I answered, "Lord God, you are the one who knows."
He said to me, "Prophesy over these bones. Say to them: Dry bones, hear the word of the Lord!
Thus says the Lord God to these bones: I am about to make breath enter you, and you will live.
I will put sinews on you, make flesh grow on you, and stretch skin over you; I will put breath in you, and you will live. Then you will know that I am the Lord."
I prophesied as I had been commanded. And as I was prophesying, there was a noise, then a rattling, and the bones came together, bone to bone.
I looked: sinews and flesh had grown on them, and skin had covered them. But there was no breath in them.
He said to me, "Prophesy to the breath, prophesy, son of man. Say to the breath: Thus says the Lord God: Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live!"
I prophesied as he had commanded me, and the breath entered them: they came to life and stood up on their feet, a vast army, beyond counting.
He said to me, "Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. They keep saying, 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is gone, we are cut off.'
Therefore prophesy. Say to them: Thus says the Lord God: I am about to open your graves; I will bring you up out of them, O my people, and lead you back to the land of Israel.
You will know that I am the Lord, when I open your graves and bring you up out of them, O my people.
I will put my Spirit within you, and you will live. I will settle you on your own soil, and you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken and will act, oracle of the Lord."
The word of the Lord came to me in these terms:

"And you, son of man, take a stick and write on it: For Judah and the sons of Israel joined to him. Take another stick and write on it: For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim and all the house of Israel joined to him.
Bring them close to each other to make a single stick: they will be one in your hand.
And when the children of your people ask you, 'Will you not explain to us what these mean for you?'

say to them: Thus says the Lord God: I am about to take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, along with the tribes of Israel joined to him, and I will join it to the stick of Judah. I will make them a single stick: they will be one in my hand.
The sticks on which you have written will be in your hand, before their eyes.
Say to them: Thus says the Lord God: I am about to take the sons of Israel from among the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from every side and bring them back to their own soil.
I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel. One king will reign over them all. They will no longer be two nations, no longer divided into two kingdoms.

They will no longer defile themselves with their idols, their horrors, and all their crimes. I will save them from all the unfaithfulness by which they sinned, and I will cleanse them: they will be my people, and I will be their God.
My servant David will be their king, and there will be one shepherd for them all. They will follow my laws, keep my commandments, and put them into practice.

They will dwell in the land I gave to my servant Jacob, the land their fathers dwelt in. They will dwell there, they, their children, and their children's children, forever; and my servant David will be their prince forever.
I will make with them a covenant of peace: it will be an everlasting covenant. I will establish them, multiply them, and set my sanctuary among them forever.
My dwelling will be over them; I will be their God, and they will be my people.
And the nations will know that I am the Lord who sanctifies Israel, when my sanctuary is among them forever."

titres.titre: The invasion of Gog of Magog

versets.t: The word of the Lord came to me in these terms:
"Son of man, set your face toward Gog, in the land of Magog, the chief prince of Meshech and Tubal. Prophesy against him. Say:
Thus says the Lord God: I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.

I will turn you around, put hooks in your jaws, and lead you out, you and all your army, horses and horsemen, all magnificently equipped, a vast host, all armed with large and small shields, wielding swords.
Persia, Cush, and Put are with them, all with shield and helmet.
Gomer and all its troops, Beth-togarmah from the far north and all its troops, many peoples are with you.
Be ready, prepare yourself, you and all the horde gathered around you: be their commander.

After many days you will be summoned: at the end of the years you will march against a land recovered from the sword, whose people, gathered from among many nations, have come back to the mountains of Israel, long desolate. Brought back from among the peoples, they now dwell in safety, all of them.
You will advance, coming on like a storm, like a cloud covering the land, you, all your troops, and many peoples with you.
Thus says the Lord God: On that day thoughts will arise in your heart, and you will devise an evil scheme.
You will say: I will march against an unwalled land, I will fall upon peaceful people who dwell in safety, all of them without walls, without bars or gates.
You will go to plunder and take spoil, to lay your hand on ruins now inhabited again, on a people gathered from among the nations, who raise livestock and goods and dwell at the center of the world.

Sheba, Dedan, the merchants of Tarshish, and all their young lions will say to you: Have you come to plunder? Is it to take spoil that you have gathered your troops, to carry off silver and gold, to seize livestock and goods, to gather immense plunder?
Therefore prophesy, son of man. Say to Gog: Thus says the Lord God: On that day, when my people Israel dwell in safety, will you not take notice?
You will come from your land, from the far north, you and many peoples with you, all riding horses, a great host and a mighty army.

You will advance against my people Israel like a cloud covering the land. It will be at the end of days: I will bring you against my land so that the nations may know me, when through you I reveal my holiness before their eyes, O Gog.
Thus says the Lord God: Are you not the one of whom I spoke in the days of old, through my servants the prophets of Israel, who prophesied in those years that I would bring you against them?
On that day, the day when Gog marches against the land of Israel, oracle of the Lord God, my wrath will flare in my nostrils.
In my jealousy, in the fire of my fury, I declare it: on that day a great earthquake will shake the land of Israel.

Before me will tremble the fish of the sea, the birds of the sky, the beasts of the field, everything that creeps on the ground, and every human being on the face of the earth. The mountains will collapse, the cliffs will fall, and every wall will crash to the ground.
I will summon the sword against him on all my mountains, oracle of the Lord God, and each man will turn his sword against his brother.
I will judge him with plague and bloodshed; I will pour down torrents of rain and hailstones, fire and sulfur, on him, on his troops, and on the many peoples with him.
I will show my greatness and my holiness, I will make myself known before the eyes of many nations, and they will know that I am the Lord."

titres.titre: The burial in the Valley of Hamon-gog
The great feast on the mountains
Israel restored, the Spirit poured out

versets.t: "And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog. Say: Thus says the Lord God: I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.
I will turn you around, drive you on, bring you up from the far north, and lead you against the mountains of Israel.
There I will break the bow in your left hand and make the arrows drop from your right hand.
You will fall on the mountains of Israel, you, all your troops, and the peoples with you. To the birds of prey, to birds of every kind, and to the beasts of the field I give you as food.
You will fall in the open field, for I have spoken, oracle of the Lord God.
I will send fire on Magog and on those who dwell in safety in the coastlands, and they will know that I am the Lord.
I will make my holy name known in the midst of my people Israel, and I will no longer let my holy name be profaned, and the nations will know that I am the Lord, the Holy One in Israel.
Look, it is coming, it will be done, oracle of the Lord God: this is the day of which I have spoken.

Then the inhabitants of the cities of Israel will go out; they will light a fire and burn the weapons, the small and large shields, the bow and arrows, the club and the spear: they will make fuel of them for seven years.

They will not need to gather wood from the countryside or cut it from the forests, for they will make their fires with the weapons. They will plunder those who plundered them and loot those who looted them, oracle of the Lord God.

On that day I will give Gog a burial place in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers, east of the sea, and it will block the way of those who pass through. There Gog and all his horde will be buried, and it will be called the Valley of Hamon-gog.
The house of Israel will bury them for seven months, to cleanse the land.
All the people of the land will bury them, and it will be a day of glory for them, the day when I reveal my splendor, oracle of the Lord God.

Men will be appointed to go through the land continually, burying, with the help of the passersby, those left on the surface of the ground, to cleanse it. At the end of seven months they will begin their search.
As these men pass through the land, whenever one of them sees human bones, he will set up a marker beside them, until the gravediggers bury them in the Valley of Hamon-gog.
There will even be a city named Hamonah. Thus they will cleanse the land.

And you, son of man, thus says the Lord God: Say to the birds of every kind and to all the beasts of the field: Assemble, come, gather from every side to my sacrifice, the great sacrifice I am preparing for you on the mountains of Israel. You will eat flesh and drink blood.
You will eat the flesh of heroes and drink the blood of the princes of the earth: rams, lambs, and goats, bulls, all of them fattened in Bashan.
You will eat fat until you are gorged and drink blood until you are drunk, at the sacrifice I am preparing for you.
At my table you will be filled with horses and horsemen, heroes and warriors of every kind, oracle of the Lord God.
I will display my glory among the nations, and all the nations will see the judgment I execute and the hand I lay upon them.
Then the house of Israel will know that I am the Lord their God, from that day on and forever.

And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile because of their guilt, because they were unfaithful to me: I hid my face from them and handed them over to the hand of their enemies, so that they all fell by the sword.
I had dealt with them according to their uncleanness and their rebellions, and I had hidden my face from them.
Therefore thus says the Lord God: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and I will be jealous for my holy name.
They will forget their shame and all the unfaithfulness they committed against me, when they dwell in safety on their own land, with no one to disturb them.
When I bring them back from among the peoples, gather them from the lands of their enemies, and reveal my holiness through them before the eyes of many nations,
they will know that I am the Lord their God: after exiling them among the nations, I will have gathered them onto their own soil, leaving none of them behind there.
I will no longer hide my face from them, for I will have poured out my Spirit on the house of Israel, oracle of the Lord God."

titres.titre: The vision of the new temple
The east gate and its guardrooms
The outer court and the other gates

versets.t: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, fourteen years after the fall of the city, on that very day the hand of the Lord was upon me, and he brought me there.
In divine visions he brought me to the land of Israel and set me down on a very high mountain, on which, to the south, there stood what looked like a city.
He led me there, and there was a man whose appearance shone like bronze. He held in his hand a linen cord and a measuring rod, and he was standing at the gate.

The man said to me, "Son of man, look with your eyes, listen with your ears, and set your heart on everything I am about to show you, for that is why you have been brought here. Make known to the house of Israel everything you are about to see."

Now there was an outer wall surrounding the temple on every side. The man held in his hand a measuring rod about three meters long. He measured the thickness of the wall: about three meters; and its height: about three meters.
Then he went to the gate facing east, climbed its steps, and measured the threshold of the gate: about three meters wide; this first threshold was about three meters wide.

Each guardroom was about three meters long and about three meters wide; between the guardrooms there was about two and a half meters. The threshold of the gate, on the side of the vestibule facing inward, was about three meters.
He measured the vestibule of the gate, on the inner side: about three meters.
He also measured the vestibule of the gate: about four meters, and its pillars, about one meter. The vestibule of the gate was on the inner side.
The guardrooms of the east gate numbered three on each side; all three had the same dimensions, and so did the pillars on each side.
He measured the opening of the gate: about five meters wide, and the length of the gate: about seven meters.
In front of the guardrooms there was a barrier about fifty centimeters on each side, and each guardroom measured about three meters by three.
He measured the gate from the roof of one guardroom to the roof of the opposite one: about thirteen meters wide, from one opening to the other.
He reckoned about thirty meters for the pillars, up to the court surrounding the gate.
From the front of the gateway to the front of the inner vestibule there was about twenty-six meters.
The guardrooms and their pillars had latticed windows facing inward, all around; the same was true of the vestibules: windows all around, facing inward; and on the pilasters, palm trees were carved.
He then led me into the outer court: there were chambers there and a pavement laid out all around the court, thirty chambers opening onto the pavement.
The pavement ran alongside the gates along their whole length: this was the lower pavement.
He measured the distance from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner court: about fifty meters, on the east side as on the north.
As for the gate of the outer court facing north, he measured its length and its width.
Its guardrooms, three on each side, its pillars, and its vestibule had the same dimensions as those of the first gate: about twenty-six meters long and about thirteen meters wide.
Its windows, its vestibule, and its palm trees had the same dimensions as those of the gate facing east. One went up to it by seven steps, and its vestibule was directly in front of them.
The inner court had a gate facing the north gate as it did the east gate. From one gate to the other he measured about fifty meters.
He then led me toward the south, and there was a gate facing south. He measured its pilasters and its vestibule: the same dimensions as the others.
This gate and its vestibule had windows all around like the others: about twenty-six meters long and about thirteen meters wide.
One went up to it by seven steps, and its vestibule was directly in front of them; there were palm trees carved on its pilasters, on either side.
The inner court also had a gate facing south; from one gate to the other, toward the south, he measured about fifty meters.
He brought me into the inner court through the south gate, and he measured that gate: the same dimensions as the others.

Its guardrooms, its pilasters, and its vestibule had the same dimensions, and all around, as well as around its vestibule, there were windows: about twenty-six meters long and about thirteen meters wide.
All around there were vestibules about thirteen meters long and about two and a half meters wide.
Its vestibule faced the outer court; it had palm trees carved on its pilasters, and one went up to it by eight steps.
He led me into the inner court, toward the east, and measured the gate: the same dimensions as the others.

Its guardrooms, its pilasters, and its vestibule had the same dimensions, and all around, as well as around its vestibule, there were windows: about twenty-six meters long and about thirteen meters wide.
Its vestibule faced the outer court; it had palm trees carved on its pilasters, on either side, and one went up to it by eight steps.
Then he led me toward the north gate and measured it: the same dimensions.
Its guardrooms, its pilasters, and its vestibule had windows all around: about twenty-six meters long and about thirteen meters wide.
Its pillars faced the outer court; there were palm trees carved on its pilasters, and one went up to it by eight steps.
A chamber opened by its door near the pilasters of the gates: this was where the burnt offerings were washed.
In the vestibule of the gate there were two tables on one side and two on the other, on which to slaughter the burnt offerings, the sin offerings, and the guilt offerings.
Outside, on the north side for the one going up to the entrance of the gate, there were two tables; and on the other side of the vestibule of the gate, two tables.
So on the sides of the gate there were four tables on one side and four on the other: eight tables in all, on which to slaughter.

There were also four tables for the burnt offering, of dressed stone, about eighty centimeters long, about eighty centimeters wide, and about fifty centimeters high; on them were laid the instruments used to slaughter the burnt offerings and the other sacrifices.
Hooks about eight centimeters long were fixed all around, on the inside; and on the tables the flesh of the offerings was laid.
Outside the inner gate, in the inner court, there were the chambers of the singers: one beside the north gate, facing south; the other beside the east gate, facing north.
He said to me, "This chamber facing south is for the priests in charge of the service of the temple.
And the chamber facing north is for the priests in charge of the service of the altar: they are the sons of Zadok, the only ones among the Levites who may approach the Lord to serve him."
Then he measured the court: a square about fifty meters long and about fifty meters wide. The altar stood before the temple.
He then led me to the vestibule of the temple and measured its pillars: about two and a half meters on each side; the width of the gateway: about one and a half meters on each side.
The vestibule was about ten meters long and about six meters wide, and one went up to it by steps; near the pillars stood columns, one on each side.

titres.titre: The great hall and the Holy of Holies

versets.t: Then he led me into the great hall of the temple and measured its jambs: about three meters thick on each side.
The opening was about five meters wide, and its side walls about two and a half meters on each side. He measured the great hall: about twenty meters long and about ten meters wide.
He went inside and measured the jambs of the entrance: about one meter; the entrance itself: about three meters; and its walls: about three and a half meters.
He measured, at the far end, a length of about ten meters and a width of about ten meters. Then he said to me, "This is the Holy of Holies."
He measured the wall of the temple: about three meters thick; and the width of the side chambers, all around: about two meters.
The side chambers were on three stories, thirty at each story. They rested on a ledge built all around the temple, without being embedded in the temple wall itself.

They grew wider from story to story, for the surround of the temple rose in stages around it; thus the building widened toward the top, and one went from the lower story to the upper by way of the middle one.
I saw that the temple was raised up all around; the foundations of the side chambers measured about three meters, up to the ledge.
The outer wall of the side chambers was about two and a half meters thick. An open space ran along the side chambers of the temple;
and up to the chambers there was, all around the temple, a clearance of about ten meters.
The side chambers opened onto this space by a door on the north and a door on the south; the open space was about two and a half meters wide all around.
The building facing the courtyard, on the west side, was about thirty-five meters wide; its wall was about two and a half meters thick all around, and its length was about forty-five meters.
He measured the temple: about fifty meters long. The courtyard, the building, and its walls: about fifty meters long.
The front of the temple and of the courtyard, toward the east, was also about fifty meters.

He measured the length of the building facing the courtyard, at the rear, with its galleries on either side: about fifty meters. The great hall, the inner sanctuary, and the vestibule facing the court,
the thresholds, the latticed windows, and the galleries that surrounded the three, all were paneled with wood, from the threshold to the windows; and the windows were fitted with lattices.
Above the entrance, all the way to the far end of the temple, inside and out, over the whole wall all around,
cherubim and palm trees were carved, a palm tree between two cherubim. Each cherub had two faces:
a human face turned toward the palm tree on one side, a lion's face turned toward the palm tree on the other. They were carved this way over the whole temple, all around.
From the floor to above the entrance, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the great hall.
The jambs of the hall were square. Before the Holy of Holies there was something that looked like
an altar of wood, about one and a half meters high and about one meter long; its corners, its base, and its sides were of wood. The man said to me, "This is the table that stands before the Lord."
The great hall and the Holy of Holies each had a door,
and each door had two pivoting leaves, two leaves for the one, two for the other.
On these doors were carved cherubim and palm trees, as on the walls; and a wooden canopy covered the front of the vestibule, on the outside.
There were latticed windows and palm trees on either side, on the walls of the vestibule, on the side chambers of the temple, and on the canopies.
The man brought me out to the outer court, on the north side, and led me to the chambers facing the courtyard and the wall, on the north.
In length they measured about fifty meters on the side of the north entrance, and about twenty-six meters wide.
Facing the ten-meter space of the inner court and the pavement of the outer court, the galleries stood opposite one another on three stories.
In front of the chambers ran a walkway about five meters wide, leading inward by a passage about fifty centimeters; their doors faced north.
The upper chambers were narrower, for the galleries took away from them more than from the lower and middle chambers.
For they were on three stories and had no columns like those of the courts; that is why the upper chambers were more cramped than the lower and the middle ones.
The outer wall, running alongside the chambers on the side of the outer court, extended about twenty-six meters in front of them.
For the chambers on the side of the outer court were about twenty-six meters long, while on the side of the temple they reached about fifty meters.
Below these chambers there was an entrance on the east, for one coming from the outer court.
In the thickness of the wall of the court, on the east side, facing the courtyard and the wall, there were also chambers.
In front of them ran a passage, like that of the chambers on the north; they had the same length, the same width, the same exits, the same layout, and the same doors.
Like the doors of the chambers on the south, there was a door at the head of the passage, along the wall, on the east, for the one who entered.

He said to me, "The chambers on the north and those on the south, which face the courtyard, are the chambers of the sanctuary: it is there that the priests who approach the Lord eat the most holy offerings; there they deposit these offerings, the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering, for the place is holy.

Once they have entered, the priests will not go out from the holy place into the outer court without leaving there the vestments of their service, for these vestments are holy. They will put on other garments before approaching the areas set aside for the people."
When he had finished measuring the interior of the temple, he brought me out through the gate facing east and measured the enclosure all around.
He measured the east side with the rod: about one and a half kilometers all around.
He measured the north side: about one and a half kilometers.
He measured the south side: about one and a half kilometers.
He turned toward the west and measured: about one and a half kilometers.
So he measured the four sides. The temple was surrounded by a wall, about one and a half kilometers long and as much wide, to separate the sacred from the profane.

titres.titre: The return of the glory of the Lord

versets.t: Then he led me to the gate, the one facing east.
And there was the glory of the God of Israel coming from the east. His voice was like the voice of the great waters, and the earth shone with his glory.
This vision was like the one I had seen when I came for the destruction of the city, and like the one I had seen by the Kebar river. I fell face down.
The glory of the Lord entered the temple through the gate facing east.
Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court; and there the glory of the Lord filled the temple.
I heard someone speaking to me from the temple, while a man stood beside me.

He said to me, "Son of man, this is the place of my throne, the place where I will set the soles of my feet, where I will dwell forever among the sons of Israel. The house of Israel, neither they nor their kings, will defile my holy name again by their unfaithfulness and by the corpses of their kings on their high places,

they who set their threshold against my threshold and their doorposts against my doorposts, with only a wall between them and me. They defiled my holy name by the abominations they committed, and I destroyed them in my anger.
Now they will keep their unfaithfulness and the corpses of their kings far from me, and I will dwell among them forever.
You, son of man, describe this temple to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their sins; and let them measure its plan.

If they are ashamed of all they have done, make known to them the design of the temple, its arrangement, its exits and its entrances, its whole form and all its statutes; write it down before their eyes, so that they may keep its whole form and all its statutes and put them into practice."
This is the law of the temple: at the top of the mountain, its whole surrounding domain is most holy. Such is the law of the temple.

These are the measurements of the altar: its base is about fifty centimeters high and fifty centimeters wide, with a rim about twenty-five centimeters around its edge. This is the pedestal of the altar.

From the base set on the ground to the lower ledge is about one meter, with a width of about fifty centimeters; from the small ledge to the great ledge is about two meters, with a width of about fifty centimeters.
The hearth is about two meters high, and from this hearth rise four horns.
The hearth measures about six meters long by about six meters wide: a perfect square.

The ledge, on its four sides, measures about seven meters long by about seven meters wide, with a rim about twenty-five centimeters all around and a base about fifty centimeters around it. Its steps face east.
He said to me, "Son of man, thus says the Lord God: These are the statutes of the altar, for the day when it is built, so that burnt offerings may be offered on it and blood dashed against it.
To the levitical priests of the line of Zadok, who approach me to serve me, oracle of the Lord God, you will give a young bull as a sin offering.
You will take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge, and on the rim all around; thus you will purify the altar and make atonement for it.
Then you will take the bull of the sin offering, and it will be burned at the appointed place of the temple, outside the sanctuary.
On the second day you will offer a male goat without blemish as a sin offering, and the altar will be purified as it was with the bull.
When you have finished purifying it, you will offer a young bull without blemish and a ram without blemish from the flock.
You will present them before the Lord, and the priests will throw salt on them and offer them as a burnt offering to the Lord.
For seven days you will offer a male goat each day as a sin offering; a young bull and a ram without blemish from the flock will also be offered.
For seven days they will make atonement for the altar, purify it, and consecrate it.
When these days are over, from the eighth day on, the priests will offer your burnt offerings and your peace offerings on the altar, and I will be favorable to you, oracle of the Lord God."

titres.titre: The gate reserved for the prince

versets.t: Then he brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east: it was shut.
The Lord said to me, "This gate will remain shut. It will not be opened; no one will enter through it, for the Lord, the God of Israel, has entered through it: it will remain shut.
Only the prince, because he is the prince, may sit there to eat before the Lord; he will enter through the vestibule of the gate and go out by the same way."
He then led me to the north gate, in front of the temple. I looked, and there the glory of the Lord filled the temple. I fell face down.

The Lord said to me, "Son of man, set your heart, look with your eyes, and listen with your ears to all that I am about to tell you concerning the statutes of the temple of the Lord and all its laws. Set your heart on what concerns the entrance of the temple and all the exits of the sanctuary.
Say to these rebels, to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Enough of your abominations, house of Israel!

You have brought in foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and flesh, to stand in my sanctuary and profane my temple, while you offered me my food, the fat and the blood. So, by all your abominations, you have broken my covenant.
You have not kept charge of my holy things, but have put these foreigners in charge of my service in my sanctuary, in your place.
Thus says the Lord God: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and flesh, will enter my sanctuary, none of these foreigners who live among the sons of Israel.
As for the Levites who went far from me when Israel strayed away from me after its idols, they will bear the weight of their guilt.

They will perform a subordinate service in my sanctuary: as gatekeepers at the doors of the temple, they will minister there, they will slaughter for the people the burnt offerings and the sacrifices, and they will stand before the people to serve them.
Because they served them before their idols and made the house of Israel fall into guilt, therefore, I swear with uplifted hand, they will bear the weight of their guilt, oracle of the Lord God.
They will no longer approach me to serve as priests or to touch any of my holy things, the most holy things; they will bear their disgrace and the weight of the abominations they committed.
I will put them in charge of the service of the temple, for all its upkeep and everything done in it.

But the levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept charge of my sanctuary when the sons of Israel strayed away from me, they will approach me to serve me; they will stand before me to offer me the fat and the blood, oracle of the Lord God.
They are the ones who will enter my sanctuary, they who will approach my table to serve me, and who will keep my charge.
When they pass through the gates of the inner court, they will wear linen garments; they will have no wool on them while they minister at the gates of the inner court and within.
They will have linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments on their loins; they will not gird themselves with anything that makes them sweat.

When they go out to the outer court, to the people, they will take off the vestments of their service, leave them in the chambers of the sanctuary, and put on other garments, so as not to communicate holiness to the people through their vestments.
They will not shave their heads or let their hair grow long: they will keep it trimmed short.
No priest will drink wine on the day he enters the inner court.
They will not take as wife a widow or a divorced woman, but only a virgin of the descendants of Israel; they may, however, marry the widow of a priest.
They will teach my people to distinguish the sacred from the profane and make known to them the difference between the clean and the unclean.

In lawsuits they are the ones who will sit in judgment, and they will judge according to my ordinances. They will observe my laws and my statutes at all my feasts, and they will keep my sabbaths holy.
None of them will go near a dead person, so as not to make himself unclean; they may make themselves unclean only for a father, a mother, a son, a daughter, a brother, or an unmarried sister.
After his purification, seven days will be counted for him;
and on the day he enters the holy place, the inner court, to minister in the sanctuary, he will offer his sin offering, oracle of the Lord God.
This will be their inheritance: I myself will be their inheritance. You will give them no property in Israel: I myself am their property.
They will feed on the grain offering, the sin offering, and the guilt offering; and everything in Israel that has been devoted to the Lord will belong to them.
The best of all your firstfruits and all your offerings of every kind will be for the priests; you will also give them the best of your flour, so that a blessing may rest on your house.
The priests will not eat any bird or animal that has died of itself or been torn by beasts."

titres.titre: The division of the holy land
The feasts and the offerings of the prince

versets.t: "When you divide the land as an inheritance, you will set aside for the Lord a holy portion: about thirteen kilometers long and about five kilometers wide. It will be holy throughout its whole extent.
Of this portion there will be for the sanctuary a square about two hundred sixty meters on each side, with an open space about twenty-six meters all around.
Out of this area you will measure a length of about thirteen kilometers and a width of about five kilometers: this is where the sanctuary will be, the most holy place.

This will be the holy portion of the land, reserved for the priests who serve in the sanctuary and approach to serve the Lord: they will have there a place for their houses and a holy place for the sanctuary.
Another strip about thirteen kilometers long and about five kilometers wide will be for the Levites who serve in the temple: they will have there cities to live in.

As the property of the city, you will set aside a strip about two and a half kilometers wide and about thirteen kilometers long, alongside the holy portion: it will belong to the whole house of Israel.

To the prince will belong a domain on both sides of the holy portion and of the property of the city, alongside each of them, on the west side toward the west and on the east side toward the east, over a length equal to that of one of the tribal portions, from one border to the other.
This will be his domain, his property in Israel. Thus my princes will no longer oppress my people, and they will leave the land to the house of Israel, tribe by tribe.
Thus says the Lord God: Enough, princes of Israel! Give up violence and plunder, practice justice and righteousness, stop dispossessing my people, oracle of the Lord God.
Have honest scales, an honest measure for grain and an honest measure for liquids.

The measure for grain and the measure for liquids will hold the same amount, about twenty-two liters each, a tenth of the large measure, which holds about two hundred twenty liters: everything will be reckoned by it.
Your standard weight is about eleven grams and is divided into twenty small parts; sixty of these weights make a mina, that is, about seven hundred grams.
This is the offering you will set aside: about three and a half liters of wheat from every two hundred twenty liters, and as much from every two hundred twenty liters of barley.
For oil: about two liters from every two hundred twenty liters, for the large measure holds ten times as much.

You will also set aside one sheep from every two hundred, from the rich pastures of Israel, for the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make atonement for the people, oracle of the Lord God.
All the people of the land will be bound to this offering to the prince of Israel.

And it will fall to the prince to provide the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the drink offerings, at the feasts, the new moons, the sabbaths, and all the solemn festivals of the house of Israel. It is he who will provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offerings, to make atonement on behalf of the house of Israel."
Thus says the Lord God: "On the first day of the first month (around March-April), you will take a young bull without blemish and purify the sanctuary.

The priest will take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the temple, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.
You will do the same on the seventh day of the month, for anyone who has sinned by mistake or in ignorance; thus you will make atonement for the temple.
On the fourteenth day of the first month (around March-April), you will celebrate the Passover, a feast of seven days, during which unleavened bread will be eaten.
On that day the prince will offer, for himself and for all the people of the land, a bull as a sin offering.
During the seven days of the feast he will offer as a burnt offering to the Lord, each day, seven bulls and seven rams without blemish, and each day a male goat as a sin offering.
He will also offer, as a grain offering, about twenty-two liters of flour per bull and as much per ram, with about three and a half liters of oil for each measure of flour.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month (around September-October), during the feast, he will offer for seven days the same sin offerings, the same burnt offerings, the same grain offerings, and the same quantity of oil."

titres.titre: The prince's worship on sabbaths and feasts

versets.t: Thus says the Lord God: "The gate of the inner court that faces east will remain shut on the six working days, but it will be opened on the sabbath day, and opened also on the day of the new moon.

The prince will come from outside through the vestibule of the gate and stand by the doorposts; the priests will offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings. He will bow down on the threshold of the gate, then withdraw; the gate will not be shut until evening.
The people of the land will bow down before the Lord at the entrance of this gate, on the sabbaths and the new moons.
The burnt offering that the prince offers to the Lord on the sabbath day will be six lambs without blemish and one ram without blemish;
with, as a grain offering, about twenty-two liters of flour for the ram, and for the lambs whatever he wishes to give, with about three and a half liters of oil per measure of flour.
On the day of the new moon, it will be a young bull without blemish, six lambs, and one ram without blemish.
As a grain offering, he will offer about twenty-two liters of flour per bull and as much per ram, and for the lambs whatever he can, with about three and a half liters of oil per measure of flour.
When the prince enters, he will go in through the vestibule of the gate and go out by the same way.

But when the people of the land come before the Lord at the solemn festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to bow down will go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate will go out by the north gate: no one will return by the gate through which he entered, but by the one opposite.
The prince, for his part, will enter among them when they enter and go out when they go out.

At the feasts and solemn festivals, the grain offering will be about twenty-two liters of flour per bull and as much per ram, and for the lambs whatever the prince wishes, with about three and a half liters of oil per measure of flour.

When the prince makes a freewill offering, a burnt offering or peace offerings, the gate facing east will be opened for him. He will offer his burnt offering and his peace offerings as on the sabbath day, then he will go out, and the gate will be shut behind him.
Each morning you will offer to the Lord, as a daily burnt offering, a year-old lamb without blemish: you will offer it every morning.

Each morning you will add to it a grain offering of about three and a half liters of flour, with about one liter of oil to moisten it: this is a grain offering to the Lord, a lasting statute, forever.
So each morning the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil will be offered: this is the perpetual burnt offering."
Thus says the Lord God: "If the prince makes a gift to one of his sons, this gift will be that son's inheritance: it will pass to his descendants as a property.

But if he makes a gift, taken from his inheritance, to one of his servants, this gift will belong to the servant until the year of release; then it will return to the prince. Only his sons will keep his inheritance.

The prince will take nothing of the people's inheritance by driving them from their property. It is out of his own domain that he will give an inheritance to his sons, so that no one among my people will be driven from his possession."
Then he led me, by the entrance beside the gate, to the holy chambers reserved for the priests, those facing north; and there, at the very back, was a space on the west side.

He said to me, "This is where the priests will boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they will bake the grain offering, so as not to carry them into the outer court and communicate holiness to the people."
He then brought me out into the outer court and led me around the four corners of the court; at each corner there was a court.
At the four corners of the court there were enclosed courts, about twenty meters long and about fifteen meters wide: these four corner courts had the same dimensions.
A low wall surrounded all four of them, and hearths were built at their base, all around.
He said to me, "These are the kitchens where the servants of the temple will boil the sacrifices of the people."

titres.titre: The river flowing from the temple

versets.t: He brought me back to the entrance of the temple, and there water was flowing out from under the threshold of the temple, toward the east, for the front of the temple faced east. The water came down from under the right side of the temple, south of the altar.
He brought me out through the north gate and led me around the outside to the outer gate facing east; and there the water was trickling out from the right side.
The man went eastward with a cord in his hand. He measured about five hundred meters and led me through the water: it came up to my ankles.
He measured another five hundred meters and led me through: it came up to my knees. He measured another five hundred meters and led me through: it came up to my waist.
He measured another five hundred meters: it had become a river that I could no longer cross, for the water had risen, water deep enough to swim in, a river that could not be crossed.
He said to me, "Son of man, have you seen?" Then he led me back to the bank of the river.
As I returned, I saw on both banks of the river a great many trees.
He said to me, "These waters flow toward the eastern region; they go down to the plain and empty into the sea; carried into the sea, they make its waters fresh.

Wherever this river flows, every living creature that swarms in it will live; the fish there will be very many, for wherever these waters reach, they bring healing, and life teems wherever the river goes.
On its banks fishermen will stand; from En-gedi to En-eglaim, nets will be spread. The fish there will be of every kind, very many, like the fish of the Great Sea.
But its marshes and its lagoons will not be made fresh: they will be left to the salt.

On both banks of the river will grow all kinds of fruit trees, with foliage that will not wither and fruit that will never fail. Each month they will bear fresh fruit, for their waters flow from the sanctuary. Their fruit will be good to eat, and their leaves will serve for healing."
Thus says the Lord God: "These are the borders of the land that you will divide among the twelve tribes of Israel, Joseph receiving two portions.
You will each have an equal share in it, this land that I swore with uplifted hand to give to your fathers, and it will come to you as an inheritance.
These, then, are the borders of the land. On the north: from the Great Sea, by the road of Hethlon to the entrance of Zedad,
Hamath, Berothah, and Sibraim, between the border of Damascus and that of Hamath, then Hazer-hatticon, toward the border of Hauran.
The border will run from the sea to Hazar-enan; the territory of Damascus and that of Hamath will lie to the north. This is the north side.
On the east: from the boundary between Hauran and Damascus, the border will run between Gilead and the land of Israel, along the Jordan, to the eastern sea. This is the east side.
On the south: from Tamar to the waters of Meribah, at Kadesh, then along the Wadi to the Great Sea. This is the south side, toward the Negev.
On the west: the Great Sea will serve as the border, up to a point opposite the entrance of Hamath. This is the west side.
You will divide this land among yourselves, according to the tribes of Israel.

You will allot it as an inheritance, for yourselves and for the resident aliens who live among you and who have had children among you. You will treat them as native-born Israelites: they will be allotted a share of inheritance with you, among the tribes of Israel.
In the tribe where the resident alien lives, there you will give him his share of inheritance, oracle of the Lord God."

titres.titre: The holy portion, the city, and the prince
The twelve gates; The Lord is there

versets.t: These are the names of the tribes. At the far north, along the road of Hethlon to the entrance of Hamath and Hazar-enan, with the border of Damascus to the north, alongside Hamath, from east to west: Dan will have one portion.
Alongside Dan, from east to west: Asher, one portion.
Alongside Asher, from east to west: Naphtali, one portion.
Alongside Naphtali, from east to west: Manasseh, one portion.
Alongside Manasseh, from east to west: Ephraim, one portion.
Alongside Ephraim, from east to west: Reuben, one portion.
Alongside Reuben, from east to west: Judah, one portion.

Alongside Judah, from east to west, will lie the portion that you will set aside: about thirteen kilometers wide, and as long as each of the other portions, from east to west; the sanctuary will be in its center.
The portion that you will set aside for the Lord will be about thirteen kilometers long and about five kilometers wide.

This holy portion will belong to the priests: about thirteen kilometers on the north, about five kilometers wide on the west, about five kilometers wide on the east, about thirteen kilometers on the south; the sanctuary of the Lord will be in its center.
It will belong to the consecrated priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept my charge and did not go astray when the sons of Israel went astray, as the Levites went astray.
It will be for them a portion taken from the holy portion of the land, a most holy portion, alongside the territory of the Levites.
The Levites, alongside the territory of the priests, will have about thirteen kilometers long by about five kilometers wide: in all, thirteen kilometers long and five wide.
They may not sell or exchange any of it, and this firstfruit of the land will not pass to others, for it is holy to the Lord.
What remains, about two and a half kilometers wide along the thirteen kilometers, will be common land for the city, its dwellings, and its outskirts; the city will stand at its center.

These are its dimensions: on the north side, about two and a half kilometers; on the south side, about two and a half kilometers; on the east side, about two and a half kilometers; on the west side, about two and a half kilometers.
The city will have an open space of about one hundred thirty meters on the north, as much on the south, the east, and the west.
The rest, alongside the holy portion, about five kilometers on the east and about five kilometers on the west, will yield crops to feed those who work in the service of the city.
Those who work in the service of the city, drawn from all the tribes of Israel, will till it.
