Therefore I am going to block her way with thorns; I will build a wall against her, and she will no longer find her paths.
She will pursue her lovers but not overtake them, she will seek them but not find them. Then she will say, 'I will go back to my first husband, for I was happier then than now.'
She did not acknowledge that it was I who gave her the grain, the new wine, and the oil, I who lavished on her the silver and gold that they used for Baal.
Therefore I will take back my grain in its time and my new wine in its season; I will take away my wool and my linen that covered her nakedness.
Now I will uncover her shame before the eyes of her lovers, and no one will tear her from my hand.
I will put an end to all her rejoicing, her feasts, her new moons, her sabbaths, all her appointed festivals.
I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees, of which she said, 'These are the wages my lovers gave me'; I will turn them into a thicket, and the wild beasts will devour them.
I will call her to account for the days of the Baals, when she burned incense to them, when, adorned with her ring and her necklace, she ran after her lovers; but me she forgot, oracle of the Lord.
Therefore, behold, I am going to allure her, lead her into the desert, and speak to her heart.
There I will give her back her vineyards, and I will make the Valley of Achor a door of hope; there she will answer me as in the days of her youth, as on the day she came up out of the land of Egypt.
On that day, oracle of the Lord, you will call me 'my husband,' and no longer call me 'my Baal.'
I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and they will no longer be mentioned.

On that day I will make a covenant for them with the wild beasts, the birds of the sky, and the creatures that crawl on the ground; I will break the bow, the sword, and war out of the land, and I will let them lie down in safety.
I will betroth you to myself forever; I will betroth you to myself in righteousness and justice, in love and tenderness;
I will betroth you to myself in faithfulness, and you will know the Lord.
On that day I will answer, oracle of the Lord, I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth;
the earth will answer the grain, the new wine, and the oil, and they will answer Jezreel.
I will sow her for myself in the land, I will show my love to Not-loved, and I will say to Not-my-people, 'You are my people,' and he will say, 'My God.'

titres.titre: The redemption of the unfaithful wife

versets.t: The Lord said to me: "Go again, love a woman loved by a lover and an adulteress, just as the Lord loves the children of Israel while they turn to other gods and are fond of raisin cakes."
So I bought her for fifteen pieces of silver and about three hundred and thirty litres of barley,
and I said to her: "You will remain mine for many days; you will not prostitute yourself, you will belong to no man, and I too will be so toward you."
For the children of Israel will remain for many days without king or leader, without sacrifice or sacred pillar, without ephod or household idols.
Afterward the children of Israel will return; they will seek the Lord their God and David their king, and they will come trembling to the Lord and to his goodness, at the end of days.
Hear the word of the Lord, children of Israel! The Lord has a case against the inhabitants of the land: there is no faithfulness, no love, no knowledge of God in the land.
They perjure themselves and lie, they kill, they steal, they commit adultery; violence overflows, and bloodshed follows bloodshed.
Therefore the land mourns, and all who dwell in it waste away, together with the beasts of the field and the birds of the sky; even the fish of the sea disappear.
Yet let no one accuse, let no one rebuke! For it is against you, priest, that this case is brought.
You will stumble in broad daylight, and the prophet too will stumble with you in the night, and I will silence your mother.
My people perish for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I will reject you from my priesthood; because you have forgotten the law of your God, I too will forget your children.
The more they multiplied, the more they sinned against me: I will change their glory into disgrace.
They feed on the sin of my people and crave nothing but their guilt.
It will be with the priest as with the people: I will make him pay for his conduct and repay him for his deeds.
They will eat but not be satisfied, they will prostitute themselves but not multiply, because they have forsaken the service of the Lord.
Debauchery, wine, and new wine steal away the heart.
My people consult a piece of wood, and their stick gives them oracles! A spirit of prostitution has led them astray: they prostitute themselves, forsaking their God.

They offer sacrifices on the mountaintops and burn incense on the hills, under the oak, the poplar, and the terebinth, whose shade is pleasant. That is why your daughters prostitute themselves and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.

I will not punish your daughters for their prostitutions, nor your daughters-in-law for their adulteries; for the men themselves slip away with prostitutes and sacrifice with the temple courtesans. So a people without understanding rushes to its ruin.
If you, Israel, prostitute yourself, at least let Judah not become guilty! Do not go to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear, 'As the Lord lives!'
Israel has balked like a stubborn heifer; how then could the Lord now pasture them like lambs in a broad meadow?
Ephraim is bound to idols: leave him be!
When their drinking is over, they give themselves to debauchery; their rulers dearly love disgrace.
The wind will carry them off in its wings, and they will be ashamed of their sacrifices.

titres.titre: Judgment against the priests and the king
The punishment of Ephraim and Judah

versets.t: Hear this, priests! Pay attention, house of Israel! House of the king, give ear! For the sentence is aimed at you: you have been a snare at Mizpah, a net spread over Tabor.
The rebels have dug a deep pit; but I will discipline them all.
I myself know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me: yes, you have prostituted yourself, Ephraim, and Israel has defiled itself.
Their deeds do not let them return to their God, for a spirit of prostitution dwells within them, and they do not know the Lord.
Israel's pride testifies against him; Israel and Ephraim will stumble by their own guilt, and Judah will stumble with them.
With their sheep and their cattle they will go to seek the Lord, but they will not find him: he has withdrawn from them.
They have betrayed the Lord, for they have fathered children of adultery; now, within a month, they will be devoured, they and their fields.
Blow the horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah, raise the war cry at Beth-aven! Behind you, Benjamin!
Ephraim will be laid waste on the day of punishment; over the tribes of Israel I announce a thing that is certain.
The rulers of Judah have become like those who move boundary stones; on them I will pour out my wrath like a flood.
Ephraim is oppressed, crushed by judgment, for he chose to run after worthless idols.
And I am like a moth to Ephraim, like rot to the house of Judah.
When Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah his wound, Ephraim turned to Assyria and sent to the great king for help; but that king cannot heal you or close your wound.
For I will be like a lion to Ephraim, like a young lion to the house of Judah; I, yes I, will tear and go away, I will carry off my prey, and no one will rescue it.
I will go away, I will return to my dwelling, until they acknowledge their guilt and seek my face; in their distress they will search for me.
"Come, let us return to the Lord! For it is he who has torn, and he will heal us; he has struck, and he will bind up our wounds.
After two days he will revive us, on the third day he will raise us up, and we will live in his presence.
Let us seek to know the Lord, let us press on to know him: his coming is as sure as the dawn, he will come to us like the downpour, like the spring rain that waters the earth."
What shall I do with you, Ephraim? What shall I do with you, Judah? Your love is like the morning cloud, like the early dew that evaporates.
Therefore I have cut them to pieces by the prophets, I have struck them by the words of my mouth; and my judgment will rise like the light.
For it is faithful love that I desire, and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
But they, like Adam, have broken the covenant; there they betrayed me.
Gilead is a city of evildoers, covered with tracks of blood.
Like bandits lying in ambush, a band of priests murders on the road to Shechem: yes, they commit outrage.
In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: there Ephraim prostitutes himself, Israel defiles itself.
For you too, Judah, a harvest is appointed, when I restore my people.
When I wanted to heal Israel, the guilt of Ephraim and the wickedness of Samaria were laid bare; for they practice deceit: the thief breaks into houses, the band of robbers raids outside.
And they do not say in their hearts that I remember all their wickedness. Now their deeds hem them in, they are there, before my eyes.
With their wickedness they gladden the king, and with their lies the princes.
They are all adulterers, burning like an oven that the baker stops stoking from the kneading of the dough until it rises.
On the festival day of our king, the princes make themselves sick with the heat of wine, and the king joins hands with mockers.
In their plotting their heart is burning like an oven; all night their fury smolders, and in the morning it blazes up like a raging fire.
They are all burning like an oven and devour their judges; all their kings have fallen, and not one of them cries out to me.
Ephraim mixes with the peoples; Ephraim is a flat cake not turned over.
Foreigners have devoured his strength, and he does not know it; gray hairs are scattered on his head, and he does not know it.
Israel's pride testifies against him: for all this, they do not return to the Lord their God, nor seek him.
Ephraim has become like a silly dove, without sense: they call to Egypt, they go off to Assyria.
But as they go, I spread my net over them; I will bring them down like the birds of the sky, I will discipline them as was announced to their assembly.
Woe to them, for they have fled far from me! Ruin upon them, for they have betrayed me! I would redeem them, but they speak lies against me.
They do not cry out to me from the heart, but wail on their beds; they distress themselves over grain and new wine, and turn away from me.
I strengthened their arms and trained them, yet they plot evil against me.
They turn, but not to the Most High; they are like a treacherous bow. Their rulers will fall by the sword, because of the insolence of their tongue; and they will be mocked in the land of Egypt.
The trumpet to your lips! Like an eagle, the enemy swoops down on the house of the Lord, because they have broken my covenant and sinned against my law.
They cry out to me, 'My God, we know you, we, Israel!'
But Israel has rejected the good: let the enemy pursue him!
They have made kings, but without me; they have set up rulers, but without my knowledge; from their silver and their gold they have made themselves idols, to their own ruin.
Your calf disgusts me, Samaria! My anger has flared up against them. How long will they be incapable of purity?
For it comes from Israel, this calf: a craftsman made it, and it is no god. Yes, it will be smashed to pieces, the calf of Samaria!
Since they sow the wind, they will reap the storm: a stalk without ears, yielding no flour; and even if it did, foreigners would devour it.
Israel is devoured; there it is, among the nations, like a worthless thing.
They have gone up to Assyria, like a wild donkey off on its own; Ephraim has bought himself lovers.
Even though they hire allies among the nations, I am about to gather them against them; and soon they will tremble under the burden of the great king.
Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, and these altars have made him fall into sin.
Though I were to write for him the thousand articles of my law, he would regard them as something foreign.
They offer sacrifices, they slaughter meat and eat it: the Lord takes no pleasure in it. Now he remembers their guilt and punishes their sins; they will return to Egypt.
Israel has forgotten his Maker and built himself palaces; Judah has multiplied his fortified cities. But I will send fire on his cities, and it will devour his strongholds.
Do not give yourself to joy, Israel, do not rejoice like the other peoples; for you have prostituted yourself far from your God, you have loved the wages of a prostitute on every threshing floor.
Neither the threshing floor nor the winepress will feed them, and the new wine will fail them.
They will not stay in the land of the Lord: Ephraim will return to Egypt, and in Assyria they will eat unclean food.

They will no longer pour out wine offerings to the Lord, and their sacrifices will not please him; it will be for them like the bread of mourning, which makes all who eat it unclean; for their bread will be for themselves alone, it will not enter the house of the Lord.
What will you do on the festival day, on the day of the Lord's solemn feast?
See, they are going off, escaping the ruin; Egypt will gather them, Memphis will bury them. As for their treasures of silver, the thistle will take them over, thorns will invade their tents.

They have come, the days of punishment! They have come, the days of retribution! Let Israel know it: 'The prophet is a fool, the inspired man is raving!' So great is your guilt, so great your hostility.
Ephraim keeps watch against my God; for the prophet, a fowler's snare is set on all his paths, and hostility even in the house of his God.
They are corrupt to the core, as in the days of Gibeah; the Lord will remember their guilt, he will punish their sins.

Like grapes in the desert, I had found Israel; like the first fruits of a young fig tree, I had seen your fathers. But they, as soon as they reached Baal-peor, devoted themselves to the shameful idol and became as detestable as the thing they loved.
Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird: no more birth, no more pregnancy, no more conception.
And even if they raise children, I will bereave them before they become men; for woe to them when I turn away from them!
Ephraim, I saw him like a young palm planted in a lovely meadow; and yet Ephraim is going to lead his children out to the slaughterer.
Give them, Lord... What will you give them? Give them a barren womb and dry breasts.

All their wickedness showed itself at Gilgal; there I began to hate them. Because of the wickedness of their deeds, I will drive them out of my house, I will love them no longer: all their rulers are rebels.
Ephraim is struck down, his root is dried up: they will bear no more fruit. And even if they give birth, I will put to death the cherished fruit of their womb.
My God will reject them, because they have not listened to him, and they will wander among the nations.

titres.titre: The vine and the altars of Israel

versets.t: Israel was a luxuriant vine, laden with fruit. The more his fruit increased, the more he multiplied altars; the more beautiful his land, the more he adorned his sacred pillars.
Their heart is divided: now they must bear the penalty. He himself will overturn their altars and destroy their sacred pillars.
Soon they will say, 'We have no king, for we did not fear the Lord; and the king, what could he do for us?'
They pile up words, false oaths, covenants that come to nothing; and litigation sprouts like a poisonous weed in the furrows of the fields.
The inhabitants of Samaria tremble for the calf of Beth-aven; its people mourn over it, and its priests wail for its glory, which is departing from it.
It too will be carried off to Assyria, as tribute to the great king; Ephraim will be covered with shame, Israel will blush for its schemes.
Samaria is destroyed, its king swept away like a twig on the surface of the water.
The high places of Aven, that sin of Israel, will be destroyed; thorns and thistles will grow over their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, 'Cover us!' and to the hills, 'Fall on us!'
Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, Israel; there they have stayed. Will not war overtake them at Gibeah, the war declared against the sons of crime?
I will discipline them as I please; the peoples will gather against them, when I bind them for their double guilt.
Ephraim was a well-trained heifer that loved to thresh the grain; but I laid the yoke on her fine neck. I will harness Ephraim, Judah will plow, Jacob will drag the harrow.
Sow according to righteousness, reap according to love, break up your fallow ground; it is time to seek the Lord, until he comes to rain righteousness upon you.
But you have plowed wickedness, reaped crime, eaten the fruit of lies. You trusted in your own ways, in the multitude of your warriors;

therefore the tumult of war will rise against your people, and all your fortresses will be ravaged, as Shalman ravaged Beth-arbel on the day of battle, when the mother was dashed to pieces on her children.
This is what Bethel has brought upon you, because of your extreme wickedness. At dawn it will be all over for the king of Israel.
When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
But the more they were called, the more they went away: they offered sacrifices to the Baals and burned incense to idols.
It was I who taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by the arms; but they did not understand that I was caring for them.
I led them with human ties, with bonds of love; I was to them like one who lifts an infant to his cheek, and I bent down to feed him.
He will not return to the land of Egypt, but Assyria will be his king, because they refused to return.
The sword will fall upon his cities, break their bars, and devour, because of their schemes.
My people persist in turning away from me; they are called to the Most High, but not one of them rises.
How could I abandon you, Ephraim? How could I hand you over, Israel? How could I treat you like Admah, make you like Zeboiim? My heart recoils within me, all my compassion is stirred.
I will not give free rein to the heat of my anger, I will not destroy Ephraim again; for I am God and not man, the Holy One in your midst, and I will not come in fury.
They will follow the Lord, who will roar like a lion; when he roars, his children will come trembling, from the west.
They will come trembling like a bird, from Egypt, like a dove, from Assyria; and I will settle them in their homes, oracle of the Lord.

titres.titre: The case and the example of Jacob

versets.t: Ephraim surrounds me with lies, and the house of Israel with deceit; Judah too is unbridled before God, before the Holy One, who is faithful.
Ephraim feeds on wind, he chases the east wind all day long; he heaps up lies and violence, he makes a covenant with Assyria and carries his oil to Egypt.
The Lord also has a case against Judah; he will punish Jacob for his conduct, he will repay him for his deeds.
From the womb Jacob supplanted his brother, and in his vigor he wrestled with God.
He wrestled with the angel and prevailed; he wept and begged for his favor. At Bethel he found him, and there he spoke with us.
The Lord, the God of hosts, the Lord is his name.
And you, return to your God! Keep faithful love and justice, and hope in your God always.
Like a merchant, Ephraim holds false scales, he loves to defraud.
Ephraim says, 'Yet I have grown rich, I have made myself a fortune; in all my gains no fault will be found against me that would be a sin.'
But I am the Lord your God from the land of Egypt; I will make you dwell in tents again, as in the days of the feast.
I spoke to the prophets, I multiplied visions, and through the prophets I spoke in parables.
If Gilead is but nothing, its inhabitants will be but wind; at Gilgal they sacrificed bulls, so their altars will be like heaps of stones on the furrows of the fields.
Jacob fled to the land of Aram; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he tended the flocks.
Then, through a prophet, the Lord brought Israel up out of Egypt, and through a prophet he was kept safe.
Ephraim has stirred up bitter anger; his Lord will bring back on him the blood he shed and repay him for his outrage.
When Ephraim spoke, people trembled; he was exalted in Israel. But he became guilty through Baal, and he died.

And now they sin more and more: from their silver they make themselves cast statues, idols shaped to their own fancy, all of it a craftsman's work! People say of them, 'They sacrifice men and kiss calves!'
Therefore they will be like the morning cloud, like the early dew that vanishes, like the chaff swept away from the threshing floor, like smoke escaping through the window.
But I am the Lord your God from the land of Egypt; you will know no God but me, and apart from me there is no Savior.
It was I who knew you in the desert, in the land of drought.
But once satisfied in their pastures, they were sated, their heart grew proud, and that is why they forgot me.
So I will be to them like a lion, like a leopard lying in wait by the roadside.
I will fall upon them like a bear robbed of her cubs, I will tear open the covering of their heart; I will devour them there like a lioness, and the wild beasts will rip them apart.
What destroys you, Israel, is that you have risen against me, against the one who is your help.
Where then is your king, to save you in all your cities? And your judges, of whom you said, 'Give me a king and princes'?
I give you a king in my anger, and I take him back in my fury.
Ephraim's guilt is bound up in a sheaf, his sin is held in store.
The pangs of childbirth seize him; but he is a child without wisdom, who, when the time comes, does not present himself to be born.

I will deliver them from the power of the realm of the dead, I will redeem them from death. Where is your plague, O death? Where is your destruction, O realm of the dead? Compassion is hidden from my eyes.

Though Ephraim may flourish among his brothers, the east wind will come, the breath of the Lord rising from the desert: his spring will run dry, his fountain will be parched, it will plunder his treasure, all his precious objects.

titres.titre: The punishment and the call to return

versets.t: Samaria will be punished, for she has rebelled against her God; they will fall by the sword, their little children will be dashed to pieces, their pregnant women ripped open.
Return, Israel, to the Lord your God, for it is your guilt that has made you fall.
Take words with you and return to the Lord; say to him, 'Take away all guilt, accept what is good; instead of bulls, we will offer you the fruit of our lips.
Assyria will not save us, we will no longer ride on horses, and we will no longer say to the work of our hands that it is our God; for it is in you that the orphan finds compassion.'
I will heal their unfaithfulness, I will love them freely, for my anger has turned away from them.
I will be like the dew to Israel: he will blossom like the lily, he will strike his roots like the cedars of Lebanon.
His branches will spread out, his splendor will be like the olive tree, his fragrance like Lebanon.
They will return to dwell in his shade, they will make the grain flourish again, they will blossom like the vine, and his renown will be like the wine of Lebanon.
Ephraim, what has he still to do with idols? It is I who answer him and watch over him; I am like an evergreen cypress, and from me comes your fruit.
Whoever is wise, let him understand these things; whoever is discerning, let him acknowledge them! For the ways of the Lord are straight: the righteous walk in them, but the rebels stumble in them.

titres.titre: A Call to Mourning and Fasting

versets.t: The word of the Lord that came to Joel son of Pethuel.
Hear this, you elders! Listen, all you who dwell in the land! Has anything like this ever happened in your days, or in the days of your fathers?
Tell it to your children, and let your children tell it to theirs, and their children to the generation that follows.
What the cutting locust left, the swarming locust has devoured; what the swarming locust left, the hopping locust has devoured; what the hopping locust left, the destroying locust has devoured.
Wake up, you drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you drinkers of wine, for the new wine is snatched from your lips.
For a nation has come up against my land, mighty and beyond number; its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and it has the fangs of a lioness.
It has laid waste my vine and splintered my fig tree; it has stripped them bare to the white wood and strewn the ground with their branches.
Wail like a young woman clothed in sackcloth, grieving for the bridegroom of her youth!
Grain offering and drink offering have vanished from the house of the Lord; the priests, the servants of the Lord, are in mourning.
The fields are ravaged, the ground mourns; for the grain is destroyed, the new wine has run dry, the oil has failed.
Be dismayed, you farmers! Wail, you vinedressers, over the wheat and the barley, for the harvest of the fields is lost!
The vine is withered, the fig tree droops; the pomegranate, the palm, the apple, all the trees of the field are dry. Truly, joy has withdrawn in shame, far from the children of men.

Priests, put on sackcloth and wail! Lament, you servants of the altar! Come, spend the night in sackcloth, servants of my God, for grain offering and drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.
Proclaim a fast, call a solemn assembly, gather the elders and all who dwell in the land to the house of the Lord your God, and cry out to the Lord!
"Ah, what a day!" For the day of the Lord is near: it comes like a devastation sent from the Almighty.
Has not the food been cut off before our very eyes, and joy and gladness from the house of our God?
The seeds have rotted beneath the clods, the storehouses are empty, the barns are falling into ruin, for the grain has failed.
How the cattle groan! The herds of oxen wander in confusion, for they have no pasture; even the flocks of sheep suffer.
To you, O Lord, I cry, for fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and flame has burned all the trees of the field.
Even the wild beasts long for you, for the streams of water are dried up, and fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.

titres.titre: Return to Me with All Your Heart

versets.t: Blow the horn in Zion, sound the alarm on my holy mountain! Let all who dwell in the land tremble, for the day of the Lord is coming, for it is near:

a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness. Like the dawn spreading over the mountains, a people numerous and strong now comes, such as has never been before, and never will be again through all the ages to come.
Before them a fire devours; behind them a flame burns. Before them the land is like the garden of Eden; behind them it is a desolate wilderness, and nothing escapes them.
They look like horses; they gallop like cavalry.
With a din of chariots they leap over the mountaintops; it is the crackling of flame devouring stubble, a mighty people drawn up for battle.
Before them the peoples tremble, and every face grows pale.
They charge like warriors, they scale the wall like soldiers; each keeps to his course and does not swerve from his path.
They do not jostle one another; each goes straight ahead; they plunge through the weapons without breaking ranks.
They rush upon the city, they run along the walls, they climb into the houses, they enter through the windows like a thief.
Before them the earth quakes and the heavens shake; the sun and the moon grow dark, and the stars lose their brightness.
The Lord lifts up his voice at the head of his army; his camp is vast, and mighty is the one who carries out his word. Great indeed is the day of the Lord, and terrible: who can endure it?
Yet even now, declares the Lord, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning.
Rend your hearts and not your garments, and return to the Lord your God; for he is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and rich in love, and he relents from the calamity he announces.
Who knows whether he will not turn back and relent, and leave behind him a blessing, a grain offering and a drink offering for the Lord your God?
Blow the horn in Zion, proclaim a fast, call a solemn assembly!
Gather the people, consecrate the assembly, assemble the elders, gather the children and the nursing infants! Let the bridegroom come out of his chamber, and the bride from her wedding tent!

Between the portico and the altar, let the priests, the servants of the Lord, weep and say: "Spare your people, O Lord, and do not make your heritage an object of shame, a byword among the nations. Why should it be said among the peoples: Where is their God?"
Then the Lord became jealous for his land, and he had pity on his people.
The Lord answered his people: I am now sending you grain, new wine, and oil, and you will have your fill; and never again will I make you an object of shame among the nations.

The enemy from the north I will drive far from you, banishing them to a parched and desolate land, their vanguard toward the eastern sea, their rear guard toward the western sea; their stench will rise, their foul odor will go up, for they have done great destruction.
Do not be afraid, O land; be glad and rejoice, for the Lord has done great things!
Do not be afraid, you beasts of the field, for the pastures of the wilderness have turned green again; the tree bears its fruit, the fig tree and the vine yield their riches.

And you, children of Zion, be glad and rejoice in the Lord your God! For he has given you the autumn rain in due measure, he sends down the showers for you, autumn rain and spring rain, as in former times.
The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
I will repay you for the years devoured by the swarming locust, the hopping locust, the destroying locust, and the cutting locust, my great army that I sent against you.
You will eat your fill and be satisfied, and you will praise the name of the Lord your God, who has done wonders for you; and never again will my people know shame.
Then you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, that I am the Lord your God, and there is no other; and never again will my people know shame.
After this, I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh: your sons and your daughters will prophesy, your old men will dream dreams, your young men will see visions.
Even on the male and female servants, in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
I will show wonders in the heavens and on the earth: blood, fire, and columns of smoke.
The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood, before the coming of the day of the Lord, great and terrible.

Then everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, as the Lord has said, and among the survivors, those whom the Lord calls.
For behold, in those days and at that time, when I restore Judah and Jerusalem,

I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat; there I will enter into judgment with them on behalf of Israel, my people and my heritage, whom they scattered among the nations, and for my land, which they divided up.
They cast lots for my people, they gave a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine, and drank it down.

And you, what do you want with me, Tyre and Sidon, and all you regions of Philistia? Do you seek to take vengeance on me? If you strike at me, swiftly, in an instant, I will bring back upon your own heads what you have done;
you who took my silver and my gold, and carried off my finest treasures into your temples;
you who sold the sons of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to remove them far from their own land!
Behold, I will rouse them from the place where you sold them, and I will bring back upon your own heads what you have done.
I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hands of the sons of Judah, who will sell them to the Sabeans, to a nation far away. Truly, the Lord has spoken.
Proclaim this among the nations: Declare a holy war! Rouse the warriors! Let them draw near, let them come up, all the men of war!
Beat your plowshares into swords, and your pruning hooks into spears! Let the weakling say: "I am a mighty man!"
Hurry and come, all you surrounding nations, and gather yourselves together! There, O Lord, bring down your warriors.
Let the nations rouse themselves and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat! For there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe! Come, tread, for the winepress is full, the vats overflow, so great is their wickedness!
Multitudes upon multitudes in the Valley of Decision! For the day of the Lord is near in the Valley of Decision.
The sun and the moon grow dark, and the stars lose their brightness.
From Zion the Lord roars; from Jerusalem he raises his voice; the heavens and the earth tremble. But the Lord is a refuge for his people, a stronghold for the children of Israel.
Then you will know that I am the Lord your God, who dwells in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be a holy place, and strangers will pass through it no more.

On that day, the mountains will run with new wine, the hills will flow with milk, and all the streams of Judah will run with water; a spring will flow from the house of the Lord and water the Valley of Acacias.
Egypt will become a desolation, and Edom a devastated wilderness, because of the violence done to the sons of Judah, whose innocent blood they shed in their own land.
But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from age to age.
I will avenge their blood, which I had not yet avenged; and the Lord will dwell in Zion.
The words of Amos, one of the shepherds of Tekoa. What he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah, and of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
He said: The Lord roars from Zion, from Jerusalem he raises his voice; then the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel withers away.
Thus says the Lord: For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not revoke my sentence. Because they threshed Gilead with sledges of iron,
I will send fire against the house of Hazael, and it will devour the palaces of Ben-hadad;
I will break the bar of Damascus, I will cut off those who dwell in the Valley of Aven and the one who holds the scepter in Beth-eden; and the people of Aram will go into exile to Kir, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: For three transgressions of Gaza, and for four, I will not revoke my sentence. Because they carried whole peoples into deportation to hand them over to Edom,
I will send fire against the walls of Gaza, and it will devour her palaces;
I will cut off those who dwell in Ashdod and the one who holds the scepter in Ashkelon; I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish, says the Lord God.

Thus says the Lord: For three transgressions of Tyre, and for four, I will not revoke my sentence. Because they handed over to Edom whole peoples of captives, without remembering the covenant of brotherhood,
I will send fire against the walls of Tyre, and it will devour her palaces.

Thus says the Lord: For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not revoke my sentence. Because he pursued his brother with the sword, stifling all compassion; because his anger tore without end and he kept his rage forever,
I will send fire against Teman, and it will devour the palaces of Bozrah.
Thus says the Lord: For three transgressions of the sons of Ammon, and for four, I will not revoke my sentence. Because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead to enlarge their territory,
I will kindle a fire against the walls of Rabbah, and it will devour her palaces, amid the shouting of a day of battle, in the storm of a day of whirlwind.
And their king will go into exile, he and his princes with him, says the Lord.
Thus says the Lord: For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not revoke my sentence. Because he burned the bones of the king of Edom until he reduced them to lime,
I will send fire against Moab, and it will devour the palaces of Kerioth; Moab will die in the uproar, amid war cries and the sound of the horn.
I will cut off the ruler from among them, and I will slay all his princes with him, says the Lord.

Thus says the Lord: For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not revoke my sentence. Because they rejected the law of the Lord and did not keep his commandments, and their lying idols, the ones their fathers had followed, led them astray,
I will send fire against Judah, and it will devour the palaces of Jerusalem.
Thus says the Lord: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not revoke my sentence. Because they sell the righteous for silver, and the poor for a pair of sandals;
because they crush the head of the weak into the dust and turn aside the way of the humble; because father and son go to the same girl, and so profane my holy name;
because they stretch out beside every altar on garments taken in pledge, and in the house of their God they drink the wine of those they have fined.
Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them, tall as the cedars and strong as the oaks; I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.
It was I who brought you up out of the land of Egypt and led you forty years through the wilderness, to give you the land of the Amorite in possession.
I raised up prophets from among your sons, and Nazirites from among your young men. Is it not so, sons of Israel? oracle of the Lord.
But you made the Nazirites drink wine, and to the prophets you gave the order: "Do not prophesy!"
Now then, I will crush you where you stand, as the cart loaded with sheaves crushes the ground.
The swift will no longer be able to flee, the strong will no longer find his vigor, the warrior will not save his life;
the archer will not stand his ground, the runner will not escape, the horseman will not save his life;
and on that day the bravest of the warriors will flee away naked, oracle of the Lord.
Hear this word that the Lord speaks against you, sons of Israel, against the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt:
You only have I known of all the families of the earth; therefore I will call you to account for all your iniquities.
Do two people walk together unless they have agreed to meet?
Does the lion roar in the forest when it has no prey? Does the young lion cry out from its den when it has caught nothing?
Does a bird fall into a snare on the ground when no bait has been set for it? Does the snare spring up from the ground when it has taken nothing?
Is the horn sounded in a city without the people trembling? Does disaster strike a city unless the Lord has caused it?
Surely the Lord God does nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets.
The lion has roared: who will not fear? The Lord God has spoken: who will not prophesy?

Proclaim it over the palaces of Ashdod and over the palaces of the land of Egypt, and say: Gather yourselves on the mountains of Samaria, and see the great disorders within her, the acts of violence in her midst.
They no longer know how to act with uprightness, oracle of the Lord, they who pile up violence and plunder in their palaces.
Therefore, thus says the Lord God: An enemy will surround the land, he will bring down your strength, and your palaces will be plundered.

Thus says the Lord: As the shepherd rescues from the mouth of the lion two shanks or the tip of an ear, so will the sons of Israel be rescued, they who sit enthroned in Samaria on the corner of a couch and on the cushions of their bed.
Hear and testify to this in the house of Jacob, oracle of the Lord God, the God of hosts:
on the day I call Israel to account for its transgressions, I will also strike the altars of Bethel; the horns of the altar will be broken off and fall to the ground.
I will strike the winter house and the summer house; the houses of ivory will be devastated, the great mansions wiped out, oracle of the Lord.

titres.titre: You did not return to me

versets.t: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on the mountain of Samaria, you who oppress the weak and crush the poor, you who say to your husbands: "Bring, that we may drink!"
The Lord God has sworn by his holiness: Behold, days are coming when they will drag you away with hooks, and the last of you with fishhooks.
You will go out through the breaches, each one straight ahead, and you will be flung out toward Hermon, oracle of the Lord.
Come to Bethel, and sin! At Gilgal, multiply your transgressions! Offer your sacrifices every morning, and your tithes every three days!
Send up in smoke an offering of praise with leaven, proclaim with loud voice your freewill offerings; for this is what you love, sons of Israel, oracle of the Lord God.
And I, for my part, gave you clean teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your villages; yet you did not return to me, oracle of the Lord.
I withheld the rain from you, three months still before the harvest; I made it rain on one city and not on another; one field received the rain, and another, deprived of rain, withered.
Two, three cities staggered to another to drink water, without quenching their thirst; yet you did not return to me, oracle of the Lord.
I struck you with blight and mildew; your many gardens, your vineyards, your fig trees and your olive trees, the locust devoured them; yet you did not return to me, oracle of the Lord.

I sent among you the plague, as in Egypt; I killed your young men with the sword, while your horses were captured; I made the stench of your camp rise into your nostrils; yet you did not return to me, oracle of the Lord.
I overthrew you as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a brand snatched from the fire; yet you did not return to me, oracle of the Lord.
Therefore, this is how I will deal with you, Israel. And since I am going to deal with you in this way, prepare to meet your God, Israel!

For it is he who shapes the mountains and creates the wind, who reveals to man his thought, who turns the dawn to darkness and treads on the heights of the earth: the Lord, the God of hosts, is his name.
Hear this word that I raise over you, this lament, house of Israel:
She has fallen, she will rise no more, the virgin of Israel! Cast down on her own soil, no one raises her up.
For thus says the Lord: The city that marched out to battle with a thousand men will keep only a hundred, and the one that sent out a hundred will keep only ten, for the house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord to the house of Israel: Seek me, and you will live!
Do not seek Bethel, do not come to Gilgal, do not cross over to Beersheba; for Gilgal will go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing.
Seek the Lord, and you will live! Otherwise he will sweep like fire upon the house of Joseph, and it will devour it, with no one at Bethel to quench it.
They turn justice into bitter poison and cast righteousness to the ground!
He who made the Pleiades and Orion, who turns the darkness into dawn and the day into dark night, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth, the Lord is his name.
He makes ruin burst upon the strong, and devastation comes down upon the fortified city.
They hate the one who defends justice at the gate, they loathe the one who speaks with integrity.

Now then, because you trample the poor and extort from him a tribute of grain: these houses of dressed stone that you have built, you will not live in them; these splendid vineyards that you have planted, you will not drink their wine.
For I know your countless transgressions and your enormous sins, you who oppress the righteous, take bribes and turn away the poor at the gate.
That is why, in such an evil time, the prudent keep silent.
Seek good and not evil, that you may live; then the Lord, the God of hosts, will truly be with you, as you claim.
Hate evil, love good, establish justice at the gate; perhaps the Lord, the God of hosts, will have pity on the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore, thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, the Lord: In all the squares there will be wailing, in all the streets they will cry: Alas! alas! They will call the farmer to mourning, and to lamentation those skilled in wailing.
In all the vineyards there will be wailing, for I will pass through your midst, says the Lord.
Woe to those who long for the day of the Lord! What will that day be for you? Darkness, and not light.
It will be like a man who flees from the lion and meets the bear; he enters his house, rests his hand against the wall, and the serpent bites him.
Will not the day of the Lord be darkness, and not light, gloom without the least glimmer?
I hate, I despise your feasts, I can no longer bear your assemblies.
When you offer me your burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I take no pleasure in them; your peace offerings of fattened beasts, I will not look at them.
Take away from me the noise of your songs, that I may not hear the sound of your harps!
But let justice roll down like water, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream!
Did you bring me sacrifices and offerings during the forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?
You carried the tent of your king and the star of your god, those idols you made for yourselves.
So I will send you into exile beyond Damascus, says the Lord, whose name is the God of hosts.
Woe to those who live at ease in Zion, to those who feel secure on the mountain of Samaria! Notables of the foremost of nations, to whom the house of Israel comes running,
cross over to Calneh and see, go on from there to Hamath the great, go down to Gath of the Philistines: are these kingdoms better than yours, is their territory larger than yours?
You think you are pushing away the day of disaster, but you are bringing near the reign of violence.
Lying on beds of ivory, sprawled on their couches, they eat the lambs of the flock and the calves fattened in the stall;
they improvise to the sound of the harp and, like David, invent for themselves instruments of music;
they drink wine by the bowlful, they anoint themselves with the finest oils, but they are not grieved over the ruin of Joseph.
Therefore they will go into exile at the head of the captives, and the feasting of those who sprawl will be over.
The Lord God has sworn by himself, oracle of the Lord, the God of hosts: I loathe the pride of Jacob, I hate his palaces, I will hand over the city and all it contains.
And if ten men are left in a single house, they too will die.

When a relative comes to carry off the dead to burn his bones and bring them out of the house, he will ask the one at the far end of the dwelling: "Is there anyone still with you?" He will answer: "No one!" And the first will say: "Hush! The name of the Lord must not be spoken."
For behold, the Lord commands: he will reduce the great house to rubble and the small house to fragments.
Do horses run on the rock? Does one plow it with oxen? And yet you have turned justice into poison, and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood!
You rejoice over what is nothing, you say: "Was it not by our own strength that we became powerful?"
Now then, behold, I am raising up against you, house of Israel, oracle of the Lord, the God of hosts, a nation that will oppress you from the entrance of Hamath to the Wadi of the Arabah.

titres.titre: Amos and the priest of Bethel

versets.t: This is what the Lord God showed me: he was forming locusts at the time when the late growth was springing up, that late growth which comes after the cutting reserved for the king.
When they had finished devouring the grass of the land, I said: "Lord God, forgive, I beg you! How will Jacob stand? He is so small!"
Then the Lord relented: "This will not happen," said the Lord.
This is what the Lord God showed me: the Lord God was summoning fire to punish; the fire devoured the great deep and was about to devour the land.
And I said: "Lord God, stop, I beg you! How will Jacob stand? He is so small!"
Then the Lord relented: "This too will not happen," said the Lord God.
This is what he showed me: the Lord was standing on a wall built with a plumb line, a plumb line in his hand.
And the Lord said to me: "What do you see, Amos?" I answered: "A plumb line." The Lord went on: "Behold, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of my people Israel; I will no longer pardon them.
The high places of Isaac will be devastated, the sanctuaries of Israel destroyed, and I will rise with the sword in hand against the house of Jeroboam."
Then Amaziah, priest of Bethel, sent word to Jeroboam, king of Israel: "Amos is conspiring against you in the very midst of Israel; the land can no longer bear all his words.
For this is what Amos says: Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will be deported far from its land."
And Amaziah said to Amos: "Seer, go away, flee to the land of Judah; there earn your bread and prophesy.
But at Bethel, prophesy no more, for it is a royal sanctuary, a house of the kingdom."
Amos answered Amaziah: "I was no prophet, nor the son of a prophet; I was a shepherd and I tended sycamores.
But the Lord took me from behind the flock, and the Lord said to me: Go, prophesy to my people Israel.
And now, hear the word of the Lord. You say: Do not prophesy against Israel, do not speak against the house of Isaac!

Now then, thus says the Lord: Your wife will play the harlot in the city, your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword, your land will be divided up by the measuring line; you yourself will die on unclean soil, and Israel will be deported far from its land."
This is what the Lord God showed me: a basket of ripe fruit.
He said to me: "What do you see, Amos?" I answered: "A basket of ripe fruit." And the Lord said to me: "The end is ripe for my people Israel; I will no longer pardon them.
The songs of the palace will become howls, on that day, oracle of the Lord God. Everywhere, corpses in throngs, flung down in silence."
Hear this, you who crush the poor to wipe out the humble of the land,

you who say: "When will the new moon be over, that we may sell our grain? When will the sabbath end, that we may open our storehouses, to shrink the measure, inflate the price and rig the scales that cheat?
We will buy the weak for silver, the poor for a pair of sandals, and we will sell even the sweepings of the grain!"
The Lord has sworn by the pride of Jacob: Never will I forget any of their deeds.
Is it not for this that the earth will tremble, that all its inhabitants will mourn? It will rise entirely like the Nile, surge up and subside like the river of Egypt.
On that day, oracle of the Lord God, I will make the sun go down at high noon, I will wrap the earth in darkness in broad daylight.

I will turn your feasts into mourning, all your songs into laments; I will put sackcloth on every waist, I will shave every head; I will make this land mourn as for an only son, and its end will be a day of bitterness.
Behold, days are coming, oracle of the Lord God, when I will send famine on the land: not a famine of bread nor a thirst for water, but for hearing the words of the Lord.
Then people will wander from sea to sea, from north to east; they will roam everywhere seeking the word of the Lord, without finding it.
On that day the beautiful young women and the young men will faint with thirst.
Those who swear by the idol of Samaria, who say: "By the life of your god, O Dan! By the life of the way to Beersheba!", they will fall to rise no more.

I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and he said: "Strike the capital, that the thresholds may tremble, shatter them on the heads of all! Those who remain I will slay by the sword; not one will flee, not one will escape.
If they dig down into the realm of the dead, my hand will drag them up from there; if they climb up to the heavens, I will bring them down from there.
If they hide on the summit of Carmel, I will find them there and seize them; if they conceal themselves from my eyes at the bottom of the sea, there too I will command the serpent to bite them.
And if they go into exile before their enemies, there I will command the sword to slay them. I will fix my eyes on them for harm and not for good."
The Lord, the God of hosts, touches the earth and it melts away, and all its inhabitants mourn; it rises entirely like the Nile, then subsides like the river of Egypt.
He builds his stairs in the heavens and sets his vault over the earth; he summons the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth: the Lord is his name.
Are you not to me like the Ethiopians, sons of Israel? oracle of the Lord. Did I not bring Israel up out of the land of Egypt, as I brought the Philistines from Caphtor and the Arameans from Kir?
Behold, the eyes of the Lord God are fixed on this sinful kingdom: I will wipe it off the face of the earth. Yet I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, oracle of the Lord.
For behold, I am about to give my orders and shake the house of Israel among all the nations, as grain is shaken in a sieve, without a single good kernel falling to the ground.
They will die by the sword, all the sinners of my people, they who say: "Disaster will not come near us, it will not reach us."
On that day I will raise up the fallen tent of David; I will repair its breaches, I will raise up its ruins, I will rebuild it as in the days of old,
so that the remnant of mankind may seek the Lord, along with all the nations over whom my name is invoked, oracle of the Lord, who accomplishes all this.

Behold, days are coming, oracle of the Lord, when the plowman will follow close on the reaper, and the treader of grapes on the sower; the mountains will drip with new wine, and all the hills will flow with it.

I will bring back the captives of my people Israel; they will rebuild the devastated cities and live in them, they will plant vineyards and drink their wine, they will cultivate gardens and eat their fruit.
I will plant them on their own soil, and never again will they be uprooted from the land I have given them, says the Lord your God.

titres.titre: The Pride and Fall of Edom

versets.t: The vision of Obadiah. Thus says the Lord God concerning Edom. We have heard a message from the Lord, and a herald has been sent among the nations: "Up! Let us rise against Edom and do battle with it!"
See, I am making you small among the nations; you are deeply despised.
The pride of your heart has led you astray, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock and make the heights your home, you who say in your heart, "Who can bring me down to the ground?"
Though you soar like the eagle, though you set your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, declares the Lord.

If thieves had come to you, if plunderers by night, how ruined you now are! would they not have carried off only what they needed? If grape-gatherers had come to you, would they not have left a few grapes to glean?
How Esau has been ransacked, how his hidden treasures have been laid bare!

They have driven you back to the border, all your allies; they have deceived you, they have prevailed against you, your friends; those who ate your bread have set a trap beneath your feet, and you never suspected it.
On that day, declares the Lord, will I not destroy the wise of Edom, and understanding from the mountain of Esau?
Your warriors, Teman, will be struck with terror, and every man will be cut off from the mountain of Esau in the slaughter.
For the violence done to your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.
On the day you stood aloof, while enemies carried off his wealth and strangers passed through his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.
Do not feast your eyes on the day of your brother, on the day of his misfortune; do not rejoice over the sons of Judah on the day of their ruin, and do not boast on the day of distress.

Do not enter the gate of my people on the day of their disaster; do not feast your eyes, you too, on his misery on the day of his disaster, and do not lay a hand on his goods on the day of his disaster.
Do not lie in wait at the crossroads to cut down his fugitives, do not hand over his survivors on the day of distress.
For it is near, the day of the Lord, for all the nations: as you have done, so it will be done to you; your deeds will fall back upon your own head.
For just as you have drunk on my holy mountain, so all the nations will drink without end: they will drink, they will swallow, and it will be as though they had never been.
But on Mount Zion there will be survivors: it will be a holy place, and the house of Jacob will take back its possessions.

The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau will be the stubble: they will set it ablaze and devour it, and nothing will survive of the house of Esau. For the Lord has spoken.

Those of the Negeb will possess the mountain of Esau, and those of the lowland the land of the Philistines; they will possess the territory of Ephraim and the territory of Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.
The exiles of this army, the sons of Israel, will possess the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath; and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad will possess the towns of the Negeb.
Deliverers will go up on Mount Zion to judge the mountain of Esau; and the kingship will belong to the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to Jonah son of Amittai in these terms:
"Get up, go to Nineveh, the great city, and cry out against it, for their wickedness has risen up to me."

But Jonah got up to flee to Tarshish, away from the Lord. He went down to Joppa, found there a ship bound for Tarshish, paid his fare, and boarded it to sail with them to Tarshish, away from the Lord.
But the Lord unleashed a great wind upon the sea, and there was so violent a storm that the ship threatened to break apart.

The sailors, terrified, each cried out to his own god and threw the cargo into the sea to lighten the ship. Jonah, meanwhile, had gone down into the hold of the boat, where he had lain down and fallen fast asleep.
The captain came up to him and said, "How can you be sleeping? Get up, call on your God! Perhaps this God will think of us, and we will not perish."
Then they said to one another, "Come, let us cast lots to find out who is bringing this disaster upon us." They cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
So they said to him, "Tell us, then, who is bringing this disaster upon us. What is your occupation? Where do you come from? What is your country, and what people are you from?"
He answered them, "I am a Hebrew, and I worship the Lord, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land."
The men were seized with great fear and said to him, "What have you done!" For they knew that he was fleeing away from the Lord, since he had told them so.
They said to him, "What should we do to you to make the sea grow calm for us?" For the sea was rising higher and higher.
He answered them, "Take me and throw me into the sea, and it will grow calm for you; for I know well that it is because of me that this great storm has come upon you."
The men rowed hard to get back to land, but in vain, for the sea rose higher and higher against them.
Then they cried out to the Lord, "Ah, Lord, do not let us perish for the life of this man, and do not hold us guilty of innocent blood! For you, Lord, have done as you willed."
Then they took Jonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea ceased its raging.
Then these men were seized with great fear of the Lord; they offered him a sacrifice and made vows.
The Lord sent a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah remained in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
From the belly of the fish, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God. He said:
"In my distress I cried out to the Lord, and he answered me; out of the belly of the realm of the dead I called, and you heard my voice.
You had cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the current swirled around me; all your waves and all your billows swept over me.
I said to myself: I am driven away from your sight; yet I will look again upon your holy temple.
The waters closed in on me up to my throat, the deep surrounded me, seaweed coiled around my head.
I had gone down to the roots of the mountains, the bars of the earth had closed upon me forever; but you brought my life up out of the pit, Lord my God!
When my soul was failing within me, I remembered the Lord, and my prayer reached you, in your holy temple.
Those who cling to worthless idols forsake the source of their grace.
But I, with a song of praise, will offer you a sacrifice; the vow I have made, I will fulfill. Salvation belongs to the Lord!"
Then the Lord commanded the fish, and it spat Jonah out onto the dry land.
The word of the Lord came to Jonah a second time:
"Get up, go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim to it the message that I will tell you."
Jonah got up and set out for Nineveh, according to the word of the Lord. Now Nineveh was an immense city before God: it took three days to cross it.
Jonah went into the city a day's journey, and he proclaimed, "Forty days more, and Nineveh will be destroyed!"
The people of Nineveh believed in God; they proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest to the least.
The news reached the king of Nineveh: he rose from his throne, took off his robe, put on sackcloth, and sat down in ashes.
Then a proclamation was made in Nineveh, by decree of the king and his nobles: "Let neither human beings nor animals, neither herd nor flock, taste anything; let them not eat or drink water;
let humans and animals put on sackcloth, let them cry out to God with all their strength, and let each one turn from his evil ways and from the violence of his hands!
Who knows? Perhaps God will relent, will turn back from his burning anger, and we will not perish."
God saw what they were doing, how they turned from their evil ways; then he relented of the disaster he had threatened to bring upon them, and he did not do it.
This displeased Jonah greatly, and he became angry.

He prayed to the Lord, saying, "Ah, Lord, is this not what I said when I was still in my own country? This is why I first wanted to flee to Tarshish: I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger, rich in love, and ready to relent from disaster.
Now, Lord, take my life, please, for death is better for me than life."
The Lord answered, "Are you right to be angry?"
Jonah went out of the city and settled to the east; there he made himself a shelter and sat under it, in the shade, to see what would happen to the city.
Then the Lord God made a castor plant grow up, which rose above Jonah to give shade over his head and relieve his discomfort; and Jonah felt great joy because of the plant.
But the next day, at the break of dawn, God sent a worm that struck the plant, and the plant withered.
Then, at sunrise, God sent a scorching east wind; the sun beat down on Jonah's head, and he grew faint. He begged for death and said, "Death is better for me than life."
God said to Jonah, "Are you right to be angry because of this plant?" He answered, "Yes, I am right to be angry, angry enough to die!"
The Lord replied, "You feel pity for this plant, which cost you no labor and which you did not make grow, which came up in a night and perished in a night;

and should I not feel pity for Nineveh, the great city, where there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand human beings who cannot tell their right hand from their left, and a great many animals?"

titres.titre: Lament over the cities of Judah

versets.t: The word of the Lord that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah; the visions he received concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
Listen, all you peoples! Pay attention, earth, and all that fills you! The Lord God will testify against you, the Lord, from his holy temple.
See, the Lord is coming out of his dwelling; he comes down and treads upon the heights of the earth.
Beneath his steps the mountains melt and the valleys split open, like wax before the fire, like water rushing down a slope.
All this is because of the rebellion of Jacob, because of the sins of the house of Israel. What is the rebellion of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what is the high place of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?
I will make Samaria a heap of stones in a field, a place for planting vines; I will roll her stones down into the valley and lay her foundations bare.

All her images will be shattered, all her earnings given to the fire; of all her idols I will make a field of ruins. She gathered them from the wages of her prostitution, and they will become the wages of prostitution once more.
For this I lament and wail, I walk barefoot and stripped bare; I howl like the jackals, I mourn like the ostriches.
For the wound of Samaria is incurable, and it reaches all the way to Judah; it comes up to the gate of my people, up to Jerusalem.
Do not announce it in Gath, hold back your tears; in Beth-leaphrah, roll yourselves in the dust.
Pass on your way, inhabitant of Shaphir, in shameful nakedness! The inhabitant of Zaanan dares not come out; in Beth-ezel there is mourning, and it withdraws from you all support.
The inhabitant of Maroth trembles for her goods, for disaster has come down from the Lord to the gates of Jerusalem.
Harness the horses to the chariot, inhabitant of Lachish: you were the beginning of sin for the daughter of Zion, for the crimes of Israel were found in you.
Therefore you will have to give up Moresheth-gath; the houses of Achzib will deceive the kings of Israel.
I will bring a conqueror against you, inhabitant of Mareshah; the glory of Israel will have to take refuge as far as Adullam.
Shave your head, cut off your hair for the children who are your joy; make yourself bald as the vulture, for they are leaving you, going far away into exile.
Woe to those who on their beds plot evil and devise wicked schemes! At daybreak they carry them out, because they have the power to do so.
They covet fields and seize them, houses and take them; they oppress a man and his family, the owner and his inheritance.

Therefore, this is what the Lord says: Against this breed I am preparing a disaster from which you cannot free your necks; you will no longer walk with your heads held high, for it will be a time of disaster.

On that day people will make a mockery of you, they will strike up a bitter dirge: 'We are utterly ruined! He hands over to others the portion of my people. How dare he take it from me? He shares out our fields to those who betray us!'
That is why there will be no one in the assembly of the Lord to cast the lot for your portion of inheritance.
'Do not prophesy!' they say by way of prophecy. 'Let no one prophesy such things; disgrace will not overtake us.'
Is it to be said, house of Jacob, that the Lord has lost patience? Is this how he acts? Are his words not kind to the one who walks in uprightness?
But only yesterday my people rose up as an enemy: from those who passed by peacefully, with no thought of war, you tear off the cloak that covers their garment.
You drive the women of my people out of their beloved homes; from their young children you take away forever the honor I had given them.
Get up, be gone! This land is no longer a place of rest, for it has defiled itself, and that defilement brings on a relentless ruin.
If a man came chasing after the wind, spinning out lies, and declared, 'I will prophesy to you wine and beer!', he would be just the prophet for this people.
One day I will gather all of you, O Jacob, I will bring together the remnant of Israel; I will herd them like sheep in the fold, like a flock in the midst of its pasture, a place teeming with people.
The one who breaks open the way marches at their head; they force the passage, they pass through the gate and go out by it. Their king passes on before them, and the Lord is at their head.

titres.titre: Against the rulers who devour the people

versets.t: Then I said: Listen now, rulers of Jacob, leaders of the house of Israel! Is it not for you to know what is just?
Yet you hate good and love evil; you tear the skin from my people and the flesh from their bones.
You devour the flesh of my people, you strip off their skin and break their bones; you cut them up like meat put in the pot, like flesh at the bottom of the cauldron.
Then they will cry out to the Lord, but he will not answer them; he will hide his face from them at that time, because of the evil they have done.

This is what the Lord says concerning the prophets who lead my people astray: as long as they have something to bite, they proclaim peace; but against anyone who does not fill their mouths, they declare war.
'Therefore you will have night instead of visions, darkness instead of divination; the sun will set on these prophets, and the day will grow dark over them.
The seers will be covered with shame, the diviners will blush; all of them will cover their lips, for God will no longer answer.'
I, on the contrary, am filled with power, with the Spirit of the Lord, with justice and courage, to denounce to Jacob its rebellion and to Israel its sin.
Listen to this, then, rulers of the house of Jacob, leaders of the house of Israel, you who abhor justice and twist all that is straight,
you who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with crime!
Her rulers judge for bribes, her priests teach for a fee, her prophets divine for money; and they lean on the Lord, saying, 'Is the Lord not in our midst? No disaster can reach us.'
Well then, because of you, Zion will become a plowed field, Jerusalem a heap of ruins, and the temple hill a wooded height overrun with thickets.

titres.titre: The mountain of the Lord and the peace of the nations

versets.t: In the days to come, the mountain of the house of the Lord will be established at the summit of the mountains, it will tower above the hills; toward it the nations will stream.

Many peoples will set out and say, 'Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, to the house of the God of Jacob! He will teach us his ways, and we will follow his paths.' For out of Zion will go forth instruction, and from Jerusalem the word of the Lord.

He will be the arbiter of many nations, the judge of mighty peoples far and wide. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation will no longer lift up sword against nation, and they will learn war no more.
Everyone will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, with no one to trouble him; for the mouth of the Lord of hosts has spoken.
All the peoples walk, each in the name of its god; but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God, now and forever.
On that day, declares the Lord, I will gather the lame sheep, I will bring together those that were scattered, those I had struck down.
Of the lame I will make a remnant; of the exiles, a mighty nation. And the Lord will reign over them, on Mount Zion, from now and forever.
And you, tower of the flock, hill of the daughter of Zion, to you the former dominion will return, the kingship that belongs to the daughter of Jerusalem.
Why do you now cry out so loudly? Do you no longer have a king? Has your counselor perished, that anguish grips you like a woman in labor?

Writhe in pain, groan, daughter of Zion, like a woman giving birth! For you will leave the city and camp in the open fields, you will go as far as Babylon. There you will be delivered; there the Lord will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
Now many nations are gathered against you; they say, 'Let her be profaned, let our eyes feast on Zion!'
But they do not know the thoughts of the Lord, they do not understand his plan: he has gathered them like sheaves on the threshing floor.

Get up and thresh the grain, daughter of Zion! For I will make you a horn of iron and hooves of bronze, and you will crush many peoples. You will devote their gains to the Lord, their riches to the Master of all the earth.
Now muster your troops, daughter of warriors! A siege has been laid against us; with a rod they strike the judge of Israel on the cheek.

titres.titre: The remnant of Jacob among the nations

versets.t: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, too small to count among the clans of Judah, from you will come forth for me the one who is to rule Israel; his origins go back to ancient times, to the days of eternity.
Therefore God will give them up until the time when she who is to give birth has given birth; then the rest of his brothers will return to the sons of Israel.
He will stand and shepherd his flock by the strength of the Lord, in the majesty of the name of the Lord his God. They will dwell in security, for his greatness will reach to the ends of the earth.
And he himself will be peace. When the Assyrian invades our land and tramples our palaces, we will raise up against him seven shepherds, eight leaders of the people.
They will shepherd the land of Asshur with the sword, the land of Nimrod even at its gates. He will deliver us from the Assyrian when he invades our land and tramples our territory.
Then the remnant of Jacob will be, in the midst of many peoples, like dew that comes from the Lord, like showers of rain on the grass, which wait for nothing from man and place no hope in him.

The remnant of Jacob will also be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among the flocks: when it passes through, it tramples and tears, with no one to rescue.
Let your hand be lifted against your foes, and let all your enemies be cut off!
On that day, declares the Lord, I will remove your horses from your midst and destroy your chariots.
I will ruin the cities of your land and tear down all your fortresses.
I will wrench the sorceries out of your hand, and you will have no more diviners.
I will remove from your midst your idols and your standing stones, and you will no longer bow down before the work of your hands.
I will tear out from your midst your sacred poles and destroy your cities.
In my anger and fury I will take vengeance on the nations that have not listened.

titres.titre: The Lord's case against his people

versets.t: Listen now to what the Lord says: Stand up, plead your case before the mountains, let the hills hear your voice!
Listen, mountains, to the Lord's case; give ear, you enduring foundations of the earth! For the Lord has a case against his people, he is bringing a charge against Israel.
My people, what have I done to you? How have I burdened you? Answer me.
For I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, I redeemed you from the house of slavery; I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
My people, remember what Balak, king of Moab, was plotting, and what Balaam, son of Beor, answered him; remember the way from Shittim to Gilgal, that you may acknowledge the saving acts of the Lord.
'With what shall I come before the Lord, and bow down before the God on high? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
Will the Lord be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my rebellion, the fruit of my body for my own sin?'
He has shown you, O man, what is good, what the Lord requires of you: nothing other than to do justice, to love faithful love, and to walk humbly with your God.
The voice of the Lord cries out to the city, and wisdom is to fear his name: heed the rod of punishment and the one who has appointed it.
Are there still, in the house of the wicked, treasures ill-gotten and a rigged measure, an accursed thing?
Can I hold innocent the one who has false scales and a bag of dishonest weights?
The rich of the city are full of violence, its inhabitants speak lies, their tongues are nothing but deceit in their mouths.
I, in turn, will strike you hard, I will lay you waste because of your sins.
You will eat but not be satisfied, hunger will remain deep within you; you will store up but save nothing, and what you do save I will hand over to the sword.
You will sow but not reap, you will press the olive but not anoint yourself with oil, you will tread the grapes but drink no wine.

You keep the decrees of Omri and all the practices of the house of Ahab, you walk according to their counsels: therefore I will hand you over to ruin, your inhabitants to derision, and you will bear the disgrace of my people.

titres.titre: Prayer and a finale of mercy

versets.t: Woe is me! I am like the last days of the harvest, like the gleanings after the grape gathering: not a cluster left to eat, not one early fig that I long for.
The faithful have vanished from the land, not one upright person left among men. All of them lie in wait to shed blood, each one hunts his brother with a net.
Their hands are skilled at doing evil: the prince makes his demands, the judge takes his pay, the powerful man dictates his desires, and together they weave their scheme.
The best among them is like a briar, the most upright like a thorn hedge. The day announced by your watchmen, the day of your punishment, is coming: now is when they will be thrown into confusion.
Do not trust a friend, do not rely on a close companion; from her who sleeps on your breast, keep your mouth shut.
For the son despises his father, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; each has for enemies the people of his own household.
But as for me, I look to the Lord, I hope in the God of my salvation; my God will hear me.
Do not rejoice over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will rise again; though I sit in darkness, the Lord is my light.
I will bear the anger of the Lord, for I have sinned against him, until he takes up my cause and gives me justice; he will bring me out into the light, and I will behold his justice.
Then my enemy will see it and be covered with shame, she who said to me, 'Where is the Lord your God?' My eyes will gaze on her; she will be trampled like the mud of the streets.
The day is coming when your walls will be rebuilt; on that day your borders will be pushed far out.
On that day people will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, from Egypt to the River, from sea to sea and from mountain to mountain.
But the earth will become a desert because of those who dwell in it: such is the fruit of their deeds.
Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock of your inheritance, that dwells apart in the forest, in the midst of an orchard. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old!
As in the day when you came out of the land of Egypt, show us wonders.
The nations will see it and be confounded, for all their power; they will put their hands over their mouths, their ears will grow deaf.

They will lick the dust like the serpent, like the crawling things of the earth; they will come trembling out of their strongholds, they will come, seized with dread, to the Lord our God, and they will fear you.
