What God is like you, who takes away guilt and forgives the rebellion of the remnant of your inheritance? You do not keep your anger forever, for what pleases you is to show mercy.
Once again he will have compassion on us, he will tread our sins underfoot. You will cast into the depths of the sea all their sins.
You will show your faithfulness to Jacob, your faithful love to Abraham, as you swore to our fathers, from the days of old.

titres.titre: Judgment on Nineveh, deliverance for Judah

versets.t: An oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum of Elkosh.
The Lord is a jealous and avenging God; the Lord takes vengeance and is filled with wrath. The Lord takes vengeance on his foes and holds a grudge against his enemies.
The Lord is slow to anger and great in power, but he leaves nothing unpunished. The Lord makes his way in the storm and the whirlwind, and the clouds are the dust beneath his feet.
He rebukes the sea and dries it up; he makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the green of Lebanon fades.
Before him the mountains quake and the hills dissolve; the earth heaves before him, the world and all who live in it.
Who can stand before his fury? Who can withstand the heat of his anger? His wrath pours out like fire, and the rocks are shattered before him.
The Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; he knows those who take refuge in him.
But with an overflowing flood he will bring this place to an end, and he will pursue his enemies into the darkness.
What are you plotting against the Lord? He himself will bring it to an utter end; trouble will not rise up a second time.
Tangled together like thorns, drunk with their wine, they will be consumed like dry stubble.
From you came out the one who schemes evil against the Lord, the counselor of ruin.
Thus says the Lord: However intact and numerous they may be, they will be cut down and pass away. I have afflicted you, Judah, but I will afflict you no more.
Now I will break the yoke that weighs on you and snap your bonds.

Against you, Nineveh, this is the Lord's decree: Your name will have no descendants; from the temple of your gods I will cut off the carved and molten idols; I am preparing your grave, for you are worth nothing.

titres.titre: The end of the lions' den

versets.t: Behold, on the mountains the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace! Keep your feasts, Judah, fulfill your vows! For never again will the wicked one pass through you: he is utterly destroyed.
A destroyer advances against you, Nineveh. Guard the fortress, watch the road, brace yourself, gather all your strength!
For the Lord is restoring the glory of Jacob like the glory of Israel, for plunderers had stripped them and ruined their vines.
The shields of his warriors are dyed red, his soldiers are clothed in scarlet; the steel of the chariots flashes on the day he makes them ready, and the spears are brandished.
In the streets the chariots storm in a frenzy, they rush through the squares; they look like torches, like lightning darting to and fro.
The king summons his officers; they stumble as they march, they hurry to the wall, where the siege shelter is already being set up.
The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace collapses.
It is done: Nineveh is stripped bare and carried off; her handmaids moan like doves and beat their breasts.
Nineveh was like a pool of water, from time long past; and now they flee. Stop! Stop! But no one turns back.
Plunder the silver, plunder the gold! Her treasures are without end, she overflows with precious things.
Devastation, ravage, ruin! Hearts fail, knees give way, every waist trembles, every face turns pale.
Where is it now, the lions' den, that feeding ground of the young lions, where the lion prowled, the lioness and the cub, with nothing to disturb them?
The lion tore prey enough for his cubs, he strangled for his lionesses, he filled his lairs with prey and his dens with spoil.

Behold, I am against you, declares the Lord of hosts: I will turn your chariots to smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions; I will cut off your prey from the land, and the voice of your messengers will be heard no more.

titres.titre: Woe to the city of blood

versets.t: Woe to the city of blood, all deceit and violence, that never stops plundering!
The crack of the whip, the rumble of wheels, galloping horses, bounding chariots!
Charging horsemen, flashing swords, glittering spears! A multitude of wounded, heaps of dead, corpses beyond counting; people stumble over the bodies.
This is the price of the harlot's debaucheries, so beautiful and so skilled in sorcery, who enslaved nations by her debaucheries and peoples by her sorcery.
Behold, I am against you, declares the Lord of hosts: I will lift the skirts of your robe over your face, I will show your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms.
I will pelt you with filth, I will treat you with contempt, I will make a spectacle of you.
Then all who see you will flee from you, saying, 'Nineveh is destroyed!' Who will mourn for her? Where can I find anyone to comfort you?
Are you better than Thebes, seated by the Nile, surrounded by the waters, protected by the river as by a rampart and a wall?
Ethiopia and Egypt were her strength, without limit; Put and the Libyans were among her allies.
Yet she too went into exile, into captivity; her little children were dashed to pieces at every street corner, lots were cast for her nobles, and all her great men were bound in chains.
You too will be made drunk and will go under; you too will seek a refuge from the enemy.
All your fortresses are fig trees laden with ripe figs: shake them, and they fall into the mouth of the one who wants to eat them.
Behold, your people within you are nothing but women; before your enemies the gates of your land are thrown wide open, and fire devours your bars.
Draw water for the siege, strengthen your fortresses, tread the clay, knead the mortar, take up the brick mold!
There the fire will devour you, the sword will destroy you, it will devour you like the locust, even if you were as numerous as the locust, as numerous as the grasshopper.
You multiplied your merchants beyond the stars of heaven; but the locust spreads its wings and flies away.
Your guards are like locusts, your officers like swarms of grasshoppers settling on the walls on a cold day: when the sun appears, they fly off, and no one knows where they have gone.
Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria; your mighty men lie down. Your people are scattered on the mountains, with no one to gather them.
Your wound has no cure, your injury is fatal. All who hear the news of you will clap their hands over you; for who has not felt your relentless cruelty pass over them?
The oracle that the prophet Habakkuk received in a vision.
How long, Lord, must I cry for help before you listen? How long must I call out to you against violence before you save?
Why do you make me look on injustice? Why do you stand by and watch such misery? All I see before me is ruin and violence; strife breaks out, and quarrels flare up.
So the law grows numb, and justice never sees the light of day; the wicked hem in the righteous, and what comes out of the courts is justice twisted.
Look among the nations, watch, and be utterly astounded! For in your own days I am going to do something you would never believe if you were told.
See, I am rousing the Chaldeans, that fierce and headlong people who sweep across the wide expanses of the earth to seize dwellings that are not their own.
They are terrible and dreaded; their own will is the source of their justice and their greatness.
Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves at dusk; their horsemen charge, they come from far away, they fly like an eagle swooping on its prey.
All of them come bent on violence; their faces set forward, greedy, they gather up captives like sand.
They scoff at kings, and princes are their plaything; they laugh at every fortress: they heap up a little earth and take it.
Then they sweep on like a storm and press ahead, laden with guilt, they whose own strength is their only god.
Are you not from all eternity, Lord, my God, my Holy One? We shall not die. Lord, you have appointed them for judgment; my Rock, you have set them firm to punish.
Your eyes are too pure to look on evil; you cannot gaze upon misery. Why then do you look on the treacherous and keep silent while the wicked devours one more righteous than himself?
You have made mankind like the fish of the sea, like the swarming creatures that have no ruler.
This people hauls them all up with a hook, drags them off in their net, gathers them in their dragnet; and so they rejoice and exult.
That is why they offer sacrifice to their net and burn incense to their dragnet: thanks to these, their portion is rich and their food is choice.
Are they then to keep emptying their net forever, slaughtering the nations without pity?

titres.titre: The righteous shall live by his faith

versets.t: I will stand at my watch post, upright on the watchtower; I will keep watch to see what he will say to me, and what answer I am to give to my complaint.
The Lord answered me: Write down the vision, inscribe it clearly on tablets, so that it can be read at a glance.
For it is a vision for an appointed time; it presses on to its fulfillment and will not disappoint. If it seems to delay, wait for it: it will surely come, it will not fail.
The one whose heart swells with pride is not on the right path; but the righteous shall live by his faith.

What is more, wealth is treacherous; the arrogant man will not endure, he who opens his throat wide as the realm of the dead and remains, like death, insatiable; he gathered all the nations to himself, he swept up all the peoples.

But will they not all, one day, take up against him the taunt, the satire, and the riddle? People will say: Woe to the one who piles up what is not his, how long will it go on? Woe to the one who loads himself with a weight of pledges!
Will your creditors not suddenly rise up, your tormentors wake? You will become their prey.

Because you have plundered many nations, all the peoples who remain will plunder you, because of the human blood you have shed and the violence done to the land, to the city, and to all who live in it.
Woe to the one who builds his house on dishonest gain, to set his nest on high and escape the hand of disaster!
You have decreed shame for your own house: by cutting down many peoples, you have sinned against yourself.
For the stone will cry out from the wall, and the beam will answer it from the woodwork.
Woe to the one who builds a town with bloodshed and founds a city on injustice!
Is it not the will of the Lord of hosts that peoples toil only for the fire and nations wear themselves out for nothing?
For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as the waters cover the depths of the sea.
Woe to the one who makes his neighbor drink, to you who pour out your venom until he is drunk, so as to gaze on his nakedness!
You have had your fill of shame, not of glory. Now drink in your turn, and show your own disgrace! The cup in the Lord's right hand will come around to you, and shame will cover your glory.

The violence done to Lebanon will fall back on you, and the slaughter of the beasts will terrify you, because of the human blood you have shed and the violence done to the land, to the city, and to all who live in it.
What use is an idol, carved by its craftsman, a cast image, that teacher of lies, that its maker should trust his own handiwork while fashioning gods that cannot speak?
Woe to the one who says to the wood, 'Wake up!', to the silent stone, 'Arise!' Can it give guidance? See, it is plated with gold and silver, but there is no breath of life within it.
The Lord, though, is in his holy temple: let all the earth be silent before him!
A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, in the manner of a lament.
Lord, I have heard the report of you, and I was seized with fear. Lord, revive your work through the years; make it known through the years; in your wrath, remember to have mercy.
God comes from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His majesty covers the heavens, and the earth is filled with his praise.
It is a brightness like the light itself; rays flash from his hand, where his power lies hidden.
Before him goes the plague, and burning fever follows in his steps.
He halts, and the earth trembles; he looks, and the nations are shaken; the age-old mountains shatter, the ancient hills sink down: his are the everlasting ways.
I saw the tents of Cushan in distress, and the dwellings of the land of Midian shuddering.

Is it against the rivers, Lord, that you are angry? Is it against the rivers that your wrath is aimed, against the sea that your fury breaks loose, when you mount your horses, your chariots of victory?
You lay your bow bare, you fill its string with arrows to the full. Selah. You split the earth open into torrents.
The mountains see you and tremble, a cloudburst sweeps down; the deep raises its voice and lifts up its hands on high.
The sun and the moon stay in their dwelling, at the light of your speeding arrows, at the lightning flash of your spear.
In fury you stride across the earth; in anger you trample the nations.
You have gone out to save your people, to save your anointed; you have struck down the roof of the wicked man's house, laid its foundations bare to the rock. Selah.
With his own weapons you have pierced the head of his chiefs, when they charged to scatter me, gloating as if they were about to devour the poor in secret.
You trample the sea beneath your horses, in the churning of the mighty waters.

I heard, and my inmost being trembled; at that sound my lips quiver, decay creeps into my bones, and my steps falter beneath me. Yet I will wait in peace for the day of distress, which will rise against the people that assails us.

For the fig tree will no longer blossom, the vine will yield nothing; the fruit of the olive tree will fail, the fields will produce no food; the sheep will vanish from the fold, and there will be no more oxen in the stalls.
But as for me, I will exult in the Lord, I will rejoice in the God of my salvation.
The Lord my God is my strength: he makes my feet like the feet of deer and lets me walk on the heights. To the choirmaster, on my stringed instruments.

titres.titre: The Day of the Lord against Judah
The Great Day of the Lord

versets.t: The word of the Lord that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
I will sweep everything away from the face of the earth, declares the Lord.

I will sweep away man and beast, I will sweep away the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea; I will bring down the wicked along with their idols, and I will cut off mankind from the face of the earth, declares the Lord.
I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against all who live in Jerusalem; I will cut off from this place what remains of Baal, and the very name of the idolatrous priests,
those who bow down on the rooftops before the host of the sky, those who bow down and swear by the Lord and by Milcom at once,
and those who turn away from the Lord, who do not seek him and do not care about him.
Silence before the Lord God! For the day of the Lord is near: the Lord has prepared a sacrifice, he has consecrated his guests.
On the day of the Lord's sacrifice, I will punish the princes and the king's sons, and all who dress in foreign fashion.
On that day I will punish all who leap over the threshold, who fill their master's house with violence and deceit.
On that day, declares the Lord, a cry will go up from the Fish Gate, a wail from the new quarter, a great crash from the hills.
Wail, you who live in the Mortar, for all the merchant people are destroyed, all who weigh out silver are cut off.
At that time I will search Jerusalem with a lamp, and I will punish the men grown thick on their dregs, who say in their hearts, "The Lord does neither good nor harm."
Their wealth will be plundered, their houses laid in ruins; they will build houses but not live in them, they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.
It is near, the great day of the Lord; it is near, and it comes at great speed. Listen: the day of the Lord is bitter, and even the warrior cries out.
That day is a day of wrath, a day of anguish and distress, a day of devastation and ruin, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness,
a day of the trumpet and the battle cry against the fortified cities and the high corner towers.
I will bring the people into distress; they will grope like the blind, because they have sinned against the Lord. Their blood will be poured out like dust, and their bowels like dung.

Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to save them on the day of the Lord's wrath. In the fire of his jealousy the whole earth will be consumed; for he will bring about a total and sudden destruction of all who live on the earth.

titres.titre: The Call to Seek the Lord

versets.t: Gather yourselves together, come to your senses, you shameless nation,
before the decree takes effect and the day flies away like chaff, before the burning of the Lord's anger comes upon you, before the day of the Lord's anger comes upon you.
Seek the Lord, all you humble of the land, who carry out his commands; seek righteousness, seek humility: perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the Lord's anger.
For Gaza will be abandoned and Ashkelon left desolate; Ashdod will be driven out at high noon, and Ekron uprooted.

Woe to those who live along the coast, to the nation of the Cherethites! The word of the Lord is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines: "I will destroy you, and you will have no one left to live in you."
The coast will become pastureland, with shelters for shepherds and pens for sheep.

This territory will fall to the remnant of the house of Judah: there they will graze their flocks, and at evening they will lie down in the houses of Ashkelon; for the Lord their God will visit them and restore their fortunes.
I have heard the insults of Moab and the taunts of the sons of Ammon, who insulted my people and enlarged themselves at their expense.

Therefore, as I live, declares the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Moab will become like Sodom, and the sons of Ammon like Gomorrah, a place of nettles, a pit of salt, a wasteland forever. The remnant of my people will plunder them, the survivors of my nation will inherit them.
This is what their pride will earn them, because they insulted and defied the people of the Lord of hosts.
The Lord will be terrible against them: he will starve all the gods of the earth, and before him all the coastlands of the nations will bow down, each from its own place.
You too, people of Cush, will be run through by my sword.
He will stretch out his hand toward the north and destroy Assyria; he will make Nineveh a desolation, dry as the desert.

In her midst the flocks will lie down, beasts of every kind; the pelican and the hedgehog will spend the night on her capitals; a cry will ring out at the window, ruin will be on the threshold, for the cedar panelling will have been torn away.

There she is, the exultant city, dwelling in her security, who said in her heart, "I am, and there is none but me!" How has she become a wasteland, a lair for beasts? All who pass by her will hiss and shake their fist.

titres.titre: The Conversion of the Peoples and the Humble Remnant
The Song of Joy of Zion

versets.t: Woe to the rebellious city, the defiled, the tyrannical one!
She has listened to no call, she has accepted no correction; she has not trusted in the Lord, she has not drawn near to her God.
Her princes within her are roaring lions; her judges are wolves of the evening that leave nothing for the morning.
Her prophets are braggarts, traitors; her priests profane what is holy, they do violence to the law.
The Lord, however, is just within her, he does no wrong; morning after morning he renders his judgment, at the light of day, never failing; but the unjust know no shame.
I have wiped out nations, their corner towers are destroyed; I have laid waste their streets, and no one passes through; their cities are ravaged, without a soul, without an inhabitant.

I said to myself, "Surely you will fear me, you will accept correction"; then her dwelling would not have been destroyed, despite all that I had in store for her. But they were only the more eager to corrupt all their deeds.

So wait for me, declares the Lord, for the day when I rise up as a witness; for I have determined to gather the nations, to assemble the kingdoms, to pour out on them my fury, all the heat of my anger. Yes, in the fire of my jealousy the whole earth will be consumed.
Then I will give the peoples pure lips, so that they may all call on the name of the Lord and serve him with one accord.
From beyond the rivers of Cush my scattered faithful will bring me my offering.

On that day you will no longer be ashamed of all the deeds by which you rebelled against me; for I will remove from your midst those who exult in their arrogance, and you will no longer strut on my holy mountain.
I will leave within you a people humble and poor, who will take refuge in the name of the Lord.
The remnant of Israel will do no more wrong, will speak no more lies; in their mouth no deceitful tongue will be found. They will graze and lie down, with no one to disturb them.
Shout for joy, daughter of Zion! Raise the cry, Israel! Rejoice and exult with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem!
The Lord has lifted the sentence that weighed on you, he has turned back your enemy. The King of Israel, the Lord, is in your midst: you need no longer fear misfortune.
On that day it will be said to Jerusalem: "Do not fear, Zion, do not let your hands grow weak!"
The Lord your God is in your midst, a mighty saviour! He will rejoice over you with gladness, he will hold himself in silence in his love, he will dance for you with shouts of joy.
I will gather those who grieve far from the festivals, those who were your own: on them lay reproach.

Behold, at that time I will deal with all your oppressors; I will rescue the lame sheep, I will gather the one that was driven away, and I will give them praise and renown in all the lands where they knew shame.

At that time I will bring you back; at the time when I gather you, I will give you renown and praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your very eyes, says the Lord.

titres.titre: The call to rebuild the temple

versets.t: In the second year of King Darius, on the first day of the sixth month (around August-September), the word of the Lord came through the prophet Haggai to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jozadak, the high priest:
Thus says the Lord of hosts: This people claims that the time has not yet come to rebuild the house of the Lord.
Then the word of the Lord came through the prophet Haggai:
Is it a time for you to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?
Now, thus says the Lord of hosts: Consider carefully how you are living.

You have sown much and harvested little; you eat but are never satisfied, you drink but never quench your thirst, you clothe yourselves but no one is warm, and the laborer puts his wages into a purse full of holes.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: Consider carefully how you are living.
Go up into the hills, bring back timber, and rebuild the house; then I will take pleasure in it and reveal my glory there, says the Lord.

You expected abundance, and behold, it all came to little; what you did bring in, I scattered with a breath. Why? declares the Lord of hosts. Because my house lies in ruins, while each of you hurries off to his own.
That is why the heavens have withheld the dew from you, and the earth its crops.
I called down a drought on the fields and the hills, on the grain, the new wine, and the oil, on all that the ground brings forth, on man and beast, and on all the labor of your hands.

Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jozadak the high priest, and all the rest of the people obeyed the voice of the Lord their God and the words of the prophet Haggai, whom the Lord their God had sent; and the people were filled with awe before the Lord.
And Haggai, the messenger of the Lord, delivered this message from the Lord to the people: "I am with you, declares the Lord."

So the Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, the spirit of Joshua son of Jozadak the high priest, and the spirit of all the rest of the people; they came and set to work on the house of the Lord of hosts, their God,
on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month (around August-September), in the second year of King Darius.

titres.titre: The glory of the new temple

versets.t: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month (around September-October), the word of the Lord came through the prophet Haggai:
Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, to Joshua son of Jozadak the high priest, and to the rest of the people. Say to them:
Is there anyone still among you who saw this house in its former glory? And how do you see it now? Does it not seem to you like nothing at all?

But take courage, Zerubbabel, declares the Lord! Take courage, Joshua son of Jozadak, high priest! Take courage, all you people of the land, declares the Lord, and get to work! For I am with you, declares the Lord of hosts.
This is the promise I made with you when you came out of Egypt; and my Spirit remains in your midst: do not be afraid!
For thus says the Lord of hosts: In a little while longer, I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
I will shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will flow in; then I will fill this house with glory, says the Lord of hosts.
The silver is mine, the gold is mine, declares the Lord of hosts.
The glory of this present house, the latter one, will be greater than that of the former, says the Lord of hosts; and in this place I will grant peace, declares the Lord of hosts.
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month (around November-December), in the second year of Darius, the word of the Lord came through the prophet Haggai:
Thus says the Lord of hosts: Ask the priests for this ruling:
If a man carries consecrated meat in the fold of his garment, and with that fold he touches bread, a cooked dish, wine, oil, or any other food, will it become consecrated? The priests answered: No.
Haggai went on: If a man defiled by contact with a corpse touches any of these things, will it become unclean? The priests answered: It will become unclean.
Then Haggai declared: So it is with this people, so it is with this nation before me, declares the Lord; so it is with all the works of their hands: what they offer there is unclean.
And now, consider carefully what things were like, before one stone was laid upon another in the temple of the Lord.
In those days, when one came to a heap expected to yield twenty measures, there were only ten; when one came to draw fifty measures from the winepress vat, there were only twenty.
I struck you with blight, mildew, and hail, I struck all the labor of your hands; yet you did not return to me, declares the Lord.
Consider carefully what will come to pass, from this day onward. From this twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the foundation of the temple of the Lord was laid, consider carefully:
was there still any seed left in the barn? The vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, the olive tree had yielded nothing. But from this day on, I will bless.
The word of the Lord came a second time to Haggai, on the twenty-fourth day of the month:
Speak thus to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah: I will shake the heavens and the earth,

I will overturn the thrones of kingdoms, I will shatter the power of the pagan kingdoms, I will overturn the chariots and their riders; the horses and their horsemen will fall, each by the sword of his brother.

On that day, declares the Lord of hosts, I will take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, my servant, declares the Lord, and I will make you like a signet ring; for it is you whom I have chosen, declares the Lord of hosts.
In the eighth month of the second year of Darius (around October or November), the word of the Lord came to the prophet Zechariah, son of Berechiah, grandson of Iddo:
The Lord blazed with anger against your fathers.
You will say to them: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Return to me, declares the Lord of hosts, and I will return to you, says the Lord of hosts.

Do not be like your fathers, to whom the earlier prophets cried out: "Thus says the Lord of hosts: Turn back from your evil ways and your evil deeds!" But they did not listen; they paid no attention to me, declares the Lord.
Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, could they live forever?

But my words and my decrees, with which I had charged my servants the prophets, did they not overtake your fathers? Then they turned back and admitted: "The Lord of hosts has dealt with us according to our ways and our deeds, just as he had resolved to do."

On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius (around January or February), the word of the Lord came to the prophet Zechariah, son of Berechiah, grandson of Iddo:
I had a vision during the night. There before me: a man was riding a red horse; he stood among the myrtle trees deep in a ravine, and behind him were red, chestnut, and white horses.
I asked: "What are these, my lord?" And the angel who was speaking with me said: "I will show you what they are."
Then the man standing among the myrtle trees spoke up: "These are the ones the Lord has sent to range through the earth."
And they addressed the angel of the Lord who stood among the myrtle trees: "We have ranged through the earth, and there before us: the whole earth is at rest and quiet."
The angel of the Lord replied: "Lord of hosts, how long will you withhold your mercy from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, against which you have been angry these seventy years?"
And the Lord answered the angel who was speaking with me with kind words, words of comfort.
Then the angel who was speaking with me said to me: Proclaim this. Thus says the Lord of hosts: I feel a burning jealousy for Jerusalem and for Zion,
and great anger against the nations at their ease; for my anger was measured, but they made the disaster worse.
Therefore, thus says the Lord: I return to Jerusalem with compassion; my house will be rebuilt there, declares the Lord of hosts, and the measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.
Proclaim this as well. Thus says the Lord of hosts: My cities will again overflow with prosperity; the Lord will again comfort Zion, and again he will choose Jerusalem.

titres.titre: The man with the measuring line

versets.t: I looked up, and this is what I saw: four horns.
I asked the angel who was speaking with me: "What are these?" He answered: "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."
Then the Lord showed me four smiths.

I asked: "What are these coming to do?" He answered: "These are the horns that scattered Judah so thoroughly that no one dared raise his head; and these smiths have come to terrify them, to strike down the horns of the nations that had risen against the land of Judah to scatter it."
I looked up, and this is what I saw: a man with a measuring line in his hand.
I asked: "Where are you going?" He said to me: "To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide and how long it will be."
Now the angel who was speaking with me went forward, and another angel came to meet him.
He said to him: "Run, speak to that young man! Tell him: Jerusalem will remain open like open country, so many will be the people and livestock within it.
And I myself will be a wall of fire all around her, declares the Lord, and I will be her glory in her midst."
Away! Away! Flee from the land of the north, declares the Lord, for I have scattered you to the four winds of heaven, declares the Lord!
Away, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon!
For thus says the Lord of hosts, who for his glory has sent me to the nations that plundered you: whoever touches you touches the apple of his eye.
See, I am raising my hand against them: they will become the prey of those they enslaved. Then you will know that the Lord of hosts has sent me.
Shout for joy, rejoice, daughter of Zion! For here I come to dwell in your midst, declares the Lord.
On that day many nations will join themselves to the Lord; they will become my people, and I will dwell in your midst. Then you will know that the Lord of hosts has sent me to you.
The Lord will take Judah as his portion in the holy land, and again he will choose Jerusalem.
Let all flesh be silent before the Lord, for he is rising from his holy dwelling!
Then he showed me Joshua the high priest, standing before the angel of the Lord, and the Accuser standing at his right hand to accuse him.
The Lord said to the Accuser: "May the Lord rebuke you, Accuser! May the Lord rebuke you, he who has chosen Jerusalem! Is this man not a brand snatched from the fire?"
Now Joshua was clothed in filthy garments as he stood before the angel.
The angel spoke to those standing before him: "Take off his filthy garments." Then he said to Joshua: "See, I have taken your guilt away from you, and I clothe you in festal robes."
Then I said: "Let them put a clean turban on his head." So they set the clean turban on his head and clothed him, while the angel of the Lord stood by.
Then the angel of the Lord made this solemn declaration to Joshua:
Thus says the Lord of hosts: If you walk in my ways and faithfully keep my service, you will govern my house and watch over my courts, and I will give you free access among those who stand here.
Listen, then, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions seated before you, for you are men who are a sign: here, I am going to bring my servant, the Branch.

See the stone I have set before Joshua: on this single stone are seven eyes; I myself will engrave its inscription, declares the Lord of hosts, and I will remove the guilt of this land in a single day.
On that day, declares the Lord of hosts, each of you will invite his neighbor under the vine and under the fig tree.

titres.titre: The lampstand and the two olive trees

versets.t: The angel who was speaking with me came back and woke me, as one wakes a man from his sleep.
He asked me: "What do you see?" I answered: "I see a lampstand all of gold, with a bowl on top of it, with seven lamps and seven pipes for the lamps that crown it;
and two olive trees beside it, one to the right of the bowl and the other to its left."
I spoke again and said to the angel who was speaking with me: "What does all this mean, my lord?"
The angel who was speaking with me answered: "Do you not know what it means?" I said: "No, my lord."
Then he replied: This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel: Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit, says the Lord of hosts.
Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become a plain! And he will set the capstone in place amid shouts of: Grace, grace upon it!
The word of the Lord came to me:
The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will complete it, and you will know that the Lord of hosts has sent me to you.
For who has despised the day of small beginnings? People will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven lamps are the eyes of the Lord, ranging over all the earth.
I spoke again and said to him: "What are these two olive trees, to the right and to the left of the lampstand?"
Then I asked once more: "What are these two olive branches, beside the two golden pipes from which the golden oil flows?"
He said to me: "Do you not know what these are?" I answered: "No, my lord."
He said to me: "These are the two anointed ones, who stand beside the Lord of all the earth."
I looked up again and saw: a flying scroll.
The angel said to me: "What do you see?" I answered: "I see a flying scroll, about ten meters long and five wide."
He said to me: This is the curse going out over the whole land; for, according to this scroll, every thief will be swept away from here, and every perjurer will be swept away from here.

I have sent it forth, declares the Lord of hosts, and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of whoever swears falsely by my name; it will lodge within his house and consume it, timbers and stones alike.
The angel who was speaking with me came forward and said to me: "Look up and see what is coming forward."
I asked: "What is it?" He answered: "It is the measuring basket coming forward." And he added: "This is what they are like, throughout the land."
Then a lead cover was lifted, and there was a woman sitting inside the basket.
He said: "This woman is Wickedness." He thrust her back into the basket and pressed the lead disk down over its mouth.
I looked up and saw: two women were coming forward, the wind filling their wings, wings like a stork's; they lifted the basket up between earth and sky.
I said to the angel who was speaking with me: "Where are they carrying the basket?"
He answered me: "They are going to build her a house in the land of Shinar; there, when it is ready, she will be set down on her pedestal."
I looked up again and saw: four chariots coming out from between two mountains, and these mountains were of bronze.
The first chariot had red horses; the second, black horses;
the third, white horses; the fourth, dappled horses, all of them strong.
I spoke up and said to the angel who was speaking with me: "What are these, my lord?"
The angel answered me: "These are the four winds of heaven, going out after standing before the Lord of all the earth."
The chariot with the black horses set out toward the land of the north, the white ones went out after them, and the dappled ones set out toward the land of the south.
These strong steeds came forward, eager to range through the earth. The angel said to them: "Go, range through the earth!" And they ranged through the earth.
Then he called out to me and said: "See: those who went out toward the land of the north have set my Spirit at rest in the land of the north."
The word of the Lord came to me:
Receive the offerings from the exiles, from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah; go yourself, that day, to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, where they have arrived from Babylon.
You will take the silver and the gold, make a crown of it, and set it on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
You will say to him: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Here is a man whose name is Branch; where he is, he will branch out, and he will build the temple of the Lord.

Yes, it is he who will build the temple of the Lord; he will bear the royal insignia and sit enthroned as sovereign; he will be a priest upon his throne, and between the two there will reign a counsel of peace.
The crown will remain in the temple of the Lord, as a memorial to Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen son of Zephaniah.

Then those who are far off will come to work on the building of the temple of the Lord, and you will know that the Lord of hosts has sent me to you. This will come to pass if you faithfully obey the voice of the Lord your God.
In the fourth year of King Darius, on the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Kislev (around November or December), the word of the Lord came to Zechariah.
Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech, with his men, to seek the favor of the Lord
and to ask the priests of the house of the Lord of hosts and the prophets: "Should I weep and fast in the fifth month, as I have done for so many years?"
Then the word of the Lord of hosts came to me:
Say to all the people of the land and to the priests: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months these seventy years, was it really for me that you fasted?
And when you eat and drink, is it not for yourselves that you eat and drink?
Are these not the very words the Lord proclaimed through the prophets of old, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at peace, with her surrounding cities, and the Negev and the lowlands were populated?
The word of the Lord came to Zechariah:
Thus said the Lord of hosts: "Render true judgments, show kindness and compassion, each to his brother.
Do not oppress the widow and the orphan, the resident alien and the poor, and do not plot evil in your hearts against one another."
But they refused to listen; they turned a stubborn shoulder and stopped their ears so as not to hear.
They made their hearts hard as diamond, so as not to hear the law and the words the Lord of hosts sent them by his Spirit, through the prophets of old. Then great anger came from the Lord of hosts.
And so it happened: since he had called and they would not listen, so they will call and I will not listen, says the Lord of hosts.
I scattered them among all the nations they did not know, and behind them the land was left desolate, with no one to pass through or return. They turned a land of delight into a wasteland.
The word of the Lord of hosts came:
Thus says the Lord of hosts: I feel a jealous love for Zion, a great ardor for her.
Thus says the Lord: I return to Zion, I want to dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the Faithful City, and the mountain of the Lord of hosts, the Holy Mountain.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: Once again old men and old women will sit in the squares of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand for their great age.
The squares of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing there.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: If this seems impossible to the remnant of this people in those days, would it be impossible for me as well? declares the Lord of hosts.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: See, I am going to save my people from the land of the east and from the land of the west.
I will bring them back, and they will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; they will be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and justice.

Thus says the Lord of hosts: Take courage, you who hear today these words from the mouth of the prophets, on this day when the foundations of the house of the Lord of hosts are being laid, so that the Temple may be rebuilt.
For before those days there was no wage for man nor wage for beast; there was no safety from the enemy for anyone coming or going, and I set everyone against one another.
But now I am no longer to the remnant of this people what I was in the days of old, declares the Lord of hosts.
For there will be a sowing of peace: the vine will give its fruit, the ground its harvest, the sky its dew, and I will give the remnant of this people possession of all this.
As you were a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid; take courage!
For thus says the Lord of hosts: As I resolved to bring disaster on you when your fathers provoked my anger, says the Lord of hosts, and I did not relent,
so, in these days, I resolve instead to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid!
This is what you must do: let each of you speak the truth to his neighbor; at your gates render judgments of truth and peace;
do not plot evil in your hearts against one another, and do not love the false oath; for all this I hate, declares the Lord.
The word of the Lord of hosts came to me:

Thus says the Lord of hosts: The fast of the fourth month (around June or July), that of the fifth (around July or August), that of the seventh (around September or October), and that of the tenth (around December or January) will become for the house of Judah days of gladness, joy, and glad feasts. So love truth and peace!
Thus says the Lord of hosts: Peoples will come again, and the inhabitants of many cities.
The inhabitants of one will go to another, saying: "Let us go and seek the favor of the Lord and seek the Lord of hosts! I too am going."
Many peoples and mighty nations will come to seek the Lord of hosts in Jerusalem and to seek his favor.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: In those days ten men from all the languages of the nations will take hold of the robe of a Jew and say: "We want to go with you, for we have heard that God is with you."

titres.titre: The humble king mounted on a donkey

versets.t: An oracle. The word of the Lord against the land of Hadrach; it comes to rest on Damascus, for the Lord has his eye on humankind as on all the tribes of Israel,
on Hamath too, its neighbor, and on Tyre and Sidon, for all their skill.
Tyre has built herself a fortress, she has heaped up silver like dust and gold like the mud of the streets.
But see, the Lord is going to seize her: he will cast her power into the sea, and she herself will be devoured by fire.
Ashkelon will see it and be afraid, Gaza too will writhe in pain, and Ekron, for its hope will be dashed; there will be no more king in Gaza, and Ashkelon will lie deserted.
A mongrel people will settle in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
I will take the blood out of its mouth, its abominations from between its teeth; then it too will be left for our God, it will be like a clan of Judah, and Ekron will be like the Jebusites.
I will encamp around my house to defend it against the armies that march to and fro; no oppressor will ever pass through them again, for now I keep watch with my own eyes.
Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout for joy, daughter of Jerusalem! See, your king comes to you: he is righteous and victorious, humble, mounted on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.

I will cut off the chariots from Ephraim and the horses from Jerusalem, and the war bow will be broken. He will proclaim peace to the nations; his rule will extend from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth.
As for you, because of the blood of your covenant, I will set your captives free from the waterless pit.
Return to the stronghold, captives full of hope! This very day I declare it: I will restore double to you.
For I bend Judah as my bow, I fit Ephraim to it; I will rouse your sons, O Zion, against your sons, O Greece, and I will make you like the sword of a warrior.
Then the Lord will appear above them, his arrow will flash out like lightning; the Lord God will sound the trumpet and advance in the storms of the south.

The Lord of hosts will protect them; they will devour and trample the slingstones, they will drink and roar as if with wine, they will be full like the sacrificial bowl, like the corners of the altar.
On that day the Lord their God will save them, like the flock that is his people; they will be like the stones of a diadem, sparkling over his land.
What happiness, what beauty! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine the young women.

titres.titre: The rain and the false shepherds

versets.t: Ask the Lord for rain in the season of the spring rains. It is the Lord who makes the lightning; he will give you abundant showers, and to each the grass of his field.

For the household idols speak nothing but wind, the diviners have only false visions; they tell deceitful dreams and give empty comfort. That is why people wander like a flock, wretched, for want of a shepherd.
My anger blazes against the shepherds, and I will punish the he-goats. For the Lord of hosts is visiting his flock, the house of Judah, and he makes of it his proud warhorse.
From him will come the cornerstone, from him the tent peg, from him the war bow, from him will come forth all the rulers, all together.
They will be like warriors trampling the mud of the streets in battle; they will fight, for the Lord will be with them, and they will put the horsemen to shame.

I will strengthen the house of Judah, I will save the house of Joseph; I will bring them back, for I have compassion on them, and they will be as though I had never rejected them; for I am the Lord their God, and I will answer them.
Ephraim will be like a warrior, their heart glad as with wine; their children will see it and rejoice, their hearts will exult in the Lord.
I will whistle to gather them, for I have redeemed them, and they will be as numerous as they once were.
I scattered them among the peoples, but in the distant lands they will remember me; they will survive with their children, and they will return.
I will bring them back from the land of Egypt, I will gather them from Assyria, I will lead them to the land of Gilead and to Lebanon, and there will not be room enough for them.

They will pass through a sea of distress; he will strike the waves of the sea, and all the depths of the Nile will be dried up. The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will pass away.
I will make them strong in the Lord, and they will walk in his name, declares the Lord.

titres.titre: The two staffs and the thirty pieces

versets.t: Open your gates, Lebanon, and let the fire devour your cedars!
Wail, cypress, for the cedar has fallen, the magnificent trees are ruined! Wail, oaks of Bashan, for the impenetrable forest is felled!
Listen to the wailing of the shepherds, for their splendor is ruined; listen to the roaring of the young lions, for the pride of the Jordan is laid waste.
Thus says the Lord my God: Shepherd this flock destined for slaughter,
whose buyers slaughter it and go unpunished, and whose sellers say: "Blessed be the Lord, I have grown rich!", while their own shepherds have no pity for it.

For I will no longer have pity on the inhabitants of the land, declares the Lord; see, I am handing everyone over into the hands of one another and into the hands of their king: they will devastate the land, and I will rescue no one from their hand.
So I became the shepherd of the flock destined for slaughter, yes, of the most wretched of the flock. I took two staffs: one I called Favor, and the other Union, and I shepherded the flock.
In a single month I removed the three shepherds. But I lost patience with the sheep, and they too grew disgusted with me.
Then I said: I will no longer shepherd you! Let the one that is to die, die; let the one that is to perish, perish; and let those that remain devour one another!
I took my staff Favor and broke it, to annul the covenant I had made with all the peoples.
It was annulled that day, and the most wretched of the flock, who were watching me, knew that this was a word of the Lord.
I said to them: If it seems good to you, give me my wages; if not, keep them. So they weighed out my wages: thirty pieces of silver.
The Lord said to me: Throw it to the potter, this fine price at which they valued me! So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the house of the Lord, to the potter.
Then I broke my second staff, Union, to break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
The Lord said to me: Take once more the gear of a foolish shepherd.

For see, I am going to raise up in the land a shepherd who will not care for the lost sheep, will not seek the straying one, will not heal the injured, will not feed the healthy; but he will devour the flesh of the fattest and tear off even their hooves.
Woe to the worthless shepherd who deserts the flock! May the sword fall on his arm and on his right eye! May his arm wither and his right eye go blind!

titres.titre: The look toward the pierced one

versets.t: An oracle. The word of the Lord concerning Israel. The word of the Lord who spread out the heavens, founded the earth, and formed the spirit of man within him:
See, I am going to make Jerusalem a cup that brings dizziness to all the surrounding peoples; and Judah itself will be caught up in the siege of Jerusalem.
On that day I will make Jerusalem a stone to be lifted by all the peoples: whoever lifts it will be torn to pieces, and all the nations of the earth will band together against her.

On that day, declares the Lord, I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness; over the house of Judah I will keep my eyes open, but I will strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.
Then the rulers of Judah will say in their hearts: "The inhabitants of Jerusalem are my strength, through the Lord of hosts, their God."

On that day I will make the rulers of Judah like a brazier in a woodpile, like a flaming torch in a sheaf: they will devour to the right and to the left all the surrounding peoples, while Jerusalem remains in her place.
The Lord will save the tents of Judah first, so that the pride of the house of David and of the inhabitants of Jerusalem may not rise above Judah.
On that day the Lord will protect the inhabitants of Jerusalem: the weakest among them will be like David, and the house of David will be like God, like the angel of the Lord before them.
On that day I will set myself to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

And I will pour out on the house of David and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplication. They will look toward me, the one they have pierced; they will mourn for him as one mourns for an only son, and weep bitterly over him as one weeps over a firstborn.
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be great, like the mourning of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
The land will mourn, each family apart: the family of the house of David apart, and their women apart; the family of the house of Nathan apart, and their women apart;
the family of the house of Levi apart, and their women apart; the family of Shimei apart, and their women apart;
and all the remaining families, each family apart, and their women apart.
On that day a fountain will spring up for the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to wash away sin and defilement.

On that day, declares the Lord of hosts, I will wipe out from the land the names of the idols: they will be remembered no more. And I will drive out of the land the prophets and the spirit of impurity.

If anyone still wants to prophesy, his father and mother, the very ones who gave him birth, will say to him: "You will not live, for you speak lies in the name of the Lord." And his father and mother, the ones who gave him birth, will pierce him through while he prophesies.
On that day every prophet will be ashamed of his vision when he tries to prophesy; they will no longer put on the hairy cloak to deceive.
Each will say: "I am no prophet, I am a man who works the soil; the land has been my livelihood since my youth."
And if someone asks him: "What are these wounds on your body?", he will answer: "I received them in the house of my friends."

Sword, awake against my shepherd, against the man who is close to me, declares the Lord of hosts! Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered; then I will turn my hand against the little ones.
Then, throughout the land, declares the Lord, two-thirds will be cut off and perish, and one-third will be left in it.

This third I will pass through the fire; I will refine them as one refines silver, I will test them as one tests gold. They will call on my name, and I will answer them. I will say: "They are my people", and they will say: "The Lord is my God."

titres.titre: The Lord, king of all the earth

versets.t: See, a day is coming for the Lord, when the spoil taken from you will be divided in your midst.

I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for battle: the city will be taken, the houses plundered, the women raped; half the city will go into exile, but the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.
Then the Lord will go out and fight against those nations, as on the day when he fights, a day of battle.

On that day his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, facing Jerusalem to the east; and the Mount of Olives will split down the middle, from east to west, into an immense valley; half the mountain will draw back to the north, the other half to the south.

You will flee through this valley of my mountains, for it will reach as far as Azal; you will flee as you fled before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah. Then the Lord my God will come, and all the holy ones with him.
On that day there will be no more light, but cold and frost.
It will be a unique day, known to the Lord alone, with neither day nor night; and when evening comes, there will be light.
On that day living waters will flow out from Jerusalem, half toward the eastern sea, the other half toward the western sea; it will be so in summer as in winter.
The Lord will be king over all the earth; on that day the Lord will be one, and his name one.

The whole land will become a plain, from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem. And Jerusalem will be lifted high and remain in her place, from the Gate of Benjamin to the site of the former gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.
People will dwell there, there will be no more curse of destruction, and Jerusalem will rest in security.

This is the plague with which the Lord will strike all the peoples who have fought against Jerusalem: their flesh will rot while they stand on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, their tongue will rot in their mouth.
On that day a great panic from the Lord will seize them: each will grab the hand of his neighbor, and they will raise their hands against one another.
Judah itself will fight for Jerusalem. The wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered, gold, silver, and clothing in enormous quantity.
A similar plague will strike the horses, the mules, the camels, the donkeys, and all the animals in those camps.
And all the survivors of the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship before the King, the Lord of hosts, and to celebrate the feast of Booths.
If any of the families of the earth does not go up to Jerusalem to worship before the King, the Lord of hosts, there will be no rain for them.

And if the family of Egypt does not go up and does not come, they will have no rain either; they will be struck by the plague with which the Lord strikes the nations that do not go up to celebrate the feast of Booths.
Such will be the punishment of Egypt and of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the feast of Booths.
On that day there will be inscribed on the bells of the horses: "Consecrated to the Lord"; and the pots of the house of the Lord will be like the bowls before the altar.

Every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be consecrated to the Lord of hosts; all who offer sacrifices will come and take some of them to boil the meat in. And there will no longer be any trader in the house of the Lord of hosts, on that day.
An oracle. The word of the Lord addressed to Israel through Malachi.
I have loved you, says the Lord. And you say, "How have you loved us?" Was not Esau the brother of Jacob? oracle of the Lord. Yet I loved Jacob,
but I rejected Esau: I made his mountains a wasteland and gave his inheritance over to the jackals of the desert.

Edom may well say, "We are shattered, but we will rebuild our ruins." Thus says the Lord of hosts: They may rebuild, but I will tear down; and they shall be called the Territory of Wickedness, the people against whom the Lord is angry forever.
Your own eyes shall see it, and you shall say, "The Lord is great, beyond the territory of Israel!"

A son honors his father, and a servant his master. If then I am a father, where is the honor due to me? If I am your Lord, where is the fear I am owed? says the Lord of hosts to you, priests, who despise my name. And you say, "How have we despised your name?"
By offering defiled bread on my altar. And you say, "How have we defiled you?" By claiming that the table of the Lord is contemptible.

When you present a blind animal in sacrifice, is that not wrong? When you offer one that is lame or diseased, is that not wrong? Offer it to your governor: will he be pleased with you, will he receive you kindly? says the Lord of hosts.
And now, plead for the favor of God, that he may have mercy on us! From your own hands these offerings have come: will he receive you kindly? says the Lord of hosts.

If only one of you would shut the doors, so that you no longer kindle the fire on my altar in vain! I take no pleasure in you, says the Lord of hosts, and I will not accept the offerings from your hands.

For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering; yes, my name is great among the nations, says the Lord of hosts.
But you profane it by claiming that the table of the Lord is defiled and that what it yields is nothing but contemptible food.
You say, "What a burden!" and you sniff at it in disdain, says the Lord of hosts. You bring stolen animals, lame or diseased, and these you offer me: can I accept them from your hands? says the Lord.
Cursed be the cheat who has a male in his flock, yet vows and sacrifices to the Lord a blemished animal! For I am a great king, says the Lord of hosts, and my name is feared among the nations.
And now, priests, this decree is addressed to you.

If you will not listen, if you will not take it to heart to give glory to my name, says the Lord of hosts, I will send the curse against you, I will curse your blessings; indeed I have already cursed them, because none of you takes it to heart.
See, I am about to break your arm, I will fling refuse in your faces, the refuse of your festivals, and you will be carried off along with it.
Then you will know that I sent you this decree so that my covenant with Levi might endure, says the Lord of hosts.
My covenant with him was one of life and peace, and I granted them to him; it was a covenant of fear, and he feared me, he trembled before my name.
True teaching was in his mouth, and no injustice was found on his lips; he walked with me in peace and uprightness, and he turned many away from evil.
For the lips of the priest guard knowledge, and from his mouth people seek instruction, since he is the messenger of the Lord of hosts.
But you have turned aside from the way, you have made many stumble by your teaching, you have broken the covenant of Levi, says the Lord of hosts.
So in my turn I have made you despised and lowly before all the people, because you do not follow my ways and you show partiality in applying the law.
Do we not all have one father? Did not one same God create us all? Why then are we unfaithful to one another, profaning the covenant of our fathers?
Judah is unfaithful, and an abomination is committed in Israel and in Jerusalem: Judah profanes the sanctuary that the Lord loves, by marrying the daughter of a foreign god.
May the Lord cut off from the tents of Jacob the man who does this, whoever he may be, even though he presents an offering to the Lord of hosts!
And here is a second thing you do: you drench the altar of the Lord with tears, you weep and groan because he no longer looks upon your offerings nor receives them with favor from your hands.
And you say, "Why?" Because the Lord is a witness between you and the wife of your youth, to whom you have been unfaithful, though she was your companion, the wife of your covenant.

Did he not make a single being, having flesh and the breath of life? And this one being, what does he seek? Offspring given by God. So take heed to yourselves, and let none be unfaithful to the wife of his youth.
For I hate divorce, says the Lord, the God of Israel, and the man who covers his garment with violence, says the Lord of hosts. So take heed to yourselves and do not be unfaithful.

You weary the Lord with your words. And you say, "How do we weary him?" By claiming, "Everyone who does evil is good in the eyes of the Lord, and it is in such people that he delights"; or again, "Where is the God of justice?"

titres.titre: The day of the Lord and the return of Elijah

versets.t: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me; and suddenly the Lord whom you seek will come to his temple, the messenger of the covenant whom you desire. See, he is coming, says the Lord of hosts.
But who can endure the day of his coming? Who can stand firm when he appears? For he will be like the refiner's fire, like the launderers' lye.
He will sit to refine and to purify; he will purify the sons of Levi, he will refine them like gold and silver, and they will present offerings to the Lord in righteousness.
Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will please the Lord as in the days of old, as in years long past.

I will draw near to you for judgment, and I will be a swift witness against sorcerers, adulterers, and perjurers, against those who cheat the laborer of his wages, oppress the widow and the orphan, deny the resident alien his rights, and do not fear me, says the Lord of hosts.
For I, the Lord, do not change; and you, sons of Jacob, have not been destroyed.
Since the days of your fathers you have turned aside from my laws and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you, says the Lord of hosts. And you say, "How are we to return?"
Can a man cheat God? Yet you are cheating me. And you say, "How have we cheated you?" In the tithe and the dues.
You are struck with a curse, and yet you keep cheating me, the whole nation of you!

Bring the full tithe into the treasury, so that there may be food in my house; and put me to the test in this way, says the Lord of hosts: you will see whether I do not open the floodgates of heaven for you and pour out upon you blessing beyond all measure.
For your sake I will rebuke the devouring locust: it will no longer destroy the fruit of your soil, and the vine will no longer fail to bear in your fields, says the Lord of hosts.
All the nations will call you blessed, for you will be a land of delight, says the Lord of hosts.
Your words against me are harsh, says the Lord. And you say, "What have we said against you?"
You have said, "Serving God brings no reward; what have we gained by keeping his precepts and by walking in mourning garb before the Lord of hosts?
From now on we call the arrogant blessed: those who do evil prosper, they put God to the test and get away with it."
Then those who fear the Lord spoke with one another. The Lord paid attention and heard them, and before him a book of remembrance was written in favor of those who fear him and honor his name.
On the day I am preparing, says the Lord of hosts, they will be my own special treasure, and I will spare them as a father spares the son who serves him.
Then once more you will see the difference between the righteous and the wicked, between the one who serves God and the one who does not serve him.

For see, the day is coming, burning like a furnace: all the arrogant and all the evildoers will be like stubble, and the day that comes will set them ablaze, says the Lord of hosts, leaving them neither root nor branch.
But for you who fear my name the sun of righteousness will rise, with healing in its rays; and you will go out and leap like calves let loose from the stall.
You will trample the wicked, reduced to ashes under the soles of your feet, on the day I am preparing, says the Lord of hosts.
Remember the law of Moses, my servant, to whom I gave at Horeb, for all Israel, statutes and ordinances.
See, I will send you the prophet Elijah, before the great and terrible day of the Lord comes.
He will turn the hearts of the fathers back to their children and the hearts of the children back to their fathers, lest I come and strike the land with a curse of destruction.
The genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
Abraham was the father of Isaac; Isaac the father of Jacob; Jacob the father of Judah and his brothers;
Judah was the father of Perez and Zerah, whose mother was Tamar; Perez the father of Hezron; Hezron the father of Ram;
Ram was the father of Amminadab; Amminadab the father of Nahshon; Nahshon the father of Salmon;
Salmon was the father of Boaz, whose mother was Rahab; Boaz the father of Obed, whose mother was Ruth; Obed the father of Jesse;
Jesse was the father of David the king. David was the father of Solomon, whose mother had been the wife of Uriah;
Solomon was the father of Rehoboam; Rehoboam the father of Abijah; Abijah the father of Asa;
Asa was the father of Jehoshaphat; Jehoshaphat the father of Joram; Joram the father of Uzziah;
Uzziah was the father of Jotham; Jotham the father of Ahaz; Ahaz the father of Hezekiah;
Hezekiah was the father of Manasseh; Manasseh the father of Amon; Amon the father of Josiah;
Josiah was the father of Jeconiah and his brothers, at the time of the exile to Babylon.
After the exile to Babylon, Jeconiah was the father of Shealtiel; Shealtiel the father of Zerubbabel;
Zerubbabel was the father of Abiud; Abiud the father of Eliakim; Eliakim the father of Azor;
Azor was the father of Zadok; Zadok the father of Achim; Achim the father of Eliud;
Eliud was the father of Eleazar; Eleazar the father of Matthan; Matthan the father of Jacob;
Jacob was the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary; of her was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
So there are in all fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the exile to Babylon, and fourteen from the exile to Babylon to the Christ.
This is how Jesus Christ was born. Mary, his mother, was betrothed to Joseph; but before they had come to live together, she was found to be with child by the working of the Holy Spirit.
Joseph, her husband, who was a righteous man and did not want to expose her to shame, resolved to send her away quietly.

As he was pondering this, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, 'Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife into your home, for the child she is carrying comes from the Holy Spirit.
She will give birth to a son, and you shall give him the name Jesus, for it is he who will save his people from their sins.'
All this took place to fulfil the word the Lord had spoken through the prophet:
'Behold, the Virgin shall conceive and give birth to a son; they shall give him the name Emmanuel,' which means, 'God with us.'
When Joseph awoke, he did what the angel of the Lord had commanded him: he took his wife into his home,
but he had no relations with her until she gave birth to a son, to whom he gave the name Jesus.

titres.titre: The Massacre of the Children of Bethlehem
The Return and Settling in Nazareth

versets.t: Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, in the time of King Herod. Now, magi from the East arrived in Jerusalem
and asked, 'Where is the newborn king of the Jews? We have seen his star rise, and we have come to pay him homage.'
When he heard this, King Herod was deeply troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
He gathered all the chief priests and the scribes of the people, and asked them where the Christ was to be born.
They answered him, 'In Bethlehem in Judea, for this is what the prophet has written:
And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means the least among the great cities of Judah, for from you will come a ruler who will be the shepherd of Israel, my people.'
Then Herod summoned the magi secretly; he found out from them the exact time the star had appeared,
and sent them to Bethlehem, saying, 'Go and search carefully for the child. When you have found him, let me know, so that I too may go and pay him homage.'
On hearing the king, they set out. And behold, the star they had seen rise went ahead of them, until it stopped above the place where the child was.
When they saw the star, they were filled with very great joy.
On entering the house, they saw the child with Mary, his mother; they fell down and paid him homage. Then, opening their treasure chests, they offered him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Then, warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they went back to their own country by another route.

After they had left, behold, an angel of the Lord appears to Joseph in a dream and says, 'Get up, take the child and his mother, flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod is going to search for the child to put him to death.'
Joseph got up; that very night he took the child and his mother and withdrew to Egypt.
He stayed there until the death of Herod, to fulfil the word the Lord had spoken through the prophet: 'Out of Egypt I have called my son.'

When Herod saw that the magi had tricked him, he flew into a violent rage. He sent and killed, in Bethlehem and throughout the whole region, all the children under two years old, according to the time he had found out from the magi.
Then was fulfilled the word spoken through the prophet Jeremiah:
A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and long lamentation: it is Rachel weeping for her children and refusing all consolation, for they are no more.
After the death of Herod, behold, an angel of the Lord appears in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
and says, 'Get up, take the child and his mother, and go back to the land of Israel, for those who sought the child's life are dead.'
Joseph got up, took the child and his mother, and entered the land of Israel.
But hearing that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. Warned in a dream, he withdrew to the region of Galilee
and went to live in a town called Nazareth, to fulfil the word of the prophets: 'He shall be called a Nazarene.'

titres.titre: The Preaching of John the Baptist

versets.t: In those days John the Baptist appeared, proclaiming in the wilderness of Judea:
'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.'
It was of him that the prophet Isaiah spoke: 'A voice cries out in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.'
John wore a garment of camel hair and a leather belt around his waist; he fed on locusts and wild honey.
Then Jerusalem, all Judea, and the whole region of the Jordan came out to him,
and they were baptized by him in the Jordan, confessing their sins.
Seeing many Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, 'Brood of vipers, who showed you how to flee from the wrath that is coming?
Produce, then, fruit that shows your repentance,
and do not presume to say to yourselves, We have Abraham as our father. For I tell you: God can raise up children for Abraham from these very stones.
Already the axe is laid to the root of the trees: every tree that does not bear good fruit is going to be cut down and thrown into the fire.
I baptize you with water, for repentance; but the one who comes after me is mightier than I, and I am not worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
He holds the winnowing shovel: he will clear his threshing floor, gather his wheat into the barn, and burn the chaff with fire that never goes out.'
Then Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him.
John tried to prevent him: 'It is I who need to be baptized by you, and yet you come to me!'
But Jesus answered him, 'Let it be so for now, for it is fitting that we should thus fulfil all righteousness.' Then John lets him.
Once baptized, Jesus came up at once from the water; and behold, the heavens opened: he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon him.
And behold, a voice from the heavens said, 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.'

titres.titre: The Beginning of the Preaching in Galilee
The Call of the First Disciples

versets.t: Then Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness, to be tempted by the devil.
After fasting forty days and forty nights, he was hungry at last.
The tempter approached and said to him, 'If you are the Son of God, command these stones to become bread.'
But Jesus answered, 'It is written: Man does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.'
Then the devil takes him to the holy city, sets him on the highest point of the Temple,

and says to him, 'If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down, for it is written: He will command his angels concerning you, and they will bear you up in their hands, so that your foot does not strike a stone.'
Jesus said to him, 'It is also written: You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.'
The devil takes him yet again to a very high mountain; he shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,
and says to him, 'All this I will give you, if you fall down and worship me.'
Then Jesus says to him, 'Away with you, Satan! For it is written: You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve.'
Then the devil leaves him. And behold, angels approached, and they served him.
When Jesus heard that John had been arrested, he withdrew to Galilee.
He left Nazareth and went to live in Capernaum, by the sea, in the territory of Zebulun and Naphtali,
to fulfil the word of the prophet Isaiah:
'Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, on the road by the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations!
The people who lived in darkness have seen a great light; on those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned.'
From that moment, Jesus began to proclaim, 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.'
As he was walking along the Sea of Galilee, Jesus saw two brothers, Simon, called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting their net into the sea: they were fishermen.
He said to them, 'Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.'
At once they left their nets and followed him.
Farther on, he saw two other brothers, James, son of Zebedee, and John, his brother, in the boat with their father Zebedee, mending their nets. He called them.
At once they left the boat and their father and followed him.
Jesus went throughout all Galilee; he taught in their synagogues, proclaimed the Good News of the Kingdom, and healed every disease and every affliction among the people.
His fame spread throughout all Syria. People brought to him all who were suffering, afflicted with various ills and torments: the demon-possessed, epileptics, and paralytics; and he healed them.
Great crowds followed him, coming from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan.

titres.titre: Against Adultery and the Impure Gaze

versets.t: Seeing the crowds, Jesus went up the mountain. He sat down, and his disciples came to him.
Then he began to speak and to teach them:
'Blessed are the poor in heart, for the kingdom of heaven is theirs!
Blessed are those who weep, for they will be consoled!
Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth!
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be satisfied!
Blessed are the merciful, for they will obtain mercy!
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God!
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God!
Blessed are those who are persecuted for righteousness, for the kingdom of heaven is theirs!
Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and speak all kinds of evil against you falsely on account of me.
Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in the heavens: this is how the prophets before you were persecuted.
You are the salt of the earth. But if salt becomes tasteless, how will its flavour be restored? It is no longer good for anything: it is thrown outside, and people trample it underfoot.
You are the light of the world. A city set on a height cannot be hidden.
No one lights a lamp to put it under a bushel: it is placed on the lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house.
