In the same way, let your light shine before others: then, seeing the good you do, they will give glory to your Father who is in the heavens.
Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets: I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfil them.
For, amen, I say to you: before heaven and earth pass away, not the smallest letter, not the smallest stroke of the Law will pass away, until all is accomplished.

So whoever sets aside one of the least of these commandments and teaches others to do the same will be declared least in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever practises them and teaches them will be declared great in the kingdom of heaven.
For I tell you: unless your righteousness surpasses that of the scribes and the Pharisees, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
You have heard that it was said to the ancients: You shall not commit murder; whoever commits murder will answer for it before the court.

But I say to you: everyone who is angry with his brother will answer for it before the court. Whoever says to his brother, 'Imbecile!' will answer for it before the high council. Whoever says, 'Madman!' will be liable to the fire of Gehenna.
So when you are about to present your offering at the altar, if there you remember that your brother has something against you,
leave your offering there, before the altar, and go first to be reconciled with your brother; then come back and present your offering.
Come to terms quickly with your adversary while you are still on the way with him, lest he hand you over to the judge, the judge to the guard, and you be thrown into prison.
Amen, I say to you: you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny.
You have heard that it was said: You shall not commit adultery.
But I say to you: everyone who looks at a woman with lust has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
If your right eye leads you to sin, tear it out and throw it away from you: better for you to lose one of your members than to have your whole body thrown into Gehenna.
And if your right hand leads you to sin, cut it off and throw it away from you: better for you to lose one of your members than to have your whole body thrown into Gehenna.
It was also said: Whoever sends his wife away must give her a certificate of divorce.
But I say to you: everyone who sends his wife away, except in the case of an illegitimate union, exposes her to adultery; and whoever marries a woman who has been sent away commits adultery.
Again, you have heard that it was said to the ancients: You shall not break your oath, but you shall fulfil your oaths to the Lord.
But I say to you not to swear any oath at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God,
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet, nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
And do not swear by your head either, for you cannot make a single one of your hairs white or black.
When you say yes, let it be yes; when you say no, let it be no. Anything more than this comes from the Evil One.
You have heard that it was said: Eye for eye, tooth for tooth.
But I say to you not to resist the wicked. On the contrary, if someone strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other to him as well.
To the one who wants to take you to court to take your tunic, leave your cloak as well.
If someone forces you to go one kilometre, go two with him.
Give to the one who asks you; do not turn your back on the one who wants to borrow from you.
You have heard that it was said: You shall love your neighbour and hate your enemy.
But I say to you: love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat and persecute you.
Thus you will be sons of your Father who is in the heavens, for he makes his sun rise on the wicked and the good, and sends rain on the righteous and the unrighteous.
If you love those who love you, what reward do you deserve? Do not the tax collectors themselves do as much?
And if you greet only your brothers, what are you doing that is extraordinary? Do not the pagans themselves do as much?
You, therefore, be perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect.'

titres.titre: The Eye, Lamp of the Body

versets.t: 'Be careful not to practise your righteousness before others in order to be noticed by them; otherwise there is no reward for you with your Father who is in the heavens.

So when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that people will admire them. Amen, I say to you: they have already received their reward.
You, when you give alms, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
so that your almsgiving may remain in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.

And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites: they love to pray standing in the synagogues and at the street corners, to be seen by people. Amen, I say to you: they have already received their reward.
You, when you pray, go into your room, close the door, and pray to your Father who is present in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.
When you pray, do not babble on like the pagans: they imagine that by their many words they will be heard.
Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need, even before you ask him.
You, then, pray like this: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name,
thy kingdom come, thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us this day our daily bread.
Forgive us our debts, as we ourselves forgive those who are in debt to us.
And do not let us enter into temptation, but deliver us from the Evil One.
Yes, if you forgive others their faults, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
But if you do not forgive others, neither will your Father forgive your faults.

And when you fast, do not put on a gloomy face, like the hypocrites: they disfigure their faces to make it clear to people that they are fasting. Amen, I say to you: they have already received their reward.
You, when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,
so that your fasting may be known, not by others, but by your Father who is present in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will repay you.
Do not store up treasures for yourselves on earth, where moths and rust devour, where thieves break through the wall and steal.
Store up for yourselves treasures in heaven instead, where neither moth nor rust devours, where thieves do not break through the wall and steal.
For where your treasure is, there also will your heart be.
The lamp of the body is the eye. So if your eye is clear, your whole body will be full of light;
but if your eye is bad, your whole body will be in darkness. If then the light within you is only darkness, how great is that darkness!
No one can serve two masters: either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and Money.

This is why I tell you: do not worry about your life, about what you will eat or drink, nor about your body, about what you will wear. Is not life worth more than food, and the body more than clothing?
Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow, they do not reap, they store nothing in barns; and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth much more than they?
Besides, which of you, by worrying, can add a single hour to the span of his life?
And about clothing, why worry? Observe how the lilies of the field grow: they do not labour, they do not spin.
Yet I tell you, Solomon himself, in all his glory, was never dressed like one of them.
If God so clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow will be thrown into the fire, will he not do much more for you, you of little faith?
So do not worry, saying, What will we eat? What will we drink? What will we wear?
It is the pagans who seek after all these things. But your heavenly Father knows that you need them.
Seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
So do not worry about tomorrow: tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.'

titres.titre: Do Not Profane What Is Holy
A Tree Is Known by Its Fruit

versets.t: 'Do not judge, so that you will not be judged.
For with the judgment you use to judge, you will be judged, and with the measure you use to measure, it will be measured out to you.
Why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye, while you do not notice the beam in your own eye?
Or how will you say to your brother, 'Let me take the speck out of your eye,' while there is a beam in your own?
Hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye.
Do not give to dogs what is sacred, do not throw your pearls before pigs: they would trample them underfoot, then turn to tear you apart.
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives; the one who seeks finds; and to the one who knocks, the door will be opened.
Which of you, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, will give him a snake?
If then you, who are evil, know how to give good things to your children, how much more will your Father who is in the heavens give good things to those who ask him!
So, whatever you want others to do for you, do it yourselves for them: this is the Law and the Prophets.
Enter by the narrow gate. For wide is the gate and spacious the road that leads to perdition; and there are many who take it.
But narrow is the gate and hard the road that leads to life; and there are few who find it.
Beware of false prophets: they come to you disguised as sheep, but inside they are ravenous wolves.
It is by their fruits that you will recognize them. Are grapes gathered from thorns, or figs from brambles?
So every good tree bears good fruit, but the diseased tree bears bad fruit.
A good tree cannot bear bad fruit, nor a diseased tree bear good fruit.
Every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
So it is by their fruits that you will recognize them.
It is not enough to say to me, 'Lord, Lord!' to enter the kingdom of heaven; one must do the will of my Father who is in the heavens.
On that day, many will say to me, 'Lord, Lord, was it not in your name that we prophesied? In your name that we cast out demons? In your name that we did many miracles?'
Then I will declare to them openly, 'I never knew you. Away from me, you who do evil!'
So everyone who listens to the words I have just spoken and puts them into practice is like a wise man who built his house on rock.
The rain fell, the torrents came, the winds blew and beat against that house; it did not collapse, for it was founded on rock.
But everyone who listens to the words I have just spoken and does not put them into practice is like a foolish man who built his house on sand.
The rain fell, the torrents came, the winds blew and struck against that house; it collapsed, and its ruin was complete.'
When Jesus had finished this discourse, the crowds were struck by his teaching,
for he taught them with authority, and not like their scribes.
When Jesus came down from the mountain, great crowds followed him.
And behold, a leper approached, fell down before him, and said, 'Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.'
Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, 'I am willing, be made clean.' At once he was cleansed of his leprosy.
Then Jesus said to him, 'See that you tell no one; but go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering prescribed by Moses: it will be a testimony for the people.'
As Jesus was entering Capernaum, a centurion came to him
and pleaded with him, 'Lord, my servant is lying at home, paralyzed, in terrible suffering.'
Jesus said to him, 'I will come and heal him.'
The centurion replied, 'Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof; but say only a word, and my servant will be healed.
For I myself am under authority, with soldiers under my command; I say to one, 'Go,' and he goes; to another, 'Come,' and he comes; and to my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it.'
When he heard this, Jesus marveled and said to those who were following him, 'Amen, I say to you, in no one in Israel have I found such faith.
So I tell you: many will come from east and west and take their places at table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven;
but the sons of the kingdom will be thrown outside, into the darkness: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'
Then Jesus said to the centurion, 'Go, may it happen to you according to your faith.' And at that very hour the servant was healed.
Jesus then came to Peter's house, where he found Peter's mother-in-law lying in bed with a fever.
He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and began to serve him.
When evening came, they brought him many who were possessed. With a word he drove out the spirits, and he healed all the sick,
thus fulfilling the word of the prophet Isaiah: 'He took our weaknesses and bore our diseases.'
Seeing himself surrounded by a great crowd, Jesus gave the order to cross to the other shore.
A scribe approached and said to him, 'Master, I will follow you wherever you go.'
Jesus answered him, 'Foxes have their dens, and the birds of the sky have their nests; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.'
Another, one of his disciples, said to him, 'Lord, let me first go and bury my father.'
But Jesus answered him, 'Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their dead.'
He got into the boat, and his disciples followed him.
And behold, a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves. He, however, was sleeping.
The disciples came and woke him, crying out, 'Lord, save us! We are lost!'
He said to them, 'Why are you afraid, you of little faith?' Then he stood up, rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
Filled with amazement, the men said, 'What kind of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?'
Jesus arrived on the other shore, in the country of the Gadarenes. Two demoniacs then came out of the tombs to meet him; they were so dangerous that no one could pass by that road.
And behold, they began to cry out, 'What do you want with us, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the appointed time?'
Now there was, some distance away, a large herd of pigs feeding.
The demons pleaded with Jesus, 'If you drive us out, send us into that herd of pigs.'
He said to them, 'Go.' They came out and went into the pigs; and behold, the whole herd rushed down the cliff into the sea, and the pigs perished in the waters.
The herdsmen fled, went off to the town, and reported everything, including the matter of the demoniacs.
Then the whole town came out to meet Jesus; and when they saw him, they begged him to leave their territory.

titres.titre: The Official's Daughter and the Sick Woman

versets.t: Jesus got into the boat, crossed over again, and came to his own town.
And behold, they brought him a paralytic, lying on a stretcher. Seeing their faith, Jesus said to the paralytic, 'Take heart, my child: your sins are forgiven.'
Then some scribes said to themselves, 'This man is blaspheming!'
Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said, 'Why these evil thoughts in your hearts?
Which is easier? To say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
Well then, so that you may know that the Son of Man has, on earth, the power to forgive sins...' He then said to the paralytic, 'Get up, take your stretcher, and go home.'
The man got up and went home.
When they saw this, the crowds were seized with fear and gave glory to God, who has given such power to men.
As he was going along, Jesus saw a man called Matthew, sitting at the tax office. He said to him, 'Follow me.' The man got up and followed him.
Now, as Jesus was at table in the house, behold, many tax collectors and sinners came and took their places with him and his disciples.
When they saw this, the Pharisees said to his disciples, 'Why does your master eat with tax collectors and sinners?'
Jesus, who had heard, said to them, 'It is not the healthy who need the physician, but the sick.
Go, then, and learn what this means: It is mercy I desire, not sacrifice. For I have come to call not the righteous, but sinners.'
Then the disciples of John came and asked him, 'We and the Pharisees fast often; why do your disciples not fast?'
Jesus answered them, 'Can the wedding guests mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But days will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast.
No one mends an old garment with a piece of new cloth: the added piece pulls on the garment, and the tear becomes worse.
Nor does anyone put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wineskins burst, the wine spills out, and the wineskins are ruined. New wine is put into new wineskins, and both are preserved.'
He was still speaking to them when an official approached, fell down before him, and said, 'My daughter has just died; but come, lay your hand on her, and she will live.'
Jesus got up and followed him, with his disciples.
And behold, a woman, who had suffered from hemorrhages for twelve years, approached from behind and touched the fringe of his cloak.
For she said to herself, 'If I only touch his cloak, I will be saved.'
Jesus turned, saw her, and said, 'Take heart, my daughter: your faith has saved you.' And at that very hour the woman was healed.
When he arrived at the official's house, Jesus saw the flute players and the crowd in commotion;
he said, 'Withdraw: the little girl is not dead, she is sleeping.' And they laughed at him.
When the crowd had been put outside, he went in, took the little girl by the hand, and she got up.
The news of this spread throughout that whole region.
As Jesus was going along, two blind men followed him, crying out, 'Have pity on us, son of David!'
When he had entered the house, the blind men came to him. Jesus said to them, 'Do you believe that I can do this?' They answered him, 'Yes, Lord.'
Then he touched their eyes, saying, 'May it happen to you according to your faith.'
And their eyes were opened. Jesus warned them sternly, 'See that no one knows of this!'
But once they had left, they spoke of him throughout that whole region.
They had barely gone out when a man who was mute, possessed by a demon, was brought to him.
When the demon had been driven out, the mute man began to speak. The crowds, in amazement, said, 'Never has anything like this been seen in Israel!'
But the Pharisees said, 'It is by the prince of demons that he drives out demons.'
Jesus went through all the towns and villages; he taught in their synagogues, proclaimed the Good News of the Kingdom, and healed every disease and every affliction.
Seeing the crowds, he was moved with compassion for them, for they were exhausted and dejected, like sheep without a shepherd.
Then he said to his disciples, 'The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.
So ask the master of the harvest to send out workers for his harvest.'
Then Jesus called his twelve disciples and gave them the power to drive out unclean spirits and to heal every disease and every affliction.
These are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon, called Peter, and Andrew, his brother; James, son of Zebedee, and John, his brother;
Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James, son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
Simon the Zealot and Judas Iscariot, the one who betrayed him.
These twelve Jesus sent out on mission with these instructions: 'Do not go among the pagans, do not enter a town of the Samaritans;
go instead to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
Along the way, proclaim that the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse the lepers, drive out demons. You have received freely: give freely.
Do not procure gold, or silver, or coins to slip into your belts,
no bag for the road, no second tunic, no sandals, no staff; for the worker deserves his food.
In every town or village you enter, find out who is worthy to receive you, and stay with him until you leave.
When you enter the house, greet it.
If this house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
And if anyone refuses to welcome you and to listen to your words, leave that house or that town, shaking the dust from your feet.
Amen, I say to you: on the day of judgment, the land of Sodom and Gomorrah will be treated less harshly than that town.
Behold, I am sending you like sheep in the midst of wolves. So be as shrewd as serpents and as innocent as doves.
Beware of people: they will hand you over to the courts and flog you in their synagogues.
Because of me, you will be dragged before governors and kings: this will be to bear witness before them and before the pagans.
When they hand you over, do not worry about how to speak or what to say: what you are to say will be given to you at that moment.
For it is not you who will speak: it is the Spirit of your Father who will speak in you.
Brother will hand over brother to death, and the father, his child; children will rise up against their parents and have them put to death.
You will be hated by all because of my name; but whoever holds firm to the end will be saved.
When they persecute you in one town, flee to another. Amen, I say to you: you will not have finished going through the towns of Israel before the Son of Man has come.
The disciple is not above the master, nor the servant above his master.

It is enough for the disciple to be like his master, and for the servant to be like his master. Since they have called the master of the house Beelzebul, what will they not say about the members of his household!
So do not fear them. For nothing is veiled that will not be unveiled, nothing hidden that will not be made known.
What I tell you in the dark, say in broad daylight; what you hear whispered in your ear, proclaim from the rooftops.
Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; fear rather the one who can destroy, in Gehenna, both soul and body.
Are not two sparrows sold for a penny? Yet not a single one falls to the ground without your Father willing it.
As for you, even the hairs of your head are all counted.
So have no fear: you are worth more than all the sparrows.
So everyone who declares himself for me before others, I too will declare myself for him before my Father who is in the heavens;
but whoever denies me before others, I too will deny him before my Father who is in the heavens.
Do not think that I have come to bring peace on earth: I have not come to bring peace, but the sword.
Yes, I have come to set a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law:
one's enemies will be the members of one's own household.
Whoever loves his father or his mother more than me is not worthy of me; whoever loves his son or his daughter more than me is not worthy of me;
whoever does not take up his cross to follow me is not worthy of me.
Whoever wants to keep his life will lose it; whoever loses his life for my sake will keep it.
Whoever welcomes you welcomes me; and whoever welcomes me welcomes the One who sent me.
Whoever welcomes a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet's reward; whoever welcomes a righteous person because he is righteous will receive a righteous person's reward.
And whoever gives even a cup of cool water to one of these little ones because he is my disciple, amen, I say to you, he will not lose his reward.'

titres.titre: The Question of John the Baptist
The Praise of John the Baptist
The Towns That Refuse to Believe
The Father Revealed to the Little Ones

versets.t: When Jesus had finished giving instructions to his twelve disciples, he left there to teach and to proclaim the Good News in the towns of the region.
Now John, in his prison, had heard what the Christ was doing. He sent his disciples
to ask him, 'Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?'
Jesus answered them, 'Go and report to John what you hear and see:
the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the Good News is proclaimed to the poor.
Blessed is the one for whom I am not an occasion of stumbling!'
As the messengers were leaving, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: 'What did you go out to the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind?
Then what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? But those who wear fine clothes are in the palaces of kings.
Then what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and far more than a prophet.
It is of him that it is written: Behold, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, to prepare the way before you.
Amen, I say to you: among the children of men, none greater has arisen than John the Baptist; and yet the least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
From the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven suffers violence, and the violent try to seize it.
For all the Prophets, as well as the Law, prophesied until John.
And if you are willing to accept it, he is the Elijah who is to come.
Whoever has ears, let him hear!
To what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces, who call out to others:
We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a song of mourning, and you did not beat your breast.
For John came: he does not eat, he does not drink, and they say he has a demon.
The Son of Man came: he eats, he drinks, and they say: he is a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners. But Wisdom has been proved right through her works.'
Then Jesus began to reproach the towns where he had done most of his miracles, because they had not repented:
'Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, those towns would long ago have repented, in sackcloth and ashes.
So I tell you: on the day of judgment, Tyre and Sidon will be treated less harshly than you.
And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will go down to the realm of the dead. For if the miracles done among you had been done in Sodom, it would still be standing today.
So I tell you: on the day of judgment, the land of Sodom will be treated less harshly than you.'
At that time, Jesus spoke up: 'I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth: what you have hidden from the wise and the learned, you have revealed to the little ones.
Yes, Father, for such was your gracious will.
Everything has been handed over to me by my Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son, and the one to whom the Son wishes to reveal him.
Come to me, all you who labour under the weight of your burden, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble of heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
Yes, my yoke is easy, and my burden light.'

titres.titre: The Ears of Grain Plucked on the Sabbath
The Healing on a Sabbath Day
The Return of the Unclean Spirit

versets.t: At that time, on a Sabbath day, Jesus was passing through fields of grain. His disciples, who were hungry, began to pluck ears of grain and eat them.
When they saw this, the Pharisees said to him, 'Look, your disciples are doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath!'
He answered them, 'Have you not read what David did, one day when he was hungry, he and his companions?
He entered the house of God, and they ate the bread of the offering, which he had no right to eat, neither he nor his companions, but only the priests.
Or have you not read in the Law that, on the Sabbath day, the priests in the Temple profane the Sabbath and yet are without fault?
Now I tell you: there is something greater than the Temple here.
If you had understood what this means: It is mercy I desire, not sacrifice, you would not have condemned the innocent.
For the Son of Man is master of the Sabbath.'
Leaving there, Jesus went into their synagogue.
Now there was a man there with a paralyzed hand. To have grounds for accusing Jesus, they put this question to him: 'Is it permitted to heal on the Sabbath day?'
He answered them, 'Which of you, if he has only one sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath day, will not take hold of it to lift it out?
Now, a man is worth far more than a sheep! So it is permitted to do good on the Sabbath day.'
Then he said to the man, 'Stretch out your hand.' He stretched it out, and it became healthy again like the other.
Once they had gone out, the Pharisees held a council against him, looking for how to put him to death.
But Jesus, knowing this, withdrew from there. Many followed him, and he healed them all;
and he ordered them not to make him known,
to fulfil the word of the prophet Isaiah:
Behold my servant, whom I have chosen, my beloved, in whom I am well pleased. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice to the nations.
He will not quarrel, he will not cry out, no one will hear his voice in the streets.
He will not break the bruised reed, he will not quench the smoldering wick, until he makes justice triumph.
And in his name the nations will place their hope.
Then a demoniac, blind and mute, was brought to him; Jesus healed him, so that the mute man spoke and saw.
All the crowds, astonished, said, 'Is this not the son of David?'
But the Pharisees, hearing this, said, 'If he drives out demons, it is by Beelzebul, the prince of demons.'
Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, 'Every kingdom divided against itself is headed for ruin; no town, no household divided against itself will stand.
If Satan drives out Satan, he is divided against himself: how then will his kingdom stand?
And if I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? They, therefore, will be your judges.
But if it is by the Spirit of God that I drive out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
How can anyone enter the house of a strong man and seize his goods, unless he first ties up that strong man? Only then will he plunder his house.
Whoever is not with me is against me; whoever does not gather with me scatters.
This is why I tell you: every sin, every blasphemy will be forgiven men, but blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
Whoever speaks against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, either in this world or in the world to come.
Take a good tree: its fruit will be good; take a diseased tree: its fruit will be bad. For it is by its fruit that a tree is known.
Brood of vipers! How could you say good things, you who are evil? For the mouth speaks of what overflows from the heart.
The good man draws good things from his good treasure; the evil man draws evil things from his evil treasure.
I tell you: on the day of judgment, people will give account for every empty word they have spoken.
For by your words you will be declared righteous, and by your words you will be condemned.'
Then some scribes and Pharisees said to him, 'Master, we would like to see a sign from you.'
He answered them, 'This evil and adulterous generation demands a sign! As for a sign, none will be given it except that of the prophet Jonah.
For just as Jonah remained three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the Son of Man will remain three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

On the day of judgment, the people of Nineveh will rise up with this generation, and they will condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and there is something far greater than Jonah here.

On the day of judgment, the queen of the South will rise up with this generation, and she will condemn it; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and there is something far greater than Solomon here.'
'When the unclean spirit has gone out of a man, it roams through arid places seeking rest, and finds none.
Then it says to itself: I will go back to my house, the one I left. On its arrival, it finds it unoccupied, swept, and put in order.
It then goes off to fetch seven other spirits more evil than itself; they enter and settle there, and the last state of that man is worse than the first. So it will be for this evil generation.'
While he was still speaking to the crowds, behold, his mother and his brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak with him.
Someone said to him, 'Your mother and your brothers are there, outside: they are seeking to speak with you.'
Jesus answered the one who had just spoken, 'Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?'
Then, stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said, 'Here are my mother and my brothers.
For whoever does the will of my Father who is in the heavens, that one is for me a brother, a sister, a mother.'

titres.titre: The Explanation of the Parable of the Sower
The Mustard Seed and the Yeast
The Explanation of the Parable of the Weeds
The Treasure, the Pearl, and the Net

versets.t: That day, Jesus went out of the house and sat down by the sea.
Around him gathered a crowd so large that he got into a boat and sat down; the whole crowd stood on the shore.
He told them many things in parables: 'Behold, the sower went out to sow.
As he was sowing, some seeds fell along the path, and the birds came and ate them.
Others fell on rocky ground, where they did not have much soil; they sprang up at once, because the soil was shallow.
But when the sun rose, they were scorched and, having no roots, they withered.
Others fell among the thorns; the thorns grew up and choked them.
Others fell on good soil, and they produced fruit: one a hundredfold, another sixtyfold, another thirtyfold.
Whoever has ears, let him hear!'
The disciples came and said to him, 'Why do you speak to them in parables?'
He answered them, 'To you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; but to them it is not given.
To the one who has, more will be given, and he will have in abundance; but from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away.
This is why I speak to them in parables: they look without seeing, they listen without hearing or understanding.
In them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah: You will listen and listen, but never understand; you will look and look, but never see.

For the heart of this people has grown dull: they have become hard of hearing, they have shut their eyes, lest their eyes see, their ears hear, their heart understand, and they turn back; otherwise I would have healed them.
But you, blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear!
Amen, I say to you: many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see, and did not see it, to hear what you hear, and did not hear it.
You, then, listen to what the parable of the sower means.
When someone hears the word of the Kingdom without understanding it, the Evil One comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart: this is the one who received the seed along the path.
The one who received the seed on rocky ground is the man who hears the word and receives it at once with joy;
but he has no roots in himself, he is an inconstant man: when distress or persecution comes because of the word, he falls at once.
The one who received the seed among the thorns is the man who hears the word; but the worries of the world and the deceptive lure of wealth choke the word, which produces no fruit.
The one who received the seed on good soil is the man who hears the word and understands it: he bears fruit, and yields one a hundredfold, another sixtyfold, another thirtyfold.'
He put before them another parable: 'The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
Now, while everyone was sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat, then went away.
When the stalk grew and formed the ear, then the weeds appeared as well.
The master's servants came and said to him: Master, was it not good seed that you sowed in your field? Where then do the weeds come from?
He answered them: It is an enemy who has done this. The servants said to him: Do you want us, then, to go and pull them out?
He answered: No, for in pulling out the weeds, you risk uprooting the wheat along with them.
Let them grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time, I will say to the reapers: First pull out the weeds and bind them in bundles to be burned; but the wheat, gather it into my barn.'
He put before them another parable: 'The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed, which a man takes and sows in his field.
It is the smallest of all seeds; but when it has grown, it surpasses the other garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and shelter in its branches.'
He told them yet another parable: 'The kingdom of heaven is like the yeast that a woman takes and buries in a large quantity of flour, until all the dough rises.'
All this Jesus told the crowds in parables; he spoke to them only in parables,
fulfilling the word of the prophet: I will open my mouth in parables, I will reveal what has been hidden since the foundation of the world.
Then, leaving the crowds, he went back into the house. His disciples came to him and said, 'Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.'
He answered them, 'The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.
The field is the world; the good seed, these are the sons of the Kingdom; the weeds are the sons of the Evil One;
the enemy who sows them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; the reapers are the angels.
Just as the weeds are pulled out to be burned in the fire, so it will be at the end of the world.
The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will remove from his Kingdom all who cause others to fall and all who do evil;
they will throw them into the furnace: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Whoever has ears, let him hear!'
'The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field; the man who finds it hides it again; in his joy, he goes and sells all that he owns, and he buys that field.'
'The kingdom of heaven is also like a merchant looking for fine pearls.
Having found one pearl of great value, he goes and sells all that he owns, and he buys it.'
'The kingdom of heaven is also like a net thrown into the sea, which brings in all kinds of fish.
When it is full, it is pulled onto the shore; people sit down, gather the good ones into baskets, and throw away those that are worthless.
So it will be at the end of the world: the angels will go out to separate the wicked from among the righteous,
and they will throw them into the furnace: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'
'Have you understood all this?' They answered him, 'Yes.'
And he added, 'This is why every scribe who has become a disciple of the kingdom of heaven is like a master of a house who brings out of his treasure what is new and what is old.'
When Jesus had finished these parables, he left there.
Coming to his own country, he taught the people in their synagogue, so that they were astounded and said, 'Where does he get this wisdom and these miracles?
Is he not the carpenter's son? Is his mother not called Mary? And his brothers, James, Joseph, Simon, and Jude?
And his sisters, are they not all here among us? Where then does he get all this?'
And he was for them an occasion of stumbling. But Jesus said to them, 'A prophet is despised only in his own country and in his own house.'
And he did not do many miracles in that place, because of their lack of faith.

titres.titre: The Death of John the Baptist
The First Multiplication of the Loaves

versets.t: At that time, Herod the tetrarch heard what was being said about Jesus,
and he said to his servants, 'It is John the Baptist! He has risen from the dead, and that is why the power to work miracles is at work in him.'
For Herod had had John arrested, chained, and put in prison, because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip.
For John kept telling him, 'It is not permitted for you to have her as your wife.'
Herod wanted to put him to death, but he was afraid of the crowd, who held John to be a prophet.
Now, at Herod's birthday celebration, the daughter of Herodias danced among the guests, and she pleased Herod,
so that he promised on oath to give her whatever she asked.
Prompted by her mother, she said, 'Give me here, on a platter, the head of John the Baptist.'
The king was saddened; but because of his oath and the guests, he ordered that it be given to her
and had John beheaded in his prison.
The head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she carried it to her mother.
John's disciples came and took the body and buried it; then they went and told Jesus.
When he heard this, Jesus left there by boat to withdraw alone to a deserted place. But the crowds heard of it and, leaving their towns, they followed him on foot.
When he disembarked, he saw a great crowd; he was moved with compassion for them and healed their sick.

When evening came, the disciples approached and said to him, 'The place is deserted and the hour is already late; so send the crowds away, that they may go into the villages to buy themselves something to eat.'
But Jesus said to them, 'They do not need to go away. Give them something to eat yourselves.'
They answered him, 'We have here only five loaves and two fish.'
'Bring them to me here,' he said.

He ordered the crowd to sit down on the grass, took the five loaves and the two fish and, raising his eyes to heaven, pronounced the blessing; then, breaking the loaves, he gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowd.
All ate their fill, and they gathered up the pieces that were left over: twelve baskets full.
Those who had eaten numbered about five thousand men, not counting the women and children.
At once, Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other shore, while he would send the crowds away.
After sending them away, he went up the mountain to pray alone. When evening came, he was there, alone.
The boat was already a good distance from the land, battered by the waves, for the wind was against them.
Toward the end of the night, Jesus came toward the disciples, walking on the sea.
When they saw him walking on the sea, they were terrified: 'It is a ghost!' And in their fright they began to cry out.
But at once Jesus spoke to them: 'Take heart! It is I; do not be afraid.'
Peter spoke up: 'Lord, if it is really you, command me to come to you on the waters.'
Jesus said to him, 'Come.' Peter got out of the boat and walked on the waters to go to Jesus.
But, seeing the force of the wind, he was afraid; and, as he began to sink, he cried out, 'Lord, save me!'
At once, Jesus stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and said to him, 'You of little faith, why did you doubt?'
And when they had got into the boat, the wind dropped.
Then those who were in the boat fell down before him, saying, 'Truly, you are the Son of God!'
After the crossing, they landed at Gennesaret.
The people of the place recognized him; they sent word throughout the whole region, and they brought him all the sick.
They begged him to let them touch just the fringe of his cloak; and all who touched it were healed.

titres.titre: The tradition of the elders and the commandment of God
The faith of the Canaanite woman
The second multiplication of the loaves

versets.t: Then some scribes and Pharisees who had come from Jerusalem approached Jesus and said,
"Why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders? They do not wash their hands before eating."
He answered them, "And you, why do you break the commandment of God for the sake of your tradition?
For God said, 'Honor your father and your mother,' and also, 'Whoever curses his father or mother shall be put to death.'
But you say that if anyone declares to his father or mother, 'Whatever help you might have had from me is given to God,'
then he is excused from honoring his father. So, for the sake of your tradition, you nullify the word of God.
Hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied well about you when he said,
'This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
In vain do they worship me, teaching as doctrines the mere precepts of men.'"
Then he called the crowd to him and said, "Listen and understand!
It is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person; it is what comes out of the mouth that defiles a person."
Then the disciples approached him and said, "Do you know that the Pharisees were scandalized when they heard this word?"
He replied, "Every plant that my heavenly Father has not planted will be uprooted.
Leave them alone. They are blind guides leading the blind. And if one blind man guides another, both will fall into a pit."
Peter spoke up, "Explain this parable to us."
Jesus said, "Are you still without understanding, even you?
Do you not see that whatever enters the mouth passes into the stomach and is then expelled into the drain?
But what comes out of the mouth comes from the heart, and that is what defiles a person.
For from the heart come evil intentions: murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, slander.
These are what defile a person; but eating with unwashed hands does not defile a person."
Leaving that place, Jesus withdrew to the region of Tyre and Sidon.
And a Canaanite woman from that region came and began to cry out, "Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is cruelly tormented by a demon."
But he did not answer her a word. His disciples came and urged him, "Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us."
Jesus answered, "I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel."
But the woman came and knelt before him, saying, "Lord, help me!"
He replied, "It is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the little dogs."
She said, "True, Lord; yet even the little dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table."
Then Jesus answered her, "Woman, great is your faith! Let it be done for you as you wish." And her daughter was healed at that very hour.
Jesus went on from there and walked beside the Sea of Galilee. He went up the mountain and sat down there.
Great crowds came to him, bringing the lame, the blind, the crippled, the mute, and many others; they laid them at his feet, and he healed them.
When the crowds saw the mute speaking, the crippled made whole, the lame walking, and the blind seeing, they were amazed, and they gave glory to the God of Israel.

Jesus called his disciples and said, "I have compassion for this crowd: they have already stayed with me three days and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry, or they may collapse on the way."
The disciples said to him, "Where in this wilderness could we find enough bread to satisfy so great a crowd?"
Jesus asked them, "How many loaves do you have?" They answered, "Seven, and a few small fish."
Then he ordered the crowd to sit down on the ground;
he took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowd.
They all ate and were satisfied, and they gathered up seven baskets full of the pieces that were left over.
Those who had eaten were four thousand men, not counting women and children.
After sending the crowds away, Jesus got into the boat and came to the region of Magadan.

titres.titre: The leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees
The first prediction of the Passion

versets.t: The Pharisees and Sadducees came to Jesus and, to test him, asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
He answered them, "In the evening you say, 'It will be fair weather, for the sky is red';
and in the morning, 'Today there will be a storm, for the sky is red and gloomy.' You know how to interpret the appearance of the sky, but you cannot read the signs of the times!
This evil and adulterous generation asks for a sign! Yet no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah." And with that he left them and went away.
On crossing to the other shore, the disciples had forgotten to bring bread.
Jesus said to them, "Watch out! Guard yourselves against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees."
The disciples reasoned among themselves, "It is because we did not bring any bread."
Aware of this, Jesus said to them, "You of little faith, why are you reasoning that you have no bread?
Do you still not understand? Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many baskets you gathered?
Or the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many baskets you gathered?
How is it that you do not understand that I was not speaking to you about bread? Guard yourselves against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees!"
Then they understood that he had not told them to guard against the leaven of bread, but against the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
When he came to the region of Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asked his disciples, "Who do people say the Son of Man is?"
They answered, "Some say John the Baptist; others, Elijah; still others, Jeremiah or one of the prophets."
Jesus said to them, "And you, who do you say that I am?"
Simon Peter answered, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."
Jesus replied, "Blessed are you, Simon son of Jonah, for it was not a human being who revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven.
And I say to you: you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church; and the gates of the realm of the dead will not prevail against it.
I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven: whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven."
Then he ordered the disciples to tell no one that he was the Christ.

From that time on, Jesus began to show his disciples that he had to go to Jerusalem, suffer greatly at the hands of the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, be put to death, and on the third day be raised.
Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him sharply, "God forbid, Lord! No, this shall never happen to you!"
But he turned and said to Peter, "Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, for your thoughts are not those of God, but those of men."
Then Jesus said to his disciples, "If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.
What will it profit a man to gain the whole world, if he pays for it with his life? And what can a man give in exchange for his life?
For the Son of Man is going to come in the glory of his Father, with his angels, and then he will repay each one according to his conduct.
Amen, I say to you: some of those standing here will not taste death before they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom."

titres.titre: The healing of the epileptic boy
The second prediction of the Passion

versets.t: Six days later, Jesus took with him Peter, James, and his brother John, and led them up a high mountain by themselves.
He was transfigured before them: his face shone like the sun, and his clothes became white as light.
And behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with him.
Peter spoke up and said to Jesus, "Lord, it is good that we are here! If you wish, I will set up three tents here: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
While he was still speaking, a bright cloud overshadowed them; and behold, from the cloud a voice said, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Listen to him!"
When the disciples heard this, they fell face down on the ground, gripped by great fear.
But Jesus came, touched them, and said, "Rise, do not be afraid."
And when they looked up, they saw no one but Jesus alone.
As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus gave them this command, "Tell no one about this vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead."
The disciples asked him, "Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
He answered them, "Elijah does come, and he will restore all things.
But I say to you: Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him; instead they did to him whatever they pleased. So too the Son of Man is going to suffer at their hands."
Then the disciples understood that he was speaking to them about John the Baptist.
As they were returning to the crowd, a man approached and knelt before Jesus.
He said, "Lord, have mercy on my son: he is an epileptic and suffers terribly; often he falls into the fire, often into the water.
I brought him to your disciples, but they could not heal him."
Jesus answered, "Faithless and perverse generation, how long must I still be with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring him here to me."
Jesus rebuked the demon, and it came out of the boy, who was healed at that very hour.
The disciples came to Jesus privately and asked, "Why could we not cast it out?"

Jesus answered them, "Because of your lack of faith. Amen, I say to you: if you had faith the size of a mustard seed, you would say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it would move; nothing would be impossible for you.
But this kind of demon is driven out only by prayer and fasting."
As they were traveling together in Galilee, Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man is going to be handed over into the hands of men;
they will put him to death, and on the third day he will rise." And the disciples were deeply saddened.
When they had returned to Capernaum, the collectors of the Temple tax came to Peter and said, "Does your master not pay the tax?"
"Yes," said Peter. When he entered the house, Jesus spoke first, "What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth collect duties and taxes? From their own sons, or from strangers?"
Peter answered, "From strangers." Jesus said, "Then the sons are exempt.

But so as not to give offense to these people, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up; open its mouth, and you will find a coin. Take it and give it to them, for me and for you."

titres.titre: The greatest is the one who becomes small
Do not cause the little ones to fall
The parable of the unforgiving servant

versets.t: At that time the disciples came to Jesus and said, "Who then is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?"
Jesus called a little child, placed him in their midst,
and said, "Amen, I say to you: unless you change and become like little children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
Whoever makes himself small like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
And whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me.
But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to fall into sin, it would be better for him to have a great millstone hung around his neck and to be drowned in the depths of the sea."
"Woe to the world because of the occasions of sin! It is inevitable that they come, but woe to the one through whom they come!

If your hand or your foot causes you to fall, cut it off and throw it away from you: it is better for you to enter life crippled or lame than to be thrown, with both hands or both feet, into the eternal fire.
And if your eye causes you to fall, tear it out and throw it away from you: it is better for you to enter life with one eye than to be thrown, with both eyes, into the fire of Gehenna."
"See that you do not despise one of these little ones, for I tell you, their angels in heaven always behold the face of my Father who is in heaven.
For the Son of Man came to save what was lost.
What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them strays, will he not leave the ninety-nine others on the mountain and go in search of the one that has strayed?
And if he manages to find it, amen, I say to you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not stray.
In the same way, it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven that a single one of these little ones should be lost."
"If your brother sins against you, go and speak with him alone, and correct him. If he listens to you, you have won back your brother.
If he does not listen to you, take one or two others along with you, so that every matter may be settled on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the Church; and if he refuses to listen even to the Church, let him be to you as a pagan and a tax collector.
Amen, I say to you: whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven."
"Again I say to you: if two of you on earth agree to ask for anything, it will be granted to them by my Father who is in heaven.
For where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I in their midst."
Then Peter came and said to him, "Lord, when my brother wrongs me, how many times must I forgive him? Up to seven times?"
Jesus answered him, "I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.
Therefore the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wished to settle accounts with his servants.
He had scarcely begun when a man was brought to him who owed him millions in gold coins.
Since he had no way to repay, the master ordered him to be sold, along with his wife, his children, and all he possessed, to repay the debt.
The servant fell at his feet and begged him, 'Be patient with me, and I will repay you everything.'
Moved with compassion, the master of that servant let him go and forgave him the debt.
But as soon as he had gone out, that servant met one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred silver coins. He seized him and began to choke him, saying, 'Repay what you owe me!'
His fellow servant fell at his feet and begged him, 'Be patient with me, and I will repay you.'
But he refused; he went off and had him thrown into prison until he should repay the debt.
When his fellow servants saw this, they were deeply grieved, and they went and reported to their master everything that had happened.
Then the master summoned him and said, 'Wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you begged me.
Should you not have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?'
And in his anger his master handed him over to the torturers until he should repay the whole debt.
So too will my heavenly Father treat you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from the heart."
After these words, Jesus left Galilee and came into the territory of Judea, beyond the Jordan.
Great crowds followed him, and there he healed them.
Some Pharisees approached him to test him, "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife for any reason at all?"
He answered, "Have you not read that in the beginning the Creator made them male and female, and that he said,
'For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh'?
So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore, what God has joined together, let no one separate!"
They said to him, "Why then did Moses command that a certificate of divorce be given when a man sends his wife away?"
He answered them, "It was because of the hardness of your hearts that Moses permitted you to divorce your wives; but in the beginning it was not so.
And I say to you: whoever divorces his wife, except in the case of an unlawful union, and marries another, commits adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery."
The disciples said to him, "If such is the situation of a man with his wife, it is better not to marry."
He answered them, "Not everyone can accept this word, but only those to whom it is given.

For there are eunuchs who were born that way; there are others whom men have made so; and there are those who have made themselves so for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Whoever can accept this, let him accept it."
Then children were brought to Jesus, that he might lay his hands on them and pray over them. But the disciples pushed the people away roughly.
Jesus said, "Let the children be, do not prevent them from coming to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to those who are like them."
He laid his hands on them, and then he departed from there.
And behold, a man approached Jesus and said, "Teacher, what good must I do to obtain eternal life?"
Jesus answered him, "Why do you ask me about what is good? One alone is good. If you want to enter into life, keep the commandments."
"Which ones?" he asked. Jesus answered, "You shall not murder, you shall not commit adultery, you shall not steal, you shall not bear false witness,
honor your father and your mother, and you shall love your neighbor as yourself."
The young man said to him, "All these I have kept; what do I still lack?"
Jesus answered him, "If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you own, give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me."
When he heard this word, the young man went away sad, for he had great possessions.
Then Jesus said to his disciples, "Amen, I say to you: it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven.
I say it again: it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God."
When they heard this, the disciples were greatly astonished and said, "Who then can be saved?"
Jesus looked at them and said, "For human beings this is impossible, but for God everything is possible."
Then Peter spoke up, "Look, we have left everything to follow you: what then will there be for us?"

Jesus said to them, "Amen, I say to you: at the renewal of all things, when the Son of Man sits on his throne of glory, you who have followed me will also sit on twelve thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
And everyone who has left houses, brothers, sisters, father, mother, children, or lands for the sake of my name will receive a hundredfold, and will inherit eternal life.
Many who are first will be last, and many who are last will be first."

titres.titre: The workers of the eleventh hour
The third prediction of the Passion
The request of the sons of Zebedee
The two blind men of Jericho

versets.t: "For the kingdom of heaven is like the owner of an estate who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
He agreed with the workers on a wage of one silver coin for the day, and he sent them into his vineyard.
Going out at about nine in the morning, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace.
He said to them, 'You also go into my vineyard, and I will pay you what is fair.'
So they went. He went out again about noon, and then about three in the afternoon, and did the same.
About five in the evening he went out again, found others, and said to them, 'Why have you been standing here all day idle?'
They answered him, 'Because no one has hired us.' He said to them, 'You also go into my vineyard.'
When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his steward, 'Call the workers and give each one his wages, beginning with the last and ending with the first.'
Those who had started at five in the evening came and each received one silver coin.
When the first came, they thought they would receive more; but they too each received one silver coin.
On receiving it, they grumbled against the owner of the estate,
'These who came last worked only one hour, and you have treated them the same as us, who bore the burden of the day and the heat!'
But he answered one of them, 'Friend, I am doing you no wrong. Did you not agree with me on one silver coin?
Take what is yours and go. I choose to give to this last one as much as to you.
Do I not have the right to do as I please with what is mine? Or are you going to look at me with an evil eye because I am good?'
So the last will be first, and the first will be last."
As he was going up to Jerusalem, Jesus took the twelve disciples aside and said to them along the way,
"Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death
and hand him over to the pagans to be mocked, flogged, and crucified; and on the third day he will rise."
Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee approached Jesus with her sons, and knelt before him to make a request.
He said to her, "What do you want?" She answered, "Command that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your kingdom."
Jesus answered, "You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I am about to drink?" They said to him, "We can."
He said to them, "My cup you will indeed drink; but to sit at my right and at my left is not mine to grant: these places are for those for whom my Father has prepared them."
When the ten heard this, they were indignant at the two brothers.
Jesus called them to him and said, "You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and the great ones make their authority felt.
Among you it must not be so. On the contrary, whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant,
and whoever wants to be first among you shall be your slave.
In the same way, the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for the many."
As they were leaving Jericho, a great crowd followed Jesus.
And behold, two blind men sitting by the roadside, hearing that Jesus was passing by, began to cry out, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!"
The crowd scolded them to make them be quiet, but they cried out all the louder, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!"
Jesus stopped, called them, and said, "What do you want me to do for you?"
They answered him, "Lord, let our eyes be opened!"
Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes; at once they regained their sight and followed him.

titres.titre: The sellers driven from the Temple
The parable of the two sons
The parable of the murderous tenants

versets.t: When they drew near to Jerusalem and came within sight of Bethphage, on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples,
saying to them, "Go into the village ahead of you; you will find at once a donkey tied there, and a colt with her. Untie them and bring them to me.
And if anyone says anything to you, answer, 'The Lord needs them'; and he will let them go at once."
This took place so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled:
Say to the daughter of Zion, 'Behold, your king comes to you, full of gentleness, mounted on a donkey and on a colt, the foal of a beast of burden.'
The disciples went and did as Jesus had commanded them.
They brought the donkey and the colt, laid their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.
Most of the crowd spread their cloaks on the road; others cut branches from the trees and strewed them on the way.
The crowds that went ahead of him and those that followed cried out, "Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest heavens!"
As he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred. People asked, "Who is this?"
And the crowds answered, "This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth in Galilee."
Jesus entered the Temple and drove out all those who were selling and buying in the Temple; he overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those who sold doves,
and he said to them, "It is written: 'My house will be called a house of prayer'; but you are making it a den of robbers."
In the Temple the blind and the lame came to him, and he healed them.
But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonders he was doing and the children crying out in the Temple, "Hosanna to the Son of David!", they were indignant
and said to him, "Do you hear what they are saying?" Jesus answered them, "Yes. Have you never read this text: 'From the mouths of infants and nursing babies you have brought forth praise'?"
Then he left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where he spent the night.
The next morning, on his way back to the city, he was hungry.
Seeing a fig tree by the road, he went up to it but found nothing on it but leaves. He said to it, "May no fruit ever come from you again!" And instantly the fig tree withered.
When the disciples saw this, they were amazed and said, "How did the fig tree wither so instantly?"

Jesus answered them, "Amen, I say to you: if you have faith and do not doubt, not only will you do what I did to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, 'Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,' it will be done.
And whatever you ask for in prayer with faith, you will receive."
He entered the Temple, and while he was teaching, the chief priests and the elders of the people approached him and said, "By what right do you do these things? Who gave you this authority?"
Jesus answered them, "I too will ask you a single question; if you answer it for me, I will tell you by what right I do these things.
The baptism of John, where did it come from? From heaven or from men?" They reasoned among themselves,
"If we say 'From heaven,' he will say to us, 'Why then did you not believe him?' And if we say 'From men,' we have the crowd to fear, for everyone holds John to be a prophet."
So they answered Jesus, "We do not know." And he said to them in turn, "Neither will I tell you by what right I do these things."
"What do you think? A man had two sons. He said to the first, 'Son, go and work in the vineyard today.'
He answered, 'I will not.' But afterward he changed his mind and went.
Turning to the second, the father said the same thing. This one answered, 'Yes, sir!' But he did not go.

Which of the two did the will of the father?" They answered, "The first." Jesus said to them, "Amen, I say to you: the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going into the kingdom of God ahead of you.

For John came to you on the path of righteousness, and you did not believe him; but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. And even when you saw this, you did not afterward repent and believe him."
"Listen to another parable: A man, the owner of an estate, planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a watchtower. Then he leased it to tenants and went abroad.
When the time for the fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect the produce of his vineyard.
But the tenants seized the servants: one they beat, another they killed, and a third they stoned.
Again the owner sent other servants, more than the first; but they were treated the same way.
Finally he sent his son to them, saying to himself, 'They will respect my son.'
But when they saw the son, the tenants said to one another, 'This is the heir: come, let us kill him, and we will have his inheritance.'
So they seized him, threw him out of the vineyard, and killed him.
Now, when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?"
They answered him, "He will bring those wretches to a wretched end. And he will lease the vineyard to other tenants, who will give him the produce at the proper time."
Jesus said to them, "Have you never read in the Scriptures: 'The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; this is the Lord's doing, a marvel in our eyes'?
Therefore I say to you: the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will make it bear its fruits.
Whoever falls on this stone will be broken to pieces; and anyone on whom it falls will be crushed."
When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard these parables, they understood that Jesus was speaking about them.
They sought to arrest him, but they feared the crowds, who held him to be a prophet.

titres.titre: The parable of the wedding guests
The Christ, son and Lord of David

versets.t: Jesus spoke again and addressed them once more in parables:
"The kingdom of heaven is like a king who gave a wedding feast for his son.
He sent his servants to call those who had been invited to the wedding, but they would not come.

He sent other servants again, with this instruction, 'Tell those invited: Behold, I have prepared my banquet; my oxen and fattened cattle have been slaughtered; everything is ready. Come to the wedding.'
But they took no notice and went off, one to his field, another to his business;
the rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.
The king was enraged; he sent his troops, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
Then he said to his servants, 'The wedding banquet is ready, but those invited were not worthy.
Go therefore to the crossroads, and invite to the wedding everyone you find.'
The servants went out into the roads and gathered everyone they found, the bad as well as the good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests.
The king came in to look at the guests, and he saw there a man who was not wearing a wedding garment.
He said to him, 'Friend, how did you get in here without a wedding garment?' The man was silent.
Then the king said to the servants, 'Bind his hands and feet, and throw him outside, into the darkness: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'
For many are called, but few are chosen."
Then the Pharisees withdrew and took counsel about how to trap Jesus in his own words.

They sent their disciples to him, along with the supporters of Herod, to say, "Teacher, we know that you are truthful and that you teach the way of God according to the truth; you let no one influence you, for you show no regard for a person's station.
So tell us your opinion: Is it lawful, yes or no, to pay taxes to Caesar?"
Knowing their malice, Jesus said, "Hypocrites! Why are you trying to test me?
Show me the coin for the tax." They handed him a silver coin.
He said to them, "Whose likeness and inscription are these?"
They answered, "Caesar's." Then he said to them, "Render therefore to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's."
When they heard this, they were amazed. They left him and went away.
That same day some Sadducees came to Jesus. They hold that there is no resurrection. They questioned him,
"Teacher, Moses said, 'If a man dies without children, his brother shall marry the widow to raise up offspring for his brother.'
Now there were among us seven brothers. The first married and then died without offspring, and left his wife to his brother.
The same happened with the second, then the third, down to the seventh.
Finally, after them all, the woman also died.
At the resurrection, whose wife of the seven will she be, since all of them had her as wife?"
Jesus answered them, "You are in error, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God.
For at the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage: they are like the angels of God in heaven.
And concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what God said to you:
'I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living."
When the crowds heard this, they were astounded at his teaching.
When the Pharisees learned that Jesus had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together,
and one of them, an expert in the Law, put a question to Jesus to test him,
"Teacher, in the Law, which is the great commandment?"
Jesus answered him, "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.
This is the great, the first commandment.
And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
On these two commandments hang the whole Law and the Prophets."
While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus questioned them,
"What is your opinion about the Christ? Whose son is he?" They answered him, "David's."
He said to them, "How is it then that David, inspired by the Spirit, calls him Lord, when he says,
'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies under your feet'?
If David then calls him Lord, how can the Christ be his son?"
No one was able to answer him a word; and from that day on, no one dared to question him any further.

titres.titre: Do not imitate the scribes and Pharisees

versets.t: Then Jesus addressed the crowds and his disciples,
"The scribes and the Pharisees sit on the seat of Moses.
So do and observe whatever they tell you; but do not act as they do, for they say and do not do.
They tie up heavy burdens, hard to carry, and lay them on people's shoulders; but they themselves will not lift a finger to move them.
All their deeds they do to be noticed by others: they widen the Scripture bands they wear on their forehead and arm, and they lengthen the tassels of their garments.
They love the place of honor at banquets, the seats of honor in the synagogues,
the greetings in the marketplaces, and being called 'Rabbi' by people.
But you, do not let yourselves be called 'Rabbi,' for you have only one master, and you are all brothers.
And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have only one Father, the one who is in heaven.
Nor let yourselves be called masters, for you have only one master, the Christ.
The greatest among you shall be your servant.
Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of heaven against people! You yourselves do not enter, and you do not let in those who would.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you devour the property of widows while making a show of long prayers! You will be judged all the more severely.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you travel over sea and land to make a single convert, and when he becomes one, you make him a son of Gehenna twice as bad as yourselves!
Woe to you, blind guides, who say, 'If anyone swears by the sanctuary, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the gold of the sanctuary, he is bound.'
Foolish and blind! Which is greater: the gold, or the sanctuary that makes the gold sacred?
You also say, 'If anyone swears by the altar, it means nothing; but if anyone swears by the offering that is on it, he is bound.'
Blind! Which is greater: the offering, or the altar that makes the offering sacred?
So whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it;
whoever swears by the sanctuary swears by it and by the One who dwells in it;
and whoever swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by the One who sits on it.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you pay tithes of mint, dill, and cumin, and you neglect the weightier matters of the Law: justice, mercy, and faithfulness! These you ought to have practiced, without neglecting the others.
Blind guides! You strain out the gnat and swallow the camel!
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you clean the outside of the cup and the dish, while the inside is full of the fruit of your greed and self-indulgence!
Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup, and the outside also will become clean.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like whitewashed tombs: on the outside they look beautiful, but inside they are full of the bones of the dead and every kind of decay!
So too you: on the outside you appear righteous to others, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and evil.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous,
and you say, 'If we had lived in the days of our fathers, we would not have joined them in shedding the blood of the prophets.'
Thus you testify against yourselves: you are indeed the sons of those who murdered the prophets.
