Well then, fill up the measure of your fathers!
Serpents, brood of vipers! How will you escape the condemnation of Gehenna?
This is why I am sending you prophets, wise men, and scribes: some of them you will kill and crucify; others you will flog in your synagogues and hound from town to town.
So upon you will fall all the innocent blood shed on the earth, from the blood of Abel the righteous to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.
Amen, I say to you: all this will fall upon this generation.
Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you, how often have I longed to gather your children, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings! But you would not.
Behold, your house is left to you deserted.
For I say to you, from now on you will not see me again, until you say, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!'"

titres.titre: The prediction of the Temple's ruin
The beginning of the birth pangs
The coming of the Son of Man
The lesson of the fig tree
Keep watch, for the day is unknown
The faithful servant and the unfaithful servant

versets.t: Jesus was coming out of the Temple and going on his way, when his disciples came to point out to him the buildings of the Temple.
He said to them in reply, "You see all this, do you not? Amen, I say to you: not one stone here will be left upon another; everything will be destroyed."
Then, as he was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately and asked, "Tell us, when will this happen, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the world?"
Jesus answered them, "See that no one leads you astray.
For many will come under my name, saying, 'I am the Christ!' And they will lead many astray.
You will hear of wars and rumors of war. Take care, do not be alarmed, for this must happen; but it is not yet the end.
Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and there will be, in various places, famines and earthquakes.
All this will be only the beginning of the birth pangs.
Then they will hand you over to tribulation and put you to death, and you will be hated by all the nations because of my name.
Then many will fall away; they will betray one another and hate one another.
Many false prophets will arise and lead many astray.
And because evil will spread more and more, the love of many will grow cold.
But whoever holds firm to the end will be saved.
This Good News of the Kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole world, as a testimony before all the nations. And then the end will come.
So when you see the Abomination of Desolation, spoken of by the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place (let the reader understand!),
then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains;
let the one who is on the rooftop not go down to take the belongings from his house;
and let the one who is in the fields not turn back to take his cloak.
Woe to the women who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!
Pray that your flight may not occur in winter or on a Sabbath day.
For there will then be a great tribulation, such as there has never been from the beginning of the world until now, and such as there will never be again.
And if those days were not cut short, no one would survive; but for the sake of the elect, those days will be cut short.
Then, if anyone says to you, 'The Christ is here!' or 'He is there!' do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise, and they will produce great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if that were possible, even the elect.
Behold, I have warned you.
So if they say to you, 'Look, he is in the wilderness!' do not go out; 'Look, he is in the inner rooms!' do not believe it.
For as the lightning comes from the east and shines as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will gather.
Immediately after the tribulation of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will no longer give its light, the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky; then all the tribes of the earth will beat their breasts, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven, with great power and great glory.
He will send his angels with a great trumpet blast, and from the four corners of the horizon, from one end of heaven to the other, they will gather his elect.
Learn from the comparison of the fig tree: as soon as its branches become tender and its leaves come out, you know that summer is near.
So too, when you see all this, know that the Son of Man is near, at the very door.
Amen, I say to you: this generation will not pass away before all this happens.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
As for the day and the hour, no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, nor the Son; no one, except the Father alone.
As it was in the days of Noah, so will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.
In those days before the flood, people were eating, drinking, and marrying, up to the day when Noah entered the ark;
they suspected nothing, until the flood came and swept them all away. So will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.
Then, of two men who will be in the fields, one will be taken and the other left;
of two women who will be grinding at the mill, one will be taken and the other left.
Keep watch, then, for you do not know on what day your Lord will come.
Understand this well: if the master of the house had known at what hour of the night the thief would come, he would have kept watch and would not have let his house be broken into.
So you also must be ready: for at an hour you do not expect, the Son of Man will come.
Who then is the faithful and prudent servant whom the master has put in charge of his household, to give them their food at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whom his master, on arriving, will find doing so!
Amen, I say to you: he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
But if that wicked servant says to himself, 'My master is delayed,'
and begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards,
the master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know;
he will punish him severely and make him share the fate of the hypocrites: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth."

titres.titre: The parable of the ten young women

versets.t: "Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten young women who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
The foolish ones took their lamps but brought no oil,
while the wise ones took, along with their lamps, a supply of oil.
As the bridegroom was delayed, they all grew drowsy and fell asleep.
In the middle of the night a cry rang out, 'Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!'
Then all those young women woke up and trimmed their lamps.
The foolish ones said to the wise, 'Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.'
The wise ones answered, 'There would not be enough for us and for you; go instead to the merchants and buy some.'
While they were away buying it, the bridegroom arrived. Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut.
Later the other young women arrived and said, 'Lord, Lord, open for us!'
But he answered, 'Amen, I say to you: I do not know you.'
Keep watch, then, for you know neither the day nor the hour."
"It is like a man about to go on a journey: he called his servants and entrusted his property to them.
To one he gave five bags of gold, to another two, to another one, to each according to his ability; then he set off.
At once the one who had received five bags of gold went and put them to work, and he gained five more.
In the same way, the one who had received two gained two more.
But the one who had received only one went and dug in the ground and hid his master's money there.
After a long time, the master of those servants returned and settled accounts with them.
The one who had received five bags of gold came forward and presented five more, 'Master, you entrusted me with five bags of gold; here are five more that I have gained.'
His master said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful servant: you have been faithful in a few things, I will put you in charge of many; enter into the joy of your master.'
The one who had received two bags of gold also came forward, 'Master, you entrusted me with two bags of gold; here are two more that I have gained.'
His master said to him, 'Well done, good and faithful servant: you have been faithful in a few things, I will put you in charge of many; enter into the joy of your master.'
The one who had received one bag of gold came forward in turn, 'Master, I knew that you are a hard man: you reap where you did not sow, and you gather where you did not scatter the grain.
I was afraid, and I went and hid your bag of gold in the ground. Here it is: you have what belongs to you.'
But his master answered him, 'Wicked and lazy servant! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter the grain.
You should then have put my money in the bank: on my return I would have got it back with interest.
So take the bag of gold from him and give it to the one who has ten.
For to the one who has, more will be given, and he will have in abundance; but from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away.
As for this worthless servant, throw him outside, into the darkness: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.'"
"When the Son of Man comes in his glory, escorted by all the angels, then he will sit on his throne of glory.
All the nations will be gathered before him; he will separate the people one from another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats:
he will place the sheep at his right and the goats at his left.
Then the King will say to those at his right, 'Come, you who are blessed by my Father, receive as your inheritance the Kingdom prepared for you since the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry, and you gave me food; I was thirsty, and you gave me drink; I was a stranger, and you welcomed me;
I was naked, and you clothed me; I was sick, and you visited me; I was in prison, and you came to me.'
Then the righteous will answer him, 'Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you? or thirsty and give you drink?
When did we see you a stranger and welcome you? or naked and clothe you?
When did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?'
And the King will answer them, 'Amen, I say to you: whatever you did for one of these least of my brothers, you did for me.'
Then he will say to those at his left, 'Depart from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry, and you gave me no food; I was thirsty, and you gave me no drink;
I was a stranger, and you did not welcome me; naked, and you did not clothe me; sick and in prison, and you did not visit me.'
Then they too will answer, 'Lord, when did we see you hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not serve you?'
He will answer them, 'Amen, I say to you: whatever you did not do for one of these least ones, you did not do for me.'
And these will go away to eternal punishment, but the righteous to eternal life."
When Jesus had finished all these discourses, he said to his disciples,
"You know that in two days it will be the Passover, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified."
Then the chief priests and the elders of the people gathered in the palace of the high priest, who was named Caiaphas,
and they took counsel to seize Jesus by cunning and put him to death.
But they said, "Not during the feast, to avoid a riot among the people."
While Jesus was at Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
a woman came to him with an alabaster jar of very costly perfume, and she poured it on the head of Jesus while he was at table.
When the disciples saw this, they were indignant, "Why this waste?
This perfume could have been sold for a great price and the money given to the poor."
But Jesus, aware of this, said to them, "Why do you trouble this woman? What she has done for me is a beautiful thing.
The poor you will always have with you; but me you will not always have.
In pouring this perfume on my body, she has prepared me for burial.
Amen, I say to you: wherever this Good News is proclaimed, in the whole world, what she has just done will also be told, in memory of her."
Then one of the Twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and said to them, "What are you willing to give me if I hand him over to you?" They paid him thirty pieces of silver.
And from that moment he looked for a favorable chance to hand him over.
On the first day of the feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus and asked, "Where do you want us to prepare the Passover meal for you?"
He said to them, "Go into the city to a certain man, and tell him, 'The Teacher says: My time is near; it is at your house that I want to celebrate the Passover with my disciples.'"
The disciples did as Jesus had commanded them and prepared the Passover.
When evening came, Jesus was at table with the Twelve.
During the meal he declared, "Amen, I say to you: one of you is going to hand me over."
Deeply grieved, they began to ask him one after another, "Surely it is not I, Lord?"
He answered, "The one who has dipped into the dish with me, that is the one who is going to hand me over.
The Son of Man is going away, as it is written of him; but woe to the man by whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would be better for that man if he had never been born."
Judas, the one who was betraying him, spoke up, "Surely it is not I, Rabbi?" Jesus answered him, "You have said so yourself."
During the meal, Jesus took bread, said the blessing, broke it, and giving it to his disciples, he said, "Take, eat: this is my body."
Then, taking a cup and giving thanks, he gave it to them, saying, "Drink from it, all of you,
for this is my blood, the blood of the covenant, poured out for the many for the forgiveness of sins.
I say to you: from now on I will not drink of this fruit of the vine until the day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father."
After singing the psalms, they set out for the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them, "This night I will be for all of you an occasion of falling, for it is written: 'I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.'
But once I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
Peter spoke up and said to him, "Even if all the others stumble because of you, I never will!"
Jesus declared to him, "Amen, I say to you: this very night, before the cock crows, you will deny me three times."
Peter said to him, "Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you." And all the disciples said the same.
Then Jesus came with them to an estate called Gethsemane. He said to the disciples, "Sit here, while I go over there to pray."
He took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and he began to feel sorrow and anguish.
Then he said to them, "My soul is sorrowful to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with me."
Going a little farther, he fell face down on the ground, praying, "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass far from me! Yet not as I will, but as you will."
He came back to the disciples and found them asleep. He said to Peter, "So, you did not have the strength to keep watch with me for one hour!
Keep watch and pray, so as not to enter into temptation: the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak."
Again, a second time, he went away to pray, "My Father, if this cup cannot pass without my drinking it, may your will be done!"
Then, coming back, he found them asleep again, for their eyes were heavy.
He left them, went away again, and prayed a third time, repeating the same words.
Then he came back to the disciples and said to them, "Are you still sleeping and resting? Behold, the hour is near when the Son of Man is handed over into the hands of sinners.
Get up! Let us go! Behold, the one who hands me over is approaching."
He was still speaking when Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived, and with him a large crowd, armed with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people.
The one who was betraying him had given them a sign, "The one I kiss is the man: arrest him."
At once, going up to Jesus, he said, "Greetings, Rabbi!" and he kissed him.
Jesus said to him, "Friend, do what you came to do." Then they stepped forward, laid hands on Jesus, and arrested him.
And behold, one of those with Jesus reached for his sword, drew it, struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
Jesus then said to him, "Put your sword back in its place, for all who take the sword will perish by the sword.
Do you think that I cannot call upon my Father, who would at once put at my disposal more than twelve legions of angels?
But then, how would the Scriptures be fulfilled? For it must happen this way."
At that moment Jesus said to the crowds, "Am I a robber, that you have come out to arrest me with swords and clubs? Day after day I sat teaching in the Temple, and you did not arrest me.
But all this has happened so that the writings of the prophets might be fulfilled." Then all the disciples abandoned him and fled.
Those who had arrested Jesus led him away to Caiaphas, the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered.
Peter followed him at a distance, as far as the courtyard of the high priest; he went inside and sat down with the guards, to see how it would end.
The chief priests and the whole Council were seeking false testimony against Jesus in order to have him put to death;
but they found none, although many false witnesses came forward. Finally two came forward
who declared, "This man said, 'I can destroy the sanctuary of God and rebuild it in three days.'"
The high priest stood up and said to Jesus, "Have you no answer? What do you say to the testimony these men bring against you?"
But Jesus kept silent. The high priest said to him, "I put you under oath, by the living God, to tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God."
Jesus answered him, "You have said so yourself! And I declare to you: from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Almighty and coming on the clouds of heaven."
Then the high priest tore his garments, saying, "He has blasphemed! What further need have we of witnesses? You have just heard the blasphemy.
What is your verdict?" They answered, "He deserves death."
Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists; others slapped him,
saying, "Prophesy for us, Christ: tell us who struck you."
Meanwhile Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. A servant girl came up to him and said, "You too were with Jesus the Galilean."
But he denied it before everyone, "I do not know what you mean."
As he was going out to the gateway, another servant girl saw him and said to those who were there, "This man was with Jesus of Nazareth."
Again Peter denied it with an oath, "I do not know the man."
A little later, those standing there came up and said to Peter, "Surely you too are one of them! Besides, your accent gives you away."
Then he began to call down curses and to swear, "I do not know the man!" And at once a cock crowed.
Peter remembered the word that Jesus had spoken, "Before the cock crows, you will deny me three times." He went outside and wept bitterly.
Early in the morning, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to have him put to death.
They bound him, led him away, and handed him over to Pontius Pilate, the governor.
Then Judas, who had betrayed him, seeing that Jesus was condemned, was struck with remorse and brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and the elders,
saying, "I have sinned: I have betrayed innocent blood." They replied, "What is that to us? That is your concern."
Then, throwing the pieces of silver into the sanctuary, he withdrew and went off and hanged himself.
The chief priests picked up the silver and said, "It is not lawful to put it into the Temple treasury, since it is the price of blood."
After consulting together, they used the money to buy the Potter's Field, as a burial place for foreigners.
This is why that field is called, to this very day, the Field of Blood.
Thus was fulfilled the word of the prophet Jeremiah: They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one who was priced by the sons of Israel,
and they gave them for the Potter's Field, as the Lord had commanded me.
Jesus stood before the governor, who questioned him, "Are you the king of the Jews?" Jesus declared, "It is you who say so."
And while the chief priests and the elders were accusing him, he made no reply.
Then Pilate said to him, "Do you not hear all the testimony they bring against you?"
But Jesus did not answer him on a single point, so that the governor was greatly astonished.
At each feast the governor was accustomed to release one prisoner, the one the crowd demanded.
Now they had at that time a well-known prisoner named Barabbas.
So when the crowd had gathered, Pilate said to them, "Whom do you want me to release for you: Barabbas, or Jesus, the one called Christ?"
For he knew that it was out of envy that they had handed Jesus over.
While he was seated on the tribunal, his wife sent word to him, "Have nothing to do with the case of that righteous man, for today, in a dream, I have suffered greatly because of him."
But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds to demand Barabbas and to have Jesus put to death.
The governor spoke to them again, "Which of the two do you want me to release for you?" They answered, "Barabbas!"
Pilate said to them, "What then shall I do with Jesus, the one called Christ?"
They answered, "Let him be crucified!" The governor said, "What evil has he done?" But they cried out all the more, "Let him be crucified!"
Seeing that he was getting nowhere, but that the uproar was growing, Pilate took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying, "I am innocent of this blood. That is your concern."
And all the people answered, "Let his blood be on us and on our children!"
Then he released Barabbas for them; and as for Jesus, he had him flogged and handed him over to be crucified.
The governor's soldiers led Jesus into the praetorium, the governor's palace, and gathered the whole cohort around him.
They stripped him of his garments and put a scarlet cloak on him.
They wove a crown of thorns, placed it on his head, and put a reed in his right hand. Then, kneeling before him, they mocked him, "Hail, king of the Jews!"
They spat on him, took the reed, and struck him on the head.
When they had finished mocking him, they took off the cloak, put his own garments back on him, and led him away to crucify him.
On the way out, they came upon a man of Cyrene named Simon, and they forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.
When they came to the place called Golgotha, that is, Place of the Skull,
they gave Jesus wine mixed with gall to drink; but when he had tasted it, he would not drink it.
After crucifying him, they divided his garments among them by casting lots.
Then they sat down there to keep watch over him.
Above his head they placed the charge against him, written thus: "This is Jesus, the king of the Jews."
Two robbers were crucified with him, one on the right and one on the left.
Those who passed by hurled insults at him, shaking their heads
and saying, "You who destroy the sanctuary and rebuild it in three days, save yourself, if you are the Son of God, and come down from the cross!"
In the same way the chief priests, with the scribes and the elders, mocked him,
"He saved others, and he cannot save himself! He is the king of Israel: let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in him!
He put his trust in God. Let God deliver him now, if he loves him! For he said, 'I am the Son of God.'"
The robbers crucified with him insulted him in the same way.
From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness came over the whole land.
About three o'clock, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, "Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?", that is, "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"
When they heard this, some of those standing there said, "He is calling Elijah!"
At once one of them ran to take a sponge, soaked it in sour wine, put it on the end of a reed, and gave it to him to drink.
But the others said, "Wait! Let us see whether Elijah will come to save him."
Jesus, crying out again in a loud voice, gave up his spirit.
And behold, the veil of the sanctuary was torn in two, from top to bottom; the earth quaked, the rocks split,
the tombs opened, and the bodies of many saints who had died were raised:
coming out of the tombs after the resurrection of Jesus, they entered the holy city and appeared to many people.
At the sight of the earthquake and all that was happening, the centurion and those keeping watch over Jesus with him were gripped by great fear and said, "Truly, this man was the Son of God!"
There were also many women there, watching from a distance; they had followed Jesus from Galilee to serve him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph arrived, who had also become a disciple of Jesus.
He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus, and Pilate ordered that it be given to him.
Joseph took the body, wrapped it in a clean shroud,
and laid it in the new tomb that he had had cut for himself in the rock. Then he rolled a great stone across the entrance of the tomb and went away.
Now Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, seated opposite the tomb.
The next day, the Sabbath, the chief priests and the Pharisees went together to Pilate
and said to him, "Sir, we remember that this impostor said, while he was still alive, 'After three days I will rise.'

So order that the tomb be guarded until the third day; otherwise his disciples may come and steal the body and tell the people, 'He is risen from the dead.' This last deception would be worse than the first."
Pilate said to them, "You have a guard. Go, make it as secure as you know how."
So they went and secured the tomb: they sealed the stone and posted the guard.

titres.titre: The sending of the Eleven on mission

versets.t: After the Sabbath, at dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
And behold, there was a great earthquake: the angel of the Lord came down from heaven, went and rolled back the stone, and sat on it.
He had the appearance of lightning, and his garment was white as snow.
The guards, in their terror, began to tremble and became like dead men.
The angel spoke and said to the women, "You, do not be afraid! I know that you are looking for Jesus, the crucified one.
He is not here, for he is risen, as he said. Come and see the place where he was lying.
Then go quickly and tell his disciples, 'He is risen from the dead, and behold, he is going ahead of you into Galilee: there you will see him.' This is what I had to tell you."
Quickly they left the tomb, filled with both fear and great joy, and they ran to bring the news to his disciples.
And behold, Jesus came to meet them, "Greetings!" They approached, took hold of his feet, and knelt before him.
Then Jesus said to them, "Do not be afraid! Go and tell my brothers that they must go to Galilee: it is there that they will see me."
While they were on their way, some of the guards went into the city to report to the chief priests everything that had happened.
These gathered with the elders; after taking counsel, they gave the soldiers a large sum of money,
with this instruction, "You are to say this: 'His disciples came by night and stole him while we were asleep.'
And if this comes to the governor's ears, we will satisfy him and keep you out of trouble."
The soldiers took the money and did as they were instructed. And this story has been spread among the Jews to this very day.
As for the eleven disciples, they went to Galilee, to the mountain that Jesus had indicated to them.
When they saw him, they knelt before him; but some had doubts.
Jesus approached and spoke these words to them, "All power has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
Go therefore! Make disciples of all the nations: baptize them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit;
teach them to observe all that I have commanded you. And behold, I am with you always, until the end of the world."

titres.titre: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus

versets.t: The beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in the prophet Isaiah: "Behold, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, to prepare your way.
A voice cries out in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight."
John appeared, baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of conversion for the forgiveness of sins.
All Judea and all the people of Jerusalem went out to him, and they were baptized by him in the Jordan, confessing their sins.
John was clothed in camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and he fed on locusts and wild honey.
He proclaimed: "After me comes one who is stronger than I, and I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the strap of his sandals.
I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."
In those days, Jesus came from Nazareth in Galilee, and he was baptized by John in the Jordan.
The moment he came up out of the water, he saw the heavens torn open and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.
And a voice came from heaven: "You are my beloved Son; in you I have placed all my love."
At once, the Spirit drove Jesus out into the wilderness.
In the wilderness he stayed forty days, tempted by Satan. He lived among the wild beasts, and the angels waited on him.
After John was arrested, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the Good News of God.
He said: "The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near. Be converted and believe in the Good News."
As he was passing along the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and his brother Andrew casting their nets into the sea, for they were fishermen.
Jesus said to them: "Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of men."
At once they left their nets and followed him.
A little farther on, he saw James, son of Zebedee, and his brother John, who were mending their nets in the boat.
At once he called them; and leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men, they went off after him.
They entered Capernaum. At once, on the Sabbath day, Jesus went to the synagogue and began to teach.
They were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as one who has authority, and not like the scribes.
Now there happened to be in their synagogue a man tormented by an unclean spirit, who began to cry out:
"What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God."
Jesus rebuked him: "Be silent, and come out of this man!"
The unclean spirit shook the man violently and came out of him with a loud cry.
They were all seized with amazement and asked one another: "What is this? A new teaching, given with authority! He even commands the unclean spirits, and they obey him!"
And his fame at once spread everywhere throughout the whole region of Galilee.
As soon as they left the synagogue, they went, with James and John, to the house of Simon and Andrew.
Now Simon's mother-in-law was in bed with a fever. At once they told Jesus about her.
He came, took her by the hand and helped her up. The fever left her, and she began to wait on them.
That evening, after sunset, they brought him all who were sick and those possessed by demons.
The whole town was gathered at the door.
He healed many who were suffering from all kinds of diseases, and he drove out many demons; but he would not let the demons speak, because they knew who he was.
The next day, well before dawn, Jesus got up, went out and made his way to a deserted place, where he began to pray.
Simon and his companions went to look for him.
When they found him, they said to him: "Everyone is looking for you."
But he answered them: "Let us go elsewhere, to the neighboring villages, so that I may proclaim the Good News there too; for that is why I have come."
So he traveled throughout all Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and driving out demons.
A leper came to him and pleaded with him, falling on his knees: "If you are willing, you can make me clean."
Moved with compassion, Jesus reached out his hand, touched him and said: "I am willing. Be clean."
At once the leprosy left him, and he was made clean.
Sternly, Jesus sent him away at once,
saying to him: "See that you say nothing to anyone; but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses prescribed: it will be a testimony to them."

But once he had gone, the man began to proclaim it and to spread the news, so that Jesus could no longer enter a town openly. He stayed outside in deserted places; and people came to him from everywhere.
A few days later, Jesus came back to Capernaum, and it was reported that he was at home.
So many people gathered that there was no longer any room, not even in front of the door; and he was speaking the word to them.
Some people came, bringing him a paralytic carried by four men.
Since they could not get near him because of the crowd, they opened the roof above the place where he was and, through the opening, they lowered the mat on which the paralytic was lying.
Seeing their faith, Jesus said to the paralytic: "My child, your sins are forgiven."
Now some scribes were sitting there, reasoning in their hearts:
"Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins but God alone?"
At once Jesus perceived in his spirit that they were reasoning in this way, and he said to them: "Why do you hold such thoughts in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say to the paralytic, Your sins are forgiven, or to say, Get up, take your mat and walk?
Well then, so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins,"
"I command you," he said to the paralytic, "get up, take your mat and go home."
The man got up, took his mat at once and walked out in front of everyone, so that they were all astounded and gave glory to God, saying: "We have never seen anything like this."
Again Jesus went out beside the sea; the whole crowd came to him, and he taught them.
As he passed by, he saw Levi, son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax booth. He said to him: "Follow me." The man got up and followed him.
While Jesus was at table in his house, many tax collectors and sinners took their places with him and his disciples, for there were many who followed him.
When the scribes of the party of the pharisees saw that he was eating with sinners and tax collectors, they said to his disciples: "What! He eats with tax collectors and sinners?"
Hearing this, Jesus said to them: "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
Now the disciples of John and the pharisees were fasting. Some people came and said to Jesus: "Why do the disciples of John and those of the pharisees fast, while yours do not?"
Jesus answered them: "Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
But days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them; on that day they will fast.
No one sews a piece of new cloth onto an old garment; otherwise the new patch pulls away from the old, and the tear gets worse.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wine bursts the skins, and both the wine and the skins are lost. New wine, new skins!"
One Sabbath day, Jesus was passing through the grain fields; and as they went along, his disciples began to pluck the heads of grain.
The pharisees said to him: "Look! Why are they doing on the Sabbath what is not permitted?"
He answered them: "Have you never read what David did, one day when he was in need and hungry, he and his companions?
In the time of the high priest Abiathar, he entered the house of God and ate the bread of the offering, which only the priests are allowed to eat; and he even gave some to his companions."
And he said to them: "The Sabbath was made for man, and not man for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is master even of the Sabbath."

titres.titre: The Man with the Withered Hand

versets.t: Again Jesus entered the synagogue; there was a man there whose hand was withered.
They were watching him to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse him.
He said to the man with the withered hand: "Stand up, here, in the middle."
Then he said to them: "On the Sabbath day, is it permitted to do good or to do evil? To save a life or to destroy it?" But they were silent.
Then, looking around at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their hearts, he said to the man: "Stretch out your hand." He stretched it out, and his hand was made whole again.
Once they had gone out, the pharisees at once held counsel with the supporters of Herod against Jesus, to see how they might destroy him.
Jesus withdrew toward the sea with his disciples, and a great multitude followed him, from Galilee, from Judea,
from Jerusalem, from Idumea, from beyond the Jordan, and from the region of Tyre and Sidon: a great multitude who, having heard all that he was doing, came to him.
He told his disciples to keep a boat ready for him, so that the crowd would not crush him.
For he had healed so many people that all who suffered from any affliction were pressing in on him to touch him.
And the unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him and cried out: "You are the Son of God!"
But he strictly forbade them to make him known.
Then Jesus went up the mountain. He called those he wanted, and they came to him.
He appointed twelve, whom he named apostles, to be with him and to send them out to proclaim the Good News,
with the power to drive out demons.
So he appointed the Twelve: Simon, to whom he gave the name Peter,
James, son of Zebedee, and John, brother of James, to whom he gave the name Boanerges, that is, "sons of thunder",
Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James, son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot,
and Judas Iscariot, the very one who betrayed him.
Jesus came home, and again the crowd gathered, so that they could not even eat.
When his relatives heard of this, they came to take charge of him, for they said: "He has lost his mind."
The scribes who had come down from Jerusalem said: "He is possessed by Beelzebul," and: "It is by the prince of demons that he drives out demons."
So Jesus called them and spoke to them in parables: "How can Satan drive out Satan?
If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
If a household is divided against itself, that household will not be able to stand.
So if Satan rises up against himself and is divided, he cannot stand: it is the end of him.
But no one can enter a strong man's house and plunder his goods without first tying him up; only then will he plunder his house.
Amen, I say to you: everything will be forgiven the children of men, the sins and the blasphemies they utter.
But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never obtain forgiveness: he is guilty of an eternal sin."
Jesus said this because they were saying: "He is possessed by an unclean spirit."
Then his mother and his brothers arrived. Standing outside, they sent word to call him.
A crowd was sitting around him, and they told him: "Your mother and your brothers are outside, looking for you."
But he answered them: "Who is my mother? Who are my brothers?"
And looking around at those seated in a circle about him, he said: "Here are my mother and my brothers.
Whoever does the will of God, that is my brother, my sister, my mother."

titres.titre: The Seed and the Mustard Seed

versets.t: Again Jesus began to teach beside the sea. Such a large crowd gathered around him that he got into a boat and sat down in it, out on the water; and the whole crowd was on the shore, facing the sea.
He taught them many things in parables, and in his teaching he said to them:
"Listen! Behold, the sower went out to sow.
As he sowed, some seed fell along the path; the birds came and ate it.
Other seed fell on rocky ground, where it had little soil; it sprang up at once, because the soil was shallow;
but when the sun rose, it was scorched and, having no roots, it withered.
Other seed fell among thorns; the thorns grew up and choked it, and it bore no fruit.
And other seed fell on good soil; coming up and growing, it bore fruit: some thirty, some sixty, some a hundredfold."
And he added: "Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!"
When he was alone, those who were around him, together with the Twelve, questioned him about the parables.
He said to them: "To you the mystery of the kingdom of God is given; but to those outside, everything comes in parables,
so that they may look and look yet not see, hear and hear yet not understand; otherwise they would be converted and forgiven."
Then he said to them: "Do you not grasp this parable? How then will you understand all the others?
The sower sows the word.
There are those along the path where the word is sown: no sooner have they heard it than Satan comes and takes away the word sown in them.
And there are, likewise, those who receive the seed on rocky ground: as soon as they hear the word, they welcome it at once with joy,
but they have no roots in themselves; they are unstable; when distress or persecution comes because of the word, they fall away at once.
There are those who receive the seed among thorns: these are the ones who hear the word,
but the cares of the world, the lure of riches and other desires invade them and choke the word, which remains without fruit.
And there are those who received the seed on good soil: they hear the word, they welcome it and bear fruit, some thirty, some sixty, some a hundredfold."
He said to them: "Is a lamp brought in to be put under the basket or under the bed? Is it not to be put on the lampstand?
For there is nothing hidden that is not meant to be brought to light, nothing secret that is not meant to come into the open.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!"
He said to them: "Pay attention to what you hear. The measure you use will be used for you, and you will be given more still.
For to the one who has, more will be given; but from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away."
He said: "The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground:
whether he sleeps or rises, night and day, the seed sprouts and grows, he does not know how.
Of itself the earth produces fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
And as soon as the grain is ready, he puts in the sickle, for it is the time of harvest."
He said: "To what shall we compare the kingdom of God? By what parable shall we present it?
It is like a mustard seed: when it is sown in the ground, it is the smallest of all the seeds on earth;
but once sown, it comes up and becomes greater than all the plants of the garden, and it spreads such large branches that the birds of the sky can shelter in its shade."
With many parables like these he proclaimed the word to them, as much as they were able to hear it;
he spoke to them only in parables, but to his own disciples he explained everything in private.
That day, when evening came, he said to them: "Let us cross over to the other side."
Leaving the crowd, they took him with them in the boat, just as he was; and other boats went along with him.
Then a violent storm arose, and the waves broke over the boat, so that it was already filling up.
He was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. They woke him and said to him: "Teacher, we are perishing, and you do not care?"
Awakened, he rebuked the wind and said to the sea: "Silence! Be still!" The wind dropped, and there was a great calm.
Then he said to them: "Why are you afraid? Do you still have no faith?" Seized with great fear, they said to one another: "Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?"

titres.titre: The Daughter of Jairus and the Sick Woman

versets.t: They arrived on the other side of the sea, in the country of the Gerasenes.
No sooner had Jesus stepped out of the boat than a man possessed by an unclean spirit came out of the tombs to meet him.
He lived among the tombs, and no one could restrain him any longer, even with a chain:
he had often been bound with shackles and chains, but he had snapped the chains and broken the shackles, and no one had the strength to subdue him.
Constantly, night and day, among the tombs and on the mountains, he cried out and gashed himself with stones.
Seeing Jesus from a distance, he ran up and fell down before him
and cried out in a loud voice: "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I implore you by God, do not torment me!"
For Jesus was saying to him: "Unclean spirit, come out of this man!"
He asked him: "What is your name?" The man answered: "My name is Legion, for we are many."
And he pleaded with him insistently not to drive them out of the country.
Now there was there, on the mountainside, a large herd of pigs feeding.
The unclean spirits pleaded with Jesus: "Send us into the pigs; let us enter them."
He gave them leave. Coming out of the man, the unclean spirits entered the pigs, and the herd rushed down the cliff into the sea: about two thousand animals, which drowned there.
The herdsmen fled and carried the news to the town and the countryside. The people came to see what had happened.
When they reached Jesus, they saw the possessed man sitting there, clothed and in his right mind, the man who had had the legion; and they were seized with fear.
Those who had seen it told them what had happened to the possessed man and to the pigs.
Then they began to plead with Jesus to leave their territory.
As he was getting back into the boat, the man who had been possessed pleaded to stay with him.
Jesus did not allow it, but said to him: "Go home to your own people, and tell them all that the Lord has done for you, and how he has had mercy on you."
The man went off and began to proclaim in the Decapolis all that Jesus had done for him; and everyone was amazed.
When Jesus had again crossed over to the other side, a great crowd gathered around him; he was beside the sea.
Then comes one of the leaders of the synagogue, named Jairus. Seeing him, he falls at his feet
and pleads with him urgently: "My little daughter is at the point of death; come and lay your hands on her, so that she may be saved and live."
Jesus set off with him. A great crowd followed him and pressed in on him from all sides.
Now there was a woman there who had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years.
She had suffered greatly at the hands of many doctors, and had spent all she had without any improvement; on the contrary, her condition had grown worse.
Having heard about Jesus, she came up behind him in the crowd and touched his cloak.
For she said to herself: "If I only touch his clothes, I will be saved."
At once the flow of her blood stopped, and she felt in her body that she was cured of her affliction.
At once Jesus, aware that power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd and asked: "Who touched my clothes?"
His disciples said to him: "You see the crowd pressing in on you from all sides, and you ask, Who touched me?"
But he kept looking around to see the woman who had done this.
Then the woman, trembling with fear, knowing what had happened to her, came and threw herself at his feet and told him the whole truth.
Jesus said to her: "My daughter, your faith has saved you: go in peace, and be cured of your affliction."
He was still speaking when people came from the house of the synagogue leader and said: "Your daughter is dead; why trouble the Teacher any further?"
But Jesus, overhearing these words, said to the synagogue leader: "Do not be afraid; only believe."
And he let no one accompany him except Peter, James, and John, the brother of James.
They arrive at the house of the synagogue leader; Jesus sees the commotion, the people weeping and wailing loudly.
He goes in and says to them: "Why this commotion and these tears? The child is not dead: she is asleep."
And they laughed at him. But he, having put everyone out, takes the child's father and mother, and those who were with him, and enters the room where the child was.
He took the child by the hand and said to her: "Talitha koum," which means: "Little girl, I say to you, get up!"
At once the girl stood up and began to walk, for she was twelve years old. And they were overcome with utter amazement.
Jesus firmly ordered that no one should know of it, and he told them to give the child something to eat.

titres.titre: The Death of John the Baptist

versets.t: Setting out from there, Jesus came to his hometown, and his disciples followed him.

On the Sabbath day, he began to teach in the synagogue. Many who heard him were astonished and said: "Where does he get all this? What is this wisdom that has been given to him, and these great miracles worked by his hands?
Is he not the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, Joses, Jude and Simon? Are not his sisters here among us?" And he was for them an occasion of stumbling.
Jesus said to them: "A prophet is despised only in his hometown, among his relatives and in his own house."
And he could work no miracle there, except to heal a few sick people by laying his hands on them;
and he was amazed at their lack of faith. He went around the neighboring villages, teaching.
He called the Twelve and began to send them out two by two, giving them authority over the unclean spirits.
He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff: no bread, no bag, no money in their belts,
but to go wearing sandals and not to put on two tunics.
He said to them: "When you enter a house, stay there until you leave.
And if in any place they do not welcome you and do not listen to you, leave there, shaking the dust off your feet: it will be a testimony against them."
They set out and proclaimed that people should be converted.
They drove out many demons, anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.
King Herod heard about Jesus, for his name had become well known. People were saying: "John the Baptist has risen from the dead, and that is why the power of miracles is at work in him."
Others said: "It is Elijah"; others again: "It is a prophet, like one of the prophets of old."
When Herod heard this, he said: "This John, whom I had beheaded, it is he: he has risen!"
For it was Herod himself who had sent to arrest John and had him chained in prison, because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, whom he had married.
For John kept saying to Herod: "It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife."
Herodias held a grudge against him and wanted to have him put to death, but she could not,
for Herod feared John: he knew that he was a righteous and holy man, and he protected him. When he listened to him, he was greatly perplexed, and yet he liked to listen to him.
Then came a favorable day: for his birthday, Herod gave a banquet for the great men of his court, his officers and the leading people of Galilee.
The daughter of Herodias came in and danced; she pleased Herod and his guests. The king then said to the girl: "Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you."
And he swore this oath to her: "Whatever you ask me, I will give you, up to half my kingdom."
She went out and said to her mother: "What shall I ask for?" Her mother answered: "The head of John the Baptist."
At once she hurried back to the king and made her request: "I want you to give me, right now, on a platter, the head of John the Baptist."
The king was very distressed; but because of his oath and his guests, he did not want to refuse her.
At once he sent a guard with orders to bring John's head. The guard went and beheaded him in the prison;
he brought his head on a platter, gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
When John's disciples heard of this, they came and took his body and laid it in a tomb.
The apostles gathered around Jesus and told him all that they had done and taught.
He said to them: "Come away by yourselves to a deserted place, and rest a while." For there were so many coming and going that they did not even have time to eat.
So they set off in the boat, by themselves, toward a deserted place.
Many saw them leaving and realized where they were going; from all the towns, people ran there on foot and arrived ahead of them.
As he stepped ashore, Jesus saw a great crowd. He was moved with compassion for them, for they were like sheep without a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things.
When it was already late, his disciples came up to him and said: "This place is deserted, and it is already late;
send them away, so that they may go to the surrounding farms and villages to buy themselves something to eat."
He answered them: "Give them something to eat yourselves." They said to him: "Are we to spend two hundred pieces of silver to buy them bread to eat?"
He said to them: "How many loaves do you have? Go and see." When they had found out, they said to him: "Five, and two fish."
Then he ordered them to have everyone sit down in groups on the green grass.
They sat down in rows of a hundred and of fifty.

Taking the five loaves and the two fish, he looked up to heaven, spoke the blessing, broke the loaves and gave them to the disciples to serve to the crowd; he also divided the two fish among them all.
They all ate and were satisfied,
and they gathered up twelve baskets full of broken pieces of bread and fish.
Those who had eaten the loaves were five thousand men.
At once Jesus made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, toward Bethsaida, while he himself dismissed the crowd.
After sending them away, he went off to the mountain to pray.
When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.
Seeing that they were straining at the oars, for the wind was against them, he came toward them near the end of the night, walking on the sea, and he meant to pass them by.
When they saw him walking on the sea, they thought it was a ghost and cried out;
for they all saw him and were terrified. But at once he spoke to them: "Take heart! It is I; do not be afraid."
He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind dropped. They were utterly astounded,
for they had not understood about the loaves: their hearts were hardened.
Having completed the crossing, they came to land at Gennesaret and moored there.
As soon as they got out of the boat, the people recognized Jesus;
they hurried through the whole region and began to carry the sick on their mats to wherever they heard he was.
Wherever he went, into villages, towns or farms, they laid the sick in the marketplaces and pleaded with him to let them touch even the fringe of his cloak; and all who touched it were saved.

titres.titre: The Healing of the Deaf Man

versets.t: The pharisees and some scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus.
They saw some of his disciples eating their meal with unclean hands, that is, unwashed.
For the pharisees, and all the Jews, do not eat without carefully washing their hands, holding to the tradition of the elders;
and on returning from the marketplace, they do not eat without performing ablutions. They cling to many other traditional customs as well: the rinsing of cups, jugs and dishes.
So the pharisees and the scribes asked him: "Why do your disciples not follow the tradition of the elders, but eat their meal with unclean hands?"
He answered them: "Isaiah rightly prophesied about you hypocrites, as it is written: This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
In vain do they worship me, teaching as doctrines nothing but human precepts.
You set aside the commandment of God to hold on to human tradition."
And he added: "How well you set aside the commandment of God in order to keep your own tradition!
For Moses said: Honor your father and your mother, and: Whoever curses his father or mother must be put to death.
But you say: If a man declares to his father or his mother, Whatever help you might have had from me is corban, that is, an offering to God,
then you no longer let him do anything for his father or mother.
So you nullify the word of God by the tradition you hand down. And you do many other things like this."
Then he called the crowd to him again and said to them: "Listen to me, all of you, and understand.
Nothing that enters a person from outside can make him unclean; but what comes out of a person, that is what makes him unclean."
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!
When he had gone into the house, away from the crowd, his disciples questioned him about this puzzling saying.
He said to them: "Are you also without understanding? Do you not see that nothing that enters a person from outside can make him unclean,
since it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and then passes out into the latrine?" Thus he declared all foods clean.
He said: "What comes out of a person, that is what makes him unclean.
For it is from within, from the human heart, that evil thoughts come: sexual immorality, thefts, murders,
adulteries, greed, malice, deceit, licentiousness, envy, slander, pride, folly.
All this evil comes from within and makes a person unclean."
Setting out from there, he went off to the territory of Tyre. He entered a house, wanting no one to know it, but he could not remain hidden.
At once a woman, whose little daughter was possessed by an unclean spirit, heard about him; she came and threw herself at his feet.
This woman was Greek, a Syrophoenician by birth. She begged him to drive the demon out of her daughter.
He said to her: "Let the children first be satisfied, for it is not right to take the children's bread and throw it to the little dogs."
She answered him: "Lord, but the little dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs."
Then he said to her: "Because of this word, go: the demon has left your daughter."
She went home and found the child lying on the bed: the demon had left her.
Jesus left the territory of Tyre and returned, by way of Sidon, to the Sea of Galilee, through the territory of the Decapolis.
They bring him a deaf man who could barely speak, and they plead with him to lay his hand on him.
Taking him aside, away from the crowd, he put his fingers into the man's ears, and with his saliva he touched his tongue.
Then, looking up to heaven, he sighed and said to him: "Ephphatha," that is: "Be opened!"
His ears were opened, his tongue was loosened, and he spoke plainly.
Jesus ordered them to tell no one; but the more he ordered them, the more they proclaimed it.
They were utterly astonished and said: "He has done all things well: he makes the deaf hear and the mute speak!"
In those days, as there was again a great crowd with nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples and said to them:
"I am moved with compassion for this crowd, for they have already stayed with me three days and have nothing to eat.
If I send them home hungry, they will faint on the way; and some of them have come from far off."
His disciples answered him: "Where could anyone find enough bread to satisfy them here, in a deserted place?"
He asked them: "How many loaves do you have?" They said: "Seven."
Then he orders the crowd to sit down on the ground. Taking the seven loaves, he gave thanks, broke them and gave them to his disciples to serve; and they served them to the crowd.
They also had a few small fish; having blessed them, he said to serve these as well.
They ate and were satisfied, and they took up seven baskets of the leftover pieces.
There were about four thousand of them. Then Jesus sent them away.
At once he got into the boat with his disciples and came to the region of Dalmanutha.
The pharisees came out and began to argue with him; to test him, they asked him for a sign from heaven.
With a deep sigh, he said: "Why does this generation demand a sign? Amen, I say to you: no sign will be given to this generation."
He left them, got back into the boat and crossed to the other side.
The disciples had forgotten to bring bread; they had only one loaf with them in the boat.
Now Jesus gave them this warning: "Keep your eyes open; beware of the leaven of the pharisees and the leaven of Herod."
And they said to one another: "It is because we have no bread."
Aware of this, Jesus said to them: "Why are you arguing about having no bread? Do you not yet grasp or understand? Are your hearts hardened?
You have eyes and do not see, ears and do not hear! Do you not remember?
When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of pieces did you take up?" They said to him: "Twelve."
"And for the seven loaves shared among the four thousand, how many baskets full of pieces did you take up?" They said: "Seven."
Then he said to them: "Do you not yet understand?"
They arrive at Bethsaida. They bring him a blind man and plead with him to touch him.
Taking the blind man by the hand, he led him out of the village. He put saliva on his eyes, laid his hands on him and asked him: "Do you see anything?"
The man looked up and said: "I see people: I see them like trees, but walking."
Jesus laid his hands on the man's eyes again; the man saw clearly, he was healed, and he saw everything distinctly.
Jesus sent him home, saying: "Do not even go into the village."
Jesus went off, with his disciples, to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way, he questioned his disciples: "Who do people say that I am?"
They answered him: "John the Baptist; for others, Elijah; for others, one of the prophets."
He questioned them: "And you, who do you say that I am?" Peter spoke up: "You are the Christ."
Then he strictly forbade them to speak to anyone about him.
He began to teach them that the Son of Man had to suffer greatly, be rejected by the elders, the chief priests and the scribes, be put to death and, three days later, rise again.
He said this openly. Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
But he, turning around and looking at his disciples, reprimanded Peter: "Get behind me, Satan! Your thoughts are not those of God, but those of men."
Then he called the crowd together with his disciples and said to them: "If anyone wants to follow me, let him deny himself, take up his cross and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake and for the Good News will save it.
What good is it for a man to gain the whole world, if he loses his life?
What can a man give in exchange for his life?
Whoever is ashamed of me and of my words before this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man too will be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father, with the holy angels."

titres.titre: The Coming of the Kingdom of God
The Boy with a Mute Spirit

versets.t: He said to them: "Amen, I say to you: among those standing here, some will not taste death before they have seen the kingdom of God come with power."
Six days later, Jesus takes Peter, James and John with him and leads them, just them, up a high mountain by themselves. And he was transfigured before them:
his clothes became dazzling, so white that no launderer on earth could bleach them so.
Elijah appeared to them, along with Moses, in conversation with Jesus.
Peter spoke up and said to Jesus: "Teacher, it is good that we are here! Let us set up three tents: one for you, one for Moses, one for Elijah."
He did not know what to say, for they were seized with fear.
A cloud came, overshadowing them, and from the cloud came a voice: "This is my beloved Son: listen to him!"
At once, looking around, they no longer saw anyone: Jesus alone was with them.
As they came down the mountain, he ordered them to tell no one what they had seen, until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
They kept this word to themselves, while wondering among themselves what "to rise from the dead" meant.
And they questioned him: "Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
He answered them: "Yes, Elijah does come first to restore all things. But then, how is it written of the Son of Man that he must suffer greatly and be despised?
Well, I say to you: Elijah has come, and they treated him as they pleased, as it is written of him."
When they came back to the disciples, they saw a great crowd around them, and scribes arguing with them.
As soon as it saw Jesus, the whole crowd was overcome with awe and ran up to greet him.
He asked them: "What are you arguing about with them?"
Someone in the crowd answered him: "Teacher, I brought you my son: he has a mute spirit.
Whenever it seizes him, it throws him to the ground; the boy foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth and becomes rigid. I asked your disciples to drive it out, but they did not have the strength."
In answer, Jesus said to them: "Faithless generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him to me."
They brought him to him. As soon as it saw Jesus, the spirit shook the boy violently, and he fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.
Jesus asked the father: "How long has this been happening to him?" He answered: "Since childhood.
Often the spirit has thrown him into fire and into water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have pity on us and help us!"
Jesus said to him: "If you can!... Everything is possible for the one who believes."
At once the boy's father cried out: "I believe! Help my lack of faith!"
Seeing the crowd running up, Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit: "Deaf and mute spirit, I command you, come out of this boy and never enter him again!"
The spirit shrieked, shook the boy violently and came out. The boy became like a corpse, so that many said: "He is dead."
But Jesus, taking him by the hand, raised him up, and he stood.
Once he had gone into the house, his disciples asked him privately: "Why could we not drive it out?"
He said to them: "This kind can come out only through prayer and fasting."
Setting out from there, they passed through Galilee, and Jesus did not want anyone to know it,
for he was teaching his disciples. He said to them: "The Son of Man is handed over into the hands of men; they will put him to death, and three days after his death he will rise."
But they did not understand this saying, and they were afraid to question him.
They came to Capernaum. Once in the house, he asked them: "What were you arguing about on the way?"
They were silent, for on the way they had argued among themselves about who was the greatest.
Sitting down, he called the Twelve and said to them: "If anyone wants to be first, let him be the last of all and the servant of all."
Then, taking a little child, he placed him in their midst and, having embraced him, he said to them:
"Whoever welcomes in my name a child like this one welcomes me; and whoever welcomes me welcomes not me but the one who sent me."
John said to him: "Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us."
Jesus answered: "Do not stop him, for no one who works a miracle in my name can, right after, speak evil of me.
Whoever is not against us is for us.
And whoever gives you a cup of water because you belong to Christ, amen, I say to you, he will not lose his reward.
Whoever causes the fall of one of these little ones who believe in me, it would be better for him to have a great millstone tied around his neck and to be thrown into the sea.
If your hand is an occasion of stumbling for you, cut it off: it is better for you to enter life maimed than to go, with both your hands, into Gehenna, into the fire that never goes out,
where the worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
And if your foot is an occasion of stumbling for you, cut it off: it is better for you to enter life lame than to be thrown, with both your feet, into Gehenna,
where the worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
And if your eye is an occasion of stumbling for you, tear it out: it is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to be thrown, with both your eyes, into Gehenna,
where the worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
For everyone will be salted with fire.
Salt is good; but if the salt loses its flavor, how will you restore it? Have salt in yourselves, and live in peace with one another."

titres.titre: The Request of James and John

versets.t: Setting out from there, Jesus came into the territory of Judea, beyond the Jordan. Again the crowds gathered around him and, as was his custom, he began to teach them again.
Some pharisees came up and asked him, to test him: "Is it lawful for a husband to divorce his wife?"
He answered them: "What did Moses command you?"
They said: "Moses allowed a man to write a certificate of divorce and to send her away."
Jesus replied: "It was because of the hardness of your hearts that he wrote you this commandment.
But at the beginning of creation, God made them male and female.
For this reason a man will leave his father and mother to be joined to his wife,
and the two will become one flesh. So they are no longer two, but one flesh.
What God has joined together, then, let no one separate!"
At home, the disciples questioned him again about this.
He said to them: "Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her;
and if a woman divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery."
People were bringing little children to him for him to touch; but the disciples sharply turned them away.
When he saw this, Jesus was indignant and said to them: "Let the little children come to me; do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to those who are like them.
Amen, I say to you: whoever does not welcome the kingdom of God like a little child will not enter it."
He took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hands on them.
As Jesus was setting out on the road, a man ran up, knelt before him and asked him: "Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
Jesus said to him: "Why do you call me good? No one is good but God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not commit murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not defraud anyone, honor your father and your mother."
The man answered: "Teacher, all this I have kept since my youth."
Jesus looked at him and loved him; then he said to him: "One thing you lack: go, sell what you have, give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me."
But at these words the man's face fell, and he went away sad, for he had great possessions.
Looking around, Jesus said to his disciples: "How hard it will be for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of God!"
The disciples were bewildered at his words. But Jesus went on: "My children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God."
More and more astounded, they said to one another: "Then who can be saved?"
Jesus looked at them and said: "For men it is impossible, but not for God; for everything is possible for God."
Peter began to say to him: "Look, we have left everything to follow you."
Jesus answered: "Amen, I say to you: no one who has left, for my sake and for the Good News, a house, brothers, sisters, a mother, a father, children or fields,
will fail to receive, even now, in the present time, a hundred times more, houses, brothers, sisters, mothers, children and fields, amid persecutions, and, in the world to come, eternal life.
Many who are first will be last, and the last first."

They were on the road going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them. They were filled with dread, and those who followed were afraid. Taking the Twelve aside again, he began to tell them what was going to happen to him:
"Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes; they will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles.
They will mock him, spit on him, flog him and kill him; and three days later he will rise."
James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to him and said to him: "Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask you."
He said to them: "What do you want me to do for you?"
They answered: "Grant us to sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your glory."
Jesus said to them: "You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I am going to drink, be baptized with the baptism with which I am going to be baptized?"
They said to him: "We can." Jesus replied: "The cup that I am going to drink, you will drink; and the baptism with which I am going to be baptized, you will be baptized with.
But as for sitting at my right or my left, it is not mine to grant: those places are for those for whom they are prepared."
The other ten, who had heard, were indignant at James and John.
Jesus called them and said to them: "You know that those regarded as rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great ones make their authority felt.
Among you it must not be so. On the contrary, whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant,
and whoever wants to be first among you will be the slave of all.
For the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for the many."
They came to Jericho. As Jesus was leaving the town with his disciples and a large crowd, a blind beggar, Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, was sitting by the roadside.
Hearing that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out: "Jesus, Son of David, have pity on me!"
Many rebuked him to make him be quiet, but he cried out all the more: "Son of David, have pity on me!"
Jesus stopped and said: "Call him." They called the blind man, telling him: "Take heart! Get up, he is calling you."
Throwing off his cloak, he sprang up and came to Jesus.
Jesus said to him: "What do you want me to do for you?" The blind man answered: "Rabbouni, let me see again!"
Jesus said to him: "Go, your faith has saved you." At once he regained his sight and followed Jesus along the road.

titres.titre: Jesus Drives the Merchants from the Temple

versets.t: As they were approaching Jerusalem, near Bethphage and Bethany, toward the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two of his disciples,
saying to them: "Go to the village ahead of you. As soon as you enter it, you will find a colt tied up, one that no one has yet ridden. Untie it and bring it.
And if anyone says to you, Why are you doing that? answer: The Lord needs it, but he will send it back here at once."
They went off, found the colt tied up outside, near a door, in the street, and they untied it.
Some people standing there said to them: "What are you doing, untying that colt?"
They answered as Jesus had told them, and they were allowed to go on.
They brought the colt to Jesus, threw their cloaks over it, and Jesus sat on it.
Many spread their cloaks on the road, others leafy branches they had cut in the fields.
Those who walked ahead and those who followed cried out: "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming kingdom of David our father! Hosanna in the highest heavens!"
Jesus entered Jerusalem, into the Temple. After looking at everything around him, since the hour was already late, he went out to Bethany with the Twelve.
The next day, as they were leaving Bethany, he was hungry.

Noticing from a distance a fig tree covered with leaves, he went up to it to see if he might find anything on it; but when he reached it, he found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.
Then he said to the fig tree: "May no one ever again eat fruit from you!" And his disciples heard it.

They came to Jerusalem. Entering the Temple, Jesus began to drive out those who were selling and buying in the Temple; he overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those who sold doves,
and he would not let anyone carry anything through the Temple.
And he taught them: "Is it not written: My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations? But you have made it a den of robbers!"
The chief priests and the scribes heard of this, and they were looking for a way to destroy him; for they feared him, because the whole crowd was astonished at his teaching.
When evening came, Jesus and his disciples went out of the town.
As they passed by early in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered to the roots.
Remembering the word, Peter said to Jesus: "Rabbi, look: the fig tree you cursed has withered."
Jesus answered them: "Have faith in God!
Amen, I say to you: if anyone says to this mountain, Be lifted up and thrown into the sea, without doubting in his heart but believing that what he says will happen, it will be granted him.
That is why I tell you: whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have already received it, and it will be granted you.
And when you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may also forgive you your sins.
But if you do not forgive, your Father in heaven will not forgive you your sins either."
They came back to Jerusalem. As Jesus was walking about in the Temple, the chief priests, the scribes and the elders came up to him
and said to him: "By what authority are you doing these things? Who gave you the authority to do them?"
Jesus said to them: "I will ask you a single question; answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
Was the baptism of John from heaven or from men? Answer me."
They reasoned among themselves: "If we say, From heaven, he will say, Why then did you not believe him?
But are we to say, From men?" They were afraid of the crowd, for everyone held that John was a true prophet.
So they answered Jesus: "We do not know." And Jesus said to them: "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."
Jesus began to speak to them in parables: "A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress in it and built a tower; then he leased it to tenants and went away on a journey.
When the time came, he sent a servant to the tenants to receive from them his share of the fruit of the vineyard.
But they seized him, beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
Again he sent them another servant: that one they struck on the head and heaped with insults.
He sent another, whom they killed; then many others, whom they beat or killed.
He still had one left: his beloved son. He sent him to them last, saying to himself: They will respect my son.
But these tenants said to one another: This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours!
They seized him, killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.
What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come, destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not read this passage of Scripture: The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone;
this is the Lord's doing, a marvel in our eyes?"
