They were looking to arrest him, for they had understood that it was against them that he had told this parable; but they were afraid of the crowd. So they left him and went away.
They sent to him some pharisees and some supporters of Herod, to trap him in his own words.

They came and said to him: "Teacher, we know that you are truthful and that you let no one influence you; for you show no regard for a person's rank, but teach the way of God according to the truth. Is it lawful, yes or no, to pay the tribute to Caesar? Should we pay, yes or no?"
Knowing their hypocrisy, he said to them: "Why are you setting a trap for me? Bring me a coin, that I may see it."
They brought one. Jesus said to them: "Whose image and inscription are these?" They answered: "Caesar's."
Jesus said to them: "Give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's." And they were filled with amazement at him.
Some sadducees, who claim that there is no resurrection, came up to him and questioned him:
"Teacher, Moses wrote for us: If a man has a brother who dies leaving a wife but no child, he must marry the widow to raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife and died leaving no offspring.
The second married the widow and died leaving no offspring. The third likewise.
None of the seven left any offspring. And after them all, the woman died too.
At the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be, since the seven had her as wife?"
Jesus said to them: "Are you not mistaken, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God?
When people rise from the dead, they neither take a wife nor a husband: they are like angels in heaven.
And about the dead rising, have you not read, in the book of Moses, at the passage of the bush, how God said to him: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob?
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are completely mistaken!"
A scribe came up; he had heard them arguing and saw that Jesus had answered them well. He asked him: "Which is the first of all the commandments?"
Jesus answered: "This is the first: Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is the one Lord.
You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your mind and with all your strength.
This is the second: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. There is no commandment greater than these."
The scribe said to him: "Well said, Teacher! You have spoken the truth: God is the One, and there is no other than him;
and to love him with all one's heart, with all one's understanding and with all one's strength, and to love one's neighbor as oneself, is worth more than all burnt offerings and all sacrifices."
Seeing that he had answered wisely, Jesus said to him: "You are not far from the kingdom of God." And no one dared to question him any longer.
As he was teaching in the Temple, Jesus said: "How can the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
David himself, inspired by the Holy Spirit, said: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies under your feet.
David himself calls him Lord: how then can he be his son?" And the large crowd listened to him with delight.
In his teaching, he said: "Beware of the scribes, who like to walk about in long robes and to be greeted in the marketplaces,
to have the front seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.
They devour the property of widows and make a show of long prayers: they will be judged all the more severely."
Sitting opposite the Temple treasury, Jesus watched how the crowd put money into it. Many rich people put in a great deal.
A poor widow came forward and put in two small bronze coins, the smallest there are.
Calling his disciples, Jesus said to them: "Amen, I say to you: this poor widow has put into the treasury more than all the others.
For they all gave from their surplus; but she, out of her poverty, gave everything, all she had to live on."

titres.titre: The Announcement of the Temple's Destruction
The Coming of the Son of Man
The Lesson of the Fig Tree

versets.t: As Jesus was leaving the Temple, one of his disciples said to him: "Teacher, look: what stones, what buildings!"
Jesus answered him: "You see these great buildings? Not one stone here will be left upon another: everything will be destroyed."
Then he sat down on the Mount of Olives, opposite the Temple. Peter, James, John and Andrew questioned him privately:
"Tell us when this will happen, and by what sign we will know that all this is about to be fulfilled."
Then Jesus began to speak to them: "See that no one leads you astray.
Many will come in my name, claiming: I am the Christ; and they will lead many astray.
When you hear the din of wars and rumors of war, do not be alarmed: this must happen, but it will not yet be the end.
Nation will rise against nation, kingdom against kingdom; there will be earthquakes in various places, there will be famines. This will be the beginning of the birth pangs.
As for you, be on your guard. They will hand you over to the courts, they will beat you in the synagogues, you will stand before governors and kings because of me: it will be a testimony to them.
But first the Good News must be proclaimed to all the nations.
When they lead you away to hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what you will say: say what is given to you at that moment, for it is not you who will speak, but the Holy Spirit.
Brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child; children will rise up against their parents and have them put to death.
You will be hated by all because of my name; but whoever holds firm to the end, that one will be saved.
When you see the abomination of desolation set up where it must not be (let the reader understand!), then let those in Judea flee to the mountains.
Let the one on the rooftop not go down to go into his house to take anything;
and let the one in the fields not turn back to get his cloak.
Woe to the women who will be pregnant and to those who will be nursing in those days!
Pray that this may not happen in winter.
For those will be days of distress such as there has never been from the beginning of the world that God created until now, and such as there will never be again.
If the Lord had not cut short those days, no one would be saved; but for the sake of the elect whom he has chosen, he has cut short those days.
Then, if anyone says to you, Look, the Christ is here! or, He is there! do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise; they will perform signs and wonders to lead astray, if it were possible, even the elect.
You, then, be on your guard: I have told you everything beforehand.
But in those days, after that distress, the sun will be darkened, the moon will no longer give its light,
the stars will fall from the sky and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds, with great power and great glory.
He will send the angels to gather his elect from the four corners of the horizon, from one end of the world to the other.
Learn the lesson of the fig tree: when its branches become tender and its leaves come out, you know that summer is near.
In the same way, when you see these things happening, know that he is near, at the gates.
Amen, I say to you: this generation will not pass away before all this happens.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
As for that day and that hour, no one knows them, not even the angels in heaven, not even the Son: only the Father.
Be on your guard, stay awake, for you do not know when the moment will come.
It is like a man who has gone on a journey: leaving his house, he has given authority to his servants, to each his task, and he has ordered the doorkeeper to keep watch.
Keep watch, then, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming: in the evening, at midnight, at cockcrow or at early morning.
Let him not find you asleep when he arrives unexpectedly.
What I say to you, I say to all: keep watch!"
It was two days before the Passover and the feast of Unleavened Bread. The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to arrest Jesus by cunning and put him to death.
For they said: "Not during the feast, to avoid a riot among the people."

Jesus was at Bethany, at table in the house of Simon the leper. A woman came in with an alabaster jar full of a perfume of pure nard, very costly. She broke the jar and poured the perfume on Jesus' head.
Some were indignant among themselves: "Why this waste of perfume?
It could have been sold for more than three hundred pieces of silver and the money given to the poor." And they scolded her harshly.
But Jesus said: "Leave her alone. Why trouble her? She has done a beautiful thing for me.
The poor you will always have with you, and you can do good to them whenever you wish; but me you will not always have.
What she could do, she has done: in advance, she has anointed my body for burial.
Amen, I say to you: wherever the Good News is proclaimed, in the whole world, what she has done will also be told, in memory of her."
Then Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, went to the chief priests to hand Jesus over to them.
When they heard this, they were glad and promised to give him money. And Judas kept looking for a favorable moment to hand him over.
On the first day of the feast of Unleavened Bread, when the Passover lamb was sacrificed, the disciples said to Jesus: "Where do you want us to go and prepare the Passover meal?"
He sent two of his disciples, saying to them: "Go into the city. A man carrying a jar of water will come to meet you; follow him.
Where he enters, say to the master of the house: The Teacher asks: Where is the room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?
He will show you, upstairs, a large room, furnished and ready. That is where you will make the preparations for us."
The disciples set out and came to the city; they found everything just as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
When evening came, Jesus arrived with the Twelve.
While they were at table and eating, Jesus said: "Amen, I say to you: one of you, who is eating with me, is going to hand me over."
They became sad and began to ask him one after another: "Could it be me?"
He answered them: "It is one of the Twelve, the one who is dipping his hand with me into the dish.
The Son of Man is going away, as the Scripture says of him; but woe to the man by whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would be better for him never to have been born."
During the meal, Jesus took bread and, after the blessing, he broke it, gave it to them and said: "Take, this is my body."
Then he took a cup and, after giving thanks, he gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
He said to them: "This is my blood, the blood of the covenant, poured out for the many.
Amen, I say to you: I will never again drink of the fruit of the vine until the day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God."
After singing the hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them: "This night you will all fall away, for it is written: I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.
But after my resurrection, I will go ahead of you into Galilee."
Peter declared to him: "Even if all fall away, I will not!"
Jesus said to him: "Amen, I say to you: today, this very night, before the cock crows twice, you will have denied me three times."
But Peter insisted all the more: "Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you." And they all said the same.
They came to an estate called Gethsemane, and Jesus said to his disciples: "Sit here while I go and pray."
He took Peter, James and John with him, and he began to feel dread and anguish.
He said to them: "My soul is sorrowful to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch."
Going a little farther, he fell to the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, this hour might pass from him.
He said: "Abba, Father, everything is possible for you: take this cup away from me. Yet not what I want, but what you want."
He came back and found them asleep. He said to Peter: "Simon, are you asleep? Did you not have the strength to keep watch a single hour?
Keep watch and pray, so as not to enter into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak."
Again he went away and prayed, repeating the same words.
When he came back, he found them asleep again: their eyes were heavy, and they did not know what to answer him.
He came back a third time and said to them: "Sleep on now and take your rest! It is over. The hour has come: behold, the Son of Man is handed over into the hands of sinners.
Get up, let us go! Behold, the one who is handing me over is close at hand."
At once, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrives, and with him a troop armed with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, the scribes and the elders.
The betrayer had given them a prearranged signal: "The one I kiss, that is he: arrest him and lead him away under guard."
As soon as he arrived, he went up to Jesus, saying: "Teacher!", and he kissed him.
The others laid hands on him and arrested him.
One of the bystanders drew his sword, struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
Jesus said to them: "Am I a robber, that you have come out to arrest me with swords and clubs?
Every day I was among you, teaching in the Temple, and you did not arrest me. But this is so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled."
Then they all abandoned him and fled.
A young man was following him, wrapped only in a linen cloth. They seized him,
but he let go of the cloth and fled naked.
They led Jesus away to the high priest, where all the chief priests, the elders and the scribes gathered.
Peter had followed him at a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest. Sitting with the guards, he was warming himself by the fire.
The chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin were looking for testimony against Jesus to put him to death, but they found none.
For many were bearing false witness against him, but the testimonies did not agree.
Some stood up to bear this false witness against him:
"We heard him say: I will destroy this sanctuary made by human hands, and in three days I will build another, not made by human hands."
But even on this point their testimonies did not agree.
The high priest stood up in the midst of the assembly and questioned Jesus: "Have you no answer? What is this that these men testify against you?"
But Jesus kept silent and made no answer. Again the high priest questioned him: "Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?"
Jesus answered: "I Am. And you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Almighty and coming with the clouds of heaven."
Then the high priest tore his garments and said: "What further need do we have of witnesses?
You have heard the blasphemy. What do you think?" They all declared that he deserved death.
Some began to spit on him, to cover his face and to strike him with their fists, saying to him: "Play the prophet!" And the guards showered him with blows.
While Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the high priest's servant girls comes along.
Seeing Peter warming himself, she stared at him and said: "You too were with Jesus, the Nazarene."
But he denied it: "I do not know, I do not understand what you are saying." He went out into the entryway, and a cock crowed.
The servant girl, seeing him, began again to say to those standing there: "This man is one of them!"
Again he denied it. A little later, those standing there said to Peter again: "Surely you are one of them: besides, you are a Galilean."
Then he began to curse and to swear: "I do not know this man you are talking about!"
And at once, for the second time, a cock crowed. Peter remembered the word that Jesus had said to him: "Before the cock crows twice, you will have denied me three times." And he broke down in tears.

titres.titre: Jesus Condemned in Place of Barabbas

versets.t: Early in the morning, the chief priests held counsel with the elders, the scribes and the whole Sanhedrin. After binding Jesus, they led him away and handed him over to Pilate.
Pilate questioned him: "Are you the king of the Jews?" Jesus answered him: "It is you who say so."
The chief priests brought many accusations against him.
Pilate questioned him again: "Have you no answer? See how many charges they bring against you."
But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate was amazed.
At each feast, he would release for them one prisoner, the one they asked for.
Now there was a man named Barabbas, imprisoned with the rioters who had committed murder during an uprising.
The crowd came up and began to ask him to do what he usually did for them.
Pilate answered them: "Do you want me to release for you the king of the Jews?"
For he realized that it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed him over.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas instead.
Pilate spoke again: "What do you want me to do, then, with the one you call the king of the Jews?"
They shouted again: "Crucify him!"
Pilate said to them: "Why, what evil has he done?" But they shouted all the louder: "Crucify him!"
Pilate, wanting to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them; and, after having Jesus flogged, he handed him over to be crucified.
The soldiers led him inside the palace, that is, into the praetorium, and they gathered the whole cohort.
They dressed him in a purple cloak, wove a crown of thorns and put it on him.
Then they began to salute him: "Hail, king of the Jews!"
They struck his head with a reed, spat on him and, bending the knee, bowed down before him in mockery.
After mocking him, they took off the purple cloak and put his own clothes back on him. Then they led him out to crucify him.
A passerby, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was coming in from the fields; they forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.
They brought Jesus to the place called Golgotha, which means: "the place of the Skull."
They offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.
Then they crucified him and divided his clothes among them, casting lots to decide what each would take.
It was nine in the morning when they crucified him.
The notice stating the charge against him read: "The king of the Jews."
With him they crucified two robbers, one at his right, the other at his left.
Thus was fulfilled the Scripture that says: "He was counted among the criminals."
Those who passed by insulted him, shaking their heads: "Aha! You who would destroy the sanctuary and rebuild it in three days,
save yourself by coming down from the cross!"
In the same way, the chief priests and the scribes mocked him among themselves: "He saved others, and he cannot save himself!
Let the Christ, the king of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe!" And those crucified with him also insulted him.
At noon, darkness covered the whole land until three in the afternoon.
At three o'clock, Jesus cried out in a loud voice: "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani," which means: "My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?"
Hearing this, some of the bystanders said: "Look, he is calling Elijah!"
One of them ran to soak a sponge in vinegar, fixed it on the end of a reed and gave it to him to drink, saying: "Wait, let us see whether Elijah will come to take him down."
But Jesus, with a loud cry, breathed his last.
And the veil of the sanctuary was torn in two, from top to bottom.
The centurion, standing opposite him, seeing how he breathed his last, declared: "Truly, this man was the Son of God."
There were also women looking on from a distance, among them Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the Younger and of Joses, and Salome,
who used to follow Jesus and wait on him when he was in Galilee; and many others who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
Evening had already come, and since it was the day of Preparation, the eve of the Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathea arrived. He was a respected member of the great council, who was himself also waiting for the kingdom of God. He had the courage to go to Pilate and ask for the body of Jesus.
Pilate was surprised that he was already dead. He summoned the centurion and asked him how long Jesus had been dead.
Informed by the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
Joseph bought a shroud, took Jesus down from the cross, wrapped him in the shroud and laid him in a tomb cut out of the rock; then he rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses watched where he was laid.

titres.titre: The Empty Tomb and the Announcement of the Resurrection
The Appearances of the Risen Lord

versets.t: When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices to go and embalm the body of Jesus.
On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came to the tomb as the sun was rising.
They said to one another: "Who will roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb for us?"
Looking up, they see that the stone has already been rolled aside; and it was very large.
Entering the tomb, they saw, seated on the right, a young man clothed in a white robe, and they were seized with dread.
But he said to them: "Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus of Nazareth, the Crucified: he is risen, he is not here. Here is the place where they had laid him.
But go and tell his disciples and Peter: He is going ahead of you into Galilee; there you will see him, just as he told you."
They went out and fled from the tomb, trembling and overwhelmed; and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.
Risen on the morning of the first day of the week, Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had driven out seven demons.
She went to announce it to those who had lived with him and who were in mourning and tears.
When they heard that he was alive and that she had seen him, they did not believe her.
Afterward, he showed himself in another form to two of them who were walking to the countryside.
These went back to announce it to the others, who did not believe them either.

Finally, he showed himself to the Eleven while they were at table. He reproached them for their lack of faith and the hardness of their hearts, because they had not believed those who had seen him risen.
Then he said to them: "Go into the whole world, proclaim the Good News to all creation.
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved; whoever refuses to believe will be condemned.
These are the signs that will accompany those who have believed: in my name, they will drive out demons, they will speak new tongues;
they will pick up serpents in their hands, and if they drink any deadly poison, it will do them no harm; they will lay their hands on the sick, and these will be healed."
So the Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, was taken up into heaven and sat at the right hand of God.
As for them, they set out to proclaim the Good News everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word by the signs that accompanied it.

titres.titre: The birth of John the Baptist

versets.t: Many have undertaken to draw up an account of the events that have been fulfilled among us,
just as they were handed down to us by those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the Word.
And so I too, having carefully investigated everything from the start, decided to write an orderly account for you, most honorable Theophilus,
so that you may know how firm is the teaching you have received.
In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah, of the priestly division of Abijah. His wife was a descendant of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
Both of them were righteous before God, following all the commandments and precepts of the Lord blamelessly.
But they had no child, for Elizabeth was barren, and both were now well on in years.
One day, while Zechariah was serving as priest before God during the turn of his division,
he was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to enter the sanctuary of the Lord and offer the incense.
At the hour of the incense offering, the whole assembly of the people was praying outside.
Then an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right of the altar of incense.
When Zechariah saw him he was shaken, and fear gripped him.
But the angel said to him, "Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall name him John.
He will be your joy and your delight, and many will rejoice at his birth,
for he will be great before the Lord. He shall drink no wine or strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb.
He will bring back many of the sons of Israel to the Lord their God.

He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers toward their children and lead the rebellious to the wisdom of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a people made ready."
Zechariah said to the angel, "How can I be sure of this? For I am an old man, and my wife is well on in years."
The angel answered him, "I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God, and I was sent to speak to you and bring you this good news.
Now you will be silent, unable to speak, until the day this comes to pass, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time."
Meanwhile the people were waiting for Zechariah, wondering why he lingered in the sanctuary.
When he came out he could not speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the sanctuary. He kept making signs to them and remained mute.
When his time of service was over, he returned home.
Some time later his wife Elizabeth conceived, and for five months she kept herself hidden, saying,
"This is what the Lord has done for me, when he looked with favor on me and took away my disgrace before others."
In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent by God to a town in Galilee called Nazareth,
to a virgin pledged in marriage to a man of the house of David named Joseph; and the virgin's name was Mary.
The angel came to her and said, "Rejoice, full of grace: the Lord is with you."
At these words she was deeply troubled, and she wondered what this greeting could mean.
The angel said to her, "Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
Behold, you will conceive and bear a son, and you shall name him Jesus.
He will be great and will be called Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him the throne of David his father.
He will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and his reign will have no end."
Mary said to the angel, "How can this be, since I have no relations with a man?"
The angel answered her, "The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the one to be born will be holy, and he will be called Son of God.
And behold, your relative Elizabeth has also conceived a son in her old age; she who was said to be barren is now in her sixth month.
For nothing is impossible with God."
Then Mary said, "Behold the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word." And the angel left her.
In those days Mary set out and hurried to the hill country, to a town of Judah.
She entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
Now when Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, the child leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She cried out in a loud voice, "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.
And how is it granted to me that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For the moment your greeting reached my ears, the child leaped for joy in my womb.
Blessed is she who believed that what was spoken to her by the Lord would be fulfilled!"
Then Mary said, "My soul magnifies the Lord,
and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior,
for he has looked with favor on his lowly servant. From now on all generations will call me blessed,
for the Mighty One has done great things for me. Holy is his name,
and his mercy reaches from generation to generation on those who fear him.
He has shown the strength of his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thoughts of their hearts.
He has cast down the mighty from their thrones and lifted up the lowly.
He has filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.
He has come to the help of Israel his servant, remembering his mercy,
as he promised to our fathers, to Abraham and his descendants forever."
Mary stayed with Elizabeth about three months and then returned home.
When the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, she brought forth a son.
Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown her the greatness of his mercy, and they rejoiced with her.
On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they wanted to name him after his father, Zechariah.
But his mother spoke up: "No," she said, "he is to be called John."
They said to her, "No one in your family has that name."
So they made signs to the father to find out what he wanted to name him.
He asked for a tablet and wrote, "His name is John." And they were all astonished.
At that very moment his mouth was opened and his tongue was freed, and he began to speak, praising God.
Fear came upon all their neighbors, and throughout the hill country of Judea these events were talked about.
All who heard of them kept them in their hearts and said, "What then will this child be?" For the hand of the Lord was with him.
Zechariah his father was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied in these words:
"Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who visits and redeems his people.
He has raised up for us a mighty savior in the house of David his servant,
as he foretold through the mouth of his holy prophets from ages past:
salvation that rescues us from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us.
So he shows mercy to our fathers and remembers his holy covenant,
the oath he swore to Abraham our father: to grant us
that, delivered from the hand of our enemies, we might serve him without fear,
in holiness and righteousness before him all the days of our life.
And you, little child, will be called prophet of the Most High, for you will go before the Lord to prepare his ways,
to give his people knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins.
Through the tender mercy of our God, the dawn from on high has visited us,
to shine on those who dwell in darkness and the shadow of death, and to guide our feet into the way of peace."
The child grew and became strong in spirit. He lived in the wilderness until the day he appeared openly to Israel.

titres.titre: The circumcision and the presentation in the Temple
Jesus at twelve in the Temple

versets.t: In those days a decree went out from Caesar Augustus ordering a census of the whole empire.
This first census took place when Quirinius was governor of Syria.
Everyone went to be registered, each to his own town.
Joseph too went up from Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, to Judea, to the town of David called Bethlehem, because he belonged to the house and lineage of David.
He went to be registered with Mary, his betrothed, who was expecting a child.
While they were there, the time came for her to give birth,
and she brought forth her firstborn son. She wrapped him in swaddling clothes and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the guest quarters.
In that same region there were shepherds living out in the fields, keeping watch over their flocks by night.
An angel of the Lord stood before them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were struck with great fear.
But the angel said to them, "Do not be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy for all the people:
today in the town of David a Savior has been born to you, who is Christ the Lord.
And this will be the sign for you: you will find a newborn wrapped in swaddling clothes and lying in a manger."
Suddenly a great host of the army of heaven joined the angel, praising God and saying,
"Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to those he loves!"
When the angels had left them and returned to heaven, the shepherds said to one another, "Let us go over to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us."
They hurried off and found Mary and Joseph, and the newborn lying in the manger.
When they had seen him, they made known what had been told them about this child.
And all who heard were amazed at what the shepherds told them.
But Mary treasured all these things and pondered them in her heart.
Then the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen, just as they had been told.
On the eighth day, when the time came to circumcise the child, he was named Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived.
When the time came for their purification according to the law of Moses, they brought the child to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord,
as it is written in the law of the Lord: Every firstborn male shall be consecrated to the Lord.
They also came to offer in sacrifice, according to what the law of the Lord says, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.
Now there was in Jerusalem a man named Simeon. He was righteous and devout, awaiting the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
The Holy Spirit had revealed to him that he would not see death before he had seen the Christ of the Lord.
Moved by the Spirit, he came to the Temple. And when the parents brought in the child Jesus to do for him what the Law required,
he took him into his arms and blessed God, saying,
"Now, sovereign Master, you let your servant go in peace, according to your word,
for my eyes have seen your salvation,
which you have prepared in the sight of all the peoples:
a light for revelation to the nations, and the glory of your people Israel."
The child's father and mother were amazed at what was said about him.
Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother, "Behold, this child is destined for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed,
and a sword will pierce your own soul too. Thus the secret thoughts of many hearts will be revealed."
There was also a prophetess, Anna, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was very old; she had lived seven years with her husband after her marriage,
and then, having remained a widow, she had reached the age of eighty-four. She never left the Temple, serving God night and day with fasting and prayer.
Coming up at that very moment, she began to give thanks to God and to speak of the child to all who were awaiting the deliverance of Jerusalem.
When they had accomplished everything the law of the Lord required, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom, and the grace of God was upon him.
Every year his parents went to Jerusalem for the feast of Passover.
When he was twelve years old, they went up as they always did for the feast.
When the days of the feast were over and they were returning, the boy Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem without his parents knowing it.
Thinking he was in the company, they went a day's journey before looking for him among their relatives and acquaintances.
When they did not find him, they returned to Jerusalem searching for him.
It was after three days that they found him in the Temple, sitting among the teachers of the Law, listening to them and questioning them.
All who heard him were amazed at his understanding and his answers.
When his parents saw him they were astonished, and his mother said to him, "My child, why have you done this to us? Look, your father and I have been searching for you in anguish."
He answered them, "Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?"
But they did not understand what he said to them.
Then he went down with them and returned to Nazareth, and he was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
And Jesus grew in wisdom, in stature, and in grace, before God and before others.

titres.titre: The preaching of John the Baptist

versets.t: In the fifteenth year of the reign of the emperor Tiberius, when Pontius Pilate was governor of Judea, Herod tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias tetrarch of Abilene,
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, son of Zechariah, in the wilderness.
He went through the whole region of the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of conversion for the forgiveness of sins,
as it is written in the book of the words of the prophet Isaiah: A voice cries out in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
Every valley shall be filled, every mountain and hill made low; the winding ways shall be made straight, and the rough roads smooth.
And all flesh shall see the salvation of God.
John said to the crowds who came to be baptized by him, "You brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath that is coming?
Produce, then, fruit that shows your conversion. And do not begin to say among yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father.' For I tell you, God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
Already the axe is laid to the root of the trees: every tree that does not bear good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire."
The crowds asked him, "What then should we do?"
He answered them, "Whoever has two tunics should share with the one who has none, and whoever has food should do the same."
Tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, "Teacher, what should we do?"
He said to them, "Demand no more than what is set for you."
Soldiers too questioned him, "And we, what should we do?" He answered them, "Do not intimidate anyone, do not accuse anyone falsely, and be content with your pay."
The people were in expectation, and everyone was wondering in their hearts whether John might be the Christ.

So John declared to them all, "I baptize you with water. But one who is mightier than I is coming, and I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
He holds his winnowing fork in his hand to clear his threshing floor and to gather the wheat into his barn, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire."
With many other exhortations, he proclaimed the Good News to the people.
But Herod the tetrarch, whom John had rebuked over Herodias, his brother's wife, and over all the evil he had done,
added this to all his misdeeds: he had John shut up in prison.
Now while all the people were being baptized, Jesus too was baptized. And as he was praying, the heavens opened,
and the Holy Spirit descended upon him in visible form, like a dove. And from heaven came a voice: "You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased."
When Jesus began his ministry he was about thirty years old. He was, as was thought, the son of Joseph, son of Heli,
son of Matthat, son of Levi, son of Melchi, son of Jannai, son of Joseph,
son of Mattathias, son of Amos, son of Nahum, son of Esli, son of Naggai,
son of Maath, son of Mattathias, son of Semein, son of Josech, son of Joda,
son of Joanan, son of Rhesa, son of Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, son of Neri,
son of Melchi, son of Addi, son of Cosam, son of Elmadam, son of Er,
son of Joshua, son of Eliezer, son of Jorim, son of Matthat, son of Levi,
son of Simeon, son of Judah, son of Joseph, son of Jonam, son of Eliakim,
son of Melea, son of Menna, son of Mattatha, son of Nathan, son of David,
son of Jesse, son of Obed, son of Boaz, son of Salmon, son of Nahshon,
son of Amminadab, son of Admin, son of Arni, son of Hezron, son of Perez, son of Judah,
son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, son of Terah, son of Nahor,
son of Serug, son of Reu, son of Peleg, son of Eber, son of Shelah,
son of Cainan, son of Arphaxad, son of Shem, son of Noah, son of Lamech,
son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalalel, son of Kenan,
son of Enosh, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.

titres.titre: The man with the unclean demon

versets.t: Jesus, filled with the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan. He was led by the Spirit through the wilderness,
where for forty days he was tempted by the devil. He ate nothing during those days, and when they were over, he was hungry.
The devil then said to him, "If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread."
Jesus answered him, "It is written: Man shall not live by bread alone."
The devil took him up higher and showed him in an instant all the kingdoms of the earth.
He said to him, "I will give you all this power and the glory of these kingdoms, for it has been handed over to me and I give it to whomever I please.
So if you bow down before me, it will all be yours."
Jesus answered him, "It is written: You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone shall you serve."
The devil then led him to Jerusalem, set him on the pinnacle of the Temple, and said to him, "If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here.
For it is written: He will command his angels concerning you, to guard you;
and again: They will bear you up in their hands, so that your foot does not strike a stone."
Jesus answered him, "It is said: You shall not put the Lord your God to the test."
Having exhausted every temptation, the devil left him until an appointed time.
Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and his fame spread throughout the whole region.
He taught in their synagogues, and everyone praised him.
He came to Nazareth, where he had grown up. As was his custom, he entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day and stood up to read.
The scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. He unrolled it and found the passage where it is written:

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring the Good News to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to set the oppressed free,
and to proclaim a year of the Lord's favor.
He rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. In the synagogue, all eyes were fixed on him.
Then he began to say to them, "Today this passage of Scripture that you have just heard is fulfilled."
All bore witness to him and were amazed at the gracious words that came from his mouth. They said, "Is this not the son of Joseph?"
He said to them, "Surely you will quote me this proverb: Physician, heal yourself. Do here in your own town all that we have heard you did at Capernaum."
Then he added, "Amen, I say to you: no prophet is welcome in his own town.
In truth I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was closed for three years and six months and a great famine came over the whole land.
Yet Elijah was sent to none of them, but to a widow of Zarephath in the land of Sidon.
And there were many lepers in Israel in the days of the prophet Elisha. Yet none of them was cleansed, but only Naaman the Syrian."
At these words, everyone in the synagogue was filled with fury.
They rose up, drove him out of the town, and led him to the brow of the hill on which their town was built, to throw him down.
But he passed through the midst of them and went on his way.
He went down to Capernaum, a town of Galilee, and taught there on the Sabbath day.
They were struck by his teaching, for his word had authority.
In the synagogue there was a man possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon. He cried out in a loud voice,
"Ah! What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God."
But Jesus rebuked him sharply, "Be silent, and come out of this man." The demon threw him down in the midst of the assembly and came out of him without doing him any harm.
They were all seized with astonishment and said to one another, "What is this word? With authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!"
And his fame spread to every place in the region.
Leaving the synagogue, Jesus entered the house of Simon. Now Simon's mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever, and they appealed to him on her behalf.
He bent over her, rebuked the fever, and the fever left her. At once she got up and began to serve them.
At sunset, all who had any who were sick with various diseases brought them to him. He laid his hands on each of them and healed them.
Demons also came out of many, crying out, "You are the Son of God!" But he rebuked them and would not let them speak, because they knew he was the Christ.
At daybreak, Jesus went out to a deserted place. The crowds were looking for him; they came to him and tried to keep him from leaving them.
But he said to them, "To the other towns also I must proclaim the Good News of the kingdom of God, for that is why I was sent."
And he went on proclaiming the Good News in the synagogues of Judea.

titres.titre: The miraculous catch and the first disciples

versets.t: One day, as the crowd was pressing around Jesus to hear the word of God, he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret.
He saw two boats moored by the shore; the fishermen had gotten out of them and were washing their nets.
He got into one of the boats, the one belonging to Simon, and asked him to pull out a little from the shore. Then he sat down and taught the crowds from the boat.
When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, "Put out into deep water, and lower your nets for a catch."
Simon answered him, "Master, we have worked hard all night and caught nothing; but at your word I will lower the nets."
They did so and caught such a great number of fish that their nets were tearing.
They signaled to their companions in the other boat to come and help them. These came, and they filled both boats so full that they were sinking.
At this, Simon Peter fell at Jesus' knees: "Depart from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man."
For astonishment had seized him and all who were with him at the catch they had made,
and likewise James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon's partners. Jesus said to Simon, "Do not be afraid. From now on you will be catching people."
They brought the boats to shore, left everything, and followed him.
While Jesus was in a certain town, a man covered with leprosy appeared. At the sight of Jesus he fell face down and begged him, "Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean."
Jesus reached out his hand, touched him, and said, "I am willing; be clean." At once the leprosy left him.
He ordered him to tell no one: "Go instead and show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses prescribed; this will be a testimony to them."
His fame spread all the more, and large crowds came to hear him and to be healed of their illnesses.
But he would withdraw to deserted places and pray.

One day, as he was teaching, Pharisees and teachers of the Law were sitting there, having come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was at work for him to heal.
Some men came, carrying a paralyzed man on a bed. They were trying to bring him in and lay him before Jesus,
but finding no way to get him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and lowered him with his mat through the tiles into the midst of the assembly, in front of Jesus.
Seeing their faith, he said, "Friend, your sins are forgiven."
The scribes and Pharisees began to reason, "Who is this man who speaks blasphemies? Who can forgive sins but God alone?"
Knowing their thoughts, Jesus replied, "Why do you reason this way in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins," he said to the paralyzed man, "I say to you, get up, take your mat, and go home."
At once the man stood up before them, took what he had been lying on, and went home glorifying God.
They were all seized with amazement and glorified God. Filled with awe, they said, "We have seen extraordinary things today."
After this, Jesus went out and noticed a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office. He said to him, "Follow me."
The man left everything, got up, and followed him.
Levi gave a great banquet for him in his house, and a large crowd of tax collectors and others were at table with them.
The Pharisees and their scribes grumbled and said to his disciples, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
Jesus answered them, "It is not the healthy who need a physician, but the sick.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to conversion."
They said to him, "The disciples of John fast often and say prayers, and so do those of the Pharisees; but yours eat and drink."
Jesus answered them, "Can you make the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them?
The days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them; then, in those days, they will fast."
He also gave them this image: "No one tears a piece from a new garment to sew it on an old one; otherwise he will have torn the new one, and the piece taken from the new will not match the old.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the new wine will burst the skins, it will spill out, and the skins will be ruined.
New wine must be put into new wineskins.
And no one who has been drinking old wine wants new, for he says, 'The old is good.'"

titres.titre: The heads of grain plucked on a Sabbath
The man with the withered hand
The Sermon on the Plain: the Beatitudes

versets.t: One Sabbath, Jesus was passing through fields of grain. His disciples were picking heads of grain, rubbing them in their hands, and eating them.
Some Pharisees said, "Why are you doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath?"
Jesus answered them, "Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?
He entered the house of God, took the bread of the offering, ate it, and gave some to his companions, though it is permitted to none but the priests to eat it."
And he added, "The Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath."
On another Sabbath, Jesus entered the synagogue and began to teach. A man was there whose right hand was withered.
The scribes and Pharisees watched him to see whether he would heal on the Sabbath, looking for something to accuse him of.
But he knew their thoughts. He said to the man with the withered hand, "Get up and stand here in the middle." The man got up and stood.
Jesus said to them, "I ask you: is it permitted on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to destroy it?"
He looked around at them all, then said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." He did so, and his hand was restored.
But they were filled with fury and discussed with one another what they might do to Jesus.
In those days, Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and he spent the whole night praying to God.
When day came, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he named apostles:
Simon, to whom he gave the name Peter, and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot,
Jude son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
Jesus came down with them and stopped on a level place. There was a crowd of his disciples and a great multitude from all Judea, from Jerusalem, and from the coast of Tyre and Sidon.
They had come to hear him and to be healed of their illnesses. Those tormented by unclean spirits were cured,
and the whole crowd tried to touch him, for power was going out from him and healing them all.
Then, raising his eyes toward his disciples, he said, "Blessed are you who are poor, for the kingdom of God is yours!
Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled! Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh!
Blessed are you when people hate you, when they reject you, insult you, and denounce your name as vile, because of the Son of Man.
Rejoice on that day and leap for joy, for your reward is great in heaven; for that is how their ancestors treated the prophets.
But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your consolation!
Woe to you who are full now, for you will be hungry! Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep!
Woe to you when everyone speaks well of you; for that is how their ancestors treated the false prophets!
But I say to you who are listening: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
bless those who curse you, pray for those who slander you.
To the one who strikes you on one cheek, offer the other also; and from the one who takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic either.
Give to everyone who asks you, and from the one who takes what is yours, do not demand it back.
Do to others as you would have them do to you.
If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.
If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.
If you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners to be repaid in full.

But you, love your enemies, do good, and lend without hoping for anything in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, for he is kind to the ungrateful and the wicked.
Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.
Do not judge, and you will not be judged; do not condemn, and you will not be condemned; forgive, and you will be forgiven.
Give, and it will be given to you: a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and overflowing, will be poured into the fold of your garment. For the measure you use will be used for you."
He also told them a comparison: "Can a blind man guide a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?
A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.
Why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

How can you say to your brother, 'Brother, let me remove the speck in your eye,' when you do not see the beam in your own? Hypocrite, first remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck in your brother's eye.
There is no good tree that bears rotten fruit, nor a rotten tree that bears good fruit.
Each tree is known by its fruit: figs are not gathered from thorns, nor grapes picked from brambles.
The good person brings good out of the good treasure of the heart, and the evil person brings evil out of an evil treasure; for the mouth speaks from what overflows the heart.
Why do you call me 'Lord, Lord,' and do not do what I say?
I will show you what everyone is like who comes to me, hears my words, and puts them into practice.
He is like a man building a house: he dug deep and laid the foundation on rock. When the flood came, the torrent struck that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.

But the one who hears and does not put into practice is like a man who built his house on the ground without a foundation. The torrent struck it, and at once it collapsed; and great was the ruin of that house."

titres.titre: The son of the widow of Nain
The question of John the Baptist

versets.t: When Jesus had finished speaking all his words in the hearing of the people, he entered Capernaum.
A centurion had a servant who was dear to him, sick and about to die.
Having heard about Jesus, he sent some elders of the Jews to him, asking him to come and save his servant.
When they came to Jesus, they earnestly begged him, "He deserves to have you do this for him,
for he loves our nation, and he is the one who built us the synagogue."
So Jesus went with them. He was not far from the house when the centurion sent friends to say to him, "Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy to have you come under my roof.
That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to you. But say the word, and let my servant be healed.
For I too am a man under authority, with soldiers under me; I say to one, 'Go,' and he goes; to another, 'Come,' and he comes; and to my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it."
When Jesus heard this, he was filled with admiration. He turned to the crowd following him and said, "I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such faith."
When the messengers returned to the house, they found the servant in good health.
Soon afterward, Jesus went to a town called Nain; his disciples and a great crowd traveled with him.
As he approached the town gate, a dead man was being carried out for burial, the only son of a mother who was a widow; and a large crowd from the town was with her.
When the Lord saw her, he was moved with compassion for her and said to her, "Do not weep."
He came forward and touched the bier; the bearers stood still. He said, "Young man, I say to you, get up."
The dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him back to his mother.
Fear seized them all, and they glorified God: "A great prophet has risen among us, and God has visited his people."
And this report about him spread throughout the whole of Judea and the surrounding region.
The disciples of John reported all these things to him. He called two of them
and sent them to say to the Lord, "Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?"
When they came to Jesus, they said, "John the Baptist has sent us to you to ask: Are you the one who is to come, or should we wait for another?"
At that very time, Jesus healed many people of their diseases, their afflictions, and evil spirits, and he gave sight to many who were blind.

Then he answered the messengers, "Go and report to John what you have seen and heard: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the Good News is proclaimed to the poor.
Blessed is the one who does not stumble because of me!"
When John's messengers had gone, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: "What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
Then what did you go out to see? A man dressed in fine clothes? But those who wear sumptuous garments and live in luxury are in royal palaces.
Then what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written: Behold, I send my messenger ahead of you; he will prepare your way before you.
I tell you: among those born of women, none is greater than John; and yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he."
All the people who heard him, even the tax collectors, acknowledged the justice of God by receiving John's baptism.
But the Pharisees and the experts in the Law rejected God's plan for them, refusing to be baptized by him.
"To what, then, shall I compare the people of this generation? What are they like?
They are like children sitting in the marketplace who call out to one another: We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang laments, and you did not weep.
For John the Baptist has come, eating no bread and drinking no wine, and you say, 'He has a demon.'
The Son of Man has come, eating and drinking, and you say, 'Look, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.'
But Wisdom is vindicated by all her children."
A Pharisee invited Jesus to eat with him. He entered the Pharisee's house and reclined at table.
Now a woman of the town, a sinner, learned that he was at table in the Pharisee's house. She brought an alabaster jar full of perfume
and stood behind him at his feet, weeping. She began to bathe his feet with her tears, to wipe them with her hair, to cover them with kisses, and to anoint them with the perfume.
When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself, "If this man were a prophet, he would know who this woman is who is touching him, and that she is a sinner."
Jesus spoke up, "Simon, I have something to say to you." "Speak, Teacher," he replied.
"A creditor had two debtors: one owed him five hundred pieces of silver, the other fifty.
Since neither of them had the means to repay, he canceled the debt of both. Which of them will love him more?"
Simon answered, "The one, I suppose, whose debt was greater." Jesus said to him, "You have judged rightly."
Then, turning to the woman, he said to Simon, "Do you see this woman? I entered your house, and you gave me no water for my feet; but she has bathed them with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You gave me no kiss, but she, from the moment I entered, has not stopped covering my feet with kisses.
You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with perfume.
And so I tell you: her many sins are forgiven, for she has shown great love. But the one who is forgiven little shows little love."
Then he said to the woman, "Your sins are forgiven."
The other guests began to think, "Who is this man, who even forgives sins?"
But Jesus said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you. Go in peace."

titres.titre: The mother and brothers of Jesus
The daughter of Jairus and the healed woman

versets.t: Afterward, Jesus traveled through towns and villages, proclaiming and announcing the Good News of the kingdom of God. The Twelve accompanied him,
along with some women he had healed of evil spirits and diseases: Mary, called of Magdala, from whom seven demons had gone out,
Joanna, wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, Susanna, and many others, who supported them out of their own means.
As a large crowd gathered and people came to him from every town, Jesus spoke in a parable:
"The sower went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the path; it was trampled, and the birds of the sky ate it up.
Some fell on rock; and when it came up it withered for lack of moisture.
Some fell among thorns; the thorns grew up with it and choked it.
Some fell on good soil; it grew and yielded fruit a hundredfold." As he said this, he cried out, "Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!"
His disciples asked him what this parable meant.
He answered, "To you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God; but to the others it is spoken only in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.
This is the meaning of the parable. The seed is the word of God.
Those along the path are the ones who hear, and then the devil comes and takes the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
Those on the rock are the ones who receive the word with joy when they hear it, but they have no root; they believe for a while, and in the time of testing they fall away.
What fell among the thorns are those who hear, and then are choked along the way by the cares, riches, and pleasures of life; they do not come to maturity.
What is in the good soil are those who hear the word with a good and generous heart, hold it fast, and bear fruit through perseverance.
No one who has lit a lamp covers it with a vessel or puts it under a bed; instead, he sets it on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
For nothing is hidden that will not be made manifest, nothing secret that will not be known and brought to light.
So take care how you listen: to the one who has, more will be given; and from the one who has not, even what he thinks he has will be taken away."
The mother and brothers of Jesus came to see him, but they could not reach him because of the crowd.
He was told, "Your mother and your brothers are standing outside; they want to see you."
He answered them, "My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and put it into practice."
One day Jesus got into a boat with his disciples and said to them, "Let us cross to the other side of the lake." And they set out.
As they were sailing, he fell asleep. A squall of wind swept down on the lake; the boat was filling with water, and they were in danger.
They came and woke him, "Master, Master, we are perishing!" He awoke, rebuked the wind and the raging waves; everything calmed, and there was a great stillness.
Then he said to them, "Where is your faith?" Seized with fear and amazement, they said to one another, "Who then is this, who commands even the wind and the water, and they obey him?"
They landed in the country of the Gerasenes, opposite Galilee.
As Jesus stepped ashore, a man from the town, possessed by demons, came to meet him. For a long time he had worn no clothing and had lived not in a house but among the tombs.
At the sight of Jesus he cried out, fell at his feet, and said in a loud voice, "What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me."

For Jesus was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times, in fact, the spirit had seized him; he would then be bound with chains and shackles to keep him, but he would break his bonds, and the demon would drive him into deserted places.
Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" He answered, "Legion," for many demons had entered him.
And they begged him not to order them to depart into the abyss.
Now there was a large herd of pigs feeding on the mountain. The demons begged Jesus to let them enter the pigs, and he gave them permission.
Coming out of the man, they entered the pigs, and from the top of the steep bank the herd rushed into the lake and was drowned.
When the herdsmen saw what had happened, they fled and spread the news in the town and in the countryside.

The people came out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting at his feet, clothed and in his right mind; and they were seized with fear.
Those who had seen it told them how the possessed man had been delivered.
Then all the people of the country of the Gerasenes asked Jesus to leave them, for they were gripped by great fear. So he got into the boat and returned.
The man from whom the demons had gone out begged to stay with him, but Jesus sent him away, saying,
"Return home and tell all that God has done for you." So the man went off, proclaiming throughout the whole town what Jesus had done for him.
On his return, Jesus was welcomed by the crowd, for they were all waiting for him.
And there came a man named Jairus, a leader of the synagogue. He fell at Jesus' feet and begged him to come to his house,
for he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, who was dying. As Jesus went, the crowds pressed in on him from all sides.
Now a woman who had suffered from a flow of blood for twelve years, and had spent all she had on physicians without anyone being able to heal her,
came up behind him and touched the fringe of his cloak. At once her flow of blood stopped.
Jesus asked, "Who touched me?" As everyone denied it, Peter said, "Master, the crowds are pressing and crushing you."
But Jesus said, "Someone touched me, for I felt that power had gone out from me."
Seeing that she was discovered, the woman came forward trembling and fell at his feet. She declared before all the people why she had touched him, and how she had been healed at once.
He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace."
While he was still speaking, someone came from the house of the synagogue leader, "Your daughter is dead; do not trouble the Teacher any longer."
At these words, Jesus answered the father, "Do not be afraid; only believe, and she will be saved."
When he came to the house, he let no one enter with him except Peter, John, and James, and the child's father and mother.
Everyone was weeping and mourning for her. Jesus said, "Do not weep; she is not dead, but sleeping."
They laughed at him, for they knew she was dead.
But he took her by the hand and said in a loud voice, "Child, get up."
Her spirit returned, and she got up at once. Jesus ordered that she be given something to eat.
Her parents were astonished, but he ordered them to tell no one what had happened.

titres.titre: The first announcement of the Passion
The boy possessed by a spirit
The second announcement of the Passion

versets.t: Jesus called the Twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, as well as the power to heal diseases.
He sent them to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
He said to them, "Take nothing for the journey: no staff, no bag, no bread, no money; and do not have two tunics.
When you enter a house, stay there until you leave the place.
If people refuse to welcome you, leave that town and shake the dust from your feet as a testimony against them."
So they set out and went through the villages, proclaiming the Good News and healing everywhere.
Herod the tetrarch heard about all that was happening, and he did not know what to think. Some said that John had risen from the dead,
others that Elijah had appeared, still others that one of the ancient prophets had risen.
But Herod said, "John, I had him beheaded. Who then is this man about whom I hear such things?" And he was trying to see him.
When the apostles returned, they told Jesus all they had done. Taking them with him, he withdrew privately toward a town called Bethsaida.
But the crowds found out and followed him. He welcomed them, spoke to them about the kingdom of God, and healed those who had need of it.

As the day began to wane, the Twelve came and said to him, "Send the crowd away, so that they may go to the surrounding villages and farms to find lodging and food, for here we are in a deserted place."
He answered them, "Give them something to eat yourselves." They said, "We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we ourselves go and buy food for all these people."
There were about five thousand men. Jesus said to his disciples, "Have them sit down in groups of about fifty."
They did so and had everyone sit down.
Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish, raised his eyes to heaven, said the blessing, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the crowd.
They all ate and were satisfied, and the leftover pieces were gathered up: twelve baskets.
One day, while he was praying alone with his disciples, Jesus asked them, "Who do the crowds say that I am?"
They answered, "For some, John the Baptist; for others, Elijah; for others, one of the ancient prophets risen again."
He said to them, "But you, who do you say that I am?" Peter answered, "The Christ of God."
Then, firmly, he ordered them to tell this to no one.
And he added, "The Son of Man must suffer greatly, be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, be put to death, and on the third day rise again."
Then he said to all, "If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross each day, and follow me.
For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake will save it.
What good is it for a man to gain the whole world, if he loses or ruins himself?
If anyone is ashamed of me and my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when he comes in his glory, the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
Truly I tell you: there are some standing here who will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God."
About eight days after these words, Jesus took with him Peter, John, and James, and went up the mountain to pray.
While he was praying, the appearance of his face changed, and his clothing became dazzling white.
And behold, two men were talking with him: Moses and Elijah,
who appeared in glory. They were speaking of his departure, which he was to accomplish in Jerusalem.
Peter and his companions were weighed down with sleep; but staying awake, they saw the glory of Jesus and the two men beside him.
As these were leaving him, Peter said to Jesus, "Master, it is good that we are here! Let us set up three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah." He did not know what he was saying.
As he was speaking, a cloud came and overshadowed them; and the disciples were seized with fear as they entered the cloud.
From the cloud came a voice: "This is my Son, the Chosen One; listen to him!"
When the voice had spoken, Jesus was found alone. The disciples kept silence and, in those days, told no one anything of what they had seen.
The next day, as they came down from the mountain, a great crowd came to meet him.
From the middle of the crowd a man cried out, "Teacher, I beg you, look at my son, for he is my only child.
A spirit seizes him; suddenly he screams; the spirit throws him into convulsions until he foams at the mouth, and it barely leaves him after battering him.
I begged your disciples to cast it out, and they could not."
Jesus answered, "Faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and put up with you? Bring your son here."
As the boy came forward, the demon threw him to the ground in convulsions. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
And all were astounded at the greatness of God. While everyone was marveling at all that he was doing, Jesus said to his disciples,
"Listen carefully to these words: the Son of Man is going to be handed over into the hands of men."
But they did not understand this saying; it remained veiled to them, so that they did not grasp its meaning, and they were afraid to ask him about it.
An argument arose among them: which of them was the greatest?
Jesus, knowing the thoughts of their hearts, took a little child and placed him at his side
and said to them, "Whoever welcomes this child in my name welcomes me; and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. For the least among you all is the one who is great."
John spoke up, "Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he does not follow with us."
Jesus answered him, "Do not stop him, for whoever is not against you is for you."
As the time approached when he was to be taken up from this world, Jesus resolutely set out on the road to Jerusalem.
He sent messengers ahead of him, who went and entered a Samaritan village to prepare a welcome for him;
but the people would not receive him, because he was heading toward Jerusalem.
Seeing this, the disciples James and John said, "Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from heaven and consume them?"
But he turned and rebuked them.
And they went off to another village.
As they were on the road, a man said to Jesus, "I will follow you wherever you go."
Jesus answered him, "Foxes have dens and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head."
To another he said, "Follow me." The man replied, "Lord, let me first go and bury my father."
Jesus said to him, "Let the dead bury their dead; you, go and proclaim the kingdom of God."
Still another said to him, "I will follow you, Lord; but let me first say farewell to my family."
Jesus answered him, "No one who puts his hand to the plow and then looks back is fit for the kingdom of God."
After this, the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them out two by two ahead of him into every town and place where he himself was about to go.
He said to them, "The harvest is abundant, but the workers are few. So ask the master of the harvest to send out workers for his harvest.
Go! Behold, I am sending you like lambs among wolves.
Carry no purse, no bag, no sandals, and greet no one on the way.
Whatever house you enter, say first, 'Peace to this house.'
And if a man of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; if not, it will return to you.
Stay in that house, eating and drinking what they offer you, for the worker deserves his wages. Do not move from house to house.
Whatever town you enter and where they welcome you, eat what is set before you,
heal the sick who are there, and say to them, 'The kingdom of God has come near to you.'
But whatever town you enter and where they do not welcome you, go out into the streets and say,
'Even the dust of your town that clings to our feet, we wipe off against you. Yet know this: the kingdom of God has come near.'
I tell you: on that day it will be more bearable for Sodom than for that town."
"Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles done among you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would long ago have repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
So at the judgment it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon than for you.
And you, Capernaum, will you be raised up to heaven? You will go down to the realm of the dead.
Whoever listens to you listens to me, whoever rejects you rejects me; and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me."
The seventy-two returned full of joy, "Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!"
He said to them, "I was watching Satan fall from heaven like lightning.
Behold, I have given you the power to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy; nothing will be able to harm you.
Yet do not rejoice that the spirits are subject to you; rejoice rather that your names are written in heaven."

At that very hour, Jesus exulted with joy in the Holy Spirit and said, "I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, for hiding these things from the wise and learned and revealing them to little children. Yes, Father, for such was your good pleasure.
Everything has been handed over to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, nor who the Father is except the Son, and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him."
Then, turning to his disciples, he said to them privately, "Blessed are the eyes that see what you see!
For I tell you, many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it."
And behold, a teacher of the Law stood up and said, to test him, "Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
Jesus said to him, "What is written in the Law? How do you read it?"
He answered, "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself."
Jesus said to him, "You have answered rightly; do this, and you will live."
But wanting to justify himself, he said to Jesus, "And who is my neighbor?"
Jesus replied, "A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho when he fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, beat him, and went off, leaving him half dead.
By chance a priest was going down that road; he saw the man and passed by on the other side.
Likewise a Levite, when he came to the place, saw him and passed by on the other side.
But a Samaritan who was traveling came upon him; and when he saw him, he was moved with compassion.
He came near, bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine, set him on his own mount, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
The next day he took out two pieces of silver, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, 'Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you on my return.'
Which of these three, in your opinion, proved to be the neighbor of the man who fell into the hands of the robbers?"
The teacher answered, "The one who showed him mercy." Jesus said to him, "Go, and you also do the same."
As they were on their way, Jesus entered a village, and a woman named Martha welcomed him into her home.
She had a sister, Mary, who sat at the Lord's feet and listened to his word.
Martha, meanwhile, was busy with the many tasks of serving. She came up and said, "Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her to help me."
The Lord answered her, "Martha, Martha, you are worried and troubled about many things.
Only one thing is necessary. Mary has chosen the better part, and it will not be taken from her."

titres.titre: The return of the unclean spirit
