Against the Pharisees and the experts in the Law

versets.t: One day Jesus was praying in a certain place. When he had finished, one of his disciples said to him, "Lord, teach us to pray, as John taught his disciples."
He said to them, "When you pray, say: Father, hallowed be your name, your kingdom come.
Give us each day our daily bread.
Forgive us our sins, for we ourselves forgive all who are indebted to us. And do not let us enter into temptation."
He said to them, "Suppose one of you has a friend and goes to him in the middle of the night to say, 'My friend, lend me three loaves,
for a friend of mine has arrived from a journey and I have nothing to offer him,'
and the other answers from inside, 'Do not bother me; the door is already locked, and my children and I are in bed; I cannot get up to give you anything.'
Well, I tell you: even if he will not get up and give to him because he is his friend, he will get up because of his persistence and give him whatever he needs.
And I say to you: Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, whoever seeks finds, and to the one who knocks the door will be opened.
Is there a father among you who would give his son a serpent when he asks for a fish?
Or if he asks for an egg, would he give him a scorpion?
If you then, who are evil, know how to give good things to your children, how much more will the Father in heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him!"
Jesus was casting out a demon that was mute. When the demon had gone out, the mute man began to speak, and the crowds were amazed.
But some of them said, "It is by Beelzebul, the prince of demons, that he casts out demons."
Others, to test him, kept demanding of him a sign from heaven.
Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is heading for ruin, and its houses fall one upon another.
If Satan is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out demons by Beelzebul.
But if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your disciples cast them out? So they themselves will be your judges.
But if it is by the finger of God that I cast out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
When a strong man, fully armed, guards his domain, his possessions are safe.
But when someone stronger comes and overpowers him, he takes away the weapons on which he relied and divides up his spoils.
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
When the unclean spirit has gone out of a man, it wanders through arid places seeking rest. Finding none, it says, 'I will return to my house from which I came.'
On arriving, it finds the house swept and well ordered.
Then it goes and brings seven other spirits more wicked than itself; they enter and settle there, and the last state of that man becomes worse than the first."
As he was saying this, a woman in the crowd raised her voice, "Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breasts that nursed you!"
But Jesus replied, "Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and keep it!"
As the crowds were increasing, Jesus began to say, "This generation is an evil generation: it demands a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.
For just as Jonah was a sign for the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will be a sign for this generation.

The queen of the South will rise at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.
The people of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for they repented at the preaching of Jonah, and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.
No one, after lighting a lamp, puts it in a hidden place or under a basket; instead, he sets it on the lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
The lamp of your body is your eye. When your eye is sound, your whole body is full of light; but if it is bad, your body too is in darkness.
So take care: is not the light within you darkness?
If then your whole body is full of light, with no part in darkness, it will be wholly bright, as when a lamp shines on you with its rays."
As he was speaking, a Pharisee invited him to dine with him. Jesus went in and reclined at table.
The Pharisee was surprised to see that he did not wash his hands before the meal.
The Lord said to him, "You Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but your inside is full of greed and wickedness.
Fools! Did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?
Give rather as alms what is within, and everything will be clean for you.

But woe to you Pharisees, who pay the tithe of mint and rue and every garden herb, but neglect justice and the love of God! These are the things you should have practiced, without neglecting the others.
Woe to you Pharisees, who love the front seat in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces!
Woe to you, for you are like those unseen tombs that people walk over without knowing it!"
An expert in the Law spoke up, "Teacher, when you speak this way, you insult us too."
Jesus answered, "Woe to you also, experts in the Law! You load people with burdens impossible to carry, and you yourselves do not touch them with a single finger.
Woe to you, who build the tombs of the prophets, though it was your ancestors who killed them!
So you bear witness that you approve of the deeds of your ancestors: they killed them, and you build their tombs.
That is why the Wisdom of God said: I will send them prophets and apostles; some they will kill, others they will persecute,
so that this generation may be held accountable for the blood of all the prophets shed since the foundation of the world,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, killed between the altar and the sanctuary. Yes, I tell you, this generation will be held accountable for it.
Woe to you, experts in the Law, who have taken away the key of knowledge! You yourselves did not enter, and those who wanted to enter, you prevented."
When Jesus left there, the scribes and Pharisees began to harass him and to press him with questions on many subjects,
setting traps for him to catch some word from his mouth.
Meanwhile, the crowd had gathered by the thousands, so that they were trampling one another. Jesus began to say first to his disciples, "Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
Nothing is veiled that will not be unveiled, nothing secret that will not be known.
So whatever you have said in the dark will be heard in broad daylight; what you have whispered in the ear behind closed doors will be proclaimed from the housetops.
I tell you, my friends: Do not fear those who kill the body and after that can do nothing more.
I will show you whom to fear: fear the one who, after killing, has the power to cast into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear that one.
Are not five sparrows sold for two coins? Yet not one of them is forgotten before God.
Indeed, even the hairs of your head are all numbered. Do not be afraid: you are worth more than many sparrows.
I tell you: whoever acknowledges me before others, the Son of Man will also acknowledge before the angels of God.
But whoever denies me before others will be denied before the angels of God.
Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven; but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
When they bring you before the synagogues, the magistrates, and the authorities, do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say;
for the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you must say."
Someone in the crowd said to Jesus, "Teacher, tell my brother to share our inheritance with me."
Jesus answered him, "Man, who appointed me to judge or divide property between you?"
Then he said to all, "Beware of all greed; even in abundance, a person's life does not depend on possessions."
And he told them this parable: "A rich man's land had produced a good harvest.
He asked himself, 'What shall I do? I have nowhere to store my crop.'
'Here,' he said, 'is what I will do: I will pull down my barns and build larger ones, and there I will store all my grain and my goods.
And I will say to myself: You have goods stored up for many years to come; rest, eat, drink, and be merry.'
But God said to him, 'Fool! This very night your life is demanded of you; and the things you have stored up, whose will they be?'
So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself instead of being rich toward God."
Then Jesus said to his disciples, "That is why I tell you: do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.
Life is more than food, and the body more than clothing.
Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have neither storehouse nor barn, and God feeds them. How much more are you worth than the birds!
Besides, which of you by worrying can add a single hour to the span of your life?
If then the smallest thing is beyond your power, why worry about the rest?
Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of them.
If God so clothes the grass that is in the field today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith!
You too, do not seek what you will eat or what you will drink, and do not be anxious.
For all these things the pagans of the world seek endlessly, but your Father knows that you need them.
Seek rather his kingdom, and these things will be given to you as well.
Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom.
Sell what you own and give it as alms. Make for yourselves purses that do not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
Stay dressed for service, with your lamps lit.
Be like people waiting for their master to return from the wedding, to open for him as soon as he comes and knocks.
Blessed are the servants whom the master, on his arrival, finds keeping watch! Amen, I tell you, he will dress for service, have them recline at table, and come to wait on them.
Whether he comes in the second watch or the third, if he finds them so, blessed are those servants!
Understand this well: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have let his house be broken into.
You too, be ready, for the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect."
Then Peter said, "Lord, are you telling this parable for us, or for everyone?"
The Lord answered, "Who then is the faithful and wise steward whom the master will put in charge of his household to give them their ration of grain at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whom the master, on his arrival, finds so occupied!
Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
But if that servant says to himself, 'My master is delayed in coming,' and begins to beat the menservants and maidservants, to eat and drink and get drunk,
the master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know; he will cut him off and assign him his lot among the unfaithful.
The servant who knew his master's will and did not prepare or act according to that will, will receive a great many blows.

But the one who did not know it, yet deserved blows by his conduct, will receive few. From everyone to whom much has been given, much will be required; and from the one to whom much has been entrusted, more will be demanded.
I have come to cast fire on the earth, and how I wish it were already kindled!
I have a baptism to receive, and what anguish is mine until it is accomplished!
Do you think that I have come to bring peace on earth? No, I tell you, but rather division.
For from now on, in a household of five, they will be divided: three against two and two against three.
They will be divided: father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law."
He also said to the crowds, "When you see a cloud rising in the west, you say at once, 'The rain is coming,' and so it happens.
And when the south wind blows, you say, 'It will be hot,' and it happens.
Hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the earth and the sky; how is it that you do not know how to interpret the present time?
And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

When you go with your adversary before the magistrate, try on the way to settle with him, so that he does not drag you before the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
I tell you: you will not get out until you have paid the very last penny."

titres.titre: The woman healed on a Sabbath
The mustard seed and the yeast

versets.t: At that time, some people came to tell Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mingled with that of their sacrifices.
He answered them, "Do you think that these Galileans were greater sinners than all the others, because they suffered such a fate?
No, I tell you; but unless you turn back to God, you will all perish as they did.
Or those eighteen people killed when the tower of Siloam fell on them: do you think they were more guilty than all the other inhabitants of Jerusalem?
No, I tell you; but unless you turn back to God, you will all perish in the same way."
He also told this parable: "A man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard. He came looking for fruit on it and found none.
So he said to the vinedresser, 'For three years now I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree and found none. Cut it down. Why should it use up the soil?'
The vinedresser answered him, 'Master, leave it one more year, while I dig around it and put in manure.
Perhaps it will bear fruit next year; if not, you will cut it down.'"
One Sabbath day, Jesus was teaching in a synagogue.
And there was a woman there who for eighteen years had been possessed by a spirit that left her crippled: she was bent over and could not straighten up at all.
When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said to her, "Woman, you are set free from your infirmity."
He laid his hands on her, and at once she straightened up and began to glorify God.

But the leader of the synagogue was indignant that Jesus had performed this healing on the Sabbath, and he said to the crowd, "There are six days for work; come and be healed on those days, then, and not on the Sabbath day."
The Lord answered him, "Hypocrites! On the Sabbath day, does not each of you untie his ox or his donkey from the manger and lead it out to drink?
And this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen years, should she not have been set free from this bond on the Sabbath day?"
At these words, all his opponents were put to shame, while the whole crowd rejoiced at all the wonderful things he was doing.
So he said, "What is the kingdom of God like? To what shall I compare it?
It is like a mustard seed that a man took and threw into his garden; it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches."
Again he said, "To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
It is like the yeast that a woman took and buried in a large amount of flour, until the whole batch of dough had risen."
Jesus went through towns and villages teaching, while making his way toward Jerusalem.
Someone asked him, "Lord, are only a few going to be saved?" He said to them,
"Strive to enter through the narrow door; for many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able to.
Once the master of the house has got up and shut the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, 'Lord, open the door for us.' But he will answer you, 'I do not know where you are from.'
Then you will say, 'We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.'
He will answer you, 'I do not know where you are from; away from me, all you who do injustice.'
There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there, when you see Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, and yourselves cast out.
Then people will come from east and west, from north and south, to take their places at the banquet in the kingdom of God.
And behold: some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last."
At that time, some Pharisees came and said to him, "Go away, leave this place, for Herod wants to kill you."
He answered them, "Go and tell that fox: Behold, I cast out demons and perform healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will have finished.
But today, tomorrow and the next day I must continue on my way, for it is not fitting that a prophet should perish outside Jerusalem.

Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who are sent to you, how often have I longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not!
Behold, your house is left to you. I tell you: you will not see me again until the day you say, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!'"

titres.titre: The healing of a man on a Sabbath
The parable of the invited guests

versets.t: One Sabbath day, Jesus had gone to share a meal at the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees, and they were watching him closely.
Now there before him was a man whose body was swollen with fluid.
Jesus addressed the teachers of the Law and the Pharisees, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath, or not?"
They kept silent. Jesus took hold of the man, healed him and sent him away.
Then he said to them, "If one of you has a son or an ox that falls into a well, will you not pull it out at once, even on the Sabbath day?"
And they were unable to answer.
Noticing how the guests were choosing the places of honor, he told them this parable:
"When someone invites you to a wedding feast, do not take the place of honor, in case he has invited a guest more distinguished than you.
Then the one who invited you both would come and say to you, 'Give up your place to this man,' and you would have to go, red with shame, and take the lowest place.
Instead, when you are invited, go and take the lowest place; then, when your host arrives, he will say to you, 'My friend, move up higher.' This will do you honor in front of all the guests.
For whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted."

He also said to the man who had invited him, "When you give a lunch or a dinner, do not invite your friends, your brothers, your relatives, or your rich neighbors, in case they invite you back in return and repay you.
Instead, when you give a feast, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind.
You will be blessed, because they have no way to repay you: you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous."
Hearing this, one of the guests said to him, "Blessed is the one who will share in the meal in the kingdom of God!"
Jesus answered him, "A man was giving a great dinner and invited many people.
At the hour of the dinner, he sent his servant to say to those invited, 'Come, everything is now ready.'
But they all, as if by common agreement, began to make excuses. The first said to him, 'I have bought a field, and I must go and see it; please excuse me.'
Another said, 'I have bought five pairs of oxen, and I am on my way to try them out; please excuse me.'
Another said, 'I have just got married, and that is why I cannot come.'

When the servant returned, he reported all this to his master. Then the master of the house, in anger, said to his servant, 'Go out quickly into the squares and streets of the town, and bring in here the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame.'
The servant came back and said, 'Master, what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.'
The master said to the servant, 'Go out to the roads and along the hedges, and press people to come in, so that my house may be filled.
For I tell you, none of those men who were invited will taste my dinner.'"
Great crowds were traveling along with him. He turned and said to them,
"If anyone comes to me without loving me more than his father, his mother, his wife, his children, his brothers, his sisters, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple.
Whoever does not carry his cross and follow after me cannot be my disciple.
For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down to work out the cost and see whether he has enough to see it through to the end?
Otherwise, if he lays the foundation and is unable to finish, all who see it will start to mock him,
saying, 'This man began to build and was not able to finish.'
Or what king, going to war against another king, does not first sit down to consider whether, with ten thousand men, he can face the one marching against him with twenty thousand?
If he cannot, he sends a delegation, while the other is still far off, to ask for terms of peace.
In the same way, then, none of you can be my disciple unless he gives up everything he has.
Salt is a good thing; but if the salt itself loses its flavor, how will it be restored?
It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure heap: it is thrown out. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!"
All the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to Jesus to listen to him.
The Pharisees and the scribes grumbled, "This man welcomes sinners and eats with them."
So he told them this parable:
"Which of you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine others in the wilderness and go after the one that is lost, until he finds it?
When he has found it, he joyfully hoists it onto his shoulders,
and, back home, he gathers his friends and neighbors to say to them, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep, the one that was lost.'
I tell you: in the same way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of repentance.
Or what woman, if she has ten pieces of silver and loses one of them, does not light a lamp, sweep the house and search carefully until she finds it?
When she has found it, she gathers her friends and neighbors to say to them, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found the coin that I had lost.'
In the same way, I tell you, there is joy among the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
He went on: "A man had two sons.
The younger said to his father, 'Father, give me the share of the estate that is to come to me.' And the father divided his property between them.
A few days later, the younger son gathered together all he had and set off for a distant country, where he squandered his fortune living a dissolute life.
When he had spent everything, a great famine struck that country, and he began to be in need.
So he went and hired himself out to a citizen of that country, who sent him into his fields to look after the pigs.
He would gladly have filled his belly with the carob pods that the pigs were eating, but no one gave him anything.
Then he came to himself and said, 'How many of my father's hired workers have more than enough bread, while here I am, dying of hunger!
I will get up and go to my father, and say to him: Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you;
I no longer deserve to be called your son; treat me as one of your hired workers.'
So he got up and went to his father. While he was still a long way off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and threw his arms around his neck and covered him with kisses.
The son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you; I no longer deserve to be called your son.'
But the father said to his servants, 'Quick, bring the finest robe and put it on him; put a ring on his finger and sandals on his feet.
Bring the fattened calf and kill it: let us eat and celebrate,
for this son of mine was dead, and has come back to life; he was lost, and is found.' And they began to celebrate.
Now the elder son was out in the fields. On his way back, as he drew near the house, he heard music and dancing.
Calling one of the servants, he asked what was going on.
The servant answered him, 'Your brother has come home, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has got him back safe and sound.'
Then the elder son became angry and refused to go in. His father came out and pleaded with him.
But he replied to his father, 'Look, all these years I have served you and never once disobeyed an order of yours, and you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends.
But when this son of yours comes back, the one who has devoured your property with prostitutes, for him you kill the fattened calf!'
The father said to him, 'My child, you are always with me, and everything I have is yours.
But we had to celebrate and rejoice, for this brother of yours was dead, and has come back to life; he was lost, and is found.'"
Jesus also said to his disciples, "A rich man had a steward who was accused before him of squandering his property.
He summoned him and said, 'What is this I hear about you? Give an account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be my steward.'
The steward said to himself, 'What am I to do, now that my master is taking the stewardship away from me? To dig, I have not the strength; to beg, I am ashamed.
I know what I will do, so that once I am removed from my post, there will be people to welcome me into their homes.'
So he called in his master's debtors one by one. He said to the first, 'How much do you owe my master?'
He answered, 'A hundred barrels of oil.' The steward said to him, 'Here is your bill; sit down quickly and write fifty.'
Then he said to another, 'And you, how much do you owe?' He answered, 'A hundred sacks of wheat.' The steward said to him, 'Here is your bill; write eighty.'
And the master praised this dishonest steward, because he had acted shrewdly. For the children of this world are shrewder in dealing with their own kind than the children of light.
Well then, I tell you: use dishonest wealth to make friends for yourselves, so that when it runs out, these friends may welcome you into the eternal dwellings.
Whoever is faithful in a small matter is also faithful in a great one, and whoever is dishonest in a small matter is also dishonest in a great one.
If, then, you have not been faithful with dishonest wealth, who will entrust you with the true riches?
And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to another, who will give you what is your own?
No servant can serve two masters: either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve both God and Money."
The Pharisees, who loved money, heard all this and sneered at him.
Jesus said to them, "You are the ones who pass yourselves off as righteous in the sight of others, but God knows your hearts; for what is exalted in human eyes is an abomination before God.
The Law and the Prophets lasted until John; since then, the kingdom of God is proclaimed as the Good News, and everyone strives to enter it.
It is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a letter of the Law to fall.
Any man who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery; and the man who marries a woman divorced by her husband commits adultery.
There was a rich man, dressed in purple and fine linen, who feasted splendidly every day.
A poor man named Lazarus, covered in sores, lay at the rich man's gate.
He would gladly have satisfied his hunger with what fell from the rich man's table; but even the dogs would come and lick his sores.
Now the poor man died, and the angels carried him to Abraham's side. The rich man also died, and was buried.
In the realm of the dead, in the midst of his torments, he looked up and saw Abraham far off, and Lazarus close beside him.
He cried out, 'Father Abraham, have pity on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am in terrible agony in these flames.'
But Abraham answered, 'My child, remember: you received your good things during your lifetime, and Lazarus received the bad things; now, here, he is comforted, while you are in agony.
Besides all this, between us and you there is a great chasm, so that those who would cross over from here to you cannot, nor can anyone cross over from there to us.'
The rich man said, 'Then, father, I beg you to send Lazarus to my father's house,
for I have five brothers; let him warn them, so that they too may not come to this place of torment.'
Abraham said to him, 'They have Moses and the Prophets; let them listen to them.'
The rich man replied, 'No, Father Abraham; but if someone comes to them from the dead, they will repent.'
Abraham answered him, 'If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, they will not be convinced even if someone rises from the dead.'"

titres.titre: The coming of the kingdom of God
The days of the Son of Man

versets.t: Jesus said to his disciples, "It is inevitable that there should be occasions for stumbling; but woe to the one through whom they come!
It would be better for him to have a large millstone tied around his neck and to be thrown into the sea, than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
Be on your guard. If your brother does wrong, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
Even if he sins against you seven times a day and seven times comes back to you saying, 'I repent,' you must forgive him."
The apostles said to the Lord, "Increase our faith."
The Lord answered, "If you had faith the size of a mustard seed, you could say to this mulberry tree, 'Be uprooted and planted in the sea,' and it would obey you.
Which of you, if he has a servant plowing or tending the flock, will say to him when he comes in from the fields, 'Come at once and take your place at table'?
Will he not rather say to him, 'Prepare my meal, get yourself ready and wait on me while I eat and drink; after that you may eat and drink in your turn'?
Does he thank the servant for doing what he was ordered to do?
In the same way, when you have done all you were ordered to do, say, 'We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.'"
On his way to Jerusalem, Jesus was traveling along the border between Samaria and Galilee.
As he entered a village, ten lepers came to meet him. They stopped at a distance
and raised their voices, "Jesus, Master, have pity on us!"
When he saw them, he said to them, "Go and show yourselves to the priests." And as they were going, they were cleansed.
One of them, seeing that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God at the top of his voice;
he threw himself face down at the feet of Jesus to thank him. Now he was a Samaritan.
Then Jesus said, "Were not all ten cleansed? Where are the other nine?
Was there no one to come back and give glory to God except this foreigner?"
Then he said to him, "Get up and go: your faith has saved you."
The Pharisees asked him when the kingdom of God would come. He answered them, "The kingdom of God does not come in a way that can be observed.
No one will say, 'Here it is,' or, 'There it is,' for behold, the kingdom of God is among you."
Then he said to his disciples, "Days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it.
People will say to you, 'Here it is,' or, 'There it is.' Do not go, do not run after them.
For as the lightning that flashes lights up the sky from one end to the other, so will it be with the Son of Man on his day.
But first he must suffer greatly and be rejected by this generation.
As it was in the days of Noah, so it will be in the days of the Son of Man.
People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, up to the day when Noah entered the ark: the flood came and destroyed them all.
It was the same in the days of Lot: people were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building;
but on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from the sky and destroyed them all.
It will be just the same on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
On that day, anyone on the housetop with his belongings inside the house must not go down to get them; likewise, anyone in the fields must not turn back.
Remember Lot's wife.
Whoever tries to preserve his life will lose it, and whoever loses it will save it.
I tell you: on that night, of two people lying in one bed, one will be taken and the other left;
of two women grinding grain together, one will be taken and the other left."
They asked him, "Where, then, Lord?"
He answered them, "Where the body is, there also the vultures will gather."

titres.titre: The Pharisee and the tax collector
The third announcement of the Passion

versets.t: Jesus told them a parable to show that they should pray at all times and never lose heart:
"In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor had regard for anyone.
There was also in that town a widow who kept coming to him and saying, 'Grant me justice against my adversary.'
For a long time he refused; but later he said to himself, 'It is true that I neither fear God nor have regard for anyone,
but because this widow keeps wearing me out, I will grant her justice, so that she does not keep coming and pestering me endlessly.'"
The Lord added, "Listen to what this unjust judge says.
And will God not grant justice to his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night? Will he keep them waiting?
I tell you: he will grant them justice without delay. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?"
He also told this parable to some who were convinced of their own righteousness and looked down on everyone else:
"Two men went up to the Temple to pray: one was a Pharisee, the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed to himself in this way, 'My God, I thank you that I am not like the rest of humanity, thieves, unjust, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week and pay a tithe on everything I earn.'
But the tax collector stood at a distance and did not even dare to raise his eyes to heaven; instead he beat his breast, saying, 'My God, have mercy on me, a sinner.'
I tell you: it was this man who went back home justified, and not the other; for whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted."
People were also bringing their little children to him for him to touch them. Seeing this, the disciples rebuked them.
But Jesus called the children to him and said, "Let the children come to me, and do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to those who are like them.
Amen, I tell you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter it."
A certain ruler questioned him, "Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?"
Jesus said to him, "Why do you call me good? No one is good but God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery, do not commit murder, do not steal, do not give false testimony, honor your father and your mother."
The man answered, "All these I have kept since my youth."
Hearing this, Jesus said to him, "There is still one thing you lack: sell everything you have, distribute it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me."
When he heard this, the man became very sad, for he was extremely rich.
Seeing him like this, Jesus said, "How hard it is for those who have riches to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God."
Those who were listening said, "Then who can be saved?"
He answered, "What is impossible for human beings is possible for God."
Then Peter said, "Look, we have left everything to follow you."
Jesus said to them, "Amen, I tell you: there is no one who has left house, wife, brothers, parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
who will not receive much more in this present time, and in the world to come, eternal life."
Jesus took the Twelve aside and said to them, "Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything the prophets have written about the Son of Man is going to be fulfilled.
He will be handed over to the Gentiles, mocked, insulted and spat upon;
after they have flogged him, they will put him to death, and on the third day he will rise again."
But they understood none of this: this saying remained hidden from them, and they did not grasp what was being said.
As Jesus was approaching Jericho, a blind man was sitting by the roadside, begging.
Hearing the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.
They told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
He cried out, "Jesus, Son of David, have pity on me!"
Those walking ahead scolded him and told him to be quiet, but he cried out all the louder, "Son of David, have pity on me!"
Jesus stopped and ordered that the man be brought to him. When he was near, Jesus asked him,
"What do you want me to do for you?" He answered, "Lord, let me see again."
Jesus said to him, "Receive your sight: your faith has saved you."
At once he received his sight, and he followed Jesus, glorifying God. And all the people, seeing this, gave praise to God.

titres.titre: The parable of the gold coins

versets.t: Jesus entered Jericho and was passing through the town.
Now there was a man named Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector and a rich man,
who was trying to see who Jesus was; but he could not because of the crowd, for he was short in stature.
So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus, who was going to pass that way.
When he reached the place, Jesus looked up and said to him, "Zacchaeus, come down quickly: today I must stay at your house."
Zacchaeus came down at once and welcomed him with joy.
Seeing this, everyone grumbled, "He has gone to stay with a sinner."
But Zacchaeus stood up and said to the Lord, "Behold, Lord: I give half of my possessions to the poor, and if I have cheated anyone of anything, I pay back four times as much."
Jesus said to him, "Today salvation has come to this house, for he too is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of Man came to seek and to save what was lost."
As the crowd was listening, Jesus went on to tell a parable, because he was near Jerusalem and they thought that the kingdom of God was going to appear at any moment.
So he said, "A man of noble birth set out for a distant country to be appointed king and then to return.
He called ten of his servants, gave them ten gold coins and said to them, 'Put these to work until I come back.'
But his fellow citizens hated him, and they sent a delegation after him to say, 'We do not want this man to reign over us.'
When he returned, having been made king, he sent for the servants to whom he had entrusted the money, to find out what each one had earned.
The first came forward, 'Lord, your gold coin has earned ten more.'
The master said to him, 'Well done, good servant; since you have been faithful in such a small matter, take charge of ten towns.'
The second came, 'Lord, your gold coin has made five.'
To that one too he said, 'You, be in charge of five towns.'
Another came, 'Lord, here is your gold coin; I have kept it wrapped in a cloth,
for I was afraid of you: you are a demanding man, you take out what you did not deposit and you reap what you did not sow.'
The master replied, 'I judge you by your own words, wicked servant. You knew that I am a demanding man, taking out what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow;
why, then, did you not put my money in the bank? On my return I would have withdrawn it with interest.'
Then he said to those standing there, 'Take the gold coin away from him and give it to the one who has ten.'
They said to him, 'Lord, he already has ten!'
I tell you: to everyone who has, more will be given; but from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away.
As for my enemies, those who did not want me as their king, bring them here and put them to death before me."
After saying this, Jesus went on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
When he approached Bethphage and Bethany, near the hill called the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,
saying, "Go into the village ahead of you. As you enter it, you will find a colt tied up, that no one has yet ridden. Untie it and bring it here.
And if anyone asks you why you are untying it, say, 'The Lord needs it.'"
Those who were sent went off and found everything just as Jesus had told them.
As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, "Why are you untying that colt?"
They answered, "The Lord needs it."
They brought the colt to Jesus, threw their cloaks over it and helped Jesus mount.
As he went along, people spread their cloaks on the road.
He was already approaching the descent from the Mount of Olives when the whole crowd of disciples, filled with joy, began to praise God at the top of their voices for all the miracles they had seen.
They said, "Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!"
Some Pharisees in the crowd said to Jesus, "Teacher, rebuke your disciples."
He answered, "I tell you: if they keep silent, the stones will cry out."
When he came near and saw the city, Jesus wept over it,
saying, "If only you too had recognized, on this day, what brings peace! But now it is hidden from your eyes.
Days will come upon you when your enemies will surround you with ramparts, encircle you and press in on you from every side;
they will crush you, you and your children within your walls, and they will not leave one stone upon another in you, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation."
Jesus entered the Temple and began to drive out those who were selling there,
saying to them, "It is written: My house shall be a house of prayer; but you have made it a den of robbers."
Every day he taught in the Temple. The chief priests, the scribes and the leaders of the people were trying to put him to death,
but they could not find a way to do it, for all the people were hanging on his words, listening to him.

titres.titre: The Christ, son and Lord of David

versets.t: One of those days, as Jesus was teaching the people in the Temple and proclaiming the Good News, the chief priests and the scribes came up, together with the elders.
They said to him, "Tell us by what authority you are doing these things, or who gave you this authority."
He answered them, "I too will ask you a question. Tell me:
was John's baptism from heaven or from human beings?"
They reasoned among themselves, "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will reply, 'Why did you not believe him?'
And if we say, 'From human beings,' all the people will stone us, for they are convinced that John was a prophet."
So they answered that they did not know where it came from.
Jesus said to them, "Then neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."
He began to tell the people this parable: "A man planted a vineyard, leased it to tenants and went abroad for a long time.
When the time came, he sent a servant to the tenants so that they would give him a share of the produce of the vineyard. But they beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
He sent yet another servant; that one too they beat, insulted and sent away empty-handed.
He sent a third; that one also they wounded and threw out.
Then the owner of the vineyard said, 'What am I to do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.'
But when they saw him, the tenants plotted together, 'This is the heir; let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.'
They threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What, then, will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
He will come, destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others." At these words, they said, "May this never happen!"
But Jesus looked straight at them and said, "What, then, does this passage of Scripture mean: The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone?
Everyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, and the one on whom it falls will be crushed."
The scribes and the chief priests sought to lay hands on him at that very hour, but they were afraid of the people; for they had understood well that this parable was aimed at them.
They kept their eyes on him. They sent agents who pretended to be honest men, to catch him out in something he said and so hand him over to the power and authority of the governor.
They questioned him, "Teacher, we know that you speak and teach rightly, showing no partiality, but teaching the way of God in accordance with the truth.
Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?"
Jesus saw through their trickery and said to them,
"Show me a silver coin. Whose image and inscription does it bear?" They answered, "Caesar's."
He said to them, "Then give back to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's."
They were unable to catch him out in anything he said in front of the people, and, amazed at his answer, they fell silent.
Some Sadducees, those who deny the resurrection, came up and questioned him,
"Teacher, Moses prescribed this for us: If a married man dies without a child, his brother must marry the widow and raise up descendants for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers. The first took a wife and died without a child.
The second,
then the third married the widow, and likewise all seven: they died leaving no child.
Finally the woman died too.
At the resurrection, whose wife will she be, since the seven had her as their wife?"
Jesus said to them, "The children of this world take a wife or a husband;
but those who have been judged worthy to share in the world to come and in the resurrection of the dead take neither wife nor husband.
They can no longer die, for they are like the angels; they are children of God, being children of the resurrection.
And that the dead rise, Moses himself made clear in the passage about the Bush, when he calls the Lord the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.
Now God is not the God of the dead, but of the living; for to him all are alive."
Some of the scribes spoke up, "Teacher, you have spoken well."
And they no longer dared to question him about anything.
Jesus said to them, "How can people say that the Christ is the son of David?
David himself says, in the book of Psalms: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand,
until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.
David therefore calls him Lord: how, then, can he be his son?"
In the hearing of all the people, he said to his disciples,
"Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes, to be greeted in the squares, to take the front seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at feasts.
They devour the property of widows and, for show, say long prayers: they will receive a heavier condemnation."

titres.titre: The announcement of the Temple's ruin
The coming of the Son of Man
The parable of the fig tree

versets.t: Looking up, Jesus saw rich people putting their offerings into the Temple treasury.
He also saw a poor widow put in two small bronze coins,
and he said, "Truly, I tell you: this poor widow has put in more than all the others.
For all of them gave their offering out of their surplus; but she, out of her poverty, has put in all she had to live on."
As some were remarking that the Temple was adorned with beautiful stones and votive offerings, Jesus declared,
"These things that you are looking at, days will come when not one stone will be left upon another: everything will be destroyed."
They asked him, "Teacher, when will this happen? And what will be the sign that it is about to take place?"
He answered, "Take care not to be led astray; for many will come in my name, saying, 'It is I,' and, 'The time is near.' Do not follow them.
When you hear of wars and uprisings, do not be terrified: these things must happen first, but the end will not come immediately."
Then he said to them, "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
There will be great earthquakes and, in various places, plagues and famines; there will also be terrifying phenomena and great signs from the sky.
But before all this, they will lay hands on you, persecute you, hand you over to the synagogues and prisons, and drag you before kings and governors, because of my name.
This will be your opportunity to bear witness.
Make up your minds, then, not to prepare your defense in advance;
for I will give you speech and wisdom that none of your adversaries will be able to resist or contradict.
You will be handed over even by your parents, your brothers, your relatives and your friends, and some of you will be put to death.
You will be hated by everyone because of my name.
But not a hair of your head will be lost.
By your perseverance you will gain your life.
When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its devastation is near.
Then let those in Judea flee to the mountains, let those in the city leave it, and let those in the countryside not enter it;
for these will be days of punishment, when all that is written will be fulfilled.
Woe to those who are pregnant or nursing in those days! For there will be great distress upon the land, and wrath against this people.
They will fall by the edge of the sword and be led away captive into all the nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled underfoot by the nations, until the time of the nations is fulfilled.
There will be signs in the sun, the moon and the stars; on the earth, the nations will be in anguish, bewildered by the roaring of the sea and the waves.
People will faint from fear, in dread of what is coming upon the world, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud, with power and great glory.
When these things begin to happen, stand up straight and raise your heads, for your deliverance is drawing near."
And he told them a comparison: "Look at the fig tree and all the trees:
as soon as they bud, you know of yourselves, by looking at them, that summer is near.
In the same way, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
Amen, I tell you: this generation will not pass away before all this takes place.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
Be on your guard, so that your hearts are not weighed down with dissipation, drunkenness and the cares of life, and that day close in on you unexpectedly,
like a snare; for it will fall upon all the inhabitants of the whole earth.
Stay awake and pray at all times, so that you may have the strength to escape all that is going to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man."
By day, Jesus taught in the Temple; at night, he went out to spend it on the hill called the Mount of Olives.
And early each morning, all the people came to him in the Temple to listen to him.

titres.titre: The plot and the betrayal of Judas
The Last Supper and the institution of the Eucharist
The agony on the Mount of Olives

versets.t: The feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called Passover, was drawing near.
The chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to put Jesus to death, for they were afraid of the people.
Then Satan entered into Judas, called Iscariot, one of the Twelve.
He went to the chief priests and the officers of the guard to arrange with them how he might hand Jesus over to them.
Delighted, they agreed to give him money.
He consented and began looking for an opportunity to hand him over to them away from the crowd.
The day of Unleavened Bread came, on which the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
Jesus sent Peter and John, "Go and prepare the Passover meal for us."
They asked him, "Where do you want us to prepare it?"
He answered them, "As you enter the city, you will meet a man carrying a jug of water. Follow him to the house he enters,
and say to the master of the house, 'The Teacher sends word: Where is the room where I am to eat the Passover with my disciples?'
He will show you a large upstairs room, all furnished; make the preparations there."
They went off, found everything just as Jesus had told them and prepared the Passover.
When the hour came, Jesus took his place at table, and the apostles with him.
He said to them, "I have earnestly longed to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
For I tell you, I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God."
Then, taking a cup, he gave thanks and said, "Take this and share it among yourselves.
For I tell you, from now on I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."
Then he took bread, gave thanks, broke it and gave it to them, saying, "This is my body, given for you. Do this in memory of me."
After the meal, he did the same with the cup, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood, poured out for you.
But behold, the hand of the one who is betraying me is with me on the table.
The Son of Man is going away, as has been decided; but woe to that man by whom he is betrayed!"
And they began to ask one another which of them was going to do this.
A dispute also arose among them: which of them was to be regarded as the greatest?
Jesus said to them, "The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who exercise power have themselves called benefactors.
With you it is not to be so: the greatest among you must be like the youngest, and the one who leads, like the one who serves.
For who is the greater: the one at table or the one who serves? Is it not the one at table? Yet I am among you as one who serves.
You are the ones who have stood by me in my trials;
and I confer a kingdom on you, just as my Father conferred one on me:
you will eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and you will sit on thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel.
Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has demanded to have you all, to sift you like wheat.
But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail; and you, once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers."
Peter said to him, "Lord, with you I am ready to go to prison and to death."
Jesus answered, "I tell you, Peter: today the rooster will not crow until you have three times denied that you know me."
Then he said to them, "When I sent you out without purse, bag or sandals, did you lack anything?" They answered, "No."
He said to them, "But now, whoever has a purse, let him take it, and likewise a bag; and whoever has no sword, let him sell his cloak to buy one.
For I tell you, this word of Scripture must be fulfilled in me: He was counted among the criminals. Yes, what concerns me is reaching its end."
They said to him, "Lord, here are two swords." He answered them, "That is enough."
Then he went out and made his way, as was his custom, to the Mount of Olives, and his disciples followed him.
When he reached the place, he said to them, "Pray that you may not enter into temptation."
Then he withdrew from them about a stone's throw and, kneeling down, he prayed,
"Father, if you are willing, take this cup away from me! Yet not my will, but yours, be done."
Then an angel from heaven appeared to him, giving him strength.
In his anguish, he prayed more earnestly, and his sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground.
Rising from his prayer, he came to the disciples and found them asleep, worn out by sorrow.
He said to them, "Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray, that you may not enter into temptation."
While he was still speaking, a crowd arrived. The man called Judas, one of the Twelve, was leading them; he approached Jesus to kiss him.
Jesus said to him, "Judas, is it with a kiss that you betray the Son of Man?"
Seeing what was about to happen, those around Jesus said, "Lord, shall we strike with the sword?"
And one of them struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear.
But Jesus said, "Stop, no more of this!" Then he touched the man's ear and healed him.
To the chief priests, the officers of the Temple guard and the elders who had come for him, Jesus said, "Am I a bandit, that you have come out with swords and clubs?
Every day I was with you in the Temple, and you did not lay a hand on me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness."
They arrested him, led him away and took him to the house of the high priest. Peter followed at a distance.
A fire had been lit in the middle of the courtyard, and people had sat down around it; Peter sat among them.
A servant girl, seeing him sitting in the firelight, stared at him and said, "This man was with him too."
But Peter denied it, "Woman, I do not know him."
A little later, someone else saw him and said, "You are one of them too." Peter replied, "No, I am not."
About an hour later, another man insisted, "Surely this man was with him too, for he is a Galilean."
Peter answered, "I do not know what you are talking about." And at that moment, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
The Lord turned and looked at Peter; and Peter remembered the word the Lord had spoken to him, "Today, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times."
He went out and wept bitterly.
The men who were guarding Jesus mocked him and beat him.
They blindfolded him and asked him, "Prophesy: who struck you?"
And they heaped many other insults on him.
When day broke, the council of the elders of the people met, along with the chief priests and the scribes. They had Jesus brought before their assembly
and said to him, "If you are the Christ, tell us." He answered them, "If I tell you, you will not believe;
and if I question you, you will not answer.
But from now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the almighty God."
Then they all said, "So you are the Son of God?" He answered them, "You say so yourselves: I am."
They said, "What further need do we have of testimony? We have heard it ourselves from his own mouth."
Then the whole assembly rose and led Jesus before Pilate.
They began to accuse him, "We have found this man stirring up trouble in our nation: he opposes paying taxes to Caesar and claims to be Christ, a king."
Pilate questioned him, "Are you the king of the Jews?" Jesus answered, "It is you who say so."
Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, "I find no grounds for condemning this man."
But they insisted, "He stirs up the people by teaching throughout the whole of Judea; he began in Galilee, and here he is now."
When he heard this, Pilate asked whether the man was a Galilean.
Learning that he came under Herod's authority, he sent him to Herod, who happened to be in Jerusalem himself in those days.
At the sight of Jesus, Herod was overjoyed: for a long time he had wanted to see him, because he had heard about him and hoped to see him perform a miracle.
He plied him with many questions, but Jesus made no answer.
The chief priests and the scribes were standing there, accusing him vehemently.
Then Herod, along with his soldiers, treated him with contempt and mocked him; he dressed him in a splendid robe and sent him back to Pilate.
That day, Herod and Pilate became friends, though before they had been enemies.
Pilate called together the chief priests, the leaders and the people,

and said to them, "You brought me this man on the charge that he was inciting the people to revolt. Now, I have examined him in your presence and found in him none of the crimes of which you accuse him;
neither has Herod, since he sent him back to us. As you can see, he has done nothing that deserves death.
I will therefore have him flogged and release him."
Now at each feast he was obliged to release one prisoner for them.
But they all cried out together, "Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us!"
This Barabbas had been thrown into prison for an uprising that had taken place in the city, and for murder.
Pilate, who wanted to release Jesus, addressed them again;
but they shouted back, "Crucify him! Crucify him!"
For the third time he said to them, "What wrong has he done, then? I have found in him no grounds for the death penalty. I will therefore have him flogged and release him."
But they kept insisting with loud shouts, demanding that he be crucified, and their clamor prevailed.
Pilate decided to grant what they were asking.
He released the man they were demanding, the one thrown into prison for uprising and murder, and he handed Jesus over to their will.
As they led him away, they seized a man named Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the fields, and they laid the cross on him to carry it behind Jesus.
A great crowd of the people followed him, along with women who were beating their breasts and lamenting for him.
Turning to them, Jesus said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me! Weep rather for yourselves and for your children.
For behold, days are coming when people will say, 'Blessed are the barren women, those who have never given birth, those who have never nursed!'
Then they will begin to say to the mountains, 'Fall on us!' and to the hills, 'Cover us!'
For if they treat the green wood like this, what will happen to the dry wood?"
Two others, criminals, were also led out to be executed with him.
When they came to the place called the Skull, they crucified him there, along with the two criminals, one on his right and the other on his left.
Jesus said, "Father, forgive them: they do not know what they are doing." And to divide his garments, they cast lots for them.
The people stood by, watching. The leaders, for their part, sneered, "He saved others; let him save himself, if he is the Christ of God, the Chosen One!"
The soldiers also mocked him; coming up, they offered him sour wine,
saying, "If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself!"
There was also an inscription above him: This is the king of the Jews.
One of the criminals crucified there insulted him, "Are you not the Christ? Save yourself, and us with you!"
But the other rebuked him, "Have you no fear of God at all, you who are under the same sentence?
For us, it is just: we are paying for our deeds; but this man has done nothing wrong."
And he said, "Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom."
Jesus answered him, "Amen, I tell you: today you will be with me in Paradise."
It was already about noon when darkness came over the whole land, until three o'clock in the afternoon.
The sun was veiled. And the veil of the sanctuary was torn down the middle.
Jesus cried out with a loud voice, "Father, into your hands I commend my spirit." With these words, he breathed his last.
Seeing what had happened, the centurion glorified God and said, "Truly, this man was righteous."
And all the crowd that had gathered for this spectacle, seeing what had happened, went home beating their breasts.
All those who knew him stood at a distance, along with the women who had accompanied him from Galilee, and they watched.
Now there was a man named Joseph, a member of the council, a good and righteous man,
who had not agreed to their decision or their actions. He was from Arimathea, a town of the Jews, and he too was waiting for the kingdom of God.
He went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
He took it down from the cross, wrapped it in a linen shroud and laid it in a tomb cut in the rock, where no one had yet been laid.
It was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was beginning.
The women who had come from Galilee with Jesus followed Joseph; they looked at the tomb and saw how the body had been laid there.
Then they returned and prepared spices and perfumes. And on the Sabbath day they rested, according to the commandment.

titres.titre: The disciples on the road to Emmaus

versets.t: On the first day of the week, at early dawn, the women went to the tomb, carrying the spices they had prepared.
They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
When they went in, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
As they stood there bewildered, behold, two men in dazzling clothes appeared to them.
Seized with fear, they bowed their faces to the ground. But the men said to them, "Why do you look for the Living One among the dead?
He is not here; he has risen. Remember what he told you while he was still in Galilee:
The Son of Man must be handed over into the hands of sinners, be crucified, and on the third day rise again."
Then they remembered his words.
Returning from the tomb, they reported all this to the Eleven and to all the others.
It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James; the other women with them also told the apostles.
But in their eyes these words seemed like nonsense, and they did not believe them.
Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb; bending down, he saw only the linen cloths. And he went back home, amazed at what had happened.
That same day, two disciples were making their way to a village called Emmaus, about eleven kilometers from Jerusalem,
and they were talking with each other about all that had just happened.
Now, as they talked and discussed, Jesus himself drew near and walked along with them;
but their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
He said to them, "What are you discussing as you walk along?" They stopped, their faces downcast.
One of them, named Cleopas, answered him, "Are you the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know what has happened there these last few days?"
He said to them, "What things?" They answered him, "The things about Jesus of Nazareth, a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people:
how our chief priests and leaders handed him over to be condemned to death, and crucified him.
We had hoped that he was the one who would set Israel free; but here it is, the third day since all this happened.
It is true that some women of our group have astonished us: they went to the tomb early in the morning
and, not finding his body, they came back saying that they had even seen a vision of angels who declared him alive.
Some of our companions went to the tomb and found things just as the women had said; but him they did not see."
Then he said to them, "How foolish you are, and how slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!
Was it not necessary that the Christ should suffer these things to enter into his glory?"
And, beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he explained to them what was said about himself in all the Scriptures.
They drew near to the village they were going to, and Jesus made as if to go on farther.
But they urged him strongly, "Stay with us, for evening is coming and the day is already drawing to a close." And he went in to stay with them.
Now, when he was at table with them, he took the bread, said the blessing, broke it and gave it to them.
Then their eyes were opened and they recognized him; but he vanished from their sight.
And they said to one another, "Were not our hearts burning within us while he was speaking to us on the road and opening the Scriptures to us?"
That very moment they got up and returned to Jerusalem. There they found the Eleven and their companions gathered together,
who said to them, "The Lord has truly risen, and he has appeared to Simon!"
Then they told what had happened on the road, and how they had recognized him in the breaking of the bread.
While they were still speaking, Jesus himself stood in their midst and said to them, "Peace be with you."
Seized with fear and terror, they thought they were seeing a ghost.
But he said to them, "Why are you troubled, and why do these doubts rise in your hearts?
Look at my hands and my feet: it is really I! Touch me and see: a ghost does not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have."
As he said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.
As, in their joy, they still could not believe it and stood there amazed, he said to them, "Have you anything here to eat?"
They offered him a piece of grilled fish.
He took it and ate it in front of them.
Then he said to them, "This is what I told you while I was still with you: everything written about me in the law of Moses, the prophets and the psalms had to be fulfilled."
Then he opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
He said to them, "Thus it is written that the Christ would suffer and rise from the dead on the third day,
and that in his name conversion would be proclaimed, for the forgiveness of sins, to all the nations, beginning from Jerusalem.
You are the witnesses of these things.
And behold, I am sending upon you what my Father has promised. As for you, stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high."
Then he led them out toward Bethany and, lifting up his hands, he blessed them.
Now, as he was blessing them, he parted from them and was carried up into heaven.
They bowed down before him, then returned to Jerusalem, filled with great joy;
and they were continually in the Temple, blessing God.

titres.titre: The Prologue: the Word Made Flesh
The Testimony of John the Baptist

versets.t: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was in the beginning with God.
Through him all things were made, and nothing that exists was made without him.
In him was life, and the life was the light of men.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
There was a man sent from God; his name was John.
He came as a witness, to bear witness to the light, so that through him all might believe.
He was not the light, but he came to bear witness to the light.
The Word was the true light, which enlightens every man as it comes into the world.
He was in the world, and the world was made through him, yet the world did not know him.
He came to his own, and his own did not receive him.
But to all who did receive him, to those who believe in his name, he gave the power to become children of God.
They were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
And the Word became flesh and pitched his tent among us; and we have seen his glory, the glory he holds from his Father as the only Son, full of grace and truth.
John bears witness to him. He cries out: "This is the one I spoke of: he who comes after me has passed ahead of me, for he existed before me."
Indeed, from his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace.
For the Law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God; the only Son, who is turned toward the Father's heart, he is the one who has made him known.
This is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him: "Who are you?"
He acknowledged it plainly; he declared: "I am not the Christ."
They asked him: "What are you then? Are you Elijah?" He said: "I am not." "Are you the Prophet?" He answered: "No."
So they said to him: "Who are you? So that we may give an answer to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?"
He declared: "I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness: Make straight the way of the Lord, as the prophet Isaiah said."
Now those who had been sent were Pharisees.
They questioned him again: "Why then do you baptize, if you are neither the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?"
John answered them: "I baptize with water; but among you stands one whom you do not know,
the one who comes after me, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to untie."
This took place at Bethany, on the other side of the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
The next day, John sees Jesus coming toward him, and he says: "Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world.
This is the one of whom I said: After me comes a man who has passed ahead of me, for he existed before me.
I myself did not know him; but if I came baptizing with water, it was so that he might be revealed to Israel."
And John gave this testimony: "I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove, and it remained on him.
I myself did not know him; but the one who sent me to baptize with water had told me: The one on whom you see the Spirit come down and remain, he is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.
And I have seen, and I bear witness: he is the Son of God."
The next day, John was there again, with two of his disciples.
Watching Jesus pass by, he said: "Behold the Lamb of God."
The two disciples heard him say this, and they followed Jesus.
Jesus turned around, and seeing that they were following him, he said to them: "What are you looking for?" They answered him: "Rabbi, where are you staying?" (this word means: Teacher.)
He said to them: "Come, and you will see." They came, they saw where he was staying, and they remained with him that day. It was about four o'clock in the afternoon.
Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who had heard John's words and followed Jesus.
He first finds his brother Simon and says to him: "We have found the Messiah" (this word is translated: Christ).
He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said: "You are Simon, son of John; you shall be called Cephas" (which is translated: Peter).
The next day, Jesus decided to leave for Galilee. He finds Philip and says to him: "Follow me."
Philip was from Bethsaida, the town of Andrew and Peter.
Philip finds Nathanael and says to him: "The one Moses spoke of in the Law, and the prophets too, we have found him: it is Jesus, son of Joseph, from Nazareth."
Nathanael replied: "Can anything good come out of Nazareth?" Philip said to him: "Come and see."
Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him, and he said of him: "Here truly is an Israelite in whom there is no deceit."
Nathanael said to him: "How do you know me?" Jesus answered him: "Before Philip even called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you."
Nathanael responded: "Rabbi, you are the Son of God, you are the King of Israel!"
Jesus answered him: "Because I told you that I had seen you under the fig tree, you believe! You will see greater things still."
And he added: "Amen, amen, I say to you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man."

titres.titre: The Wedding at Cana: the First Sign

versets.t: On the third day, there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee. The mother of Jesus was there,
and Jesus too had been invited to the wedding, along with his disciples.
Now the wine ran out. The mother of Jesus said to him: "They have no more wine."
Jesus answered her: "Woman, what do you want of me? My hour has not yet come."
His mother said to the servants: "Do whatever he tells you."
There were six stone jars there, meant for the purifications of the Jews; each could hold about eighty to a hundred and twenty litres.
Jesus said to the servants: "Fill these jars with water." And they filled them to the brim.
He said to them: "Now draw some out, and take it to the head steward." They took it to him.
The head steward tasted the water that had become wine, without knowing where it came from, but the servants who had drawn the water knew. So he called the bridegroom
and said to him: "Everyone serves the good wine first, and the lesser wine when the guests are merry; but you have kept the good wine until now!"
Such was, at Cana in Galilee, the first of the signs that Jesus performed. In this way he revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
After this, he went down to Capernaum with his mother, his brothers, and his disciples; but they stayed there only a few days.
The Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
In the Temple he found the sellers of oxen, sheep, and doves, as well as the money changers, all set up there.
With cords he made a whip, and he drove them all out of the Temple, with their sheep and oxen; he scattered the money changers' coins and overturned their tables.
And he said to the sellers of doves: "Take these away from here. Do not make my Father's house a house of trade."
His disciples remembered that it is written: "Zeal for your house will consume me."
Then the Jews spoke up: "What sign can you show us, to act like this?"
Jesus answered them: "Destroy this sanctuary, and in three days I will raise it up."
The Jews replied: "It took forty-six years to build this sanctuary, and you would raise it up in three days?"
But he was speaking of the sanctuary of his body.
So, when he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.
While Jesus was in Jerusalem for the feast of the Passover, many believed in his name when they saw the signs he was performing.
But Jesus did not entrust himself to them, for he knew them all;
he had no need of any testimony about man, for he himself knew what is in man.

titres.titre: The Final Testimony of John the Baptist
The One Who Comes from Above

versets.t: There was, among the Pharisees, a man named Nicodemus, a leading man among the Jews.
He came to Jesus by night and said to him: "Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher who has come from God; for no one can perform the signs you do, unless God is with him."
Jesus answered him: "Amen, amen, I say to you: unless a man is born anew, he cannot see the kingdom of God."
Nicodemus said to him: "How can a man be born when he is old? Can he enter his mother's womb a second time and be born?"
Jesus answered: "Amen, amen, I say to you: unless a man is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.
What is born of the flesh is flesh; what is born of the Spirit is spirit.
Do not be surprised that I told you: You must be born anew.
The wind blows where it wills: you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit."
Nicodemus responded: "How can this happen?"
Jesus answered him: "You are the teacher of Israel, and you do not know these things!
Amen, amen, I say to you: we speak of what we know, we bear witness to what we have seen, and yet you do not accept our testimony.
If you do not believe when I speak to you of earthly things, how would you believe if I spoke to you of heavenly things?
No one has gone up to heaven except the one who came down from heaven, the Son of Man.
Just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up,
so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life.
For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that whoever believes in him may not be lost, but may have eternal life.
For God did not send his Son into the world to judge the world, but so that through him the world might be saved.
Whoever believes in him is not judged; whoever does not believe is already judged, because he has not believed in the name of the only Son of God.
And this is the judgment: the light has come into the world, and men preferred the darkness to the light, because their deeds were evil.
For whoever does evil hates the light: he does not come to the light, for fear that his deeds may be exposed.
But whoever acts according to the truth comes to the light, so that it may be clearly seen that his deeds have been done in union with God."
After this, Jesus went with his disciples into the Judean countryside; he stayed there with them and baptized.
John too was baptizing, at Aenon near Salim, for there was plenty of water there; people came and were baptized.
For John had not yet been thrown into prison.
Now a dispute arose between John's disciples and a Jew about the purifications.
They came to John and said to him: "Rabbi, the one who was with you on the other side of the Jordan, the one to whom you bore witness, here he is baptizing, and everyone is going to him."
John answered: "A man can receive nothing, unless it is given to him from heaven.
You yourselves are witnesses that I said I am not the Christ, but that I am sent ahead of him.
