The one to whom the bride belongs is the bridegroom; but the friend of the bridegroom, who stands there and listens to him, is filled with joy at the bridegroom's voice. Such is my joy, and it is complete.
He must increase, and I must decrease.
The one who comes from above is above all; the one who comes from the earth is of the earth, and speaks as a man of the earth. The one who comes from heaven is above all.
What he has seen and heard, he bears witness to, and no one accepts his testimony.
Whoever accepts his testimony certifies that God is true.
For the one whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God gives the Spirit without measure.
The Father loves the Son, and has placed everything in his hand.
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life; whoever refuses to believe in the Son will not see life: the wrath of God remains upon him."

titres.titre: The Samaritan Woman and the Living Water
The Healing of the Official's Son

versets.t: The Lord learned that the Pharisees had heard that he was making more disciples than John and baptizing more
(in fact, it was not Jesus himself who baptized, but his disciples).
So he left Judea and set out again for Galilee.
Now he had to pass through Samaria.
So he comes to a town of Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of land that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
Jacob's well was there. Tired from the journey, Jesus simply sat down at the edge of the well. It was about noon.
A woman of Samaria comes to draw water. Jesus says to her: "Give me a drink."
His disciples, in fact, had gone off to the town to buy something to eat.
The Samaritan woman said to him: "How is it that you, a Jew, ask me, a Samaritan woman, for a drink?" (For the Jews avoid all contact with the Samaritans.)
Jesus answered her: "If you knew the gift of God, and who it is that says to you: Give me a drink, you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water."
She said to him: "Sir, you have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: where would you get this living water?
Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well, and drank from it himself, along with his sons and his flocks?"
Jesus answered her: "Whoever drinks of this water will be thirsty again;
but whoever drinks of the water I will give him will never be thirsty again. The water I will give him will become in him a spring welling up to eternal life."
The woman said to him: "Sir, give me this water, so that I may not be thirsty and may no longer have to come here to draw."
Jesus said to her: "Go, call your husband, and come back."
The woman answered: "I have no husband." Jesus replied: "You are right to say: I have no husband.
You have had five, and the one you have now is not your husband: there you have spoken the truth."
The woman said to him: "Sir, I see that you are a prophet.
Our fathers worshiped God on this mountain, and you say that the place where one must worship is in Jerusalem."
Jesus said to her: "Woman, believe me: the hour is coming when it is neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem that you will worship the Father.
You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, for salvation comes from the Jews.
But the hour is coming, and it is now, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; such are the worshipers the Father seeks.
God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship him in spirit and truth."
The woman said to him: "I know that the Messiah is to come, the one called Christ; when he comes, he will announce everything to us."
Jesus said to her: "I am he, the one speaking to you."
Just then his disciples arrived, and they were surprised that he was speaking with a woman; yet none said: "What are you looking for?" or: "Why are you speaking with her?"
The woman left her jar there, went off to the town, and said to the people:
"Come and see a man who told me everything I have done! Could he be the Christ?"
They came out of the town and set out toward him.
Meanwhile, the disciples were urging him: "Rabbi, do eat something."
But he said to them: "I have food to nourish me that you do not know about."
The disciples said to one another: "Could someone have brought him something to eat?"
Jesus said to them: "My food is to do the will of the one who sent me and to complete his work.
Do you not say: Four months more, and the harvest comes? Well, I say to you: Lift up your eyes and look at the fields: they are already white for the harvest.
Already the reaper receives his wages and gathers fruit for eternal life, so that the sower rejoices together with the reaper.
For in this the saying proves true: One sows, and another reaps.
I sent you to reap what has cost you no labor; others have toiled, and you benefit from their work."
Many Samaritans from that town believed in him because of the word of the woman, who testified: "He told me everything I have done."
So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them; and he stayed there two days.
Far more came to believe in him because of his own word,
and they said to the woman: "It is no longer because of what you said that we believe: we have heard him ourselves, and we know that he is truly the Savior of the world."
When those two days were over, Jesus left from there for Galilee.
He himself had declared that a prophet is not honored in his own homeland.
On his arrival in Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him warmly, for they had seen all that he had done in Jerusalem during the feast, which they too had attended.
So he came again to Cana in Galilee, where he had changed the water into wine. Now there was a royal official whose son was ill at Capernaum.
Having heard that Jesus was coming from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son, who was dying.
Jesus said to him: "Unless you see signs and wonders, you will not believe!"
The official said to him: "Sir, come down before my child dies."
Jesus says to him: "Go, your son lives." The man believed the word that Jesus had spoken to him, and he set off.
He was still on his way down when his servants came to meet him and tell him that his child was living.
He asked them at what hour he had begun to improve, and they said to him: "Yesterday, at one o'clock in the afternoon, the fever left him."
The father recognized that it was the very hour when Jesus had said to him: "Your son lives." And he believed, he and his whole household.
This was the second sign that Jesus performed on returning from Judea to Galilee.

titres.titre: The Healing at the Pool of Bethesda
The Father and the Son at Work
The Authority of the Son: to Give Life and to Judge

versets.t: After this, there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
Now in Jerusalem, near the Sheep Gate, there is a pool called in Hebrew Bethesda, which has five roofed colonnades.
Under these colonnades lay a multitude of the sick, the blind, the lame, and the paralyzed, waiting for the water to stir.
For from time to time an angel of the Lord would come down into the pool and stir the water; and the first to go down, after the water had been stirred, was healed, whatever his illness.
There was a man there who had been ill for thirty-eight years.
Jesus sees him lying there, and knowing that he had been there a long time, he says to him: "Do you want to be healed?"
The sick man answered him: "Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water stirs; and by the time I get there, someone else goes down before me."
Jesus said to him: "Get up, take your mat, and walk."
At once the man was healed: he took his mat and began to walk. Now that day was a Sabbath.
So the Jews said to the man who had just been healed: "It is the Sabbath, you are not allowed to carry your mat."
He answered them: "The one who healed me told me: Take your mat and walk."
They asked him: "Who is the man who told you: Take it up and walk?"
But the healed man did not know who it was, for Jesus had slipped away, taking advantage of the crowd that was there.
Later, Jesus finds him in the Temple and says to him: "Look, you are healed. Sin no more, so that nothing worse happens to you."
The man went off and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had healed him.
This is why the Jews were persecuting Jesus: because he acted in this way on the Sabbath.
But Jesus answered them: "My Father is at work until now, and I too am at work."
This is why the Jews sought all the more to put him to death: not only did he fail to keep the Sabbath, but he called God his own Father, making himself equal to God.
Jesus spoke up again: "Amen, amen, I say to you: the Son can do nothing by himself, he does only what he sees the Father doing; and whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.
For the Father loves the Son and shows him everything he does. He will show him even greater works, which will fill you with amazement.
Just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so the Son gives life to whomever he wills.
The Father judges no one: he has entrusted all judgment to the Son,
so that all may honor the Son as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.
Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever hears my word and believes in the one who sent me has eternal life; he does not come under judgment, he has already passed from death to life.
Amen, amen, I say to you: the hour is coming, and it is now, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who have heard it will live.
For, just as the Father possesses life in himself, so he has granted the Son to possess life in himself.
And he has given him the power to judge, because he is the Son of Man.
Do not be surprised at this: the hour is coming when all those who are in the tombs will hear his voice
and will come out: those who have done good, for a resurrection of life; those who have done evil, for a resurrection of judgment.
I can do nothing by myself. I judge according to what I hear, and my judgment is just, for I do not seek my own will, but the will of the one who sent me.
If I bear witness to myself, my testimony is not valid.
Another bears witness in my favor, and I know that the testimony he gives about me is true.
You sent a delegation to John, and he bore witness to the truth.
It is not from a man that I receive testimony; but I say this so that you may be saved.
John was the lamp that burns and shines, and you were willing, for a moment, to rejoice in his light.
But I have in my favor a testimony greater than John's: the works that the Father has given me to accomplish, these very works that I do bear witness that the Father has sent me.
And the Father who sent me has himself borne witness in my favor. But you have never heard his voice nor seen his face,
and his word does not remain in you, since you do not believe the one he has sent.
You search the Scriptures, thinking to find eternal life in them: yet it is they that bear witness to me,
and you refuse to come to me to have life.
I do not seek glory from men;
but I know you: the love of God is not in you.
I have come in my Father's name, and you do not receive me; if another comes in his own name, him you will receive.
How could you believe, you who receive your glory from one another, and do not seek the glory that comes from the one God?
Do not think that it is I who will accuse you before the Father; your accuser is Moses, in whom you have placed your hope.
For if you believed Moses, you would believe me too, since he wrote about me.
But if you do not believe what he wrote, how would you believe my words?"

titres.titre: The Discourse on the Bread of Life
The True Bread Come Down from Heaven
Eating His Flesh, Drinking His Blood

versets.t: After this, Jesus crossed to the other side of the Sea of Galilee, also called the Sea of Tiberias.
A great crowd was following him, because they saw the signs he was performing on the sick.
Jesus went up the mountain and sat down there with his disciples.
The Passover, the feast of the Jews, was near.
Lifting up his eyes, Jesus saw that a great crowd was coming to him. He said to Philip: "Where could we buy bread for all these people to eat?"
He said this to test him, for he himself knew well what he was going to do.
Philip answered him: "Even two hundred pieces of silver worth of bread would not be enough for each to have a morsel."
One of his disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, said to him:
"There is a young boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish; but what is that for so many people?"
Jesus said: "Have them sit down." There was plenty of grass in that place. So they sat down, about five thousand men in number.
Then Jesus took the loaves, gave thanks, and distributed them to those who were seated; he did the same with the fish, as much as they wanted.
When they were satisfied, he said to his disciples: "Gather up the pieces that are left, so that nothing may be lost."
They gathered them up and filled twelve baskets with the pieces of the five barley loaves, what was left over after the meal.
At the sight of the sign that Jesus had just performed, the people said: "This is truly the Prophet who is to come into the world."
But Jesus, knowing that they were going to carry him off to make him king, withdrew again, alone, to the mountain.
When evening came, his disciples went down to the edge of the sea.
They got into a boat and set out across toward Capernaum. It was already dark, and Jesus had not yet joined them.
A strong wind was blowing, and the sea was rough.
They had rowed about five or six kilometres when they saw Jesus walking on the sea and drawing near the boat. They were afraid.
But he said to them: "It is I, do not be afraid."
Then they wanted to take him on board, and at once the boat reached the shore where they were heading.

The next day, the crowd that had stayed on the other side of the sea realized that there had been only one boat there, and that Jesus had not gotten into it with his disciples: they had left by themselves.
Meanwhile, other boats, coming from Tiberias, had landed near the place where they had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
When the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they got into these boats and came to Capernaum looking for Jesus.
Having found him on the other side of the sea, they said to him: "Rabbi, when did you get here?"
Jesus answered them: "Amen, amen, I say to you: you are looking for me, not because you have seen signs, but because you have eaten bread to your fill.
Work, not for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you; for it is on him that the Father, God himself, has set his seal."
They said to him: "What must we do to work the works of God?"
Jesus answered them: "The work of God is that you believe in the one he has sent."
They responded: "What sign will you perform, so that we may see it and believe in you? What work will you do?
Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, as it is written: He gave them bread from heaven to eat."
Jesus answered them: "Amen, amen, I say to you: it was not Moses who gave you the bread from heaven; it is my Father who gives you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread of God is the one who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world."
They said to him: "Sir, give us this bread always."
Jesus answered them: "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never hunger, whoever believes in me will never thirst.
But I have told you: you have seen me, and yet you do not believe.
All those the Father gives me will come to me, and whoever comes to me I will never turn away.
For I have come down from heaven to do, not my own will, but the will of the one who sent me.
Now the will of the one who sent me is that I should lose none of those he has given me, but should raise them up on the last day.
This is the will of my Father: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him may have eternal life; and I will raise him up on the last day."
The Jews were grumbling about him, because he had said: "I am the bread come down from heaven."
They said: "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How can he now say: I have come down from heaven?"
Jesus answered them: "Stop grumbling among yourselves.
No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him; and I will raise him up on the last day.
It is written in the prophets: They will all be taught by God. Whoever listens to the Father and lets himself be taught by him comes to me.
Not that anyone has seen the Father: only the one who comes from God has seen the Father.
Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever believes has eternal life.
I am the bread of life.
Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.
This is the bread that comes down from heaven: whoever eats of it will not die.
I am the living bread, come down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will live forever. And the bread that I will give is my flesh, given for the life of the world."
At this, the Jews began to argue sharply: "How can this man give us his flesh to eat?"
Jesus said to them: "Amen, amen, I say to you: if you do not eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you.
Whoever feeds on my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
For my flesh is truly food, and my blood is truly drink.
Whoever feeds on my flesh and drinks my blood remains in me, and I in him.
Just as the living Father sent me, and I live by the Father, so whoever feeds on me will live by me.
This is the bread come down from heaven: it is not like the bread your fathers ate, who died. Whoever feeds on this bread will live forever."
This is what Jesus said, teaching in the synagogue at Capernaum.
Many of his disciples, on hearing this, said: "This word is hard! Who can listen to it?"
Knowing within himself that his disciples were grumbling about this, Jesus said to them: "Does this scandalize you?
And what if you see the Son of Man going back up to where he was before?
It is the Spirit that gives life, the flesh is of no avail. The words I have spoken to you are spirit and life.
But there are some among you who do not believe." For Jesus knew from the beginning who those were who did not believe, and who was going to betray him.
And he added: "This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless it is granted him by the Father."
From that moment, many of his disciples turned back and no longer walked with him.
Then Jesus said to the Twelve: "And you, do you also want to leave?"
Simon Peter answered him: "Lord, to whom would we go? You have the words of eternal life.
And we believe, and we know that you are the Holy One of God."
Jesus replied: "Did I not choose you, the Twelve? And one of you is a devil!"
He was speaking of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot; for it was he who was going to betray him, he, one of the Twelve.

titres.titre: The Secret Journey Up to the Feast of Booths
Where Does the Christ Come From?
The People Divided; Nicodemus Defends Jesus

versets.t: After this, Jesus went about Galilee; he did not want to travel in Judea, because the Jews were seeking to put him to death.
Now the Jewish feast of Booths was near.
His brothers said to him: "Leave here and go to Judea, so that your disciples too may see the works you do.
No one acts in secret when he wants to be known publicly. Since you are doing these things, show yourself to the world."
For even his brothers did not believe in him.
Jesus said to them: "My time has not yet come, while yours is always ready.
The world cannot hate you; but me it hates, because I bear witness against it that its works are evil.
You go up to the feast; I am not going up to this feast, for my time is not yet fulfilled."
With these words, he stayed in Galilee.
But when his brothers had gone up to the feast, he went up too, not openly, but in secret.
The Jews were looking for him during the feast and asking: "Where is he?"
In the crowd, there was much whispering about him. Some said: "He is a good man." Others: "No, he is leading the people astray."
But no one spoke of him openly, for fear of the Jews.
It was already the middle of the feast when Jesus went up to the Temple and began to teach.
The Jews, astonished, said: "How does he know the Scriptures, he who has never studied?"
Jesus answered them: "My teaching is not my own, but comes from the one who sent me.
If anyone wants to do the will of God, he will know whether my teaching comes from God or whether I speak on my own.
Whoever speaks on his own seeks his own glory; but whoever seeks the glory of the one who sent him, that man is truthful, and there is no deceit in him.
Did not Moses give you the Law? And yet none of you keeps it! Why are you seeking to put me to death?"
The crowd answered: "You have a demon! Who is seeking to put you to death?"
Jesus responded: "I did only one work, and you are all astounded.
Moses gave you circumcision (it does not, however, come from Moses, but from the patriarchs), and you circumcise a man on the Sabbath.
If a man is circumcised on the Sabbath so that the law of Moses may not be broken, why are you angry with me because, on the Sabbath, I healed a whole man?
Do not judge by appearances, but judge with right judgment."
Then some inhabitants of Jerusalem said: "Is this not the one they are seeking to put to death?
Here he is speaking openly, and they say nothing to him! Could our rulers really have recognized that he is the Christ?
Yet this man, we know where he comes from; but when the Christ comes, no one will know where he is from."
Jesus, who was teaching in the Temple, then cried out: "You know me, and you know where I come from! Yet I have not come on my own. But the one who sent me is true, and you do not know him.
I know him, because I come from him and it is he who sent me."
Then they sought to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him, for his hour had not yet come.
In the crowd, many believed in him and said: "When the Christ comes, will he perform more signs than this man has done?"
The Pharisees heard the crowd whispering this about him; the chief priests and the Pharisees then sent guards to arrest him.
Jesus said: "I am with you for only a little while longer, then I am going to the one who sent me.
You will look for me and you will not find me; where I am, you cannot come."
The Jews said to one another: "Where is he going to go, that we cannot find him? Is he going to join the Jews scattered among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
What does this word mean: You will look for me and you will not find me; where I am, you cannot come?"
On the last day of the feast, the most solemn one, Jesus, standing, cried out: "If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me, and let him drink.
Whoever believes in me, as Scripture says, from his heart will flow rivers of living water."
He was speaking of the Spirit that those who believed in him were to receive; for the Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
On hearing these words, several in the crowd said: "This is truly the Prophet."
Others said: "He is the Christ." But some objected: "Is it then from Galilee that the Christ comes?
Has not Scripture said that the Christ comes from the line of David and from Bethlehem, the village of David?"
So the crowd was divided about him.
Some wanted to arrest him, but no one laid a hand on him.
So the guards went back to the chief priests and the Pharisees, who said to them: "Why did you not bring him?"
The guards answered: "No one has ever spoken like this man!"
The Pharisees replied: "Have you too been led astray?
Is there a single ruler or a single Pharisee who has believed in him?
But this crowd, which does not know the Law, they are accursed!"
One of them, Nicodemus, the one who had come to Jesus by night, said to them:
"Does our Law condemn a man without first having heard him and knowing what he has done?"
They answered him: "Are you from Galilee too? Study the Scriptures, then, and you will see that from Galilee no prophet arises."
And each went back to his own home.

titres.titre: I Am the Light of the World
You Will Die in Your Sins
The Truth Will Set You Free

versets.t: As for Jesus, he went off to the Mount of Olives.
At daybreak, he came back to the Temple. All the people came to him; he sat down and began to teach them.
The scribes and the Pharisees then bring a woman caught in adultery. Placing her in the middle,
they said to Jesus: "Teacher, this woman was caught in the very act of adultery.
Now, in the Law, Moses commanded us to stone such women. And you, what do you say?"
They spoke this way to set a trap for him, so as to have grounds to accuse him. But Jesus, bending down, began to write on the ground with his finger.
As they kept insisting, he straightened up and said to them: "Let the one among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her."
And, bending down again, he wrote on the ground.
On hearing this, they withdrew one by one, beginning with the eldest, down to the last. Jesus was left alone with the woman, still standing there before him.
He straightened up and said to her: "Woman, where have they gone? Has no one condemned you?"
She answered: "No one, Lord." And Jesus said to her: "Neither do I condemn you. Go, and from now on sin no more."
Again, Jesus spoke to them: "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life."
The Pharisees said to him: "You bear witness to yourself: your testimony is not valid."
Jesus answered them: "Even if I bear witness to myself, my testimony is valid, for I know where I come from and where I am going; but you, you do not know where I come from or where I am going.
You judge in a merely human way; I judge no one.
And if I do happen to judge, my judgment is true, for I am not alone: there is I, and the Father who sent me.
In your own Law it is written that the testimony of two persons is valid.
Now, I bear witness to myself, and the Father who sent me also bears witness to me."
They said to him: "Where is your Father?" Jesus answered: "You know neither me nor my Father; if you knew me, you would know my Father too."
He spoke these words near the treasury, while he was teaching in the Temple; and no one arrested him, for his hour had not yet come.
He said to them again: "I am going away, and you will look for me, but you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you cannot come."
The Jews said: "Is he going to take his own life, since he says: Where I am going, you cannot come?"
He answered them: "You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world.
This is why I told you that you will die in your sins. Yes, unless you believe that I Am, you will die in your sins."
So they said to him: "You, who are you?" Jesus answered them: "Just what I have been telling you from the beginning.
I would have much to say and to judge about you; but the one who sent me is true, and what I have heard from him, I say to the world."
They did not understand that he was speaking to them of the Father.
Jesus then said to them: "When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I Am, and that I do nothing on my own: I say what the Father has taught me.
The one who sent me is with me; he has not left me alone, because I always do what pleases him."
As he was speaking in this way, many believed in him.
Jesus then said to the Jews who had believed in him: "If you remain in my word, you are truly my disciples;
you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free."
They replied: "We are the descendants of Abraham, and we have never been anyone's slaves. How can you say: You will become free?"
Jesus answered them: "Amen, amen, I say to you: everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.
Now, the slave does not remain in the house forever; the son, however, remains there forever.
So if the Son sets you free, you will be truly free.
I know that you are the descendants of Abraham; but you are seeking to put me to death, because my word finds no place in you.
I say what I have seen with my Father; and you do what you have learned from your father."
They replied: "Our father is Abraham." Jesus said to them: "If you were the children of Abraham, you would act as Abraham did.
But here you are, seeking to put me to death, me who has told you the truth that I heard from God. This, Abraham did not do.
You do the works of your father." They said to him: "We are not illegitimate children! We have only one Father: God."
Jesus said to them: "If God were your Father, you would love me, for it is from God that I came forth and that I come. I have not come on my own: it is he who sent me.
Why do you not understand my language? Because you are unable to listen to my word.

Your father is the devil, and you want to carry out the desires of your father. From the beginning he was a murderer; he did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks out of his own resources, for he is a liar and the father of lies.
And I, because I speak the truth, you do not believe me.
Which of you can convict me of a sin? If I speak the truth, why do you not believe me?
Whoever is of God listens to the words of God. If you do not listen to them, it is because you are not of God."
The Jews replied to him: "Are we not right to say that you are a Samaritan and that you have a demon?"
Jesus answered: "I do not have a demon; but I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.
I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it, and who judges.
Amen, amen, I say to you: if anyone keeps my word, he will never see death."
The Jews said to him: "Now we know that you have a demon! Abraham died, and the prophets too, and you say: If anyone keeps my word, he will never know death.
Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets too died. Who do you claim to be?"
Jesus answered: "If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, he of whom you say: He is our God.
Yet you do not know him, while I know him. If I said that I do not know him, I would be, like you, a liar. But I know him, and I keep his word.
Abraham, your father, rejoiced with joy at the thought of seeing my day: he saw it, and he was glad."
The Jews said to him: "You are not yet fifty years old, and you have seen Abraham!"
Jesus answered them: "Amen, amen, I say to you: before Abraham even existed, I Am."
Then they picked up stones to throw at him; but Jesus hid himself and left the Temple.

titres.titre: The Healing of the Man Born Blind
The Second Interrogation; the Blind Man Cast Out
The Blind Man Sees and Believes

versets.t: As he was passing by, Jesus saw a man blind from birth.
His disciples asked him: "Rabbi, who sinned for him to be born blind: he, or his parents?"
Jesus answered: "Neither he nor his parents sinned; it is so that the works of God may be revealed in him.
As long as it is day, we must do the works of the one who sent me; the night is coming, when no one can work.
As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world."
Having said this, he spat on the ground, made mud with his saliva, and applied it to the blind man's eyes.
Then he said to him: "Go wash at the pool of Siloam" (this name is translated: Sent). The man went, washed, and came back seeing clearly.
His neighbors and those who had seen him begging before said: "Is this not the one who used to sit and beg?"
Some said: "It is he." Others: "No, but he looks like him." He himself insisted: "It is indeed I."
They asked him: "How were your eyes opened?"
He answered: "The man called Jesus made mud, applied it to my eyes, and told me: Go to Siloam, and wash. I went, I washed, and I recovered my sight."
They said to him: "Where is he, this man?" He answered: "I do not know."
They bring to the Pharisees the man who had been blind.
Now, it was on a Sabbath day that Jesus had made the mud and opened his eyes.
In their turn, the Pharisees asked him how he had recovered his sight. He said to them: "He put mud on my eyes, I washed, and I see."
Some Pharisees said: "This man does not come from God, since he does not keep the Sabbath." But others objected: "How could a sinner perform such signs?" And they were divided.
They spoke to the blind man again: "And you, what do you say about him, since he opened your eyes?" He answered: "He is a prophet."
The Jews would not believe that he had been blind and now could see; so they summoned his parents
and questioned them: "Is this indeed your son, who you say was born blind? How is it that he now sees?"
His parents answered: "We know that this is indeed our son, and that he was born blind.
But how he now sees, we do not know; and who opened his eyes, we do not know. Ask him: he is old enough to speak for himself."
His parents spoke this way out of fear of the Jews, for these had already decided to expel from the synagogue anyone who acknowledged Jesus as the Christ.
This is why his parents said: "He is old enough, ask him."
The Pharisees summoned a second time the man who had been blind and said to him: "Give glory to God! We know that this man is a sinner."
He answered: "Is he a sinner? I do not know. I know one thing: I was blind, and now I see."
They said to him: "What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?"
He replied to them: "I have already told you, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Do you too want to become his disciples?"
They heaped insults on him: "You are the one who is his disciple! We are disciples of Moses.
We know that God spoke to Moses; but this man, we do not know where he is from."
The man answered them: "Here is what is astonishing: you do not know where he is from, and yet he opened my eyes!
We know that God does not hear sinners; but if anyone honors him and does his will, that man he hears.
Never has it been heard that anyone opened the eyes of a man born blind.
If this man did not come from God, he could do nothing."
They replied: "You were born entirely in sin, and you are lecturing us?" And they threw him out.
Jesus learned that they had cast him out. Having found him, he said to him: "Do you believe in the Son of Man?"
He answered: "And who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?"
Jesus said to him: "You are seeing him; the one speaking to you, it is he."
Then the man said: "I believe, Lord." And he bowed down before him.
Jesus declared: "It is for a judgment that I have come into this world: so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind."
Some Pharisees who were with him heard this and said to him: "Are we blind too?"
Jesus answered them: "If you were blind, you would have no sin. But you say: We see; so your sin remains."

titres.titre: The Feast of the Dedication: the Father and I Are One

versets.t: "Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever does not enter the sheepfold through the gate, but climbs in some other way, that man is a thief and a robber.
The one who enters through the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
The gatekeeper opens for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. His own sheep, he calls each by name, and he leads them out.
When he has brought out all his own, he walks ahead of them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
They will never follow a stranger; they will flee from him, for they do not know the voice of strangers."
Jesus used this image, but they did not understand what he meant to tell them.
So Jesus spoke again: "Amen, amen, I say to you: I am the gate of the sheep.
All those who came before me are thieves and robbers; but the sheep did not listen to them.
I am the gate. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved; he will be able to come in and go out, and he will find pasture.
The thief comes only to steal, to slaughter, and to destroy; I have come so that the sheep may have life, and have it in abundance.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep.
The hired hand, who is not the shepherd and to whom the sheep do not belong, sees the wolf coming; he abandons the sheep and flees, and the wolf seizes them and scatters them.
He flees because he is a hired hand and has no concern for the sheep.
I am the good shepherd: I know my sheep, and my sheep know me,
just as the Father knows me and I know the Father; and I lay down my life for my sheep.
I have other sheep too, which are not of this fold; those also I must lead. They will listen to my voice, and there will be one flock, one shepherd.
This is why the Father loves me: I lay down my life, to take it up again afterward.
No one takes it from me; it is I who lay it down, freely. I have the power to lay it down, and the power to take it up again: such is the command I have received from my Father."
Because of these words, a division broke out again among the Jews.
Many said: "He has a demon, he is raving. Why do you listen to him?"
Others said: "These are not the words of a man possessed. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?"
At that time the feast of the Dedication was being celebrated in Jerusalem. It was winter,
and Jesus was walking back and forth in the Temple, under Solomon's colonnade.
The Jews gathered around him and said to him: "How long will you keep us in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us openly."
Jesus answered them: "I have told you, and you do not believe. The works that I do in my Father's name bear witness in my favor;
but you do not believe, because you are not of my sheep.
My sheep listen to my voice; I know them, and they follow me.
I give them eternal life: they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand.
My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all, and no one can snatch anything out of the Father's hand.
The Father and I are one."
Again, the Jews picked up stones to stone him.
Jesus responded: "I have shown you many good works that come from the Father. For which of these works do you want to stone me?"
The Jews answered him: "It is not for a good work that we want to stone you, but for blasphemy: you, a man, make yourself God!"
Jesus replied to them: "Is it not written in your Law: I said: you are gods?
If it calls gods those to whom the word of God was addressed, and if Scripture cannot be set aside,
how can you say to the one whom the Father has consecrated and sent into the world: You blaspheme, because I said: I am the Son of God?
If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me.
But if I do them, even if you do not believe me, believe these works, so that you may finally recognize that the Father is in me and that I am in the Father."
Again, they sought to arrest him, but he escaped their hands.
He went back to the other side of the Jordan, to the place where John had first baptized, and he stayed there.
Many came to him, and people said: "John performed no sign,
but everything he said about this man was true." And there, many believed in him.

titres.titre: The Illness and Death of Lazarus
I Am the Resurrection and the Life

versets.t: There was a sick man, Lazarus, from Bethany, the village of Mary and her sister Martha.
Mary is the one who poured perfume on the Lord and wiped his feet with her hair; it was her brother Lazarus who was sick.
The two sisters sent word to Jesus: "Lord, the one you love is sick."
At this news, Jesus said: "This illness does not lead to death; it is for the glory of God, so that through it the Son of God may be glorified."
Now, Jesus loved Martha, her sister, and Lazarus.
When he heard that Lazarus was sick, he nevertheless stayed two more days in the place where he was.
Then he said to his disciples: "Let us go back to Judea."
The disciples said to him: "Rabbi, just now the Jews were seeking to stone you, and you are going back there?"
Jesus answered: "Are there not twelve hours in a day? Whoever walks during the day does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
But whoever walks during the night stumbles, because the light is not in him."
He said this, then added: "Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep; but I am going to wake him."
The disciples said to him: "Lord, if he is asleep, he will be saved."
Jesus had spoken of his death, but they thought he was speaking of ordinary sleep.
So Jesus told them plainly: "Lazarus is dead.
And I rejoice, for your sake, that I was not there, so that you may believe. But let us go to him."
Then Thomas, called Didymus, that is, the Twin, said to the other disciples: "Let us go too, to die with him."
On his arrival, Jesus found Lazarus already four days in the tomb.
Bethany was near Jerusalem, about three kilometres away.
Many Jews had come to Martha and Mary to console them over the death of their brother.
When Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went out to meet him, while Mary stayed sitting at home.
Martha said to Jesus: "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.
But I know even now: whatever you ask of God, God will grant you."
Jesus said to her: "Your brother will rise again."
Martha answered: "I know that he will rise again at the resurrection, on the last day."
Jesus said to her: "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, even if he dies, will live;
and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?"
She answered him: "Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, the one who comes into the world."
With these words, she went off to call her sister Mary discreetly: "The Teacher is here, he is calling you."
As soon as she heard this, Mary got up quickly and went to him.
Jesus had not yet entered the village: he was still at the place where Martha had met him.
The Jews who were with Mary in the house to console her, seeing her get up abruptly and go out, followed her, thinking she was going to weep at the tomb.
Arriving where Jesus was, Mary, on seeing him, fell at his feet and said to him: "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died."
When Jesus saw her weeping, she and the Jews who had come with her, he was deeply moved within, profoundly troubled,
and he asked: "Where have you laid him?" They answered him: "Lord, come and see."
Then Jesus wept.
The Jews said: "See how he loved him!"
But some objected: "He who opened the eyes of the blind man, could he not have kept Lazarus from dying?"
Again seized with emotion, Jesus came to the tomb. It was a cave, closed by a stone.
Jesus said: "Take away the stone." Martha, the sister of the dead man, said to him: "Lord, he already smells: it has been four days since he was laid there."
Jesus answered her: "Did I not tell you? If you believe, you will see the glory of God."
So they took away the stone. Then Jesus raised his eyes to heaven and said: "Father, I thank you for having heard me.
I knew well that you always hear me; but I say this because of the crowd around me, so that they may believe that it is you who sent me."
Having said this, he cried out in a loud voice: "Lazarus, come out!"
And the dead man came out, his feet and hands bound with strips of cloth, his face wrapped in a cloth. Jesus said to them: "Unbind him, and let him go."
Many Jews, who had come to Mary and witnessed what Jesus had done, believed in him.
But some went to the Pharisees and reported to them what Jesus had done.
The chief priests and the Pharisees then convened the Sanhedrin. They said: "What are we to do? This man performs many signs.
If we let him carry on, everyone will believe in him; then the Romans will come and destroy our Temple and our nation."
One of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them: "You understand nothing!
You do not see where your interest lies: it is better that one man die for the people, than that the whole nation perish."
This he did not say on his own; but, being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was going to die for the nation,
and not for the nation only, but also to gather into unity the scattered children of God.
From that day, they resolved to put him to death.
So Jesus no longer moved about openly among the Jews; he withdrew to the region near the wilderness, to a town called Ephraim, where he stayed with his disciples.
The Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up from the countryside to Jerusalem before the Passover, to purify themselves.
They were looking for Jesus and, standing in the Temple, said to one another: "What do you think? Will he not come to the feast?"
For the chief priests and the Pharisees had given the order to denounce him if anyone knew where he was, so as to arrest him.

titres.titre: The grain of wheat fallen into the earth
Unbelief and the word that judges

versets.t: Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus lived, the man he had raised from the dead.
There they gave a meal in his honor; Martha served, and Lazarus was among those at table with him.

Then Mary took about three hundred grams of pure nard, a costly perfume; she anointed the feet of Jesus with it and wiped them with her hair. And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
But one of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, the one who was going to betray him, said,
"Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred pieces of silver and the money given to the poor?"
He said this not out of concern for the poor, but because he was a thief: he kept the common purse, and he used to help himself to what was put into it.
Jesus said, "Leave her alone! She has kept this perfume for the day of my burial.
The poor you will always have with you, but me you will not always have."
A great crowd of the Jews learned that he was there, and they came, not only because of Jesus, but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.
So the chief priests decided to put Lazarus to death as well,
since it was because of him that many of the Jews were breaking away from them and believing in Jesus.
The next day, the huge crowd that had come for the feast heard that Jesus was arriving in Jerusalem.
They took palm branches and went out to meet him, shouting, "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the king of Israel!"
Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, as it is written,
"Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion: behold, your king is coming, seated on the colt of a donkey."
At the time his disciples did not understand this; but when Jesus was glorified, they remembered that Scripture had said this of him, and that this was indeed what had been done for him.
The crowd that had been with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead kept bearing witness to him.
And if the crowd came out to meet him, it was because they had heard that he had performed this sign.
So the Pharisees said to one another, "You see, you are getting nowhere: the whole world has gone off after him."
Now among those who had gone up to worship at the feast there were some Greeks.
They approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and made this request: "Sir, we would like to see Jesus."
Philip went and told Andrew; then together Andrew and Philip went and told Jesus.
Jesus answered them, "The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
Amen, amen, I say to you: unless the grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
Whoever loves his life loses it; whoever lets go of it in this world will keep it for eternal life.
If anyone would serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there also will my servant be. If anyone serves me, the Father will honor him.
Now my soul is troubled. What shall I say? Father, save me from this hour? But it is for this very hour that I have come.
Father, glorify your name!" Then a voice came from heaven, "I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again."
The crowd standing there, who had heard it, said, "It was thunder." Others said, "An angel has spoken to him."
Jesus said, "This voice came not for my sake, but for yours.
Now is the judgment of this world; now the prince of this world is about to be cast out.
And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself."
He said this to show by what kind of death he was going to die.
The crowd answered him, "We have learned from the Law that the Christ remains forever. How can you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?"
Jesus said to them, "The light is among you still, for a little while. Walk while you have the light, before the darkness overtakes you: whoever walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become children of light." After Jesus had said this, he went away and hid himself from them.
Though he had performed so many signs before their eyes, they did not believe in him,
so that the word of the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled: "Lord, who has believed what we have heard? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?"
They could not believe, because Isaiah had also said,
"He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they may not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, nor turn back, and be healed by me."
Isaiah said this because he had seen the glory of Jesus, and it was of him that he was speaking.
Yet many, even among the leaders, believed in him; but because of the Pharisees they would not admit it, for fear of being expelled from the synagogue:
they loved the glory that comes from men more than the glory that comes from God.
Jesus cried out, "Whoever believes in me believes not in me but in the one who sent me;
and whoever sees me sees the one who sent me.
I have come as light into the world, so that no one who believes in me may remain in the darkness.
If anyone hears my words and does not keep them, I am not the one who judges him, for I came not to judge the world but to save it.
Whoever rejects me and does not receive my words already has his judge: the word I have spoken, that is what will judge him on the last day.
For I have not spoken on my own; the Father who sent me has himself commanded me what to say and what to proclaim,
and I know that his commandment is eternal life. So what I say, I say just as the Father has told me."
Before the feast of the Passover, Jesus, knowing that the hour had come for him to pass from this world to his Father, having loved his own who were in the world, loved them to the end.
During the meal, when the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, to betray him,
Jesus, knowing that the Father had put everything into his hands, that he had come from God and was returning to God,
rose from the table, laid aside his garment, and took a towel, which he tied around himself.
Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet and to wipe them with the towel that was tied around him.
So he came to Simon Peter, who said to him, "You, Lord, wash my feet?"
Jesus answered him, "What I am doing you cannot understand now; later you will understand."
Peter said to him, "No, you shall never wash my feet!" Jesus answered him, "If I do not wash you, you will have no share with me."
Simon Peter said to him, "Then, Lord, not only my feet, but my hands and my head as well!"
Jesus said to him, "Whoever has bathed has no need to wash, except for the feet: he is clean all over. And you are clean, but not all of you."
For he knew who was going to betray him; that is why he said, "You are not all clean."
When he had washed their feet, he took his garment again, sat back down at the table, and said to them, "Do you understand what I have just done for you?
You call me the Master and the Lord, and you are right, for so I am.
If I then, the Lord and the Master, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
I have given you an example, so that you also may do as I have done for you.
Amen, amen, I say to you: the servant is not greater than his master, nor is the messenger greater than the one who sends him.
Knowing this, blessed are you, if you actually do it.
I am not speaking of all of you: I know those whom I have chosen. But the Scripture must be fulfilled: The one who eats my bread has raised his heel against me.
I am telling you this now, before it happens, so that when it does happen you may believe that I Am.
Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever receives the one I send receives me; and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me."
After saying this, Jesus was troubled in the depths of his being, and he declared openly, "Amen, amen, I say to you: one of you is going to betray me."
The disciples looked at one another, not knowing whom he meant.
One of them, the disciple whom Jesus loved, was reclining at table close beside him.
Simon Peter signaled to him to ask whom Jesus meant.
Leaning back against the breast of Jesus, this disciple said to him, "Lord, who is it?"
Jesus answered, "It is the one to whom I am going to give the piece of bread I dip." He dipped the piece of bread and gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot.
As soon as Judas had taken it, Satan entered into him. Jesus then said to him, "What you are doing, do quickly."
But none of those at table understood why he said this to him.
Since Judas kept the purse, some thought that Jesus was telling him to buy what was needed for the feast, or to give something to the poor.
So Judas took the piece of bread and went out at once. And it was night.
When Judas had gone out, Jesus said, "Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in him.
If God is glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and will glorify him soon.
My little children, I am with you only a little while longer. You will look for me, and what I said to the Jews I now say to you as well: where I am going, you cannot come.
I give you a new commandment: love one another. As I have loved you, so you also must love one another.
By this everyone will know that you are my disciples: by the love you have for one another."
Simon Peter said to him, "Lord, where are you going?" Jesus answered, "Where I am going, you cannot follow me now; but you will follow me later."
Peter said to him, "Lord, why can I not follow you now? I will lay down my life for you!"
Jesus answered, "You will lay down your life for me? Amen, amen, I say to you: the cock will not crow before you have denied me three times."

titres.titre: I am the way, the truth, and the life
Whoever has seen me has seen the Father
The promise of the Spirit, the Advocate

versets.t: "Do not let your heart be troubled. You believe in God; believe also in me.
In my Father's house there are many dwelling places; if there were not, would I have told you that I am going to prepare a place for you?
And when I have gone and prepared a place for you, I will come back and take you to myself, so that where I am, you also may be.
And where I am going, you know the way."
Thomas said to him, "Lord, we do not know where you are going; how could we know the way?"
Jesus answered him, "I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
If you had known me, you would have known my Father also. From now on you do know him, and you have seen him."
Philip said to him, "Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us."
Jesus answered him, "Have I been with you so long, and you still do not know me, Philip? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, Show us the Father?
Do you not believe that I am in the Father and that the Father is in me? The words I say to you I do not speak on my own: it is the Father, dwelling in me, who does his works.
Believe me: I am in the Father, and the Father is in me. Or at least believe because of the works themselves.
Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever believes in me will also do the works that I do; he will even do greater ones, because I am going to the Father.
And whatever you ask in my name, I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
If you ask me anything in my name, I will do it.
If you love me, you will keep my commandments.
And I will pray to the Father, and he will give you another Advocate, to be with you forever,
the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees him nor knows him. But you know him, because he dwells with you; and he will be in you.
I will not leave you orphans: I am coming back to you.
In a little while the world will see me no more; but you will see me, because I live, and you also will live.
On that day you will know that I am in my Father, that you are in me, and I in you.
Whoever holds to my commandments and keeps them is the one who loves me. And whoever loves me will be loved by my Father; I too will love him and will reveal myself to him."
Judas, not the Iscariot, said to him, "Lord, how is it that you mean to reveal yourself to us and not to the world?"
Jesus answered him, "If anyone loves me, he will keep my word; my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him.
Whoever does not love me does not keep my words. And the word you hear is not my own: it comes from the Father who sent me.
I have told you all this while I am still dwelling with you.
But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you everything and remind you of all that I have told you.
Peace I leave with you, my peace I give you; I do not give it to you as the world gives. Do not let your heart be troubled, and do not let it be afraid.
You heard me say to you, I am going away, and I am coming back to you. If you loved me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, for the Father is greater than I.
I have told you these things now, before they happen, so that when they do happen you may believe.
I will not speak with you much longer, for the prince of this world is coming. Over me he has no power;
but the world must know that I love the Father and that I act just as the Father has commanded me. Rise up! Let us go from here."
"I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser.
Every branch in me that does not bear fruit he takes away; and every branch that does bear fruit he prunes, so that it may bear more.
You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.
Remain in me, as I remain in you. Just as the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it remains on the vine, so neither can you unless you remain in me.
I am the vine, you are the branches. Whoever remains in me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for without me you can do nothing.
Whoever does not remain in me is thrown out like a branch and withers; such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned.
If you remain in me and my words remain in you, ask whatever you want, and it will be done for you.
This is the glory of my Father: that you bear much fruit and be my disciples.
As the Father has loved me, so I too have loved you: remain in my love.
If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and remain in his love.
I have told you this so that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be complete.
This is my commandment: love one another, as I have loved you.
There is no greater love than to lay down one's life for those one loves.
You are my friends, if you do what I command you.
I no longer call you servants, for the servant does not know what his master is doing; I call you my friends, for everything I have heard from my Father I have made known to you.

It was not you who chose me; it was I who chose you and appointed you, so that you may go and bear fruit, and that your fruit may remain. Then whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you.
This is what I command you: love one another.
If the world hates you, know that it hated me before you.
If you belonged to the world, the world would love what is its own. But you are not of the world, since I chose you out of the world; that is why the world hates you.
Remember the word I spoke to you: the servant is not greater than his master. If they persecuted me, they will persecute you too; if they kept my word, they will keep yours as well.
But all this they will do to you because of my name, for they do not know the one who sent me.
If I had not come, if I had not spoken to them, they would be without sin; but now their sin is without excuse.
Whoever hates me hates my Father as well.
If I had not done among them works that no one else has ever done, they would be without sin; but now they have seen, and they hate both me and my Father.
So is fulfilled the word written in their Law: They hated me without cause.
When the Advocate comes, whom I will send you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness to me.
And you also will bear witness, because you have been with me from the beginning."

titres.titre: The coming of the Spirit of truth

versets.t: "I have told you all this so that you may not be shaken.
They will expel you from the synagogues; indeed, the hour is coming when whoever kills you will think he is offering worship to God.
And they will do this because they have known neither the Father nor me.
I have told you this so that when the hour comes you may remember that I told you of it. I did not tell you this from the beginning, because I was with you.
But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, Where are you going?
Instead, because I have told you this, sorrow has filled your heart.
Yet I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go away; for if I do not go, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment.
Concerning sin: they have not believed in me.
Concerning righteousness: I am going to the Father, and you will see me no more.
Concerning judgment: the prince of this world is already judged.
I still have much to tell you, but you cannot bear it now.
When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth. For he will not speak on his own: he will say all that he hears, and he will announce to you what is to come.
He will glorify me, for he will receive from what is mine and announce it to you.
Everything the Father has is mine; that is why I told you: he will receive from what is mine and announce it to you.
A little while, and you will see me no more; then again a little while, and you will see me again."

Then some of his disciples said to one another, "What does he mean by this: A little while, and you will see me no more; then again a little while, and you will see me again? And: I am going to the Father?
What does this 'a little while' mean? We do not understand what he is saying."

Knowing that they wanted to question him, Jesus said to them, "You are asking one another what I meant by this: A little while, and you will see me no more; then again a little while, and you will see me again.
Amen, amen, I say to you: you will weep and lament, while the world rejoices; you will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will turn into joy.
The woman in labor is in pain, because her hour has come; but once the child is born, she forgets her suffering, in her joy that a man has come into the world.
So you too are now sorrowful; but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take that joy from you.
On that day you will question me about nothing. Amen, amen, I say to you: whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you.
Until now you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.
I have spoken to you of all this in figures. The hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures, but will tell you about the Father openly.
On that day you will ask in my name, and I do not even say that I will pray to the Father for you,
for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God.
I came from the Father and came into the world; now I am leaving the world and going to the Father."
His disciples said to him, "Now you are speaking openly, no longer in any figure.
Now we know that you know everything, and that you have no need for anyone to question you. This is why we believe that you came from God."
Jesus answered them, "Do you believe now?
Behold, the hour is coming, and has already come, when you will be scattered, each to his own, and will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, for the Father is with me.
I have told you this so that in me you may have peace. In the world you will have suffering; but take courage: I have overcome the world."

titres.titre: The prayer for the glory of the Son
The prayer for the unity of all believers

versets.t: So Jesus spoke; then, lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said, "Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, so that the Son may glorify you.
For as you have given him power over every human being, he will give eternal life to all those you have given him.
And eternal life is this: that they know you, the only true God, and the one you have sent, Jesus Christ.
I have glorified you on earth by finishing the work you gave me to do.
And now, Father, glorify me in your presence with the glory I had with you before the world existed.
I have made your name known to those you took out of the world to give to me. They were yours, you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.
Now they know that everything you have given me comes from you;
for the words you gave me I have given to them, and they have received them. They have truly recognized that I came from you, and they have believed that it was you who sent me.
I pray for them. I do not pray for the world, but for those you have given me, for they are yours.
All that is mine is yours, and all that is yours is mine; and in them I am glorified.
From now on I am no longer in the world; they are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, the name you have given me, so that they may be one, as we are.
While I was with them, I kept them in your name, the name you have given me. I watched over them, and not one was lost, except the one destined to be lost, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled.
But now I am coming to you, and I say these things while in the world, so that they may have my joy within them, in full.
I have given them your word, and the world has hated them, because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
I do not ask you to take them out of the world, but to keep them from the Evil One.
They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
Consecrate them in the truth: your word is truth.
As you sent me into the world, so I too have sent them into the world.
And for them I consecrate myself, so that they too may be consecrated in the truth.
I pray not only for them, but also for those who, through their word, will believe in me:
that they may all be one, as you, Father, are in me and I in you; that they also may be one in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me.
And the glory you gave me I have given them, so that they may be one as we are one,
I in them and you in me, so that they may reach perfect unity, and that the world may know that you sent me and that you have loved them as you have loved me.
Father, those you have given me, I want them to be with me where I am, so that they may contemplate my glory, the glory you gave me because you loved me before the creation of the world.
Righteous Father, the world has not known you, but I have known you, and these have recognized that it was you who sent me.
I have made your name known to them, and I will make it known still, so that the love with which you have loved me may be in them, and I too in them."

titres.titre: My kingdom is not of this world

versets.t: After saying this, Jesus went out with his disciples and crossed the Wadi Kidron. There was a garden there, which he entered with his disciples.
Judas, the one who was betraying him, also knew the place, for Jesus had often met there with his disciples.
So he took with him a detachment of soldiers, along with guards supplied by the chief priests and the Pharisees, and came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.
Then Jesus, knowing all that was going to happen to him, came forward and said to them, "Whom are you looking for?"
They answered him, "Jesus of Nazareth." He said to them, "I Am." Judas, the one who was betraying him, was standing there with them.
When Jesus said to them, "I Am," they drew back and fell to the ground.
Again he asked them, "Whom are you looking for?" They said, "Jesus of Nazareth."
Jesus answered, "I told you: I Am. So if it is me you are looking for, let these men go."
Thus was to be fulfilled the word he had spoken: "I have not lost one of those you gave me."
Then Simon Peter, who was carrying a sword, drew it, struck the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.
But Jesus said to Peter, "Put your sword back into its sheath. Shall I not drink the cup the Father has given me?"
The detachment of soldiers, with its commander and the guards of the Jews, then seized Jesus and bound him.
They led him first to Annas: he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, the high priest that year.
Now it was Caiaphas who had given the Jews this advice: "It is better that one man die for the people."
Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple. Since this disciple was known to the high priest, he entered with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest;
but Peter stayed outside, near the gate. The other disciple, the one known to the high priest, went back out, spoke to the woman at the gate, and brought Peter in.
The servant girl who kept the gate then said to Peter, "Are you not also one of this man's disciples?" He answered, "I am not."
The servants and the guards were standing around a charcoal fire they had lit, because it was cold, and they were warming themselves. Peter was standing there too, warming himself with them.
The high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and his teaching.
Jesus answered him, "I have spoken openly to the world. I have always taught in the synagogue and in the Temple, where all the Jews gather, and I have said nothing in secret.
Why do you question me? Question those who heard me about what I told them: they know well what I taught."
At these words, one of the guards standing there struck Jesus in the face, saying, "Is that how you answer the high priest?"
Jesus answered him, "If I have spoken wrongly, show what was wrong; but if I have spoken rightly, why do you strike me?"
Annas then sent him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.
Simon Peter was still there, warming himself. They said to him, "Are you not also one of his disciples?" He denied it: "I am not."
One of the servants of the high priest, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, insisted, "Did I not see you in the garden with him?"
Again Peter denied it. And at once a cock crowed.
From the house of Caiaphas they led Jesus to the praetorium. It was morning. They themselves did not enter the praetorium, so as not to become unclean and to be able to eat the Passover.
So Pilate came out to them and asked, "What accusation do you bring against this man?"
They answered him, "If he were not a criminal, we would not have handed him over to you."
Pilate said to them, "Take him yourselves, and judge him according to your Law." The Jews said to him, "We are not allowed to put anyone to death."
Thus was to be fulfilled the word by which Jesus had shown by what kind of death he was going to die.
Pilate went back into the praetorium, summoned Jesus, and said to him, "Are you the king of the Jews?"
Jesus answered, "Do you say this on your own, or have others told you about me?"
Pilate replied, "Am I a Jew? Your nation and the chief priests have handed you over to me. What have you done?"
Jesus answered, "My kingdom is not of this world. If it were of this world, my guards would have fought to keep me from being handed over to the Jews. But no, my kingdom is not from here."

Pilate said to him, "So you are a king?" Jesus answered, "You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world: to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to my voice."
Pilate said to him, "What is truth?" With these words he went back out to the Jews and told them, "I find no case against him.
But according to your custom, I am to release one prisoner for you at the Passover. Do you want me to release for you the king of the Jews?"
Then they began to shout again, "Not this man! Barabbas!" Now Barabbas was a bandit.

titres.titre: Mary and the disciple at the foot of the cross
The thrust of the lance; the burial

versets.t: Then Pilate had Jesus taken and scourged.
The soldiers wove a crown of thorns and placed it on his head; they clothed him in a purple cloak,
and they kept coming up to him and saying, "Hail, king of the Jews!", and they struck him in the face.
Pilate came out again and said to the Jews, "Look, I am bringing him out to you, so that you may know that I find no case against him."
So Jesus came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple cloak. And Pilate said to them, "Behold the man."
But when the chief priests and the guards saw him, they began to shout, "Crucify him! Crucify him!" Pilate said to them, "Take him yourselves and crucify him: I find no case against him."
The Jews answered him, "We have a Law, and according to that Law he must die, because he has made himself the Son of God."
When Pilate heard this, he was even more afraid.
He went back into the praetorium and said to Jesus, "Where are you from?" But Jesus gave him no answer.
Pilate said to him, "You refuse to speak to me? Do you not know that I have the power to release you and the power to crucify you?"
Jesus answered, "You would have no power over me if it had not been given to you from above. That is why the one who handed me over to you bears the greater sin."
From then on, Pilate tried to release him. But the Jews shouted, "If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Anyone who makes himself a king sets himself against Caesar."
When Pilate heard these words, he had Jesus brought outside and sat down at the tribunal, at the place called the Stone Pavement, in Hebrew Gabbatha.
It was the day of Preparation for the Passover, about midday. Pilate said to the Jews, "Behold your king."
But they began to shout, "Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!" Pilate said to them, "Shall I crucify your king?" The chief priests answered, "We have no king but Caesar."
Then he handed him over to them to be crucified. They seized Jesus and led him away.
Carrying his own cross, he went out to the place called the Skull, called in Hebrew Golgotha.
There they crucified him, and with him two others, one on each side, and Jesus in the middle.
Pilate had written a notice, which he had placed on the cross; it read, "Jesus of Nazareth, the king of the Jews."
Many of the Jews read this notice, for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and the text was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.
The chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, "Do not write, The king of the Jews, but, This man said, I am the king of the Jews."
Pilate answered, "What I have written, I have written."
When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they took his garments and divided them into four parts, one for each soldier. There remained the tunic: it was seamless, woven in one piece from top to bottom.

They said to one another, "Let us not tear it, but cast lots to see who will get it." Thus was to be fulfilled the word of Scripture: They divided my garments among them, and for my tunic they cast lots. This is what the soldiers did.
Near the cross of Jesus stood his mother, his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
Seeing his mother, and near her the disciple whom he loved, Jesus said to his mother, "Woman, behold your son."
Then he said to the disciple, "Behold your mother." And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home.
After this, knowing that everything was now finished, and so that the Scripture might be fulfilled to the end, Jesus said, "I thirst."
There was a jar there full of sour wine. The soldiers fixed a sponge soaked in this wine on a branch of hyssop and lifted it to his mouth.
When he had taken the sour wine, Jesus said, "It is finished." Then, bowing his head, he handed over the spirit.

Since it was the day of Preparation, the Jews asked Pilate to have the legs of the crucified men broken and the bodies taken away, so that they would not remain on the cross during the sabbath; for that sabbath was a great day.
So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first, then of the other man crucified with him.
But when they came to Jesus and saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs.
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a lance, and at once there came out blood and water.
The one who saw this bears witness, and his witness is true; he knows that he tells the truth, so that you also may believe.
For this happened so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: Not one of his bones will be broken.
And another passage says as well: They will look on the one they have pierced.

After this, Joseph of Arimathea, a disciple of Jesus, but a secret one for fear of the Jews, asked Pilate to let him take away the body of Jesus. Pilate gave him permission. So he came and took the body away.
Nicodemus, the one who at first had come to Jesus by night, also came, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about thirty kilos.
They took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths, with the spices, according to the Jewish custom of burial.
At the place where Jesus had been crucified there was a garden, and in this garden a new tomb, in which no one had yet been laid.
There, because of the Jewish day of Preparation and because the tomb was near, they laid Jesus.

titres.titre: Jesus appears to the disciples; the gift of the Spirit
Thomas: My Lord and my God

versets.t: On the first day of the week, early in the morning, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene went to the tomb, and she saw that the stone had been taken away from it.
So she ran to Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved, and said to them, "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have put him."
So Peter set out with the other disciple, and they went to the tomb.
They were both running together, but the other disciple ran faster than Peter and reached the tomb first.
Bending down, he saw the linen cloths lying on the ground; yet he did not go in.
Simon Peter, who was following him, arrived in turn. He went into the tomb and observed the linen cloths lying on the ground,
as well as the cloth that had covered the head of Jesus, not lying with the others but rolled up in a place by itself.
Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, also went in. He saw, and he believed.
Until then, in fact, they had not understood the Scripture, according to which Jesus was to rise from the dead.
Then the disciples went back home.
But Mary stood outside, near the tomb, weeping. Still weeping, she bent down toward the tomb
and saw two angels dressed in white, seated where the body of Jesus had lain, one at the head and the other at the feet.
They said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping?" She answered them, "They have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have put him."
As she said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there; but she did not know that it was he.
