So I ask: have they not heard? Of course they have: Their voice has gone out through all the earth, and their words to the ends of the world.
I ask again: has Israel not understood? Already Moses said: I will make you jealous of a people that is not one; I will provoke you against a nation without understanding.
And Isaiah dares to say: I was found by those who were not seeking me; I made myself known to those who were not asking for me.
But concerning Israel he says: All day long I have held out my hands to a disobedient and rebellious people.

titres.titre: The salvation of the nations and of Israel
The mystery of the salvation of all
Hymn to the wisdom of God

versets.t: So I ask: has God rejected his people? Certainly not! For I too am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
God has not rejected his people, whom he knew beforehand. Do you not know what Scripture says about Elijah, when he pleads before God against Israel:
Lord, they have killed your prophets, they have torn down your altars; I alone am left, and they seek my life.
But what does the word of God reply to him? I have kept for myself seven thousand men who have not bent the knee to Baal.
In the same way, at the present time, there is a remnant, chosen by grace.
Now if it is by grace, it is no longer on the basis of works; otherwise grace would no longer be grace.
What then are we to conclude? What Israel seeks, it has not obtained; those whom God has chosen have obtained it, but the others were hardened,
as it is written: God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that do not see, ears that do not hear, to this very day.
And David says: May their table become for them a snare, a net, an occasion of downfall, and a just retribution!
May their eyes be darkened so that they see no more, and make them bend their backs forever!
So I ask: have they stumbled so as to fall for good? Certainly not! But through their false step salvation has come to the nations, to stir them to jealousy.
Now if their false step has meant the riches of the world, and their diminishment the riches of the nations, how much more will their fullness mean!
I am speaking to you, the nations: precisely insofar as I am the apostle of the nations, I honor my ministry,
hoping to stir to jealousy those of my own blood, and to save some of them.
For if their being set aside reconciled the world, what will their return be, if not a passage from death to life?
If the firstfruits are holy, so is the whole batch of dough; and if the root is holy, so are the branches.
Some branches were cut off, and you, a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among the others to share in the root and the sap of the olive tree:
do not boast at the expense of the branches. If you do boast, remember that it is not you who support the root, but the root that supports you.
You will say: Branches were cut off so that I might be grafted in.
That is true. They were cut off because of their unbelief, and you stand by faith. Do not be proud; rather, be in awe.
For if God did not spare the natural branches, he will not spare you either.
See then the kindness and the severity of God: severity toward those who fell, kindness toward you, provided you remain in that kindness; otherwise you too will be cut off.
As for them, if they do not remain in unbelief, they will be grafted in; for God has the power to graft them in again.

For if you were cut off from the wild olive tree that was yours and grafted against nature onto the cultivated olive tree, how much more will they, the natural branches, be grafted onto their own olive tree!
For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of this mystery, so that you may not think yourselves wise: the hardening of part of Israel will last until the fullness of the nations has come in.
And so all Israel will be saved, as it is written: From Zion will come the deliverer; he will remove ungodliness from Jacob;
and this will be my covenant with them, when I take away their sins.
According to the Good News, they are enemies of God, and this for your sake; but according to God's choice, they are loved, for the sake of their fathers.
For the gifts of God and his call are irrevocable.
Just as you once disobeyed God and have now received mercy because of their disobedience,
so they too have now disobeyed, because of the mercy shown to you, so that they in turn may receive mercy.
For God has shut up all people in disobedience so as to show mercy to all.
O the depth of the riches, the wisdom, and the knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and how untraceable his ways!
Who has known the mind of the Lord? Who has been his counselor?
Who has given to him first, so as to be repaid?
For all things are from him, and through him, and for him. To him be the glory for ever! Amen.
I urge you therefore, brothers, by the mercy of God, to offer yourselves as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God: this is the spiritual worship suited to you.
Do not be conformed to the present world, but be transformed by the renewal of your minds, so that you may discern what is the will of God: what is good, what pleases him, what is perfect.

In the name of the grace given to me, I say to each one of you: do not think of yourselves more highly than you ought; instead, have measured thoughts, each according to the measure of faith God has given him.
Just as our body, which is one, has many members, and these members do not all have the same function,
so we, though many, form but one body in Christ, and each for his part we are members of one another.
We have different gifts according to the grace given to us. Is it the gift of prophecy? Let it be exercised in agreement with the faith.
Is it service? Let the person serve. The one who teaches, let him teach;
the one who exhorts, let him exhort; the one who gives, let him give without calculation; the one who leads, let him do so with zeal; the one who shows mercy, let him do so with joy.
Let your love be without hypocrisy. Abhor evil, hold fast to good.
Love one another with brotherly affection; outdo one another in showing esteem.
With zeal that never flags, with a fervent spirit, serve the Lord.
Have the joy of hope, patience in distress, perseverance in prayer.
Share in the needs of the saints, practice hospitality eagerly.
Bless those who persecute you; bless, and do not curse.
Rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep.
Have the same regard for one another; do not aim at what is too high, but let yourselves be drawn to what is humble. Do not think yourselves wise.
Repay no one evil for evil; seek what is good in the eyes of all.
If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
Do not take revenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for the wrath of God, for it is written: Vengeance is mine, I will repay each one, says the Lord.
On the contrary, if your enemy is hungry, give him something to eat; if he is thirsty, give him something to drink: by doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head.
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

titres.titre: Love, the fulfillment of the Law

versets.t: Let everyone submit to the established authorities. For there is no authority that does not come from God, and those that exist have been ordered by God.
So whoever opposes authority sets himself against the order willed by God, and those who set themselves against it will bring condemnation on themselves.
For magistrates are not to be feared when one does good, but when one does evil. Do you want to have no reason to fear authority? Do good, and you will receive its praise;

for it is in the service of God to encourage you toward good. But if you do evil, be afraid: it is not for nothing that it bears the sword. For it is in the service of God to do justice and punish the one who does evil.
It is therefore necessary to submit, not only for fear of punishment, but also for reasons of conscience.
This is also why you pay taxes: those who collect them are in the service of God, devoted to this very task.
Give to each what is owed: tax to whom you owe tax, duty to whom you owe duty, fear to whom you owe fear, honor to whom you owe honor.
Owe no one anything, except to love one another; for whoever loves his neighbor has fully fulfilled the Law.

Indeed, the commandments: You shall not commit adultery, you shall not commit murder, you shall not steal, you shall not covet, and all the others, are summed up in this word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
Love does no wrong to the neighbor: love is therefore the full fulfillment of the Law.
Understand, moreover, what time we are in: now is the hour to wake at last from your sleep. For salvation is now nearer to us than when we first believed.
The night is far gone, the day is near. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness and put on the weapons of light.
Let us conduct ourselves honorably, as in broad daylight, without excess of the table or drunkenness, without debauchery or dissoluteness, without quarreling or jealousy.
Instead, put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not give in to the cravings of the flesh.

titres.titre: Do not lead the weak into sin

versets.t: Welcome the one who is weak in faith, without arguing over his scruples.
One person believes he may eat anything; another, weaker, eats only vegetables.
Let the one who eats not despise the one who abstains, and let the one who abstains not judge the one who eats: God has welcomed him.
Who are you to judge someone else's servant? Whether he stands or falls is his own master's concern. And he will stand, for the Lord has the power to hold him up.
For one person, one day counts more than another; for another, all days are alike. Let each be fully convinced in his own mind.
The one who observes the days does so for the Lord; the one who eats does so for the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and the one who abstains does so for the Lord, and gives thanks to God.
For none of us lives for himself, and none of us dies for himself:
if we live, we live for the Lord; if we die, we die for the Lord. In life as in death, we belong to the Lord.
For Christ died and came back to life so as to be the Lord of the dead and the living.
But you, why do you judge your brother? And you, why do you despise your brother? For all of us will appear before the judgment seat of God;
for it is written: As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow before me, and every tongue will give glory to God.
So each of us will render an account of himself to God.
Let us therefore stop judging one another. Judge rather that you must put nothing before your brother that would make him stumble or fall.
I know, and I am convinced in the Lord Jesus, that nothing is unclean in itself; a thing is unclean only for the one who considers it unclean.
Now if because of a food you grieve your brother, you are no longer conducting yourself according to love. Do not, over a food, cause the ruin of the one for whom Christ died.
Do not let the good that is yours become an object of blasphemy!
For the kingdom of God is not a matter of food or drink; it is righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.
Whoever serves Christ in this way pleases God and gains the esteem of others.
Let us therefore pursue what makes for peace and mutual edification.
Do not destroy the work of God over a food. Everything is pure, to be sure; but one does wrong by becoming, through what one eats, an occasion of downfall.
What is good is to eat no meat, to drink no wine, to do nothing that makes your brother stumble.
The conviction that you have, keep it to yourself, before God. Blessed is the one who does not condemn himself by what he approves!
But whoever has doubts and yet eats is condemned, because he does not act out of conviction; and whatever does not come from conviction is sin.

titres.titre: Welcoming the weak, after the example of Christ
Christ, for the Jews and for the nations

versets.t: We who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of those who are not, and not to please ourselves.
Let each of us seek to please his neighbor, for his good, so as to build him up.
For Christ did not seek to please himself; on the contrary, it is written: The insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
Now everything that was written in the past was written for our instruction, so that through the perseverance and the encouragement of the Scriptures we might keep hope.
May the God of perseverance and encouragement grant you to be in agreement with one another, according to Christ Jesus,
so that with one heart and one voice you may give glory to the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Welcome one another, then, as Christ has welcomed you, for the glory of God.
I declare it: Christ made himself a servant of the circumcised, to show the faithfulness of God by fulfilling the promises made to the fathers;
as for the nations, it is out of mercy that they give glory to God, as it is written: So I will praise you among the nations, and I will sing to your name.
It is said again: Nations, rejoice with his people.
And elsewhere: Praise the Lord, all you nations; let all the peoples praise him.
Isaiah says in turn: He will appear, the root of Jesse, the one who rises to rule the nations; in him the nations will place their hope.
May the God of hope fill you with all joy and all peace in faith, so that you may abound in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
Brothers, I for my part am convinced about you that you are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, and able to warn one another.
Nevertheless, I have written to you with a certain boldness, in places, to stir up your memory, by virtue of the grace God has given me
to be a minister of Christ Jesus for the nations, carrying out the sacred service of the Good News of God, so that the nations may become a pleasing offering, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
So I have reason to be proud in Christ Jesus, in what concerns the service of God.
For I would not dare to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me to bring the nations to obedience, in word and in deed,
by the power of signs and wonders, by the power of the Spirit. So, from Jerusalem all the way around to Illyricum, I have brought the Good News of Christ to its full completion.
I have made it a point of honor to proclaim the Good News where the name of Christ had not yet been spoken, so as not to build on foundations laid by another,
but as it is written: Those to whom it had not been announced will see, and those who had not heard of it will understand.
That is why I have often been prevented from coming to you.
But now, having no more field of work in these regions, and having desired for many years to come to you
when I set out for Spain, I hope to see you as I pass through and to be sent on my way there by you, after first enjoying your company for a while.
For now, I am setting out for Jerusalem in the service of the saints.
For Macedonia and Achaia have been pleased to show solidarity with the poor among the saints of Jerusalem.
They were pleased to do so, and indeed they owed it to them: since the nations have shared in their spiritual goods, they in turn owe it to serve them with their material goods.
When I have settled this matter and officially handed over the fruit of this collection, I will set out for Spain, passing through your city.
And I know that in coming to you, I will come with the full blessing of Christ.
I urge you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to strive together with me in the prayers you offer to God for me,
that I may escape the unbelievers of Judea and that my service for Jerusalem may be well received by the saints;
so that, by the will of God, I may come to you with joy and find rest among you.
May the God of peace be with you all! Amen.
I commend to you Phoebe, our sister, who is in the service of the Church at Cenchreae:
welcome her in the Lord in a way worthy of the saints, and assist her in any matter in which she may need you; for she has been a support to many, and to me as well.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus:
to save my life, they risked their own necks; not only I but all the Churches of the nations give thanks to them.
Greet also the Church that meets in their house. Greet my dear Epaenetus, the firstfruits of Asia for Christ.
Greet Mary, who has worked hard for you.
Greet Andronicus and Junia, my kinsmen and fellow prisoners, apostles of note, who were even in Christ before me.
Greet Ampliatus, who is dear to me in the Lord.
Greet Urbanus, our fellow worker in Christ, and my dear Stachys.
Greet Apelles, who has proved himself in Christ. Greet those of the household of Aristobulus.
Greet Herodion, my kinsman. Greet those of the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who work hard in the Lord. Greet my dear Persis, who has worked very hard in the Lord.
Greet Rufus, that chosen one of the Lord, and his mother, who is a mother to me as well.
Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are with them.
Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, as well as Olympas and all the saints who are with them.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the Churches of Christ greet you.
I urge you, brothers, to be on guard against those who cause divisions and scandals, contrary to the teaching you have received: keep away from them.
For such people do not serve Christ our Lord, but their own belly; with fine words and flattering speeches, they deceive simple hearts.
Your obedience is known to all, and I rejoice over you. But I want you to be wise about good, and uncompromised by evil.
The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet. May the grace of our Lord Jesus be with you!
Timothy, my fellow worker, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen.
I greet you in the Lord, I Tertius, who wrote this letter.
Gaius, who offers hospitality to me and to the whole Church, greets you. Erastus, the city treasurer, greets you, as does Quartus, our brother.
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all! Amen.
To the One who has the power to strengthen you, according to the Good News that I proclaim in preaching Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery kept hidden through the eternal ages,
but now made manifest and, through the writings of the prophets, by the command of the eternal God, brought to the knowledge of all the nations to bring them to the obedience of faith;
to God, who alone is wise, through Jesus Christ, to him be the glory for ever and ever! Amen.
Paul, called by the will of God to be an apostle of Christ Jesus, and Sosthenes our brother,

to the Church of God that is at Corinth, to those who have been sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be holy, together with all who everywhere call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours:
to you, grace and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I give thanks to my God constantly on your account, for the grace of God given to you in Christ Jesus;
for in him you have been enriched with every gift, in all speech and all knowledge.
So the testimony of Christ has been confirmed among you,
so that you lack no gift of grace as you wait for the revealing of our Lord Jesus Christ.
It is he who will keep you firm to the end, so that you may be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful, the God who has called you into fellowship with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
I urge you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to be all in agreement: let there be no divisions among you, but be united in the same mind and the same conviction.
For it has been reported to me, my brothers, by Chloe's people, that there are rivalries among you.
Let me explain. Each of you says: I belong to Paul. And I to Apollos. And I to Cephas. And I to Christ.
Is Christ then divided? Was it Paul who was crucified for you? Was it in the name of Paul that you were baptized?
I give thanks that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
so that no one can say he was baptized in my name.
(Yes, I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that, I do not think I baptized anyone else.)
For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to proclaim the Good News, and not with eloquent wisdom, so that the cross of Christ might not be emptied of its power.
Yes, the message of the cross is folly to those who are on the way to ruin, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
For it is written: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the understanding of the learned I will reject.
Where is the wise one? Where is the scholar? Where is the debater of this age? Has not God made the wisdom of the world foolish?
For since the world, with all its wisdom, did not come to know God in the wisdom of God, it pleased God to save believers through the folly of what we preach.
The Jews demand signs and the Greeks seek wisdom;
but we proclaim a crucified Christ, a scandal to the Jews and folly to the Gentiles,
but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, a Christ who is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
For the folly of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men.
Consider, brothers, how you were called: not many of you were wise by human standards, not many powerful, not many of noble birth.
But God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame what is strong;
God chose what is lowly and despised in the world, things that are nothing, to reduce to nothing the things that are,
so that no creature might boast before God.
It is because of him that you are in Christ Jesus, who has become for us wisdom from God, and righteousness, sanctification, and redemption,
so that, as it is written, whoever boasts should boast in the Lord.
And I, brothers, when I came to you, did not come proclaiming the mystery of God to you with any prestige of speech or of wisdom.
For I had resolved to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and Jesus Christ crucified.
It was in weakness, in fear, and with much trembling that I came before you;
my speech and my preaching had nothing of the persuasive arguments of wisdom, but were shown in the power of the Spirit,
so that your faith might rest not on human wisdom but on the power of God.
Yet we do speak a wisdom among the mature, but a wisdom that is not of this age nor of the rulers of this age, who are doomed to pass away.
What we speak is the wisdom of God, mysterious and hidden, which God destined beforehand, before the ages, for our glory.
None of the rulers of this age knew it; for if they had known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
But, as it is written: What no eye has seen, what no ear has heard, what has not entered the human heart, this is what God has prepared for those who love him.
And it is to us that God has revealed it through the Spirit; for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.
For who among men knows what is in a man except the man's own spirit within him? In the same way, no one knows what is in God except the Spirit of God.
Now we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who comes from God, so that we may know the gifts freely given to us by God.
And we speak of these things not in words taught by human wisdom, but in words taught by the Spirit, expressing spiritual realities in spiritual terms.
The natural man does not accept what comes from the Spirit of God: it is folly to him, and he cannot understand it, because it is judged spiritually.
The spiritual man, however, judges all things, and he himself is judged by no one.
For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to instruct him? But we have the mind of Christ.
And I, brothers, could not speak to you as to spiritual men, but as to people of flesh, as to little children in Christ.
I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, for you were not yet able to take it. And even now you still are not able,
for you are still worldly. Since there is jealousy and rivalry among you, are you not worldly, behaving in a merely human way?
When one says, I belong to Paul, and another, I to Apollos, are you not acting in a merely human way?
What then is Apollos? What is Paul? Servants through whom you came to faith, each according to what the Lord gave him.
I planted, Apollos watered; but it was God who gave the growth.
So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything; only God who gives the growth counts for anything.
The one who plants and the one who waters stand on equal footing, and each will receive his wages according to his own labor.
For we are God's coworkers, and you are God's field, God's building.
According to the grace God gave me, like a skilled architect, I laid the foundation, and another builds upon it. But let each one take care how he builds.
For no one can lay any foundation other than the one already laid: Jesus Christ.
On this foundation one may build with gold, silver, precious stones, or with wood, hay, straw:
the work of each will become visible. For the day of judgment will make it known, since it will be revealed in fire, and the fire will test the worth of each one's work.
If the work built on the foundation endures, one will receive wages;
if it is burned up, one will suffer the loss; yet one will be saved, but only as through fire.
Do you not know it? You are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you.
If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him; for the temple of God is holy, and that temple is you.
Let no one deceive himself: if any of you thinks he is wise by the standards of this age, let him become a fool so as to become wise.
For the wisdom of this world is folly before God. For it is written: He catches the wise in their own cunning.
And again: The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise: they are nothing but wind.
So let no one take pride in men, for everything belongs to you:
Paul, Apollos, Cephas, the world, life, death, the present, the future: everything belongs to you;
but you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
Let us then be regarded as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.
Now what is asked of stewards is that each be found faithful.
For my part, it matters very little to me to be judged by you or by any human court; indeed, I do not even judge myself.
My conscience, it is true, reproaches me with nothing, but that does not make me justified: the one who judges me is the Lord.

So do not judge before the time, before the coming of the Lord: it is he who will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and make manifest the intentions of hearts. Then each will receive from God the praise that is due to him.

Brothers, I have applied all this to Apollos and to myself for your sake, so that through our example you may learn the rule: Nothing beyond what is written, and that none of you may be puffed up with pride, favoring one against another.
For who sets you apart? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?
Already you are filled! Already you are rich! Without us you have become kings! Ah, if only you were kings, so that we too might reign with you!
For God, it seems to me, has exhibited us apostles in the last place, like men condemned to death: we have been made a spectacle to the world, to angels and to men.
We are fools for Christ's sake, and you are so wise in Christ! We are weak, and you are strong! You are held in honor, and we in contempt!
To this very hour we suffer hunger and thirst and are poorly clothed; we are beaten, we are homeless;
we wear ourselves out working with our own hands. When insulted, we bless; when persecuted, we endure;
when slandered, we speak kindly. We have become like the refuse of the world, the scum of all, to this very day.
I am not writing this to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.
For even if you had thousands of guides in Christ, you do not have many fathers: it was I who, through the Good News, begot you in Christ Jesus.
I beg you, then: imitate me.
This is why I have sent you Timothy, my beloved and faithful child in the Lord: he will remind you of my ways in Christ Jesus, as I teach them everywhere, in every Church.
Some have become puffed up with pride, as though I were not coming to you.
But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out not the words of these arrogant people, but what they are capable of;
for the kingdom of God is not a matter of words, but of power.
What do you prefer? That I come to you with a rod, or with love and in a spirit of gentleness?
It is widely reported that there is immorality among you, and immorality of a kind not found even among the Gentiles: one of you is living with his father's wife!
And you are puffed up with pride! Should you not rather have mourned, so that the one who did such a deed might be removed from your midst?
For my part, absent in body but present in spirit, I have already judged, as if I were present, the one who committed this act:
in the name of our Lord Jesus, when you are all assembled and I am present in spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus,
such a man is to be handed over to Satan for the destruction of his flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord.
Your boasting is not good! Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole batch of dough?
Cleanse out the old leaven so that you may be a new batch, since you are unleavened bread. For our Passover, Christ, has been sacrificed.
Let us therefore celebrate the feast, not with the old leaven, the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with the immoral:
I did not mean the immoral of this world in general, or the greedy, the swindlers, the idolaters; otherwise you would have to leave the world.

In fact, I wrote to you not to associate with anyone who, while bearing the name of brother, is immoral, greedy, an idolater, a slanderer, a drunkard, or a swindler: with such a person, do not even share a meal.
For is it my business to judge those outside? Is it not those inside whom you are to judge?
Those outside, God will judge. Remove the wicked person from your midst.

titres.titre: The body, temple of the Spirit

versets.t: When one of you has a dispute with another, does he dare to go to law before the unrighteous rather than before the saints?
Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is to be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the most trivial cases?
Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more, then, the matters of this life!
Yet for the matters of this life, you appoint as judges people whom the Church counts as nothing!
I say this to your shame. Is there really no one among you wise enough, not a single one able to arbitrate between his brothers?
But a brother goes to court against a brother, and this before unbelievers!
In any case, it is already a defeat for you to have lawsuits among yourselves. Why not rather suffer the wrong? Why not rather let yourselves be cheated?
But it is you who do the wrong and the cheating, and this to your own brothers!
Do you not know it? The unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God. Do not be deceived: neither the immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor men of infamous ways,
nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor slanderers, nor swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God.
And such were some of you. But you have been washed, you have been sanctified, you have been justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and by the Spirit of our God.
Everything is permitted to me, but not everything is beneficial. Everything is permitted to me, but I will not let myself be enslaved by anything.
Food is for the stomach and the stomach for food; and God will destroy both the one and the other. But the body is not for immorality: it is for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
And God, who raised the Lord, will also raise us up by his power.
Do you not know that your bodies are the members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them the members of a prostitute? Certainly not!
Do you not know it? Whoever unites himself to a prostitute becomes one body with her, for it is said: The two will become one flesh.
But whoever unites himself to the Lord becomes one spirit with him.
Flee immorality. Every other sin that a person commits is outside the body; but whoever gives himself to immorality sins against his own body.
Do you not know it? Your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit who is in you, whom you have from God, and you do not belong to yourselves.
You were bought at a great price. So glorify God in your body.

titres.titre: Remaining where the call found us

versets.t: Now for what you wrote to me. It is good for a man to abstain from woman;
yet, to avoid all immorality, let each man have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.
Let the husband fulfill his duty toward his wife, and likewise the wife toward her husband.
It is not the wife who has authority over her own body, but her husband; likewise, it is not the husband who has authority over his own body, but his wife.

Do not refuse one another, except by mutual consent and for a time, in order to devote yourselves to prayer; then come together again, so that Satan may not take advantage of your lack of self-control to tempt you.
What I say here is a concession, not a command.
I wish that all men were as I am; but each receives from God his own gift, one in one way, another in another.
To the unmarried and to widows I say that it is good for them to remain as they are, as I do.
But if they cannot control themselves, let them marry: it is better to marry than to burn.
To those who are married I give this command, not I but the Lord: that a wife should not separate from her husband
(if she does separate, let her remain unmarried, or else be reconciled to him), and that a husband should not send away his wife.
To the rest I say, I and not the Lord: if a brother has an unbelieving wife and she consents to live with him, let him not send her away;
and if a woman has an unbelieving husband and he consents to live with her, let her not send her husband away.
For the unbelieving husband is sanctified through his wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified through the brother; otherwise your children would be unclean, whereas in reality they are holy.
But if the unbelieving partner wishes to separate, let there be separation: in that case the brother or the sister is not bound. God has called you to live in peace.
For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? How do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
For the rest, let each one live according to the lot the Lord has given him, as God has called him. This is the rule I lay down in all the Churches.
Was someone circumcised when he was called? Let him not try to undo it. Was he uncircumcised? Let him not get circumcised.
Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing; what counts is keeping the commandments of God.
Let each one remain in the condition in which he was when he was called.
Were you a slave when you were called? Do not let it trouble you; and even if you can become free, make the most of your condition instead.
For the slave who has been called in the Lord is a freedman of the Lord; likewise, the free man who has been called is a slave of Christ.
You were bought at a great price: do not become slaves of men.
Brothers, let each one remain before God in the condition in which he was when he was called.
Concerning virgins, I have no command from the Lord; but I give my opinion, as one whom the Lord in his mercy has made trustworthy.
I think, then, that this is a good thing, because of the present distress: yes, it is good for a person to remain as he is.
Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you free of a wife? Do not seek a wife.
But if you do marry, you do not sin; and if a virgin marries, she does not sin. Yet such people will face distress in the flesh, and I would like to spare you that.
This is what I mean, brothers: the time is short. From now on, let those who have wives live as though they had none,
those who weep as though they did not weep, those who rejoice as though they did not rejoice, those who buy as though they possessed nothing,
those who use the things of this world as though they did not use them; for the form of this world is passing away.
I would like you to be free from anxiety. The unmarried man is concerned with the affairs of the Lord: he seeks to please the Lord;
the married man is concerned with the affairs of the world: he seeks to please his wife,

and so he is divided. Likewise, the unmarried woman, like the young girl, is concerned with the affairs of the Lord, so as to be holy in body and in spirit; but the married woman is concerned with the affairs of the world: she seeks to please her husband.
I say this for your own good, not to set a trap for you, but to lead you to what is fitting and to attach you to the Lord without division.
If anyone thinks he is acting improperly toward his betrothed, if she is past the flower of her age and it must come to this, let him do as he wishes: he does not sin, let them marry.
But the man who, without being under constraint, master of his own decision, has firmly resolved in his heart to keep his betrothed a virgin, that man does well.
So the one who marries his betrothed does well, and the one who does not marry her does better.
A wife is bound as long as her husband lives; but if the husband dies, she is free to marry whom she wishes, provided it be in the Lord.
Yet she will be happier if she remains as she is: this is my opinion, and I think that I too have the Spirit of God.
Now for meat offered to idols. We know that we all have knowledge. But knowledge puffs up with pride, while charity builds up.
If anyone thinks he knows something, he does not yet know as he ought to know;
but if anyone loves God, that one is known by him.
So, as for eating meat offered to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no God but one.
For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth (and indeed there are many gods and many lords),
yet for us there is but one God, the Father, from whom all things come and for whom we exist, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things exist and through whom we exist.
But not everyone has this knowledge. Some, still accustomed to idols, eat this meat as though it were offered to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled by it.
Food will not bring us closer to God: if we do not eat, we are no worse off; if we do eat, we are no better off.
But take care that this liberty of yours does not become an occasion of stumbling for the weak.
For if someone sees you who have knowledge reclining at table in an idol's temple, will not the conscience of that weak person be led astray to eat meat offered to idols?
And so your knowledge destroys the weak one, this brother for whom Christ died!
By sinning in this way against your brothers and wounding their still weak conscience, it is against Christ that you sin.
This is why, if food is to make my brother fall, I will never eat meat again, so as not to make my brother fall.
Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?
If to others I am not an apostle, at least I am to you; for the seal of my apostleship is you, in the Lord.
This is my defense against those who call me into question.
Do we not have the right to eat and to drink?
Do we not have the right to take along with us a wife, a sister, as the other apostles do, and the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas?
Or is it only Barnabas and I who have no right to be excused from working?
Has anyone ever seen a soldier serve at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard without eating its fruit? Who tends a flock without feeding on its milk?
Is this merely a human point of view? Does not the Law itself say the same?
It is written in the law of Moses: You shall not muzzle the ox while it treads out the grain. Is it about oxen that God is concerned?
Is he not clearly speaking for our sake? Yes, it was written for us: the one who plows should plow in hope, and the one who threshes, in hope of sharing in the harvest.
If we have sown spiritual goods for you, is it too much to reap your material goods?

If others have this right over you, do we not have it all the more? Yet we have not made use of this right; on the contrary, we endure everything so as to put no obstacle in the way of the Good News of Christ.
Do you not know it? Those who perform the service of the Temple live from the Temple, and those who serve at the altar receive their share from the altar.
In the same way, the Lord has directed that those who proclaim the Good News should live from the Good News.
But I have made use of none of these rights, and I am not writing this so that they may be granted to me: I would rather die than let anyone deprive me of this ground for pride!
For proclaiming the Good News is no ground for boasting for me: it is a necessity laid upon me. Woe to me if I do not proclaim the Good News!
If I did it of my own accord, I would have a right to wages; but if I do it against my will, it is a charge entrusted to me.
What then are my wages? To proclaim the Good News free of charge, without making use of the right it gives me.
Yes, free with respect to all, I have made myself a slave to all, so as to win over as many as possible.
With the Jews I became like a Jew, to win the Jews; with those under the Law, as though I were under the Law (though I am not myself), to win those under the Law;
with those without the Law, as though I were without law (not that I am without the law of God, since I am under the law of Christ), to win those without the Law.
With the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all, so as to save at least some by every means.
And all this I do for the sake of the Good News, so that I too may share in it.
Do you not know it? In the stadium all the runners take the start, but only one receives the prize. Run, then, so as to win it.
Every athlete submits to complete discipline; they do it for a perishable crown, but we for an imperishable one.
So I run, not aimlessly; I box, but not as though beating the air.
On the contrary, I treat my body hard and master it, for fear that after proclaiming the message to others, I myself should be disqualified.

titres.titre: The table of the Lord and the table of demons
Everything for the glory of God

versets.t: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud, and all passed through the sea,
and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
and all ate the same spiritual food,
and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from a spiritual rock that followed them, and that rock was Christ.
Yet God was not pleased with most of them, for their bodies were strewn across the desert.
All this happened as an example for us, so that we might not have evil desires as they did.
Do not become idolaters, as some of them did, as it is written: The people sat down to eat and drink, and then rose up to revel.
Let us not give ourselves to immorality, as some of them did: twenty-three thousand of them fell in a single day.
Let us not put Christ to the test, as some of them did, and were destroyed by the serpents.
Do not grumble, as some of them did, and were destroyed by the Destroyer.
All this happened to them as an example, and it was written to warn us, upon whom the end of the ages has come.
So let the one who thinks he is standing take care not to fall.

No trial has come upon you that exceeds human measure; and God is faithful: he will not let you be tried beyond your strength, but with the trial he will also provide the way out and the strength to endure it.
Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
I speak to you as to sensible people; judge for yourselves what I say.
The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a communion in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a communion in the body of Christ?
Since there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all share in the one bread.
Look at Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices in communion with the altar?
What am I saying, then? That meat offered to idols is anything, or that an idol is anything?
No! But what the Gentiles offer in sacrifice, they offer to demons and not to God; and I do not want you to enter into communion with demons.
You cannot drink both the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; you cannot share in the table of the Lord and the table of demons.
Or do we want to provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?
Everything is permitted, but not everything is beneficial; everything is permitted, but not everything builds up.
Let no one seek his own interest, but that of others.
Eat whatever is sold in the market, without raising questions of conscience,
for the earth is the Lord's, and everything it contains.
If an unbeliever invites you and you wish to go, eat whatever is set before you, without raising questions of conscience.
But if someone says to you: This has been offered in sacrifice, then do not eat it, for the sake of the one who told you and for conscience' sake.
This conscience, I mean, is not your own, but the other's. For why should my liberty be judged by another's conscience?
If I eat with thanksgiving, why should I be blamed for that for which I give thanks?
So whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God.
Be no occasion of stumbling to Jews or to Greeks or to the Church of God;
just as I myself try to please everyone in everything, seeking not my own advantage but that of the many, so that they may be saved.

titres.titre: Man and woman in the assembly

versets.t: Imitate me, as I myself imitate Christ.
I commend you for remembering me in everything and for keeping the traditions just as I handed them on to you.
But I want you to know this: the head of every man is Christ; the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.
Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered brings shame on his head;
and every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered brings shame on her head: it is exactly as if she were shaved.
If a woman does not cover her head, let her have her hair cut off! But if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut off or her head shaved, let her cover her head.
A man ought not to cover his head, because he is the image and glory of God; the woman, for her part, is the glory of the man.
For it was not man who was drawn from woman, but woman from man;
and man was not created for woman, but woman for man.
This is why a woman ought to wear on her head a sign of her authority, because of the angels.
Nevertheless, in the Lord, woman is not without man, nor man without woman;
for if woman was drawn from man, man is born of woman, and everything comes from God.
Judge for yourselves: is it fitting for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
Does not nature itself teach you that it is dishonorable for a man to wear his hair long,
while it is a glory for a woman to wear hers so? For her hair has been given to her as a veil.
If anyone is inclined to be contentious, know that this is not our practice, nor that of the Churches of God.
In giving you this warning, I have nothing to commend: your gatherings, far from doing you good, do you harm.
First, I hear that when you gather as an assembly there are divisions among you, and I believe it in part.
There have to be opposing factions among you, so that those among you who have proved themselves may become evident.
So then, when you gather, it is no longer the Lord's Supper that you eat;
for as soon as you are at table, each one hurries to take his own meal, so that one is hungry while another is drunk.

Do you not have homes to eat and drink in? Or do you despise the Church of God and want to humiliate those who have nothing? What am I to say to you? Commend you? On this point, no, I do not commend you.
For here is what I received from the Lord, and what I handed on to you: the Lord Jesus, on the night he was handed over, took bread,
and, after giving thanks, he broke it and said: "This is my body, which is for you. Do this in memory of me."
In the same way, after the supper, he took the cup, saying: "This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Whenever you drink it, do this in memory of me."
So then, whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the death of the Lord until he comes.
Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily is guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.
Let each one, then, examine himself before eating of this bread and drinking of this cup;
for whoever eats and drinks without discerning the body eats and drinks his own condemnation.
This is why there are many among you who are sick and infirm, and why a number have died.
If we examined ourselves, we would not be judged;
but by his judgments the Lord corrects us, so that we may not be condemned along with the world.
So, my brothers, when you gather for this meal, wait for one another.
If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that your gatherings may not turn to your condemnation. As for the rest, I will set it in order when I come.
Concerning spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to remain in ignorance.
You know that when you were pagans you were led astray to mute idols, drawn wherever you were led.
So I declare to you: no one speaking under the action of the Spirit of God says, "Cursed be Jesus"; and no one can say, "Jesus is Lord," except under the action of the Holy Spirit.
There is a diversity of gifts, but it is the same Spirit;
a diversity of ministries, but it is the same Lord;
a diversity of activities, but it is the same God who accomplishes everything in everyone.
To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the good of all.
To one, through the Spirit, is given a word of wisdom; to another, a word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit;
to another, faith, in the same Spirit; to another, the gift of healing, in the one Spirit;
to another, the power to work miracles; to another, prophecy; to another, the discernment of spirits; to another, various kinds of tongues; to another, the gift of interpreting them.
But all this is the work of the one and the same Spirit, who distributes his gifts to each one individually, as he wills.
Take a comparison: the body is one, and yet it has many members; and all the members of the body, though many, form but one body. So it is with Christ.
For we were all baptized in one Spirit to form one body, Jews or Greeks, slaves or free; and all of us were given the one Spirit to drink.
For the body is not made up of one member, but of many.
If the foot were to say, "Since I am not the hand, I am not part of the body," would it for that reason cease to belong to the body?
And if the ear were to say, "Since I am not the eye, I am not part of the body," would it for that reason cease to belong to the body?
If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If it were all hearing, where would the sense of smell be?
But God has arranged each of the members in the body as he willed.
If the whole were a single member, where would the body be?
There are, then, many members, but one body.
The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you," nor the head say to the feet, "I have no need of you."
On the contrary, the members of the body that seem to be the weakest are the most necessary;
and those we judge less honorable we surround with greater honor; our less presentable members are treated with the greatest respect,
which our presentable members do not require. But God has composed the body, giving greater honor to the part that lacked it,
so that there may be no division in the body, but that the members may have the same care for one another.
If one member suffers, all the members share its suffering; if one member is honored, all share its joy.
Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you, for his part, is a member of it.

Those whom God has appointed in the Church are first the apostles, second the prophets, third those who teach; then come miracles, then the gifts of healing, of assistance, of governance, and the gift of speaking various tongues.
Are all apostles? All prophets? All teachers? Do all work miracles?
Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret them?
Aspire to the greatest gifts. And I will show you a way that surpasses them all.
If I were to speak the tongues of men and of angels, but had not charity, I would be a resounding bronze, a clashing cymbal.
If I had the gift of prophecy, and understood all mysteries and all knowledge, and had faith in its fullness, the faith that moves mountains, but had not charity, I would be nothing.
If I gave away all my goods to feed the hungry, and handed over my body to the flames, but had not charity, it would profit me nothing.
Charity is patient, charity is kind; it is not envious, it does not boast, it is not puffed up with pride,
it does nothing improper, it does not seek its own interest, it is not irritable, it holds no grudge;
it does not rejoice in injustice, but finds its joy in the truth.
It excuses everything, believes everything, hopes everything, endures everything.
Charity will never pass away. Prophecies? They will be abolished. Tongues? They will cease. Knowledge? It will be abolished.
For our knowledge is partial, and partial our prophecy;
but when what is perfect comes, what is partial will be abolished.
When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I thought as a child, I reasoned as a child; when I became a man, I left behind what belonged to the child.
At present we see in a mirror, dimly; but then it will be face to face. At present my knowledge is partial; but then I will know as I am known.
So now these three remain: faith, hope, and charity; but the greatest of the three is charity.

titres.titre: Let everything be done with order

versets.t: Pursue charity; aspire also to spiritual gifts, above all to that of prophecy.
For the one who speaks in a tongue speaks not to men but to God: no one understands him, he utters mysterious things in spirit.
The one who prophesies, on the contrary, speaks to men: he builds them up, encourages them, comforts them.
The one who speaks in a tongue builds up himself; the one who prophesies builds up the Church.

I would be glad for you all to speak in tongues, but I prefer that you prophesy. The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets, so that the Church may be built up.
Consider, brothers: if I came to you speaking in tongues, what good would I be to you, if my words brought you neither revelation nor knowledge nor prophecy nor teaching?
It is the same with lifeless instruments that produce a sound, whether flute or lyre: if they do not give distinct notes, how will anyone recognize the tune played on the flute or the lyre?
And if the trumpet gives an uncertain sound, who will get ready for battle?
So it is with you: if your tongue does not utter a clear word, how will anyone know what you are saying? You will be speaking into the air.
There are in the world a great number of languages, and none is without meaning;
but if I do not grasp the meaning of the sounds, I will be a foreigner to the one who speaks, and he a foreigner to me.
So it is with you: since you aspire to the gifts of the Spirit, seek to have them in abundance for the building up of the Church.
This is why the one who speaks in a tongue should pray for the power to interpret it.
For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit is at prayer, but my mind bears no fruit.
What then shall I do? I will pray with the spirit, but I will also pray with the mind; I will sing with the spirit, but I will also sing with the mind.
Otherwise, if you give thanks only with the spirit, how will the one who has the place of a mere listener be able to answer "Amen" to your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?
Your thanksgiving is fine, no doubt, but the other is not built up by it.
I give thanks to God that I speak in tongues more than all of you;
but in the assembly I would rather say five words with my mind, to instruct others, than ten thousand in a tongue.
Brothers, do not be children in judgment; in evil be little children, but in judgment be adults.
It is written in the Law: By people of another tongue and by foreign lips I will speak to this people, and even so they will not listen to me, says the Lord.
So tongues are a sign not for believers but for unbelievers; prophecy, on the contrary, is for believers, not for unbelievers.
If, then, the whole Church gathers and all speak in tongues, and some uninstructed people or unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are mad?
But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or an uninstructed person comes in, he is convicted by all, judged by all;
the secrets of his heart are laid bare; then, falling on his face, he will worship God and proclaim: God is really among you!
What then, brothers? When you gather, each one may have a hymn, a teaching, a revelation, a message in a tongue, an interpretation: let everything be done for building up.
If anyone speaks in a tongue, let there be two, or at most three, each in turn, and let someone interpret.
If there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the assembly; let him speak to himself and to God.
As for the prophets, let two or three speak, and let the others judge.
And if another, seated, receives a revelation, let the first one keep silent.
You can all prophesy, but one after another, so that all may be instructed and all encouraged;
for the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets:
God is not a God of disorder, but of peace. As in all the Churches of the saints,
let the women keep silent in the assemblies, for they are not permitted to speak there; let them remain in submission, as the Law also says.
If they wish to learn about some point, let them ask their husbands at home; for it is improper for a woman to speak in the assembly.
Was it from you that the word of God went forth? Or is it to you alone that it has come?
If anyone thinks he is a prophet or inspired by the Spirit, let him recognize in what I write to you a commandment of the Lord.
And if anyone does not recognize it, he will not be recognized.
So, my brothers, aspire to the gift of prophecy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues;
but let everything be done with dignity and in order.

titres.titre: Christ, the firstfruits of those who rise

versets.t: I remind you, brothers, of the Good News that I proclaimed to you, which you received and in which you stand firm.
Through it you are being saved, if you hold to it as I proclaimed it to you; otherwise you would have believed in vain.
I handed on to you, above all, what I myself had received: Christ died for our sins, according to the Scriptures;
he was placed in the tomb, he rose again on the third day, according to the Scriptures;
he appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve.
Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, most of whom are still alive, though some have fallen asleep.
Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
And last of all he appeared to me too, as to one born abnormally.
For I am the least of the apostles, unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the Church of God.
But what I am, I am by the grace of God, and his grace toward me has not been barren: I have worked harder than all of them, not I, but the grace of God that is with me.
In short, whether it be they or I, this is what we proclaim, and this is what you have believed.
Now if it is proclaimed that Christ has been raised from the dead, how can some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
If there is no resurrection of the dead, then neither has Christ been raised;
and if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation is empty, and empty too is your faith.
It even turns out that we are false witnesses of God, since we have testified against God that he raised Christ, when he would not have raised him, if it is true that the dead do not rise.
For if the dead do not rise, then neither has Christ been raised;
and if Christ has not been raised, your faith is an illusion, you are still in your sins,
and then those who have fallen asleep in Christ are lost.
If we have set our hope in Christ for this life only, we are of all people the most to be pitied.
But no! Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
For since death came through a man, it is through a man also that the resurrection of the dead comes.
Just as all die in Adam, so all will be brought to life in Christ,
but each in his own order: first Christ, as the firstfruits; then, at his coming, those who belong to Christ.
Then will come the end, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, after destroying every Principality, every Authority, and every Power.
For he must reign until he has put all his enemies under his feet.
The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
For he has put everything under his feet. But when Scripture says that everything is subjected to him, it is clear that this excepts the One who subjected everything to him.
And when everything has been subjected to him, then the Son himself will be subjected to the One who subjected everything to him, so that God may be all in all.
Otherwise, what would those be doing who have themselves baptized for the dead? If the dead do not rise at all, why do they have themselves baptized for them?
And we ourselves, why do we face danger at every hour?
Every day I am exposed to death, as surely, brothers, as you are my pride in Christ Jesus our Lord.
If it was for merely human ends that I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what does it profit me? If the dead do not rise, let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.
Do not be deceived: bad company ruins good morals.
Come back to your right senses and sin no more; for some have no knowledge of God, I say this to your shame.
But someone will say, how are the dead raised? With what kind of body do they come back?
You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies;
and what you sow is not the plant that is to be, but a mere seed, a grain of wheat, for example, or some other seed;
then God gives it a body as he has willed, to each seed the body proper to it.
Not all flesh is the same: one is that of men, another that of cattle, another that of birds, another that of fish.
There are also heavenly bodies and earthly bodies; but the splendor of the heavenly is one thing, that of the earthly another.
The splendor of the sun is one thing, the splendor of the moon another, the splendor of the stars another; and one star even differs from another in splendor.
So it is with the resurrection of the dead. Sown corruptible, the body rises incorruptible;
sown in dishonor, it rises in glory; sown in weakness, it rises in strength;
sown a natural body, it rises a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
So it is written: The first man, Adam, became a living being; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
It is not the spiritual that comes first, but the natural; the spiritual comes afterward.
The first man, drawn from the earth, is earthly; the second man comes from heaven.
As was the earthly man, so are the earthly; and as is the heavenly man, so will the heavenly be.
And just as we have borne the image of the earthly man, so we will also bear the image of the heavenly man.
What I am saying, brothers, is that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, and that corruption does not inherit incorruptibility.
Behold, I reveal to you a mystery: we will not all die, but we will all be transformed,
in an instant, in the blink of an eye, at the sound of the last trumpet. For it will sound, and the dead will rise incorruptible, and we will be transformed.
For this corruptible being must put on incorruptibility, and this mortal being must put on immortality.
And when this corruptible being has put on incorruptibility, and this mortal being immortality, then the word of Scripture will be fulfilled: Death is swallowed up in victory.
Where is your victory, O death? Where is your sting, O death?
The sting of death is sin; and the power of sin is the Law.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
So, my beloved brothers, be firm, unshakable, always more devoted to the work of the Lord, knowing that in the Lord your labor is not in vain.
Concerning the collection for the saints, you too are to follow the directions I gave to the Churches of Galatia.
On the first day of the week, let each of you set aside at home whatever he has been able to save, so that there may be no collections to make when I come.
When I arrive, I will send those whom you have judged worthy, with letters, to carry your gifts to Jerusalem;
and if it is worth my going too, they will make the journey with me.
I will come to you after passing through Macedonia, for I am only passing through it;
but with you perhaps I will stay, or even spend the winter, so that you may then send me on my way, wherever I go.
This time I do not want to see you only in passing: I hope to remain some time with you, if the Lord permits.
I will stay at Ephesus until Pentecost,
for a door has opened there, wide and active, and the adversaries are many.
If Timothy comes, see that he is without fear among you, for he is working, as I am, at the work of the Lord.
So let no one despise him. Send him on his way in peace, so that he may come to join me, for I am waiting for him with the brothers.
As for our brother Apollos, I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers; but it was not at all his will to go now: he will go when he finds the opportunity.
Be watchful, stand firm in the faith, be courageous, be strong.
Let everything you do be done in charity.
One more request, brothers. You know that the household of Stephanas is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that it has devoted itself to the service of the saints:
well then, in your turn be submissive to such men, and to everyone who labors and toils with them.
I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus: they have made up for your absence,
for they have set my spirit and yours at rest. Learn to appreciate such men.
The Churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Prisca, with the Church that meets in their house, greet you warmly in the Lord.
All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a kiss of peace.
This greeting is in my own hand, mine, Paul's.
If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be accursed! Marana tha: Lord, come!
May the grace of the Lord Jesus be with you!
My love is with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, to the Church of God that is at Corinth, together with all the holy ones throughout the whole of Achaia:
grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed be God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation!
He consoles us in all our afflictions, so that we may be able to console those who are in any affliction, with the consolation we ourselves receive from God.
For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow into us, so through Christ our consolation also overflows.
If we are afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation. If we are consoled, it is for your consolation, which makes you able to endure the same sufferings that we endure.
And our hope for you is firm: we know that as you share in the sufferings, so you also share in the consolation.
We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the affliction that struck us in Asia: we were crushed beyond measure, beyond our strength, to the point of despairing even of staying alive.
Indeed, we carried within ourselves the sentence of death, so that we might place our trust not in ourselves but in God, who raises the dead.
He it is who delivered us from so great a death and who will deliver us again; in him we have this hope, that he will deliver us still,
as you yourselves help us by your prayer. So the grace obtained for us through many will also, on the part of many, become a cause of thanksgiving on our behalf.

This is our pride: the testimony of our conscience that we have conducted ourselves in the world, and above all toward you, with the sincerity and integrity that come from God, not by any merely human wisdom but by the grace of God.
We write you nothing other than what you read and understand; and I hope you will understand fully,
as you have already understood us in part, that we are your pride, as you will be ours, on the day of our Lord Jesus.
In this confidence I wanted to come to you first, so that you might have a second grace;
to pass through your city on my way to Macedonia, then to return from Macedonia to you, and to be sent on my way by you to Judea.
In forming this plan, was I then acting lightly? Or are my decisions made according to the flesh, so that with me there is 'yes, yes' and 'no, no' at once?
As surely as God is faithful, our word to you is not 'yes' and 'no' at the same time.
For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, whom we proclaimed among you, Silvanus, Timothy, and I, was not 'yes' and 'no': in him there has only ever been 'yes.'
For all the promises of God find their 'yes' in him; and so it is through him that we say the Amen to God, for his glory.
And the one who strengthens us together with you in Christ, the one who has anointed us, is God;
he has also marked us with his seal and put the Spirit in our hearts as a first down payment.
I call on God as witness upon my life: if I have not returned to Corinth, it was to spare you.
It is not that we want to lord it over your faith; on the contrary, we work for your joy, for in the faith you stand firm.
So I made up my mind not to come to you again in sorrow.
For if I cause you sorrow, who then can gladden me but the very one I have grieved?
And if I wrote to you as I did, it was so that on my arrival I might not be saddened by those who ought to gladden me; I am confident of you all that my joy is the joy of all of you.
It was out of great distress and anguish of heart, and with many tears, that I wrote to you, not to sadden you but to let you know the overflowing love I have for you.
If someone has caused sorrow, he has not saddened me but, to some degree (let us not overstate it), all of you.
For this man, the rebuke inflicted by the majority is enough;
so it is better now to forgive him and comfort him, lest he be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
I urge you, then, to reaffirm your love for him.
For in writing to you, I also wanted to put you to the test and to know whether you are obedient in everything.
Anyone you forgive, I forgive too; and if I have forgiven anything, if indeed I had anything to forgive, it was for your sake, in the presence of Christ,
so as not to let Satan gain the advantage over us, for we are not unaware of his designs.
When I came to Troas for the Good News of Christ, though a door was opened for me there in the Lord,
my spirit had no rest, because I did not find Titus my brother there; so I took my leave of them and set out for Macedonia.
Thanks be to God, who always leads us in the triumphal procession of Christ and who, through us, spreads in every place the fragrance of the knowledge of him!
For we are, for God, the sweet aroma of Christ, both among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing:
to the one, an odor that leads from death to death; to the other, a fragrance that leads from life to life. And who then is equal to such a task?
For we are not, like so many others, peddlers of the word of God; it is with sincerity, from God, before God, in Christ, that we speak.

titres.titre: The glory of the new covenant

versets.t: Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?
You yourselves are our letter: it is written on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
It is clear that you are a letter of Christ, entrusted to our care, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of flesh, on your hearts.
Such is the confidence we have before God, through Christ.
It is not that we are capable by ourselves of claiming anything as coming from us: our capability comes from God,
who has made us capable of being ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.

Now if the ministry of death, carved in letters on stone, was surrounded with such glory that the sons of Israel could not gaze on the face of Moses because of its brightness, fleeting though that brightness was,
how much more will the ministry of the Spirit be surrounded with glory!
If the ministry of condemnation was a glory, how much more does the ministry of righteousness abound in glory!
Indeed, what was once glorified is glorified no longer, in view of this glory that surpasses it.
For if what was passing came with glory, how much more will what endures be in glory!
With such a hope, we speak with complete confidence.
We do not act like Moses, who used to put a veil over his face to keep the sons of Israel from seeing the end of what was fading away.
But their minds were closed. To this very day, indeed, that same veil remains over the reading of the Old Testament; it is not lifted, for it is in Christ that it is taken away.
Yes, to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their hearts;
but whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil falls away.
Now the Lord is the Spirit; and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
And all of us, with unveiled faces, reflecting as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into that same image, from glory to glory, by the Lord, who is Spirit.
This is why, entrusted with this ministry through the mercy shown to us, we do not lose heart.

We renounce shameful, hidden ways; we do not act with cunning, and we do not falsify the word of God; on the contrary, by the open manifestation of the truth, we commend ourselves to every human conscience before God.
And if our Good News remains veiled, it is veiled for those who are perishing,
for the unbelievers whose minds the god of this world has blinded, so that they may not see the radiance of the Good News of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
For it is not ourselves that we proclaim, but Christ Jesus as Lord; and we ourselves are your servants for the sake of Jesus.
For the God who said, Let light shine out of the darkness, is the one who has shone in our hearts, to make the knowledge of the glory of God shine forth, radiant on the face of Christ.
But this treasure we carry in earthen vessels, so that this extraordinary power may be seen to be God's and not ours.
Pressed on every side, but not crushed; perplexed, but not driven to despair;
persecuted, but not abandoned; struck down, but not destroyed;
we always carry in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus, too, may be revealed in our body.
For we, the living, are constantly being handed over to death for the sake of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus, too, may be revealed in our mortal flesh.
So death is at work in us, and life in you.
But we have that same spirit of faith of which it is written: I believed, and so I spoke. We too believe, and so we speak,
knowing that the one who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and will place us at his side, together with you.
And all of this is for you, so that grace, as it reaches more and more people, may make thanksgiving overflow, to the glory of God.
This is why we do not lose heart; and even though our outer self is wasting away, our inner self is being renewed day by day.
For our momentary affliction, so slight, is preparing for us, beyond all measure, an eternal weight of glory;
and so we look not to what is seen but to what is unseen: what is seen is passing, what is unseen is eternal.
We know that if our earthly dwelling, this tent, is destroyed, we have a building that is the work of God, an eternal dwelling in the heavens, not made by human hands.
And so we groan in this tent, longing to be clothed over it with our heavenly dwelling,
if indeed we are found clothed and not naked.
Yes, as long as we are in this tent, we groan under our burden; we would not wish to be unclothed but to be clothed over, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
And the one who has made us for this very thing is God, who has given us his Spirit as a first down payment.
So we are always full of confidence, knowing that while we dwell in this body we are away from the Lord;
for we walk by faith, not by sight.
Yes, we are full of confidence, and we would rather leave this body and dwell with the Lord.
And so, whether we remain in this body or leave it, our ambition is to please him.
For we must all appear, laid bare, before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each may receive the recompense for what he has done during his bodily life, whether good or evil.
Knowing, then, what the fear of the Lord is, we seek to persuade people. In the eyes of God we are laid bare, and I hope we are so in the eyes of your conscience as well.
We are not commending ourselves to you again; rather, we are giving you occasion to be proud of us, so that you may have an answer for those who take pride in appearances and not in the heart.
If we have lost our reason, it is for God; if we are reasonable, it is for you.
For the love of Christ compels us, once we are convinced that one has died for all, and that therefore all have died.
Yes, he died for all, so that the living may no longer live for themselves but for the one who died and was raised for them.
From now on, then, we regard no one according to the flesh; and even if we once knew Christ according to the flesh, now we no longer know him in that way.
And so, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation: the old world has gone, a new world has already been born.
All of this comes from God, who has reconciled us to himself through Christ and has entrusted to us the ministry of reconciliation.
For it was God who, in Christ, was reconciling the world to himself, not counting people's trespasses against them, and who has placed in us the word of reconciliation.
So we are ambassadors of Christ, and through us it is God himself who makes his appeal: in the name of Christ, we beg you, be reconciled to God.
The one who had not known sin, God made to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

titres.titre: The temple of the living God

versets.t: Since we are his fellow workers, we beg you: do not receive the grace of God in vain.
For he says: At the favorable time I heard you; on the day of salvation I helped you. Now is the favorable time; now is the day of salvation.
We give no one any occasion for stumbling, so that our ministry may not be discredited.
