On the contrary, in everything we present ourselves as ministers of God: by great endurance in afflictions, hardships, distresses,
under beatings, in imprisonments, riots, labors, sleepless nights, times of hunger;
by purity, knowledge, patience, kindness, by the Holy Spirit, by a love without pretense,
by the word of truth, by the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;
in honor and dishonor, in ill repute and good repute; taken for impostors, though we are truthful;
for unknown, though we are well known; for dying, and yet we live; for punished, but not put to death;
for sorrowful, though we are always joyful; for poor, though we make many rich; for having nothing, though we possess everything.
We have spoken to you with complete frankness, Corinthians, and our heart has opened wide.
You are not cramped in us; it is in your own selves that you are cramped.
Give us the same in return (I speak to you as to my children): you too, open wide your heart.
Do not be mismatched in a common yoke with unbelievers. What partnership is there between righteousness and lawlessness? What fellowship between light and darkness?
What agreement between Christ and the Accuser? What common share between the believer and the unbeliever?

What accord between the temple of God and idols? For we ourselves are the temple of the living God, as God has said: I will dwell among them and walk among them; I will be their God, and they will be my people.
Therefore come out from among these people, set yourselves apart, says the Lord; touch nothing unclean, and I will welcome you.
I will be a father to you, and you will be sons and daughters to me, says the Lord Almighty.
Since we have such promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, and complete our sanctification in the fear of God.
Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, we have ruined no one, we have exploited no one.
I do not say this to condemn you; I have already told you: you are in our hearts, in life and in death.
I have great confidence in you, great pride in you; I am filled with consolation, overflowing with joy in all our afflictions.
On our arrival in Macedonia, we had no rest; on every side there was affliction: without, conflicts; within, fears.
But the one who consoles the lowly, God, consoled us by the arrival of Titus;
and not only by his arrival, but by the comfort he had received from you: he reported to us your deep longing, your tears, your devotion to me, so that my joy was all the greater.
So even if I saddened you by my letter, I do not regret it. I had regretted it, seeing that this letter had saddened you, if only for a moment;
but now I rejoice, not because you were saddened, but because that sadness led you to conversion. For it was a godly sorrow, and so you suffered no harm from us.
For godly sorrow produces a salutary repentance that one does not regret; the sorrow of the world, however, produces death.

See instead what it has produced in you, this godly sorrow: what earnestness, and even more, what excuses, what indignation, what fear, what deep longing, what zeal, what readiness to punish! In every way you have shown your innocence in this matter.
So if I wrote to you, it was neither for the offender nor for the offended, but so that your earnestness toward us might become clear among you, before God.
This is what consoled us. And to this consolation was added a far greater joy still: seeing Titus so happy, his spirit set at rest by you all.
If I had boasted a little about you to him, I had no cause to blush: just as we have always told you the truth, so also the praise we had given you before Titus proved true.
And his affection for you grows all the greater, as he recalls the obedience of you all, and the fear and respect with which you welcomed him.
I rejoice that in everything I can count on you.
We want to make known to you, brothers, the grace that God has poured out in the Churches of Macedonia:
in the midst of the many trials that afflicted them, their overflowing joy and their deep poverty overflowed into riches of generosity.
According to their means, I testify, and even beyond their means, of their own accord,
they urgently begged us for the favor of taking part in this service for the holy ones.
And, exceeding our expectation, they gave themselves, first to the Lord, then to us, by the will of God.
So we urged Titus to go and complete among you this work of generosity, as he had begun it.
You excel in everything: in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in zeal of every kind, and in the love you have for us; so excel in this work of generosity as well.
I am not giving an order; but through the zeal of others, I want to test the sincerity of your love.
For you know the generosity of our Lord Jesus Christ: though he was rich, he made himself poor for your sake, so that by his poverty you might become rich.
This is my advice to you in this matter, and it is in your own interest: since last year you were the first not only to act but to form the desire.
Now, then, complete the work: just as you were eager to want it, so be eager to accomplish it according to your means.
For when the eagerness is there, one is pleasing to God according to what one has, not according to what one does not have.
It is not a matter of putting you in hardship to relieve others, but of following a rule of equality:
for the moment, your surplus provides for their want, so that their surplus may provide for your want. In this way there will be equality,
as it is written: The one who had gathered much had nothing left over, and the one who had gathered little lacked nothing.
Thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same eagerness for you:
he responded to our appeal and, more eager still, is going to you of his own accord.
With him we are sending the brother whom all the Churches praise for his service of the Good News;

more than that, he has been appointed by the vote of the Churches as our traveling companion in this work of generosity that we are carrying out for the glory of the Lord himself and to show our good will.
We want to avoid any reproach concerning these generous sums that we are administering;
for we are intent on doing what is right, not only before the Lord but also before people.
With them we are also sending our brother, whose zeal we have often tested, on many occasions, and who shows it even more now, so great is his confidence in you.
As for Titus, he is my companion and my fellow worker for you; as for our brothers, they are the envoys of the Churches, the glory of Christ.
So give them, before all the Churches, the proof of your love, and show that we were right to be proud of you.
About this service for the holy ones, it is unnecessary for me to write to you;
for I know your good will, of which I boast about you to the Macedonians: Achaia, I tell them, has been ready since last year; and your zeal has stirred up a great many of them.
Still, I am sending the brothers, so that our pride in you may not be proved empty on this point, and that you may be ready, as I have declared.
Otherwise, if some Macedonians were to come with me and find you unprepared, what shame it would be for us (not to say for you) to have had such confidence!

So I judged it necessary to urge the brothers to go ahead of me to you and to prepare in advance the generous gift you have promised, so that it may be ready as a true bounty and not as something grudging.
Keep this in mind: whoever sows sparingly will reap sparingly; whoever sows generously will reap generously.
Let each one give as he has decided in his heart, without regret or compulsion; for God loves a cheerful giver.
And God has the power to fill you with every grace, so that, having always and in everything all you need, you may still have a surplus for every good work,
as it is written: He has distributed, he has given to the poor; his righteousness endures forever.
The one who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed, and will increase the fruits of your righteousness.
You will thus be enriched in every way, for a full generosity that, through us, will make thanksgiving rise up to God.
For the ministry of this offering not only meets the needs of the holy ones; it also overflows into many acts of thanksgiving to God.
Through the proven worth of this service, they will give glory to God for your obedience in professing the Good News of Christ, and for the generosity of your sharing with them and with all.
And in their prayer for you, they will show you their affection, because of the surpassing grace that God has placed in you.
Thanks be to God for his indescribable gift!

titres.titre: The authority the Lord gave to Paul

versets.t: I, Paul, appeal to you by the gentleness and kindness of Christ, I who am so humble when face to face with you, but so bold toward you when I am far away.
I beg you: do not force me, once present, to show that boldness, that assurance with which I intend to deal with certain people who think we are conducting ourselves according to the flesh.
We live in the flesh, no doubt, but it is not according to the flesh that we wage war.
The weapons of our warfare are not fleshly; they have from God their power to tear down strongholds. We tear down arguments
and every pretension that rises up against the knowledge of God, and we take captive every thought to make it obey Christ.
And we are ready to punish every disobedience, as soon as your obedience is complete.
Look, then, at the plain facts. If anyone is convinced that he belongs to Christ, let him consider this within himself: just as he is Christ's, so are we too.
And even if I boast a little too much about our authority, which the Lord gave us to build you up and not to tear you down, I would have no cause to blush.
I do not want to seem to be trying to frighten you by my letters.
'His letters,' people say, 'are severe and forceful; but when he is present, his person is weak and his speech contemptible.'
Let the one who says this be sure of this: what we are in word through our letters when absent, that we will also be in deed when present.

We certainly do not dare to rank or compare ourselves with certain people who commend themselves; measuring themselves by their own standard and comparing themselves with themselves, they are without understanding.
As for us, we will not boast beyond all measure, but according to the measure of the field that God has assigned us as our portion, a field that reaches even to you.
We are not overreaching our limits, as if we had not come to you; for it was indeed all the way to you that we came with the Good News of Christ.
We do not boast beyond measure of the labor of others; but we have the hope that, as your faith grows, our work among you may be enlarged, according to the field that falls to us, and greatly so,
and that we may proclaim the Good News beyond your borders, without boasting of work already done by others in their own territory.
But let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.
For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
Ah, if only you could bear with a little foolishness from me! But yes, do bear with me.
I feel for you a jealousy that comes from God: for I betrothed you to a single husband, to present you to Christ as a pure virgin.
But I am afraid that, as Eve was seduced by the serpent's cunning, your thoughts may be corrupted and turned away from sincerity and purity toward Christ.

For if someone comes and preaches to you another Jesus than the one we preached, or if you receive a different spirit than the one you received, or a different Good News than the one you welcomed, you bear with it very well!
Yet I consider that I have been in no way inferior to these extraordinary apostles.
Even if I am unskilled in speech, I am not so in knowledge; in every way and before all we have shown it to you.
Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself to lift you up, by proclaiming to you the Good News of God free of charge?
I robbed other Churches, taking pay from them to serve you.

And when I was present with you and found myself in need, I was a burden to no one: it was the brothers who came from Macedonia who supplied what I lacked. In everything I kept myself from being a burden to you, and I will keep myself so.
As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, this boast of mine will not be taken from me in the regions of Achaia.
Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do.
But what I am doing, I will keep on doing, to cut off any pretext from those who look for one to be found our equals in the very thing they boast of.
Such people are false apostles, deceitful workers, who disguise themselves as apostles of Christ.
No wonder: Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light.
So it is no surprise that his servants too disguise themselves as servants of righteousness. Their end will match their works.
I say it again: let no one take me for a fool; or else accept me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
What I am about to say, I say not according to the Lord, but as in a fit of folly, now that I have launched into boasting.
Since so many others boast according to the flesh, I too will boast.
You put up so gladly with fools, you who are so sensible!
You put up with it when someone enslaves you, devours you, robs you, treats you with contempt, strikes you in the face.
I say it to my shame: we were apparently too weak for that! Yet whatever others dare, I speak as a fool, I dare it too.
Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.
Are they servants of Christ? I am going to say something foolish: I am more so than they. Far more in labors, far more in imprisonments, immeasurably more in beatings; often in danger of death.
Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes less one.
Three times I was beaten with rods, once stoned; three times I was shipwrecked, I spent a day and a night in the depths of the sea.

Journeys without number, dangers from rivers, dangers from robbers, dangers from my own people, dangers from the Gentiles, dangers in the city, dangers in the wilderness, dangers at sea, dangers among false brothers;
toil and hardship, sleepless nights without number, hunger and thirst, frequent fasting, cold and nakedness.
And, not to mention all the rest, there is the daily pressure on me: the anxiety for all the Churches.
Who is weak without my being weak? Who is made to fall without a fire burning in me?
If I must boast, it is of my weakness that I will boast.
The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is blessed forever, knows that I am not lying.
At Damascus, the governor under King Aretas had the city guarded in order to seize me;
but I was lowered in a basket through an opening in the wall, and I escaped his hands.

titres.titre: Visions, revelations, and the thorn in the flesh
The announcement of a third visit

versets.t: Must I boast? It serves no purpose; yet I will come to the visions and revelations of the Lord.
I know a man in Christ who, fourteen years ago, was caught up to the third heaven; was it in his body? I do not know; out of his body? I do not know; God knows.
And I know that this man, in his body or out of his body? I do not know, God knows,
was caught up to paradise and heard inexpressible words that no one is permitted to repeat.
Of such a man I will boast; but of myself I will boast only of my weaknesses.
If I wanted to boast, I would not be a fool, for I would be telling the truth; but I refrain, so that no one may think more of me than what he sees in me or hears from me,
and because of the very excess of these revelations. This is why, to keep me from becoming proud, a thorn was put in my flesh, an angel of Satan to buffet me, to keep me from becoming proud.
Three times I begged the Lord to remove it from me.

But he said to me: 'My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.' So it is most gladly that I will boast rather of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
That is why I delight in weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions, and distresses, for the sake of Christ; for when I am weak, then I am strong.
Here I am, become a fool! You forced me to it. You are the ones who should have commended me, for I have been in no way inferior to these extraordinary apostles, even though I am nothing.
The signs of an apostle I performed among you, with all perseverance: signs, wonders, and miracles.
In what way were you treated worse than the other Churches, except that I, for my part, was not a burden to you? Forgive me this injustice!

Here I am, ready to come to you for the third time, and I will not be a burden to you; for what I seek is not your possessions but you. It is not for children to store up for their parents, but for parents to do so for their children.
For my part, I will most gladly spend and be spent entirely for your souls. If I love you more, am I to be loved less?
So be it! I myself was not a burden to you; but, crafty fellow that I am, I supposedly took you in by trickery!
Did I exploit you through any of those I sent to you?
I urged Titus to go to you, and I sent with him the brother you know. Did Titus exploit you? Did we not walk in the same spirit, in the same footsteps?
You have long been imagining that we are trying to justify ourselves before you. It is before God, in Christ, that we speak; and all of this, my beloved, is for your building up.

For I am afraid that when I arrive I may not find you as I would wish, and that you may find me such as you would not wish; that there may be quarrels, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalries, slander, gossip, arrogance, disorder.

I am afraid that on my next visit my God may humble me again before you, and that I may have to grieve over many of those who sinned in the past and have not turned away from the impurity, the immorality, and the debauchery they committed.
This is the third time I am coming to you. Every matter will be settled on the word of two or three witnesses.

I have said it before, and I say it again in advance, as I did on my second visit and, now while absent, to those who sinned in the past and to all the others: if I come again, I will not spare anyone,
since you are seeking proof that Christ speaks in me, he who is not weak toward you but is powerful among you.
For he was crucified in weakness, but he lives by the power of God. And we too are weak in him, but we will live with him by the power of God, for you.
Examine yourselves, to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves. Do you not recognize that Jesus Christ is in you? Unless perhaps you fail the test.
But you will recognize, I hope, that we are not among those who fail the test.
We pray to God that you may do no wrong; not so that we may appear to have passed the test, but so that you may do what is good, even if we should appear to have failed.
For we have no power against the truth; we have power only for the truth.
Yes, we rejoice to be weak when you are strong; and what we ask in our prayers is your perfecting.
This is why I write all this while absent, so that when present I may not have to be severe, according to the authority the Lord gave me to build up and not to tear down.
Finally, brothers, rejoice, strive for perfection, encourage one another, be of one mind, live in peace, and the God of love and peace will be with you.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the holy ones greet you.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with you all!

titres.titre: There Is No Other Good News

versets.t: Paul, an apostle, sent not by human beings nor through any human being, but by Jesus Christ and God the Father, who raised him from the dead,
and all the brothers who are with me, to the churches of Galatia:
grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,
who gave himself for our sins to rescue us from the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,
to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.
I am astonished that you are so quickly deserting the one who called you by the grace of Christ and turning to a different good news.
There is no other; there are only certain people who are troubling you and want to distort the Good News of Christ.
But even if we ourselves, or an angel from heaven, should proclaim to you a good news other than the one we proclaimed to you, let him be cursed!
As we have said before, so now I say again: if anyone proclaims to you a good news other than the one you received, let him be cursed!
Is it human approval I am now seeking, or God's? Is it people I am trying to please? If I were still trying to please people, I would not be a servant of Christ.
For I want you to know, brothers, that the Good News I proclaimed is not of human origin.
I did not receive it from any human being, nor was I taught it; it came through a revelation of Jesus Christ.
You have heard of my former way of life in Judaism, how savagely I persecuted the church of God and tried to destroy it,
and how I was advancing in Judaism beyond many of my own age among my people, far more zealous as I was for the traditions of my ancestors.
But when God, who had set me apart from my mother's womb and called me through his grace, was pleased
to reveal his Son in me so that I might proclaim him among the nations, at once, without consulting flesh and blood,
without going up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, I went off to Arabia and then returned to Damascus.
Then, three years later, I went up to Jerusalem to get to know Cephas, and I stayed with him for fifteen days.
But I saw none of the other apostles, except James, the Lord's brother.
In what I am writing to you, I assure you before God that I am not lying.
Then I went into the regions of Syria and Cilicia.
But I was personally unknown to the churches of Judea that are in Christ;
they had only heard it said, The man who once persecuted us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy,
and they glorified God because of me.

titres.titre: Paul Acknowledged by the Apostles at Jerusalem
Justified by Faith, Not by the Works of the Law

versets.t: Then, fourteen years later, I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along with me as well.

I went up in response to a revelation, and I set before them the Good News that I proclaim among the nations; I did so privately, before those who were held in the highest regard, for fear that I might be running, or might have run, in vain.
Yet not even Titus, who was with me and was a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised.
This came up because of the false brothers, those intruders who had slipped in among us to spy on the freedom we have in Christ Jesus, in order to reduce us to slavery;
but we did not yield to them for a moment, so that the truth of the Good News might remain with you.
As for those who were held to be something (what they once were makes no difference to me: God shows no partiality), these men of repute added nothing to my message.
On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted with the Good News for the uncircumcised, as Peter had been for the circumcised,
for the one who had worked in Peter for his apostolate to the circumcised had also worked in me for the nations,

and recognizing the grace that had been given to me, James, Cephas, and John, reputed to be pillars, gave Barnabas and me the right hand of fellowship: we would go to the nations, and they to the circumcised.
They asked only that we remember the poor, the very thing I have been eager to do.
But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he was in the wrong.
For before certain people came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles; but when they arrived, he drew back and kept himself apart, out of fear of the circumcision party.
And the rest of the Jews joined him in this pretense, so that even Barnabas was swept along by their hypocrisy.

But when I saw that they were not walking straight according to the truth of the Good News, I said to Cephas in front of them all, "If you, though a Jew, live like the Gentiles and not like the Jews, how can you force the Gentiles to live like Jews?"
We ourselves are Jews by birth and not Gentile sinners;

yet we know that a person is not justified by the works of the Law, but through faith in Jesus Christ. So we too have believed in Christ Jesus, in order to be justified by faith in Christ and not by the works of the Law; for by the works of the Law no one will be justified.
But if, in seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, does that make Christ a servant of sin? Certainly not!
For if I rebuild what I once tore down, I prove myself to be a transgressor.
For through the Law I died to the Law, so that I might live for God. With Christ I have been crucified;
it is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. The life I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
I do not set aside the grace of God; for if righteousness comes through the Law, then Christ died for nothing.

titres.titre: Faith or the Works of the Law
The Faith of Abraham and the Promise
All Sons of God Through Faith

versets.t: You foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you, before whose very eyes Jesus Christ was portrayed as crucified?
There is only one thing I want to learn from you: did you receive the Spirit by the works of the Law, or by hearing with faith?
Are you so foolish? Having begun with the Spirit, are you now going to end with the flesh?
Did you go through so much for nothing, if it really was for nothing?
Does the one who gives you the Spirit and works miracles among you do so by the works of the Law, or by your hearing with faith?
So it was with Abraham: he believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.
Understand, then, that those who have faith are the true sons of Abraham.
And Scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the nations by faith, announced the Good News to Abraham in advance: In you all the nations will be blessed.
So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
For all who rely on the works of the Law are under a curse, since it is written: Cursed be everyone who does not hold fast to everything written in the book of the Law, and do it.
And it is clear that no one is justified before God by the Law, for the righteous will live by faith.
But the Law does not rest on faith; on the contrary, whoever practices these precepts will live by them.
Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law by becoming a curse for us, for it is written: Cursed be everyone who hangs on a tree,
so that in Christ Jesus the blessing of Abraham might come to the nations, and so that through faith we might receive the promised Spirit.
Brothers, I am speaking in human terms: no one annuls or adds to a will that has been properly ratified, even a human one.
Now the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his offspring. Scripture does not say, "and to his offsprings," as though speaking of many, but of one: and to your offspring, that is, Christ.
What I mean is this: a will previously ratified by God is not annulled by the Law, which came four hundred and thirty years later, so as to nullify the promise.
For if the inheritance comes from the Law, it no longer comes from the promise; but it was through a promise that God graciously gave it to Abraham.
Why then the Law? It was added because of transgressions, until the offspring should come to whom the promise had been made; it was put into effect through angels, by the hand of a mediator.
Now a mediator is not for one party alone; but God is one.
Is the Law then opposed to the promises of God? Certainly not! For if a law had been given that could impart life, then righteousness would indeed come from the Law.
But Scripture has imprisoned everything under sin, so that the promise, through faith in Jesus Christ, might be given to those who believe.
Before faith came, we were held in custody under the Law, imprisoned until the faith that was to come would be revealed.
So the Law was our guardian until Christ came, so that we might be justified by faith.
But now that faith has come, we are no longer under this guardian.
For you are all sons of God through faith, in Christ Jesus.
For all of you who were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
There is no longer Jew or Greek, there is no longer slave or free, there is no longer male and female: for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
And if you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise.

titres.titre: The Two Covenants: Hagar and Sarah

versets.t: What I am saying is this: as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, even though he is the owner of everything;
he is under guardians and stewards until the date set by the father.
So it was with us too: while we were children, we were enslaved to the elemental forces of the world.
But when the fullness of time came, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the Law,
to redeem those who were under the Law, so that we might receive adoption as sons.
And because you are sons, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying out, "Abba! Father!"
So you are no longer a slave, but a son; and if a son, then also an heir, through the grace of God.
In the past, it is true, when you did not know God, you were enslaved to beings that by nature are not gods.
But now that you know God, or rather are known by God, how can you turn back to those weak and worthless elemental forces? Do you want to be enslaved to them all over again?
You are observing special days and months and seasons and years!
I am afraid that I may have labored over you for nothing.
Become like me, since I too have become like you, brothers, I beg you. You have done me no wrong.
You know that it was because of a bodily weakness that I first proclaimed the Good News to you,
and though my condition was a trial to you, you did not treat me with contempt or scorn; instead, you welcomed me as an angel of God, as Christ Jesus.
Where, then, is the happiness you felt back then? For I testify to you that, had it been possible, you would have torn out your own eyes and given them to me.
Have I now become your enemy by telling you the truth?
These people are zealous to win you over, but not for a good purpose; they want to cut you off from me, so that you will be zealous for them.
It is a fine thing to be the object of zeal in a good cause at all times, and not only when I am present with you.
My children, for whom I am again enduring the pains of childbirth until Christ is formed in you,
I wish I could be with you right now and change my tone, for I am at a loss about you.
Tell me, you who want to be under the Law, do you not listen to the Law?
For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by the slave woman and the other by the free woman.
But the son of the slave woman was born according to the flesh, while the son of the free woman was born by virtue of the promise.
There is an allegory here: these women are two covenants. One, from Mount Sinai, bearing children for slavery, is Hagar.
Now Sinai is a mountain in Arabia, and Hagar corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is in slavery with her children.
But the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother;

for it is written: Rejoice, barren one who bears no children, break into shouts of joy, you who have never known the pains of labor, for the children of the deserted woman are more numerous than those of her who has a husband.
Now you, brothers, like Isaac, are children of the promise.
But just as then the one born according to the flesh persecuted the one born according to the Spirit, so it is now.
But what does Scripture say? Drive out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman will not share the inheritance with the son of the free woman.
So then, brothers, we are not children of the slave woman, but of the free woman.

titres.titre: The Works of the Flesh and the Fruit of the Spirit

versets.t: It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not let yourselves be put back under the yoke of slavery.
Look, it is I, Paul, who tell you: if you get yourselves circumcised, Christ will be of no benefit to you.
Once again I declare to everyone who gets circumcised that he is bound to keep the whole Law.
You who seek righteousness by the Law are cut off from Christ; you have fallen away from grace.
For it is by the Spirit, on the basis of faith, that we eagerly await the righteousness we hope for.
For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but only faith working through love.
You were running well: who cut in on you to keep you from obeying the truth?
That kind of persuasion does not come from the one who calls you.
A little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough.
I am confident about you in the Lord that you will take no other view; but whoever is troubling you will bear the condemnation, whoever he may be.
As for me, brothers, if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? In that case the scandal of the cross would have been done away with!
As for those who are throwing you into turmoil, I wish they would go all the way and castrate themselves!
You, brothers, were called to freedom. Only, do not let this freedom become a pretext for the flesh; rather, through love, serve one another.
For the whole Law is fulfilled in a single command: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
But if you bite and devour one another, watch out that you are not destroyed by one another.
This is what I say: walk by the Spirit, and you will not carry out the desire of the flesh.
For the flesh desires against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh; they are opposed to each other, so that you do not do what you would like.
But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the Law.
Now the works of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity, debauchery,
idolatry, sorcery, hostilities, strife, jealousy, outbursts of anger, rivalries, dissensions, factions,
envy, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these. I warn you, as I warned you before: those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness,
gentleness, self-control. Against such things there is no law.
Those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit.
Let us not seek empty glory, provoking one another, envying one another.

titres.titre: What Truly Matters: A New Creation

versets.t: Brothers, if someone is caught in some sin, you who are spiritual should restore him in a spirit of gentleness; and watch yourself, so that you too are not tempted.
Bear one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
For if anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself.
Let each one examine his own work, and then he will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not by comparison with someone else;
for each will carry his own load.
The one who is taught the Word should share all good things with the one who teaches him.
Do not be deceived: God is not mocked. Whatever a person sows, that he will also reap.
Whoever sows in his flesh will reap corruption from the flesh; whoever sows in the Spirit will reap eternal life from the Spirit.
Let us not grow weary of doing good; for at the proper time we will reap, if we do not give up.
So then, as long as we have the opportunity, let us do good to all, and above all to our brothers in the faith.
See what large letters I am using as I write to you with my own hand.
Those who want to make a good impression in the flesh are the ones trying to compel you to be circumcised, and only so that they will not be persecuted for the cross of Christ.
For even those who get circumcised do not keep the Law themselves; but they want you to be circumcised so that they may boast in your flesh.
As for me, may I never boast in anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world.
For what counts is neither circumcision nor uncircumcision, but the new creation.
And upon all who follow this rule, peace and mercy, and upon the Israel of God.
From now on, let no one cause me trouble, for I bear on my body the marks of Jesus.
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen.

titres.titre: The blessing: the plan of God

versets.t: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, to the holy ones who are at Ephesus, to the faithful in Christ Jesus:
grace to you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ.
Blessed be God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! In Christ he has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavens.
In him he chose us before the foundation of the world, to be holy and blameless before him, in love.
He destined us to become his adopted sons through Jesus Christ; such was the good pleasure of his will,
to the praise of the glory of his grace, which he has lavished on us in the Beloved.
In him, through his blood, we have redemption, the forgiveness of our sins, according to the riches of his grace
that he poured out on us in abundance, with all wisdom and understanding.
He made known to us the mystery of his will, the plan of his good pleasure that he had formed beforehand in Christ,
to bring it to fulfillment when the times had run their course: to unite all things under one head, Christ, the things of heaven and the things of the earth.
In him we too have received our share of the inheritance, we who were destined for this according to the plan of the one who accomplishes all things after the decision of his will,
so that we might live for the praise of his glory, we who were the first to hope in Christ.
In him you too, when you had heard the word of truth, the Good News of your salvation, and had believed in him, were marked with the seal of the promised Holy Spirit.
This Spirit is the pledge of our inheritance, until the full deliverance of the people God has made his own, to the praise of his glory.
That is why I too, having heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the holy ones,
do not cease to give thanks for you, remembering you in my prayers.
May the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, give you a spirit of wisdom to reveal him to you and to make him truly known to you.
May he enlighten the eyes of your heart, so that you may know what hope his call opens up, what are the riches and the glory of the inheritance he holds in store for the holy ones,
and how surpassing is the greatness of his power toward us who believe, measured by the working of the might and strength
that he displayed in Christ when he raised him from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavens,
far above every authority, every power, every dominion, every sovereignty, and every name that can be named, not only in this present age but also in the age to come.
He put all things under his feet, and gave him, above all things, as head to the Church,
which is his body, the fullness of the one who fills all things in every way.

titres.titre: From death to life by grace
The two peoples reconciled in Christ

versets.t: And you were dead, because of your offenses and your sins.
This is how you lived in the past, following the ways of this world, following the ruler of the realm of the air, that spirit who is now at work in those who are rebellious.
All of us too once lived like this, driven by the cravings of our flesh, doing the will of the flesh and of our thoughts; and by nature we were exposed to the wrath of God, like everyone else.
But God is rich in mercy; because of the great love with which he loved us,
when we were dead because of our offenses, he brought us back to life with Christ. It is by grace that you have been saved.
With him he raised us up and seated us in the heavens, in Christ Jesus,
to show to the ages to come the boundless riches of his grace, in the kindness he shows us in Christ Jesus.
For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God.
It does not come from works, so that no one may boast.
For we are his handiwork, created in Christ Jesus for the good works that God prepared beforehand for us to do.
Remember, then, that in the past you, the Gentiles in the flesh, called the uncircumcised by those who call themselves circumcised, with a circumcision made in the flesh by human hands,
remember that at that time you were without Christ, excluded from the community of Israel, strangers to the covenants and to the promise, without hope and without God in the world.
But now, in Christ Jesus, you who were once far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ.
For he himself is our peace, he who made the two peoples one, tearing down the wall that separated them, the hostility.
In his flesh he put an end to the Law with its commandments and their regulations, to create in himself, out of the two, one new man, thus making peace,
and to reconcile them both with God in one single body, through the cross: on it he put the hostility to death.
He came to proclaim peace to you who were far off, and peace to those who were near.
For through him we both have access to the Father, in one Spirit.
So you are no longer strangers or passing guests; you are fellow citizens of the holy ones, you belong to the household of God.
You have been built on the foundations laid by the apostles and the prophets, and Christ Jesus himself is the cornerstone.
In him the whole structure is fitted together and rises to form a holy temple in the Lord.
In him you too are being built into this structure to become, through the Spirit, the dwelling place of God.

titres.titre: Prayer to know the love of Christ

versets.t: That is why I, Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus for you, the Gentiles...
You have surely heard how God entrusted to me the grace of this charge for your benefit:
it was by revelation that he made known to me the mystery, as I have just written in a few words.
As you read this, you can grasp the insight I have into the mystery of Christ.
This mystery had not been revealed to people of past generations as it is now: the Spirit has disclosed it to his holy apostles and prophets.
This mystery is that the Gentiles now share the same inheritance, form one same body, and share in the same promise, in Christ Jesus, through the Good News.
Of this Good News I have become a servant by the gift of the grace that God granted me with the working of his power.
To me, the least of all the holy ones, this grace was given: to proclaim to the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ,
and to bring to full light how the mystery is fulfilled, the mystery hidden for all ages in God, the creator of all things.
So now, through the Church, the authorities and powers in the heavens come to know the wisdom of God in its infinite variety.
Such is the eternal plan that God has accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord.
In him, through faith in him, we have the freedom to approach God with confidence.
So I ask you not to lose heart over the trials I endure for you: they are your glory.
That is why I bend my knees before the Father,
from whom every family, in heaven and on earth, takes its name.
May he grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be powerfully strengthened by his Spirit in your inner being;
may Christ dwell in your hearts through faith; and may you, rooted and grounded in love,
be able to grasp, with all the holy ones, what is the breadth and length and height and depth,
and to know the love of Christ that surpasses all knowledge, so that you may be filled with the whole fullness of God.
To the one who can, by his power at work in us, do infinitely more than all we ask or imagine,
to him be glory in the Church and in Christ Jesus, through all generations, forever and ever! Amen.

titres.titre: Gifts to build up the body
The old self and the new self

versets.t: So I urge you, I who am a prisoner in the Lord: lead a life worthy of the call you have received,
with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
striving to keep the unity that the Spirit gives, through the bond of peace.
There is one body and one Spirit, just as one hope was given to you by your call.
There is one Lord, one faith, one baptism,
one God and Father of all, who reigns above all, works through all, and dwells in all.
But to each one of us grace has been given according to the measure of Christ's gift.
That is why Scripture says: "He ascended on high, he led captives away, he gave gifts to men."
Now what does "he ascended" mean, except that he had first descended into the depths of the earth?
The one who descended is the very one who ascended above all the heavens, to fill all things.
It is he who gave some to be apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, some pastors and teachers,
to equip the holy ones for the work of ministry, to build up the body of Christ,
until we all together reach unity in the faith and in the knowledge of the Son of God, and become mature, attaining the full stature of Christ.
Then we will no longer be children, tossed about and carried away by every wind of doctrine, taken in by the cunning of men and their skill in leading others astray.
Professing the truth in love, we will grow in every way toward the one who is the head, Christ.
From him the whole body receives its fitting together and cohesion, through the working of every joint: when each member does its part, the body grows and builds itself up in love.
So this is what I say and testify in the Lord: do not live any longer like the Gentiles, whose thinking leads to nothing.
Their understanding is darkened, they are strangers to the life of God, because of the ignorance within them and the hardness of their hearts.
Having lost all moral sense, they have given themselves over to debauchery, greedy to commit every kind of impurity.
But that is not how you learned to know Christ,
if indeed you really listened to him and were taught, according to the truth that is in Jesus,
to strip off the old self that belongs to your former way of life, that old self corrupted by deceitful desires,
to be renewed by an inner transformation of your thinking,
and to put on the new self, created according to God in the righteousness and holiness that come from the truth.
So renounce falsehood: let each one speak the truth to his neighbor, for we are members of one another.
"If you become angry, do not sin": do not let the sun go down on your anger,
and give no foothold to the devil.
Let the thief steal no longer; rather, let him work honestly with his hands, so that he may have something to share with those in need.
Let no evil word come out of your mouth, but only good words, able to build up when needed and to do good to those who hear them.
Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God: it is by him that you have been marked with a seal for the day of redemption.
Banish from among you all bitterness, all irritation, all anger, all shouting, all insults, and every form of malice.
Be kind to one another, full of tenderness; forgive one another, as God has forgiven you in Christ.

titres.titre: Marriage, image of Christ and the Church

versets.t: So be imitators of God, since you are his beloved children;
live in love, after the example of Christ who loved us and gave himself up for us, as an offering and sacrifice whose fragrance is pleasing to God.
Debauchery, impurity of every kind, greed: let these not even be mentioned among you, as befits the holy ones.
No coarse talk, foolishness, or off-color jokes, for these are out of place; instead, let there be thanksgiving.
Be sure of this: no one who is debauched, impure, or greedy, which is to be an idolater, has any share in the inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.
Let no one deceive you with empty words: it is for all this that the wrath of God comes upon those who are rebellious.
So have nothing in common with them.
Once you were darkness; now, in the Lord, you are light. Live as children of light,
for the fruit of the light is all that is good and righteous and true.
Discern what is pleasing to the Lord;
take no part in the fruitless works of darkness, but rather expose them.
For what these people do in secret is shameful even to speak of;
but everything that is exposed the light brings into full clarity,
and everything that becomes clear is light. That is why it is said: "Awake, you who sleep, rise from among the dead, and Christ will shine on you."
So watch carefully over how you live: do not live as fools, but as wise people,
making the most of the present time, for the days are evil.
So do not be thoughtless, but understand what the will of the Lord is.
Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to debauchery; instead, let yourselves be filled with the Spirit.
Recite together psalms, hymns, and inspired songs; sing to the Lord and praise him with all your heart;
at all times and for everything, give thanks to God the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Submit to one another out of reverence for Christ.
Let wives submit to their husbands as to the Lord,
for the husband is the head of the wife, as Christ is the head of the Church, he, the Savior of his body.
Now as the Church submits to Christ, so let wives submit in everything to their husbands.
Husbands, love your wives as Christ loved the Church: he gave himself up for her,
to sanctify her by cleansing her with the bath of water accompanied by the word,
to present her to himself in splendor, without stain or wrinkle or anything of the kind, but holy and blameless.
In the same way, husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies. To love one's wife is to love oneself.
No one has ever hated his own body; rather, he feeds it and cares for it, as Christ does for the Church,
because we are the members of his body.
"For this reason a man will leave his father and his mother to be joined to his wife, and the two will become one."
This mystery is great: I say it with Christ and the Church in mind.
In any case, let each one of you love his wife as himself, and let the wife respect her husband.
Children, obey your parents in the Lord, for this is right.
"Honor your father and your mother": this is the first commandment to which a promise is attached,
"so that you may be happy and live long on the earth."
And you, fathers, do not exasperate your children; rather, raise them by correcting them and instructing them according to the Lord.
Servants, obey your earthly masters with respect and reverence, with a sincere heart, as you would obey Christ,
not merely with an outward show of service to please men, but as servants of Christ who do the will of God wholeheartedly.
Serve willingly, as though you were serving the Lord and not men,
knowing that each one, whether slave or free, will receive from the Lord the reward for the good he has done.
And you, masters, act in the same way toward them; give up your threats, knowing that their Master and yours is in the heavens, and that he shows no partiality.
Finally, draw your strength from the Lord and from his almighty power.
Put on the whole armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the schemes of the devil.

For it is not against opponents of flesh and blood that we struggle, but against the authorities, against the powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the spirits of evil that haunt the heavenly regions.
So take up the whole armor of God, so that you may be able to resist on the evil day and to stand firm after you have overcome everything.
So stand firm: have truth as the belt around your waist, put on the breastplate of righteousness,
and for shoes, the readiness to proclaim the Good News of peace.
In every situation, take up the shield of faith: with it you will be able to quench all the flaming arrows of the Evil One.
Take also the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God.
At all times, pray in the Spirit with all kinds of prayers and supplications; to this end, keep watch with constant perseverance, and intercede for all the holy ones,
and for me as well, so that the word may be given to me when I open my mouth, to make known with boldness the mystery of the Good News,
of which I am an ambassador in chains. Pray that I may proclaim it with the boldness that is fitting for me.
Do you want to know how I am and what I am doing? Tychicus, that beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord, will tell you everything.
I am sending him to you for this very purpose, so that you may have news of us and that he may comfort your hearts.
May peace be given to the brothers, along with love and faith, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
May grace be with all who love our Lord Jesus Christ with an undying love.

titres.titre: For Me, to Live Is Christ

versets.t: Paul and Timothy, servants of Christ Jesus, to all the holy ones in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi, together with the overseers and the deacons:
grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I give thanks to my God every time I remember you,
always praying with joy for all of you in every one of my prayers,
because of the share you have taken in the Good News, from the first day until now.
I am confident of this: the one who began a good work in you will carry it through to completion until the day of Christ Jesus.

It is only right that I should feel this way about all of you, for I hold you in my heart, you who, both in my chains and in the defense and confirmation of the Good News, all share the same grace with me.
Yes, God is my witness that I cherish you all with the tenderness of Christ Jesus.
And this is my prayer: that your love may grow ever richer, more and more, in full knowledge and in all discernment,
so that you may discern what is best and be pure and blameless for the day of Christ,
filled with the fruit of righteousness that comes through Jesus Christ, for the glory and praise of God.
I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has actually served to advance the Good News.
Indeed, it has become clear throughout the whole praetorium and to everyone else that I am in chains for Christ,
and most of the brothers, emboldened in the Lord by my chains, dare all the more to proclaim the Word fearlessly.
Some, it is true, proclaim Christ out of envy and rivalry, but others do so with good intentions.
These act out of love, knowing that I am here to defend the Good News;
the others proclaim Christ in a spirit of contention, with impure motives, thinking to add hardship to my chains.
What does it matter? Either way, whether with hidden motives or in truth, Christ is proclaimed, and in that I rejoice. Yes, and I will go on rejoicing,
for I know that this will turn out for my salvation, through your prayer and the help of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,

according to my eager expectation and my hope: that I shall in no way be put to shame, but rather that with all boldness, now as always, Christ will be glorified in my body, whether by my life or by my death.
For to me, to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
But if living on in the flesh means fruitful labor for me, then I do not know which to choose.
I am torn between the two: I have the desire to depart and be with Christ, which is by far the better;
but to remain in the flesh is more necessary for your sake.
And of this I am convinced: I know that I will remain, that I will stay on with all of you, for your progress and your joy in the faith,
so that, when I come back to you, your pride may overflow in Christ Jesus on my account.

Only, live a life worthy of the Good News of Christ, so that, whether I come and see you or remain absent, I may hear about you that you are standing firm in one spirit, striving side by side with one heart for the faith of the Good News,
not intimidated in any way by your opponents. This is for them a sign of their ruin, but for you a sign of your salvation, and this comes from God.
For it has been granted to you, on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in him but also to suffer for him,
waging the same struggle that you saw me wage and now hear that I am still waging.

titres.titre: Humility After the Example of Christ
Shining Like Stars in the World

versets.t: If, then, there is any encouragement in Christ, any comfort in love, any communion in the Spirit, any warmth of tenderness and compassion,
make my joy complete: be of one mind, one love, one soul, one purpose.
Do nothing out of rivalry or vain conceit, but let each one, in humility, regard the others as better than himself.
Let each of you look not to your own interests, but also to those of others.
Have among yourselves the same mind that was in Christ Jesus:
who, being in the form of God, did not count equality with God as a prize to be seized,
but emptied himself, taking the form of a slave, becoming like men; and, recognized in his appearance as a man,
he humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even death on a cross.
Therefore God has raised him on high and given him the Name that is above every name,
so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend, in heaven, on earth, and under the earth,
and every tongue proclaim: 'Jesus Christ is Lord', to the glory of God the Father.
So then, my beloved, you who have always obeyed: work out your salvation with fear and trembling, not only when I am present, but all the more now that I am absent;
for it is God who works in you both the willing and the doing, according to his gracious purpose.
Do everything without grumbling or arguing,
so that you may be blameless and without deceit, children of God beyond reproach in the midst of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you shine like stars in the world,
holding firm to the word of life. Then, on the day of Christ, I will have reason to boast that I did not run in vain or labor in vain.
And even if my blood is to be poured out as a libation over the sacrifice and offering of your faith, I am glad and I rejoice with all of you;
in the same way, you too, be glad and rejoice with me.
I hope, in the Lord Jesus, to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be encouraged by news of you.
For I have no one so united to me in mind, who cares so sincerely for you;
they all, in fact, seek their own interests, and not those of Jesus Christ.
But you know how he has proved himself: like a son with his father, he has served with me for the Good News.
He, then, is the one I hope to send to you, as soon as I see clearly how things stand with me;
and I am confident, in the Lord, that I myself will come soon.
Still, I have judged it necessary to send back to you Epaphroditus, my brother, my fellow worker and fellow soldier, whom you sent to attend to my needs;
for he was longing for all of you, and was distressed because you had heard that he was ill.
Indeed, he was ill, close to death; but God had mercy on him, and not on him only, but also on me, to spare me sorrow upon sorrow.
So I am all the more eager to send him back, so that seeing him again may bring you joy, and I myself may be less sorrowful.
Welcome him in the Lord with all joy, and hold such men in honor;
for it was for the work of Christ that he came close to death, risking his life to render me the service that you could not render me yourselves.
Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is no burden to me, and for you it is a safeguard.
Beware of the dogs, beware of the evil workers, beware of the false circumcision!
For it is we who are the true circumcision, we who worship by the Spirit of God, who take our pride in Christ Jesus, and put no confidence in the flesh.
Yet I too could have confidence in the flesh. If anyone else thinks he can be confident in the flesh, I have more:
circumcised on the eighth day, of the race of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew born of Hebrews; as to the Law, a Pharisee;
as to zeal, a persecutor of the Church; as to the righteousness of the Law, blameless.
But these gains I have counted as loss for the sake of Christ.
Indeed, I now count everything as loss because of the surpassing good of knowing Christ Jesus, my Lord. For his sake I have lost everything, and I regard it all as refuse, in order to gain Christ
and be found in him, having not a righteousness of my own, the one that comes from the Law, but the one that comes through faith in Christ, the righteousness that comes from God and rests on faith;
so as to know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the sharing in his sufferings, becoming conformed to his death,
in order to attain, if I can, the resurrection from the dead.
Not that I have already won the prize, or already reached perfection; but I press on in my course, trying to lay hold of it, since I too have been laid hold of by Christ Jesus.
Brothers, I do not consider that I have yet laid hold of it. But this one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining toward what lies ahead,
I run toward the goal, for the prize to which God calls me on high in Christ Jesus.
Let all of us, then, who are mature, be of this mind; and if on some point you think otherwise, that too God will make clear to you.
Only, from the point we have reached, let us go forward along the same line.
Brothers, join together in imitating me, and look to those who conduct themselves according to the model you have in us.
For there are many, as I have often told you and now tell you again with tears, who conduct themselves as enemies of the cross of Christ.
Their end is destruction; their god is their belly; their glory is in their shame; they have taste only for the things of the earth.
But our citizenship is in heaven, and from there we await as Savior the Lord Jesus Christ,
who will transform our lowly body to make it conformed to his body of glory, by the power that enables him to subject all things to himself.

titres.titre: Exhortations and the Peace of God
Gratitude for the Gifts of the Philippians

versets.t: So then, my beloved brothers whom I long to see again, my joy and my crown, stand firm in the Lord, my beloved.
I urge Euodia and I urge Syntyche to be of the same mind in the Lord.
Yes, I ask you too, my true companion: help them, for they have struggled at my side for the Good News, together with Clement and my other coworkers, whose names are in the book of life.
Rejoice in the Lord always; I say it again, rejoice.
Let your gentleness be known to everyone. The Lord is near.
Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything, by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, make your requests known to God.
And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.

Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is noble, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever brings good repute, if there is any virtue and anything worthy of praise, these are the things to fill your thoughts.
What you have learned and received, heard and seen in me, put it into practice, and the God of peace will be with you.
I rejoiced greatly in the Lord to see your concern for me flower again at last; you were indeed thinking of me, but the opportunity was lacking.
It is not out of need that I speak, for I have learned to be content with what I have.

I know how to live in want, and I know how to live in plenty. In every circumstance and in all things I have learned the secret of being well fed and of going hungry, of having plenty and of being in need.
I can do all things in the one who gives me strength.
Still, you did well to share in my distress.
You yourselves know, Philippians, that in the early days of the Good News, when I left Macedonia, no Church shared with me in an account of giving and receiving except you alone.
Even at Thessalonica, and more than once, you sent me what I needed.
It is not the gift that I seek; what I seek is the fruit that increases to your account.
I have received everything, and more than enough; I am fully supplied, having received from Epaphroditus what came from you, a fragrant offering, a sacrifice that God welcomes and that pleases him.
And my God will supply all your needs according to his riches, in glory, in Christ Jesus.
To our God and Father be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
Greet every one of the holy ones in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me greet you.
All the holy ones greet you, especially those of Caesar's household.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother,
to the holy ones at Colossae, faithful brothers in Christ: grace to you and peace from God our Father.
We give thanks to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, praying for you without ceasing,
since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of the love you have for all the holy ones,
because of the hope laid up for you in heaven, the hope of which you heard in the word of truth, the Good News
that has reached you. In all the world it is bearing fruit and growing, as it does among you from the day you heard and truly knew the grace of God,
according to the teaching of Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, a faithful minister of Christ on your behalf,
who has made known to us your love in the Spirit.
For this reason we too, from the day we heard of it, have not ceased praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the full knowledge of his will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding,
so as to live a life worthy of the Lord and please him in every way, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God,
strengthened in every way by his glorious power, to endure everything with patience. With joy,
give thanks to the Father, who has made you able to share in the inheritance of the holy ones in the light.
He has rescued us from the power of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of his beloved Son,
in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins.
He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation,
for in him all things were created, in heaven and on earth, the visible and the invisible: Thrones, Dominions, Principalities, Powers. All things were created through him and for him.
He is before all things, and in him all things hold together.
He is the head of the body, which is the Church; he is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that in everything he might have the primacy.
For God was pleased to have all fullness dwell in him,
and through him to reconcile all things to himself, on earth and in heaven, making peace by the blood of his cross.
And you who were once strangers and enemies, in your thoughts and your evil deeds,
he has now reconciled in the fleshly body of his Son, through his death, to present you before him holy, without blemish and without reproach,

provided that you remain grounded and firm in the faith, without turning away from the hope of the Good News that you heard, the one proclaimed to every creature under heaven and of which I, Paul, have become the minister.
Now I find my joy in the sufferings I endure for you, and what is lacking in the afflictions of Christ I complete in my flesh for his body, which is the Church.
Of this Church I have become the minister, according to the charge God entrusted to me for you: to bring the word of God to its full accomplishment,
the mystery hidden for ages and generations, but now revealed to his holy ones.
To them God has willed to make known the riches of glory of this mystery among the nations: Christ in you, the hope of glory.
He is the one we proclaim, warning everyone and teaching everyone in all wisdom, so as to present everyone perfect in Christ.
For this I labor and struggle, with his strength that works powerfully in me.

titres.titre: Paul's Struggle for the True Knowledge

versets.t: For I want you to know what a struggle I am waging for you, for those at Laodicea, and for all who have never seen me in person,
so that their hearts may be encouraged and that, united in love, they may reach all the riches of full understanding, the knowledge of the mystery of God: Christ,
in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
I say this so that no one may lead you astray with persuasive arguments.
For even though I am absent in body, I am with you in spirit, glad to see your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
So then, just as you received Christ Jesus, the Lord, walk in him,
rooted and built up in him, established in the faith just as you were taught, overflowing with thanksgiving.
See to it that no one makes you his prey through philosophy, that empty deceit based on human tradition, on the elements of the world, and not on Christ.
For in him dwells bodily all the fullness of the divinity,
and in him you find your own fullness, he who is the head of every principality and power.
In him you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made by human hands, by the stripping away of the body of flesh, the circumcision of Christ.
Buried with him in baptism, in it you were also raised with him through faith in the power of God, who raised him from the dead.
You who were dead through your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, he brought to life with him, forgiving us all our trespasses.
He wiped out the record that stood against us, with its decrees that accused us; he removed it by nailing it to the cross.
He stripped the Principalities and the Powers, made a public spectacle of them, dragging them in his triumphal procession by the cross.
So let no one pass judgment on you about food and drink, or in matters of a feast, a new moon, or a sabbath:
all this was only a shadow of the realities to come; the reality is the body of Christ.
Let no one rob you of your prize by delighting in false humility and the worship of angels, dwelling on his visions, puffed up with empty pride by his fleshly mind,
and not holding fast to the head, the one through whom the whole body, nourished and held together by its joints and ligaments, grows with the growth that God gives.
If you died with Christ to the elements of the world, why, as if you were still living in the world, do you submit to these rules:
'Do not take! Do not taste! Do not touch!'?
All these things are meant to perish with use. They are nothing but human precepts and teachings.

These rules may have an appearance of wisdom, with their scrupulous devotion, their false humility, and their harshness toward the body, but they are of no value whatever and serve only to gratify the flesh.

titres.titre: Seek the Things That Are Above
The Old Self and the New Self

versets.t: If, then, you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.
Set your minds on the things above, not on the things of the earth,
for you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
When Christ, your life, appears, then you too will appear with him in glory.
So put to death whatever in you belongs to the earth: sexual immorality, impurity, passions, evil desires, and greed, which is idolatry.
These are the things that bring the wrath of God upon the rebellious.
You too once lived this way, when you were living in them.
But now, you too, put away all these things: anger, rage, malice, slander, and foul talk from your mouth.
Do not lie to one another any longer, for you have stripped off the old self with its deeds,
and have put on the new self, which is being renewed unceasingly for the knowledge of God, after the image of its Creator.
Here there is no longer Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free; but Christ is all, and in all.
So then, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved, clothe yourselves with tender compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience,
bearing with one another, and forgiving one another if one has a grievance against another. As the Lord forgave you, so you also must do.
And above all these, clothe yourselves with love, which is the bond of perfection.
Let the peace of Christ reign in your hearts, that peace to which you were called so as to form one body. And be thankful.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you in all its richness; teach and admonish one another in all wisdom; with psalms, hymns, and songs inspired by the Spirit, sing to God in your hearts with gratitude.
And whatever you do, in word or in deed, do it in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks through him to God the Father.
Wives, be subject to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives, and do not be harsh with them.
Children, obey your parents in everything, for this pleases the Lord.
Fathers, do not exasperate your children, lest they lose heart.
Servants, obey your earthly masters in everything, not to be seen, as though seeking to please men, but with a sincere heart, in the fear of the Lord.
Whatever you do, do it wholeheartedly, as for the Lord and not for men,
knowing that from the Lord you will receive the inheritance as your reward. It is the Lord, the Christ, whom you serve.
For whoever does wrong will be repaid for the wrong he has done, and there is no favoritism.
Masters, grant your servants what is just and fair, knowing that you too have a Master in heaven.
Persevere in prayer; let it keep you watchful, in thanksgiving.
Pray at the same time for us, that God may open a door for our word, to proclaim the mystery of Christ, for which I am in chains;
that I may make it known as I ought to speak of it.
Conduct yourselves wisely toward those outside, making the most of the time.
Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you know how to answer each person as you should.
As for all that concerns me, Tychicus will inform you, he the beloved brother, faithful minister and fellow servant in the Lord.
I am sending him to you for this very purpose, so that you may have news of us and that he may encourage your hearts,
together with Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you all that is happening here.
Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, as does Mark, the cousin of Barnabas, about whom you have received instructions: if he comes to you, welcome him.
Jesus, called Justus, also greets you. Among the circumcised, these are the only ones who work with me for the kingdom of God; they have been a comfort to me.
Epaphras, one of you, greets you; a servant of Christ Jesus, he never ceases to struggle for you in his prayers, that you may stand firm, perfect and fully devoted to all the will of God.
I bear him witness that he works hard for you, for those at Laodicea, and for those at Hierapolis.
Luke, the beloved physician, greets you, as does Demas.
Greet the brothers at Laodicea, as well as Nympha and the Church that meets in her house.
And when this letter has been read among you, see that it is also read in the Church of the Laodiceans, and you yourselves read the one that will come from Laodicea.
Say to Archippus: 'See to the ministry you received in the Lord, that you fulfill it well.'
The greeting is in my own hand, mine, Paul's. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the Church of the Thessalonians which is in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ: grace and peace to you.
We give thanks to God for you all, without ceasing, remembering you in our prayers.
Before God our Father, we recall without pause the work of your faith, the labor of your love, and the steadfastness of your hope in our Lord Jesus Christ.
We know it, brothers loved by God: you have been chosen.
For our proclamation of the Good News did not reach you in word only, but with power, with the Holy Spirit, and with full conviction. You know, moreover, how we acted among you, for your good.
And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, welcoming the word amid great distress, with the joy that the Holy Spirit gives.
So you became a model for all the believers of Macedonia and Achaia.
From you the word of the Lord has rung out, and not only in Macedonia and Achaia: everywhere your faith in God has become known, so that we have nothing to say about it.
For everyone tells of the welcome we received among you, and how you turned to God, abandoning idols to serve the living and true God,
and to await from heaven his Son, whom he raised from the dead, Jesus, who delivers us from the wrath that is coming.

titres.titre: The welcome of the word and the persecutions
Paul's longing to see them again

versets.t: You yourselves know, brothers, that our coming to you was not in vain.
We had just suffered and been humiliated at Philippi, as you know; yet, with the boldness that God gives, we dared to proclaim to you his Good News amid a hard struggle.
Our preaching does not come from error, nor from impure motives, nor from deceit.
God judged us worthy to entrust us with the Good News, and we speak to please him, the one who searches our hearts, not to please men.
Never, as you know, did we resort to flattery, nor seek any hidden profit, God is our witness.
Nor did we seek the glory that comes from men, either from you or from anyone else.
As apostles of Christ, we could have made our weight felt; yet we were full of gentleness among you, like a mother nursing her little children and surrounding them with care.
In our tenderness for you, we would have wished to give you not only the Good News of God, but our very lives, so dear had you become to us.
You remember, brothers, our labor and our toil: it was by working night and day, so as not to be a burden to any of you, that we proclaimed to you the Good News of God.
You are witnesses, and God as well, how holy, upright, and blameless our conduct was toward you who believe.
You know it: we were for each one of you like a father for his children,
exhorting you, encouraging you, pleading with you to lead a life worthy of God, who calls you to his kingdom and his glory.

And this is why we too give thanks to God without ceasing: when you received the word of God that we made you hear, you welcomed it not as a word of men, but as what it truly is, the word of God, which is at work in you who believe.
For you became, brothers, imitators of the Churches of God that are in Judea, in Christ Jesus: you suffered from your own countrymen what they suffered from the Jews,
those who put the Lord Jesus and the prophets to death, and who persecuted us. They do not please God and are opposed to all men,
hindering us from proclaiming salvation to the Gentiles. Thus they constantly fill up the measure of their sins; but wrath has come upon them, to the very end.
And we, brothers, separated from you for a while, in body but not in heart, longed all the more keenly to see your face again.
We wanted to come to you, I, Paul, once, twice; but Satan hindered us.
For what is our hope, our joy, our crown of glory, if not you, before our Lord Jesus, at his coming?
Yes, you are our glory and our joy.
That is why, unable to bear it any longer, we agreed to be left alone at Athens,
