and we sent you Timothy, our brother, God's fellow worker in proclaiming the Good News of Christ, to strengthen you and encourage you in your faith,
so that no one would be shaken by these trials. You know it well: this is our lot.
Already, when we were with you, we warned you that we would have to undergo trials; and that is what has happened, as you know.
That is why, unable to bear it any longer, I sent to find out about your faith, fearing that the tempter had tested you and that our toil had become useless.

But Timothy has just returned to us from you, and he has brought us the good news of your faith and your love; he has told us of the fond memory you always keep of us and your desire to see us again, just as we ourselves long to see you.
And so, brothers, amid all our distress and our trials, your faith has been a comfort to us concerning you.
For we live again, now that you are standing firm in the Lord.
What thanksgiving could we render to God for you, for all the joy you give us before our God?
Night and day we pray to him earnestly to let us see your face again and to complete what is still lacking in your faith.
May God himself, our Father, and our Lord Jesus smooth our way to you.
May the Lord make you increase and overflow with love for one another and for all, as we ourselves do toward you.
May he strengthen your hearts and make them blameless in holiness before God our Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all his saints. Amen.

titres.titre: The dead and the coming of the Lord

versets.t: Finally, brothers, you have learned from us how to live so as to please God, and this is indeed how you are already living; we beg you and encourage you in the Lord Jesus: go on making progress.
For you know the instructions we gave you from the Lord Jesus.
What God wills is your sanctification: that you abstain from immorality,
that each of you know how to master his own body in holiness and respect,
without being carried away by passion, like the Gentiles who do not know God.
Let no one, in this matter, wrong his brother or deceive him, for the Lord brings justice for all this, as we have already told you and firmly declared.
God did not call us to impurity, but to holiness.
So whoever rejects this teaching rejects not a man, but God, who gives you his Holy Spirit.
About brotherly love, you have no need for anyone to write to you, for God himself has taught you to love one another,
and this is indeed how you act toward all the brothers throughout Macedonia. But we encourage you, brothers, to do better still:
make it your ambition to live quietly, to mind your own affairs, and to work with your hands, as we have urged you,
so as to lead a worthy life in the eyes of those outside and to be a burden to no one.
Brothers, we do not want to leave you in ignorance about those who have fallen asleep, so that you may not grieve like the others, who have no hope.
For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, let us also believe that God, through Jesus, will bring with him those who have fallen asleep in him.
This is what we declare to you according to the word of the Lord: we, the living, still here for the coming of the Lord, will not go ahead of those who have fallen asleep.
For at a given signal, at the voice of the archangel, at the sound of the trumpet of God, the Lord himself will come down from heaven, and those who have died in Christ will rise first.
Then we, the living, still here, will be caught up together with them on the clouds, to meet the Lord, in the air; and so we will be with the Lord forever.
Comfort one another, then, with these words.
As for the times and the seasons, brothers, you have no need for anyone to write to you:
you yourselves know very well that the day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night.
When people say, 'Peace and security!', that is when ruin will suddenly fall upon them, like labor pains upon a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.
But you, brothers, are not in the darkness, for that day to take you by surprise like a thief.
You are all children of the light, children of the day. We belong neither to the night nor to the darkness.
So let us not sleep like the others, but stay awake and sober.
Those who sleep, sleep at night, and those who get drunk, get drunk at night.
But we, who belong to the day, let us be sober: let us put on faith and love as a breastplate, and the hope of salvation as a helmet.
For God did not destine us for wrath, but to receive salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
who died for us so that, awake or asleep, we might live together with him.
So comfort and build up one another, as you are already doing.
We ask you, brothers: have consideration for those who labor among you, who lead you in the Lord and admonish you.
Surround them with overflowing affection, because of their work. Live in peace among yourselves.
We urge you, brothers: correct those who live in disorder, encourage the fainthearted, support the weak, be patient with everyone.
See that no one repays evil for evil; always seek the good, among yourselves and toward all.
Rejoice always.
Pray without ceasing.
Give thanks in every circumstance, for this is what God wills for you in Christ Jesus.
Do not quench the Spirit,
do not despise prophecies;
examine everything, hold on to what is good,
keep yourselves from every form of evil.
May the God of peace himself sanctify you completely, and may your whole being, spirit, soul, and body, be kept blameless for the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
The one who calls you is faithful: it is he who will bring this about.
Brothers, pray also for us.
Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
I charge you by the Lord: have this letter read to all the brothers.
May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the Church of the Thessalonians, in God our Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ:
grace and peace to you from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
We must give thanks to God at all times for you, brothers, and rightly so, for your faith is growing greatly and the love of each of you for all the others keeps increasing.
And so we ourselves are proud of you among the Churches of God, because of your perseverance and your faith in all the persecutions and trials you endure.
This is the sign of the just judgment of God, who wills to make you worthy of his kingdom, for which you suffer.
For it is just, in the eyes of God, to repay with affliction those who afflict you,
and to give you who are afflicted rest with us, when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven, with the angels of his power,
in a blazing fire, to bring justice upon those who do not know God and those who do not obey the Good News of our Lord Jesus.
They will undergo the punishment of eternal ruin, far from the face of the Lord and from the glory of his power,
on the day when he comes to be glorified in his saints and admired in all who have believed; and you are among them, for you believed our testimony.
This is why we pray without ceasing for you: that our God may make you worthy of his call and bring to fulfillment, by his power, all your resolve to do good and the work of your faith,
so that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and of the Lord Jesus Christ.

titres.titre: Stand firm in the traditions you received

versets.t: Concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering to him, we ask you, brothers:
do not let yourselves be so quickly shaken in mind or alarmed by any inspiration, any word, or any letter said to be from us, as though the day of the Lord were already here.
Let no one deceive you in any way. For first the apostasy must come, and the man of lawlessness must be revealed, the son of perdition,
the adversary who rises up against all that is called God or is worshiped, to the point of seating himself in the sanctuary of God, presenting himself as though he were God.
Do you not remember that I used to tell you this when I was still with you?
And now you know what restrains him, so that he may be revealed only at the appointed time.
For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who now restrains it must first be removed.
Then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will destroy with the breath of his mouth and annihilate by the splendor of his coming.
The coming of this lawless one, by the power of Satan, will be accompanied by all manner of false miracles, signs, and wonders,
and by every deception of wickedness, for those who are perishing because they did not welcome the love of the truth that would have saved them.
This is why God sends them a power of delusion that makes them believe the lie,
so that all who refuse to believe the truth and take pleasure in wickedness may be judged.

But we must give thanks to God at all times for you, brothers loved by the Lord, because God chose you from the beginning for salvation, through the sanctification of the Spirit and faith in the truth.
It is to this that he called you through our Good News, so that you might obtain the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So then, brothers, stand firm, and hold to the traditions you learned from us, whether by word of mouth or by letter.
May our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God our Father, who loved us and gave us, by grace, an eternal consolation and a good hope,
comfort your hearts and strengthen you in every good work and word.
Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may run its course and be glorified, as it is among you,
and that we may be delivered from wicked and perverse people; for faith is not the lot of all.
But the Lord is faithful: he will strengthen you and guard you from the Evil One.
We have, in the Lord, this confidence about you: what we prescribe to you, you are doing and will do.
May the Lord direct your hearts toward the love of God and the perseverance of Christ.
We command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from every brother who leads a disorderly life, contrary to the tradition you received from us.
You know well how you must imitate us: we did not live among you in disorder,
we did not eat anyone's bread for free; on the contrary, in toil and weariness, night and day, we worked so as not to be a burden to any of you.
Not that we do not have the right, but to offer ourselves to you as a model to imitate.
And when we were with you, we gave you this rule: if anyone is unwilling to work, let him not eat either.
Now we hear that some among you are leading a disorderly life, not working, but busybodies in every direction.
To such people, we command and urge, in the Lord Jesus Christ, to work quietly and to eat the bread they have earned.
As for you, brothers, do not grow weary of doing good.
If anyone does not obey what this letter says, take note of him, and no longer associate with him, so that he may be ashamed;
but do not treat him as an enemy, admonish him as a brother.
May the Lord of peace himself give you peace, always and in every way. The Lord be with you all.
The greeting is in my own hand, mine, Paul; it is the mark that distinguishes each of my letters: this is how I write.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.
Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope,
to Timothy, my true child in the faith: grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
When I was leaving for Macedonia, I urged you to stay on at Ephesus so that you might charge certain people not to teach other doctrines,
and not to devote themselves to myths and endless genealogies, which promote arguments rather than the plan of God, which is accomplished through faith.
The aim of this instruction is love, which comes from a pure heart, a good conscience, and a sincere faith.
Some have strayed from these and wandered off into empty talk;
they want to be teachers of the Law, without understanding either what they are saying or the things they so confidently assert.
Now we know that the Law is good, if one uses it lawfully,

aware that the Law is not laid down for the righteous, but for the lawless and the rebellious, the ungodly and sinners, the sacrilegious and the profane, those who strike their father and mother, murderers,
the immoral, homosexuals, slave traders, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is opposed to sound doctrine,
according to the Good News of the glory of the blessed God, which has been entrusted to me.
I give thanks to the one who has strengthened me, Christ Jesus our Lord, for judging me trustworthy and appointing me to his service,
though I was once a blasphemer, a persecutor, a violent man. But mercy was shown to me, because I acted out of ignorance, in my unbelief;
and the grace of our Lord overflowed, along with the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
This saying is sure and worthy of full acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the first.
But mercy was shown to me for this reason, that in me, the first, Christ Jesus might display all his patience, as an example to those who would come to believe in him for eternal life.
To the King of the ages, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
This is the charge I entrust to you, Timothy, my child, in keeping with the prophecies once made about you: relying on them, fight the good fight,
holding on to faith and a good conscience. By rejecting it, some have made shipwreck of their faith;
among them Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have handed over to Satan so that they may learn not to blaspheme.

titres.titre: Men and women in the assembly

versets.t: First of all, then, I urge that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for everyone,
for kings and for all who hold authority, so that we may lead a peaceful and quiet life, in all godliness and dignity.
This is good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior,
who wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
For there is one God, and one mediator between God and mankind: a man, Christ Jesus,
who gave himself as a ransom for all. This is the testimony given at the appointed time,
and it is for this that I was appointed a herald and an apostle (I am telling the truth, I am not lying), a teacher of the nations in faith and truth.
So I want the men everywhere to pray, lifting up holy hands, without anger or dispute.
Likewise, the women should dress decently, adorning themselves with modesty and restraint, not with braided hair, gold, pearls, or costly clothes,
but with good works, as befits women who profess godliness.
Let a woman learn in silence, in full submission.
I do not permit a woman to teach or to take authority over a man; let her keep silent.
For Adam was formed first, then Eve;
and it was not Adam who was deceived, but the woman who, deceived, fell into transgression.
Yet she will be saved through becoming a mother, if she remains in faith, love, and holiness, with modesty.
This saying is sure: if anyone aspires to the office of overseer, he desires a noble task.
The overseer, then, must be beyond reproach, the husband of one wife, sober, level-headed, courteous, hospitable, able to teach;
not a drunkard or a violent man, but kind, peaceable, free from the love of money;
he must manage his own household well, keeping his children in submission, in all dignity.
For if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he care for the Church of God?
He must not be a recent convert, or he may be blinded by pride and fall under the condemnation of the devil.
He must also be well regarded by those outside, so that he does not fall into disgrace and into the devil's trap.
Deacons, likewise, must be worthy of respect, not double-tongued, not given to too much wine, not greedy for dishonest gain,
holding the mystery of the faith with a clear conscience.
Let them first be tested, and then, if they are without reproach, let them serve.
The women, likewise, must be worthy of respect, not slanderers, sober, faithful in everything.
Let deacons be husbands of one wife, managing their children and their own households well.
For those who serve well gain an honorable standing and great confidence in the faith that is in Christ Jesus.
I am writing this to you in the hope of coming to see you soon;
but if I am delayed, you will know how one ought to behave in the household of God, which is the Church of the living God, the pillar and support of the truth.
Yes, great is the mystery of godliness: he was revealed in the flesh, justified in the Spirit, seen by the angels, proclaimed among the nations, believed in throughout the world, taken up in glory.

titres.titre: The deceivers of the last times

versets.t: The Spirit says expressly that in the last times some will turn away from the faith, giving themselves to deceiving spirits and to doctrines of demons,
led astray by the hypocrisy of liars whose consciences are branded with a hot iron,
who forbid marriage and the eating of foods that God created for believers, those who know the truth, to receive with thanksgiving.
For everything God created is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving,
for it is made holy by the word of God and by prayer.
By setting these things before the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished on the words of the faith and of the good doctrine that you have faithfully followed.
Reject the profane myths, those old wives' tales. Train yourself instead for godliness.
For the training of the body is of little use, but godliness is useful for everything: it holds the promise of the present life and of the life to come.
This saying is sure and worthy of full acceptance.
If we labor and struggle, it is because we have set our hope on the living God, the Savior of all, especially of believers.
These are the things you must command and teach.
Let no one despise your youth; instead, be a model for the believers, in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.
Until I come, devote yourself to the reading, to exhortation, to teaching.
Do not neglect the gift of grace that is in you, the one given to you through a prophetic word, when the council of elders laid their hands on you.
Attend to these things, be wholly given to them, so that your progress may be evident to all.
Watch over yourself and over your teaching; be diligent in them, for by doing so you will save both yourself and those who listen to you.
Do not sharply rebuke an older man, but appeal to him as a father, the younger men as brothers,
the older women as mothers, the younger as sisters, in all purity.
Honor widows, those who are truly widows.
But if a widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to practice godliness toward their own family and to repay their parents what they owe them, for this is pleasing to God.
She who is truly a widow, left all alone, has set her hope on God and perseveres night and day in supplications and prayers.
But she who lives for pleasure is dead, even while she lives.
Remind them of these things, so that they may be without reproach.
If anyone does not care for his own, especially for his own family, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
Let a widow be enrolled only if she is at least sixty years old and has had but one husband;
she must be known for her good works: having raised children, shown hospitality, washed the feet of the saints, helped the afflicted, devoted herself to every good work.
But refuse the younger widows; for when their desires draw them away from Christ, they want to marry again,
and so incur guilt for having broken their first pledge.
At the same time, being idle, they get into the habit of going from house to house, and not only idle but gossips and busybodies, saying things they ought not to say.
So I want the younger widows to marry, have children, manage their households, and give the adversary no occasion for slander;
for some have already turned aside to follow Satan.
If a believing woman has widows in her family, let her provide for them, so that the Church is not burdened and can help those who are truly widows.
The elders who lead well deserve double honor, especially those who labor at preaching and teaching.
For Scripture says: you shall not muzzle the ox while it treads out the grain; and: the worker deserves his wages.
Do not accept an accusation against an elder, except on the word of two or three witnesses.
Those who sin, rebuke before all, so that the rest also may feel fear.
I charge you before God, before Christ Jesus, and the chosen angels: observe these things without prejudice, doing nothing out of favoritism.
Do not lay hands on anyone too quickly, and do not take part in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure.
Do not drink only water any longer; take a little wine, because of your stomach and your frequent ailments.
The sins of some are obvious even before the judgment; for others, they come to light only afterward.
Likewise, good works are obvious, and even those that are not cannot remain hidden.

titres.titre: Godliness and the love of money

versets.t: Let all who are under the yoke of slavery consider their masters worthy of all respect, so that the name of God and the doctrine may not be blasphemed.

And those who have believing masters must not despise them on the grounds that they are brothers; rather, let them serve all the better, since those who benefit from their good service are believers and beloved. This is what you must teach and urge.
If anyone teaches otherwise and does not hold to the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and to the doctrine that accords with godliness,
he is a proud man who knows nothing, a mind sick with arguments and quarrels about words, from which come envy, disputes, insults, malicious suspicions,
the endless wrangling of men with corrupt minds, deprived of the truth, who see godliness as a source of profit.
Now godliness is great wealth, when it is content with what it has.
For we brought nothing into the world, and we can take nothing out of it.
If we have food and clothing, that will be enough for us.
Those who want to get rich fall into temptation, into a trap, into a host of foolish and harmful desires that plunge people into ruin and destruction.
For the love of money is a root of all evils; and by giving themselves to it, some have wandered far from the faith and pierced themselves with countless torments.
But you, man of God, flee from all this. Pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, gentleness.
Fight the good fight of faith, take hold of the eternal life to which you were called, you who made your fine profession of faith before many witnesses.
I charge you, before God who gives life to all things and before Christ Jesus who bore witness with his fine confession before Pontius Pilate,
to keep the commandment without stain or reproach until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
which the blessed and only Sovereign will bring about at the appointed time, the King of kings and the Lord of lords,
the only one who possesses immortality, who dwells in unapproachable light, whom no one has seen or can see. To him be honor and eternal power. Amen.
As for the rich of this world, charge them not to be proud and not to set their hope on uncertain riches, but on God, who gives us everything in abundance for our enjoyment.
Let them do good, be rich in fine works, give generously, and be ready to share,
storing up for themselves a fine treasure for the future, so that they may take hold of the true life.
O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you. Turn away from profane chatter and the objections of what is falsely called knowledge;
by professing it, some have strayed from the faith. Grace be with you.

titres.titre: Do not be ashamed of the testimony

versets.t: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, to announce the promise of the life that is in Christ Jesus,
to Timothy, my beloved child: grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
I give thanks to God, whom I serve with a clear conscience as my ancestors did, when I constantly remember you in my prayers, night and day.
Recalling your tears, I long to see you again, so that I may be filled with joy.
I remember your sincere faith, which lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and which, I am sure, lives in you as well.
That is why I remind you: rekindle the gift of God's grace that is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God did not give us a spirit of fear, but a spirit of power, of love, and of self-control.
So do not be ashamed to bear witness to our Lord, or of me, his prisoner; but suffer with me for the Good News, by the power of God.
He is the one who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not because of our works, but according to his own purpose and the grace given to us in Christ Jesus before the eternal ages,
and which now has been revealed through the appearing of our Savior, Christ Jesus: he destroyed death and made life and immortality shine out through the Good News.
It is for this that I was appointed a herald, an apostle, and a teacher.
That is also why I suffer as I do; but I am not ashamed, for I know the one in whom I have put my faith, and I am certain that he has the power to guard what has been entrusted to me until that day.
Take as your model the sound words you heard from me, in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
Guard the good deposit, through the Holy Spirit who dwells in us.
You know this, that all those in Asia have turned away from me, among them Phygelus and Hermogenes.
May the Lord show mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chains.
On the contrary, when he arrived in Rome, he searched for me eagerly and found me.
May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day. And all the services he rendered at Ephesus, you know better than anyone.
You then, my child, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
What you have heard from me before many witnesses, entrust to trustworthy people who will be able in turn to teach others.
Take your share of suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
A soldier on active duty does not get entangled in the affairs of civilian life, so as to please the one who enlisted him.
Likewise, an athlete does not receive the crown unless he has competed according to the rules.
And it is the hardworking farmer who should be the first to receive his share of the crop.
Understand what I am saying: the Lord will give you insight into everything.
Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from the line of David, according to the Good News that I proclaim,
and for which I suffer to the point of chains, like a criminal. But the word of God is not chained.
That is why I endure everything for the sake of the chosen, so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory.
This saying is sure: if we have died with him, we will also live with him;
if we hold firm, we will also reign with him; if we deny him, he too will deny us;
if we are unfaithful, he remains faithful, for he cannot deny himself.
Remind them of these things, charging them before God to avoid quarrels about words: they serve no purpose, except to ruin those who listen.
Do your best to present yourself before God as one tested and approved, a worker who has no need to be ashamed, who rightly handles the word of truth.
Avoid profane chatter, for those who give themselves to it sink deeper and deeper into ungodliness,
and their word eats away like gangrene. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
who have strayed from the truth by claiming that the resurrection has already taken place, and who overturn the faith of some.
Yet the solid foundation laid by God stands firm, bearing this seal: the Lord knows those who are his; and: let everyone who names the name of the Lord turn away from wickedness.
In a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay: some for noble use, others for common use.
If, then, anyone cleanses himself of all this, he will be a vessel for noble use, made holy, useful to the master of the house, ready for every good work.
Flee the passions of youth; pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace, together with those who call on the Lord from a pure heart.
Avoid foolish and senseless debates: you know that they breed quarrels.
Now the servant of the Lord must not quarrel, but be kind toward everyone, able to teach, patient in hardship,
correcting his opponents with gentleness, in the hope that God will grant them to repent and to know the truth,
and that, coming back to their senses, they will escape the trap of the devil, who held them captive to enslave their will to his own.
Know this: in the last days difficult times will come.
For people will be selfish, greedy for money, boastful, proud, blasphemers, rebellious toward their parents, ungrateful, sacrilegious,
heartless, merciless, slanderers, without self-control, brutal, enemies of good,
treacherous, reckless, blinded by pride, loving pleasure more than God,
keeping the appearance of godliness but denying its power. Turn away from such people.
These are the ones who slip into homes and seduce women weighed down with sins, driven by all kinds of passions,
always learning yet never able to arrive at the knowledge of the truth.
Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these people oppose the truth, with corrupt minds, disqualified in the faith.
But they will not get very far, for their folly will become plain to all, as happened with those two men.
You, on the contrary, have closely followed my teaching, my conduct, my purposes, my faith, my patience, my love, my perseverance,
my persecutions, my sufferings, such as came upon me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra. What persecutions I endured! and from all of them the Lord delivered me.
Indeed, all who want to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
As for the wicked and the impostors, they will go from bad to worse, deceiving others and deceived themselves.
You, remain firm in what you have learned and firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it;
from childhood you have known the holy Scriptures, which are able to give you the wisdom that leads to salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
All Scripture is inspired by God and useful for teaching, refuting, correcting, and training in righteousness,
so that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work.
I charge you before God and before Christ Jesus, who is going to judge the living and the dead, by his appearing and his reign:
proclaim the Word, be insistent whether it is convenient or not, refute, warn, encourage, with complete patience and a concern to teach.
For a time will come when people will no longer put up with sound doctrine; following their own desires, and with itching ears, they will gather for themselves a host of teachers,
and, turning away from the truth, they will turn toward myths.
You, in everything, keep a cool head, bear suffering, do your work as a bearer of the Good News, carry out your ministry to the full.
For as for me, I am already being poured out as a libation, and the time of my departure has come.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
From now on there is reserved for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will award to me on that day; and not to me only, but to all who will have loved his appearing.
Do your best to come and join me as soon as possible,
for Demas has deserted me out of love for the present world and has gone to Thessalonica; Crescens has gone to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.
Luke alone is with me. Get Mark and bring him along, for he is useful to me for the ministry.
I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
When you come, bring the cloak I left at Troas with Carpus, and the books, especially the parchments.
Alexander the coppersmith did me a great deal of harm; the Lord will repay him according to his works.
You too, be on your guard against him, for he violently opposed our words.
At my first defense, no one stood by me: everyone deserted me. May it not be held against them.
But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the message might be fully proclaimed and all the nations might hear it; and I was delivered from the lion's mouth.
The Lord will deliver me from every evil work and will save me for his heavenly kingdom. To him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus.
Erastus stayed at Corinth; I left Trophimus sick at Miletus.
Do your best to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, as do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers.
May the Lord be with your spirit. Grace be with you.
Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, to bring God's chosen ones to the faith and to the knowledge of the truth that leads to godliness,
in the hope of eternal life, promised before the beginning of time by the God who does not lie,
and who, at the appointed time, has made his word known through the proclamation entrusted to me by the command of God our Savior:
to Titus, my true child in the faith we share: grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
I left you in Crete so that you might finish setting everything in order and appoint elders in every town, according to my instructions:
each one must be blameless, the husband of one wife, with children who are believers and cannot be charged with wild living or rebellion.
For the overseer, as the steward of God's house, must be blameless: not arrogant, not quick-tempered, not a drunkard, not violent, not greedy for dishonest gain;
but hospitable, a lover of good, level-headed, upright, holy, and self-controlled,
holding firmly to the trustworthy word that agrees with the teaching he received, so that he may be able to encourage others with sound doctrine and to refute those who contradict it.
For there are many who are rebellious, full of empty talk and deceit, especially among the circumcised.
They must be silenced, for they are upsetting whole families, teaching for shameful gain what they ought not to teach.
One of them, their own prophet, said: "Cretans are always liars, vicious beasts, lazy gluttons."
This testimony is true. So rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,
and pay no attention to Jewish myths or to the commands of people who turn away from the truth.
To the pure, everything is pure; but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure: their very minds and consciences are defiled.
They claim to know God, but they deny him by their actions: they are detestable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.
But you, teach what is consistent with sound doctrine.
The older men are to be sober, dignified, level-headed, and sound in faith, in love, and in perseverance.
Likewise, the older women are to conduct themselves as befits a holy life, not given to slander, not enslaved to wine, but teachers of what is good,
so that they may train the young women to love their husbands and their children,
to be level-headed, pure, devoted to their homes, kind, and submissive to their husbands, so that the word of God may not be blasphemed.
In the same way, urge the young men to be level-headed.
In everything show yourself to be a model of good works: in your teaching, show integrity and dignity,
and sound, blameless speech, so that any opponent may be put to shame, having nothing bad to say about us.
Slaves are to be submissive to their masters in everything, seeking to please them and not talking back,
not pilfering anything, but showing complete and genuine faithfulness, so that in every way they may bring honor to the teaching of God our Savior.
For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people,
and it trains us to renounce ungodliness and worldly desires, and to live in the present age with self-control, uprightness, and godliness,
as we wait for the blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,
who gave himself for us, to redeem us from all wrongdoing and to purify for himself a people that is his own, devoted to good works.
This is what you must say; encourage and rebuke with full authority. Let no one look down on you.
Remind everyone to be subject to rulers and authorities, to obey them, to be ready for every good work,
to speak evil of no one, to avoid quarrels, to be gracious, and to show perfect gentleness toward everyone.
For we ourselves were once foolish, disobedient, and led astray, slaves to all kinds of desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful and hating one another.
But when the kindness of God our Savior and his love for humanity appeared,
he saved us, not because of any works of righteousness that we had done, but according to his mercy, through the washing of new birth and the renewal by the Holy Spirit,
whom he poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
so that, justified by his grace, we might become heirs, in hope, of eternal life.
This word is trustworthy, and I want you to insist on it firmly, so that those who believe in God may be careful to excel in good works. This is what is good and beneficial for everyone.
But avoid foolish controversies, genealogies, quarrels, and disputes about the Law: they are useless and pointless.
As for anyone who stirs up divisions, after a first and a second warning, have nothing more to do with him,
knowing that such a person is corrupt and sinful, and stands self-condemned.
When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, do your best to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to spend the winter there.
Do all you can to help Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way, so that they lack nothing.
And let our own people, too, learn to excel in good works to meet urgent needs, so that they may not be unfruitful.
All who are with me send you greetings. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all.
Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, to Philemon, our dear friend and fellow worker,
to Apphia our sister, to Archippus our fellow soldier, and to the church that meets in your house:
grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always thank my God as I remember you constantly in my prayers,
for I hear of your love and of the faith that you have toward the Lord Jesus and for all the saints.
I pray that your fellowship in the faith may become effective, leading you to recognize all the good that is in us for the sake of Christ.
Your love has given me great joy and comfort, for through you, brother, the hearts of the saints have been refreshed.
For this reason, although in Christ I have full freedom to command you to do your duty,
I prefer, for the sake of love, to make an appeal to you. Being what I am, I, Paul, an old man, and now also a prisoner of Christ Jesus,
I appeal to you for my child, the one I have fathered while in chains, Onesimus,
who was once useless to you, but who now is truly useful both to you and to me.
I am sending him back to you, and with him goes my very heart.
I would have liked to keep him with me, so that he might serve me in your place during the chains I bear for the Good News;
but I did not want to do anything without your consent, so that your kindness might not be forced but voluntary.
Perhaps this is why he was separated from you for a while: so that you might have him back forever,
no longer as a slave, but as more than a slave: as a dear brother. He is so much a brother to me; how much more will he be to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
So if you consider me your partner, welcome him as you would welcome me.
And if he has wronged you in any way or owes you anything, charge it to my account.
I, Paul, write this with my own hand: I will repay it, not to mention that you owe me your very self.
Yes, brother, let me gain this benefit from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in Christ.
I write to you confident of your obedience, knowing that you will do even more than I ask.
And at the same time, prepare a guest room for me, for I hope that through your prayers I will be restored to you.
Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends you greetings,
as do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.

titres.titre: God Has Spoken Through the Son
The Son Superior to the Angels

versets.t: In the past God spoke to our fathers through the prophets, at many times and in many ways;
but in these days, which are the last, he has spoken to us through the Son, whom he appointed heir of all things and through whom he also created the worlds.

This Son is the radiance of God's glory and the exact imprint of his being; he sustains the universe by his powerful word. After accomplishing the purification of sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty in the highest heavens,
having become as superior to the angels as the name he has inherited is more excellent than theirs.
For to which of the angels did God ever say, "You are my Son; today I have begotten you"? And again, "I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me"?
And when he brings the firstborn into the world again, he says, "Let all God's angels bow down before him."
Concerning the angels he says, "He makes his angels winds, and his servants a flame of fire."
But to the Son he says, "Your throne, O God, is established for ever and ever, and the scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your kingdom.
You have loved justice and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions."
And again, "You, Lord, laid the foundations of the earth in the beginning, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They will perish, but you remain; they will all wear out like a garment.
Like a cloak you will roll them up, and like a garment they will be changed. But you are the same, and your years will never end."
And to which of the angels did he ever say, "Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet"?
Are they not all spirits charged with a service, sent out for the good of those who are to inherit salvation?

titres.titre: Do Not Neglect So Great a Salvation
The Son Made Man to Save His Brothers

versets.t: This is why we must hold all the more firmly to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.
For if the word spoken through angels held the force of law, and every transgression and disobedience received its just penalty,
how shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? It was first announced by the Lord, and confirmed to us by those who heard him,
while God supported their testimony with signs, wonders, and all kinds of miracles, and with the gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to his will.
For it was not to angels that God subjected the world to come, of which we are speaking.
Someone has testified somewhere, "What is man, that you should remember him, or the son of man, that you should care for him?
You have made him a little lower than the angels; you have crowned him with glory and honor,
and you have put all things under his feet." In subjecting all things to him, God left nothing that is not subject to him. Yet at present we do not yet see everything subject to him.
But we do see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because of the death he suffered; so that by the grace of God he tasted death for everyone.
For it was fitting that God, for whom and through whom all things exist, in bringing many sons to glory, should make the leader who guides them to salvation perfect through sufferings.
For the one who sanctifies and those who are sanctified all have one origin. That is why he is not ashamed to call them brothers,
when he says, "I will proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will sing your praise."
And again, "I will put my trust in him." And again, "Here I am, I and the children God has given me."
Since these children share flesh and blood, he too shared in them in the same way, so that through his death he might render powerless the one who held the power of death, that is, the devil,
and set free those who all their lives had been held in slavery by the fear of death.
For it is not angels he comes to help, but the descendants of Abraham.
So he had to become like his brothers in every way, in order to be a merciful and faithful high priest in the service of God, able to make atonement for the sins of the people.
For since he himself has suffered when tested, he is able to help those who are being tested.
Therefore, holy brothers, who share in a heavenly calling, fix your eyes on Jesus, the apostle and high priest of the faith we profess,
faithful to the one who appointed him, just as Moses was faithful in all God's house.
But Jesus was counted worthy of a glory as far above that of Moses as the builder of a house is honored more than the house itself.
For every house is built by someone, and the one who built all things is God.
Moses, to be sure, was faithful in all God's house as a servant, to bear witness to what was to be spoken later;
but Christ is faithful as a son, over his own house. And we are his house, provided we hold on to the confidence and the pride of our hope.
This is why, as the Holy Spirit says, "Today, if you hear his voice,
do not harden your hearts as on the day of rebellion, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
where your fathers put me to the test and tried me, though they had seen my works
for forty years. That is why I was indignant with that generation, and I said: their hearts are always going astray, and they have not known my ways.
So I swore in my anger: they shall never enter my rest."
Take care, brothers, that none of you has an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God.
Instead, encourage one another every day, as long as it is still called "today," so that none of you is hardened by the deceit of sin.
For we have come to share in Christ, provided we hold firmly to the end the confidence we had at the beginning.
As it is said, "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as on the day of rebellion."
Who were those who heard and rebelled? Was it not all those who came out of Egypt under the leadership of Moses?
And with whom was God indignant for forty years? Was it not with those who had sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
And to whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, if not to those who had disobeyed?
So we see that they could not enter because of their unbelief.

titres.titre: The Rest Promised to the People of God

versets.t: Let us fear, then, that while the promise of entering his rest still stands, any of you should be found to have fallen short.
For the Good News was announced to us just as it was to them; but the word they heard did them no good, because it was not united with faith in those who listened.
We who have believed enter that rest, as God said, "So I swore in my anger: they shall never enter my rest." Yet God's works had been finished since the foundation of the world,
for somewhere he has said this about the seventh day: "And God rested on the seventh day from all his works."
And again in the same passage: "They shall never enter my rest."
So then, since it remains for some to enter it, and since those who first received the Good News did not enter because of their disobedience,
God again sets a day, a "today," saying through David long afterward, as has been said, "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts."
For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later of another day.
So there remains a rest, a Sabbath rest, for the people of God;
for whoever enters God's rest also rests from his own works, as God rested from his.
Let us then be eager to enter that rest, so that no one falls by following the same example of disobedience.
For the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword; it pierces to the point of dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow; it judges the intentions and thoughts of the heart.
Nothing that is created is hidden from his sight; everything is naked and exposed to the eyes of the one to whom we must give an account.
So then, since we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to the faith we profess.
For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses; he was tested in every way, as we are, yet without sin.
Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence, to receive mercy and find grace, so that we may be helped in our time of need.

titres.titre: Christ, High Priest Called by God
Growing to Maturity in the Faith

versets.t: Every high priest is taken from among men and appointed to act on their behalf in the service of God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
He is able to sympathize with the ignorant and the wayward, since he himself is surrounded by weakness;
and it is because of this weakness that he must offer sacrifices for his own sins as well as for those of the people.
No one takes this honor upon himself; he is called to it by God, just as Aaron was.
In the same way, Christ did not take upon himself the glory of becoming a high priest; he received it from the one who said to him, "You are my Son; today I have begotten you."
As he also says in another place, "You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek."
During the days of his mortal life he offered up prayers and pleas, with loud cries and tears, to the one who could save him from death, and he was heard because of his reverence.
Son though he was, he learned obedience through his sufferings;
and once made perfect, he became the source of eternal salvation for all who obey him,
proclaimed by God a high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
On this subject we have much to say, and it is hard to explain, because you have become slow to understand.
By now you ought to be teachers, yet you need someone to teach you the first elements of the words of God all over again; you have come to need milk rather than solid food.
Anyone who still lives on milk does not know the word of righteousness, for he is an infant;
solid food is for the mature, those whose judgment has been trained by practice to distinguish good from evil.
Therefore, leaving behind the elementary teaching about Christ, let us press on toward what is perfect, without laying again the foundations: the renunciation of dead works and faith in God,
the teaching about baptisms and the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment.
And this we will do, if God permits.
For it is impossible, in the case of those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit,
who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the world to come,
and who have then fallen away, to renew them again to repentance, since they are crucifying the Son of God all over again for themselves and holding him up to contempt.
When land drinks in the rain that often falls on it, and produces a crop useful to those for whom it is cultivated, it receives God's blessing;
but if it bears thorns and thistles, it is worthless and near to being cursed, and in the end it is burned.
Yet, beloved, even as we speak this way, we are convinced of better things in your case, things that belong to salvation.
For God is not unjust; he will not forget your work and the love you have shown for his name, in serving the saints, as you still do.
We desire only that each of you show the same zeal, so as to keep your hope full to the very end,
so that you do not grow sluggish, but imitate those who through faith and perseverance inherit the promises.
When God made his promise to Abraham, since he could swear by no one greater than himself, he swore by himself,
saying, "I will surely bless you and multiply you."
And so Abraham, having persevered, obtained what was promised.
People swear by someone greater than themselves, and the oath is for them a guarantee that puts an end to all dispute.
So God, wanting to show the heirs of the promise even more clearly the unchanging nature of his purpose, guaranteed it with an oath,
so that through two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we might be strongly encouraged, we who have fled for refuge by taking hold of the hope set before us.
This hope we hold as an anchor for the soul, sure and firm, reaching beyond the veil,
where Jesus has entered ahead of us as a forerunner, having become a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
This Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, met Abraham as he was returning from the defeat of the kings, and he blessed him;
and Abraham gave him a tenth of everything. His name means first "king of righteousness," and then he is also king of Salem, that is, "king of peace."
Without father, without mother, without genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, made like the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.
Consider how great he is, to whom Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth of the finest spoils.

Those of the sons of Levi who receive the priesthood have, according to the Law, a command to collect a tenth from the people, that is, from their brothers, though they too are descended from Abraham.
But this man, who does not belong to their line, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed the one who held the promises.
And there is no dispute that it is the lesser who is blessed by the greater.
Moreover, here it is mortal men who receive the tenth; there it is someone of whom it is testified that he lives.
And Levi himself, who collects the tenth, so to speak paid it through Abraham,
for he was still in the loins of his ancestor when Melchizedek met him.

Now if perfection had been attainable through the levitical priesthood, under which the people received the Law, what need would there have been for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, rather than according to the order of Aaron?
For when the priesthood is changed, a change of Law necessarily follows.
Now the one of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar:
for it is well known that our Lord came from Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priests.
This becomes even clearer if, in the likeness of Melchizedek, another priest arises,
appointed not by a rule of the flesh, but by the power of an indestructible life.
For this testimony is given of him: "You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek."
So the former rule is set aside because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the Law brought nothing to perfection; and a better hope is introduced, through which we draw near to God.
And this was not done without an oath. The others became priests without an oath;
but he became a priest with an oath from the one who said to him, "The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind: you are a priest forever."
And so Jesus is the guarantor of a better covenant.
Moreover, the former priests were many in number, because death kept them from continuing in office;
but he, because he remains forever, holds a priesthood that does not pass away.
This is why he is able to save completely those who come to God through him, since he always lives to intercede for them.
Such indeed is the high priest we needed: holy, innocent, without stain, set apart from sinners, raised higher than the heavens.
He has no need, like the other high priests, to offer sacrifices day after day, first for his own sins and then for those of the people; this he did once for all when he offered himself.
For the Law appoints as high priests men subject to weakness; but the word of the oath, which came after the Law, appoints the Son, made perfect forever.

titres.titre: The High Priest of the New Covenant

versets.t: The main point of what we are saying is this: we have such a high priest, who has sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
a minister of the sanctuary and of the true tent, the one set up by the Lord and not by man.
Every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices; so this one too must have something to offer.
If he were on earth, he would not even be a priest, since there are already those who offer the gifts according to the Law.

They serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly realities, as Moses was warned when he was about to set up the tent: "See that you make everything," he was told, "according to the pattern shown you on the mountain."
But our high priest has received a ministry as far superior as the covenant he mediates is better, founded on better promises.
For if that first covenant had been faultless, there would have been no need to seek a second.
But God does find fault with them when he says, "The days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah,

not like the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt. Since they did not remain faithful to my covenant, I too abandoned them, says the Lord.

This is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their minds and write them on their hearts; I will be their God, and they will be my people.
No longer will anyone have to teach his fellow citizen or his brother, saying, "Know the Lord," for they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest.
I will forgive their wrongdoing and remember their sins no more."
By speaking of a new covenant, God has made the first one old; and what is aging and growing old is close to disappearing.

titres.titre: The Sanctuary and the Old Worship
The Blood of Christ, Eternal Redemption

versets.t: The first covenant, then, also had regulations for worship and an earthly sanctuary.
A tent had been set up. In the first part, called the holy place, were the lampstand, the table, and the bread of the offering.
Behind the second veil was the part called the Holy of Holies,

which held the golden altar of incense and the ark of the covenant, entirely covered with gold, in which were a golden jar containing the manna, the staff of Aaron that had budded, and the tablets of the covenant;
and above it the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat. But this is not the time to speak of these things in detail.
With everything thus arranged, the priests enter the first part of the tent at all times to perform their service;
but only the high priest enters the second part, and only once a year, and never without blood, which he offers for himself and for the sins the people commit in ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit shows that the way into the sanctuary is not yet open as long as the first tent still stands.
This is a symbol for the present time: the gifts and sacrifices offered there cannot perfect the conscience of the one who offers this worship.
They deal only with food and drink and various washings, regulations of the flesh imposed until the time of reformation.
But Christ has come as high priest of the good things to come; passing through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by human hands, that is, not of this creation,
he entered the sanctuary once for all, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood, obtaining an eternal redemption.
For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are defiled, sanctify them so that their flesh is clean,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself to God without blemish, cleanse our conscience from dead works, so that we may serve the living God!

This is why he is the mediator of a new covenant: through his death, which took place to redeem the transgressions committed under the first covenant, those who are called receive the eternal inheritance that was promised.
For where there is a will, the death of the one who made it must be established;
a will takes effect only after death, since it remains without force as long as the one who made it is alive.
This is why even the first covenant was not inaugurated without the shedding of blood.

When Moses had proclaimed to all the people every commandment of the Law, he took the blood of the calves and goats, with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled the book itself and all the people,
saying, "This is the blood of the covenant that God has commanded for you."
In the same way he sprinkled with blood the tent and all the vessels used in worship.
And according to the Law almost everything is cleansed with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
It was necessary, then, for the copies of the heavenly realities to be purified in this way, but for the heavenly realities themselves to be purified with better sacrifices than these.
For Christ did not enter a sanctuary made by human hands, a mere copy of the true one, but heaven itself, to appear now on our behalf before the face of God.
Nor was it to offer himself again and again, as the high priest enters the sanctuary each year with blood that is not his own;
otherwise he would have had to suffer many times since the foundation of the world. But now, once for all, at the end of the ages, he has appeared to abolish sin by his sacrifice.
And just as it is the lot of men to die once, and after that comes judgment,
so Christ, offered once to bear the sins of the many, will appear a second time, no longer to deal with sin, but to bring salvation to those who are waiting for him.

The Law has only a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the realities; with the same sacrifices, offered continually year after year, it can never make perfect those who draw near.
Otherwise, would they not have stopped being offered? Once cleansed, those who offer this worship would no longer have had any consciousness of sin.
On the contrary, these sacrifices are a yearly reminder of sins,
for it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
This is why Christ, on coming into the world, says, "You wanted neither sacrifice nor offering, but you have prepared a body for me;
you took no pleasure in burnt offerings and sin offerings.
Then I said: Here I am, I have come, O God, to do your will, as it is written of me in the scroll of the book."
First he says, "You wanted neither sacrifices, nor offerings, nor burnt offerings, nor sin offerings, and took no pleasure in them," even though they are offered according to the Law;
then he adds, "Here I am, I have come to do your will." He thus sets aside the first in order to establish the second.
And it is by this will that we have been sanctified, through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ, once for all.
Every priest stands day after day at his service, offering again and again the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.
But this priest, after offering a single sacrifice for sins, sat down forever at the right hand of God,
and now waits for his enemies to be made a footstool for his feet.
For by a single offering he has made perfect forever those whom he sanctifies.
The Holy Spirit also testifies to us; for after saying,
"This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their hearts and write them on their minds,"
he adds, "Their sins and their wrongdoings I will remember no more."
Now where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer any offering for sin.
So then, brothers, since we have confidence to enter the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way that he opened for us through the veil, that is, through his flesh,
and since we have a great priest over the house of God,
let us draw near with a sincere heart, in the fullness of faith, our hearts cleansed from a guilty conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
Let us hold firmly to the profession of our hope, for the one who made the promise is faithful.
Let us look out for one another, to spur each other on to love and good works;
let us not desert our assemblies, as some are in the habit of doing, but let us encourage one another, all the more as you see the Day drawing near.
For if we sin deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains any sacrifice for sins,
but only a fearful expectation of judgment and a raging fire ready to consume the rebellious.
Anyone who rejects the law of Moses dies without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses;

how much worse a punishment, do you think, will be deserved by the one who has trampled on the Son of God, treated as unholy the blood of the covenant that sanctified him, and outraged the Spirit of grace?
For we know the one who said, "Vengeance is mine; I will repay." And again, "The Lord will judge his people."
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
Remember those early days when, after being enlightened, you endured a great and painful struggle:
sometimes made a public spectacle amid insults and afflictions, sometimes standing in solidarity with those who were treated this way.
You suffered along with the prisoners, and you joyfully accepted the seizure of your property, knowing that you have a better and lasting possession.
So do not throw away your confidence; a great reward is attached to it.
For you need perseverance, so that after doing the will of God you may obtain what is promised.
For yet a little while, a very little while, and "the one who is coming will come and will not delay.
My righteous one will live by faith; but if he shrinks back, my soul takes no pleasure in him."
But we are not among those who shrink back to their destruction, but among those who have faith and so save their souls.
Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
It is because of it that the ancients received a good testimony.
By faith we understand that the worlds were formed by the word of God, so that what is seen did not come from what is visible.
By faith Abel offered God a better sacrifice than Cain's; through it he was declared righteous, God bearing witness to his offerings; and through it, though dead, he still speaks.
By faith Enoch was taken up so that he would not see death; he was not found, because God had taken him. Before he was taken up, he was commended as one who had pleased God.
And without faith it is impossible to please God; for whoever draws near to God must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who seek him.

By faith Noah, warned about things not yet seen and moved by holy fear, built an ark to save his household; through it he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes by faith.
By faith Abraham, when called by God, obeyed and set out for a land he was to receive as an inheritance; he set out without knowing where he was going.
By faith he went to live in the promised land as in a foreign country, dwelling in tents, with Isaac and Jacob, heirs of the same promise;
for he was waiting for the city with firm foundations, whose architect and builder is God.
By faith Sarah herself, despite her age, received the power to establish a line of descendants, because she considered faithful the one who had made the promise.
And so from one man, already as good as dead, came descendants as numerous as the stars of heaven and as countless as the grains of sand on the seashore.
It was in faith that they all died, without having received what was promised; they had only seen it and greeted it from afar, confessing that they were strangers and travelers on the earth.
Those who speak this way show clearly that they are seeking a homeland.
If they had been thinking of the one they had left, they would have had time to return;
but it was a better homeland they longed for, the heavenly one. So God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham, when he was tested, offered up Isaac; he who had received the promises was offering his only son,
the one of whom he had been told, "It is through Isaac that your descendants will be named."
He reasoned that God had the power to raise even the dead; and so, figuratively speaking, he received his son back.
By faith, and with an eye to the future, Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau.
By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, at the end of his life, spoke of the exodus of the sons of Israel and gave instructions about his bones.
By faith Moses, at his birth, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they did not fear the king's edict.
By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,
choosing to be mistreated with the people of God rather than to enjoy the fleeting pleasures of sin,
and regarding the humiliation of Christ as greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking to the reward.
By faith he left Egypt, not fearing the anger of the king; he held firm, as though seeing the Invisible One.
By faith he kept the Passover and sprinkled the blood, so that the destroyer would not touch the firstborn of Israel.
By faith they crossed the Red Sea as if on dry land, while the Egyptians, when they tried to do the same, were drowned.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell, after the people had marched around them for seven days.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with the rebellious, because she had welcomed the spies in peace.
What more shall I say? Time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets,
who through faith conquered kingdoms, administered justice, obtained what was promised, shut the mouths of lions,
quenched the fury of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, found strength in weakness, proved valiant in war, and put enemy armies to flight.
Women received back their dead, raised to life again. Some were tortured, refusing release in order to obtain a better resurrection.
Others endured mockery and beatings, and even chains and imprisonment.
They were stoned, sawn in two, put to death by the sword; they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, oppressed, and mistreated,
men of whom the world was not worthy, wandering in deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the ground.
And all of these, though the faith they showed earned them a good testimony, did not receive what was promised,
since God had provided something better for us: they were not to reach perfection apart from us.

titres.titre: Running with Our Eyes Fixed on Jesus

versets.t: So then, since we too are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us throw off every burden and the sin that clings so closely, and let us run with perseverance the race set before us,

looking to Jesus, who opens the way of faith and brings it to completion. Instead of the joy that was offered him, he endured the cross, scorning its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Think of the one who endured such hostility from sinners, so that you do not grow weary and lose heart.
In your struggle against sin you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding your blood,
and you have forgotten the exhortation that addresses you as sons: "My son, do not despise the Lord's discipline, and do not lose heart when he corrects you;
for the Lord disciplines the one he loves, and he chastises every son he receives."
It is for your discipline that you endure: God is treating you as sons. What son is there whom his father does not discipline?
If you were without the discipline in which all share, you would be illegitimate children and not sons.
Besides, we had our earthly fathers to discipline us, and we respected them; shall we not much more submit to the Father of spirits, and so have life?
They disciplined us for a short time, as they thought best; but he does it for our good, so that we may share in his holiness.
At the time, all discipline seems a cause for sorrow rather than joy; but later, to those trained by it, it yields a harvest of peace and righteousness.
So strengthen the drooping hands and the weak knees,
and make straight paths for your feet, so that the lame may not be put out of joint, but rather healed.
Pursue peace with everyone, and holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.
See to it that no one falls short of the grace of God, that no bitter root grows up to cause trouble and defile the many,
and that there is no one immoral or profane like Esau, who for a single meal sold his birthright.
You know that afterward, when he wanted to receive the blessing, he was rejected; he found no way to reverse it, though he sought it with tears.
You have not come to something that can be touched, a blazing fire, or to darkness, gloom, and storm,
or to the sound of a trumpet and a voice whose words made those who heard it beg that no more be said to them.
They could not bear the command that was given: "If even an animal touches the mountain, it must be stoned."
The sight was so terrifying that Moses said, "I am trembling with fear."
But you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to myriads of angels in festal gathering,
to the assembly of the firstborn enrolled in the heavens, to God the judge of all, to the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.

See that you do not refuse the one who is speaking. For if those who refused to listen to the one who warned them on earth did not escape, how much less will we escape if we turn away from the one who speaks from the heavens!
His voice shook the earth then; but now he has made this promise: "Once more I will shake not only the earth, but the heavens as well."
These words, "once more," indicate the removal of what is shaken, that is, of created things, so that what cannot be shaken may remain.
So then, since we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, let us hold on to grace, and through it offer God worship that pleases him, with reverence and awe;
for our God is a consuming fire.
Let brotherly love continue.
Do not forget hospitality, for through it some have welcomed angels without knowing it.
Remember the prisoners, as though you were chained with them, and those who are mistreated, since you too have a body.
Let marriage be honored by all, and the marriage bed kept undefiled, for God will judge the immoral and adulterers.
Keep your life free from the love of money; be content with what you have, for God himself has said, "I will never leave you; I will never forsake you."
So we can say with confidence, "The Lord is my helper; I will not be afraid. What can anyone do to me?"
Remember your leaders, who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their lives, and imitate their faith.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
Do not be led astray by all kinds of strange teachings; it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by foods, which have been of no benefit to those who devote themselves to them.
We have an altar from which those who serve the tent have no right to eat.
The bodies of the animals whose blood is brought by the high priest into the sanctuary as an offering for sin are burned outside the camp.
This is why Jesus too suffered outside the gate, in order to sanctify the people by his own blood.
Let us then go out to him, outside the camp, bearing his humiliation.
For here we have no lasting city, but we are seeking the one that is to come.
Through him, then, let us continually offer God a sacrifice of praise, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name.
And do not forget to do good and to share what you have, for such are the sacrifices that please God.
Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they keep watch over your souls as those who must give an account. Let them do this with joy and not with groaning, for that would be of no benefit to you.
Pray for us, for we are convinced that we have a clear conscience, resolved to conduct ourselves well in every way.
I urge you all the more earnestly to do this, so that I may be restored to you the sooner.
May the God of peace, who brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great Shepherd of the sheep, by the blood of an eternal covenant,
equip you with everything good so that you may do his will, working in us what is pleasing to him, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
I urge you, brothers, to bear with this word of exhortation, for I have written to you only briefly.
Know that our brother Timothy has been released; if he comes soon enough, I will see you together with him.
Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those from Italy send you greetings.
Grace be with you all.
James, servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes of the dispersion: greetings.
Consider it pure joy, my brothers, whenever you meet with trials of every kind,
knowing that the testing of your faith produces perseverance.
And let perseverance finish its work, so that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing.
If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to all generously and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
But let him ask in faith, without wavering; for the one who wavers is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.
Let no such person imagine that he will receive anything from the Lord:
he is a divided man, unstable in all his ways.
Let the brother of humble condition glory in his exaltation,
and the rich man in his lowliness, for he will pass away like the flower of the field.
The sun rises with its scorching heat, it withers the grass, its flower falls, and its lovely appearance is gone; so too will the rich man fade away in the midst of his affairs.
Blessed is the man who perseveres under trial! Having stood the test, he will receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised to those who love him.
Let no one, when tempted, say, "It is God who tempts me." For God cannot be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.
Each person is tempted by his own desire, which lures him and entices him.
Then desire, having conceived, gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is fully grown, brings forth death.
Do not be deceived, my beloved brothers:
every good gift and every perfect grace comes down from above, from the Father of lights, in whom there is no change nor shadow of variation.
Of his own will he brought us forth by a word of truth, so that we might be as the firstfruits of his creatures.
Know this, my beloved brothers: let each one be quick to listen, slow to speak, slow to anger,
for the anger of man does not accomplish the righteousness of God.
Therefore rid yourselves of all filth and every excess of wickedness, and receive with meekness the word planted in you, which is able to save your souls.
But put the word into practice; do not merely listen to it, deceiving yourselves.
