For if anyone listens to the word without putting it into practice, he is like a man who looks at his natural face in a mirror:
he looks at himself, then goes away, and immediately forgets what he was like.
But the one who looks closely into the perfect law, the law of freedom, and holds to it, not to hear it and forget, but to put it into practice, he will be blessed in what he does.
If anyone thinks he is religious without keeping a tight rein on his tongue, he deceives himself, and his religion is worthless.
Religion that is pure and undefiled before God our Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
My brothers, do not mix favoritism with your faith in our Lord of glory, Jesus Christ.
Suppose a man with gold rings and in splendid clothing comes into your assembly, and a poor man in dirty clothing comes in too.
If you pay attention to the one wearing the splendid clothing and say to him, "You, sit here in this good seat," and say to the poor man, "You, stand there," or, "Sit at the foot of my footstool,"
have you not made distinctions among yourselves, becoming judges with evil thoughts?
Listen, my beloved brothers: has God not chosen the poor in the eyes of the world to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom promised to those who love him?
But you, you despise the poor! Is it not the rich who oppress you and drag you before the courts?
Is it not they who blaspheme the noble name that was invoked over you?
Indeed, if you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, "You shall love your neighbor as yourself," you do well.
But if you show favoritism, you commit sin, and the Law condemns you as transgressors.
For whoever keeps the whole Law but stumbles on a single point becomes guilty of all of it.
For he who said, "You shall not commit adultery," also said, "You shall not commit murder." So if, without committing adultery, you commit murder, you are a transgressor of the Law.
Speak and act as those who are going to be judged by a law of freedom.
For judgment is without mercy for the one who has shown no mercy; but mercy triumphs over judgment.
What good is it, my brothers, to say one has faith if one does not have works? Can such faith save?
If a brother or sister is without clothing and lacks daily food,
and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, keep warm, eat your fill," without giving them what the body needs, what good is it?
So too with faith: if it has no works, it is dead in itself.
But someone will say, "You have faith; I have works." Show me your faith without works, and I, by my works, will show you my faith.
You believe that there is one God? You do well. The demons also believe it, and they tremble.
Do you want to understand, foolish man, that faith without works is barren?
Was not Abraham our father justified by works, when he offered his son Isaac on the altar?
You see that faith was working with his works, and that by works faith was brought to its perfection.
So the Scripture was fulfilled: "Abraham had faith in God, and it was counted to him as righteousness," and he was called the friend of God.
You see that a person is justified by works, and not by faith alone.
In the same way, was not Rahab the prostitute justified by works, when she welcomed the messengers and sent them off by another road?
As the body without breath is dead, so faith without works is dead.
Do not be many who become teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will be judged more strictly.
For we all stumble in many ways. If anyone does not stumble in what he says, he is a perfect man, able to keep a tight rein on his whole body.
When we put a bit in the mouths of horses to make them obey us, we also guide their whole body.
Consider ships: so large, driven by fierce winds, they are steered by a very small rudder wherever the pilot wishes.
So too the tongue is a small member, and it boasts of great things. See how small a fire sets ablaze a great forest!
The tongue too is a fire; it is the world of injustice, set among our members: it stains the whole body, it inflames the course of our existence, itself set ablaze by hell.
Every kind of beast and bird, of reptile and sea creature, is being tamed and has been tamed by man;
but the tongue no one can tame: a restless evil, it is full of deadly venom.
With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse men, who are made in the image of God.
From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. This, my brothers, ought not to be so.
Does a spring pour out, from the same opening, both fresh water and bitter?
Can a fig tree, my brothers, produce olives, or a vine figs? Neither can a salty spring give fresh water.
Who among you is wise and understanding? Let his good conduct show his works, in the meekness of wisdom.
But if you have bitter jealousy and a spirit of rivalry in your heart, do not boast and do not lie against the truth.
Such wisdom does not come down from above; it is earthly, carnal, demonic.
For where there is jealousy and rivalry, there is disorder and every evil deed.
The wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, kind, considerate, full of mercy and good fruits, without favoritism or hypocrisy.
And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace, for those who make peace.
Where do the wars come from, where do the quarrels among you come from? Is it not from your passions, which wage war in your members?
You covet and you do not have; you kill, you are jealous and you can obtain nothing; you fight and you make war. You do not have because you do not ask.
You ask and you do not receive, because you ask wrongly, to spend it all on your pleasures.
Adulterers! Do you not know that friendship with the world is enmity against God? Whoever wants to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.
Or do you think the Scripture speaks in vain when it says that God jealously longs for the spirit he has made to dwell in us?
But he gives an even greater grace; that is why it says, "God resists the proud, but to the humble he gives his grace."
Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee far from you.
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, sinners; sanctify your hearts, you divided men.
Acknowledge your wretchedness, mourn, and weep; let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to sadness.
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and he will lift you up.

Do not speak evil of one another, brothers. Whoever speaks evil of a brother or judges his brother speaks evil of the Law and judges the Law; but if you judge the Law, you are no longer a keeper of the Law, but its judge.
There is only one lawgiver and judge, the one who can save and destroy. But you, who are you to judge your neighbor?
Now to you who say, "Today or tomorrow we will go to such and such a city, we will spend the year there, we will do business and make profits,"
you who know nothing of tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist, which appears for a moment and then disappears.
Instead you ought to say, "If the Lord wills, we will live and do this or that."
But here you are, boasting in your presumption; all such boasting is evil.
So whoever knows how to do good and does not do it commits a sin.

titres.titre: Patience until the coming of the Lord
Prayer and the anointing of the sick

versets.t: Now to you, the rich! Weep and wail over the miseries that are coming upon you.
Your riches have rotted, your garments are moth-eaten.
Your gold and silver are corroded, and their corrosion will testify against you and devour your flesh like fire. You have hoarded, in the last days!
Behold, it cries out, the wages of the laborers who harvested your fields and of which you defrauded them; and the cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of hosts.
You have lived on the earth in luxury and pleasure; you have fattened yourselves for the day of slaughter.
You have condemned, you have killed the righteous one: he does not resist you.
Be patient, then, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. See the farmer: he waits for the precious fruit of the earth, patient over it until the autumn and spring rains.
You too, be patient, strengthen your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is near.
Do not grumble against one another, brothers, so that you may not be judged: behold, the judge is standing at the door.
Take as models of suffering and patience, brothers, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.
See: we call blessed those who have stood firm. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and you have seen the end the Lord brought about for him, for the Lord is full of tenderness and mercy.
Above all, my brothers, do not swear, neither by heaven, nor by earth, nor by any other oath. Let your yes be yes, and your no, no, so that you may not fall under judgment.
Is any of you suffering? Let him pray. Is anyone joyful? Let him sing.
Is any of you sick? Let him call the elders of the Church, and let them pray over him, after anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord.
The prayer of faith will save the sick person, and the Lord will raise him up; if he has committed sins, they will be forgiven him.
Confess your sins, then, to one another, and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. The prayer of the righteous, in its fervor, has great power.
Elijah was a man like us; he prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and no rain fell on the land for three years and six months.
Then he prayed again, and heaven gave rain, and the earth brought forth its fruit.
My brothers, if any of you strays from the truth and someone brings him back,
know that whoever brings a sinner back from his wandering will save his soul from death and cover a multitude of sins.
Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen ones who live as strangers, scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in the sanctification of the Spirit, to obey Jesus Christ and to be sprinkled with his blood: grace and peace to you in abundance.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! In his great mercy he has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven for you,
you whom the power of God guards through faith, for a salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
In this you rejoice, even though for a little while you may still have to suffer through various trials,
so that the tested worth of your faith, more precious than perishable gold, which is nonetheless tested by fire, may prove to be for your praise, glory, and honor when Jesus Christ is revealed.
Though you have not seen him, you love him; though you do not yet see him, you believe in him, and you rejoice with a joy inexpressible and full of glory,
certain of obtaining the goal of your faith: the salvation of your souls.
Concerning this salvation the prophets searched and inquired, those who prophesied about the grace that was to be yours.

They sought to discern the time and the circumstances that the Spirit of Christ within them pointed to, when he testified in advance to the sufferings destined for Christ and the glory that would follow them.

It was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but you, in the things that have now been announced to you by those who proclaimed the Good News to you through the Holy Spirit sent from heaven. Even the angels long to look into these things.
Therefore, with your minds alert, be sober; set all your hope on the grace that will be brought to you when Jesus Christ is revealed.
As obedient children, do not conform to the desires of former times, when you lived in ignorance;
but, like the Holy One who called you, be holy yourselves in all your conduct,
for it is written: "Be holy, because I am holy."
And if you call on as Father the one who judges each person impartially according to their works, live in reverent fear during the time of your exile.
You know that it was not with perishable things, silver or gold, that you were ransomed from the empty way of life inherited from your ancestors,
but with precious blood, that of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ,
known in advance before the foundation of the world, and revealed at the end of the ages for your sake.
Through him you believe in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope are in God.
By obeying the truth you have purified your souls for a sincere love of your brothers and sisters; so love one another wholeheartedly, intensely,
for you have been born anew, not from perishable seed but from imperishable, through the word of God, living and enduring.
For "all flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flower of the field: the grass withers, the flower falls,
but the word of the Lord endures forever." And this word is the Good News that was announced to you.

titres.titre: The Living Stone and the People of God
The Example of the Suffering Christ

versets.t: So rid yourselves of all malice, all deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and all slander;
like newborn infants, long for the pure milk of the word, so that through it you may grow toward salvation,
if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is good.
Come to him, the living stone, rejected by men but chosen and precious before God;
and you yourselves, like living stones, let yourselves be built into a spiritual house, for a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices pleasing to God through Jesus Christ.
For this is in Scripture: "See, I lay in Zion a cornerstone, chosen and precious; whoever puts their faith in it will not be put to shame."
To you who believe, then, the honor; but for the unbelieving, "the stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,
a stone of stumbling and a rock of scandal." They stumble because they disobey the word; this is what they were destined for.

But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people God has made his own, so that you may proclaim the mighty deeds of the one who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light;
you who once were not a people, but now are the people of God; you who had not received mercy, but now have received mercy.
Beloved, I urge you, as strangers and exiles, to keep away from the desires of the flesh, which wage war against the soul.
Conduct yourselves well among the pagans, so that, even where they slander you as evildoers, they may give glory to God when they see your good works, on the day of his visitation.
Submit yourselves to every human authority for the sake of the Lord: whether to the king, as supreme,
or to governors, sent by him to punish evildoers and to praise those who do good.
For it is the will of God that by doing good you should silence the ignorance of foolish people.
Live as free people, not using freedom as a cloak to cover malice, but as servants of God.
Honor everyone, love your brothers and sisters, fear God, honor the king.
You servants, submit to your masters with all respect, not only to the good and gentle but also to those who are harsh.
For it is a grace to endure, out of regard for God, sufferings borne unjustly.
For what credit is there in enduring blows when you have done wrong? But to endure suffering while doing good, this is a grace before God.
To this you have been called, for Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example so that you might follow in his footsteps.
He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth;
when he was insulted, he did not return the insult; when he suffered, he did not threaten, but entrusted himself to the one who judges justly;
he bore our sins in his body on the wood, so that, dead to sin, we might live for righteousness. By his wounds you have been healed.
For you were straying like sheep, but now you have returned to the shepherd and guardian of your souls.
In the same way, you wives, submit to your husbands, so that, if some refuse to believe the word, they may be won over without a word by the conduct of their wives,
when they see your pure and reverent life.
Let your adornment not be outward, braided hair, gold jewelry, elaborate clothes,
but the hidden self of the heart, the imperishable adornment of a gentle and peaceful spirit: this is what is precious before God.
This is how the holy women of old adorned themselves, those who hoped in God, submitting to their husbands.
Such was Sarah, who obeyed Abraham and called him her lord. You have become her daughters, if you do good and let no fear trouble you.
In the same way, you husbands, live together with understanding, as with a more delicate being; honor your wife, coheir with you of the grace of life, so that nothing may hinder your prayers.
Finally, all of you, be of one mind and one heart, loving one another as brothers and sisters, tender and humble.
Do not repay evil with evil, or insult with insult; on the contrary, bless, for it is to this that you have been called, to receive a blessing as your inheritance.
For "whoever wants to love life and see happy days, let them keep their tongue from evil and their lips from deceitful words;
let them turn away from evil and do good, let them seek peace and pursue it.
For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears attentive to their prayer; but the face of the Lord is set against those who do evil."
And who will harm you if you devote yourselves to what is good?
But even if you should suffer for righteousness, blessed are you! Do not fear their threats, and do not be troubled;
but in your hearts sanctify Christ as Lord. Always be ready to defend the hope that is in you before anyone who asks you to account for it,
but with gentleness and respect, keeping a good conscience, so that, even where you are slandered, those who insult your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame.
For it is better to suffer for doing good, if that is the will of God, than for doing evil.
Christ himself died once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, in order to lead you to God; put to death in the flesh, he was brought to life in the Spirit.
It was in him that he went to proclaim his message to the spirits in prison,
to those who long ago had refused to believe, when the patience of God waited, in the days of Noah, while the ark was being built, in which a few, eight persons, were saved through the water.

It is this water that now saves you in turn through baptism, of which it was the figure; not the removal of dirt from the body, but the pledge to God of a good conscience, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
who is at the right hand of God, having ascended into heaven, with the angels, sovereignties, and powers made subject to him.
Since Christ suffered in the flesh, arm yourselves also with the same resolve: whoever has suffered in the flesh is done with sin,
so as to live the time that remains in the flesh no longer according to human desires but according to the will of God.
You have spent enough time in the past doing the will of the pagans, living in debauchery, lust, drunkenness, orgies, carousing, and the criminal worship of idols.
They find it strange that you no longer run with them into the same flood of dissipation, and they insult you.
They will have to give an account to the one who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
For this is why the Good News was announced even to the dead, so that, though judged in the flesh according to human standards, they might live according to God in the spirit.
The end of all things is near. So be level-headed and sober, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer.
Above all, have a fervent love for one another, for love covers a multitude of sins.
Practice hospitality toward one another without grumbling.
Let each one, according to the grace received, put it at the service of others, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.

If anyone speaks, let it be as the word of God; if anyone serves, let it be with the strength that God supplies, so that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong glory and power forever and ever. Amen.
Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal that is taking place among you to test you, as though something strange were happening to you.
Rejoice, rather, insofar as you share in the sufferings of Christ, so that you may also be filled with joy and gladness at the revelation of his glory.
If you are insulted for the name of Christ, blessed are you, for the Spirit of glory, the Spirit of God, rests upon you.
Let none of you suffer as a murderer, a thief, an evildoer, or as a meddler in other people's affairs.
But if it is as a Christian, let them not be ashamed; let them rather give glory to God for that name.
For this is the time when judgment begins with the household of God. And if it begins with us, what will be the end of those who refuse to believe the Good News of God?
And if the righteous are saved only with difficulty, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?
So let those who suffer according to the will of God entrust their souls to him, the faithful Creator, while doing good.
So I urge the elders among you, I who am an elder like them, a witness of the sufferings of Christ and a sharer in the glory that is ready to be revealed:
shepherd the flock of God entrusted to you, watching over it, not by compulsion but willingly, according to God; not for shameful gain but with devotion;
not lording it over those in your charge, but becoming examples to the flock.
And when the chief shepherd appears, you will receive the crown of glory that does not fade.
In the same way, you who are young, submit to the elders. And all of you, toward one another, clothe yourselves with humility, for "God opposes the proud, but to the humble he gives his grace."
So humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that he may lift you up in due time.
Cast all your cares on him, for he takes care of you.
Be sober, keep watch. Your adversary, the devil, prowls like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour.
Resist him, firm in the faith, knowing that the same sufferings are being endured by your brothers and sisters throughout the world.

The God of all grace, who has called you to his eternal glory in Christ, after you have suffered a little while, will himself restore you, strengthen you, make you strong, and set you on a firm foundation.
To him be the power forever and ever. Amen.
Through Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother, I have written to you briefly, to encourage you and to testify that this is the true grace of God in which you stand firm.
She who is in Babylon, chosen like you, greets you, as does Mark, my son.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.

titres.titre: The Testimony of the Apostles and the Prophets

versets.t: Simeon Peter, servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have received, through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ, a faith as precious as ours:
grace and peace to you in abundance, through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.
His divine power has given us everything that leads to life and godliness, through the knowledge of the one who called us by his own glory and power.
Through them he has granted us his precious and very great promises, so that through them you may become sharers in the divine nature, escaping the corruption that desire spreads in the world.
For this very reason, make every effort to add virtue to your faith, and to virtue knowledge,
and to knowledge self-control, and to self-control perseverance, and to perseverance godliness,
and to godliness brotherly affection, and to brotherly affection love.
For if these qualities are yours and abound in you, they will keep you from being idle or unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Whoever lacks them is blind, shortsighted, having forgotten the cleansing of their past sins.
So, brothers and sisters, be all the more eager to confirm your call and election; if you do this, you will never stumble.
In this way you will be richly granted entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
This is why I will always remind you of these things, even though you know them and are established in the truth you now have.
I consider it right, as long as I am in this tent, to keep you alert by my reminders,
knowing that I will soon leave it, as our Lord Jesus Christ has made known to me.
But I will make sure that after my departure you will be able, at any time, to recall these things.
For it was not by following cleverly devised fables that we made known to you the power and the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ; we were eyewitnesses of his majesty.
For he received from God the Father honor and glory when, from the majestic Glory, this voice came to him: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I have placed all my love."
This voice, coming from heaven, we ourselves heard when we were with him on the holy mountain.
So the word of the prophets is confirmed for us; you do well to hold fast to it, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
Know this above all: no prophecy of Scripture is a matter of private interpretation,
for no prophecy was ever brought by human will; it was carried along by the Holy Spirit that men spoke on behalf of God.

There were false prophets among the people; in the same way, there will be false teachers among you, who will secretly introduce destructive doctrines, going so far as to deny the Master who bought them, and bringing sudden ruin upon themselves.
Many will follow their debauchery, and because of them the way of truth will be slandered.
Out of greed they will exploit you with deceitful words; but their condemnation, long ago pronounced, is not idle, and their ruin does not sleep.
For if God did not spare the angels who had sinned, but cast them down into the abyss, handing them over to dungeons of darkness, where they are kept for judgment;
if he did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah, the herald of righteousness, with seven others, when he unleashed the flood on a world of the ungodly;
if he reduced to ashes the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, condemning them to destruction, as an example to the ungodly of ages to come;
and if he rescued the righteous Lot, worn down by the unbridled conduct of those debauched men,
for this righteous man, living among them, had his soul tormented day after day by the lawless deeds he saw and heard:
then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial and to keep the unrighteous under punishment until the day of judgment,
especially those who, in impure desire, run after the flesh and despise Sovereignty. Bold and arrogant, they do not tremble to insult the Glories,
whereas the angels, though greater in strength and power, do not bring an insulting judgment against them before the Lord.
But these people, like irrational beasts, born to be caught and destroyed, insult what they do not understand; they will perish by their own corruption,
receiving the wages of their unrighteousness. They find their pleasure in reveling in broad daylight in debauchery; blots and blemishes, they delight in their deceptions while feasting with you.
Their eyes full of adultery, insatiable for sin, they seduce unsteady souls; their hearts trained in greed, they are children of a curse.
They have left the straight path and gone astray, following the way of Balaam, son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness,
but was rebuked for his fault: a dumb beast, speaking with a human voice, halted the prophet's madness.
These people are springs without water, clouds driven by the storm; the gloom of darkness is reserved for them.
With pompous and empty talk, they seduce, through the desires of the flesh and debauchery, those who are barely escaping from a life of error.
They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves of corruption; for a person is a slave to whatever dominates them.

Indeed, if those who, through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, had escaped the defilements of the world, let themselves be caught and dominated by them again, their last condition becomes worse than the first.
It would have been better for them never to have known the way of righteousness than, having known it, to turn away from the holy commandment that had been handed on to them.
What happens to them is what the proverb says, truly: "The dog returns to what it has vomited," and, "The washed sow returns to wallow in the mud."

titres.titre: The Coming of the Day of the Lord

versets.t: Beloved, this is now the second letter I am writing to you. In both of them, I stir up your sound understanding by my reminders,
so that you may remember the words spoken long ago by the holy prophets, and the commandment of the Lord and Savior, handed on by your apostles.
Know this above all: in the last days will come mockers full of scorn, driven by their own desires,
saying: "Where is the promise of his coming? Since our ancestors died, everything remains as it was from the beginning of creation."
They deliberately forget that the heavens existed long ago, and an earth drawn out of the water and held together in the midst of the water by the word of God;
and that through these the world of that time perished, flooded by the water.
But the heavens and the earth of the present, by the same word, are kept for fire, reserved for the day of judgment and the ruin of the ungodly.
There is one thing, beloved, that you must not forget: for the Lord, a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like a day.
The Lord is not slow in fulfilling his promise, as some think; he is patient with you, not wanting anyone to be lost, but wanting all to come to conversion.
The day of the Lord will come like a thief; then the heavens will vanish with a roar, the elements will be dissolved in fire, and the earth, with all its works, will be laid bare.
Since all this is to be dissolved in this way, how holy and godly your lives must be,
as you wait for and hasten the coming of the day of God, when the blazing heavens will be dissolved and the elements will melt in the fire!
But, according to his promise, we wait for new heavens and a new earth, where righteousness dwells.
In this expectation, beloved, do everything to be found by him without spot, without blame, in peace.
And regard the patience of our Lord as your salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul wrote to you, according to the wisdom given to him.

He does so in all his letters where he speaks of these matters; in them there are some passages hard to understand, which the ignorant and the unsteady distort, as they do the rest of the Scriptures, to their own destruction.
You, then, beloved, forewarned, be on your guard, lest, carried away by the error of the ungodly, you lose your firm footing.
Grow instead in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be the glory, now and to the day of eternity. Amen.
That which was from the beginning, that which we have heard, that which we have seen with our own eyes, that which we have looked upon and our hands have touched, concerning the Word of life,
for the Life was made manifest, and we have seen it; we bear witness to it and we proclaim to you the eternal Life, which was with the Father and was made manifest to us;
that which we have seen and heard we proclaim to you as well, so that you too may be in communion with us. And our communion is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.
And we write this so that our joy may be complete.
This is the message we have heard from him and proclaim to you: God is light, and in him there is no darkness at all.
If we say that we are in communion with him while walking in darkness, we are lying and we do not act in the truth.
But if we walk in the light, as he himself is in the light, we are in communion with one another, and the blood of Jesus, his Son, cleanses us from all sin.
If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
If we confess our sins, he who is faithful and just forgives us our sins and cleanses us from all injustice.
If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a liar, and his word is not in us.
My little children, I am writing this to you so that you may not sin. And if anyone does sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ, the just one.
He himself is the sacrifice of atonement for our sins, and not for ours only, but for those of the whole world.
This is how we know that we know him: if we keep his commandments.
Whoever says, "I know him," while not keeping his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
But in whoever keeps his word, the love of God is truly made perfect; this is how we know that we are in him.
Whoever claims to remain in him must conduct himself as he himself conducted himself.
Beloved, it is not a new commandment that I am writing to you, but an old commandment, which you have had from the beginning; this old commandment is the word you have heard.
And yet it is a new commandment that I am writing to you, which is true in him and in you, for the darkness is passing away and already the true light is shining.
Whoever claims to be in the light while hating his brother is still in the darkness.
Whoever loves his brother remains in the light, and there is nothing in him to make him stumble.
But whoever hates his brother is in the darkness; he walks in it not knowing where he is going, for the darkness has blinded his eyes.
I am writing to you, little children, because your sins are forgiven you for the sake of his name.
I am writing to you, fathers, because you know the one who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have conquered the evil one.

I have written to you, children, because you know the Father. I have written to you, fathers, because you know the one who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, because the word of God remains in you, and because you have conquered the evil one.
Do not love the world, nor what is in the world. If anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him;
for all that is in the world, the craving of the flesh, the craving of the eyes, and the pride of riches, does not come from the Father, but from the world.
Now the world is passing away, and its craving with it; but whoever does the will of God remains forever.
Little children, it is the last hour. You have heard that the antichrist is to come; and now, already, there are many antichrists: by this we know that it is the last hour.
They went out from among us, but they were not of us; if they had been of us, they would have remained with us. But it had to be made clear that not all are of us.
You, however, have received the anointing that comes from the Holy One, and you all know.
I have written to you, not because you do not know the truth, but because you do know it, and because no lie comes from the truth.
Who is the liar but the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the antichrist: the one who denies the Father and the Son.
Everyone who denies the Son does not have the Father either; whoever confesses the Son has the Father also.
As for you, let what you have heard from the beginning remain in you. If what you have heard from the beginning remains in you, you too will remain in the Son and in the Father.
And this is the promise that he himself has made to us: eternal life.
This is what I have written to you about those who are leading you astray.

As for you, the anointing you have received from him remains in you, and you have no need for anyone to teach you; but as his anointing teaches you everything, and is true, without any lie, remain in him, just as it has taught you.
And now, little children, remain in him, so that when he is made manifest we may have confidence and not be covered with shame, cast far from him, at his coming.
If you know that he is just, recognize that everyone who practices justice is born of him.
See what love the Father has given us: to be called children of God! And that is what we are. If the world does not know us, it is because it did not know him.
Beloved, we are children of God now, and what we shall be has not yet been made manifest. We know that, when it is made manifest, we shall be like him, for we shall see him as he is.
And everyone who has this hope in him purifies himself, as he himself is pure.
Everyone who commits sin also commits iniquity, for sin is iniquity.
Now you know that he was made manifest to take away sins, and that there is no sin in him.
Everyone who remains in him does not sin; everyone who sins has not seen him and has not known him.
Little children, let no one lead you astray. Whoever practices justice is just, as he himself is just.
Whoever commits sin is of the devil, for the devil has sinned from the beginning. It was to destroy the works of the devil that the Son of God was made manifest.
Everyone who is born of God does not commit sin, for God's seed remains in him; and he cannot sin, because he is born of God.
This is how the children of God and the children of the devil are recognized: everyone who does not practice justice is not of God, nor is the one who does not love his brother.
For this is the message you have heard from the beginning: that we should love one another.
Not like Cain, who was of the evil one and slaughtered his brother. And why did he slaughter him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's were just.
Do not be surprised, brothers, if the world hates you.
We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love our brothers. Whoever does not love remains in death.
Everyone who hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life remaining in him.
This is how we have come to know love: he laid down his life for us. We too must lay down our lives for our brothers.
If anyone has the goods of the world and, seeing his brother in need, closes his heart to him, how could the love of God remain in him?
Little children, let us not love with words or with the tongue, but in deed and in truth.
This is how we shall know that we are of the truth, and before him we shall set our hearts at rest;
for if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and he knows everything.
Beloved, if our heart does not condemn us, we have confidence before God,
and whatever we ask, we receive from him, because we keep his commandments and do what pleases him.
And this is his commandment: to believe in the name of his Son Jesus Christ and to love one another, as he commanded us.
Whoever keeps his commandments remains in God, and God in him. And this is how we know that he remains in us: by the Spirit he has given us.
Beloved, do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they come from God, for many false prophets have gone out into the world.
This is how to recognize the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses Jesus Christ come in the flesh is of God;
and every spirit that does not confess Jesus is not of God: it is the spirit of the antichrist, which you have heard is coming, and it is already now in the world.
You, little children, are of God, and you have conquered them, for the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world.
They are of the world; that is why they speak according to the world, and the world listens to them.
We are of God; whoever knows God listens to us, whoever is not of God does not listen to us. This is how we recognize the spirit of truth and the spirit of error.
Beloved, let us love one another, for love comes from God, and everyone who loves is born of God and knows God.
Whoever does not love has not known God, for God is love.
This is how the love of God was made manifest among us: God sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him.
This is what love consists in: not that we have loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son as the sacrifice of atonement for our sins.
Beloved, if God has loved us in this way, we too must love one another.
No one has ever seen God; but if we love one another, God remains in us, and his love is brought to perfection in us.
This is how we know that we remain in him, and he in us: he has given us of his Spirit.
And we have seen, and we testify, that the Father sent the Son as Savior of the world.
Whoever confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him, and he in God.
And we have come to know the love that God has for us, and we have believed in it. God is love; whoever remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.
This is how love is brought to perfection in us, so that we may have confidence on the day of judgment: that as he is, so also are we in this world.
There is no fear in love; on the contrary, perfect love casts out fear, for fear has to do with punishment; whoever fears is not brought to perfection in love.
We love, because he loved us first.
If anyone says, "I love God," while hating his brother, he is a liar; for whoever does not love his brother, whom he sees, cannot love God, whom he does not see.
And this is the commandment we have from him: "Whoever loves God must also love his brother."

titres.titre: The faith that conquers the world

versets.t: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God; and everyone who loves the one who begets loves also the one who is born of him.
This is how we know that we love the children of God: when we love God and keep his commandments.
For to love God is to keep his commandments; and his commandments are not burdensome,
since everything that is born of God is victorious over the world. And the victory that has conquered the world is our faith.
Who then is victorious over the world but the one who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?
He is the one who came by water and by blood, Jesus Christ; not with the water only, but with the water and with the blood. And it is the Spirit that bears witness, for the Spirit is the truth.
So there are three that bear witness:
the Spirit, the water, and the blood; and these three point to the same end.
If we accept the testimony of men, the testimony of God is greater; now this is the testimony of God: he has borne witness to his Son.
Whoever believes in the Son of God has this testimony within himself. Whoever does not believe God makes him a liar, since he has not believed the testimony that God has borne to his Son.
And this is that testimony: God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life.
I have written this to you so that you may know that you have eternal life, you who believe in the name of the Son of God.
And this is the confidence we have before him: if we ask anything according to his will, he listens to us.
And if we know that he listens to us, whatever we ask, we know that we already have what we have asked of him.

If anyone sees his brother commit a sin that does not lead to death, let him pray, and God will give him life, for those whose sin does not lead to death. There is a sin that leads to death; it is not for that one that I say to pray.
All injustice is sin, but there is a sin that does not lead to death.
We know that everyone who is born of God does not sin; but the one who is born of God keeps himself, and the evil one does not touch him.
We know that we are of God, and that the whole world lies in the power of the evil one.
We know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding to know the True One; and we are in the True One, in his Son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and eternal life.
Little children, keep yourselves from idols.
The Elder, to the chosen Lady and to her children, whom I love in the truth, and not I alone, but also all those who have come to know the truth,
because of the truth that remains in us and will be with us forever.
With us will be grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and from Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
I had great joy in finding some of your children walking in the truth, according to the commandment we have received from the Father.
And now, I ask you, Lady, not as a new commandment that I would write to you, but the one we have had from the beginning: let us love one another.
And love consists in walking according to his commandments. This is the commandment, as you have heard it from the beginning: walk in love.
For many deceivers have gone out into the world, who do not confess Jesus Christ come in the flesh: this is the deceiver and the antichrist.
Be on your guard, so that you do not lose the fruit of our labor, but receive a full reward.
Everyone who goes too far and does not remain in the teaching of Christ does not have God; whoever remains in this teaching has both the Father and the Son.
If anyone comes to you without bringing this teaching, do not receive him into your house and do not say to him, "Greetings!";
for whoever says to him, "Greetings!" shares in his evil works.
I have much to write to you, but I have not wanted to do so with paper and ink; I hope to come to you and speak with you face to face, so that our joy may be complete.
The children of your sister, the chosen one, greet you.
The Elder, to Gaius, the beloved, whom I love in the truth.
Beloved, I pray that in every way you may be well and in good health, as your soul is well.
I had great joy when brothers came to bear witness to your truth, to the way you walk in the truth.
I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in the truth.
Beloved, you act faithfully in all that you do for the brothers, and this for strangers.
They have borne witness to your charity before the Church; you will do well to provide for their journey in a manner worthy of God.
For it is for the Name that they set out, receiving nothing from the pagans.
We must therefore support such men, so as to be their fellow workers in the service of the truth.
I wrote a few words to the Church; but Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, does not receive us.

That is why, when I come, I will call to mind the deeds he is doing, spreading malicious talk against us; and not content with that, he himself does not welcome the brothers, he prevents those who would like to do so, and drives them out of the Church.
Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good. Whoever does good is of God; whoever does evil has not seen God.
As for Demetrius, everyone bears witness to him, and the truth itself does too; we also bear witness to him, and you know that our testimony is true.
I have much to write to you, but I do not want to do so with ink and pen.
I hope to see you soon, and we will speak face to face.
Peace to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends, each by name.

titres.titre: Against the ungodly who have crept in

versets.t: Jude, servant of Jesus Christ, brother of James, to those who are called, beloved in God the Father and kept for Jesus Christ:
to you, mercy, peace, and love in abundance.
Beloved, I greatly desired to write to you about our common salvation, when I found myself compelled to write and urge you to contend for the faith once for all handed down to the saints.

For certain men have slipped in among you, whose condemnation was written long ago; they are ungodly people who turn the grace of our God into debauchery and who deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.
I want to remind you, though you already know all this, that Jesus, after saving the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who refused to believe;
and that the angels who did not keep their rank, but abandoned their own dwelling, he holds in reserve for the judgment of the great day, bound with eternal chains, in the darkness.
Likewise Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighboring cities, which gave themselves over to the same debauchery and went after strange flesh, stand as an example, undergoing the penalty of eternal fire.
In the same way, these people, in their delusions, defile the flesh, despise Dominion, and insult the Glories.

Yet the archangel Michael, when he was disputing with the devil and contending over the body of Moses, did not dare to bring an insulting judgment against him; he said only, "May the Lord rebuke you!"
But these people insult what they do not understand, and what they do know by instinct, like unreasoning beasts, leads them to their ruin.
Woe to them! They have followed the way of Cain, they have thrown themselves, for a wage, into the error of Balaam, they have perished in the rebellion of Korah.
They are reefs at your love feasts, where they feast shamelessly, caring only for themselves; waterless clouds, carried along by the winds; autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, uprooted;
wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shame; wandering stars for whom the gloom of darkness is reserved forever.
It was also about them that Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied, saying, "Behold, the Lord has come with his holy myriads,
to judge all men and to convict all the ungodly of all the works of ungodliness they have committed and of all the harsh words that ungodly sinners have spoken against him."
These are malcontents who complain about their lot, led by their desires; their mouths utter arrogant words, and they flatter people for their own advantage.
But you, beloved, remember the words foretold by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.
They told you, "In the last times there will be scoffers, led by their ungodly desires."
These are the ones who cause divisions, men given over to their nature, devoid of the Spirit.
But you, beloved, build yourselves up on your most holy faith, pray in the Holy Spirit,
keep yourselves in the love of God, awaiting the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ, unto eternal life.
On some, who waver, have mercy;
save others by snatching them from the fire; on still others have mercy mixed with fear, hating even the garment stained by the flesh.
To him who is able to keep you from all falling and to present you, blameless and in gladness, before his glory,
to the only God, our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, majesty, strength, and power, before all ages, now and for all ages. Amen.

titres.titre: The vision of the Son of Man

versets.t: The revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave him to show his servants what must soon take place. He made it known by sending his angel to his servant John,
who bears witness to the word of God and to the testimony of Jesus Christ: all that he saw.
Blessed is the one who reads, and those who hear the words of this prophecy and keep what is written in it, for the time is near.
John, to the seven churches of Asia: grace and peace to you from him who is, who was, and who is to come, and from the seven spirits who are before his throne,
and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth. To him who loves us, who has freed us from our sins by his blood,
and who has made us a kingdom, priests for God his Father, to him be glory and power for ever and ever. Amen.
Behold, he is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see him, even those who pierced him; and all the tribes of the earth will beat their breasts because of him. Yes. Amen.
I am the Alpha and the Omega, says the Lord God, he who is, who was, and who is to come, the Almighty.
I, John, your brother, who share with you the distress, the kingship, and the perseverance in Jesus, was on the island called Patmos, because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.
I was seized by the Spirit on the Lord's day, and I heard behind me a mighty voice, like a trumpet,
which said: Write in a book what you see, and send it to the seven churches: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea.
I turned to see the voice that was speaking to me; and when I had turned, I saw seven golden lampstands,
and in the midst of the lampstands one like a son of man, clothed in a long robe and girded at the chest with a golden sash.
His head and his hair were white as white wool, like snow; his eyes were like a flame of fire;
his feet were like bronze glowing in a furnace; his voice was like the sound of many waters.
In his right hand he held seven stars; from his mouth came a sharp, two-edged sword; and his face was like the sun shining in full strength.
When I saw him, I fell at his feet as though dead; but he laid his right hand on me and said: Do not be afraid. I am the first and the last,
the living one. I was dead, and behold, I am alive for ever and ever; I hold the keys of death and of the realm of the dead.
Write, then, what you have seen, what is now, and what must take place afterward.

Here is the hidden meaning of the seven stars that you saw in my right hand, and of the seven golden lampstands: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches.
To the angel of the church in Ephesus, write: These are the words of him who holds the seven stars in his right hand, who walks among the seven golden lampstands.
I know your works, your toil and your perseverance; I know that you cannot bear the wicked, that you have tested those who claim to be apostles but are not, and have found them to be liars.
You have perseverance; you have suffered for my name, and you have not grown weary.
But I have this against you: you have abandoned your first love.
Remember from where you have fallen, repent, and return to your first works. Otherwise, I will come to you and remove your lampstand from its place, unless you repent.
Yet you have this in your favor: you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
Let the one who has ears listen to what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who conquers I will give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God.
To the angel of the church in Smyrna, write: These are the words of the first and the last, who was dead and came to life again.
I know your distress and your poverty, and yet you are rich; I know the slander of those who claim to be Jews but are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.

Do not fear what you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison, to test you, and you will have ten days of distress. Be faithful unto death, and I will give you the crown of life.
Let the one who has ears listen to what the Spirit says to the churches. The one who conquers will suffer no harm from the second death.
To the angel of the church in Pergamum, write: These are the words of him who has the sharp, two-edged sword.

I know where you dwell: where the throne of Satan is. And you hold fast to my name; you did not deny my faith, even in the days of Antipas, my faithful witness, who was put to death among you, where Satan dwells.

But I have a few charges against you: you have there people attached to the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to set a trap for the sons of Israel, so that they would eat meat sacrificed to idols and give themselves over to immorality.
So you too have people attached in the same way to the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
Repent, then. Otherwise, I will come to you without delay, and I will make war against them with the sword of my mouth.

Let the one who has ears listen to what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who conquers I will give some of the hidden manna; I will give him a white stone, and on that stone is written a new name, which no one knows except the one who receives it.
To the angel of the church in Thyatira, write: These are the words of the Son of God, who has eyes like a flame of fire and feet like glowing bronze.
I know your works, your love, your faith, your service, and your perseverance, and your recent works more numerous than the first.

But I have this against you: you tolerate Jezebel, that woman who calls herself a prophetess, who teaches and leads my servants astray, drawing them into immorality and into eating meat sacrificed to idols.
I gave her time to repent, but she refuses to repent of her immorality.
Behold, I am about to throw her onto a bed of suffering, and those who commit adultery with her into great distress, unless they repent of her works.
I will strike her children dead, and all the churches will know that I am the one who searches minds and hearts; and I will repay each of you according to your works.
But to you, the rest in Thyatira, who do not follow this teaching and have not learned what they call the deep things of Satan, I say: I lay no other burden on you;
only hold fast to what you have until I come.
To the one who conquers, to the one who keeps my works to the end, I will give authority over the nations:
he will rule them with a rod of iron, as one shatters vessels of clay.
Just as I myself have received it from my Father. And I will give him the morning star.
Let the one who has ears listen to what the Spirit says to the churches.
To the angel of the church in Sardis, write: These are the words of him who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars. I know your works: you are reputed to be alive, but you are dead.
Become watchful, and strengthen what remains and was about to die, for I have not found your works complete before my God.
Remember, then, how you received and heard the word; keep it and repent. If you do not stay awake, I will come like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I will come upon you.
Yet you have a few people in Sardis who have not soiled their garments; they will walk with me, in white, for they are worthy.
The one who conquers will be clothed in white garments; I will not blot his name out of the book of life, and I will proclaim his name before my Father and before his angels.
Let the one who has ears listen to what the Spirit says to the churches.
To the angel of the church in Philadelphia, write: These are the words of the Holy One, the True One, who has the key of David, who opens and no one will shut, who shuts and no one will open.
I know your works. Behold, I have set before you a door that no one can shut, for you have little strength, and yet you have kept my word and have not denied my name.

Behold what I will do with the synagogue of Satan, with those who claim to be Jews but are not, but are lying: I will make them come and bow down at your feet, and they will know that I have loved you.
Because you have kept the word of my perseverance, I too will keep you from the hour of trial that is about to come upon the whole world, to test the inhabitants of the earth.
I am coming soon: hold fast to what you have, so that no one may take your crown.

The one who conquers, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God, and he will never leave it. I will write on him the name of my God and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem that comes down from heaven, from my God, and my own new name.
Let the one who has ears listen to what the Spirit says to the churches.
To the angel of the church in Laodicea, write: These are the words of the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the source of God's creation.
I know your works: you are neither cold nor hot. If only you were cold or hot!
So, because you are lukewarm, neither hot nor cold, I am about to spit you out of my mouth.
You say, 'I am rich, I have made my fortune, I need nothing,' and you do not know that you are wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked.

I advise you to buy from me gold refined in fire, so that you may become rich; white garments to clothe yourself and cover the shame of your nakedness; and ointment to anoint your eyes, so that you may see.
All those whom I love, I rebuke and correct. So be zealous and repent.
Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in to him, I will share the meal with him, and he with me.
The one who conquers, I will seat with me on my throne, just as I myself conquered and sat down with my Father on his throne.
Let the one who has ears listen to what the Spirit says to the churches.
After this I looked: a door stood open in heaven, and the voice I had first heard, like a trumpet speaking to me, said: 'Come up here, and I will show you what must take place afterward.'
At once I was seized by the Spirit; and behold, a throne stood in heaven, and on the throne someone was seated.
The one who was seated had the brilliance of jasper and carnelian, and around the throne was a rainbow with the brilliance of an emerald.
Around the throne were twenty-four thrones, and on these thrones sat twenty-four elders, clothed in white, with golden crowns on their heads.
From the throne came flashes of lightning, voices, and peals of thunder; before the throne burned seven torches of fire, which are the seven spirits of God.
Before the throne was something like a sea of glass, like crystal. In the center, around the throne, were four living creatures, covered with eyes in front and behind.
The first living creature resembled a lion, the second a young bull, the third had a face like a man's, and the fourth resembled an eagle in full flight.

The four living creatures each had six wings, all covered with eyes, outside and within; and day and night, without rest, they say: 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord, the Almighty God, who was, who is, and who is to come.'
And whenever the living creatures give glory, honor, and thanksgiving to the one who sits on the throne, to the one who lives for ever and ever,
the twenty-four elders fall down before the one who sits on the throne, they worship the one who lives for ever and ever, and they cast their crowns before the throne, saying:
'You are worthy, our Lord and our God, to receive glory, honor, and power; for it is you who created all things: by your will they existed and were created.'

titres.titre: The Lamb and the scroll with seven seals

versets.t: Then I saw, in the right hand of the one who sits on the throne, a scroll written on the inside and on the outside, sealed with seven seals.
And I saw a mighty angel proclaiming in a loud voice: 'Who is worthy to open the scroll and to break its seals?'
But no one, in heaven or on earth or under the earth, could open the scroll or look into it.
And I wept much, because no one had been found worthy to open the scroll or to look into it.
Then one of the elders said to me: 'Do not weep. Behold: he has conquered, the lion of the tribe of Judah, the shoot of David; he will open the scroll and its seven seals.'

And I saw, in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, in the midst of the elders, a Lamb standing, as though slain; he had seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent out over all the earth.
He came and took the scroll from the right hand of the one who sits on the throne.

When he had taken the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each holding a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.
And they sang a new song: 'You are worthy to take the scroll and to open its seals, for you were slain, and by your blood you ransomed for God people from every tribe, language, people, and nation.
You have made them a kingdom and priests for our God, and they will reign on the earth.'
Then I looked, and I heard the voice of a multitude of angels around the throne, the living creatures, and the elders; they numbered myriads of myriads, thousands of thousands.
They said in a loud voice: 'Worthy is the Lamb who was slain to receive power, riches, wisdom, strength, honor, glory, and blessing.'

And every creature in heaven, on earth, under the earth, and on the sea, all that is in them, I heard saying: 'To the one who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be praise, honor, glory, and power for ever and ever.'
And the four living creatures said: 'Amen.' And the elders fell down and worshiped.
And I saw the Lamb open the first of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures say in a voice like thunder: 'Come!'
And I looked: a white horse appeared; its rider held a bow; a crown was given to him, and he went out as a conqueror, to conquer still.
When the Lamb opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature say: 'Come!'
Then out came another horse, fiery red; to its rider it was granted to take peace from the earth, so that people would slaughter one another; and a great sword was given to him.
When the Lamb opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature say: 'Come!' And I looked: a black horse appeared; its rider held a scale in his hand.

And I heard, in the midst of the four living creatures, what sounded like a voice saying: 'A measure of wheat for a day's wages, and three measures of barley for a day's wages; but do not touch the oil and the wine.'
When the Lamb opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature say: 'Come!'

And I looked: a pale horse appeared; its rider is named Death, and the realm of the dead followed him. They were given power over a quarter of the earth, to kill by the sword, by famine, by plague, and by the wild beasts of the earth.
When the Lamb opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been slaughtered because of the word of God and the testimony they had borne.
They cried out in a loud voice: 'How long, holy and true Master, before you do justice and avenge our blood on the inhabitants of the earth?'

Then each of them was given a white robe, and they were told to wait a little longer, until the number of their fellow servants and their brothers, who were to be killed as they had been, should be complete.
And I saw, when he opened the sixth seal: there was a great earthquake, the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, the whole moon became like blood,
and the stars of heaven fell to the earth, as a fig tree, shaken by a strong wind, drops its unripe figs.
The sky was rolled up like a scroll, and every mountain and every island was torn from its place.
Then the kings of the earth, the great men, the commanders, the rich, the powerful, every slave and every free man hid themselves in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains,
and they said to the mountains and the rocks: 'Fall on us and hide us from the face of the one who sits on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb;
for it has come, the great day of their wrath, and who can stand?'

titres.titre: The vast crowd in white robes

versets.t: After this I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth; they held back the four winds of the earth, so that no wind would blow on the earth, or on the sea, or on any tree.
And I saw another angel rising from the east, holding the seal of the living God. He cried out in a loud voice to the four angels who had been given power to harm the earth and the sea:
'Do not harm the earth, or the sea, or the trees, until we have marked with the seal, on the forehead, the servants of our God.'
And I heard the number of those who were marked with the seal: one hundred forty-four thousand, from all the tribes of the sons of Israel.
From the tribe of Judah, twelve thousand marked with the seal; from the tribe of Reuben, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Gad, twelve thousand;
from the tribe of Asher, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Naphtali, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Manasseh, twelve thousand;
from the tribe of Simeon, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Levi, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Issachar, twelve thousand;
from the tribe of Zebulun, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Joseph, twelve thousand; from the tribe of Benjamin, twelve thousand marked with the seal.

After this I saw a vast crowd, which no one could count, from every nation, tribe, people, and language. They stood before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands,
and they cried out in a loud voice: 'Salvation belongs to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb.'
And all the angels stood around the throne, the elders, and the four living creatures; they fell down before the throne, faces to the ground, and worshiped God,
saying: 'Amen! Praise, glory, wisdom, thanksgiving, honor, power, and strength be to our God for ever and ever. Amen.'
Then one of the elders spoke and said to me: 'These who are clothed in white robes, who are they, and where have they come from?'
I answered him: 'My lord, it is you who know.' He said to me: 'These are the ones who come from the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
That is why they are before the throne of God and serve him day and night in his sanctuary; and the one who sits on the throne will spread his tent over them.
They will hunger no more, they will thirst no more; neither the sun nor any scorching heat will strike them,
for the Lamb who is at the center of the throne will be their shepherd and will lead them to the springs of the waters of life; and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.'

titres.titre: The seventh seal and the trumpets

versets.t: When the Lamb opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.
And I saw the seven angels who stand before God; they were given seven trumpets.
Then another angel came and stood near the altar, holding a golden censer; he was given much incense, to offer, with the prayers of all the saints, on the golden altar that is before the throne.
And the smoke of the incense rose, with the prayers of the saints, from the hand of the angel, before God.
Then the angel took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and threw it on the earth; and there were peals of thunder, voices, flashes of lightning, and an earthquake.
Then the seven angels who held the seven trumpets prepared to sound them.
The first sounded: there came hail and fire, mixed with blood, thrown on the earth. A third of the earth was burned up, a third of the trees was burned up, and all green grass was burned up.
The second angel sounded: something like a great blazing mountain was thrown into the sea, and a third of the sea became blood.
A third of the living creatures in the sea died, and a third of the ships was destroyed.
The third angel sounded: from heaven fell a great star, burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water.
The name of this star is Wormwood. A third of the waters turned to wormwood, and many people died from these waters that had become bitter.

The fourth angel sounded: a third of the sun was struck, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that they were darkened by a third; the day lost a third of its light, and the night likewise.

And I looked, and I heard an eagle flying at the zenith, crying out in a loud voice: 'Woe, woe, woe to the inhabitants of the earth, because of the remaining trumpet blasts, those of the three angels who are about to sound!'
The fifth angel sounded: I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to the earth; it was given the key to the shaft of the abyss.
It opened the shaft of the abyss, and from the shaft rose smoke like that of a great furnace; the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke of the shaft.
Out of the smoke came locusts that spread over the earth; they were given power like that of the scorpions of the earth.
They were ordered not to harm the grass of the earth, or any green plant, or any tree, but only the people who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads.
They were not allowed to kill them, but to torment them for five months; and the torment they cause is like that of a scorpion when it stings a person.
In those days people will seek death and will not find it; they will long to die, and death will flee from them.
These locusts resembled horses equipped for battle; on their heads were what looked like crowns of gold; their faces were like human faces,
their hair like women's hair, their teeth like lions' teeth;
they had breastplates, like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the din of many horse-drawn chariots rushing into battle.
They have tails and stingers like those of scorpions, and it is in their tails that they have the power to harm people for five months.
They have as king the angel of the abyss; his name, in Hebrew, is Abaddon, and in Greek, Apollyon, the Destroyer.
The first woe is past. Behold, two more woes are still to come.
The sixth angel sounded: I heard a voice coming from the four horns of the golden altar that is before God;
it said to the sixth angel, the one who held the trumpet: 'Release the four angels bound near the great river, the Euphrates.'
Then the four angels were released, held ready for the hour, the day, the month, and the year when they were to kill a third of humankind.
The number of the cavalry troops was two hundred million; I heard their number.

And this is how the horses and their riders appeared to me in the vision: they had breastplates the color of fire, of hyacinth, and of sulfur; the heads of the horses were like lions' heads, and from their mouths came fire, smoke, and sulfur.
By these three plagues, the fire, the smoke, and the sulfur that came from their mouths, a third of humankind was killed.
For the power of these horses is in their mouths and in their tails; their tails, like serpents, have heads, and it is with them that they do harm.

The rest of humankind, those who had not been killed by these plagues, still did not renounce the works of their hands; they did not stop worshiping the demons and the idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk.
And they did not repent of their murders, or their sorceries, or their immorality, or their thefts.

titres.titre: The angel and the little scroll

versets.t: Then I saw another mighty angel come down from heaven, wrapped in a cloud, with a rainbow over his head; his face was like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire.
He held in his hand a little scroll, open. He set his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land,
and he cried out in a loud voice, like a lion roaring. When he had cried out, the seven thunders sounded their voices.
After the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to write, but I heard a voice from heaven saying: 'Keep secret what the seven thunders have said; do not write it down.'
Then the angel I had seen standing on the sea and on the land raised his right hand toward heaven
and swore by the one who lives for ever and ever, who created heaven and all it contains, the earth and all it contains, and the sea and all it contains: there will be no more delay;
but in the days when the seventh angel makes his voice heard, when he sounds the trumpet, then the mystery of God will be accomplished, as he announced to his servants the prophets.
And the voice I had heard from heaven spoke to me again: 'Go, take the open scroll in the hand of the angel who stands on the sea and on the land.'
I went to the angel and asked him to give me the little scroll. He said to me: 'Take it, and devour it; it will be bitter in your stomach, but in your mouth it will be sweet as honey.'
I took the little scroll from the hand of the angel and devoured it: in my mouth it was sweet as honey, but when I had swallowed it, my stomach was filled with bitterness.
Then I was told: 'You must prophesy again about many peoples, nations, languages, and kings.'
Then I was given a reed, like a measuring rod, and told: 'Get up and measure the temple of God, the altar, and those who worship there.
But the outer court of the temple, leave it aside, do not measure it, for it has been handed over to the nations, and they will trample the holy city for forty-two months.
And I will grant my two witnesses to prophesy, clothed in sackcloth, for one thousand two hundred sixty days.'
These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth.
If anyone tries to harm them, fire comes out of their mouths and devours their enemies; yes, if anyone tries to harm them, this is how he must perish.

They have the power to shut the sky, so that no rain falls during the days of their prophecy; they have power over the waters, to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with every kind of plague, as often as they wish.
When they have finished their testimony, the beast that rises from the abyss will make war against them, will conquer them, and will kill them.
Their corpses will lie in the square of the great city, symbolically called Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord was crucified.
People from every people, tribe, language, and nation will gaze at their corpses for three and a half days and will not allow them to be laid in a tomb.
The inhabitants of the earth will rejoice over them, they will celebrate and send gifts to one another, for these two prophets had tormented the inhabitants of the earth.
But after the three and a half days, a breath of life from God entered them; they stood up on their feet, and great fear fell on those who were watching them.
And they heard a mighty voice from heaven, saying to them: 'Come up here.' And they went up to heaven in the cloud, before the eyes of their enemies.
At that hour there was a great earthquake: a tenth of the city collapsed, seven thousand people perished in the quake, and the rest, seized with terror, gave glory to the God of heaven.
The second woe is past; behold, the third woe is coming soon.
The seventh angel sounded, and there were loud voices in heaven, saying: 'The kingship of the world has passed to our Lord and to his Christ, and he will reign for ever and ever.'
Then the twenty-four elders, seated before God on their thrones, fell down with their faces to the ground and worshiped God,
saying: 'We give you thanks, Lord, Almighty God, you who are and who were, for you have seized your great power and established your reign.

The nations had raged, but your wrath has come, and the time for judging the dead, the time to reward your servants the prophets, the saints, and those who fear your name, small and great, and to destroy those who destroy the earth.'
Then the sanctuary of God in heaven was opened, and the ark of his covenant appeared in his sanctuary; and there were flashes of lightning, voices, peals of thunder, an earthquake, and a heavy hail.
A great sign appeared in heaven: a woman, clothed with the sun, the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.
She was pregnant, and she cried out in the pain and labor of giving birth.
Another sign appeared in heaven: a great fiery red dragon, with seven heads and ten horns, and on its heads seven diadems.
Its tail swept away a third of the stars of heaven and hurled them to the earth. The dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, to devour her child the moment it was born.
She gave birth to a son, a male child, who is to shepherd all the nations with a scepter of iron. But her child was caught up to God and to his throne,
and the woman fled into the wilderness, where God has prepared a refuge for her, so that there she might be nourished for one thousand two hundred and sixty days.
Then there was a battle in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon. The dragon and its angels fought back,
but they were not the stronger, and there was no longer any place for them in heaven.
